name: Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case
detailed_description: Check out Blazing Griffin's upcoming game Check out other investigations of Hercule Poirot! About the Game From the brilliant mind of the BAFTA Award-Winning studio, Blazing Griffin, get ready in 2023 for a new adventure as the famous detective Hercule Poirot travels to London for a seemingly simple task of delivering a painting for an exhibition, that will be unfortunately stolen during the grand opening. For the first time ever, players will have the opportunity to team up with Poirot’s beloved sidekick in the books, Hastings, as they uncover a new mystery. Expérience a new location, adventure, and partner in this exciting next chapter of Hercule Poirot in his youth. In this detective adventure game, you will take on the role of the famous detective, Hercule Poirot, as he joins forces with Lloyd's of London to ensure the transportation, protection, and sale of a valuable painting of Mary Magdalene. The painting is to be the centerpiece of a new exhibit at a London Museum, featuring other works of ecclesiastical art on loan from Brussels. As an employee of Lloyd's of London, your colleague, Hastings, will assist you in handling the insurance of the artworks and the sale of the painting. Upon arriving at the museum, you will meet with the new owner of the painting, Mortimer Ailsworth, and the curator of the museum, Evelyn Warbeck. Use the resources at your disposal to examine the security and protect the painting from any potential threats. One week later, a Preview Gala will take place where all of the main characters will be in attendance. However, things take an unexpected turn when the painting is stolen from under everyone's noses. Your sharp detective skills will be useful to uncover the truth and find the culprit behind the theft. Will you be able to solve the mystery and retrieve the stolen painting? FEATURES Continue the journey in the Award-winning saga with the second episode, set in London. Discover iconic locations in London as you play as the famous detective Hercule Poirot and experience the thrill of being a detective and solve the mystery with investigation features such as interviewing suspects and collecting evidence. Immerse yourself in a dedicated original story, with fully voiced characters in English, French, and German. A script faithful to the Agatha Christie's original material, as you uncover the story and characters of Poirot's youth. A brand-new mystery Written by Blazing Griffin Studio comes a gripping new adventure for Poirot with a whole new cast of characters to challenge the great detective. Witnesses and Suspect Interrogations Solve mysteries and challenge suspects using the new match puzzle system to spot inconsistencies on the spot. Environment and Item Inspection Explore all new environments and get up close with new first person inspection puzzles for a more cinematic view of the scenes. Mindmaps and Character Profiles The game’s trademark mindmaps return allowing you to ese Poirot’s famous little grey cells to build challenging mindmaps and then draw the correct links that can solve the case. The same now applies to the various suspects as Poirot gathers facts and information about each one to build detailed character profiles, key to solving the case and finding the true criminal among them.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm rating this game positive since I'm a fanboy of Poirot and I genuinely had fun playing it, however there are quite a few issues and "mixed" rating would probably be deserved.In general TLC plays very similarly to the previous title with some changes here and there. In my review of the first game I said it had potential and it was a good foundation to build upon. Sadly after finishing the sequel I don't see any meaningful progress. I feel like the developers listened to the feedback and tried to open the game a little and make it less linear. Unfortunately it was done without too much consideration and resulted in spreading the game too much, having a few illogical conversations or investigations due to me doing things in different order than assumed.Due to the "scope" of the game we also don't get to know the characters that well meaning I didn't really get attached to them. The game feels wider, but shallower with less content and generally shorter.To not be entirely negative I like the addition of analyses and matching to conversations and the main theme is really nice, it reminds me theme of the TV show. Voice acting was also really good.As a side note: at the moment the game is riddled with technical bugs. Nothing game breaking, especially with chapter select, but I think QA wasn't as thorough as in the previous game.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoyed the previous Hercule Poirot games, this was a big disappointment. It was far too short (my time is a few hours longer than I actually spent playing due to my having a nap and leaving the game running) and really boring. The characters looked like they were from an old game though the backgrounds were nice. One area - Theatre Square - was very annoying to visit since you had to slowly walk down the street and then back down it every time. I genuinely did not care about the characters or the plot at all in all honesty. If it had been a random new detective and not Hercule Poirot himself, I think I may very well have given up on the game. There were at least 2 points where I got hopelessly stuck and could not figure out how to move on - the answer to the first one I found in a YT vid and the other was just me doing everything over and over again until I could move on. Very much doubt I will ever play this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this. A huge fan of murder mysteries, Poirot and Adventure games,  the first game was a decent enough game albeit with some mechanical flaws and a story that was  just shy of admittedly High agatha christie standards.The sequel, however, could be summed up in one word - clunky. It feels like 20 years of refinement of the genre has been undone, with the game playing as awkwardly as bad point & click from the mid nineties. Movement is incredibly slow, talking to characters is just a hassle due to seemingly randomized times when you can skip a dialogue you have already read and when you just miss out on the rest of the conversation. I'm maybe 30% through the game and even if the story would pick up, I still could not recommmend this to anyone.I get a feeling dvelopment was very rushed. I bought this on release but will not do so with future titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case

_childDocuments_.review: I think the total percentage score for this game is unjustified as there are certainly worse games than this one, however this game is a tad mediocre. Take the first game, The First Cases, apply a new lick of paint and characters, and remove interrogations, and you have The London Case. The story is fine but, coupled with the repetitive gameplay, the whole experience is a bit bland and I was never really gripped, but I was happy to play on. On the plus side, I did not encounter a single bug during my ~10 hour playthrough like other reviews referred to so either I was very lucky or the game was since been patched from the earlier reviews. I bought the game on the 30% off sale and still struggle to justify that the purchase was well spent; if I apply the generic £1 per hour rule the game has failed in this regard. With the game's length, it has to be story and gameplay to win it back but it's just mediocre. It's not terrible, however, and you can still enjoy the story and deductions and feel that the game is worth the cost if this was on sale for around £10. If, like me, you love Poirot and other detective games, then maybe it's worh a try if you have money to spare as there are way worse games to spend your cash on.TLDR: overpriced because it's mediocre but the accumulated review percentage score makes it look way worse than it actually is.

_childDocuments_.review: As I really enjoyed playing the previous game "the first cases", I kind of expected the same joy from "the london case". But I really disappointed now after finishing this game, because the character's motions have some bugs like keeping walking on the same point not stopping, and mouse-clicking points are unstable to find some evidences by myself (anyway, I succeeded to find them out, though). And I faced multi-endings playing "the first cases", but "the london case" has only lineal story-line to meet only one ending, which makes players just be like audience, not "active story-weaving player" at all. My expectation on the new version of "oriental express" is now a bit lower than before. However, I want to compliment on your effort to make cinematic scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: short and easy but too buggy for comfort.The game at its core is ...fine. Not great, not terrible. A little weaker than the previous one: The First Cases but also feels more ambitious, with more varied environments than TFC's house in the prologue and a single mansion for the entire rest of the game.The game overall is short. My playtime of under 7 hours already includes my replaying one chapter to investigate a sequence break I ran into earlier, and replaying the better part of another, lengthy chapter to chase down an achievement I missed in my playthrough for the sake of closure.Initially, my biggest gripe with the game was the return of utterly awful facial animations from The First Cases; I'd hoped they'd improve this particularly weak link for the sequel. I ran into some annoying bugs before long, however, so I gave the game a few months to patch them out between August last year and now. Nearly three quarters of a year later, the game is still badly in need of thorough polish and bug-squashing. Even today, it doesn't feel fit for release. Whether it was rushed to bail out an ailing publisher or to beat another Poirot game (the film tie-in Murder on the Orient Express) to market by mere weeks, I couldn't say, but it feels like either of those had to have been the case.What kind of bugs are there? Objectives don't match the tasks required to progress (e.g., you're told to talk to a certain character but all you can say to them is a goodbye, instead you have to find and examine a specific item at a specific spot), interaction hotspots are unmarked/unlabelled, Poirot moves his mouth in some spoken lines that are meant to be his thoughts (with comedic effect, like when he mutters his intention to manipulate his interlocutor right to their face before proceeding to do so), mild sequence breaks (the worst in the penultimate chapter, when talking to a character before developing some photographs through a series of interactions skips the whole process and goes straight to discussing the revelations in the contents of a picture you've yet to produce, robbing you of making some important environmental observations), Poirot struggling to get into position to examine an object or interact with a door, subtitles not matching the spoken line, and plenty more.

_childDocuments_.review: A stark step backwards from its predecessor, Hercule Poirot: The First Cases. I bought this on the strength of that game which I loved and while Poirot's voice actor makes a welcome return, the awful animations let him and everyone else down. Instead of the lovely character art in the dialogue boxes we got last time, we get characters staring blankly into space, lip movements not syncing with what's been spoken (or not moving at all), characters sometimes not even appearing on the screen when you're speaking to them, etc.... I feel like the actors and the animations are in two completely different universes. Plus there are weird glitches and bugs which pop up too. Simply put, it feels like it's an unfinished game and the charm we got in The First Cases is merely a memory. Disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of point&click games & oldschool detective stories. Bought this because the other games like "First Cases" were decent.This one is not. It's rather a disapointment. Both graphics and gameplay feel unfinished. Very clunky models and animations. Zero consequences for wrong deductions and heavy focus on conversations.It's more like clicking yourself through an interactive book, rather than playing a full fletched P&C. 30€ are way to expensive for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case

_childDocuments_.review: While the case of the game is intriguing, it was unfortunately, not substantial enough to carry the entire game. Compared to "The ABC Murders" and "The First Cases" it only took a fraction of the time to complete the game (7.5 hours). Furthermore, the game still doesn't have consequences for incorrect deductions so you can just click through the options until you reach the right conclusion. (The Sherlock Holmes games actually allow you to draw the wrong conclusion and arrest an innocent person). Coupled with the fact that the game suffered from some bugs (misnamed evidence items) and a lack of guidance, it devolved into moving back and forth between multiple locations and pixel hunting for the right place to click on multiple occasions.Only recommended for people who truly love the genre and want all the games in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case

_childDocuments_.review: Not like a slow-paced mystery thriller; just terrible slow controls and UI.Unlike , this title features (and requires the use of) rotating camera, but it rotates slowly AND you can't rotate it while the character is moving. Character walks around slowly. Text - you guessed it - has a slow text crawl that can't be disabled, even slower than the spoken dialogue and is sometimes skippable and sometimes not, encouraging you to hammer the space bar hoping to get on with it, which in turn could easily end up skipping dialogue if you're not careful. Going into the mind map or main menu triggers an animated, unskippable fade animation that takes a couple seconds, discouraging you from switching screens. Mind map is clunky and annoying to navigate on mouse & keyboard. I found the whole user experience an excruciating chore.It's too bad playing this is such a tiresome slog because the voice acting is delightful and the visuals are stylish.  The game content itself seems fine.  I just wish the interface wasn't so relentlessly awful.

_childDocuments_.review: It absolutely pains me to say to disregard this game, but it was dull, plodding, and buggy. Nothing in this made me think, "Yes, this is a younger, post-Belgian police Poirot."When my irritation resulted in a actual swearing fit and I was EXTREMELY glad to 100% it so I'll never have to play it again... yeah, I can't say I didn't give it a chance.Oh, and Hastings was just insulting. Yes, he was written as Christie's representation of the everyman and/or the reader, but here it's like he's Bullwinkle to Poirot's Rocky. (That is not a comparison I thought I'd ever make.)

_childDocuments_.review: The story was enjoyable enough however I found this entry to be far buggier than its predecessor.  Pathing, animations, cut scenes that didn't trigger their completion.  Voice acting I found to be delightfully done.  The game's complexity, light to maybe moderate.  Seemed easier than the first.  I would recommend the game but only for having something to do whilst you wait for another game to release.  That isn't meant to be as harsh as it sounds.  It was an ok game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Decent voice acting- Graphics are nice, good lighting lots of details- Entirely playable with mouse- Poirot is as fiesty as ever.- Story was okay but takes along time to get going.Cons- My game suffered this weird graphical artifact that kind of looks like screen tearing but I think its something probably in relation to the anti-aliasing. Its like a weird blurly scan line. The effect is lessened by lowering the graphics preset. I didn't see any difference in fidelity by lowering either.- Lots of missing animations for voice acting.- Lots of pathing issues, character frequently getting stuck on things and other characters, flailing about at doors and other interaction points, can get very fustrating.- There is only a few locations in the game but you will be constantly jumping between them and in some locations the fast travel or scene exit is quite a bit a way so there will be plenty of just waiting for the character to slowly navigate the scene to leave. Gets a bit tedious.- A lot of the time to progress you just need to go to another location and now something is different or a character has suddenly appeared there, just seemed a bit random.I felt the story and pacing were not as strong as the first title although it plays a lot more casual in my opinion which might be appreciated by some. The pass/fail style of questioning which was used extensively in the previous game (especially in the case wrap up at the end) is mostly gone. Also they got rid of the annoying sounds when using in the mind map which drove me mad in the first title. However as you can see from the cons it lacks a lot of polish. Overall its a mixed bag,  but I think it deserves a recommendation just about.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my god, what a mess. I have no idea how we concluded who the thief is, though there were signs, but missing motivation etc...I didn't mind the crappy game mechanics, the lame graphics, but an extremely dumb story is not OK for a detective game...and this so far has been a total mess - and an uninteresting one. This is even worse than the Early Cases and incomparably worse than the ABC Murders...I'll try to finish the game, but the motivation is getting lower and lower with every minute spent walking up and down searching for the next and only possible next thing to do.UPDATE: finished the game in 6 hours...and i regret every single hour of it. The investigation probably made some sense, but we were jumping from one thing to another and the mind map was only used rarely to connect either something obvious or something obscure and weird. The end solution made zero sense, but that was my first happy moment - it's finally over! And what is worse, the games terrible behaviour made conversations even more awkward - seemed like i was missing significant plot parts somehow because we were  suddenly talking about things i had no idea about. So overall: really NOTHING was good in this, except for the intro music, which was catchy.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with the technical stuff first.- the game runs well, even on the best graphic settings.- audio is okay but i sometimes felt like the voice over was done by AI, there were so many weird pronunciations!- the animation is ... meh. people often don't even open their mouths while talking, if they do it's just open and shut, no more detailed movements. other expressions are raised eyebrows at max and i think poirot smiled once or so.- there are a few graphic bugs in there too, missing parts of clothing in cutscenes, opening doors well before reaching them, getting stuck on random things, walking into people instead of around them, ...Other than that, the story isn't great either to be honest. Poirot has always been more of a contained story for me, maybe because of the movies. The london case is an endless journey back and forth, talking to the same people x-times and visiting certain locations more often than i cared to count. This is what i would have expected from one of the old sherlock holmes games maybe... Poirot also looks very stupid when he tries to combine things. he makes baby steps connecting things that are so obvious that i had to look up guides to see what i was missing because i was already trying to enter the solution to everything. there is a bookcase with very obvious scratches on the floor around it. what might that mean? let me combine the fallen chess piece and the presence of the globe to realise that the suspect was at the bookcase! You don't even get to look behin the secret door after all that...The whole case is played out in a very boring manner. after you have been confused by countless storylines, endless alibis, the undoing of said alibis and new storylines over and over again, you have to connect the dots one last time for the british detective. At no point was there every any suspense or wonder at poirot's genius, he is very unlikable and slow in his thinking.After 5.5hours i had played through the entirety of the game and was left feeling empty after hoping it might get better, only for the story to be so disappointing in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey together, another review by me on the "Poirot-Series"...Sadly i have to say, it´s way not at the height as "ABC-Murders" was and is - and this was a very low-budget-project too though... They pushed everything into the gfx, forgetting about the mechanics, "the red line" and with it the story-flow... Sad to say, that a "black-screen-issue" still resists, even after multiple call-outs to the devs. 6h on and dont want to continue to play. Thank you, but no thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet but so far it has been a pleasure to play. Solid Poirot style gameplay like the predecessor with about the same amount of jank. Those games look like plastic so don't expect AAAA level graphics. The mindmap deduction mechanic is back and it's still a nice way of combining thoughts that takes the place of usual inventory puzzles in adventure games.If you liked the previous game, this one will be probably also good for you. If not then look elsewhere for an adventure game fix

_childDocuments_.review: After the awesome 'First Cases' game, unfortunately this one falls quite short. There is a sense that things were rushed here - typos, bugs in the worst form of characters and objects disappearing from locations during conversations/interactions, and the level of 'holding your hand' through puzzles was a bit too much. This felt like Poirot for beginners and, aside from a couple of achievements, it was fairly simple to get the majority. I am still giving this a thumbs up for the story and frankly any Poirot game will always rate highly but I wish for the next game to go back to what made the last one amazing and treat people who love a good detective game with actions that leads to other consequences, and yet maintain that theme that has been done so well.The graphics are very shiny on full settings but again there was a scene at the cafe where clearly there is no furniture inside the store, merely a shell for people to interact outside of it - a bit sloppy.And yet again I give this a thumbs up, probably more a sideways thumb if I could, because I love these games and the journey we are taken on. I look forward to the next installment

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish i could recommend the game but i was so poor, i love all detective games and have a soft spot for Poirot especially as the other games had been good to average but this just seems very rushed and so much of the game goes against the logic that his books and character is famed, the tick box nature of the game made it more confusing than fluid as you deduced what was going on and where to go about 5 steps before the game as you were forced to do the rather dull click and collect nature of going around speaking to people you really had no need to before you could get where you already knew where you had to go, for the cost it was still too much and i really hope the developers have a hard look at themselves the cut scenes are very bad as its rare the audio matches the mouths which is like something from the early 00s, its put me off the next one which i doubt i will now get majorly disappointed 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ The Mary Magdalene, a valuable picture, has just been sold and will be the main exhibit at a Gala that will take place in a London Museum. You, Mr. Hercule Poirot, will be in charge of the transportation and security of the artwork during its voyage. Mr Mortimer Ailsworth, the new owner of the painting, has insured it through Lloyd's of London, and one of its representatives, a certain Mr Arthur Hastings, will also accompany the picture from the port of Antwerp to Dover and its final destination, London. Perhaps Mr. Ailsworth is afraid that his new acquisition will disappear during its transit or, even worse, a murder will take place. Of course, it is just speculation. Let's jump into Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case, shall we?Agatha Christie - Hercule Poirot: The London Case is a point-and-click adventure game developed by Blazing Griffin and published by Microids on the 29th of August 2023 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS4/PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch.The game consists of nine chapters, and the story will be told by visiting nine locations throughout the game.  The prologue takes place on the ship, which is one of the nine locations. Having finished the game, I am very pleased to inform you that the story is rather good and will keep you guessing who the murderer is until you reach the end of chapter 8. Although it is linear, you must follow the process step by step to move from one chapter to the next. You can always access this information via the mind maps, which will tell you what to do if you get stuck somewhere.Point and Click games will always involve reading, finding objects and solving puzzles. I do like the way they present the puzzles. If you have played the previous game, you'll already know about this, but if you haven't, it is quite fun. You see, in most chapters you'll unlock mind maps. As you discover objects and clues, those findings will be placed in the mind maps of the current chapter. There are two types of mind maps. The main one is Hercule Poirot's deduction system, and the other is for his sidekick, Mr. Hastings, which you can access when you need his help. Ultimately, all findings will be transferred to Hercule Poirot's main deduction system. There, you'll have to link the appropriate findings to each other to uncover the truth. But you have to acquire link points to do so, which you'll get as you progress through the story. Throughout the nine chapters, there are a few objects that you’ll find along the way and can use to assist your progress. I like the fact that you can zoom in on some of the objects and see around them to find clues. My biggest problem with this game is the animation; there are bugs everywhere. The main one is Poirot's inability to stop walking when he reaches a place of interest, such as clicking on items or opening doors. He also keeps walking while the next scene starts to load. Additionally, in the apartment scenes, clicking for Poirot to go downstairs will occasionally trigger the opposite, and you’ll find yourself going upstairs. In conversation scenes, characters will have arms going through their bodies on multiple occasions. No need to be Hercule Poirot to notice this error. The voiceover is good and clear, but it feels like you are in an acoustic room. That would work for a scene in a museum hall, for example, but not in an office. It's odd. The camera view is adequate, as you can move Poirot's perspective by 90-degree increments at any time, which is important as you need the ability to see each room you are in from different angles.Despite the animation issues, I really like the graphics, and the story is pretty good too. The game has been translated into English, French and German at this stage. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Good graphics+	Good story+	Ability to move the camera 90 degrees at any given time+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	No trading cards as yet-	Plenty of issues with animations-	The voiceover feels like you are constantly in an acoustic placeA fun point-and-click adventure game, but full of annoying animation bugs! Not quite right, Mr. Poirot, not quite right.6/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Although I would recommend this game overall, it does have both pros and cons.Pros:-The character of Poirot is exactly what I expect Poirot to be like. I appreciate when games based on already established characters can reflect them as they have already been written. It makes the game more enjoyable for fans that already love the established character. Even in smaller details, Poirot was Poirot. For example, in the books Poirot is religious and the game included this fact by having him knowledgeable concerning the Bible and church.-The character of Hastings. I so much loved his inclusion! The interactions between the two were fun, especially for someone who enjoys both these characters. I won't give it away, but Hastings does something so very Hastings. It was fun seeing these two come together.-I also enjoyed a character returning from the previous game. I totally remembered him when he showed up and he was a fun addition.-I thought the voice acting was very well done. I rarely got bored listening to anyone and rarely skipped dialogue.-There were fun areas to explore. They looked very nice and were fun to poke around in.-There were some fun deductions to make. I still like the way the deductions connections are done. However, there is also a con. More below.Cons:-The characters were varied, and although they were interesting at times, overall they were a bit cliche. I don't mind some cliche as that is part of the fun of creating something based on Agatha Christie's mysteries, but they felt more disjointed than the previous game, just several people brought together at a gala, each happening to have some secret. I guess they didn't feel as natural as they did in the previous game. I actually cared about some characters in the previous game; I didn't really care about any of the characters in the second aside from Poirot, Hastings, and the character from the previous game.-Speaking of caring, the plot of this game just didn't measure up to its predecessor. I think that's because the previous game set up a scenario that made you care: someone is accused unjustly, Poirot is disbelieved. This set up made me want Poirot to achieve and prove the case. The plot here is more straightforward and without characters I cared about, far less compelling. Maybe that's because most of the characters were unlikable from the beginning or at least didn't give me any reason to care about them above any of the others.-Bugs. I hate to say it but there are just several bugs in the game. I had to close and restart multiple times, mainly because something didn't light up that I was supposed to interact with or because the mouse pointer didn't appear on screen. There were a couple bugs I had to restart several times before I could get past them and I was afraid at first I couldn't complete the game because of them.-The deduction maps are fun. I love the way they are done. But there are some mental leaps where it doesn't quite make sense what goes together so that at times you just randomly connect things to figure out until they connect. I did turn off the hints because I want to figure it out myself, but that sometimes left me just hunting and pecking.-The game felt shorter than its predecessor, so much so I was surprised when I came to the last chapter. I checked and I played this game two hours less than I did for the previous game.If you like Poirot, I think this game is worth playing. I did enjoy Poirot and Hastings and their interactions and plot. The mystery and its ensuing characters are typical, though unfortunately not as compelling as in the previous game. Still, the game does reflect Agatha Christie's works and characters and is thus enjoyable enough to give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure I would make it past the prologue of this game due to clunky controls, but then... I realized it's not actually a point and click game. You can use P&C (if you'd like to watch Poirot get stuck on the furniture), and I thought I'd seen game referred as P&C though I can't say where, there are no keybinding customization options, but there are really only a couple of mechanics you actually have to use your mouse for - and the movement is SO MUCH SMOOTHER using keyboard controls. Like, audible sigh of relief when I decided to try before giving up and it worked. I have few memories of this game's predecessor besides feeling lukewarm about it, and now I must replay it in case I made the same mistake.So, moving on from that and focusing on the gameplay and story, this game really charmed me in the end. We get to meet Hastings!! Poirot and Hastings both felt in character and I loved them both. One thing I do remember about The First Cases is feeling overparented, and while this game does hold your hand as well, the narrative manages to incorporate the deductions in a way they don't feel shoehorned most of the time. Though, on a few occasions I was tripped up by needing Poirot to "figure out" things I thought we'd already figured out.The story is deeper than it appears at first and I found myself sympathizing with several of the characters even as they all come to appear less innocent. I appreciate that there are moments the brilliant detective sees his own flaws, and enjoyed the journey of his coming to trust Hastings.Overall while there is room for improvement gameplay-wise, this narrative won me over and I thoroughly enjoyed the game and recommend it for mystery lovers.

Race on 20 different DreamWorks-themed tracks, including Shrek’s Swamp, New York City Zoo from Madagascar, Isle of Berk, and more! 20 of the most iconic DreamWorks characters: Shrek, Po, Tigress, Puss in Boots, Hiccup, Astrid, Boss Baby, and other top favorites all come together in a kart racing experience like no other. Extend these magical paths by hitting more switches in series! - MULTIPLE RACING MODES: Awesome online and split-screen local multi-player for non-stop action the entire family will love.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game but it's absolutely filled with jank. Mechanically it's just fine, but the developers did all kinds of really freaky crap that just gets in the way. The game is severely lacking in artistic polish but more importantly it is littered with technical issues.Maybe as a console game this would pass, but on PC it's not worth 40 dollars. Get it during a summer sale or somethingSome issues I've found not even 1 minute into playing:- It constantly tries to open SteamVR even though the game has no VR support at all, and there is no option to make it stop doing this.- For whatever reason, even though the game has native controller support, the developers set the recommended Steam Input configuration to... first person shooter binds? So by default the analog sticks don't work and you have to enable them yourself in the Steam client.- The tutorial is annoying. You don't need to pause every 5 seconds to remind me how to press a button.- The voice impressionists are annoying. I know sometimes getting the original voice actors on a licensed IP video game is hard, but you could have at least either found better actors or made the voice lines play less often. Luckily you can mute them.- Game breaks on GeForce 40 series cards when in fullscreen mode. It won't render anything unless you alt-tab out of the game. You have to blindly go to the settings and set it to borderless. What?- Character models are poor and there are almost no graphics options at all. Was this game made in 2023 or 2012? I don't really care about visual quality all too much, but this game looks less like Dreamworks and more like a beta. Puss in Boots especially looks bad. The lighting quality in the screenshots on the store page is misleading, some environments are undersaturated in the actual game. Come on, you can make a game for PC with low system requirements without making it look like baby's first UE4 project. I'm not asking for RTX or some Nanite + Lumen implementation, but what I am asking for is for the visuals to be tweaked so they feel more in line with the artistic presentation of the movies these characters are from.There are positives though, albeit unremarkable. Controls and mechanics are solid, sense of speed is there, the AI is actually somewhat competent. It's essentially Mario Kart 8 on PC, with a couple extra bells and whistles plus some furry bait. If you can look past the jank factor there is an enjoyable experience to be had. I just think that for a game funded and licensed by Dreamworks it should have had more care put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to love about this game. The IP's the interesting track layouts, the attention to detail about the models, the choice of dialogue for each characters and the attention to detail and how it ties into each movie. The things that kinda drive me away and make me feel that this game has very little replay value are just the way the game plays and ties together. The Music it way too campy and and feels like a straight up copy of Nickelodeon Karts Series. DreamWorks Original Games and Film are known for their original Musical scores and orchestra. There is none of that and it kinda tarnishes the experience. The sound effects also feel a little cheep, Drawn out in places. The Chase distance or model size is too small. The troll Characters that you collect are very detailed, but are hardly noticeable and don't feel like the add any value aside from dangling off the tail end of the carts. The Kart Customization's also feel like there is no added value because the part stats aren't upfront and center. The Karts are way too maneuverable and have very little penalty's after stunts, hitting walls, flying through the air off jumps (they float around). I wanna Love this game, but i can't, It's just ok. love the devs, And Nickelodeon Karts but This game needed a little bit of a different approach and a little more polish to have been a great game. Looking forward To their next project. I hope My review Helps either in the purchasing process or the development of a better gaming experience to the development team. Best regards from a fan :-)

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is a step up from 2011's Dreamworks Superstar Kartz... that is not saying much.This game has some of the WORST AI I've ever encountered in a racing game. Even on the hardest difficulty and the fastest speed, they still lag behind you quite a ways if you're an experienced arcade racing gamer. No challenge whatsoever, fwlt pointless to go beyond the first cup after seeing how poorly they kept up with you. Not only that, but the roster and kart selection is way more limited than Bamtang's last kart racer, Nickelodeon Kart Racers 3: Slime Speedway. Dreamworks has a pretty wide selection of movies that could've been represented, but all you get here is the obligatory super-classics (i.e. Shrek and Madagascar) and more recent productions (The Boss Baby and The Bad Guys) with very little in the way of deep cuts or even fanservice picks (seriously, where's characters like the Guardians, Tulio & Miguel, Chel, Moses, and Captain Underpants?). I know some of the ones I listed would never happen (mainly Chel and Moses for different reasons), but when over a quarter of the roster is Shrek-universe characters and Megamind didn't bring Minion or even Titan along... it's a bit jarring.The Trolls... oh my word, the Trolls.This kinda ties back into my previous point, but the main characters of that movie are delegated to "pit crew" status while the more disgusting side characters take up roster slots. Not only that, but the whole "Troll Surprise" mechanic is basically a worse and simplified version of the Pit Crew in the Nickelodeon Kart Racers series. Not only that, but different trolls do not give you any thing meaningful in the way of different abilities or bonuses and only serve as decoration most of the time. It also makes all the racers' karts have these tacky-looking handle bars mounted to the back of their karts... which just look awful from a vehicle design perspective.As for the gameplay itself, the tracks are very wide with little to no challenge. It just feels empty most races, especially when coupled with the AI lagging behind you most of the time. Unless you've watched all the movies featured in this game, there's nothing indicating what tracks are from what properties. For example, "Greater Los Angelos" didn't click with me being from The Bad Guys... because the movie NEVER once said where it takes place (sure, there was some indication, but it was never outright said). And the game's Rainbow Road equivalent, "Galactic Sky", is a half-baked tribute to the iconic Dreamworks "moon child" logo... it doesn't even try to replicate the studio's newer intro. Drifting is just the same as it was in NKR3, but the wide track design makes it all but too easy to get Level 3 drift boosts on every turn.In conclusion...DON'T BUY THIS GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: I cant in good faith recommend this to anyone. I played for maybe 30mins and it felt very boring and lifeless. The ground work could be there if updates were to be implemented for more tracks or fixes of visuals for this game but for now i just feel it needs more time in the shop. For being a game based on Dreamwork characters the voices do not sound remotely close to what we all grew up with. They sound very VERY off. The controls for the game compared to other racers feel very unusual RB to accelerate, LB for drift and i believe Y was to jump and A was to throw weapons.  The tracks feel very slow and repetitive. To unlock characters they are locked behind challenges (Thats better than paying for them as dlc) However speaking of DLC for $15 you can obtain 2 races master Ugway (Kung Fu Panda) or Death (Puss in Boots The Last Wish) I think thats  bit steep especially since the game itself is already $40. Like i said the game has potential but i feel that comes with more updates for the game that can provide longevity and polish or a sequel which hopefully grows upon what they have here. I played about an hour more of this game and i explored more of the challenges and Multiplayer and kart customization's. As far as the multiplayer goes Well, the community might as well be non existent good luck finding anyone to play against online. The kart customization.. Is a joke!! So your telling me not only do i need to win cups or challenges to unlock characters but when i do i now need to not only have in game currency but i have to complete specific character missions to unlock the ability to buy kart parts to make my kart faster, handled better, ect?? Why? Was there really not enough confidence in the game that they had to throw in extra fluff to keep the players playing and grinding for these parts?? The missions to unlock racers and some kart pieces arent too bad just a bit repetitive and this is also where i seemed to find alot of my game breaking bugs such as my kart getting stuck in mid air after performing air jumps, Falling off the track while being nowhere near the edge and more ridiculous things that should have been ironed out before launching! _childDocuments_.review: I haven't seen a kart racer this terrible since Rascal Racers in 2004, its a special kind of terrible.Firstly the tutorial is long, boring and you can't skip the starting terrible voice over, not to mention the controls are binded like a six year old did them, Right Bumper for gas??? We've been using the triggers for two decades now get cmon now. You thankfully can rebind the controls but you have to either skip or complete the tutorial.Now I know this game doesn't have millions to waste on getting the actual voice actors again but the replacements are a special kind of bad, Mr Wolf was the main offender and the reason I turned voices off. After that I turned the music off because it was honestly so bland, I'd say it wasn't fitting music but the tracks are just as bland honestly.The 20 "fantastical worlds" the blurb describes are all about the same length and have so many moving parts just thrown onto them without a second thought. Magic paths stutter and slow you down despite being called a shortcut, the tracks themselves will also kill your speed at certain points in the geometry, going downhill while boosting also just kills momentum.The steam achievements are also a major distraction when you first boot the game due to a tracking achievement for boosting, doing tricks and hitting opponents, it's just a constant flood until you clear them which is about 4-5 races in.The game also claims to have 4 speeds but all of them are unlocked at the start so only the 200cc in this case matters, though you can unlock characters and parts on the lower speeds certain stuff is locked behind the lighting speed cups.Speaking of cups, I dunno what criteria they had for grouping these cups but they're honestly all over the place, not to mention the six cup is just a rehash of older tracks put together with this games "Rainbow Road" as the last track, despite the fact you race on it on the cup before in the THIRD race.I used the Mario kart comparison for speeds and honestly the devs just cut and pasted a ton of other stuff too, the dragon in the keep is just used as a Bowser hazard, drift boosts go from red to blue to purple, and cups are 4 tracks each with a 3 star rating for if you get 40 points or not. I don't care about your terrible podium animation that eats a full 60 seconds each and every time I complete a cup just let me back to the menu so I can go and buy the ♥♥♥♥ I unlocked. _childDocuments_.review: So lets be real here, this game isn't a bad kart racer, but its not a amazing one either. Its enjoyable for what it is and honestly I can look past the rough edges but what I don't understand is this game is just dead on arrival. What caused this to happen?One thing could be advertising or the lack there of, I hadn't even heard this was coming out until a month just before release through word of mouth. But I want to discuss the pro's and cons of this game.Pros-Unique (at least to me) mechanics, things like the magic paths and super jumps make it stand out to me, I like their inclusive and it does feel like its not just trying to be a cash grab.-Troll hosts, At first I rolled my eyes at their inclusion but once I learnt what they actually do, I found it kind of cool, each of them effect the track in some way whether it is boost tracks, bumpers or something simple like more music notes to collect. Also depending on the host is the genre the music on the track will try to capture. This makes some songs very hit and miss (Pro-tip, pick Barb, all her tracks are good)-2 weapon system, In this game there are two types of weapons, music note related weapons that every one can get and the standard box weapons which have an assortment of weapons and also one weapon unique to the racer you are playing.-The online mode actually has a cup mode where players can vote what 4 tracks will be raced and creating a custom cup. There's also a single race mode for those who just want a quick race.-Online races (when you can find them) are actually a lot of fun and really allows the mechanics of the game to be used to the fullest potential.Cons-Too easy, The only time I struggled on this game was the "rainbow road" time trail, but even then I got it on my third attempt, everything else was very one and done so I think the difficulty needs tweaking.-Where are all the Villains? Literally the only villain in this game (Base game I do not count the DLC) is Farquad, Where's Tighten? Where's Tai Lung? Where's Lord Shen? Where's Prince Charming? Where's the fairy godmother? Where's Professor Marmalade? Like they dropped the ball on the character selection here by only starring one villain?- Day 1 DLC, That locks 2 characters behind a paywall, Death and Oogway. - Dead on Arrival Online mode, Now this really isn't the fault of the game but seriously, where is everyone? Even on day 1 absolutely no-one was playing this online and it ain't even that bad.-Visual Style, Now graphics don't make a great game, but it can help it present itself better. This game looks like they made it so it can run on the Switch and then ported it to everything else rather than make it look amazing and then downgrade the Switch version.-The voicelines/acting, Just... turn it down... they missed a ton of opportunities for some themed voicelines for the characters in a kart setting, its mostly just screaming and laughing, very little actually dialogue, the one plus is the kart racers do address each other when passing or hitting. But its safe stuff like "Out of the way [character name here]" The only fun one I heard is Fiona passing Megamind and saying "What a noggin!" ConclusionHonestly if you want a kart racer with your favourite Dreamworks characters then you can really do a lot worse, you can tell they tried and at least they didn't cram it full of micro-transactions which a lot of kart racers are doing these days, if you're looking for a kart racer with a solid online player-base. This ain't it chief, I feel like this game got done dirty massively because it is by no means terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: I GIVE THIS GAME A SOLID 8/10! DreamWorks All-Star Kart Racing is a little rough around the edges, but that doesn't mean you can't have fun with it! It's definitely no Mario Kart 8 (yet). But if you're a huge fan of crossovers and seeing the iconic characters from your childhood films interact and show up in one game, while also having fun and goofing around with your friends, then this is DEFINITELY a game I highly recommend! It definitely needs more work done, but that doesn't mean it's unplayable, allow me to explain the pros and cons that I found throughout my first play-through:Okay, first of all, what the flying fudge was going on with the voice-acting? The only voices that were even remotely good were Hiccup's & Po's. I understand that it would have been WAY TOO EXPENSIVE to get the original VA's back, but they could have at least had a better voice direction. Also, WHAT KIND OF KART RACER DOESN'T HAVE CONTROLLER SUPPORT!? D:<Now then, with the negatives out of the way, there's definitely potential with this game, unfortunately, the gameplay feels way too sluggish, regardless of who you're playing as. Hopefully they fix this in a later patch. I do like how each character has special voice lines that are specifically being said towards other characters, name-drops and all. Nothing cracks me up more than seeing Death from Puss In Boots talking smack to Mr. Wolf from the Bad Guys. The levels are very vibrant and stand out from each other, albeit a little basic in terms of track design. The power-ups are okay, they're not Mario Kart levels of exciting, but it's still nice seeing what items you got and recognizing what said item is from whatever DreamWorks movie you fondly remember. The Kart customization is a nice addition, but it barely changes the stats of your kart, perhaps if they add a little more to what it strengthens and weakens about your kart in a future patch, then maybe it'll be more fun to use. The best thing about this game though is: DEATH & DIANE ARE BOTH PLAYABLE!!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of good ideas in this one, but execution is quite poor. Gameplay wise it should be similar to Mario Kart but it is severely lacking the level of polish and fine-tuning Nintendo puts into their kart racing mechanics. There's a lot to be said about Nintendo's use of rubber banding AI and terrible balancing, but the driving always feels tight. This game, on the other hand, feels quite sloppy with a lot of very weird slowdowns in speed, like before approaching a ramp, that breaks what could have been an otherwise fluid experience. The game also seems buggy, with changes to control mapping either not applying at all or becoming randomized.Doesn't help that things like the obviously cheapo impersonation or AI-powered voice acting ruins the game's atmosphere. Old fans aren't going to be enthused with how they sound, and kids are not as stupid as the developers/publisher seem to think they are. Also, the forced tutorial race is HORRIBLY done. For one thing, if your kart racer has so many mechanics that need to be communicated in a tutorial rather than being learnable through gameplay, it's a failure. Second, the abrupt slow down that happens when explaining a mechanic destroys the flow of gameplay and makes it VERY easy to mess up whatever it is they're trying to teach.

_childDocuments_.review: Background: I play a lot of racing and arcade games. From racing sims to very arcade battle racing.INTRO:The game is developed by Bamtang, which has previously developed various games like this, most recently the Nickelodeon Kart Racers 3 game, which ended up being very decent. None of their games have been better than Mario Kart 8 which IMO is still king in the genre, but they're certainly good enough and a non-experienced player or kid wouldn't probably care.GRAPHICS:The graphics are very attractive, not mind blowing or anything, but the atmosphere is there. Some stages feel very good but a couple feel like half baked and not good. The underwater stage feels very half baked. I'd say it's a the graphics overall look better than Nickelodeon Kart Racing, but might be just that Dreamworks CGI characters obviously translate better to videogames.MUSICI didn't like the music at all, it makes the game feel generic or something, I don't recognize any melody, they all feel like built from modifying some other song. Not that they were any better in earlier Bamtang games.GAMEPLAYThe battle mechanics are nice, you got the usual boxes with random items and a team of trolls that have special abilities (all speed related) when you collect enough music notes (they're scattered in the map). There's also a lyre mechanic that spawns an alternative path temporarily through the stage usually allowing shortcuts.The usual slide/boost mechanic and the jump/trick mechanic is also present. Boosts, jump, bounces, all is present in the stages, also different terrains and a piano mechanic that acts like a racing line that gives you extra music notes.It doesn't feel like an evolution from it's predecessor, just different.GAME MODES/CONTENT: It has less games modes than it's predecessor Nickelodeon Kart Racing 3, most notably it doesn't have a Battle Mode which is a must have for this kind of games IMO. Overall it keels like it has less content overall than the earlier game.PERFORMANCE/ENGINE:Unlike it's predecessor Nickelodeon Kart Racers 3 that ran at 120fps, this game has a 62 fps hardcap, which just killed it for me. It made no sense to half the game speed, when they have probably the same unreal engine fmod base game, why not offer 2 modes for PC which is the easiest fix to engine speed inconsistencies and maintain cross-platform multiplayer. This kind of stuff was maybe acceptable in 2012 but today it's retrograde, ancient nonsense.TL;DR: The game is fun and visually attractive, the mechanics are fun but it's a downgrade from it's predecessor Nickelodeon Kart Racing 3. Still among the better Mario Kart 8 alternatives out there, specially for Dreamworks fans.Would I pay full price ? NoI recommend the predecessor from Nickelodeon, since it's currently cheaper, has more content and runs better.

_childDocuments_.review: I played all the needed challenges so I could unlock Diane Foxington and I refuse to explain why.barring that, with a little more polish to all the tracks, some new additions of tracks and some more varied (And I'd say improved voice acting but I can't fault the team that worked on the voice acting as it sounds like they actually gave it one helluva shot) voice lines across the board and this game could actually become an alright competitor with the likes of other titles.Now it'll never touch anything like Diddy Kong Racing (Best of luck with that one unless you do something crazy, such as think like me), or Crash™ Team Racing but the core mechanics of the game are legitimately here and there is a good work of polish with the over-all art style that Bamtang has done. I thoroughly enjoyed the maps they designed - granted I do wish a few were a little longer in regards to their over-all track lengths and, perhaps, a few maps based around the villains in the various series presented in the game would be a welcome addition for track idea's/inspirations.There is a strong amount of jank at times, but out of the gate (and I've only played the challenges, mind you) it was not that bad of an experience at all, and I feel that if the team can be given a lot of creative freedoms with the maps ((As per example I'll submit all the "Out of place" highway/freeway maps that Mario Kart has done. When has there ever been a highway in mainstream Mario? I really don't know))I feel that the games' upcoming additions if any are planned would come out exceptionally well considering all the core mechanics are present, even with the jank and unpolished sections here and there. I mostly walked in, buying this over more a meme than anything ((and I must admit the tutorial is kinda cringe. I am not sure if it's the voice acting, dialogue - maybe both - but it was cringe)) passing through the tutorial via a skip and working to unlock Diane in the challenge mode showed me that the game has a lot more to it than the surface.The only concern I would have would be repetition in it's gameplay which could only be adjust with additional maps, characters, themes and perhaps even a battle inspired mode - such as what existed with Mario Kart on the N64 and other copies long ago.I feel that if this game is genuinely going to be supported by both Bamtang games and its' publisher, GameMill, this child friendly combat racer can be one really well done game. For 20 dollars (I did not buy the DLC as to sell that to me, I'd say add a track to it or something a little more than just Wolf and Oogway) I feel the game is worth at least a try beyond it's tutorial. I even was able to convince a friend to buy it too.I say that, yes, this game is worth a purchase on sale as is and with more polish and a few more updates - varied tracks, more antagonists to add (A wolf character from Kung-Fu Panda or Tai Lung) and hell, even if you have access to the characters from Chicken Run or Wallace and Gromit or Sinbad - they may have been all 1994 - 2004 but Dream Works has a lot to choose from, especially if the distribution agreement with Paramount Pictures is still a legitimate thing to consider and could be utilized through the right conversations and connections for the game.You could even add Felix the Cat (Not to be confused with Fritz now) as I believe that fits under Dreamworks Classics and if this trademark can expand into this specific game or idea for one. There is a huge amount of potential for the game to become as good as Diddy Kong racing if these kind of ideas were to be explored and expanded upon solely due to the amount of IP's genuinely available to Dreamworks and their sub-companies. These are all just idea's off the top of my head and if I can think of them, I guarantee you someone in your board room has and that individual probably deserves a raise if the creative aspects of all these can be thoroughly investigated. I believe Dreamworks Classics even has The Filmation library, which includes ARCHIE.Jughead could LITERALLY be in a game like this since Dreamworks won the bid to acquire "Classic Media" in 2012 and, I feel, it wouldn't be the worst thought for Bamtang and the Publisher GameMill to explore idea's such as these in the future. From maps to mechanics to characters to customization.It's a crazy thought, but a use of all the intellectual properties can be considered, and with a dedicated team as Bamtang has shown themselves to be with the release so far, if they put in the time, money and speak with the right people the game can expand quite a lot and could even catch onto the likes and depth that newer title Mario Kart games have today, and that Diddy Kong Racing achieved back in 1997.TL:DRIt's worth on sale and I hope that the team will put out a roadmap of what they are interested in doing as they've got one helluva shot to start making something fairly big.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has 20 charming cast of DreamWorks characters, each with their unique driving style and special abilities! The tracks are beautifully designed and packed with twists, turns, and shortcuts and even hidden paths.One of the game's most appealing features is its branching tracks. As you race, you'll encounter keys that unlock secret passages and alternate routes, adding an extra layer of strategy to the gameplay. This element of choice keeps the races fresh and unpredictable, ensuring that no two runs are ever the same. Of course time trial will have the optimal lines and paths but for races it doesn't make a difference.There is also a clever item system that rewards skillful driving. Other than the items you collect from boxes, collecting musical notes (yellow and purple) scattered throughout the tracks allows you to unlock extra items. There are plenty of ways to sabotage your rivals and secure victory.The voice acting is just great as their banter is consistently witty, sarcastic, and downright hilarious. Of course my favorite is the noble steed (aka Donkey) and his love for waffles.============================Edit: 15/12/2023I've been thoroughly enjoying this game for quite some time now. I've 100%ed everything except for the shop, which requires me to complete quests for each character. I also tried the online matchmaking with few people, which was okay but had a few missing features. While the overall experience is positive, I've noticed several key areas that could be improved for a better kart racing experience.Here are my detailed observations and suggestions: Currently, when other racers drift, it's not visually apparent; they seem to be driving normally but gain speed unexpectedly. This makes the race less captivating, specially during split-screen or online races, as there are no drift visuals for any karts except your own.Suggestion: Introduce visual effects for all players' drifting maneuvers to enhance race clarity. In both Private Room and online matchmaking, the track selection is restricted to only 7 out of the 20 available tracks, which feels quite limiting. I'd like to see more options for track selection, so that we can choose the tracks we prefer.Suggestion: Expand track selection to include all available tracks for a more varied racing experience. The items, especially when racing against real players, seem unbalanced. The first-place racer often receives multiple boost items that further their lead, while offensive items for chasing players have a very short range, making it hard to hit other racers with them. There are some homing items but they disappear after 1 second which is not enough to track other racers.Suggestion: Balance item distribution and effectiveness to ensure fair competition. The option to adjust CPU difficulty in private lobbies is missing. While 'Lightning Mode' is available, having the ability to race against 'No Mercy' difficulty would be a welcome challenge, especially since the current setting feels too easy. Online public matchmaking is even worse since my friend and I can lap the CPU in a 3-lap race!Suggestion: Introduce more difficulty setting options for CPU racers in private lobbies and possibly the online lobbies.  There's an inconsistent buggy area involving, particularly at a shortcut involving metallic beams and bouncy surfaces where karts often get stuck. Sometimes the kart just stops completely in midair or gets stuck during the bounce to clear the shortcut.Suggestion: Address this collision issue to ensure consistency in time trials, specially since it is the shortest path. Sometimes, after charging a drift to purple and releasing it for a boost, the kart abruptly stops before boosting. This is notably frequent in the 'Far Far Away' track.Suggestion: Investigate and rectify this erratic kart behavior. The kart's reaction to downhill slopes is unpredictable, often leading to excessive bouncing that affects both speed and control. This is mainly due to the ramps before the downhill sections, which cause the kart to fall from a height and bounce repeatedly until it reaches a flat surface. The bounces also have unpredictable effects on the kart’s speed, sometimes slowing it down and sometimes maintaining it. This makes it hard to drive downhill consistently and smoothly, as the kart does not follow the downward direction after landing from a jump. Moreover, the kart angle doesn't match the surface inclination during landing which might be a bug.Suggestion: Refine the physics to provide a more consistent downhill driving experience. The magical paths, while a novel idea, mostly end up slower than normal routes due to the lack of drifting and boosting on them, making them less viable in time trials. This is because on the normal roads, you can drift and charge your boost, but on the magical paths, there are only ramps that do not give any landing boost.Suggestion: Adjust these paths to offer competitive speed by making the ramps give higher landing boosts or add some turbo pads. The current boost gain from landing is minimal and often non-existent. This makes the landing boost unreliable and ineffective, as it does not reward the player for performing trick jumps most of the time. As a result, I usually prefer to drift and charge boost on the normal roads, rather than using the ramps and the magical paths. This reduces the variety and the fun of the gameplay, as well as the potential for strategic choices.Suggestion: Enhance the boost from landings, making it more noticeable and consistent. One possible way to do this is to scale the boost based on the duration of the jump, or to give a temporary speed increase on landing that is proportional to the current speed.  Collecting trophies/items for 100% completion requires playing through all 5 CUPs using all character and taking all magical paths, which seems excessively demanding. Furthermore, this must be done in all different modes namely "Relaxed", "Regular", "Turbo" and "Lightning" to have 100% displayed there (a total of 400 CUPs if math didn't fail me).Suggestion: Consider adjusting the requirements to make this more attainable, specially since all the items can be collected with one character. _childDocuments_.review: "Trackmania" has never been better!In its essence, "Trackmania" is all about driving the best time possible on a given track. Sometimes that means finding the shortest route, and other times you need to find ways to keep up your speed instead. Every decision matters; where to jump, air brake, drift, or perhaps just let go from the gas for a moment. You drive again and again, learning how to improve your personal best time over and over, all to gain medals or beat your opponents in the session. Tracks are diverse! They can employ various types of grounds - such as asphalt, gras, dirt, or even ice - and they all drive and handle differently, even when transitioning between them. There are wall rides, loops, donoughts, jumps, and even water elements. Sometimes a track focuses on a specific discipline - like full speed, technical, or endurance - and often times it's a mix of all.There is a bunch of content available. I love the new campaigns Nadeo releases every 3 months, consisting of 25 official tracks with increasing difficulty. The "Cup of the Day" is a daily tournament where players drive a curated track for the first time and try to win by being the last man standing, and it is a lot of fun. The great community also makes sure that there are always lots and lots of custom maps to drive and servers to join, and of course you can always create and share your own tracks as well. Generally speaking, "Trackmania" has one of the best (if not the best) game community there is!While I am happy that Ubisoft returns to Steam, their integration into the Steam ecosystem and community is rather lackluster. For "Trackmania" specifically it is a bit of a different story, because the game does not have any achievements or unlockables in Ubisoft Connect / UPlay either. Still, I would love to see at least some wallpapers or other items arriving in the Points Shop. And they should definitely update the Store page to include details and explanations regarding the pricing model.Ah yes, the pricing.So here we go: I do fully support the way the game is priced.I usually don't talk much about pricing in my reviews, but reading some of the negative reviews on this game here is forcing me to do so. I have been continuously playing this "Trackmania" game since its original release in 2020, probably about 300 hours or so (the genious Ubisoft Connect / UPlay launcher randomly decided to stop tracking my play time at some point, something that won't happen again on Steam). And for the longest time I was totally satisfied with the free tier. It gives you access to the quaterly campaigns, and grinding those to author medals on online servers, especially with friends, is a lot of fun.If you want access to more features and activities, you will need to pay a yearly subscription fee of either 10€ / year for standard access or 30€ / year for club access. Again, *per year*. This is where some people get angry. But why? What would an alternative monetization of "Trackmania" look like? Release a completely new Trackmania game every two or three years for 60€, like Call of Duty or Fifa? Release dozens of DLCs, like Dirt Rally 2.0 or the many train simulators? Make it completely free to play but plaster it with an in-game store, a battle pass and tons of micro-transactions? "Trackmania" is the perfect example of a healthy live service game that has been running successfully for nearly three years, and may just continue doing so for the next 20 years to come. Having a yearly subscription fee - with a price that is more than fair! - keeps servers running and developers working. The game can continuously receive new features and activities, and you can continuously play new tracks, collect new medals and rank up. And not a single thing is locked behind ever-changing in-game stores or other often so intransparent monetization schemes that many greedy companies like so use.Overall, I do highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to take a moment to defend the subscription model, because I think it's a real shame that this is what's causing the game to get negative reviews, when I believe it was geniuinely the best route they could've taken. I understand it can be annoying seeing the "free to play" and then being surprised with a subscription prompt right away, but let's take a moment to consider the options.Trackmania is a game heavily focused around community content. In the past they would regularly release new Trackmania games, which meant they would constantly split the community and harm the games overall. Moving to a live service model was necessary, but then they would need a continuous revenue source to justify keeping the servers alive and releasing new content every season. Microtransactions are the obvious choice, but let's think about what they could monetize: - Skins are currently created by the community and with club access you have access to unlimited skins. If Nadeo tried to monetize skins, it would be a backstab to all the skin creators, and overall you would need to pay far more money to recieve far less skins that you currently do. - Selling map packs could be another option. In the current model with standard access you can play any community map ever made. With map packs you would end up needing to pay far more to have access to this many maps. Plus this would come with limitations to how community mappers can release their maps, because Nadeo would need to create enough demand to make people actually buy the map packs.- Selling custom blocks/scenery could be another option, but personally I think it's a terrible idea adding additional costs for mappers who dedicate insane amounts of time creating content for the game, often with little reward/appreciation. Overall I understand that this subscription model can be off putting initially, but I think we should appreciate a rare occasion that Ubisoft has a very reasonable monetization system, where you can gain access to all content in the game for the same price of a single skin in most F2P games.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Trackmania for about 30 hours, I can say that while the core gameplay is solid, the monetization is a huge downside. The game nails the fast-paced, skill-based racing that fans of the series love, but the subscription model is just hard to justify.Trackmania offers a tiered access system: the base game is free, but to access the full experience, you need to pay for one of the higher-tier subscriptions. The Club Access, which is $60 for three years, is required for features like advanced track creation, participation in major tournaments, and more seasonal content. This feels like a cash grab, especially since Trackmania has always been about user-created content and community-driven competition. Locking most of that behind a paywall fragments the player base and limits how much you can do if you’re not willing to pay extra.To be clear, the gameplay itself is fun. It’s the same Trackmania charm with ridiculously high-speed tracks and precision-based driving. But after the first few hours, the content starts to dry up unless you dive into user-generated tracks, and even then, some of the coolest community stuff is gated behind that Club Access. The editor is fantastic, but I can’t help but feel it’s wrong that you need to pay to fully utilize it.It’s not that the game isn’t worth supporting—I would have preferred a one-time purchase or something less aggressive than a subscription. Paying for access to content that might disappear if you let your subscription lapse just doesn’t sit right with me. In a world where there are plenty of excellent racers that don’t force this model, Trackmania feels outdated and, frankly, a bit exploitative in how it handles monetization

_childDocuments_.review: Trackmania is a fun game to participate in as a spectator, but learning it is the most miserable experience in a game I have ever had. As a player that isn't heavily invested into the franchise, I come into this game knowing nothing, wanting the game to have a mechanism to teach me what I need in order to excel at the game; the game does nothing of the sort.Some maps have loops, and in these, the camera suddenly, and confusingly, changes perspective. As a new player, this change is very disorienting and leaves me wondering what way is up and what way is down. The slot camera is fairly intuitive for driving, and having it taken away at great speed is not what I would call a newbie friendly experience.When you suddenly do something right (but still fall short of a specific in-game track, or map goal), there's no real way to figure out what you did right. The player is left to wonder and engage in trial-and-error gameplay to learn. Where is the tutorial? Where is the in-game hints and guided gameplay?All that said, the game is particularly "more-ish," with a very compelling gameplay loop of driving incrementally faster until the goal is reached. But I don't really find the actual mechanics of the game helping me into that gameplay loop.As an aside, the new car (in the Summer 2024 campaign) is wildly irritating to control properly. If you, like me, find the slightest movement on your controller to flip you on your side, go into the settings and change the sensitivity from the default 1.000 to something much smaller.In summary: Great gameplay loop, but the mechanics really get in the way for novice players. I really wish the game developers included proper newbies into their UAT panels.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to agree that the monetization system is a sore spot for a lot of people, however as a live service game it is simply another way to keep money coming in. Trackmania is not built for monetization like a battlepass and would seriously dampen the experience if they tried to shoehorn something like that in. The subscription model DOES make sense, however I feel like there should have been an option for a full-price perpetual license. Paying $90.00 CAD for 3 years did feel a little expensive, but in a game like Trackmania the value prospect for those 3 years is very good with many, many hours of playtime. It's also probably one of the best "Open it for 10 mins while Im waiting for something else"-type game I play.Overall, I think they should boost the features for free players as a goodwill gesture. Especially the creative aspects of the game, in a game where user generated content is king putting that behind a paywall only dampens the experience. Let people make maps (on advanced) AND play them. Let people make all the custom liveries that they want and USE them. It costs them nothing and makes the game WAY more appealing while also boosting the paid users experience. It would be a win-win.Note: Time played is low but I have spent hundreds of hours in Uplay.

Playing past seasons and other people's levels however, the real fun part, comes at a price. You'll need to pay a sort of subscription (I would suggest the long term payment) to unlock this. If you're really into arcade racing and competitive gaming, this game is for you. If you just want a free racing game to play like I did and don't want to pay a subscription, that's fine, but don't expect it to be addicting, because you're limited to your creativity and levels occasionally updated every four months. The one other thing I guess that's fun with no subscription needed is Royal mode. As a team you'll try to advance through increasingly harder levels in a battle royale format. It's pretty fun and is worth as  much as you put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me explain why this game opted for a subscription model and why it works well for this game.While the game is Free 2 Play, in reality this is more of a "generous" demo. So why not a buy to play model like most other Trackmania games.First of all, Nadeo (the devs) are actively and constantly working on this game with new blocks, tweaks, improvements and official maps. These OFFICIAL maps alone are well worth the 10$ yearly sub. (almost at a 1$ per 10 maps or less than 1$ per month), so yes while Trackmania games are famous for how community based they are, this time there is also massive support from the devs. Trackmania 2020 is designed to be THE trackmania game. That means no new trackmania game is on the horizon any time soon. That also means no splitting the community every time a new game comes out. Keeping the devs AND the community in ONE place.
