_childDocuments_.review: I currently have about *4000* hours total on both this game (with a majority of playtime coming from Uplay) and TMNF.If you love the series then I cannot think of a single reason why this one wouldn't be the best title so far. Nadeo is very very lucky to have a community that keeps things fresh, with new interesting maps, ideas, plugins, events and competitions coming out on a weekly basis. Just look at how long TMNF is kept alive for.On a positive note, the game brought over a lot of what made TMNF fun: nearly identical physics, creative map editor and a lot of funny techniques & bugs that cater for players of all map styles. The addition of new surfaces and movable objects expands the possibilities exponentially. I am almost exclusively a lol/short map player only and have not thought the game is repetitive since it launched in Summer 2020.Nadeo added a Track of the Day mode, which then leads into a Cup of the Day event that everyone with purchased subscription can join. Every single day the competition is huge and the variety of maps is pretty decent, although it would be nice to have themed Cups of the Day more frequently. Big names play the cups on a daily basis and so the competition, if anything, is bigger than ever. On a negative note, I found that the subscription model is probably the worst thing about the game. I love the game enough to pay the same amount each year, but it's annoying that you will never be able to fully own the game unless you keep your subscription active (or if Nadeo changes the pricing model down the line). Free access includes the campaign as well as some online rooms, and sometimes the Cup of the Day is open to free access players.A big aspect of TMNF that is no longer present in this game is a permanent campaign. To this day, nothing holds more prestige in the series than holding a world record in any of the original campaign maps. The campaign now changes every three months and while it keeps things fresh and the room for hunting is still very much there, there will never be another A01 that people will hunt for decades to come. Nonetheless, I think that this is a good thing which will help TMNF to stay alive for as long as Trackmania is.I also believe the ranked mode could be better executed with perhaps a larger and frequently changing map pool (instead of just the campaign).

_childDocuments_.review: The positive reviews are 100% correct.The negative reviews are also 100% correct.Simplified, one-sided claims don't actually communicate much to new players (like myself) who just want to play a good game. So, I thought I'd summarise the general arguments on both sides, and my perspective after familiarizing myself with Trackmania (atm I'm half-silver, half-gold on the Campaign tracks; gold on all Training tracks).These are the three big spheres of discussion, as far as I see (there might be more, but these are what the Steam reviews are generally obsessed with); and it's right for this set of Pros and Cons to result in a Mixed general score. But Trackmania as an experience, as a thing to sit down with a controller and to have fun with, forgetting for a moment the studio politics and video game industry blues, is second to very few games. At 13 hours of completely free play-time, I'm in love with learning the tracks, minimizing my time, learning to drive on the different surfaces, and being braver on the sharp turns. I expect to spend at least a few more free hours trying to get gold on the second half of Campaign tracks. If you can look at the Cons above, but still bite your lip and say "well... I'll take a chance anyway" -- you won't regret it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game enough.I have played hundreds of hours of this game on the ubisoft launcher and will continue to do so on Steam.If you are a racing game fan and have not played Trackmania yet, you have to give this game a try. The free version offers a good preview of the game and the 10€ per year subscription is great value for a game that continues to grow and evolve year after year.For me Trackmania (2020) is the perfect distillation of a racing game. No extras, no car unlocks, no (micro-)transactions, no opponents that can crash you. Just you, your car, the track, and the timer.The driving mechanics feel amazing. They might seem arcady at first, but they are very indepth and mastering them (or at least getting better) is doable and very satisfying. Getting closer and closer to those author medals you are trying to beat, or climbing up your cities leaderboard on your favorite tracks feels very rewarding. There are 4 new official campaigns every year and thousands of community made tracks that you can drive, practice and set times on. And there is something for everyone. Be it the very accessible daily tournaments with thousands of players, a ranked mode or an arcady (battle-) royal mode.And don't let the ubisoft launcher scare you off, it's really not that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a racing game. This is a rage game. This is I Wanna Be The Guy but with cars. This is Getting Over It with an esports division. This is what a middle schooler with a Newgrounds account would do with a AAA budget. This game is not for normal people. It has a subscription model. The game itself will not teach you how to play it. There are a hundred hidden and unexplained mechanics you will never even know about, let alone understand how to implement, without hours upon hours of youtube tutorials. No in-game tutorial exists whatsoever. They have 'training maps' you'll be unable to complete without doing homework first. Some of these mechanics come across as niche speedrunning tricks at first, the kind of stuff you'd assume the casual player would never be expected to bother with, but you will soon find that they are 100% required to get anything beyond silver medals in any given track. Half of the things you need to even play the game at a base-line level are user-made plugins you need third-party software to gain access to. I'm talking about a Speedomoter on the UI. I'm talking about being able to see gear shifts. None of that is in the game without mods. This game is cross-platform. Console players do not have access to mods. I have 250 hours and I still don't understand drifting. There are around 5 types of drifts in this game with 4 buttons, and you will never know which one is coming out until you hit the button for them. Sometimes you'll do an actual drift, sometimes you'll just stay on the same trajectory without slowing down, and sometimes you'll slide out and go shooting off the track. There's a special drift that makes you go 1% faster that you will literally never pull off correctly, but you need to perform perfectly to get anything above bronze on track of the day. At times it feels like Mario Kart levels of RNG, but without anyone ever actually benefiting from any of it. There are ice physics in this game that require you to drive sideways in order to go as fast as the game wants you to, and this is a major mechanic you have to learn in order to play at all. Sometimes you drive on ice walls that you need an exact angle on, or you'll go so slow that you might as well be restarting. This angle is not explained or marked anywhere, and the difference is imperceptible to the naked eye. You need the angle, even for the vanilla campaign. The ice physics change every 6 months to prevent people from getting used to them. Any tracks with ice made from before 6 months ago are now impossible to complete, but are still available to try and struggle against anyway. There's such a disparity between keyboard and controller that they have 5 extra buttons that increment your steering percentage by 20% and expect you to be able to use that well in the heat of the moment, on top of 7 more buttons for camera controls. You either use a controller or you learn brain surgery, there's really no in-between for people without enough USB ports for a controller and a mouse at the same time. You need at least two of those buttons to get the ice wall angle. Users can purposefully break the game's physics in their maps. Some maps will feel more sluggish than normal. Others will be slipperier than normal. Most of the time they will not tell you they did this, gaslighting you into thinking you did something wrong somehow. You can only make maps in-game with preset minecraft blocks. Other people can model whole racetracks in Blender, but you will use minecraft blocks. In order to change the colors of the minecraft blocks, you need to alter each individual vertex of the block one by one over the course of 5 minutes per block. Or learn Blender. For in-game mapmaking. Everyone always chooses Blender. You will use minecraft blocks. The game lags at the strangest times, mostly when opening menus, like the ones that open at the start and end of every single race. Sometime you'll be starting a new round of a race and start 3 seconds behind every other racer because the game couldn't load properly. You'll lag at the finish line and finish a second and a half behind when you actually crossed it, losing you the finals of the in-game tournament you were playing. This happens to the game's most popular influencers OFTEN and has not been fixed after three full years. Despite all of these horrendous, mind-boggling issues, you will never be able to stop playing it. Turn away now and never look back. This was made by the devil. Why does it have a subscription model?

_childDocuments_.review: On August 8, 2004, a tour bus belonging to the Dave Matthews Band dumped an estimated 800 pounds (360 kg) of human waste from the bus's blackwater tank through the Kinzie Street Bridge in Chicago onto an open top passenger sightseeing boat sailing in the Chicago River below.As part of a 2005 legal settlement, the band agreed to pay $200,000 to environmental protection and other projects (equivalent to $312,000 in 2023). The band also donated $100,000 to two groups that protect the river and the surrounding area (equivalent to $156,000 in 2023).[1] The band's bus driver, Stefan Wohl, pleaded guilty to dumping the waste in April 2005.[2] The Dave Matthews Band had booked rooms at the Peninsula Hotel of 108 E. Superior Street for a two-night show at Alpine Valley Music Theatre in East Troy, Wisconsin.[3] The incident occurred between the first and second night of the concert. The band booked five buses for its show; Stefan Wohl drove the bus of the band's violinist Boyd Tinsley.During warm months, the Chicago Architecture Center offers a boat tour of the buildings along the Chicago River.[4] The boats have open-roof seating, where passengers sit during the tour.The riveted grate surface of the bridge allows liquids to pass through. The Chicago River is visible through the holes in the grate.Most Chicago bridges feature riveted grating, which is used for its strength and anti-slip properties.[5] Riveted grating allows rain, snow, and other liquids to pass through, removing the need for complicated drainage systems or to salt the bridge deck during snow, and assuring it does not ice over in wintry weather.IncidentOn Sunday, August 8, 2004, at 1:18 p.m.,[6] Wohl was alone in Tinsley's bus and driving to a downtown hotel when he emptied the bus' blackwater tank as it crossed the metal grates of the Kinzie Street bridge.[7]Passenger boat Chicago's Little Lady was hosting the 1 p.m. Chicago Architecture Foundation tour of the Chicago River. While passing under the bridge, the boat received the full contents of the tank on the seats of its open-roof terrace. Roughly two-thirds of the 120 passengers aboard the tour boat were soaked.[8] The boat immediately returned to its dock, where all passengers were issued refunds. Five passengers went to Northwestern Memorial Hospital for testing. According to the Illinois Attorney General, passengers aboard included persons with disabilities, elderly, a pregnant woman, a small child, and an infant. The filing describes the incident:The liquid waste was brownish yellow in color, and had a foul, offensive odor. The liquid human waste went into passengers' eyes, mouths, hair, and onto clothing and personal belongings, many of which were soaked. Some of the passengers suffered nausea and vomiting as a result of exposure to the human waste.[6]The boat's deck was swabbed by its crew, and service was resumed for its scheduled 3 p.m. tour.[9]

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played every Trackmania installment and has followed the series consistently since 2011, this installment in the Trackmania series is a bitter disappointment on many levels and probably the worst Trackmania ever...with the exception of the Nintendo exclusive titles.The gameplay itself is good enough, which is to be expected with the fact that this is now the fourth time Nadeo has recycled the Stadium environment. Credit must also be given to the constant updates and feature enhancements that are gradually flowing into the game, as well as the commitment to actively help shape Trackmania eSports instead of leaving it exclusively to others, as was the case before Trackmania 2020. The biggest problem for me personally are that for casual players like me, there are no real reasons to do much with the game. Royal is nice sometimes, but a team only mode. Ranked is the same, which leaves Free-To-Play players that don't want to play in a group with just the campaign and arcade mode. For everything else you have to pay, which is why I can understand the statement "free-to-play" from a marketing point of view, but only from that one.But there is the other problem ... I don't want to harp too much on Nadeo's attempts to avoid the word "subscription" as much as possible, but...it is a subscription. Kind of, because you have to keep paying to keep using the perks. Just because there's no auto-renewal option doesn't make it less of a problem, just that I don't suddenly get a message at 3am that Ubisoft has charged me 30 euros for the next year. Nice is at least that after your Access ended, you can still play the already released campaign tracks and Tracks of the Day and use all the skins you've downloaded before and the creative editors like the advanced track editor. From my point of view, only a few things are split between the Standard Access and the Club Access, where I still can't understand why they did it that way. For example, why can't I use the skins I made myself in the skin editor in Standard Access? Why can I only see ghosts with Club Access? And why can't I host my own dedicated servers until i pay for Club Access? For casual players Standard Access offers too little while Club Access costs too much somehow. Club Access is really only worth the money for those who are willing to contribute a lot to the community and want to use all the features of this access tier on a regular basis.After ManiaPlanet 4, however, I'm still skeptical about how long Nadeo will keep its promise of long-term support. I'm still a little pre-damaged with how Trackmania² or Shootmania was handled by them.Since I now have Club Access until October 2024 anyway, I'll play the game more often and see if anything changes for the better for me in that time. Not really worth the 40 euros spent on it. Please check out content about the game in advance - preferably not only from absolute Trackmania enthusiasts or eSports fanatics - to see if this game is for you or if you would rather get one or some of the other Trackmania games. For only 5 euro more than the 1 year Club Access you can get Trackmania Turbo and Trackmania United Forever in a sale - both amazing Trackmania games with more environments, tracks, custom content and skins, 3D models etc. (at least for United Forever) and - you get to keep them after you paid for them and have access to all features of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably one of the very few exceptions of Ubisoft's generic game formula. No micro-transactions or DLC, almost everything in this game is skill-based. And the skill ceiling is high, very high. However, that doesn't mean that new players can't enjoy the game - in fact, I don't think you have to be good at the game at all to be able to enjoy it. You're not going to have a bad time because people are better than you, as this game is very much based on improving your performance compared to yourself instead of others. All of this is even more true when you consider how amazing the community is in this game. Almost everyone is friendly and willing to help, so don't be afraid to ask! Trackmania heavily relies on the community and that is absolutely a good thing. The game can also be played on pretty much any input device (seriously - people play on keyboard, controller, mouse, joystick and even steering wheels).The main draws of the game itself are: - Campaign (25 maps playable for everyone including the free-to-play players, changes every 3 months to 25 new tracks at which point the leaderboards close) - Track of the day (daily, user-created and developer-curated track - switches every day at 19:00 CET) - Cup of the day (a competition driven on the TOTD, 15 minutes of qualifying which puts you in a division of 64 players based on your time, followed by knock-out rounds where the slowest drivers go out every round until 1 player wins. Usually has around 2500-3000 players. There's also a Cup of the Night and Cup of the Morning for different time zones.) - Matchmaking (ranked PvP matches driven on the campaign (and at higher ranks Esports) maps) - Royal (wacky maps with a Battle Royale-esque knockout format) - Track builder (create your own tracks)Trackmania has a high skill ceiling but also a very low barrier to entry, so just try out the free version to see if you like it. The training maps and the first few campaign maps are very easy, and you will learn the more advanced mechanics along the line if you stick with the game (you'd be surprised how crazy a game that essentially requires throttle, brake, and steering can get, which also makes it incredibly fun).As for which version to get,  gives you a clear overview of what each version offers. If you're serious about the game, I recommend club. IMO it is worth it. I'm glad they're finally bringing this game to other stores - it deserves the discoverability.

_childDocuments_.review: this game always rubbed me the wrong way even before the very first announcements of its development, specially since it was at a time where ManiaPlanet 4 was released as a mandatory update with several quality-of-life and gameplay feature changes that became actively broken or straight-up removed¹, making a scrap of everything Trackmania 2 had to offer as the successor of Trackmania Nations Forever. now with this title, it claims to be free but essentially everything that keeps the game alive (i.e community interaction, community maps, overall social features, etc) is behind a paywall. that would be okay if it wasn't for the renting model. you are not allowed to buy a license and keep it forever, not allowed to buy the up-to-date patch and keep it regardless of updates, or anything similar. you can only choose to either rent for 1 to 3 years, or play the bare bones of what it could have been.  can't do anything if still you choose to pay. the community is great and friendly, the gameplay loop is all about you against yourself (talk about Celeste and the speedrunning community in general), and the community-made content is fun to explore. just know that the rent is plaguing this game along with tons of other computer software these days, and by paying you're further supporting this.¹ edit because i forgot: some examples of changed features in the game was: removal of Local Splitscreen mode, you can no longer instantly skip the finish line animation by pressing Restart, removal of the main menu animations (it used to have a background almost resembling Midnight Club 3), texture changes imported from Trackmania Turbo that looks completely out of place in ManiaPlanet, the minimalist hud used to be similar to Trackmania 2020, but was changed into a crowded screen with a huge circle for a speed indicator, lights no longer casts multiple shadows when nearby multiple light sources, the starting position in all ManiaPlanet titles got an insignificant change which invalidated each and every replay file and world record that was sent ever since the very first releases of ManiaPlanet, the netcode became broken to the point where a lot of live events that were hosted in Trackmania 2 in general became discontinued, the list goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 55.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

_childDocuments_.review: Great racing game with a friendly, growing community. The mechanics are simple on the surface, but they hide a world of nuance and optimization that makes for consistent and rewarding skill progression. You don't even realize just how much you've improved until you come back to a map and crush your old PB with ease. Definitely recommend trying it out, especially considering it's free.Or rather, free*, as many others have pointed out. But while I agree with the complaints about the required Ubisoft launcher, regarding the pricing model I can only find fault with Nadeo's unclear communication. I spent about 50 hours free-to-play before deciding to upgrade, mostly spent doing the following:Honestly, if I dropped back down to the free tier, the only major things I'd miss would be the Track/Cup Of The Day and the ability to chat in online servers. I'm still spending most of my time doing the same things I did before I subscribed, although of course paying the $10/year gets you other things that I'm just not really using. The best part for me, though, is that if you do cancel your plan, you retain access to all the content from the year you were subscribed. (Specifically, that's 4 sets of 25 campaign tracks, 365 tracks of the day, and the advanced map editor.) So at least in that sense, it's less a SAAS‑style subscription, and more like a single $10 price to buy a year's worth of new content that you can keep indefinitely.So in conclusion: while the pricing model may at first seem convoluted or disingenuous, once you get to know the game and everything you can do in it, I suspect you'll agree that with its great gameplay and consistent new content, this free-to-play is a lot more than just a demo.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:The gameplay in TrackMania is all about speed, precision, and skill. The game features a variety of tracks, each with its own unique design, obstacles, and challenges. Players must navigate through the tracks as quickly as possible, using drifting, boosting, and jumping techniques to gain an advantage over their opponents.One of the unique aspects of TrackMania is the ability to create and share custom tracks with other players. The game includes a robust track editor that allows players to create their own tracks, complete with custom scenery, obstacles, and even custom music.Graphics:TrackMania features colorful and vibrant graphics that enhance the game's fast-paced gameplay. The tracks are designed with a variety of environments, including deserts, cities, and snow-covered mountains. The game also includes a replay editor that allows players to watch and share their best races with other players.Multiplayer:The multiplayer aspect of TrackMania is where the game truly shines. The game features both local and online multiplayer modes, allowing players to compete against each other in real-time races. The game also includes a ranking system that tracks players' progress and allows them to compete against players of similar skill levels.The game's community is incredibly active, with thousands of custom tracks and online servers available for players to join. The game also includes a social hub where players can connect with other players, share tracks, and participate in community events.Conclusion:Overall, TrackMania is a fun and addictive racing game that offers a unique blend of fast-paced gameplay, creative track design, and community features. The game's vibrant graphics, custom track editor, and multiplayer modes make it an enjoyable experience for both casual and hardcore gamers. If you're a fan of racing games or looking for a game with a strong community, TrackMania is definitely worth checking out.

The current highest ranked player (in campaign points) is granady, a wheel player, and he's a good example of how much smooth steering helps with the new car to get speed.Now onto the trick: You can go on the trackmania exchange website and download maps, and then open them with trackmania, by dropping them onto the trackmania.exe file in your game directory or right clicking the map file, clicking "open with", finding the game executable (trackmania.exe), and opening it with that. Note: some, maybe even most maps will open and say something along the lines of can't open cause "blocked user". I don't know a way to bypass this. Nadeo (official) maps should still open though, even if you don't have access to them normally.

_childDocuments_.review: Trackmania is not just a racing game; it's a finely tuned instrument of madness designed to test your patience, sanity, and ability to navigate gravity-defying loops at breakneck speeds. Ever wondered what it's like to go from feeling like a world-class racer to questioning every life choice you’ve ever made in the span of 30 seconds? Well, look no further, because Trackmania delivers that experience in spades.The game is a beautiful paradox: it’s simple yet impossibly hard, exhilarating yet soul-crushing, and somehow manages to make you feel like a driving god and a complete idiot all at once. One minute, you’re nailing every turn with surgical precision, and the next, you’re flying off the track into oblivion because you took a corner 0.1 degrees off the optimal angle. But hey, that’s just part of the Trackmania charm.The real magic of Trackmania is the community-created tracks that range from "casual Sunday drive" to "architectural fever dream." You'll be soaring through tracks that defy physics, logic, and occasionally, your will to live. And just when you think you’ve finally mastered a track, you discover that some lunatic out there shaved another half-second off the world record, making you realize that no matter how hard you try, you’ll never be good enough. But who needs self-esteem when you have a shiny gold medal taunting you?And let’s not forget the Trackmania community, a delightful group of masochists who spend hours perfecting every pixel of their car's trajectory. These are the people who willingly choose to spend their free time racing against ghost cars that mock your every mistake, reminding you that perfection is always just out of reach. But don’t worry—you’ll fit right in after you’ve restarted the same track for the 472nd time, just to nail that one jump that’s 0.01 seconds faster.In the end, Trackmania is a game that doesn’t just test your driving skills; it tests your very soul. It’s an endless loop of triumph and despair, where victory is fleeting, and failure is inevitable. But despite all the rage, the frustration, and the existential crises, you’ll keep coming back for more. Why? Because deep down, you know that maybe—just maybe—this time, you’ll hit that perfect run.Trackmania: the only game that makes you question why you even have a driver's license in the first place. 10/10 would launch my car into the stratosphere again.

In small bowl, mix flour, baking soda and salt; set aside.2 In large bowl, beat softened butter and sugars with electric mixer on medium speed, or mix with spoon about 1 minute or until fluffy, scraping side of bowl occasionally.3 Beat in egg and vanilla until smooth. _childDocuments_.review: To start; the game is not free to play, its free to try. You get 25 training maps, 10 official campaign maps, an arcade room with some community generated content, ranked 3v3, and access to the simple track editor which is barely enough to create a functional track. The paid version of the game ($20/year) gives you access to everything the game has to offer, over 100,000 community made maps, custom skins, Cup of the Day (daily competition on never before seen tracks picked by the developers), and whole multitude of other things. You will without a doubt get your 20$ worth of content, and there are no micro-transactions offered.With all that out of the way, this is the only negative thing I can possibly say about this game. The main thing to takeaway from the game is the community. It has the nicest and most helpful community from any game I have ever seen or played. If you have a question about anything there are people lined up to help you. There are discord servers for every possible niche in the game so you can find people with similar interests as you. While its sometimes frustrating that the developers rarely interact with the community, the community steps up and runs things themselves. There are competitions held and funded by community members on a weekly basis. There are community made plugins published all the time that help with QoL, UI, or even new multiplayer game modes. Having spent so much time in looter shooter games and things completely unrelated to Trackmania, I personally would have never seen myself becoming addicted to a racing game. I'm glad it happened and I wish I could experience the game for the first time again.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are someone that enjoys both racing games and competitive games, Trackmania is for you. I have hundreds of hours on this game before it has come to steam, but I suspect I'll be using Steam from now on.Pros:- Astronomical skill ceiling- Addictive, can be played in short bursts- You can be as serious about this game as you want to be- It has an extremely generous monetization model (you really only need the $10 version).- An extremely dedicated community that is constantly pumping out new maps, content, etc- The community for the game consists of people from many different nations. You will get to meet and talk with people from all over the world, and the vast majority of them are very friendly. This is genuinely the least toxic gaming community you will find in a competitive gameCons:- If you're new to the game, you will suck. And you will probably suck for a long time. That's just how it is with games like this. The resources for improvement/tutorials/guides etc are out there if you're willing to put in effortI'm biased, as TM is one of my top multiplayer games of all time. At the very least, give it a try since it's free!

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my go to game for the past 2-3 years. Just wanted to clear up a few things about the mixed reviews if you were on the fence about trying this:-There is enough free content to play to know if you would like this game. Go for the gold/author in the current campaign, some old training maps, royal, ranked, and arcade. If you do like the game standard and club are INCREDIBLY cheap and worth buying. $10-30 for a whole year is basically nothing nowadays, especially for how much I get out of it. -I'm not a huge fan of Ubisoft, but the launcher isn't any worse than Rainbow6 or any other Ubi game. Now that the 2 main criticisms everyone seems to have are out of the way, the main draw of the game to me is the community. Least toxic gaming community I've ever been in. So many creative, competitive, and nice people. I used to spend my time grinding campaign maps and cup of the day / track of the day leaderboards, but now I spend most of my time in a group that does speed mapping where we all create maps in 15 minutes and play on each others maps after in the TM US discord (don't have to be from the US to join). Side note: Rocket League used to be one of my main games and this rivals the car control and consistency/fairness of the game. I find TM much more relaxing due to the more well behaved community and knowing that it's okay to just mess up and restart. I do also feel it would be wrong to not include some of the actual pitfalls of this game so:-Slightly too addicting-You need club access to view ghosts which can be a huge advantage knowing the current best strategy.-A lot of the quality of life stuff relies on having open planet (which is a free software you can and should get for the game if you have standard/club).-There have been a couple physics updates that made some old map's author times harder/impossible to get.This game is +++, but there is a huge learning curve. Don't be too surprised when you can't immediately drive as fast as Wirtual.Also I make the French maps and i'm not even French. Sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: The Hypnagogic Marketplace: Advocating for Advertising in DreamsIn the bustling landscape of modern advertising, innovation knows no bounds. From billboards to social media, marketers constantly seek new avenues to engage consumers. Amidst this pursuit, a provocative concept has emerged: advertising within dreams. While initially met with skepticism, the notion of integrating ads into the subconscious realm warrants exploration. This essay posits that incorporating advertisements into dreams could revolutionize the advertising industry and enhance consumer engagement.Dreams have long captivated human imagination. They serve as a gateway to the subconscious, offering insights into our deepest desires, fears, and aspirations. Within this ethereal realm, the mind is unbound by the constraints of reality, allowing for surreal experiences and creative exploration. Moreover, dreams play a vital role in cognitive processes, aiding memory consolidation, problem-solving, and emotional regulation.In the digital age, advertising has permeated virtually every aspect of daily life. From online banners to sponsored content, consumers are inundated with promotional messages. However, amidst this saturation, traditional advertising channels face diminishing returns as audiences grow increasingly adept at filtering out marketing noise. Consequently, advertisers are compelled to seek novel strategies to capture consumer attention and drive engagement.Dreamvertising, the practice of embedding advertisements within dreams, represents a bold frontier in the realm of marketing. Drawing inspiration from the science fiction trope of "incepting" ideas into dreams, proponents argue that dreams offer a unique opportunity to deliver targeted messages directly to the subconscious mind. By leveraging the suggestibility of the dreaming brain, advertisers can create immersive brand experiences that resonate on a deeply emotional level.Advocates of dreamvertising cite several potential benefits. Firstly, dreams offer a captive audience, as individuals spend a significant portion of their lives asleep. By infiltrating this dormant state, advertisers can access consumers' minds when they are most receptive, bypassing conscious resistance. Moreover, the malleable nature of dreams allows for seamless integration of advertising content, ensuring that it blends seamlessly with the dream narrative. This subtlety reduces the risk of consumer backlash and enhances the effectiveness of the message. Additionally, dreamvertising has the potential to enhance brand recall and emotional engagement by forging deep associations between the brand and the dream experience.Despite its potential advantages, dreamvertising raises ethical concerns regarding privacy, consent, and manipulation. Critics argue that infiltrating individuals' dreams without their explicit consent violates their autonomy and undermines the sanctity of the subconscious realm. Moreover, there are concerns about the potential psychological impact of inundating the dreaming mind with commercial messages, leading to cognitive overload or even subconscious manipulation. Additionally, the prospect of advertisers gaining access to intimate aspects of individuals' inner lives raises troubling questions about privacy and surveillance.In conclusion, the concept of advertising within dreams represents a provocative yet polarizing idea. While proponents tout its potential to revolutionize advertising and enhance consumer engagement, skeptics raise valid concerns about privacy, consent, and manipulation. As society grapples with the ethical implications of dreamvertising, it is imperative to engage in thoughtful discourse and rigorous regulation to ensure that any implementation prioritizes individual autonomy and psychological well-being. Ultimately, whether dreams become the next frontier of advertising remains to be seen, but the conversation surrounding dreamvertising underscores the ever-evolving nature of marketing in the digital age.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this review with the very misrepresented elephant in the room: the subscription model.The subscription gives you access to a years worth of campaigns, track of the days and the track editor. You keep all of these after your subscription is lapsed. The subscription is basically just $10 to get a years worth of content, which you can then play as much as you want after your sub is done. You only lose access to custom servers and car customization at the $30 tier, which means you lose access to either optional gameplay cosmetics which every game on the planet now charges you for, and access to servers which many MMOs and similar games would make you pay to maintain anyway. You would have to play this game for more than 7 years before it became more expensive than a AAA game, at which point I think its safe to argue you got your moneys worth. I find it worrying that almost all reviews right now omit the fact that you keep what you payed for during your subscription time.I also find the complain about lack of steam achievements strange. What achievements would you even put in a trackmania game that aren't just "play 1000 tracks"? The game has a medal system to track your performance in every map in the game (including player made ones), and grinding author medals is the traditional trackmania past time. I will leave comments open on this review because I would like to hear what genuinely interesting achievements could be added to the game that many of the negative reviewers believe are missing beyond what is already tracked in the game itself.The game itself is the best Trackmania has been, thanks to the subscription model allowing continued development of the game including new blocks/track options, plenty of official maps, and general polish. It is probably the best trackmania right now in terms of gameplay, where it ultimately matters most. There is an inherit satisfaction in improving yourself and your own times, which the game heavily encourages, and is refreshing from many of the direct PvP games and similar on the market.My major complaint is on the tutorial side. The game doesn't explain its mechanics very well, and there a lot of subtle tricks that can even be critical on player made maps, but the game never teaches them to you. It isn't a hard game to pick up and play, but if you start trying to push for better times and medals, you will find the game doesn't really prepare you for them.I also think the soundtrack is pretty repetitive and bland. Definitely bring your own music for this one.Overall, the game is good value and plays very well.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning, it's pretty addicting. It'll be 10 o'clock at night, and you'll say "Oh I'll just finish one more level and then I'll be done for the night." Then you finish the level but you're really close to getting the gold medal. So you say "Oh, I'll just get the gold medal for this track and call it a day." Then you finally get a good run and get the gold medal, but it was such a good run that you're only a few tenths of a second off of the author medal. So you say "Oh, well I'll just get this author medal and then call it there." And when you finally get the author medal you'll pump your fist in celebration, look at the clock, and realize it's 3 am.And to talk about the "negatives" people seem to have with it. I don't mind it launching through the ubisoft launcher after I press "play" on steam, as it only opens for a second and then I'm in the game. I'd rather it launch through steam, but it's not that much of a hassle at all. I also don't mind the subscription model. It's pretty cheap as far as games go these days and it ends up paying the developers to make more maps every 3 months. You don't even need the subscription to play the new maps when they release. They're free. I got the sub because I finished all of the current season's maps to a point where I wanted to play some others, and found out you can play all of the previous maps from all of the other campaigns. So there are literally hundreds of official maps I can play now because I paid $10 (per year btw, not month). Not to mention the near infinite amount of user made levels. That is such a better system than the alternative, which would be what every other free game uses. Where they lock stuff behind pay walls constantly and make it to where you'd have to play an ungodly amount of the game to unlock the stuff you want, or just pay money. And with a lot of games, they make it to where you CAN'T unlock it without paying money. Trackmania's subscription service is way better than that. Don't get me wrong, I'd rather not pay it, I'd rather pay once and be done. But this is the best we can ask for, for receiving the amount of support this game gets (Which is quite a lot of support).

_childDocuments_.review: I've put many hours into this game since release using Ubisoft's launcher. It always had 3 payment levels: Paying a big yearly subscription, a smaller one with slightly less content or paying nothing and have access to even less content. More than 90% of that content belongs to the hard-working community, and you still have to pay to be able to access all of it. With no surprise, the same applies to skins. The subscription method has always been a big no for me but at least I had a seasonal campaign I could play for free and a few online modes. With the last update, however, the free version has been reduced to a mere demo. And that sucks. It seems to me Ubisoft/Nadeo are willing to ruin the little fun this title had left at this point for people like me if that means they can make more money.I feel very underwhelmed by their decision making and very sad about not playing again, but this is goodbye. I won't touch this beautiful game until I can really buy it and not every single year (even if it's ''cheap''), just like any other game. I would gladly pay 60 bucks once and be done with it.I really hope things change in the future but at their current state I can only uninstall and write this review.TLDR: Free version no longer worth our time

_childDocuments_.review: Hotwheels meets F1. Drive on the walls and ceiling, bounce on water, navigate many challenging surface types and boosts, launch thousands of feet across the map, and learn to navigate each unique and puzzle-like route before fine-tuning your lines to shave off a few more hundredths. Amazing community-created content with custom scenery; you'll never run out of incredible tracks to play. Or build your own with powerful track builder. Instant race and checkpoint restarts. Has both serious time-attack with a high-skill ceiling and easy-to-learn, silly, no-crash-damage arcade fun simultaneously. Go as hard as you want and go for author medals and leader board placement or just enjoy the tracks and scenery with gold medals. Runs great on almost any machine, including the Steam Deck. Inexpensive subscription is well worth it. Recently added to Steam, but have been playing via Ubisoft Connect for over 300 hours. Love. This. Game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've noticed that many people dislike the fact that the game is subscription-based, and I have to agree – it seems rather impractical. I would prefer to simply buy the game once and be done with it. However, if the game is good, it's good. I've always had a soft spot for Trackmania, and I regret not having played more of Trackmania Nations Forever (TMNF) when I had the chance to do so back then.Recently, a friend and I revisited TMNF and had a blast. We quickly discovered speed maps and found ourselves enjoying the gameplay on those servers immensely. This led me to discover that Trackmania received a reboot in 2020 and was coming soon to Steam.I began playing it on the Ubisoft Launcher, and I was mostly frustrated with its peculiar payment model and the fact that it was only available through Ubisoft. When it finally arrived on Steam, I played a bit more. Recently, I picked up the game again and got even more into it than before. All I can say is that this game is incredible. It introduces new surfaces like Ice, Plastic, and water, along with new types of boosters that allow your car to hover or be pushed down, defying gravity. These additions enable players to be even more creative than ever before.Mastering a map in Trackmania feels like solving a highly enjoyable puzzle. You need to figure out how to minimize airtime, prevent slipping, and maintain maximum speed without hitting a wall. Depending on the map, gear changes can significantly affect the car's speed, adding numerous variables to optimize. Furthermore, in Trackmania, there's only one car, so any failures can be attributed to the player, which can be frustrating at times, but it's something I personally enjoy in games. The satisfaction that comes from clearing a challenging author medal is akin to the feeling you get after defeating a notoriously difficult boss after countless attempts. The main difference is that in Trackmania, hundreds of attempts can be quite common, so a great deal of patience may be required. This is why, before considering a subscription, I recommend completing the entire campaign with all author medals to determine if this game suits your taste.To be honest, even while playing for free, I find that there's a considerable amount of content available. With just the campaign, training maps, royal mode, and ranked play, there's a substantial amount of grinding required to earn all the author medals for the first time. You could easily spend 20 hours or more on this content alone, so, in my opinion, it's already a great deal for free and helps you decide if you want to invest in the game.In conclusion, I believe this game is exceptionally good. It consistently receives new content at a decent pace, which justifies the subscription plan. Moreover, it's free from any fear of missing out (FOMO) or gambling elements.Additionally, I'd like to mention that Trackmania Nations Forever still has active servers and is also great for playing full-speed maps and RPGs, which are very long puzzle maps. If you can find it on sale, I highly recommend getting it to experience that old-school Trackmania vibe.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to go against the grain here and say that this game has one of the most reasonable price models I've seen in a very long time. I know it's easy to have a knee-jerk reaction to a game that was once a buy-to-own product switching to a subscription/F2P model but hear me out.The game is fantastic, it hits all the notes you want in a Trackmania game, if you've never played TM before then try it, if you have played TM before you'll probably enjoy it. My only real gripe with the game is I wish loading times were shorter, server queues were shorter and there was less downtime. In older games it felt like you could hop in and out of races much faster.The biggest problem Nadeo had with TM was that they gave the community the tools to make an infinite amount of content, why would you ever buy any other TM related content when the community maps can keep the game alive indefinitely? This led to a FIFA/Cod style release plan of new game ever year or two to keep revenue up and unfortunately, also split the playerbase. Remember playing Canyon or Lagoon? Yeah, me neither, barely.Instead, here you have a F2P offering that is very generous in what it gives to free players, thousands of maps for free, access to thousands more community maps, Royal mode, Ranked, the map editor, etc. €10/year is enough to give you 100% of the content you need to enjoy the game, anything over that is extra support for the Devs basically. What I really appreciate is that it doesn't use the same microtransaction techniques that full €70 games use, no "buy this skin now or it's gone", no sunsetting of content, no bundles, no map packs, etc.Instead, Nadeo curate entire campaigns every 3 months, pick community made maps for daily tracks and championships and seem to genuinely engage with the community they have fostered. Best of all they don't split the community across several games anymore.For the price of Trackmania Stadium, Canyon and Lagoon, you get 3 years of access to an insane amount of content with ongoing support for the next several years. For the price of nothing, you still get access to most of it. Unfortunately the studio still needs to make money to keep the game alive but this is the best possible way they could have done it. Oh, and if you stop paying for the subscription you get the keep all the content you received up to that point, which sounds like it's not a big deal but think how many devs would be happy to take it away from you if given the chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Trackmania is the Counter-Strike of racing games: instantly understandable, impossible to truly master; a simple concept, perfected, yet with near-infinite depth. A game where your character doesn't get better, YOU get better. Both feature mechanics are as crisp and clean as they come. Several tricks that top players use were originally bugs from past games the developers have since embraced. These unconventional features allow both games to be as silly and goofy or serious and technical as players want -- entirely held up by a wealth of user-made content.I personally don't care for a lot of the newer content (specifically the new cars), but the beauty of a game like this is that official, developer-made content is just one of many ways to enjoy the game, and thus can simply be ignored.Yes, the free-tier experience is truly terrible, and Ubisoft does an awful job marketing as a free-to-play game rather than something more accurate like free-to-try. And yes, I am generally not a fan of subscription service-based games. I think it would be a lot more palatable with even a simple change like, paying for a new season of tracks, than the Haaaaving said all that, this game frankly just *is* worth $20 a year. And considering the fact that there are NO micro-transactions in this game, I think that $1.67/mo is more than fair for a game who's developers are constantly releasing new content, hosting community events like Cup of the Day, etc, not to mention the server costs associated with allowing players to create essentially INFINITE tracks, alongside a persistent, global leaderboard for each one of those tracks, letting people host their own games on Ubisoft servers, upload custom skins, vehicle and terrain models, etc.Yeah, a couple bugs could be fixed here and there, and major community-solutions like OpenPlanet could be implemented directly into the game, making them far more accessible for new players. But all of these things are just tiny blemishes on a game that is utterly best-in-class, and by a crazy margin.TL:DR - the best racing game you'll ever play, with an endless wealth of incredible, community-made tracks, but with a somewhat imperfect business-model.

_childDocuments_.review: Just as a heads up, I probably have an extra 2 - 3 thousand hours on Epic before I moved to Steam. While this may look like a racing game, in reality this is a speedrunning game. Barring a few in-game competitions, the only opponent is yourself and the leaderboards. A surprisingly addicting game when most maps are 30-60 seconds long and a reset is just a button press away. I think you can see where I'm going with this.A robust history and dedicated community. With the number of surfaces, cars, racing styles, and tricks/bugs found by the community, there is something for everyone and, for the most part, a never ending variation of maps and styles. If you're the creative type, the map editor is grid based and pretty intuitive to use, but you can also choose to go off grid if you're feeling a little reckless. Perhaps you can join that community and possibly have your map chosen as the Track of the Day, where a new community made map is chosen every day to be featured in the game.I do understand some peoples gripes with the pay-to-play, although I feel like 20 dollars a year is not that steep, just as a personal opinion. You can also turn off in-game ads, which are only seen when you are actually on a map in the stadium and they are displayed on giant screens. I may be a bit biased as I've spent years now engrossed in the community, but that's half of the game really. A game that seems shallow on the surface, but when you start digging, it gets endlessly deep.

_childDocuments_.review: In the past trackmania games felt zany but physics intuitive and in alignment. Every wheel exerting forward force or spinning delivering absolutes. Even if you hadn't encountered a map or situation before, you could assume by instinct after 2 hours of playing how your vehicle would function. This would let you play and just drive... simply drive and refine.Now they have implemented wet dry or dirty tires, plastic ice wood penalty surfaces ect ect ect. The problem isn't the surfaces. Its great to have the new surfaces. But none of them feel like they are from the same game. They spit in the face of the games own established basic physics and simplicity. Stupid ♥♥♥♥ like burning a turn on ice in gear three might shoot you straight back and out as if you had 0 forward pull all of a sudden, but if you are one KM into 4th you will be drifting slightly forward. These non sense micro game mechanics based off nothing are pervasive, and not at all fun.Worse is the effect of this multitude of diverse low friction surface implementation on the state of the games maps. 99% contain them. Functionally on these surfaces you are moving side ways and driving forward. The camera is optimal for navigating the turn your in, but in such side driving, its impossible to line up your next turn; doubly so as it has to be both lined up started in advance on ice. It makes the act of just driving impossible. Every map is hitting a slip spot blind and guessing at what comes next inevitably crashing and repeating. It ruins what I liked about the game. To even enter and be competative at a copper level, you really need to have at minimum 10 hours of dry boring practice game play. We're talking tutorial search hard corner practice maps, and pre-running tourny maps game play to enter copper and have a chance at all, not win, but have a chance... All the maps are made for that level of player using the new surfaces. I myself would practice them and do them, but they are a nerdy level of outside reality dumb mechanics to learn and simply not at all fun. Replaying failure to practice something you don't even like more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: The "paywall" people are complaining about is currently $21 a year. While I would prefer to buy the game outright and not have to deal with subscriptions, $21 a year is not too much to ask when it comes to supporting a game that is very well made and alot of fun to play.Hopefully someday we can get away from this whole "Free to Play" model. There is a certain type of gamer that sees Free to Play and somehow expects the entire game to be completely free. I am the exact opposite. If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is. If I enjoy a game that somebody worked hard to make, I have no problem supporting them as long as I don't feel like they are trying to rip me off. There is a ton of content in Trackmania, the graphics are very nice and $21 a year a very fair price to pay to have unlimited access to this game, IMHO.The game is basically time trials. It's not something I love to do everyday, but every now and then it is alot of fun to see how far you can advance up the leaderboards. There is alot of restarting, alot of mistakes, it's an easy game to play and a hard game to master, but if you make a mistake you're one button push away from restarting anytime you want. The tracks aren't very long in most cases, so it's a very fast paced game but you can spend as much time as you like on each track. There is nothing sim about the tracks, it is very arcade, but I find it alot of fun to try and get the gold medal on every track. I would prefer the tracks to be a bit more realistic, but that's just me.Not everyone that loves racing will like this game, but if you like working on lap times and seeing where you stack up on the leaderboard, Trackmania is absolutely worth trying. Everyone has a right to their own opinion, but IMHO, the negative reviews for this game are not justified in most cases.

_childDocuments_.review: Polished, next-gen Trackmania game handicapped by an annoying monetization scheme.Key word here is . Notice I didn’t use  word in describing how Ubisoft wants to empty your wallet. In current year of FOMO battle passes, overpriced skin packs and sacrificing gameplay elements into a microtransaction hellhole, Trackmania’s scheme seems to be relatively tame in comparison when it comes to price and fairness.However... it is still baffling and flabbergasting how you can turn Trackmania – a game simple as a shovel – into a subscription service with literal hundreds of rows of a features checklist (splitted between different paying plans!). It simply makes me sad and tired that we cannot just buy the game and enjoy it, just like I can install old games from that series and boot them without a purchase popup waiting for me at the main menu... and Ubisoft Connect, which is maintaining its cancer status.Still, you can get some fun by not paying anything. Ubisoft dislikes effort and you would need to try really,  hard to screw up Trackmania’s twist on the racing genre. It is a formula known for years and it is still a competitive and perfectionist dreamscape, true to its Nations roots. I would lie, if I said that fun of doing some fullspeed drifts on banked corners evaporated over all those years.Additionally, new blocks and modes that are also available to non-buying customers do bring some fresh air into Stadium’s environment. While there is some truth to the opinion that this is still a rehash of a nearly 20 year old game, I feel that, for me, Nadeo brought enough to the table to ease on criticizing them for sticking to the same cars and physics over the years.However, that doesn’t mean it is all roses and rainbows in the gameplay department. Ice physics are a complete miss and I definitely wouldn’t miss them being cut entirely from the game. They are extremely unfun to play with and they go against the keyboard-centric appeal of the game. Additionally, friends with which I did play with online in the competitive 3vs3 mode had annoying disconnecting issues - making them abandon the game.There is no higher pondering here. It’s an another good game tainted by a greedy company. Thus, review verdict stands as it is right now. There is hope somebody will eventually come to their senses and offers a product unsoiled with purchase checklists and subscription popups.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like it.Sure, the game has quite a bit of third party tools to make more detailed tracks with new scenery, but i still liked TMNF and TM2 more than this.First off, we gotta talk about the pricing. For free, you get the current seasonal campaign, ranked matchmaking and the arcade multiplayer rooms. Car customization is locked behind a 30$ paywall, which is already inferior to TMNF. For 60$, you can keep your car customization for 3 years. I don't want to pay another 60$ after three years just to play this game with the same functionality of a free game from 2009 (?). Nor do i want this to be normalized.In terms of modding, this game is a lot more closed off. Sure, games are more than just what the community can make of it, but i miss the ability to completely change the way my car looked. Now you can't do that because the speedometer is attached to the car, and not the HUD. Which means without plugins, you can't see how fast you're going if your car is facing a certain direction away from the camera. You can't mod the music either, which was something i really liked in TMNF. Having an in-server jukebox really was a nice time.Also, i really miss the old environments. Canyon was my favorite, the cars drifted easily and it felt satisfying to drive. All that's in this game is the Stadium environment, along with the fact that we have regressed from a stadium in the middle of a city like in TM Turbo, back to a floating stadium in the middle of the sky, which kinda takes the personality away from it.Ultimately, i don't like the new Trackmania. I liked TMNF more than this. TMU will always be my favorite.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on UbiSoft Launcher before the release on Steam. It's an incredibly fun game, it's difficult to start with but the more practice you get the more you improve and there's room for lots of improvement so you'll never get bored. Yes, there is subscriptions in this game but to buy Standard access it is incredibly cheap - club access is quite a bit more expensive if you wanted to get car skins/join a club/see world records.However, even without the subscriptions you can still get a nice taste of the game, you can experience Ranked mode as well as Royal mode (which is incredibly fun if I do say so myself). You can also unlock skins from Royal mode that you can use any time too, there's no paywall for that I believe.I understand people being frustrated with subscriptions but you aren't forced to pay for it unless you want to participate in Cup of the Day or Campaign. _childDocuments_.review: Trackmania is a dazzling showcase of high-speed thrills and creativity that takes the racing genre to exhilarating new heights. Developed by Nadeo and published by Ubisoft, this game offers a unique blend of precise control, mind-bending tracks, and an expansive community-driven content creation platform that keeps you coming back for more.Gameplay: 9/10Trackmania’s gameplay is a testament to the "easy to learn, hard to master" philosophy. The controls are simple and intuitive, allowing players to dive right into the action. However, mastering the intricate tracks and achieving those perfect times requires precision and practice. The game’s physics are spot-on, providing a satisfying balance between arcade fun and realistic handling.Graphics: 8/10Visually, Trackmania is stunning. The tracks are beautifully designed, with a variety of themes ranging from lush forests to futuristic cityscapes. The attention to detail in the environments and the sleek car models add to the immersive racing experience. While the graphics might not push the boundaries of modern gaming technology, they are polished and fit perfectly with the game’s fast-paced aesthetic.Sound: 7.5/10The soundtrack of Trackmania complements the high-energy gameplay with an upbeat and adrenaline-pumping selection of tracks. Sound effects, from the roar of the engines to the screeching tires, enhance the immersion. However, the audio experience, while solid, doesn’t particularly stand out or elevate the game to another level.Content and Replayability: 10/10One of Trackmania’s strongest points is its vast amount of content and endless replayability. The game features a robust single-player campaign with a plethora of challenging tracks to conquer. However, the real magic lies in its community-driven content. Players can create, share, and compete on custom tracks, ensuring a virtually limitless supply of new challenges. The competitive leaderboards and frequent in-game events keep the community engaged and motivated to improve their skills.Multiplayer: 9/10Trackmania shines in its multiplayer modes, offering a variety of ways to compete with friends and players around the world. Whether you’re racing head-to-head in real-time or battling for the top spot on the leaderboards, the multiplayer experience is seamless and thrilling. The social aspect, combined with the intense competition, makes for an engaging and dynamic racing environment.Community and Support: 9/10Nadeo and Ubisoft have done an excellent job supporting Trackmania with regular updates, events, and community engagement. The developers listen to player feedback and continually refine the game, ensuring a vibrant and active player base. The strong community support, along with the extensive customization options, helps foster a dedicated and passionate player community.Overall: 9/10Trackmania is a must-play for racing enthusiasts and gamers looking for a high-octane, creative, and endlessly replayable experience. Its blend of precise controls, stunning tracks, and robust community features make it a standout title in the racing genre. Whether you’re a casual player or a competitive racer, Trackmania offers something for everyone, making it a timeless addition to any gaming library.Pros:Intuitive and precise controlsGorgeous track designsEndless replayability with community-driven contentEngaging multiplayer modesCons:Audio experience is good but not exceptionalSome tracks can be extremely challenging, which might frustrate newcomersVerdict:Trackmania delivers a perfect blend of high-speed action and creative freedom, making it a racing game that will keep you on the edge of your seat and coming back for more. Don’t miss out on this exhilarating ride!

_childDocuments_.review: Is it wrong to be sad when my Trackmania friends are playing a different game when I'm on by myself? Because I am. Ranked is a rush. I am forcefully pushed when absolute monsters come into the matchmaking lobby and it's a huge rush pulling runs out of your ass knowing it's all or nothing when you've already put your soul on the track and there's no looking back now because you've already queue'd. I'm relatively new to the game. In fact, I am a new player. Logging almost 2k hours in the span of a year between console and pc (switched to pc) should tell you enough of my opinion on the GEM of a game and how it can potentially bring out the best of your abilities in one match and at the same time humble you in the next match against the exact same players. This is coming from a nobody who is ranked top 33 world in ranked and currently grinding the climb. If you're a competitive player who loves SPEED and sitting on the edge of your seat with F1 mechanics and physics with player skill levels ultimately deciding the difference within thousands of a second to decide a winning team than yes, this is the game for you. The community is another experience as well. I've played some toxic games but the community here in Trackmania 2020 is by far the best player positive community I've ever had the privilege of playing with. With the Community in control of the content in this game, the content is almost infinite. Player created tracks. Player created Custom Car Skins and even the clubs with Custom Campaigns and Challenges and Modes. Possibilities are almost endless. The size of the game is also tiny. I remember when I started back in spring 2023 the game may have been all of 3 gigs of space, maybe doubled now to 6 gigs.. if that. So it's never a burden of space in your game library unless you're just terrible with your Storage Management. Even then, you'll more than likely replace a 30+ gigabyte game with this one. I haven't played another racing game since I was a kid when Need for Speed Hot Pursuit 2 came out for Ps2 or again maybe close to a decade ago.. Forza was it, for Xbox and I probably won't play another racing game and have as much enjoyment as I do with Trackmania 2020. Cheers! Happy Hunting. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT on 11/21/2023:I still highly recommend this game. It is one of those games that gets continually more enjoyable the more that you play it. With that said, I do not believe that the "Free to Play" tag necessarily still applies to this game. Instead, I think it should now be labelled free to try. Starting in January the game will no longer allow free players to play the entire seasonal campaign. There are other changes as well, but this is the big one. With that said, I still think everyone who enjoys racing games should give it a try and if they decide that they enjoy it, they should buy the $20 paid access.Original:This game is one of the few examples of a crazy high skill ceiling, but able to be enjoyed by all. I'm painfully average at TrackMania games, but I still get more enjoyment out of this game, and the series as a whole, than most other games I've played. This game is a rare instance of Ubisoft doing something right. If you are at all interested in the game, I implore you to download it and give it a shot. Even with the free tier, you will have plenty of content to keep you busy for quite some time.And concerning the subscription model, I think there needs to be some clarification. I too was confused when i saw the game was subscription-based, but I think a lot of confusion could have been avoided had Nadeo and Ubisoft used different terminology. The "subscription" does not auto-renew. Instead, using terminology more commonly used in video games nowadays, you are paying for a 1 or 3 year season or content pass. So, when your pass (or subscription) runs out, you get to keep all of the content you unlocked and earned while your subscription was active. You do not lose access to it.Either way, just try the game out for free. As I previously said, there is plenty available in the free tier for newcomers to be kept busy for quite some time. If you then decide you enjoy the game, you can go ahead and buy either standard or club access at that time.

_childDocuments_.review: Trackmania is my favourite racing game by a long way. It controls equally as well with keyboard controls as it does with controller and always offers up an opportunity to improve, regardless of how skilled you are at the game.The main part of Trackmania is the racing, you're given a course, usually between 30 seconds and 2 minutes long and you're tasked with setting the best possible time on. You can race against a bronze medal time, if you beat that you can race against the faster Silver, then Gold and finally Author times. If you conquer that time the game will offer you ghosts of the fastest people in your region, country or even the world to race against and try and beat. And, of course, you can always take on the most consistently annoying opponent of all: Personal Best.The lack of randomness in the physics of this game means that any mistakes you make feel like your own fault and you can learn from them, the most other racers can do is distract you from your race (there's no physical interaction with other cars) so when you do mess up, it's never anyone else's fault, this I find refreshing in an online multiplayer game.The player-made tracks featured are as varied as they can be gorgeous which gives the game essentially infinite replayability. The community around the game has meant it's grown to much more than the base offering.I've so far played 50 hours on Steam but almost 300 in total and still enjoy coming back to it. Highly recommended, the standard yearly subscription is currently super good value too, which I appreciate.The only downside to this game is that they insist it uses the Ubisoft launcher, this can cause issues, especially on Steam Deck (though the game runs quite well on that system) and it's a shame the achievement system is through that instead of Steam.

For the most part, this is the only way I play the campaign. There are club rooms with the full campaign, but I have yet to see any of them with more than 3 people in them at a time. I like playing in full lobbies, I don't care what place I finish, I just enjoy playing the campaign with other people and I don't feel like I can do that anymore because all of the campaign lobbies are empty.Then there's Royal. It used to be a fun game mode that was kind of more of a cooperative puzzle mode where you worked with your team to get through progressively harder tracks and tried to progress as far as you could, as a team, in the time limit. When a member on your team passed a track, the rest of the team could move forward (after a delay) and try the harder tracks. This helped let everyone on the team contribute to progress because different people are better at different types of tracks and kept players who weren't great at a track from holding the team back. It also didn't matter very much if you didn't have a full team. With the new changes, completing a section no longer moves you forward, but gives you stars based on your placement (1 for bronze, 2 for silver, etc) which means that, even if you're setting world record times, you still have to pass a track multiple times to move on. The stars are also tied to the player, not the team, meaning everyone has to complete the track to move on. This completely removes the teamwork from this mode and, as a result, having (or being) a less skilled player on your team will hurt your team's progress. It also means that playing a match takes about twice as long with you potentially being stuck on the same section for the entire time. Having fewer players on your team now also puts you at a very big disadvantage, a team of 1 now has to complete 3 times as many sections to keep up with a team of 3.Hopefully, this season was just a misstep and these modes will be fixed moving forward. At its core, the game is still good, and worth checking out for free if you like racing games, but until the free-to-play restrictions are removed from the paid mode, I don't think it's worth paying for anymore.Ubisoft connect also should not be required, or if it's going to be required, it should at least carry over club access with it. If you buy club access on one platform it only unlocks for that platform even though the same account is shared between platforms. No other cross-platform game that I know of works like this.
