_childDocuments_.review: I have been following this franchise for over 15+ years. I own every. single. TrackMania. title. This game in particular, which I have played for over 3,000 hours ALONE, is the newest one..... and it has been one hell of an adrenaline shot for the 20 year long franchise (the first one debuted in 2003!!). Gonna be honest here folks..... it was waning. TrackMania Turbo brought some more visibility to the table with it being released on consoles as well as PC, but it absolutely PALES in comparison to what this one brings. It helps a great deal that, unlike ManiaPlanet before it (TrackMania 2 + ShootMania), TrackMania 2020 is way more accessible, which is saying a lot for Ubisoft Nadeo, one of the smaller studios under Ubisoft. This is prevalent in the gameplay; easy to learn and hard to master is the bang-on accurate description of the driving. The skill ceiling is INSANE..... to this day, I personally have seen nothing that comes close in the competition that's doing things the way TrackMania does. There are multiple surfaces and effects you'll encounter while playing, and combined with the stellar driving create an experience unlike any other. It's the best part of the game..... and that's a good thing.Even better is the User Generated Content..... most of which is community hosted! Sites like  are the backbone of this community, and the community often collectively outputs more than the developers!That's not to say the devs don't do anything, far from it...... Nadeo have really stepped up to the plate versus ManiaPlanet and have (for the most part) delivered consistent seasonal updates throughout the game's now almost 3 year lifespan. While some are small, others are game-changing; the recent Winter 2023 update added a TON of new blocks to the game!Speaking of blocks..... the map editor. Where to begin....... my connection to this feature runs deep. I first found TrackMania as a young boy, a young boy of which had a particular fascination with building Hot Wheels sets and LEGOs! Playing with the editor was indeed a similar feeling..... and that feeling remains in the present.The map editor in general is powerful...... you have Blocks and Items to work with; Blocks being based on grid versus the more flexible off-grid Items allows for versatility with what you want to create. With just the basic vanilla blocks by themselves, the community has made some INCREDIBLE stuff. It gets even better when you realize this game has a mesh modeler that allows you to create, IN THE GAME, custom items and blocks that further add to what is possible. There's also the 3 block placement modes..... standard, ghost mode (for blockmixing), and free mode for going CRAZY. You can literally make WHATEVER YOU WANT. The game does have limitations though..... but those limitations are at a far enough away point that in most cases it's a nonfactor! It is up to each player/mapper to discover for themselves what they wish to create! This doesn't even get into all the community tools and plugins people have made!This TrackMania has also stepped up it's content offerings beyond the seasonal campaigns and user maps; Track of the Day (available with Standard Access and beyond) offers a brand new map every day that's handpicked by the developers via Map Review, where people can submit their maps for review. Cup of the Day also happens in tandem with TOTD, and occurs 3 times a day for different timezones, offering a competitive experience every. single. day. That's AWESOME.In addition there's also the Ranked mode, which occurs on the 25 seasonal campaign maps and, at higher rankings, TrackMania World Tour maps (e-sport maps). The 3v3 dynamic of Ranked adds a good bit to the competitive aspect of the game alongside Royal (also 3 player), although Ranked does so more than Royal.Then there's Club Access for the more hardcore players, fully opening up the game. You get to create your own "club", which functions as a hub for any content of yours you wish to put up in the game. You can create campaigns, link to your socials, etc. etc.! On top of that, you get to have your own car skin should you so choose! There's actually a lot of content to unpack with TrackMania...... with so many maps being made EVERY day you won't run out of content to play in a hurry, and it's actually affordable?!?! Ok wait, let's talk about this......The subscription model as a whole went through some unfortunate press when it was first announced..... Ubisoft kept saying "this is not a subscription model" when it CLEARLY was..... but is being a subscription model in this case a bad thing? Especially considering the overall pricing of: $10 USD for 1 year of Standard Access, $30 for 1 year of Club Access, and $60 for 3 years of Club Access, TrackMania is actually priced in a VERY consumer friendly way! Like I mentioned before, Club Access is made for and targeted to the hardcore players among us, so Standard Access is what most people will likely end up getting. Folks...... TEN BUCKS!!! How does it get better than THAT?!?! Oh.... and the free Starter Access lets you get your feet wet on top of this?!?!? :OFor what this game offers...... you can't miss out. I'm not just saying that as a random person on the side of the street either..... I am deeply invested in this community as one of the many top-tier mappers in the community, having been nominated by the community website  for 2022's Mapper of the Year Award, alongside having been featured by Nadeo for Track of the Day NUMEROUS times. I don't say this lightly.....  Despite all past and future potential hurdles, TrackMania has, honestly, defied the odds and lived to tell the tale. Whether you spend hours upon hours squeezing every millisecond out of your favorite track, detailing maps to no end in the map editor, or spending time with your friends in Ranked/Royal or in the MANY community events on offer, TrackMania has loads of value.At the very least, try Starter Access and poke around a bit for ole Rexy! Trust me, this game is not one to miss. :D

_childDocuments_.review: TrackMania encapsulates the skill of racing games like Forza with the chaos and ingenuity of abstracts maps like Hot Lap League. A well-known and beloved franchise for years, TrackMania takes all the original elements from previous games and improves them with updated graphics and a WAY more expansive variety of default blocks and items to construct amazing routes. Thanks to the most recent update in 2023, there's even more blocks to ask for when building any route you desire. Not enough blocks for you to build a map? It's easy to implement any custom items from the community, including various styles of rocks, trees, buildings, vehicles and other props. The minimal limitations of the editor allow you to construct basically anything you can imagine!One of the common complaints seen about the game is in regards to its subscription model, charging $10/year for Standard Access ($30 for Club, $60 for 3 years of Club) to access more than 50 maps in a season. But the tracks provided straight out of the gate include 25 Training maps to learn the basic skills required to complete most maps, and 25 cycling Seasonal maps. Every 3 months, you get 25 new tracks to race on and optimise. These tracks are constructed by some of the best mappers in the game, so a level of quality is guaranteed with each new season. The difficulty scales fairly so once you master the White maps, you can move to Green, then Blue and so on. It never feels like a massive skill jump so it's easy to jump into the game and learn how to play.After you finish the 50 maps provided to you, paying $10/year for  access to released community tracks is not a bad deal. Considering some of the recently released games can be in excess of $70-$100, this same value is 7 years of unlimited map playing. You can play the Track of the Day, which is a curated track picked by the developers showing some of the coolest maps created by the community. There's a style for everyone, including grass, dirt, tech, fullspeed, ice, plastic and more! Not a fan of the style today? See what gets released tomorrow! Thanks to TrackMania Exchange, you have access to over 75,000 more tracks to play and there's a style for everyone. There's so much in the game to explore and that's just solo play. You can play Ranked on the Campaign maps, you can play the Royal mode and experience a whole new gamemode focused around survival on harder platform-based tracks. Want to go even more competitive? We have a new World Tour that's an open league with regional qualifiers for you to test your mettle against some of the best amateur players the game has to offer in your region. There's plenty of other competitions frequently being run, including 1v1v1v1 competitive play, map hunting competitions, KO competitions and more. There's so much content in the game - and at $10 a year, what more could you ask for?
_childDocuments_.name: Trackmania

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably one of the few exceptions to Ubisoft's generic formula. No micro-transactions or DLC, almost everything in this game is skill-based. And the skill ceiling is high, very high. However, that doesn't mean that new players can't enjoy the game - in fact, I don't think you have to be good at the game at all to be able to enjoy it. You're not going to have a bad time because people are better than you, as this game is very much based on improving your performance compared to yourself instead of others. All of this is even more true when you consider how amazing the community is in this game. Almost everyone is friendly and willing to help, so don't be afraid to ask! Trackmania heavily relies on the community and that is a good thing. The game can also be played on pretty much any input device (seriously - people play on a keyboard, controller, mouse, joystick and even steering wheels).Trackmania has a high skill ceiling but also a very low barrier to entry, so try out the free version to see if you like it. The training maps and the first few campaign maps are very easy, and you will learn the more advanced mechanics along the line if you stick with the game (you'd be surprised how crazy a game that essentially requires throttle, brake, and steering can get, which also makes it incredibly fun).As for which version to get,free version:25 Campaign maps updated every 3 months.25 Tutorial MapsSee your Personal best times world ranking on maps (enable this in the settings)2 Arcade servers - one with custom player-created maps.Ranked 3v3 - recommended.Royal game mode with new maps every week.Simple map editorNow there are some features locked behind the subscription. Note: the sub is yearly (or every 3 years) and it does not auto-renew. Also, it's less than 1$ a month for standard.These are the most prominent features:Access to ALL Community maps EVER MADECup of the day. - massive online tournament 3 times a day.All Track of the days - Player-made maps handpicked by devs, one from each day since November 2020.ALL ONLINE SERVERSAll previous Campaign maps. (11x25 official maps)Advanced map editorAbility to in-game chatThese are all standard subscription features. there is a tier above this called club. Core features include:Ability to spectate world record ghosts on all maps.Join and create clubs (only 1 person needs a club to create a room, all standard access players can join it)access to all skins in clubs - basically unlimited skins with the subscription.EXTRA INFO: The game has a community-made modding scene called 'Openplanet'. It is honestly amazing and sports multiple extra ways to play the game, including Speedrunning, Bingo mode, Random Map Challenge and many more quality-of-life features.In conclusion, try the game, get good at the campaign maps and play ranked (is what i would do) and then see if the games deserved your subscription. It's honestly a great game with an unimaginable amount of player-made content.If i was to recommend a subscription, it would be standard access if you want to play casually.Get club if you wish to hunt for world records or be highly competitive, as spectating world record ghosts is a very good to analyze inputs and learn from others.

Bobsled and ice and dirt and sausage blocks all require very different ways to drive and its never explained. it was very clearly made to appease its existing audience as when you go to the play page the seasonal campaign is front and center. just below it is the training courses but those are a misnomeri figured the training courses would be set up in a way to introduce me to a mechanic and let me practice it. maybe by pausing the game and telling me when to steer/break/let off the gas or by drawing a line on the track to show the best way to take the curve. nope you get none of that. its just you and the track and the timer. if you have had some experience with the series, then you will probably understand what the training tracks are for but as a new player who's never touched anything close to a sim racer, your better off ignoring themyou will have much better luck learning the ropes by going into the seasonal campaign, sicking to the easy tracks, and trying to follow what the silver medal ghost is doing. the bronze ghost spins out and takes bad lines so dont try to do what they do. The training tracks do not have a ghost to follow which makes you wonder why they are thereIf you stick with the game enough, by hour 10 you should be capable of beating all bronze ghosts in the easier tracks. it wasn't until i had 15 hrs in game just practicing different tracks did i finally get all bronze in the winter campaign. so if this is a game where you want to see continual improvement in yourself and dedicate the time needed to learn it all, by all means buy it. but if you want to casually play dont bother. you will probably not even get all the medals by the time the next season releases.also if you are having issues getting a non-standard controller to work with the game (i use a gamecube controller because its what i have) try launching the game from big picture mode from steam using said controller

_childDocuments_.review: I've played about 50 hrs or so on the other launcher before the steam release and so far love this game. It is very rewarding to see your times improve as you continue to practice -- especially when you begin to generalize what you've learned across a larger selection of maps and can use that knowledge to learn and improve on a new map more quickly.For free you get access to the current campaign and training maps. I would view this as a very in-depth, updating demo that you could easily sink 10s of hours into. Then, for only 10$/yr you get access to basically all of the content the game has too offer. Playing previous campaigns is cool, but my favorite is to play in the arcade on the servers dedicated to specific map types. Playing on these servers is where you really get to interact with the community, which is very welcoming and helpful in the chat. Plus, its always fun to see the car that you're following screw up and go flying out of a loop.The subscription model is NOT like a battle pass. Instead of a one-time 60$ price, its a lower sum which recurs on a yearly basis (I don't believe it auto-renews, you have to choose to give them your money again). If you don't enjoy the game, paying 10$ once is less than you would've paid otherwise. If you do enjoy the game and end up continually playing it for over 6 years, at that point you'd be glad to pay another 10$ to continue supporting a game you love. I think its a clever and fair payment model.

_childDocuments_.review: TM is a great game series with an amazing community around it. The way Ubisoft and Nadeo have handled TM2020 is... very disappointing. Instead of seasonal DLCs, you get a subscription service. To play older maps, or to join clubs, or play track of the day, or **play more than 10 campaign maps**, you have to pay $20/year. This, presumably, is on Ubisoft's side. On Nadeo's side, they have constantly ignored community feedback, pushing content and half-baked gamemodes that no one wants or plays. Remember how TMNF was about precision and tricks, with one car and a few surfaces? TM2020 is about learning to drive the combinations of ~4 cars, 3 tyre states, a bunch of surfaces, and a bunch of effect blocks, switching many times per map. If you don't like that, you are not going to have fun with most campaign maps. Also, every campaign has a few annoying/bad maps, and you need Gold in all the previous maps to unlock the final set. Better go back to TMNF.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game series of all time. This installment brings exciting new things to the table:-Tons of new road surfaces-TONS of new blocks-Off-grid block editing-Any surface on any block-Tons of new little features, like launch respawn, boosters within checkpoints, and on and on and on.It's perhaps the most featureful trackmania to date, and playing the game is a treat.=====However, this experience is completely tainted by things I can sum up in one word: Ubisoft.=====-Requires ubisoft connect to even run the game, which requires yet another account you have to manage inthis day and age.-Ubisoft connect is always running on your computer with EIGHT background processes doing god knows what. They will continue to run EVEN WHEN YOU AREN'T PLAYING THE GAME ANYMORE.-The intro cutscene is 480p for some reason, probably because it's through some web player. Couldn't even be arsed to make a proper cutscene.-The moment you boot up the game, you receive an advertisement for clubs (the game's premium subscription), because yes, like literally everything in 2023, trackmania is now subscription-based. You have two buttons, labeled "continue" and "go now". The wording of these is intentionally ambiguous; either could mean getting to the game or purchasing club. Ontop of that, the cursor is placed on the button to purchase a club by default. Absolute scum of the earth business practice.-Throughout the game you are presented things to do, only to find out almost EVERYTHING is club only. The features you get in TM2020 can be had in the older installments for 30 dollars, and you have them for life. Now they cost 60 dollars and it's not even yours to own, making this game a FAR worse value even though it's  "free".-If you relent and purchase club, because it's the only way the game is remotely enjoyable, chances are you AREN'T able to, because Ubisoft's payment-handling servers are constantly malfunctioning or down. Thanks to this, I now have 60 dollars into my steam account that I can't get back.

_childDocuments_.review: Why is Ubisoft Connect gobbling up my CPU and GPU like it’s training for an eSports tournament? I mean, come on, I get that you need all that extra horsepower for your world-renowned data-mining and surveillance ops, but could you at least try to hide it a little better? I feel like my system's working harder on sending you my personal data than it does running your games. Subtlety clearly isn’t in the Ubisoft playbook, but this is next-level.

Free for players to race solo or multiplayer on quarterly renewed official campaigns, including 25 tracks, allowing players to earn medals and record scores in the regional rankings. Players will be able to enjoy other player’s creations on the Arcade Channel, try various editors (tracks, replays and skins) and map review servers. The weekly Nations League is also available for casual competitions. 

    Standard Access: In addition to the free content, Standard Access expands the content available with player creations, including the “Track of the Day” selection, and full access to replay, track editors and map review servers. Additionally, players can participate in daily competitions and keep every “Track of the Day” and “Official” campaign track. One year of standard access is available for $9.99.

    Club Access: Including the above, Club Access allows players to join their favorite clubs to access exclusive content and activities such as skin customization, special campaigns, online rooms, training tracks and competitions. They can also create their own club to share their creations and organize events. Players can participate in the Open Grand League, organized by Ubisoft Nadeo, and try to qualify for the Trackmania Grand League. One year of the Club Access is available for $29.99 or three years for $59.99.

name: Zet Zillions
detailed_description: Zet Zillions is a story-driven roguelike deckbuilder where you will navigate through vast space maps with Foam Gun and her planet-ship Baby Violence, in search of a new home for humanity. Create chaos with the unique fusion system, with more than 100 possible combinations to discover. Overpopulate planets (by throwing your own crew at them) and blow them into smithereens! With easy onboarding and engaging mechanics, Zet Zillions wastes no time throwing you into action. Think ten steps ahead, strategize carefully but boldly, and find the best tactical approach to defeat COLOSSAL enemies. Build not one, but many mega decks and strategies on-the-go. Master the fusion system to combine your cards, revealing new, spectacular effects…. Or embarrassing bluffs. There are more than 100 combinations available, and some may not go as well as others. Hey, no risk no glory, amirite? Traverse randomly generated galaxies and visit thrilling locations. Scavenge abandoned shuttles, discover hidden portals, and meet tons of characters while embarking on side quests. Oh, and don’t forget to make good use of your pineapples. …Pineapples, yes. Why that face? Wolfstride is one of the “best games from 20xx” you missed, “hidden gems you need to play before you die” and all that. It is also the previous game by Ota Imon, the studio behind Zet Zillions. You don't need to play Wolfstride to enjoy Zet Zillions, but if you want extra credit* (and extra FUN), we recommend you give it a try, as you'll learn more about Zet Zillion's universe. *Credit can be redeemed on our social media, where we will compliment you and tell you that you are very cool.'

_childDocuments_.review: So stylish. Art is such a trip. So cool. The trash and junkLove the story,  ENGAGING, QUALITY voice acting. Characters and dialog are legit funny. Cool mechanics. Love the population and the different quests and how it ties into the cards you get...Tons of ways to ditch cards, get cards, just a super satisfying deck building in the BUILDING sense. Just not enough variation or meta progression. The UI sugggggesssttsss I'll get a different deck. But I don't. Maybe i'll go back to finish the story one day but I'm not running the same thing 4 times when I know I'm going to be able to steamroll it again. Card unlocks are slow and honestly a pet peeve in the genre -- 1 or 2 cards per run doesn't change ♥♥♥♥. Give big batches of related synergy cards and abilities, not efficiency-cards as meta progression. Its not changing the experience at all.No signs of more challenge or modes... Such a nice 3 runs but that's all that's here? More meat required on the (really awesome) bones. At least some difficulty settings? Maybe I'm cutting too soon but that's my critique -- I don't want to do the same thing again.

_childDocuments_.review: Zet Zillions, made by the creators of Wolfstride, is a very similar kind of game.  That is to say, its stylish, cool and completely shallow.ZZ is a roguelite deckbuilder, but most of unlockable starting bonuses are only obtained after you've beaten the final boss.  I unlocked Gilgamesh's Eye, the second companion, on the same run that I killed Super Duper Thanatos, or whatever his name is.  I haven't even unlocked any of the other starting cards (like Frag-a-Jam).  In addition, most of the cards that you can add to your deck are quite ♥♥♥♥, meaning that only a few strategies are properly good.The game has a fair few gamebreaking bugs (one time in act 3 I got booted to the map instead of act 4 when I beat the boss of the area), and another time I crashed everytime I tried to go to a mission planet.The base mechanic is fun: fuse your cards together to do cool ♥♥♥♥.  The problem is that you don't know what fuses with what.  This unicorn thing, what do I fuse it with?  This bomber plane thing, what do I fuse that with?  You'll only know when you add to your deck, which results in adding ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cards that don't work with your build.  Instead, just add deal 15 + 15 population for 2 cost.  That ♥♥♥♥ is useful 100% of the time.  Fusion is a cool idea, but it rarely does anything really strong and its impossible to know how it works.  Another thing that really needs improving is the art.  The art is great, super cool, when its completed.  Many cards, like the various event pets, don't have finished art, most of them have only a placeholder sketched art.The game is hilariously short, I beat it in 6 hours.  Not like, won my first run, no I beat the final boss over multiple runs in a measly 6 hours.Tl;dr: cool idea. bad execution.  There's almost no substance.  If you want to sell a game for 20 dollars, try making the game better.  This game could be good, it just isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I’ve said I’m not fond of roguelike deckbuilders, and that I’m bad at them. But I made an exception with Zet Zillions, because it’s a very special game, made by the same creators of Wolfstride and set in the same universe, but in the very distant future. With the same vibe and mega style of their first game, Zet Zillions takes us on an interstellar adventure where well command the "Baby Violence", a ship planet in which we’ll make our way through the cosmos, and through our enemies, in a chaotic roguelike experience that radiates charisma. We'll have a fusion and population system, to combine our cards and send our crew to populate enemy terrain, respectively, along with peculiar humor and a gameplay that will test our tactical skills.As I mentioned, Zet Zillions places us in the same universe as Wolfstride, but many, many years later. Humanity took flight to the stars, the interstellar dream, with an armada they called the Starborne Vanguard. As players, we'll embody the role of the commander, in charge of the planet ship nicknamed Baby Violence and its extravagant crew, among them the iconic protagonist, Foam Gun. It will be our duty and priority to keep everyone alive, while escaping from a cosmic threat called Thanatos.The story progresses in chapters and the narrative will be presented to us in the form of acts, represented by galactic sectors through which we'll have to navigate. At first glance the humor stands out a lot, but it has more serious moments when reaching the last stretch, and the truth is that I felt it was very broad compared to other titles of the genre (that I’ve tried), very enjoyable. As an added bonus, there are quite a few events and dialogues that serve as a complement between acts, episodes that we'll have to find while exploring the galaxy.The exploration in Zet Zillions is represented by star charts, where we can advance through squares with different events, from combat encounters to special situations such as making a wish to a star, or receiving a massage from a giant floating hand. It is quite absurd at times, but very entertaining. In general, each place has its corresponding icon, such as those marked by a question mark, which means that the event can be random. Most notable are the places to get new cards, upgrade them, or even sacrifice them for pineapples on a mystical altar. Yes, pineapples are the space currency, who would have thought.The main thing to keep in mind is that Thanatos will chase us through the cosmos, and will devour the squares through which it travels, as well as the adjacent ones. So there isn’t much chance to go back to previous tiles, and we'll not be able to explore the whole sector. It is imperative that we plan our flight path so as not to run into this cosmic entity, and although we can face it early, we do not really get anything beneficial out of it.Leaving exploration aside, let's move on to the cards! To begin with, we'll have a predefined deck at our disposal, and we'll get more cards as we advance through space. Eventually, we'll be able to unlock two additional decks, with their own characteristics. The cards are divided into several types, and serve different functions. The one I would say is the most important is the 'population' archetype which generally encompasses the 'Trash', glycerin-based life forms that we can shoot at planets, and enemies, to board or populate them. Don't worry, they don't feel anything, I’m almost certain of it. This mechanic consists of filling the relevant bar of the enemy to stun and delay their turn, and in the case of planets to colonize them and get better rewards. There are also simpler effects such as increasing our damage, or weakening the opponent, and each card has its own energy cost, so that we can plan how to use them. Some cards have special conditions, such as requiring to discard a card to perform its effect, or even to be discarded, or also the "pulverize" label that means that they have only one use (unless we acquire the card again). But what really stands out in Zet Zillions is the fusion system. Several cards can be combined with others, while on hand, to generate different results. There are some that increase the amount of armor generated as they merge, others that cause damage for each combination, and even some that cannot be played on their own and whose potential lies in making use of this system.The mechanics are very well thought out and super intuitive. It encourages creativity and lets us think about which cards to pick and build our deck, since we always have to consider not only the card itself, but also the possible related fusions. At the same time, we'll have at our disposal companions that will benefit us in our adventure. For example, the first one is Junker, who focuses on increasing our armor. Just like the decks, we'll have up to three unlockable companions.As a last addition, we'll also have passive traits, which can vary from starting the combat with a power-up, to drawing cards for every three fusions performed, among several others. The truth is that it keeps you well entertained, especially when you find that one winning combination, and it feels great.Zet Zillions is a very charismatic game, its visuals are eye-catching and extremely cool. I love their character design since Wolfstride, and with this installment they did nothing but validate my inner fanboy (and outer one at that). The soundtrack and voice acting are no slouches either, demonstrating a stupendous quality on par with the first game, and it was very easy for them to capture my attention through these sections.But without a doubt, this was nothing more than the lure, and they ended up hooking me with the core gameplay, which I can say was a very rewarding experience, even though I'm not very good at this genre. Among so many similar games, Zet Zillions stands tall and shouts 'look at me!' in a very crazy way, and I can't help but agree with that sentiment. A well-deserved recommendation for fans of card roguelikes, and those who might be looking for a title to get into the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: :  is fun, unique gimmick is intuitive, and art is gorgeous.  is bittersweet and short.Zet Zillions is a genuinely novel deckbuilder experience with catchy music, silly humor, and interesting gameplay. It's greatest issues are found in its humor and its short nature. It is still a fun game experience first and foremost. The humor will bother those who dislike, or are offended, by juvenile stuff. For example, you simultaneously are fighting pirates, space bugs, angry planets, cosmic monsters, and . For deckbuilder fans, equate the gimmick of the turds to encounters/enemies that fill your deck with curses and dilute your card draw. They have a mechanical purpose. I found it funny and silly.The short nature is a problem for the mechanical deckbuilder purist who values 100's of hours of gameplay over a gameplay experience. You will likely be 100% done with this game at 15-20 hours max. Sooner if you do not game over or just focus on using the same strategy that wins you your first run.... you are looking for:... you are looking for:For its price, it is easily a valuable $10 experience since I like Trigger style art, the music was sweet, the gameplay was novel, and I got to win with multiple archetypes (discard, poison/burn, big deck, shuffle poison/burn, pulverize, etc). There were some stinkers and deck building traps, but the number of viable picks outweighed those. By the time I started to think critically about the balance, I was nearing the end of the campaign, and had gotten my value from the game.That being said, if there were more chapters (different captain/story/crew) or a genuinely interesting challenge mode (new archetypes, cards, bosses, events, and/or interesting balance/progression) that would be great. A continuation, even if that is silly, would still make me laugh if I got to see credits every two chapters after the story 'ended' each time. Would remind me of MGS5, and seeing 'Kojima' in the opening credits of each mission every-time. But, elaborating further:Regardless, fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good rougelike deckbuilder that needs quite a bit of polish.The good:- Fun animations.- Armor persisting allows for a unique experience to a lot of other deckbuilders.- Fusion mechanic allows for deck thinning in unorthodox ways.- It doesn't feel unfair when you lose.The bad:- Lack of characters even though I'm 20 hours in. There's 3 decks you can select with 2 needing to be unlocked but the exp gain is ♥♥♥♥ even when you go deep in a run. Imagine Slay the Spire but before you unlock your 2nd character you'd already beaten more than 5 times and are still waiting.- Lack of variety. You start the game selecting power ups each run so you in a way, you can tail make the experience you want going in which is nice however, to get there, you need to select power x and level that up too. I get having to unlock the relics but leveling to unlock a relic slot just feels cheap.- Lack of information. I could get an event that asks me to trade a trait for another trait but I can't open up my menu to see what traits I have prior to agreeing. The fusion mechanic is fun and I understand not giving information on fusions you haven't seen before however there are some very unique fusions you won't even know about unless you happened to have those two specific cards in hand and happen to glance them together (e.g. Poison + Signature card = 1 use Poison*2X people). This is probably the worst part since the game is about giving choice and mitigating luck but not being able to see what fusion potentials I could have could sway my decision to try out cards I would otherwise ignore.- UI and another lack of information relating to the act of fusing. You cannot see what cards you have fused together which is okay most of the time but there are cards who's whole purpose is to fuse to reduce the waste in your hand. One thing you can do is fuse a bunch of cards together and discard it so for one discard you've removed 4 cards. However, if you have 2 cards that are the same and they're both maxed fused you'll have to remember which one has the cards you want to go back into your deck. This is important because some boss' give you status cards where you need to play them to remove them or they'll give you status effects at the end of turn. So after playing my combo I'm left down to pot luck as to which card I should be discarding which has costed me a run at the final boss before.- Some archetypes are downright awful. For example, to play a Corpse deck (cards that disappear when played, do 1 damage and do 1 damage when played) you will need (1) a corpse corpse generator card and (2) a corpse payoff card. One card that comes to mind is the corpse hat which makes 1 corpse at end of turn but is unplayable until you fuse it. When you fuse it you it becomes the captain which does 5 damage per corpse in your deck (which also includes your hand in this game) at a cost of 2 energy to play him. So if you'll have to wait 4 turns to do 20 damage at a cost of 10 damage/energy and now you have to cycle through your deck to get the captain hat back in hand which is harder to do because you added 4 dead cards to your deck that either need to be fused or played or they'll clutter up your hand.For 8 bucks it's definitely still worth it because the actual game is probably worth at least 25 euros, you'll just need to grind to unlock everything to get it to that point.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a mixed option for reviews, because that's what I'd prefer to give this. The game itself is very stylish, and the first run is fun. After that though.. a lot of little cracks start showing. It seems like the game was designed with a larger scope in mind, but cut very short. Even more confusing is that when you beat the final boss the credit roll after calls this Zet Zillions part 1, and the normal runs after are called the interlude, but nowhere else is it mentioned whether this is a part 1?I guess I thought I'd list out the things that feel unfinished, and if these matter to you then maybe its not worth picking up:- The game seems to have been designed with the idea of multiple decks or characters (evidenced by the 'deck selection screen' and character level ups), but only features one deck at the time of 1.0 release.- Lots of placeholder card art for a full release.- Enemy variety is non-existent, there's no difference between different areas either.- Game is waaay too easy, with no difficulty scaling post-game. It really seems like no balance or scaling was considered at all.Overall, I wanted to like this game for its style but it just isn't that fun in it's current state, and from how it's been released I wouldn't hold my breath waiting for improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Space-punk aesthetics not seen in a game since Void Bastards and before that you'd have to go all the way back to Human Occupied Landfill. Between the population and fusion mechanics, plenty of original ideas. Team obviously tried hard and worked hard.Cons: Very frequent loading, even more if you install the game in a slow drive. It's hard to make enough content for a roguecardlite, and you'll probably see most of it through a single play cycle. Once you learn the ropes, most of the game is trivial, except that the third "final boss" (T____ Z___) ridiculously outscales every other threat in the game, which becomes an exercise in patience as you grind through harmless enemies attempting to build whatever passes for Best Deck Ever.

_childDocuments_.review: So if you're not familiar with OTA IMON Studios, they're a group that likes to take risks with their strange and unusual game designs even though their only other game is "WolfStride" which I highly recommend picking up, which incorporates many distinct systems that are both full of character and story, as well as motivational goals and growth rather than 100% random choice and not to mention, dirt cheap for the hours of gameplay available. Putting it in perspective, half the price of Slay The Spire and other such games at 25-30+ or more.When I say random choice, I mean that it gets incredibly boring with Action Roguelikes, especially linear deck builders, where your only purpose is to get to the boss and plot your way to do so safely, but Zet Zillions exploits the idea of. "Hey! We will reward you with AMAZING cards and attributes if you can manage to get here to finish these quests and survive!" This makes traversing each segment of the map chapter much more enjoyable and tension-filled, while also allowing you to go back rather than just forward. It uses the same feature as FTL, the danger zone, which isn't used too often, I'm quite happy to see it reappear in this game since you could risk even more to gain even more cards and power. The soundtrack is as banger as ever!This game approaches things a little differently with combat. You're entire goal is to colonize planets with your population of Meat robots for humanity, which is hilarious because it gives off the same vibe as StarShip Troopers or HellDivers 2 Humanity, where you're fighting for humanity, but in this case you're just a bunch of power hungry overlords attempting to take over the galaxy. When you fully populate a planet it will become stunned, then you erase that population and do it again with cards that grant you tons of damage and reset the value. Certain events have you actually needing to colonize powerful planets to get massive rewards and it's honestly no easy feat with the effects that they have at their disposal. You'll mostly be blowing planets up, which you'll come to want to do, I don't wanna spoil it. If you tend to click things too quickly or not let certain sections of the game load in like the Rescue Pod, etc, the game can and will crash, but the game saves every encounter so while it is annoying to have to log out and back in, it doesn't hinder progression. A handful of other bugs as well that eventually can become game breaking not being able to interact with the event like the Space Dragon and trading cards for currency. One big issue is the danger zone, it does nothing meaning with a shuffle deck you can roam and soak up thousands of pineapples at the end of the stage to buy out the entire shop. His left hand is the only thing that will show up (Thanatos) and the giant mouth does nothing, so that needs to be fixed immediately.Zet Zillion is a unique spin on the overcrowded deck building genre expanding on the ideas of Slay the Spire thoroughly. If you've played them all and many others, it seems fresh, unique, and inventive while still being difficult and full of charm and fantastic voice actors, not to mention a very impressionable visual art style that you're sure to love and maybe be a bit scared by (you'll know when you know) haha.Definitely going to love playing this one.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆Super fun roguelike deckbuilding game; the main mechanic here is fusing cards and populating planets to stun them. The story is simple, the art style is beautiful, the characters are interesting, and Thanatos is an absolutely formidable titan. I loved the different events, enemies and bosses, and all the cards and traits that you can unlock, their synergies and the randomness of each run that kept me hooked to playing for "one-more-run". Every defeat levels you up and eventually unlocks new starting cards and traits. There were a few bugs in my experience, one example is when the game was stuck in animation when I tried to open an "escape pod". One time, the game crashed when I was in a boss fight. But these issues are few and didn't impact my enjoyment of the game since I could always continue my journey from the last node I'd completed. I'm super excited for Zet Zillions' future updates! Keep it up devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Building on top of the initial review; it has potential but I'm not sure if it's still bugged or just lacking in content.I think i've beaten the whole game, seen the final boss and kept playing even beyond that. I can't seem to unlock new decks, and the progression is really slow for helper unlocks. It doesn't seem to have a scaling difficulty? And it's really easy to boot, I've lost once even when trying out different archetypes. Build variety is ok, but not great. I've been able to get poison working somewhat, a combo deck with fusion, a population-based stunlock deck and just raw damage. It's just that I'm fiddling with the same old cards a lot of the time. The 1.0 patch fixed some bugs, like the progress-blocking one, but some remain, like animation/damage desync, card ui being sluggish and some card effects not working all the time. It's got good bones, but after 12-or-so hours of intense grinding, I think I've seen what it has to offer. First impressions are positive, but not perfect. I think there's a ton of bugs in the game. Card art flipping around, card interactions just not working - fusing cards not getting bonuses (Garbage Pile, looking at you). The ui sometimes lags out, you can't set resolution beyond 1920x1080 and I think I have a game-breaking bug where I can't progress beyond stage 2-2. The boss is dead and the game won't go forward, so there's that. It is fun though, and I've been able to put out some super wacky combos pretty fast, which makes the game feel thinky and rewarding. It's real pretty and the sounds are on point too. The price is really low too, surprisingly so. I'd wait for a patch or two to get it, but after they REALLY iron the game out, it's probably a really solid deckbuilder.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there were mixed reviews, I don't want to give a negative score to the developer at launch because we already know how Steam positions.... But if this was a big company I would give it to them.The game is very good, having some mechanics to polish and always with room for improvement. It could have come out in early access and I could have better understood that there are many things "to be polished". But what is totally unacceptable are the few configuration options it has. I've tried it on Steam Deck and on a PC and to start with, playing with a controller is practically impossible. They should have paid more attention to these accessibility options and given more importance to the in-game configuration. The game runs perfect on Steam Deck, they just need to polish the controls.Otherwise, for its price, pretty decent. I would like the developers to polish a little more a system that seems to work. Being able to combine cards is refreshing for the genre, but it doesn't revolutionize or reinvent the wheel. The deck builder genre has been heavily exploited since traditional board games and, unfortunately, it's very difficult not to compare it to Slay the Spire. Balatro achieved something different by moving away from Slay's theme. It is unfair to compare it, it is like comparing the new metroidvanias with Hollow Knight. Not because Hollow Knight is almost perfect the rest are going to be bad. In this case you find a good game, not mediocre, saving the previously mentioned.

_childDocuments_.review: A quick review of Tengen Toppa Gu... no sorry... Zet ZillionHonestly, it's a mixed bag for me, but mostly positive. I just have issues with some bugs that are occuring fairly often and hinder the experience a lot. I will change my review once those issues are adressed.PROS- Aesthetique: The anime feeling and the humor is really really good and punch way above its weight- Good Storytelling: The storytelling isn't intrusive and well paced, every bits of narrative progression is a reward in its own.- the "Fusion" USP: I was expecting something along the line of the card fusion from other deckbuilders such as Monster Train or Inscryption, but it's more, and unfortunately a bit less also.- Many builds: I completed 3 runs, everytime with a different strategy, there is some "Go to" cards that goes in every decks, but overall the variety and power fantasy is really there- Very easy to "clear" the deck and passing new cards is a blessingCONS- Some bugs: Releasing a card to fuse them sometimes end up using the card if it had no target, the illustration often swap, when there is a controller plugged the game have troubles to switch between mouse & keybord and controller, sometimes I couldn't exchange cards at the Ananas God. There is still some work but the fundations are solid.- The french translation: It isn't very good, there is a lot of confusion wording, I may switch back in English to see if its better.- The Fusions: A bit confusing, sometime overwhelming and some other underwhelming. The rational behind it is that its wider at the entry, to allow multiple cards, but there is always only one end. It's kind of good for the learning curve, but it's also a game of guessing of "why can't a I fuse this card and this card, it should give me that" which creates frustration.- RNG on effects: I'm not a fan of Heartstone, and usually doesn't like when the outcome of my actions isn't known by advance. There is a lot of effect that affect "A random target" or "Does X, then repeat X on Y random targets" and it can be frustrating also, but that's more a matter of taste.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Oozing style. Yes, it's a roguelike deckbuilder, but the elevator pitch is that in this hyper-stylish game, you're fighting planets/giant enemies, you can fuse cards, and you use "population" as a stagger mechanic. Is it enough? Yes.Fooooor a few hours. There's a game breaking bug that forces you to exit the game, then come back. Unfortunately, unlike other games in the genre, your in-battle progress isn't saved. This game breaking bug is related to the discard mechanic and occurs nearly every battle. No joke. (Specifically, the bug prevents the mouse from interacting with any object, so you can't play cards or end turns) Finally, JFC who wrote this script? I love love love that there are stylized, splashy characters who actually have a voice. But that voice is...grating. sO rAnDom!! cOw LOL! This game could really be a top contender if they eliminated game breaking bugs, added in different more starter deck options and hired an actual script writer (please on this last one - it's dangerously close to unbearable). Not recommending because of the game breaking bugs.Expect 10ish hours of gameplay before you've had enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I randomly found out about this game from trawling Steam and the fact that it's not getting talked about more is absolutely criminal. For what you get in this cheap little $10 package this game is an absolute steal.Aesthetics - This game is wild, from planets with faces to crazy space thieves. This isn't Beneath Oresa in terms of 3D animation, but it's gorgeous. There are so many interesting designs and it screams Gurren Lagann for some of the characters. It's a gorgeous game. It's kind of hard to discuss the look because you're gonna see so many different kinds of designs that all work together.Audio - The voice acting is perfect. I believe these are a ragtag band of borderline sociopaths in the best way, and the main cast are earning their paychecks. The little quips you hear from enemies and your teammate are little drips of funny as well.Story - I haven't played every deckbuilder, but this one's puts the ones I have played to shame in terms of story. Every time I think I'm done, there's more, and every time I'm still hooked. It's a wonderful mix of insane, but interesting, sci-fi craziness and a lot of humor and jokes, meta and otherwise. I've screenshot so many dialogue boxes. Gameplay - I gotta say, this game feels damn good to play. They've got very strong systems in place and the fusion system, that I can't recall having run into before, makes the gameplay so dynamic that unless you're trying to make the same deck every time you can see so many different crazy combinations play out. If you're thinking about buying this game, buy this game. Absolutely.

_childDocuments_.review: To summarize my thoughts really quickly: Game is great overall, it's arguably got a bit of 'style over substance' going on, but that's mostly just because the style is so very *very* good. ...Possibly slightly too good, as it likely makes it harder to add content when everything in the game feels this high-effort.The game just drips with style, it has a very Studio Trigger aesthetic and feel, and it just adds so very much. The writing is entertainingly wacky, the presentation is just great. However, we only have one main character, compared to STS's 3 (at launch,  4 now) - but in contrast to being a mute sprite that doesn't really animate much, she's voice acted, animated, has a whole crew with her who also have all their own art and voice assets, she has anime cutscenes and a real personality to her...This one character does feel a bit more varied than a single slay the spire character, and she has various minions she can take that tweak her deckbuilding a bit, but you will end up seeing a lot of the same cards after a while.So you can see what I mean about the game's greatest selling point, its pretty undeniable visual flair and style, might make it a lot harder to add new characters. If they come in with any less effort, it'll feel a bit weird, and if they come in with the same amount, it's going to be a LOT of work. Hence the style over substance comment.However, the mechanics that we do have are cool. It brings a bunch of unique stuff to the table; drawing cards works differently to your average roguelite deckbuilder, there's a whole mechanic of fusing cards, there's a fair bit here that feels truly fresh. It is a bit on the shorter side for a roguelike, but more content is promised soonish - and frankly, at the absurdly low price point, I already feel like I've gotten my money's worth. It's a blast to play through that doesn't drag itself out or overstay its welcome - though may at present leave you wanting a bit more once you're finished. Even so, well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game is amazing, and it's what got me wishlisting it 3 month prior to it's release. Soundtrack is great, the game's aesthetic is great. Chapters 1 and 2 were great. However the game hits a roadblock immediately once you start unlocking more stuff. There is barely a sense of progression, variety and replayability that is a MUST for ALL roguelikes. The events (mostly) feel lackluster, card mechanics are cool on paper but aside from a few, they're mostly useless. Battles boil down to using whatever card has higher damage. Comparing the game to the likes of Slay the Spire, Inscryption or even Balatro might be a bit much but it really doesn't hold a candle to them.Main complaints:The fact that you don't naturally discard card cards but have a limit to your hand feels so unintuitive. Card mergers rarely do anything but bump up damage.The shop is cool in the sense that you can access it anytime once it's available but it sells the same stuff everytime.The buddies are cool but wish there were more of them.Hopefully the devs add some new stuff in the future and make the game moddable.Maybe someone else might find it more enjoyable than I did even with all of it's flaws, but it's a 5/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a really good artstyle! I've been loving spending a lot of time just looking at the card illustrations and just the game overall. That said, my one and biggest gripe with the game in its current state is the UI lag. This lag is very frequent in every battle section of each run and it just sometimes kills the flow for me. To paint a better picture, I'll list some of the cases:- Stats of both sides only updating after ending turn, which means that sometimes, you or the enemy is already dead but you find yourself sending attacks that for some reason aren't registering.- Your armor may update later than expected after an enemy attacks, possibly causing some miscalculations.- In the reward selection screen, sometimes the selected card indicator is outside the border? Not as annoying but just annoying.In spite of that, it looks like the developers are being very responsive and I believe these problems will eventually be fixed. If you enjoy slay the spire like games like I do, specially for this price, I think it's a game worth getting.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the two hours that I've played so far? Honestly excellent. The fusion system is tight and satisfying, though it is somewhat obtuse what cards can fuse. Not sure if that's an intentional gameplay decision. If it is, it would be great if there were a way to see what something in your hand can fuse with in your deck for planning purposes after you've done that fusion.Still too early to speak on the amount of variety (seems to be 3 'decks' and 3 'companions', not sure if the base decks are just starters or if they share a card pool; companions seem to offer a passive effect), but it's promising so far.Strong mood and a unique vibe. Makes me want to Clockwork Orange some Gurren Lagann while mindlessly grinding Disgaea, wearing a Gainax grin all the while.Only complaint for me rn is launch day bugs. Notably, I've had "+X on fuse' cards fail to trigger when similar cards are in hand. My last session ended after I cleared act 3. No idea if there's a fourth act or if that's the end, but it put me right back on an inaccessible map and necessitated /ff, which was a real shame. Nevertheless, looking forward to playing again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm quite a fan of   since I've felt in love with one of their previous games  however I myself am not particularly fond of roguelite deck building games but I had to try it anyway.Main reason why I love this developer is the art they create, it looks almost identical as the one from the cult classic animated film . Now moving to the core – gameplay and here's why I keep pouring hours into this gem:First few tries I suffered from a severe case of skill issue where I couldn’t even get past the first act, however as time went on, I started to notice some trends on enemies and my cards. The game has an interesting progression system where each time you die, you come back stronger than before with new unlockables, thus providing a  type of replayability. The map is very cool where the encounters are never on the same spot as before and the missions are fun where you have a choice to pick one of three and complete them for a bonus trait, new card or an add-on effect where you place it on any card you want for extra power. The number of cards there are along with their effects provide this card battling game tons and tons of different options and tactics you can use each run. At the time of writing this, I've STILL haven't finished the campaign and judging from the achievements, I haven't even come halfway! So, for 10 measly bucks you're setting yourself up for a long journey across the galaxy, ready to deal with any bastards and blowing up planets or repopulate them if you prefer.

_childDocuments_.review: C-Art style and presentation are definitely the highlight here and worth the price of admission alone. All the designs are bursting with character and it was enjoyable to see the visuals behind each new enemy and card unlock. The UI has issues in terms of ease of use/access to information but it looks great. Theme ties into gameplay with the combination of junk and trash being manipulated by a oppressive human armada, which is a bonus.I appreciate the layout of the map that allows backwards movemetn and variable pathing. There probably should have been a larger deterrent to moving back against the encroaching danger zone since the only downside is having to fight a boss that is easily defeated turn 1 halfway through a run. Still, it provided more interesting routing compared to other games with purely binary choices.The card game and roguelike mechanics lack a level of depth that I see in other games. For gameplay, the central focus on combining cards of different types is pretty interesting but doesn't go far enough with the concept to create a truly memorable experience. The main deck only has 3 starting loadouts which is somewhat disappointing though side powers had a nice bit of variety and customziation. Theres a good amount of different playstyles to build around but at the end of the day I didn't feel excited to play any of them. For the roguelike: While I enjoy the freedom of the pathing, the choices for and at each individual node weren't particularly compelling. Runs started to feel repetitive towards the end of my time with the game.Little bit lack of impact and variety in terms of sfx, music, and visual hits indicators. Plot is pretty bare bones, and the dialogue is worse. Voice acting was just okay for your allies, though I did enjoy the overdramatic performance of the villain.Not a deckbuilder that you'd go back to over and over again but considering I got it for 7$ it was well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: OK card roguelike for a few runs, but not longer - it's not another Wildfrost, Slay the Spire or Monster Train. The main problem is that it's really repetitive with deckbuilding as there no decks based on different idea - the difference is mainly with one important card and some addons from one of 3 followers, nothing game-changing - StS had much more different runs. The fushion mechanic (merge two cards to get another one) is a nice touch and sometimes that's the good part of this game. The balance is off - the game tends to be too simple and there are possibilities of forming (too easily) infinite loop with small decks and just one card upgrade.Still, for that price it's worth it :)

_childDocuments_.review: !00%ed and feel like I've seen everything I'd care to in less than 10 hours.  There's potential, so maybe one day after many content updates I'll get to completely rewrite this review positively.Combine cards to get fun new cards. Awesome idea! Sadly, not well executed. One might think 'combining' would imply the end product to have some characteristics of its components, but not Zet Zillions! You'll hover two cards to see what comes out, and it's some completely unrelated. I'm not expecting to literally mash cards together for a combined effect, but maybe some kind of rhyme or reason for me to expect what will happen. Heck, even just giving me something exciting to want to combine would be cool. For this mechanic to work and shine, there need to be unique combinations for basically every card, and then combos for those combos. Really lean into it. Current state, it's unexciting 'turn a block card and a population card into a damage card,' or 'combine cards into this for an increased effect'.Oh yeah, and the controls are frustrating. Soooo many times I'll try to combine a card and the game won't like it for some reason, so you have to drop the card and pick it up again. Completely forget about it once your hand gets a bit crowded. Tried on Steam Deck and it was even worse.Even after 100%ing, I'm still not sure what can even be combined or not, or how the different card types differ from eachother other than arbitrary names. Why does junk sometimes combine with beasts and not other times? Sometimes junk deals damage, and sometimes its for increasing population. The lack of identity makes deckbuilding less interesting, and for a game trying so hard to be thematic, fails to be thematic in it's cardplay.Thematically, neat! Gameplaywise, a stun meter with a dedicated damage type. Fill the bar in a planet encounter and you win, and stun the enemy in other encounters (there are also cards that care about population in the same way cards might care about poison, infect, burn, counters, any card buff/debuff in other games). It would be cool if colonizing a planet actually did something to affect the world in a run. As is, each run you have a sidequest going while navigating, each quest with a card, charm, or relic reward. Populating planets is just a sidequest, and thus also blends in as just a thing you do on the way to the final boss, rather than something exciting. The art style is neat and everything is fully voiced. Sorry devs, but I muted the game and skipped every possible cutscene and line of dialogue. I'm playing card games for the good chemicals from big brain plays, finding the fun combos that break the game and push numbers to maximum silliness. The lil bit of the story I did pay attention to was amusing, buuuut I just don't care sorry, I want to fling digital cardboard. And as for flinging the digital cardboard, it's too easy. Players with a passing knowledge of good deckbuilding practice will not find any challenge without cranking up the ascension, but because the deckbuilding itself isn't interesting, I kinda don't care to keep pushing for harder runs or even repeating 'em like I would in STS, Wildfrost, Tainted Grail, etc. I don't need A20H out of the gate, but there should be some resistance and an actual possibility of losing. I don't hate the game by any means, I liked it enough to finish. My critiques come from a place of seeings its potential and wishing it could reach such heights.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute gem. It is easily one of the funnest deckbuilder games I have every played. _childDocuments_.review: I can’t even begin to tell you how much I loved , a deckbuilding card game with spunk, style, and soul.Thake the most over-the-top anime you’ve ever seen, multiply it by 100 and maybe, just maybe you’ll have a fraction of the awesomeness and energy this game brings to the table.(get it? Because it’s a card game, eh? Eh? … aw shut up)Foam Gun, Ziggy, and DOK are some of the most delightful characters I had the pleasure to experience, from their design, to the stellar voice acting, to their personalities, everything about them is great.The game oozes style with it’s thick lines, toothy smiles, and over the top silly plotlines while still delivering a gut punch if it wants to, will drag you into its world(s).Alright, deadpan moment to talk about mechanics:Each turn you draw cards until you have 7 and are given 3 points of energy to play them, reduce the enemies to 0 hp to win.Different card types can be combined during play to obtain new cards or power up existing ones opening new possibilities.Enemies also have a stun meter, fill it and they’ll skip their next action, a lot of cards are built around this mechanic.After a battle and other events you may choose one of three cards to add to your deck.You select locations to proceed on based on your position the map, not all of them are battles so there’ll be a lot of planning to do around them too as these extra locations and quests rewards you with cards, improvements on current ones, or character improvement.The hand of death is always close behind you and it will start to encroach on you the longer you stay in a single zone so you have some leeway to explore without feeling on rails but you’ll get actively pushed towards the next area.Tasked to both escape, survive, and eventually kill a multidimensional alien god of reality you and crew will find yourselves stuck in a time loop while unraveling the secrets behind it as you uncover a deeper plot Maybe “runs” drag on for a little too long, especially in the final chapters…That is until you realize this is a story game first and the roguelike elements are used as a means to tell it while keeping variety in your going through the gameplay loop itself.Story starts off with good pacing but at the very end it feels like a lot of things just start to happen all at once in an effort to wrap things up.I feel motivated to make a game like this, not the deckbuilding type, but one that you know despite the few reviews you just know it’s someone’s favorite game of all time.Price-to content ratio is a steal even at full price, do yourself a favor and get this immediately.Wholeheartedly recommended.This is a message for the developer:If you feel self-doubt that so much effort is met with such little popularity… don’t!You made a phenomenal game, Zet Zillions means a lot for a few people instead of meaning nothing for many.

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork immediately caught my attention but the gameplay exceeded my expectations. The mechanics are very unique and refreshing. Such amazing voice acting was also a big surprise. Great game overall. Now some cons:- I think there could be some more information about what fuses with what, especially for the Altar of Gaia.- Many cards get stronger each time you draw them, but I never cycle through my deck fast enough for that to matter because the unused cards are retained in my hand and sometimes limit the amount of cards drawn each turn; so, depending on the deck size, it takes many turns to discard and reshuffle the whole deck and draw the same cards again. Also, the vast majority of battles are very short. TLDR the On Play/On Fusion/On Draw mechanics just don't fit with the game pace.- The store is really disappointing, it always has the same cards and they're all boring, which in turn makes pineapples pretty useless.Some people are complaining about bugs and performance issues but the game runs perfectly fine and I only had minor harmless bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game. The art design, voice acting, and writing are all incredible (a bit goofy, but in a well balanced way IMO). I'd say that if you're looking for a Slay the Spire or Monster Train amount of infinite replay-ability, this likely won't be for you. At least for now, the game is story driven and has a set number of chapters (that once you complete you can't go back to, tho based on some discussion boards I think that's a work in progress feature). If you're looking for a cheap (in cost, but not production value) 20ish hours, I can't recommend this enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game when it first released and initially played for like an hour. I thought: "this is so strange." Then I turned it off and didn't play again until a few days ago. Upon coming back to the game it's still really weird, but I've also discovered that it's a delight and genuinely very well designed. _childDocuments_.review: This game is actual peak. The style and flair soars past most games I've ever played. The charming story, characters, and voice over are all such a pleasant little journey to go through. The game itself is even more of a vibe, the beautiful presentation extends to the cards themselves with sleek artwork and super wild effects that just feel nice to sling at enemies. _childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of the experience with deck builders and let's face it, those of us with interest in this genre hold everything up against Slay the Spire as a reference.This game is definitely NOT STS although it shares some similar mechanics.To be perfectly honest, in the first couple hours of play, my quick judgement was this title was a Below average deck builder compared to STS.  I think that initial impression was mostly due to my confusion in understanding the unconventional terms used in this game and not comprehendiing the card fusion mechanic very well.But before long things started to click and I raised my opinion to this being an ABOVE average STS "adjacent" title, meaning some mechanics are similar and some are novel takes on the genre.Without spoiling any plot points, my favorite part of this title is how the "story" progresses after each completed run.  Instead of just doing the same thing with some difficulty modifiers, you're actually trying to accomplish something slightly different within the framework that's been established.It was definitely entertaining and a decent challenge as well.It took me about 20 hours of slow methodical play to reach the ending credits.  And I'm pretty sure there's even more to experience.After a short break of exploring other titles I plan to return and play it through again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. Obligatory "if you like StS, Monster Train, Wildfrost etc."  A lot of times when I play a new roguelike deckbuilder, they are a little too close to one of those, and while this isn't doing anything drastically new, the card combination system is a breath of fresh air. On top of that, the unlockable starter decks feel a little different than the standard "this one hits hard"  "this one uses poison/ extra hits" meta. The styles are a lot more about how you manage cards than particular gimmicks. I'm excited to see how it grows and evolves. I'd love to see another general and more minions.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-puts a unique spin on the Roguelite deck building genre by using cards to populate planets and other such things-the cards you and deck build with feel great to play and fusing them to tilt your strategy midturn feels satisfying -the characters and random dialogue used by your sidekick are enjoyable even if confusing thing like "I have to pee" are said.-Cool and unique fights (my favorite is the one with the ship that attacks you by adding the hostage cards to your deck and you then have to figure out how to mitigate it.)-the story warrants replays though I'm not certain how many-With the most recent update the deck unlocking is now fixed and I will say each different starting deck has changed my approach so much it's great!Cons: -Missions feel unbalanced. You may be offered an easy mission like defeat x enemies for a decent reward or be offered an insanely hard mission where you have to add 9 hand clogging cards to your deck all of which must be played and all of which ups the amount of damage you receive when you play them and all of which cost one of your 3 energy you get that turn and the mission reward is mediocre at best. Conclusion: This game is worth checking out and is an update away from being one of the best in the genre!Right now this sits at a strong 9 out of 10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: TL,DR: Recommended but lacks some polish in mechanics and general aspects.The Good things: Fun, new mechanics like fusions that add variety and can make you lean towards one style of gameplay or another. Charismatic characters, absolutely broken combos that make you feel like a professional card thrower dealing zillions of points of damage.The best time I had was when I reduced my deck to seven cards, achieving brutal consistency and damage with the second deck.The Bad: There are many bugs in general. Cards acquiring the icon of others, not being able to select cards in certain events to offer them if you right-click at any point, weird interactions with certain combos.What Could Be Improved: Many quality-of-life changes are missing, like being able to go back off if you regret a choice in a multi-option (for example, in the event to upgrade a card, if I regret it after selecting), being able to know which cards will be affected by card-changing events (making them never worthwhile to pick unless it's at the beginning of a run), the fact that certain missions can replace health recharge points (planet population events can do this if you are close to the end of the act)...The grind is horrible, it takes a disproportionate amount of effort/time to level up each companion, and honestly, I've finished the game (and done several runs afterwards) and still haven't unlocked the third deck, nor do I have the slightest clue how to do so.The zillionpedia is atrocious regarding card combinations. They list over 500 entries with 8(?) entries per page, making you click endlessly to find the one you want. Additionally, the fusions really work by card type, and having them divided by individual cards instead of by type makes it extremely difficult to know if you're missing any fusion to discover.Similarly... the Gaia Altar is poorly designed in my opinion... it's barely functional and doesn't offer previously achieved "recipes" for combining, ending up being just a way to discard cards from your hand.I think this game can learn a lot from recently released games such as Balatro in these points. Definitely improveable, which I think the devs are engagaed with as per other comments.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend if you are looking to scratch that itch of a StS-like game: learn fun mecanics, looking for combos, and finaly one-shot the final boss.BUT this is not a good 1.0.Still some bugs after a few patches and a lack of content (more below).I got enough for my money. The music is awesome, the visuals are amazing, the story is funny. I m bought.BUUUUUUT... where daf*ck is the rest?*** some details about lack of content- Only 2 starter decks, the second deck getting available laaaate in the farming. (there are still some starter options to customise the setup you start with each turn, so there is some variety possible).- The other starting options are the same for both starting decks.- All decks play out of the same card pool. You ll always meet the same card reward during runs.- There is about 1 simple way make infinite decks with at least infinite damage. It s quite easy to pull off once you know. So late game is stomp.- There is no difficulty slider/ progression. No ascension levels in StS terms. So the runs don't get harder once you completed the game.It s like an awesome early access. If the devs puts in more content, it could even be an amazing game.Buy for the scratch, but if you dont have it, you can skip this game.With more content, it might be on the top of StS-like game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Love every part of this game from the writing to the art to the gameplay. The art is incredibly charming and fun to look at, the cards have fun and unique art that when combined with the player character firing their cannon can make it feel like these cards pack a punch. I love the characters, the main three are wonderful to hear from and the special event characters feel fun and wacky but still fit in. Card fusing makes deckbuilding more complex but nonetheless fun as you have to consider the possible fusions and the likelyhood you can actually make them.A few points to improve on, firstly, the card library includes a fusion library that show what cards combine to create what cards but because of the layout and amount of fusions it requires the player to click through tons of pages just to see them. Secondly, there is a way to view your deck when choosing to take or skip a card but there is no way to tell what fusions a card can make with the cards already in the deck even if you've already discovered the fusions, this leads to remembering cards with fusions you like and just skipping any others.

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic audio-visual presentationvery snappy gameplayeven better writing, VO and scenarionot into card-games that much, and when i read "roguelike" i usualy run for the hills (talk about oversatturation)but this one struck a cordhowever i can only recommend the game with a caviat: it is very, and i do mean VERY buggy at the momentshould've released into EA and needs probably couple months worth of patchingsoftlocks, hardlocks mid run, probably tied to issues with the U.I. or scriptsno crashes per se, but boy did i run into many hard locks, which i could only solve via ALT F4so i'd probably wait atleast 2 to 3 months, and check if patches happend prior to spending time and money if they ever fix this game it will be a pure shining little pearlwith a scenario, writing, athmosphere that just radiats pure chaotic sci-fi-fun, mixed with driving beats and a very tight gameplay loop
