_childDocuments_.review: Right now the game is full of bugs, mainly regarding controls and interface. Sometimes you want to fuse cards and end up playing them, you try to make a screen capture and pass the turn...  controls need a redesign and are really frustrating. However, this game is full of potential. I really want it to succeed.The art style has a lot of personality, rendering a more twisted version of Studio Trigger (specially Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann), combined with fascist imagery to give a sense of parodic ultraviolence akin to Starship Troopers.The gameplay is really interesting, and the fusion system and the philosophy behind not discarding the hand change greatly the feel and the thinking with respect to the archetypes of the genre like Slay the Spire.The music selection is small, but each song is fantastic and makes me enter the tank faster than I can shoot synthetic life forms to strange face.having planets.

_childDocuments_.review: Zet Zillions represents a notable addition to the roguelike deckbuilder genre, offering players a distinctive space opera experience. Its engaging fast-paced card battles and fusion system, allowing for creative combinations, set it apart from other titles in the genre. With its sci-fi twist and unique art style, it serves as a refreshing alternative to games like Slay the Spire.However, it's important to note that the game still has some unresolved bugs. Despite this, the innovative mechanics and enjoyable gameplay make it a worthwhile investment for fans of the genre seeking a new experience. If you enjoyed Slay the Spire and are looking for something different, Zet Zillions is certainly worth considering.
_childDocuments_.name: Zet Zillions

_childDocuments_.review: Zet Zillions is a whimsical card game that invites players into a universe bursting with vibrant colors, quirky characters, and an unforgettable soundtrack by Isadora Penna. Its combination of accessible gameplay, unique art style, and humorous scenarios offers a refreshingly enjoyable experience that stands out in the crowded realm of digital card games.From the moment you dive into Zet Zillions, you're greeted with a world that's as visually grabbing as it is entertaining. The unique art style immediately catches your eye, setting the tone for an adventure that's anything but tame. The card game combat system is designed with accessibility in mind, making it easy for newcomers to jump in and start playing without a steep learning curve. The fusion card system was an important foundation for this game and it stands out as a really fun mechanic.One of the unforgettable standout aspects of Zet Zillions is its humor. The game is filled with hilarious scenarios and characters that keep you laughing as you navigate through various challenges. This lighthearted approach makes it a joy to play and keeps the experience fresh and engaging.The soundtrack deserves special mention. The music in Zet Zillions is nothing short of amazing, perfectly complementing the game's atmosphere and enhancing the overall experience. Whether you're in the heat of battle or simply exploring the game's world, the music adds an extra layer of enjoyment.Accessible Gameplay: Easy to jump in and learn, making it suitable for both new and experienced players.Unique Art Style: The vibrant and distinctive visuals make the game a feast for the eyes.Fantastic Music: The soundtrack is top-notch, adding to the immersive experience.Hilarious Characters: The humor and quirky characters bring a sense of fun and personality to the game.Zet Zillions is a delightful addition to the world of digital card games. Its accessible gameplay, unique art style, fantastic music, and hilarious characters make it a must-try for anyone looking for a fun and engaging game. Its charm and entertainment value more than worth the value. If you're in the mood for a lighthearted and visually appealing card game, Zet Zillions is well worth your time and $.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally posted a negative review and said "watch list and wait" I'm extremely happy to say 90% of my original gripes have been fixed by the devs and i'm very much enjoying the game. On top of that the devs are EXTREMELY responsive on the discord and are working on several great updates. Its truly refreshing to find a bug make a post and a dev fixes it within 48hrs.PROS: Unique concept with tons of room for improvement/expansion. Hyper engaged and responsive Dev team- The love child of STS and FTL (best way I could put it)- Amazing art style- Soundtrack Slaps- potential for a lot of unique strategies- Good run length, comparable to STS. So it makes a great evening session gameCONS: Still needs some polish, significantly improved since launch but not quite STS level yet- Bugs, the devs have handled most major bugs I was able to find at launch (including the softlocks you will see referenced in older reviews), and have been extremely responsive to the community. Anything you come across at this point will likely be good to go in the next few weeks. There were a few that I reported personally that were addressed very quickly- Balance, The game could still use a balance pass, but if you are playing now and communicate with the devs on discord nows a great time to help shape where things end up.- UI, The game could still use some UI improvements but the devs are aware of the information players have been asking for since launch. You have the minimum but there are def some nice to haves that arent in. (filters for you deck, link to your deck from the card reward screen, a clean way to understand card fusions)- Progression and unlocks are still slow :( (fix likely coming soon based on the feedback I got)All and all its a great card game, still more content coming for it. Def worth a try if you like the genre, more importantly im all about supporting devs that actually listen to what the players want.

_childDocuments_.review: Good little deck-budilder game. Doesn't feel repetitive but may not last long.LIKEInteresting twist with their two special features: - fusion of cards- population (stagger jauge) which can also trigger other effects with specific cards.I like the funny spatial universe (pig planets) and the variety of events.NOT SUREStill some minor bugs (card over / progression save / UI update). It's more quirky than really damageable.The game is not that hard so a campagne might not last very long if you don't want collect everything.The progression system seems a bit long. _childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeously stylistic game that gets one thing very right, it's theme.  The art style, character, and card designs are top notch.   All of it takes cues from a lot of other famous works to create it's own unique style that makes the game stand apart from the rest.  It is for this reason alone that I'd recommend it.Mechanically it does enough things different that I can safely say it's unique enough to catch the attention of someone used to this genera.  The most different aspect is the card merger mechanics, which allow for some different strategies, and could theoretically open up a lot of depth.Unfortunately, that gets into the rest of my review.  I recommend this game with caveats.  It has a lot of hinted depth.  It doesn't actually have a lot of it.  The cards are a bit limited, and the encounters are likewise.  Basically after a few runs you've encountered most everything and there's not much variation.  More may come, but I'm reviewing the game as is.To summarize, good game.  Love the theme.  Good for about a day or two, and then you're done.

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically, this game is standard roguelike deckbuilding fare. Improve your deck, take on harder enemies, die valiantly, then start over again with some more cards and options unlocked. If you've played Slay The Spire, or a hundred other deckbuilders, you know what's going on here, and should pick up a lot of the game quite quickly. There are a few quirks, semi-original ideas, but nothing that especially makes it stand out from the crowd.However, where this game does stand out, is with the art style, audio, and humour that exists within the game world. Trying to populate a planet for the first time, and seeing what new face I was going to be presented with, made me laugh on more than one occasion, and the oddball cast of supporting characters add something that a lot of games in this genre miss with, personality.In a year of so many great deckbuilding games, this isn't quite my favourite. There are a couple of issues, had the game become unresponsive for me once (though a quick restart and I was right back where I was), and there were multiple times where the controls caused me to play cards accidentally. Mechanically, there isn't quite as much going on as some deckbuilders, and I feel a few of the mechanics (specifically around the combination of cards) are either missing some explanation, or don't quite always work the way I thought they would. However, it's still a great game, there's a lot here to like, and on top of everything, it's priced very nicely for the experience you get, and I see myself playing and streaming it again soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Zet Zillions

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of a placeholder for now, but wanted to get my 2c in for this one. Fun time! Still on my first run, 'cos I've been busy with work, but the design is AMAZING and the battles are just the right blend of challenging but fair. Fusion is certianly a unique system, but while the game was sold on that, it's the population mechanic that's been making the fights work for me - a kind of second health bar/stun meter for your enemies. It makes fights more than just 'throw numbers at the other side till they die'; and provides an alternate end to some fights via Colonization. Fusion has some fun possibilities, but so far it's mostly been 'make a bigger number to throw at the other guy'.

name: [REDACTED]
detailed_description: Black Iron, a state-of-the-art penitentiary located on Jupiter’s icy moon Callisto, is overrun with hordes of infected inmates. As a modest prison guard your job is simple – get to the last escape pod and get out alive. But you aren’t the only survivor looking to escape. Your rivals – a deranged custodian, a violent gangster, a maniacal lunch lady, and more – can’t wait to step over your corpse and save themselves. Only one of you can make it off the moon – make sure it’s you! FIGHT/DIE/ADAPT Each death is a learning experience. Starting fresh each run, build up your loadout with powerful experiments, weapon schematics, and buffs to battle through Black Iron. When you die (and you will die), use your hard-earned loot to purchase new permanent weapons, suits, and skills. Get stronger, experiment with your strategy, and get out! ROUT YOUR RIVALS You're not the only person to survive the initial outbreak or willing to use a bit of violence to get to the last escape pod. Some prisoners and even your correctional services colleagues are just as eager to escape and will make escaping harder by attacking you remotely or challenging you to a one-on-one duel. Race them, attack them back remotely, and fight them to the death to make it out in one piece. FIGHT YOUR LAST CORPSE When you die, you leave more than a coverall-clad carcass. Defeat the reanimated corpse of the last guard to succumb to the prison’s dangers to earn a powerful experiment. But beware, it’s not going to be an easy fight. The semi-alive guard has the same loadout they had when they met an untimely end and a few extra tricks up its sleeve to keep things spicy. DO OR DIE You’ve made the perfect build, battled through bosses, ran through rivals, killed your corpse, found all the files, and now you’re standing in front of that last escape pod. Sure, you could leave it all behind for the sweet taste of freedom… or risk it all in one last hardcore do-or-die run back through the prison. Fail and you lose all your purchased gear, skills, suits, and weapons. But IF you succeed, you’ll unlock new powerful permanent gear. FUTURE PUNK An irreverent attitude, unique presentation, vivid graphic novel style, and a 180bpm original arcade-punk soundtrack by Mutato Muzika enhance [REDACTED]’s sci-fi setting and fast white-knuckle action.

_childDocuments_.review: When I wishlisted this game, I didn't know it's set in the Calisto Protocol universe.I haven't played that game because I thought they were just trying to one up Dead Space and get back at EA (seeing as Krafton are the original DS makers iirc)That being said, I didn't know I was buying their product and let me tell you that I have been pleased to no end by this game.It has 0 bugs or crashes. This is unheard of in modern gaming. This is a finished and polished product.The gameplay is smooth and pleasing, some rooms, mechanics and bosses are challenging, but it never frustrated me like Hades or Elden Ring. It just made me "lean forward".I best the game on my 32nd run, took me roughly a day. For the price, this is more than enough.The graphics are cool, and the game only demands like 10gigs of drive space. The soundtrack is amazing and fresh, the dialogue is nice and not cringe.This is a solid 9/10 for me and a statement by Krafton that game devs can ship full finished products that are fun and fresh, cost under 40€ and do not require you delete something else from your drive just to install.Bravo and thank you. I have found this game because I was bored out of my mind and no game could hold my attention for more than 10 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: You can clearly tell a lot of love went into this game. I just played it for 20 hours straight... Iv'e loved it so far although I do find the game play and loop to be quite simple and wish there could be more complex/unique builds. (I'll get more into that later.) You DO NOT need to play Callisto Protocol before playing this game. This is a slower Hades twin stick shooter. (That is not a bad thing at all) It does some very unique things I haven't seen other Roguelite games do!! And that is saying something considering I try to play every Roguelite I can get my hand on lol. There was a moment where I was so stressed and locked in.. (IFYKYK) and I rarely have those feelings while gaming (except good ol fromsoft), it was an amazing satisfying feeling when I acomplished this games REDACTED, but man did I have to Lock in.Things the game does great:- Art (comic book art style? Chef's kiss!)- Music (Punk rock, almost as if REDACTED is playing it himself)- Fun Humor (there were many moments I laughed out loud)- Character Lore - Satisfying weighty combat- Smooth optimization (the polish is S tier. I never had a crash or bug or frame dip, the devs alone should be praised for that in this day and age)- Plenty of cool unlocks- Unique twists on the roguelite genre (Seriously I love how they put this game together with their own twist and spin on the genre) Things I wish the devs will add in a DLC or in a sequel- More build diversity (Let us break the game with our builds making each run unique and exciting, if you don't want us to break the game then at least make the builds more diverse)- Boss variations after beating a boss for the first time. (Fighting the same bosses over and over gets old fast, to make it fun I tried to no hit every boss lol) - Alternate weapon mods (the weapons feel very simple after quite a few runs)- Ranged > Melee (you can clearly see the power of ranged weapons vs melee weapons and that made melee feel unsatisfying and unrewarding when you get a experiment focused on melee) All in all I spoiled myself with this early access release and need to go to bed. If you are a fan of the genre and are looking for a fun game to sink your teeth into, look no further. I think this is the best roguelite to FULLY (not counting early access) release this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Redacted makes a strong first impression thanks to great production values across the board, but it feels like the gameplay is missing something. The experience feels largely the same run-to-run, and the game's most interesting ideas (like the Rival system) simply don't do enough to mix things up each attempt. Really, I think the core problem is that all of the gameplay elements are bog-standard genre affectations without any real unique spark to them. The in-run upgrades use the same system we've seen copy/pasted from Hades a million times by now, and not one aspect of the metaprogression has really piqued my interest. It's the same "+Max HP" or "+Starting Money" perks that literally every single roguelite released in the past decade has. Frankly, I'm finding myself somehwat bored after an hour. Is Redacted a bad game? No. But it doesn't feel worth playing over another run in Hades, or Wizard of Legend, or Ember Knights. Considering Redacted is also more expensive than all of those games, I feel like I can't quite recommend it. Overall, I think this game is FINE. But, in a world where we have a litany of amazing games at our fingertips, that's not enough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's very challenging, but super fun. It has a lot of cool systems in place that make it more interest. If you're looking for something similar to Hades that isn't Hades this is a great place to be. Similar boon systems to Hades with permanent upgrades that can be unlocked throughout the game. It has a last corpse system that lets you fight your previous death to get a boon that you had last run. A rival system that has others gunning for the end before you do that you have to kill off (I haven't managed to kill one yet). A permanent upgrades system that makes subsequent runs easier (I still haven't completed a run though). Overall I highly recommend this game, one of my favourite games I have played in awhile.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm exactly that kind of guy. After Hades got released on Steam and took it by storm, I wanted to play it, but wasn't really a fan of this ancient Greek religion and mythology. 4 years later KRAFTON decided to make a spin on their existing and presumed dead The Callisto Protocol universe, and lemme tell you, turning oppressive isolated prison filled to the brim with inhumane experiment and taken over by unknown infection into joyful comics style action packed playground with pumping soundtrack is nothing but masterful.For all you Callisto Protocol fans . Yes, it's no longer a horror game, but seeing familiar elements left and right as well as things that imho should've been in the original game is splendid. There is no better feeling than putting good old Stun Baton and Hand Cannon to good use, especially cool is that the . And seeing upgrades that can change the way you use said weapons significantly open up multiple paths for consecutive playthroughs. It's by no means close the quality that Hades provides. For example It has balance issues, mainly after 30 hours in I still couldn't properly grasp the melee combat in the game, and you have plenty of different weapons to choose from. It seems more like an afterthought because I mainly rely on ranged weapons. Oh, also final boss being a massive difficulty spike is a  pain. game without much story going on. And obviously I'd love to see more about the universe game set in, maybe it's for the best they decided to not bombard us with all that information. Because game is trying to be comedic all the way through. Everything from comments of our mysterious observer to redacted information of inmates you unlock (you have to fight them btw) is just so lightweight and delightful There isn't much known about game development. Having literally no marketing campaign and seeing the amount of reviews on Steam it feels like Striking Distance made the same mistake as Microsoft did with Hi-Fi Rush. And there is a reason I'm talking about that game. It seems to me at least that after Striking Distance acquired Tango Gameworks they put them to work immediately. According to the timeline Tango Gameworks was purchased somewhere in August and REDACTED came out in October. Meaning the game was obviously in development for quite some time before Tango could do any significant changes to the game. But looking at Hi-Fi Rush, I can't get rid of feeling that it wasn't just a coincidence REDACTED turned out the way it did.Overall I hope this game will gain the attention it deserves. I'd love to see KRAFTON putting more of these smaller but addictive and fun experiences, and who knows, maybe we do exist in the timeline where Callisto Protocol 2 can happen.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually up on my action roguelites (they're kind of my thing), but this baby comes out of nowhere like an atom bomb...it's that much of a blast! First up, I've never played the callisto protocol, and that doesn't matter the slightest to enjoy redacted...this game takes place "in the world" of callisto protocol like your average street vendor is "in the world" of Spiderman. Second, despite this being a smaller, less triple A endeavor, the graphics here are absolutely stunning, they move fast, the particle effects are really cool looking, and there are a lengthy list of stylistic touches that I've never seen in a game before...it's probably the closest to playing a comic book (and not that it's cell shaded...it just has very flashy effects akin to comic book panels). Third, and obviously most importantly, this game has absolutely dialed-in mechanics...like Hades dialed in, and it didn't need any early access to get that polish...it's really impressive! Here, the focus is more on mixing up something like twin stick shooter gameplay with the melee of something like hades to rack up interesting combos and ways of killing mobs. There's also an emphasis on utilizing environmental kills, as your character has the ability to remote detonate environmental hazards. This is expressed via an EXTREMELY robust upgrade and unlock system across several different areas, but as of my play time, there are at LEAST 4 different guns, and 4 different melee weapons...and there's a good chance there's quite a bit more (there aren't any interface spoilers, so you only see the next unlock available). Each weapon plays completely differently, and the play can be further mixed up by getting certain items throughout your run (similar to a deadalus hammer in Hades). Lastly, there's a novel mechanic of "rivals" who you're racing to the end of the game against. They'll toss abuse at you, spawn in hazards, and occasionally show up as a mini boss...all of which you can partake in too...adding a novel "big picture" strategy layer to the gameplay. So, if you're even slightly a fan of the action Roguelite genre (Hades/World of Ink/Gungeon/wizard of legend/ember knights) or arcade shooters and beat-em-ups (golden axe, streets of rage) Redacted is a must buy...this game deserves way more hype for how incredible it truly is.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly solid and fun roguelike. Good variety of weapons (which is pretty funny coming from Callisto Protocol), 4 different biomes with unique enemies, fun cast of characters and a pretty unique rivals mechanic that I haven't really seen in any other roguelike, forcing the player to compete with 3 other people for the final escape pod. I'm surprised the game doesn't have coop or even pvp, since both would fit pretty well with the game's design. The game is also pretty cheap. My main issue are the questionable PC controls. While devs do recommend gamepad, KB/M for the most part works fine, but one glaring issue is the inability to aim charged attacks or GRP strikes with the mouse. Mouse itself is only used to aim your ranged weapon, everything else is aimed via movement keys. It is possible to get used to it and there are some workarounds that allow you to aim with the mouse, such as using GRP while firing, but it would've been nice if the game had proper KB/M controls. Overall a well made game that is a pleasant surprise. I expected a cheap cash grab, but got an enjoyable roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is just ok, but can't help feel like it's missing something to keep your interest for long.Pros:- The combat has good weight to it.  You can feel the hits.- The visual production is incredible, game looks great- Rival system and Last Corpse system are cool additions to the roguelike formulaCons:- Combat is weighty, but doesn't flow very well.  The melee doesn't smoothly combo with the gun or the charged attack so it all feels clunky.  It would be much better if you could string the different attack options more smoothly.- Way too many currencies for progression.  Game forces you get the resources for the meta-progression DURING your runs.  Not a terrible system in theory, but because there's so many different currencies you need for different unlocks, you often choose those resources to unlock more stuff rather than focusing on creating builds.- Melee needs to be changed.  Once you realize that the better option will always be the gun, the game really just becomes a slow twin stick shooter.  - No boss variety from run to run.  The first boss will always be the first boss, and so on.  Got really tired of beating the same boss over and over each run. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic roguelite. Really cool visual style. Performance is fantastic. Even on Steam deck this thing barely uses any juice. Plays at a fluid 60 and feels great. Still early days but i couldn't put it down once i started last night. The loop of each run is farming specific resources to then unlock specific upgrades back at your base. Each time you die you can spend your resources to improve your weapons, suit or various other little things that will make your next run easier.Its a difficult game but also feels fair. Combat is nice. I saw someone complain about the mele saying its not worth using vs ranged but i disagree. You can pick a perk after some rooms that allows you to upgrade ranged, mele or your dash etc. Even spending a single point in mele makes a significant difference. I've been mostly using mele to take out enemies and its been really effective.The combat is really nice. Mele varies by weapon and upgrade but you can also add in dash moves. Dash mele attack or dash kick to knock back  and stun enemies. Environmental traps are littered around (just like in Calisto protocol) that deal significant damage to groups of enemies - or if you kick, push, throw an enemy into an obstical it does even more damage. You can unlock modifiers that then increase that damage. Both active and passive. P{er run upgrades can then add additional elemental damage or stats effects to your dash, mele, kick attacks. I honestly find the dash and mele combos increadibly fun to use.You then have a choice of ranged weapons which are also passively upgradable at the hub as well as additional active upgrades available after each room you clear. Each room ends in a choice of doors that offer specific upgrades or resources.They also have some other really nice systems at play. You have these other human enemies controlled by the game - but they are your rivals racing to get to the escape pod. You can gain energy to set traps / slow them down but they can also do the same for you. It's a really nice wildcard element that adds an extra layer ontop of everything.'Loads of little progression systems are littered throughout the game as well.Feels like there is alot to discover and unlock.I really like the pacing and progression. The game starts off really difficult but once you get to grips with the mele / ranged combat and understand enemy movements and attacks it starts to become very manageable and really damned fun.Very fun addition to my rougelite collection that i think i'll be playing more than some of the others for now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could not be more different from the Callisto Protocol. It drops the generic grimy space prison for a colorful, comic booky visual style that looks fantastic as it fills the screen with tons of VFX. Instead of being a third person Dead Space-like, it takes the mechanics of Hades and puts its own spin on them into something that's satisfying both in the moment to moment gameplay and the long term decision making. While the game feel is excellent, mixing combinations of melee and ranged weapons, the real star of this game is the addition of the rivals systems. You're trying to escape from Black Iron Prison in the middle of an outbreak, but you're not the only one. You'll face off with other rivals that are racing to the same escape pod you are. As you go, you can do "attacks" on them that slow them down or hurt them, but they can also afflict you with specific room conditions. It's really fun to try to balance all these elements, adding just enough complexity to the formula without overwhelming you.Even if you didn't care for the Callisto Protocol, this game is definitely worth a look, and it keeps me coming back for one more run.

_childDocuments_.review: After many hours and runs this game is fun, but the progression for weapons needs a rework and makes the game utterly frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: I will start this review by saying I don't usually like roguelites. What interested me about this game was its weirdness. An action roguelite with a gorgeous cel-shaded artstyle...where you fight a bunch of stuff from the Callisto Protocol universe? I was intrigued. This game follows the basic tenets of a satisfying roguelite: You feel a little stronger and a little better with every run. The permanent buffs you unlock with the games currencies make SURVIVING till the very end relatively easy. What makes this game challenging is the Rival system. You MUST beat the AI controlled opponents in a race to the final escape pod of a crumbling prison. If you lose the race, you lose the run and have to start over. This makes every run an adrenaline fueled sprint. The feeling of clearing out a room in seconds before dashing to the next door without a second thought is truly exhilarating. Here's an important note: this is NOT the game to do multiple runs in a single session. A single run in this game feels like a workout. By the time I reached the final boss, I could feel tension in almost every muscle in my upper body. I've very much enjoyed my time with the game, but I simply don't think I have the endurance or reflexes to actually beat it. At least not right now. To sum up this review: REDACTED might be the LEAST relaxing game I've ever played, and I say that affectionately.

_childDocuments_.review: [REDACTED] is a solid roguelite that draws heavily from Hades, particularly in its gameplay mechanics and in run upgrades. However, the game does do some unique things that allow it to differentiate itself, notably in its Rivals system, which puts you against other characters in your escape attempts. The game has very satisfying meta progression, and a good variety of weapons/upgrades that help to keep replayability high. It is by no means an easy game. I've got a lot of experience in Roguelites, having beaten Hades at 50+ heat, and I did not get my first win until my 22nd run. There also is a robust suite of difficulty modifiers available to you after winning a run, a la the Hades Pact of Punishment, and that should keep challenge enthusiasts busy for a long time.Surprisingly the writing for the game is pretty decent;  something you don't see often in this genre, and that helps to make the runs, even the unsuccessful ones, fun and interesting, as you are learning more about the world and characters on top of gaining all important meta-progression.Most importantly, the game feels good to control and play. Overall, I would definitely recommend this game to roguelite fans, particularly ones who are fans of the Hades gameplay style. Would some people call this a Hades Clone? Almost certainly. I wouldn't go that far, but even if you would, it's still a very well done one, and that's enough for me to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: pretty great game play, game clearly takes inspiration from hades with it's upgrade and level progression, but unlike hades which was moslty melee focused this one is more focused on a mix of range and melee, with ranged being the bigger focus, melee weapons are useful and even have charged attacks although in my experience you don"t really get a chance to use the charge attacks as if leaves you too vulnerable for too long and the speed of this game can get pretty fast, the game does do another thing different with you basically being on the clock at all times with you needing to race against the games' "rivals" who are all trying to get to the end of same as you and who will interfere with your progress as if any of them are ahead of you they can add dangerous elements to the level like enemies who explode on death, or explosives raining from the sky, but you can slow them down as well and even fight them (although early game they are very formidable and using melee against them feels like a death sentence)pretty bad writing with it's speaking characters (which the player is not) particularly with the shadowy figure who follows you throughout as a sort of semi-narrator for your journey, the other characters although are decently charming and actually have pretty good character design to them as well, luckily tho this game isn't story heavy like Hades where you can chat with NPCs, so if you can you just ignore what the characters are sayingoverall it's a pretty good game, doesn't cost a whole lot but if the writing is a bit of a drawback you can wait for a sale

_childDocuments_.review: I am so on the fence about recommending this, but I think I ultimately will despite the games flaws.On one hand, the combat is incredibly fun and there are some unique mechanics that help this game stand apart from the inevitable comparisons to Hades. The Rival system is mostly good, offering a bit of randomness to each run and giving you a bit more to worry about outside of the normal encounters. I love the art style as well, it's very flashy, colorful and over the top. On the other hand, it feels like there are almost too many progression options and currencies. I don't think it's objectively bad, but some may find it to be far too tedious. I also hate the art style for the same reasons I listed above. There can be a bit of clutter on screen when things get crazy. And the voice acting.... lolThe major problem for me is the lack of controller keybind options. The options may be perfectly fine for some, but for any game to release in current times without this option just seems strange. I also tried KBM, and there are some pretty annoying oversights as well. The main one is not allowing you to keybind aim and shoot to separate keys. I swear I thought my game was bugged for like an hour, until I moved the "shoot" key to my mouse right click. This allowed me to aim, but then I still had to left click to fire. Small oversights like this exist in a few places.I have had enough fun in my 6 hours so far, and I plan to continue exploring what this game has to offer. An update to tighten up some of the issues would push this into a much easier recommendation. Fingers crossed.

_childDocuments_.review:
Black Iron, a state-of-the-art penitentiary located on Jupiter’s icy moon Callisto, is overrun with hordes of infected inmates. As a modest prison guard your job is simple - get to the last escape pod and get out alive.

But you aren’t the only survivor looking to escape. Your rivals - a deranged custodian, a violent gangster, a maniacal lunch lady, and more - can’t wait to step over your corpse and save themselves.

Only one of you can make it off the moon - make sure it’s you!

name: Fae Farm
detailed_description: Editions Purchase the Deluxe Edition of Fae Farm and get a 25% discount on: • Fae Farm - base game • Fae Farm - Original Soundtrack • The "Coasts of Croakia" DLC • The "Skies of Azoria" DLC About the Game Escape to the world of Fae Farm and create your own cozy home in the enchanted world of Azoria. As you nurture and grow your homestead, you'll get to meet charming characters, foster deep relationships and discover ways to infuse magic into everything you do. Customize your character, master the arts of crafting, cooking, potion-making and discover so much more. Unfold the mysteries of the island on your own or with up to three other players. You can invite your family and friends or visit their homestead to progress together, playing beside you or online. As the seasons change, you'll be able to unlock new areas and restore the world around you. Embark on a ship and set sail to Azoria, there's a magical world waiting for you! Cozy and customizable Create your own character and customize your adventure with unlockable styles and decorations for your farm. The cozier your home, the better your experience! The story unfolds independently from the in-game calendar, allowing you to play at your own pace. Magical Creatures As you tend your farm, you can care for a variety of cuddly animals where you can collect eggs, wool, and more. You can also raise baby animals in many different colors and explore the island to discover magical critters that drop rare potion ingredients. But not all creatures are friendly: beware the jumbles; mischievous spirits that block your path! Adventure is at your doorstep Explore the realms of Azoria as you traverse the island with your skills and spells. Forage caves to gather resources and battle jumbles! Progress at your own pace as you uncover new mysteries and restore peace to Azoria. Budding Friendships Azoria is home to a cast of colorful characters! As you progress through the story, you can build bonds with many islanders along the way. You can even find romance by going on dates and eventually getting married at Town Hall. One for all You can play on your own or with up to 3 of your friends online* or over local wireless. Share your progression, build a farm together where everyone’s efforts count. and support each other through the quests and challenges of the world around you. *You’ll need to create a Phoenix Labs account in order to play online together, invite your friends and visit their homestead. The Phoenix Labs account isn’t required to play on your own.

_childDocuments_.review: I have quite mixed feelings about this game. It is a typical life/farm simulator, with some nice features and some oddities.Fae Farm is nice and colourful but with quite boring conversations. Part of that is probably due to to NPC´s lack of awareness about what you as a player do or did, one example of that is that the NPC´s keep mentioning stuff I did ages ago. Gets annoying quite quickly.  Sound design is nice, except that I hate the laugh your character makes when they succeed or find something (It´s OK the first 20 times...). There is no voice acting but I did not expect that. And the farming is bit odd, you need to craft containers with soil and then place them to grow stuff.You have to unlock things to craft (all stuff to craft it visible in a catalogue) by doing stuff (talking to NPC´s, wandering around, doing quests).  Else it´s charming and cozy to play. Love the auto pick tools and the swift traversing (especially the pink jump pillows).Strengths:  Adorable graphics - very colourful world, charming  art style, runs well - no crashes or performance problem on a GTX 1060, activities are fun and Quality of life features like auto selecting tools are great likewise the swift movements. Likewise the "jump high pillows" on steeper terrain makes for an even swifter travelling. Cozy ambient sounds and sfx.Weaknesses: Annoying laugh. Using your Steam user name as name of your character and you cannot change that. Very simple combat not much dept in that part. Relation and marriage is very lacking and have to little impact.Still the good outweighs the bad! If you like this genre its a weak 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Pros - Fae Farm is a super cute with beautiful, whimsical aesthetics. There are some great innovative game mechanics, and so many things to make, decorate, and grow. The dates you go on with characters are super cute with stunning artwork. I'm still holding out that the game will redeem itself with an update that fixes  some of its flaws, such as...Cons - The characters are shallow and the quests/mines are a little uninspired and grindy. Many people compare this to Stardew Valley, but it felt more like Animal Crossing New Horizons. There isn't much plot but it is still fun to run around a pretty world - to a point - but the lack of depth leaves a lot to be desired.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to getting value for your money, this game barely squeaks by. The graphics are bright, cute, and clean. The game play and controls on the Steam Deck were good and without issue. The animals are so cute and easy to take care of. Most reviews I've read say the relationships in this game are shallow. To elaborate on this, I did not like how the status would go from Acquaintance to Flirting automatically. Pretty early on I just flat out stopped talking to any of the villagers. The marriage in the game was basically nothing. I was married to the white haired fairy guy by the end of the 2nd season in the 1st year. That is insanely fast. I also did not like that every one of the marriage candidates was marked as "Former Sweetheart" after getting married. That was just weird. By the time I finished the main story I was glad it was over. The mine for Chapter 7 was kind of annoying. I did not like how the main story ended as it was extremely quick to end and was anticlimactic. Chapter 8 ended so quickly that I thought the game actually glitched out. I would only buy this game on sale, if at all. Lastly, I'm disappointed to have found out that this game is no longer being developed further. 2 paid DLC's for everyone not on the Switch version is not enough to justify the price of this bare minimum game.

It's super cute, the little quality of life things that are missing from other games is there; like tools auto swapping, not getting fined for being out too late, the way fishing works, etc. The fact furniture has a purpose is great! It's a good mix between Animal Crossing & Stardew Valley in my personal opinion.The story seems to be abit short, which makes me a little sad but honestly; as with most games like this, the endless farming & decorating is there so it makes up for it.Now I will say, the price tag is a bit steep given that the story is shorter than say some other games of the same nature, but I suppose the quality of the animations & how everything is put together can make up for it - though that being said, I def did wait until it was cheaper and grabbed it then as 40CAD is abit much for me for such a game.Otherwise, I recommend it. Can't put it down and if you're into games like this that are cute, cozy & addicting... this will be for you!

_childDocuments_.review: I personally really enjoy this game for what it is: a watered-down uncomplicated and casual farm sim with little to no stress-inducing elements. It attempts to streamline prevalent genre mechanics and mostly succeeds on a basic level to add some quality of life features. That being said, I would say this game is priced a bit high for what it is and has the veneer of more depth and interesting mechanics without actually offering such things. It's a weird mix of having very polished visuals but very undercooked systems. Also contains a myriad of issues which on the surface look like easily fixable low-hanging fruit things. To give a few examples:- There's leveling for most activities in the game such as farming, mining, fishing, et cetera. However, the rewards for leveling up are very flat: Each category only has two types of upgrade (e.g. "chance to not use stamina when mining" and "chance to deal extra damage when mining") which alternate per levelup. To compare this to some other farm life sims with leveling systems, other games offer exciting things like unlocking new recipes giving access to new gameplay mechanics, or offer skills or interesting choices between upgrades.- Pausing is completely inconsistent. When the game pauses, all it really pauses is in-game daytime passing. Monsters can still attack you, debuffs timers still increase, timed buffs still run out. Additionally, opening some menus do pause the game while others don't. Weirdly the building menu doesn't pause the game, which makes it kind of stressful to quickly think about where to put stuff. This seems like such a trivial thing to fix and make consistent.- Animals keep running up to you. This is extremely annoying when watering/harvesting crops or accessing crafting stations, since everything is mapped to the same context-sensitive button, resulting in your character hunching down and brush an animal whereas you were trying to water your crop field. Worse still, animals stand on top of each other in barns making it kind of impossible to "target" and care for the intended animal, wasting quite a lot of time. This could be solved by just allowing each interaction once per day, which again seems like an annoying issue with a trivial fix.It's kind of mind boggling since this game is by no means lazily put together, but there's quite a lot of these minor inconveniences stacking up and undermining the feeling of a modern game which seem like they are all quite fixable with minor tweaks. Since the game is set up to be relaxing and casual, whenever one of these issues rears its' head and some of the frustrations resultant of the inconsistent dungeon delving difficulty crop up it's more jarring.All in all, if you're into farm-life sims and don't mind or are actively looking for a very casual one to let your stinky brain relax, I can recommend this. Depending on how much you're willing to spend on games, I would pick this up when it's on sale. 20 bucks seems like a more reasonable price considering the competition.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game and got my moneys worth but it is no way a polished game ready for final release. For the 40 USD that I bought it for, the game is very much over priced. Wait for a sale of AT LEAST 20% because there are many other better farming sims out there like Rune Factory 3 or Cornucopia (an early access farming sim).But the game is playable and the core is there. _childDocuments_.review: faefarm is everything that makes a great modern farming game and much more!!everything you'd expect from games like story of seasons and stardew valley, with the addition of magic~faefarm has an adorable artstyle, tons of story content, new areas to unlock teeming with new things. it starts off quite standard, but furthering the story allows you to unlock the 'fae realm', with new characters, new animals, new creatures to catch, and new crops to grow, and you're even given a new farm situated within the fae realm itself! you unlock fairy wings that give you a double jump, allowing you to explore much further than before, aswell as magical spells that can be used in combat as well as for other purposes too! out of the farming games i've played, this is the one that felt like it had the most things to experience. so what doesn't faefarm do well?- the social systemfaefarm's social aspect is definitely lacking. many of the npcs have shared repetitive dialogue, and the friends and romance systems are weird to say the least. you have six romance candidates, but you will automatically begin romancing them just by talking to them, there is no option to be friends with them. if you talk to them enough, you'll suddenly be 'dating', which is a little weird. marriage also costs 10k, but comes with absolutely no benefits, not even unique dialogue. it's weird it costs so much when there is really no benefit to it at all, they just wonder your farm in the day. - it's a little buggyfaefarm has it's fair share of bugs, most of which seem to be fixed by simply quitting to the title screen, such as your animals getting stuck or a ui getting stuck on your screen. i haven't personally experienced anything that ruined the experience, and have faith the devs will fix these early release bugs. an annoying one is that previous romance candidates will continue to have their quest indicator above their head which you can no longer complete once you're married.- some small oversights:- when fighting in the mines, you're staff will constantly switch out to your pickaxe when near minerals, causing you to start randomly mining whilst getting your ass beat. - you can only use the watering can spell on a targeted centre spot, instead of positioning where you want to.- you aren't able to move flowers and crops between your farms, so if you have any rare colour hybrids for example you have to regrow them from scratch on another farm, as picking them means you cant replant them.- the game doesnt pause in most menus, animals and monsters will continue moving and attacking- so it can be pretty hard to get out the potion you need in the middle of a fight.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot, I still play it just to finish the achievements...but if I were to recommend it to friends/others, I would either say wait or just don't. The art is so pretty, I enjoy the dungeons and I like that you don't have to specifically be a farmer to make money and progress...but holy moly bug city. It's towing that line where I can't even tell if certain things are bugs or weird design choices. Sometimes the bugs require me to back out of the game and reload just to not have stuff like farming UI errors on my screen. This game feels like it didn't have a lot of QA or testing done. And the UI bugs are really annoying, especially with pinned quests becoming unpinned if another quest was finished, or having an exclamation point in a menu you can't get rid of...I think with proper testing or fixes I would recommend this game? But I seem to be apart of a larger crowd that wonders if these bugs will be addressed and fixed (I do think they did one round of bug fixes however!).I also have some small gripes that I just gotta get out there. Buying colors (and tbh items in general) - it is painful to remember what you need, what flowers to breed, and who sells certain colors/things. I wish they were all monetary. I know there's extra incentive to make flowers or craft things but it feels too complex to remember.Clothes - I wish you could preview outfits on yourself before buying them. Housing - I also don't like that some housing items you can craft over and over, especially not having a counter of how many are in your inventory. If I want a certain wall design, I feel like I should only have to make it once and then it'll hide it from the menu. I've ended up wasting materials making the same wallpaper over and over because I forgot I already made it once and thought it'd disappear after in the menu. Also I do wish you could place items on other items in your house if it makes sense.Relationships - why is someone interested in me and wants to flirt after I've talked to them maybe like twice in the game's playtime?Co op - I don't feel like there's enough content like Stardew has where you can explore with a friend without doing main quests all together. There are mainline quests, job quests, relationship quests, and community board quests...which I feel is good for solo playing but I'm not really sure how you'd juggle quests without missing out on the gameplay. Maybe everyone has their own questlines? Guess I wont know til I try it with someone.I've spent a lot of time thinking about how I feel about this game. It's hard not to compare it to Stardew Valley, Wyldeflower's, etc...and at this price point with how much content and bugs there are, I think it should be at least a little cheaper to pick up. I think there are a lot of good things here but they need support and extra polish. Maybe if it were $20 instead I'd feel a little different, but not completely.

_childDocuments_.review: As an indie game reviewer, I'm delighted that I was able to receive this game to review - no strings attached! All opinions are my own. This is only a small portion of the review that I ended up writing! If you'd like to listen to the FULL review in video format, check out my video! Let's discuss the gameplay! The gameplay loop is as one would expect from a farming sim: plant/water crops, feed your animals and grab their harvestables, then go explore! There are mines to explore, critters to catch, and ample fish to fish up. Bug catching and fishing are as one would expect - swing your bug catching net at the bug when it is close to you, get a bug! Whereas fishing has a smaller minigame to go with it that isn't too complex. Cooking is acceptable, as you have to use separate cooking stations to make food. There is a drink station, a prep station, and a basic cooking oven. Crafting stations are much the same: put the base items in and wait a certain amount of time for the end product! Very simple. One of the things that makes all of this so enjoyable is the introduction of tool skills and magic. Want to water all of your crops at once in a 3x3 area? The iron watering can does it for you! With a little bit of mana and a certain magical staff, you can harvest everything around you at once. It adds a certain depth to the game while still also enabling you to get the busy work out of the way so you can go do something fun. Despite being a farming sim, you also have a bit of combat to do! In the mines, there are creatures called jumbles. Smack them with your staff! You can even keep track of how many jumbles you've defeated by checking your almanac. Speaking of the almanac, it is such a nice addition to the game. The almanac keeps track of everything you have unlocked thus far, enabling you to keep track of completionist goals in the game itself.As I said before in our section about The Town, the graphics themselves are gorgeous! Given this is the same developers who made and actively work on Dauntless, the cartoon-y style was expected. However, what wasn't expected was the sheer deft they use to create the fae aesthetic. The town itself is colorful and enjoyable to navigate, with many different sights to see along the way - an inn, the beach, the town square.. The mountain area is purposefully menacing when you think you might be freezing! Don't forget the bouncing mushrooms you can use to easily traverse the land! And the Spooky Forest has dimmed lighting and coloring that makes it appropriately spooktastic. A later area notches this up to an 11 and really makes you feel as if you've been transported into a realm of magic, fae creatures, and beauty. Overall, the stylistic design choices in the game concerning the areas and most of the characters are on point!Honestly, despite some of the major issues I had with the decision making for this game, it has been an overall enjoyable experience for me. Aside from the relationship system, the game itself was near perfect and I spent over 20 hours playing it and likely will spend many more. If you love games like Sun Haven, Stardew Valley, and Rune Factory, then you will absolutely enjoy this game!

_childDocuments_.review: So many glitches!  Multiplayer mode - Had to get an invite from my friends to join them.  There was no actual way to join up unless they paused the game and made a multiplayer invite.  Then a good portion of the time, after I connected to him, my animals / bugs / etc would disappear as I interacted with them.  Using the portals, I would try to teleport and my portals would loose their seals so I couldn't use them anymore.  The only way to fix them was to log entirely out of the game and restarting it.  And if you have any potions or buffs active, you loose them when you do this.  My friend was trying to turn in a quest, and somehow got pushed onto a chair, and then he couldn't interact with anyone or anything until he closed out the game and logged back in.  We have played for roughly 24 hours, and the bugs keep happening.  I would LOVE to give this game a thumbs up, but I just can't.  It's very cute, and interactions are smooth.  But then the bugs start up and one or both of us are ready to uninstall.  With some work on the developers part, it could be a real gem of a game. _childDocuments_.review: So people have criticized the game for having one dimensional characters. And I won't even refute that, the character writing is pretty bland. BUT! And this is a big butt. I will fight any and all gods for Argyle's honor. They are, without a doubt, the shining star of this game. I came into this game "I'm going to date a cute fairy." Met Argyle, and those plans went right out the window. This little autistic man with his love of frogs, and weird desire to be gifted "frog sweat" must be protected at all costs. Later found out that Argyle is actually female, and uses they/them pronouns, and I can't tell you how much I love that. I am agender fluid, and tend to use they/them pronouns for simplicity's sake. So seeing some nonbinary representation in the game (their name is a random noun, and they use they/them pronouns... they are absolutely nonbinary) was incredible. And, as I've said, I'm fairly confident in my assessment that Argyle is also autistic. And if they aren't I still love them, and will protect them from all harm. You know that meme from Brooklyn 99 about the dog? Well I've only known Argyle for 51 hours, but if anything happened to them I would kill everyone in this room... you get the idea. Argyle is a precious bean.Now that I'm done gushing about my favorite character in anything at the moment, let's get to the gameplay,. It's got a great gameplay loop. I'm almost done with year 1, and I presume the storyline. It's been a fun little ride. It's no Morrowind or Baldur's Gate, but it has a fun little story that keeps you fairly decently engaged. But more than that is just the farming. I love farming sims so much, and the fact that I can plant, say, turnips year round is nice. I don't have to necessarily keep track of seasonal seeds if I don't want to. They are absolutely a thing, and you can make them at the gardening table. Or you can just plant some Turnips, throw down some Magic Change Fertilizer... I think that's what it's called... and it can turn into the seasonal (or Fae, if in a Fae soil) variety... makes resource management so much easier.Overall, I highly recommend this game. It's a lot of fun, has the best character to exist in fiction at the moment (eat your heart out, Astarion!), and I am far more invested in this little island than I care to admit...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... okay. I think the gist of my thoughts are: get it on sale, because it's not worth it at full price. While visually beautiful, this game doesn't offer enough content to be worth spending $15-20 more than other farming sims. I've only put a little over 40 hours into this, and that's half the time I've put into most other farming sims before I got bored. THINGS I LIKED:- The art and graphics are beautiful. The world is very pretty, I like the character designs, etc. - The mining is fantastic. I love the designs for the mines, and the monsters are just challenging enough to be interesting without being frustrating. There's an abundance of resources to be found in mines, not just ore and rocks. The mechanics are very typical--hit stuff for resources, find a thing to unlock the level to keep it open, etc.--but the visuals really make the mines stand out. - Mobility in the game is fantastic. There are very few invisible walls, so you can move about the world very freely, especially after you unlock the wings and can jump better. - The furniture you craft for your house has an effect on your stats, which is really creative. I do wish there were more options for the furniture, especially since you're given several houses to decorate, but I like the concept of the furniture affecting you. - The fishing mechanics aren't very original, they work similarly to other games I've played, but I like that you can easily see the fish in the water and know what kinds you're fishing for. THINGS I DIDN'T LIKE:- The NPCs are probably the worst I've encountered so far in a farming game. They are just so boring. Most of them are shopkeepers that never leave their market stands or shops. A few of them wander around here and there, but for the most part they're just so... stationary. The dialogue is boring and repetitive. Friendships mean nothing. I haven't even bothered with the romance, because none of the very few options you get are interesting enough for me to want to advance with them. It makes the world feel very lifeless, because it's just you and some bugs wandering around most of the time.- The festivals, and it's generous even calling them that, are terrible. There's only one per season, and the only thing that happens is some decorations appear around the village. Nothing else occurs. - The farming itself is overly complicated. I hate that the shop only sells a few crops year round--and they're not even really year round, because they will die at the end of the season, despite the fact that it's exactly the same plants sold in the next season. You have to plant those crops and use a special fertilizer to magically change them into different crops, and even after you unlock them, they won't be available in the shop. You have to make more seeds yourself with a crafting table, or keep magically changing them. There's an unnecessary number of planters to choose from. Overall, I can tell they were trying to make their farming different enough to stand out, but it's standing out in a bad way. It's all so pointless and unnecessary. - Crossbreeding flowers. Holy crap is this an annoying process. And you need crossbred flowers to unlock so much. Maybe it's just a me problem, but I've found that this ties into my thoughts on farming, in that it's unnecessarily complicated. - The main story took just over 40 hours to complete, and now that it's done, I feel very little motivation to continue. There are only a few things left I haven't completed or discovered and after those, the only thing left to do will be farming and mining, but... there won't be any real point to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna preface this review by saying I absolutely love the vibe of this game.  Overall the atmosphere is very cozy, and I genuinely enjoy the world itself, and the theme of using magic to do, and aid with farming is something that immediately held my attention.  Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game in its current state, and I will detail why, below.The main way to progress the story is by clearing the dungeons.  This wasn't so bad for the first dungeon because you can just go in, push as far as you're able to gather materials used to craft "seals" that are used to unlock the shortcuts as you go farther in, and then come back out.  This is fine on its own.  Starting with the second dungeon, however, you find yourself needing to use something called a Fairbreath Potion so you can breathe the miasma that fills the entire dungeon and will knock you out in around 30 seconds.  This obviously puts a time limit on how long you can stay in the dungeon, because potions have limited duration, but it's not so bad for this one because the ingredients are easy enough to get.  Chop clovers outside of the dungeon, put em in an ingredients table, and catch little slime blob critters and squeeze em for juice.  A day of work could produce a few days worth of these potionsThe problem came when I cleared the second dungeon and needed to go to the third, which is in the middle of the frozen northern part of the map.  This needs shells you get from snails and crabs, which are fairly common in the main part of the map, and spore essence.  Spore essence drops by grinding up plants that can only be found in the deeper parts of the second dungeon.  The same dungeon that you cannot enter without a potion of its own.This is also after dealing with the various other issues the game had that I was willing to tolerate until now.  Such as the fact that you can only sell 32 items a day.  It's slightly offset by the fact that you eventually get a crafting table that lets you convert normal crops to artisan foods that sell for a ton more, but since these recrafted foods sell for way more than the individual crops and sell for a fixed amount, there's no reason to ever grow the other veggies.Additionally, the seed vendor only sells all season seeds that can be grown whenever.  In order to get seasonal veggies, you have to take them and spread magic fertilizer on them, which at the end of every day, has a small chance to convert these seeds into their seasonal variant.  To get the seeds, you throw them into a gardening table, which destroyed the veggie, and gives new seeds.  This is the only way to get seasonal seeds, so you'll have to dedicate a portion of every harvest to making new seeds if you want to grow seasonal veggies, and you'll have to repeat this at the start of every new season.  Given you just convert them into materials to make artisan foods, you have no reason to do this besides the fact that seasonal veggies give slightly more materials for this (3 chopped veggies instead of 2 from all season, when you need 25 chopped veggies for the artisan stuff).The farming is all pointless, however, because the gems you can gather in the mines drop in massive amounts once you upgrade your tools, and sell for as much as the artisan foods, and by the end of the second mine, more, while being plentiful enough that you can have a few going out every single day if you just grind the mines.The seasons also bring their own issues.  On top of killing all growing crops when a season changes (including the all season stuff), summer makes it so you randomly have to stop and catch your breath if you're working on sunny days, any rainy day may have you stop and shiver, and winter will probably do the same every day (I am unsure about this part, I have yet to make it to winter, and likely wont for a long time.This all lends itself to an air of tedium that doesn't really improve how the game feels, and just makes progressing through the story a largely unfun experience that heavily misses what a farming game like this is meant to be about given the reasons to farm are largely pointless, and acquiring seeds to grow different veggies are muddied by further pointless tedium.All this is to say I dont think this is a terrible game, and hopefully these issues can be fixed, because I would love the game otherwise, but at the moment, because of these issues, I can not recommend the game at its current price point.

_childDocuments_.review: The game possesses an immense amount of untapped potential. While it excels in various aspects, there are areas where it seems to fall short, only doing the bare minimum. To elevate this game from its current 7/10 rating to a resounding 10/10, a few critical improvements are necessary:1) Meaningful NPC Interactions: NPCs play a vital role in shaping the game's world, and it's crucial that they feel more integral to the player's experience. One way to achieve this is by adding depth to their characters. For instance, birthdays should offer unique dialogues and interactions, and we should have the option to give gifts to NPCs not only on their birthdays but on other days as well. This would foster a deeper connection between players and the in-game community.2) Immersive Events: Events in the game hold great promise but currently lack the uniqueness and depth that would make them truly memorable. Each event should have a distinct theme, offering players the chance to immerse themselves fully in the world and the festivities. Adding unique interactions and challenges during events would make them more engaging and enjoyable.3) Progression with Purpose: The game currently provides players with access to many crafting stations and resources early on, which can be overwhelming. To enhance the sense of achievement and provide players with lasting content, progression should be restructured. Players should have to work their way up to acquiring advanced stations and animal housing. This would create a more rewarding sense of accomplishment and encourage exploration of new content as the game unfolds.4) Enhanced Animal Mechanics: The game's animals currently feel like mere dispensers of rewards. They often obstruct interactions with crops, and the tools meant to manage them, such as fencing, do not work effectively. To make animals a more engaging part of gameplay, they should be given more nuanced behaviors. This includes addressing their tendency to disrupt crop farming and improving the functionality of containment measures.Addressing these four key areas of improvement would undoubtedly elevate the game significantly, making it a more meaningful and immersive experience for players.

The world has something akin to magic affecting multiple aspects on the island, as you complete more Quests and "beat" story bosses you unlock more regions of the map and with it, NEW FARMS! Fae farm also shows you all NPCs in this List no matter if you have met them before or not so you can decide on a romance target early on and not accidentally start it too early, even tho talking to dating targets levels up to flirting really quickly so make sure to stop chatting them up once it reaches there if you're waiting on a different NPC. The Art style is really cute and you have a lot to level up and maintain on your farm so no day feels dragged out or locked behind skills. All in all Fae Farm is a magical farming sim that I just can't get enough of!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite fun at first but my experience was completely destroyed by TONS of game-breaking bugs. A random different game breaking bug literally occurs every 15 min or so. I really can't recommend this game at launch to anyone. With the high sale price, I don't understand why it's so broken. I've seen alpha builds and many early releases much more playable than this. For a mid-sized studio like Phoenix Labs, the game REALLY shouldn't have been released in this state. I've encountered at least 30+ different bugs that severely hamper progression or just break the game entirely. Here're some of the most game-breaking bugs I remember. All these have occurred in single player mode. 1. Cannot accept almost any side quest. Just doesn't show up in quest list even after clicking accept multiple times. 2. Cannot complete some relationship quests, even though quest is in quest list. NPC has no reaction to me talking to them3. Random loss of ALL items after passing out. Nothing shows up in inventory next day4. Health, Energy, Mana suddenly revert back to the beginning stage of the game 25h in, even though house is full of cozy furniture. Restarting game does not fix this. Removing and replacing all furniture does not fix this. Stuck with extremely low stats forever???5. Coop animals suddenly stop producing or eating. Had to sell all and re-buy6. Seller NPC menus suddenly stop working. When talking to a seller, there's no option to open shop. Had to restart game. 7. Main quest (yes, even main) NPCs suddenly stop working. When turning in a quest, they only have the chat and goodbye options. This includes the spirits (?) like Grell, Wisp Mother etc.  8. Invisibility potion works for 75% of the duration, then suddenly disappears even though there's 25% left9. Forageables don't spawn correctly. Some forageable spawns are 'fake' meaning you can pick them up but they do not register in inventory. Sometimes when you pick up the forageable, it stays on the screen. 10. Not a bug but the game day is wayyyyy too short for the amount of stuff that needs to be done. Please add options to adjust length of day AND pause the game in all menus. I haven't even tried a single of the notoriously buggy shipping contracts. PLEASE fix these basic functionalities soon, this is actually quite shocking. If the major bugs are fixed, this game will actually be a rather engaging experience and it has great potential. Thank you devs and fellow players for hearing me out.

_childDocuments_.review: The most shockingly unfinished cozy game I've ever seen released on multiple platforms.After seeing this game for sale for the Switch I figured it must be a complete and good game. When I saw it on sale on Steam I decided to ask my boyfriend for it.If you're looking for a mindless farming game where you complete the quest, build the thing, decorate the space and raise the animals.. Then sure, it's fun. I've played it to the end of the story quest and more. I enjoyed it well enough because I like these things... But objectively, it's terrible and so unfinished.Relationships with characters are shallow and boring. Everything happens all at once and far too suddenly. I was shocked when I completed the first dungeon. As soon as I left after being told to "Come back tomorrow" (after bringing the food to the first sprite) and found that the whirlpools were already cleared and there were suddenly fae people walking around everywhere and every npc was going on about how great it was that the whirpools were gone and visitors could finally return.I can't even remember some of the things I mentioned to my boyfriend as I played, but things that stand out in my mind as being so bad are:Item placement in your home - you can't put anything on top of anything.. Fae jewelry box on a desk? Nope... Not even on the "display stand" that you can build.The farms - You have the opportunity to have and run/furnish three farms and make any your home base.. But why on earth would you? The resources needed to make a home "cozy" are a grind to get and it's incredibly simple to travel from any base to another once you've unlocked the travel platforms.Quests - There were several times when I had to google how to get things done because the game just didn't give instructions.Animals - I thought (based on the "tips" popping up to always interact with your animals, that you needed to interact with them and pet and/or brush them daily or they would not be happy enough to produce or something... and when I started breeding that the happiness would potentially have an effect on how many resources you got... But none of that seems to be true. Once they're happy, as long as there is food... They just stay happy. Harvesting is painful for the chicken and rabbit creatures as there is no way to autoharvest, even at the end of the game, despite being able to unlock an autofeeder almost immediately. The game is glitchy in that the totem you can build to keep them out of your way just doesn't seem to do anything half the time. Animals that don't require brushing sometimes DO suddenly want brushing and despite showing as available to harvest, you can't because the action just brushes them instead.Some animals will come outside on their own, while other farm buildings/animals require you to call them out each time.I never used or really needed or made 90% of the potions, you just don't need them. There are far too many, as well as far too many things to craft that just aren't required and you never really have reason to make or use.Honestly I could go on and on about what's wrong with this game, I find more each time I log in. I'm still so baffled as to how such a bad/incomplete/over-engineered/and yet under thought out game made it to so many platforms and was even used as a prize for something like McDonald's in their Canadian Monopoly game. I've certainly gotten my (boyfriend's) money's worth out of the game, but I do NOT recommend you spend yours on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I put off buying this game, because I’m a huge stardew fan, coral island fan etc.. and for some reason, I found other reviews and videos not convincing enough. WELL, I am very happy I decided to try out the demo and then buy the game! I find it to be a huge chore to have to interact with the NPCs daily, you don’t have to do that in this game! I also heard there’s not a good story in this game, but all the characters have personalities and I find them adorable! Being a huge fan of farming sims, I’ll list some reasons to try and convince you to try out the game. The graphics and cute cottages are beautiful and cozy. You can jump off a cliff, there’s almost no boundaries besides the game border. If I want to run and jump off a water fall, I can. The bouncy mushrooms are so much fun. I feel free when I play. Watering crops is fun and not tedious. Catching random bugs and critters is one of my favorites. You just quickly swipe and you’ve caught one or two at once. The fishing is not hard, I would say in-between compared to other games. I just unlocked the mines, finding a gemstone ore and watching gemstones pop out, about 2-3 is so cool! In most farming games, it’s rare to find an actual gemstone. When you level up tools, your tool harvests more. There seems to be a ton of different furniture, decorations and I love how you’re able to easily change the color of them. I haven’t gotten around to breeding flowers, but I was excited to find out how many different varieties there are and that each flower leaves behind a seed! I also can’t wait to start beehives. The “magic” aspect of the game is unique! Apparently, you can give gifts to the NPCs and I had thought this game didn’t have that. I originally thought this game was a flop, I’ve even watched videos on it and I’m here to say, please at-least try the demo! You’ll most likely end up loving it, if you love the other popular cozy games. I find each game unique, this one is worth it, as long as you’re alright with not having a deep story. It’s also multiplayer, which is awesome. I hope this helps someone! 😃
