_childDocuments_.review: I know people will probably come at my neck for this review, but I have always been the "be honest" person when it came to reviews and feedbacks. Been waiting for this game for over a year and I'm extremely impressed, enough to actually recommend it if you have a controller. What it does, does it right for a simple cozy game in a pseudo-fantasy eviroment and you will have tons of fun with it just like I actually am.However, the reason my review is negative is because of the game not being refined enough for mouse&keyboard users, which should've been the first thing working perfectly in a PC port . It seriously lacks polishing on controls and is extremely bugged.- Keys will often not rebind correctly. You cannot use the "X" key on anything as the game will not rebind it to anything du to it being in use on the menu.- You can't rebind the confirm action to anything, it's on the left mouse button by default and it cannot be changed.- Keys often do not perform the action they're supposed to do, you will have to smash keys for a while to have them work as intended.- You cannot navigate menus (including the inventary) using the keyboard. this means you do need the mouse, it IS a requirement for even basic sorting of items and have dialogues go forward (you can't press the interact key to have them keep going, only the mouse will do that).- Can't deactivate the "keep pressing" function on confirm buttons (which can hurt your hands after a while). Once again, only the mouse will work on it anyway even if you rebinded the interaction key.- Character will only interact with tiles/items/characters if your mouse is pointing at their direction. This is something almost every game on the "cozy farming" game genre does unfortunately, here however simply becomes even more frustrating than usual since you will have to continuosly use your mouse for almost everything but movement. (Seriously Devs please stop this trend, have your games the ability to NOT use the mouse at all as accessibility feature, it's way easier to remap if you give us the option to turn the mouse off.)If you plan on playing this on Mouse&Keyboard, please don't buy it just now, wait for fixes or buy a controller first.I'm having fun and trying to overlook those issues, I'm doing my best, and I don't plan refunding the game because I really like what Phoenix Labs pulled off. However my review cannot be positive until those things are addressed, I'm sorry.While I love the game I'm not reviewing it just for the content (which is perfectly in line with the pricetag), I'm reviewing the PC port as a whole and it is unfortunately lackluster as of now.My review will likely change if those issues get at least partly fixed over time because really, the game would be perfect already if only those things were adjusted.

_childDocuments_.review: Should you get Fae Farm for Steam Deck?Spoiler Free!Gameplay:This game is insanely captivating, it has everything I love in a cozy game and more. You can fish, mine, catch bugs, do *light* combat, talk to characters, romance, and more!Though I do think the story *so far* is a bit bland and characters have alot of the same dialogue, the actual gameplay makes up for it IMO.Hopefully they will improve on dialogue options and characters soon.PC vs. Steam Deck:I started off playing this game on PC, and the game looked great, but the controls were horrible. They were kinda all over the place and didnt have normal keybinds you see on other games (for example you had to right click to exit instead of press esc which irked me) and there is no way to change them.So I switched to playing on the Steam Deck and had a way better time, especially with controls. You can set your keybinds and make it to your liking with no trouble, and of course have customizable buttons on the back.The graphics were the same if not better than my PC on high and there was absolutely no frame-rate issues or lag.In my opinion, cozy games like this are just best served hand-held. Games like Animal Crossing would feel so weird to play on a PC, it just works when you can snuggle into your couch and relax.TLDR- Game is good and works well on Steam Deck  👍🏼

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute with its whimsical music and adorable fae characters. It feels like a blend of Portal Knights and Story of Seasons, and I'm absolutely smitten with it. The controls are superb, offering a seamless and responsive experience. The sound design is a standout feature with stunning ambient sounds, delightful twinkles, and satisfying dings. It just feels great to play. For example, there's these little purple bouncy things that you can use to launch your character into the air to scale cliffs, and I just love them. It's a small detail but it's so much fun. Overall, I'm having such a blast and can't wait to log off work and return to my little fae farm.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this a recommend, but only because I enjoyed playing the game for a short while.On the good side:There are plenty of commodities, making money is easy, the artwork is easy on the eyes.My irritations are:There are plenty of bugs which is bad for a game sold as "finished", shipping is limited, low number item stacks, the controls are not in-line with other cosy farm games (though if you can adapt, its fine), targeting animals is difficult (you often accidentally pet or brush a different animal), the story is shallow, you can complete it too quickly because there isn't as much content as you'd think - and I don't think its worth the £50 asked for it, I've played better for half of that price.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played my fair share of this category of game, and I think for these games, the characters are crucial to making the world feel alive and compelling. Fae farm did not achieve this in my eyes. The world is crowded. Theres soo many npcs and barely any of them seem to have any depth. The market place has 8 npcs there permanently stationed when they're open, and completely unromancable, to put it into perspective. They have filled this world with NPCS but only have 6 that are romancable (and of those, you can only speak to 2 at the beginning  of the game, you have to unlock other areas/story events to meet the other 4, so get to the mines). Meanwhile, the second you have a story quest active or just finished one that'll be all you hear about from the npcs. Everyone has 4 different variations of the phrase "thanks for clearing those vines!" that I heard constantly for a while. Beyond flat, most of these characters.The visuals are stunning and I really enjoyed the mines but the rest of the game feels lacking to me. Most of my negative thoughts revolve around the lack of interaction with npcs and how flat that makes the game feel, which kept me from playing past the end of chapter 2, so take that as you will. Maybe it gets better after that, but I can't say.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay lets start with the PROS. -It's got a beautiful, calming, serene soundtrack. -It has a lovely color palette-A lot of the ideas for mobs and critters are very cute-The housing decor system has very tasteful options-Cross pollination is fun -- if it works!That being said, I have a list of Cons for this game and I am so bummed to say that because I bought this during a steam sale because I couldn't afford that AAA price tag. Having purchased and sunk 20 hours into this game now, I can say confidently that even at a discount, almost 40.00 was still way too much. So here we go with the CONS: -The face style is lazy and really hurts the character design-The NPCs are worse than cardboard, and some of them greet you as besties even though its your first time meeting them-Everyone looks like a toddler, yes, even bearded guy. So no, no I do not want to romance any of them. -Several quests unlock important things like a secondary attack, and a spell. WELL it turns out you get the attack, and spell, well before the quest is finished, which is weird.-The place they call the Plains looks like a patch of grass next to some stairs. When I see Plains I think a wide open space with lots of grass, but this looked like that sad patch of grass you might see in front of an apartment complex. -Cross pollination seems hit or miss. I made 3 1x3 boxes, and followed the instructions for the pink flower quest in all three, hoping to sell the additionals. It only worked in one box? And it took over a week in game for the seed to show up? Going onto reddit there was a ton of confusion there too, with lots of different right answers. If your players are having to guess, that means you didnt do a good enough job explaining it.-The controlssss. No one, and I mean, no one, is using that Almanac enough for you to put it front and center. Also I hate that if I accidentally open the almanac, once I finally, finally navigate out of it, it resets my item menu to the top left of my inventory and I have to start over if I was trying to use a specific item way down the list. -It couldnt be that hard to support the icons for Playstation controllers can it? This is an accessibility issue. -It feels RUSHED. I wish we could have seen more fleshed out character development for the NPCs, a more robust character design system that doesnt look like the faces are drawn with crayons, etc. The price tag tells me either ya'll really thought this was a done game, or you had investors breathing down your neck, but either way, I didnt feel good about the purchase. I can't recommend this game in good conscience without significant improvements to gameplay, world building, and accessibility, but it has the makings of something that could be pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Farm is a very enjoyable farming game with lots of things to keep you busy.First of all, I finished the story in around 35 hours mainly focusing on the main quest.All achievements were done at almost 80 hours, DLC ones included.I didn't fill the collection, but I'd say I was close to a complete book in the end.The best thing about this game is that tools automatically switch to whatever you need them to be.It's comfortable to have it that way and I feel like this will spoil me when I hop into other games without this feature.Everything looks very appealing and perfect for a fantasy world with bright colors, soothing sounds, and a generally happy atmosphere.The farming is a bit weirdly done with being forced to use fertilizer to get different crops, but that was ok.Dungeons were the most fun in my eyes with all 3 of them being different, a lot of monsters, and ore to farm.There are a lot of different skills to level like critter catching, animals, fishing, cooking, potion brewing, and so on.At some point, I felt a bit overwhelmed with all the different possibilities and stuff to keep track of.Now to the more negative parts of Fae Farm:The social aspect is very lackluster and I had no fun talking to the characters other than for the sound that popped when the friendship with them went up.That was the only satisfying part about it.While making friends, they often ask you to fetch them something that only improves your relationship with them, but with mostly no other reward than that.If there were events with the villagers and marriage candidates that made it worth it to improve the friendship I would've loved it, but well, you just get higher friendship and their dialog doesn't seem to change.I noticed that they mostly talked about the same stuff over and over again until I didn't bother talking to them again because it was not worth it.The game would perfect in my eyes if it hadn't done the social aspect so poorly.Still, I recommend it since it was a fun experience and I spent a lot of time enjoying the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons first: most characters dialogues are bland, the day cycle can feel too fast and could use an option to choose its lenght, in the online multiplayer you create a new character for each of your friends worlds (well this can be a pro depending on your tastes), map and right click to go back with m/kb controls are clunky at first (but they feels good after a little bit)Cons out of the way, this game has a lot of content, after 14 hours spent in the world i realized that was just the first area, the game opens up even more. The traversal around the map is my favourite part, you can jump anywhere, swim like a mermaid and twirl around; once you unlock certain things (spoiler? i dont know, its even on the game cover) you can jump even higher, it just feels super fun to go around this way - lots of things hidden around to unlock this way too.Gameplay feels fluid and fun, it doesnt have some of the things that can make me stop playing the other games in this genre. The map felt clunky at first but once i got used to it, it worked well and i could track quests and npcs very easily and fast. Lots of things to manage, it auto selects the tool to use for the resource you are gathering, the critters looks adorable and everything flows well... its hard to stop playing.There is combat as well and multi-layer dungeons, very simple at first but the monsters telegraph their attacks and have nice animations. The game destroyed my already bad sleep schedule, i seriously couldn't put it down for 10+ hours and this didn't happen for a long time. Not perfect, not revolutionary but with way more content than it seems at first and very well done

_childDocuments_.review: I usually love these kinds of games, and I was so excited for Fae Farm, but it was disappointing. I don't know how it is on Switch or in non-multiplayer mode, but it was very buggy and some interaction issues. The fact that my partner had to create a separate character to do multiplayer with me was weird. We could only do one shipping contract when the season changed. My chickens and sheep things would just stop eating and producing stuff. I had to sell them and get new ones after a few days. Sometimes I couldn't get the magic swap to work with no explanation why. I would have a red x in front of my character and couldn't get rid of it. Sometimes I couldn't jump when I entered a dungeon unless I pressed B. Sometimes my storage items would flicker if my partner's character jumped. Fetch quests you have to activate twice--first give them item, and then the NPC walks away and then I have to talk to them again to finish the quest. Some quests my partner couldn't complete but I could. Getting married is boring because they won't have deep conversations with you anymore and just stand around doing nothing. The story just wasn't engaging for me, and the main game was very short. It is hard to craft almost everything and a lot of the home items weren't appealing to me. I didn't have the motivation to try to get all the seeds, flowers, stuff, and some of that was because I just didn't know how. Overall, disappointed :(

_childDocuments_.review: This review will be updated once I progress further in the game.I've seen a lot of people who bought this game and weren't happy about it. Even though I received this game for free, I can honestly say this is one of the best farming games that I've played in quite some time now. I've played Stardew Valley, SOS, Harvest Moon, and other farming games out there. Yes, I wish the NPCs had portraits, or at least allowing us to see how they look; that would be nice and would add more depth because that's the main issue with the NPCs. But honestly, the quality of features, when it comes to other aspects, is absolutely enjoyable, and it's not boring at all. The world itself feels alive, with way more animation than I've ever seen in these AAA companies that make farming games, to be honest. Comparing this to other titles, I can feel the love that they put into this game.However, the fact that you can't rotate your camera and the lack of customisation options make it not recommended for everyone. We rarely see games being released in their full state, but at least this one feels polished, even the animations are great, which we hardly see in other titles.When it comes to the progression of the game, it is slow-paced. At first, you won't feel that much progress, but as you go through your day, you will see the world of Fae Farm opening up to you more and more. Even exploration is fun in this game; I've never felt bored at all while playing this game, and I consider myself very picky when it comes to the games I play.My suggestion: if you are truly a fan of farming games and you have the money, go buy it and support the developers. We hardly get a full release that is polished, and at least there are no game-breaking bugs. We should support more developers who have a passion for their games and not give them a bad review just because you can't rotate your camera or there's a lack of customisation.If you don't have the money right now, I would suggest to wait for sale. But I highly recommend this, to people who truly love farming games.With all due respect, but I find this absurd. This is your own taste in the game, but I don't believe it's appropriate to not recommend it to anyone just because it didn't meet your expectations. As I mentioned above, give us more meaningful reasons why you can't recommend this game.PS: If I wouldn't get a copy, I would still buy and recommend the game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's 7/10 good, but...It's a 3D farming/crafting/mining sim, in the style of Animal Crossing. Explore the island, meet people, get quests, build a farm, and go into the scary mines. As that, it works pretty well. It's fun, and has some really interesting story elements that are unique to this game.The dungeon mines are fun, each with its own mechanics and creatures that evolve as you level through them. Sometimes they are frustrating, and sometimes they are hard, but you quickly get over those hurdles with some upgrades and things get better.The storage-house mechanic is really solid. Store your items there, and you can usually use those ingredients and completed goods for almost everything you need to do, with an exception below.The farming mechanic is fun. You try to work your way through and into different crops, ensure you have the right seeds, and make sure you have coverage of the various types when you need them.But it has some major negatives, which didn't make me dislike it, but are worth knowing about:First, the game is very gated. You are offered lots of abilities, quests, and crafting, and it's all locked behind "not discovered  yet" message--some of which you don't clear until the end game. I specifically had one quest given to me relatively early to use a recently acquired spell to charm monsters, and I didn't get to those monsters until the game was done.The vendors have upgrades, new items, etc, but they often cost coins and crafted goods. You don't find out what those are until you show up at the vendor to get it. One example is upgrading your house. You show up, and need 3 of two different items--easily obtained, but you have to have them with you when you go to upgrade. Oh, you wanted logs instead of sticks? You need 5 instead of 4? Too bad. Go back, get the right things, and return.The game is absolutely about the mines. You can almost ignore everything else. Mine to get seals to open the mines more, to finish the mines, to get the new spell, to go to the next set of mines. And the money you get from the items in the mines dwarfs what you'd get from farming.Farming/gathering some items can be fun, but some of the items are just reskinned versions of each other. So it's great that you're growing beets instead of turnips, but they both end up as chopped vegetables in the end.The NPCs are pretty bland. I couldn't tell you any of their names,  and "Wow, great that you cleared the thorns in the first 10 minutes of the game, 40 play hours ago" is not wonderful dialog to tell me who those people are.And finally, there's no endgame to speak of. You can rerun the dungeons to get more materials, now with almost no risk or effort. You can grow out your gardens, but they aren't that important anymore. You can make your houses look nicer, but it's hard because of the vendor issues, and the fact that things you might want are with very weird vendors. (Oh, the mayor has the wood color upgrade you wanted, when she doesn't really sell anything else?)As I said, the negatives didn't keep me from enjoying the game, but they did make me not care about a lot of the optional content, either.

_childDocuments_.review: Why I don't recommend the game:- Your character will be named after your Steam account name unless you jump through some hoops to change it.-Unable to pause totally the game (bug)-Sometimes unable to place workstation for no reason (bug)-unintuitive and clunky user interface. No hotbar for eating food for example. You have to open the menu and eat food/potion one at a time while enemy is attacking you cos game cannot pause totally (UI issue)-Animal tether item does not work and the stupid animals will run all over your crops and block your way (bug)-unrewarding quests that require higher value items to be given in return for cheap rewards that you can craft yourself - Boring NPCs with only a few lines of dialogue. Also boring marriage candidates.- Forced flirting with NPCs just because you have interacted with them too often. You don't get a choice of who you choose to flirt with. - Lack of character customization (especially in the mouth and eye area)- Lack of repetition for instructions/badly written instructions. Meaning if you accidentally clicked too fast in the fishing tutorial for instance, you have to google it because they don't repeat the instructions anywhere. Sometimes you rush to NPC with quest item only to find they don't want it anymore when there is no clear indicator that it expires. Quests also don't autoppin well, so sometimes you have to hunt for it in your almanac.- Lack of NPC names in the map and lack of item names in the storage (♥♥♥♥♥♥ UI) means you gotta memorize your info.- MAJOR Gameplay annoyance: the usage of special fertilizer to grow seasonal crops. You wanna grow a variety of crops? Be prepared to buy the crop swap fertilizer or hunt frogs to make it. To me this is a major annoyance in a farming game. Just let me buy the seasonal seeds dammit!.- The flower breeding mechanic feels like a ripoff of Littlewood.- No Autosort or Autostack feature for inventory management. You cannot even move items from one slot to another by dragging. So troublesome to have to do multiple clicking just for something simple. Did the devs not even bother to play their game?For such an expensive game, the enjoyability is hampered by a lot of factors. Also despite the long playtime available there are lots of people who feel that the price is not worth it. Me included.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the trailer for Fae Farms and was so excited for its release. I thoroughly enjoy cozy games, such as Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing and the Sims. I thought Fae Farms would be another one of those games I could throw hundreds of hours into but I was very disappointed.As a concept the Fae Farms is fleshed out but the gameplay is severely lacking. There's not a lot to the game and each story beat is the same gameplay loop with the only variation being the look of the monsters in each mine. You will go down levels of the mines, find the gems and metal types, unlock the levels permanently, then go on a fetch quest for a bunch of items you probably already have most of if you rarely sell items.On a positive note I do love the ease of Co-op within the game and the art style is adorable.However for me this game is severely lacking and should have been an early access game since that's what it feels like. If you are interested in the game don't buy at full price, wait for a sale. $40 USD is far to steep a price for this game

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't too bad of a game, but I don't think its worth the money. First of all, the characters are very dull.  There is no story to any of them really. You can become good friends with people by talking to them but whats the point? There's no reward. The animals are kind of buggy. Everyday one gets stuck somewhere. I also really dislike the storage options. Trying not to give spoilers, but there's a point where you get more areas of land and more items, yet only ONE STORAGE shed to cover multiple areas! WHY? Don't bother saving too many items because you won't have the space. Some things in the game are good.  Its nice that you don't have to select your item to say, chop wood or water your crops. The game will automatically select that for you. The farming and animal care aspect of the game is nice. Its was also surprising to find out there is a lot more areas of the map than it makes it out to be. The dungeons are fun to explore. Overall I wouldn't recommend this game. I think the story and the shallowness of the game out weighs any positive aspect. I'm finishing up the game just because I spent the money for it. But I won't be playing the game again or getting any DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was pretty fun at first but the longer I played multiplayer with my friends the more issues we began running into. Animals would randomly go missing, items in our inventory would just disappear... one time we dropped a pile of fertilizer on the ground and when we picked it up it turned into bug juice. It was nonsensical chaos. BUT we were able to ignore these flaws and keep forging on until my friend's character was randomly deleted. He joined my game as he normally would but instead he was a totally different character with no upgrades/levels/gear/items. We thought "oh that's fine, we have enough money to upgrade him" but the upgrades were entirely broken. He was unable to upgrade anything. He left, rejoined, that didn't fix it. He literally could not play with us anymore. I rebooted the world, it did not fix it. We thought "oh it's whatever, we're on the final quest of the final chapter so let's just stream for him and finish it!" but then my game crashed. I re-opened it and my world was deleted. I lost everything. My save data, my world, my character, everything. My friends and I are no longer able to play without starting the entire game over again. I do not recommend this game in it's current state. Wait a few years before playing, it's just not ready right now but it does have potentialTLDR;Pro's: Automatic switching tool is pretty dopeCon's: The rest of the game

_childDocuments_.review: My friend got me this game so we could play it together since we were looking for a casual farming simulator similar to Stardew. I don't think this game is worth its price tag unfortunately. It's riddled with bugs (one of the more annoying ones being that my character's voice will randomly change, so I just muted the sounds), the quests and character interactions are pretty shallow, and it doesn't feel like a game that I would be able to play alone without being overwhelmed. I think that this game really tried to do it all, which ended up leaving it to be very broad without much substance to it.I think one of my least favorite parts of this game is the lack of character depth. The dialogue between the NPCs is very lackluster and empty. In Stardew, I quite liked pretty much every single character I interacted with. I had a motivation to get close to the characters, marry, and help them with their requests. With this game, I tried to interact with the characters but quickly noticed that the dialogue was stale and repetitive. The dates were underwhelming. I gave up that portion of the game and instead spend my time fishing and catching bugs while my friend mines. The one main thing that I like about this game is the art style. It's very charming and has lovely details to it. I just wish the rest of the game had more immersive elements.

_childDocuments_.review: subject to change but for now... it's positive![The Good]+ customization is nice, decent options for hair/colours/markings+ the world looks lovely+ you can jump and swim which makes exploring a lot more fun vs a lot of other farming sims that are more restricted+ quests are straight forward and gives the game a sense of accomplishment with a cozy feel+ catching bugs is a lot of fun and it's really simple+ no toolbar, your character just auto selects the correct tool needed for a task which makes it quick and easy+ lots of crafting items and it appears there are a lot of cosmetic items for your home too+ you can buy and im guessing eventually make new outfits+ there's a mirror recipe you get very early on that lets you change your entire appearance whenever you want+ you can track NPCs which means finding them is easy[The Bad]- the NPCs only laugh and it's really creepy and constant- the map leaves a lot to be desired- i hate the fishing in this game and swapping to "simple fishing" makes it even worse. it took me almost 15 irl minutes to get a fish on the line, after that part it's easy but it's insanely tedious... by far the worst fishing system in any farming sim i've played so far- the way you sell stuff is annoying. rather than selling directly to NPCs you toss your items onto tables and it sells overnight but there's limited space so you can't sell that much at a time. i can see this easily becoming a hurdle with a huge backlog of things to sell.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. I was put off by the price but bought it as I really loved what I saw of the game play, I figured I could refund it, if needed. I have to say, reading some of the complaints, I really expected myself to refund this but I'm still playing and I'm addicted. Keep in mind, I'm currently playing single player. This game does have some minor bugs and is not as 'cozy' as advertised, the "mines"/dungeons are anything but, they can get pretty difficult and the combat is frustrating at times. I'm not a huge fan of relationships in video games but the dialogue is pretty repetitive, if that bugs you, you may want to wait for an update, otherwise it's not a huge deal for me.This game has so much to do, collect and explore. The creatures are just so adorable and I love that you're in control of the breeding. There are some bugs but if you love adventure games with farming and crafting, I highly recommend.Pros:Almost all furniture can be customized with the color palette.Can breed specific color of animals.Unlimited storage.Crafting Queue.Lots of seasonal forage.Unique critters.Unique recipes and crops.Beautiful scenery.Cons:Lots of bugs when in storage.Current bug with shipping contracts.Not able to move or customize buildings.Relationships are pretty boring, no real dialogue, they also move a little too fast.Keyboard and mouse don't respond as fluid as they should, sometimes requiring a restart.

_childDocuments_.review: It is rare that I am actually compelled to write a review, but this game has just enough potential that ends in mediocrity that I felt the need. I have also seen enough glowing positive reviews to really wonder what it is they are seeing in the game that I am not. This review was written after about 13 hours of gameplay. I will probably play more just because... well, that is where the review comes in. I will try to avoid any spoilers but it isn't like there is some deep story so it won't be hard.First, I will get the positives out of the way.The general production quality is high. The graphics (whether they are to your personal taste or not) are done nicely and the game runs smoothly. The little animals and creatures are cute, and the concept is good. The world is a nice size with variety and fun ways of moving around it.And now for the rest.It feels like everything, all the little things that make simulation games like this fulfilling, have been dumbed down so much that they are now just vague shapes. It is like they looked at a list of what people liked in farming sims and cosy games, made a really slick promotional video, then checked off each feature after adding it in the most basic form without even a hint of depth.Farming (which feels like it should be a really big mechanic in the game) is extremely limited. There are only a handful of possible crops and the end path for all of them is ... food that is really similar. The money you make from crops/food is so incredibly low that it is pointless as a money source (you can only sell a small, non-stacking number of items each day.) The animal side is a brilliant demonstration of how things feel shallow. Animals have needs that you seemingly need to take care of every day - you get a list with check boxes when you get close to them. Common sense would tell me that fulfilling these will lead to the animal providing something. But... no. Every morning the barn/animal will reset. There will be a product dropped on the animal's bed (in the case of chicken/rabbit things) or you can harvest from the animal (cow/sheep things). This seems to have no relationship to whether they were fed/petted/brushed/etc. the day before. Everything resets between days. Forget to pick up the items the previous day? There is only ever one to pick up in the barn. Put food in the trough despite the animal already having the fed box checked? It will be empty in the morning anyway. They aren't actually eating anything, it just seems to randomly be checked - I have gone into the barn for the first time that day (no food having been left in the trough the day before) on a rainy day when the animals stay inside and they have been "fed". I think it just pops up sometime during the day. You have the option of planting feed for them outside, but it isn't like it is depleted when they are outside, so it doesn't really matter whether you plant it or not. The animal's friendship with you seems to go up based on doing the stuff but it maxes out in a few days, never decreases, and doesn't affect the products they make so it is a meaningless metric.There are dungeons, I guess, but they are just kind of a place to go to get raw mining materials. Each one has maybe 3 floor patterns, no surprises or treasure, and the enemies are more annoying than anything else, even later on. When it comes to the NPCs... Most people say one line/season and then never change. Some got one line after an early story event and never changed again so they mention the same thing seasons later. You can romance characters, but they are also one-dimensional parody style people. All the friendship quests are random and 99% identical for everyone, with the exact same lines. I don't actually care much about relationships in sim games so it wouldn't have bothered me... except for how blatant the lack of care was. People would say the same quest completed line every interaction despite me never even starting that quest. One character ONLY EVER said something along the lines of "How did you know? That's my favorite!!" despite me not doing a quest for them, not giving them a gift, or anything. There is also no real point to collecting. You technically have an almanac to fill, but there is no meaning beyond that. Most items just get converted into the same small handful of things. There are numerous fish, but the only difference is the number of a single item you get when processing them. There are also a lot of "critters" and insects to catch... but just like fish, you pop them into their device for processing and only get a different number of the same item. In addition, there are countless bugs and things that *feel* like bugs because of the controls. You technically have tools for each activity like in every other farming sim type game - but this one automatically switches between them. Which sounds nice in theory. But how they have implemented it is a NIGHTMARE. You cannot manually control it; tools switch to items (that get wasted) then not back and so on. And animals milling around make farming impossible because they steal focus, and there is no way to prevent it. The special tools you can manually select get deselected randomly for no reason.Add to this that time passes no matter what you are doing. Looking at the map? Time is passing. Decorating? Time is passing. Selecting items for anything? Time is passing. I have seen complaints about the days being too short; I don't think they are - they wouldn't be if time wasn't passing in menus and on the map and when you were moving items, etc. At least there is no penalty for the day ending - in fact, there is no hint of it being bad. The day just ends at a time and you start again from your room in the exact same way as any day. That's it. At this point, I can only think that it exists to look cute and everything else is just window dressing. You can make a cute looking little farm with cute looking little animals in a cute looking little world - and I guess invite your friends? I haven't tried multiplayer and definitely won't be recommending this to any of my friends so never will. There are more decoration options than anything else in the game, which lends to this assessment. Even things that seem like they would be functional are just decorative (looking at you, fences that animals can just walk through.) Everything just feels hollow and kind of pointless, which is the saddest thing. Because it has a good start to almost everything - it just never goes anywhere with it (other than to collect the materials to make decorative items). It feels like there is so much potential... that never gets used.I thought I would really enjoy this; I knew that the relationship side was shallow from the earliest reviews but I don't tend to care much about that so thought it would be perfect for me. It just isn't. Everything is too shallow on top of there being way too many small annoying issues with controls and a scattering of bugs that result in it feeling frustrating to just get to work properly.I wanted so much to love this game, and it does a great job of making it feel like "surely this can't be it? maybe if I just play a little longer it will get better? maybe it will all change after I get to the next part of the story??" But I have come to the conclusion that there is no point at which it gets better. This really is it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I saw a lot of potential in the early information of Fae Farm, I did not see a lot that stood out among its contemporaries (at least in a good way) and nearly decided to skip it. I did give it a chance, however, and unfortunately it is just kind of bland and takes as much as it gives.It is generally functional, of course. Quests, combat, farming, fishing, etc. Shame the story and characters are pretty lifeless. They did not even put up a facade throughout the on rails tutorial, with half the town asking me if I had spoken to the mayor while running her errands. For anyone that says they love these characters, I ask you to list their names-- Because I sure cannot. I am not usually in favor of cutting the cast, but fewer people with personality makes it way more endearing than a large, lifeless city.There is also what feels like really weird tradeoffs for every good feature. For example, I was looking forward to shops always being open (a small frustration of mine in other titles), but, not only are the days pretty short, you can only sell a limited number of items a day so your purchases are throttled anyway. Coop is locked behind a third party account (supposedly for crossplay, but personally the trade is not worth it), and while there is a single player mode naming your character anything other than your Steam name is locked behind this third party account. Who thought this was okay?There are definitely some things I like. It is nice to swim in these games, and I was really looking forward to the AC style house decorating because it should be in more things. Critter catching is also fun (though I will never get over finding out the hard way that the conservatory is actually a bug blender). They just cannot carry Fae Farm alone… It reeks of MMO without the support and scale of an MMO, and to its credit if you are just cutting up with friends these things might not matter to you (even the multiplayer peculiarities). I, though, cannot justify the lack of core charm even with all the good ideas here.My two cents: get it on sale, if you are not already put off.

_childDocuments_.review: While bored and on the verge of turning to my darker gaming habits, in the form of spending WAY too much money on gacha games, my wife not-so-subtly said to me 'Hey, have you seen this new farming game that just came out?' Well 35 hours later and buying another copy of the game so that we could play it together, I have to whole heartily recommend Fae Farm to anyone who is looking for something to DO. There are some obvious comparisons one could make to other games in the genre (Stardew, Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, etc.) but I think Fae Farm comfortably cuts its own niche. The game really exudes charm, and, perhaps setting it apart from its contemporaries, builds on many of its systems as the game progresses. The first dungeon, for instance, had me concerned with its similarities to Stardew, but it quickly broke free from those in the second dungeon, introducing new mechanics and vastly expanding in size of areas. I saw then that this wasn't just a clone of its betters with a 3D models, but rather a unique and satisfying installment in the genre.  Also, Job Quests in a farming game!? For me, Stardew's museum system, while a reason to continue to collect all the different items, felt more like an achievement in Steam rather than a huge reward in game. But if you are going to give me a WHOLE OUTFIT because I'm a good farmer? Sign me up 100 times over. Also, flowers.

_childDocuments_.review: With all of the hate that this amazing little creation has received, I feel I must write something good based on the experience I've had only playing 10 hours. I got the full game demo on the switch to try it out, and honestly got hooked. The farming aspect is so well done, with a ton of quality of life improvements added. You don't have to switch between your tools, the game automatically does it for you. You can: 1.) Jump and go anywhere you want 2.) Swim 3.) Make a cute as ♥♥♥♥ house and decorate it with a ton of different options 4.) Become a fairy and get different wing variations 5.) Catch tons of cute little critters in not only your own realm but a fairy realm as well 6.) Cook a multitude of different meals that add buffs to various things 7.) _childDocuments_.review: FaeFarm is another entry in the long list of farming/crafting games recently, positioning itself next to Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Rune Factory, My Time at Portia/Sandrock, Coral Island, Stardew Valley, My Farm Story, Sun Haven, Littlewood, Moonstone Life, and many many more.In such a crowded space, how does FaeFarm stand out? Despite the gorgeous graphics and amusing starting premise that everyone's trapped here by magical whirlpools, the game falls short on the important bit: the people.Let's start with the three-tier relationship system. Most of the games in the genre have the ability to develop relationships with the many characters around town, and there's a split between those you can romance and those you can just be friends. FaeFarm iterates on that by introducing a third tier of soulless shopkeepers that have no relationship stat. Doomed to never see you as more than a source of commerce, the people you're interacting the most with are flat and lifeless.Second, the gifting system. You cannot gift friendship characters. There is a button on romance characters to gift them a specific item (that changes daily). Gone are the days of learning what people like and giving them thoughtful gifts to friends. As an extra snub, characters still have birthdays shown on the calendar but I was unable to determine if that meant anything because no gifting and their dialogue didn't seem to change.Speaking of dialogue, I hope you're ready to hear the same lines out of every character. Everyone seems to have the same rotating lines about it being spring and the 5-minute "clear some thorns" quest I did 3 hours ago. The game seems aware of how bland its own speech is, relegating conversations to the bottom of the screen as low contrast italicized text that your eyes skim right past. Compared to the eye catching text for item descriptions, quests, and shopping interface - the game knows how to make standout UI and they also knew that interacting with people was the least interesting thing you would be doing.I have some additional complaints about specific mechanical choices, but those reflect my preferences in the genre rather than shortcomings of the game itself. I prefer planting directly in the ground rather than needing to construct a plot to plant in. They use the system where how you decorate your house affects your stats, but don't have a lot of decorating options. There seems to be no penalty for staying out late and getting teleported back.In summary: if FaeFarm had shown up around the time Stardew Valley did, in front of an audience hungry for farm sims on PC, it would have knocked it out of the park. But in 2023, it's only the sim of the month and can easily be skipped past by those who want to feel like part of the community.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give my opinion on Fae Farm after playing daily for the past week and how it compares (in my opinion) to other cozy games (ex. Coral Island, Stardew Valley). Fae Farm's UI design is a standout feature, seamlessly integrating its tools, menus, and map into the game's visual style. The result is a beautifully cohesive and immersive experience. Coral Island, still in early access, shows promise but feels unfinished. Stardew Valley, known for its stunning visual and UI design, sets a high standard. Fae Farm, in particular, excels in creating a magical atmosphere, complete with enchanting 'Fae' creatures that require upgraded tools to catch. This attention to detail enhances the overall enjoyment of the game.After getting the hang of the menu controls, navigating through NPC dialogues, shop menus, and storage was a breeze. The tool swapping mechanic (mouse wheel) in this game stands out as one of the smoothest I've ever experienced; it makes other games like Stardew Valley and Coral Island seem somewhat clunky and less polished by comparison. The automatic tool selection when collecting resources is an absolute joy. In games where resource management becomes overwhelming (I'm looking at you, Stardew), the experience can sometimes feel less cozy and more taxing.For me, Fae Farm is an absolute blast because my character enjoys a remarkable degree of freedom and agility. Swimming doesn't deplete stamina, and the jumping height is quite impressive. The sheer joy of running off cliffs, leaping from bridges, and swimming without constraints is truly unparalleled. Even Animal Crossing: New Horizons doesn't quite offer that level of liberation.Stardew Valley's 2D pixel art style, while charming, does impose certain limitations. Meanwhile, Coral Island's demanding graphics and CPU requirements can result in frequent lag, freezing, and slow texture loading, turning the simple act of movement into a somewhat nerve-wracking experience. In comparison, Fae Farm manages to strike a unique balance, delivering a more focused and refined experience reminiscent of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild.Among all the cozy games I've had the pleasure of playing, Fae Farm boasts one of the most enchanting soundtracks. It seamlessly complements the game's theme, and the music that accompanies your descent into a dungeon floor teeming with enemies? A solid 10/10, would listen again. While musical taste is subjective, I find Fae Farm's music to be one of the very few where I truly sat back and savored the melodies.Despite its shorter days and faster time, offers what feels like a swifter progression. In just 6 hours of gameplay, I've managed to upgrade my tools to copper and enhance my net and fishing rod once. Fae Farm adopts a chapter-based storytelling approach, and upon completing each chapter, it treats you to a delightful animation. This adds a tangible sense of accomplishment, making you feel like you're truly advancing in the game. The animations themselves are not only enjoyable but also carry a charming, sparkly, and satisfying touch. The game employs a similar animation style when you successfully complete quests. Fae Farm strikes a balance between a brisk pace that keeps players engaged and a deliberate one that ensures every step of progression feels well-earned.It's definitely worth trying out if you have the budget for it.

_childDocuments_.review: *I received this game key for free through KeyMailer*Update after 30hours of gameplay:- ok so there ARE other seed types that ARE season specific, but you have to use a certain kind of fertilizer to increase odds of spawning them - then you can make seeds from the crops. This is not super obvious, but I concede I am bad at reading tutorials.- Fae finally appear after clearing the first mine, and then everyone acts like its normal for winged people to be walking around, even though according to lore, the townspeople *shouldn't* know fae exist. - map is deceptively bigger but I won't spoil that for you.I still think its overpriced, I would compare quality to that of Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town. IMO go for Sun Haven instead of this.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Gutted, absolutely gutted. (td;lr, overpriced, plays like it is in early access or a basic phone game.)Build Mode: Pros: You can move around your crops to redecorate without ruining their growth state; you can reclaim the full materials used on a piece of decor or machine if you change your mind; you can rotate most machines and furniture objects; the cozy rating is a cute and unique mechanic.Cons: Build mode is based on where your character is standing, which can make moving and placing objects an incredibly irritating experience; the short keys are not intuitive, and clunky. I am constantly exiting out of “construction” on accident. The cozy rating is hard to increase because so few items count towards the score.Character design:Pros: I love the diverse options, not just in hair but there are 4 gender neutral body types to choose from. I think the art style is cute.Cons: You don't name your character unless you register BEFORE starting a new game, so it uses your steam username?? No warning that this happens eitherFarming:Pros: there is a flower breeding system similar to ACNH that seems the perfect level of difficulty. The animals and livestock are so CUTE OH MAN, they have a unique design and can follow you around if you want, so my chicken thing comes EVERYWHERE (that it is able to route lol).Cons: At the end of spring, my crops died and I was told to go buy summer ones - only the same 3 seeds were available and state that they can be grown ANY season??? Then why do they die??? Why are there only like 6 crops to grow in total?General:Pros: The game auto uses whatever tool is required for the basic controls, meaning you only have to cycle through 4 and you won't accidentally hit your crops with a ax; crafting has a queue so you can have a bunch of items going while you run around the map; teleport system is the perfect difficulty to unlock. JUMPING! I love open world games that allow you to jump up on buildings and explore, and this game definitely offers that. I love no fall damage, lol. Mining offers the ability to teleport to other levels if you craft specific items that you can get early game, which makes mining less of a headache. The “enemies” have a unique design and fun descriptions in your almanac. Cons: CONSTANT NOTIFICATIONS, anytime you learn a new material, EVERYTHING that you could possibly craft appears on the side of the screen. Tips for things like mining are collapsible but are always there. When you discover new items, you have to physically go look in the almanac and hover over everything to get rid of the lil exclamation point. The controls are so bad oh my god. aiming is USUALLY spot on, but it's unreliable to try to jump to dodge in combat, I constantly accidentally end interactions with npc. speaking of npc's: I was so excited with how many npc's i was coming across, only to figure out that you can only romance 6 of them (3 of which you don't meet until you find the fae, see below), and the romance-able ones are the only people you can give gifts to. They still include a calendar with NPC birthdays, but you can't give them a gift???? There are festivals but they don't do anything?? You get a quest from the mayor to HELP, and then the day of you can buy some decor. No festival.There were multiple obvious typos in early dialogue with the mayor - arguably the most important npc. The merchants are glued to their stalls and can't befriend. They don't even really sell goods except for the gardening npcs (3??), you can buy decor items/recipes if you bring all the materials to them. But for example, the "general goods" literally sells decor and upgrades your backpack. That's it. There is a “bookstore” - you can’t buy books, but you can buy wallpaper that LOOKS like books (if you have unlocked the materials). I haven’t met a single fae. They appear in my relationships tab - I can see who I will meet at SOME point. The mayor referred to one of them early in our conversations. But other than that there are no references, clues, hints, nada. It’s in the title, it should be an early game feature. As of right now, I think it is incredibly overpriced, and plays like it is early access. NONE of their competitors price this high, and are more in depth with less bugs. Palia offers the same amount of gameplay, for free. Coral Island is early access and offers more npc relationships and slightly more gameplay. Stardew is 6 yrs old, more in depth characters, and still getting free content that massively expands the gameplay. I have played nearly every “cozy” game on the market for my stream content, but I dont think this is one I will reach for to stream unless/until they add more and streamline the controls. I would wait for at least 50%, unfortunately 🙁

_childDocuments_.review: It's not worth the price at the moment but it's not a terrible waste of time as is - it's just shallow.There are four farms you unlock as you progress. The first three farms have their own barn where you can host two set animals. You cannot mix the animals nor can you move the barns. So plan to teleport to three separate farms a day to collect mats. Crops are annoying - you buy 5 basic seed types - then use a fertilizer to change them to a special crop that ties to the season - or a fae version later on. There is little reason to manage this. The flower breeding is required as you'll have to mix 5 different colors/flowers into different colored versions of each flower as certain flowers are tied to how you'll change the colors of your clothes and buy new clothing/dyes. This is needlessly tedious.The decorations are also tied directly to your stats - if you want more health, you'll have to build all the cozy items - ect for magic and stamina. These items are from a small pool and don't mesh well. It's a way to force you to make each item and toss them into one of the four farms. Finishing the game and then trying to decorate is actually what made me stop playing and left a bad taste.It's not the game I saw being advertised and it's a little upsetting seeing in the promo art that all the barn animals are mixed together since it's impossible in game.

_childDocuments_.review: Having a lot of fun with this, solo and as a co-op pair. There's a bunch of quality of life improvements over similar games such as automatic use of the appropriate tool, the ability to jump and swim to shortcut trips across town, being able to drop items into storage and craft from storage, etc. The game days feel exceptionally short, but this isn't too much of an issue for me. Would I increase the day length if I could? Probably. Will it stop me playing the game? No.Not overly far into the game but the mechanics seem to be smooth and the game runs really well. The range of romance options is fairly limited. This matters less when considering that most of the NPCs are lifeless and void of much actual personality. The writing and individuality of the characters doesn't really hold up to some of the competitors (Stardew, Rune Factory, 	Wylde Flowers, etc.)If you're in this for the gameplay loops (farming, cooking, mining), this is smooth and the QoL additions make it more satisfying to play. _childDocuments_.review: This is hard for me to give a thumbs up, but I don't think it fully deserves a thumbs down. As MANY people say: Steam needs a better review system. It's an overpriced collection game (where you literally just collect everything with little to no purpose). The selling point is the cute graphics and fun traversal. After you forget the oh, so forgettable story, you realize you are grinding your way only to fill your almanac and get achievements. All this with a bag of bugs that only get worse as they "fix" it. - when collecting things, planting things, bouncing on mushrooms, etc, it's great. HOWEVER, when you run out of water in your can, it makes the WORST noise possible. (A horrible metal squeak.) Also the character "voices" are horribly annoying and pitchy. -The jumping, collecting, fishing, crops, fighting are all fun and the game can be VERY addictive, especially if you like to hoard in games. They've taken a terrific step with QOL improvements many other games should take. I LOVE the 3D design as I'm getting pretty tired of the pixel art and "retro" game looks. (I'll always be a Stardew fan though.) I lived through "retro" games from the end of Atari , early Mac, first Nintendo, up to now. I'm glad to have something not "retro" and I love the little world they created. Unfortunately, the second and third dungeons are too annoying, with platforming and resources spread out. In the story there's talk of doing something about the dungeon enemies, but nothing happens there (maybe one of the planned DLC?).Then there's the things that are there just to prolong game-play after the short 30-40 hour storyline.The animals are just another chore. The breeding is annoying, as one job quest achievement is to breed every color of each animal. This means tons of time spent in dungeons for gems (which the story forces you to do also). Then you only have a chance - which seems more rare than not, to get the color you want. The flower breeding is ridiculous and people make full 3 page sheets on which flowers get you which colors.Then you have the tree propagation which takes forever to get the cross breed of trees and you use a TON of bees. And the stupid thing? The game never tells you ANY of this other than your almanac has tree saplings to unlock and you have a propagation hive with zero instructions. Decorating is nice, but the game doesn't pause in single player which really sucks. Color palettes depend on you getting all the breeds of flower colors too.  - The "world" is maybe a little larger in size than of most farm games. There are teleporters which is good. It's easy to learn where items are and get around. Being able to jump is a great plus. It's not overly big and there are reasons to leave your farm. You get multiple farms which is kind of annoying to me.There is NO reason to talk to citizens other than for world and job quests. Friend quests are garbage. You don't learn much of anything about the people. They are flat NPC's with repeated dialog. You have garbage choices for romance. Only the romance-able characters have cut-scenes and they are pretty lacking really. I haven't wanted to marry any of them. This is a HUGE downfall for the game as it makes the world far less interesting.For the price, you get about $1 per story hour or more, depending on how long it takes you to complete the story. The story itself is forgettable and not super unique. The mechanics for completing achievements draws out playtime in a way that can get old fast. However it is still really fun to play as you can do whatever you want. Animals won't die or run off. Crops grow based on how many times they are watered. Though ALL crops die at the turn of the season, even non-seasonal crops or crops in seasonal beds. This is just stupid. They fixed a ton of the worst bugs after the first 2 or so weeks, when most everyone already finished the story. There are still some annoying bugs, but mostly it's fine for new players. I don't really care for the devs and that makes another negative point for me. (Discussions and email interactions are my reasons why.)I recommend it to people who don't care about an interesting populated world, but want to do the grind of collecting and jumping around and other "cozy" things. I don't play mulitplayer so I can't comment there. If you're looking for a newer farm game with interesting characters, check out Blue Oak Bridge as I have been loving the little world and the dev is terrific. It's a very small team and they take feedback to heart. Don't bother with Fae Farm if it's interesting people and stories you want.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this? Only if it's on sale, that is. Otherwise at full price I don't think it's worth it. First, let me say that it's very cute game that I had fun playing through the story, seeing what happens next. It's not deep, typically you show up, you do things that people couldn't be bothered to fix, you fix things, yaaaaay you're hero blah blah. What I like about it that it feels like mixture of Animal Crossing and Story of Seasons; especially when it comes to catching bugs and fishing. That being said as farming game I don't... really want to play this mainly as farming game, I think it was too bothersome. Since you can only sell up to 8 items per table - how the game handles it instead of shipping bins, there's tables at middle of town centre and as time goes on you can unlock product stands for your farms (yes you can have up to 4 farms, though one is basically next to first one) and what's worse is that you can only sell ONE of said item. You have 50+ of veggie you just harvested from hard work? Well, you can't just put 50 of them on one slot. It's *one* item per slot, no exceptions. Getting milk and wool from this game's cows and sheep is so slow, at first it's very cute but as time goes on it can wear you down - and there's no option for extra barn/coop/whatever so you get what you get given. Relationships are just whatever. Everyone says same thing, they're celebrating the fact you did VERY FIRST thing you did in the game, sometimes treating you as if you're new citizen to the area even on Year 2,  and when there are "friend quests" they're basically just... boring, all reward you get is friendship boost which doesn't really change much at all.Romance is rubbish, I will be frank. Before marriage it was cute, short date conversations but once married all they did was being in your way when you're trying to do farm way (I had mine sitting on my crops when eating picnic... I couldn't water or whatever lol) and they don't get mad if you ignore them, and if you talk to them they talk to you without anything too different. So yeah, unless  you want achievement for getting married, save your 10,000 moneys. It's not worth it.There are quite good amount of bugs, like in barn (where cows and sheep are) there's really weird graphical error on floor where it flickers a lot. Hurts my eye, it doesn't happen every session - sometimes, it's fine. But more often than not it's there.Multiplayer is, well, let's be frank, is very disappointing. I bought this with intention of playing with a friend only to learn that there's no text chat - just emotes and pre-made messages. I guess they thought we'd just use voice chat but the thing is?I am deaf. I cannot Voice Chat. Both of us agreed to just play this as singleplayer game. So yeah, as far as farming games I think it's my least favourite. But I treated it as cute small adventuring game and I was having fun, thought it was good enough for price I paid at. Full price though I cannot recommend, so get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on my Switch for my birthday this year. I loved it enough that I bought it here on Steam so I can play it on both of my main gaming systems. The graphics are beautiful, the music is super relaxing. Signing up for multiplayer is a very quick and easy thing to do, and makes the game 100x more fun when playing with a friend. Solo and multiplayer are amazing. Sure, sometimes it freaks out a little when it's saving or loading a new area and takes a few more seconds. And if you're someone that needs to stick to the main story quest... well, don't. It's a very easy to understand game that doesn't hold your hand too much and lets you do things at your own pace. 120/10, definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: as someone who plays nothing but indie horror games, this game is the perfect inbetween to help lower my anxiety and decrease that build up of numbness you get inbetween playing so many horror games for so long. This game is really fantastic. I was going into it thinking it would be just a cutesy game I could let my gf play but it really ended up being so much fun. for the genre it is placing itself in I could definitely rate it a 10/10 cause it has pretty much everything you could need out of a cozy game.- they/them pronouns to include more people- expansive decoration and clothing options to be who you truly want to be- changing seasons to break up the repetitive farming because most items you harvest will be seasonal and require changing your go to recipes every season. - a pretty heavy grind, but if you have friends it can easily become light work. I however personally don't have friends but I'm lucky enough to really love games that make me grind so it works for me- everything is just really cute from the animals and being able to pet them to the critters roaming around even to the simple animations of sitting down- there is an amazing balance of different things you can do dependent on how you like to play. you can explore a dungeon if you're into combat and fight creatures to get to the rare resources or you can sit at home brushing sheep to get wool and making decorations for the house or go around town building friendships and even romances with the right people- there is too much to do (and i mean this in a good way) im the type of person to get bored of one thing easily and switch to something else and this game has that in spades. there are so many different tasks, daily quests, things that you can do that make it really hard to want to log off for me because i want to do them all!As great as any game can be every game has some faults and here are some changes I would like to see- I would like to see bigger magic radius for the watering can upon new tiers (i'm only at fayrite so it might already do this once I get to silver so idk) but for a game that centers around farming its pretty hard to farm without it feeling really repetitive (if you're building big plots of farming land like me.- i've recently gotten to the 2nd dungeon and the requirement of a potion to even be inside is a little hindering as it relies on rng of the correct critters spawning (which i have gone a full in game day of running around the fay area to never find the critters i need to make the potions) - there isn't really a tutorial for cross breeding flowers so you're kinda just forced into guessing- food doesn't restore as much energy as it honestly should. i find myself in the dungeon having to eat practically 10 meals to sustain my venture. which when you sell your valuable findings you have to spend that money you made on food again unless you dedicate a full day or 2 to mass cooking.i love this game i do. i find myself always coming back and playing it to destress and relax. its a perfect game to be all cozy to and nothing feels too overwhelming because nothing is forcing you to do anything. you dont have to cook meals to do things you can just sleep and continue the next day full on stam and magic again. You dont have to pet your animals everyday they will be fine. You dont have to do friendship quests everyday to remain friends with people. everything is at your won pace and thats what makes the game so relaxing and fun to play

_childDocuments_.review: I've been seeing a lot of negativity in the reviews and patch comments.  The game is brand new and yes, it has flaws, but that's what the dev team is clearly trying to address.  Concerns and suggestions for the game's future are absolutely valid, but this is still a beautifully made game that has a TON of potential.My current criticisms with Fae Farm involve the uncertainty or inconsistency in character progression, the length of the days, and quest objectives that we haven't yet encountered or that disappear the next day.  I mentioned this in the latest patch discussion as well, but I figured I would go ahead and put in my 40-hour review.Two things I think would INSTANTLY make the game feel better:1. Remove the time limit for the day.  Just let the day progress from morning until night and have it stay night until the player chooses to go to sleep and advance to the next day.  So many items are date-gated anyway (including plants, flowers, animal drops, and several major story quests) that players will be forced to sleep regardless.  Along with this, disassociate crafting from the clock advancing and instead apply a flat crafting timer to the various activities (10 seconds, 30 seconds, etc.).2. Block Quest objectives that the player has not yet crafted, doesn't yet have the equipment to make, or doesn't have the equipment necessary to capture (I'm looking at you, fishing poles and nets).  Yes, that means it may seem a little sparse on side quests early game, but it'll feel a lot more like "I learned how to make/catch/grow this new thing, look at all the folks who want it!" than "What the heck are they even asking for? I've never seen this!"  Another alternative would be to make the almanac more instructional or make it clear that the almanac has player guidance.  When the game starts it feels more like a collection journal than anything even though it contains some pretty valuable information.There are plenty of other things that could improve QOL (like significantly improving relationship progression and depth, removing the link between the action cooldown and the animation [which makes catching some creatures an absolute pain] or reducing the number of menus we have to go through to collect items), but the above are the two big things that I think could help the most players the fastest.The foundation is there, I'm excited to see what opens next for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy for a single player experience. The NPC's have no soul. They are all boring clones of each other. This really makes the world feel dead and bland. The dates are all the same with every character. All you do is sit on a log and listen to them ramble on about their one and only personality trait. The NPC's really need a total rewrite and I think they would benefit from having portraits with emotions displayed next to the text. As it stands they just  dump a wall of text on you. They never visit your farm, they never approach you of their own accord. They never give you gifts. They just ignore you entirely. The 'festivals' are also a joke. They don't do anything. No mini-games, nothing. You might be given a quest to go craft something, that's about it. The world feels utterly dead and static. Outside of the boring NPC's the game is serviceable. I have found the best way to enjoy the game is through multiplayer. But not everyone has that luxury. In multiplayer I can focus on making a pretty looking farm as I have way more resources to work with and don't need to grind so much. Multiplayer does have some minor annoying bugs that occasionally require me to save and reset the world. Tool-tips not showing up (or getting stuck on the screen and never goign away!), not being able to talk to npcs, being unable to collect items from the ground etc. The combat, unsurprisingly, is awful and very simple. There are no bosses to fight. There is no challenge. Enemies are just a time sink to annoy you when you want to mine a particular ore. The dungeons themselves are boring as well. Randomly generated rooms with resources and a handful of mobs. Thats it, and then you repeat it 25 times. I would avoid the game and get something like Rune Factory instead. At least for now.
