_childDocuments_.review: These cozy farm sims are a known quantity by now, but how often do they have an unlockable double jump? Fae Farms farming and relationship-building mechanics pull from the usual suspects in the cozy gaming pantheon, but it’s the emphasis on character-level powerups and progression that give the game its own unique flair. A lifeless cast with repetitive and boring personalities prevents Fae Farm from entering that pantheon itself, but some smart convenience features, a beautiful presentation, and simple unlocks ensure that it’s always a breezy and enjoyable adventure–even if it’s never an essential one.You know the drill by now: you find yourself in a small, self-sustaining pastoral town with an unkempt plot and dreams of romance in your heart. You introduce yourself to all of the patronizingly welcoming villagers and learn what function they’ll serve in your farming, and then it’s time for some labor.You’ll notice a few things on your first lap through the routine, most interestingly is a simplification of the farm laboring processes themselves. The starting farm and the trees, stumps, rocks, and weeds choking it of life don’t demand any inventory swapping to remove their presence. Through the magic of context sensitivity, clicking the X button will just auto-swap to whatever the correct tool for the job is, expend a little of your stamina bar, and then the jobs done.It’s an input-level pleasantness that you’ll quickly notice is a game-wide design mantra: a conscious effort Fae Farm is taking to never fight you. Getting low on stamina won’t require that you open up your inventory and select which food you want to eat, you’ll instead get a pop-up that presents you with whatever relevant meal you’re carrying with you and a single press will do the job. All the crafting tables can source material not just from your inventory but your storage box too, so you can just empty your pockets into the endless bounds of your storage unit and they’ll be accessible to you when you need them.You can’t even really fail any of your animals: completely ignore your chickens for a week and you’ll just miss out on a week's worth of eggs, you can pick right back up where you left off if you start petting and feeding them again whenever you want.It’s welcoming and simple, it de-emphasizes some of the actual minutiae of farm maintenance and frees you up for some of Fae Farms other pursuits: exploring, fighting, and fulfilling quests for your fellow villagers.Fae Farm is a very quest heavy game: its a game of discrete objectives and increased efficiency in completing them. One of the earliest long-term mainline quests is a multi-day plunge into the 25 levels of a nearby mine to discover a secret at the bottom. A combination of transporters, more powerful pickaxes, and stamina-sustaining food is required to complete this dive in any reasonable amount of time, and the impact of that progression is tangible. On my third tier of pickaxe, upgraded with materials acquired from prior delves, I got a magic strike that mined a small area at once–a marked improvement from needing to chip away at nodes individually.Everything feeds into and out of crafting. Even the Tom Nook types in town don’t just sell items for cash: they’re often selling recipes that demand you come with some of the materials yourself.The good news is that this process is hypnotic. You find yourself rolling into these progression snowballs, where gathering materials lets you upgrade to get better materials to get better upgrades. It even ties the decoration of your home into a systems-level increase in power: upping the ‘coziness’ of your home (that’s literally what the stat is called), gives you more stamina, health, or mana which aids you in your gathering and you can see where this is going. It’s telling that one of my strongest lingering memories coming off of Fae Farm is its quest completion sound: a soft chime that evokes the game's comfy atmosphere and its small tinge of magic.But maybe it's a little bit concerning that my primary motivations were so… transactional. The town itself and some of the tangential towns that splinter off of it are beautiful, but their inhabitants suffer from a little same-face and a little same-personality. A lot of the secondary NPCs cycle through the same simple dialogues and even the primary NPCs like the romance options and major merchants have the same put-on soft-niceness just sprinkled with whatever their singular personality quirk or interest is.It makes the progression of the meters that correspond to the relationships far more interesting and fun than engaging with the relationships themselves; it gives added meaning to the inclusion of local and online co-op, involving real friends is a handy way to distract from how boring your digital ones are.But even with so central a pillar as friendship being kind of a miss, Fae Farm manages to land a lot of the other aspects associated with the best of these experiences. The delicate sprinkling of magic is a nice touch. There’s delightfully springy mushrooms all over the place that let you jump to high places or just generally glide around. Whenever you’re swimming you do this hilarious little dolphin jump when you press A. When your crafting tables are in gear they get this soft bouncy effect, you can imagine Belle walking around the corner any minute. It’s a carefree and lighthearted world, There’s a hilarious line that introduces your bug net that implies that the insects just love being caught by it: it’s like they’re being absorbed by a friendly cloud.You eventually escalate into more discrete magic with the introduction of some mystical matriachs, and the game grows its wings right around the time you do: giving you a double jump to close long gaps and just kind of floof around town. Magic also lets you be a sprinkler system in and of yourself: the same magic wand you unlock that can aid in combat or progress to new areas can also water your plants, giving you the boon of a farm-sims late-game equipment suite but localized into your character.This also coincides with the introduction of some additional biomes you can explore, with their own inhabitants and dungeons you can fold into your daily routines. The best moments in your routine are oftimes the quietest though: like when you’re fishing and the piano in the background hits just right. It’s all a bit twee, and your fondness for Fae Farm will likely be owed to how much you can be carried by the pleasantry of that tweeness: or the satisfaction you get from checking off checklists.Fae Farm is a pleasant game, both at the aesthetic and gameplay level. Its airy mix of simple systems comes together into crafting and progression that’s greater than the sum of its parts, and it always gently pulls you forward to the next upgrade or area. It’s character-centric and consequence-free approach to farming teases out more of a life-sim than a farm-sim, which will be a pro or con depending on what you’re seeking.But without any memorable characters to ground its world in or any truly new systems to call its own, it ends up being a little forgettable. Fans of cozy games will find a worthy title with Fae Farm, but compared to its inspirations: it's more of a short-term fling than a long-term relationship.

_childDocuments_.review: About 150 hours in and I love the game. I finished the main story and now I'm working on breeding multiple colored animals and organizing all my farm areas I've unlocked. I didn't realize the benefit of the DLC (outside of obtaining the extra achievements in the game) until I realized the trinkets and animals in there help me with so many valuable potions I like to use to make farming and harvesting easier on the day to day basis. My main goal right now is to unlock all the different breeds of flower colors and all the crops and maximize all my houses and decorate like crazy. (I'll soon have a huge flower sea of all colors organized by type and all the cross breed colors)You also can unlock soft and vibrant color palettes for clothing and decor items. No section of the game's map is visited once and that's it. EVERY part of the map has you revisiting because each area has items that you'll need to recreate potions, ingots, polished gems that can be sold for money or used in other recipes to create lavish items. So it's a constant revisit for every inch of Azoria and I think that's what I like the most. The devs also have more to add so I'm excited for more. I get on this game, blink and 6 hours have already flown by. That's how locked in I've become when I open it. This game + music = vibes. I'm also trying to discover all recipes alone, I've only had to search up something in the community hub once involving how to unlock fruit trees because it really was not making sense to me and I was already one year in the game with no luck. All in all,  W farm game, cute art style and lots to do after the main story is finished with so many relationships to build, job quests from sooooo many people (you unlock things at the end of each one) so I will be here for a while. Can't wait for more.Idek when I started to like farm games (I blame Slime Rancher: my first farm love ♥) but this one I recommend to people as well :)I will say in every farm game FISHING is my least favorite part so hopefully it's updated soon to be more efficient, maybe some kind of marker on the map once you've unlocked a type of fish to let you know where they are within a section of the map because right now we only have the main map, but no maps within a map for example there are tons of areas in the Fae Realm once you arrive. These are my thoughts for now but I like it a lot so far.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Just hit 100% achievements but what I love about this game is I still have so much more to do. I'm decorating all 4 of my houses room by room and as I'm unlocking the rest of the recipes in the game and flower colors and color palettes I still don't know how I'm going to do my layouts for all 4 farms. W game. Love it a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this by saying - I do like Fae Farm and will probably play it a decent amount. That said, I just cannot recommend this game. It feels like a soulless simulacrum of farming games.First and foremost, the game should be called Fae Mine instead - all story progression is tied to traversing the mines, with the titular farming mechanics being an afterthought at best. As far as I've been able to tell, the mines are also the best profit potential. The gameplay loop from tier to tier is almost exactly the same.The game has a lot of fun mechanics that lack any depth whatsoever. There's no perks or major bonuses to levelling skills, just minor chance increases. There's basically no benefit to increasing relationship with villagers. There is a tiny amount of variance with regards to cookable food, with most foods just providing the same base 50 energy. This tiny variance also means that farming doesn't matter much - beyond collecting crops for quests, there's no real reason to farm much.For $40, this game feels like an EA title, and it's almost disappointing that it's not, because it feels like more depth won't be coming. If all you want is a cozy farming game and you like the mines in other farming sims, then you may still like the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Stardew Valley, Archevale, Dinkum, etc, then Fae Farm would 100% be fore you. I would say that this would have to be my favorite of all of those games combined (Though I have a ton of hours on Stardew Valley). The graphics, music, mechanics, etc have all been very fun. HOWEVER, If you are looking for a muliplayer player game, BEWARE this game is just stock full of bugs. I honestly don't understand how they show of this game with 4 players. I let my fiance' host the game and let me share some of the bugs we have experienced in our last 20 hours of game time together (Please note that some of these things happen on occasion and not every time we play)- No sound when mining , fishing, planting, etc. (on occasion)- Quest/New season screens get stuck on the screen- Non Host players tend to not see the host walking around at all- Non Host players tend to warp around randomly- Players that log in mid day sometimes start with 1/2 mana, energy and health- Entering the mines for the first time every day causes the basic panning screen video (very annoying)- Ore and stuff in the mine sometimes disappears but you can still mine it completely- There have been times where I have joined and don't have the same things in my inventory as when I logged off- Sometimes the fish are not visible, but you can tell something is there b/c of the twinkling star showing the rarityOf course this is not everything that we have experienced. And sure it may not sound that bad, but when it happens almost every day or every other day , it gets extremely annoying. However, my fiance' and I both love the game so we will continue to play through the garbage bugs that seem to not be getting fixed yet. But if you are looking for a fun SINGLE player farming sim game, this is 100% for you. And I don't see problem with the price of the game or anything as I have paid a lot more for a lot less content.

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically an easier version of Stardew Valley. Unfortunately it's also a less developed version of Stardew Valley when it comes to the NPCs which are a major let down. You cannot befriend the majority of them. Their birthdays are shown in the calendar but it's meaningless information as you can only give gifts to the marriage candidates. Regarding the marriage candidates, to start off you are forced to romance them. If you build a friendship with them it will automatically become a romantic one no matter what. Since your relationship with them is solely defined by your romantic relationship to them once you get engaged all the other candidates might as well cease to exist. Your relationship gets locked in place depending on how far you had advanced and instead of a friendship they are now a "lost love", "past sweetheart", "past flirt", or if you hadn't advanced very far with them, a "stranger". You can talk to them but they no longer accept gifts or offer quests. They're just waiting in the wings in case you decide to reset your relationship with your spouse. There's also a lot of thoughtlessness to quest dialogue with NPCs you've interacted with several times introducing themselves or proclaiming they haven't seen you in days despite you interacting with them every day.tl;dr if you want a less stressful version of Stardew Valley and don't care about NPC relationships you'll probably enjoy this game. If the NPC relationships are something you enjoy you won't enjoy Fae Farm.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game that gets fishing right! Fae Farm is an adorable farm/adventure sim with lots of cute animals, people, and scenery. Each area you unlock is unique and adds not only fun new places to explore, but also critters, foliage, and resources to gather. With dynamic weather and seasons, dungeons to explore, and friends and romances to cultivate, this cute farm sim gives you plenty to do. It's a little grindy (but what farm sim isn't). A couple of things that took me by surprise, was that fact that though you can romance, then marry anyone of the suitable candidates, once they are your spouse, they become absolutely useless. Considering you do get multiple farms and animals, which becomes time consuming, it would be nice if your lazy spouse could help out with the daily chores, be it taking care of the animals, or watering the crops. The devs are suppose to be releasing new content in the coming year, so hopefully this issue will be addressed, otherwise, there is no point of getting hitched in Fae Farm.  My second beef, which is a small one, is when you are in pause, the countdown for your potions should be paused too. Also, when working a machine or table, time should also be paused there as well, as it can take a lot of time when dealing with the seed table, the prep table, etc., and time is precious. All in all, I found Fae Farm to be a cozy and enjoyable farm sim and look forward to the new content the developers are looking to release.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, and it's not inherently bad, but it is just not worth the £30 asking price. Fae Farm is the bare bones of a fantasy farming sim, with some sinew tying it all together. It's got everything you would expect, with growing crops, caring for animals, catching bugs, fishing, mining, and some basic combat, with a fantasy-like twist with some minor spells and potion brewing...and that's it.This game feels like the dev team wanted to do a Stardew Valley but Magic, yet this was their first foray into the genre. The skeleton of what a farming game is here with the magical twist, but there's nothing else - it feels like a first attempt. Farming mechanics are basic, though the crop system is needlessly complicated. Simply: you have access to 3 basic seeds to begin: beans, turnips and cauliflower (you gain 3 more later as your farming level increases). From these base seeds you get your other crops using magic compost, which has a chance of turning the crop its placed on into the seasonal variety (or the fae variety if place in the fae world that you get access to later). You can make seeds of these new crops later, but it seems such a needless faff when you could have just sold these crop seeds seasonally like every other farming game does. I understand the fae crops like the frost turnip needing the magic compost, but why do I need magic compost on top of turnips in order to grow carrots in spring? It feels like needless faff that's just wasting my time.Caring for animals is very basic and laughably easy to exploit - the only things animals care about is being fed. Pet them up to their max happiness when you first get them and then just feed them. There's no grading of crops and products, so there's no need to care about letting your animals out for the 'time outside' bar. It seems very cold to say it, but the way time runs in this game you'll appreciate the time saved.I reckon this is probably stemming from the multiplayer aspect of Fae Farm, but there are very few moments where time will pause, which is very annoying when you're trying to think about what to do. All but sitting in the Esc or item menu causes the day to tick along, and it's relatively fast, too. It's probably a relief then that the penalty for not going to bed before midnight is pretty light, but with few opportunities to just sit and *think* for a bit, especially in single player, it means you start cutting corners, like mentioned above. This has the unfortunate side-effect of pulling you out of the game, loosening the immersion.There's relationships in the game, but aside from the veneer of 'this person is nerdy/bookish', 'this person is more adventurous', none of the characters have a personality beyond 'MMO NPC'. Or if they did, I didn't see it. Aside from 'this romance looks nice', I have no memory of any one of them, and they can all be safely ignored, as I don't think there's even a friendship degradation mechanic. They're all pretty cardboard cutouts, and that's fine for the vendors, but romance options need a little more...something? Being memorable at all would be a good start.The magic of Fae Farm that it really touts itself with it is, like the rest of the systems here, basic and painfully underdeveloped. You can brew magic potions that create a magic cloud above your head to automatically water crops, or surround yourself with bees or the necessary 'thing that means I don't instantly pass out in the 2nd of the 3 dungeons in the game', and you get a couple of magic spells from your staff and upgrading your tools. I only ever used 3 tool abilities: the watering can's area of effect watering ability (which makes the rain-cloud potion obsolete immediately unless you've got a large crop field), the sickle's AoE harvest ability or the axe's 'throw axe and it counts as multiple hits of a the tree for a couple of seconds if it's touching it'; the last one I used out of pure curiosity and found it was just easier to cut the tree normally, instead of potentially throwing the axe and missing the tree entirely. The staff magic is more situational, like blowing away dark clouds or activating some torches, and whilst they can be used in combat, it's just easier to smack enemies.Oh yeah, about that. Dungeons are where this game's charm rubs off, and where its controls, especially with keyboard and mouse (which I used) are at their worst. The amount of times I would be in the middle of an attack animation, miss my target and be left helpless was dangerously high. You can get hit multiple times in a row that will quickly whittle your health down, ESPECIALLY in the Floating Ruins dungeon where multiple statues can land on you, throwing you around and trapping you in the 'ouch I'm hurt' animation. Be aware that even if the time says 'paused' when you bring up the menu in a dungeon, the rest of the game is not, and your potions effects will still tick away (which sucks in the Floating Ruins since you always need a potion effect up to not pass out) and enemies will still attack you and kick your health down, which can be highly frustrating at times.Fiddly mouse controls also spill over into the main game too - have fun when your animals stack on top of one another, and when you're trying to pet the one your mouse is hovered over but no! Actually you'll pet the other one you've just pet because I guess the game wanted to do that instead. Most egregious currently is the trough in the animal pen for the cow/sheep - your mouse has to be in a specific position on the left side for it to activate; enjoy the slow waving you need to do to find out where though, it's never where you expect.The story, for what I experienced before I tapped out, isn't really anything write home about. People and magical creatures have problems to solve, so you go and solve them. There's nothing offensive here and everything is rather sweet, so if you just want the story equivalent of a little sweet treat, then it's here for you.You could be forgiven for forgetting that I said I liked this game at the opening of this review after this deluge on complaints - it's because there's *heart* in this game. This feels like a first draft - they have the main structure here with the basic elements, but there's no flesh on these bones, only the barest of connective tissue and sinew with the magic bits (and in my opinion, needlessly so with crops, that aspect feels shoe-horned in). It feels like it needs to grow into the £30 asking price. Right now, I'd recommend waiting for more content for this game, and or for a sale to drop its price to something more in the £15 range.There's a gem in the rough here, but right now it's unfortunately more stone than gem.

_childDocuments_.review: I've now played this game for 40 hours, and I still can't decide if I would recommend it or not. The good:The game play itself feels nice. Movement and the environments feel nice. The double jump after you get wings is amazing and I love that so much. The fast travel system is neat. I like crafting the seals to create fast travel portals and the placements for them feel fine.The animals are cute. I love that you can breed different colors of animals.The farming is fun. I like that you mutate crops to find seasonal varieties. The dungeon journal/travel system. Really neat that you can craft seals to teleport directly to certain floors, and I like that the journal will tell you what you'll find on floors once you visit them and how likely you are to see specific nodes.Flower mutations. Lol, I've probably wasted a whole in-game month at this point to flower mutations for the wings, and I'm not upset by it.Love that you can craft multiple things at a single crafting station! Seriously so good. I can make a handful of different ingots at the same time without having to wait for the current one to be done/build another smelter.The bad:The relationships. I play farm sim games for the relationship aspect. The characters felt SO flat, you only have until the end of the day to do friendship/relationship quests, so there was a lot of pressure to do those and I didn't like that/rarely accepted them. There's no reward for leveling up friendship/romance with the characters from what I can tell. Limited romance options (♥♥♥♥ Argyle and whomever made him a dateable character too. How do you have Argyle, a literal child who builds sand castles and blows bubbles on the beach, and Jack, an sensitive, grown ass mountain man, be marriage-able characters in the same game? Feels gross.) Once you get married, which is also an expensive scam, you can no longer get any relationship/friendship with your previously dateable characters. There's no benefit to getting married, your spouse literally does nothing nor gets any special dialogue, so that's a 10k gold thing I did solely for the achievement.Fishing. This is literally the worst skill in the game, and I haven't even gotten past skill level 5 because I hate it so much. The fishing is tedious, it takes forever to reel fish in, and buying upgraded fishing rods/bug nets don't even help you capture low level fish/bugs easier? Wtf? It only makes it accessible to catching more difficult fish/bugs, but you're still going to spend a good minute trying to reel in a fish or 5 swings of your net to get the medium difficulty bugs. When you upgrade your gathering tools, they make lower level stuff super easy to get with a single swing or two, why are bugs and fish not like this too? Awful.Combat. I'm still mid on this, but I think leaning towards a negative. Combat itself is fine, almost on the fun side. The animation lock during your attacks is painful.Dungeons. I'm fine with mines, but along with the tedious combat, I hate that I still need potions to visit the dungeons. I still need miasma/heat resistant potions even after clearing them. Also, the last dungeon? Horrible. The only way I pushed through was crafting seals ahead of time and unlocking the floors that way. No way in hell am I going to farm all the nodes in the hopes this sprite will drop and then complete a timed race to get to its pedestal while enemies are everywhere and the floor is dropping out underneath me. Also, those maps are unnecessarily massive. Also, no matter what I had equipped in my hands (gathering tool or staff), sending me to a new floor will automatically reset it to the gathering tool. The amount of times I've charged into combat to clear the room before gathering, and had my gathering tool equipped when I KNOW I ended the previous floor with my staff? Rage inducing.The bugs. Holy ♥♥♥♥, the bugs. The shipping containers are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrible because once a month, I just can't accept an assignment. I wouldn't care so much, but as someone who is achievement driven and there's one tied into the shipping containers, I'm very annoyed by this. Ran into a VERY annoying bug with the breeding job quest. Literally cannot finish the quest, because the game will not recognize that I've bred a cottontail. Only about half of the animals will give me the announcement at the start of a day when there's a new baby animal born. This is probably where the issue is happening with the quest, but again, with their being an achievement tied to this, I'm absolutely annoyed by this bug. Certain things just don't work right either. There's an animal leasher (I don't remember what it's called), but you place it on your farm and your animals are supposed to stay within that range. Because I'm so tired of trying to pick up my crops, and my stupid chicken runs over and forces me to pet it all the time.Job quests. Overall, I like the concept of it a lot, but it gets a negative because I can only do one job quest at a time. Like, you can only accept one from one person, even though there's like 15 people who have job quests. Why tf can't I accept them all and just have them in my quest log like a normal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game?Speaking of animals. There's literally no reason to level the friendship with them? No higher production for higher stat animals. Friendship doesn't drop if you don't pet/feed/attend them (which I do low key love, plz don't change that), but at least give them a higher output for the max stat/max friendship ones. Give me a reason to actually care about them.I also low key don't love the farms. I forget about my fae land farm for days at a time. I would love to be able to relocate the animal pens all into one location, solely for convenience. I also feel disappointed that the frost farm doesn't even give you frost animals? C'mon, give me a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ penguin knockoff or something. It's been over an in-game month and I haven't even bothered to clear it out that farm and make it use-able. The character models. I streamed this and a friend said the heads look like Lego bobblehead people, and I can't unsee this and hate it now. I LOATHE that my character will have a grimace on its face anytime it's raining. I know I can just drink a tea to fix this for three in-game hours or whatever it is, but why the ♥♥♥♥ do I make this face in the first place? Stop it.This was a lot more long-winded than I intended, and apparently I had more to complain about rather than compliment. And I'm sure there are things I'm missing. Despite all this, I really still can't decide if I'd recommend this game or not, but good ol' Steam is going to force me to make a recommendation. I know during my stream a few friends who were on the fence did decide against the game, so maybe that'll speak for itself. Honestly, just fix the bugs with the quests and I'll be content-ish.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I originally would have wanted to, I can't recommend this game. It's beautiful, the graphics are freaking ADORABLE and so are the sound effects and beginning story-line. When you start out, you think you're in for the BIGGEST faerie-themed treat. But, that's where my compliments about the game kind of end...Setting the hefty price tag aside, there are three reasons why I don't think this is worth buying:1. Lack of customisationAs commendable as the character customisation is in the beginning, I've played for nearly 20 hours and haven't been able to find a single cute outfit for my character. Same for house furniture. The options are so limited and colouring your objects seems to be possible much later, to the point where I'm not even motivated to do it anymore. I just want to not wear my starting outfit for a month in a row and actually have more than 5 pieces of starting furniture in my house. Is that too much to ask?2. Co-op problemsWhen you're playing with a partner, unfortunately it's bugs galore. My partner has a male character but the game forces this high-pitch voice on him no matter how many times we try to fix it and it's just weird, plus, even if we had no wings equipped we could still 'fly' or double jump (I think that one's fixed now). Lots of small things around town wouldn't work 100% correctly and it kept becoming a bit annoying.3. NPCs are just so bland The NPCs in this game really want you to know they are NPCs. They have like one dialogue and no depth, we couldn't find a way to actually become friends apart from gifting them a highly specific thing, which when starting the game, you're like "What even is that?" and it just feels pointless to talk to them. The sellers also have even less personality.Don't get me wrong, there are some details I like about the game. No need for chests? Fantasy ranch animals? Faerie aesthetic? All great. But there's no point to all this when the only way I can think of describing Fae Farm is "a boring book with a really, really pretty cover".

_childDocuments_.review: My partner and I picked up Fae Farm as an alternative to Stardew Valley, which I have played to death. This review is made with a history of playing Stardew.Pros:- character creation is simple yet detailed enough and with a decent amount of (some unconventional) options, you can have heterochromia, be mute, and choose your pronouns, and if you change your mind later you can change it pretty easily- tool selection is (mostly) automated, most gathering tools are selected based on what you're targeting, with the exception of the bug net, fishing rod, and magic staff- the start of the game is a lot of fun, running through the first dungeon, getting the first few animals, planting your first crops- you can jump and swim- swimming (and rain) refills your watering can automatically- fishing is pretty easy (although I found the 'simple' fishing option more confusing)Cons:- cooking, crops, and later dungeons feel a bit lazy, the crops die at the end of each season for no reason since they can be planted in any season, there aren't real seasonal crops, you can create seasonal crops but there's no point because you can't create different food from different crops, while the dungeon designs are fairly interesting, for the most part the enemies look and act the same, and combat isn't much more than hit them with a stick- some enemies are annoying and unavoidable, making combat occasionally more frustrating than fun- there were a lot of lag issues when playing co-op- after the first dungeon is completed, job quests are unlocked, which feels very late for this to be unlocked since the first few quests assume you're just starting out when that isn't the case at this point, so you either have to backtrack to complete them (which is tedious) or just ignore them- our experience was that once friend quests were unlocked we seemed to have a backlog to deal with, with everyone having multiple quests for us the first day, this improved on subsequent days, but the initial level of requests was overwhelming- marriage is incredibly buggy, after we got married there wasn't a day without some sort of issue (time freezing, character unable to move, outfit glitches, etc), also both my partner and I ended up 'spouse' to the people we married even though we married different people- you can only have one each of the coop, barn, etc, which is sad- the amount of items you can sell per day is restricted, which is perplexingWhile it may seem that this is heavily negative, the start of the game was fun enough that I would still recommend giving it a go. Just be aware that the farming element is clearly secondary to the dungeon delving, and the last 2/3 of the game just feel lazy.

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game is the vibe but unfortunately that is where the good stuff ends.I felt like it wasn't taken into consideration what actually makes a farming/ranching simulator fun when they made this game.You can't get to know the merchants or the non-romance-able characters which is over 2/3rds of the NPC in game. You CAN get to know the romance-able NPC by dating them, which if you talk to them at all you end up doing automatically whether or not you want to which also means you can wind up dating the remaining 3rd at the same time which is not my cup of tea nor something I've seen before in games like this. Now if you could also marry more then one person that would be interesting. Outside of the dating cut scenes no one has anything new or different to say from the first time you met them. There are no festivals, mini-games, or work that actually goes into the town or growing relationships. Having these be big themes in games like Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, or Wylde Flowers is what has made them my favorite games in the past so it was a real let down when they were missing in this one. This is probably my biggest complaint.You can make a gem polisher very early on in the game which means it's pointless to farm to make money and there aren't any other reasons to really farm. At least 80% of my time is spent in the mines to progress the game cause that is the only thing to do. For lack of a better way to put it, you can't build up a relationship with your animals either not that it matters because there are no festivals to put them in or golden produce to try to achieve. They CAN follow you around which is cute but they are so slow you out run them immediately making them continuously spawn in which is not so cute. You buy one at a time then run it home and then run back to buy another one which is annoying. You end up having 3 farms and have to manage them in their separate locations which is quite a hassle. It is taking forever for me customize anything. I feel like I am about/over half way through the game and only now can I barely start to customize. It is one of the easiest games I've ever played which is also kind of a let down.While I do have many other complaints you can read those in the other negative reviews.I really like the art style and the over all vibe but honestly I wish much more work was put into this game. I will give props to the fact that you can go by They/Them pronouns though! At $40 I really wish I could get a refund back but I had to be stubborn and stick it out. I would not recommend getting this game for anything over $20. Seriously go get Wylde Flowers instead. Edit: there are 'festivals' on the last day of the season but you have to go into the Mayors house on those days or you will miss it and it isn't much more than a party with some of the towns folk gathered.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the standard version of this game as I wasn't sure if I was going to love it or not (I've made quite a few expensive mistakes in the past and the price did give me pause) and I thought I would buy the DLC as and when it came out rather than upfront. Have I regretted paying full price? Not even for a second!This game is so much addictive fun. There is a detailed and enjoyable story line to follow, besides which you can farm, breed flowers (which I'm loving!), catch critters, fish, craft, design your farm, fulfil quests and more. The only downside is the romance and social side of the game. It is very repetitive and shallow, but I don't mind this as I find some farming sims a little overwhelming when you have 70 plus people you have to keep gifting and speaking to. If you want a deep social and romance side, you will probably be better off buying a different game. I recommend either My Time at titles or Coral Island for that kind of game. The combat in this game isn't too bad either. I suffer with anxiety, so this is something I always worry about in a game. The mines do get harder, but you can craft invisibility potions so jumbles don't see you if you want to avoid it. They do wear off, so make sure you take enough with you. I really appreciate this feature! I do combat in this game, but I can choose when I feel okay to do so and love that I can just go and get materials without having to fight my way through the floors! There is also fast travel through the mines that you can open up and a list of probability for materials on each floor which makes finding what you want so easy. Really lovely addition. There are so many quality of life features from automatic tool selection (no scrolling through tools! I wish more farming games would adopt this) to a great tracker feature on the map and fast travel you can open up for quick movement as you progress. I do see how much love and thought has gone into this game. There is so much quality here, I could go on and on!I know there was a lot of debate about price point on this game. Honestly, I think it's worth the asking price. If I compare it to Story of Seasons titles I have bought that actually cost more, this is way, way better. I got bored in those games really quickly. I can't see me getting bored with this game for a long time to come. I want to complete all crops, flowers etc and will definitely buy the DLC when it comes out. If you are strapped for money, I would put it onto your wish list and wait for a sale to pick it up. If not, what are you waiting for? I hope you have as much fun in it as I do. It is a beautiful, colourful world that just makes a person feel happy. No stress at all. Just a perfect, cosy game that helps you unwind and feel good.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a revolutionary farming sim. It has the same overall mechanics that others do. Same overall plot in the story that they all come with (come to a new land, get a farm bequeathed to you somehow, befriend villagers and sprites, romance). This one has a few things that set it apart though. I know a lot of people complain that the villager back stories are weak, and that just chatting with someone starts a romance relationship. For me this is a plus; the grind to be friends with all the villagers is actually taxing for me. So for me this is a major plus. Same with the animals, by day three they are content and there are no friendship requirements to meet to get higher quality items. I love the tool system. Need an ax? Walk up to a tree and you're holding it. Need your watering can? Ditto. The tools are automatic to your need and they don't take up space in your inventory. You do have to toggle to get to the wand, fishing net, and bug catching net but its easy to do and they also don't take up precious inventory space. Purple bouncing mushrooms. Can't stress enough how much of a quality of life bonus this is. I bounce everywhere for shortcuts. Also, along that thread, the way points in the mines. You can't skip to a level, but if you no longer have to find the key/switch to open the door if you have it activated for that level.If you need to increase your health, stamina, or mana (cause you're a magic user in this farm!) you can decorate your house to add items that will increase these. In games like My Time at Sandrock/Portia it wasn't really needed; in this game it is essential to progress easily!All of the crafting stands are not resource heavy to build, so it is easy to get all of that built up in early game. Early tools and house upgrades are also inexpensive so making advances in the beginning isn't hard. A couple draw backs for me. I do wish mana was better balance. I get that it is designed to take mana potions but I can get hit a ton before having to pop a health potion where mana is gone in a few spells. The teleport system could be better. I feel like its good if your at home for fast travel to mines but otherwise I never use them.  I would have like a system that you could fast travel to a portal from anywhere! There have been bugs (as expected with a new game) but they have not been major bugs. So far I have been able to exit to the title screen and reload to fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been on a bit of a game-buying spree lately, hunting for that perfect cozy escape, and this game has been such a lovely discovery. There’s so much to adore about it. The quality-of-life features are everything you’d wish for in every game—centralized storage that you can access from any crafting machine, plus infinite storage at your base. It just takes away all the little stresses, letting you focus on the fun parts of the game. The story moves along at a perfect pace, never dragging, and you won’t find yourself stuck or frustrated.One of my absolute favorite things is how relaxed it feels compared to games like Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing. In those, you’re constantly worried about missing events, birthdays, or special moments. Here, it feels like you can just breathe and enjoy the experience without FOMO (fear of missing out) looming over you.That being said, I do have a couple of small critiques. Relationships with the villagers seem to develop a bit too quickly. I would love to see more gradual build-up, with moments that let you savor those connections. It would add depth to the village life. In multiplayer, while it’s generally easy to invite a friend, we ran into some confusion with quests. Sometimes they sync up, but other times we weren’t sure if we were on the same page, and the game doesn’t always make that clear.Overall, I picked this game up on sale for around $25, and I think that’s a fair price for what’s offered. At $40, though, I’d hesitate. There’s not quite enough content to justify that higher price point. Still, it’s an adorable, well-executed game that’s exactly what I was looking for in terms of a cozy experience. My only real concern is the price compared to the amount of content, but otherwise, I have no significant complaints.-------When I started seeing hearts I thought I was at max affection. It's not. My comment about building relationships over time is moot. Game did a great job!

_childDocuments_.review: I saw Fae Farm when it got announced as I wanted to play it with my partner as it looked like a cute-cozy-farming sim game. The hype behind Fae Farm was also real at the time so it was really taking off. I left it for a little bit as games were releasing in a really poor state. Decided to pick it up recently for me an my partner and... I am sorry but... some aspects of the game are just... terrible. Below I will state my opinion, any issues I had and what could have been done better, so, let's get to it.⚫The HOUSE STORAGE is a joke to find items. They are sorted alphabetically BUT, finding the item YOU want is a pain because when you hover your mouse over the item in storage it doesn't tell you its name meaning if you do not know what THAT item is or the item you are looking for is, then it just becomes a click fest until you find it. Yes you can press "X" for the "almanac" on the item to see what it is called but that means you have to do it NUMEROUS times before you find YOUR item.⚫Another thing about the HOUSE STORAGE -  There is no SEARCH function to search for a specific item such as potions. Specific food items. e.t.c⚫The NPCS are so boring and poorly written/designed. No personality behind any of them. They are very bland is what I am saying.⚫Another thing about the NPC's. Their "relationships"/"Marriage" quests are all the EXACT same. The same scenes and basically the same dialogue. Me and my partner chose 2 different NPC's to marry and they had the exact same background on all the dating scenes. This completely negated who they were. So for instance if JACK likes outdoors and say  QUINN likes indoor activities, both scenes will still be outdoors making what they like  useless.⚫The animals. Well, one simple, really ANNOYING, FRUSTRATING reason. On your farm, they stand in your way when you go to plant or harvest crops meaning you cannot REACH THE CROP to plant or fertilise or water. Now, the game does not tell you that you can ring the bell outside of the "coop" to make the animals go into it. (if it does, it went over my head. Will amend this if it does). They also can walk through your "fences" that you build.⚫The combat is very.... poor. What I mean by  this is this - You get a "stick" (magic wand/staff) to kill stuff with.  All you do is "left click, left click, left click, left click"  you see the point. You cannot DODGE, ROLL or BLOCK ANY attack. You have to stop attacking, move out of the way to avoid attacks. You do get "magic spells" but right now we only have vortex and it is UTTER garbage.⚫There is a loading screen to enter and exit your house. Also one for entering Croakia (think thats how its spelt), the dungeons + dungeon floors and the Fae realm. So you best get ready to see those screens, A LOT.⚫Going through a teleporter or room, resets what you had in your hand. If you had your BUG net in your hand for instance it will no longer be the "ready-to-equip" tool when you spawn in sometimes making you miss a critter or getting struck by an enemy in a dungeon.⚫You can plant cauliflower, potatoes, turnip, beans, corn and one other crop all year round but at the end of the year they DIE. Why? The developer calls them "SEASONAL CROPS". How is that seasonal? If you use the magic crop swap on them then they should die... not before when it states that they can be planted in A N Y season. ⚫Got stuck with the "feed animal" thing on my screen several times meaning I had to quit and re-log to fix the issue. This has happened over 5 times now and it is getting REALLY frustrating taking care of the animals because of this. Not only can I not use my F ability at all,  it messes with my camera angle and I cannot talk to ANY NPC either.  ⚫The game is really cozy and peaceful⚫The music is nice and chill⚫The art design and game world are absolutely gorgeous in its own way⚫Game would benefit from a "museum" of some kind. Each season has its own unique insects/bugs/critters and It would be really nice to see them on display in a museum. Think... Dinkums museum or Animal Crossings museum.⚫More variety in NPC content would be nice. Like, if they like specific activities/foods/drinks you get scenes with them either drinking/eating or being in those areas they like. This would add an extra layer of "identity" onto the NPC in question.⚫A search option in the house storage or the ability to hover over an object and see its name with your mouse (in your storage)All in all, this game was way to overhyped. Yeah, me and my partner are still going to play it because... well... its a game we can both play together and not stress out on. Sadly, with the lack of "settings" in the game and the NPC's being so boring and bland... it ruins the whole "relationship" aspect of the game entirely. If it was just me and my partner on a little island selling crops and farming with the dungeons and stuff with NO other NPCs then I think the game would have been so much better, in my own opinion of course.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews for games. In fact this is might be my first review ever.Fae Farm seems like a fun game when you first start playing, but its lack of depth and grindy nature reveal themselves after some time. Almost as if devs nowadays realize you must have less than 2 hours of play time to be able to return the game, so the game is just good enough to draw you in past the return window.I agree with a lot of the other negative reviews. The NPCs are boring, and their quests are boring and repetitive. It would be ok if each NPC had a set of unique dialog that they repeated, so each NPC is different at least (as they do in Animal Crossing). In Fae Farm however there is only a limited set of dialog overall for all NPCs which they all repeat. They also all share the same limited set of quests which are all fetch quests.For a game with "farm" in the name, the farming is very limited. You get the same crop seeds every season, and then you must use a 'transformation fertilizer' to transform them into seasonal crops. There are also no sprinklers or other mechanic to automate watering crops, so planting large areas will become tedious even with the watering can upgraded all the way. Especially because to use the AOE water effect you have to expend mana, as it is a spell attached to the can, and not a function of the can itself.Ranching is also shallow, your animals are more like vending machines. After you buy them and get their comfort level up, they will provide you with their item in the morning regardless if you take care of them or not. The animals also frequently get in the way, as the totem pole for gathering them in one spot doesn't seem to work and they wander around and steal focus while you're trying to do other things. The game has NPC ranchers whose animals are shown staying inside a fenced area, but your own animals will walk right through fences. When you end up petting the same animal for the third time instead of watering your crop because it stole focus, you'll want to quit the game too.The most lucrative items in the game are the polished gems, which means you'll actually be spending a bulk of your time in the dungeons mining gems. This would at least be fine if the combat was fun. Repeatedly swinging your weapon is not a bad thing, that's all you do in Stardew Valley as well. But Stardew Valley gives you a wide variety of weapons, and you also get non-melee weapons (slingshot). In Fae Farm, you only get one weapon, and you only get upgrades for that weapon when you complete a dungeon, in the form of a spell.The first dungeon is fine, but at least for me the first spell you get after completing that dungeon seems useless in combat and doesn't really affect your combat style. And that's all you have to get through the whole second dungeon.Energy and mana both seem to deplete fast, but mana especially fast. Going back to the spell you get for your weapon. Well that spell uses mana. Want to use your upgraded pickaxe to mine a little faster? Well that's also a spell and also uses mana. You get a handful of spell casts before running out of mana.To brew more mana options, you've got to grind critter collection. The ingredients for the potions all involve the items you collect from critters in your conservatory. They are all also one time drops, the critters leave the conservatory.The best loop in the game seems to be to spam the first dungeon, collect gems, polish them and sell them. Then go buy health and mana potions for 50G each to carry into the second dungeon so you can actually use your spells for combat and mining.The game had my interest (steadily decreasing) enough to finish the first dungeon. I got 5 floors into the second dungeon and decided to stop. And write this review, in lieu of being able to refund the game. And uninstall.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it so far. My big cons: the characters are so boring- they don't move from their spots and the dialogue is extremely repetitive and bland. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just very....soulless? Bland? I don't know. It's missing that something that good magical farming games like Stardew Valley have. It is VERY cute and very beautiful but a lot of it is....meh. I'm going to keep playing it because it's cute and mindless and I rely on little magical cosy games to keep mental stability but I don't think I'd recommend anyone purchasing it with having a fun well-built farming game in mind (which is what the devs hype it up to be).Firstly, you're immediately given a fully functioning farm. You don't have to do anything except upgrade your house if you WANT to. The barn & coop are built and at max capacity. They're both locked at first but each become unlocked and are fully available very very early into playing. You literally just have to play the normal quests to get these unlocked, no effort. Disappointing for me, honestly, because I do like the "you have to work to have a great farm" aspect of the cozy farming games.There also aren't a lot of NPC's with actual unique dialogue at first. There's not even really any heart quests? There's little "dates" they can take you on but even those seem empty. You get more NPCs coming to town as you complete main quests but this doesn't seem to be an objective in the quests, which is a little confusing considering this is one of the only things advancing main quest gives you that's of any significance. I would've liked this to be more obviously displayed in the town, like stores closed down and certain vendors unavailable until you've progressed (there is one vendor who doesn't become applicable until progression but she's still present and so is her shop before she's unlocked). You do unlock different areas as you progress but there's not really a ton of build up to them at all or urgency behind it. They also don't seem to benefit the actual people of the town a ton, which is an aspect of games I've enjoyed in the past.It's just a very, very anti-climatic game. The story isn't that great. Like it may have been if they had put more soul and depth within it but...I don't know. Again, I am going to keep playing this when I just want something mindless but it's definitely on the more boring end of all the cozy games I've played.
