_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Stardew Valley, Dinkums, and Harvest Moon / "Story of Seasons", you'll like this. The vibe is great and it's uber relaxing. I enjoy the music and the animals are very cute. I really hope this game continues to expand. Pros: Amazingly cute, multi-player modes, customization of avatar (clothes, hair, skin tone, eyes, eyebrows, mouth, etc...), fun game mechanics, really cute products / mining stuff, and did I mention it's UBER relaxing? I play before work to get in my chill zone. If you dislike the voices: there is a SILENT mode!Neutrals:I'd like to see more clothes, hair, and mouths, but then again, I always do! I'd also love more animals, more dungeons, more bachelors / bachelorettes. If you're into they/them, that's available.Cons:5 save slots. That's it; including your multiplayer slots. Whoever hosts uses a save slot. If you like creating a ton of characters / games like me? You're pretty... out of luck. The voices are pretty annoying, but somewhat cute. I'm torn about them, but I wish there were... different choices. I LOVE the silent mode however, in mutli-player for me, the other player will hear a random voice sometimes. (So your burly guy could be squeaking like a chipmunk for someone else... which is almost a hilarious pro, imo.) I really hope the game developers continue to expand. There's a lot of great potential to this game!Notes: I discovered this game through CallMeKevin. (Whoda thought?!) This needs more advertisement if that's how I, a farming game nut, discovered this! It's a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a fun game.  It is a lot like sunhaven except it adds the stamina mechanic back and has a lot bigger budget behind it.  It is had a good story, good gameplay, tons of things to do in general.  You get tons of items, you have a lot to craft, the graphics are cute, its fae themed.  Playing with friends is also very satisfying.  Overall if you are looking for a farming sim with a mining dungeon aspect, livestock, crops, villager interactions, and magic you can't go wrong with fae farm.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of people complain about this game but honestly I really like it. I just wish there were more clothes and maybe more crop variety. Also 1 big farm would’ve been better than the two tier I think (homestead & hazy haven as one big one). I have both DLCs and I also really like those. The flower breeding system is really nice and all the animals are so cute. There is definitely a lot to do. I don’t really care about NPCs (in any game) so I can’t comment on that, but all in all I think this is a really nice game. It doesn’t really have replay value unfortunately so once I finish my play through I will probably wait for new content. I’m sure this game is also amazing to play with friends, I just don’t have any LOL
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Pros.- You can swim.- You can jump, so you don't have to walk aaaaaall the way around things, as you have had to in every farm sim to ever exist.- You're not forced to play Hide and Seek with the villagers. They're all on the map and you can set waypoints on them.- The initial character customization is a bit barebones, but hey, you can be fat. You don't have to look like an anorexic child anymore... I mean, you can if you want, but it's not the only option. - It's ACTUALLY cosy. Though some quests do have timers, I haven't once felt rushed into doing anything.- Co-op. My sister, who is the only person I ever co-op games with would never in a million years play a farm sim, but it is an option.- The UI has bugged on me a couple times, but it's nothing a reload didn't fix. As someone who has played many, many EA games (which this definitely is, regardless of advertising), this is a lot less buggy than I was expecting.Cons.- Price. I won't say it's not worth it because I don't know yet, but when I've paid less than 35NZD for every farm sim game I've ever played, asking me for 60 is... risky. They're lucky I was bored enough.- The mines. I loathe unnecessary reptition. It has that stardew valley floor system, where you have to do the same ones again and again, except you can unlock teleports between the levels, assuming you have the resources, which you get in the mine. Awful.- The main story is connected to the mining system. It has not had time to become compelling enough before they expect you to tolerate the tedium.I do recommend because if it wasn't fun, I wouldn't have played 5+ hours in one sitting, but I would also recommend waiting for a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good. If you haven't played other farming games like Stardew, it will probably be the most enjoyable!  It's lacking in some things compared to other games of a similar concept, so go into it expecting it to not be as fulfilling. It's a little bit pricey vs. play time. I do enjoy playing it though, and at 60 hrs see myself going for another 10-15 more to really completely collect stuff and beautify. It's a good game to just relax and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: As much as i love the art style the time in game seems to move way too fast, and as it is right now its a little shallow with not much room for variety with building limitations and livestock or combat. Even when romancing a character they still seem to say the same few lines over and over.Clothing options have been limited and I've put in over 11 hoursonly 6 options for eyes and less for mouths so there isn't much room for character diversity Honestly I'd say wait a while to see what else they add into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Unplayable multiplayer, feels like we're alpha testing the multiplayer mode. Nothing works, characters get deleted. game saves disappear. Full of bugs and glitches mostly related to multiplayer but also related to quests, and npc interactions. There are items in game that should not be there (medium honey comb) and some items (tree sprouts) don't work at all. Feels rather unfinished. How come it's acceptable to sell a half finished product and be like, we will fix it later on... maybeI should also mention that my gameplay is not reflected here as I also bought the switch version. I Had high hopes for this game but after 50h I can say its a hot mess really. Not in any way worth the price tag, it's not even complete. Multiplayer just doesn't work.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. I think it's well paced for casual play and thoroughly enjoy the dungeons. Sometimes I feel like the farming sim dungeons are too hard for when I'm just trying to relax, and this feels like a good mix of just hard enough to keep me engaged but not too hard to make me frustrated. The graphics are beautiful, but I do agree that the NPC dialog options are lackluster and I almost don't interact with anyone in the game. I don't really miss that tho because I like to focus on farming and the decorating. For those saying that as well, even games like Animal crossing don't have more dialog options. I think if you want an NPC dialog story game, play something more like Elder Scrolls.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game and I honestly can't really figure out why I don't. Something about it just doesn't pull me in. I found myself a little lost at times on what to do, and struggling to find the resources I needed. Unlocking the mines were also really confusing as well. It's gotten an update since I last played, so maybe I'll give it another chance in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lovely game BUT there is no way to make a save point when you must leave the game. The game is so linear it's not even funny.How unfortunate. The game has potential but I do not have time to be stuck in a game if I need to like .. yanno, feed the fam, take care of real life things, etc.Terrible design.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game, I enjoyed it a lot. It's obviously a copy of Stardew Valley, but it honestly feels much better to play, there are several improvements that this game has over SV, the animations are cleaner and more satisfying, the graphics are better, and making money is more consistent and balanced, EVERYTHING can be profitable, not just farming, which is great.HOWEVER, the game is really very short. It only really has around 50 hours of content if you are progressing at a casual rate, which for a game of this price, is really not very much. It needs more than 3 dungeons, more than 6 farm animals, more than two or three options for romance, just more of a lot. There is also almost nothing to spend large amounts of money on, so earning it usually feels pointless.The game is also chock full of fairly minor bugs that they seem to be patching out quickly, but still worth mentioning.They just released a DLC that, from what I've heard, adds less than an hour of content to the game, so I don't think it is worth buying either.So if you don't care about price and want 50 hours of fun, I actually DO recommend this game. However, if you want a more permanent investment in a game, this one simply has no replayablity, so I would not recommend it to the average player.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Very shallow, in a “smart” way, on paper, when you start the game, it looks like they have a lot to offer and different things to do…. Well that’s basically it. There’s a lot of thing that seems to be implemented just to be there but they are just not developed enough to matter or for you to care.There’s nothing rewarding about it. If you want to try it wait for a huge sale cause this feels like a huge waste of money to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it at first and really did want to invest more time with it. But once I completely stopped playing it, I didn't feel like I needed to play it again. (Thanks to Sun Haven)It opens up great, it has it's charm, and it's aesthetically pleasing... but it became prevalent over time to me that it was shallow. The characters are there just to fulfill a romance or quest dialog. I'm not sure what age demographic this targets, but it definitely felt too empty of a world with little to dive into.I really do like it's art, style and animations. AND I love playing games of this concept: a 3D open adventure, co-operative, farming sim. Though here, it was just the framework of a game like that. Tough to say if it's even worth picking up for half the price.There's just little to no identity for itself here. At least not now.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Farm is an all right game- I strongly recommend buying it on sale like I did as it's flaws make it not worth full price.I enjoy the farming/stuff collecting/etc and like the appearance of the island and fairy stuff in general, however the characters are bad. Like breathtakingly flat. And this extends sadly to the romanceables. And the dating system in general sucks. In most games you have to kind of initiate dating vs friendship with a romanceable. Here.. it happens just by talking to them and then they are immediately flirting with you and dates happen pretty quick.Which is obviously a little shaky- can I not talk to the others? Is there a jealousy system? No idea.The romance and friendship quests are identical. Like worded identically, same exact quests in same order regardless of character. I have frog kid, the mayor and the wizard all asking for a dazzlefly, an oak log and 10 citrine all with the same wording. WTF.And then the characters are so underdeveloped.Lets take Argyle for example since they are used in a lot of the ads:Argyle's design is very NPC looking, like if they had given the poor kid a bag or a pin or something but instead its just... plain green sweater. Argyle when you talk to them outside of a date tells you 2 things about themselves: they are a potter, and they like frogs.Then you go on your first date with Argyle where you proceed to learn.. they are a potter and they like frogs. In practically the same wording. Like I recognize that Argyle is autistic but like, the writers couldn't mix it up a little bit for the date?? Like?? Come on?? And then like regular townies will be way  more cute and dateable looking than the actual dateabes- especially the seed vendors. I assume the shopkeeps can't be dated for coding reasons since they have to stay put to do their job.Which brings me to the one character with layers: Alaric. Alaric is the town wizard and is non-romanceable. Alaric sticks out to me because he bears a striking resemble to a character from a Disney Jr cartoon: Mateo de Alva from Elena of Avalor. I am positive they based Alaric on him. Here's some of their similarities:- Wear a hoodie style robe- same personality of dorky nice dude- Described as 'the wisest wizard in ___' while both being the only wizard- Both want a magic library and both refer to their wizard workshop as a laboratoryI'm pretty sure there are more similarities but I'm tired.But it's pretty damning when the character with the most noticeable layers is almost certainly based off of one from another media.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: All in All a fairly good farming game. Similar to games like Harvest Moon or Seasons of Stories. Would recommend purchasing it on Switch vs PC as it is very much optimised for controller- Very Cute Graphics- The Animals are adorable- Multiplayer- The recipes for building/cooking are great, gives you some adventure to collect everything- The areas you unlock are beautiful-Romances feel flat, and 2D, like the characters aren't fully fleshed-Placing items is a headache, you have to walk the items to where you want to place them instead of having a free roaming placement system- Glitchy! It needs some updates to fix the glitches, eg. The build mode not bringing up the grid so you can't place anything
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm having an absolute blast! The grind or game loop is enjoyable, the game isn't overly punishing, and I'm really excited to try multiplayer when I get a chance. The music for this game is incredibly relaxing! The change-up to more suspenseful music in the mines elevates the sense of urgency. I'm only about 20 hours in, but I'm sure this game will easily push me well beyond 100 hours before too long!
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. It has a cute world. NPCs feel a bit lifeless, but since I am more focused on crafting and building a little world, this doesnt bother me much. It may be annoying to those that are big on relationship building with the NPCs though. I understand they are working on adding more life to the NPCs so even its not really fleshed out yet, it may be in the future. I really enjoy the Fae twist on the traditional farm sim though. I really enjoy the flower breeding and the seeding mechanic. For what it is, it could be a bit cheaper, but I have played it enough to have gotten my money out of it
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Farm is an absolute delight to play. It is a great blend of magic and farming vibes. I haven't been this engaged in a farming sim since Sun Haven. The character creation is so cute and has some body diversity. The art style in game is gorgeous. All the items have such a soft and magical feeling to them. As a person who loves rainbows there's just so many in the game and it makes my brain happy. There is flower breeding for those who like that. The crop system is fun as you can change it with magic and there are fun ways to water your plants too! There's multiple farm areas to customise and explore. You can change the decorations in your home so easily too which is a big bonus compared to most farm sims that charge you so much to craft or buy one item. You can buy recipes and craft most of your decorations at craft tables. The mines are engaging as well as challenging at some points with whimsical creatures to battle if you like. I haven't finished the main story arch yet but I am excited/sad to see the ending. I've played with my friends as well which is super nice to have multi-player in farm sim like this. Oh and the animals are adorable! I play with a controller and it works great too. If you get the game I hope you have fun ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly fourteen hours in and so far I love this game, It's cute/cozy and I love that not *everything* uses up energy.Not sold on the fishing mechanic but it's still less frustrating to me than in other games similar to this one, so I'm mostly okay with it.My younger sibling lives pretty far away and Fae Farm has given me a way to spend time with them from a distance doing something we both enjoy and can just goof around with, which I appreciate so very much.Edit: over 50 hours of playtime after I left the above review I am nearly in year four of my main playthrough and still loving this game, It's laid back and one of my go to games for when i just want to relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just here to say the graphics are delightful, the game play pleasurable and I am thoroughly enjoying the game play. Not to hardcore farm unless that's your thing but i have enjoyed what I've played so far! Its a great game for the price and am i excited ill get the dlc for what i payed absolutely. i support game developers that are passionate about what they do! Why is this not more of a thing instead of blaming a price tag. Sometimes its worth it. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game is very cute! I really like the art-style and how it's similar to other games that I enjoy that incorporate farming, mining, fishing, etc. I also like how easy the navigation system is while trying to find the cute characters for any of the quests and the decoration you're able to do on your character and house. Would recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not finished, and should not be advertised or sold as such. To me, it feels like an early access game. Don't get me wrong, it's a beautiful and cozy game with many nice features, but there are simply too many bugs.I play with my wife, and we constantly deal with the following. These are just what I can remember off the top of my head:- She keeps getting logged out of our multiplayer lobby, and she loses all her progress that day. A full day of harvesting crops, cooking, collecting animal produce and going to the mines, all of it gone from her inventory. Money spent is gone too. - Sometimes her game just crashes, and she loses all progress again- Her voice keeps changing, often to a male voice- Sometimes we are invisible to each other- Sometimes, those big NPC you need to feed are just invisible- All these issues force us to restart the game and set up a new multiplayer lobby, which really sucks the fun out of the game- Animals are bugged out and don't produce anything, and keep coming back even after we sell them- She could not finish the quest about waving to an animal, but this was recently fixed- She can see NPCs/storyline areas and character before they are unlocked, like the ice seller- When she joins my game, she always has half health, energy and mana for some reason. Which sucks, especially after being forced to restart the game due to an error- If you wake up with rested bonus and quit your game, then next time you start your game, the rested bonus is gone- Shipping contracts were bugged and could not be accepted, but this was recently fixed- Sometimes, 50 different quests unluck/complete at once, with some of them having no name- The game does not pause between days in multiplayer, which forces us to quit when we want to take a break- When hovering over an item, the description says to use my "R stick" to scroll in the textbox. I am playing on PC, not Switch.. And it only works if I somehow get my mouse over into the textbox without accidentally hovering over another item- Local multiplayer isn't available on PC. Instead you have to add a friend to your Fae Farm account, and then invite them through Steam, but only if they are currently in the game..? And in general, the game is just a bit shallow:- The NPCs are incredibly shallow with no real life in the town. I was able to go on a date with 7 different NPCs without even really knowing their names, story or trying to romanticize them- "Festivals" are just two fetch quests- Once you reach the Fae area, there's just.. nothing. Just another mine and farm, and that is all.- Once you reach the Mountain/Volcano area, there is even less. - Most fish use the same model/texture- Critters spawn in the same locations- There is no reason to farm anything in this game. Many different vegetables, but they don't really do anything special. They all turn into chopped vegetables or diced roots or chopped fruits anyway. And they are worth almost nothing if you sell them. And you can only sell items one at a time, and a maximum of 8*4 per day, obviously so you don't make too much money. It feels weird.Overall, it's a really promising game with a lot of cool features and ideas - especially the animations and how the farm sheds work, but it's simply not finished. There are SO many game breaking bugs, even after the last few rounds of bug patches. If I could, I would ask for my money back, or travel back in time and tell myself to wait another half year before playing this :)
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, the game play is about 100 hours.  I wish there was an option for maybe, and not just yes or no. I wouldn't discourage someone from buying the game, but I also wouldn't recommend it. It was fun, but not at that price. I am past the main story line, and I don't think I will continue on playing out the job quests and side quests.Added: I came back to play multiplayer, and I am even more disappointed in this game. I can not add my friends on steam to the game. This is the only multiplayer game I have this problem with. I now change my view of this game and would never recommend it to anyone and would actively discourage anyone from getting it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun game! We played Coop the entire time and we're both pretty used to Farm Sims so 30h might be on the more ''optimised'' side for play time.I really like the quality of life they made compared to Stardew Valley. (For example you can buy seed on Wednesday lol) It doesn't feel like a remake, it's got a  lot of new ideas as well.By far the best controller experience I had in this genre! It might be a downside if you are die hard on mouse and keyboard tho because the menus really feel optimised for controllers.Bug wise, they were all small visual things (character voice, music,table dissapearing for one day) and all on the second player side. So i guess if one of your friend HATES bugs make him host the game.I saw a lot of players saying the NPCs are boring compared to the other games, for me it's never the main reason why I play these games so I don't really have an opinion on that.Not much for endgame either, I think it's the kind of game we'll pretty much 100% once and be okay with it. (There's a decent amount of grind, I would need a decent break before restarting from scratch)
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is fun so far, I do see some blandness to the gameplay. NPCs share the same dialog, the combat system feels very weird. Like a magic staff? More like a melee staff that I haven't seen do any magic unless you buy potions for that. As others have stated, it's not worth the full price as there's really not a whole lot going on. If you're wanting something related to Stardew Valley, Dinkum, or AC, this game probably isn't it. While they all have similar game styles, I do fear that this game won't be getting QOL updates we want just like Hokko Life when that came out. If you're wanting to play something to pass time, feel free to get it. I'm still going to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Now that Nintendo Switch players have Palia, and will have Sun Haven in the future, I don't recommend this game. I played it with my spouse and it's boring. I have it here on Steam. I couldn't stay awake while playing it. The biggest thing I hate is how restrictive they are with the caves. I also don't like having to cultivate multiple plots for harvesting different items. There are a lot of elements that are tedious. Devs, please go and try to understand why games like Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, Sun Haven, etc. are fun.I recommend this game for Nintendo Switch players because they don't have as many choices for farming sims as PC players do. It's good, but I prefer Sun Haven over this game. If you like games like Dreamlight Valley, you'll appreciate this game. Once again, on PC, I'd choose Sun Haven, Coral Island, or something like Kynseed over this title. I bought this on sale. I wouldn't pay full price for it at this time. I also don't like that I can't carry anything over from my multiplayer sessions into my solo sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cozy and fun if you previously enjoyed games like My Sims & Animal Crossing or Stardew Valley. Bonus kudos if you love frogs and magical creatures! This game has it all: build you own farm, decorate your house, play alone or with friends and sell your crafts and critter on the market to make profit and upgrade your tools.Great game for people who love to explore open world games.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRCozy farm life sim with a heavier emphasis on mining to progress rather than farming, dating, or cooking. Not TL;DRThis is a perfect game when you want to play something  but don't want have to keep track of an intricate detail heavy plot and does a great job at giving you enough to do without needing to worry too much about forgetting about something. Each level of progression split between each chapter gets a bit repetitive at times by the end with each major progression step tending to have a lot of time spent in the mines gathering resources and the benefits of farming aren't as viable in comparison since they don't sell for as much. The result during my Fiancee and I's second play through, we felt like there wasn't as much of a farming side as we would have hoped. Overall, the past 73 hours (at the time of this review) have been positive. If the team shows the same devotion towards bug fixing and improvements as the past couple of weeks I'd be more than happy to attempt a third play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT RELEASE DLC FOR A GAME THAT STILL HAS BUGS, CRAP UI, BORING NPCS, AND FEELS LIKE IT IS IN EARLY ACCESS!!!!TLDR: It is a good game, not as bad as spirit of the island (that one is HORRIBLE all around). I like the auto tool switch, ability to choose pronouns, and how freely you can move around. Copies and pastes a lot from the genre and is nothing special. Game is not fully fleshed out and is over priced, it feels like it is missing a lot. Stardew Valley is three times cheaper on sale right now and about a billion times better. I got it for free so I will play it but don't bother wasting your money unless there is a huge sale and the devs stop being lazy and money hungry. Longer Review: I like this game a lot but Stardew is infinitely better. All the negative reviews have a point and they word things much better than I can. I like the art style and concept. Moving through the world and being able to interact with just about everything is super fun. The UI and controls are not great. This game is meant for a controller. For 30 bucks on steam this is a decently expensive game, in its current state its worth 20. My best friend got this for me for Christmas so I did not spend any money on it. I probably wouldn't have gotten it if it wasn't for her. The gameplay is not innovative and it is just the normal farming sim type things. The NPCS are BORING and the options with them feels like it is in alpha. The UI to talk to them is gross and they just don't have any substance. Stardew has really spoiled us when it comes to farming games. Farming is not difficult. Nothing is really hard in this game, besides fishing. That mechanic is crap. A lot of things feel like crap and half arsed. Character creation is bare bones besides the pronouns section which I really respect. Animals are fun but there are a lot of bugs with them. I really wanted to love this game but this is not finished and not worth the asking price. This is LAZY and GREEDY by the Devs. They will not take anything into account that people have to say and will probably release more crappy DLCs then abandon the game without fixing any bugs because that is the state of gaming in 2023. There are way more developers deserving of your money than these guys. Bear and Breakfast is a great cosy game I genuinely loved, Hades is a masterpiece, and I really enjoyed Red Dead Redemption 2 this year (which is infintiely better than this game and only 20 USD on sale).
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: This game has truly become my happy place, filled with countless memories and endless opportunities for fun ♥♥. From embarking on main quest and side quests to diving into dungeons for materials and upgrading weapons, there is no shortage of things to do. Personally, I find the most joy in designing my farm and house while my partner focuses on gathering materials ♥^O^♥. There's something incredibly satisfying about customizing every aspect of the game, from colors and seeds to clothes and interior design.The overall experience is both fun and calming, making it the perfect escape from reality. I highly recommend this game for anyone looking to unwind and create lasting memories ♥O♥.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift off of my wish list for Christmas (2023). I've been playing for 60 hours now, and am on Spring year 2. It's a loooot of fun so far, but has a decent amount of minor bugs. I feel like even though I've already played so much, there's a lot more content. The crafting system is a teeny bit bloated and there's a difficulty spike between the first and second dungeon. The first one was super easy and the second one threw me for a loop a little bit. I got way too into the flower breeding mechanic for the sole purpose of clothing. Maybe I haven't seen enough, but I wish there were more clothes and I wish they didn't need so many rare flowers, but maybe that's the game's way of making you slow down and take the time to get what you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the Stardew Valley like games I've played, I find this one to be the coziest. It has beautiful colors, easy to use controls, magic, and fairy wings. What more could you ask for?There are two quality of life mechanics that I wish every other cozy sim had. You can jump. This makes traversal a lot easier and also allows your ADD brain to just jump everywhere. But my favorite is how the tools are used. You don't have to keep them in a place in your bar or select the correct tool. No matter what chore you are doing it selects the correct tool for you. This is one of my favorite innovations in this genre and hope it becomes a staple.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately there's just better farming games like this out there. Its very cute and fun but uh there isn't much to do? You finish the little Chapters and then there's not much other goals to go for. Festivals and romances are extremely... last minute thrown together it feels like. Festivals are just a special vendor and romances are just pointless. You get three separate farms you unlock for animals and its so spread out and there's not an ounce of automation to help with that. The time in the game keeps rolling when you're in your shed inventory or crafting menu or loading screen. Then there's just a lot of bugs still in the game???
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game a few months ago upon release. Originally due to the price I had planned to get it on sale but due to what a wonderful mix of MySims and a fantasy farming sim it looked like, I couldn't wait. It was an unfortunate decision for me because this game really is not worth it unless you get it on sale. The world is beautiful, it has that going for it. I also enjoyed the quests and the fact that you have unlimited storage right off the bat. However, the world just doesn't feel very immersive. All the bosses are just the same script over and over again. Fight to the bottom of the mine, make a potion, fill their little basket quests. And the villagers have pretty much no unique or enticing dialogue or events to keep you engaged. I got to the third mine and just kind of gave up because I felt like I was just grinding through, figuring I'd go back once I'd had a little break. It's been six months and I haven't felt the need to open it again.If you want this game, wait until you get get it on sale. It's probably worth it at that price, just can't help but feel disappointed with the amount I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: My Fiance' got me this game as a gift, while I usually I find it hard to get into farming/crafting themed games I found this one to be much better and way more easy going to get into, The graphics are sweet and the game has a nice cosy feel to it, quests are easy to track and follow, item and quest descriptions explain a lot if you get confused during gameplay. I love the mining and fishing, it's fun and rewarding. tools automatically change to suit what you're working on which is amazing. You don't get punished for not making it to sleep on time, running out of stamina just prevents you from doing more till resting, death just kicks you from a dungeon. and you can JUMP! I love this game, and from someone who has never clicked with games like Stardew, Rune Factory, Animal Crossing etc, it says a lot that this has become such a favourite that I love to play with my partner, highly recommend to people trying to get a friend or partner into a farming type game that is easy going on newbies but still fun for fans of this style of game too. I'd give it a solid 8/10 and I'm only 3 hours into it!
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited for this game. Placed a pre-order for myself and a friend. I wanted to love this game, but it just falls short. Graphics are adorable, but game play is clunky (so much so that it makes the game difficult to enjoy). This game in it's current form is not worth $60.*Also never received the additional pre-order content...
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, i regret buying this game. Something about it just doesn’t do it for me. It feels limited, and after playing it for 4 hours I can’t find it in me to play it again. I just don’t understand what warrants the $40 price tag after playing. You get cute graphics, cute world. Obviously tons of effort has gone into the look… but somehow the substance is just completely lacking. It feels empty and uninteresting. The world is littered with characters and buildings, none of which seem to have any real depth. Nobody is ever in the buildings. The dialogue totally breaks the immersion. It sucks, because the game functions well and ultimately the main features work pretty flawlessly; it’s just that there’s no motivation to interact with them. Adding more interesting dialogue as opposed to a sad, scripted game monologue would be huge for these characters. The only one I found myself remotely endeared to was Eddy, the fisherman. Playability is simply stunted by the fact that the main quest is a little all over the place, and frankly kind of janky. It sucks to say, but it just really feels like an incomplete early access game. I had really high hopes and frankly I’m disappointed for the price point. However, that said, there’s major potential here to fix some of the weird features. The dialogue needs work. Characters just repeat themselves, there’s no additional “response” dialogue most of the time. You should be able to name your character. The town should feel busy, not just crowded. It just feels too plastic right now. Again, the environment and graphics are wonderful, so much time has been put into the world… I only wish the gameplay itself had been more of the focus here.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: * Updated find: NO PENALTIES for not sleeping!! Not sure if bug or a great add since mining can be time consuming but its defiantly a huge perk! *This game is extremely adorable. The time spent playing has been very much enjoyable. Keyboard and mouse controls may take a second to get used to but not horrible and you can in fact REMAP them. Controller works fine no complaints there. You have to beat chapter one to get bonus rewards as the first chapter is a tutorial and it's pretty short I don't understand how people didn't just complete it first before complaining about missing rewards. The color schemes & locations is very pleasant on the eye holes.Defiantly worth the buy. Can't wait to find the mother trucking faeries!
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: this game is...absolutely dazzling,i played 9 hours straight only stopping to make real food lol theres main story,side quests,crafting,upgrading,fishing,swimming,bug catching,cooking,decorating,mining,a bit of exploration,farming,taking care of animals,fluid combat so far not too hard,theres weather conditilns u can make potions for,decent customization with thiccer body options finally a character that looks like me AND you can do all this with coop. theres crossplay too i play on steam deck on high settings no problem my daughter played on switch, only things bad on her end were lag and game kicked her 1 time in 7 hours of her playing. theres xp,quests are shared,money is shared but if you ugrade tools or back it only counts for 1 person which i dont mind cause it gives us more to do. there might be more to do later and im all 4 it so rar already 10/10 i havent even started on getting into relationship with npc yet im excited for that and the future dlc you get with deluxe version, ive paid $60 for worse games. i highly recommend especially if you have family and friends to play my daughter and i love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a few bugs which I hope will get patched soon. I got the impression that the game is somewhat fast-paced as there's so much to do everyday. Crafting system is complex, mining not too stressful. I also love the graphics. In-game relationships are bland and repetitive but otherwise I really enjoy the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: ETA: To be fair, I am a story-line based, completion-ist cozy gamer, so YMMV. Overall, yes, I would recommend this to other cozy gamers and completion players.  I have thoroughly enjoyed Fae Farm. I have completed the main story-line and while it was darling, there's nothing left but grinding. I was rather disappointed with the DLC, as well as with the update/patch. I was expecting more content not just more grinding, decor, and romance.  The best thing that was added was the toggle to slow down the day.This game was gifted to me by a friend, so I don't know if that counts for free or not. Also, there are spoilers below, so read at your own risk. I really adored the gift and can't wait to continue. I've only played through the first 2 chapters but the story line is interesting and the game play has easy to pick up controls. The game, itself, is cute and cozy, with plenty of quests both in and outside of the main story line, so you are able to proceed at your own pace.  The storage capacity is out of sight and I really enjoy the farming sim aspects as well as the adventure RPG lines. Downsides are few that I have found so far, but I do have a couple of issues. Most of them are most likely preference based, so YMMV. I am on the fence about being pulled to bed at midnight but if you go to bed before that, there is a bonus on the next mornings activities. I wish there was a better marketing system as the items don't stack on the marketplace, so there is limited room to sell off extra items.All in all a really adorable, fun and easy to play adventure/sim/rpg.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: The game is BEAUTIFUL and runs super smooth, controls feel great and the day cycle is so fun I don't want to stop playing!It would be the most perfect life sim/ farm sim ever made if the actual cute characters were romanceable (Alaric? Dominic? Bjorn? Holly? Rosalind? Miles? Sven? Cinder?) It seems like they chose the less appealing characters to be dateable options - this is my only criticism.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I was super hesitant on getting this game, as i am with most games. Especially when they are expensive. So far i do not have any regrets, even though i do find this game a little over priced and should be priced lower. It is super cute. There is lots to do. You can farm, grow flowers, work on the main story line, side quests, and even romance quests. You can decorate your house, and farm. AND as the main story line progresses you gain multiple homes, and farm spaces. I do wish the days were longer, as i feel like i can not get everything done in one day. There are multiple Mines, and they are A LOT of work.. Its actually annoying because i thought this game was suppose to be more of a cozy game. To progress the main story, you have no choice but to do the mines. So that is annoying. The side quests are all repetitive, and most ask for the same item. ; I also find it super odd that the fences have zero purpose. The animals can walk right through them. You can walk all over your crops and flowers and they don't move or make a sound. I do feel like the game lags often, and when clicking to pet your animals, its hard to get it lined up on each one separately. I'll end up petting the same one 3 times. It is also hard to click on the animal feeders, as you have to wait for the mark to pop up above them to click it and feed them. Sometimes i have this issue when trying to talk to people as well. I found a bug in the game a couple days ago where i couldn't progress in the main story without completing it, and i did this part 4 times before it finally went through. I have also noticed if you play for to long, the game will lag and everything becomes unclickable. I find restarting the game fixes it. Its just annoying. Especially when you're in the middle of a quest or decorating. I TRIED to contact the Fae Farm developers multiple times and had zero luck. I got no response. So if you have issues like i have been having.. i doubt they'll hear your complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game for the first 15 or so hours, but I can't recommend it because of how badly the multiplayer is bugged. If you're planning on playing it solo, it's probably fine. But do not play this for multiplayer. It is unacceptably broken for a released game. Your guests will have hours of progress randomly lost, and then be locked out even from re-grinding those hours again, with no way to recover or even start over. Or major progression milestones become locked out with no way to get them back. After this happened to us, I started looking around and found lots of other people with the same issues and no solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: 6, going on 7 hours usually isn't enough time to make a final decision on a thumbs up or thumbs down in this genre but I don't think I'm going to change my mind too much on this. Fae Farm is infectiously fun and it always takes some effort to tear myself away from each play session. Was questioning the price, but I'd say it is worth the standard edition's $40 from all I've played. Comparing to other farming RPGs in this price range, it's better than many recent Story of Seasons entries (barring the remake of A Wonderful Life) but not as great as Rune Factory 4 (nothing is, IMO.) The visuals are very cute and noticeably crisper than many $20-30 offerings I've played. The UI is highly polished and functional. Gameplay loop is addictive as mentioned prior. I am always shocked when checking the in-game clock. Or even a real life clock, time melts away. Breadth of character development and character dialogue needs some work and falls behind the competition. All-around gameplay is getting an easy A.

_childDocuments_.review: fae farm is so addicting, i love it. ~75 hours, 28/35 achievements. another game in a similar realm that i really love playing is dinkum.first, to address some annoyances: now onto what i love about this game! wooo!i'm almost done with spring year 2 and have my fav skills maxed at 20. even though i've finished the main story quest there's still so much i want to do. i've become obsessed with breeding hybrid flowers, there are outfits and items i want work on collecting, job quests i can finish, and i can work on decorating my homesteads!!   the style reminds me of "my sims" on the wii. i also get chibi dauntless vibes from the town. i wonder if the two games take place in the same world?  i love jumping around because my character looks like she has jelly bones. none of the tracks are out of place or annoying. running around town is not tedious at all. the terrain has practically no boundaries. if you ever played other games and wondered why you couldn't jump over a fence into the river, this game lets you.a lot of classic mechanics have a refreshing and fun spin to them. really neat quality of life features that games of this genre lack.progression feels balanced.your character isn't locked out of important content (item upgrades, farm upgrades, etc) by season. most of it is tied to main story progress, some depend on your skill level (new seeds). so i recommend just taking it easy and playing at your own pace. there are even ways to grow seasonal crops at any time of the year. you can't even buy all the festival items in year 1, so just enjoy the ride cause spring comes again.this question is so lame, but to put it plainly i paid $50 cad for this game. at the time of writing this i've played ~75 hrs and will play more until i'm ready to move onto my next game. that's 66 cents per hour of entertainment. yeah, i'd say it's been worth it.

_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Picked up this game on launch because it looked really cute and I wanted to give my wrists a break from more taxing games I'd been playing (rogues, metroidvanias, etc.). Within my first few hours, the game felt like a combination of some of my favorite games from similar genres (Rune Factory, Fantasy Life, Animal Crossing) and took a little bit from each whether it be style or a part of the game; I'd also previously played Sun Haven and Fae Farm is a much more charming version of Fae Farm, although the NPCs in Fae Farm are a bit bland.I focused on the story and finished the main storyline in <30-40 hours. It's a relatively quick story and easy to focus on specifically because the NPCs are not super interesting. There's variety in their personality, but you don't really have to try hard. Fae Farm is especially charming because of how wholesome it is, but it definitely falls short on the love interests and how you build relationships with others. It could also be seen as a gateway game into similar games (Harvest Moon, Stardew, etc.) for kids and younger folks because of how wholesome it is (monsters in the dungeons, but fetch requests instead of big intense bosses).There are some frustrating things, especially if you're comparing to other games with similar mechanics that you might be used to: fishing can feel insufferable at first (it's the last skill I chose to max out and finished the story while I neglected the skill at Level 6), pets/animals can get in the way of farming if you don't have fences up (they follow you around outside sometimes when they're happy to see you and you can automatically switch to petting them when you're really just trying to plant seeds), trying to place objects can be imprecise (thankfully you can move things easily, including seeds), and being able to breed flower hybrids but not make seeds of the hybrids is slightly disappointing.While the game is still buggy, it's been enjoyable even if I have to reboot sometimes. I've mostly played on the SteamDeck and so my hours don't sync all the time, and at this point I'm just grinding to get the rest of the achievements and have over 150 hours clocked. I would recommend for how wholesome and lovely the aesthetic is, but would also recommend waiting for more bugfix patches from the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: All i can say, this game is great, especially the ability to jump is super nice and makes a lot of things easier, it feels also like the walking speed isn't too slow which i really welcome.Also the fact that it switches your tools automatically is great, no searching through your inventory for the right tool, love it.The Game overall is very cute designed. I am not one to talk much about mechanics and all these things so i just sit here enjoy the Game and recommend it to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Not talking about the price... this game is full of nonsense. The most appreciated part is the action (fighting) element which is really smooth, this is the only WOW point in this Farming Sim game.The overall game design is really weird:- Story is too short. It takes me only 30hr to finish the whole main story. Things are repetitive starting from the dungeons.- The price in game is very extreme that you can make money easily with gem stone but you will never earn enough with farming, fishing, cooking, etc. But in fact money is not very important in the game.- I finished the game and found there is no reason to feed animals. Skills like fishing is totally no use but to finish the main story line.- Vegetables seems to have some variety but in fact there is no need to consume food when you have enough "furnitures"- Festivals are boring and contradictory. There is no direction to finish the missions but a few words of description. Player need to guess what is happening.- Shipping contract concept is good, but I could never accept a contract successfully.Long story in short, by comparing to the maturity and content of other "early access" games, Dev Team could develop 70% more content before releasing this alpha version. I feel lucky of not purchasing the Deluxe version :)

_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: If you are into cozy games like Stardew or Animal Crossing, this game is for you. However, the game is gorgeous, the story engaging and enjoyable, BUT... the multiplayer (which I bought it to play with my bf) has a problem. Once your character as visitor logs out of the game and the main account continues to play, the progress of the visitor is DELETED entirely. It happened once, and I decided to save every game play. We spent 3 hrs upgrading things to make it easier for us to achieve recipes and gather items, only for us to log in later and find my bf's character reset (has 0 tools and 0 bag slots) and all the items I crafted for him are GONE in the inventory. Now I get characters visiting is one thing... but if I'm on helping him continuously I EXPECT the stuff we spend game coins on to still BE on the character when I log in. Otherwise what's the point as registering as a friend on this account? Don't get me wrong but I love Fae farm, they just need to work these kind of setbacks so we are freely enjoying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Way too buggy. Sheering sheep doesn't work; milking cows often doesn't work; harvesting crops sometimes doesn't work; using crafting tables sometimes doesn't work (and also explodes the table and everything it's processed into grass???); the second and third mines are very empty; all the animations are frustratingly slow; you cannot do more than one mission at a time despite some of them being very tedious and long-winded; the general colour palette for the game and everything in it is washed out browns and dark greens that don't fit the fairy theme; customisation is dull as you are limited to these 6 ugly colours, and the clothing options are all boring anyway; you are forcefully given a haircut whenever you try to wear a hat; none of the characters are particularly lovable or interesting, and very few of them are even romance candidates; the marriage ceremony used a placeholder instead of my name and froze midway through; my spouse doesn't interact with me, she lives outside, and all she does all day is poke the ground with a stick; multiplayer is not very functional and results in a wide array of glitches such as losing literally all of your progress; lots of sound effects from me play for my friend who is in a different part of the world entirely; sometimes items one of us gathers teleports to the other person; the camera is awfully restricting and often gets stuck; menus often get stuck resulting in you being unable to do anything without restarting; catching bugs is a joke; fishing is more reliant on level than skill or equipment; levelling is slow and unbalanced, resulting in my friend reaching level 20 in fighting while always avoiding monsters while still being level 11 in farming after focusing on it from the start; and the price tag for the game is too much for what it offers.The animations are really good, and the animals are super cute, but unfortunately there isn't much more I can say about the game that's positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: All quests have no time limit making play through less stressful, the calendar is a weather forecast for the next few days to make planning my day easier, characters and farm animals are just too cute. I hear multiplayer glitches, but I don't have friends to play with, and also the dialogues that the NPC say are repetitive, but I don't read those anyway. Also, you don't get achievement awards, but unlocking things and experiencing new areas are satisfying enough in itself. In conclusion - I LOVE IT!
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Idk for the price, there's better out there. I only put 2 hours in, but the game had no draw for me. I kept trying to convince myself to play and it just wasn't happening. The game is beautiful and that's about where anything positive ends for me. I found the game to be fairly over and underwhelming at the same time. I'm someone who has sunk in at least 5k hours in crafting/farming sims and there was a lot that confused me in this game. Crafting in general was confusing. Where to stand in order to craft, how to craft and how to find the item you needed to craft. The map was confusing since it doesn't show exactly where you and everyone else is. It just kind of chunks into different areas. Not being able to name your character is very off putting. I was also unable to name my world. It just wouldn't let me delete "my world." Having no portrait of the npc when you talk to them makes it hard to visualize what they look like. I thought the characters just looked like fancy legos lmao. And for the love of god, can game devs please stop with the short days? I have very severe ADHD and it's so easy for me to forget what all I needed to do in such a short time span and end up missing out on things. No one buys these games expecting to grind on a clock and feel stressed tf out. They play it for the cozy vibes. Thankfully, I was able to get the game refunded. I recommend anyone on the fence to wait for a massive sale or watch gameplays before buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Just started this game but so far it is all the fun of a farm/community sim without a lot of the annoying things. Its also super cute lookings, the graphics style is very sweet and charming. The inventory system is great, tool swapping and upgrading is easy and intuitive (I have been using a controller). I love that you can easily track any of the NPCs on the map and get an on screen indicator for their location. Overall seems like its a lovely addictive farm sim that does a lot of things right. A nice relaxing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Found it relatively inaccessible. I purchased it on Switch instead, but even then I hope they remove the holding down buttons to confirm, and perhaps add an auto-fish option. As someone with wrist pain due to carpal tunnel and such, I can't really recommend this game until that's fixed. On top of that, the characters are pretty lifeless, and the game feels a bit empty, which I didn't expect for such a big pricetag. The villagers all rotate the same basic comments and dialogue, which is a shame. I dislike the current trend in newer 'cozy' games like this one and Palia for instance-- the lack of accessibility and the emptiness and lifelessness of the world is just sort of ... cold. I'll keep an eye on Switch updates and maybe come back to PC, but who knows.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels lifeless and bug filled. The story itself feels hallow. You work through a main quest line that just isn't captivating. The NPCs feel like dolls that you can pull the string for the same four dialogues. The actual farming and crafting is ok, although it's made quickly useless with a few crafting tables that basically break the games economy. The worst part of this game is how early access it feels. The UI consistently glitches when petting or feeding animals locking you into that menu and the only way to fix it is to reload the game. Upgrading the watering can into the copper can broke the game, it was immediately empty on upgrade and could never be filled no matter what method was attempted. The only remedy was to upgrade into the next tier. Certain quests seem bugged where you either can't hand in the material or - better yet - the game takes the materials but doesn't complete the quest. The crafting stations sometimes consume materials without actually making the item your looking to make, same with placing crafting stations and decor. It's closed itself a few times for seemingly no particular reason. I'm just disappointed in how incomplete the game feels. If it were early access it would be one thing but this many bugs and problems in a full release just sucks. Save yourself the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I've played about 7 hours of this game so far in the last few days. I have enjoyed it for what it is. It takes aspects of other farming sims I enjoy and build upon it. There are several things I enjoy, upgrading my tools (and the fact that it's an instant upgrade) is probably one of my favorite things lol. The world is very cute. That is not to say that is perfect by any means. There are some issues and bugs but nothing that makes it horrible to play. Fishing is a little janky but honestly I've never been big on the fishing aspect of any farming sim I've played. The art style is cutesy and I can see why some people don't like it. I feel like they designed the world and the critters and then built the npcs around how that looked. It's not bad but it took some getting used to. It does feel a bit empty but that could be because I'm so early in the story. But I haven't run out of stuff to do yet. The grindy aspect in the dungeons and farm and trying to make money have kept me busy. All in all I do recommend if you're looking for a cute little game, but I would tell people to take into account some of the small little issues it has.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as farm sims go, this is one of my favorites. Fae Farm offers an extremely cute, charming, and relaxing game. I paid $60 for it and I don't regret it at all. I think most people would prefer a cheaper price, but if you're particularly enamored by the style I'd say full price is worth it.The automatic tool switching is nice, the flower hybrid system is robust but not required, the story is adequate as well as lengthy, and the combat is neither too hard or meaningless. I love the job quests, and I've yet to feel bogged down by the main/side quests. Most paramount to me, though, is how good the game feels to play. Animations are expressive and adorable. The art style is super pleasing and the amount of customization you can unlock for your character is quite nice. Decorating your homes and farms is a great long-term goal while breeding different colored animals adds even more vibrancy to your farms. I was surprised to see some say there was no soul in this game because I feel the exact opposite.I'm not particularly fond of romance/friendship systems in these games. They're kind of a low priority for me. Fae Farm has a simple, streamlined version of these mechanics. That's great for players like me, but it might be lacking if you're looking a deep social aspect.Playing on Steam Deck and solo has been completely hassle-free. I did encounter a weird bug with optional quests at the end of chapter, but nothing adverse seem to happen because of it. Fae Farm is just a really fun farm sim. Nothing feels too overwhelming or like busy work. I'm still unlocking new things and it's been an almost addictive 30 hours. I'm looking forward to even more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying the game.....when I'm not having to force-close it and lose progress because of a specific bug: Sometimes, in menus where you are choosing a job quest, you can't exit that menu once something's selected.  Oh, it recognizes that you're right clicking/hitting B on the controller, because it plays the corresponding sound.....but it will not allow an exit of the menu.  So I'm stuck in an everlasting menu until I get sick of trying and force close, forcing me to restart the day and lose progress.  This also happens in many other menus, but you can usually get out of it in those if there is ANY other click-to-do-something option (so clicking Q to view info, etc); once it's gone to the second menu, you can (usually) get out of it. But the having to force close the app is getting tiresome.  Over the many times this happens in an irl day playing, I've lost a LOT of progress this way.  If and when they fix this bug, I'll be happy to update my review.  Until then......player beware.Also, please, as someone with some disabilities that make it slooooow to read and harder for me to find something specific I'm looking for in the storage shed: PLEASE PAUSE THE GAME IN *ALL* MENUS!  Most especially the storage shed - I was entire in-game hours each day trying to find specific things because I routinely don't see it the first (or second) time I scrolled by it.  Mail is also a good example - sometimes there's a lot to read annnnnddd.....suddenly I'm already 2 in-game hrs into my day, wasted because it doesn't pause while I read a block of text.  This is an accessibility feature that's desperately needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely need an ok button for this game. It has a lot that it does right but there’s so much it does wrong. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very enjoyable and has some quality of life things I wish to see in other games like this, but it also has a number of issues as well.Pros:- Staying up too late has no bad effects, the day will just tick over no matter where you are and take you back to your house- You can pause time when in the menu or in conversations.- The crop system is pretty cool with a base set of seeds, and the ability to magically transform those base seed into seasonal crops.- Flower breeding system!- Bug catching but with the ability to catch other 'crittters' such as crabs.- Tool upgrading doesn't steal your tool for the day and also has magical effects (Can mine a 3x3 area for example)- You can have multiple farms, similar to Trio of Towns (Story of Seasons). - Reasons to explore for unlocking crafting recipes. - You can wear fairy wings and slightly customize them. The wings also allow double jump.Cons:- You can pause however, timers on potions will tick down.- No pausing when decorating your farm, decorating your house, or even when inside your storage shed.- Haven't seen a way to turn flowers into seeds for any rearrangements of your flower beds.- Currently there are a number of bugs, some of which are shipping contracts won't get accepted, Chapter titles getting frozen on screen despite hitting A, Almanac is auto opening almost every time you access the storage shed.- Combat animations can get you trapped in enemy attacks. (Had issues in the Floating Ruins with multiple statues bombing me because attack combo animation couldn't be cancelled.)- Item stacking is ridiculous. Berries only stack to 10, but other items can stack to 100? Meaning foraging runs become nightmarish with how quickly the backpack gets full.- Day length feels way too short, especially as the game expands when you progress. Taking care of my 5 animals and my crops doesn't leave much time for doing anything else. Not to mention care for the Fae animals. By the time farm chores complete, the day is almost over.- Can only accept 1 Job Quest at a time, which is negative design choice. Some of these requests are too simple to not allow taking on multiple. Others are RNG based on if you can find the rare item etc.I give this game a 7/10. If other changes are made besides bug fixes, this game can easily be a 10/10 for me. If only bug fixes are applied 8/10. There is promise for more but there is a ton of other things that need fixing as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Farm is a cute game that tries hard to fit into the cozy game category. At first glance, it appears to be a farming sim with a cute story including the option to romance and marry a character of your choice.But upon playing you'll find that there is no variation in the characters from day to day, the conversations are unnecessary and exist only to allow you to build friendship, friendship that serves no purpose outside of letting you marry one of six possible options. If you marry someone it just changes their location, nothing is added to the story or changed by this choice. The farming isn't fully necessary, it can help you gain money but ultimately the crops do not need to change by the season and even the season-less crops disappear when the season change. The only gameplay required to advance the story is in the mines,  There are also a few bugs that make gameplay much more annoying and take away from the cozy feeling, for one the game doesn't totally  which isn't a major problem unless you need to use a potion as those will continue to tick down while the game is paused. This can cause you to fail in the mines. The animals love to follow you around on the farm and will get in your way, preventing you from being able to water crops without waiting for them to decide to move, even a device that is meant to attract them does not fix this. There are other bugs as well but those two are worth mentioning as they can really mess with your gameplay. The game is repetitive and the story is rather boring. The game is not worth anywhere near full price, if you really love cozy games and don't mind monotonous gameplay and story it may be a decent timesink, but buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- The world looks pretty nice. Its refreshing in a genre dominated by samey pixel art to get vibrant 3D in game graphics.- The movement is very fluid and allows for a lot of freedom. The first thing I did after getting control of my character was jumping into the ocean. I expected to get teleported back to the shoreline but no, you can go swimming, where upon I got sucked into a whirlpool and shot into the sky, landing on top of a nearby house. This freedom of movement is one of the most enjoyable things about this game.- You don't need to lug around all your tools and switch to each one manually. In this game your tools are always on hand and the game will automatically switch to the tool required to perform the job for the thing you are standing in front of.- Its becoming increasingly common these days but you can date any of the romanceable townsfolk, regardless of your characters gender.- The addicting game play that comes with any farm / life sim. In here I would lump fishing, critter collecting, harvesting and things of that nature - nothing revolutionary but completely fine.The Mixed:- The game offers lots of ways to decorate your house but you there are some limitations on what you can do, namely you cannot alter the position of your house at all and the area closest to your house is off limits, so you can't build a path going to your door for example. You also acquire a second almost identical farm just steps away from your first farm was odd to me. It made the game less comfy to me, if that makes sense. Feels like some sort of multiplayer idea.- I like that the game has combat but its very basic. You have one type of weapon, a staff that you use more like a club 95% of the time. It has a 3 hit combo and you just whack enemies until they disappear. Unless you are asleep at the keyboard you will never be in any danger of being defeated. I do like some of the enemy designs though.- The world is pretty small. It makes getting to where you want to go a breeze but may feel confining after spending many hours with the game.- Your bag space is pretty small, even at max upgrade level. Thankfully you have limitless storage at your farm.- You have a mana bar which is used to cast spells and do area of effect farming actions but it only replenishes by drinking mana potions. It discourages the player from using these features. It would feel better if it regenerated slowly over time.- The game is stingy with outfits until quite a ways into the game.The Bad:- Everyone looks vaguely the same due to the quite limited character creation options. Male, female, it doesnt matter. EVERYONE has the same featureless potato head, 1 of 4 bodies (2 vaguely feminine, the others masculine), no nose, and a smiley mouth. The only area where you get some variety are the eyes and their hair / choice of headwear.- I get the game is going for a lighter tone but the NPCs are soulless, oppressively inoffensive robots. After making my first character and playing for just a few minutes, one of the town merchants said they hadnt seen me in a long time. Hello, I just arrived to your island! And presumably I will be speaking with you often! Why are you saying this? This sets the stage as to what to expect from these townspeople. The ONLY way to get more than a couple lines of throwaway dialogue out of these NPCs is to go on "dates" with them, of which you can date about a dozen or so of all the NPCs. I use quotation marks because they are rarely romantic at all and just a way for the NPC to actually tell your more about themselves, which should be standard for all the NPCs.- The social aspect as a whole is poor. Festivals are little more than a way to buy some limited time items because NPCs dont actually do anything or care. Shopkeepers will NEVER move from their designated locations - they may as well be vending machines. NPCs barely acknowledge each others existence and I dont think ever actually talk to each other, just to you the player. You can increase relationship levels with NPCs but these don't actually do anything, except if the person is a love interest, in which case you can eventually marry them where they can just be an expensive decoration for your farm. Honestly I could go on and on about this aspect which is such a crucial part to keep the player immersed and subsequently spend more time in the world the developers crafted.  - The main story is completely uninteresting. It is a lifesim farming game so I expected that going in but expectations were not subverted.- There is no farm helper system here - you must do everything yourself. And if you plan to make full use of both farms the game throws at you, it can feel like a chore. And no your spouse wont help - they are the definition of trophy wife / husband and utterly useless.I am going to keep my eye on this game for any major updates - I think a lot of this can be fixed and if it does I will change my review to Positive. That said, I don't regret my purchase and its decent enough in its current state if you just want to grow vegetables with some fun bouncy movement but its hard to recommend over something like My Time at Sandrock or Sun Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 33 hours into this game and feel I can accurately rate it. Like other comments have said, there are pros and cons. The Almanac is useless. You have to google a lot of things to do them properly, and do not feel like a ten year old is going to want to do that. The pacing also makes this a great game for kids. It's simple with a lot of moving parts and it will keep anyone entertained for a while. it's cozy. the romances are simple and cute. lots of ways to make money. Now, there are cons. Tons of glitches and bugs! Not explaining things clearly that forces you to use google. Wish there was a way to add to the romances, Other than that, I love this game. I wanted a very simple, easy, cozy game and this was it. I'm going to let my son play. 4 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoy this. I will say as someone who has played a lot of Stardew, including modded, and Story of Seasons AWL (even back when it was Harvest Moon on GameCube) this game does feel hollow in comparison. Most of the features of the game have a solid base, but don't feel finished. I've read some similar reviews with everything from mentions of bugs, quality of life gripes, and general disinterest. These are all fair thoughts and I will list my own to share as hopefully constructive criticism that could be fished with updates to the game should the developers decide to flesh out the hollow areas into something more appealing. I will avoid story spoilers and will mainly be discussing functions.Bugs: Luckily, I personally haven't had many. The only one that stood out was a frozen in place banner from a season change. It would just stay there at the top of the screen at the turn of the day, despite clicking the button it indicates to continue. Open menus, walking into buildings, nothing cleared it until I exited to the main menu and rejoined. Quality of Life: Certain things like the travel in the game are great. You feel very nimble traversing the land and the waypoint system is handy. The tools auto shifting depending on the target item is great as well. I would enjoy the map more if i could hover over peoples icons and see names, not just clicking on the location for a list. It would simplify the map more, but that isn't a huge thing. I think what does make a difference is the time moving while in menu. A common complaint I have seen in other reviews. Crafting: Over all the crafting system is good. Challenging for resource accumulation while also feeling rewarding when you complete something. Same as the Cooking which goes hand in hand with the craft idea. I do wish the artisan goods had a higher selling price. Especially given the time and processing involved to get them. Not only upping their worth by making them part of the shipping contract system, which pays a high lump sum for a number of a certain good. Even then, i would enjoy the price for those to be even higher, and the goods a better value. Cooking meals seems reserved for utility, as they don't sell very highly.Relationships: Unfortunately this seems very hollow in the game. While it can mostly be ignored, for a game that has so many characters, i don't feel like i have the time or desire to talk to many of them. The romance characters i have spent time with so far, have their quirks that seem to make them worth acknowledging. But the rest. not really. The incentive to do their quests is next to nothing in the scheme of things. And they don't  carry over into the next day. So unless you can get the item easily, you might as well not take it. The reward if there is one won't be much. Dungeons: I think the approach to these places is fun and they're interesting. The first is very basic almost tutorial like. The second has some more quirks. The only enemies i find more annoying, or rather i have to pay attention to, are those that jump up over head and slam down. They are difficult to dodge in a mob setting and if you are in a chained multi attack. Other than that, enemies are mostly there to slow you down or drop a few materials.Farming: You would think i would place farming higher on this list, but frankly i haven't been planting much. Mainly there are a few irritations. In general the fertilizer idea is great. A quick grow, a variant, and a moisturizing. But some crops labeled "will grow all year" are not permanent. They will die off at the start of every season and need replanted. An inconvenience, and if you didn't bank some seeds from the crops you harvested, a costly one. It would be better if it was more intuitive, that certain crops lasted two seasons or if at least this was made more clear they had an expiration. The animals seem rather pointless. They supply certain products, but their happiness seems so pointless. They do not produce more, or higher quality materials. Nor do the color variants you can breed. Also selling certain animals earns almost no money, so breeding and selling is not a viable option for cash like in some games. All in all, i was hoping for a cute cozy style that could also feel like a fruitful endeavor, with characters that were charming. That to me is the mark of a good cozy game. Despite these flaws, i do still really like the style of the game, and the foundation for these systems. It's my hope the developers take in the feedback and make some changes that will really boost the game up and feed into it's unique charm they are tying to accomplish. If you like a game to mess around in and check out, I would still recommend this game. Form your own thoughts, and know you can still have some fun along the way.
