_childDocuments_.review: Received the game from a friend and while I still had a great time with Fae Farm, I feel like the game could have used more time to bake to justify its price point since I can see where people are coming from regarding it. In terms of time, I've put in around 60 hours and have finished the main story, taken my time decorating my farm and house, as well as breeding for farm animals with different colors as well as flower breeding and a good chunk of the job quests. There are areas, however, the game does lack in compared to other farming life sims with a lower price point.My main issues were the lack of depth from any of the NPC's, the lack of being able to do more than 1 job quest at a time, and the flower breeding. If you want any dyes to customize your furniture this is a must-do, but sometimes I felt like even though I was planting things correctly I wasn't getting my desired hybrids. But my main issue boils down to how lifeless the NPC's are. After two in-game years, I know nothing about them. I can't form any deep connections with a character that repeats the same phrases to me again and again. I got married, but the dates felt so lacking. This was the most I ever got out of character development, and it isn't saying much. You go to sit down, talk to them for a bit, and be on your way. Nothing deep or meaningful here. I would have preferred to wait longer for the game if it meant more time to work on the NPC's personalities otherwise this would have easily been an S tier farming sim for me. That said, if you don't care about the social aspect the gameplay itself was fun. I will say the farming does feel like an afterthought when compared to the dungeons, which is what you will be doing mostly to get through the main story apart from crafting your main tools and making seals to traverse the dungeons faster on each next attempt. I felt like the farming aspect was mainly to complete job quests and make money to pay to upgrade your equipment, expand your house, etc. And the artwork is GORGEOUS! If you are like me who loves that colorful and soft fantasy storybook aesthetic, you're going to love how the game tells its story in the cut scenes. And design-wise I adore the game, Overall I would put Fae Farm between an "A" and a "B" if I was doing a cozy game, farming sim tier list. I do recommend waiting for a sale if you are unsure regarding the price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Fae Farm is a game that instantly steals my breath away, captivating me right from the title screen. The stunning art and graphics, coupled with dynamic animations and a vibrant color palette, create an immersive experience that feels like a journey into a magical world.One standout feature that I adore is the extensive character customization options. The diverse range of customization choices reflects the developers' acknowledgment of the richness of diversity in the world. There were some clothing options that pleasantly surprised me, as they are rarely seen in games, and I genuinely appreciate the attention to detail in this aspect!Not only that, the major charm in Fae Farm, I believe, lies in its mystery. While wandering through Azoria, you'll encounter blocked areas and pedestals, sparking curiosity and tempting you to explore beyond the confines of your home farm. It's a gentle reminder to balance your exploration with farm responsibilities – don't forget you have a farm (and animals, later) to tend to!On the flip side, I do feel that the in-game conversations could use a bit of a spice-up. While the game's charm primarily lies in exploration and the multiplayer feature, where socializing with friends takes center stage, adding a touch of personal information or casual chit-chat with townspeople, not just those available for marriage, could create a stronger sense of connection with the game's characters.Overall, Fae Farm is a feast for the eyes and offers a myriad of activities (farming, taking care of animals, fishing, bug-catching, exploring... Did I miss one?) to keep players engrossed in its enchanting world. As my experience is based on the base game and I haven't yet tried the newest DLC, I will be updating this review as soon as I'm back from the croak croak nation!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I would wait until I finished the game to leave my impressions. It's super cute in a Korean mmo kind of way for graphics.  It has quite a few bugs (in the process of being ironed out) which seem to mostly affect platforms other than PC.  It is playable and enjoyable.  A good story line and lots to do including three dungeons of various difficulty and  three areas to explore including the fae realm, a spooky wood, and the mountains. I won't go into the story it would ruin it for you.  What I will say is provisionally it is worth buying. On the negative side I see a few people have mentioned relationships being shallow.  I don't mind that, I skip through conversations. I only married for the achievement. I have completed all the achievements except for the job quest which is misleading.  They say finish all the job quests but fail to mention that it included the long, boring, tedious grind to complete each job achievement at the end for outfits.  If you've done the grind and don't know why your achievement didn't pop this is why. I'm currently in Autumn and I have to wait until next summer to complete the fishing achievement. Kind of annoying.  If it's finish the job quests then the job quest achievements should not be included, They are achievements not quests, wording is important.It gets very vague where animal breeding is concerned when you have to breed 20 animals of varying colours. ( breed a 5 star animal get it to joyous and then apply your charm at the breeder.  I find animals already coloured seem to breed into coloured offspring more often). Growing flowers is a mystery and thank goodness unless you want  to collect wings it's optional.  The friends quests are extremely annoying and useless. They last only the day and I found most times I simply couldn't get what they wanted in time. Again another system in the game that is redundant and poorly fleshed out and gives no real friendship progression. Feel free to ignore them. Unless you are prepared ahead of time many of the market board quests will not be achievable by the end of timetable.  Terrible spawn rates on fish for example. Enough of the bad. I'll give you some tips. Farm from day 1: you only get basic crops and those are planted in different seasons to produce different crops with some magic fertiliser. Your going to need to farm your little heart out to get it to level 10 to access some of the seeds not readily available. ( Something I wish I had done and saved myself lots of work later on job quests growing the ones I missed in seasonal fields to catch up).  Save everything, believe me it will pay off.  Money? mining got me most of my cash when I fist started. Sell gemstones, sell seals, sell your spouse( boy I wish I could send his hairy face packing the free loader).  Only grow flowers if you want wings or need them for the flower festival items. ( trading flowers and coin for blueprints for clothes and decor). Do not put your fishing on simple fishing from game options. It's a guaranteed griefer.Do your job quests when they become available; switch from one to another as you come up against a quest you can't complete yet.(Another thing I wished I hadn't waited til I had finished the game to start).All things to make your game less boring and tedious in the long run.  Do not get me wrong , there is a lot to love about this game too. I'm just a bit jaded from my 'finish all job quests super grind and wait times.'I hope this was helpful

_childDocuments_.review: I won't lie, a lot of these reviews made me very apprehensive about playing this game. However, after being recommended the game by two friends I decided to give it a go, and I am SO glad that I did. Here are my takeaways:First of all, the game is beautiful. A lot of these cozy farming sim games have that pixel art style, and while those games all have a special place in my heart, its refreshing to have a game with a different and cutesy art style. The character movement is superb. I love the ability to jump off cliffs and swim in water (that also refills my watering can). I love that I don't have to worry about switching between tools to go from chopping down a tree to hitting a rock. I love that I can track where different people are on the map and even have an arrow to help guide me to them without the need for a mod. Quality of life-wise, I'm having a blast. I did struggle with fishing at first but once I got the hang of it, it was fine! (There's also an option in settings to simplify fishing)There are definitely some quirks, like with seasonal crops, but I think that's just part of playing games. Different games do things differently, and it's not that much of a hassle overall, just a small adjustment from others in the genre. I've seen a lot of complaints about the story not being too lateral, or the NPC's being dry, however this hasn't really been a concern for me. I'm playing the main story line at my own place, going through the dungeons to get materials and upgrade my tools, foraging, farming, and decorating my farm at my own pace without any real stress or deadline to do much of anything. I've never been one to really interact with NPCs a lot, and I'm glad this game doesn't shove them down my throat. The dates are cute. There are plenty of side quests. And there is plenty to do throughout your days spent in Azoria. One review said this game was like an mmo, and as someone who played a lot of World Of Warcraft over the years, I wholeheartedly disagree. This is definitely a cozy farming game. It's the perfect middle ground between stardew and animal crossing. I'm super excited to see what the developers do with it and where it goes in future updates. I definitely recommend this to people who like those cozy games like stardew or animal crossing. I think you'll have a lot of fun playing it, just don't expect it to be the exact same as those two games. If you try to compare it too heavily I think you will end up disappointed like the majority of the negative reviews. The only thing I will say is the price tag is too steep for what it is. I was gifted the game, but if I wasn't, I would probably only be willing to pay around 25 dollars for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been putting off this game for a long time now and was hoping that after the initial enthusiasm I'd get the desire to play again. But every time I log in again I realize why I don't feel like playing this game anymore.Let's take a closer look at the individual aspects: In my opinion, swimming is very well implemented - in most farming-sims you can't swim or it feels poorly made. Not in this game - it's implemented very well here.Firstly, the dynamic weather looks good and secondly, it also has effects on the character that we have to take care about and work against. We have various options how to handle this, which I think - is very well done too.We will start on an empty farm. (as always in those kind of games) We have a variety of crops and flowers that we need to take care of. There are fruit trees, flowers, enchanted crops and more.There is the possibility of breeding different variants, but I don't want to go into this further bc of spoiler.You can decorate your farm with many items. You can also make some of these items by yourself. There is a lot to be gained from - including from the crops you've grown.You can have animals to take care of, they all look pretty cute and they are all usefull for crafting, cooking etc. I like the idea behind this game. The world is beautiful and indoors the buildings in the city are really beautiful. I like the idea of mixing farming with magic and combat, thats great.. but sadly they implemented it poorly... and thats when we will talk about the bad aspects now. They just feel very very grindy here. The first hour in the mines i had fun... but after one quest like ,,go to the mines and gather .... '' after another -  i lost my motivation. This is my biggest turn down. When characters are not well made in games its okay... but when a game is praised with ,,build a connection with the villigers and even find love...'' and the characters are so poorly written and looking like cardboard cutouts you can barely speak to.. just nooo. They just giving you one quest after another and nothing more... and they dont really have background storys.The price... for 50€ i expected a lot more to be honest. The world feels empty and lifeless most of the time. The fishing is a pain in the ass and the combat is poorly made. You cannot name your character - it has you steam username from the beginning. There are many bugs - so you get stuck pretty often. After 7 hours i gave up - i just dont enjoy the game at all. I will come back to it after a while to see if they impoved the gameplay, i am honestly a bit dissapointed because the game also takes a lot of good approaches... We will see what time brings for this. If you like my review, you may also like my curator page! I would be very happy for a follow❤

I would love if we could have a slider like in other farm sims to make the days longer or shorter. I am constantly feeling like I have to rush in the mines .- Bugs. I have experienced a few UI bugs, as well as a super frustrating bug that is not allowing me to complete a quest for shipping items. Overall, this is a very pleasant experience that I highly enjoy. For the $40 price though, I feel it could definitely be improved. A lot of other games in this genre are way cheaper and offer the same amount of content if not more.

_childDocuments_.review: 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 "Magical, Whimsical, & Utterly Captivating!" 🍄✨I've played a myriad of farming sims in my time, but Fae Farm brings an enchanting twist that genuinely stands out in the crowded field. _childDocuments_.review: At them moment, I'd say "hold off for a while". The game is gorgeous, and kind of fun, but unfortunately still full of little glitches and bugs, some of which make progress, and prosperity, hard and or impossible.Unless you are just dying to have a go, hold off,  but expect some frustration. (end of review v.1.0)Well I have played another 190 odd hours since my first review, and things are not looking better, they are looking worse. The game is just FULL of bugs. There are a lot of really bad design decisions, for instance interaction with npc is basically pointless, they have nothing to say, and it doesn't yield anything; relationship building practically is pointless. The voices of the npc - let's just say I had to turn the sound OFF. Gurgling, burbling, squeeking. No comprehensible language. Considering the price I paid for this, I'd expect decent voice acting at least. Most of the crafting is entirely pointless (sigh), for instance you can make a whole lot of furniture and decorative items that don't do anything for you, just take up space. You can make many potions, but most of them you'll never use. Some ingredients only become available practically after you have finished with the game. Way too many things are never explained, for instance said ingredient: you see a shadow of a graphic without a name ... Between the bugs and glitches, and the lousy design decisions I'd say don't pay much more than 1/3 of what they are asking for this. _childDocuments_.review: My first ever review so bare with me. I would only write a review for a game if I truly felt like recommending this game to someone and I even have recommended it to my friends and played it with them. After my many hours in the game, over 100 in fact and actually playing it not going afk (yes I know I'm sad lmao). I felt that was enough to leave a good enough review, sorry if it's long! Pros & Cons:The Pros: * The tutorial is pretty decent, tells you how to do the basics. After you do the tutorial once, you are able to skip it if you decide to make a new save or join a friend.* There's lots to do, after you finish the first chapter you think oh okay this is pretty easy and you got things going good and steady, then within the next 2 chapters you unlock so much and there are so many quests you can do. Of course some you don't have to do, its purely up to you like the friend quests options but all in all, they are quite fun! * Love the design of the game. From the creatures to the characters I personally love the design. You can capture and keep as a pet the bug creatures (it just follows you around) to the farm animals that are also adorable too. I also quite like the many outfits available in the game and hope they add more to this! The game also looks stunning, the places are beautiful.* This game is also controller friendly for any PC peeps who do and would like to use a controller! I personally use a PS4 controller myself!Cons:* Sadly, yes there are bugs. One I come across which can be annoying and I only find after playing for a long period without closing the game, is where I go to build or remove something and then you cannot exit. This can also happen if you click on the ship board to see what items people want shipping wise, then you cannot get off the board. I had to waste a whole days progress cause I got stuck on the board and couldn't get off of it. My own fault though, I knew this optionally was going to happen and wanted to just keep playing and grinding. *Another bug I notice is the controls as well. Again keep in mind these two bugs I counter are after many hours of playing. I notice when I use a controller, if I am doing an action like chopping or watering a plant, picking up plants etc. It goes all funny, either really slow or doesn't interact sometimes and I have to press it more than once like it is delayed or something. Now as I write this I'm thinking maybe it could be a server issue I ain't quite sure. I also suffer this when I switch to keyboard and mouse. And no, sadly unplugging and replugging my controller back in doesn't work but after unplugging it and switching to my keyboard and mouse it is fine, sometimes for a bit and sometimes it can just act up right away and continue to be really slow with like mining and things like that and this can be quite unbareable to play.* I haven't tried recently but when the game first came out (so keep in mind when games first release they can be quite buggy) I did play with my friends and we ran into some issues. For example, not everyone got a wand aka weapon. Even if you are there for the quest, you should get a wand but for some reason like 1 of us wouldn't get one and no it wasn't in the post either. It was weird. Also I remember I kept bugging out and I would either crash and get kicked, and another issue I ran into was my controls or something of that nature would get bugged. It was quite frustrating for me since I was in charge of the farm and I couldn't even water the crops cause of the issues I was having. Sometimes the server would be laggy as well. But I haven't played on the multiplayer since the release of the game which was back in September last year and there have been updates since then so hopefully some of these issues have been fixed? * Another thing to keep in mind, is yeah the dungeons are really easy and the combat in this game isn't like mega or that difficult. It is fairly straight forward and easy. However, I feel like it suits the game as I don't believe it's meant to be a super difficult game after all in regards to combat and it's controls. I still have a lot of fun in the dungeons despite the combat being quite easy, I mean you can just stun lock your enemies into oblivion lol that is how easy it is. Also the enemies have like 1 to 2 moves at most but if you manage to land hits on them, again you can just stun lock them and they cannot do anything. I would not mind at all if they made the dungeons more difficult or the enemies harder to fight. I do enjoy a challenge! Both are really easy to sort out by saving then going off the game then going back on it, and you can just continue playing it for many hours. This game has a lot of content, for the price I do think its worth it. The game isn't perfect so I am very forgiving in regards to these bugs. There are a few more but they are minors ones that don't really impact your game, like one of them is a visual thing, in the second barn you get for the cows and sheep the flooring is faded out and bugged. I hope there are more DLC's to come! There is so much more they can do with this game and I look forward to finishing more chapters, do not want this story to end!

_childDocuments_.review: Had to double check the Store to see if this game was Early Access. The game feels unfinished. For a game that everyone seemed to be pushing "Harvest Moon meets Stardew meets Sun Haven" it truly lacks what most find the most enjoyable about those games, The NPCs. I could go on and on about that so I will just list my pros and cons. Pro:-Casual-Dynamic Farming -In depth Hybrid Flowers-Goth Fae Girl-I can have wings -Gems make moneyCons:-Boring NPCs-Annoying Player Character (You can silence but that just makes it dull)-Lack of Tutorials or explanation (I did not realize seasonal crops are made by using certain fertilizer until winter) This also ties in with boring NPCs as they do not help. -Lack of feminine clothing. (Large portion of the Hair and clothing are non-binary focused which tends to sway towards a more masculine side)-Restrictive Decorating (Only gives you a square portion of the farm and inside the house) -Can't wear a "wig" with accessories (Cat ears, bunny ears, etc)Overall I have had a lot of fun and distraction with this game. I can't wait to see the patches that the Devs will come out with. I did not post about the bugs and glitches as for the most part, the team seems to be actively fixing and working out the kinks. It's definitely not a game that should be turned down.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally enjoy this game a lot. The graphics are adorable and the music is great. The gameplay is simple enough to not be stressful but still fun, especially the mines. In the beginning it might seem like you can barely sell things but you can upgrade your produce stands and it is kind of endearing to see everything you are selling lined up like that on a table.The only thing  that bothers me slightly is that the menus feel a bit weird at times but I suspect that this happened to streamline the menus with between the ports. You definitely need to listen to the NPCs when they give you a quest otherwise it can be a bit hard to figure out how to do things, but I have not run into something that I couldn't figure out with a little bit of trial and error. Is it a world changing game? No, definitely not. But it is fun and addictive.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game Is very beautiful and fun, I love It! But It's hard to recommenced with how extremely buggy It Is. My co-op partner seems to have A LOT more and worse bugs than I do, but I'm still getting a lot. It really wares down the experience.We were crafting a lot of expensive things, and instead of using the work bench, I guess the game decided our workbench was a bush and just destroyed it along with all the stuff we were crafting? Fun.My friend constantly gets a bugged camera angle, or literally stuck to where he has to restart the game. The wedding cutscene didn't work AT ALL, stuff that we break constantly flies across the map, sometimes the crops get stuck mid-harvest so you have to wait for the next day to pick  them. My friends also stuck in a red outfit now for some reason?There's A LOT of other bugs I know I'm forgetting about right now. I think there's also a lot of quality of life changes the game could use, the higher level mines are really inconvenient and feel as though they are designed to WASTE your time, marriage candidates are all boring, bland and ugly (all brown and green colour pallets despite the fact the game Is meant to be all magical and fairy themed?), and basically don't acknowledge you once married and do nothing. You have to buy colours to use and only have a selection of about 6 (white and black only) from the get go. Almost every flower, crop and tree in the game has to be cross-bred which Is a kinda cool idea but gets super annoying and inconvenient if you're not into the mechanic.I think the character customisation Is nice in terms of accessibility, with many black and religious hairstyles, but feels very lacking IMO. There aren't many nice hair styles, not many colours to choose from that aren't muddy and dark (AGAIN, Its a fairy game, why can't we pick brighter colours?) and some hair has accessories with them, but I don't believe you can change the colour of the accessories? Which Is ass. Also hats in this game mostly come with 1 pre-set hairstyle, they do not adjust to the hair you pick.The progression in terms of main story quests feels.. off.. It's like there are big milestones In the story that require you to donate things, but they almost get EASIER over time. It feels very unbalanced in terms of difficulty. For example, one of the requests near the end game asks for 15 coal.. Something you can mine in 2 veins, and It spawns on floor 1 of the first mine you unlock? You probably have 100's of coal by this point. In other regards, some job quests feel stupidly HARD, like you can finish a whole line of these quests for fishing pretty easily, and get stuck near the start of the farming one.There's a quest you unlock at the start of the game, and It's BUGGED to this day, almost 2-3 months after release? Okay.. The game just feels very bug-riddled and lack-luster in areas, and like it could use a lot of fixing and improvements. I do think It's very gorgeous, addicting and fun, but It's hard to reccomend It with the price tag, which used to but almost DOUBLE the price on launch which is hilarious.I 100% reccomend the game, but only after they bother to fix ALL the bugs and problems that It has. For now, If you want to play It, do It with these issues In mind, and grab It on a sale.

I normally get tired of farming sims because they feel unchanging besides the season but Fae Farm always has a lot to do. I think that it is work the cost of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly cute and fun, BUT there are so so so many things I wish were improved. My biggest issue is being unable to have multiple Job Quests - which meant I kind of ignored them until Id done everything else, and now Im having to power through them. It would make so much more sense to have them all accessible, allowing you to garden, fish, bug hunt, etc at the same time.I also find the flower production incredibly frustrating. Why did the flower girl only have one quest? If shed had Job Quests as well, it could teach you how to cross produce normal and fae flowers effectively. Ive finished most everything else and still have, like, 30 flower colors to unlock. Which means I havent unlocked ANY of the dyes! Once you marry a villager, they contribute NOTHING, they dont even have new dialogue! They show up to the wedding in their normal clothes too haha. Why doesn't the Charm spell "pet" all your animals? That seems like a no brainer. Speaking of animals, I get having the two tiered farms with separate barns, but WHY are you making me go to the Fae Realm just to see those animals too?? It takes me half the day just to deal with the animals, let alone tending the farm itself. And when you buy charms to change their colors for breeding, it should ALWAYS work. Ive wasted so many polished gems trying to get different colored animals.ANYWAY, as you can see, theres a lot that this game could improve upon. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game, especially the graphics. They're so colorful and lovely to look at. The game itself is very cute and relaxing as is the music. I've not encountered any bugs so far, aside from the shipping quests only working properly half of the time, and everything runs smoothly on my PC and Steam Deck (with default settings). I think I'm drawn to this game more than any other farming sim right now because of the inclusion of magic and the fantasy setting. I really dig games that have magic in them and there aren't too many out there these days. I've never really been into romancing in these types of games, nor have I ever felt the need to become friends with everyone, so the dialogue doesn't bother me, nor does the lack of romantic interests, but I can see why people who are into that would be really turned off by it in this game. The NPCs really are pretty flat, but it doesn't matter much to me since that's not my main interest point of the game. I enjoy running around and collecting bugs, it's really relaxing and although fishing was really cumbersome for me at first, now that I've got it down I enjoy it too. Though the "simple mode" for fishing truly doesn't make it anymore easier to catch the fish, just enables you to press a button once to hold/release the line instead of holding it down to reel in. Also being able to jump into the water and swim, plus jump anywhere you want or climb the rocks is awesome too, it's not something you see in many games like this. Most have invisible barriers keeping you from doing any of that. Character creation is okay in my opinion. I'm not bothered by much except the fact that your character's mouth is where its nose should be. They remind me of the characters in Portal Knights, right down to the noises they make. I do wish there were more hairstyles though, particularly wavy ones.The keys are a little weird, most can be rebound, though some of them can't, and that's annoying to me so I play with my controller and honestly, you can tell it's really made to be played that way and keys were sort of an afterthought. Apparently there's an update in progress that will fix the key binding issues, but until then, controller it is. It also took me a hot minute to get used to not being able to turn the camera. It felt so weird and unnatural at first, but after adjusting to it, it's fine now and I don't try to manually turn it anymore.Price wise - if I'm honest I feel like it should be a $30 game at most, but I did buy it and I am enjoying it at its current price, so I guess $40 was worth it to me.That aside, there are a few things I don't like and think should be changed:1. NPC sounds. PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD give us an option to mute them. It's funny and cute the first three or four times they giggle or laugh whenever you talk to them, but after that it really starts to get to you. It really makes me not want to even bother talking to any of them just so I can avoid that laughter. Thankfully there is an option while creating your character that lets you silence yours, and trust me, you'll WANT to.2. The red exclamation mark on the main screen alerting you to a new almanac entry/inventory item, etc. It doesn't go away until you view every single thing that has the mark on it in the book or your inventory. It's just a minor thing, but it annoys me, especially because there are always a crud ton of things popping up and being added to the book all of the time. I like my main interface to be as clean as it can be.3. Speaking of interface, I do like how the quests are on the left side of the screen so I can track them, but I do not like how they constantly pulsate when I have something to turn in, do, or complete. It's distracting as heck and really takes me out of my moment. It's already showing on the screen I've completed what I need to to finish the quest, let me turn it in when I want to. Don't push me by pulsating constantly until I do. I feel like I'm being rushed to hurry up and complete things. I just wanna chill, yo!4. There needs to be a sort inventory option. It drives me nuts that things are all over the place in my backpack if I consume an item or sell it.Anyway, I do recommend the game to others who are looking for something just a tiny bit different than other farming sims. The game loop, although it gets repetitive, is still so satisfying, and you don't have to switch between tools while cutting trees, breaking rocks, etc, it does it for you. You start off with a good amount of energy too that doesn't run out quickly at all, and though you can cook things to regain it, there are also little green orbs all over the world you can collect while running about that give energy back too. I really liked that. Also being able to craft items from storage is a huge plus. I hope other games like this in the future take notes, because I never want to go back to switching tools or having to remove items from storage again.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game but there are some horrible issues that need looking at. I play using a controller, not mouse and keyboard.1. [FIXED] Every time you open storage, it opens up the encyclopedia and you have to "go back" two times to get to storage.2. A villager walked past me while I was fishing and I lost the fish. This is because the reel button is the same as talk. You shouldn't be able to interact with anything else in the world while you are fishing.3. There shouldn't be a countdown forcing you to wait every time you sleep. This is stupid and pointless. If I want to scrutinize my sales for the day, I'll take the time to do so. Don't force me to.4. Potion and food buffs still actively count down their effects while in inventory despite time being stopped. This includes the Fairbreath Potion that keeps you alive in the Floating Ruins. Additionally, the Miasma effect in the Floating Ruins gets applied while you are in your inventory when the Fairbreath Potion effect runs out. Despite time being stopped.5. Initial dialogues with every NPC is all the same copy and paste, they're all thanking you for cutting the thorny vines. While it makes sense for most NPCs, this is out of place and immersion breaking in many sequences.6. The game doesn't do a good job of explaining how flower breeding/hybridizing works, instead it expects you to have already played Animal Crossing: New Horizons.7. The game doesn't do a good job of explaining that you have to use a certain kind of fertilizer to grow seasonal crops.8. _childDocuments_.review: First time liking a game enough to type out a real review.  I have 40+ hours in of real game time and the Pros really outweigh any cons for me.  I don't find myself skipping days or feeling like I can't get enough ingredients to craft things.Pros:- You are auto-transported to your house at midnight.  NO penalties.  You aren't losing hours by waking up late the next day.  You aren't docked stamina.  You aren't losing the items you were collecting.  It is a beautiful thing.- Catching bugs is actually useful because they give you items for crafting potions.  I actually find myself USING potions as well because the ingredients are very easy to come by.- You don't *have* to fight the monsters in the dungeons.  You can use invisible potions and just gather what you need.  The monsters don't drop anything specific to them, they just drop the same items you'll find in the dungeon by gathering.- You can move anything on your farm (trees, flowers, crops).  Makes flower breeding easier and gives you the freedom to rearrange anytime you want without losing the crop/tree/etc.- You can "reclaim" makers/crafted items to get the materials back.- Shops are open basically all day every day until like 10pm at night.Cons:- Animals don't really stay near the animal markers you can place.  They constantly run after you and I find myself petting them when I'm just trying to water crops or harvest.- There's a bit of a delay when trying to gather from animals and targeting the right animal if it's in a group can be a little challenging.- While you can pause time by hitting Escape whatever food/potion effect you have on will continue to deplete.
_childDocuments_.name: Fae Farm

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game. A lot. And I plan to keep playing at some point.That said, I think several things need to be known:-Bug: The shipping contracts, which would a great source of income, do not work. You can complete the first one for the quest, but afterwords it cancels when attempting to accept.-Oversight: Even in single player, the game timer does not pause while doing anything other than chatting. It runs while decorating your house, looking at the map, and navigating some (not all) menus.-Oversight: There are only six romance options: three guys (one fae), two girls (one fae), and one non-binary person. You only know the two guys for the first several days of game play, and even talking to them raises their romance level. Additionally, there's no motivating factor to befriend any NPCs. It brings no apparent benefits, and they just aren't interesting.-Oversight: The tool bar resets to default constantly. For example: you are on a quest that involves killing monsters repeatedly, and you are running through the mines with your weapon out. Each time you enter a room, it will cycle you back to the tools (pick/shovel/harvest) instead of leaving the weapon (wand) out.-Bug: The issue with tool cycling also occurs when receiving messages at the top of the screen in some cases. This is very inconvenient when catching bugs at night, where many messages are likely to occur at the top of the screen.-Bug: Quests which have already completed will sometimes randomly complete a second time while completing other quests.-Oversight: Friend quests disappear at the end of the day, despite requiring a large number of resources. This is especially harrowing when someone wants you to go find a bug that is somewhat rare and only shows up at night, but you just don't have it on you right now.-Bug: The game cannot consistently switch targets properly. This sometimes results in one farm animal receiving attention repeatedly, or being unable to brush it after petting, or grass being cut down unintentionally while attempting to interact with an object, or an object opening when attempting to water/harvest crops.-Oversight: The preferred sort in the house storage doesn't save. It defaults to alphabetical, and must be changed every time it is opened if you prefer seeing things grouped together.There's things that I really love.-The cooking system is really interesting, and I like that there are different effects on some drinks. I do wish there was more variety — all drinks that I currently have access to have the same longevity, making the effects feel repetitious over time, and makes some drinks less worth making.-The various house decorations boost stats, which is a fun system. I wish this had been fleshed out more.-I genuinely appreciate that the tools cycle to the correct one on its own without needing to fiddle for the correct one each time.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game? In its current state, I have to say 'no', and it hurts me to do so. After playing for several hours, and getting into summer season, I have already stumbled over several rather large bugs that make the game more of a headache then a fun past time, even making me have to reload several times to fix some. I could recommend it, if the bugs were fixed to make it less of a chore to play, or if you could get it on a MAD discount with its current build. I will update this review if the bugs are fixed.....Bugs include:- not being able to complete quests (the early gave 'wave to your animal' will NOT finish not even with a game restart and replay to that point. Animals will respond to the wave, come over to interact but it will not complete the quest). -the house LR and RR icons for checking which furniture is going to what stat will get stuck on screen for no reason, normally in the middle of fishing. The only fix is a reload of game.-the 'second house' you unlock, once updated can NOT be built in. Reloading game and restarting day do not fix, I now have a nice empty house of nothing. You can open the build menu, click the item, and it goes back to the game, no grid, no item.-Several times NPCs have bugged out mid talking and just.... walked off.... cant complete the quests I was in the middle of doing with them, forcing a restart of game/day to fix.-Fishing/bug catching, while fun has its own set of bugs, fish getting stuck in rocks/ piers and being 'unable' to complete the reel in, so you have to abort. Bugs can be really rough to catch, even with level 12 bug catching and the 'top' net, but only sometimes, making it into a frantic waving of the net all over in hopes it will register.-pick-ups will also bug out, you might go to pick up a turnip, or a sand dollar, and they half pull then stop.... that is it, just floating there. You can keep pulling at it, and you do the pull animation, lose your energy, but nothing, just... there. Way to fix is reload day, or let day complete and the next day pull the still floating item, it will work. -farm animals have a bad habit of not staying near the lure you build and place, to the point I have found them just wandering off the farm into town, or toward the path to the other animal farms. This makes daily care a touch harder playing hide and go seek to get them first. There are some complaints as well to the game, not bugs, just complaints:-WHY ARE THERE SO MANY?! I currently have 12 different stations built on my farm to be able to make everything I need. Each day is a chore of 'move from point A to B , take B to C" before I can even get the end items to use/sell.-The Pause menu is almost a joke? Yes it stops time... if you pull it from main menu or happen to be looking in your bag/ storage shed but that is about it. Building? Time is passing, Moving items? Time is ticking, Trying to cook items? Better hurry up! -Along the same complaint as before, the pause menu doesn't stop some things IN game even if it does stop time. Enemies/characters will still move around, so watch it if you pause in the dungeons you aren't safe. Pausing does not stop the timers on potions you use, pause to check something, better have extra potions because they are gone when you get back! Now that isn't to say its ALL bad, there are some upsides to the game!-having all the main tools on a single button makes farming a breeze! Water and harvest all with a click. Go from clearing weeds to rocks then trees without having to rotate which tool you have. Add in that NONE of the tools you have to use take up bag space and its a breath of fresh air to the genre. -Having the same crops work in all seasons makes prepping for 'next season' a touch easier, some might say the game is 'simple' for it, but I like it. Add in you have to figure how to change those crops to special types? Adds a nice flavor to things. -controller support has been added and seems to work pretty smoothly (using pro controller currently) without input lag or troubles. -load times for PC seem very good, graphics are bright colorful and cute, giving that nice cozy feelings. As for multiplayer, since I have not tried it, I can not say for sure how it is. I do hope to try it at some point, again will update the review if I do get a chance to. Lastly, as of right now, the DLC doesn't seem worth it? I feel this is because it never was "DLC" it was "add on patches" to start, but when people complained about the cost of the game being 60 dollars, for steam it got split off into 'base game' and became 'DLC'. Do NOT get the DLC expecting a huge area and new stuff, it feels more like just an add on area that was polished up, and doesn't bring anything special to the table as of right now. That might change when the second 'DLC" comes out, but we shall have to wait and see.

_childDocuments_.review: *Recommended only if you buy it on sale*I’ve played over 100 hours of this game and thought I’d share my experience. I played this on PC using a controller so I won’t be referencing mouse and keyboard controls. I know using different controls can be easier than others but this is what I experienced.Fae Farm is a beautiful game, the different farms that you have, each has their own unique style and the scenery is amazing. Beautiful music. Definitely a chill game. But despite its looks, I feel it is severely lacking in several areas which I’ll explain below. I am a huge Stardew Valley fan so some of these might be comparisons but I feel would improve quality of life for the game tremendously.First off, the story is basic and generic, nothing wrong with it, you end up in a land that becomes your new home and you get your first farm. There are simple fetch quests and job quests that you can complete along with the story if you plan it right. Can’t really go wrong here except sometimes when doing the story quests, it gives you no direction in some parts on how to advance so you’re running around like a jack@$$ trying to find the next NPC that you have to talk to. Some of the job quests can be completed by dropping the items that you need and picking them back up again. Which is kind of a nice exploit.The NPCs are another thing that drove me nuts, I know it’s not a huge deal with farming games in general of them having a lot of dialogue, but the characters are so bland and such a waste of time it’s almost sad to look at. They had no substance to them at all. The romance choices are so awful you might as well stay single. But if you do decide to get married, like I did, it was a glitchy mess. So here’s what happened with weddings in my game:I ended up having two weddings. You have to pay the marriage fee in order to get married in the first place, never got a chance to wear wedding attire thinking I had time to do it later. But when starting up the next day, it automatically threw me into the wedding cutscenes… the text during the wedding had placeholder text for your character name.. after the wedding, I decided to go back to the NPC to pay for the wedding fee and ended up having ANOTHER wedding where the text was correct and I was able to pick out my clothes. No clue how they messed that up. Oh and not to mention if you have any love interests prior to getting married, the quests for them are stuck on your quest log forever. Also, after you get married there is no new dialogue for your spouse whatsoever. Can’t we get at least one new line of dialogue? Also your spouse does absolutely nothing besides walking around on the farm/town. My husband in game feels more absent than my father who went to go get cigarettes when I was 5. He’s less useful than using the popcorn button on a microwave.Anyways, now with farming and tending to your animals, there are some major annoyances here. First off, I’m still waiting for a fix on the animal lure as it just doesn’t work and hasn’t been fixed since the game released. So animals get in your way while you are trying to harvest/water crops. If you even get too close to a chicken by one pixel, it f***ks your whole day up.When petting/brushing/milking/shearing animals is annoying because the prompts do not automatically pop up when next to them. After milking a cow for example, the options to pet or brush do not pop up afterwards, you have to step back and go up to the animal for it to register. Some animals will bum rush you as soon as they come outside while you’re taking care of your crops and they will warp right in front of you and you start petting them instead of watering or harvesting them. I also wish they had sprinklers in the game to help save time during the day.Dungeons in the game are pretty basic, enemies can be annoying in the beginning but not too bad. However when using potions in the later dungeons, while paused or in a crafting menu, the potions are still depleting. Same with crafting benches, while using them the game does not pause. They fixed the pause issue with the storage but other areas would be nice considering how quickly the day goes by.There are a lot of other glitches in the game that sometimes made the game unplayable for me and had to save and quit to desktop to get it to work properly again.In the end, I wouldn’t recommend buying this game unless it’s on sale, I would even say it’s worth only $30-$35 (can’t believe they tried to sell this for $60). And without knowing what the DLC will be like, I can’t say if that’s a good deal until we know what the new content is and if they will fix a lot of known issues in the game. I may change my review later after the two DLCs come out. Despite all these problems that I had, I can agree that the game is fun and addicting but wish it had a lot more to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect farming simulator for the perfect cozy gamer.Between cute graphics, adorable game world design and gameplay that seems made for extreme relaxation, Fae Farm seems like the perfect title for all those gamers who love playing with maximum tranquility mixed with what I like to call " cuteness”.Basically, everything you would expect in a game heavily inspired by Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing: you can prepare the soil and plant seeds, collect fruit and vegetables to eat or sell, you can catch fish and catch insects, and you can build useful tools or objects to furnish your home.The game excels is in how it makes doing all of these tasks extremely simple.Changing instruments requires pressing a key or at most two; on the map it is possible to trace the position of a character and reach him in an instant. Above all, the ability to run, dive and jump more or less anywhere makes moving across the island much more immediate than in many other similar games.However, the freedom to explore is limited by walls of brambles and other obstacles, and it will be necessary to face small dungeons to be able to bring the area back to normal.As you obtain new furniture and objects, your performance in battle also improves, as the health and stamina indicator increases, as does the damage inflicted.The pace of the game is marked by the passing of the days and the presence of numerous missions to complete, both main and secondary.The game can be divided into two broad areas, namely daily life in Azoria and dungeon exploration.In Azoria we will be able to interact with the environment through different tools, all typical of this genre of games: we will be able to fish with our fishing rod, use our shovel to dig, the scythe to cut bushes, the ax to cut down trees and make wood and so on.The role-playing component is very strong: each tool can be improved several times and we will also receive experience for each completed action; for example, catching a butterfly will earn us x experience points in the "animal catching" field, and for each level we will improve our skill with the net.However, the impression is that the fights were inserted more to add a further activity to the already long list of the game.In the first few hours you don't really realize how many things you can do in Fae Farm and it's only when you start to reach new locations and unlock additional farms that you get an idea of the amount of systems and content Fae Farm could have been a exceptional exponent of its genre, except that the developers have sensationally underestimated one of the most important aspects in a game that promises to make you live a life inside a village: the cast of characters.All the inhabitants of Azoria are dummies that are impossible to get attached to.Yes, they have their uses, they buy and sell items, assign missions and give useful information on how the game works.However, they have no personality, tend to always be cheerful and condescending, never tell interesting stories and do not seem to have a character of their own.In Animal Crossing the other inhabitants can have a bad day, be a little sad and share little stories that make their tastes better known; They could have been more or less nice to us. We had a crush on someone and we hated someone else.In Fae Farm this feeling is completely missing and even the possibility of marrying someone therefore becomes useless, put there just for the sake of it.It's a real shame that a game that fails to characterize the characters is a game that instead excels in their personalization and inclusiveness: the editor allows you to modify the aesthetics of your alter ego regardless of any gender distinction, you can largely modify the build, and it is possible to wear a hijab or turban from the start.This diversity is also seen in the appearance of the other inhabitants, and this is precisely why it is sad to see such a disappointing writing job.VerdictAlready in the preview phase it was understood that Fae Farm would be a good game and this long-distance test did nothing but confirm those initial sensations. Phoenix Labs has in fact created a simple farm sim experience, accessible to everyone and not without light role-playing and survival elements that make it a truly complete and enjoyable exponent of the genre. More could have been done on the "human" side and increased the level of challenge a bit, but even so Fae Farm fully convinces.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most adorable game I've played so far. It brought me so much joy it easily became my 4th perfect game, but I also understand the negative feedback. It's definitely not a 40€ game, it actually feels like an Early Access Indie, which I don't mind too much because I'm used to playing those. I bought it (and later the DLCs) on sale though and would advise to do the same. I'll make a list of the different aspects of the game, beginning with the bad ones:The main reason why this feels like Early Access. The social aspect feels extremely barebone. NPCs have like 3 different lines each they rotate through, they still greet you like a stranger after regularly talking to them for a year, keep mentioning the thorns you cleared a year ago before saving the entire island, the romance options each have 1 personality trait and 1 interest their entire being revolves around, birthdays do literally nothing, marriage does nothing except that your spouse hangs out in your main home and "old flames" that get dumped by your marriage act like nothing ever happened. I'm not a very social person and don't care too much about it but if socializing is important to you it would probably be better to look into other games. There are a few, from visual ones over Interfaces sometimes messing up to really annoying ones, like field watering and flower growth stages getting messed up or your wedding not happening at all. I forwarded the wedding bug to the devs and they seem to be interested in solving the problem so l have hope there will be fixes.I got the impression that certain things were done without thinking about them too much. These being:. They are just "bring me item x" and you get nothing in return. I think it doesnt even progress the relationship but can't really check. Not that this would change much xD have a weird timing with what they give you. Like, each season Festival gives you an outfit for the respective season although they are at the very last day of that season. So you gotta run around in your autumn outfit the entire winter until you can buy the winter outfit on the very last day with spring starting the next morning. Thats even worse if you consider that you play through the entire storyline in less than a year and be done with the game before year 2 starts. Some festival rewards also have impossible requirements like the vibrant purple color palette that is only buyable on Fae Festival Day in winter requiring 10 purple tulips. You can't breed them that fast because flower breeding is  horribly slow, so I basically waited through another year with nothing to do to get collectibles I couldn't really use anymore because I'm done with the game. There is no . You can have 1 environmental effect (like heat resistance) plus another more short timed one and if you drink another potion it will overwrite the effect. Means you can't have both invisibility and movement speed for example and if you permanently use speed but wanna use a little whirlwind to gather crops inbetween you have to renew the speed pot afterwards.  aren't really well thought through. For example the magic job line wants you to combat and complete dungeons and usually goes through them in chronological order. But after the "use spell X" quest for the spell you get for finishing the dungeon, it gives you a "dispatch 30 jumbles" quest for that same dungeon, so sending you back after already completing it. Or the third alchemy quest wants you to craft a potion that you need a late game ingredient for. And other things like that.  is an interesting system but it restricts you a lot in how you can furnish your house because you want all of them to get the passive effects and they take a lot of space. You also need to have that house as your main home to get the effects which makes it worse. I basically just puzzle the Cozys into the upstairs room and only actively use the downstairs rooms. could be better. Having the wells next to the animal homes on the first 2 farms is "unfortunate" because you wanna have your crop fields close to the well but dont want your animals running around your fields. That being said, animals interfere with you trying to interact with anything else which is very annoying.  seem very random sometimes. For example, most of the alchemy potions are worth less than what you would get for the ingredients but a few are quite profitable and there is no pattern. Like, small and medium zoom potions for example give you a profit, the large ones a loss, others are the other way round and several kinds are losses in all sizes. Cooking also isn't profitable, basically just making jewels is (which I dont mind because I love shinies <3)The staff is the one weapon you can use against enemies and (sadly) works like a close combat blunt weapon. You learn spells as you progress the story which can also be used for certain things outside of combat, but they use too much mana to be effectively used for combat. Personally I'm the avoid-combat-type of person and I like that this is absolutely doable because enemies are only in the dungeons and you can use invisibility pots to sneak past them. They also don't drop any key items so fighting is only required for the magic job quests. The fighting mechanic itself is ok I guess? The only annoying thing I noticed is that some animations (like mining or using a potion) take quite long and make you immobile so you often get hit by enemy attacks without being able to dodge. What is rather unique I think and very handy is that your  (pickaxe, axe, water can, sickle, shovel) are selected automatically depending an what you target, so you just have the fishing rod, critter net and staff (and conch if you have the DLC) seperate and can rotate through them rather fast. In dungeons you even only have the staff and tool to switch around. They also don't take any inventory slots.  is nearly exclusively built, not bought and will transform back into the ingredient materials if you disassemble them. Generally nice, certain furnishings that you need in quantity like fences and rugs use a LOT of material though. Furniture placement is restricted to a grid system and the 4 cardinal directions, like in Animal Crossing. What I really like is that you can dye most of the furniture (and clothes) freely with your unlocked palettes, what I dislike is that this excludes wall items and that those can only be put on the back walls of your house. This game is very LGBTQ and poc friendly and mostly cruelty free (All enemies are animated objects, you can't kill farm animals). Fishing (a very cruel way to kill something) still being included is a weird exception of that rule but apparently every game needs to have this horribly boring mechanic ^^' Sadly you even need it to progress the storyline. Theres a bit of disability representation too, all social interactions are wholesome and in general the FF world is a nearly perfect fairytale utopia. For everyone except fishes. General aesthetics and theme, cuteness, customization options, magic, lack of cruelty and pace of progression and discoveries tick all the right boxes for me. I was looking for a peaceful, pretty world to build up a cozy life in and got exactly that. The only wishes it leaves me with is fixing some of the mentioned problems and more content ^-^Sell! No need to hoard anything except materials and flowers. Look up requirements for festival purchases early though, dont wanna wait a year because you're missing 1 item. Breed flowers and farm animals asap. Its free and you will need the progression.Have fun :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game! I'm not sure where the negativity I've been seeing is coming from. Despite what people claim, it is NOT a direct Stardew-clone. While it is a farming/crafting/mining sim in the same way, both the style and feel of the game are extremely different. Fae Farm reads younger, certainly, but that isn't bad, just different. Try to think of it as a Stardew meets Animal Crossing, in terms of vibes. I've barely scraped the surface, but I'm so impressed with how enjoyable they've made even basic tasks like fishing. I can't wait to learn more magic and dig deeper into this world. Note: I'm playing on Steam Deck, and it's absolutely fantastic. Looks great, controls feel good, no performance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, but I can't, not for this price-tag. There are a lot of things to like about this game, and if these issues are dealt with, I'll really enjoy this game a lot, but until then, it's just not worth the money. I'll briefly go over some of my gripes, which are in two categories: bugs and unintended things that could get patched, and intended game elements that the devs would need to recognize as not great in order to even begin to change.  Addendum: Since first writing my review, I have continued playing. I currently have 70 hours in the game. This probably says more about my personality than it does about the game, BUT it also is a strong indication that I really do want to love it.  And I give the devs credit for making something compelling enough to keep me in for this long.  But that's not necessarily a good thing considering how I actually felt while I was playing. I'm struggling to think of a good analogy to describe my experience.  It's NOT like when you see the gorgeous pictures of the tall, perfectly proportioned burgers on a restaurant's menu but then the burger you get is a flaccid grey mess... It's more like if the burger you got actually looked EXACTLY like the picture, but then when you excitedly bite into it, you realize that it looks like that because they used all the advertising tricks that make the food LOOK good in the burger they serve customers... So like, there's actual cardboard hidden in it to make it look bigger, the melting cheese has been mixed with glue, the "grill marks" are painted on with shoe-polish, etc. Bugs and glitches:1.  Interacting with farm animals is so irritating.  When animals are in close proximity, it's impossible to single one out to pet it or brush it.  Even when they are alone, their hitboxes seem impossible to figure out. Often, I will be far away from any animals just trying to water crops, and an animal will be inexplicably dragged over to me as if I had clicked on it. Then, as that animal is now on my crops, it makes working on them incredibly difficult. It's small, but happens enough to be extremely annoying.2. After unlocking the Fae Farm and moving there, breeding became glitched and would not work, and shortly after, my Fae animals also just stopped creating resources at all. They have filled bars (although not many since I can't breed them), but they still don't produce. 3. Any time I move from one screen to another (i.e. entering a building or using a waypoint) there is a significant chance that the game will glitch out and put me in front of Townhall. This would be annoying enough, except while in the loading screen, the in-game timer is still going.  So not only am I teleported far away from where I want to go, but I've also lost a decent portion of the in-game day. There have been many days when I leave my farm around 8am trying to go straight to the Volcano dungeon, which should take less than an in-game hour, but through multiple time-consuming glitches, I don't end up getting into the dungeon until 3pm or later.  Not by getting distracted and wandering, but just because of glitches. EDIT: I found a work-around to this, so if anyone else is having the same issue try this: right after you enter a door or choose a destination in a waypoint, hit the hotkey to open your inventory. For some reason, that seems to prevent the game from brainfarting itself into forgetting where you want to go. I hope it works for you all, too.4. The latest bug that happened completely gutted my max health, stamina, and mana.  I woke up one morning and all my stats were tiny.  I tried reclaiming all my cozy furniture and replacing it, but it didn't do anything.  With this glitch, I run out of stamina in just a few actions, I will get killed in one or two hits from the Volcano enemies, and I have to drink a potion after each use of any of my spells. It's awful.EDIT: After more experimentation, it seems reclaiming then replacing all your furniture actually DOES seem to work to reset the stats... after you sleep.  You lose a day, but hopefully that won't affect you too much.  Now for the intended game elements that are just not fun:1. NPCs are BORING. They are all so similar, with basically the exact same conversations, the exact same quests, the exact same consequences on the player.  Some of the job quests are kinda unique and enjoyable, but most of the friend quests or side-quests are complete wastes of time. 2. Marriage is absolutely awful in this game.  The dating stuff is kinda cool, and could have potential, but then as soon as you actually get married, everything stops. You can no longer give gifts to your spouse, or interact with them in any way other than "chatting". They "move in" with you, but that just means that they spawn outside your house in the morning. They cannot even enter the house.  They wander around your farm with animations that look like they are interacting with stuff, but they do NOTHING. I feel bad for marrying my spouse because their life became WAY worse afterward. At least before we got married, she would wander aimlessly around the island, aimlessly swinging a bugnet at nothing once in awhile. Afterwards, she doesn't even do that.3. On the surface, there are a ton of interesting critters, fish, crops, items, etc and that is exciting.  But then you realize that there are really just a few CATEGORIES of things and all the individual members are exactly the same.  All "greens" like arugula or dandelions are exactly the same.  Berries?  All the same.  Most of the fish?  All the same.  When I first started the game, I felt like there was a rich world of many different things to explore, but the more I play the game, the more I realize that this is just a thin veneer painted over one tiny gameplay loop.  If you have played the first season, and the first dungeon... that's it.  Just imagine that, again and again, with ever so slightly different skins... and that's EVERYTHING. EDIT: 4. I finally got the spell that opens those super enticing lava-glyph doors that are scattered across the island that had me really wondering how to open them, what was behind them, what cool new places and adventures they must lead to and.......  the word "anti-climatic" can't even begin to describe how ridiculously disappointing this is.  It was a New Year's Eve ball-drop countdown where the "ball" turns out to be a single egg dropped on your head and immediately begins to stink that sulfur--ass stank. Ai yai yai.I think this game has potential to be good.  The art design, the amount of options for decorations, the quality of life choices the devs have made... all are wonderful. But the story, the NPCs, the ACTUAL amount of game that is not just a reskin of something else... It's all so vapid. At 1/4 of the price?  Maybe it'd be worth it. I personally have some disposable income, so I don't regret this purchase TOO much, but if you need to budget your money for games, I suggest you go elsewhere, at least until some big improvements are made. Sorry devs. I really, really wanted to love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Some answers to your potential questions:If this game fun? Yes.Could it be better? Yes.Does it have game breaking bugs? Yes.Are they working to fix them? Seemingly.Do they have a QA team? Really unsure at this point.Have updates fixed things they said it would fix? No.Do I miss the days when games worked and there were only minor bugs? Ohhhh yes.This game has been fun, it got me playing it for 18 hours in a few days. So yes, it's cool. It sometimes has struggled to keep me playing, getting a bit bored etc. Economy stuff needs to be better. The game is supposed to only let you accept a shipping contract once every two weeks... and that means it's slow. It is a grinddddd game. I'm not wholly against those but then it needs to be fun and have other things to fill in the grind and I'm not sure it has that to keep me playing past a the first full year of the game...This all being said, ultimately I have stopped playing because the shipping contract bug is game breaking. It makes accruing money sooooooooo slow without the ability to use shipping contracts. This should have been fixed in the latest patch, and it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: While I am sure the game would be an exceptional game to play, these games, for me, are a multiplayer experience (as presented in the video for the game). However, depending on your internet provider, you may have to jump through hoops going back and forth to unblock the ability to make an account with the game devs' website. This currently has no workaround from the devs except to request a white list with the internet provider or router/modem (If you have one that allows you to). So until the ability to create an account with their site does not rely on the game (Such as an ability to make the accounts and link to Steam via the site), I cannot give this game a positive review.Please, however, note that this is a review of the game's multiplayer aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Coasts of Croakia update:No one wants an animal constantly following them around, you won't even keep animals inside of fences, let alone listen to us.Also, why is the frog allowed to fast travel on a broom, but I am not even allowed to use my wings to fly, or are offered the same luxury?It's a frog, it's supposed to swim......it doesn't even swim......You basically are going to farm gems to farm trinkets in this update, as long as another material "riffs" which you get from, I am not making this up, the magic conch (cue Spongebob jokes)Please do not buy this game or even play this update, its just going to make you grind even harder and run in circles for nothing.The new map itself is also half jump puzzle, and timing lily pads that move you up and down.The devs have stated on discord they do not plan to slow down time or make it more enjoyable, none of the bugs I have in game were fixed in the 2.0 """QOL""" update, they all still remain.You know the game is unfinished when they left a spot open on the pause menu, and have since "filled" it with DLC that should have just been apart of the base game should this studio have taken the game, and the community who has purchased this game seriously.I wish I could get a refund not just for the money someone spent to gift this game to me, but I want a refund of my time with how badly this game has just wasted it sending me in circles to just deal with bugs as roadblocks.Pros:Soundtrack is nice and really prettyGraphics are okay, I have a monster of a PC and get really bad pop ins, and half the time stuff doesn't load.Cons: the UI is terrible, and even after bug fixes still feels clunky, and unfinishedALL NPCs repeat the same lines. My first day in town the Mayor told me she would "check up on the elves"Festivals suck, there's nothing much to them.Outfits are lacking if you enjoy feminine optionsSpouses are lawn furniture and me personally, none of my spouses have ever even been kind to me, or referred to me as their spouseDays go by in the blink of an eye, and most things you do don't pause the game in single player stillBugs have been really bad, even now as of October I experience crashes, and still can't leave my fae coop.Romance is beyond mid, you get a :30 cut scene, and you don't learn much about everyone.The world feels extremely hollow, people talk about places we will probably never see or go to, and you can't even walk inside of half of the buildingsMiles still has a bug where if he is on the map, I am only able to speak to him even if he isn't nearby,also you can't even date Miles?????Story has no heart, every quest in the story is the exact sameCut scenes aren't even animated, and your custom character isn't even in itCharacter creation is pretty mid, and most of the colors they showed are extremely dull, and not vibrant at all. For example, there's no true "pink" hair color, every shade is brown or grey.Everything about this game, is beyond sweaty and a grind, and I enjoy grinding in games. This feels pointless, and for nothing. I felt no reward from any achievement or milestone.Not a cozy game in the least, if you want to do anything, you'll need an excel spread sheet, physical notes, and to play with 3 other people minimum, you don't get to enjoy this game single player.You are punished severely in game for absolutely nothing. Missed a jump in the fae mines? You're brought back to the beginning because you didn't time your jumps properly, and you lost hp, time in game, and your pots are now gone.Also, pots don't work properly. They don't pause when the game pauses, and I have recorded proof of two pots running out with plenty of time left. No mounts, only zoom potions, and good luck you'll be spending two days in game collecting mats. Every friendship quest is the same, so if you just keep citrine ore, sardines, and copper ore on you plus a few drinks, guess what :) That's literally it, for EVERY NPC even romanceables. Decorating isn't fun at all, once you unlock the color palettes you can customize any piece of furniture, but moving it around your home is a nightmare and will make you tear your hair out, also, you have 15 minutes to decorate so you better decide quickly where you want things. Yes, you are speed running decorating. You MUST keep food/drink/potions on you all at once. Food replenishes energy, drinks replenish energy, but you must have potions for health and mana, most mundane things require energy and you will need mana, if you want to do ANYTHING. The mines are a platforming game, and as someone who doesn't enjoy platforming games, I feel this must be  brought to people's attention. You cannot enter the mines without potions, and the negative effects of the volcano and miasma will stack on you even as you are trying to select a floor to descend to, if you aren't careful you will lose health, and be booted from the dungeon completely, ALSO if you fall at any point into lava, you lose health and must restart the level of the mines over.To unlock levels in the two later mines, you must also /beat the clock/ you are speed running your day, and also you are timed and must get packages within the mines to certain delivery points to unlock the next level of the mines, let me be clear: You need potions to get into these places, you must be aware of your surroundings, and all the while you are on a puzzle hunt that is TIMED and if you do not beat it, you are punished brutally, and must start over. Sure you can just use seals to go down once they're unlocked, but until you have the entire mine unlocked this isn't viable, and won't be viable until you put minimum 100h of gameplay and grind to /simply unlock a place where you must mine materials/You are not allowed to sell more than one item at a time, items do not stack and you are limited in the beginning to the amount of slots to sell at, and it is an extreme grind to get more produce stands, off the top of my head at least 30k florins JUST TO UNLOCK MORE SPACE TO SELL ONLY ONE SINGULAR ITEMYou must dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge all over the platform of the mines, and dodge enemies constantly, and yes, you can use invis potions, but in order to unlock every achievement, you'll need to slay enemies.I feel most reviews on here aren't being up front and truthful, and this game is not cozy, and it's not fun. It's a grind, it's brutal, and it's just unfinished, should have spent 1-2 years more on it, and not been early access.

_childDocuments_.review: "Character Creation Review - Fae Farm offers all you need to create a simple and satisfyingly unique Fae Farmer. Many options, good representation, vibrant and cute cartoony style."Fae Farm let's you create the perfect little Fae Farmer in a pretty fantastic and simple cartoony style. The options available are all pretty easy to throw together and use effectively and allow for a pretty decent variety of character types, ages, and styles, which is quite impressive for this type of creation system. The simple yet satisfying art style of the character models, and the rest of the game for that matter, is pretty reminiscent of the Animal Crossing in the best possible way. I imagine the character creation options combined with the no doubt massive selection of outfits, hats, and all the rest that you can access in the game itself will be more than enough to keep most people happy. As for the specifics... there are multiple male and female body types to pick from, some decent skin tones, eye options, a few too few mouth options (one of my only complaints), a great selection of hairstyles and accessories, bears, interesting facial details, pronouns, and both male and female voices. You can mix and match any of the options onto both the male and female body types, it is all shared and there don't seem to be any restrictions in place. That's it! Overall I am quite impressed by the lot of it and had a good time going through all the options. You can find my full character creation video linked below for my reactions and all the rest. Remember to use the timestamps to jump to what you want to see. Enjoy!
