_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Very fun game, kept me engaged for the whole 24 hours of my first completion, which is probably as far as it's gonna go for most people.For my fellow Rabi-Ribi autists: the first play through is a bit more on the linear side but after that you can play free roam mode which also gives you back your secret tech wall jump and changes some item locations to account for skipping the intro. There's also an achievement to kill an early boss with an item you get like halfway through normally, without picking up anything else, so probably pretty open past the first play through.As of writing i played on Normal, finished a play through and am going for 100%, dipped my toes in one of the extra modes. (and also a total of 200ish hours of Rabi-Ribi across 3 platforms, so this isn't through a completely fresh lens and i might be familiar with things that might annoy someone new that i am blind to)Going into the game i was worried about a couple things, one being the crafting system. but i am happy to say that it is largely unintrusive and for me was just something to keep me engaged with minor enemies. it largely replaces buying consumables, some things you buy once and then get the recipe along side it and are then no longer able to purchase it. another one was some things i saw in the only negative review i saw when purchasing. they did play on the hardest difficulty so that might make a difference, but they talked about having to respect a lot more enemies than they would have liked to, but pretty much from the start you have multiple options to ignore whatever enemy. one is just jump kicking over them, or you can damage them (even with your orbitars) and just walk through them while they still flash, early on you get a move activated by hitting jump during a combo making you do a big flip in whatever direction you hold, if nothing else helped this got me though even the largest hitboxes. the rest is powerup related and pretty self explanatory and irrelevant right now. the next thing was the missing wall jump secret tech and linearity, which is largely true for the first play through. you are of course always free to back track with whatever new toy you just got and find more power ups, and the wall jump secret tech returns in free roam mode, so yay replayability. next one was badges, or sigils, and while i do find myself in agreement that there are waaaaay too many to the point that it's sometimes hard to find one you know you have, i do like that there's more ways to augment your moveset (sometimes only when near enemies, or at certain combo, or rank). one of my favorite things i found was the one that replaces your double jump with an upward spin, like link's smash up+B, coupled with all the quickdrop into enemy sigils re casting the spin on every kick, while on the topic of combat, input and complexity wise it's basically rabi ribi with aerial combos give or take a hand full moves. think devil may cry with like one weapon or two on swordmaster in terms of move list. the early bosses are quite the pushovers with patterns that a normal hitbox could easily dodge so it can feel a bit overkill with the bullet hell game hitbox (which basically sits between the collarbones). later on though the bosses do pick up with cool patterns that are fun and challenging to dodge for the most part. a few patterns are either callbacks to rabi ribi or recycled in a new context. like one of the lillith 2 patterns, but you're grounded this time around, cheers to fanservice. Movement is an absolute joy throughout (the quickdrop is no longer faster than walking, and jumping out of a slide isn't either so that's a bit of a hit to early movement speed, oh well) tevi has a pretty brisk walking speed and platforming is buttery smooth, once you get some more movement items it gets reeeeeally fun. maps are just super fun to move through, with the exception of two areas. they're not bad at all to just get through, but completing them is a pain because of the structure with non euclidean rooms i guess you could call it. i'm not too much of a story person, but it kept me entertained enough to not skip anything so that's sometthing i guess. there's lots of cool or cute characters, it's not neccesarily all black and white so that's cool too. there are a bunch of kinda pointless or one off type characters, it's non intrusive so whatever. There's tons of stuff to collect (like 240 sigils over 180 stat increase potions, and one of the crafting materials is in block form as well, and some miscellaneous stuff), and secrets to find pretty much everywhere. The map is pretty damn huge as well, there's even some side activities, namely; races and arena challenges, nothing to write home about but cool nevertheless.All in all i really quite enjoyed my time with this game, i can wholeheartedly reccommend it with very few caveats. I'm gonna come back and definitely play some more of this game. might be up there with its sister; Rabi-Ribi and Super Metroid for me. could also be the recency bias, but time will tell.Lastly all the bugs i encountered, one of which is keeping me from 100%-in sinner's oath one of the potions there is unobtainable and the full map not possible due to a missing loading zone (i think). it's the one in the larger room with a save point in it and a guardian thingy right of said save point, the compass gives me a signal in the top left of the room. two screens to the right you can bomb the ceiling and jump through, but you're just on top of the current map. all the way to the right is a pit and to the left the screen doesn't scroll and tevi just gets lost.-Veena isn't to be found anywhere she said she would be, and after about two hours of running around all the towns she said she'd be i randomly took a train from Tartarus to Ana Thema and she loaded in on a platform at the train station.-in Gloamwood there's a hidden kiwi potion at the bottom of a long shaft and you have to take a bomb flower from 2/3rds of the way up, but on the way is a sign which breaks the bomb falsely making me believe they couldn't fall too far, or that bombs just break at that height of the shaft.

_childDocuments_.review: My overall feelings on Tevi are complicated, but I think they're mostly positive.I thought about going back and writing a proper review for this after I finish it, but as I'm probably roughly 80% through the game, I figured I should write my thoughts down while I'm still down in it, so to speak.Just over a year ago, I completed Rabi-Ribi. It was an absolute masterpiece. Needless to say, I was beyond excited to hear of another Metroidvania from the same team. Tevi is something of a successor to Rabi-Ribi, but it's also a very different Metroidvania. Rabi-Ribi always felt like a marriage of intentional simplicity to masterfully crafted complexities in many of the finer details. The story, which began as nothing particularly remarkable, concluded in a way that left me almost with more questions than answers.Where Tevi diverges from this is in its identity as something far more serious and complex from the very beginning. The story is deeper and darker. There's more world to explore, more mechanics to master, more enemies to battle than in Rabi-Ribi. There's much more to the soundtrack, and it's more varied. Everything feels a little more polished and the controls feel tighter. However, the game's DNA is so obviously the same as Rabi-Ribi's. It's a familiar place.You could probably say that, in this particular way, if Rabi-Ribi was Quake, then Tevi is Half-Life.Tevi's soundtrack is genuinely fantastic. There hasn't been a single song on it that I dislike. I don't seem to find it quite as memorable as Rabi-Ribi's, but that could also be due to the sheer number of areas and related tracks.All that said... I have some gripes, and these gripes lead me to the conclusion that I prefer Rabi-Ribi. Tevi improves on many of the core mechanics of Rabi-Ribi, but it loses some of what made Rabi-Ribi so excellent.In particular, there are simply  too many sigils in Tevi. Rabi-Ribi had a total of 32 badges. Each and every one had its own distinct purpose, and I considered the usefulness of each as I obtained it. I have absolutely no idea how many sigils are in Tevi, but I cannot possibly keep track of what they all do or when I'm even using one of them. I appreciate the opportunity for extremely specific technical runs through the game, but... isn't this a little much?Level design suffers a bit in this one, in my opinion at least. It's not objectively bad by any means, but there are points where I feel like it comes uncomfortably close to resembling an early stage of Super Meat Boy, with the added difficulty that you have to backtrack to the starting position every time you mess up. None of them felt impossible, but several were super annoying. I am enjoying Tevi's story itself, but the dialogue at times unfortunately reminds me of the worst parts of the Persona series' stories: unnecessarily verbose explanations of events that the player has already long figured out. It's perhaps even more frustrating when paired with the wonderfully colorful voiceover work, because I feel bad skipping the dialogue even though I'm bored to tears by it at times.Lastly, and perhaps worst of all, coming from someone who has been told by many that they are simply terrible at video games, this game is  Rabi-Ribi was a genuine challenge for me...on  I've turned up the difficulty in Tevi a couple of times and I'm still beating bosses on the first try. Admittedly, it's a little bit of a relief, but Rabi-Ribi was, for the first time in my life, making me enjoy failing. Some of those endgame fights took me multiple evenings to win. Not a single battle in Tevi has had the same effect.To be clear, I don't necessarily consider this an objectively bad thing, either. It's more like... it feels extremely off-brand. And that aspect is simply disappointing. What ultimately saves Tevi is that it still  charm, just like Rabi-Ribi. I'm never bored by the game's presentation; the environments, sounds, music, and art all come together in such a pleasing way. I think its weaknesses are all derived from building too many additional mechanics onto the core of Rabi-Ribi. There is an ideal complexity and an ideal (non-)linearity to a Metroidvania. Rabi-Ribi balances those almost perfectly, but Tevi falls slightly too far on the wrong side. But don't let that stop you from picking it up and playing it! Rabi-Ribi is hard to surpass, but Tevi is still brilliant in many ways. I have finally completed Tevi. Sheesh, it took forever; real life and other hobbies kept getting in the way. My opinions haven’t changed much, but the final hours of the game caused me to realize my gripe with the difficulty (or lack thereof): recovery options are so available that I was subconsciously brute forcing every fight. I rarely died for two separate reasons. Firstly, I could simply heal with all the consumables I crafted in downtime. In Rabi-Ribi, this wasn’t such a good option, as your only recovery options were items only purchasable at Miriam’s shop, all the way back in Rabi Rabi Town. You had to use your consumables wisely. Secondly, I had a ridiculous amount of health for the whole second half of the game. I guess I could’ve increased the difficulty more, but that felt silly, because it genuinely was hard at first. Later, I just felt like, why bother memorizing these attack patterns if I can just eat most of the hits and be fine? I never had that thought in Rabi-Ribi; all the battles were far more technical even on the lower difficulties. Additionally, the boss battles in Tevi felt rather spongy. I’m having a far easier time staying alive than in Rabi-Ribi, but oh my gosh my thumb is burning. Every boss has like 5 health bars that each take nearly as long as the one health bar in Rabi-Ribi. This would be fine in a came where attacks were heavier and less frantic, but in Tevi, it was often nothing short of exhausting. I still thoroughly enjoyed the game, and the story really got me at the end. I just hope that wherever the devs go next, they find the best of both worlds. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I think just like a lot of other people, I went into the game expecting Rabi-Ribi and ended up kind of disappointed that it's designed very differently. Sure, there's cute anime girls, many of them scantily-clad, but the metroidvania gameplay and especially map design just aren't as interesting or fun. There's no exploration, story progress locks off practically every route, optional areas are few and far between, etc... But after a while I stopped comparing it to rabbit ribbit and just learned to enjoy the game as it was, and I ended up having a lot of fun. I think what saved Tevi for me are the bosses (there's quite a few of them, and they all have unique attacks and bullet patterns) and the combo-oriented combat. There's a lot of experimentation with the sigils system, and often times when I was hardstuck on a boss I could squeak my way through by changing up my sigils based on the boss. In fact, the game is very forgiving, with tons of ways to boost how many sigils you can equip and a lot of overpowered consumables. (That might be a con to some people but I'm garbage at video games so yeah I appreciated it lol)tl;dr it's a "decent" metroidvania but a really fun arpg/bullet hell, do not go into it expecting rabi-ribi 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a well produced, large metroidvania that feels very much like it's predecessor; Rabi-Ribi.I have to testify to not loving the combo-style combat system and how grindy that feels even on many basic enemy types, but that just comes down to my personal tastes.  I bounce off of most games that have combo-combat systems.  Such systems feel to me like they are bloating and convoluting combat by adding delays, button mashing, having your character zip all over the screen (to take damage) or locking you into animations.  Give me a jump, dash, and slash button and i'm golden.  As far as those sorts of games go though, i do find this one to be quite fun and approachable even in spite of my preferences.  One of my biggest peeves was with the backflip that you will use a lot to get i-frames.  There are plenty of times where I would go to use it and it wouldn't trigger.  I'd be locked into some combo attack and it just wouldn't activate.  I wish something this fundamental was more straightforward, and that the ability would just cancel whatever i'm doing whenever I press it and activate.Most bosses are unfortunately humanoid-shaped enemies, though i was expecting that, as it was also the case in Rabi-Ribi. Fortunately some of their attack patterns and bullet hell moments at least made them a bit more interesting. I mixed up my moves, used offensive trinkets and kept the combo bar at max rank as much as possible.  But even on casual difficulty, the bosses are a complete slog to fight.  I actually dropped it to casual for the last 4 bosses because i didn't want to risk them taking more than a single attempt, due to the sheer slog that fighting a boss in TEVI is.  This was despite usually one shotting the bosses on Normal+ difficulty (Some exceptions) up until that point, and in most games enjoying a good long or tricky boss fight.It wasn't specifically the fight length either, but i think has more to do with the spamminess of the combat system.  A similarly lengthed fight in other games that don't use a spammy combat system like this don't feel like slogs.The only thing I can think to compare it too, would be like a Shmup where you can't hold down the fire button, and most enemies are bulkier ships.For me, long epic boss fights and spammy combat systems like these aren't a happy marriage.This impacted my enjoyment of exploring the world as well. In any other game, monsters don't take this long to dispatch.Areas feel exactly like the ones in Rabi-Ribi did, there's plenty to explore and backtrack for in TEVI.  While there are a lot of biomes, they are for the most part very similar to one another, but the level design was interesting and kept me engaged.The anime story doesn't appeal to me, but i predicted that would be the case going into the game. _childDocuments_.review: Ever since TEVI was first announced, I was really excited for it’s release.After my experience with Rabi-Ribi, I knew this new game was in good hands and had a lot of potential with it’s gameplay and boss design.Now that I have finished the main story of TEVI, I can confirm that, at least for me, they didn’t only live up to that potential, but also surprised me with the amount of quality and love this game has.First, I want to say that this game looks absolutely beautiful!TEVI has lots of pretty close up shots during cutscenes that make them more enjoyable to read, not to mention the game itself overall looks amazing with its Pixel art.Every area in this game is full of colors and great scenery that I found myself taking photos for hours, the same thing goes for the characters and enemies too, they are full of life and look fantastic.Even while the game looks amazing, the biggest highlight for me in TEVI was actually it’s combat.Of course you won’t get to fully enjoy it until you level up a few times and search the world for some items but, the final result are a lot of options for achieving satisfying combos with cool effects that make them feel powerful, combined with some customization you can can get from the badges while exploring, and you’ll be able to fight enemies in your own style.But fighting won’t be fun if the enemies aren’t enjoyable to battle.thankfully, TEVI‘s bosses offer a great challenge, it’s noticeable that a lot of thought has been put Into each boss fight since every one of them feels unique and has a lot of different special attacks, sometimes so much that I needed to fight some bosses twice to see all they can do.While most of this game is really great, it is not perfect.One of the most disappointing things is that the story isn't really interesting to follow, it tries to take itself a bit too seriously and ended up failing.It feels like they tried to shove up a lot of ideas with not enough time to make them feel important, one thing happens after another so the characters don't get much time to reflect on it or even react.Not to mention that most of the events feel pretty generic and something you will see in a lot of "serious stories".It has gotten to the point that it was hard for me to fully care about what was going on.Maybe if some characters had more time to grow and develop, it wouldn't have felt rushed and i could have cared some more. Despite some of it's issues, I had a fantastic time with TEVI, I enjoyed fighting bosses, exploring the world and best of all...petting bunnies, and I can see myself continuing to play it for many more hours!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game overall, with some polishing issues sometimes noticeable.Starting with the positives:+++Very interesting and challenging areas to explore. Re-exploring areas is made easier due to the design of allowing movement items to shine in late-ish game. (Exception being one area where there are IWBTG-like traps...)+Good graphics, especially the backgrounds in the cities.++Overall nice music tracks, but some seem a bit too much for just background music.+++Almost all bosses range from well designed to incredibly creative. Shoutouts to the last few bosses in particular, they were unbelievably great. The exception to this are two bosses, one early game, one mid game. I'd rather see them removed from the game...And of course: +++The combat in this game (melee) in the late game feel fantastic. I do think it is the most "fluid" out there.Negatives:---The two aforementioned bosses, the one mecha dude being the worst offender and the pyramid guardian being the second worst. You can guess why.--The Map controls very weirdly. Due to the sheer size of the world, I found it very hard to navigate for most of the game. In particular, I wished the areas were grouped and the first selection (i.e. when pressing arrow keys) would be to switch between them in a geometrically intuitive way (rather than down some arbitrary list as in the teleporter selection). Then after selecting one group, you should enter free navigation immediately, instead of switching between quests, jumping around the whole map...--Polishing issues: Noticeable in the Katu boss fight: The Boss Health bar should immediately shrink if it blocks the vision of you or the enemy, rather than wait a few seconds. Same goes with HP bar etc. for some other areas. It should go away the moment it can possibly obstruct anything, not seconds after. Also one cannot immediately access the map when transitioning between areas. You have to - for some reason - walk a few steps.--Too many suicide enemies. This one's weird, because there are a lot of different enemies with their own unique attacks. But there more than one type of enemy just... explode in your face. Thats basically all they do. Charge and you and explode, while shooting different patterns of bullets. It would be ok if there is a singular enemy that does this in an area, but there are just too many.-Maybe there are some balancing issues. I have not messed around too much with different builds, but melee focus seems to be so much better than range. Range feels kind of useless for the most part, or is simply passive damage. Also, you may have 6 different shot types, but Sables A type was just so much better than anything Celia had to offer. So I mostly used Sable A/C for combat and B for some niche explorationg situations. The bombs also do not... help much in combat, even with all the related sigils.-I think there are a little bit too many sigils for the menu. There should be a search function, i.e. keywords or something.-No post game. I don't think that (even if a DLC is released) there will be anything after the main story since it feels conclusive. But instead of getting to enjoy newfound peace and perhaps seeing the world change for the better, you just get send back to before the final boss à la Fire emblem or Legend of Zelda. Kind of a bummer.Lastly, my personal gripe: This journey Tevi is on just seems so lonely. When I first saw Vena, I actually thought she would take the role of a Pokemon Rival, someone you fight in almost every city, with increasingly harder patterns and team up if there is a common advesary (which there are. A lot.). But NO. You fight her once and then... well, she sells you bombs that youll never use. The same goes for so many other "allies" or "friends". They are introduced, but then play no more role in your adventure. The people you have befriended? Their goons/military still attack you on sight. It just feels so inconsequential what you do in most of the game. The world does not change due to your actions, even though the dialogues imply otherwise. Most NPCs also are stuck in their last story dialogue, so even if a lot has happened, they won't acknowledge it.tl;dr: Great game, minor issues.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Its such a mixed bag, but still a good experience that is probably worth it on a sale. Even if you want something harder, its a great intro to how cre-spirit does fight systems, and thus, as preparation for their harder games. (Even if the older stuff might have way less QOL.)The good.- Its incredible how much they have improved the regular enemies and enemy varieties are compared to what they have done previously.- Its incredible how much more the fight system is. The combo variety/combo tree is very advanced, and you have a lot of tools to make sure you are using options you like using.- Its incredible how good music variety is and how large the world is.- Its nice how there are a few areas that are near fully plot irrelevant, with enough small interesting things to at least reward you for being curious and searching in the corners of the world where nothing happens.- One of the areas where you meet an early game boss again is one of the most charming encounters I've seen in the game in recent memory, I couldn't help but smile the entire time I was in this encounter. Its so. So good. The music worked perfectly here.- Its nice the voices add a bit of character to your sociopathic bombing every tile individually so you don't miss anything.- There are good serious chunks as well, even if parts of it are flubbed to.The bad.- Its a shame the bosses spend so long telegraphing things while waiting voice lines I don't understand to finish ,as the slow pacing does make the threat level feel way down. This never lets up and is at odds with what the stories about.- Its a shame item progress is heavily tied to cutscene viewership/things given to you, as it feels like there is a 75% rate of the things you were looking for being given to you in a down time from dialogue, rather then being discovery. So even when you enable a lot of the sequence breaks, most of what you might want to do is still gated behind dialogue.- Its a shame it all feels very... Distracted, short attention span ish. Very few things still matter after the second time they are mentioned or shown, and most things are resolved the first time they appear. They wanted to show us a lot, but I sort of find myself wishing they had focused on a few strong elements and left more things as plot threads for us to pick up in the future, rather then spilling their whole hand at once.They tried to show us a lot in this game, and I feel this could have been a 10/10 instead of a 7.5/10 if we had been trusted to have a more patience and exploratory spirit. Still, the extreme feeling of being front-loaded and dialogue-first does.... Limit the experience.I appreciate the bravery in trying to give a cinematic experience with this, but it often does feel like it masks a lot of the things I know you (Crespirit) are absurdly good at.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Metroidvanias ever made.The world is massive and the exploration is super fun, the backgrounds look beautiful and the music is outstanding, the combat is amazing and so are the bosses. If you like Metroidvanias, i consider this a must play. It has everything a Metroidvania needs and it pulls it off perfectly, from exciting exploration to dozens of fun puzzles and hidden items you come back to as you unlock all of the abilities that make the game play so great, all accompanied by fluid controls, fun characters and a captivating story. It also offers a bunch of different modes and difficulties making for a lot of replayabillity and everything is super polished.Very much recommanded for every Metroidvania fan!
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I would not call this game a masterpiece in metroidvania genre, but its pretty damn close to being one. It has a fantastic combat system that is both fast paced and responsive/fluid in terms of controls and how character acts on your inputs. This game features a quite big map, probably one of the 5 biggest maps on metroidvanias ive seen, it also is an open map, cause you can reach many places and do a lot of sequence breaking here.The story is very interesting and characters are loveable to the point i found myself binging this game in around 10-15 hour long sessions. This is further enhanced by good art and fantastic voice acting done by some of the best and most memorable japanese voice actors, like LYNN, Rie Kugimiya and Youko Hikasa.There are some problems in terms of liking the character arts as shown during converstations, as those are not of as same quality that the games pixel art and the images shown in some scenes. And while i did not really mind it or get bugged by it, ive seen some people be literally dead hurt and straight up offended by this art so keep that in mind.Finally something i wanna addresse as something i did not really like, is the accessibility of changing the games difficulty at any given time, i dont mind games adding difficulties for people who dont like a challenge, but having the chance to lower the setting when you reach a wall becomes pretty damn alluring, and will lead to some later distaste if someone actually does lower the difficulty down for 1 or 2 bossfights, even i was struggling to keep the difficulty at the highest possible on first playthrough. Also read with caution before you rage on me in comments, i dont say game should not have normal or easy difficulties, i say you choice should matter and you should not be able to change it at any given time in game.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I have really really enjoyed Tevi as someone who has played and owned Rabi-Ribi for years.   Metroidvania + Bullet Hell -Better combat, with more variety on how you play with the Sigils, -Large map with lots of exploration -Good difficulty (I played on Expert and never felt like the game was holding me back) -Good visuals -Good OST -Good story ( I don't see it as rushed as some others may have) -Good boss variety + enemy variety -Really good Voice acting wasn't expecting VA in the first place but they really picked good people for the job)-Good replay-ability with difficulties, speedrun, low percent, randomizer for sigils and more options -Large variety of Sigils that can be used to make your play style drastically different, some are more percent based things but others are moves or small details that change how you can play.-Plays good on Steam deck A few small hiccups are -Exploration can feel like a slog at times or might make you frustrated since with compass you'll know where an item is in a sense but you won't know how to get it. (Sinners oath one in particular for me at least) -Some characters in the story feel like they should have a larger role but don't and or a character you'd have to fight but don't (But I guess DLC could change that which would be cool) -Kinda wish there was a boombox that you could carry with you to play specific tracks (after you've been to an area the OST would be added or something) while exploring -The L1-R1 (Your hitbox/slow-walk) setting should be activated right away and then prompted to turn off or leave on, and explained in a small tutorial window IMO, it wasn't for me (Have to manually go in the settings to turn on and I didn't realize until the end of the game almost thought I was crazy when I was thinking about Rabi-Ribi's) But just my opinion nothing big honestly.Overall recommend if you want a difficult but fair Bullet Hell Metroidvania game, with good combat that has decent replayability variety .
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly well tuned, well tested, high precision metroidvania with incredible boss fights.The soundtrack is amazing, and if you've played a lot of games and are wary about too much similarity to a lot of experiences you've had in the past, I can assure you, it's going to surprise you.I recommend playing the hardest difficulty available from the start, it will HIGHLY ENCOURAGE you to explore your approach to combat until you adapt to using all of the mechanics available.Game keeps giving at only 4 hours, I can tell there is an INCREDIBLE journey ahead.  The story is fine, the characters are fine, it has voice acting, the visuals are absolutely fantastic~10/10 until I find something that isn't astonishingly high quality, will update if there's anything that makes it not worth the price~ Which totally isn't going to happen.  Can't believe how nice this is day 1. x_x;;;;

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Rabi-Ribi, you will feel right at home but everything is improved, from the movement to combat feeling to map exploration. Great atmosphere and ambient ost, fun to discover all the secret paths and items.The team is very actively and daily working on bugfixes and sees people's reports in the discord server.However the game could've used another half a year of dev time for finishing touches. The ending and final area in general feel rushed, many plot points forgotten and holes left open. Kinda feels like setup for story dlc, which the game will hopefully get and expand on the events of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches a unique itch combining a metroidvania with combos and a style system akin to DMC.I greatly enjoyed my playthrough, but in retrospect there were two key flaws.-The sigil system gets overly complicated the more you have, and there's way too friggin many that could have just been permanent abilities that instead add to the mountain of sigils available.-The plot really trips over itself the further it goes. The number of plot twists just feels like lazy writing as it progresses, and things just happen and it refuses to elaborate.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I immediately came to this game because one of the developers of this game, GemaYue, developer of the game Rabi-Ribi, developed it.I came expecting an "Spiritual successor" of Rabi-Ribi and I was very disappointed with certain aspects of this game.The Worst part:The Metroidvania aspect of this game is almost non-existent. Map design is bad and the backtracking aspect is realy, realy bad. Who made the decision to show the player the message to not proceed to certain area? Who was the one that restricted our freedom? And no, I do not want play free-roam mode after playing the game the first time. Using the history narrative to block players progress was really in bad taste. Rabi-Ribi almost achieved what I would call the "Golden Number" of the Metroidvania genre and I was disappointed with TEVI because of it.I CANNOT GO BACK TO PLAY ANOTHER METROIDVANIA GAME BECAUSE OF RABI-RIBI. MY EXPECTATIONS ARE TO HIGH!The Really Bad:Ok, after my rant on the Metroidvania aspect of this game. we have another problem.The art style of the characters.There is something wrong with this art style. There are some problems of consistence with some portraits of the characters and they are somehow "ugly". It's like the artist made the character art while he/she was intoxicated with some drug or I could say, "plage". Tevi and Vena are good though.The Bad:This game promised to have a better story than Rabi-Ribi but could not deliver it (It also made me furious that we sacrificed the Metroidvania aspect for this incomplete story). This story starts well but at the 3/5 of the story something goes wrong and a lot of things starts to feel rushed and incomplete. It also feels like some characters were discarded mid way. Something needs to be done/fixed with the story. Maybe a DLC?The Neutral:Balancing problems.The slightly Good:I like the faces that the first boss makes.The Good:I like the chosen VAs. I do not really care that much but it was a nice touch.Bullet Hell boss battles feels different but it was still good. The dark theme of the game is really cool.Game play was expanded horizontally. Some builds are interesting.The Awesome:The soundtrack of TEVI is awesome. It really fits TEVI as much as the soundtrack of Rabi-Ribi fits Rabi-Ribi.I like Vena, she is cute and funny. It is sad that this character does not have that much use in the story though.So, why this game has a negative review? Because the bad things are greater than the good things. Also for the developer to evaluate if the points made above makes sense to him/her. Please, do not take this as something rude, these are just my feelings.I rest my case.

Definitely recommend.Finished game on normal Edit:Loved this game. Super fun combat with decent platforming and exploring. Movement abilities being locked behind the story was occasionally frustrating, but not the end of the world. _childDocuments_.review: Rabi-Ribi with the production value amped up. Like its predecessor, it's some of the best 2D combat in any genre, let alone the Metroidvania.  It's like a combination of Symphony of the Night, Viewtiful Joe, and Touhou and keeping up combos in boss fights feels fantastic, with tons of emergency options at your disposal. The search-action feels more significant and rewarding with items than RR.  Plot is similarly... there to string everything together I suppose.  While more aesthetically and aurally polished than RR I think that game's simplicity gives it a unique charm.  Both of these are well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic action-adventure from the developers of peak Metroidvania Rabi-Ribi. The visuals are pretty, the music is certified bangers, the combat is complex but ultimately learnable and fun to master, and you can play it without your friends and family questioning your tastes in anime girls (most of the time, anyway. Celia is pushing it). The most important thing to note is that this game isn't very Metroidvania-like in its execution - your first run of the game will follow a linear path of item and story progression, and only after that do you unlock additional game modes that let you explore the game world more freely. It's more a JRPG than a Metroidvania, to be honest... which is still pretty rad. If non-linearity is an important quality to you when choosing a Metroidvania, do consider thinking twice before getting this game.Many call this the spiritual successor to Rabi-Ribi, and while I do see the similarities and references peppered throughout, TEVI feels like it's trying to be its own thing more often than not. A deeper and darker story, the linear gameplay style mentioned above, a complete shift in art style and aesthetic... it's definitely good enough to stand on its own two feet.Overall, TEVI is a long and exciting 2D adventure waiting for you to sink 30-40 hours in... and even more, perhaps. Maybe not a pure Metroidvania, but hey, it's good!
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: So, as a big ol' Rabi Ribi fan, I was really excited for Tevi.In the 2.5 hours I've played so far I can say:  this is Rabi Ribi but better.  The new Cocoa is so much more likeable and adorable.  Tevi is a *much* more likeable MC.  Tevi is a strong female character who has her own goals and friends.  This is *far* better than Rabi Ribi's MC, who was passive AF.If you play on Normal difficulty, the game is... lackluster.  Bosses aren't... really all that hard, if you're a danmaku fan.  If you played through Rabi Ribi without 100%+, bosses are pretty standard.  So difficulty doesn't really matter outside of boss fights, but if you're coming from Rabi Ribi you know that boss fights are the core.  Just skip on up.  We're here for the danmaku metroidvania.  If you play on Normal, you'll... not really have to worry about damage.  What you *really* want is the added bullet patterns of higher difficulties.  You'll always have a save point near to the boss fight.  Embrace the suck.  Fight them like eighteen times.The music is.... somewhat less loveable?  It's hard to say considering how much I loved Rabi Ribi's music.  I'd put Rabi Ribi on par with or above Hollow Knight, because they're very different games.  Tevi's music is a lot more... generic.  It's still pretty good, but it's not nearly as adorable.The characters... the characters are better.  This is the biggest improvement from Rabi Ribi.  Every.  Single.  Character.  Is so much better.The art... Eh, it's similar.  If you liked Rabi Ribi, you'll like this.  Lots of really high-quality very-sexualized anime girls.  If you don't want to see a whole lot of really sexualized anime girls, you should... reconsider this game.  That said, this one is way, WAY less sexualized than Rabi Ribi was.  Tevi (the MC) even actively fights against it.The fights:  This is the core of the game.  If you're playing Tevi, you've probably played Rabi Ribi and Hollow Knight and other similar games.  This is a bullet hell metroidvania, and it does an absolutely disgustingly good job at it... assuming you're not playing on an easy difficulty.  So, the fights are really tight.  Normal map enemies give you *really* small* dodge windows and action timings, on higher difficulties, which is a *lot* of fun.  But this is a Touhou-made-into-metroidvania, so we care about the bosses.The exploration:  Excellent, for current-era games.  Lots of secrets.  Lots of meandering.  LOTS of going back to old areas once you get new abilities.  There's teleporters to help you pop around, so it's... very modern metroidvania.  The areas to explore *very* obvious, which is... basically modern metroidvania, like Hollow Knight.  You don't need to worry about finding secrets in normal walls.  Overall, this game is a Hollow Knight danmaku.The bosses are really, *really* good.  We've gone ahead from the Rabi-Ribi bosses, which were just normal Touhou bosses that you had to work through as a 2d platformer.  We're now at Rabi-Ribi bosses with Hollow Knight mechanics, and that is *so good*   ---remember, Rabi Ribi came out before Hollow Knight.Finally, we've come a *long* way from Chelsea and the Seven Devils, and I do sort of miss that style of metroidvania - before metroidvania was a phrase.Epilogue: as far as bunnygirl-based games, this one is one of the better ones mechanically and design-wise.  The biggest failure of the game is that Tevi isn't actually a bunny.Verdict:  Recommended at full price, *if* you like metroidvanias and danmaku.  Play on Normal difficulty if you don't enjoy danmaku, but maybe buy on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Spiritual sequel to Rabi Ribi that fans have been waiting for; if you enjoyed that game definitely get this game.A great metroidvania with responsive combat, challenging bullet hell bosses, gorgeous pixel art, and a great soundtrack.  More wordy than Rabi Ribi but the characters are interesting (though they do fall into some classic anime tropes) and brought to life by a surprisingly stacked Japanese voice cast.tl;dr: better game than Starfield desu wa.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Metroidvania, very similar to their earlier game Rabi-Ribi. It's got good exploration, good level design and an ok story, but the real selling point is the cool bullet-hell bosses. They're varied and well-designed, with each one having unique attacks/gimmicks and multiple stages that evolve said attacks.The player is given some fun and varied offensive abilities very early and mildly encouraged to mix-and-match them, but really you'll mostly be spamming a melee combo until your safe window ends and/or taking ranged potshots whenever your MP refills. Both attack modes feel good (though the soft cap on how long you can melee attack is a bit annoying) and give the bosses good pacing. A few of the regular enemies do feel way too tanky for no good reason though.Just like their earlier game I compared it to, it does a nice job of letting you explore in whatever direction you want and fight the bosses in whatever order. It also has a neat *optional* mode where you can scale the bosses to your collection percentage to allow for a fighting chance even if you're not hunting for upgrades, but if you prefer the more traditional approach of "find most of the upgrades to make things easier" you can do that. There's also an even more explore-where-you-want-friendly option that's recommended only for second playthroughs but I haven't tried it.Overall, if the bosses in the trailer look fun you'll enjoy this game. If they don't, it's not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game: it's a good step up from Rabi Ribi in general.Most have been said better by other and I mostly agree to it:-Story could be really interesting with a good enphasis on lore....I said could be because the several plot twist in the end were...weird and came from nowhere. Also the game tried to be too dark for no reason sometime and it felt...cheap, especially in the end.-Area music range from good to some stellar track.-The one way exit is one of the rare, step down comparing to RR : they are not distinct to the rest and give a sense of punishment...the same for the no ledge drop mechanic althrough they are some alternatives ways close by.- Graphically, the background are really pleasant to the eye, a bit static but manage to give proper charm to each zones.- Still a really enjoyable experience for all the explorer enthusiast: lot's of upgrade, some requiring a bit of observation.I have to say that the early game felt a bit too linear but , fortunately, it dosn't stay.- Difficulty is fair (except the Cloister of Redemption and all of it's...trap) but a bit of off tracking make late game a bit too easy. A solid sequel, not perfect but still something I could recommand if you like to off track in order to dig out upgrade.

_childDocuments_.review: As most other reviews have mentioned, the main flaws with TEVI are its oppressive map design with one-way paths (forcing you to loop if you want to fully explore an area) and the fact that all of your movement abilities are locked behind the story. To call it a "Metroidvania" would be a stretch because it seems much more concerned with having you experience the narrative rather than explore the world at your leisure. It really feels more like a narrative platformer with light exploration elements rather than a full Metroidvania. While you can backtrack through the game world and find badges or stat potions you may have missed, most of the time you'll be following quest markers. This is somewhat alleviated with NG+ having a Free Roam mode, but the problem is playing through the main plot to get there.One question that might come up then is "Is the story good?" I wouldn't say so. For the most part the story is a by and large paint-by-numbers affair with plot elements that you either see coming a mile away or are completely out of the realm of possibility that they become incredibly jarring, and this happens a lot through the last act of the game to the point where it becomes difficult to care about what anyone is talking about. It's kind of a shame because the game has decent world building, but it tends to go nowhere fast. That said, I am recommending this based on the overall feeling of the game. When you're actually allowed to play the game it's incredibly fun to control and a huge improvement over Rabi-Ribi. Combat flows incredibly nicely and the boss design is incredible, really letting you test your skills either in dodging the bullet spam they can perform or allowing you to exercise your free-flowing combos. And while there is a problem with the badge system with there being so many of them, it does open up a lot of customization options for different builds that you can try at any point. Overall: when the game manages to shut up and let you play, it's a really fun time. Just don't expect to carve your own path since Tevi'd rather take you on a ride through its world at its pace.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Tevi is an expansive metroidvania with what I believe is quite the large world for said genre. With a lot of content packed into it. There is variety in its world, there is variety in its regular mobs, there are plenty of bosses and there is PLENTY to do. This is all wrapped into a box along with a Story, Characters, Voice Acting (some well known actors if you know who to look out for) and plenty of fitting musical scores.You have lots of flat upgrades to stats such as your HP, MP, Equipment amount, etc. There is also lots of customisability in terms of character skills/specs you can perform using its "Sigil" system. Which allows you to equip sigils on the fly to complement your preferred playstyle.Along with all this the game incorporates the "Bullet Hell" genre into its gameplay. Which in turn allows truly skilled players to show their character control and perception skills, especially on harder difficulties.As of writing this, I have completed the game fully once. 100%'d the map and got all items and fully upgraded them plus did some secret content and I plan to do some more playthroughs including one on the hardest difficulty.Combat in Tevi is fluid with just the right amount of depth (depth is provided via the Sigil system whist the amount of moves and inputs is mild) Attacks and moves feel good and responsive; finely tuned. The hitlag in the game makes certain attacks feel meaty and remind me of Monster Hunter: World levels of meaty hitlag, you feel like you are dealing damage. In turn you will also feel the damage being dealt to you. Especially with the various levels of knockback.The system is satisfying and not overly complex to grasp.A common gripe I see other reviewers struggle with, I have to admit that I fully relate to. Is that Tevi, in terms of exploratory upgrades, is fully railroaded. There is "exploration" in the game, but it's artificial. What I mean with that is that you need to imagine the world of Tevi as boxes. With every special movement enhancement/item the box becomes bigger. You CAN explore, but only within the confines of the box and no further. Having these progression locks on the movement upgrades for "boss" reasons isn't an excuse as when replaying the game you get the option to start with all movement options unlocked from the start, so locking it for boss reasons, isn't a great excuse.There is also a weird disconnect in receiving upgrades and items through story progression which should aid in the exploration of new area's, yet you never having been to said area's. As you World and level design wise the game is good. Its massively expansive, there are a ton of places to visit and they all feel distinct. This is helped by a colourful splash of beautiful pixelart and great animations on everything. If anything I only have 2 gripes in terms of level design:1. There are quite a few 1-way trips in places which feel constrictive and annoying to traverse, especially if you have to do it multiple times due to either failing something or needing to pass through something to get somewhere.2. There is 1 level design gimmick they use twice. Without spoiling what it is, it happens first within a forest environment. This gimmick should've just been limited to its use within that forest environment as repeating it. It outstays its welcome uniqueness by doing it again later in the game. Mind you, the gimmick is good, but only if it's used once, not twice like they did.Other than that, the level & world design is more than serviceable.My biggest pet peeve with the game is the Story. It wants to do too much, is too bloated and constantly loses its way. It suffers from the classic  trope.A lot of plotlines and characters that get introduced are left by the wayside when convenient and a lot of characters feel like they are just there as discardable plot advancement tools. There is no focus in the story with narrative pillars which the player can cling through as story naturally thickens as you progress. All this is coupled with a final arc which is just a roller-coaster ride until the end. It reminds me of what happened story-wise in Final Fantasy 15. Which is BAD. The ending doesn't properly wrap up the various plotlines and doesn't give satisfactory closure on various characters that were introduced in the world. Especially on one of the main characters.The only saving grace that keeps the story from completely imploding in on itself is that various characters are likeable and relatable. Without these, it would just be a mess.The frustrating part is that there is so much potential in the story, but it's just unfocussed and too fat in places whilst being almost too lean in others. It wants to do too much and branch out too wide, too fast and conveniently forgets about plot pieces and characters when needed. Plus lack of accountability for some characters frustrates me to no end. I think that some threads might be fixable with DLC but I'm sure that most cannot.I do recommend this game, its a lot of fun, and you can tell the developers really cared about it, they did their absolute best to deliver the best product they could. If you are able to forgive a story that at times might feel good, but will potentially leave you dissatisfied with the ending & the way it handled various characters and plotlines then this game will be for you. The combat is great, customizability and moveset feel great to play with. Bosses are fantastic and varied, and will put you to the test at higher difficulties. The world design is good, there are a ton of places to visit, its expansive and diverse. The downside being the gatekeeping of movement abilities hampering natural exploration.But other than that I do recommend playing this game, its tons of fun if you let it. Lets pray that there might be DLC in the future that addresses the story issues and gives proper closure on various plotlines/holes.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two prevalent cons that most reviewers tend to point out about this game:1. Exploration tied behind story progression.2. Bad writing.I concede point #1. Sure. Not being able to fully explore an area to my heart's content did disappoint me at times when I got started, but I understand why that is the design choice they went with. The gated off areas are essential to the plot of the story, and for them to be accessible too early would break the sequence of events. What you can access with the abilities you already have for any given point in the game is more than enough to venture and discover. Those items you can't obtain now you can grab later on, or through the game's free explore mode.As for #2... I personally loved it. I adore our three heroes and every character I got to know thereafter. The story is easy to digest, and features gripping moments where the tension in the dialogue is palpable. To tear jerking scenes that admittedly had me tearing up. It would take me 20-30 pages to describe everything I love about Tevi's story. Whether it's the relationship between Tevi and her father or Tevi and Vena, to our lovely companions Sable and Celia. Every character has a story-- a reason for being. A motivation behind their existence, yet we also have opportunities to see their doubts. Their fears. During my time playing the game I felt like I got to know the characters I was journeying alongside on this grand adventure throughout the world of Az.To summarize the rest: The controls are clean and responsive, the voice acting is impeccable, the art is stunning, the character design is golden, the animations are fluid, and the music, oh my goodness the MUSIC is DIVINE. The composers did not need to go this hard on the soundtrack but I'm THRILLED that they did! Every OST is an absolute BANGER, and for the first time I purchased a video game's soundtrack because GOOD. LORD.I love this game. I really do. I hope this release rakes in the funding the devs need to make a sequel. I desperately need to see more of this story-- and I can't wait to see what happens next.I most likely won't edit my review much if at all. I stand by every word I've written here.

_childDocuments_.review: Tevi is one of the best metroidvanias I've played in recent times, with fluid combat, a satisfying combo system, plenty of flashy boss battles and a massive world to explore filled to the brim with secrets and collectibles. I see some disappointment in these reviews that Tevi doesn't live up to the bar set by Rabi-Ribi, the devs' previous big metroidvania. I don't agree. I think Rabi-Ribi and Tevi can stand next to eachother as a pair of masterpieces.Whereas Rabi-Ribi focuses more on freedom and sequence-breaking, Tevi is more interested in worldbuilding and telling a story, though that doesn't mean freedom is absent, not by a longshot. The story told here admittedly starts off a bit slow in the first few chapters, but it really starts to pick up after that. I was especially surprised by how dark the game eventually became. You really feel like this world was handcrafted with its own history, and the story allows you to be part of said history. I also love pretty much all of the main characters. Sable and Vena are my favourites and I want to give them headpats.If you love metroidvanias, you owe it to yourself to check out this game. And Rabi-Ribi as well while you're at it.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat system in general is almost perfectly balanced, but there's just too much moves or sigils(badge/charm) that it's simply impossible to get everything right before playing this game for 100 hours.Boss fights are made carefully to always be not too stupid, or too simple. That also means there's a lack of adventurous design, or a strong impression. It's not a big problem. They all have solid high quality that it's hard to hate any of them.Boss stats are not quite balanced right, at some point in the late game it gets much easier due to higher damage and survivability player has. (basically your survivability is doubled while the time takes to kill the boss remains the same)But at least the final boss stays the hardest one.Well, fights are hella fun.The story? I liked some parts, hated the rest. It gets serious and dark, the immersion wasn't too bad but it's not high quality.The world doesn't provide a vivid interaction to the player. Aside from main story dialogue, talking to the characters does almost nothing. You also never get a re-fight of any early bosses. It feels strange because the lore is good enough to plot interactions but there's none until the end. It's just.. weird. Before realizing it I loved the earlier parts.It's a complaint but that just shows how much I wanted to interact with this world. I hope future DLC content would solve some of this problem, if there is any.For me the soundtrack was notably worse than Rabi-Ribi. This might be a big issue to some people without even realizing.I played the game for combat and I enjoyed it. I would expect nothing less from Cresprit.

There are melee attacks, multiple range attacks and deployable bombs, as well as buffs. Enemies have varied moveset even the recolored and reskinned ones. _childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Rabi-Ribi's gameplay mechanics, you will enjoy Tevi, as the combat and movement are both very fluid and well-refined, and it keeps quite a few mechanics from Rabi-Ribi, such as swappable ranged attacks and the ability to quickly drop in mid-air.If you enjoyed Rabi-Ribi's exploration and non-linearity, Tevi will be disappointing, as Tevi is (at least from what I can tell from 30-odd hours of playing) a very strictly linear game that looks like a metroidvania, much like Metroid Fusion, with progression gated behind story events and even outright blocking you from moving to other locations when the game wants you to stay put. Some hidden movement mechanics present in Rabi-Ribi were also removed or nerfed, presumably to prevent sequence breaking.Overall, in spite of Tevi's linearity, I enjoyed it. I spent too long jumping at a wall trying to perform early walljumps and wallkicks only to find out they weren't a mechanic in Tevi, got poisoned and then murdered by a rabbit, and then later someone threw a steamroller at my face.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game was made for me specifically, I've been a fan of rabi ribi, waero, and dance with the dead for a long time. Never would I ever have expected all of those things to come together in one place.As far as a review of the game goesPositives:Combat is fun! I found rabi ribi to be a little clunky at times, especially with how often boss fights were split into "hit the boss time" and "dodge the bullets time", this game does a lot better job of balancing the gameplay so you can wail on the boss while working through their patterns and still feel rewarded for it.I think the presentation is stellar. The visuals are fantastic, the music is great, and I actually liked the voice acting. While this is short words wise, I think playing the game the presentation speaks for itself, it's really good! I think the fact the soundtrack is 5 hours long says a lot by itself. When I first heard a dance with the dead song I recognized, I immediately paused, looked up the soundtrack, was shocked, and fell in love with this game even more.The map feels very cohesive, while I do think it sometimes feels a little big, especially at the start, the fact that there are often multiple routes to every objective really jives with the exploration and flow of the game. They also spaced the map goodies really well so even if you go somewhere early and don't have enough powerups to explore, you usually will still leave with something for your troubles.I actually really liked the writing! I'm normally a stickler for writing in games like metroidvanias that don't necessarily need a ton of it, but I feel like it was really well done in this game. Most characters feel really well fleshed out, and when I got to the end of the plot, it was fun to connect the dots from the beginning to the end. I do have a mild criticism that maybe there were a little bit TOO many characters, it was hard to keep track at some points, but overall I think it worked out.Criticisms:The start is very poorly paced, you don't really get anything from a few of the questlines besides an astral gear, but since the gear doesn't actually unlock any new abilities, as a player I don't feel the growth at the start (this feeling lasted about 6 hours of the 15 I spent on my first run, I'm sure it'd cut down a lot on a second playthrough). A lot of the storylines from the start are also put on pause until much later in the game, but I do appreciate that the fact you did them was not ignored.I also found traversing the map to sometimes be a little tedious. Since enemies respawn the moment you re-enter a room, I often found myself checking a room, then walking back into a room full of enemies. Other games I've played let you revisit the previous room and keep the enemies dead, and I think that would have helped the exploration a bit.Once you get deeper into the game, I feel like a lot of the issues solve themselves. The powerups make moving around the map feel a lot less bad, and the pacing tightens up quite a bit around chapter 4-ish.Overall:This is a really really good game, it might boot out iconoclasts from my favorite game/favorite metroidvania throne. It's funny how both had kinda slow starts and plots that didn't really pick up steam til midway through. I think the excellent aesthetic, visuals, and music are what really push this to the top for me. I'm not sure how much other people would enjoy this game, since it definitely suits my tastes very specifically, but my biased opinion is that this is definitely worth a try!

_childDocuments_.review: I watched various friends play Rabi-Ribi, and other bullethell games years ago, and enjoyed what I got to see. However, I have always been intimidated by bullethell games.When I saw Tevi had a demo, I decided to give it a try. I 100%'d the demo achievements, finishing the demo three times. To say I enjoyed it would be an understatement.So here we are with the full title..Tevi is a wonderful game.It took me about 37 hours to beat the game on expert difficulty with plenty of exploring.Combat is far too much fun! As you progress the number of tools made available to you, both through upgrades as well as sigils allow for so many entertaining options during fights.Boss fights are challenging, but I never felt out of my depth as a non-bullethell player. Between all the consumables, and various defensive mechanics you unlock, pretty much everything feels very doable! The majority of fights took a second try, with about three or four fights taking more than three attempts. Some were beaten on the first attempt.The story was pretty great! I had some issues with it towards the end, but thoroughly enjoyed both the story, and characters overall. I look forward to seeing what more comes in the future via dlc.I continue to play for now. _childDocuments_.review: Was that a JoJo reference?! 11/10Actual review:TEVI is a bullet hell metroidvania much like Rabi Ribi before it. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely play it if you like the Metroidvania genre.Gameplay is the main focus of this game ; it feels extremely polished, like frankly, if I had to judge a game by its gameplay and only its gameplay, then Tevi would be hands down the best metroidvania ever and with a decent margin.Tevi has fluid movements like you've never seen before, lots of customization, and very intuitive control. The level design feels good as it allows you to make full use of the upgrades you will find along the way, moreover you will never be bored when exploring a place for the first time as common ennemy will never fail to entertain you. I like how the different gameplay mechanics are taught to the player and how easy it is to get the hang of it.The bossfights are very well designed. While it's true that they all follow the same basic principle of "I will shoot multiple patterns at you, dodge or suffer" (it is a bullet hell metroidvania after all) ; in most of the bossfights you really feel like there are actual interaction between them bosses and your character when you land a hit. Which is a huge deal, as "boss feeling like unmovable wall doing their stuff until you land the final hit" is quite frankly the worst thing about most good metroidvania.I do have a few complaints about the gameplay thought. Mostly, I don't really like how every single "main" upgrade is story-locked as this feel like you don't have as much freedom as you'd like to have in a metroidvania. Don't get me wrong, the game DOES encourages you to explore the map by rewarding you with stats upgrade and more customization options, but you ain't getting something like a double jump or airdash until you've experienced 'X' part of the story.Another complaint I have is how unbalanced the difficulty feels : It's great at first, but get far enough in the game and it becomes noticeably easier and easier as long as you give two thoughts about your build. (I'd say that this start being noticeable only after you've beat Malphage) Still, the game feels really good despite these last two points, this isn't what should keep you from playing the game unless you feel like being extremely picky.So huh, if you have a favorite metroidvania, you must have a few good words about it on how good the immersion feels or how the story is great. Yeah well, my take on Tevi, to put it as politely as possible, is that it really is a game that shine thank to its gameplay.The story isn't bad by any means but it really does lack impact, it didn't fail to keep me interested but I probably will forget about it in a matter of months. Characters are likeable but the vast majority of them feel like they have wasted potential. And you might as well forget about immersion, Things will feel out of place fairly often. Be it some over the top line of dialogue, an artistic direction which despite always being coherent feels unimpressive overal, or a few BGM that don't fit : Immersion isn't a strong quality of Tevi. But don't misunderstand me on that last point ; The OST is nothing short of excellent, those tracks are really really good, my complaint is that there were a few time where I felt they didn't fit with everything else, not comically so, but they might feel out of place.VA is excellent you can feel how hard the seiyus worked on it, I have nothing to add on that particular point, the cast speak for itself.So overall, great game, great experience. It also seems to have decent replayability. I may have highlighted some issues but please believe me when I say that the gameplay more than makes up for it.All melee damage +1.5%

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely mediocre game 4/10. Which compared to its predecessor, Rabi, being an 11/10 game makes it even more disappointing.TLDR; almost every single thing to comment on in this game shows it in a negative light or makes it mediocre at best.No home town to rest (Rabi had the best town music and all your friends were there).Story driven game mean upgrades are locked behind progression not exploration. Story is just downright bad. Story driven means constant dialogue, and long cutscenes.Dialogue is always too bloated. Sable dialogue is always pointing out the obvious while Celia dialogue is pure exposition and lore dump (a shame that someone as talented as Yoko Hikasa is used as an info dump character). Cutscenes are jammed in all over the place, sometimes with a 1 line cutscene then 5 seconds of player movement, then another short cutscene. Or worse certain boss battles have cutscenes in the middle of them, and some are even cut short by a cutscene, making you wonder why the devs even gave it another health bar if the battle ends before you finish all the health of the boss.Most of the map is built like a maze with one-way paths that trick you into going into the same circle about 5 times, usually with annoying rooms in those loops. You'll often come across areas looking like they should have a secret but are either nothing, or just something that opens up from the other side later. Nothing about exploration feels like it makes any sense, from the direction you are going to the location of items.Money is limited (as far as I am aware) and unfarmable, making it harder to buy out shops or even to craft items (which many require money to craft for some silly reason). But it doesn't even matter because, besides a few potions which you definitely will get, the shops are just full of sigils, most of them aren't even that good.Killing enemies serves only the purpose of getting materials to craft. (and also possibly leveling up, which shouldn't even be a system in a metroidvania)Crafting system is completely unnecessary and only truly serves to upgrade certain gear (could be done any other way) and get consumables (which could be store bought or respawning items or anything else).Sigil system is WAAAAAY over complicated with WAAAAY too many sigils, many of them giving you abilities that feel like they should be part of your core move-set. The order of sigils and their placement in the menu will also constantly change as you acquire more sigils, making it even harder to keep track of which is which. Sigils are just a horrible copy of Badges from Rabi, and have been done wrong is every way possible.Combat it decent but is very floaty which is easy to not like (but isn't really a problem). Even after unlocking, what feels like, hundreds of new moves to bring to combat, it still feels like you're just mashing the attack button and adding in some 'this and that' to keep the combo flowing. The only exciting thing about combat is dodging boss attacks while trying to dish out some damage, but the battles aren't that difficult and once you've seen the attacks once there's no gimmick to throw you off and it just becomes easy.That's what most of this game feels like: A gammick. Almost a mockery to its predecessor. I easily spent 1000 hours in Rabi but I can't bring myself to even spend 50 hours in Tevi.Not worth it, just go play Rabi instead. Or basically any other metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review: I found TEVI to be a delightful experience within the metroidvania genre, offering solid gameplay that kept me engaged for hours. It was really fun to play, providing ample enjoyment along with occasional moments of challenge, since the game wasn't really hard but have it challenging moments which takes more time to beat. As with any game, TEVI has its share of pros and cons, but with a few tweaks, it could easily ascend to greatness.Pros:- The game have a visually enchanting art style, from its charming characters designs to the well-crafted levels, creating an aesthetically pleasing world. While also Tevi is not just cute but also impressively designed character, making playing alongside her and all environment a visual treat for the eye.- The combat system, while intricate, is well-executed, offering diverse possibilities for approaching fights. It allowed me to experiment with various combat combo strategies, ensuring an enjoyable experience.- The level design stands out, ensuring each area feels distinct, keeping monotony at bay. Moreover, the enemies posed a genuine threat, adding depth instead of merely serving as obstacles.- The music is a standout feature, providing an immersive backdrop whether exploring or engaged in combat. It was truly a pleasure listen to it while playing.- Plus, the ability to pet the bunny added an adorable touch that brought extra joy for meCons:- The abundance of sigils felt overwhelming, leading to confusion due to the extensive scrolling required to find specific sigils. Streamlining this aspect by focusing on fewer but more impactful sigils could enhance the gameplay experience while also make player focus on different builds.- Some crucial items being locked behind story progression limited the freedom to explore and try different strategies in subsequent runs, slightly detracting from the overall experience.The storyline, while not objectionable, didn't leave a significant impression, falling into a neutral territory for me.In summary, TEVI stands as a solid game worthy of exploration. Its captivating visuals, fluid animations, and enjoyable gameplay make it an experience worth trying. Recommend to give it a try and play.

_childDocuments_.review: I have greatly mixed feelings on Tevi, it's clearly a passion project with a ton of work put into it and the core platforming, combat, and exploration are rock solid.  Boss fights with their bullet hell attacks are a lot of fun and the map is big enough to get lost in.  I always enjoy that feeling of stumbling across a new area in a metroidvania and deciding to explore.  But it has a lot of major issues right now.  The story is really overwritten, the balance between bosses and exploration is a mess (I beat several late game bosses without needing to use a single one of my 10 consumables, but couldn't turn up the difficulty because exploration was already harder than I liked) and some of the map design is really bad, with a ton of one-way passages that force backtracking, some of which are traps that you can't see until you touch them.  Music is a tossup, there are some excellent tracks like Verdazure Sea, Evernight Garden, Angelomania, and Replica, but a lot are forgettable.Overall I'd recommend it, but only to people who already played and enjoyed the spiritual prequel Rabi Ribi since I think that's ultimately the better game even if it's not as flashy.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: TEVI is a Bullet Hell - Spectacle Fighter - Metroidvania that follows the in the footsteps of its predecessor Rabi-Ribi, while elevating gameplay and story to new heights.Demo is permanent and free, give it a whirl.Like Erina before her, Tevi is an agile and nimble character that attacks with fast-paced movement, aided by the angel Celia and demon Sable for ranged support. What separates Tevi from Erina is having much more attack variety, including actual air combos, a backflip dodge, attacks that ragdoll enemies, Boost Magic (now called Core Expansion) providing a bullet shield, and a massively expanded badge system (called Sigils) that alter existing abilities and will influence her playstyle. Tevi does not have stamina, but instead enemies now accumulate armor to resist hitstun, and bosses have a BREAK gauge to render them vulnerable to crowd control. Enemies and especially bosses are also much more reliant on buffs/debuffs than in Rabi-Ribi.Rabi-Ribi has no RPG elements aside from currency. TEVI now has material drops and crafting but they are very streamlined compared to typical Vanias: there are exactly 10 material types with very reasonable drop rates that can be increased with backpack expanders and has material conversion, all crafting for consumables and Sigils and upgrading for powerups is done on the fly, money only comes from blocks instead of enemies (thus removing the need to grind and money sink), and leveling is done through map exploration and bosses instead of traditional EXP.In Rabi if I wanted to buy out the whole shop I'd have to farm Icy Summit. In TEVI, not once have I never needed to grind with enemies showering me in materials and finishing off with a surplus of extra currency.TEVI is a massive world of varying biomes: numerous forests, Tevi's oasis home in the middle of a canyon and desert, the skies of Valhalla, the dark depths of Tartarus, the cold mountain of Snowveil, steampunk industrial zones, and more.Level design starts out initially as fairly basic as Rabi-Ribi's, though several areas contain Blastorbs - tree bombs that can knocked into certain destructible blocks and enemies. Later on though, there are some surprisingly tough puzzles with the Cross Bombs, labyrinth mazes, and some involved platforming.This game features 40+ areas, 70+ original soundtracks, and 30-35 hours long excluding full exploration, making it one of the largest Metroidvanias to date.There are two gameplay modes that alter the exploration:Changeable in-game on Tevi's bed.That being said TEVI feels more balanced and overall easier and accessible, whereas Rabi-Ribi had some really nasty difficulty spikes on bosses, though I'd imagine anyone who's never played a bullet hell or dipped 100 hours into Rabi will struggle. On the other hand, common enemies and platforming are much more of a force to be reckoned with over Rabi's largely non-threatening fodder and mostly basic platforming.Rabi-Ribi was almost entirely light-hearted with slice-of-life shenanigans among its cast, but could essentially be summed up as an excuse plot. TEVI still has some happy friendly banter within its 50+ characters with the main trio effectively being a circus troupe, but brings a much more darker and ominous tale to the forefront.A notebook details and compiles all acquired lore, information on the game's races (humans, animal-eared beastkin, and magitech), factions, and so on and so forth.TEVI sports numerous characters of varying personalities. Tevi herself is a mischievous badass, Sable is best innocent boi,  Busty Biggs the victim of Tevi's antics, Professor Zema is a hilarious goofball with great contributions and inventions to improve Tevi's life, and Vena's just a tsundere pokemon rival Cocoa.The entire game is voiced by A-list Japanese actors that add life and personality, including Takehito Koyasu, Rie Kugimiya, Tomokazu Sugita, and Lynn. I'm still wondering where the hell CreSpirit got the budget for that!Yeah, that's it. Pettable bunny.Lol. Just watch Jojo's Bizarre Adventure Part 3 and you'll understand this.Rabi-Ribi still holds up incredibly well in terms of exploration, whereas TEVI improves on every other aspect.I think most of the negative complaints are pretty overblown, TEVI deviates a fair bit from Rabi-Ribi particularly with story progression and that is somehow deemed as "bad" which is pretty disheartening to see. But by and large, TEVI is one of the best Metroidvanias in existence.
