_childDocuments_.review: Better than I hoped for.  Coming from Rabi-Ribi this feels like your right at home.  Responsive controls, Runs perfect on the Steam Deck, Graphics are polished and highly detailed, especially love all the dialogue art and multiple expressions and poses are a step up from Rabi-Ribi.  The story is a lot more interesting and I look forward to every dialogue sequence because there is a lot of funny and genuine moments throughout.  Boss battles are tough, but not too crushing (playing on Normal). The amount of perk customizations and upgrades you can get for Tevi is super fun and makes game progression feel like your always chasing a new skill. Enemies in the game have a greater variety from super cute to very scary and tough. Soundtrack and voice acting is top-notch although i'd argue Rabi-Ribi's soundtrack was perfection. Still have a lot of exploring and quests to do and looking forward to playing more.  Definitely worth every penny and the hype surpassed my expectations.  9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Beat main story on hard difficulty.Come for the gameplay. Map is a blast to fly through, enemies and bosses are a blast to fight. The movement and controls are very tight with the exception of some of the spanner moves which require multiple buttons that I always happened to be holding down and accidentally used. Same for dodge meter which I never did figure out how to use effectively during combat. There were keys for those though. Really like the sigil system as well. Great music as well. Personally liked all the characters and art but the story is just okay. Fun enough but definitely a wild ride in terms of tone and pacing.

_childDocuments_.review: Rabi Ribi but newer, better, and freshif you liked Rabi RIbi you will absolutely like Tevi.Story is rather simple but enough to keep you invested; you can follow and predict the story but it still has surprises and that makes it fun and enjoyable.Characters are very cute and very nicely voiced. They all have unique personalities and are just fun to follow around.Combat is amazing. Take Rabi Ribi and make it better. The sigils are very unique and non-formulaic, they change many aspects of your actions, enabling so many customizable unique playstyles and combos; there is no obvious one true way to do it, and I love it. I played on Expert difficulty and it's very challenging but not unfair, it's very well balanced.I realize that this game is not for everyone; the difficulty may be on the higher end (and it is IMO one of its strongest appeal), but definitely give the game a try. The rest of what the game has to offer makes up for a nice fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty decent metroidvania/bullet hell game. I beat the game on "hard" difficulty and didnt think it was particularly hard to be honest. Difficulty allegedly adjust the bullet hell portion of the game so you don't have to discard the game if you are afraid of the bullet hell locking you on any fight.PROS:- Large map, lots to explore.- Customizable combat style via sigils.- Quite the variety of enemies/attack patterns, doesnt get boring quick.- Some fun challenges.- A lot of clever mini puzzles to reach hidden or hinted areas/items.CONS:- SUPER EXTREME ludonarrative dissonance. If this bothers you a lot I do not recommend forcing yourself through this, it goes from bad to cringe hell as game progress. Story would'v been ok if it wasn't for the ludonarrative dissonance being present on EVERY mayor event through the game.- Many of the hidden spots require you to spam bombs in places that are not obvious at all, this is a bit of a chore considering placing bombs is a slow action that locks you in place while doing it.MID:- Movement and combat is very solid but a couple things could use a tweak - Dialogue is voiced, which is cool, but it can be super slow to go through the dialogue and there is A LOT of dialogue on this considering the genre of the game.- Markers are neat, but placing them is a bit akward, could be moved to the map instead of consumables menu.

_childDocuments_.review: [Content Spoilers, Mild Story Spoilers][tl;dr]This is a very difficult review to write. It is a good game and I recommend it but it certainly has flaws especially compared to Rabi Ribi.Tevi that does enough to be not the same game twice, with cohesive Story and new mechanics. However, way too easy and due to major difference introduced compared to Rabi Ribi makes it a less enjoyable experience.[Review]For those that have not played Rabi Ribi yet and are interested in it but are a bit turned of by it's fanservice or difficulty, then this is might be the game for you.For those that like me that already have played Rabi Ribi, it is not Rabi Ribi and of course it doesn't want to be. Never make the same game twice. And yet it still kinda is?It does feel a lot like a Rabi Ribi Redo but with a bigger budget which allows it to have a story with voice actors and a much bigger explorable world. And some problems stem from this.[Story]The story isn't bad nor good but you do have characters that are more fleshed out this time and grow attached to. Also the voice acting is phenomenal. However the story isn't like with Rabi Ribi where cute girls do be cute bullet hell things and it takes a darker turn. Not sure how I feel about the ending yet.And while it does that, it also behaves a lot like Rabi Ribi that when the character served it's purpose it is pretty much forgotten. Some characters do reappear, but even some characters you'd think would impact the story may not and only serve as a boss battle or appear for a single cutscene.[Gameplay]Again kinda Rabi Ribi and kinda not. The exploration is pretty much 1:1 Rabi Ribi and that is a good thing, but there could've been some item that changed it.Battles are much more different. Tevi mostly plays like Erina did but is given more defensive options and with the inclusion of our two companions can even clear enemy bullets. Most of the changes come from the difference between Ribbon and the combo of Celia and Sable.[Enemies, Bosses]As for Enemies, they introduced a Dominant State that makes them immune to hitlag, in Rabi Ribi this was more of the inverse as you had a window where they were susceptible to damage.This even is true for Boss Battles and is were my biggest issues come into play.Bosses now seem to just attack for a short period and then you can spam them with attacks to do massive damage.Additionally you can "Break" them, which puts them in a state where you can give them extra damage and they will not attack you at all. And with the help of equipable Sigils you can do that often thus ignoring most of their attacks.This mechanic needs to be fixed, Bosses need to have a period where you cannot damage them at all and the will spam you with attacks that you have to dodge. There is a single boss that does that with the most eerily calming boss music, which was the only Boss battle I truly enjoyed.What could be done to the others bosses is to put them in a constant Dominant state with additional Buffs that can only be outdone by putting them in the Break state and then you can go ham with them. That would also make more sense, given these states where meant to visualize when Mobs are actively attacking. And that way the fights are more active compared to Rabi Ribi as you have to dodge their attacks and hit them in order to get the window where they are receiving damage.[Difficulty]Playing this on Hard, I was very underwhelmed since I expected it to be Rabi Ribi Hard.As mentioned in the previous section, the battle mechanics make the game way too easy and for the most part I didn't even have to bother dodging enemies especially later on. I think for only 3 bosses I bothered to actually dodge their attacks. Furthermore you can always press Up to do a Backflip that will just Dodge attacks and you can also active something similar to the Amulet in Rabi Ribi, but I never bothered to use that.[Exploration]This world is much bigger than Rabi Ribi to the point where exploring for collectibles becomes a bit to tedious, and I do love Metroidvanias. Some of the levels have very weird paths that make no sense, such as blocking you off to be able to traverse back just for the next room to allow you to go back instead. Why?And some rooms suggest to have a hidden item only for you coming back to it after every upgrade you get and it just being some useless addition to the map.In general, lot of the times it was that some items or resources are too hidden and on such a big map this is a problem. However, you gain after finishing the game a way to make this easier, but then again there is no reason for it as there is no Post Game content.[Replayablity]This was one of the big reasons why Rabi Ribi is that good. You can replay it in many ways and it offers so much content. Tevi offers this too, but in Tevi's case I don't think it will translate well here due to the length and the story progressions. However, you will unlock Free Roam Mode which apparently will make playthroughs to be objective oriented and less linear.However, it feels less like a game that I want to come back to and replay, if I want to do that I would just go back to Rabi Ribi where I have much more of a challenge. I might still give Inferno BBQ a chance in Free Roam Mode.[Music]The music is again great, but to me it also falls short to Rabi Ribi. Overall it is less catchy.While some areas have massive bangers, but as for jams you just wanna vibe with you have noneand.As for Boss Themes, since bosses are already underwhelming as is, quite some Boss Themes didn't made them more epic.[Conclusion]It is overall a good game that just sadly pales in comparison with it's predecessor that achieves more with less. I also have to say I did play Rabi Ribi when all additional content already was released so it might be an unfair comparison to playing the game Day 1. While there are certainly things that cannot be fixed, but given the Devs some credit, this game might shine much brighter with future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr1 - Whether or not TEVI surpasses Rabi Ribi is a matter of opinion... but for me it did not.tl;dr2 - TEVI is a solid metroidvania, with great visuals, gameplay, polish and a lot of content! But unfortunately, questionable story and characters.Rabi Ribi is my favorite indie game and favorite metroidvania of all time, and I was so excited to play this game knowing it was made by the same creators, and even MORE excited to realize it's a spiritual successor! Many things are the same, from the way exploration and movement upgrades work, to how boss battles flow and how combat works, how the music and other sound effects sound, visual effects and bullet patterns... very Rabi Ribi. Even if the game was going to have its differences (which it also definitely does), I was eager to give this a fair shot and even willing to call this game GOTY 2023 if it lived up to high expectations.After 142 hours, I finally 100%ed the game with all achievements, and have had many complete runs across all difficulties and modes, so I have a lot to say. I also finished my first run 100% after about 60 hours, which I'd say is a lot for a metroidvania game, but I also spent a lot of time experimenting, exploring, and looking up words, both japanese and english. Quick note about that: this game has by far the most sophisticated vocabulary I've seen out of the steam games I've played. Off the top of your head, do you know the meanings of the words temerarious, pellucid, alembic, geas, welter, sartorial, "quid est pax", scion, or egress? I'm the kind of person who likes to look up words I'm not sure of, and this game has had me doing a lot of that, haha...Let's talk about the strengths of this game, cause there are many! The visuals are beautiful, especially the parallax-scrolling backgrounds. Parallax is an effect many gamers know about by now, but still, this game does it especially well with highly detailed pixel art even in areas you would consider "indoors". It really helps add to the immersion. A lot of the gameplay strengths of Rabi Ribi are here, from precise movement to well-balanced combat damage numbers, to carefully thought-out world exploration, etc. Many things are improved too: you might recognize "dominant" and "BREAK" like states in Rabi Ribi's battles, but this game makes it very explicit and gives you extra control over how you want to customize around it through "sigils" (basically the badge system but heavily expanded). If you didn't like grinding for En, this game has a different system that I found to be very well handled, rewarding you just enough from defeating enemies but not necessarily letting you have too many resources for free. There's so much to talk about, but one thing to focus on....VOICE ACTING!!! I was stunned when I first saw the VA list for this game. Rabi Ribi didn't have voice acting, and now all of a sudden, you have a list of some of the most well-known names in the anime industry?! Tomokazu Sugita, Rie Kugimiya, Takehito Koyasu.... if you know anything about anime at all, you're sure to recognize these names and a heckton more. It must not have been easy to pull together an all-star cast like this for an indie game, and I think it's effort very well-spent. The voice acting in this game is wonderful, it really adds personality to the characters and makes dialogue scenes you'd normally skip, into things you'll be glad you stuck around for. I do think some voices don't perfectly fit the character designs they're given to, but either way, I found the voice acting to be one of the most impressive features of this game that set it apart from Rabi Ribi.Speaking of characters and dialogue though.... let's get to some flaws. For me personally, Rabi Ribi is a near-perfect game with one minor issue: story and characters. I still think Rabi Ribi's story is very confusing, and I couldn't help but want a little more screentime and development out of the characters who I generally really enjoyed. This wasn't a big deal to me though, because Rabi Ribi has a silly magical world with many wholesome moments and a few moments of intrigue and mystery, while focusing more on good gameplay, and that was enough for me. But TEVI, I could tell it wanted to address this weakness and really take lore and drama to the next level. Even if I don't think it was well-executed, I will always respect that. The devs could have easily made a Rabi Ribi 2 knowing how beloved that first game was (and you can easily tell the devs themselves love Rabi Ribi too), but instead, they went for something ambitious, which I think is absolutely wonderful and the right thing to do. I'm sure they will take this as a learning experience and the devs are not done making games yet! I'll gladly wait another few years for their next shot at making better and better works!The main issue for me is that characters are not developed enough, probably because there are too many of them, because this game wants to have lots of boss battles and also tie them to plot. But if you look at say, metroid or hollow knight, the boss characters arent fleshed out through dialogue and plot progression, but rather through subtle atmospheric lore. In TEVI, to keep things spoiler-light, I'll just say that there are a lot of important boss characters that arent revealed until very late in the game, right as you're about to fight them. This is a big no-no, because that means "important" characters lack impact and we hardly know or care about them by the time we need to fight them. It also makes us lose touch with the protagonists, because we don't really see them think about things or change and develop enough for us to relate to them. Some character interactions you would naturally expect after important plot moments just dont happen, and I'll just say (to be spoiler-light again), "two important mid-game boss characters" have such confusing and occasionally contradictory characterizations that even by the end of the game, questions around them don't feel conclusively answered.Music also... I mean, TEVI's music is "good". I think the tracks are well-made, appropriate to the environments and moods, and have some nice melodies. But again, it's hard not to compare it to Rabi Ribi. I think Rabi Ribi had exceptionally memorable music, and honestly while playing through TEVI, I had a lot of Rabi Ribi's music stuck in my head even though I haven't played that game in a long time. Meanwhile, even after over 100 hours of playtime, I still struggle to remember what some of TEVI's music sounded like. Again, I don't think TEVI's music is bad, I just think it's hard to live up to Rabi Ribi which had so many strong tracks......There's a lot more that can be said (I originally went 4488 characters over steam's review limit so I've had to trim it down a lot), but there is one last thing I've had in mind throughout playing TEVI. Which is, this game has helped me realize that Rabi Ribi is my "happy place". Playing Rabi Ribi just made me happy, and every single time TEVI made nods to Rabi Ribi (and there are plenty such moments), I felt happy and remembered how much I enjoyed that game. The music, the world, the characters, everything. It's just such a magical and wholesome world with so much to love. Maybe that's the reason TEVI fell a bit flat for me - I really do think it has a lot of strengths and is not a "bad" game, it's certainly more polished than a lot of other games you'll see out there. But TEVI never really made me feel "happy" or in love with the characters or music or pretty much anything like that. On it's own, TEVI is still a really good game that probably blows a lot of other games out of the water. But Rabi Ribi exists, and is a major reason why people know about this game, so it's difficult not to make comparisons like this. I'm generally not someone who likes comparing things and saying one thing's better than another, so I'll just say in the end, it's a matter of opinion!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I'm very impressed with Tevi. The creators of Rabi-Ribi looked at their work and decided they could do better, and they were incredibly correct. Tevi is basically Rabi-Ribi, but with solid, substantial improvement to every single aspect. The movement, the combat, the upgrade mechanics, the art, the music, the story, all of it. There are massive improvements to everything, and the game is an absolute joy to play. I gladly 100%-ed the game on normal, and I'm pretty tempted to come back and try the higher difficulty levels and some of the additional options unlocked after beating the game, which is very rare for me. I'm probably going to let it percolate for a bit, but I think once the post game content update comes later, I'll give the game a shot on the highest difficulty. 10 out of 10, would recommend to anyone, but especially folks who like metroidvanias, bullet hell, or just liked Rabi-Ribi.

_childDocuments_.review: Generally, TEVI is an enjoyable metroidvania with ~25-35hrs worth of main story content depending on difficulty. The combat flows well, the bosses are unique, and the sigils allow for varied playstyles. Combos feel natural, especially during break. From a pure combat standpoint the game is phenomenal. It is what carries the game, as it is fun to apply what you've unlocked leading up to a boss in a fight and learning a different way to approach dealing damage. Unfortunately the other aspects of the game can feel unintuitive or lacking. To begin with, the story feels all over the place and very inconsequential until the absolute end of the game. Rabi-ribi sidestepped this issue by making the story optional in a sense; It never presented itself as a grand or mysterious story, just go find people to help find Miru. TEVI tries to make it's story interesting and relevant throughout the entire game, but fails to deliver on any real payoff. There is too many side stories that feel forced to explain why you should be exploring a given area. They are dull, and have zero bearing on the actual story of the game leaving the characters involved easily forgotten. This wouldn't be a huge issue if it wasn't blended with the fact that the game is on rails after Chapter 3. There is nothing to do but explore to get powerups or progress with the story. You are heavily incentivized to progress with the story as all mobility/exploration items are locked behind it. Rabi-ribi does this as well, but doesn't put a core mobility item exceptionally late into the game -- TEVI has  not only locked behind story, but close to the end of the game. Suffice to say that you are supposed to engage with the story as any real progress is gated behind it.If you skip the story, you'll realise just how much there is in the game. Everything you do that isn't exploring has a lengthy description as to why you are doing it. Of course the obvious nothing will make sense will apply, but the amount of dialogue you will need to skip over is somewhat absurd. Enter a new area? Gotta make a comment about that. Going to fight a boss? There has to be some preamble followed by an often redundant arena fight, followed by another comment. Sure, it makes the main cast seem more alive, but it also shows the how meaningless everyone else is. Even the (non main cast) main story relevant characters feel half baked. In particular: And with the story out of the way, it paves way to the actual game issues. In no particular order:- Map design is just weird. -- Too many rooms feel like they should have a secret or at least something, but end up empty. -- Way too many "Connector" rooms (i.e rooms like above)-- Way too many one way exits. You often will go in one direction, only to realise it was the "wrong way" and have to play through the same screens just to pick the right way-- The forest maze. Have fun trying to find everything there- Large bosses feel awkward to fight. This is primarily because the fights feel gimmicky in nature.-- Of the large bosses, - Spanner attacks feel underwhelming and unnecessary-- Mana pillar has crazy hit lag, and isn't worth using till the endgame-- Spanner bash requires being aerial and makes you grounded, meaning it's not good for either aerial or grounded fights-- Tornado whirl animation locks you for an excessive amount of time for little damage without sigils. You want to use it during break, but usually there are better combo lines for damage- Backflip feels like it's just there to be cool. It's only truly relevant while you have nothing else that can proc dodge, and seemingly gets in the way more times than not.-- The sigils related to backflip sound nice on paper, but in practice trying to use them is hell.- Secrets are either shoved in your face or hidden randomly-- This is not helped by the fact that the item which tells you if you're close to a secret isn't available until after you finish the game- Town passes feel like a remnant of another system. They exist as a backup to not finding a teleporter in a city, but they are not hard to find.-- To double down, you can warp from the train station to the shop, but not to/from the city teleporter.- Some areas you can get to early are blocked by dialogue saying you can't go in. Some areas are blocked by physical walls that can't be removed. Pick one not both.-- This is especially frustrating when you explore an area, thinking there was a secret there only to be told to go back to the area because there was a(n undistinguishable) wall stopping you. - Consumables feel annoying. They are very relevant in bossfights, but are a chore to make until later on when you get and item that helps you.-- Bosses feel very challenging without them, and "difficult" at best with them.-- This is doubled down with the fact that you get to carry a lot more as you progress the game.- It feels like half the secrets/collectables are zennies. There is a lot more zennies in the game than needed to buy out the shops.- Too many sigils with varied effects. Customisation is good, but there is too many to remember and an endgame loadout can have 40-50.- Too many i-frames by the endgame. -- Dodge is good, but trying to use it when you aren't mashing your faces against a boss is tricky.-- Soul burst feels forgettable since you unlock it later, and being able to hold more than one stack is gated by story progression.-- Core expansion can last for a hilariously long amount of time, and you get is back relatively easy.-- Mana pillar becomes just a better core expansion when you get the sigils for it.I finished this game on expert for my first playthrough. I can appreciate that the game can be difficult for others on this mode, but it felt like after the midgame bosses became easy to just faceroll. While I will come back to finish the game on infernal, I believe that there is some needed patches to the game. By the end, I was aggressively trying to just push through the rest of the game to say that I was done. It felt like the game was falling apart, as the story was just getting worse as I progressed. I have hope that the game will receive some additional content and overall improvements. I'm not expecting Rabi-ribi levels of DLC or changes, but at least something extra. We are already confirmed to be getting a boss rush, and mid playthrough I noticed some changes to the map that were much appreciated. It is clear that (at least at time of writing) there is intention to making the game better, and potentially additional story/dlc content.

_childDocuments_.review: TEVI is a game that defies easy categorization, offering players a surreal and thought-provoking journey into the unknown. While it has its flaws, its unique atmosphere and innovative gameplay make it a title worth experiencing for those looking for something outside the mainstream.- Atmospheric World: TEVI excels in creating an atmospheric world that feels both haunting and strangely beautiful. From its minimalist art style to its ambient soundtrack, every element contributes to a sense of immersion that draws players into its enigmatic universe.- Innovative Gameplay Mechanics: The game introduces innovative gameplay mechanics that challenge players to think outside the box. From manipulating time to solving puzzles using unconventional methods, TEVI keeps players on their toes with its fresh approach to gameplay.- Thought-Provoking Narrative: TEVI's narrative is cryptic and open to interpretation, leaving players to piece together the story from fragmented clues scattered throughout the game world. It's a narrative that encourages reflection and invites players to ponder deeper philosophical questions.- Stunning Visuals: Despite its minimalist art style, TEVI features stunning visuals that make the most of its surreal setting. From dreamlike landscapes to otherworldly creatures, every aspect of the game's visual design is meticulously crafted and visually striking.- Lack of Clarity: While TEVI's cryptic narrative adds to its mysterious atmosphere, it can also be frustratingly vague at times. Some players may find themselves confused or disoriented by the lack of clear direction, leading to moments of frustration.- Pacing Issues: The game's pacing can be uneven, with periods of slow exploration punctuated by sudden bursts of action or puzzle-solving. This uneven pacing can disrupt the flow of the gameplay experience and detract from its overall enjoyment.- Limited Replay Value: Once the mystery of TEVI's narrative has been unraveled, there's little incentive for players to revisit the game. While its innovative gameplay mechanics may offer some replayability, the lack of alternative paths or endings limits its long-term appeal.Overall, TEVI is a game that offers a unique and thought-provoking experience for those willing to embrace its unconventional approach. While it may not be without its flaws, its atmospheric world, innovative gameplay mechanics, and thought-provoking narrative make it a title worth exploring for fans of experimental indie games.You can check out my TEVI playthrough here:

_childDocuments_.review: Breaks my heart because the game has so many good qualities: art, music, enormous map and tight controls.  But combat is the biggest part and it's just... tedious.  Fighting anything takes way longer than it should and is just not fun.  Thankfully you can simply run past most enemies, but I shouldn't want to do that.  Combat should be engaging and rewarding, but instead it's a slog and a half.  Boss fights are insane; their health pools are ridiculously big.  The only good thing about the fights taking so long is you can see how much effort went into all the many boss mechanics and phases.  In other games, when you beat a boss you normally feel that sense of accomplishment; here you're just shouting FINALLY before moving on and dreading the next fight.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system is way too complicated. There's an in-game dictionary of status effects with over a hundred entries, a move list with a few dozen, tons of sigils (equippable upgrades) with complex effects like "when combo counter is below 7, using basic ground combo II will be followed by basic air combo II; additionally, basic air combo I and basic air combo II attack speed +40% and both become a 2-hit attack". That's verbatim one of the sigils you can equip! And in late game I have more than 50 sigils equipped at once. There's no way I can possibly remember all these effects.The game's fundamental mechanics are also too complex. Late in the game I spent a very frustrating half hour trying to figure out why my invulnerable dodge moves only sometimes worked. There's some kind of dodge meter that gives you a status effect that makes the next use of certain moves invulnerable. I really thought I'd learned from experience that some of them were invulnerable without that status, but maybe not? I'm honestly still not sure. And I don't know what the difference between knockback and blowback is. And I don't know the full rules about what gives you orbitar crystals. And I can never remember the 6 different modes I can switch my ranged attacks to, so I mostly only use 2.Oh yeah, and the game often pauses itself during boss fights to explain new mechanics it's introducing on the spot.Attacking is boring because your melee attacks hitstun enemies and lock you into an animation, so you're basically just mashing the X and Y button until the enemy starts to resist hitstun then getting away. As for those dozens of combos I mentioned? I have no idea how you'd even go about determining which one lets you do damage the fastest; the damage of each hit seems to be wildly different every time and could be being affected by a dozen sigils. So you'll probably just end up button mashing like I do. And even if you did figure out that maybe repeating X-X-X-A is better than repeating X-X-X-X, how's that any more fun?The normal enemies are not very interesting to fight because they can usually be stunlocked to death so they never get to do anything once you start hitting them.Exploration is much less enjoyable than in other metroidvanias I've played, for several reasons:First thing that bothers me about the story is the glorification of monarchy. Of course, glorifying monarchy is hardly unusual for fantasy stories, but Tevi's case is worse, since it not only portrays monarchic rule as justified but also the queens as cool, beautiful, and likable people; and a past "rebellion" was supposedly the worst thing to ever happen to the world and characters can't stop talking about how bad it was and how the police fought so bravely to crush the rebellion; and at least twice it uses the word "anarchy" in connection with this rebellion, a word which actually refers to just the lack of belief in a cult of violence that most people in real life happen to believe in.Now, let's move on to less ideological complaints. Tevi, the protagonist, is unlikable for the first half of the story. She's over-glorified, being the best at everything she does and the coolest and the bravest, and often praised by other characters and herself, and she never suffers. And she's a jerkass: she often ♥♥♥♥♥ on other characters, including her dad, who've done nothing to deserve it. She gets better in the second half of the story, but that doesn't make the first half any more enjoyable.The plot is meandering and usually lacks stakes or pathos. It feels less like a cohesive story and more like the random adventures of our wish fulfullment girl with bunny ears. And it often doesn't make sense logically. For example, there's a part where you find out that the #2 person in charge of a seemingly good organization has been doing eugenics, abducting and murdering the unfit (don't ask me how this was kept secret for so long). You do a boss fight against him, and then... you let him walk away. And go back to his position of power. You don't even report this to the #1 person in charge. You later find out that the #1 person was on board with it, and... she's still treated like a benevolent figure after that. You later seek her out as an ally. The writers haven't forgotten, because Tevi brings it up in the meeting with her. It's just like the characters considered that not enough to render her a villain.Overall, the story is so bad that I started skipping some dialogue around halfway through, just skimming and reading the objective marker descriptions afterward.There's also this conspicuous gender trend. Basically every male character is either a villain, a doofus, or often both. All the cool, glorified characters are female.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at the bottom“the story is that one meme with the horse that suddenly becomes low quality at the end” - A random discord user summing up the story of TEVI.The plot of TEVI is honestly it’s weakest part, so if you’re looking for an amazing story then look further. (But then why are you looking for that in a metroidvania genre?)The story starts off great. It has nice intrigue, a goofy and interesting cast… but then the plot happens and the developers don’t really seem to know how to actually write an interesting plot. A lot of the info we (the player) get is in something like “hey, did you know that” format, or the characters basically reading off wikipedia articles. Some of those parts would actually be fine if the dialogue got rewritten a bit to make them feel a bit more natural.Besides the story, everything else was a step-up from the studio’s previous game: Rabi-Ribi. The combat is more fluid and varied, if even more bonkers than in the previous game.. The game gives you a set of two basic combos, loads of other melee moves, and 2 ranged characters to support you; each one having 3 different sets of normal and charged attacks. One specs into multi-hit attacks, piercing, or explosions. The other into heavy single blows, bounces and homing.Tons of options to pick from in order to make those flashy combos straight out of DMC.The music is simply gorgeous, nuff said about it.Exploration is made even more important than in most games, as you gain XP only by exploring or defeating bosses. Cash is also made by exploration. You find rocks with golden cracks, destroy them, and get money. That means fighting trash mobs won’t make you stronger. They will give you crafting resources though. And even then, the “good stuff” you use to make upgrades has a very small chance to drop and is more often found by, you guessed it, exploration. The puzzles were also pretty nice, enough to make me pause and think for a moment on how to solve them in order to get the loot.However there is one glaring issue behind the exploration, and that is (once again) the story. The developers have locked all of the essential upgrades behind it. Which means you cannot fully explore until chapter 8 or so. There IS a lot of freedom in the game though. However you won’t be able to 100% it until you complete the game.TL;DR: Great combat. Good exploration.Amazing music.Good story at the start, meh at the end.Essential upgrades locked behind the story.Try out the demo to see if you like combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:>Combat is fluid and engaging>World is large and diverse with interesting lore (at least for a while)>Good amount of customization - items and emblems can be crafted and turned on/off at will to support different playstyles and adjust risk/reward balance>Boss fights feel mostly unique from one another>The first half or so of the story is fun and interesting>The soundtrack is fitting; not incredibly memorable, but enjoyable enough.Cons:>Controller scheme feels overloaded - Over the course of the game, more and more moves get added with very similar inputs. I found it increasingly difficult to transition between different moves while also trying to avoid attacks without accidentally triggering the wrong one and getting locked into an animation that sent me plummeting down a hole or into a wave of bullets. (And yes, I know this sounds like a skill issue. It is. I doubt I'm the only one.)>Restrictions on how/when you can trigger dodge animations make utilizing it frustrating, especially early on (before you unlock other ways to trigger dodge animations). Pressing UP+Jump at the instant one of your melee attacks lands while your attack buffer is clear to dodge an enemy attack at point blank is hard to do.>The latter half of the story is pretty terrible. Almost every character in the game is just used as outrage fodder in one way or another. The main antagonist reveal is cheesy  - the characters and world lore have information that you, the player, aren't given until just before it's needed by the plot. As soon as you get said information, it's pretty obvious what is about to happen. The "why" it happened, which gets explained near the end, is very shallow. Many characters also deprive Tevi of information that could dramatically improve her decisions because the plot needs her to be uninformed. The ending lacks any meaningful resolution to a bunch of open questions about important characters and the plot. Overall (TL;DR) - If you like platformers with bullet hell mechanics, it's a decent game. Play for the exploration and combat, facepalm at the story content, and good luck mastering what I found to be a finicky set of inputs to clear the game.

_childDocuments_.review: SOOOOO Pleasantly surprised with how great this game is! Bought it on a whim looking for a new Metroidvania title to play through the holiday season, and am loving this one so far! Story is pretty good... I enjoy the translated banter but tend to skip through quite a bit since there is a lot. The art style is awesome. The music works very well for this game. The gameplay is perfect, albeit I'm a bit confused on how I'm unlocking new moves/techniques since XP doesn't seem to be a prominent thing. The pacing is perfect though. And then there's the combat. It's the best Metroidvania combat with ranged weapons as a focal point that I've played to date. In my opinion, MV games work best with melee focused combat with skill based parry or evade systems. This is quite the contrary. Both ranged and melee combat aspects work very well in concert with each other. I just started to unlock parry/evade techniques but I haven't used them much. There is a "bullet h377" aspect to the boss encounters where the deliberate concise character movement seems to be more effective then leaning on an evasion ability. The bosses are TOUGH though. I wandered around and came across a later game boss. I spent about 10 attempts and decided that I need to come back later. I'm about 4 legitimate boss battles in and I'd say 2 were pushovers, but the other 2 took about a half dozen attempts each over the course of about 10-15 minutes. Take a lot out of  you, but definitely fair. This game is a GREAT recommendation to anyone who enjoys Action RPG Platformer (Metroidvania) games (like Hollow Knight, the Shantae Series, Monster Boy Series, Rabi-Ribi, Luna Nights, etc). Not really game of the year material, but definitely a fun game that blew away all expectations I had!

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Metroidvania overall don't let simps of the previous game lure you away. "Flow": I see a lot of complaints about the story breaking up the pacing of the game or gating you behind things, which both are true but I feel are pretty normal for games like this. Even going back to the progenitors while without dialogue, you get gated behind beating a certain boss first. Now of course these days in super metroid you can get around that by exploiting minor glitches but until those were found it's the same thing. Beat spore spawn to get supers or get stuck. These types of games almost always lock you behind beating a path to progress with some kind of movement option or something to break a wall; this one just happens to have dialogue. Now is the story good? It's relatively enjoyable, nothing fancy, has some cheeky dialogue with lots of tropes which is about what I expected. Going in with the expectation of a relatively goofy cast with some serious beat sprinkled in I am having a good time. If it's not your cup of tea, no need to get upset about your "flow" just skip it.Difficulty: Started on hard so it's hard for me to say how normal is but it's nothing too difficult. Hard is just enough for me to get punished for just mashing and going ham but not too crazy for a blind try.Systems: Lots and lots of sigils, I think at the point of this review I have about 160. Now is every single one some game changer that changes a move? No, but when you get those it feels great. Am I going to complain about having more min/max and playstyle options? Also no, this "bloat" is easy to bypass by just picking what you like. Overall the combat and options feel quick and responsive and fun.Map: This is where most of the problems are, there are definitely a lot of spaces where you feel should be something but aren't, I think they were setting up gaps for enemies to jump out of or for you to hide from things attacks in but some seem pretty unnecessary. It can be a little disappointing at times but overall I don't hate bombing every single thing, it's what I did when I first played super metroid when it came out so I can't really complain. There do seem to be a lot of dead ends for just health though which is weird, unless these are just elite combat rooms I haven't found the guy to unlock the fight for hard to say.Lots of content to find and do that being said, I'm not going to say no to more game and exploration/back tracking with my new gizmos to see if I missed anything. Thankfully the map tells you exactly how many items and resources are in each zone, so I don't have to guess if I missed anything.Not flawless, I'd say an 8 or 9 out of 10, will have to try more to find out

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad game, but personally I didn't like it from the very beginning.The reason for it was primarily how the cast of characters are straight out of a cliché, run-of-the-mill, subpar anime.If you're a seasoned anime watcher and have seen all the stereotypes and tropes in the book already, you'll want to deafen and blind yourself whenever any of the characters come on screen. They have to utter a single sentence, and you know their entire personality already. But unlike some series that manage to make these tropes actually enjoyable, TEVI - like the majority of anime - makes its cast unbearably obnoxious to anyone older than a teenager chock-full of hormones who just stumbled upon the medium (like me when I was one).If you are such a teenager or are able to endure such a cast of characters OR perhaps do enjoy these tropes (which is totally fine, but just not my cup of tea), then TEVI might have a lot of fun in store for you. Though, I do want to note that it doesn't really do anything revolutionary. If you've played similar games in the past, and are looking for a game that spices things up, I don't think TEVI will fulfill those hopeful wishes. It's quite standard, and even under-performs in some fields, such as the areas you explore - which are very linear and boring and don't even look all that great, despite the very appealing screenshots you can see on the store page.It's quite an alright game, definitely not bad, but the cast may be very undesirable, and its price tag is very steep for a game that doesn't deliver anything outstanding or innovative. Hence, I don't recommend TEVI.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've been browsing the reviews, chances are you've seen a common sentiment for Tevi: "It's like Rabi Ribi, but not as good", and like... yeah; that's the short of it.To be fair, I think a lot of the reviewers (me included) have a bias. Rabi Ribi is my favourite game ever, and while it is still recognized as one of the best metroidvanias by its playerbase, I also played it when I was younger, so I carry some unfair nostalgia. Tevi is a very faithful spiritual sequel that feels remarkably similar, but ultimately it  the same game. Cynically, the game can feel simultaneously shackled by the legacy mechanics of Rabi Ribi it tries to replicate but also bloated by the attempts to expand on them.Yet, this is not a productive way of looking at games. No, Tevi is not my favourite game of all time. But it is a worthwhile Metroidvania experience, a solid 8/10 game. Instead, I want to ignore the existence of Rabi Ribi from here on out and try to analyze Tevi by its own merits. Obviously, the boss fights are meant to be the main feature of Tevi, and they remain a superb showing that CreSpirit truly understands what makes combat fun. When it works, every fight in Tevi is a masterful dance between you and your target: skillfully weaving between lasers waiting for even the smallest opening to close in with a slide or an airdash; taking your turn then backing off when the enemy is ready to strike anew.And it works most of time! Early and mid-game bosses are exciting and legitimately require you to understand and dodge their bullet patterns to topple them. The design of bosses does not get weaker per se, you just tend to stat-check a lot of the later fights, especially if you've been properly bombing every floor block like a good metroidvania gamer. This is compounded by the absurdly powerful builds you gain access to when collecting sigils (more on this later). Don't get me wrong, the later bosses  good and can still be challenging, but your higher HP and increased offensive options turns the deliberate ebb and flow I love into a tidal wave ramming against a wall with 5 health bars.The only universal complaint I have about bosses is that the combo counter is mismanaged. Many builds requir a certain combo rank to come online, but the combo disappears far too quickly unless you're permanently hitting the enemy in some way. Unfortunately, getting hit both doesn't put you in stun (usually) and doesn't  penalize your combo nearly as much as it should. As you might expect, the optimal strategy here then just sort of devolves into mindlessly charging at the enemy, purposefully tanking hits to not lose that precious rank.Again, the bosses are ultimately a high point here. Those life and death one-hit situations this system puts you in creates some of the highest dopamine rushes in a video game. On top of this, the boss designs are all very distinct and cool, being (mostly) both visually appealing and usually having a gimmick that gives the fight its own flavour. The golden concept you can't afford to mess up in metroidvanias is (say it with me...), . Tevi manages it's exploration adequately: it's a bit more linear than I'd like, sometimes resorting to artificial "You can't go there yet" text boxes to prevent the player from advancing in the wrong direction. This is because Tevi has a chapter-based story system, and it needs you to accomplish things in a certain order for it's story to make any sense.On the whole though, you are given lots of room to explore, and you often have multiple objectives to accomplish at once, so it's not like you're  limited in where you can go. Plus between stat-boosting potions (which are legitimately impactful), sigils, and good old money, there are enough collectibles to rummage around for wherever you go. Unfortunately the coolest items, the movement and/or progression ones, all feel pretty scripted. You usually get one a chapter so you can access the next boss, and the game makes sure it's impossible to get any of them early.However, in the endgame, the map is , and it feels soooo good when you're finally let off the reins and have access to every corner of it. Once you've gotten all your movement tools, zooming around looking for hidden items does hit the way a good metroidvania should. I especially love the short speedrun challenges peppered in, which require you to go from point A to B in a certain amount of time and without getting hit too much. These moments really highlight how delightful travelling is in Tevi, mostly thanks to the ingenious quickdrop, available at the start of the game, but shining when used in tandem with later techniques. (♥♥♥♥ I love quickdrop).Potions are the main reason you explore, and sigils (think Hollow Knight charms) are like loot boxes, in that their usefulness will vary greatly based on your build and playstyle. The game has in total 257, a ludicrous number, and it allows for  varied ways of approaching combat. Some combinations I've been able to find are just flat-out broken, able to put bosses in pseudo-infinite combos if you have the right setup (). A lot of the sigils are solidly niche though, and while I'm sure they have their uses, more often than not I found myself just equipping the ones that offer simple damage increases. The amount of text and conditions and (de)buffs you need to understand for some of these sigils is a lot. On top of that, there is a lot of unnecessary retread ground; for example, you have 3 separate "Perseverance" sigils that allow you to tank a hit before dying. It's a very good system that does allow for a lot of depth, but you need to really understand the game mechanics to get the most out of it, and be willing to theorycraft with trial and error to discover how certain things interact. So Tevi has made a bit of a gamble: taking away some of the mystique and excitement from its huge game map, removing the ability to explore it unencumbered and stumble into a unexpected boss, all to set up grandiose showdowns to hype the story it's trying to tell. It's a bold choice and a clear indicator that Tevi wants its narrative to be a driving force to keep the player's attention. Unfortunately, Tevi's story is quite bad. Not just bad... it's .Without getting into specifics, when you saturate your game with this many abruptly ended plot threads, twist villains, last-minute reveals, hidden information, and utterly nothing characters, what tangible thing is there even left to hold on to? The story is not complicated or convoluted, it is simply ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Trying to understand Tevi is like trying to finish a 4-piece puzzle but every second someone swaps in a piece from an entirely different puzzle. Yes the character designs are great. Tevi, Sable, and Celia are adorable together (especially Tevi, her personality is one of the few things that made me watch the cutscenes), and the voice acting is ok, but they are not enough to make me care about this awful story that the game forces you to sit through.Or kind of forces you to sit through. I'd be remiss not to mention that a lot of Tevi's lows are fixed by its own in-game modifiers. Freeroam mode allows for a more personalized progression through the map, and Potion Scaling makes late-game bosses more threatening. I had a substantially better experience on my second, harder playthrough of Tevi. Plus the new boss rush mode highlights the game's best parts. With both free and paid end-game DLC planned, I'm really looking forwards to coming back a third time a few months from now. Tevi is a great game today, and with enough patches and new content, maybe one day it won't remain forever stuck in the shadow of its older sibling.

_childDocuments_.review: Tevi is a pretty big and fun game I'll be going in depth on for this review, spoilers ahead past this tl;drtl;dr: If you're looking for fun bullet hell gameplay then pick up this game. The exploration aspect is fun but a bit weak. The story is somewhat engaging but falls flat a few moments. if you played Rabi-Ribi you'll find the story to be better and gameplay to be more engaging, however it isn't as open as its predecessor and many bosses and key items are locked behind the story progression. You can unlock free roam once you beat the game though. The game is a solid 7/10, might rise a rank after the next few updates though.Now for the deeper, spoilery review. I'll be going in order from what I think the game is best at to what its weakest points are:Gameplay (Combat):TEVI takes its predecessor's combo and badge system and runs with it. As you explore more and find new items your abilities expand as well! You can virtually customize your experience in almost every way. Want to spec into ranged damage? Sure thing. Want to be a glass cannon and be three shot by everything in exchange? Maybe you want to have the most survivability and dodges possible? Or maybe you prefer aerial melee combat over grounded combat? The combinations are limitless. This makes every single encounter unique in its own way and you can save multiple loadouts with the different loadout options TEVI gives you. Not only that but you can change your loadout if a fight proves to be difficult! Of course if you're skill enough it ultimately won't matter but for those who need that little extra help they can adjust their builds to fit the current encounter. Lastly, Tevi can learn some skills over time as well that adds more variety to her combat. In terms of the fights themselves, each fight felt unique and fun! Some bosses felt easier than others despite being later bosses, but I was never bored with them. The difficulty settings also feel far better than they did in Rabi Ribi. Bullet patterns feel fair and not just "slap extra bullets in random spots and call it a day" no bosses actually get more patterns and properly thought out additions to existing attacks.Gameplay (Exploration): The exploration factor of the game is pretty good, as expected of a metroidvania. However it suffers from a similar problem I have with starbound: Much of the upgrades and bosses are locked behind the story. Don't get me wrong, the game opens up a lot more as the story progresses however any major upgrades and pretty much all bosses cannot be accessed just by exploring which means you'll run into dead end after dead end anytime you want to go explore. This basically means that the ideal exploring method is to do it at the end of the game unless you want to constantly backtrack to the multitude of areas. Speaking of areas, there are a multitude of unique areas and towns to visit, however many areas also just feel like older areas with a new coat of pain. This one place is an ocean with a beach, that's cool. This other area is also underwater but its basically atlantis! That's really cool! But then we have... green forest, orange forest with exploding leaves, poison forest with exploding leaves...  you get the point. Ultimately, exploring is fun and doing so as you go with the story does help, but you aren't encouraged to do so at all due to all the dead ends. This game doesn't even have secret techniques like its predecessor! Much less an achievement that encourages you to sequence break everything as much as possible. Small sequence breaks do exist but they only let you access an extra sigil or potion. By the way, having 5 kinds of potions (6 if you include the rainbow potion) feels like a cheap way to increase the item count.Art:The art is really cute! The pixel art is really well done and I never had to hide my screen from people walking in my room. The non-pixel portraits do seem more mature and less cute than its predecessor though, not that I mind! Only minor issue is sometimes its hard to tell the foreground from background when platforming.Music:The music ranges from "it adds to the environment" to "This music SLAPS". It pretty much always does what it needs to do but some songs are forgettable. Not much else to say about this topic.Story:Possibly the weakest part of the game. Its definitely a lot more engaging than rabi-ribi, but i'd prefer that if it meant having a far more open world to explore. The characters are pretty good and I found myself caring about them, especially the main crew. However I feel as if its too story heavy if its holding back the exploration factor of a metroidvania. Lastly, some parts of the story felt weak. Many characters were introduced and used sparingly, yet were treated like very important characters, like Tevi's orphan friend. Other characters are killed off quickly for seemingly a reaction from the player to no avail, such as the waffle robot or Sable's brother. Ultimately though, you're here for the gameplay, not the story, so it doesn't hurt the game much other than the linearity the game forces. Not that linearity is necessarily a wrong thing, games such as Metroid Fusion prove so, its merely that this game doesn't really encourage you to go out and explore early on, even on higher difficulties.Ultimately I found it to be a fun game and worth the price, but its definitely lacking in some aspects that could have made it even more fun

_childDocuments_.review: Tevi feels great to control, move and fight with, and the upgrades you get come at a very satisfying pace. Despite a very simple base, your combat toolkit quickly unfolds into a pretty deep toolkit which is really satisfying to get better at (although the complexity can be slightly overwhelmingly at times).Exploration is... fine. It's a decent tile-based metroidvania map with some interesting setpieces, encounters and secrets thrown in, but combat against normal enemies isn't quite bland. However I'm glad these sections are here as a palette cleanser and a way to give the player and the world space to breath in between the real draw of the game, the boss fights.The boss fights in this game are some of the amazing. The many and varied bosses have huge varieties of attack patterns which manage to be thematically appropriate, visually interesting and fun to dodge. If you have a low tolerance for frustration in games, I'm sure these would still be fun spectacle fights on easier difficulties, but I recommend setting the difficulty level to something that challenges you. Because the attacks properly telegraphed and very rarely have "cheap" moments, the feeling of losing and retrying on a boss, learning the attack patterns, getting better, and finally overcoming one is as satisfying as in the best soulslikes. You can also change the difficulty level in-game at your player character's house so you can always tone it down if you feel you've really hit a brick wall.The story is mediocre, but not anything worse than the average game. The world is interesting if trope-y and the character writing has been surprisingly decent. I think the characters talk a bit too much though, especially early on, and pre-boss dialogue isn't auto-skipped for some reason so you need to do that manually every time. Perhaps with English VA this would be less of a problem? The music is fantastic and many tracks from the OST are going in my personal playlist.The art is great too, both the in-game pixel sprites and the larger character images used for menus and conversations.I'm honestly very surprised that this game's Steam rating is so low. The previous game by this developer, Rabi-Ribi, had a dedicated audience, and I'd guess that this one has proved divisive amongst its fanbase? It does seem to have aimed for wider appeal than the original, ditching the extremely cute aesthetic for one that's more broadly appealing, and while I consider this a massive upgrade, I'd understand if others disagree.(Edited after having now finished the game)

_childDocuments_.review: There's a trans girl in this game and she's loved by her village, and arguably one of the hottest characters. Also, hey, ladies; take your hormones! Your boobs won't grow overnight, especially if you keep forgetting to take them!But no, fr fr, Tevi is cute, Celia is hot, but also annoying at times, Sable is just adorable, literally every single character in this game is likeable. I don't have a single character I hate for the wrong reasons, and not a single character who is badly written, or unlikeable. Story? Fantastic. Characters? Fantastic. Exploration? Eh... Okay, this is where ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan for me. Is it overall, GOOD? Yes... HOWEVER... You can't descend from thinner platforms like in other Metroidvania games. THIS is the fatal flaw in exploration. The game is TRYING to encourage exploration and getting upgrades, but at the cost of the map being artificially stilted at points. It feels like the game time could have been reduced in half with the amount of times I have encountered a platform I COULD have slipped through had I been given the opportunity. Also, combat can get VERY repetitive at times. You'll find yourself mashing buttons in an attempt to deal as much damage as possible within the shortest amount of time. The abilities and combo learning does little at first to mitigate how much of a CHORE combat can feel at times. The combat is good, don't get me wrong, but GOOD GRIEF does it have its moments where you're just MASHING to get it over with. Enemies have WAY too much health, being the fatal flaw here. If enemies died quicker, combat wouldn't feel like a chore. Also, boss fights take WAY too long.It can get exhausting trying to navigate the environment and just trying to get from point A to point B. Maybe it's a problem with ME, and I am absolutely willing to accept that it could just be me being bad at the game and complaining about it. I COULD be just bad, but man... Bloodstained is a much better Metroidvania in every single way possible, and it feels like a massive disservice to the genre to have such flawed elements so front and center. Overall, it's a great game with a LOT of potential, but man... The map design and combat need some serious fleshing out in a possible sequel. Overall, the game is an 8/10 with the bulk of the weight being carried by the cool abilities, story, characters and immersive soundtrack. The map design makes the game take artificially long and pads out game time unnecessarily, and combat can feel like a chore. Other than that, I can safely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many things to complain about.Where are your Moe features and lovely scenarios, GemaYue? The hidden movement skills are also canceled, which is a great design for this kind of game. What's more, the movement items are harder or impossible to get in the early stages of the story, making the game more linear.There are still some bugs to be fixed even though TEVI was released over half a year ago. (Some redundancies of badges are displayed on the map; the map will remain with lots of holes which you can never collect.)The bosses’ skills are designed conservatively, requiring less tech to avoid the bullets. Also, because of the missing items such as the Super Carrot and Bunny Strike, the boss fights are now simple but boring.I would say I am really disappointed; it’s not the game I expected. _childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game.It's a very good Metroidvania with plenty to do. There're many varied maps with plenty of secrets to uncover, combat is fun, soundtrack is great, graphics are pleasant for eye. It's quite long yet I had fun till the end - and I could squish a lot more of playtime, if I decided to 100% the game (I missed a lot of items and omitted some additional challenges like Arena or alternate game modes).+ Big map with many different zones, each having it's own theme.+ Lots of exploration, many secrets to uncovers, various traversal abilities.+ Fun combat system. It's very simple at start, but it builds on with more and more moves.+ Many varied bosses.+ Absolute metric ton of Sigils (talismans/charms/passives) + Good visuals.+ Really great soundtrack.+ It's quite long with plenty to do+ Many additional challenges + Alternative game modes+ Varied difficulties which affect both pure stats and enemy attack patterns+ You actually can adjust difficulty in-game (in main character house), which isn't that common for Metroidvanias+ Likeable set of characters = Story is a bit of mixed bag. I'd say it's interesting and worth following, but it's rushed. Despite game being quite long there are a bit too many various plots and things happening, which doesn't give individual parts enough time. In the end I liked the story, but it's riddled with holes and unresolved plot points. There's a lot of unrealised potential.= It's bullet hell type game, so just be aware of it.- ... I don't have any issues big enough to be worth giving a "-". There're things that could be improved, yes, but nothing is really worth pointing out as "bad".Bunny / 10

I'll probably unequip that Sigil later when I want to get really good at combat.As a side note, I'm learning game development right now, and I'm using Tevi as an example of what makes a good 2D combat platformer. But, damn... 33 hours in when I was done, I was really done.
