_childDocuments_.review: Shout out to that one person that gift me this one, love you friend, I couldn’t be more grateful. I played the demo last year, really liked the fast paced combat and the system just grew way more from what I've been seen in-game.I played a bit of Rabi-Ribi, the devs’s preceding game. Both games are very fun metroidvanias, but the big main difference is that with TEVI, they went all in making a very sound and customizable combo system for the main character; new moves unlock as you level up and progress, with even more moves added thank to the sigil system in game that you can edit as you like. Seriously, check the trailer and GemaYue’s twitter (Developer), they have an amazing display of the things you can do, its nuts.Ten hours in, with a lot of them focused on exploration more than progressing the story, I finally covered all the material that was condensed in the demo, plus a sizeable chunk that is not in it. As for the actual plot, while in the demo all the characters act like the player already knows what’s going on, the actual game takes it’s time to build its characters and the world. I liked the story for what it told, wouldn’t call it groundbreaking either but it’s not a bad story by all means unlike a lot of negative reviews seem to latch on. If anything, props to the director and writers for the good execution of tropes.If I had to say something bad about the game, it would be that its kindaish short, but so it was Rabi-Ribi until it was filled to the brim with content, which I expect the same happening to TEVI in the future. And that maybe as a metroidvania, there is little backtracking since most of the game feels very linear, and unless you want/need collectibles, you rarely will be returning to already explored areas with new tools. Since said areas are also kind of tiny, doing so also takes very little time anyway.Overall, very recommended to enjoyers of fast paced action games and metroidvania beginners, the game also has an amazing amount of customization for the difficulty so even if you feel it’s too easy, you can still change things to make it way more hard on top of the actual difficulty, like scaling the bosses’ stats as you get more power ups.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Very very very very very fun - a rare example of a game I'm sad to put down after 80 hours. Basically just Rabi-Ribi more: more shot types, fleshed out melee combat, more build customization and more areas to explore; it retains its predecessor's best aspect: the fluid combat and insanely hype boss roster that pushes you to use your entire toolkit to string combos and eke out a win amidst technicolor explosion bullet hells. It doesn't deviate in any major ways, but it doesn't need to - it's a more polished version of a great thing. CreSpirit's games just have the special sauce and I really wouldn't mind if they made two or three more of these.While I have grown to appreciate a lot of Rabi-Ribi's silliness, I maintain that its overworld graphics are butt-ugly. Tevi’s are MUCH better: it’s a really pretty game, and its environments are way more memorable (even if they still don’t try at all to make areas look like they would connect in a physical space). The UI and localization are much less headache inducing and obviously reflect a higher budget.The story here is pretty schlocky - it’s a trope-y, amateurish JRPG plot that often feels like your friend loredumping their OCs to you for twenty minutes, and there are a lot of valid criticisms to make about its structure and dialogue and certain plot choices. Still….eh, I dunno, I thought most of the characters were cute and likable. Their interactions are fun, only occasionally going TOO far into anime cringe, and the shockingly high profile voice acting certainly helps. It all feels incredibly earnest, and I couldn’t help but be endeared to it. “It’s made with passion” feels like such a cop out, but it's honest to my connection with the experience. Besides, it's hard not to get invested in what's happening when you’re sweating your ass off for 8 minutes in these amazingly presented boss-fights.Tevi and Rabi-Ribi have some of the best gameplay out of all of the 2d side scrollers I’ve ever played, and it kills me that they’re so infrequently talked about. Seriously, when I searched “Tevi” on Twitter I found three (3) english posts about the game that were 1: not from a news/review site and 2: not porn. And I scrolled for like 10 minutes. More people owe it to themselves to play these games because they are, to quote your coworker who’s trying to justify why they like a phase 4 MCU movie, “a blast.”Definitely play this game on Hard+ or Expert though. Normal is way too easy - even for your first playthrough as a mediocre bullet hell player.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This is my first metroidvania.Here is what I like about the game:-Combat is nice. Coupled with the excellent basic and fundamental movesets, the sigil system allows insane customization as to how I fight. It allowed me to adapt to the enemies I face, and makes the combat fun.-Art is cute. I like cute things.-The music complements the areas it is in. It properly sets the mood of the fights.-The exploration can be satisfying as it is often times filled with puzzles and whatnot. Furthermore, the arrow markers were good for remembering one way paths.-The bosses are what I looked forward to the most. Knowing this is a bullet-hell, I knew I'm in for some nasty, flashy boss fights. And my god, they do not disappoint. It feels good learning their patterns and attacks, then thrashing them.Now, what I not like:-The provided markers feel inadequate. It sometimes mix up with the already placed ones, and there are no other unique markers I could use to distinguish areas that need different abilities, making me backtrack to places I thought I could pass after getting a new ability but not. But at least this the the only gripe I have.Overall, I think Tevi is a great game. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I like how different it is from Rabi Ribi, I went in expecting it to essentially be the same but no. Completely different, and I really appreciate the changes in quality of life and how its structured. BUT I do have one issue with the game. I feel like the boss fights could be restructured as the attack patterns are pretty easy to dodge but the boss fights themselves take a long time to complete (Basically Normal difficulty feels a bit too easy).
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: This game...is very good.  It's a side-scroller action-rpg , with an emphasis on the action.  I started the game at hard+ (in between hard and extreme) bc I saw "bullet-hell" in the description and have a bit of experience playing danmaku shooters, including Crimzon Clover, Mushihimesama, etc.  Haven't finished Tevi yet.The game starts a little slow, feeling like a Zelda game, but as you progress there are so many upgrades and mechanics introduced that it evolves into something much more enjoyable for an action game fan.  The combat feels like there is depth to it, with the "sigil" system giving you different abilities and buffs depending on which you choose to equip.  I don't have nearly all of them yet and it already feels like there is a lot of customization you can do, depending on how you want to play the game, if you like doing melee combos, air combos, ranged attacks, or a mixture of them.  As far as the "bullet hell" aspect of the game goes, the bosses have attack patterns and phases that are reminiscent of danmaku shooters.  Since this game is a side scrolling platformer,  you have to jump and dodge around projectiles and attacks instead of maneuvering a ship thru them.  The common enemies are less intense in that regard but can still provide a challenge if you're not careful.  Looking forward to New Game+ and Boss Rush mode, and the higher difficulty settings, to see how deep the action of this game gets.My Rating - 8.5/10, subject to change since I haven't finished the game.  Already feel like I've gotten my money's worth out of it and will keep an eye on the developer.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Like 99.9% of other reviewers, apparently, I, too, came to TEVI after Rabi-Ribi; and because of that, watching the trailers, I was super hyped for a new CreSpirit game. This isn't LoveBunny (once spiritual successor of Rabi-Ribi now turned bona fide coming sequel as Rabi-Ribi2), but I was still excited to play some more of this genre (even when I'm not exactly the greatest).Was I as satisfied by the end, or was it a let down?... Drum roll...... Satisfied. Not 100%, I feel Rabi-Ribi excels more than TEVI, but it's still a solid game. VERY good. For what it's worth, I struggle to do some boss fights legit in Rabi-Ribi on first playthroughs (meaning, without extra laps where you retain skills and power ups), and especially stuggle with some DLC fights, while I managed to finish all of TEVI legit, with just the tools from the game (unlike R-R, where I had to retort to third-party tools *cough*CheatEnging*cough* on some fights in my first playthrough to get unstuck on some bosses). This is a testament to how there have been improvements in some areas.All in all, I think I find Rabi-Ribi even more fun and exciting to play, the gameplay feels just lovely once you have everything unlocked... but TEVI is also so damn good in that aspect! I find it that it's not to the level of its predecessor, but it's a valid new entry to the CreSpirit Metroidvania bullet hells!I've played 50 hours of this and while I can still unlock plenty more (so I can dump another 100 hours at least, especially with the free Coloseum update), I've seen a good chunk of what's offered by TEVI, so I can say I recommend this! Play Rabi-Ribi first, or after, but don't skip out on TEVI either!Oh, the music and art is so very good; and damn, the voice acting adds so much to the experience. They also got some BIG names in the industry, some very big VAs, which left me speechless at times.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit in a love-hate-relationship with this game. There are certain aspects that make me really love it, but in the other hand there some points that prevent me from playing longer than one to two hours at once.==== First of all the positives: ==== - Great Music in any given scenario: It always fits the surrounding area, biome or boss encounter. The main menu theme makes me melancholic and emotional for unknown reasons (but in a positive way)!- Character Design: Every single story character stays in my mind because everyone has an individual design, outfit and personality that makes them stand out from every other person. The main character Tevi for example feels very sympathetic, likeable and smart and I can understand her thinking process and behavior in most conversations.- A good mix of seriousness and humor during story telling.- Difficulty: Similar to certain other games, you can also design your difficulty according to your own requirements, beyond a simple difficulty slider (which does exist too though). This increases replayability for those who want it- UI and Game Menus are really well designed and are not overwhelming, unlike some other games I've played previously. They also perfectly scale with my tested resolutions of 1920x1080 and Ultrawide 3440x1440. No bugs or issues noticed for this point.==== The negatives: ==== - Too much backtracking: During exploration you find tons (and I really mean TONS!) of ways that you'll only be able to explore when unlocking certain items later in the game (such as the increased jump height). But I don't really want to keep walking back through the same areas to explore and reach certain locations, so I usually just skip that content, which doesn't feel very satisfying though.- SUBJECTIVE POINT: In my opinion the game contains a bit too many dialogues, which are also a bit too long. This regularly brings me out of pace when jumping from exploration to one or multiple dialogues to a boss fight, then back to one or multiple dialogues and then to exploration, only to be then distracted by a dialogue a couple of minutes later again. YOU DON'T NEED TO HOLD MY HAND, I'M NOT A CHILD!- In addition to the above point, it also bothers me that the game has no english vocalization. I have set the language to english, but the game only has vocalization in japanese. It's rather difficult to read english text with the eyes, but then hear japanese dialogues in the ears - especially if you're not a native speaker of either language and you need to invest more focus because you also translate internally. I would like to have text AND voice acting in the same language that I can understand visually and aurally/audioally (?) simultaneously.Just like every medal has two sides, next to the positives there are some aspects that range from a minor inconvenience to actually terrible annoying. But so far the positives outweigh the negatives by far in my opinion, so I can recommend this game to you IF you love the mix of 2D Metroidvania, Danmaku (Bullet Hell) and Anime-Artstyle.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: A very good game overall, despite some weaknesses on the dialogues !: you do NOT need to be a rabbit lover to enjoy this game ^^ But I suppose that furry "enthusiasts" may fall in love quickly !If you like dynamic combats, "not too hard" bullet hell mechacnics, metroidvania-ish games, you may have a very good time playing at Tevi !As a player of Rabbi Ribbi, I found the difficulty to be more accessible (I played Tevi in "Expert" mode" to feel the same difficulty as the "Hard" mode of Rabbi Ribbi).The bullet hell part is still present, but the screen is a bit more readable (less "bullets" at a time) in Tevi, which feels more immersive than Rabbi Ribbi, without being really easier, so that's nice !Combos and the level of combat customization are quite satisfying (and more complex/varied than in Rabbi Ribbi).But don't expect much from the dialogues, they are excessively long and "flat", just like a boring VN would take ages to say something obvious. Hopefully, the very good Voice Acting help to remain a bit focused on the story.The story is OK-tier, besides the dialogues, with some intersting twists, but nothing ground-breaking though.Characters illustrations are quite polished, a bit "fan service" too but enjoyable enough (at least they provide a welcoming distraction from the dialogues ^^). The characters' sprites are finely sculpted pixel-arts textures.In conclusion, I highly recommend this game ! Even at its full price (30€ ATM), just be sure to try out the demo first (Given how many Early Accesses we have to endure nowadays,  we should enjoy and encourage developers when they propose a proper, free and honest Demo !).
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: From the get-go TEVI is something that quickly piqued my interest. From the art style to the combat system and the pedigree of the developer of Rabi-Rabi which I enjoyed but never got around to finishing it (plan to eventually). Fast-forward to it's release and like with many metroidvania style games it's the kind of game that starts good and just gets better as you progress and get more abilities.I think what sets TEVI apart is the combat system and the vast amount you can customize your perks and fighting style with the Sigil system. It is similar to badges in other games but can be changed on the fly in the menu and you equip dozens at a time as you level up. Some are very simple perks or status boosts while others change focus in what kinds of attacks you use as they have both positive and negative effects.I think the thing that could be a turn off for some people who are fan of this genre is the focus on story and the mostly linear progression. Personally I loved TEVI herself as a character from the get-go and the other supporting characters I grew to enjoy. As for exploration I think this game does mostly linear exploration right unlike something like Metroid Fusion. There was always a good handful of secrets you can go out of your way to find in every zone as you slowly follow along the marked waypoints.I started the game on Normal but quickly switched to Hard as I found exploration and boss fights didn't really have much agency to them after the first couple of bosses. I highly recommend if you have any experience with these kinds of games to start on Hard as I found I enjoyed the game as a whole much more.I did notice that for the most part the boss music didn't stick out too much. They fit great in context but thinking back I couldn't recall almost any of them. The overworld themes on the other hand were fantastic. Many of them are bangers or atmospheric when they needed to be. I am definitely going to add some to my playlists.Overall I really loved TEVI there are many moments when the game felt great to control narrowly dodging crazy attacks with great precision or getting through platforming sections. And really captures the fun in discovering some of its' secrets. I'm looking forward to going back and doing some of the already added free content like the platforming and boss challenges as well as collecting the remaining items. And excited for the already announced DLC to come later.Once again if you are fan of the genre I think this is worth trying. I think the Demo gives you a nice preview of how the game feels early game and the trailers show you how crazy it can get once you get more mobility abilities.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Great GameplayVery good level and hidden goddy designCombat is fun, even if a little easy for bullet hell fans (or rabi ribi fans)The world is huge, you get a ton of upgrades and can even get some goddies too early with enough skill.The Art and music is great and gives off fun, fast gameplay vibes while still keeping some sense of mystery.Sadly, the story sucks. I tried to find a way to sugarcoat it, but i can'tIt's a "Win the fight (often by a landslide), but then lose in a cutscene" simulator.Every bossfight from a certain point is that way. You fight, you win, you lose in the cutscene.I HIGHLY advise skipping every post bossfight dialogue. Makes the game better.If you like metroidvanias but don't care to much about story, this will be one of your favorites for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: A game that suffers from the comparison with its predecessor, Rabi-Ribi, imho.Which is kind of weird, because there is no doubt that technically, Tevi is a better game. The graphics are better. The OST is imho better. The gameplay might be better as well.But, and I'll sound like a romantic here but whatever, the connexion with the game is not there. It doesn't pull you in its world like Rabi-Ribi does. It has less charm, I think because it is more standard. It's an adventure game where you kick the baddies' behind and save the world. That's itI mean, it does that well, it's a good 2D metroidvania - the platforming is good, the combat is good, there's no doubt about that. If you like 2D metroidvanias, you'll have a good time with this, that's for sure.Just, eh. It feels a bit whatever. I'd say it's a 7/10, solid but without any element to ever make you say "hey, that's amazing !"
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Storywise, the game kinda feels like a Xenoblade title where the characters start off feeling pretty meh, but most of them become very enjoyable as the plot progresses. Gameplay wise, it's an interesting combination of Bullet Hell and Metroidvania. The exploration itself can be kinda limiting at first, but it's still decent fun when it starts to go full swing, and the environments themselves are quite aesthetically pleasing. The real fun of this game, though, are the bosses. Bullet Hell elements combined with a surprisingly in-depth combat system leaves most of the bosses feeling like fun, hectic romps, Malphage being a personal favorite of mine. Finally, I absolutely adore the music. Most of the tracks are enjoyably atmospheric, and the boss themes are all bangers. Special mention has to go to, again, Malphage's boss theme, Abolumania.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished it- The story has potential to be good, but too many character arcs left unfinished- Possibly the worst game design decision i've seen in all metroidvania i played recently, such as can't drop down platform resulting to unnecessary backtracks, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ convoluted puzzles (heck i love iconoclast's puzzles, but not with this one, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible)- Also probably the worst traversal tools ever in all metroidvania games that i've played, jetpack is HORRENDOUS as ♥♥♥♥!! full upgrade jetpack should be allowed for more lighter lift off, but no its the same horrendous ♥♥♥♥- Boss fights depend on luck? too much luck factor in the game, since you can't possibly dodge all those bullet hell ♥♥♥♥The pros are amazing cute arts and top notch seiyuu, but i really hate solving the stupid puzzles using horrible traversal kit (bombs, jetpack, wall kick)Overall just okayish

_childDocuments_.review: Cant go wrong with this one if you like metroidvanias.In story mode youll encounter some invisible walls early on where Tevi goes "this is the wrong way" or something to funnel you towards some story bits. _childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: TEVI caught me by surprise. I thought initially that it might have been fluffy or intended for a younger audience, but I was highly incorrect. It has a cute, lighthearted aesthetic early on in the game, which gives way to serious, hard-hitting cutscenes and crazy boss battles against  Overall, TEVI is one of the top Metroidvania games on PC, it's up there with Axiom Verge, Timespinners and Yohane the Parhelion. It combines solid writing, very good quality Japanese voiceovers, cute but believable characters, with best-in-class gameplay for one of these. The controls are very tight and responsive, you will see zero Souls-like combat lag in this. Tevi herself is a high-energy, magic-fueled bunny with power beyond her stature. She realizes this power with Sigils, hundreds of active and passive abilities that seamlessly layer themselves into her melee, ranged, combo, and other abilities as you choose.  There are some Sigils that cause massive, noticeable power spikes, if you can find them in the world.Its difficulty on Normal felt right for for someone who has played similar games before, but if you are an avid Metroid player, I might recommend turning it up one difficulty. It tracked just like a Metroid game as far as difficulty - it's harder in the beginning until you start to get mobility and more HP.Overall, if you are a fan of Metroidvanias on the PC platform, you should absolutely pick this one up. Even more so if you like waffles. (play the game to see what I mean!)
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of good things in this game. In fact, there are so many good things, I'm too lazy to even list all of them (go find other reviews, there's enough praise of this game).However, there is one thing that really bothered me.For those who played the previous game of the devs, Rabi Ribi, some people might remember the enormous health bars late / post game bosses have. Sadly that's still the case here. If your planning to play on expert, it's not unusual for bosses after chapter 6 to take more than 15min, which for a metroidvania is incredible long. I didn't have a problem with the damage I was taking nor with the harder patterns of those bosses, but due to the amount of their health, I dropped the difficulty after chapter 7 to hard+. And here comes the next problem. The difference between hard+ and expert is so unbelievably big that it feels more like the difference that should be between normal and expert. While on expert most bosses took me ~10 min to beat, I breezed through them on hard+ in ~2 min. I kind of wished I had the option for expert damage and patterns but hard+ health.Oh also, game is pretty dialogue heavy for a metroidvania. Sometimes I had like 30min of dialogue in a 1h gaming session. So that might not be for everyone. Don't let my rant discourage you from playing tho, the game itself looks and plays great and for those with little to no experience in bullet hell games, hard difficulty is plenty hard already.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Rabi Ribi and I loved playing this. Combat felt very fluid and customizable, was fun to fight things just because I wanted to. I enjoyed the Story a lot even if I had some issues with it at points, Voice Cast did great, and all the art is amazing.Can't wait for the DLC, and working more towards 100%

_childDocuments_.review: The game is absolutely great. The gameplay, story, VAs, artstyles, everything is well made, but the English translation kind of felt like it's too short or too straightforward for me like it's translated online. It's not like it's a bad translation, the translation is great, but I kind of wish it was a little bit longer than that.As for the difficulty, to be honest, I never tried testing out the difficulties, but I do know that bullet counts increases per difficulty (makes it harder to dodge easier/find safe spots), the same as their last game, so I started with Expert, and felt like this is my kind of difficulty so I am happy with this difficulty for now  As a player of Rabi-ribi many years ago, some of the references in this game made me heartwarming, and one of the reference got me crying (very nostalgic moment), and is probably my first time I ever cried to a reference from a game.You can still play this game even without playing Rabi-ribi. It's not like it's a sequel to this game, but it has the references of them.This game is totally one of the best game that I ever bought and played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a genuinely great game with a lot of character in its story. I hope to see more from this world in particular.Difficulty wise, this game is much better balanced than Rabi Ribi was, but leans slightly on the side of being too easy (which is just fine since there are two harder modes to choose from). Favorites of mine are Ulvosa, Plagued Forest, Verdawn Forest, Morose, Shopping Time, Valhalla, and Cloister of Redemption.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is kind of a mixed bag for me. I think if you enjoyed Rabi-Ribi you're probably going to enjoy this game. Although that being said, I'd like to list my personal pros and cons for the game.Cons:The Story: I'm sure the story might be interesting, however the length of the dialogue and my ADHD made the skip button all too tempting to skip over everything around four hours in.Perverted characters: If it isn't obvious from the game's promotional art, this game is full of what you might call "attractive" animated characters. However, there are several moments where the father of the main character makes really weird/creepy comments toward the main character, who as far as I'm aware is likely underage. Plus, it's her dad. I suppose it might be in a difference in culture but it just made the character unbearable to listen to, and gave me all the more reason to skip everything. The world and exploration: While this game is a Metroidvania, it is extremely linear on a first playthrough. You are given quest markers that tell you exactly where to go. There is some incentive to explore with upgrade potions and sigils lying around, but often times going off the main path only leads to the character stopping to play a cutscene of her saying: "Let's go back to (LOCATION)" before backing away. If you play the game, I'd recommend going with the easiest difficulty on the first run, because there are essentially some new-game plus options that negate this problem.Pros:Combat: The fighting in this game is so incredibly fluid and fun. It's one of the reasons I loved Rabi, and it feels even better in this game. With how easy it is to get EP, or points to equip sigils, you can get some insanely powerful builds.Boss Fights: I really love all of the boss designs in this game, and the bullet-hellish parts of them don't feel nearly as impossible as some of the fights I remember in Rabi. Granted there are some difficult moments, but it still feels like a hitless run could be possible with some skill and luck involved.Art: Of course the art is dang good. The backgrounds, sprites, character art and all that looks great. Like mentioned before, I'm not so fond of the perverse/objectifying style of some character, but it's good art.While I did bring up more cons than pros, I would say this game is worth at least one playthrough. I enjoyed the experience overall, however this is coming from someone who skipped most of the story, so, do with that what you will.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Im not a fan of the "backtracking" in metroidvania games though its really really hard to make those good and fun to to go to the same places again just to collect 1 item. This game has crazy insane backtracking tho depending on how you play it. I suggest just following the story and getting all the unlocks for the collectibles and only backtrack if you cant beat a boss. This game shines in the sigil system tho, so many tweaks to power up your character and finding new sigils and powering up your character, as someone who hates backtracking the sigil system kept me intresested to backtrack just to know how much more I can power up my character. They are deep enough to make u think which one to choose but you can easily overpower your character so I suggest playing this on hard at first and even increasing the difficulty as you get more stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: A very worthy successor to Rabi-Ribi. Almost everything that Rabi-Ribi did well, TEVI has done better - and Rabi-Ribi is already a fantastic game.The gameplay feels great. The world is huge, there's tons to explore, and Tevi controls crisply and smoothly. The boss fights are some of the most fun I've had with a game in a while. The overall art style is gorgeous - beautiful splashes, cute characters, and the pixel work is wonderfully well done. The artstyle of this game is one that will age beautifully. I found the sidekick characters a little annoying initially, but they really grew on me over time. Excellent OST that I bought and paid for without a second thought (and full disclosure - I usually pirate almost all my music). I don't think a single song annoyed me. A very nice touch by the developer was "Streamer Mode" - if you turn it on, tracks that may get sniped by Content ID are swapped for safe ones. On the negative side, the story was too weak for the amount of dialogue there is. While the overall narrative is solid and interesting, plot threads are rapidly dropped and left unresolved and the pacing is poor - most of the major story developments take place in the last 15% of the game. There was also a lot of railroading that limits your exploration. You can't freely roam as much as you think you can and exploration is locked behind movement upgrades that are locked behind preset story triggers. Compared to Rabi-Ribi, freedom was sacrificed for a more serious plot.Despite that I had an enormous amount of fun and was glued to the game for weeks; I would play for 8 hours, put it down for dreaded responsibilities and find myself itching to play again not even an hour later. Highly recommend if you enjoy Metroidvania style games!DISCLAIMER: This review is based solely on my initial single playthrough of the game. It may change based on potential future DLC or replays using the custom game features.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I am near the end of the game and so far I have enjoyed the game. Is it like Rabi-Ribi? Kinda. The combat is like Rabi-Ribi and is quite nice. There are a ton of sigils to configure to help match your combat style. As for the negatives that people have posted I find it kind of pointless. This game is not Rabi-Ribi. _childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I understand perfectly well that everyone will be comparing this game to Rabi-Ribi. Rabi-Ribi stands as the crown jewel of CreSpirit's games, and was a resounding success in almost everything it tried to do. Thus, I've decided to fully play into this, so people looking into this game comparing it to such can be as informed as possible.A good portion of people will likely be coming to this game because it's portrayed as Rabi-Ribi's "spiritual successor", meaning it's meant to embody the things Rabi-Ribi did, but on a higher level. In my opinion, it does some things better, and some worse. Here are some of the main differences I observed:- Much more focused on story.- Combat is more melee-oriented.- Game is a touch more linear.- Significantly more content.- Higher-quality visuals.- Several QOL improvements.- Enemies don't drop currency. Crafting mechanics make it so you don't waste limited money on consumables.Of course, none of these are necessarily bad, just different.There were many things in this game that I thought were done well, especially compared to Rabi-Ribi:- The atmospheres and aesthetics of most of the game's areas were exceptional. One in particular nearing the end of the game I  liked. Generally, the foreground and background were a lot more detailed, even with the occasional parallax effect in areas with more depth.- The combat was very fun and fleshed out. While it was a lot more melee focused, which I personally didn't prefer, it was still incredibly enjoyable even to a person (me) who's never cared much for the combat of games like DMC.- The map is huge. Like, genuinely. It took me probably as long to go through this game normally as it did for me to 100% Rabi-Ribi.- TEVI adds map markers. This is huge. You can pull up a menu to place little markers on the room you're in. You can also change what it looks like. For example, you might use the marker shaped like a potion since you know there's one there, or perhaps you might use an arrow because there's a path in that direction you can't access but want to come back to. I loved these things so much, and they make the process of going back and looking for secrets SO much easier.- Adds a crafting mechanic, which was very versatile and adaptable, making it so you don't have to trek back to the nearest store and buy what you need.- Soundtrack is great, on par with Rabi-Ribi's.- Has the same secret-finding process of Rabi-Ribi. I personally enjoy combing the corners of each room looking for extremely obscure stuff. It's meditative.- Bombs and enemies persist through room transitions. For example, you could throw one of your bombs through a room transition, immediately walk through, and then your bomb is right in front of you, ready to explode. It really makes everything seem a lot more "connected" rather than just being a bunch of rooms thrown together.- A very wide variety of different enemies. Rabi-Ribi tended to reuse a lot of enemies such as crystals or fairies, but almost every single area in this game has its own unique set of enemies....and probably a few more small things I didn't consider to write down while I was playing the game.Next, let's talk about negatives. When it comes to personal gripes with the game, most are minor. However, some are a good bit more significant, and sadly impacted my own personal experience with the game a lot more than I would've liked. I'll start with the minor things:- No game over screen. When you die you kind of just... respawn, and it doesn't make it feel as authentic.- Text font on title screen and in most menus is too generic.- Character portraits are too zoomed in in the menu, it looks kind of awkward.- Map cannot be opened shortly after going through a map transition. I encountered this a good few times, and it broke my immersion a little bit.- I wish the extreme points of the map (e.g. highest/lowest) were made more glamorous. It would fit well with the "natural beauty" theme of the game.- Combat, comparatively, is a lot more focused on hack-n'-slash vs. bullet hell. There's still bullet hell elements in there, but they're not quite as visually appealing as Rabi-Ribi's.That's about it for the minor stuff. As for the more significant things...- Too many sigils (TEVI's badge system). Rabi-Ribi's badge system worked so well because of how limited it was, forcing you to be a lot more creative. In Rabi-Ribi, I created a lot of different sets of badges for different gameplans and whether I was exploring or fighting a boss. With TEVI, I kind of just put on stuff I thought was decent, and called it a day. It typically felt like a chore sorting through the different sigils to see what worked with what, and wasn't very rewarding.- WAY too easy. I played the base game on Hard+, and the longest amount of time that I ever spent on a boss was about an hour. In Rabi-Ribi, where I also played on hard, several of the bosses took upwards of 3 hours. I missed that difficulty, and to me personally it made the game a lot less engaging.- Too linear. A good number of progression items are locked in areas you can only reach with story progression, so even though you can explore a good bit of the world and get a ton of items before going to the next story area, you'll eventually hit a wall. This is probably because TEVI has a longer story, so if the player were to explore everything and then suddenly have to do all the story stuff, they'd have a lot of walking and reading to do.- A couple times I was prevented from leaving the path the game wanted me to go on, with the whole "I shouldn't go this way yet" spiel. This would really only be when the game wants you to go somewhere for one reason or another, typically for something important.. It's not  intrusive, but it still irked me.- Finally (and this is the biggest issue), the story was all over the place. While it had a lot more depth and was generally not difficult to follow, it completely failed to stay on a consistent path. It starts with the game's primary focus, then completely forgets about that to take you on a  path, then does the same thing AGAIN, rinse and repeat. It couldn't decide which story it wanted to focus on, and kept going here and there and everywhere. It tied everything into each other at the end, but it was quite sudden, and didn't really feel like an "A-HA!" moment for me. This also had the unfortunate side effect of making essentially all scenes meant to be emotional completely lost on me, because it barely explored the depth of any characters' relationships, save for TEVI and her father.Ultimately, when comparing Rabi-Ribi and TEVI, they're not meant to do the same things. Rabi-Ribi was a lot more lighthearted, with a bubbly cutesy aesthetic with the underlying tone of "have fun and explore". It was a lot more focused on just making its gameplay fun, rather than trying to add depth to its almost nonexistent story. TEVI, on the other hand, was a lot more serious, and did a great job adding more content to the game,   giving it a lot more depth.Ultimately, Rabi-Ribi was the better experience for me. While TEVI was a lot more intellectually attractive and was very enjoyable to look at and experience, it fell short of that which was Rabi-Ribi's purely fun and simple gameplay loop. Rabi-Ribi made it a lot easier to experience it, which is what made it better, in my personal opinion.I would still absolutely recommend TEVI, it was a joy to play through. However, if you're hoping its going to be the BEST SPIRITUAL SUCCESSOR you could hope for for Rabi-Ribi, their different intentions prevent that from being a reality. Fundamentally, they're not the same game, and so hoping for more Rabi-Ribi is sadly a futile effort. However, in most of what it tries to do it exceeds expectations, making it an incredibly solid and highly enjoyable game in of itself.Final Rating: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent metroidvania when judged on its own merits, despite not giving me the exact same feelings as Rabi-Ribi.Level design is beautiful and brilliant, with many devilishly hidden upgrades and clever puzzles. Progress is story-gated most of the time, rather than ability-locked, which isn't ideal for a metroidvania IMO but not a dealbreaker either. Boss fights are a little weird, in that some seem to be a bit too scripted and others let you just go ham and delete HP bars like they're nothing. Combat in general has quite a few subtle differences with Rabi-Ribi that make it not click quite the same way, particularly in regards to combo rank... but that's alright.While there is perhaps a bit too much focus on story, it is a nice one, and I really enjoyed it. The voice cast really enhances its impact, too. Playing the standard story mode is recommended for a first playthrough, and I understand why, given the work and care they clearly put into it.Luckily, the game offers extra modes that make it a bit more like Rabi-Ribi in its approach to progression (if you know, you know) and with built-in randomizers and the like it's very fun to break and potentially very replayable. I've already done some goofy stuff and I'm eager to jump back in for a full replay to get all the achievements I'm missing.In conclusion, it's one of my favorite games in one of my favorite genres, and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my top metroidvania next to Hollow Knight. Well polished, mostly bug-free, and no crashes. 100% map completion (not achievements) on my first playthrough on the hardest starting difficulty took 60 hours.Play the demo. The full game has 10-20x more of that. Main highlights are the combat system which encourages combo varieties and boss fights. I played mostly with the highest default difficulty (expert) and it was fairly balanced (not as hard as souls-like difficulty). Most bosses only took the first attempt. It encourages interacting with all systems (mainly crafting healing items) and allows you to experience the a proper bullet hell.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania. Very much feels like Rabi Ribi but better in every way. The way the story ends I think it's very clear we'll be getting some post-game DLC like with Rabi-Ribi.I played the game on "Hard+" difficulty but it felt a little easy at times, especially towards the end as you get more powerful. I was hesitant to crank the difficulty up to the highest level because I was afraid to run into some fights like the crazy hard post-game boss fights in Rabi-Ribi -- but those fears were ultimately unfounded as the final bosses were easier than some previous bosses (possibly due to me 100%ing the game prior to that). So, if you've played Rabi-Ribi, I'd recommend cranking up the difficulty as high as you want and not worrying too much about 100%ing the game before the final boss fight, because there isn't anything as hard as the post-game fights in Rabi-Ribi in Tevi (though perhaps there will be when DLC comes out).Overall, I highly recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: Words can not describe how amazing this game is. if you have the time to play this game, I HIGHLY recommend it. The story is just so well put together that it involves every small character you meet along the path and the game gives you reasons to connect with these smaller characters that aren't really relevant to the story (Vena!!!) The gameplay in this is very polished and well-made. The fighting feels great even though you are just spamming buttons and hitting crazy combos and it can be quite addicting. Exploring the map was one hell of a ride because i only started skipping small enemies like half way through my play through lol.I ABSOLUTELY LOVED THE BOSS BATTLES. some of the bosses were so well made and the attacks were so fun and challenging to dodge (on normal diff). That's coming from me who came from a IWBTG Avoidance background who loved dodging bullets in that game. This game had similar vibes to those type of avoidances to me and it made it more engaging to play. The only problem I really have is with the objective pinning system. Sometimes objectives can be hard to locate on the map and some times you go the path that seems obvious because it leads closer to the objective but in reality you have to loop all the way around the rooms to get there. It really just made path finding hard but it can add to the experience of a metroidvania game. PLEASE PLAY THIS GAME. IT IS SO GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOD

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved the art, music, voiceacting and satisfying gameplay with a bunch of different awesome moves that can make fights feel like a beautiful dance.I enjoyed the story although it wasn't the main attraction for me. _childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania, I bought it with no high expectations and ended up finding a masterpiece, totally got into my top 3 to recommend to my friends alongside Souldiers and Hollow Knight. The gameplay is awesome, movements are fluid and exploration is rewarding, maps are enormous but are ok to traverse after you get the right movement upgrades (so many different upgrades). Never seem a metroidvania with so many combosWhen it comes to story, I liked it, it develops slowly and shows more depth as you go, each character is different and adds something to the story, the npcs are also ok, the city looks alive differently from other games that don't pay enough attention to these kind of things. The visuals are stunning, its the first anime-like game I played and at first I was a bit unsure if I'd like it, but after playing a bit I was pleasantly surprised. The only problems I can think of are: (and I think it may be a stretch) - monster can be a bit repetitive at times, but maybe because the maps are so big? There are a lot of different monster, but because the maps are so big you end up finding the same 3-5 types for some time, but its ok, they are well designed. - the compass (item to help you find secrets) is horrible to use, I found it more confusing than useful- there are so many sigils that it becomes tiring to decide what to use, at first you may think a lot of them don't make a difference, but sometimes they combo and make you op (some players may thing this feature appealing, so maybe you like this "making a build" for your playstyle?)So many more nice things to say about this game, like the many options for difficulty and ng+ game configs. _childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to Rabi-Ribi, this is a step up for most of the aspects. Mechanics-wise, artstyle, the boss fights, and the soundtrack are all delightful. They also packed in voice acting, making the game feel less dull than Rabi-Ribi. Not present in the previous game is the crafting system, while I don't quite like having to run around killing stuff after every boss fight because I need to craft healing items, turns out to be really nice as it saves you the trip to shops for buying them, though it requires you to have a lot of materials in your stock in the first place, which means going around killing everything you see... which isn't something most players would do after they've already deep into the game and decided to just skip every enemy they see to save time.As for the combat, the game takes Rabi-Ribi combat and improves upon it. It plays roughly the same as Rabi-Ribi, where you DPS for a short time and back off to dodge bullets. Triggering combo-rank-related sigils are also easier as doing multiple varied moves quickly climbs your rank to S and above, and goes away after not attacking for a while to balance things out, compared to Rabi-Ribi where the the combo rank only drops after taking damage and requires the player to perfectly dodge everything to maintain their damage bonuses. Magic attacks are also changed, in which charged shots are shot at every 100 MP instead of having to hold a button. This allows the player to stock up tons of MP and then fire them all away at a quick succession, and while the player back off to dodge bullets, MP is being recharged for you to do it again. There's also additional mechanics like getting knockbacked to a wall deals damage to the target.But where it falters is the story. This game is heavily story-focused and quite linear, different than the light story and non-linear approach of Rabi-Ribi. The game locks exploration upgrades behind story, which ruins the metroidvania aspect. You can backtrack and explore around to find potions, money and sigils, but that's about it. There's no feeling of going to places and find something absolutely useful for your exploration experience. And even if you do go back with all of your exploration upgrades from the story, you're very close to finishing the story already, so you might as well just finish the story with what you got, and only bother getting everything after you beat the game. There's a free roam gamemode that allows you to get to the exploration upgrades without having to go through the story, but it omits the story and removes story quest markers, which means it isn't for first-time playthroughs. I suppose the option for hardcore exploration metroidvania fans is there, but I'm disappointed it isn't the default.And the plot itself is very unsatisfying at the end. The game reveals the true villain without any build-up whatsoever, it took me by surprise that  It feels like the plot is running around in circles, hinting at the true villain only to repeat the cycle again. And there's so much loose ends too at the end. The story definitely requires rewriting with how it is.Despite how good the gameplay is, I'm quite disappointed by how the story pans out. Still a worthy recommendation for me, and the price is worth it if you're a fan of metroidvania. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this by saying that I'm not a big fan of side-scroller platformers in general, so I'm not good at them nor do I have the most credible voice out there. I also finished the game on Expert, and am preparing to do Infernal BBQ currently.That said, somehow I really enjoyed Rabi-Ribi and Tevi. Here I'll compare both since those are my only frame of reference here. The story is quite serious compared to Rabi-Ribi, with more characters that play a bigger role and a big overarching story. While I enjoyed it, I also found it to be restricting, as it made the world less free roam compared to Rabi-Ribi. After the game there's an option that unlocks free roam, but it would have been better to have it in the beginning too (although for story reasons I can see why it can't happen).As for music, I personally feel that I liked Rabi-Ribi more, but the music is still pretty good here. I particularly liked the Rabi-Ribi remixes and the final few bosses' themes. Related to music, but this time the game has some voice acting, and the voice actors that were chosen were top notch. This is a real step above, which really shows their budget for the game. I especially enjoyed the fact that scenes were voiced.Moving on to graphics. Before getting into that, when I heard of the game and saw a few screenshots, I thought the art was a bit "meh" at first. After playing it, it grew on me and I can wholeheartedly say I like it a lot. It's not above or below Rabi-Ribi, it's just different, but still good. The colors are much less vibrant compared to Rabi-Ribi, but given the story and the lore, it's understandable that the colors are like this.Lastly is the gameplay. As said before, I finished the game on Expert. Before this, I really only completed Rabi-Ribi on Normal so I thought I would be bashing my head with every boss in the game. Which to be fair, I did for a few bosses in the beginning, but later on it was much more enjoyable. With the new fighting mechanics and sigil system, it makes Tevi much more maneuverable and really spices combos up, giving a better combat system. At the same time, it made tackling higher difficulties easier. It's honestly enjoyable to the point where I want to do Infernal BBQ. While I praise Tevi a lot, it isn't without its faults. One of them is, as said, is the lack of free roam. This is partly because of the story, preventing me from going to certain spots just because I'm not supposed to go there yet, and partly because of movement tech. Movement tech is evenly distributed throughout the story, so a lot of the time, I go back to areas when I unlocked a new movement tech. At the same time, this restricts roaming around. Second, it's the story. I really enjoyed it, but I felt it was a bit lacking, especially in the epilogue end of things and the big reveals at the final chapters. This might be addressed in the DLCs so I'm hopeful on it. Overall, I really recommend this game as someone not into the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible metroidvania bullet hell game. The boss fights have extremely engaging and diverse attack patterns, and while the heights reached by Rabi Ribi's post-game fights are not present in Tevi, I hope that it's only a matter of time. Rabi shines especially in its DLC, so it is probable that Tevi just needs the same treatment. That is, apart from two major issues Tevi has in its implementation of combat which, while not fatal, are concerning, especially and specifically in comparison to Rabi Ribi.The first is in regards to difficulty. Rabi Ribi offers the player four consumable healing items, not including the golden carrot, and appropriately limits it to two for the game's highest difficulty, Bunny Extermination. Tevi, on the other hard, gives the player several more consumable items, and of greater effectiveness, practically turning the game into a joke if one utilizes them. This issue is exasperated by the overpowered badge system's survival tools. The game doesn't even attempt to offer a higher difficulty experience that removes these options for more serious players.Next is the more concerning issue, as while the first could easily be remedied (although I do not believe it will be), this next problem is tied into the core gameplay of Tevi. If I were to name the most meaningful difference between the two games' combat, it would be that Rabi relies on ranged combat, while Tevi relies on melee combat. This has the disastrous effect of essentially limiting the potential of Tevi's core systems. Rabi's ranged combat is incredible because, like most bullet hell games or shmups, aggression and survival are inextricably tied to each other. Most patterns involve not only defense but also offense, and often further create risk-reward situations whether you take the risk of being more aggressive for the reward of higher damage. It is this simultaneous nature that makes these types of games constantly engaging and rewarding, and that drives personal improvement and the mastery of a game's systems. But how does Tevi's variation of Rabi's template factor into this? The emphasis on melee combat restricts the player's ability to be aggressive when put in a situation of survival. Ranged attacks can be utilized from any location, but melee attacks can only be used from short range, a distance not practical in a game where bullets often spawn from inside a boss. This is further exacerbated because melee attacks require a degree of commitment and limit movement. Given the game's lack of a good vector for safe and mobile offensive maneuvers, much of the time you are forced to just avoid anything sent your way, without any room for offensive or improvement or risk. In turn, this means that all offensive actions must be taken during downtime where the enemy cannot harm you. Unsurprisingly, this leads to even greater downtime between patterns to actually allow for melee combos to be performed.  On the other hand, the player moveset feels much better than Rabi, offering a large variety of offensive and movement tools of which the game justifies usage of through its combo system with actual combat rewards, a shockingly lacking feature in games reliant on such systems. For all of the criticisms I have made of the game's combat, it is still extremely competent and even somewhat of a breath of fresh air. I would even say that the game's final two bosses are an improvement to Rabi Ribi's four final bosses, post-game notwithstanding.Some common points of criticism for the game are its comparative linearity to Rabi Ribi as well as its character art. I believe both criticism to be lacking. First of all, the linearity, while less preferable overall, is still just relative. Tevi is overall fairly open. It is also not as if Rabi used its openness for any meaningful level of exploration, like that which you might find in a game like La Mulana. The praise for Rabi's unique freedom is, in my opinion, heavily founded on the use of repeat playthroughs, and the game does not justify actually playing the game again just to experience this sense of freedom. There is still value lost through major abilities being unlocked through story progression rather than obscure nooks and crannies all around the game world, but Rabi Ribi's exploration is neither good enough nor is the game focused enough on it for this criticism to be particularly relevant.Second, the character art discourse is absurd. Rabi Ribi itself does not have good character art, but discussion often frames Tevi's art as a massive downgrade. This is simply not true, both games are lacking in this regard. The most ridiculous element of this discussion is that character art is not really important to either game in the first place. It is very uncommon to see in the game, especially in Speedrun mode, and the content that utilizes it is not worth it in the first place. The important element of the games' art directions are the pixel art that the player is constantly made to interact with through, get this: actual gameplay. In this regard, Tevi is a beautiful looking game, boasting quality, consistency in style, and readability, all things its predecessor notably lacks in this department.If you enjoy everything meaningful Rabi Ribi has to offer, you will inevitably find enjoyment from this game and its number of improvements on the core gameplay. However, do not come into the game expecting combat complexity or depth equaling that of Rabi's post game, at least not as of now. Nonetheless, Tevi is a extremely solid game that I would recommend to any fan of bullet hell or metroidvania games.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: bnuuy (cosplay)-The game is pretty fun. Roughly a 5-6 hour speedrun real time (Which can admittedly become kind of exhausting), first time playthrough can easily take four times that length. If you like Rabi-Ribi's gameplay, you'll find a lot of familiarity in the mechanics here, but with a lot more emphasis on using Sigils to customize the player's combat moveset.However, unlike Rabi-Ribi, this game foregoes much of the titillation of Rabi-Ribi and instead brings an ominous feeling of impending doom, and a fair bit of bloodshed. This tonal difference means this game will probably appeal most to a different audience than RR.In addition, this game has a fairly cohesive narrative about an interesting setting with a variety of different types of characters. The pacing can feel a bit slow early on, especially early in when one can just wander aimlessly into a long conversation, but the game picks up as the player learns more and more about just how precarious the state of the world is.The bosses are big and bullet-hell-y. If you like big bullet patterns, you may want to start on Normal+ or Hard difficulty. However, if you don't like exploring to try to find potion upgrades to have the stats to deal with some of the rougher bosses, you may want to start on a lower difficulty. Even if you choose a difficulty that you find you don't like, you can adjust the difficulty from the main character's bed with no penalty.The devs are still updating and tweaking the game, and it sounds like DLC will be coming in the future. So while the game is already solid, I expect it to continue to get better in time. Totally worth the price tag for me, but for those on the fence, I recommend trying out the demo first to get a feel for the setting and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Words cannot describe how much I adore this game. _childDocuments_.review: Another great metroidvania from the developers of Rabi-Ribi, which is one of the top-tier best-in-the-genre titles everyone even slightly interested in the genre should play. While Tevi doesn't quite meet the heights of Rabi-Ribi, it's still an incredible offering and among the genre's best. While the exploration and traversal is a bit of a step down from Rabi-Ribi, the bosses (which are the main attraction anyways) are top notch and the game with even half the bosses would still be worth the price of entry. It's a Touhou bullet-hell type game and bosses have multiple phases with interesting, intricate patterns, and even after a dozen+ bosses the game still manages to throw creative, unique mechanics at you. If anything, the bosses just keep getting more creative and interesting as the game goes on, meaning there's always something new to see and play for.The main difference from Rabi-Ribi is this game is more melee and combo focused as opposed to the shooter focus, and while sometimes that can get frustrating in the crazy bullet-hell patterns when you can't get close, you eventually get multiple dodge and invuln mechanics that let you stay in the bosses face, and once you master your hit box you'll be ducking and weaving through the most intricate even at close range.The difficulty is also a bit of a step down, and I had to turn the game up to the highest (Expert) to really feel like I was getting the "full" experience, and even then bosses were dying in 3 to 4 tries. Incredible game though. Worth it for everyone even slightly interested in metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. I played Rabi-Ribi way too much before this, but I think I enjoyed this more.Wonderful art and music, full voice acting which is insane. The story did eventually hook me in, and now I feel empty after finishing it...Exploration, while more limited, was still really satisfying. Getting more movement options and zipping around doesn't get old. Though if you want to explore and stumble across new bosses and items, you won't find much of that here. It's mostly a linear progression, with the most you'll find from exploration being stat upgrades and sigils.The combat is *chef's kiss*, especially with the equipable sigils. You can build around a playstyle, and feel like a god in the late game. Most sigils have pretty minor effects that add up, with some sigils having drastic effects that changes your playstyle, easily my favorite part. The later craftable consumables also have interesting effects and not just "heal HP"I played on the highest difficulty available at the start, and found it challenging but not unfair. It was a bit front-heavy difficulty-wise, with some later bosses that I could just face tank, but the end game was thankfully really challenging,I also loved most of the boss fights. I was wondering how they would keep things interesting after Rabi-Ribi, and was pleasantly surprised. There's still the bullet hell, which feels great to dodge with all the available movement tech, but many fights also have mechanics to manage (though there was a lot of pausing during fights to read what some buffs/debuffs do). The 'break' system, choosing when to go full dps and when to dodge/block, the consumable you saved for that really clutch moment, the thousand different combos you can send, the sigils adding even more types of attacks and combos, the movement options and juggling the boss around in midair forever. It all made the fights feel  satisfying. Anyways. Bunny haha.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this as of 100%ing on expert, getting some of the free roam achievements, and getting into the Infernal BBQ difficulty. Also, Spoilers ahead as well.As a very avid lover of CreSpirit games, this one is no exception. I enjoy it, but it has its high highs and its low lows in terms of what they decided to do with the game overall. It is not Rabi-Ribi 2, don't expect it to be, however, there are many gameplay systems, sounds, movement tech, and battle designs that are mimicked and replicated from it's predecessor, so it will be reviewed with that in mind a bit.PositivesCombat: the combat is actually fairly fluid with a lot of diversity in how you can play from the 300 something sigils you can collect in the game. The break system and multi-bar hp system for the bosses works really well and allow for very satisfying, stylish combos to be pulled off with ease. Honestly no complaints about the combat.Music: as expected the music is grand and beautiful and very reflective of the areas and bosses they were meant for. I never tired of hearing the themes while traversing the continent of Az. Huge respect and shout-out to the artists of the ost: 3R2, Oli Jan, Triodust, Brandon, Dance with the Dead, and Bo-Xun Lin.Art: The art is phenomenal and breathtaking. Firstly, even tho Rabi-Ribi art didn't bother me, the game is a lot more approachable to a wider audience due to how more mature and less 'anime-y' it feels, which is a plus due to the amount of people I knew or saw that were immediately turned off from playing Rabi-Ribi due to its art style alone. The backgrounds and pixel art of the game is unlike anything else and the character designs and art slides during the story were just as amazing. I was also pleased that there was a gallery that was unlockable after the story was beaten in order to view them.Voice-acting: I actually enjoy the voice acting a lot and I never skipped any cut-scenes due to this fact, it was basically the only thing keeping me going throughout the story (more on the story later). They ended up bringing in some high profile and recognizable Japanese voices and it brought a smile to my faceNeutralsBosses: Adding this as a section because the bosses in this game are an integral part of the experience, and they were very hit or miss (mostly the latter). A lot of the bosses had a lot of patterns that were either very easy to dodge, tankable, iframe-able, or simply ignore-able by standing behind the boss and whacking away at them, which really takes away from what the game was trying to do with their bosses. I overall thought most of them were very boring and could be drastically enhanced by having the boss off the screen or invulnerable so you could focus on the patterns (as well as making the patterns more fun and a tiny bit more difficult on the higher settings if this were the case). There were rare cases to this however where the bosses were genuinely great and a blast to do with their own mechanics and unique patterns (Looking mainly at you Memloch, Amaryllis, and Malphage).Difficulty: Just going to come out and say it, I think the game is WAY too easy even on the hardest difficulty (infernal BBQ) so far. This would be a negative if it wasn't for me believing that the easier difficulty makes it more accessible to a wider variety of people to enjoy. Infernal BBQ mostly adds more hp and damage to the bosses, while keeping bullet density the same with a small handful of new patterns. It is honestly disappointing and I think the game even refers to Infernal BBQ as Expert++ when you want to change the difficulty so that is also funny to me. It is nice though that it is more of a gradual slope of difficulty instead of like in Rabi-Ribi where it was nice and challenging on Hell (Expert) and ball busting-ly difficult on Bunny Extinction (Infernal BBQ); Saying this as someone who has played through all of Bunny Extinction in Rabi-Ribi on console.NegativesStory: Oh boy, don't get me started on the story. I enjoyed it at the start, but as the hours went on, it became very apparent they didn't know what to do with the characters or plot.  It really felt like the story had a stoke of dementia as important plot points and characters were brought up then immediately dropped such as memloch being fought and talked to for 5 minutes then absent for the rest of the remaining 20+ hours, the beastkin-human conflict being brought up with Frankie but then dying alongside with him as they never elaborated on it any further. The plot twist of Tahlia having an evil identical twin sister out of the blue with an evil decay demon and the astral gears playing a role in the last hour of the story was particularly hilarious to me. Either way, a lot of plot points were not tied up or given lose ends for a possible DLC, but even if that was the case there are way to may to feel comfortable with.Linearity: The story hemlocks this game into a very bad form of linearity that I feel the metroidvania should not have, and they outright removed the hidden tech and locked it behind free roam (unlocked after beating the story) which was incredibly frustrating and baffling as the most enjoyable parts of Rabi-Ribi were doing 0% item runs or getting to areas unintended due to the plethora of freedom that the hidden tech allowed. That is just simply absent in this game until after completion due to the story.Map/Exploration design: At the start, the first few areas were great; The exploration was fun, refreshing and something I looked forward to. This all changed when you start to get to the Gothera Swamplands. I feel here is the turning point of where the map design and exploration begins to turn sour. There was a lot of twisting corridors and frustrating traps that were very 'kaizo' in nature as you would fall through the blocks (without being able to react) and be set back 10 seconds at the most. I would have been okay with this had it been only one area, but they are LITTERED throughout the entirety of the rest of the maps past this point and it got tiresome and frustrating. This becomes even more apparent when you try to 100% the map, it really feels like ripping off your fingernails due to all the hidden paths and areas that have no indication of there being a secret or corridor that you can blast open or slide through. The map is also VERY large, almost too large I feel for how complex it is. I would have wished that they scaled the map down while keeping its complexity, or kept the large map while making it less complex.Overall I enjoyed the experience and will probably go on to get all the achievements while eagerly awaiting the DLC and free updates. I didn't hate the game, but I feel that there are a lot of important points that could be improved upon or made better than they currently are. Recommend it at a solid 7/10, but you should also Play Rabi-Ribi if you enjoyed this game or are interested in others similar to this.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a pretty good game. The pixel perfect graphics, precise 2d controls, a complex and interesting progression system and a decent combat system are the strengths of the game. Unfortunately, the combat does not remain balanced after you have activated synergistic combat abilities in the progression system, which will trivialize enemy and boss encounters (especially the bullet hell aspect) in the latter half of the game. The story felt pretty grating and irritating for me as a person who is not that into anime, but I guess it may come off better if you like that kind of stuff. The game is generously sized, but exploration is quite strictly tied to main story progress. In hindsight, I regret spending so many hours trying to find secrets and optional paths in early and mid game, knowing now that almost all of those aspects were locked behind late main story exploration items.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid metroidvania with insanely fun combat and an entertaining story. RR had many moments where enemies would become completely untouchable, putting the player on the defensive to dodge the oncoming rain of bullets. Tevi bosses rarely did that, instead relying on the new Submissive and Dominant mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: Tevi took me 35 hours to finish and I had a great time with it. It's a linear metroidvania (along the lines of Metroid Fusion and Igavanias) because movement upgrades are usually tied to story progress, so it has a very different design philosophy from Rabi-Ribi which had a ton of freedom in exploration (along the lines of Super Metroid and Hollow Knight). Despite that, this is a very well crafted game that kept me entertained the whole time.The combat was fantastic. From the many different melee attacks, six charged shots (100 MP), six basic shots, Core Expansion (creates a barrier that absorbs small bullets and launches an attack), Soul Burst (damages all enemies and grants temporary invincibility), and an air dash that deals damage, you have plenty of options in combat.  There's a ranking system for combos that works like it does in Devil May Cry, so using different moves is encouraged to keep the combo rank high, and you'll want a high combo rank so that you can use some of the exclusive moves that are only available at a high enough rank. It is easier than a DMC game to get a high rank, but that’s likely because they want people to have access to the high ranked moves. In addition to your large moveset, you also have Sigils that can be found or purchased to change how combat in the game works. There’s over 150 Sigils and they can do things like change the air dash so that at SSS rank it moves back and forth rapidly when used during an air combo. Sigils are limited by BP, so you won’t be able to equip every Sigil you get. You can get more BP by leveling up, finding yellow potions, or equipping Sigils that adjust BP (for example, one Sigil give you more BP for the higher your max HP is). With everything the game gives you combat wise, you get to use your skills against the fantastic bosses the game throws at you. The bosses are a real test of your skill and will use a lot of different attacks so you’ll have to learn their patterns, especially on higher difficulties.There’s also a crafting system that allows you to make healing and attack items from materials you get by killing enemies. You can’t cheese the game with healing items because the items you can craft don’t really heal you by much but they give you useful buffs, there’s also a limit to how much of each item you can craft. You’re also limited by how many items you can carry by your backpack, which you can upgrade to hold a maximum of 10 items. You can also use the crafting system to improve the items you collect in the game by using magitite, like increasing the size of the cluster bomb. The only issue I have with crafting is that you need to use magitite to get some of the combat abilities like four of the shot types or the Soul Burst. The game also has a shop and when you buy enough of items you can get magitite, so that offsets the crafting requirements for combat abilities, as those only require yellow magitie (buy sigils to get yellow magitite).The game’s visuals are very good. The pixel art looks very nice, the character art and CGs look great, and the UI elements are very clean. The music was awesome, plenty of great songs and heart pumping boss themes. The overall audio design is great, it the sound effects just work so well to sell the impact of combat.While I enjoyed the story, I think it’s the weakest aspect of the game. I don’t wanna get into spoilers but I felt that the last chapter rushed through the story because some loose ends weren’t tied up, I also felt the final boss’s second phase could’ve been foreshadowed better. I think the world building was nice overall though, it was nice learning about the world and history of Az.The game also has a lot of content. Like the opening said, It took me 35 hours to complete which is pretty long for a metroidvania. Beating the game also unlocks a custom game mode that allows you to change various things about the game and the highest difficulty. One of the custom modes makes the game more like Rabi-Ribi and even brings back the hidden tech from that game and the goal is now to just beat the bosses, which you can do in nearly any order. Even if you only play the game once, there's a ton of secrets to find and boss refights you can unlock after you beat the game.Before I played Tevi I thought it was going to be an spiritual successor to Rabi-Ribi, but it ended up being something very different and I really enjoyed my time with it, it’s honestly one of my favorite metroidvanias now. I absolutely recommend the game, and will be there for CreSpirit's next game.
