_childDocuments_.review: "Would I recommend this game"? TL;DR: barely, only to fans of metroidvanias and or Rabi-Ribi. Though only for the gameplay, not the writing/story.The game has its good sides, but I also have a few bigger gripes with it after finishing the story.If you know the spiritual predecessor, Rabi-Ribi, you already (mostly) know how the basic gameplay-loop will play. In some aspects better, in others unfortunately worse.One big difference is, that Tevi is much more story driven than Rabi-Ribi. For a metroidvania game where exploration is one of the key points this poses a bit of a problem. Many key traversal items are hidden behind story events, which also results in the player having to head more towards mandatory story events instead of exploring the map. (In Rabi-Ribi you can sequence-break a lot, it even is encouraged looking at the achievements.)You can still explore areas, but you're often stopped by barriers that require specific items to overcome. In general this isn't bad, but here it really restricts you options to find buff items and making exploration somewhat pointless until you gathered a substantial amount of those key items, which is towards the last third of the game.The story itself is its own can of worms, but I won't go into detail here to avoid spoilers. I will only say two things in that regard: - A lot of characters and storylines are introduced, but also dropped/forgotten or even not resolved at all at the end of the game.- The game is overall trying to be serious, but some characterinteractions make you question the existence of a functioning brain in the characters heads. Rabi-Ribi wasn't well written either, but it at least had the excuse of being a silly game.The gameplay is the strongest part of the game, overall good. Metroidvania players will feel at home very quickly. The combat is fast and (mostly) fluid. Aside from melee attacks Tevi also employs two helping floating turrets (that also contain a character each) that can provide ranged fire support with a variety of shot-types. In addition each of those "orbitars" also comes with an activatable ability down the line that helps managing the incoming bullet-storm plus providing some extra firepower.When you do get to explore you can find a large variety of buff items that increase Tevis base stats plus "sigils" that are the counterpart to the badges from Rabi-Ribi. This system however is a bit flawed this time around. While Rabi-Ribi had a certain number of batches that you can activate/deactivate with a point-limit, Tevi dials this up to 11 by providing over 180 sigils, with very different effects.Min-Max builders can sure have a lot of fun with it, but the sheer number of stat-boosts/abilites/effects in a rather inconvenient menu feel very bloated and players will have a hard time finding anything, since the sigils are represented with a symbol and not in a list with a name.There is also a crafting system where you can craft consumables or upgrade most of your items to get stronger/provide additional effects. The materials are drops from monsters and/or money. The latter cannot be farmed and must be collected from blocks in the world that you blow up, limiting the accessible currency depending on the traversal items you have. Overall however you don't feel too short for cash, as long as you stick to buying stat-potions instead of sigils.. the latter are mostly not that important to get early on.One very good aspect of the game are the boss-fights. The amount and variety of enemies is much larger compared to RR with a larger number of bullet-patterns to avoid. One small gripe are occasional fast attacks (sometimes coming from off screen) that are very hard to avoid and feel a bit unfair. On normal difficulty you can still facetank through most bosses if necessary though.Graphically the game went quite a few steps up, the backgrounds and pixel-art are gorgeous to look at, and the effects in the different boss-fights are quite nice. Enemy design and variety is also quite high, with (almost) each region featuring its own set of enemies. Characterdesigns are overall good, althought the style between the CGs and the character-portraits clashes a bit.The soundtrack fits the respective regions in the game well, there are even a few bangers that made it into my personal playlist.For RR fans, there is also quite a bit to see/discover :) also some content is still in development (boss-rush among a few other things).In conclusion, can I recommend this game? To die-hard metroidvania fans, yes, though you still might want to wait for a small discount. But to people that want to enjoy a good story on top of it, clearly no. There is just too much wrong here.@Crespirit: If one of the devs reads this: if possible, finish the open story threads (there are quite a lot), also please stop forgetting that Vena exists at the end of the game :P and also maybe rework the UI for the sigils. It's just too hard to find what you are looking for.I really wish, steam would allow a neutral stance towards games.. I will update my review if/when things get fixed/added to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly one of the best games I've ever played. It fits perfectly into the type of action platformer exploration RPGs I enjoy. Movement feels amazing and only gets better as you get more abilities. Exploration feels super fun, and I love solving the little puzzles to get different items (though some were a lot more obtuse than others, and I did eventually resort to a guide for gathering everything I missed). Combat always felt fun, too, and I loved chaining combos together on bosses, or trying to figure out the build that worked best for me with the sigils. I did raise the difficulty to Hard, which felt adequately challenging for most of the game, but I did feel a bit overpowered by the end of the game because I explored and got so many stat-boosting potions, save for maybe the last few bosses. There are some difficulty-based achievements I'll admit I'm daunted to try, but we'll see if I feel like tackling them. If you're up for challenging achievements, the game is definitely for you. Otherwise just play on whatever difficulty is fun for you.Not only is the gameplay fantastic, but the story is incredible. The worldbuilding is beautiful, and I loved learning about all the little things about the land of Az, from the different races to the important history and more. Things may feel somewhat disjointed at first, but I promise, EVERYTHING comes together in such an incredible and heartwrenching way that I'm still coping with everything that happened. Very rarely could I guess where things were going, the surprises are always welcome, and every character felt special to me. The character growth of Tevi, Celia, and Sable are especially good, as you see them truly grow from accidental collaborators into true friends.This game is truly top notch and has earned a very special place in my heart. I would consider it in the same vein as Astlibra, another game of its type that is also incredibly special to me. It's not going to be everyone's cup of tea, and I could nitpick little things I liked and didn't like, but at the end of the day, I couldn't put it down. 10/10 from me, I wish I could forget all of it so I could play it all again. I also see some areas that I couldn't get to, so I'm looking forward to some potential DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: A great fun game. The story pretty much revolves around a crisis that happened thirty years before. The game is like a mix of cyberpunk I believe the genre is. With a mix of other things. The mechanics are smooth, but takes a while to unlock. The platforming is a bit weird, but easily adjustable as well. What I mean by weird is how certain things doesn't make sense, based on transition and time a power up would be unlocked.Aside from this, it works well. The boss battles are engaging, and the characters are quite entertaining. It is definitely a positive experience, and I'd recommend it. Just some things to note, you control Tevi. And the other two characters have a range of skills that mixes into her set.There is crafting in the game, and a pretty wide customization for building your character. These features might appear small, but once stacked in, it really opens up the gameplay. Exploration, I'd recommend leaving some markers, as there are points you'd want to get back to. There can be stat increases, or other things you can get at a later point.Gameplay:To get a bit more into this, it is a bullet hell game. However, the game's chip system allows you to free click on and off. These will make a significant difference in battles. Such as taking advantage of a dodge, chaining combos, making break more useful. You can even do a build that might debuff you, but also raise your damage. There is a ton to do. There are also quite a bit of maps, and these maps are large. You'll be backtracking for power ups, and fiddling with the chip system. Though, not so much to take you out of the game. This game really does well to keep immersion into it.Story:Following the events of a crisis 30 years before. The game follows Tevi, whose purpose for her journey is to find out about her past. As it goes along, and the pieces falls into place. There are a lot of hardships faced, such as losing a valuable friend with a simple dream. Having to fight against her friend who was forcefully transformed. Clashing against those from Valhalla and Tartarus, and really finding herself in dire situations. Getting closer to the end, these loose points connects, and former enemies becomes allies. The mysteries surrounding decay, and Tevi's past itself steadily connects in a feverish way.Characters:The characters are likable, even the antagonists. While starting off more chilled, it slowly gets into their stories. The hardships they faced, and how Tevi continuously loses those close to her. These characters builds on each other, and have their motivations well in place. A bunch of bandits finding a reason to live underneath the guidance of someone. This is after a terrible war. A demon who matures over time, and has to face someone close to him. That person valuing his family and the friends of his family. An angel who was once firm, but naive. You see how she bonds with Tevi, and her disgust for demons decrease, valuing the demon with her as a good friend. These all connecting to Tevi, and her purpose for pushing against challenges far above herself. From end to end, this was done great with the characters. And when the losses hit, it hits deep.Overall, it is a fun and engaging game to play. As it went along, the story got deeper and steadily unraveled. If anything, the highlight were the characters, and this was wonderfully done.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a fun time with it. The combat is good and the bosses are a lot of fun, it feels really nice. Exploration and the map is ok, not on par with some other metroidvania games but it does a decent job with it. Story is kind of a weak spot though, you can drive a truck through all the plot holes it opens up by the end, so don't go into this expecting peak cinema. But overall it's worth playing imo

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done Metroidvania, with a lot of Bullet Hell on top of it. The game looks great, have an amazing soundtrack and have a lot of difficult options to cover all tastes. The first playthrough is kind linear, the game wont allow you to explore that much out of the way, but when you beat it first time there is a mode that change it. If you like Rabi Ribi and it is a fan of the genre, this one is the top contender in 2023 of metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Tevi is the spirital sequel to the cult classic bunny-girl bullet-hell metroidvania Rabi-Ribi from 2016.If that means nothing to you just imagine bosses that can soak up damage like nothing else while filling the screen with projectiles that you have to bunny hop around while wailing on them. Combined with traditional metroidvania exploration and item progression (double jump, air dash, etc).This is as difficult as it sounds, if not more, but a lot of fun once you learn the boss patterns. Highly recommended if you don't mind games on the harder side or enjoy the anime look.Pros:* Bullet-Hell is perfection* Large world with exploration & secrets (albeit some of the exploration and secrets feels a tad samey after awhile)* Fighting feels very satisfying with lots of moves for combos, good pacing, varying times you have to attack, dodge, or avoid, etc.* Badg-- *ahem* sigil system allows for a lot of customizability in combat.* Large game with lots of achievements and extra difficulty levels.Cons:* Fighting a boss after you've progressed too far makes them a pushover (no level scaling in story mode AFAICT)* Somewhat more linear than the previous game (no more secret move button combos AFAICT)The plot is more fleshed out (but still fairly straightforward) compared to the previous game, with (Japanese) voice acting for the major characters.The difficulty feels slightly easier to me compared to the last game, but I'm still on my first (expert) playthrough and, well, maybe I've just gotten a bit better.(Also Sable is perfect and I just want to shelter him from everything haha)
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack. Amazing combat.Okay art, but good pixel art.Very good boss fights, although a bit on the easy side if you use healing items, which most people probably will.As for the story, I can't tell you, because the writing was so bad that I ended up just skipping every dialogue. Something I never usually do in video games.The metroidvania parts are also a bit weak, the game feels very linear with very little sequence breaking, and upgraded seems to just be for continuing the main story rather than opening up exploration.Overall, I think it is a very good game, with the only major flaw being the writing.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Rabi-Ribi was the second game I purchased on Steam. I enjoyed it so much that I cleared it about five times. When I heard the news that GameYue was releasing this game after a long time, 8 years later, I couldn't wait to play it, so I couldn't hold back my excitement.In conclusion, this game is a well-crafted Metroidvania in its genre. However, unfortunately, if one expects as much from TEVI after playing Rabi-Ribi, they might be disappointed.1. GameplayIn Rabi-ribi, there was a goal to defeat a certain number of bosses, and while there were recommended boss lists for each chapter, players could freely explore and defeat any boss first, and the story would still progress. Of course, being a Metroidvania genre, there were places that couldn't be accessed depending on acquired skills, but for the most part, I could play the way I wanted. However, TEVI clearly had limited sections to move between chapters, and apart from a few hidden bosses, the order of defeating bosses was fixed. The spaces that could be accessed were determined by the skills acquired in each chapter.2. StoryAdditionally, the story feels somewhat disappointing. While preferences for a heavier or lighter narrative can vary among individuals, I personally preferred the lighter atmosphere of the previous game. As the story became more serious, the excessive length of dialogues made it feel like the flow was interrupted while exploring the world. Despite reaching the ending, I couldn't shake the feeling that certain elements introduced during the story remained unresolved, lingering as loose ends rather than being properly concluded.3. ArtThe pixel art and CG were satisfactory, but I found the quality of the character standing art to be quite disappointing.

If I could give this game an "Okay" rating I would.The Good:The Bad:The Ugly:

The pixel-art is also really beautiful and you can tell there was a lot of effort into making each area look great, with the music complimenting it very nicely, my personal favorites probably being Morose, Solonda Beach and Oasis Cove.A solid title and I definitely recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Bunny girl metroidvania was far off my radar and certainly not what I was expecting to be one of the better games I played this year.-Fantastic music-Great and numerous boss fights-Surprisingly decent story-Huge world and tons of secrets-Battle and traversal feel goodIf you're one of those people who love to explore and collect everything then I would definitely recommend choosing Hard or Expert when you play the game. _childDocuments_.review: Following long after the Rabi-Ribi coat tails, TEVI falls into a wonderful metroidvania adventure, though be warned bosses are designed around the BULLET HELL aspect Rabi-Ribi held.That warning aside, TEVI is far more linear in destination, it also encourages a more combat flow to its melee systems rather than the issue that RabiRibi had with keeping your combo S rank, or not really doing much damage at all. Rather this time around you gain the badges and side abilities which some times have combo rank limiters you need to reach. For example you could get a badge that enhances your aerial dash ability but you need to have an S, or higher combo to use it, it also comes with a cool down. Over all, if you enjoyed Rabi-Ribi, this is amazing, and is a proper metroidvania where your adventuring abilities are useful throughout combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game since I enjoyed Rabi-Ribi and the high expectations I had were met and exceeded. The story was a lot grimmer than I was expecting but it was engaging and enjoyable. The movement items unlocked throughout the game were interesting and a welcome difference from Rabi-Ribi. There is a certain item in the game that you get after completing the story on your save that I especially love.  I also enjoyed the map system that allowed for tagging spaces with bookmarks. As with all games at launch, there were bugs that I experienced. Fortunately for me, they were all small graphical bugs with the minimap and the map completion percentages. However, restarting the game cleared this issues so it wasn't too big of a deal. Besides that, the only thing I didn't really like about the game was the achievement menu. It did fit with the book theme but I much prefer the more robust UI from Rabi-Ribi.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed how smooth the gameplay and combat are, and it's fun doing aerial combos and dodging bullet rain, alongside finding every item in the game and exploring the whole map, and combining mechanics for techniques to reach areas the game doesn't want you to. The story I also enjoyed, as the character interactions and dynamics to each other really allow for various dialogue and scenarios to happen and be experienced, alongside the interesting mystery behind Tevi's necklace and what decay is.Of course, if you have many negative things to say about the story, art, and characters, there's a friendly like-minded community in the official Tevi Discord server you might have fun conversing with.

_childDocuments_.review: Rabi ribi was a special little game, i didnt think it would be as good as it was, the art style, the music, and the absolutely unique gameplay that worked well got me instantly. I played that game to death and was dreaming, of a sequel.Now that Tevi is out, i can confirm that if you want a Rabi Ribi 2, this will sort of quench your thirst, but not completely. I like it, i really do, as a spiritual successor i think it works, it has the look and feel of Rabi Ribi on all fronts, but it does not work as good on all fronts as it did with Rabi Ribi. The exploration: People already brought up how exploration has taken a turn for the worst, half of my fun in Rabi Ribi was using my accumulated game knowledge to see how strong i could get early game and blast everything away. There is seemingly no such thing in Tevi, as all big boy upgrades (Air dash, double jump, slide etc) are locked behind story progression. You can run around the whole game and not find a single real upgrade besides stats or sigils which is in my honest opinion, a big old let down. 6 ranged weapons in total: The ranged weapons in this game are.. something. I cant decide whether i like it or not. For me sable is the winner, i dont care that much for celia at all which leaves me wirh 3 total orbitars. This is quite low compared to how many variety rabi ribi had. Sure not all where Meta, but who cares? I used the carrot shooter because its frigging hillarious. Sigils: With 250+ sigils ingame, it becomes hard to manage your equipment. Good luck putting a new build on prior to a boss, it will take you a while scrolling through the sigils with no way to save a pre set *favorite* build.Artstyle: While not the same as Rabi ribi, i think thats okay. Not all styles have to be the same, i liked the dark tone this story had in contrast to rabi ribi as a change of phase. However, i do agree after looking at screenshots laid next to each other from both tevi and rabi ribi, that in rabi ribi the overall quality seemed better? Especially in the textbox moments. Story: People complained the story was stupid, while i agree with this, i have to add: What was the story in Rabi Ribi? I played it 100 times and still have no clue, zero idea. In Tevi i kind of get it, which in my eyes, albeit not perfect is definitely a step up.Aside from this, the game is so good, and so much fun. I heard from people that Tevi is a side project and that the devs are actually working on a real Rabi Ribi 2, lads, i cant wait.

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend Tevi to anyone who’s a fan of metroidvanias. Made by the same developers as Rabi-Ribi, Tevi has a lot of similarities in gameplay design, but also feels entirely different at times (on top of being a lot bigger). Although it still is a metroidvania-bullet hell, Tevi’s focus is a lot less on the bullet hell part and much more on attacking and combos with a huge array of options.    • Tevi is a paradise for explorers. Absolutely HUGE map to explore with upgrades to find around every tile. Alongside that, Tevi offers tons of features to help with exploring that I wish other metroidvanias had such as being able to put markers on the map to remember where to come back to, info that tells you how many items you have left in each region and what % of the region you’ve explored and most importantly, you DON’T have to buy the map first before you can start filling out tiles (really hate how many metroidvanias do this).    • Combat in Tevi is extremely fun, rewarding and encourages throwing out every move in your repertoire against enemies. There are hundreds of sigils you can collect and equip to change what moves/buffs are available to customize how you want to tackle enemies and bosses.    • Absolutely love the OST. Over 70 tracks in total, every map has a different song to jam to while playing. I think it’s safe to say there’s a track in here for everyone.    • You can craft recovery / offensive items and it really feels like the game encourages crafting and using your items. Enemies drop materials frequently and I never felt like I would have to farm enemies.     • Comparing it to Rabi-Ribi for a minute, even on the highest difficulty available on the first playthrough (Expert), the game still felt too easy at times because of how many ways there are to “cheat” through boss attacks or just facetank, especially as you get more sigils.    • The story is probably my main gripe. Fortunately it doesn’t interfere with gameplay much. Unlike their previous game, Tevi’s story aims to be heavier and more serious. The story itself isn't bad, but it felt too back-loaded rather than being spread out throughout the entire game.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite metroidvania of the year!  Great gameplay, music, and voice acting made for a really enjoyable experience.  Lots of freedom and choice in how you can attack and move around.  The Sigils and upgrades really add a heck of lot of variables to keep in mind if you are trying to get some hyper optimized build.  I could see some crazy speedrun skills being necessary to make some clean attempts for this.  I liked the main characters, but I wish the ending was more fleshed out with some of the side characters' arcs being resolved more.  Maybe in a DLC or future update?

_childDocuments_.review: Tevi has great boss fights. Bosses have unique buffs or systems that you need to work around to fight effectively, and learning how to dodge the bullet pattern attacks is rewarding. The combat system is fun to experiment with, and exploration frequently rewards sigils that can be used to customize your playstyle.Upon completing the game, you unlock the free-roam custom game mode. This mode adjusts the base movement kit and a few map areas to allow for more freedom to explore early on and fight bosses out of order. I was surprised by how many screens were designed to be possible with minimal upgrades just by adding a small ledge or a flying creature for you to bounce on. It gives the game a lot of replay value, which fits well with the game's other systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so to get it out of the way, I enjoyed the game and do recommend it if you enjoy the genre in general.However, this is going to be mostly complaints, as there are also a lot of things in the game I wasn't super fond of for reasons.I enjoyed the majority of the first half of the game, but as I went further, I realized more and more things were just slightly irritating, so I'll try to cover as much of the game feel as I canAlso, this is going to contain quite a bit of spoilers, mostly for gameplay mechanics, so if you don't want to know some of the stuff you will unlock, just read above and take it at that for now.I will try to avoid comparing the game to Rabi-Ribi, since not everyone will have played it first. Instead, the game at its core is a metroid-vania style game with more beat-em-up combat, and bosses that cover the screen in bullets and/or lasers.My only comparison I can give is in terms of overall difficulty: this game is easier than Rabi-Ribi, but is still pretty difficult. I struggled initially when getting used to the controls, but eventually I was first-trying several bosses. For context, I played blind on the highest difficulty available out the gate, with only one higher difficulty being availble after completing the gameFirst, the things that felt good to use basically all of the time:Almost every attack in the game feels good to use. the only one I really never liked/used was the backflip/dodge attack, as it would only trigger dodge if you were close to the boss and could default attack them first to get into the correct state. The basic movement also felt good, double jumping, sliding, dashing, quickdrop all felt responsive and did what I wanted them to do. I'll also say I struggled a little with activating the two "spanner" moves sometimes, since they have a weird pre-requisite of "already being in melee combat" and wouldn't activate if you did the inputs if you haven't whacked anything recently.However, a lot of the movement options (especially later) feel.. not great? the jetpack feels genuinely awful, and I only used it when I needed to. Wall jumping is finnicky, and makes it hard to know if you will wall jump or burn your double jump at a wall. Almost any upwards transition can eat your wall jumps as well, causing you to fall back down whatever you were climbing. I see these as being acceptable, due to them not being necessary the majority of the time, but I still wish they felt better to use.Getting into the other mechanics, the sigil system (badges/charms/whatever else you want to call them) felt weirdly lenient. I never had to make any decisions for what to equip. I was running a melee focused build, and even though it seems to have more supporting sigils than ranged or bombs, I had so many points available all the time, I could just slap on everything I wanted and still have some left over for whatever else I thought might be useful. I'm not sure if there is an easy way to fix this, but maybe the intent was to treat them more like permanent upgrades than perks that you pick and choose between.Then there's the sigil balance. It's all over the place, and some of the costs don't feel super accurate. Most of them fall in the 3-5 range, with a few going as high as 8-9. Some of the low cost ones are super strong, and a couple high cost ones I question why anyone would ever equip. Bombs in this game explode in a + shape instead of a sphere like almost every other game out there. they will also roll to center themselves on the nearest tile before doing so, so you can only hit on the grid of tiles. I understand why they did this, after seeing how a lot of their bomb puzzles are designed, but it makes looking for hidden bombable floors a pain in the ass, where you walk one tile, drop a bomb, walk one tile, drop another. The cluster bomb upgrade is interesting, but kind of clunky to use. they're a bit bouncy and hard to land where you want them to, and the wind-up for them makes them a bit rough to use in combat, though they were also quite effective when they do land. I'm not sure I'd want anything changed on them, I just couldn't really quite get a hang of using them properly.I probably have the biggest complaint about the 'dodge' mechanic, which requires a bit of an explaination.When you hit things, you build up a meter that, when capped out, gives you a stack of dodge. certain actions will make you ignore damage and remove the stack if you are hit during them, allowing you to actively avoid damage. Where this becomes a problem, is if you get hit regularly and have a dodge stack, there is a chance that it will auto-trigger and you will just not get hit. The chance scales with how low your HP is, and I felt like I was being rewarded for playing badly. Just go up and beat the boss, get dodge stacks, and ignore bullets until the dodge triggers. There were many times where I thought I was playing horribly, only to glance up at my HP and see it still at 80% or so, and then I would go on to win the fight anyway. It felt kind of undeserved. This happened to me on the last boss as well, by the way. First time on the final phase, and I basically ended up tanking everything since I hadn't seen the attacks before, yet somehow, I still won. I kind of just felt like the game decided it was over, whether or not I actually earned victory, but man, I wish I could turn off auto-dodging.Ultimately, the issues I have with the game aren't enough to make me think it wasn't worth the time to play through. I enjoyed most of it, but if the devs are going to continue working on the game, these aspects I would appreciate getting a little bit of reworking, or just be revisited to make them feel better to interact with.tl;dr: Game good, but has some design choices I wasn't super fond of. worth a buy if you enjoy metroidvanias

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game in its current state to anyone who is an avid Metroidvania fan, or just wants to be on the wild ride earlier on in this game's inevitable wave of content updates. For bullet hell fans, this game is too easy unless you choose the highest difficulty and then limit yourself to not picking up upgrades, so caveat emptor in that regard. If you're not a genre buff and you just think this game looks interesting, then you can make your decision based on the content of this review. I think it's safe to say that even if Metroidvanias and bullet hells aren't your thing, as long as you like action platformers, then this game will be worth its price tag in a few months from now after some of its more glaring problems get patched and it gets its first wave of free content updates. Spoilers ahead, btw!This game has pretty tight controls (especially after a recent update that lets you choose how certain moves work,) great music and sprite work, STELLAR voice work (it's almost entirely voice acted!! and with a star-studded cast to boot,) overall pretty motivating gameplay pace, BUT the maps have a lot of "Metroid moments" where you're just expected to know to do things like jump down the right pit out of several that'll kill you because only that pit has a fake wall on its side, or jump in the right area to find a fake ceiling, or bomb every single square of a room, that sort of thing. I got about 95% complete and then had to start asking people in the discord server or referring to guides here on Steam for help because of these trolly map design choices. It's not like the spiritual predecessor, Rabi-Ribi, didn't do this too, though... but with Rabi-Ribi, most of those hidden items were just the easter eggs that barely did anything, whereas here, it's full blown stat boosters and sigils (the replacement for badges.)In fact, in basically every way, I can't help but compare this to Rabi-Ribi, and feel that in many ways, the older game is better, despite having less memorable characters and no VA work. But Rabi-Ribi got years of patches and content updates, workshop content including a "training mode" for movement tech, and a pretty solid speedrunning scene (for such a niche type of game, anyway), which turned it into (story/unnecessary fanservice aside) one of the greatest Metroidvania-type games of all time. If TEVI gets the same amount of patching and content updates, it'll also join those vaunted halls someday.For now, though, there are some problems, besides the sometimes-trolly map design: mostly with a story that is too slow in some parts and too rushed in others, too reliant on extended dialogue sequences, and with progression and map traversal that is locked behind the story. It ends up behooving you to ignore collectibles (for the most part) and just rush the main quest ASAP. As a result, if you play it like a proper Metroidvania, i.e., exploring the map and looking for collectibles as much as possible, you'll end up backtracking way, way, way more than you would have if you just hurried through the story.Of course, unlike Rabi-Ribi, this game doesn't really scale bosses based on how many items you have, so collectibles actually do help make fights easier, so you should still try to get them. However, you can very easily get to the point where fights are trivialized because you do so much damage, have so much health, and get so many special abilities from sigils that even on higher difficulties, you will have to actually TRY to die on late-game bosses. The difficulty curve in this game is backwards, starting off decently challenging and then quickly dying down to the point of being laughably easy. I think by chapter 3 I was no longer struggling with bosses, and I ended up turning the difficulty up to compensate, and even that didn't help (it really just made platforming challenges involving spikes more punishing, lol.) The good news is that the devs are pushing patches sometimes multiple times a day, to fix minor bugs and rebalance the game. I am confident that in a few months from now, this game will have a lot of its minor flaws ironed out. The problems with the story might take a while to fix... I can't imagine they'll just haul the VAs back in for more recording sessions to make the rushed exposition at the end not feel as such. But you know what? That's ok. Rabi-Ribi's story was more threadbare and easy to ignore, so the fact that it was full of weird deus ex machina moments didn't bother me; since TEVI's story actually has some substance, it makes the parts where it falters seem worse by comparison. So maybe it's better to have a flawed story that still has good moments than to have one that's just vestigial.My other complaints with this game mostly revolve around things like movement tech being intentionally removed until you clear the game once, same with some upgrades that help you get 100%. Going for 100% in your first playthrough is a pleasure you can only enjoy once–the feeling of waltzing into the final boss room loaded to the teeth and being THEIR final boss instead–but that is not allowed in TEVI, it seems. Yes, I know I was talking about the game being too easy earlier, but IMO final bosses exist either to be flashy, but easy little romps to just cap off a story (like how you basically can't lose once you get far enough into Undertale's final boss fight) or they should be brutal, the hardest or second hardest fights in the game, something you need to actually get as close to 100% as you can for. TEVI opts for the former, but doesn't let you enjoy the feeling of having fully conquered the game before roflstomping the final boss. It's a pity, and I hope they change it.Final thoughts: there are some funny easter eggs in here. They got Dio's seiyuu to play one of the minor antagonists, and I thought that would mean only a few lines, but nope, the guy has several full minutes of dialogue. It really makes you feel like JoJo. It is unfortunate that the localization sometimes oversimplifies what the characters are saying, though. Also, the dopamine rush when Vena thanks you for giving her zenn–I mean, your support! is out of this world. Better than when Cocoa celebrated that she wouldn't need to beg Rumi for food after you bought a bomb from her in Rabi-Ribi. If there's one thing CreSpirit is good at, it's letting you live out the primal urge to feed the neighborhood stray cat(girl.) Who just so happens to sell homemade explosives.---Adding an edit after seeing other people's reviews, especially negative ones. I agree with a criticism of the plot that it over-glorifies authority. While our protagonist Tevi ostensibly shows distrust towards organizations, especially those with authority, she still ends up collaborating with them and by the end of the game, doesn't show that distrust much at all. Also, like a lot of fantasy anime-type stuff, it glorifies monarchy and royalty, not only making them have The Most Magical Important Powers In The World but also making (most of) them be paragons of virtue, whereas in real history we all know what monarchs and aristocrats really were like. I did like that the plot shows some hypocrisy on some of these groups' part, but the main monarchy as well as the de facto new government, which is basically just a military police, are basically morally perfect and never do evil, only sometimes failing (due to not having enough power–if only the cops had more hands and funds, oh woe!) to save the day. This is all I can say before I seriously spoil the plot.I also agree with the criticisms about some characters being sexually objectified without it contributing much to the plot. Unlike some stories where a woman is sexually objectified, dislikes it, and takes action in regards to it, Celia and Tevi only sometimes protest verbally when sexually harassed, instead of whacking a certain little gremlin's head off. It's still a lot less bad than Rabi-Ribi in this regard, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly blown away by this game. The map is massive, the gameplay is smooth, there's plenty of gorgeous pixel art to go around, and the bosses are a lot more readable than the ones in Rabi-Ribi, though I guess the crazy chaotic fights were definitely a draw to Rabi, but I'm okay letting them stay there. The fights in this game have their own draw to them and honestly it was nice feeling like I was improving at the bosses rather than fluking them (I'm looking at you, crystal ring).It was a little sad to see that the nonlinearity was limited to the first two chapters of the game, though. I was half-expecting that formula to continue throughout, with each chapter adding one or two optional missions alongside the main story quest,  Like, even refights of certain bosses,  would have been very welcome, just to feel like they're more active in the story.Speaking of the story... I'm seeing a lot of hate arouind it. And honestly there's some good points raised. If you're the kind of person who can't stand plot holes, honestly... just skip the cutscenes. You'll be doing yourself a favor. Otherwise though, one thing I very much will give the story is it does an amazing job at making you itch to just cut the bosses to shreds (with a couple of intended exceptions). It is sad to see that a lot of those threads get dropped, but at least in the moment the majority of the bossfights feel important. Despite the story's issues, though, I must say I'm a fan of the world as a whole. The layout of places feels like it was thought out, with the climates moving along a gradient from desert in the west to temperate climates and finally to snowy mountains in the east,  The placement of the cities makes sense for the most part in my mind, though I will say the excuse for why the train and airship don't take you to  right off the bat is contrived as hell.Oh yeah, also the train and airship are completely useless when we have Aetherliths for fast travel right next to the stations. And they'll take you to basically any area, whereas the train and airship will take you precisely two.But yeah, overall, it's a flawed but ultimately still super fun game. Definitely a game for people who like bossfights. Despite all the things I can criticize, the game as a whole is a great experience and one I strongly recommend. I could say more but like, let's face it, not a single person read all of that. So I guess with that in mind...TL;DR: Really fun game. Has a lot of flaws, but it's really good at what it gets right. Play it if you like bossfights. Also Sable is my baby and I will skin anyone who tries to hurt him (for legal reasons this is a joke).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good Metroidvania with an anime vibe.  The world map is full of secrets (bombable walls, invisible walls, walls that are destroyable).  There are lots of zones which you can fast travel back and forth to.  Over 80 Sigils to find and purchase which give special abilities and bonuses.  The story is hilarious, and very intricate like your standard jRPG.  The Bosses can be challenging and often have bullet hell moves forcing you to learn complex patterns to avoid damage.  Very worth while game.  One side note, the audio is completely in Japanese, so if that's not your thing you can disable the Voice Event audio and there will only be text to read.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game, one of the best ones I've played. The quality in nearly every aspect is insane, especially for such a small development team. I 100% recommend it, and it would honestly be a harder task to name things that I didn't like about it, but some key points:- The world map is massive and vibrant, with detailed pixel art and an expansive soundtrack courtesy of multiple composers. Biomes have their own unique dangers and gimmicks, enemy types offer a diverse range of threats instead of being carbon copies of one another, and exploration yields plenty of secrets to be uncovered. A word of warning, those expecting Rabi-Ribi's infamous sequence breaking nonlinearity may be disappointed, as key movement upgrades are mostly locked behind progression points and the hidden techs are gone. However, I had little issue with this, as the map is so expansive that each "stage" of movement is still hours of exploration. You do unlock a free roam mode that restores the hidden techs from the previous game and lets you go wherever, but you do have to complete a normal game before unlocking it. (EDIT: This is no longer true, as you can now just start with Free Roam if you really want)- There are a ridiculous number of sigils/badges to discover, many of which can fundamentally change the way you play the game, and the game gives you plenty of points to put into them, letting you fine-tune your build as you see fit. No matter whether you want to unleash melee wombo combos, blast away with magic, proc dodges, funnel power into one of your special moves, live longer, or anything in between, it's possible.- The combat in this game is legitimately some of the most fun I've had in a while. You're extremely mobile, movement is snappy and smooth, and Tevi has a massive number of moves and an equally large number of ways to chain them together. The closest comparison I can make is that it feels like 2D Devil May Cry, with a huge emphasis on performing massive combo strings and juggling foes with unique attacks. Mastering and executing extended combos feels illegally satisfying.- The bosses retain expansive movepools that keep you on your toes for the whole fight, but their design relies less on sheer bullet hell compared to Rabi-Ribi, with a larger focus on interaction with each boss' specific fighting style or gimmick, and movement/positioning to avoid attacks. Difficulty as a whole seems to be a bit lower than the previous game, but I found myself enjoying this new style of boss design more, as it made each boss more distinct and added a variety of ways to tackle them with all the tools you have at your disposal instead of just moving to dodge, while still promoting the same proactive playstyle, lack of idle moments, and learning curve on failures. Attacks as a whole are really diverse and also seem much more intuitive than RR, meaning that you're less likely to get instantly screwed if you didn't know the solution for a pattern beforehand.- There's a fairly large spectrum of difficulty options, and you're now allowed to freely change the difficulty whenever you want, letting you adjust it on the fly to suit your preferences. I did my first run on Expert (albeit with about 300 hours of RBRB experience), and the damage seemed to strike a nice balance where you're not overly punished for making mistakes, but will very easily kick the bucket if you recklessly take hits. The game saves frequently and you lose next to nothing on death, with the game even healing you if your last autosave had you below half HP. The difficulty curve was relatively smooth over the game, although your power can spike quite a bit in the midgame to lategame sections. (EDIT: They did buff the lategame segments recently, so this is likely less of the case now)- The story is fairly standard and won't necessarily leave you musing about philosophy for the next week, but it's certainly charming and will keep you entertained in between gameplay beats. Worldbuilding is decently interesting, the character art and interactions strike a satisfactory balance between goofy and serious, and the phenomenal voice work elevates all the characters, particularly the main trio. Personally, I also liked how the game was less overtly fanservicey compared to RR (or at least I'll feel slightly less uneasy recommending it to friends). The pacing does start to rush a bit near the end, though, and certain threads seem to be setting up for future updates or DLC rather than tying up properly.- The game has more updates and content planned as of this review's writingI would absolutely recommend the game to anyone who's into metroidvanias, stylish combat, exploration, bullet hell, or any combination thereof. Those just expecting Rabi-Ribi 2 may be disappointed, but TEVI has its own distinct identity and charm to it, and I think it's damn well earned its place among the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun to play and improves on the gameplay from Rabi-Ribi, but has a couple big problems, there is almost zero exploration factor in this metroidvania because everything is story-locked. You will constantly be running into dead ends with no possible way to proceed, it feels like the game actively wastes your time by giving you labyrinthine maps only to have almost every path besides the one to the story objective lead to a room that requires a specific upgrade that you absolutely cannot get until you reach that point in the main quest.There is also the fact that you're repeatedly getting stopped to watch pointless cutscenes that add nothing to the story whatsoever. If it's so important that the player needs to know that the main characters think it's hot in an underground magma cavern, then just add some voice overs or a text bubble and let the player keep going instead of grinding the pacing to a halt every ten minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Great gameplay. Fun bosses. Lengthy campaign. Plenty of replayability. Decent exploration. Mid writing; bad story. Don't go in expecting a metroidvania for your first playthrough, you'll be disappointed; it is a very linear game. Certain game systems are needlessly complicated and/or bloated.To start off, I strongly recommend playing the DEMO first before considering buying this game. The second zone + boss is a good representation of what to expect from most of this game. If you enjoyed the boss battles, I recommend the full game.=====TEVI is a game that mixes metroidvania exploration, Devil-May-Cry inspired combat abilities, and bullet-hell enemies. The result is a game with great gameplay and a large, interconnected map. But, the game is held back by its Story Mode and suffers from some bloated systems.=====As Tevi, you'll have your genre-staple movement abilities (wall jump, double jump, etc.), but unlike most metroidvanias, the combat system is pretty complex. You have 2 ground combos, 1 air combo, and 6 different ranged attacks. In addition, you can cancel most of these moves using ground-to-air or air-to-ground techniques, allowing you to freely chain from one combo string to the next. The game also uses a Sigil system that allows you to customize/upgrade your moves, granting them additional properties or introducing special attacks. The game has a combo meter that incentives you to mix up your combo strings, especially since a lot of your best moves are locked behind it.Enemies, on the other hand, fight primarily by using bullet-hell patterns. In some cases, there will be melee attacks, but most of the time you'll be dodging projectile attack patterns. There is a ton of variety to these attacks and they are all well-designed.Bosses in this game are pretty great. They are long, often taking between 5-10 minutes (especially in the latter half of the game) and have extremely varied attack patterns that range from simple to complex multi-part attacks. These fights can be pretty intense and the'll definitely test your skills.Mechanically speaking, this game can be quite difficult. There are some patterns that I just could not avoid reliably even after my 5th time seeing it. However, there is no shortage of tools at your disposal to mitigate the onslaught of bullets headed in your general direction. You have a Shield, a Dodge mechanic and can even become temporarily invincible.Despite the intense combat, Tevi can be quite easy. This game has 7 difficulty options for players of all skill levels, gives you have like half a dozen healing consumables some of which heal over 50% of your HP, and has numerous ASSIST Sigils that can automate certain parts of the game.=====The game features a Sigil system, which works similarly to Rabi-Ribi's badges, or Hollow Knight's Charms. There are over 100 Sigils to collect, and their effects are quite varied. Some are simple passive effects (+HP), some are assists (AUTO combo), others add additional properties to your attacks (afterimages, rebound), and some just give new abilities to use (clone attack, Tornado Slam). I enjoyed it, but it is also a bloated system. There are many redundant sigils that serve little purpose:Example 1 - There is a sigil that increases ground attack speed by 15%. There is also a sigil that increases aerial attack speed by 15%. They aren't combined to form a sigil that universally increases melee attack speed by 15%. Why? Example 2 - You equip sigils by using EP. Yellow Potions are a pickup you can find that will permanently increase your EP by 5. There are multiple sigils that, when equipped, increase your EP. Why do these sigils exist in place of just more Yellow Potions?=====As a metroidvania this game is a bit disappointing. It is a very story-driven game and attempting to sequence break or go off the critical path isn't often very fruitful outside of some minor stat upgrades. This is "fixed" once you beat the game, as it unlocks the game's Free Roam mode: An alternate game mode that offers significant freedom to how you progress through the game.I found levels were fun to explore; plenty of secrets and decent enemy variety. But, I have a couple of issues with them. Firstly, some platforms blend in too well with the background, making it difficult to tell where you're suppose to go (Travoll Industry Park, Snowpeak Isle). Secondly, frequent pitfall traps that lock you into a slowfall. You often can't seem them coming, and you can't jump out of them early. Lastly, the maze levels in this game just plain suck to navigate. If there is any logic to how they work, I wasn't able to find it, and one wrong turn can mean starting from the very beginning.=====The story isn't very good, which is a big problem considering how story-driven this game is. It has its moments, and I liked some of the characters (especially the VAs) and their banter, but the actual plot could have used more work. Most of the game's story feels like "side quests"; self-contained stories. The "main quest" doesn't start until the last 1/3 of the game, and ends up relying a lot on exposition dumps and surprise twist villains.=====This game is quite long. I explored as much as I reasonably could, struggled with the bosses (Expert difficulty), read/heard dialogue and did a few (but not all) optional challenges; my playthrough was ~35 hours long, ~23 hours of it were pure gameplay (combat/exploration). In that time, I managed to explore ~90% Map and obtain ~50% Items===== TEVI has a lot of options for replayability, thanks to its post-game unlocksOnce you beat the game, you unlock Custom Game modes. Most notably is Free Roam mode. First, it auto-skips/removes all cutscenes. Secondly, it adds 2 hidden techs into the game which were present in this game's predecessor (Rabi-Ribi): Reverse Wall Jump and Wall Kick. Both techs are used to allow for sequence breaking. Finally, all previously story-gated items (Wall Jump, Air Dash, etc.) are moved to more accessible locations. The result is a return to Rabi-Ribi's non-linear metroidvania design. In addition to Free Roam, you also unlock Infernal difficulty + Turbo Mode (increased game speed) which makes the game considerably harder. There are also additional options, such as speedrun and randomizer mode, and some others I haven't yet managed to unlock.The only issue I have with the post-game options is that, for some reason, you cannot play Free Roam on Infernal difficulty until you beat Story Mode, AGAIN, in Infernal difficulty. I don't really see a point to this other than to force you to do an additional playthrough.=====Other things of note:- This game has crafting. There are like 8 different crafting items, but this game could have easily done fine with just 4. It is a straightforward once you understand it, but needlessly overcomplicated. I didn't feel the need to grind materials at any point, since the most important materials are obtained by exploration and are non-renewable.- The pacing in chapter 4 is pretty bad. Lots of dialogue and travel, and not many boss fights - There is a small difficulty spike once you reach Chapter 5.=====In conclusion: I do believe TEVI is worth the money, even at its base (not discounted) price, especially if you're someone who values memorable, tough bosses and have an inclination towards doing challenge runs. However, be aware that is a bit lackluster as a metroidvania (at least, for your first playthrough) and you must have some tolerance for dialogue (and if you can't, you can always skip cutscenes; there are plenty of map markers to guide you).

_childDocuments_.review: Depending on who you ask, this game is either better or much worse than Rabi-Ribi, it's spiritual predecessor.Personally, I played so much Rabi-Ribi that I will never touch the game again, so Tevi is a very welcome game for a few different playthroughs over the next couple of weeks.Tevis combat system is deep enough, so that not even the devs themselves were able to juggle the game's balance. At some point during development, they just said: "Screw it, let players break the game in half if they want."On my first playthrough I was way behind the curve, though. The bosses in the 2nd half got pretty challenging and I was not even playing on expert. The difficulty definitely depends on how much you are willing to backtrack. Sadly backtracking can feel a bit tedious because the map is huge this time around and there are no indicators on where items are before beating the game first.The first playthrough is very story driven and super linear. Only after you have beaten the game once, you unlock the freeroam mode which removes cutscenes and gives you a walljump from the getgo which allows for a really non-linear experience like in the best parts of Rabi-Ribi.Personally I really enjoy multiple playthroughs like in Tevi when they feel different enough. Also this is yet another fun achievement-collect-a-thon with some nice optional stuff to discover along the way. For players who just want to beat the game and move on it might be a bit too dry at times. Tevi is best in it's epic boss battles which sometimes are a bit too spread out for their own good. On the highest difficulty it's nice to catch a break after one of these fights though.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Alright! Just finished the game on hard mode and felt like I had to write a review. I'm a huge rabi-ribi fan so I was very excited for this and it really didn't disappoint, though it was quite different from what I was expecting. The combat system and sense of progression is very well done, you go from attacking three time and retreating to spending the entire fight attacking constantly, trying to get out the longest possible combos while navigating through the various lasers, bullets and blades. The sigil system is very well made though it can get a bit too cluttered near the end when you're searching for a specific one but you have nearly 200 of them in your inventory. It really does add an interesting layer of complexity to the game though. One thing that will probably be a bit divisive is how linear the game actually is. Every "important" item (stuff like double jump, bomb that can break specific wall etc) are all locked behind story progression. Basically, while you can explore around to find potions and sigils, you generally go to a location because of the story. This felt a bit too linear sometimes but it also made perfect sense since the story is front and center and the game as a whole is a lot more serious than rabi ribi. If I had to say, my favorite thing about the game is the soundtrack. There's some really amazing theme here and the diversity is through the roof! You can go the a very chopin inspired piece while exploring an underwater city to a banging synthwave theme while fighting through a corrupted forest. It's absolutely great. One thing to note is that the game is way easier than rabi ribi as well. I played on "hard" (not the hardest, and you can unlock another difficulty mode after finishing the game once) and I found it quite easy. I actually never died to any boss during my playthrough so I would recommend playing on the hardest available if you've already played rabi ribi. When you finish the game you aslo unlock additional modes, like speedrun mode and the ability to play the game in a way more "open" way. (haven't tried it yet). The only cons I have is that some enemies are annoying when traversing some areas and I absolutely dislike the "maze" levels, there's like two of them and I got stuck for like an hour on the second one ahah. All in all, I can't recommend this game enough, as well as rabi ribi if you havn't played that one already. Great from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every second playing this game. I'll admit, there are parts (namely: linear  metroidvania, and the ending) that are disappointing, but that didn't make it less fun.The combat and bosses are an absolute joy. If you're a "Yeah Rabi Ribi is trashy but the boss fights are actually really good" person, definitely get Tevi. It's a shame the exploration is on the weak side for a metroidvania but no metroidvania has bosses that are as fun to fight as Tevi. Not even Rabi Ribi.I see a lot of people saying the story is ♥♥♥♥, and while it's not the best story ever written and becomes even worse the more you think about it, I think it's pretty enjoyable if you just take it at face value as you're shown it. Though, your mileage may vary.The OST is incredible. The full screen anime CGs are gorgeous. The voice acting cast did a phenomenal job.This game's like a 9/10. The main selling point is the combat and bosses. If you're looking for the next Hollow Knight, this isn't it. If you're looking for the next Rabi Ribi, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: FAKE bun y girl literally TOO ANGRY to DIE: beats up GODS, DEMONS, and vergil instead.Aside from the story, it's an excellent game that improves on many things from it's predecessor: "the Rabi-Ribi incident".The combat system and movement are incredibly satisfying, and the devs have fixed many issues since it's initial release (such as those extremely cursed mazes).Give it a shot if you are new to the "Bullet Hell" genre, or just want a damn good feeling platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: Really liking what I'm seeing so far. If you're fan of JRPGs and/or metroidvanias, I think this will be right up your alley. You've got all the compulsory anime tropes, god-like music, satisfying progression and exploration and fun gameplay.And I really can't emphasise enough how much I love the music in TEVI. In fact, listening to the "Ulvosa" track while I was watching a streamer play this game is what made me actually buy it. Even if the rest of the game was lacking in some regard (which it isn't), I'm pretty sure I would have played through it anyway just to be able to hear all the tracks.EDIT: After finishing the game, all I have to add is that this is one of the best metroidvanias I've ever played. _childDocuments_.review: This game is good! I really enjoyed it. I will be comparing a lot in this review to Rabi-Ribi, this being their previous metroidvania game.The combat is absolutely incredible. Definitely the most fun i've had in a games combat in a really long while! A straight upgrade from rabi in every sense, really. Feels really good to come up with combos and experiment with them. Lots of variety!The movement feels really nice, although it can take a while to get all of the mobility items, it feels good to control around in here. This game is VERY massive oh my lord. Took me 36 hours to beat the game on expert with a 69% item completion and 88% on map. It can be a bit exhausting how big it is to explore for items, and i feel it will be harder to replay the game due to this, but this is personal preference more than anything. There is a lot of content you get to try (custom modes) after beating the game aswell! A DLC is likely to come later on aswell, with free content patches soon (featuring boss rush and more)Very subjective, but the game felt a lil bit too easy even on expert, no consumables and barely using core expansion. This is probably because i had a ton of hours in rabi ribi though. This does mean tho, this game is very friendly to non bullet hell players, is pretty welcoming.Now this is more due to my expectations of the game; but i was dissapointed that the game is quite linear. Every movement item is behind story progress. Coming from rabi i did expect to see non linearity but its not really here. At least though, the exploration is improved by the fact that every mob doesn't die in 1 hit anymore and you actually have to fight back in this case, however, after clearing the game: Also, ♥♥♥♥ misty maze. The story is kind of a mess. It's okay/decent, but towards the end of it is so rushed and theres so many unresolved things it really threw me off and ruined it for me, they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up really real bad, but i won't downplay the entire game because of it, it is still excellent gameplay wise. Some real weird twists too. The dialog can be fun, (although some can be. Weird.) but i really feel i would've just skipped the dialogs completely if it weren't for the VAs. They really did breathe life into the characters and that's great! But still, the story as it stands is quite the mess, but it's not rabi-ribi tier virtually 0 story tier, its pretty decent compared to it. It exists, i guess. It sucks that the game was made more plot focused and took away linearity for story, but towards the end it feels really rushed, even some of the sections non story, unfortunately. Hoping for future patches that fix this!For me this is a 8.5/10, due to some personal gripes with how linear the game felt (and this being due to it focusing in the wacky story!) mainly as my negatives, but the combat and movement feel insanely good and are top notch. Good game, i would say worth the wait.
