_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay feels a lot better compared to Rabi-Ribi, Ground Combo IV Alt gives me a rush of dopamine everytime the game freezes for a moment like Im doing something very right wwww The addition of Japanese voice acting is also really REALLY awesome.That being said, my main grime is the flow of the story, there are characters whose only purpose is to appear on a random scene  that feels really out of place (ex : The waffle robot guy at the start). The humor is also REALLY weird, like when Tevi checks on the body of a magitech and Celia covers Saber's eyes because they thought she was doing something "Lewd" while appearing serious and all. Like what the hell did they thought was Tevi gonna do, pull a fast one on a humanoid robot????Theres also the weird fanservice of "Erina" and "Ribbon" appearing on the Casino place with an entire Rabi-Ribi minigame. While it's a very surprising and welcome addition, I feel like new players experiencing that specific quest would just be confused as to why they're playing a simplified metroidvania inside a CasinoLast but not least. I dislike how the dialogues claimed certain towns have certain delicacies only for us not being able to buy them because they only exists in-lore (Why cant I buy alcohol beverages for my Tevi adventures :( )I have more grimes with Tevi but I wont bore you, dear reader, with reading my little nitpicks of the gameIm sure Tevi was made with the intention of surpassing Rabi-Ribi in terms of gameplay and oh man did they do a really good job at that. But despite peak gameplay, its other aspects seems to be a letdownStill would recommend, 9/10 gameplay, 5/10 story, 11/10 voice acting, 0 bunny girl
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is excellent. If you want challenging bosses, its fantastic. If you enjoy games like Cuphead, endgame bosses from Hollow Knight, bosses from IWBTG fangames, bosses from Touhou, etc, this game is perfect. The patterns are all fair, meaning you can go for stuff like hitless runs without using bullet clearing or invincibility tools, if you need the extra level of challenge. There are many sigils and builds you can create in the game to tailor to individual bosses, lots of different playstyles possible depending on the sigils you use.The game is pretty linear, with a more nonlinear mode being unlocked after you first beat the game. As such,  if exploration is very important to you, I would recommend you get a completed save file beforehand to enable free roam mode from the start. Personally, I played Rabi Ribi / TEVI for the boss fights, so this didn't matter to me.The story exists. I would say there are too many characters/plotlines for how long the game/story was, meaning things feel a little rushed or incomplete, and you don't develop much emotional attachment to many of the characters. DIO has voice lines though so its worth listening to.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun metroidvania. Took about 23 hours to clear the game on Hard Mode.I liked the dialogue art. Not sure about the complaints there. It's not ground breaking, but it certainly isn't ugly. The sprite art is beautiful. Story was pretty interesting after chapter 2 but I am easily entertained, so your mileage may vary.Hard mode felt difficult for the first three chapters and then I quickly felt like I out-scaled bosses and was given plenty of tools/utilities to deal with the bullet hell portion of the game. When my thumb recovers from holding a death grip on the D pad, I want to give Expert a shot. All in all, would recommend.. but maybe on sale if you have a large backlog of games.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: After mastered the art of 300++ ep, it's safe to say i gonna juggle the boss to the death again.On average difficulty, compared to Rabi ribi, the game actually much more easier. Most of the time you can unga bunga your way with the bosses as you have so many options to survive their barrage of attacks. But the game has a fun combat nonetheless.The exploration and map (or the world in a sense) side is kinda mixed feeling tho, the concept and art design is quite good. But the level design is rather not so exciting, and annoying sometime.The music is there, but I think none of them as memorable as in Rabi ribi.For character art, at first i'm kinda confused as why it's so different from previous games. But after finishing the game, now i think it's suite well to the story and world building.And for the story, it's just ok. I like the idea, it's good. But i think it's need a little bit of work to deliver well.Overall it's a solid and very fun game. It has its own charm and feel separate from Rabi ribi (as so many people, including myself compare them so much) but in an ok way.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: It completely surpassed my expectations, having played Rabi Ribi before, this just feels like an improvement in every single way, from combat feeling smoother since the beginning to cooler and so far less cheesy game mechanics, I love most of the changes to the combat since it feels more responsive, and having to charge up your burst to use it in battle makes it more challenging and satisfying when you manage to dodge an attack, although it always feels nicer to not use it at all (I die a lot). Nice environment and nice characters, the main cast has really cool synergy and I can't wait to see more of them.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, the devs have shown that they have a clear understanding of the fundamentals and specifics of the metroidvania genre, producing their second game that is among the best in the field. Compared to Rabi-Ribi, however, this game appears far more linear primarily due to the much higher emphasis on the story. Returning upgrades are once again fun to obtain and use, while the new ones are mostly passives that're nice to have. A few of the returning upgrades though do have tweaks that improve the combat, namely the dash, which comes innately as an attack but also provides 2 other attacking moves that can spice up your already diverse moveset. Even the ranged attacks have their own niches and use cases, and even against the same boss there's many reasons to switch up your orbital  at any point.The sigil system is good, although it's not something I'm particularly fond of. There's just so many of them and a lot of them are quite specific. I can appreciate that this encourages everybody to play with a different playstyle, and the abundance allows for each of them to receive buffs, even though I may prefer fewer more simple 'badges'.Not too big a fan of the story, I especially think it overstays its welcome near the end
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: From the makers of Rabi-Ribi comes another Metroidvania Tevi. Tevi shares many similarities with Rabi, like its fast-paced bullet-hell combat, intricate and varied maps, and endearing characters. You can customize your fighting style, up to a point, by adding sigils that can change your moves, add attacks to combos, or just straight-up transform that attack.I loved Rabi-Ribi, and I love this game almost as much. My main gripe is the story. It's an absolute mess. Things get thrown around in the late game, around chapter 6, with no foreshadowing. New plot-relevant characters show up out of nowhere near the end. Several times, Tevi shows you flashbacks to other characters lives, memories you couldn't have known about, so you could follow their motivations. A method that I think is very forced.If you're craving more Metroidvania with awesome combat and beautiful art design, then I highly recommend Tevi. Just turn off your brain when it comes to its senseless storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: If you like metroidvania games with some bullet hell this is the game. Combat feels very smooth as well as overall movement, very nice fluidity allowing for cool executions/combos.Pick your difficulty and gogogo (can skip through dialogues/cutscenes if that's not for you), ngl I thought the game was a bit heavy on the exposition but the great voice acting/cast make up for it. (The exposition does not get lighter but the V/A is enjoyable)As of now I encountered some minor dialogue text issues and some annoying gameplay bugs with some features of this game.Overall I'd still recommend this game but IMO probably best to pick this game up on the next sale when some of these bugs have been flushed out.EDITAfter beating the game, w/o getting too spoilerly, there is a lack of closure for most of the characters you come across, going through the game the 2nd time I'm wondering what the heck happened to these characters. I thought I'd encounter them again for a fight or finish their story but there isn't anything.There are some things missing for closure and I feel like this game was rushed out. The excellent controls, combat, music, V/A make this a game with a lot of hard work and care. I do hope for some DLC to add more content and closure ^^
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy most aspects of the game. The combat is super sharp.  The story and characters are a huge step up from Rabi-Ribi.  It looks and sounds amazing.  There is definitely a sacrifice made on the exploration side of things, though.  It's a much more linear game than Rabi was, probably to make room for the story they wanted to tell.  That's not strictly a bad thing, but it is a very different thing, and I wonder about the replay value in the end as a result.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Well, finished the Tevi storyline. Difficulty "hard", completion time is 37 hours as I explored the world and collected items. As a fan of Bullet hell platformers (of which there aren't many) this game goes into my box of awesome unique projects, although there are some cons.Pros:-Combat and combo system;-Great controls;-There are some different combat builds;-Art;-Music;-The orbitars system;-Craft;-Interesting characters and plot (although there are some frustrating moments);-Interesting world;-Erina and Ribbon.Unfortunately, there are a number of unpleasant points that come up, mostly if you've played Rabi-Ribi:-While the world is interesting, unlike Rabi-Ribi the integrity of the world doesn't feel right. In Rabi-Ribi, I was always drawn to the image of the island, and you knew you could get to any part of that island. In Tevi it feels like some locations have been piled on top of each other;-Most of the world is closed until you get to a certain chapter (thus weakening the metroidvania component a lot), on the other hand a special mode opens up for this after the game is over;-No possibility to win some battles in the second half of the game. I realize that this is limited by the story, but still, it seems that Tevi is so weak, although some bosses are very weak even on "hard" difficulty;-Broken difficulty balance. On Hard difficulty the second half of the game is very easy, even didn't get the "Bunny don't have 9 lives" achievement. Compared to Rabi Ribi, "hard" feels like "easy" or lower;-The game has a reduced Metroidvania and Bullet hell component compared to Rabi-Ribi.As a standalone project, the game is great, but unfortunately (or rather, conversely, fortunately) Rabi-Ribi exists, so I have to compare. But again, the game is worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't want to spend more cash on Steam after the last sale, but, damn, Tevi looked so good. I've downloaded the demo in hopes of disappointing myself: the bunny girl game couldn't be that great, right? Ain't metroidvanias a dime a dozen these days, after all? Couldn't I play any other one, and buy Tevi only when it gets cheap? Thing is, the game blowed my expectations away. The game is fire. The demo was really different. They made a side adventure with accelerated progression and samples of lots of different environments. It was enough to show me that Tevi has really smart progression systems, an interesting take in metroidvania map exploration, and combat so fire it melts rocks. Really, Tevi has combos for days. Bunny Girl hits like Dante, and I wasn't expecting that on a metroidvania game. Now I started the full game and I'm just flabbergasted again. The game is very anime, very horny. The first scene is kind of weird because of this: Tevi is presented to us bonded by ropes and a padlock, captured by a huge bandit. The game makes it look like something bad will happen... But then the dude goes away and you learn that Tevi ain't no damsel in distress. I would rather like that she didn't start the game captured in the first place - they did it for the perverts and for this twist (Tevi isn't the one that is scared, she is the one who knocks). Not the best taste, IMO. But I can't hold a grudge with Tevi for too long. She is a spunky, confident, cute, silly, heroic manic pixie bunny girl. She is a genius engineer. Her text and expressions are gold. And the game is such a good game, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. They nailed using the metroidvania engine to create a "escape the base" kind of experience. For a while, Tevi feels like she is Solid Snake, crossing vents and backstabbing unassuming grunts. You'll get new combos and actions in a lightning pace. The bandit base scenario quickly gives way to a sewer based one, with a whole lot of new enemies and mechanics. You fight a boss. You get two new companions: an arrogant angel with big breasts, who Tevi tolerates, and an androgynous male demon twink, naive and clumsy, who Tevi likes. Their first interaction is, again, very horny and fan-servicey. But it also establishes tropey relationships between all these characters. It is kind of fun to see Tevi talking with them. Every one of them has a lot of portraits and expressions. And the game also adds a bit of intrigue, as the angel seems like she has some ulterior motives for joining Tevi.They're rapidly incorporated into the mechanics, becoming two spheres that follow Tevi around, powering her ranged attacks with red or blue energy. Tevi says she cooks desserts as a hobby, and the game introduces you to crafting healing items. You can craft them from the menu, in a basically frictionless way. The game tells you that it will increase the drop rate of suplies if you're running low on them, so you have this incentive to always be crafting. This is good because now every enemy feels like a slot machine when you kill them, as they can drop stuff you want. Upgrades are very tied to the exploration part. Big Money, an upgrade's worth of cash, is found in nooks and cranies of the world. Badges can also be found in the world. You have a limit of "badge points" you can fill by equipping them, and they give interesting passive skills. Lots of these bonuses are conditional and can inform you on new ways to play Tevi's moveset optimally. tl;dr This game seems very good. It may have its fair share of fails, but it seems VERY special. I recommend the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, I played Rabi Ribi almost to the end so I'm accustomed to the mechanics. But I did have the same problem of Rabi Ribi (being stuck in a boss fight without proper items) that is a real ball breaker. It also happens in like the first 2 hours.I'm playing in expert, if it has any significance (inb4 git gud, I know).
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: It's great. One of the best metroidvanias out there.Keeps all the good aspects of Rabi-Ribi (exploration, bullet-hell boss fights) and then expands on the ideas that weren't necessarily developted in the previous game. The melee combat is greatly enhanced by the spectacle fighter aspects. The regular enemies are more interesting this time around. The sigils (aka badges, charms) have interesting effects, often adding more moves or maybe introducing some kind of drawback, and there's a lot of them. There's a lot of polish in things such as tutorials, readability, UI, implementation of QoL. I don't think I've had a single annoyance so far.The pixel art is really good as well. Detailed, readable and varied.The writing, story and the non-pixel art are the biggest surprice, afaik all handled by Ein Lee who proves to be a great boon to the team. The character designs are interesting and emotive, all the characters have clear personality and the quality of dialogues isn't half-bad. It certainly delivers more than expected of a typical action game or metroidvania, and is a huge step up from Rabi-Ribi.The music and sound design are good, as expected of CreSpirit. The soundtrack has a lot of variety. Sound effects fit the experience. Full voice acting is crazy for an indie metroidvania, and it absolutely gave the characters much more personality, and also was pleasant to listen to during combat.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Great customization, well written story. Charming anime style character design.Tevi is one of THE COOLEST PROTAGS OF ALL TIME.Feels amazing on steam deck. good metroidvania fun Combat feels goodSometimes not clear where you need to go to progress the storyThey look like they almost want to let you sequence break, but then they make sure to quickly spoil your fun. Fair enough, that does complicate development for a story rich game.Speaking of story rich HOLY COW THE LORE.Amazing. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun metroidvania game with cool bullet hell bosses. The map exploration has lots of freedom and hidden stuffs. The story is fully voiced with top-rated Japanese VAs. The BGMs are also pretty good. Playstyle customization is also huge with lots of sigils to fit your style of fighting. Overall a very solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: TEVI is an anime-styled metroidvania with a bunny/steampunk theme. You can see the game being compared to Rabi-Ribi, the studio's previous game. Superficially they look the same, but TEVI is not Rabi-Ribi Part 2. TEVI is more story-focused and the theme is more dark/serious, although there are still many funny/silly characters. Rabi-Ribi was all about bunny cuteness nonsense. Boss battles are less bullet hell-y. TEVI is also more linear, because of the story focus. Intro is very linear. After that you get a few branching routes. I think it's ok for metroidvania to be linear (Metroid games are very linear), it's just something to be aware of. There's more dialog compared to Rabi-Ribi, but it's all skippable, so it doesn't bother me. The dialog is still less than average JRPG.I've been playing in Normal, and the challenge is just fine, not too hard and not too easy. There's multiple more difficulty options. You also always have the natural option for backtracking, collecting items and crafting materials, if you get stuck in a boss fight.Soundtrack is still good, but there are some weaker songs. The world has many different areas with significantly different themes and monsters. There's tons of "sigils", upgrades that provide smaller or bigger benefits. You can have a certain number of sigils active at any given time.Good:+ Looks good+ Good soundtrack overall+ Voice acting+ Stable, no crashes+ You can pet bunnyBad:- TEVI is a fake bunny??- Sometimes a bit too long distance without save points- Some songs not so good
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing: Bunny, bunny. After playing: Fake bunny.I emphasize the option to consistently visualize the hitbox. The combat is aesthetically beautiful and feels smooth. Unlike Rabi Ribi, Tevi has an interesting story. The voice acting is a significant plus, giving a lot of personality and charisma, especially to Celia. I love her dialogues.It's a good game."
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Rabi-Ribi, this is a no-brainer. There's more lore compared to Rabi-Ribi, it's all 'optional' though. The small problems Rabi-Ribi had (locked into a boss fight with no going back) have been dealt with. The game takes itself more seriously while still keeping that zaniness.A fantastic 2D Platformer with Metroidvania and Bullet-hell elements that's worth the long wait.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Bnu-vania, Pretty fun map, bit strict during the story mode but "Free Roam" mode is kinda countering that complaint quite a bit. Great soundtrack and one of the more actually fun crafting systems in a game by far just over the fact you can craft anywhere by hand.Combat is very much just fun to.Though the ice maze can melt in hell.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Only a few hours in so I may update the review after more gameplay, but my first impression is that the game is absolutely phenomenal. The movement and combat feel very fluid from the beginning of the game, which is not something that I have found to be true in most metroidvanias. Additionally, the game has several difficulty options. So far, I have been playing on the hardest difficulty not locked to NG+ and it feels similar in difficulty to hollow knight. Also, keyboard and mouse compatibility is surprisingly good with fully rebind-able controls, and I have not felt pushed towards using a controller, which is a nice change from some other games in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played much, obviously, but it does feel like a solid sequel to Rabi-Ribi, which is one of the better metroidvania's with a bullet-hell spin. Just from the initial opening, it seems like all of the mechanics have been built out significantly and it's still revealing its depth as I've started playing it, which is a good sign.I really only play these types of games for the gameplay and don't really enjoy stories like this, but the story is not annoying or overbearing for players like me either.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: im not gonna sugarcoat it even though I have only an hour on this game but around probably 17 or 18 hours on the play test with a lot of it fighting one of the bosses, and i might edit it later to look backbutit truly seems to be a successor to rabi ribi with how smooth the gameplay feels and seemingly how much budget and effort was put into this gamea ton of JP VAs (even if some people consider it a quality they dont want) and around 15-26 hours (probably more if you suck at the harder difficulties or replay on harder difficulties) of gameplaynot to mention the 78 tracks including licensed that are hereAdding to this :I think the game barely suffers from how expansive the combat system works and also the amount of items you are given (at compared to rabi ribi if you played it first) because it gives you so much more tools to deal with bosses, leading to the difficulty being not the worst thing in the world.(Then again it might have to do with finding every potion in the world I dunno)I do not think its that much of an issue, as the combat feels amazing, as it feels impactful and stylish.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

_childDocuments_.review: Update after beating the game: I am very impressed, honestly the story got pretty good with some dark undertones. I'd say the story was definitely a lot stronger than Rabi-Ribi's. The entire game has been a blast to play and I will definitely be 100 percenting it eventually. Serious one of the best Metroidvania's out there. If you haven't go play it NOW!I played the demo of this back a couple months ago. I really enjoyed that. I had been so excited for the full game of this to release, and I can confidently say I am not disappointed! From the creators of Rabi-Ribi which I believe to be one of if not the best games in the Metroidvania genre comes TEVI! This game took everything Rabi-Ribi had only only made it better. The gameplay is super fun with in depth combat and combos,. And one of my favorite aspects of their games: the soundtrack. All the music is absolutely amazing. Going off of the gameplay I experienced in the demo, this game is going to far exceed Rabi-Ribi. The characters are even fully voiced in Japanese which was a nice little surprise to see as I avoided any trailers.Overall, if you loved Rabi-Ribi this game only goes up from there. This is definitely going to take Rabi-Ribi's spot for best game in the Metroidvania genre. And don't the let the cute art style fool you, this game is quite the challenge with satisfying combat and reqarding exploration. I can't wait to binge this for the next couple weeks.
_childDocuments_.name: TEVI

Step into the pixelated world of TEVI, an action-packed 2D adventure that seamlessly blends Metroidvania, bullet hell, and spectacle fighter elements.

Traverse a vast interconnected world marked by strife and uncover hidden secrets. Encounter a diverse cast of allies and enemies featuring angels, demons, and cute animal ears. Upgrade gear and collect new ones to enhance your abilities. Customize your build to suit how you want to play. Slash, dash, shoot, and execute flashy combos to vanquish bosses in epic showdowns.

name: Magical Delicacy
detailed_description: Magical Delicacy is a combat-free Metroidvania-lite with a complex cooking system. Set foot in Grat and get lost while platforming through this twisted town - find and explore open pathways or fulfill the complex orders of the townsfolk to progress and unlock new kitchen tools. Platforming and exploration lie at the heart of Magical Delicacy and are required to collect ingredients and progress within the game. Toggle the Easy Platforming mode in the settings if you want a more comfortable platforming experience or have trouble with challenging passages. Play the young witch Flora and discover a bustling town in this Metroidvania-inspired wholesome cooking game. Cook meals and potions in your customized kitchen by carefully selecting the right ingredients. Navigate the town in casual platforming to meet the townsfolk, take up their orders, and learn about this world of magic. Flora travels to a distant town to fulfill her dream of becoming a proper witch. She opens up shop in Grat, a harbor town built upon cliffs, where adventurers settled to chart an unexplored island full of mystery. As she engages in the town’s thriving economy, she stumbles upon two members of opposing covens. The witch Cassia and the magus Tauno have a lot to teach Flora, but they also know how to use her in their dispute about magical beings. EXPLORATION Visit a beautiful harbor town, a densely packed space with people to meet, history to discover, and many opportunities to improve your business. Shop at merchants to buy various keepsakes and upgrades. Accept dozens of orders from the townsfolk asking for your magical food. Meet mysterious travelers, shop owners, forgotten legends, and masters of their crafts, some of which might only appear during day or night. Unravel long-forgotten secrets of the island and its mystical creatures. RESOURCE MANAGEMENT Cooking delicious meals for your customers requires the correct ingredients. Gather ingredients directly within the nooks and crannies of the town, while some other ingredients can only be bought from merchants . Run out of an ingredient while cooking? Don’t worry - merchants will restock their shops, and forgeable ingredients eventually grow back with a little patience. Upgrade your kitchen to stash a collection of ingredients ready for cooking and experimentation or sell them to merchants for Beads, your precious currency for trading. COOKING Use your acquired ingredients to create magical dishes. Different attributes require you to think about your ingredient selection. Figure out and learn how flavors mix and how to meet customers‘ odd and complex requests for food. Closely follow recipes or experiment with your own creations , then sell or deliver your potions, meals, teas, and pastries to friends and customers. Be it local cuisine or Flora’s hometown recipes, everything to satisfy the tastebuds of different folks, from the croaking Gaball to the feline Tilin. KITCHEN Start with basic equipment and acquire new kitchen tools . Unlock more rooms to arrange and customize your tools to your liking and maximize efficiency when cooking. Put your unused creations up for sale, sort your ingredients into storage, and grow some plants in the backyard. It would be the perfect place to call your own if it wasn’t for this unwanted roommate and a lingering capitalist dread. PLATFORMING Navigate the town during your deliveries, climb bell towers and old ramparts, or delve through challenging old catacombs. Grow as a witch and acquire upgrades to your movement abilities to discover new routes and hard-to-reach places or open shortcuts that lead back to your store. Uncover and learn the twisted pathways on the map and remember the whereabouts of the townsfolk. Inspired by the Metroidvania genre and condensed into a cozy cooking game. Features Enchanting pixel art style depicting a fantastical world of witches and magic. Befriend a cast of diverse characters that love to order food from you. Traverse a 2D platformer inspired by Metroidvanias. Gain new abilities, reach new areas, and unlock shortcuts. Learn an extensive cooking system , allowing for creative choices to fulfill even oddly specific orders. Collect ingredients and new recipes through trade, questing, and exploration. Intertwined progression requiring map exploration and delivering orders. Linear story with optional encounters and opportunities for open-ended play. Plenty of accessibility features to help you experience the game on your own terms, including an Easy Platforming mode that disables various challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a middle of the road or neutral review, I would. I love the concept, and the work put into the art is gorgeous. But does it feel good as a game? Not really.This game is first a metroidvania, and second a cooking/baking game by a far margin. It's very vague on how to continue the main storyline, and at one point unless you're jumping around in the right spots, you might get stuck.The platforming is also a bit finicky, and doesn't feel good — which is a huge problem for a metroidvania game. Sometimes I simply can't jump onto a platform for some reason, even though my character visibly should have reached it.Moving around the maps to the various stores and resource locations to gather ingredients you need is also a pain until you've unlocked BOTH forms of fast travel, wherein the second form is somewhat later into the game, making the game entirely tedious when it comes to actually managing your shop. Once you unlock all your movement skills, it becomes less of an issue, but that still takes a while. I understand that metroidvania progression is correlated to unlocking more areas via obtaining items/skills/etc, but just for my regular baking? It's extremely tedious.Even for baking and cooking, the quests ramp up in difficulty too quickly, and making money by selling your goods is very tedious since the pace at which your items sell is very slow. You can't leave the store when you're selling either, which means I just leave the game open until the game progresses to night time. Another small thing, you can't nap during the day to skip to night time, so if I need to brew potions to progress the plot, I can't and have to literally wait again.I understand the baking/cooking is intended to be the cozy part of the game, but when it's combined with metroidvania styled map exploration that requires precise platforming at points, it doesn't mesh well. For this reason, I would not really recommend buying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, but I would change some things.1) You can only open the map in plain static surfaces. _childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful and delightful game!I fully recommend Magical Delicacy if you like collecting ingredients, exploring a beautiful town and its surrounding nature, talking to charming characters, cooking while not 100% sticking to recipes, and if you are a fan of Kiki's Delivery Service.The young witch Flora arrives in the coastal town of Grat to start her business of cooking and delivering food. Soon Flora meets other residents of Grat: among the artisans, royalty, Ryverfarers, merchants and townsfolk are two rivaling witch covens that rope Flora into their dispute over a mysterious egg...By cooking for the diverse inhabitants of Grat you will gradually earn their trust and friendship. If you get stuck on a recipe, explore the town and surrounding nature to find ingredients, secrets, and people to talk to. Advance the plot and explore new areas to gain more abilities for traversal, cooking and magic. Some ingredients can be planted in Flora's garden. A wide array of cooking stations can be placed in her store but have to be earned first.The platforming is not too challenging, even I made it through the entire game without getting stuck. There are some optional parcours that are tougher but reward you upon completion. It's worth exploring Grat by night as well as by day as some things are different.Cooking in Magical Delicacy is a puzzle - your customers have specific requirements that need to be fulfilled. This often necessitates experimentation with the recipes you have until you find the right combination of ingedients. There is a wide array of ingredients, each with their own set of properties. Often there is more than one "solution", and you can gain abilities that make it easier for you to foresee the outcome of a recipe.You might get frustrated if you are someone who gets overwhelmed if you cannot deliver every order right away, though for me it was a challenge I came back to every once in a while until I found a solution. Sometimes you will have to advance the game before you can cook something specific.The game is much larger than you'd think, with metroidvania-like exploration that opens paths for you as you gain abilities and knowledge. My first playthrough was 40 hours, so you can get a LOT of playtime out of the game. You are also free to take as much time as you like, aside from some cooking stations nothing is time sensitive. Even after completing the main story you will be able to explore the town, talk to its residents, cook and hunt for Steam achievements.The pixel art is absolutely beautiful and detailed and accompanied by beautiful music. You can even pet some animals! The characters are charming, interesting, and beautifully designed. You will learn a little bit about the magic and history of Grat, but not to a tedious amount.I had a really great time playing, even though I usually don't play platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Magical Delicacy

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be very confusing at first. It doesn't hold your hand and the map is quite maze-like so it's pretty easy to get lost and stuck without a clue on what to do next, but once you get past that initial frustration, it turns into a lovely and cozy cooking-platforming game where you get to open your own store, explore beautiful places, hunt for ingredients, cook a ton of different dishes, discover secrets and meet the townsfolk in order to fulfill their requests. I was very hesitant to continue at first due to being lost and having no idea how to proceed, but I decided to stick with it and the more I progressed, the more rewarding and fun it got. The art and music are also beautiful and add a huge plus to the entire experience. Highly recommend sticking with it and not giving up right away, the full game is very much worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game cause I love crafting/cooking games and from the videos it seems just that but it's mainly a platformer complete with disappearing/crumbling and moving platforms. Don't let the cooking preview fool you. You need ingredients? Go platform to find ingredients or buy them from shops(which you have to platform to btw). It doesn't help that the map is essentially a maze so for a good chunk of the start of the game you're fumbling around trying to figure out which way is the right way and where the hell are you going. There's doors where I don't know if it's because i need a key or something or do I just need to somehow find a way around it to open it on the other side. I wish that the platforming part was more rewarding since that's mainly what you're going to be doing but per area you may get lucky to get like 3-4 different ingredients, IF YOU'RE LUCKY.  Cause the ingredients have spawn times so if you've already harvested it, you gotta wait for it to spawn or choose to plant it in your garden to wait for it grow. So if you're lost and you've already harvested everything in your way, you're just platforming for no reason. It's frustrating. Several times I've just sighed and went I just want to cook, I want to get out of this maze but nope every time I need ingredients and I don't have the money cause I had to upgrade my kitchen/equipment I'm just aimlessly jumping around hoping I find an ingredient and eventually getting lost cause I've never been to this area of the map. Experimenting with recipes is frustrating too cause if you cook something with ingredients that don't work together, it fails. Which means you just wasted ingredients you spent so long trying to find or buy with your money. I also don't understand why harvesting an ingredient needs to be a mini game? If you find an ingredient in the wild, like a mushroom or carrot you have to do a mini game which is just press button when it's in the green zone to harvest. If you don't time if right, you don't get the ingredient so try again. It's not difficult but why? It's unnecessary and you need to do that every time to harvest something. You can turn it off with accessibility but why is it there in the first place? I can't wrap my head around it.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 StarsMagical Delicacy is a wonderfully crafted game with one of the best OSTs that I've listened to in a long time, beautiful artwork and deep character stories.However, it is also one thing: not for everybody.At it's core, it's a metrovania. You have a map and NPCs that are all over the place, secret passageways, a lot of upgrades that you need to find to get to new places, and you'll need a lot of backtracking.I got lost in my first ten hours more than I can count. If you're someone who is capable of organising your map, great. If not, you'll end up running around searching for that one specific ingridient for a long time.Your inventory is limited (you can upgrade it later), and, most importantly, you're not getting spoon feed what you have to do. This game is not hard, there's no life bar (I love this game for this feature alone!!!), but you need to actually think.You need to read the dialog, and sometimes even the item descriptions to know what to do (hint: marmelade), and common sense. I actually enjoyed cooking, and making new receipes. Don't get too attached to ingredients, you can find or buy them again. Have some fun ;) It took me ages until I figured out how receipes work, how to create new things, how to combine stuff... The first ten hours were a learning experience, but then it made 'click', and even thought there were times when I didn't know what to do, I just roamed around, collected ingridients, and spoke to people. I love their stories, this place feels alive. Hints that I'll give, because figuring them out was tedious:- You can craft stuff without receipes, they are a "guide", not your rules. - Seasoning is your friend for flavors, even multiple to achieve your goal.- Talk to NPCs regularly for new quests- If you have the keepssake to let you know that there's something hidden, don't ignore it, try everything to find it. (Don't forget that you can skip through certain floors)- You can switch keepssakes in your home- Gardening is your friend for ingridients you need on a regular basis/are hard to get- arrange your home so that it makes sense- buy the extra storage asap + the machines - don't hoard money, buy the things you need!- take a breath, sit down and listen to the music ;) Why only 4 out of 5 stars?- I felt like the stories of certain characters where left hanging in the middle. I wanted more- I wanted an ending-ending. I feel like the game should have reseted you to the last place you where before the last event takes place, so that the last ending feels like one.- Some characters could give you more hints, especially when you need to find something...- Sometimes the magical powers wouldn't activate if you'd just fast traveled somewhere, and there was at least one bug (couldn't pick up the chest of a character). The other bugs could easily be fixed by leaving the place and then returning, but there were hardly any.- You got to love management games, because you'll need to be on top of your ingredient game!All in all: I couldn't stop playing, and I loved my time there. The characters, the stories, the music made me want to keep playing.It was a great experience, there is the potetional for more, and I want to learn about the fates of all the characters.Please give me a DLC or a part two.Don't get discouraged if you're stuck: take breath, sit somewhere, and then travel to all the places. You'll find your answer. Take your time, at it's core that's what the game is all about. Just... Experience, and you'll love the game.If you want clear instructions, a top-notch management, a non-metrovenia play style... Play something else.If you want the unknown, brain power, a bit of the chaos that is daily life, and a lot of "figure it out, you can do it", this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game. It took quite a while before it clicked but when it did, I fell in love. It has no missable achievements and takes 25h+ to complete.  25h+ 2/10 1 There are many guides online and posts on different achievement websites, but not one guide that combines it all. I used  to know where to find specific items.  No No No No No No No No NoIn Magical Delicacy, you just arrive at a new location where you hope to find more witches, like yourself.  To learn from them the skills it takes to be a witch. However you are greeted by someone who will show you your new house, but then tell you you owe the city a bunch of money for that specific house. Does this sound like the plot of a farming sim? Well it isn't that, it is a Metroidvania without fighting or dying, but gathering and buying lots of ingredients to make dishes for the people around you. It took me quite a few hours to fall in love with the game. The beginning was so nice, the movement felt good, the platforming was fun, the world looked amazing and a bunch of nice characters to meet. However, after the first tutorial part, I felt lost. The game mechanics didn't click for me for hours and it took for me to follow a guide for 1/3 of the game to understand it and start to enjoy it without a recipe guide. So which tips do I have for others? - First is to know that it is normal you'll have to buy many many ingredients. Some are just not out there in the wilds and you are expected to buy them. For me as a cheapskate in games who mostly doesn't use any potions in games because I'm afraid I need them for late in the game... this bit me in the *ss... You're supposed to spend money in Magical Delicacy, not just for upgrades but also ingredients. - The second thing is that you will earn enough feathers to buy the recipes. I was afraid to buy the wrong one which I didn't need for quests and others that I needed but then didn't have the feathers anymore. I'm not sure if you can encounter this problem, but likely not as you'll have a bunch of quests all at once all the time. - The third thing that helped me is learning that the story-related quests show a ! in the top right corner. I have no idea why it took me hours to even notice this. - And last but not least. Tauno, a character that will teach you a second spell sells an item that is called "Notes on Flavor".  This is a lifesaver and helped me to finally let go of the recipe guides, as this one will show you the taste of the end result before making it. Don't forget to equip it! So with all those tips out of the way, what do I like about Magical Delicacy? Almost everything after that initial phase! - The artwork is beautiful and has so many details. Like candles that go out if you run past them. - So many characters and their background stories.- It has such an interesting main story that takes a bit of time to develop but gets so interesting that I wanted to see the ending! However, what I enjoyed most of all is the movement set you get. In typical Metroidvania style, you'll unlock a bunch of new movements that help you reach new areas of the map. It also came with a bunch of teleport options which made traveling around so much easier. I really enjoyed the second and third movement set you'll unlock! What is also lovely is that the game comes with settings to remove the gathering/cooking timed minigame in case you don't enjoy this or have trouble with it. Achievement-wise the game is so nice. A lot of the achievements unlock with story progression, or for buying all the cooking equipment. There are a bunch of achievements for collecting/using everything. I do recommend copying one of the lists of plantable ingredients and one of all ingredients and deleting those you have planted/used, because that achievement might take a while in the end while you can do already most of it while playing through the game. I give Magical Delicacy 4 out of 5 stars. If you're struggling at the beginning, just like me. Please check out my tips above or maybe use a recipe guide in the beginning, just to get the hang of things. It will click at some point, and it is such a lovely game.

_childDocuments_.review: A yes and no for recommendation.TLDR; After 26 hours of playing I would not consider this to be a cozy game which the game promotes itself to be. I would prefer my cozy game to not make me annoyed and frustrated on so many occasions. This game is firstly a platformer/metroidvania then a cooking simulator. Simply put, I would not recommend this game to players who are looking for a cozy game to play but if you do enjoy metroidvania style games with a twist this could be a good pickup for you.Let’s start with the good, the art and music for the game is really charming and relaxing. The main storyline is alright with a simple goal and straight forward plot. It took me about 20 hours to finish the main storyline. The game does get much easier once you have unlocked all the powerups which makes doing the quests much more easier. Now that I’m finishing up the side quests and achievement hunting, the game is much more chill although still a little confusing to try and guess what combination and what method to use to make the requested food. This is when the cozy aspect of the game shines when everything is easier to get to. I really appreciate the option to make platforming easier, I had the option turned on since I didn’t want to mald more than I already was just trying to get to an ingredient.With all that being said, I didn’t like how tedious the process is to get/find the ingredients throughout the map. Early game is when you’d be frustrated the most when even the most basic map functions have to be bought from the cartographer. The map design itself was very confusing early on. Inventory was a disaster as you couldn’t even dispose what you had in your bag unless you bought more storage or a composter for your store, you cannot drop/trash your items. Some extra skills have to be equipped manually with limited slots so you had to pick and choose which you think is necessary (map upgrades, cooking upgrades are here) and this can only be done while you are in the store. I personally do not mind the selling food function (you can only sell food while you are in the store) as I always do them while making other foods so it wasn’t that big of a deal for me. The day night cycle was annoying as you could skip the night but not the day so if I had to do my food quest that required me to cook under the moonlight I’d have to wait until night.Overall, I would say this was an alright game. Not the best and definitely not the worst. You can find enjoyment in it if you are patient. The direction of the game is creative but it just does not mesh well if it is going to promote itself as a cozy game. Highly highly recommend for people to play the demo first to try it out yourself to see if this is your cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, it's a great game. Well developed, great soundtrack, interesting worldbuilding; the world feels huge. Way more pros than cons. I think the only disadvantage this game really has is that it looks too much like a 'cozy' game, when it requires a lot of thorough investigation and thought. cozy games are typically low effort, easy-peasy, but i've found myself stuck multiple times so far, 10 hours in.it's generally difficult understanding the flow of the land, remembering where everything is until you can get map markers. the platforming can be a bit annoying, but i would expect as much from any other platformer. it can get overwhelming to have so many unfinished orders because other parts of the game haven't progressed enough for me to have the recipes needed to complete those orders. so, it LOOKS like a cozy game, but it isn't, really.i've got one suggestion: i desperately need a catalog of items. i'm gonna end up probably making a spreadsheet for myself because i can't always have one of every ingredient in my inventory to remember what ingredients correspond with what flavor profiles. like, i know i've seen bitter ingredients around, but i can't remember where i found them, and getting around the world can be difficult and time consuming. so instead of running around fruitlessly searching for something specific at every individual vendor, it'd seriously help a lot if the player can have their own little notebook full of all the ingredients they've already found.

_childDocuments_.review: Score: +20 -RECOMMENDED- Review Summary: A crafting metroid-vania platformer that is perfect for folks who like light platforming mechanics, puzzle-like crafting mechanics, and great art. A very cozy feel.Pros: +55The audience is kept interested with helpful audio queues along side the visual queues. The characters are ones that have distinct personalities even though they do not have voice acting. You never feel helpless, and you know that there will be progress once you find the right path to unlock the next set of areas. Petting random cats is nice, I am just sad you cannot pet the goats. To end this section on the highest note for me, you can tell that the developer wanted as many people as possible to enjoy their game. Along side the standard accessibility options we have come to see in games, they have legibility options, and motor function options. These are huge, and I hope to see them in more AAA games as well.  --------------------------------------------------+5 - For most titles, I expect about 1 hour per 1$ spent. I usually give some leeway for indie titles, but this game did not really need it. 23.1 hours for 25$ at the time of this review, and I tend to race through games. Great work.+5 - A very cohesive art style that attracts to the game instantly.+5 - No voice acting, but still uses "wub-wub" sound effects to keep attention. Similar to Animal Crossing.+5 - Cooking seems extremely varied right off the bat and only improves as the game goes on. +5 - Gathering quick spare change from pots as saved me more times than not. Wonderful safety net system.+5 - Early hints at power ups later on in level design. Very well suiting the genre.+5 - Can pet random animals+20 - Accessibility options include legibility for AuDHD and Dyslexic people, and contain options to make the game not require certain motor functions. Do not see this very often in platformers.--------------------------------------------------Cons: -30Controller support was clearly prioritized for this title. Even with a controller, user experience in menu flow is rough. A piece of the story seems woefully unexplored and the way you gather orders makes you feel like you are always missing something.---------------------------------------------------5 - Mouse support for menus would go a long way for keyboard players-5 - Wandering controls plague this game. Sometimes you need to use SELECT, sometimes SUBMIT, sometimes BACK. This needs to be stream lined so the user is not needing to memorize a combo move to get through menus quickly.-10 - Starts with an extremely pushy "roommate" who hints at racism being a portion of the story, but this is never explained and the roommate is just "Different" at the end, but the witches are afraid of the roommate. Poor piece of the writing in an otherwise enjoyable story.-10 - Can be difficult at times to find quests, especially if you explore early to find better ingredients. A bit of a punishing feeling for wanting explore the world first as soon as possible. Late game this makes me feel like I am hunting down NPCs to see if they need something, but they move around, so I am left with a feeling of incompleteness at the end of the game. (Maybe a notification system on the map for people who have requests?)--------------------------------------------------Hrms: -0 (usually zero)There are many things you can nit-pick in any title. This one is no different. Many ways that I can see to improve the flow of this title, but not enough to make this category a net loss. --------------------------------------------------+0 - Too much banter in the beginning. Does not feel quirky, but wordy.+0 - It feels like there should be random recipe requests. Some difficult, and some easy. This would lend to a nice continuation mechanic in the game.+0 - "Roommate" serves near zero purpose. Should be able to work the shop window while out and about? (Upgrade maybe?)+0 - Movement controls are intuitive, though a little slow feeling for a platformer.+0 - Menus are best suited or controller play, but no suggestion is given or controller.+0 - Can't throw away ruined items early on and it just becomes clutter. This is solved later on, but is frustrating none the less. +0 - Could purchase map upgrades immediately. Is a very odd addition to the equipment system and should probably just be standard, or moved to be upgrades earned as you progress the merchant's story. If I never have to live without them, their impact is lessened.--------------------------------------------------Bugs: -5 (Scored on impact)I only really ran into three bugs during gameplay. This is impressive. If these three things were fixed, this game would be extremely smooth. Cannot praise this enough.--------------------------------------------------+0 - Platform Lifts sometimes stop working and you must reload the map for them to start again. _childDocuments_.review: Magical Delicacy is like Kiki's Delivery Service, but you cook and cater to various tastebuds while platforming to reach customers. It's a unique addition to the "cozy game" genre.If you enjoy cooking games and managing food orders, this one's for you. It's visually stunning, has a great soundtrack, and offers a unique take on the "cozy game" genre. However, if platforming or getting lost in a 2D side-scroller frustrates you, this might not be your game. It could use a quality-of-life update to smooth out the gameplay loop. Unlike many games where cooking is an afterthought, here you can strategically combine ingredients with different flavors to create the requested dishes. There are multiple cooking tools, ingredients, and recipes, so you can experiment a bit. For those who enjoy real-life cooking, gathering orders and ingredients this game can be relaxing for you. The game is visually appealing, especially at night, and has a fitting soundtrack. I really like the music around the area where  is. The platforming can be fun or frustrating. You can't hang on ledges like in other platforming games, and the controls feel clunky. The game becomes enjoyable mid to late-game. Early on, it's easy to get stuck without clear guidance from objectives or quests, on how to progress. The in-game guide is hard to read. I had to open guides to learn how to combine flavors correctly, since the visual in the guide didn't help. The game also didn't really explain how to fulfill orders (like what does "avoid" mean? as in no "spicy" ingredient at all, or just avoid giving a "spicy" dish at the end?). You have to either open a guide, or spend hours combing the map to find ingredients and NPC locations. Quality-of-life upgrades come too late to be useful. You have to fetch water and fertilizer, and get to the planting spot on time. The long growth time and the tediousness of this make it easier to just buy or find ingredients. There's also very limited space for planting. The characters and story lack depth, everybody is nice to everybody, even when it seems like there's more to them.Some suggestions for the dev(s): This game desparately needs an in-game guide for ingredients, their flavors, and locations. The character section of a guide needs more details such as their locations and completed orders. The attempt to make the guide feel more part of the world of the game makes it harder to parse. Instructions on how to combine flavors and fulfilling orders should be made more clear. There should be clear objectives on how to progress the main questline. There should be more to the storefront, like idk maybe fulfilling random orders to make money on the side for upgrades. Make upgrades cheaper or available earlier (especially ). Players should have more freedom on what they can do outside of the store. Making item equipping only available inside the store limits this. Exploring the map to find NPCs and ingredients is already painful, so maps should be able to be opened even on moving platforms and inclines. Maybe the herbalist can sell a watering can and fertilizer bag upgrade to reduce the back and forth while gardening. There should be a clear indicator of whether there is water in cooking tools. You should be able to nap during the day, because . You should be able to highlight which order you are working on while cooking. You should also be able to see if an order can be delivered, not just how many you have delivered. A bit nitpicky, but spices should be able to be grinded or even dried. That's how you use them irl most of the time anyways. Story needs to be expanded. As it is now, it ended kind of flat.

_childDocuments_.review: cute cooking game, the platforming is unusual but you get used to it quick. Awesome characters, great art, cook cook cook!EDIT:After seeing all these negative reviews, I wanted to share some additional information that might help others. I can very much understand that there's confusion about the gameflow if you come from crafting games that follow a more stricter adherence to quests -> recipes -> rewards structure. You'll expect to get a request, check which recipe you have, gather or buy the ingredients, craft the thing, and hand it back in. That's simply not the way the game is meant to be played! It took me a while to realize this myself, after running into frustrations with "not being able to fulfill requests" and an ever-full inventory with no money. Instead of expecting to always have the fitting recipe for something, place yourself into the role of a cooking enthusiast for a second. What greater joy is there for a chef than to devise their own recipes? That's what gave ma true epiphany in how to approach the game and the requests given to me. I started just throwing stuff together to A) find more recipes; B) make space in my inventory; C) have something to sell. And would you look at that... after haphazardly creating new dishes until my inventory was blank, I had 3 different request items I could turn in immediately! And the rest, I just kept. Then, later, I met someone new and could solve their request on the spot because I had already made a fitting dish before.You're a witch - start acting like one! Witches don't need recipes, they make their own!

Being a witch in this universe, you are considered a talented chef with powers and knowing how to satisfy others' appetites. Upon moving to Grat, Flora was provided with a space, interest-free, to set up her kitchen. She cooks and serves delicious food to the residents. As you explore the land, you uncover new ingredients, meet various characters, and discover new delicious meals to cook. Simultaneously, you develop new powers and learn more about being a witch. The best way to describe this adventure is like being in the anime Hunter x Hunter as a Gourmet Hunter. However, in this case, there is no danger of dying, unlike your Hunter x Hunter counterparts. _childDocuments_.review: A game to tickle the tastebuds!Magical Delicacy is a game of luscious pixel art, and no doubt a labour of love from the game's single developer. Grat is a beautiful cliffside town, in all its lavish and labyrinthine verticality, and its environments are alive with detail - the flight of sparrows as you jog by, the patter of rain against the glow of a meticulously-designed shopfront at night, the teeming greenery of the gardens blowing in the wind, and the cosy yet riotously vibrant clutter of a fully-stocked kitchen, its oven glowing with magically-ignited embers. And hidden smiley faces amidst the woodgrain.The plot, as you cook your way through a town perched on the edge of the uncharted riparian wilds and navigate its witchly feuds, has a charm and environmental undercurrent that's worthy of a Ghibli film. The pace is not rushed - the game is decidedly gentle and relaxing, and it's underlaid at every moment with a lovely soundtrack, which certainly adds to the calm beauty of the atmosphere.The life of a fledgling witch is half one of cooking, and half one of navigating the town's maze of platforms, on the hunt for new areas and rare ingredients. Getting around involves plenty of jumping around precarious ledges, though once you get a few movement-enhancing spells and trinkets up your sleeves, the town soon opens up. Optional, trickier platforming puzzles await underground those looking for more hidden rewards.Just as exploration pays off amongst the crannies and catacombs of Grat, experimentation pays off in the kitchen. In reality, I'm the kind of cook who always follows a recipe, but though there are many recipes available, this game encourages (and even requires) getting creative to fulfil the orders of the towns colourful variety of likeable residents. As the options began to sprout curious new branches, I soon felt like a cooking addict, balancing flavours and substituting ingredients. Discovering new crafted ingredients and recipes by going off-script is logical and satisfying (at least for the most part - if only I could put all the juicy ingredients in the juicer!). And the interface for pinning orders and recipes is well-appreciated, once the complexity of the recipes increases.Most importantly of all, you  pet the cats.NUTRITIONAL INFORMATIONEach serving contains (% daily value):ALLERGY ADVICE: Contains nuts, wheat products, poisonous toadstools. Suitable for vegetarians.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, Magical Delicacy hung on my Wishlist until I read another gamer's review that said they couldn't stop thinking about it after they played it. I'm almost finished with the game now, and I feel that way. It can be frustrating at times, and I did Google answers when I was stumped, but I totally fell in love with this game. It's well-written, the world is interesting, the story isn't depressingly sad, and the gameplay is smart. Like actual cooking, you might need to double-up some ingredients to get the flavor profile you need, and recipes can be complex with multiple-steps that include juicing and drying fruit. Cooking is a natural fit with the witchy-woo as well - it isn't as simple as make something and then enchant it, or adding a toad to the pot. I appreciated that too - it sold me on Flora being a talented character.Once I unlocked most things and figured out how to double-up the ingredients, the quests clipped along. It's one of those games that's slow going for the first 1/3rd, and then it rolls along. My one critique is I just wish I had more storage for ingredients. I'm an ingredient hoarder, and I tried to clean up my stock by making and selling extra dishes, but it wasn't quite enough to keep 2-3 of each item.Platform-wise, I can see where cozy gamers might not like it, but I dug the creative choice. I bought up the maps and markers from Colo and once I had quick travel unlocked, it made everything easier.All-in-all, I went in skeptical from past mixed reviews, but it ended up being one of my top 3 games this year, and I will definitely be replaying it.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect blend of platforming and cooking. It's a tricky start, especially with figuring out the map and some of the cooking mechanics, but is incredibly fun and rewarding once you get the hang of it. Most of the issues that I had when I started (limited inventory, jumps falling just short etc...) appear to have been addressed by the first update which is a great sign. Exploring is fun and sometimes challenging, whilst the world and characters are vibrant and combine for an immersive story. A lot of fun can be had by simply messing around and combining random ingredients to discover new recipes, though there is also ample opportunity to acquire these through the various shops and story progression. I personally don't make much use of the gardening mechanic as I prefer to collect ingredients through exploration, but the game appears to support both types of play style. Overall it makes for a fun and relaxing game with a charming art style. And bonus points for the cute dragons!
_childDocuments_.name: Magical Delicacy

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't quite completed the main story yet, but I fully adore this game. I find the platforming fun, challenging but not terribly difficult, with a great accessibility option  I love experimenting with different ingredients in different tools to create new dishes while selling others in the shop. The pinning feature that allows you to pin both requests and recipes in a sidebar you can reference while cooking is great. The art and music are beautiful. Collecting outfit palettes (that let you change individual pieces of Flora's outfit, rather than necessarily altogether) as quest rewards or as treasures hidden around the map is super rewarding. There's just so much that this game does that I love.

This is a game that is really rewarding if you like slow, detail-oriented gameplay. Take your time exploring the world, and cooking plenty of recipes! _childDocuments_.review: This game is like Kiki's Delivery Service and Spiritfarer had a baby. The art and soundtrack are gorgeous, and the menus are very slick and well thought out. There's a lot of polish here, and it feels very lovingly designed. I especially love the quest tracking system that lets you pin quests and recipes on a side dock for quick reference. You also have the ability to filter your items by type or flavor, which makes digging through menus much less of a chore. I never really had too much difficulty figuring out what to do since there are tons of people to talk to and a lot of exploration to be done, but some of the food requests can be a bit of a challenge to puzzle out. As like most metroidvanias, the beginning can be a bit slow to start, but I think it does a good job explaining the mechanics while letting you go at your own pace. The game really prioritizes curiosity and experimentation (and rewards you jumping into oblivion sometimes), but I still found it to be a chill experience with a good balance between the adventuring and actual cooking. There is a lot of backtracking unless you're super organized (that's a metroidvania for you), but you do unlock fast travel points. Very rarely did I feel like I was being stalled by lacking specific ingredients or cookware. You can find, buy, or grow basically anything you need, so it doesn't feel like you're limited by RNG. There's no need to micromanage your garden. Money was almost never an issue since you can get it from selling, doing quests, or just running around the map and walking over breakable pottery. There's a day/night cycle but it affects a few NPCs (none of the shops from what I can tell) and making some food items and potions. Some paths in the world are only open at night.That said, there are a few drawbacks that get in the way of gameplay being a solid 10/10: A recent update made it easier to find some things on the map and see which quests progress the story, as well a few other QOL improvements. It's nice to see the feedback being implemented to make this charming cooking-vania even more polished. Despite it's flaws, I love it a ton and am lowkey addicted.

_childDocuments_.review: Magical Delicacy is a delightful game that I thoroughly enjoyed playing. At its core, the game revolves around taking orders from the townspeople and fulfilling them to learn more about them and also to advance the game's overall story. The metroidvania part comes from how the world is laid out and explored: areas gated behind abilities that you unlock as part of the natural progression through the story.The cooking/orders portion has great variability from straightforward orders to ones that feel more like a puzzle, which requires careful thought and experimentation to determine how to meet a set of requirements. There are not only different ingredients to play with but different preparation methods that can change the ingredients' effect.Although the movement could perhaps be a bit more fluid, as a way to get around the map, it works and there are some good accessibility options that can help. My only ask is to include a way to fill out an ingredient encyclopedia that can be referred to for their properties as well as where you've found them before.Overall, I have had a lot of fun in this game, between playing it and looking at the art and delighting in the music and characters.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, cozy Metroidvania platformer cooking sim game. As a fan of the crafty vibes, I have been obsessing over this game for the past few days. I've played the game for ~40 hours as of writing this review,  and have pretty much 100%'d the game without a guide (minus the last achievement, which is bugged and the dev is working on fixing). Let's start off with the cons because that list is shorter, and then I'll give you the long list of pros:Cons: > I don't think this is a bad thing, but this is probably the most divisive thing about this game: it doesn't really hold you hand during the cooking portions. You will mess up... a lot. Wrong flavors, unknown recipes, requests that you don't have the tools for yet, etc. Personally, I liked discovering new things and pondering how to complete quests; but I know a lot of people will disagree with that.> The platforming can be janky at times. Sometimes you will struggle with going up/down specific staircases, sometimes you won't reach platforms that you think you should've reached, and sometimes you will land on platforms that you didn't think you landed on (which throws off your timing). > I wish there was a better way to log where you harvested ingredients from. There is a way to generally mark the map, but that really isn't good enough imo. When you play this game, expect at least 1-2 hours of you trying to remember where that one ingredient that you need is.> There needs to be more filters for when you are searching ingredients. You can only filter your list down the type, flavor, and if it is plantable. There needs to be filters for rarity, if it can be enhanced a certain way, and if it is NOT plantable as well imo.... Those are my only major cons about the game. Now for the pros:> I'll start with probably the most underrated thing about this game: the sound design. From the chirping of crickets under the moon-basked sky to the sound of rain pattering against your window while the oven is running nearby, everything sounds perfect. The voice synthesis adds so much interesting depth to the different species in the game (and hot take: it is even better than the voices in Animal Crossing). Oh, and the soundtrack is amazing - I could gush in great length a lot of the songs in this game alone.> If you suck at platformers, don't worry! There are options in the game to make platforming way easier so that you can enjoy the game (yes... even you.)> There are also a slew of other accessibility options: most having to do with visual-impairment or dyslexia. They aren't the best I've seen in a game, but they are a very nice and welcome addition.> The gameplay loop works surprisingly well. I thought the Metroidvania aspects would make something like a cozy, cooking sim dreadful, but it is designed VERY well. Cook some things for some people => people give you new tools/abilities to get around => explore new area with new ingredients => cook some things with said new ingredients => repeat. Simple, yet not too tedious.> The characters are mostly wonderful. It was always fun to learn more about them, and the animated text in the dialogue boxes really adds a lot of personality to characters. A surprising standout is the main character Flora - there are way too many life sim games where the main character is just a blank slate for the player to self-insert. That's not a bad thing, but it's refreshing to see someone like Flora lead one of these games every once in a while.> The art style and direction is great. With cute animals, interesting character designs, and enchanting backdrops, the art does well in conveying aesthetic, vibe, and great world in general. One nice detail I like is the steam from the cooking steaming up the visuals in the game.> The world building is deeper than I expected. You can learn some details about a surprising amount of things: how magic work in the world, the history of the city, details about the royal family, the types of folk, etc. It's not super deep; but I was surprised that I got any, and that it was all written so gosh-darn well.> The difficulty of the cooking orders is very well-crafted. For 90% of the orders, it felt like they hit the exact Goldilocks spot where they weren't too easy or too hard. > It works great on the Steam Deck!All-in-all, the game's strengths outweigh its few weaknesses. It was a fantastic present from a friend, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a light Metroidvania with some cozy crafting vibes.

name: Pizza Tower
detailed_description: Pizza Tower is a fast paced 2D platformer , with an emphasis on movement, exploration and score attack. Featuring highly stylized pixel art inspired by the cartoons from the '90s, and a highly energetic soundtrack. Peppino Spaghetti, a surprisingly agile and powerful fat balding italian, is on a mission to destroy the titular Pizza Tower in order to save his restaurant from annihilation. Follow him through his rampage across the many wacky floors of the tower, collecting toppings and beating up monsters! PLAY as Peppino Spaghetti, the supersonic italian middle-aged man! And sometimes Gustavo. EXPLORE up to 5 floors leading to many levels, discover all of their secrets! FIGHT some monsters and other weirdos! DESTROY everything in your path, including those stupid rats. BECOME the Pizza Tower! Weird crazy characters and animations! An insanely energetic soundtrack! An unusual platformer formula! Play like you want! Go for the highest score or explore at your own pace!

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is so deliberately unhinged, so wildly demented in it's aesthetics, visuals, animations, and audio that it cleverly hides its spectacular level design and movement mechanics — While everything seems psychotic and completely deranged, it's all knit together exceptionally well and is an absolute joy to play. This is a tight, excellently-paced game with more than enough gameplay variance, and a ton of nuance and optimization inside an approachable, easy-to-pick-up moveset. There's a wide variance of tech and movement options that are unnecessary to complete the game, but feel fantastic and do help with a number of the tougher platforming challenges. The game continues to throw clever, unique level elements that change how you have to think about completing obstacles, and not by limiting your options: They open your eyes to more and more things you can do. "Oh wait, I can do *that?*" is going to be a recurring thought as you play. Pizza Tower does a good job of letting you go slow to learn things, but it really thrives when it can convince you to go *FAST*, by god can you move when you want to. You'll also have to, as once you hit the end of each level, the game slaps a timer on the screen and forces you to speedrun the level backwards as fast as you can. Running forwards through each level whilst trying to keep important obstacles in mind for when you have to run it backwards is a great, fairly unique way of thinking as you play. Fret not though, outside of boss fights, you cannot die in this game, meaning you can instantly retry any failed attempts at an obstacle: This game respects your time, and doesn't want you to overthink things: Just go for it, and see if it works. Fully completing this game will be a sizeable challenge, not due to a giant swath of benign content, but due to the intensity of the challenges presented, all of which are fair, if not easy.  Nothing has so expertly captured the lunacy of both mid-90's third party SNES platformers and late-00's Newgrounds, let alone at the same time, somehow. Levels all somehow follow a very coherent theme and tone, while each individual aspect seems as bizarre and disjointed as possible, yet they somehow all fit together splendidly. Animations, *especially* those for the playable characters deliberately break a ton of standard animation rules (*little appeal, squash & stretch changing the mass of the character*), and yet, much like the level elements and the visuals on the whole, work perfectly together to convey instantly exactly what they need to — This is obviously not a series of flukes: the creators here know exactly what the rules are, and where the lines are, and know them expertly, and know exactly *how* to break every rule they can while retaining everything that makes a game work. I cannot recommend this highly enough for anyone with a passing interest in either platformers or weird art projects. This game is delightfully strange, unnerving at times, and feels like a nightmare of a fever dream, whilst also being both the best Wario game and the best Sonic game made at the same time. Throw some money at these developers, they deserve it.
