_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is incredibly awesome, everything a platformer should be and one of my favourite games of the last few years. I grew up playing Wario Land, and never realised how good the concept could be until it was manifested for the modern standards in Pizza Tower. It's a great game for all audiences, but which has high appeal for those who love difficult challenges.When I first played through the game, I was mainly drawn to the fluid controls and great visual design. Pizza Tower controls like a dream, and while it seems simple at first, there's a lot of secret moves that only come with practice and the specific nuances of going fast. Yet, you can tell immediately that a lot of love has gone into making it feel fun to move in a way that I could never understood in something similar like Sonic the Hedgehog. Likewise, the developers have done an amazing job using sprites and 2-D animation to create a soulful cartoon world. In many ways, I like it better than unique hand-drawn visuals from a series like Cuphead, as Pizza Tower feels like it has more character rather than just aping on another artist's design. It's heavily inspired by television series like Courage and Eddy; but it somehow feels unique, likely due to the hilarious setting. My favourite imaginative spin was that olives were adapted as outer-space aliens. Pizza Tower has great characters and really goes far with a theme that I didn't think would really be so interesting.That said, I played through the game in about 4-5 hours and though I liked it, saw the certain charm, I wasn't sure what was so amazing. I read a bit about the buzz on forums, and I was encouraged to play Pizza Tower as a score-attack. So, I attempted to get a Perfect (P) rank on the first level. It took a few hours to get good enough, but when I did it, I was so excited I immediately wanted to try and do another. It quickly became "just one more level" and then some 40 hours later, I had gotten 101% completion with every single level at a P-ranking. Playing just to get through the levels was mediocre, but playing for the perfect score was heart-throbbing fun, even though it was also frustrating. After doing so, I can only ever play this game in the aim of getting those P-ranks and hitless boss fights. I can't overstate how good it felt to finally finish the game that way. Furthermore, Pizza Tower has amazing level design where new stages feel totally unique while still using all of your familiar skills. Each level has a gimmick like playing golf, avoiding alarm systems, dealing with intangible enemies, using unique transformations, etc. It tops it all off with one of the best endings of any game and an extremely memorable "victory lap" nobody will want to miss. If that wasn't enough, the soundtrack is phenomenal, and you'll quickly be listening to it in your spare time when you aren't enjoying its beats through each level attempt. I can't wait to see what the developers make next, and I only wish there was more Pizza Tower to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 10/10Pros: The 90s aesthetic is fully realized here, the fun cartoon nature of it is effectively in every part of the game's design. The move sets are organic, and complex at the same time, allowing for precision platform at Mach speeds with little difficulty. Adding to that, there are options to help change controls so you don't even have to have the up and down mechanics be linked to them, you can put them to any button you want. If you enjoy platformers, there is no reason to skip out on this one. Everything is well telegraphed for boss fights and combat, and there are crazy amounts of secrets to find. The best way to describe it is a merger of all the old platformers into one: Mario jumping mechanics, Sonic's momentum based platforming, Wario's exploration and combat. And it's all polished to a great feeling game. Chef kiss.Cons:  It's a bit short, but not that short for 20 bucks it asked for at it's start. It's really hard to find a con. But otherwise there is no major cons I can even think of.Recommend to: People who enjoy high speed platforming.Overall: Another good indie game showing off that old mechanics don't mean bad or outdated, and can be refined further to make an even better game. This game has my game of the year nomination already. Going to be hard to top this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard a lot of praise for Pizza Tower and decided to pick it up to see what all the fuss was about. Steam reviews and critics were absolutely right - it’s a great game. While it’s not my cup of tea, I came to appreciate the craft and love that the developers put into the game.In simple terms - it’s a platformer: you finish a few levels per stage, take down the boss and move to the next stage. That’s it, really. You can of course try to beat the level perfectly - take little to no damage and finish it as soon as possible, to get a better score. You can also find secret mini-levels to boost up the score as well. What is pretty awesome though, is that there are different characters you can play as during some of the levels and use weapons / different “game mechanics” on that level. That way every second level or so really feels different from the other, so you don’t really get bored of doing the usual “run to the end and back”. It really felt like Tour De Pizza didn’t just want to “fart out” another platformer but rather create a fun game.The art is awesome and the animations are hilarious! It felt like I was playing one of those 90s cartoons, like “The Ren & Stimpy Show”. I’ve had a lot of good laughs.I’d recommend Pizza Tower to anyone. Unless you cannot stomach platformers in any shape or form, you should add this one to your game library.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Oh I don't have the reflexes to be good at Pizza Tower'No. You do. You do and you'll find where they were in no time. Take it from someone that thought it, waited so long, finally caved, and is having a blast.I've always claimed I was more one for Super Mario Land 3 as opposed to Wario Land 4 or Shake It! but this *might've* shown me what was missing from those: tight controls, fluid movement, and stage design that ramps up nicely and is absolutely custom tailored to speedrunning. All wrapped up in a deranged Spumco vibe without all the Kricfalusi ruining it, and bumpin' music.I've literally only gotten to the second set of stages at this point and I'm already hooked on trying to improve my times and my movement. Is Peppino a bit sticky out of the gate? Yes. It took me a good half hour to unlearn 'hold forward while dashing' since the madman keeps it going as long as you hold the button. It took me even longer to unlearn 'down to super jump' from Mario. I still hump the wall a bit trying to wall jump when my brain won't disengage from going fast. But the simple fact of the matter is: that's fine.Until you hit that buzzer to start the end of the level, you can futz all you want. You can make mistakes, you can learn as you go. And that's what really does shine about Pizza Tower: despite the rankings it's not judgmental. You won't die. You'll lose points, but you won't die. And as you move through the game, you'll figure out how to keep a handle on those points. You'll learn how to parry a sentient wad of cheese, how to super taunt mid-frantic-dash to hold a combo, and the game will start praising you for it with those improving rankings.I'm just one voice but seriously. For 20 bucks, you could either get what I'd call a great way to improve your platforming skills in a fun package, or half of an actual pizza delivery that *won't* be as satisfying as beating up a giant pizza.

_childDocuments_.review: Indie games come in many shapes and sizes, but many are made with the idea of being a modern take or spiritual successor on a classic game. Both  and , for example, are modern takes on  and  respectively.  a successor to  in particular is no different. I have not played the game it takes from, but I can still say with a great deal of confidence that this grease-covered gem has charged its way straight into the upper echelon of this niche, an echelon that arguably surpasses its inspiration.  Visually, this game is an assault on the eyes in the best way possible. It's sort of like  in the sense that some of the initial learning curve is just processing what you see on the screen. However, I don't think  has an ugly visual style, rather it's just chaotic and messy - again, in the best way possible. The art style is best described as 90's Nickelodeon cartoons like  and  in a MS Paint format. I adore the aesthetic, and think they captured that surreal, geometric look perfectly with this game, and it fits the unabashedly and comically insane feel this game goes for. In addition, the animations in this game are astonishingly good. Everything is incredibly fluid and expressive. There's so many blink-and-you'll-miss-it moments, for example seeing the basic enemies become startled and wide-eyed at the sight of an anxious Italian man surpassing Usain Bolt's top speed charging right at them. Is it a Pillar John of art style and animation in games? Probably not, but this is a pie that knows a thing or two about presentation, and it does that point very well.This being a platformer, nailing the movement is key, and anxious greaseball Peppino controls remarkably well. For as overwhelming as this game can be, Peppino's moveset is both varied and tight. It takes some time to understand how to control peak Italian athleticism, but it feels immensely satisfying to master. Going fast is fun, and far more engaging than the high speeds of Sonic's preferences for autopilot. While you certainly will accidentally launch Peppino into a wall and kill your momentum at least twice per level, the game revels in its chaos. Like many a fast food joint,  does not demand perfection, it demands efficiency. Getting the highly-desired P rank isn't obtained by making zero mistakes, it's done by embracing the breakneck rhythm the game sets its tempo at and finding the most efficient routes possible to maintain your combos. As an authentic meatbag that can't keep up with some of the robotic reaction times of some players, it's refreshing to play something that embraces the odd mistake if you can quickly get back into the fray.While combat is rarely a priority, the bosses are a highlight. They test your skills in unique and interesting ways, and despite their challenge, were consistently fair in their mechanics and expectations. The final boss, in particular, was incredibly fun to fight and one of my favorite final bosses of recent memory. The level design is also a major highlight, and lends itself well to the "efficiency over perfection" approach. The core idea remains the same: Grab the Toppins, destroy Pillar John, get out quickly. However, each level has a very distinct identity, both visually and mechanically, and provides unique power ups befitting the thematic identity of the level. These are usually nice breaks in the gameplay, and they generally adhere to the core idea of moving fast. However, a few of the gimmicks did feel rather undercooked in their uses or how they controlled. It's not a significant issue, but for how polished the rest of the core gameplay feels, I did find it noticeable enough to leave a slightly underwhelmed taste.I think another point  can struggle with is in its difficulty. It's not too hard, just erratic in its expectations from level to level. I found a handful in the earlier stages of the game were more difficult than most of the later levels, even after I returned to them near the end with a greater familiarity of the mechanics and the level layouts. The game frontloads everything into its initial tutorial, which is fitting, but I still wish it did a better job of gradually introducing those mechanics. I can see this point being a turn-off for some players, which is unfortunate because I think the game's level design only gets better as you progress.However, the game largely excels in what it sets out to do. It's fast, it's tight, and it's fair. Does it play better than  Frankly, I have no idea, but I can tell you it's probably the best  game I've ever played. I don't think the story is worth considering in the rating of this game.  is a gameplay-focused experience that draws you in with its aesthetics, and it knows that. As such, the story is in the backseat and there isn't really much to talk about, other than it being present.While your taste buds may not get the satisfaction they're looking for when playing this game, your eardrums certainly will. I think the sound effects perfectly fit the cartoon aesthetic. I'm especially fond of the taunt sound effect, both as a parry and on its own. The former has a "pow" effect that makes parrying feel satisfying, while the horn sound that plays in both makes it thoroughly enjoyable to spam.The music, however, is the real star of the show here. It's playful, upbeat, and catchy, but there's also a remarkable amount of depth here. For example, the secret levels have a groovy, percussive backtrack that sets the surreal tone of the level, but each secret level has a different melody corresponding with the original level you found the secret in, which blew my leitmotif-loving mind. "It's Pizza Time" is the best track, as it perfectly encapsulates the panic of having to escape from a level, and the final boss theme is also a treat, not mentioning the Waters of Nazareth-esque track from a late-game level. takes somewhere around 6 hours to finish for a regular playthrough. However, levels are highly replayable and filled to the brim with secrets and hidden routes. While I did not go out of my way to P-Rank every level, it's definitely an appealing challenge that can easily inflate your playtime. While the game itself is pretty short, there's lots of side content and replay value to warrant the price tag.This game and  go together like pineapples on pizza. Some people will look at this strange creation and find it repulsive, but the garlic-scented freaks like myself that give it a taste will have their senses enlightened by a chaotic barrage of exciting flavors and mechanics. You do not need an attachment to this game's inspiration to appreciate it for the absolutely stellar title that it is, so I highly recommend smelling the garlic and giving this eccentric gem a shot because of that. Even with its impressive polish,  isn't quite the perfect pie for me, but don't let its minor shortcomings deter you, it's still remarkably close. Just remember, if you hurt Peppino too much, you can go to hell. - 4/5 - 5/5 - N/A - 5/5 - 4/5+ Excellent level design+ Tight & satisfying mechanics+ Great soundtrack+ Fun boss fights+ Fluid & expressive animations- Level gimmicks are hit & miss- Inconsistent difficulty progression

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is a great game. It combines the speed of sonic with many of the mechanics and aesthetics of wario land. Though simply calling it a wario-like game is selling it short. The bizarre animation, and music come together with the breakneck gameplay to create a very unique game. Unlike many other difficult platformers the difficulty of Pizza Tower does not come from the game itself, in fact I think even a novice platform gamer could finish Pizza Tower with minimal difficulty. The levels in Pizza Tower never demand precise inputs and the player character Pepino can't die. What make the game difficult is the ranking system which demands players aiming for high ranks to beat levels quickly, and intentionally, making sure to grab every collectable and secret as they go. No matter your skill level Pizza Tower will be an incredible, fun and innovative experience and I recommend highly recommend it to seasoned and novice platform gamers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Some people are downplaying this as a "successor to Wario Land" when in reality this is possibly the best indie game I've ever played (also have a lot  of hours on the most recent demos so it's more than it's displayed on steam). The way the levels, the moveset, the enemies, the bosses, the gimmicks, and the secrets are desing has in my opinion surpassed anything Nintendo (or Sega since this game is apparently compared to Sonic too) ever did, at least in the 2D department. A lot has already been said about what this game does, so I'll touch on what it doesn't do: there are no "hold right" sonic-esque portions (except one near the end, but i guess the ending warrants a cinematic scene like that), there is no annoying level desing that forces you to repeat large chunks of the game for no reason, all the enemies are completely fair, and the game has 0 filler. Plus, there's insane replayability, so even if you beat it in 6 hours or so it'll entertain you for many more. I'd recommend buying this game full price even if the audio-visual presentation wasn't amazing (and I'm biased here since I always loved the Ren and Stimpy artstyle) - in my opinion there are just no flaws to speak of. Buy this if you like fast-paced 2D platformers, but also buy this if you like good videogames.

_childDocuments_.review: After years of development, this game's long overdue was both a welcome one and thankfully, well worth the wait! This game's dedication to it's style is greatly appreciated and it's the kind of thing we just don't see from big company titles. If you're a fan of old 90's irreverent humor/art styles, you'll appreciate how much the game hits the nostalgia nail on the head; if Cuphead was flawless love letter to the 20's-30's, this is the love letter to the 90's and well appreciated. The game's overt connection to the Wario Land series is front and center, which could be an issue were it not for how much the game openly embraces that fact and does the Wario formula justice while also cranking it's energy and speed up a hundred fold! The insane pace of the game only serves to further aid it's absurd visuals and creates a gameplay experience that is highly rewarding if one can master it's demand for tight reflexes. Thankfully, this is not a requirement to simply play the game. A seasoned player could easily whip through any level in seconds, but a new comer can take their time and not be punished for that. It's really nice to play an indie game that doesn't feel the need to torture it's players for not dedicating their entire life to mastering it's mechanics and I think that's one of Pizza Tower's greatest features. Nearly anyone could take to this and enjoy it. If there is one caveat I could aim in this direction though is that at times I felt the game physics were a tad wonky; this could just be me not being great at the game or kinks that will be patched out later but they were never issues that ruined the game for me, just a few moments of unwarranted irritation. Bosses can also be frustrating but as the game isn't overly difficult, as you have no real way to die in most levels, this makes sense as to add a level of challenge to the game. Just beware before stepping into a boss room! All that said, this game is a hell of a ride and with DLC already hinted at, I can't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Serious review time. This game is outstanding. Comparing it to things like Sonic and Wario Land doesn't do it justice. The inspiration is definitely there, but Pizza Tower shines on its own outside of it with a unique, comical art style full of personality, an incredible soundtrack, snappy controls, and the most passion I've seen in a game in recent memory. The tutorial is fast and lets you take it at your own pace with visual depictions in the background and room to play around and learn. No walls of text. No hour long cutscenes. It just drops you in and lets you go for it. Play it slow, play it fast, get through levels however you want or be an insane person and go for the coveted P-rank. Blasting through the game with painstakingly perfect combos is incredibly satisfying when you finally pull it off. The bosses are fun, the Halloween update had great challenges, and I can't wait to see what comes next for this game. TL;DR: It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun and the word of mouth hype is legit. _childDocuments_.review: This game is truly remarkable. The fact that only in just 300,000 years of existence, we as a species have come up with something much more indicative of a god than man. This game is a social commentary on society and the very fundamental idea of Human Civilization. It explores the hypothetical question of what the natural order would look bar the rise of Human Civilization. The Utopian future of Cartoon like landscapes and co-prosperity among man and animal contrasts sharply with reality which shows the opposite, Humans exerting dominance on nature and a bleak and unforgiving surrounding. Despite us humans being deeply divided in thought, Pizza Tower will no doubt let us all see the true reality that faces us. After many escapes from the Pizza Tower, the game alludes to the extreme, but necessary conclusion to solve the problem that has plagued humanity and the world for so many years. That solution is the throw civilization away and live a much more basic life to restore the natural order, save humans as a species, and the world. A masterpiece by definition, Pizza Tower is perfect and to say other words would be as foolish as denying Peppino's pizza.

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is an easy to learn, hard to master Wario-like platformer with a sense of flow and speed achieved with momentum-based character movesets reminiscent of various Sonic games. The levels are designed with said moves and combo mechanics in mind, which add to that sense of flow while also creating well-balanced challenges along the journey.The game encourages you to keep mastering each stage with its ranking system, which can become addicting when you restart a stage over and over trying to keep your flow and keep going faster and faster while learning the stage as you go, trying to get that P Rank.The game's inane sense of humor gives it a charm unlike many others, delivering laughs, bewilderment, and slight eariness in some cases. This humor is very well reflected in the game's extremely cartoony animation, everything is so humorously animated that you might get caught off guard and start snickering while you're trying to keep your speed up.If you haven't played this game yet, for whatever reason, go play it already, you're missing out.

_childDocuments_.review: Endlessly inventive, hysterical, nostalgic, fun to play, and just dank as hell.Wario Land 4 is easily one of my favorite games of all time, and Pizza Tower is the successor I've been wanting since I first played it on my Game Boy Advance as a child. WL4 had everything I would grow to love about 2D platformers: tight gameplay, beautiful art and animation, excellent music, rewarding and fun exploration, and its own truly unique absurd tone. Pizza Tower has all of these qualities, but the combination of these things with the style of a 90's/early 2000's cartoon is a true stroke of genius. Playing it transported me back to a time where I would come home from elementary school and play Wario Land 4 while watching Ed, Edd 'n' Eddy on Cartoon Network, and that is a magical thing for a video game to do.It's easy at first glance to let the stellar 90's cartoon style and animation steal the show (it certainly speaks for itself, I mean just look at it, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious, and somehow ugly and beautiful at the same time). The game could have been a dumpster fire in every other regard, or a case of style over substance, and it would still be worth your money just to see the next unique animation. But it's not a dumpster fire or lacking substance, on the contrary, this is one of the most mechanically sound 2D platformers I've ever had the joy of laying my hands on.Many times when I sit down to play a modern game I'm often asking myself at certain points "Did anyone even play this before it released? Did anyone actually play it with the mindset of a consumer, test it and make sure that the game is fun and/or rewarding to play in any way?" Pizza Tower feels like a game that has been tested and adjusted to mechanical perfection by people who genuinely care about rewarding the player for investing the time to master its gameplay. Peppino's moveset strikes the perfect balance of easy to learn, hard to master. You can do a surprising amount of moves with only a couple of buttons at your disposal, and discovering the small details in the mechanics is incredibly interesting, so much so that it reminds me of discovering Samus' moveset in Super Metroid. It’s so satisfying to move Peppino around that it made me want to get into seriously speedrunning a game for the first time in my life. Every single screen in every level seems to have been carefully put together with multiple playstyles in mind, whether it's for players who are just casually exploring, hardcore speedrunners, or those trying to nail the P-Rank requirement. One night I was trying to get a P-Rank on one of the early levels, and I kept failing, but I kept trying for hours because it was equally fun to run through every time, thanks to how Peppino interacts with the stage. It feels like the developer managed to make exactly the game they wanted to play themselves, and that is an achievement in and of itself.This game kept me smiling for so long that my face started to hurt, and it took me back to those carefree days with my Game Boy and Cartoon Network. I am so grateful to the developers for that. I can't believe how this game kept me so completely entertained and full of joy while playing, it makes me emotional in a way that a ridiculous pizza game like this really shouldn't be able to. I have to give my most heartfelt thanks to McPig and the others that worked on this game for that.Video games are back, and now I too must go back. The tower beckons.

Gustavo and Brick are just adorable together and the way their story is told throughout the individual floors was pretty funny. _childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is by far one of the best indie platformers I've played in the past few years. The gameplay is fast paced, and highly reminiscent of the Wario Land series, which is its main inspiration. The game is divided into multiple hubs, all of which house four levels and a boss fight. Every level is home to five collectibles called "Toppins" (No, that's not a misspelling), that must be collected in order to face the boss of each area. The levels themselves are generally well designed and will test players' mastery of all the different movement options the game has to offer; especially during the second half of each stage.Stages are basically divided into two halves: The former being more "exploration-focused", with the latter being time-based and forcing players to return to the beginning of the level as fast as they possibly can; as they will be chased by the main antagonist once the countdown they activate at the end of the level runs out (and it's the only way they can actually lose).Not only that, every stage also has three secrets and optional challenges the player might want to give a try, as well as rank badges you get depending on your performance; giving the game a certain amount of replayability, especially now that a second character has been added.The artstyle is clearly inspired by 90's cartoons. It might be a turn off for some, but it has a certain charm to it.The soundtrack is fantastic, and one of the highlights of the game; featuring tracks that match every level perfectly. Overall, I'd recommend Pizza Tower to those who are looking for a retro-ish platformer evocative of the 90's and early 2000's.

_childDocuments_.review: This is, by far, one of my favorite video games ever made. I have been following this project since late 2018, and to see how its come from then to now is just mind blowing. But enough about that, let's get into what makes this game so amazing. For starters, the visuals. My god, the visuals. From the environments to the characters, everything is wonderfully stylized, and a certain flavor of zany and goofy. Along with the visuals, comes the kick-ass soundtrack. I really do not think there is a single song in this I do not like, props to the musicians! The gameplay as well, is just some of the finest you can get. The level design is styled to fit Peppino's tight controls, and encourages you to speed through the levels while racking up a combo. That's another aspect of this game, the combo system. It is brutally hard to keep your combo throughout the entire level (getting you a p-rank), however it never really feels unfair. I, myself, have only P ranked 2 levels (and a boss) so far, so I'm looking forward to what's ahead of me. I think the only real complaint I have with this game is how the uppercut and crouch-slide feel oddly difficult to pull off in a quick manner. This has, numerous times, caused my P-Rank runs to end, and is very frustrating. However, don't let that deter you from playing this game, it's incredible.tl;dr: Game's good, buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is an example of a spiritual successor done right. Not only is it a love letter to Nintendo's Wario Land series, but it has so much of it's own unique flair that truly gives it it's own identity. Many indie games that try to follow in the footsteps of the games they're inspired from fall into the trap of basically making it the exact same game with little of it's own personality, and sometimes not as well designed; Pizza Tower does not have this issue at all, though.Firstly, the visuals are simply outstanding. The crude, almost MS Paint-style art compliments it's homage to old 90s cartoons like Ren & Stimpy, which is what I was constantly thinking of when playing the game. Everything from the character designs, sound effects, and enemies and obstacles absolutely scream 90s cartoon. Even stuff like Peppino's scream when encountering a boss sounds like it could come straight from one. The animations themselves are also very nicely detailed, Peppino has so many frames of animation for all his moves despite being such a simple character with a simple art style; the developer really squeezed everything they could out of making this art style look as good as possible. Beyond that, there's so much little cosmetic flair that makes the game feel so alive, such as the TV in the corner of the screen at all times, or the intermission art that appears when you switch characters or fall into a pit.The gameplay is also equally amazing. The controls do take some time to get used to and it'll feel kinda janky and unintuitive at first, but it WILL eventually click, and it will feel amazingly natural. Peppino has a dash where he can reach absolutely ludicrous speeds, and this is the crux of the game. Not only that, but there's also many movement options like a diagonal dive, high jump, ground pound, and much more moves for practically every situation. It makes it feel like the game was designed with speedrunning in mind, because you can absolutely blow through levels in no time if you master the controls and know exactly how to get through a level. Every level has a ranking system that gives you a grade depending on the amount of points you earn, and this is dependant on getting high combos and finding all of the level's secrets. When you get to the end of a level, you need to run all the way back to the entrance before time runs out which further encourages you to master the controls. The movement is the heart and soul of the gameplay, and it passes with flying colors.Even past the controls themselves, almost every single level has a unique gimmick or quirk associated with it, and I truly never felt like I was playing the same level twice. There's only a handful of levels in the game, but they're so uniquely designed and are so distinct from one another that it will surprise you with the mechanics it introduces until the very end, and that is the testament of excellent level design.Basically, Pizza Tower is worthy of all the praise it's gotten. I was skeptical of it at first admittedly, but those doubts were cast away instantly, and is one of the best indie games I've played in a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna preface this review by saying that I had never got into Pizza Tower before its final trailer dropped in December of last year. I'd seen thumbnails for videos about it over the years, but never really bothered to look into it that much until it was a month away from release. Despite all of that, this is my GOTY for 2023 and if it isn't yours too, what's wrong with you?Pizza Tower is pure insanity, a platformer mostly inspired by the Wario Land series that still is able to forge its own identity through its gameplay and style. Every level could honestly have about an hour of gameplay for a first time player, as you've got 3 achievements to grab in it, toppings to collect, the treasure to find, and that's not even getting started on S and P ranks. Everything about Pizza Tower just oozes charm from every angle, the artstyle is insane and clearly inspired by 80s and 90s cartoons such as Ren and Stimpy, with character's bodies contorting and melding to whatever the artists think is funny really. The music is one of the best soundtracks I've heard in a long time, even rivalling some of my all time favourites like Super Meat Boy with how crazy the tracks can get. And the game's charm even comes down to the protagonist himself. The aptly named Peppino Spaghetti is a joy to control, and half of the fun of the game is just watching whatever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane thing is going to happen to him next, whether that be getting his ass lit on fire or getting crushed down to fit into a pizza box, he's seemingly immortal.Pizza Tower also rounds out with one of the best final levels in a game I've experienced, despite being from a game about a balding Italian trying to save his pizza business from a big pizza with a face. (whose name is Pizzaface, of course.) I honestly can't recommend this game enough to anyone who's a fan of platformers, it'll likely remain as my Game of the Year for the entire year unless something ends up trumping it.Do yourself a favour and get this game as soon as you can, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: What can be said about Pizza Tower that hasn't been said yet?Simply put, the game is a perfect capture of Wario Land 4 and adds so much of its own charm. Pizza Tower outshines WL4 by having some of the best controls a platformer. It may feel clunky at first, but once you learn every piece of movement, the game flows so well and gives an INCREDIBLE sense of control. No recent platformer has held a candle to it. Pizza Tower's art style make it stand out among other recent indies. The OST is an absolute banger. Just about every song is unique and catchy. Pizza Time should be engraved into gaming OST hall of fame.Casually beating the game is worth the price but going for 100% gives a new drive, if you can handle it. P ranks will test all your skills in controlling Peppino. The thrill of getting your first P rank is the move exhilarating experience I've had in years. Perfecting a stage gives an incredible sense of accomplishment. Everyone should attempt to P rank the first stage, John Gutter, for an idea of the challenge.Pizza Tower is a must play for anyone curious. Pick it up even for the smallest consideration. Pizza Tower will not disappoint.

The scoring works for speed and not getting hit as well as collecting all collectibles, there's isn't much challenge as it all comes down to end score rather than difficulty of the course, you can get hit and fail as much as you can as long as you beat the end timer. This is what put me off, as you'll have to replay the same level to discover all collectibles and path to them, then go thought the level as fast as you can without getting hit. Which is overall fine, but did not find it interesting enough where difficulty is in the score. The game is still good enough for a simple playthrough, it might be even better if you are into the score and collectibles which are designed nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower ,the spiritual succesor to the classic Wario Land franchise meant to capture and rekindle some of the zany energy that series had to it. This game had been through a long development cycle with  very passionate developers behind it.But did this project live up to the weight of expectations? Let's find out!In the game proper you take control of a struggling buisness owner,,taking a plunge into the pizza tower ,because of an entity threathening his pizzeria. Obviously the first thing you'll notice is probably the most important one in a platformer,the control and movment.The normal walking seems really slippery,althought the game drills the idea of   constant sprinting as soon as the tutorial and the physics  were clearly made with the intent of maintaining top speed,well when you figure that one out the movment simply clicks,you see how many opportunities for crazy combinations of moves there are and every level transforms into a gigantic playground. The core of this game is definitely rummaging through the halls as fast as you can and it only gets more satisfiying the more you play. It's safe to say that this loop is exquisitely designed.When I first looked at this game I thought ,that the artstyle seemed crude and unusual.Well it's clearly an intentional effect ,the vibrant locals  paired with the expressive characters suit the crazy and wacky tone  set by the gameplay and make for something extremely unique. Further amplifying how smooth it flows.The design obviously incentivizes thinking quickly on your feet , fast reaction and adaptation to new obstacles and going out of your way to scoure for micro improvments.What escapes a first impession and a passing glance is that this title picks up on many key  atributes from the ancient japanese storytelling technique.Hear me out this technique can be applied to more than storytelling. Well Nintendo games have been using it for years now.It is a multi facid word ,where each part of the word represents a stage in progeression,so let's take it one at a time-(), where the mechanics many uses are introduced whether that be a new set of moves,a tranformation of sorts or a new obstacle.-(),where the new mechanics are expanded and the player gets more time to toy around with the concept.-(),where everything the player knew about the powerup or obstacle gets used in an unconventional way,subverting the players expectations.-(conclusion,resolution),where the player is asked to use the knowlege they've gathered throuought their playthrought in a final test of their abilities.With this information you can see its inspiration on the design of every level..Personaly I really like games that incorporate this philosophy ,because it makes for a good expirience. The music goes for an energetic feel,but still stays very waried in genre with some rock,electronic,acapella and ambient tracks among others. The sound effects are mostly goofy and silly mimicking  something like an old cartoon.Generally the music and audio is well done and enhances everything brought on by the other aspects.I am going try and blaze through the remainder of my thougts as fast as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 pound pizza dough, at room temperature for at least 1 hour1/2 to 1 cup sauce: tomato sauce, white sauce, or other spread2 to 3 cups other toppings: sautéed onions, sautéed mushrooms, pepperoni, cooked sausage, cooked bacon, diced peppers, leftover veggies, or any other favorite toppings1 to 2 cups shredded or sliced cheese (4 to 8 ounces) such as mozzarella, Monterey Jack, provolone, fontina, or any other favoriteCornmeal or all-purpose floueeer (optional)Heat the oven to 550°F or higher. Arrange a rack in the lower-middle part of the oven (if you have a baking stone, place it on the rack) and heat the oven to 550°F or higher. Don't be afraid to really crank the heat up to its highest setting, as the high heat will help make a crunchier and more flavorful crust. Let the oven heat for at least 30 minutes.Divide the dough in half. One pound of dough makes 2 (10-inch) pizzas. Divide the dough in half and cover one half with an upside-down bowl or a clean kitchen towel while you prepare the first pizza.Método #1: Pizza Baked on Parchment: Tear off a large piece of parchment paper roughly 12 inches long. Working with one piece of the dough at a time, form it into a large disk with your hands and place it on the parchment. Use your hands or a rolling pin to flatten the dough until it is 1/4-inch thick or less. If the dough starts to shrink back, let it rest for 5 minutes and then continue rolling.Método #2: Pizza with Cornmeal or Harina and a Baking Stone: Sprinkle a handful of cornmeal or flour on a pizza peel or on an upside-down rimmed baking sheet. Working with one piece of the dough at a time, form it into a large disk with your hands and place it on the peel. Use your hands or a rolling pin to flatten the dough until it is 1/4-inch thick or less. Shake the peel or baking sheet frequently as you shape to make sure the dough isn't sticking. If the dough starts to shrink back, let it rest for 5 minutes and then continue rolling.Método #3: Pizza Baked on a Baking Sheet: Brush a thin film of olive oil on a baking sheet. Working with one piece of the dough at a time, form it into a large disk with your hands and place it on the baking sheet. Use your hands or a rolling pin to flatten the dough until it is 1/4-inch thick or less. If the dough starts to shrink back, let it rest for 5 minutes and then continue rolling.Top the pizza. Spoon half of the sauce onto the center of the pizza and use the back of the spoon to spread it out to the edges. Pile on half of the toppings and half of the cheese.Bake the pizza. Using a pizza peel or the back side of a baking sheet, slide your pizza (with the parchment or with the cornmeal) onto the baking stone. If you don't have a baking stone, bake the pizza right on the baking sheet. Bake for 5 minutes, then rotate the pizza. If using parchment, slide it out from under the pizza and discard. Bake until the crust is golden-brown and the cheese is melted and browned in spots, 3 to 5 minutes more.Slice and serve. Transfer the pizza to a cooling rack and let cool slightly, just until you're able to handle it. Transfer to a cutting board, slice into pieces, and serve. Repeat making a second pizza with the remaining dough, cheese, and toppings.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Platformer since Super Mario World and Yoshi's Island. The gameplay and animation is so smooth and refined, you can really tell they spent 5 years perfecting it.The soundtrack is surprisingly a big highlight, a lot of the time I have to do a double take and ask myself what I'm listening to? 'They're using whistling as a backing track and I'm somehow still tapping my toes to it!?' The music covers a wide variety of genres yet still sticks to a general 90's electronic soundfont kept together by a killer electronic guitar, the crisp dough elevates it all. Filled with so many left field bangers, I find something new to like about it any time I come back to it. And the music really elevates the gameplay and theatrics, especially that final boss fight. :3Gameplay wise aside from a solid foundation and mobile moveset, the game emphasises speed and exploration a lot like the old sonic the hedgehog games only I think it balances the speed aspect much better. In the gameboy advance sonic games they really pumped up the speed you could go as sonic but this ultimately led to a lot of frustration as you would end up running into enemies, obstacles or off a cliff before you could react leading to frustrating deaths and punished going fast. Pizza tower does two things to rectify this 1) once you reach a certain speed enemies will get scared of you and allow you to simply barrel through them at mach speed which allows you to keep flow and is very satisfying. 2) It removes any health or life system, enemies can only take away points rather than kill you in regular levels and falling off a cliff just takes you back to the start of the current room rather than ending the level. Instead the difficulty is moved to the end of the level where you must race back to the start of the level, rewarding you for memorising it and encouraging you to go back as fast as possible on the route you know. Each escape has enough time for the best of player's to run it through twice which leaves a generous window for anyone to complete the level whilst still requiring some small skill to get through it. Optional difficulty is provided by offering higher ranks by getting the most points or completing a second lap of each escape sequence so it has something to challenge all skill groups. Additionally the addition of being able to run up walls allows you to keep your momentum in some way rather than always grinding you to a halt. Though you must still beware of certain obstacles in your way designed to stop you.Each level has a unique power up or gimmick that makes it stand out. Impressively it's hard to find a power up that get's stale, outlives it's welcome or is straight up unfun. In fact I kind of wish there were some remixed levels that reused power ups from other levels just to get more use out of them. The only stage and gimmick I didn't really like was pizzascare which I think is a worse version of an earlier level, that could use another pass though I can't quite place my finger on what I don't like about it. Perhaps, just how much it interrupts the flow of movement?Art wise the game also throws me for a loop. Everything looks like it was made in MS Paint, yet it's overflowing with charm and attention to detail. Every enemy and character is given their own expression typical of 90's over-exaggerated cartoon character's drawn specifically off model at times for comedic effect. Each level leans 100% into it's theme and provides a visual feast and wavy wires and pastel colours, filled with plenty of details that capture the imagination. Some offering hints to the greater story and world behind a rather simple platformer. Of course I wouldn't cap this section off without discussing how great each of the boss character's were such as the annoying yet childishly charismatic Noise, each boss was entertaining to watch as much as fight against, wish we got to see more of them.I find it hard to complain about this game really. The main things are that the game is a little short and that there were a lot of cool ideas cut from the game (for quality control reasons I imagine). But there's plenty of ideas that I think could really work with more itme in the oven. For example at one point we were supposed to be able to play as some of the boss characters such as the Noise, Vigilante and Pepperman with their own movesets much like how Gustavo and Brick appear as another playable character. These would have given us more screentime with these characters as well as created mroe replay value being able to go through the same levels with different characters. Worse still is the exclusion of Snikch, a character who controls like Sonic the Hedgehog would have been perfect for a speed based platformer like this especially since this game has really improved on said speed formula. After being so used to peppino's moveset, more playable character's would add so much to replay value, though I understand it would be very difficult to tailor all levels to all character's. Old sonic games were trivialised when you played as Tails after all.Also coop, coop would be a great addition you cowards. If DLC does come out in the future I would love to see all these cut additions, maybe cut levels too like the fabled mansion.Overall I was really impressed by everything on display with this game. Whilst due to the nostalgic 90's nature it does remind me of classics such as Yoshi's Island, Sonic and Mario I stand by what I said. Objectively I think it's the best platformer since those games and I'm anxiously awaiting what DLC or new titles Tour De Pizza will make in the future.For it's price tag I would definitely recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is nothing short of gaming perfection in the platformer gerne. Watching this game since 2018 and slowly develop into this beast of a platformer has been one of the greatest honors that I had the pleasure of experiencing all the way to the end. I got the honor of playtesting it later on.Peppino moves like an absolute ballistic missile. His moveset is at first a bit hard to grasp, but once you sort of understand his incredible versatile moveset, you will hop, skip and jump across every pit like no other. It reminds me about the best parts of Rayman Legends, Origins and even Sonic, where I would even argue Pizza Tower does this fast gameplay even better than the titles described. Once you master Peppino, there is no stopping you. The levels encourage you even at times to go through absolute insane speeds, and the fast gameplay absolutely helps in the game staying unique and being its own thing, even if it wears the Wario Land title on its sleeve. It does so for all of the right reasons.The game is chuck full of fun easter eggs and goofy animations that were lovingly handcrafted. Peppino, the enemies, the environment, and the bosses are all incredibly expressive and full of that Saturday 90s cartoon flavour that has been missing since forever. There is a certain charm to this game that becomes immediately apparent once you spend a few hours in the game. There is an enemy in the hub specifically made to just mess with you, the Granny pizza constantly switches between somewhat useful tips and telling you that you go to hell if you hurt Peppino too much, and you even use your own allies as a weapon later on.The soundtrack are all hits in their own right and worth listening to. I cannot believe that a silly funny Pizza game rocks such a banger of a soundtrack, not to speak of the absolute epic finale songs that will never get tiring even after the 10th time I play it.Pizza Tower has been an absolute joy to follow, and now that it is finally out, I can say that trusting the devs to make the best game possible was right. Pizza Tower is perfect. A game practically made for me. A joyride from start to finish.Take your arm sleeves, pull them up, and go get that tower. You will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultrakill, Outer Wilds, Spiritfarer. Pizza Tower has something very important in common with those games, and that is its status as a game that everyone puts off playing for FAR too long when you consider how everyone that does play it falls in love with it.This game is f*cking amazing.Not only is there an absurd amount of high quality level design and content (which is no small thing for a platformer) there's boss fights that are genuinely tests of your skill and EXTREMELY fun to do. The final boss is an absolute treat.At 20 bucks its hard to say anything negative because there is no part of this game thats lacking. The art direction is just... unhinged. Its got that Ren and Stimpy/late night 90's cartoon crackhead energy where everything is exaggerated to the Nth degree and it all feels so lovingly animated that its easy to get caught up looking at how funny things look and then accidentally lose your combo. I'm definitely not speaking from experience. The fact that each main level manages to commit to a new core mechanic for that one level to keep the gameplay fresh while remaining true to its roots is amazing. There wasn't a single level where I felt like the "gimmick" was annoying, it was always a welcome iteration on a really great base. This is legitimately what Sonic the Hedgehog wishes it was. Sonic games are very focused around maintaining speed after learning the layout, meaning that a first run through of a level is less about gunning through it and more about finding the right route to come back through it. Pizza Tower, and I really don't know how they got it to work this way, but this game is able to really let you just gun it through the level at Mach 10 even if you haven't seen it before. There's a great level of attention to detail in the level design that really promotes going fast as hell and Peppino isn't f*ckin around, this dude has w h e e l s.Platformers are one of my favorite genres of game, and this is effortlessly in the conversation for best of the best along with Celeste and a flurry of other 2d platformers. The fact that I can say that after one measly playthrough should impart just how high quality this really felt cover to cover, because 2d platformers are a tried and tested genre, and to be able to immediately come onto the scene and set yourself apart is insane. Pizza Tower is a celebration of aesthetic, of crazy fast, crazy fun platforming, and its absolutely worth the cash. I "beat" the game in 6 hours but I only found one secret level, didn't go for any achievements, and didn't go for any P-ranks. There's a lot of mileage left on this game for me.If nothing else, go give the soundtrack a listen, every single level has an absolute bop to go along with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember Wario Land? Remember Newgrounds? Remember weird, quirked up indie games that seem to come out of nowhere but have been in development for, like, five years?Okay that last one isn't really a throwbackWell, Pizza Tower is another entry to a steeped history of long-lived passion projects released by (possibly racist) indie developers! This game is ! While it for sure can be thought of as a spiritual successor to Wario Land 4, it actually shares more in common with the DNA of your average 2D Sonic game. Sure, it has a similar move set and it superficially has the same core objectives as Wario Land 4, but the moment to moment gameplay is far more dependent on the momentum management and slick moveset of a typical 2D Sonic game. That said, while this game is fantastic, I actually  think it's necessarily for everyone, including myself. While I enjoyed the game, and played it to the end credits, I actually found the chaotic level structure and elaborate moveset difficult to get the hang of. I would find myself reaching a satisfying flow state of dashing, jumping, and taking out enemies for only a few moments before hitting a (literal) wall or otherwise falling out of rhythm. Even by the time I reached the end, I never felt like I really reached competency with the moveset, let alone  it. This, certainly, is a symptom of my own perilously smooth brain, and others who are more used to these sorts of games may acclimate to it better. I am sure this game would be immensely satisfying to play properly if I put the time into learning it, which I will not do.What I will do, however, is obsessively listen to the soundtrack for this game. Say what you will about the gameplay, but the art style of this game in undeniably rich, channeling the combined asthetic of Wario Land, Newgrounds animations and edgy 90s cartoons. The soundtrack is great in isolation, and feels mostly contextually appropriate in each level. Playing Pizza Tower feels like hearing an inside joke you're not privvy to. The game defies explanation and leaves the bulk of interpretation to you. Why is this tower here? Who are these characters? Are Italians real? All questions left to you to answer. And you know what? The game is better for it.Pizza Tower is a good game. It's a good game that I'm bad at. Watch the trailer, if you enjoy fast paced, momentum based platformers, it doesn't get better than this. If you don't... I dunno, maybe get it on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is a masterpiece indie platformer. It's just as good if not better than all the greats you can think of (Shovel Knight, Cave Story, Freedom Planet, Celeste, y'know the ones). Having just finished the game with 6.9 hours, I am legally obligated to write a review. So... let me tell you what makes Pizza Tower so great!+ Perfectly emulates the satisfying gameplay of hit GBA platformers like Wario Land 4 and Sonic Advance, but cranks up the speed, punch, and depth to absurd degrees.+ Speaking of absurd, this game will make your stomach hurt laughing. I am not going to do you the disservice of spoiling any of the jokes or setting any expectations.+ Following in the footsteps of all the indie greats before it, Pizza Tower has an absolutely immortal ost that incorporates seemingly every genre of sound. Every boss theme is a banger (ESPECIALLY the final boss), the escape music is a dissertation of both hype and anxiety, and every level track slaps your mama (mia).+ No two levels play the same. Every stage incorporates some new and absurd gimmick that is usually unique to that level, and uses it in just about every method possible before you cross the finish line.+ The game is challenging, but not punishing at all. Peppino has infinite health outside of boss battles, so the only thing you ever stand to lose is your combo... and sense of self-worth as Peppino stares at you grudgingly at the end of level ranking screen. Just don't run out of time fleeing the level!+ A legendary ending with one of the best final stages ever.+ The pixel art in this game is just as gorgeous as it is ridiculous. Pizza Tower explodes with color and has more expression than pretty much any other platformer I've played.+ The game has a lot of replay value for achievement hunters and completionists, but even for only one full playthrough it is more than worth the price.As far as indie games go, this one is a 10/10 for sure. It accomplishes emulating everything it sets out to and establishes it's own ideas with perfection. Pizza Tower is unfair to every other indie game of 2023, because it's already stolen indie game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is the greatest platformer of 2023 and a contender for my #1 game of 2023. I have never played a Wario Land game but you do not need to to truly appreciate this masterpiece. The movement has a messy and uncontrollable feel to it, at first its gonna feel a little weird controlling Peppino, but once you learn his moveset he becomes a weapon of destruction. It is so satisfying blasting all the way to the other side of the map, making split second jumps and turns, obliterating any enemy that is unlucky enough to be in your path. There is also another character that is playable in 2 out of the 19 levels in this game, yet he is given an entirely unique and in-depth moveset that is also fun to control.Every level has a unique theme to it, theres a level where you go to space, a level where you play golf, a level where you go to a chuck e cheese and get jumpscared by animatronics, the creativeness is off the charts. in each level you have one goal: get in, destroy the John Pillar, get out before Pizza Face shows up and kills you. The escape sequence isnt just doing the level in reverse, other paths open up and the old ones close, leading to entirely new rooms. You are also on a timer, if the timer reaches zero Pizza Face shows up and will start chasing you, immediately killing you if you touch him. The real fun of Pizza Tower comes in getting a high rank in the game, finding all the secrets, getting the hidden treasure, doing a Lap 2 for extra points, doing ALL OF THAT on top of keeping a continuous combo going for that sacred P rank, all while the music builds up in intensity. This is a game that DESERVES to be 100% completed.To continue on that "creativeness" point, its not just the levels. The entire game oozes with style and charm, and just by looking at a single screenshot that is immediately obvious. The way the characters look, their over-the-top movements and expressions, the humor. Half the time Peppino always looks like he's about to ♥♥♥♥ himself. The third boss of the game is called The Noise and he flips you off after he attacks. There is a character dressed up in a tower outfit that is literally called "Pizza Tower Guy" that shows up in every single level and disappears when you get close to him or a minute passes, and there is absolutely zero explanation about him. You can tell the developers put their heart and soul into this game, and they enjoyed every single minute of it.Incredible game man.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to highlight some of the things that I believe make Pizza Tower truly stand out. I'm so glad to see it getting some of the recognition it deserves and I hope that it continues to flourish just like the other breakout indie hits of years prior.- Peppino's moveset is not only impressively varied for the minimal control scheme, but he can perform actions incredibly fast. For any situation you come across, there's always a way to make it look smooth and impressive, often multiple ways to do so.- This game is keyboard friendly! I found the default controls a bit awkward but could easily change them so I could enjoy luxuries of both comfort and precision- The levels accommodate all skill levels of players quite well. Yes there is a sort of 'exam' in the form of escape sequences, but everything leading up to that point can be played as casually or as hardcore as you like. The escape sequences are quite lenient anyways - Unique power-ups exist in each level changing the fundamentals of Peppino's move-set. They freshen up the gameplay and are tethered to normal Peppino's movement, so there isn't a single one which feels bad or disruptive.- Obstacles which are unique to the individual levels can often be taken advantage of to help you speed through the finish!- Peppino's functionality at both high and low speeds combined with the many tools he has at his disposal makes even the bosses of Pizza Tower an absolute joy.- None of the secrets felt unreasonably hidden, and they reward you with a fun little segment for some bonus points for having found them.- The P ranks are where all of the aforementioned traits come together for a truly amazing experience. On several occasions I thought that one level was rather weak compared to the others until having attempted P ranking it.- Outstanding music, sound, and graphic design. Pizza Tower is such a wacky world with charming characters, enemies, and bosses. It's amazing how much character is packed into the few scenes everyone is in all without ever exchanging a bit of dialogue.- Peppino's animations deserve special recognition, they make all of his moves flow together seamlessly, make running at high speeds extremely cathartic, and cement taunts as a core feature of the game.- The ranking system is a bit odd. Getting a D rank is almost certainly intentional, C, B, A, and S care about collectibles more than anything, and then P rank is a massive leap above S in terms of difficulty.- The game doesn't make it clear what constitutes a P rank anyways. Those requirements being that you must do all optional objectives and start a combo without ever dropping it. I was certain I was meeting all of the requirements for one level, but discovered a hidden third requirement which is to kill an enemy in the starting room. Numerous attempts which were otherwise valid had been wasted from this simple bit of misinformation.- There are semi-optional collectibles that give you cash needed to unlock boss doors to progress but you can only miss a few per floor to have enough to progress. As a result, I tend to see a lot of them out in the open requiring little to no change in route at all. Some of these can't be backtracked to either so you have to restart the whole level for another chance at them.

_childDocuments_.review: really cool game, i recommend going as blind as possible, not for story reasons but just to enjoy all the wacky stuff the game throws at you. it's marketed as being inspired by wario land 4, but it also uses the best elements from the 2d sonic games and mario galaxy. i beat this game in about 21 hours (the other 20 are from leaving the computer on all night and day with this running) and it never runs out of new ideas. my first time playing, after beating the first floor i went back to level 1 and spent a few hours just on the first level trying to get it perfect, that's how addictive it was, and I'm definitely not bored of it still. play it now if this seems fun!!! the price put me off at first but for the amount of time i got on a blind playthrough I'd say it was well worth full price (i got it with a gift card, thank you jeff)my one criticism of the game is that while it adopts a mario galaxy like formula, it doesn't have the full benefit of this: you almost the maximum amount of main collectibles you get in the levels, there's 5 per level and in total to beat the game you can't skip more than 9... so really you can only skip 1 level. what made the 3d mario collectathons so good is that if you didn't like a level you could skip it. I give this some slack since this is an indie game and making more extra levels just to have a 70/120 requirement of completion is a lot more work, and I loved all the levels (except maybe golf), though it would have been nice to come back to some of them later. this is very minor though; if the art style and raw gameplay looks appealing enough then the whole game should be enjoyable. the art and music are all very good, while not groundbreaking the music very much compliments the fun cartoony style very well and provides the right mood at basically every part. the humour of this game was also really good, you won't be feeling lots of emotions but the game is funny a lot and occasionally scary (in a funny way)the difficulty is really awesome. it increases at a pretty good rate, and just beating the game any% is a decent enough challenge without being too frustrating. since taking damage usually doesn't matter, you can explore the levels at your own pace, before having to race back through with slight detours (this mechanic taken directly from wario land 4, which should be in way more games). the difficulty increases as you go for better ranks though, and you're rewarded not just with little badges but with the exhilerating feeling you get from mastering the movement and seeing your little man rampage through the levels unimpeded. this is one of those games people went absolutely rabid for, but it has been a really fun time. now to get all those pizza ranksmy name is jeff (doing this for a badge i think)

Every level is bumping with funky tunes, the animation is made by some sicko drawing Newgrounds Da Vinci in MS Paint (animations are as wacky as they are fluid), but what really strikes me is the fact that it feels like every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ level has a DIFFERENT PEPPINO POWER UP so in one you're rolling around in this smooth ass barrel, or you're turning yourself into a pepper-powered ghost or just GUN. So since every level looks, sounds, and PLAYS completely different the game never stops being as fresh as the chef's ingredients.Even just setting aside the pure effort playing it feels like a dream since once you get a hang of the controls its just pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ momentum and violence against various foodstuffs and themed inhabitants, that turns into ultra-violence and hyper-momentum once you reach the end of the level and turn back. Great stuff and I'm only saddened it'll be 6 more years until the dev can put something like this out againEDIT: I have since P Ranked every level and the sheer momentum and tension of keeping that combo going is unrivaled in any other platformer I've ever played. _childDocuments_.review: At first glance it seems like a platformer in the vein of something like Celeste, but it's much more accessible and gives you a good feeling of being able to take the game at your own pace and set your own goals for performance. The art style, music, character design and overall vibe are amazing and the creator managed to make something that feels unique and interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Pizza Tower

_childDocuments_.review: Pizza Tower is what you get when you study a formula of a game franchise for 5 years and perfect it to the point of it feeling smooth like butter. You play as Peppino Spaghetti (SAD!) and you need to take down the evil Pizzaface to save your restaurant, along the way collecting treasures and fighting bosses. The gameplay of Pizza Tower is one of my favourite feels of a loop ever. Run through the stage get all the toppings and then rush back to the beginning like Wario Land 4. Each level has its own unique gimmick and it feels very fresh to just go from level to level without stopping, its very fun and highly addictive. In addition at the end of every world you get to fight the boss which is a nice palette cleanser if you've been wanting something else new among the other stuff I have stated.The soundtrack of this game is absolutely outstanding. Crust Cove, Unexpectancy, and Cold Spaghetti are absolute BANGERS. If you can get this game spend an extra bit for the soundtrack.9.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it.What? Still need convincing?BUY IT!Still? Alright fine.This zany game has you running through platforming levels to collect goods (called Toppins), and then dashing back out as fast as you can. If you've played Wario Land 4, you know how this goes. Unlike Wario Land 4, Pizza Tower is about speed. All of Peppino's (the protagonist) movement options are about building up speed or re-directing it. Even better is that these movements transition seamlessly from one to another. Once you're comfortable with the controls and the environment, Peppino is poetry in motion.The graphics all look like they were done in MS Paint, but in contrast, the animations are buttery smooth, full of character, and hilarious. There isn't anybody who can emote better than Peppino. The soundtrack parallels this perfectly. It is funky overall, except when it isn't. Then it goes HARD. Or weird. Or weird and hard. Or weird and hard and funky. It's excellent.This game has a ton of replayability and I haven't even finished it yet. Every level has a number of secrets to find, and you're given a ranking after the level is complete. Remember when I said you have to run from the end of the level back to the beginning under a time limit? You have the option of going full swag and challenging another full lap.So go buy it.There is a button that makes Peppino breakdance.

Not to mention hilarious!Wish I heard about this game earlier so I could have backed it, but I'm more than happy to have bought it now.Outstanding work!(P.S. I don't know if I'm alone in this or not, but if I keep playing for too long I genuinely get hungry for pizza. Is this part of the experience?)

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game in 2019 when the SAGE demo released. It's been about 3 years since then. 3 years of waiting, frequently checking in on social media, and listening to whatever songs made their way over to Youtube. The game is finally out, and the wait was absolutely worth it.The sensation of speed in this game is incredible. Every level is deliberately hand-crafted to let you demolish everything that stands in your way with little to no stops whatsoever. Working your way back through a level during the escape sequences makes this especially clear. Once you're moving fast enough, enemies are literally stunned and occasionally even scream as they see how quickly you're approaching them, dropping their guard or their weapons in the process and essentially becoming living targets. All the while a killer track is driving you forward.Every one of Peppino's moves chains seamlessly into the next, making it practically effortless to retain maximum speed. Overall I'm not sure I've ever played a game that does this better.Pizza Tower personality out of every greasy, cheesy surface. Peppino is animated in such wacky and wonderful ways for everything he does. When you're not moving, he's constantly shuffling in place, trying to calm himself down, or biting his hand anxiously. Sometimes he does a little dance number for less than a second. Peppino is never idle, even when you are.Enemies, bosses, even collectibles are all similarly lively. Backgrounds are filled with fun little details and the art direction as a whole is weird and vibrant.Your dedicated taunt button doubles as a parry move, and when you build enough of a combo you can preform a Super Taunt that wipes enemies from the screen. You can also hold the taunt button for a few seconds and Peppino will pull out a boombox and begin to breakdance.I could talk about how phenomenal the soundtrack for this game is but I think instead you should just go give it a listen on Bandcamp. There's not a bad track in the mix. Some recommendations: and for obvious reasons, but also some slightly less insane tracks like  or or . This is easily one of my favorite game soundtracks. Fits the game perfectly and can definitely be listened to on its own.In terms of sound effects they're all really well done, The sounds for charging and releasing a Super Jump are fun, and I like all of the little collectible jingles. As mentioned previously certain characters have associated -style screams and there's a whole host of other cartoon-inspired sounds to be heard throughout.In conclusion, this is just a handful of things that I like about this game, there's a lot to love about it and I think if you're a fan of platformers or fast and frenetic movement then I HIGHLY recommend you give this a try.TL;DR: now....

_childDocuments_.review: On average, it'll take you about 4 hours to beat this game. For the true ending, maybe 6. For a completionist run, you'll probably beat it in about 30-ish hours. So why do I have over 42 hours? Because to me, it's not a game you simply *beat.* It's a game that you *enjoy.* And I haven't enjoyed a game this good since the series it took inspiration from: Wario Land. As usual, TL;DR at the bottom.Rather you're a casual player who just likes a fun and engaging time, or a speed demon seeking a reason to make your brain rattle in your head, Pizza Tower aims to please everyone both in and out of the scope of the game. While it won't take much convincing to get people to buy the game--there's a LOT of other reviews that are better than my own--people hear about how great this game is, but not exactly why.• The hype. Six people in one day, two of which were in my stream's chat, recommended me this game as a game "you have to play." I'm very picky with my games. I don't just play them because others tell me to, and for once, I'm glad that I did. This game DESERVES its Overwhelmingly Positive review and if there was a rating higher than that, I'd make it my mission to get there.• The gameplay. As mentioned above, this game caters to both casual players and speedrunners alike, and excels in making both audiences happy. If you feel like exploring the area, admiring the art and the funny characters/enemies, the game will not force you to hurry up--that is, until it's time to escape the level. It encourages people to try and flex their perfection bone (to go faster, to go harder, and to move better) but it doesn't *demand* it. While you will be rewarded handsomely for going faster, nobody is forcing you to but you.As far as the game -itself- goes, if you're here because you saw that it's "like Wario Land but better": I'm here to say that the rumor is 200% true. This game is Wario Land 3 & 4 dipped in Pop Rocks and cocaine, liquidized and ready to be injected straight to your arms. • The soundtrack, and oh my god, the soundtrack. There isn't a single song in this game that misses, ranging from the opening movie, to the hub area, to the stages, to the secret areas, all the way to the *♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥* pause menu. HUGE ups to the composers, because when I finally got around to streaming this game, it got to a point where I turned the SFX off on some stages *JUST* to show off the music while I played.(Personal recs are Cold Spaghetti, Oregano Mirage, Tropical Crust, and Wudpecker to name a few.)• Anti-frustration, a big point. You know how in some Sonic levels, you'll go really really REALLY fast, just to get dead-ended by some random wall spikes or fall into a pit or some other dumb stuff? You know how in games with separate characters, you'd play a totally different character that just took away any rhythm or flow you have? Not in this game. Enemies that would normally attack you cower in fear of Peppino as he sprints, and the free range of movement allows you to turn the very environment into your playground. When you get to play as the sidekicks Gustavo & Brick, they have their own moveset that works in their stages--but not so different from Peppino that it takes away all of your flow. If anything, it seeks to keep your flow going--to try something new, but familiar.**TL;DR** Peppino Spaghetti, a nervous wreck that is a force to be reckoned with, teams up with his friend Gustavo to lay the serious hurt on some cheesy-lookin' mf who picked the wrong day to be alive. With their incredible speed, boombox full of bangers and no time to lose, they will make 100% sure these hands get delivered in 30 minutes or less. Y'all ready to get funky?

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games ever created. For starters, the design of the game is incredible. From the graphics to the music, everything is perfect. The art style is one-of-a-kind and, I don't like to use this word often, honestly perfect. You can easily distinguish what things are instantly which is very important for a game like this, the animations are dynamic and fluid and everything feels great overall. The music and sound design is also good, making this game feel VERY punchy/fast with how powerful some noises are. Music and artstyle has INCREDIBLE variety, with some parts of the game having subtle, hard-to-notice details and some that are in your face. There is a vast amount of hidden details in the art and sound design. A LOT of care went into making this game look and sound good.The gameplay is nothing short of perfect... unless you're a completionist. I think getting S and P rank should be a LITTLE bit easier, as well as maintaining combos. getting all the achievements for a level pretty much requires you to know it inside and out (I don't mean the secrets and toppings, those are fine). Boss battles are greatly designed and going fast and destroying everything in your way feels incredible because of how the game looks and sounds. The mechanics all build on each other perfectly and are simple enough so that you can remember what they do. THIS GAME HAS SO MUCH VARIETY!!! I was shocked to see how radically different every level was from one another. 2D games have never been this good.That's where the review ends, really. This game is just so jam-packed with creativity and great gameplay, with amazing music and visuals to back it up. I am going to keep this review simple because I REALLY think people should play this game for themselves. One issue I had, though, which I REALLY want the developers to fix is controller inputs. Ground slams and dives SUCK on controller because you need to input down on your controller as if you were playing on keyboard or using a directional arrows pad. It feels terrible on a thumbstick. Not sure how the developers let that through since it's a huge issue that hurts the core of this game. Must act quickly!
