_childDocuments_.review: I dunno I really wanted to like it, but there's just one big problemOn one hand the game has a really good understanding on how to use its mechanics to create leniency but also challenge appropriate to both initial and repeat playthroughs.One interesting element is how the player can control the game's pace. While as Peppino the player is intended to maintain momentum by running and never stopping, many of the moves—particularly the ones that have you changing directions—have the player pause for a brief moment to let them get their bearings and take stock of their surroundings. This helps the game flow better when you’re getting used to the mechanics and learning the level layout as it makes it much easier to go quickly while keeping enough awareness of what's ahead to not crash.This serves a dual purpose however, as on repeat playthroughs where you attempt to get the best rank on levels, where you are already familiar with the mechanics and level layout, the challenge comes from trying to cut out as many of these pauses as possible. While you can use the super jump to send yourself upwards, you can climb the wall instead to go faster. While you can stop and do a belly flop, you can smoothly transition into a powerbomb instead. The simplistic catch-all moves have brief pauses, while the more complex and context specific ones can be done more smoothly and without slowing down. You gradually learn new techniques to go faster and faster.There is a great depth to the player and levels that gives the game fantastic replay value, keeping it engaging and fun even as you play the same levels over and over to get the best ranks, because the way you traverse the level will naturally change as repeated runs give you a greater understanding of it.To put a bit more emphasis on how the level design demonstrates this, there’s this bit in Don’t Make a Sound that I really liked where on repeated P rank attempts I slowly discovered that in one of the rooms I could activate the mushroom animatronic early to destroy some electric blocks without slowing down. However, in order to find that out I had to get past a few layers of abstraction; first discovering that you can destroy them early, then how to do so without slowing down, then how to do so as fast as possible. I slowly pieced this together, experimenting and discovering as I tightened up my execution.Even if I know how the level is structured and where all the enemies are placed, that doesn’t mean I fully understand the best way to get through, or how all of the parts can interact with each other. I find challenging games can quickly become stale once I’ve got the route and execution downpat as repeat runs focus primarily on not making any mistakes, and now I just feel like I’m gambling. I never felt this way with Pizza Tower though, in large part due to the fact that I was often finding faster routes—whether that be by using different moves or different paths—which meant I never had to practice a singular one for too long. It reminds me of Neon White in that sense, however unlike that game Pizza Tower is able to apply a degree of leniency that makes the game both easier for newcomers and intense for veterans.I’ve always found that having a perfect level ranking for players to strive for is a strong way to broaden a games appeal, as it encourages stronger play and allows completionists to challenge themselves but is pretty easily ignored if the player simply isn’t interested. What’s special about Pizza Tower though is the conditions mandated to get a P rank. Each condition significantly tightens the restrictions around more serious players. The lap 2 system gives both casual and completionist players a reasonable amount of time based on their skill level. The combo meter is more of a suggestion for casual players, as it hands out more points for better ranks but losing a combo isn’t a terribly big deal. To get a P rank though, the player needs to keep a singular combo going through the entire level, which always keeps them moving to the next target.What’s very much appreciated about the combo meter though is how getting hit doesn’t necessarily mean you lose the combo. You have a maximum of 7 seconds, killing an enemy or getting points refreshes the timer, getting hit makes you lose 2 seconds.Games like Celeste or Hotline Miami where you die in one hit but checkpoints are everywhere have never quite been my speed because they’re a tad too zen. There’s too much focus on perfect execution, and when I slip up I can immediately relax because I no longer have anything to lose.Slipping up in Pizza Tower doesn’t mean losing your combo, it means you have to desperately scramble to keep your combo. It makes the game more intense as your inconsistency forces you into an unfamiliar situation where you have to adapt. Another way the game keeps itself fresh.The most subtle requirement however is likely the points dynamic. Points are received through killing enemies and collecting the minor collectibles scattered through the level like coins in a Mario game. Smaller amounts are scattered in patterns to guide the player, but many more are hidden in big stashes throughout the level.Because the smaller coin-like collectibles are intended to guide the player along the critical path, the one designed for beginners, the player is going to miss plenty of them as they take shortcuts. This means that they’re already running tight on points, and if they need more they’ll need to find the stashes that can be collected most efficiently to make up for those lost points, encouraging greater familiarity with level layout and flashier play.Further, the player can lose points through taking damage, and if they do they will likely have to get some of the less easy point caches placed later in the level, that may require the player perform a stylish trick or the like. The tension and challenge is enhanced by the fact that they haven’t been practicing that specific trick as they repeatedly attempt the level, and once again the game gets more exciting as the player is forced to adapt to the consequences of inconsistency, not just try again.The game is just really strong mechanically and incredibly thoughtfully put together.On the other hand Noise and Peppingas don’t make out sloppy style and that just says it all does it.2.5 out of 10 -Too much pizza-Too many towers-No gay sex-Honestly I can't possibly harp on this enough, what were they thinking. Absolutely no gay sex. None. Nada. Unbelievable. Is this even a game anymore?So uh yeah its ok i guess but I don't recommend buying it until the sex update.

_childDocuments_.review: I was constantly hearing about how this was one of the best platformers of the era and that I needed to play this game. I played this game and I can definitely conclude that this game was most definitely way overhyped, but that is not to say it is bad per se. It controls well, runs well, has a quirky but still appealing art style and humor to it, the music is good (especially the Pizza Time music) and most of the levels are perfectly serviceable with serviceable boss fights. However, if you want to get the most out of this game, this is a game that takes an extreme level of precision and dedication to get good at and to properly experience everything, which I honestly just wasn't feeling up to doing. This game was alright, but it wasn't quite good enough for me to start no-life'ing this game to get P Ranks in all the levels or get all the collectables. The best way I can describe this is that this game is a speedrunner's paradise. The speeds in which you often get to are incredibly fast, but that becomes part of this game's problem for the average player. You get so fast that it becomes unwieldly unless you've mastered this game and you'll be constantly crashing into walls and losing your speed all the time. You might be like "well if going so fast is so bad, don't go so fast". Well that wouldn't be a problem if the second half of every level didn't require you to make a mad dash for the exit where you're basically on a timer before Pizza Phanto comes to ruin your fun. While admittedly I rarely actually had to deal with the timer running out, forcing myself to constantly go Mach speeds and constantly running into walls all the time made it lose a bit of its fun factor for me. To be able to properly handle the insane speeds the game wants you to go for and to get everything, from what I can gather, requires basically dedicating your life to this game and learning how to speedrun it. If that doesn't sound like your cup of tea, then don't expect to ever get used to the high speeds. Also another thing I don't quite like about this game is how it throws a million different gimmicks at you and hardly fleshes any of them out. I'm pretty sure every level has a different gimmick (I think there was an armor suit in a level in the first world they brought back in a level of the last world, but that is the only recurring gimmick I can think of). You hardly ever get to get good at any of these gimmicks and, by the time you might, the level's over. Most of the gimmicks did control fine at least, but there were a couple gimmicks that drove me up a wall with how annoying they were (I'm looking at you, golf level). I still put this as a "yes" for recommendation since it is perfectly serviceable for a one time playthrough, but unless you're a speedrunner who is willing to no-life this game, don't expect anything particularly amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, if I could, I would give this game a thumbs-side 'cause there are some things I like about it. Y'know it has cool music, smooth animations and all of that but, when it comes to the gameplay ehhhh, I'm not really a big fan of it. For those of you who don't know, the main gimmick of this game is just you going very fast. Or at least, that's what I think it is lolThere's nothing wrong with it on its own, it's just the camera that's the problem. When you are going very fast, the camera would just have the protagonist be in the center of the screen. Making it very hard to see what's in front of us. It doesn't have him be on the side or anything like that, just straight up in the middle. Like why did they made it like this?It would be nice if they zoomed out the camera a bit but, I prefer the "protagonist-on-the-side-of-the-screen-when-he's-going-very-fast" option. Like that's just me. But either way, thanks to the way they set this camera up, the only way to do good in a level is if you memorize it. 'Cause when you're going very fast and your depth of field is limited, you're gonna have to use that temporal lobe. Like that's just the facts.So while I may not recommend this game for the casual audience, I wouldn't even recommend it for the pros either. 'Cause when I say you gotta memorize these levels, I really mean it. For you see, the maximum rank in this game is P-rank and the only way to get it is if you find all the secrets, find the janitor & get him to unlock the door that leads to the level's treasure, do a 2nd lap across the level, all while not dropping your combo. Like what the actual heck? I mean don't get me wrong, this isn't as hard as beating clubstep on geometry dash but still, the amount of times I had to replay a level to find the optimal route where I don't drop my combo and have enough time to do a 2nd lap is ridiculous. All while having low depth of field in which I have to memorize like crazy like what the heck?To make it even worse, some of these levels have different exit paths. So while it may seem you go from point A to point B and then back to point A, sometimes you go back through a different route. Making you have to memorize even more. So while I may respect those who speedrun this game, let alone 100% speedrun it, I didn't freaking sign up for this. I didn't want to get into a game where I have to do diligent training on so many levels just to have fun. Like what the heck?So far, I've gotten P-rank on 3 levels in the 1st floor and after doing so, I now know what the P stands for. Pain. After practicing so much and pressing so many buttons on my keyboard, my fingers started to hurt during the 4th level. And after thinking to myself, "man, is it really worth it getting arthritis over some freaking levels?", I decided to uninstall. So not only did I not enjoy this game casually, I also didn't enjoy it attentively. Ain't that something.My goodness, this is very unfortunate. I didn't want to give this game a thumbs-down because art-wise, this game does a really good job on that. But when it comes to the gameplay aspect of it (which is the main reason why people play videogames in the first place), it's not really that good. It's one of those games where you have to force yourself to play it. Or at least, in my experience it was 'cause I never get excited to come back & play this. It's not like I go all, "Oh boy, I can't wait to go back into this game and crash all the time. As well as falling into hazards since I can't see what's in front of me very well. Like oh boy!" Y'know? Liiiike lolBut anyways yeah, that's my take on it. Creatively it's good like, very good but gameplay-wise, it's a bit average. Not really the best of the bunch. Get Rayman Legends instead.P.S. Some of these levels have fps drops.P.P.S If you don't want to go full speed while running, just hold the sprint button. Do not hold left/right while running. Thought I give that tip out.

_childDocuments_.review: The Long Night "climate catastrophe" mentioned in the Terminal entry is likely the same event the Streetcleaners were invented to fix.Based on the terminal data: 200 years after the start of the Final War, Earth had continued to become inhospitable to all life, so the Earthmovers were repurposed to be the last bastions of humanity.Because of all the ash and soot clouding the skies, the Earthmovers couldn't function without their solar power and began shutting down. Deployment methods to get onto them could've been similar to the way Gutterman and Guttertank, via missile cargo. Or alternatively, they would've installed a hellevator onto the Earthmover while it wasn't looking.The Guttertank's description in the terminal even states that each machine was designed specifically to counter the last, with V1's firmware being last updated around 200 years after World War I started, and the Earthmover's description stating that World War I ended 200 years later.This is further supported by how, at the start of [], the Earthmover stops attacking the Earthmover in the distance in an attempt to attack V1 instead. It could have understood, either through communication with other machines or by not recognizing its design, that V1 was made to destroy it. However, it gets interrupted by the other distant Earthmover, giving V1 a time window to start climbing it.There are signs found across the surface of the Earthmover written in Japanese, implying that it was built by the Japanese during the Final War.

name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead
detailed_description: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead is a single-player horror adventure game inspired by the critically acclaimed blockbuster movie franchise that highlights a unique survivor story after an invasion of deadly creatures. In this exclusive spin-off, experience the journey of a young woman who must endure a treacherous apocalypse in the midst of interpersonal family conflicts, all while coming to terms with her own inner fears. Unnerving Atmosphere -- Experience absolute terror as you strive for silence when hiding from, and sneaking by, horrific creatures who hunt using only sound. Untold Story -- Embark on a dramatic adventure inspired by the A Quiet Place movie franchise as a young survivor trying to navigate the new, eerily tranquil, post-apocalyptic landscape. Uncanny Ingenuity -- Discover your own path through the world by observing your environment and leveraging the tools in your surroundings. A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead features an optional 'Microphone Noise Detection' setting where creatures will react to sounds that you make through a connected microphone or headset. Stay silent to survive!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit to respond to the devs: It's not about the yellow paint, it's about that the game is designed with a single path in mind and all possible player creativity is not allowed. There can be a knee high box somewhere blocking off a path and instead of jumping over it you have to go around the entire map. All because there is no yellow paint on the one box. Same thing with the bricks, there are stones EVERYWHERE that the character could throw, but you're only allowed to throw them when they're painted yellow, all other stones are just decoration and your character would rather die than throw them to distract the monster. Removing yellow paint does not remove the horrible game design. Games should be designed in a way that extreme handholding isn't necessary for your game to be understood by most players. This is a bandaid fix option only there so they can reply to people like me saying "you can remove the yellow paint if you don't like it" rather than making a game where the characters actually act in a way that makes sense.Original review:This is the most boring and annoying game I've ever played. The movies were fun but were full of plotholes. Turns out that the game is no different. The characters are so beyond stupid it's incredibly frustrating. I'm going to list some of the things that annoyed me the most:- For some reason you can't throw any of the rocks that are everywhere. No you have to wait until there are specific YELLOW PAINTED bricks laying around before you can do that. - Speaking of yellow paint, whoever decided to walk around with HUNDREDS of buckets of yellow paint is a hero, there is yellow paint everywhere you need to go. Which turns the game into a silly and stupid mess. "oh there is a knee high object that we could climb over to get to our objective? Better not go over it because there is no yellow paint, instead let's go around the entire map to get to the same place"- There are random red painted barrels, cans, and crates EVERYWHERE. Even in the middle of the forest there are cans scattered all around all painted with the same red paint. If you touch these you make sound and the monster probably kills you.- The main character has asthma which is not in any way important to the story or any character development it's literally only there as a super annoying way to add a stress mechanic which prevents the main character from being close to the monster. - For some reason there are inhalers and pills laying everywhere, literally randomly on the forest floor. - Each inhaler can only be used once when inhalers have TONS of uses IRL.- EVERY SINGLE DOOR in this game is creaky as hell, you have to open them all so slowly. Which is fine at first but when you have to open hundreds of doors to get through the game it's incredibly boring. - The hitboxes for objects that make sound is incredibly wacky, it's way larger than the object seems. So it's easy to step on something when you were trying to go beside it.- The worst thing in the game is how the character dies 90% of the time: You will make a sound which will trigger the monster immediately, this will lock the character in a 10 second long death animation just standing there waiting for her death. Not trying to get to safety, throw a distraction, do LITERALLY ANYTHING to survive, no she just stands there and dies because you broke the gameplay rule.- You can NEVER run in this game. You can never run from the monster to get to safety like a normal person would at least try to.- I lied, there is a SINGLE chase scene where you are suddenly allowed to run from the monster for 20 seconds. This is the only time in the game the main character decides to run and be smart to avoid a certain death situation. The fact that this chase sequence exists makes the previous points so much worse. At least if there was NEVER any running that would be a consistent rule, but no, the character CAN run away from the monster. She just decides to die 99% of the time instead.- There is no creativity in this game besides the initial concept of the movie: meaning a world where there are monsters that kill based on sound. The actual gameplay is so uninspired, literally just walk as slow as possible. Throw bricks. Vault ledges. Lay down planks to get over gaps. Bring around fuses. It's all stuff we've seen 100x in much better games.- The second half of the game is completely lacking any story and there are no character scenes anymore just walking from A to B. It honestly feels like they forgot to add ANY story or conclusion at all into the second half of the game. They set up all these characters in the first half only for none of it to matter at all.- The ending is so cookie cutter and boring I called it from halfway through the game.Please do not waste your money on this.

_childDocuments_.review: *SPOILERS for some game mechanics and the whole story. *RECOMMENDATION FOR FIRST PLAY-THROUGH: Turn off the music and it will remove the awful stingers that constantly annoy when a creature hears you or jumps into frame. It becomes much more immersive.After 1st play-through on Easy difficulty: Finally finished the game and it's ALRIGHT, I'd give it a 6/10, but it's overpriced for the bare-bones amount of game-play you get (for the first 3 hours), has almost zero replay value besides collecting toy ships to unlock concept / character art, and the quality of the story, dialogue and characters ranges from extremely middling to poor. Pros+ Sound design.+ Sound-mechanics (dust, setting down planks, asthma management, etc...)+ Environments are well lit, detailed and suitably atmospheric.+ Mic detection.+ The structure of the game is solid (flipping between 1st day and current day).Issues with the game-mechanics, atmosphere and death animations- Sound mechanics are introduced too slowly.- Death animations jarringly cut from game-play to animation. A better way to have done this would have been to do what Alien: Isolation did. Let you be in control until the Alien reaches you and then blur the background to make the Violent (Key Word - Violent) death stand out more.- Sometimes you make noise / the monster gets alerted even though you can be below the area's sound level or not even moving or looking around AT ALL. It's incredibly annoying.- The stinger that lets you know when you have made too much noise is overly loud / dramatic and takes me out of the experience more than immersing me in it. ^ SOLUTION: Turn off music and it will remove the stinger effects. To know how alert enemies are without the stingers, turn on phonometer assistance in settings.- Multiple notes are strewn about the opening chapter noting the obvious. "Don't make noise." It comes off extremely condescending given that based off of how the character's act, one would figure out that you have to be quiet to survive. The tagline of the first movie is even painted in white on the wall of the lounge area.- Yellow & Red paint (can be disabled though, thankfully)- You can run around nonstop in the ranch and hospital (pre-monster) levels and you won't get killed. It makes sense why (to teach the player about base mechanics) but when you know there is no threat and start to run, it ruins the immersion. I understand that it's raining in the ranch level but come on, a monster would hear someone running. You can also run inside the hospital at no risk of death, which also makes sense game-wise so you can take the environment in. But it doesn't make sense with the mechanics presented in the world. Running doesn't attract a monster but a stupid shove does (to be fair, the dad was shoved through a door and into some supplies).- You aren't able to pick up cans or bottles lying around as a distraction until the FOREST LEVEL. There are clearly so many bins, bottles and cans lying around (with red paint on them) but they are just locked off from being useful until a certain section of the game.- The creature can bump and walk into / over cans or objects but it doesn't react to the noise they make.- The animation for when the creature rams through the wired fence looks jank.- The bear-trap death animation when climbing in through the warehouse window looks laughable due to 1. Your leg doesn't look injured at all and 2. The creature leaps out of nowhere (even though it would have no space to do so since there is a fence behind the window) and clips through the side of the window before killing you.- You can sprint to the pump station (which takes a solid 10-ish seconds) and you won't get caught by the super-fast, leaping creature. I know the movies do this sometimes (running to the hole in Part 2 and running through the building in Day One) but those were enclosed environments with multiple objects that would trip up / confuse the creatures. Why don't any of the creatures just go on top of the train and then leap? I know, I know, it's cool to have a chase sequence but you can't really have one without breaking the immersion.- Just like with the paint and notes in the ranch chapter, multiple notes are placed by you when a new feature is introduced. "Hey ... we can use sand to cover our tracks, neat huh!" or "Hey ... I don't think standing still will cut it." It breaks the immersion and suspension of disbelief.- Flares disappear mysteriously out of your inventory after the pump station level.- Throwables in the pump station glow blue which looks goofy. I know it's to help players see if a throwable is nearby but why in the world would a brick glow blue?- You can hear the creatures clicking in places they shouldn't be, specifically in the town segment (creatures click through the wall when turning the sprinklers back on & they move through shrubs which you wouldn't be able to hear when it's behind a building).- There should've been less inhalers lying around in exchange for them being able to be used multiple times. This would make the world and the capacity of inhalers more believable (inhalers wouldn't be lying around everywhere and they wouldn't all be on their last use).Story issues- Dialogue & story are written poorly.- People have guns in the forest chapter, why? So one of them shoots and can start a tedious monster sequence.- Mark shoves Alex's dad so we can have a stupid way to have a monster come to the hospital.- Alex gets her leg stuck in a tree trunk somehow, did she put her leg directly on the trunk?- Martin's death looks comical and it comes far too early, just to attempt shock value and possibly pay homage to the 1st movie's opening. The problem is that we don't even know or care that much (if at all) about either character yet.- Alex falls asleep with her pregnancy test in her hand. Illogical nonsense that only occurs because the writers couldn't have figured out a better way to cause drama between the main character and Laura.- Alex writes in her notes post Laura-gun-roof cut-scene that she wouldn't hurt her, so why did she back off and cause herself to fall off the roof?- Why do Mark and Laura have guns? Don't they know by now (119 days in) that shooting one is a death sentence?- Maybe I missed how the TV's turned on in the electronics store but from what I got out of that short cut-scene, the door closes which causes the TV's to turn on? Not necessarily a negative but it just confused me.- First of all, how did Laura survive getting hit by a creature and being flung against a cabin? And then how did she catch up to you (while wounded) even though you had to go through trains and pump stations and towns? You pass out and she just drags you (through water) to a safe place. Sure, that's believable.- Ending was fine but a bit anticlimactic. I didn't hate it, didn't love it but it felt like all of the characters were forgotten about. Past the camp segment you're just alone. Doesn't help I totally forgot the dad died like an hour after he got shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm surprised at the Mostly Positive reviews of this game.The first hour is an absolute banger. The sound design, the creature, the fear/anxiety of the world-building in incredibly well done. However, after that, the next 6+ hours are gruellingly monotonous and repetitive. The game uses the same Gameplay loop of restricting the players pacing to a snail's pace, while avoiding an incredibly sensitive and - often times - inaccurate AI creature. The game is full of 'convenient' timings of interactions and plot devices to propel the story forward. As you progress through the game, you learn of various mechanics to help your character progress through an area/zone to avoid the creatures. Unfortunately, some of these game mechanics are introduced way too late in the final act of the game, whereas it could have been beneficial to introduce significantly earlier. It kind of felt like "Oh that would have been great to know 4 hours ago" kind of moments.Don't get me wrong, I think this game had huge potential. It looks amazing, great voice-acting, and sound design was superb. The element holding this game back from achieving greatness simply fell within the Gameplay aspect, and I think that comes with Developer experience within the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a fun game and I played it on hard right from the start. A few criticisms I hope the developers see and take note of, and hopefully patch in the future. Spoilers ahead.INHALERS: While I understand what the developers were going for with the inhaler system, it was absolutely ridiculous how many inhalers I consumed without even sprinting. I went through a whopping 30 inhalers in the span of 2 in game days. That’s with me purposefully avoiding some of the mechanics intended to be used to save even more inhalers… The closer you get to a monster, the faster your lungs get irritated? While cool in concept, this was downright obnoxious in gameplay. I had a monster that wouldn’t leave me alone, causing me to die because my lungs dried out. Yeah there’s a system implemented to give you a chance to win a QTE, but in 11 hours straight of playing, I never succeeded at it once. Maybe tone down the lung mechanic a bit. It’s more like my character is 400lbs and has COPD.THE THROWING: a lot of the times when I’d try to throw an object to distract a death angel, my character’s projected throw path would be shaking back and forth like she was in an earthquake. I had a bunch of times where instead of making a precise throw, I’d miss and hit an object right next to me and then get eaten. THE NOISE LEVEL AND THE PLANKS:There comes a point when you have to walk across planks that you can move around. The noise level of the regular environment is 3-5 bars. Your character makes a whopping 4-5 bars of noise when crouched and foot planted when walking across these. When the enemies gain the ability to scan, having to wait for the environment to randomly switch to 4-5 bar from 3 caused the boards to shatter and me to die. Maybe make your character not stomp across the boards and tone it down to 3 bars of noise. ENEMY AI: I had a bunch of times where the enemy just would NOT leave me alone no matter how quiet I was. I had no noise bars and I threw a brick, then the death angel invested it for 2 seconds, then whipped around and walked across the room into me. It seems like even if you are quiet, the enemy ai is too good at guessing where you are. I understand I had it on hard, but I actually wondered if the enemy wasn’t blind because it was so accurate…

_childDocuments_.review: Currently about halfway through the game, and it's got a lot of goods! But it also has some bads that just sadly can't be ignored.THE GOODS:-The game looks and runs phenomenally, I'm so used to movie tie-in/movie-based games looking/running like absolute crap. But TRA's visuals are actually consistently above the bar. The characters don't look like they're made of rubber and the Death Angels are just *chefs' kiss*-The acting is great. The dynamic between Alex and Martin is adorable, and the rest of the cast does pretty well in their own right. -Gameplay hits the mark! I played with the microphone function on and navigating through the amazing and scary environments was made even more immersive and intense with it. The asthma system is very unique and keeps the player from getting too complacent.-The sound design is great. The Death Angels sound like they do in the movies, the heartbeat in your ears during tense moments makes you FEEL the tension. The level of quality and attention to every sound detail is stunning.THE BADS:-A few bugs took me out of it at points. For some reason the microphone function would only start working when I paused and unpaused. During the section where you discover throw-able items not only did the microphone system not work, but the asthma system also broke completely until I paused and unpaused. Still a lot of kinks that need working out.-Someone got a little too excited with the horror stings. They get set off at the most harmless of actions. The biggest thing is they go off when the Death Angel reaches where you threw a distraction item, which is annoying and confusing because you can't tell if YOU set it off or not.-The flashlight is powered by a potato. Not even a good potato, it's like a sweet potato. -The game has the same problem a lot of horror games have for me; once you die, the tension and fear turns into annoyance. The more you die, the more of a slog it may feel. -If the wooden plank is the only method of passage, ESPECIALLY in a Death Angel section, it should not make THAT much noise. -The yellow paint everywhere, while understandable due to the cluttered environments, is a bit silly. There's even one for where you put down a box of beer in one of the prequel segments. I have no doubt this is due to the results of play-testing, so it's not a deal breaker. But still very goofy.-I'm only about halfway through, but I have a feeling the gameplay may get more and more repetitive. However if they keep adding in new mechanics as the game goes on, I definitely think it'll alleviate the monotony.Overall, this is definitely a step out of the comfort zone of Stormind Games, who's previous title was an isometric fantasy RPG. But it's a step well taken, and with Saber Interactive's support, they've made one of the few actually GOOD Movie Universe Games. 7/10, Still needs some polish but is still enjoyable and immersive.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for something like this since the first movie came out. This is a wonderful game that sticks closely to its source material, and an exceptional example of a successful movie to game transition. -it's well-paced and voice-acted.-The levels are tight and well-designed without too much complexity.-The sound-design, with its brooding and foreboding music, perfectly supplants the tension.-The checkpoint system is forgiving.-You actually cast a shadow, have a body, and have your own thoughts.-The creatures are as terrifying as ever.-Your heartbeat rate increases and your asthma/panic attack chances increase the closer the creature is to you, which is a nice touch;-The story is serviceable.-You can also use their own strength against them to create escape paths by distracting them with thrown objects.-The game requires your utmost attention. All of your movements have to be measured and calculated. You always have to watch your step. Every other sound can easily lead to your death.You'll be opening doors and drawers really slowly, and you'll be trying to mentally create your paths and predict the creatures' movements. And you will play the game in total silence. The game really does test your patience in the best possible way.I had to go through some trial and error on hard difficulty before I found out that I had to listen to sound queues. Once you make too much noise, there's no going back. There's no hiding or avoiding the creature. No compromises. So you have maybe 1 or 2 tries before the sound crescendo goes up too high which is when the creature knows your location.The game definitely scratches that Alien Isolation itch.Jim Halpert must be proud.

_childDocuments_.review: The game A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead is not bad, but unfortunately, it's not particularly good either. The best word I can use to describe it is "mediocre." While some of the ideas within the game initially show promise and sound interesting, the execution leaves much to be desired.First, let's discuss the gameplay loop. It quickly becomes repetitive, and you can safely say you've seen most of what the game has to offer within just a couple of hours. Due to not-so-intelligent AI, the gameplay becomes more annoying than scary, breaking the tension rather than building it. There's little new content to keep you engaged or on edge throughout the experience, making the game feel stagnant after a short while.The story also suffers from questionable decisions. The protagonist, while fitting well into the environment, seems an odd choice—a person with asthma surviving in the world of A Quiet Place feels implausible. The main conflict feels shallow, relying on some questionable decisions by other characters that don't feel believable given the situation. However, the game's flashbacks are the most interesting part, offering some background on how everything began and delivering action-packed, engaging sequences.Where the game really misses an opportunity is in its exploration of the world. With the violence and horror of the A Quiet Place universe, the developers could have delved into the tragedies of other survivors, creating dark and emotionally gripping drama. Unfortunately, that potential is left unexplored, and the game often feels empty and soulless. Ultimately, you're better off spending your money on titles like Still Wakes the Deep, which offer a more fulfilling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is fun and tense for the first hour and a terrible drag after that. The fact that you can die from making too much noise is cool until you get into the habits that keep you alive and bored. Everything in the game feels scripted, when you make too much noise does an enemy spawn and chase you? No, you get hit from behind and die in a cut scene. The way enemies walk around feels like they always walk the same routes. The noise sensing has a 3 strikes and your out system, if you make too much noise it makes a sound effect, stand still and nothing happens. Move again and it'll make a different noise, stand still and nothing happens, move again and you die. There should be a punishment for making too much noise the first 2 times, like having a creature roam around for a bit. Quick time events are the games bread and butter, which is disappointing. Asthma attack, qte. Trap to dissarm, qte. Fail the qte, instant death. It is very quite place, but not very fun. The segments where you can see the monster are the only segments where fun can be had, as trying to balance speed to avoid the monster with stealth to not get deaded instantly is fun, until they give you 40 bricks a segment to make the monster a non-factor. For some reason, the noise system doesn't get harder in these segments despite the monster being right there, if you make too much noise 2 times the monster flairs a bit, then goes back to ignoring you, why doesn't it walk towards me?In the entirety of the game I never used the flashlight. I played the game on hard and I only ran out of asthma puffers once, the fact that you can't pick up pills and store them for later is both immersion breaking and frustrating. The quite place has the environment for a good horror game but not the game play to go with it. Having to do everything slowly could be ok if there was pressure to do it quickly, but without it it's just a game about patience. I have never felt like I had to rush anything, there should have been moments when I had to risk noise to escape, to do an objective, to collect an item. The whole game can be played crouched and slow, and you will have a pretty easy time.The game slowed you down, but also itself. The tension from the beginning is a dragon you will be chasing for the rest of your play through.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. A quiet place has always been a series I loved and seeing it come into a game made me so happy! I felt genuine stress and fear whenever I saw one of the creatures ahead of me. One thing I loved the most about that was the fact that there was rarely an audio cue or cutscene when you had to go head to head with one of the creatures. You would be walking, staying quiet and then one would just slowly walk in front of you, made for a great "I need to cover my mouth" situation. The story was great, the acting was amazing, I loved playing through it.Now there are a few things I would say need some improvement.-The AI of the creatures seems really clunky. In a game where they hunt by sound alone, it felt kinda unsatisfying when you would be staying super quiet and yet it would still follow you all the time. The creatures seemed to always know where you are, taking away the "I need to be quiet or else it will find me" and turned it more into a "well it knows where I am constantly so I always need to have a distraction handy." It could be a lot better if it was less feeling like you're being followed and more staying quiet to KEEP IT FROM following you.-There are certain times where the asthma felt like it was going way to high way to fast. Especially with the previously mentioned AI, the creatures sticking to you constantly made it even worse because now it's gonna shoot up constantly.-last thing, the planks. I have seen it mentioned before but I would also like to call attention to it. For a required game mechanic to get around certain areas, it should not be that dangerous of a mechanic to use. The noise coming from the plank even going slow, and crouching, should not be as loud as it is.Other than those things, I had an amazing time playing this, Keep up the amazing work.

_childDocuments_.review: edit as I play through the game (Hard difficulty):How good is it? Well I was supposed to go to sleep but I wanted to play for an hour just to check it out. And I haven't been able to put it down. I keep finding so many clever design decisions which improve and innovate on this type of hide and seek gameplay. For anyone who cares I'll list them at the bottom. ... Finally finished the game now. I would recommend playing on hard though, because it will be more intense and your experience will be longer. I never once got bored, each location offers new challenges and new tools/mechanicsMaybe I do like horror games after all. I wanna play something similar nowAlien Isolation walked so A Quite Place could run. It tightens the level design, provides more in depth challenges and interesting ways to solve them with constantly learning the monsters behaviour. While Alien seemed so novel  at the time, this game really makes it pale in comparison. You would just walk from A to B, flip switches. My second playthrough of Alien was rather laborious and that 'story' was just a repetition of the same problem every time. I would say "Hard" mode is mandatory though. The game was clearly designed around it and then later made easier after playtesting. If you enjoy normal then by all means, but if you feel the game isn't fun then you shouldn't be playing on normal. It completely sucks the tension out of it========Finally a game that lets you turn off the yellow paint marks. With all due respect to their utility and the people who like that stuff, .. I'm very happy to turn it off. I find horror games boring in general so I don't play them often, but this game is good so far. Minor annoyances exist, but nothing as bad as Callisto Protocol Some people say their pc has trouble running it properly, so be aware of that.  The game has plenty of graphics options so if you have a basic understanding you should have no issues========- You can't fight the monster (at least so far) but you do have an HP bar. It serves as a multi purpose stress indicator. For one, it helps to guide the player to stay away from the monster, since you can only get so close before even the smallest sounds alerts it.Secondly, it adds an extra layer of obstacles, since you often need to take actions that create stress, such as carry certain objects to a specific location. Overall, I find this system adds a meaningful layer of complexity to the experience that feels like an improvement on this type of gameplay- The game keep introducing new mechanics and utilities as you progress which keep the challenges interesting. I won't spoil what they are - Individual areas function as a sort of stealth puzzle, teaching you each mechanic and offering multiple solutions- Monster AI feels good. Not too predictable, but not too random either. I haven't encountered any situation where it felt like I had to wait for it to move (Lookin at Alien Isolation with its boring hide-in-the-closet for several uneventful minutes until the Alien finally leaves so you can resume the game)- The door/drawer opening mechanic is fun, and designed so that it has a threshold. Instead of having to sit there opening it all the way, they made it so you just need to reach a certain spot. Kinda hard to explain, but you might notice this and appreciate that they thought of this and fine-tuned this kind of stuff- Do you keep your eyes on the monster's location but give up the ability to see what you are stepping on? Or do you turn your back to the monster to make sure you have a good route but lose the awareness of where it is walking to. I really liked this dilemma. It creates a situation where you have to first perform a reconnaissance of the area to plan ahead. Because once you are carrying a puzzle object you will have to act fast and won't have room for errors.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the negative reviews. A really fun, intense and very different horror game compared to your normal ones that come out today. An excellent homage to the movies and for those fans who have already seen the movies, definitely give the game a shot. Gameplay relies heavily on your surroundings, sound and environment including your own microphone. The story is a well written one about tragedy and loss and doing whatever it takes to survive, just like the movies. 'A Quiet Place' isn't *really* for those that are expecting your traditional horror, it's much more stealthy and way more challenging. As for performance issues, there were little and slight stutters in certain areas but with the hotfix the devs released a day or so ago, the game runs perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: So. What do I do here. Pros/Cons? Smash or Pass? MFK? I unno.What did I like? I play a lot of different games. I like to be well rounded. And this game "feels" good but at the same time it feels horrible.Not in a omg skincrawling sort of vibe horrible. More of a "OMFG if I have to take another 35 mins just to move 30 feet I will kill somebody." sort of horrible.There should be an alternate title. "Inconsistency The Video Game". Or "Trial and Error Simulator". Because great gawd oh mighty is this game just that. Inconsistent. And you will be reloading check points through-out.Does the game has rules? Yes. Does game follow its own rules? Absolutely not.So let's get into it.Pros:Atmosphere: 10/10.End of Pros.Cons:AI:The "Listener" is just poor mans Xenomorph AI. It knows where you are and it WILL always know where you are no matter what you do. There are points where you will get accidentally cornered by it's really poor pathing until it just slowly but surely walks into you causing a reload of the current area.Mechanics: The DEV's treat the player like a moron. The "tutorials" are obnoxious splash screens that are poorly worded and confusing such as how to handle the Protagonists "Asthma Attacks" QTE. These "tutorials" persist until literally the very last act of the game and are just as inconsistent as the AI. It's filled with bugs that either kill you, or force you to restart the game as certain ones can make inputs, at least in my exp., with keyboard inoperable.Asthma the Protagonist:Not sure if the DEV consulted anyone with actual asthma, but discussing the game with  several friends who actually have asthma, they all agree that the protag has it so bad, they would not have survived passed childhood. Every single action, from walking too fast, sidling a waist high fence, reading some risque notes, existing, causes the protag to start wheezing and freaking out with the onset of an asthma attack.This isn't realistic, at all. And really just sours the game experience overall. Not to mention we are to believe that a world that has been picked over for resources just conveniently has Inhalers and Asthma meds just lying around everywhere? Ridiculous. The best part is when a "Listener" decides to just stand nearby, which causes the asthma "meter" to rapidly fill with no way to prevent it but rushing through your limited supply or trying to do a QTE while carrying a 50lbs bag of sand, make a path with said sand, avoid the AI, and just get 30 feet forward so you can get to the next area.Noise:....I do not ask for much. But when I get a "tutorial" saying that environment noise can mask the player noise, only to have that rule not followed or followed but kinda or not followed no matter what is happening or yes stand there and you are invisible. Like I said, inconsistent. You can read a note about the deafening noise in the upcoming area making it impossible to communicate outside of the soundproof offices but man you so much as stand up too fast OH BOY here comes Jonny!DEVs. You cannot have rules and laws that govern your AI and make it so ♥♥♥♥ like it is in this game. How is it so poorly implemented? You teach the player that fast movement is bad and slow movement is ok but then also slow movement is also bad and so is standing up, using a ladder, looking in a direction....any direction it is so bad the AI programming. This is quite possibly the most frustrating video game I have ever played simply because of bad AI mechanics. There was a section where I was literally under a waterfall, and we are told waterfalls mask noise, so I tested it, walked around made personal noise and YEP, Jonny got to me, in an area not accessible by the AI. It was inbetween sections. There is an area, doused by water sprinklers and you are told, BY THE GAME, that your noise is masked, you are invisible, and the level is DESIGNED for you to be able to make noise that the AI should not detect you YET it does, easily, as if the section modifier, the sprinklers, doesn't work. inconsistent.The game TELLS you that if you make a loud noise, move from the area and wait until the AI leaves. Nope. It does NOT tell you this may only work in areas where the AI is clearly also on the map, physically. In sections where the AI is not present, you get instantly killed with no way to avoid it. Opened a door/gate/drawer/panel too fast? Dead. Didn't open too fast? Too bad the design is buggy so you will get killed regardless. There are parts in this game where you will be forced to sneak two feet and wait then sneak two feet and wait and it goes on like this like wtf why.Here is the why:$39.99. And it takes maybe 8 hours to complete. They did this on purpose. Its over priced. Way overpriced. And if you remove those sections that force you to move at a snail's pace the game can easily be finished in under 5 hours.I don't want to type anymore. There is just so much bad and buggy in this game. It took me 14 hours spread out over a week? Because I was getting frustrated enough to contemplate breaking a keyboard. That never happens and I play OW2.And LoL.Do I recommend?Not at this price. Not at this patch level.Needs more work. Good Luck.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not really horror, more a frustrating very predictable game attempting horror. The mechanics quickly become its problem. The Death Angel/Listeners/Monsters are rubber banded to you, and have the worst AI in any horror game.So lets break it down. Like the movie sound is what the monster uses to hunt the player. And your character has asthma, both of which become more of an annoyance than anything. Some terrain make more noise than others, there's stupidly placed cans and items that make noise you gotta avoid and every action you do, like climbing builds your asthma, even sprinting, very quickly.When you face the first (Second?) monster you gotta get around, you notice small cans on the floor... Can you pick these up to your advantage? NOPE, you don't get that ability till later in the game... So you gotta avoid them until then. Even when you do, the monster goes to where you throw the item, for a second before instantly "roaming" towards you, regardless if you're sneaking and not generating noise! - This just made the entire game frustrating, there was points you're forced to sneak from throwable to throwable just to make progress to the "exit" - Seriously, that was seriously f-ing stupid mechanic.Adding onto the fact that no matter what, if you step on terrain that makes too much noise your character will just stand still and be killed. - Even if you managed to sneak away from that area the monster just be-lines straight to you. The asthma mechanic becomes more frustrating over time, because every action you do increases your asthma, and if it hits max, you get an asthma attack you gotta QTE out of. Or die. To reduce, you take pill after pill, after pill, after pill to the point you'd probably OD. Inhalers, for some ungodly reason are one time use, which, lets be honest, don't work like that. Remove the pills, just have a unlimited inhaler where the longer you use it, the lower the astham mechanic is. That would of been way better in my opinion. And more believable.The story was super predictable, all the characters were badly written into atypical horror tropes, in that sense of "Do people these people have any brains?" Concept was great, but done awfully.This for me is a one-off game that I half regret getting. I wanted to see the story and the conclusion mostly.It's not like Alien Isolation, its just worse. If the AI of the monsters were better, instead of just locked to roaming to the player, it could of been better.

_childDocuments_.review: So not a fan of "The Quiet Place" universe. But a fan of a good videogames. Game leaves with a mixed feelings. This is a great idea. But not a great implementation. The idea that you should control your actions to be as quiet as possible is a great start for core gameplay. When I learned that developers added a mic support I was pretty hyped. Imagine you COULD use your microphone and in-game mechanics to bait monsters, interact with game surroundings, you can do this right? Unfortunately the only thing you can do using your mic or making a load noise on purpose is die. So there is no reason to play this game with mic setting on your own. Assuming they've made it for streamers. But I am a streamer and... I just can't talk on stream cuz of that. Like, I can't create something fun out of it. Literally - if I speak - I die. What's the fun in that? Idk. In terms of gameplay mechanics it's not bad I suppose, but after like 2-3 hours of gameplay (and this game does not have a lot of narrative or cutscenes going on) it becomes boring as hell. You need to move your mouse REALLY slow to open EVERY SINGLE DOOR on your way. Instead of proper walking you HAVE to walk super slow, cuz if you are not - you are dead. It's just not fun, at least not for this long period of time. This game lacks of dynamic and good pacing. It's not even hard, I died like maybe 6-10 times, some of them cuz of the bug for sure and some of them cuz I did something quick, because I was frustrated.In terms of narrative - it's... fine i guess. There is not much going on and after like 3 hours your goal never changes for the next 4-5 hours until the end of the game. Honestly, can't recommend nor not recommend this game. Probably if you are not that into videogames and a fan of "The Quiet Place", you'll get a decent impression. But for me 60% of the game was boring as hell.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand the thought process of developing this game. Some stuff makes sense for a two hour game or so, but for the length it has it's like the developers had no desire to really make the game, almost like they disliked making it.Just to list a few reasons as to why it just doesn't feel like the devs cared:1. You play in a world where noise kills you. That's it. NO EVOLUTION OF THE CONCEPT. You will die if you make noise, that's it.2. There's no particularly advancing mechanics in the game. You constantly just get into a new area to repeat the "sneak around noisy objects and slowly open door". For a 9-10h game it seems like there's a certain lack of passion for the game to never evolve the concept.3. Speaking of mechanics, I can't even beat the game. They add a noise that is genuinely UNHEALTHY AND WILL DAMAGE YOUR HEARING. I have tinnitus and now I have to look forward to several days of it being worse before it settles down because the devs haven't learned that we're in 2024 and adding noises like that has NEVER been liked in ANY game ever.4. They didn't care much for your character to be logical. You're constantly just standing still and accepting death if you mildly went too far in noise making. No QTE or anything to help you get to safety.5. You can't run, but there is a run function. Why add it if it never helps you survive!? Mechanics feel like they were left in as a "this exists in this engine" but they never applied it to the gameplay.6. Asthma as a mechanic isn't a bad idea, but when your idea is that the person is meant to be terrified about a monster but you have to stay FAR away because of asthma, it takes away the feeling of fear and replaces with annoyment of having to focus on a mechanic versus being absorbed in the atmosphere.7. Who went around with yellow paint and decided what can be climbed and what can't? It really takes away the immersion when you have to climb specific spots and it's just overkill on showing where you have to go. You added a waypoint button if people get stuck, that's enough.There's way more, but unless they patch out the horrendous scanning noise this becomes unplayable to millions of players. Currently I have to recommend to avoid the game until at least THAT is patched. And personally I hope they consider revisiting the game to actually add a chance to survive when you were a bit too loud (make running useful!) and QTE (beyond the basic one that's in) for some moments to spice up its intensity. It'd help make the game actually shine instead of feeling dragged out and uninspired.And to add at the end: I WANT to like this game. I WANT to be able to beat it. So this is not me crapping on anyones favorite movie or game, I really want to see it SAVED from being remembered as "ah yes, people had to stop playing it because of one mechanic".

_childDocuments_.review: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead captures the terror of the film by placing players in a world stalked by blind, sound-sensitive creatures. Following Alex and her family, who must escape their refuge to find resources, survival depends on remaining silent. Key mechanics include using a sound meter to gauge noise and an optional mic integration that lets real-world noise impact gameplay, adding intensity for streamers and interactive players.The game’s stealth mechanics shine, with hazards like broken glass and creaky doors requiring careful navigation. While thrilling at first, issues with enemy AI dampen the suspense; monsters often stay close too long, making encounters feel frustrating rather than terrifying. Throwing objects can help with distraction, but the aim is critical to avoid alerting monsters.Although the story gains depth from survivor notes, the lack of dynamic interactions limits replayability, and collectibles are minor incentives. The game’s visuals are passable but not outstanding, and overall, it feels more suspenseful than truly scary.You can view my entire review (& more!) here:

_childDocuments_.review: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead is a game of missed potential. It's fine, very playable and even enjoyable, but it is routinely let down with its extreme and rigid linearity, lack of player agency, lackluster level design, and signposting of each and every puzzle there is.Good:- Decent story, with the animation doing the heavy lifting to make the characters somewhat relatable- Avg world building, but the writing felt something out of Until Dawn than something more serious, but not bad.- Great visuals and sound design- ShortBad:- Extremely linear to the point where there is only a single path forward and there are a series of steps you have to do to move forward- There is no variation to the gameplay. Move slowly, open doors slowly, use inhalers because your character has asthma for some reason, watch out for the monster, solve basic puzzles that are signposted every single time, and done.- Getting caught by the monster means instant death. No room to escape, no ways to trick the monster, no way to fight it. It sticks very close to the movies in this aspect, but this is a game, give players some agency, some choice, something!- Weird PC optimization. On my 12900K/RTX 3080, it ran fine at 60fps most of the time at max settings. But the implementation of DLSS is off. It blurs the visuals as it also reduces resolution scale along with the resolution, which is not how it is supposed to work. The game also plenty of UE-stuttering.This game felt like a proof of concept that was converted into a full game. It's not bad. I really wish Steam had a scoring system, because I would give it a 6/10. Nice, short enjoyable game but its too simple for my taste. $30 is decent value for the game but there is not a lot of replayability. Wait for a discount. At $15, it will be a GREAT purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: The spooky season has started, and it’s almost Halloween. Dress scary, eat some candy, carve pumpkins, and enjoy some horror movies like A Quiet Place. This brings us to the next horror game. Here is our A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead review.A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead is a single-player horror adventure game inspired by the movie franchise. If you’ve watched the movies, you know that silence is the key to survival, and that’s also the main focus of the game. Don’t make noise in the game—better yet, don’t make noise in real life! The monster can hear you through your microphone! The game was developed by Stormind Games and published by Saber Interactive.I know I don’t listen to my mother that much, but while playing this game, I discovered that I make a lot of noise—even when I need to be completely silent. My breathing is loud, and I’m not able to stay quiet when things get too exciting. I had a problem: my microphone was way too sensitive.Luckily, the game has a solution for that—you can adjust the sensitivity of the microphone. The “microphone noise detection” feature in the game is optional and can be toggled on from the menu. It’s off by default. A microphone icon in the bottom right corner of the screen indicates whether or not your input has been detected. This feature reminds me of Alien: Isolation, and I really like it.The game is set in the same universe as the films. It takes place after “Day One” and a few months before the first A Quiet Place movie. The game shares the same atmosphere, tension, and sound design, but it tells a parallel story with new characters and locations. A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead does not feature any people or places from the films; instead, it focuses on a unique narrative that complements the broader A Quiet Place universe.As I mentioned earlier, the game is all about making zero noise, and it does this very well. While playing, you have to avoid various elements. Try to avoid walking in puddles because it makes noise. Watch out for twigs and bushes, as they also create sound. Additionally, the map is full of loose objects like cans—you definitely don’t want to knock these over, as they make a lot of noise. The cans felt especially realistic to me because my room is always full of energy drink cans!If you find it difficult to know which sounds are loud, use the phonometer. This device shows you the loudness of ambient/environmental sounds on the left and the loudness of the sounds you are making on the right. The system for detecting sound waves considers the intensity, duration, and volume of the noise. A loud noise may not kill you right away, depending on the difficulty level you choose, but a series of loud noises over time will. Environmental sounds like running water can help mask the sounds you make, such as footsteps or breaking glass.You’ll have a flashlight to help you see in the dark for most of the game, but it requires new batteries to recharge because they run out of power. Personally, I didn’t use the flashlight very often. The monster actively searches for you when you hear humming and your screen becomes hazy. Stand still to avoid being detected in these moments, even if you’re covered by sound.Be cautious of sand and dust, as your character suffers from asthma. As if that’s not bad enough, she also suffers from anxiety attacks. The lung icon shows Alex’s asthma status, and this mechanic adds a challenge to the game. You need to manage Alex’s stress level to avoid asthma attacks, which can be triggered by heavy lifting, proximity to creatures, or dusty environments. Inhalers are easy to find throughout the game, and having enough of them becomes crucial in later stages, where attacks are more frequent.I played the game on “normal” difficulty and didn’t have any problems finishing it. I really liked the game. The graphics are nice, and the mechanics are cool. The average duration of the game is between 8 and 10 hours, which is perfect for a game in this price range. However, I have to admit that after a few hours, I turned off the microphone feature. In my opinion, the game could have been a little more challenging, a bit scarier, and a little faster-paced. Still, I had a great time playing this game!
