I think the only graphical issue I had were the trees have triangular leaves due to wrong textures being used and flying objects here and there, moving back to their correct position once I got close enough.Anyway, I enjoyed a few parts of the game, but sadly, most of it was just frustrating.Story's kind of simple and predictable, paired with some of the dumbest-cliché deaths, and that sucks because I think the story and characters had potential. Anyway, fortunately I wasn't expecting much from the story. I bought this expecting a good stressing and scary game, and I got it, but it came with a lot of issues.Gameplay was ok, but way slower than I expected. I hate that they gave the character asthma just for the sake of making the game more difficult. Literally, every little effort gives this character asthma and can quickly lead to an attack. Most of the time when the creatures are near you and you're about to have an attack, screen goes very dark, paired with a black and white filter and it's the most annoying thing ever.The little QTE to prevent the attacks is kind of hard to get right as well. The window is just way too small. I had to check on Youtube how to actually get it right at first, because I didn't understand it the first time, and I couldn't find any tutorial page in the game.  What's even more frustrating is when the QTE fails itself because it wouldn't trigger itself, and when it did, it literally gave me a 0,001 second window to do it (which I obviously couldn't).Item management is kind of messy and unresponsive at times (which will certainly lead you to your death in more than one occasion. Once I died because the character, for some reason, wouldn't pick the brick I had stored, while I kept pressing the right arrow. She ended up picking it, right before the creature attacked tho.Ideally, one would have the noise detector on one hand and the flashlight in the other. Well, you can't do that... for absolutely no reason, that's just how the game was designed. So it's either one or the other, again, probably for the sake of making the game harder (and less enjoyable for me).Let's talk about the flashlight...I've complained my entire life about games' flashlight batteries lasting for like barely one minute. It's even worse in this game. Batteries are extremely short. They do seem to give enough batteries for it at the beginning, but it's just so annoying having to recharge batteries every single minute. Especially in a game meant to be slow-paced. You can barely explore one dark room before the flashlight goes dark.The latter flashlight is even worse. In order to recharge it, you have to press a button 10 times (making noise) just for 30 seconds of light. I gave up, I was just running in the dark by the end of the game.Sound design was good but terribly managed. Whenever the creature is looking for you and hears your steps, there's this loud sound effect that plays to warn the player (and scare them). I love being scared personally, especially in horror games, but this just feels so cheap and undeserved. The creature making a noise is enough to make it scary, really. Sometimes that sound effect would even play when the creature hadn't even heard me. It kept glitching all the time.Also, there are moments in which you find yourself near noisy things, like falling water (which makes A LOT of noise, I could hear it). Well, the noise detector doesn't even detect that noise as "loud", so you can't use it to hide your footstep sounds which is very inconsistent with other moments in which it's the case. You can't rely on your ears in this game, you have to rely on the noise detector.Collectibles SFX is also an extremely loud SFX and I'm honestly surprised it was approved in the first place. For a game about not making a sound and staying quiet... one would expect either a very soft noise, or no noise at all. But that loud sound effect? I just kept asking myself why every time I found one of those planes.I died a lot of times due to glitches with the creature. This game just lacks features like sticking to walls or doing your best to hide yourself in corners in order not to get killed. It felt very limited. Especially because creatures always seem to have the advantage somehow. Apparently, they're blind, but sometimes they just seem to know exactly where you are even tho you didn't make a sound. They really just go straight towards your position to get you.Sometimes the creature randomly starts running out of nowhere too, and bumps into you while minding your own business in silence. Yay.I'm not gonna lie, I still liked a few levels and ideas behind those levels, because I love games like Alien Isolation in which you have to do stuff in a room while being trapped with a creature that's trying to kill you, but this game just did that, but in a way less better way.I felt more frustration than fear while playing this game, so sadly, I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: After absolutely loving games like Outlast, Alien Isolation, or any of the Amnesia series, I figured I would like just about any game that left you a defenseless protagonist hell-bent on evading, and being stealthy.  What "A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead" really does is show you  has to go into a stealth game to make it tense, make you feel strong investment in characters, and have it not get repetitive.  Unfortunately, it does this by showing what NOT to do.Without getting too deep into it, while the game introduces new gimmicks throughout, ultimately, the premise is just "sneak around and don't make noise: the game."  By the third giant "boss room" where I had to avoid an alien, I found myself sighing out of boredom and frustration much more than feeling tense.  And then, an alien would leap down from a perch directly on top of my head (when it was just trying to jump to the level below) just because it doesn't have any pathfinding limitations, and I'd be dead and have to start all over again.  So, after the 3rd time of being punished by glitchy behavior like that (another one involved the alien not spawning correctly in a campsite area, and then when I finally snaked my way around, I attempted to climb on top of the boxes leading to safety only to have the alien panic-spawn right on top of me and insta-kill me.)The character stakes are flimsy at best - I never bought into the rivaly between two primary characters - and deaths carried absolutely no weight.  So, really the game just became an exercise in avoiding frustration, which is not appealing to me.I shut the game down and uninstalled it after throwing a brick to lure the alien away, having it leap towards the brick across the room, and then teleport directly into me, about 20 meters away behind a box.  No thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: I came in not really expecting a lot. As often or not, movie games, and movie horror games in general aren't good.I left this game feeling that this assumption was right. This game is VERY linear. To the point that in one encounter I had a brick in my inventory from the last encounter, and I had to break a window. But because it wasn't the brick from that encounter, when I threw it the brick shattered like glass.The Story is also mid. It makes near no sense, and only serves to get the MC out into the world. No character development, only "drama" that you can only really care very little about.The MC her self is a walking cripple. In a world where you are hunted by monsters who have hyper hearing and enough strength to tear through almost anything with ease, being blinder then a bat and a horrible case of Asthma to the point that even climbing up a ledge causes her Asthma counter to go down is just dumb. You'd die the moment you couldn't find a inhaler. Better to save your money.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: As evidenced by the many reviews I've held off on doing (and am currently holding off on writing) until having finished a game, writing a review with an hour played is not the norm for me. However!Let me put it this way.If I was given the task of writing a story where I knew that every single line had to be delivered in a whisper for the sake of the plot, and that story was used in a game based on a movie where 95% of the nuanced acting was the actors doing facial expressions, and that game had character models that looked like rejected Blender models for a Fallout 3 fan game? Well I think I would chop my own head off. Even from the outset, the idea of a game where you are just quiet and slow for... well for the whole game? That is not a sound idea. It can't really be played a ton by streamers or content creators because their job is to talk and by hooking up their mic to the game they have to be quiet. Thats the only thing I didn't do because I didn't feel that streaming a game and just not talking for 20 hours sounded very fun. There are creators that could make fun content out of it, most are not good enough to do that, myself included. Beyond that, A Quiet Place isn't a huge market, I don't think? I'm just not really sure who this game is for. Horror fans are going to be bored by the infinity crouch walking, fans of the movie are going to be bored that its not paced as well as the movie (and even borrows some of the plot points with new characters lol)And beyond that, the characters themselves are just all really annoying? There is nothing funny in this game, there is nothing clever, the writing is flat and slow and the delivery is whispered and stilted. The real cherry on top is that the game has an absurd amount of bugs and performance issues. I have a decent PC and ran into ♥♥♥♥ I have never seen before. If I ran the game at 1440p, my native monitor resolution, and looked below the middle of the screen? It shoved the image to the upper left corner of my monitor and duplicated the scene 20 times in the other 3/4 of my monitor chugging my PC to a halt. I don't know what engine they used, but it also has that thing that happens in RE engine a lot with hair or things its trying to unload as you walk around where it kinda dithers it? Everything, hair especially is just wildly fuzzy and when you turn down the graphical settings it runs a tiny bit better but sure doesn't look very good. The one thing I guess I can give credit for is that the game managed to do environmental design fairly well, but all of the gameplay elements they introduced, the story, pretty much every aspect of this game just seemed rotten and boring, and I would very much not recommend you play it. In the time it took me to decide I had wasted my time, you could go watch almost 70% of the first Quiet Place film, which is a lot better structured, acted and overall a significantly more cohesive product. It also has Jim from the Office in it, and this doesn't, so negative points for that. Really disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, terrible execution. I didn't expect this game to be easy and I like challenging games like Alien Isolation but this game is annoying hard for 1 main reason: the character you play has asthma, creature gets too close - asthma attack, walk around in a dusty room - asthma attack, pick up something heavy - asthma attack. In my opinion making the game hard by having to pass a 'press F' situation so the creature doesn't kill you is annoying.If the character didn't have asthma then I think this game would be a great horror / stealth game but unfortunately the constant fear of having an asthma attack makes that more scary than making too much noise.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't play spoopy games, but I got this because I liked the "A Quiet Place" movies. I played thru the entire game on Medium/Normal difficulty and without the voice coming thru the mic. Took me about 12 hours to play thru the entire game. So knowing the monsters from the movie, the whole gotta be quiet sets in. What starts as a fun and scary play thru turns into a frustrating and annoying one. The AI on these things are cheaty, it is quite apparent as you see them walk, stop, and then turn and look at you constantly. Also you'll notice that as you walk thru areas that the wandering ones are leashed a certain distance from you. So if you move behind a car, they'll move behind the car as well. I have had them ignore the sound of objects I've thrown to follow me to where I was supposed to go. It was pretty much the water pumping station and Fire station I had the most issue with. It was annoying how during their patrol, I would hide under a burst pipe which was gushing water, to have them walk right to me and then clip thru the wall and get me. You'll notice ever single locked door has the same sliding latch lock. Don't even get me started on the bottle noise traps that are for some reason everywhere in the camp ground. Being frustrated with the game I stopped caring about collecting all the collectibles and just tried to speed thru the game as quickly as possible. Which at one point I pretty much ran thru a garage throwing bricks and the thing got me, but instead of dying it moved me to the next part of the map.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: There is enough in A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead to justify exploring the universe further in a future game. When the stealth and sound masking come together, there is something quite special about crawling through a post-apocalyptic world slowly and avoiding the deadly creatures. Sadly the good parts are more of the exception, with the player usually striving to stay under a volume trigger, or avoiding collisions in claustrophobic spaces. With a thin and forced story that fades, and a lack of survival elements, it does not make the best of its post-apocalyptic setting. Still, fans of stealth games might find just enough here to enjoy at a low price, while they wait to hear from the bigger franchises.***NEUTRAL RATING***
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a stealth game junkie, this game will definitely scratch that itch. It's like a diet Alien Isolation borrowing the same dynamic of sneaking through levels to avoid the giant murder alien. However Alien Isolation did a better job of creating the hunter/prey dynamic with the xenomorphs. In AQP:TRA, the Death Angels do have presence that makes any situation tense they don't feel as oppressive or dangerous as the xenomorph simply due to their AI. While the Death Angels may lack the same presence as the xenomporph, the game makes up for it with interesting asthma mechanics to ground the main character and increase moments of tension. The graphics look great. Small wish-list things would to be to better ground the death angel so it's movements had more weight. For example, when the xenomorph in Alien Isolation responded to nose, its movements were far more natural  for a creature given its size. In this game, the Death Angels 100% feel like 3D models stuck into an environment at times rather than something that exists in the world  that's been designed. On this note, it'd be great if there was just a little more visual separation between surfaces to clue players in to what can or cannot cause noise. Solid 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERSThis is important, I find it hard to believe that many people outside fans of the movies would really enjoy this game. And even as a pretty avid fan it's a hard recommendation. It's really only worth playing through once, and if I could tell my past self anything it would be to get this game on sale.Now, for the critiques of the game. First and foremost, I don't believe they thoroughly playtested survivor mode and potentially hard mode. I get that the higher difficulties are meant to better simulate what the creature is actually like in the movies. But with how railroaded you are, and with the obstacles that are in your way. It's actually impossible to get past some of the levels early on. The end of the forest level, after you encounter laura when you need to get across the plank. You can't with out the creature hearing you no matter how slow you take it. And earlier on when you're trying to cross the gap by the railroad, you're forced to cross over some gravel, which on survivor mode requires you to stop after every step for a good bit before you can move again, making it a slog.So I recommend playing on a lower difficulty unless you really like the experience of slamming your head against the wall again and again hoping to break it down, when it won't. Higher difficulties it forces tension instead of trying to organically build it. I really, really liked the part in the hospital where you're creeping down stairs and a death angel silently creeps around the corner, thats good tension building. But that type of moment is so rare, and most other times with the monster you just constantly hear the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ violin shrieking. Also, over and over again and again I was faced with the question, why? Why can't I do this? Why can't I crawl back through that gap to avoid the monster? Why do I need to do a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to get through and easily passable obstacle? It gets to the point where it doesn't make sense of why I can't crawl over something that reaches up to my knee's. It makes a lot of the "puzzle" sections a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slog.My final part of the critique is the story. I genuinely think the story is bad. Martins death was easily avoidable, he could've done a litany of other things to attract the death angels attention other than sacrificing himself. Throw his backpack, bang on the car behind him, anything other than using his voice(Or they could've, you know, left while it was still raining to get back to the hospital rather than stay somewhere dangerous). And Alex is a miserable mc who doesn't use any logic in anything she does. I find Laura's actions, while extreme, pretty reasonable. You're faced with the knowledge that the girl who you're son sacrificed his life for is hiding that she's pregnant with you're granddaughter and is very danger prone. So, keeping her safe is reasonable, locking her up? Not so much, but to instantly face with "WE NEED TO LEAVE NOW" which obviously causes and altercation which gets tens of innocent people killed was stupid. Her father, while a good man, wasn't smart either. "Yes let me wrestle with the woman carrying a gun obviously nothing can happen, cause she's totally going to hurt my daughter! The one carrying her grandchild!" Obviously someones going to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ get hurt. So Laura's "redemption" felt half-baked at best. So, pair the story with "puzzles" that force you to do the most roundabout ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ possible and you having something terrible. But, there are good things about this game that save it from falling below a 5/10.Firstly, the sound design, I don't know much about sound design, but even I can tell it was really well done. I also liked the mechanics of having to actually pull your mouse to open things, made it feel engaging and a bit stressful. There were a few parts of the game I also liked, the trainwreck sequence was actually really neat and elevated my opinion a lot. So thats where it lies, a 5/10. Something potentially worth playing through once and never again. Perfect price tag as well for a fan, but a bit high for someone who doesn't know much or care much about the franchise. Honestly, I felt the game was severely limited by how linear and railroaded it was. If they approached a more open ended level design, akin to metro 2033/last light with some tweaks to puzzles and a revamp of the story, they could've had something amazing I feel. I wish there was an option to put a meh, rather than a yes or no for recommending a game. But for now, since I have more critiques than praises, I'll have to say no to recommending it, atleast to those that aren't fans of the franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: Its actually somewhat upsetting how mediocre this game is. At first the story was fun and interesting and the gameplay was actually entertaining.....then it just repeated and repeated. The game will introduce a new feature only to have you use it once or twice and then just go back to the same old "Sneak around, dont make a noise and barely move" Another problem I had with this game is how unreasonably hard it was. They give you a sprint button but you may as well just forget about it because even walking FAST can get you killed instantly. When the monster is alerted theres no escaping it you literally get stuck in a cutscene where your character just accepts death basically. The levels are so unbelievably slow. A level will have the SIMPLEST goal but will still take 45 minutes to complete simply for the fact that again, if you move faster then crawling speed you risk dying. I do like the idea of this game but the stpry was lacking and there was nothing really special about it. My final complaint about this game is how it keeps you in the dark LITERALLY. This game either forces you to move at night or if it is during the day they throw you into this underground level where its pitch black and hard to see only for it to get you back into the sunlight right as the sun is setting and plunge you into darkness again. My ranting aside, the bugs are also bad and the stuttering is insane. This game just wasnt as fun as I would have liked it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it and...I really liked it. I really felt like I was part of the movie series. So many times I'm like, man if this was real life I'd totally be dead by now. And play the way we play. You can't please everyone all the time, they say.Hoping for new updates and adventures. Good job.

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool concept and has its own spin on the ''dont breathe'' films, but honestly after the halfway point it gets so repetitive and feels so long. If you have more patience than me I'd massively recommend it because it is quite fun, but once you've done one or two puzzley/monster sections they all feel the same and it feels like such a slog to get through.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: + Nerve-wracking (at first)+ Listening rather than watching is an interesting design mechanic+ Story isn't terrible+ Visually appealing+ Sound design was def the main focus and it showed.- Sound queues are annoying- Everything bad happens to your character, she is literally in the worst imaginable situation.- Mechanics are continually introduced, some that you'll never use in the game other than the first time you learn about it.- The trope that excites you at first only bores you later- The game does not respect the players time and the last chapter is just unfair~ the price point isnt badFirst half of the game wasn't bad, but after that, you have all of these mechanics and are basically doing the same thing each stage. For the most part dealing with an asthmatic character in a sound driven world was a great way to feel actual tension in this game. You have a clock constantly ticking on you to make your next move silently. I enjoyed that. But after the halfway point they introduce you to one off mechanics you never see again and it all seems like a trudge through mud. The ending did not satisfy the last pitiful half of the game. I was, however, having stupid fun at the beginning of the game. Peak sound design EXCEPT for the shrill shriek you get as a warning every time you make too loud of a noise. I don't remember much of the music if there was any. But they are tons of cringe scenes where your character sings to lift her spirits lolI went into this game without any real knowledge on a Quiet Place, and I do not think it dampened my experience. What I do think dampened it was the magnet of tragedy that your character is. None of it seems unlikely, but like damn, you'd think that girl would have some sort of contingency in place for tragedy at the point she is at in the game. Anyway, it wasn't the worst story, but I did kind of hate the ending. It wasn't bad per se. Just left a lot to be interpreted due to the nature of the franchise.The real world 200 and something days after the initial impact is where you spend most of your time, but you do flip between time periods. Like day 1 or day 0. Aliens, baby. They can hear you. That's the world.Visually a fantastic game. I was really immersed. They made the forests look great. The atmosphere really fit the vibe they were going for. I enjoyed the game from the standpoint of visuals.NoneI couldn't decide whether to give this game a barely passing or barely failing. In the end, I based it on if I would play it again. And I would not unless they released some DLC with a couple of improvements to the gameplay. It isn't a horrible game, but the horrible sections are so annoying that I would not relive them again even at the low price point. It should have been a bit lower.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend! Great little game.  I got 10 hours play through on hard.  Some bits were a bit stupid and kept dying for absolutely no reason which added to my play time for sure. think thew game was a bit to sensitive to movement, even when moving slowly, which did make me quit early a few times as it got few up of doing nothing wrong but still dying, very frustrating!!! but on the whole it was a nice game.Ran really well maxed out on my PC with no issues to speak of
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game; the stunning graphics and in-game audio made it incredibly fun to play. Yes, I may have died around 20 times or even more, but I absolutely loved it.The death angels are unique monsters—somewhat overpowered, but manageable by utilizing in-game objects. My personal take on this game is that I truly appreciated the gameplay; you can't rush through it, and exploring for secrets comes with its own risks. I wish this game had a multiplayer option where you could team up with four friends; I think it would be exciting to worry about whether your friends' actions will get you caught, and if everyone dies, the game would restart from the last checkpoint. On the hardest difficulty, the game would restart from the very beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Alien Isolation and Amnesia, you will get what you want here, this is clearly a smaller budget than Alien but everything works great, the story, the Monsters and the multiple gameplay mechanics makes it a really cool journey into A Quiet Place franchise.Really liked the fact that the game throws at you in (nearly) every chapter new gameplay mechanics, making the interest renewed regularly.I want also to talk about the price, 30€ is a really good price for the experience you are going to have.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the quiet place movies, I wanted to like this game and quite frankly I gave it more leniency than I should have because it was one of the most boring games I have ever forced myself to finish.The characters are all boring and forgettable, The story is Mid at the absolute best and the gameplay is just not it...Due to the repetitive nature of the game and the extremely buggy enemy AI, The game started to feel like more of a chore instead of something fun about half-way through.Speaking of enemy AI, About 90% of the deaths I had were basically not my fault. Apparently I made the grave mistake of daring to sit in a corner silently (Literally making no noise at all) and the enemy "randomly" decides to check out the corner i'm hiding in for absolutely no reason of any kind, and don't even think of trying to run away because if you make even the slightest bit too much noise than it is instant death, you don't even get to try to escape.Next major complaint would be the asthma mechanic. I get it, the devs needed to add something to actually give the game some challenge otherwise it would be embarrassingly easy but come on... Is an inhaler every 30 seconds really necessary?It feels like all the difficulty in this game comes from cheap tricks and bad enemy ai instead of genuine challenge.Finally, The "gameplay". The gameplay loop is go somewhere so you can do something so you can go somewhere else. Sound fun? If not, then go buy something else.overall, I'll give the game a solid 3/10. The potential is there but it has a REALLY long way to go before I'd consider it good
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely jank, mostly due to how unstable UE5 is on PC right now, but honestly still really heartfelt and a good time. Like I went in expecting to tear it apart but it actually got to me. Some of the poetry and notes scattered around is really touching and unique to this game.The monsters in this are great, the voice detection didn't feel to annoying and forced, you can always just turn it off at any time. Lots of settings to adjust it to your microphone sensitivity. I even played this while streaming, and it was a really tense experience trying to talk quietly enough to not be heard. Honestly can recommend! The narrative is probably what you expect but it's delivered well with good music, voice acting and animations. It's Solid B Grade Survival Horror, I respect this for being what it is, especially for what it could've been.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the game. And here are some thoughts on it. Overall, it was pretty fun. It really resembled what it would be like living in a world with the Listeners. The mechanics were cool, same with the stages. The environment was quite beautiful additionally. There were a few things I wasn't a fan of. As you progress through the parts with active Listeners, they follow you slowly as you get farther away from where you started. This is a pretty bad problem, often cornering you with no escape, pretty much guaranteed death. This made it very hard in these parts. I also thought the game got into a loop eventually, having the same things happen over and over. Overall, I would say this is a decent game, worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing, as someone who is very talkative due to ADHD and just a love for chatting, this game was a very big challenge and gave some very funny moments. I tend to get bored super quickly in certain horror games, but this game was great at keeping you engaged. It's also so nostalgic for the movie series, with certain small easter eggs you can find! It is a bit GPU intensive so keep that in mind while playing, but a solid 10/10 for me. Also to all my viewers who jumpscared me and got me killed by the monster, thanks LMAO

Some parts I did wonder how I made noise in certain cases but overall this was still such a fun experience! Definitely worth a try if you're looking for a suspenseful environment! This game does bring similar vibes to Alien: Isolation in some cases which I found really fun!The second half of the story does get a little frustrating and lost me on some points, but I still did enjoy the game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: How do i put this, This game is amazing gets your heart pumping and you feel genuinely scared not many modern horror games can say that, I love how you have to be extra careful around everything and the story is v nice.ive only got a few problems with it 1)the ai automatically seems too know where, Even if you make zero noise the fire station lvl is a prime example i could walk from one plat from onto a bridge and the monster would be jumping back and forth with me. 2) sometimes the monster would be sat on top of me not attacking or anything but i cant move, Eventually it allows me to but then i insta die. 3) there isnt enough game it took me 8 hours to beat it in 1 run and i get destracted by everything so i know some people its gonna be like 4-5 hours, not a bad thing i know people are gonna talk about it wich is why im saying it, tbf i wanna know what happens too alex and her babba tbh even if its a little photo or something. but overall this game is perfect a few bugs like ive said but its a few weeks old come on its expected 100% recommend

_childDocuments_.review: A Super Immersive Horror! Visuals in this game are amazing. Environments and lighting really nail the creepy A Quiet Place feel. If you love the movies, you’ll definitely get pulled into the atmosphere. The mic feature is cool stuff—any noise you make in real life attracts enemies and get you killed, and this adds a new level of stress and excitement. The stealth gameplay is like Alien: Isolation, keeping you in tension all time. If you’re into tense, stealth-based horror, this game is a must-try!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like the Blaire Witch game fundamentally. _childDocuments_.review: A Quiet Place The Road Ahead isn't that bad of a game when it comes to the story, but I think the performance is really critical and inconsistent. For example, in the prologue on the GTX 1650 the FPS is generally bad at 1080p LOW, with FSR quality giving around 20 FPS max on DX12. On DX11, I get 20 more FPS. Then, inside the house, I also get around 30 FPS with the same settings on DX12, and on DX11, it's double that. When I wake up in the house in the morning and go outside during the day, the FPS drops to 12, and I get up to 20 FPS max again. With DX11, I get around 30 to 40. In the hospital later, the FPS jumps to 100 with the same settings on DX11, DX12 here is not worth it at all.So, the best settings for this situation on GTX 1650 would be 1080p low with FSR quality and, ofc, using the DX11 argument in the launch options or on the game's shortcut. You'll get more stable performance and avoid fatal errors.I know it's a GTX 1650, but still, the game's performance is really strange due to the inconsistency. As for the story, I have nothing to complain about, as I said, the story is good. The graphics are decent at night, but during the day, they're just okay, maybe below average. The performance is odd because of the inconsistency, even though this is UE5, it could definitely be better. I experienced the same stutters with the RTX 2060, 3060, and 4060. DX11 solved the problem.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played many a game in my life time. I have played good and bad games. The bad games I've played are usually bad because they're just *unplayable* either through mechanics or just really bad optimization. This game is the first actually playable game I've ever absolutely abhorred playing. I gave away eight hours of my life I will never get back.At the very beginning of the game, relationships both good and bad are established, and by perhaps chapter four or so, every single person is dead. There are no opportunities in which I can bond with the other characters-- who i am supposed to be attached to! Other than flashbacks once they're already dead. It's like watching The Titanic plummet to the bottom of the ocean, only to wake up and be on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Titanic.The gameplay is repetitive, and it holds your hand the entire time. I had the displeasure of playing on Normal difficulty, in which while being completely silent, I was often decked in the back of the skull by a vine boom followed by an elbow to the face. This game is punishment over and over again. This is the only game I've ever played in which I was begging for the ending to come. Each chapter was just the same ♥♥♥♥ on a different spoon, and while I understand the motivations of wanting to make a game based off a movie which has been done many a time before, if I had to sit through this in theatres I would have left by the thirty minute mark. I had no inspiration as a character/protagonist to want to live, the game mechanics of having asthma in a world where you have to be DEAD SILENT OR ELSE, are easily circumvented on Normal because apparently inhalers and asthma medication are in high supply as every other asthmatic is currently dead. We take so many falls and tumbles I'm shocked the baby isn't dead at the end of the game, but the only thing that was dead was my will to live. I think it would have been more interesting to die at the end rather than the disappointing 'will I, won't I die" ending that took over 20 attempts to get to, and only made me more exhausted each time. It would have been easier to choke down the smoke and huff inhalers like opium than to put on that stupid gas mask. I felt absolutely nothing this entire game except a deep sense of self-loathing. The only reason I didn't give up on this game was because I had friends watching me play, and their commentary on the game was far more interesting than anything provided in this godforsaken cluster♥♥♥♥ of misery. To all who wish to purchase this game with high hopes, I hope they are thoroughly dashed now, and if they aren't, then this game will take your hopes, not only for the game, but for everything in life, and crush it under foot. The fact that I cannot refund this game will haunt me for the rest of my life. Abandon all... everything, ye who enter here. The most exciting thing that is about to happen with this game is uninstalling it from my computer.0/10 I hope I never develop asthma or a baby.

_childDocuments_.review: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead is a decent horror game overall, even if there are inconsistent and confusing mechanics, at least from what I've seen on Hard difficulty, such as getting the spotted sound cues even though your own sounds are much lower than the ambient ones which provides unnecessarily loud sound-jumpscares (spotted sound cues). it is also impossible to be fully stealthy due to that and scripted enemy movements (moving from one zone to another even if you haven't been spotted (which remains rare as you constantly walk on loud-enough grounds (i absolutely hated the water environments)) to be heard from across the level even if the visible enemies are much, much farther, and have the exact same hearing whether you're in their face or quite literally 50 metres away, which can definitely feel unfair at times at least on that difficulty.The characters don't really think before doing something, which leads to pretty goofy moments that could have been entirely avoided which can lead to the immersion being somewhat weakened; however voice acting and animation are pretty solid, which kind of alleviates the goofiness usually as they are still pretty expressive.The world itself however really looks amazing and very much alive, you're constantly on edge and tense as there are very few moments where you can make noise freely, which is a big plus, it really helps set the mood and general ambience the world is in. The protagonist's journey feels dynamic enough and even if some scenarios are definitely predictable, it still manages to remain relatively fresh until the end of the game, and seeing probably something like 90% of the whole travel really helps to immerse in the protagonist's shoes.The music is.. good enough, forgettable but serves the game well enough as it is also a game revolving around mandatory silence so it isn't as important as it may be for any other game. I really enjoyed that more and more mechanics were introduced all along the way up until the end, kept the game fresh enough to keep playing. Story is enjoyable though rather basic, but that doesn't mean it's bad at all, easily understandable by all. Some slight performance issues even on a 4070, but acceptable enough.I recommend even through these apparent flaws, whether you're a fan of the movies or not (I haven't seen them), as it doesn't require any prior knowledge of them to understand most of what's happening. The price may be a little bit steep though, but it is definitely worth to try, as I have.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game "Mixed" rating.At times, its very immersive and creepy, but other times, its tedious and repetitive.When the monster isn't around, all sound you make fills up an invisible progress bar. Avoid making too much sound and this bar seems to decrease. When the bar is full, the monster spawns behind you and instantly kills you. You have no chance to escape. This became obvious to me pretty early in the game, so that took away some of the experience for me.There are also ALOT of loud music stingers. When you make a loud noise, a stinger plays. When you step on some glass, a stinger sometimes plays. There are also seemingly random stingers that plays when nothing happens. This got old really quickly and was pretty annoying.The sections where you can see the monster and need to actively avoid it are the interesting parts of this game. You use environemental sounds to mask your own sounds to avoid alerting the creatures while completing objectives to allow you to proceed.The atmosphere is pretty decent. They really captured the silent vibe.All in all, it could be better, but it could also be much worse.

_childDocuments_.review: A [meh] stealth game, A+ for concept, F- for execution. Vibe and tensions were nice for the first hour, rest was dogsh*t. All action (stealth), no story. And even the action is repetitive.Three major issues that made the game overall tedious and a frustrating experience.1.Death is a cutscene. Did you break the sound limit? haha, die trash. Take an instant cutscene no matter where the monster is, with no chance to escape, hide, throw rocks, or silently move away, nothing but death through a cutscene. This removes the threat of death or worry of alerting the monster, all that happens is a cutscene and you have to repeat a bit of progress. Will making sounds make him roam near you? Yes. Will not making any sounds make him roam near you? Also yes.2. Characters and character building is non-existent. All of them get around 10 minutes of total screen time that makes you feel nothing towards them or yourself. The major story "cutscenes" meant nothing to me as I had no feelings nor interests toward the characters I met 30 minutes ago and who had about a total of 4 minutes of dialogue.3. Very repetitive gameplay, yes at first it's kinda neat, the tension of getting caught is good but it loses the charm after the 10th time with no meaningful change at all. On top of that, that f**king awful chase scene ruined everything. All the time they have been catching and killing you as soon as you "break the noise limit", but that doesn't matter if you are scripted to run away from them, in that case, you can run half a mile at your leisure and get away. Immediately after that, you have a flashback that looks like you are in a van but that must have been a tank, since a creature that big that could break a wall is now jumping at your fast-moving van from left/right or even on top of it without swaying it a tiny bit, then struggling to tear it up, like 10 of them failed to do you any damage, while your driver must have been a top 1 F1 driver for past millennia to get you through that area. Completely and utterly destroyed the last shred of logic and immersion in the game. There's also no explanation for the monsters or any lore or well tbh there's nothing other than F tier personal story that can be summed up by two sentences.The deada*s poker face on the mirror shows how they overestimated their game.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I am finally going to leave an honest review. I wanted to like this game so badly, but I am mixed. I will start with positives. The only reason I gave this a thumbs up, is because the voice acting, graphics, and story were great. At times you feel for the person, and start rooting for her escape. I can see the attention the Devs took in making sure the puzzles and atmosphere really nailed in the 'be quiet or you'll die.' The first few hours of the game was exciting and scary, but it quickly dulled for me around the 4th hour maybe? The cons of this game: I was on Easy mode, and there were a couple times where I was so frustrated I wanted to stop playing the game. I have ADHD, so sneaking around everywhere and having to open doors quietly through the whole game was a challenge, but Its the concept of Quiet Place, so I understood. However, the comments about it becoming repetitive is 100% true. Like I said, after 4 hours you start to get in a routine of "okay, find a board somewhere, now cross it and flip a switch. Go back and take the board to a new location so you can go to the next place and do the same thing". I would've liked to see something different toward the end of the game, but it wasn't. The story was amazing, but would have loved more. I saw someone else say they could've met other survivors and maybe we learn a little about them and team up, or at the end we can actually go to the island and see what happened to the other survivors and if she will be ok? The ending scene was especially hard, because not only do you have the creature camping you, your on a time limit, and you have to do so much stuff to get to the boat, but be quiet and slow! Otherwise its an insta death! But also don't let her asthma get too bad either because you'll die! My biggest gripe though is the monster. It becomes more annoying than scary, and by the end of the game I was speed running just so I could be done. It was as if I had a leash connected to the monster and every time I would get close, it would be right there ready to kill me. If I go to a new area, it would stalk the area so I couldn't get by or move. Also, the radar noise. Holy, hell. I suffer from migraines, and whoever had the idea to put a super high pitch in the game and SPAM IT.... I had a headache an hour after the radar was introduced because the creature kept spamming it and that high pitch noise hurts lol. All in all: I would say play it for the story and be prepared to do some tedious things to get toward the end. Like I said, I was more annoyed when the creature showed up, and relieved when I actually beat the game because I wouldn't have to play it again. I don't think a game should make you feel that once it's over. But, I could just be nit picky and you may love it? Different strokes for different folks I guess, and this one missed me.  :(

_childDocuments_.review: Game ends on Normal difficulty.Overall score: 2/5 or 4/10.Overall assessment: A very lukewarm game, without much flavour. The game's story doesn't let us get attached to the various characters in the story, either the main character or even those around him.The AI of the monsters is very haphazard, and there's a cruel lack of development when it comes to the creatures' movements. Even physically, they're done, but the developers didn't do enough to make them really come alive and not just simple, stupid killer robots.At times, the AI places the creature right in front of us and causes it to pivot on itself in the hope of hitting the player in some way. If contact is made, the character dies.It's clear that the developers were so uninspired during the game's development that they copied parts of the Alien AI from Alien Isolation (which, for that matter, was much more lively and didn't have any completely messed-up or weird random reactions). But copying bits of code or logic from creatures that don't have all the same properties or shape is just illogical.In terms of graphics and textures, the game as a whole is pretty good, although I did find 2 or 3 places where the coding wasn't finished.As for the listening mode through the player's microphone, I didn't activate it because it just seemed pointless and superfluous given that I was playing in quiet to concentrate on the game without outside distractions, but I can understand the concept if the game is played in other conditions.Some actions, such as carrying a board into confined areas, cause the board to pass through walls and other objects, making the overall immersion totally messed up.Other actions, such as being able to pick up any transportable object such as a bin bag, aren't easy to do and send it to a corner of the map to keep the creature away from you.All in all, the game clearly doesn't deserve its €30 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: After being a big fan of the films and re-watching all 3 multiple times and being actually hyped for the game, it sucks to say this game actually blows.The AI is beyond garbage, you can be stood perfectly still and still cause aggro across the current section of the map even with Mic detection off. Generic level AI that always knows where you are but just waits next to you constantly for a trigger instead of being adaptive. Lots of very boring and very repetitive level puzzles to complete. Very well detailed graphics, very atmospheric game. The asthma mechanic is actually just straight up terrible, drains during unavoidable points like climbing ladders or squeezing through walls that you have to go up or through that are almost like tiny mini cut scenes. The "Asthma stamina" being within a 200 mile radius of the creature drains it quicker than a truckers balls in a hooker. The gross yellow paint mechanic is in this game, forced paths you have to take, instead of being able to attempt to sneak over an object that's only 1 foot tall you're forced to detour around the entire section of the map just to get on the other side of that object most of time. First hour of the game felt great, really enjoyable. Rest of it just felt very very repetitive and like a chore. Very boring. Definitely a game I would of waited for a 50% or more off sale to purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to start off by saying I'm a fan of the movies and was really looking forward to this game, but was sadly let down. Here is my review.Before I begin, I want to state I played on "Hard" with voice detection on.The games story started off pretty strong, it sets up the characters, a would be villain, and a future that is bright and also grim given the circumstance, however the whole story is thrown out by chapter 2 when most of the characters die.After that, its just about reaching a destination without dying, which is rather hard to do when even the slightest sound is an instant death. No hide mechanics, no chances to flee, nothing, just 1 of 3 or 4 death animations even if the creatures arent in the play area.I really wanted to like this game, but almost 9 hours of the slowest walking simulator of my life, I cant just bring myself to enjoy it. Also the ending is a huge let down.Pros:- Sound Quality- Beautiful level design- 1 fun chase sequenceCons:- Tutorials even on the last chapter- Instant Death by doing a flippen objective (getting onto a valve to turn makes noise, and on Hard that noise is sometimes enough for an instant death)- Asthma mechanic way to aggressive (however you can bypass the mechanic by doing sprints in safe rooms and triggering an attack so you can perfect the QTE and it goes away without using an inhaler)- AI pathing is wildly sporadic and not in a good way like Alien Isolation...- Story no longer matters after 2 hours in4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give a medium review, on one hand the game is a novel experience to play with friends/stream what have you because your reaction to close calls can be very tense and entertaining, but on the other hand the game itself suffers from lack of depth and replayability.My personal favorite part of the franchise has always been the Death Angel design, and on that front this game doesn't change anything about them (which is great), the feeling you get when you finally accept them as a part of the environment and can move around them with ease is very satisfying, but the fear you still get when they walk right next to you and open their face plates is still there.Unfortunately that's kind of where the positives end, about halfway through the game (right after you see your dad die) you've already experienced everything the game has to offer. Every new section is the same exact thing, walk through sound trap area where there is no Angel, get to another area where there is an Angel, rinse and repeat for the rest of the game.The devs realize this too, right after you escape the train segment they give the Angels the power to inflict tinnitus. What does this do exactly? Nothing, it literally just makes the game longer since the gimmick of "don't move while they're scanning" is nullified because they themselves are not moving.Not even mentioning the fact that for some odd reason they can only do this RIGHT NOW after doing it a total of 0 times throughout the rest of the game.And of course, right after the section they have explaining this new bullshittery, they make you go up some massive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ladders. After reaching the top of the second, it falls down and MAGICALLY the nearest Angel knows EXACTLY where you are, if you run slightly then stop moving or attempt to hide in the big open area before the place you're supposed to go, it won't matter and it will catch you guaranteed.Another thing is, HOW are you even running from it? They've been shown to chase cars and even helicopters in that new movie and keeping on pace for the most part. HOW is this non-olympic runner asthma having pregnant woman possibly running away from the 60mph alien?? Immediately after this chase section, they give you a flashback to a CAR CHASE SEQUENCE. Where you are supposed to use a gun (on their impenetrable skin) to stop them from breaking into the car. Anybody who has watched any of the movies should not need me to explain why this is idiotic.I haven't completed the game yet, but for its own sake I REALLY hope it ends soon. If it drags on any longer I don't see myself finishing it. For $30, you get what you pay for from a no-name company making a movie license game. If you're hesitant on buying it, wait for a sale or get some friends to watch you play it. I cannot stress how boring it can be when you're in a vacuum. Saying nothing, reacting to nothing, or turning off the mic feature altogether makes the game an incredibly mid "stealth" walking sim.

As for the actual story/characters, it felt like I was playing through a trashy horror movie... _childDocuments_.review: Higly recommended: such an intense and immersive horror experience! The narrative is also very good; it has some emotional moments, and in general it helps to break the pace when needed without slowing it down; even the side content is quite interesting ;-)

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but I really can't recommend it. It has a solid start, however the mechanics within the game are mostly unimmersive, and frustrating. The monster AI is lackluster and stuck in the past, combined with arenas where you face it being too small and a frustrating asthma mechanic, the bones of a good game are there, but the end product just doesn't hit for me.While a lot of the side stories scattered in notes are tragic, they get tropey rather quick, usually involving a child being endangered and most people involved in making those notes being found as corpses. You hardly get to interact with any characters and there isn't really a story to speak of. You merely hop from area to area and survive the circumstances thrown at you. One of my personal biggest disappointments is in one specific area, there are notes teasing the existence of an alien nest, instructing you to use the rooftops over that nest to avoid it due to how horrible the inside is, and I was 100% expecting something to go wrong and for Alex to end up in some sort of cosmic horror zone filled with strange alien fungi and architecture, but nothing comes of it, and it doesn't really play a part in the story at all.I do like the idea behind the sound mechanic and the usage of sandbags to nullify the loud noises you'd make, the fact lifting them, or climbing walls to avoid them causes stress damage that can only be healed by using a consumable that's much better served during monster encounters, it ends up being pointless in 90% of cases and its more effective to just slowly walk across the noisy hazard, stop when you get the overused alert sound, wait for the monster to calm and just keep walking. This ends up making the game less of a cautious exploration, and more of a time-wasting frustration that exists to pad the play time, and that was just on Medium difficulty.I do think there's a good game in here, but ultimately for me to enjoy it, many aspects of it need to just be totally redone from the ground up. I never found myself scared at any point, surprised from the occasional sudden jumpscare and tense when dodging the monster, but never scared. Combined with survival mechanics that aren't particularly engaging, this game doesn't work as a survival horror. At best, its a walking simulator with horror paint. And yellow paint. Lots and lots of yellow paint.

_childDocuments_.review: Potentially great, but a buggy mess.TLDR; I played this game so you don't have to.-Phonometer active sound alerts Listeners even when lower than environmental noise output.-Environmental particles extremely unpolished. IE: Character steps on loud objects even when none are around. -Character steps on loud objects even while looking at feet and walking between them and not on them.-Listener constantly alerted even when character isn't moving, nor making any sounds at all resulting in death. (Microphone turned off).-Listener paths directly to character even when throwing distractions (bricks and bottles) across the map.-Listener paths directly to character breaking windows with throwables even when under sprinklers.-Listener paths to directly to objects it's personally kicked leading to instances of death.-Listener gets stuck in walls and terrain after multiple alerts preventing it from hunting. -Character makes arbitrary noise climbing story-line "F-key" interactions and can die during cut scenes.-Sand resets on map on death after saved checkpoints. IE: Train-yard where entire area is metal and gravel, resulting in trapped loops.-Sand cannot be placed on inclines, such as ramps and stairs.-Walking settings reset after every cut scene and main story interaction.-Artifacts present in Toy crawlspace in cave after waterfall level showing cracks in the map and void white space.-Floating objects in the game. IE: Birds perched in the air on nothing, vehicles with floating lights and parts without being attached.Hopefully, this will help the devs with patch updates.

But I could say I liked it, but there are some serious hassle with tech this game uses.Fourth, the tech side of things, Unreal 5 – it’s a load of absolute rubbish, I don’t know what’s going on with those bloody freezes and constant loading times on any possible settings, from low to epic. Honestly, I wish Tim to be plagued with a proper dodgy flatulence for the rest of his life for that for even trying to sell this nonsense to someone. Sure, both games are about senaking and avoiding confrontation but no, this is not even close to the greatness of Alien Isolation.The game is so completely linear it is annoying. There are almost never any choices to be made. You have to follow the yellow tape route even if you clearly can sea other plausible paths but no, they are not approved by the devs. I tried to turn of they yellow tape but it makes the game unplayable as there is no way to destinguis between approved and non apporved path. Once you make a sound (which could be random if you walk to fast) there is nothing to do but wait until the aline comes and kill you. Somitime it take 10 secounds just waiting. _childDocuments_.review: A unique horror game that  players will enjoy. The sound design is phenomenal and the environment is great. Every sound you make can have an impact, whether it's opening a door too fast or walking on glass by accident. As you play, your instincts and awareness will slowly improve, while the game starts throwing new obstacles at you. You'll also have to handle a breathing mechanic that forces you to explore the area and strategize how you'll proceed. The world is 1:1 with the movies, including many diverse sections where you'll find a new Death Angel to escape from. The main collectibles you find are references to the movies as well, and the price tag is good for the play-time. I was able to complete the game in ~10 hours, while playing on hard mode with heavy exploration.You can tell this is not a triple A game, as I experienced a few bugs where the Death Angels became stuck or my breathing mechanic stopped working altogether. Similarly, after dying a few times, I was sick of seeing the death animation. Luckily, they include a skip button for these situations. Finally, the story is nothing amazing. It's not terrible, I think many reviews exaggerate how bad it is, but it's nothing that you'll remember after you reach the credits. In my case, I was focused on the gameplay.Many players can enjoy this title, but you'll have to have patience and play at a slower pace. If you want a high intensity game, this isn't for you. If you love the movies, you'll like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: ----------A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead masterfully captures the essence of its cinematic inspiration, delivering a chilling and immersive experience in a post-apocalyptic world where silence is the best survival.The game plunges you into a hauntingly quiet world, filled with the ever-present threat of sound-sensitive creatures. The first thing you’ll notice is the exceptional sound design. Every footstep, rustling leaf, and suppressed breath feels deliberate, heightening tension at every turn. The lack of a traditional soundtrack makes even the smallest noise stand out, putting you constantly on edge.The gameplay revolves around , with a heavy emphasis on creativity. Players must use the environment to their advantage—breaking glass to create distractions or treading on soft surfaces to evade detection. This makes every encounter unique, forcing you to adapt to the unpredictable behavior of the creatures.The story unfolds in fragments, following  struggling to survive with her astma and her yet unborn child. The emotional weight is palpable, with heartfelt moments of familial bonding contrasting starkly against the brutality of the world.Visually, the game shines in its ability to create a foreboding atmosphere. Overgrown towns, desolate farmlands, and dimly lit interiors are rendered with striking detail, evoking a sense of beauty and decay. The dynamic lighting system is particularly effective, casting eerie shadows that play tricks on your mind, making you question whether you're truly alone. Sound might seem for some weird, like very loud footsteps or very heavy breathing, but for some other people it might give the impression of the quiet world where even your small step might seem like the loudest sound while staying silent.Altho the game is great, it does in fact have some bugs or errors that can be found like , or problems with interacting with certain items.A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead is not just a game; it’s an experience. It challenges players to think differently, to embrace both silence and sound as a weapon and a shield. With its gripping narrative, gameplay mechanics, and atmospheric design, it’s a must-play for fans of survival horror and narrative-driven adventures. _childDocuments_.review: Playing on Hard Mode and i'm only 7 hours in at the time of writing this. It will be updated again when I finish the game. The Death Angel AI is interesting enough to keep the game somewhat lively. My biggest complaint is that the distraction items and most notably the bricks, do not attract the AI in a significant way when they are in an elevated position such as a camper. I feel like the Asthma attacks aren't actually a big deal since the skill checks to keep going are quite easy to consistently hit and your breathing doesn't pop up on the phonometer anyway during this, which I found quite odd but it must have been found particularly annoying during play tests if it was there, I surmise. It feels unique but bordering on pointless. It would have been a fun gimmick to properly manage. Things such as slow walking don't particularly alert them to your presence even if they are close to you.The next oddity is that making noise above the environmental limit you're given in an area will play the audio queues of one of them being nearby but they simply aren't. If noise is continuously made then it puts the player into a game over cutscene. I feel like this is one of the biggest detractors to the pacing and the atmosphere of the game because they put a decent amount of work into the model and sound of the death angels. The pathing of their AI, outside of leaving an elevated position, is also quite well done even if its a simple patrol. Simply not having them physically nearby in these instances is quite the loss to the atmosphere of the game and in my opinion severely loosens the tension of when one actually is around. The most pain staking instance of this so far during my playtime was  The story is alright with some questionable moments so far. Certain moments having disappointing impact due to a lack of character interaction or meaningful build up. Currently Laura is a rather...lets say 'peculiar' character. I understand its a horror game and its quite the lazy trope to not throw any meaningful interactions with the games entity at the player in the intro due to artificial suspense building but having such a cool location as the home with the rain pouring down, and NOT having it show up there. I feel this would have been a prime introduction to the monster indoors. A sorely missed opportunity for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, I actually don't think this game should be purchased for 30$. I also think it's just barely an okay game. However, it does enough stuff uniquely, and still respects the source material, that I will BARELY give it a positive review.The Good:- Unique mechanics throughout almost the entire game. Really impressive.- Really fun little interaction puzzles. They're very simple and take maybe 5s, but they add so much to the character of the game.- The microphone system is neat. At one point I went "oh that's how I get over there" audibly and got murdered. 10/10- The concept is unique, and a faithful representation of the movies- Immersive HUD with the ability to hide yellow paint (!!!)The BAD:- >9 hours to finish the game, with 70% collectibles, on the hardest difficulty. This is the worst one in my eyes.- The only times you need an asthma inhaler, they make noise, so you can't actually use them.- The AI is downright infuriating. You make a bunch of noise 500ft. away. The mob goes there for 2 seconds, then immediately runs right back next to you, even if you make 0 noise. It makes the sections with the mobs present tedious and annoying, rather than suspensful and puzzle-y. There's basically no room for creative thinking.- The story is really bland, basically nothing. Point A to point B, and there are maybe a few characters along the way.- The flashlight system burns battery way too fast for no reason, which becomes even more annoying in late game. - There's an annoying horror movie sting every time you make any noise, which makes it feel very videogamey and destroys immersion. _childDocuments_.review: If it looks decent to you - get it, just dont expect a B+ experience. It has great potential, I would love to see this given a large budget and follow more in Alien Isolation's footsteps. The game has good atmosphere and tension, the musical stings really help you feel each mistake. The hospital, backyard, woods, & train wreck sections are extremely nerve racking. I really like the use of the audio device to see noise levels. Its a decently horror experience for the price. The overall story and dialogue is not good, definitely not the worst, but is not interesting, cheesy/predictable, and forgetful. Enemy AI is ok, and while at first the gameplay loop is fun and interesting it quickly wears off because all you are doing is just moving slowly 90% of the time inbetween the tense sections mentioned above and is kind of artificially dragged out because of this. I feel like a survival story of Tomb Raider (2013) with gameplay and AI more akin to Alien Isolation could deliver a world class horror experience in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game but unused potential. The levels are a bit stale. The mechanics to avoid the creature are lackluster and methods of traversing the levels are a bit uncreative. They were like: Players like wood. Players like boards. Here you have Bob Board Buddy. The only way to change up the map traversial. And he is made out of the creekiest wood on planet earth, so it took me 45min to finish the last part of the game, because I got caught be McGee super ears stomping away on my Buddy Board eventhough I was crouched and sneaking. I guess the game tries to fit in with the movies, so the devs were kinda restricted of what they can do. But on the other hand an inspired setting would have helped at that. The mic integration is a great idea but never came into play for me, because I was quite the entire time and the absence of any jumpscares make it even more useless since nothing makes you jump.Lastly, McGee Super ears. He is not as threating as I initially thought. His behavior is very straight forward. You make to much noise = Dead. But mostly you can sneak past him quite easily. His movement can easily predicted since it is restricted to the big areas of the level, so you kinda know where he can't get in or randomly step on you and kill you. Ok, one more thing :)  The difficulties are not what they claim to be. I played on hard for my blind playthrough and only 2 sections would I consider as hard. And again difficulty as been achieved not by introducing puzzles or other dangers. No. Just make the level as annoying to go through as possible by having Bob, your thrustee Buddy board, invisible glass shards and having you step on puddles, were I could swear on my Board that I was at least 1m away from it. Still would recommend to play. Great for couch coop and scaring your girl-/boyfriends, if they are not used to horror games

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could leave a mixed review for this, but that's unfortunately impossible, I originally left a positive review because I did still kinda enjoy the game, but after a thought or two, plus seeing other people play it, I arrived at a conclusion that this game does not deserve a positive rating.A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead is a very, very slow game and it can potentially become pretty boring or frustrating in some instances.Graphically it is very beautiful, although in classic DirectX 12 fashion - the shadows are extremely grainy, and RayTracing did not reflect my character where it should. Besides that, graphically, like I said - the game is looking absolutely fine, and the addition of RT makes the lights just absolute chef's kiss. I did not have any issues with the performance either, but I will say the game refused to stick to a locked framerate, and happily exceeded a set limit with no regards to any laws of nature or even my NVIDIA control panel setting, where I usually tend to set the cap if the game refuses to acknowledge it from the in-game settings.The actors performed very well, both the animations, both body and facial along with the voice acting. Along with that, I enjoyed the story a fair amount as well, with the main highlight for me being the little side-stories you learn from notes scattered around, funnily enough. I don't mean to flame the main story, it wasn't awful, just a little forced is all.I did run into some issues playing this game, however. Nothing serious, no crazy game-breaking bugs or just any bugs generally, even.My first problem was that the game is ridiculously slow (obviously) and I'm the kinda guy who likes, heck - prefers slow games usually, but A Quiet Place can feel a little extreme at times. You're forced to play this game in a speed of a turtle. Not even! Along with that, you're constantly looking at your feet, making sure you don't bump into anything, looking for the tiniest objects like a singular can on the floor, leaves and pebbles, avoiding every puddle of water... I get that it's literally the whole gimmick and the point of the game, I'm just meaning to say it becomes really exhausting after a while, especially if you have to replay a section a couple of times.The mechanic of course offers a bunch of really cinematic moments, where a creature is approaching you, as you slowly back away holding your breath, not taking your eyes off of the creature, before you inevitably bump into a bucket left on the floor leading to your demise. For me however, the excitement turned into boredom and boredom turned into irritation the closer I was to the finish line.I played this game on Hard difficulty and I'm not sure if that lead to me being actually pissed off essentially by the end of the game or if it was just poorly designed? I would say the last 3, maybe 4 chapters I started getting irritated by how seemingly random my deaths suddenly became. I could be in a room, prestine floors with nothing on it that would cause me to make a sound, I walk past a certain spot 5 times and nothing happens, and then 6th time I pass the same spot and suddenly the game thought it'd be funny to make a random sound play out of nowhere and just kill me on the spot. Other time I walked up to a door, grabbed the handle, I don't think I even managed to move the door itself before the game randomly just killed me again for no reason?The closer to end-game I got the more persistent this bs was. I could be on a clean floor once again, crouched and fully sneaking - the game makes a sound out of nowhere and kills me on the spot, I load the game, look at the exact spot, nothing is there, I walk over it again, nothing happens this time around.Like, at some point it just felt like the developers were laughing in my face xdI ended up dying so much and often here, I got bored of the death animations ridiculously early into the game, and that comes from a dude who always enjoys those in all the games that allow them, games such as For Honor, Friday the 13th, Aliens vs Predator or even Call of Duty takedowns... I hated them here! They're not very interesting as is, but the biggest issue with them is that the main character always just stands there like a moron when she could easily cause a distraction, or even run away. But hey, you can't really run in this game, well - besides one particular section, apparently. For no particular reason too, they just sort of introduced it out of nowhere, for no reason, it's just "oh, now you run btw" and it never comes back. Anyway, the developers graciously provided us with a "skip" button for those animations.That frustration was only further fueled whenever I would pay attention to how absolutely perfectly the noise-traps were arranged to make my life more miserable. I get it though, it's the point of the game, I know. Still, the combination just left me feeling frustrated is all, let me be mad :>I'm also not sure about this stupid jumpscare sound effect? You would think it happens when you alert the creature, but sometimes it happens when I'm not even moving. The worst part about it is how it's just constantly spammed throught the whole game and the option to turn it off is just nowhere in sight. It wasn't scary, it wasn't tense, it was just stupid, annoying and unnecessary. Oh, but my absolute biggest issue here, same issue that plagued Alien Isolation as well - the insane rubber-banding for the creature can be absolutely relentless. I hated it more than anything! I once again acknowledge why it is a thing in a game such as this, but it absolutely pissed me off seeing how wherever I went, no matter how quietly - the creature was ALWAYS on my a*s. It didn't matter how little noise I made, it didn't matter how many distractions I used, the monster always gravitated toward me regardless.I've had instances where the creature deliberately chose to ignore my distraction and shamelessly follow me around. Yes, ignore this glass window shattering to pieces, let's walk over to this random corner that I totally can't see and make sure the huge noise didn't come from here!This is more prominent in late-game once again where there's a lot more space available to you, and more places for the creature to go and check, in theory anyway, because it would rather ignore that annoying, constant noise of a burning flare and instead go and check this plank of wood that let out a tiny squeak once.In regards to the story, it was alright like I said. A bit cheesy perhaps, with how stupid the main character is at times.Like, it's all a bit forced all for the sake of plot convenience. With that said - I did still enjoy it, just don't expect anything too deep in that department here. The little side-stories were a lot more touching in my opinion.If you're curious about the game, I would say you're better off watching someone else play it, unless you really don't mind spending the money, still - I would advise against it. It's not the worst game I've ever played by any means, but far from a good experience.
