_childDocuments_.review: Good so far, kind of a pleasant surprise. A decent Alien: Isolation / Amnesia style title with a plausible reason for the player to be outmatched. Needs some tweaking of accessibility features though, I found controller inputs to struggle between slow and quick walking, making it frustrating to make some of the dexterity based movement and skill inputs. Tried with several controllers, wired and wireless, all seem to suffer. Seems the walking is binary rather than linear speed increase / decrease.Update: Finished around 12-13 hours in on easy mode. Ehhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh, this is more of a 60/40 recommend at this point. Like similar games in the genre, it drags on for WAY too long. I also ended up having to finish on mouse & keyboard, any time I have to use M&K over controller, it's already toeing a "not recommend" line. This genre is good for somewhere between 2-6 hours, after that, they get to be a real slog - look at the nearly 20 hour long Alien: Isolation and its completion rates. There are some decent mechanics and they continue to get introduced through the last segment of play, but man do they get irritating. I couldn't imagine playing this on a higher challenge, easy wasn't even fun by the end but I wanted to finish it and not keep it in my ever growing backlog.
_childDocuments_.name: A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead

_childDocuments_.review: You would think this game would take inspiration from Alien: Isolation but no. A Quiet Place takes inspiration from generic indie horror and has two ways how stages can go. You have an instant kill monster which isn't roaming around the map but comes and kills the player after three noises are being made, with the first and second noises you get a warning sound and the third one kills you. The second way is basically just that you have a monster on your map, but it follows your immediate vicinity. You can die the same way as before, but now you can also die if you touch the creature. Sometimes you have an option to throw items to make noise and the monster goes to the place where you have thrown the object but it comes back really quickly, so it's nothing like in Alien where the monster really roams around and comes to you when you make a noise. Here the creature is constantly with you. It's pretty annoying, to say the least. Constant handholding and tutorialization stops the flow of the game and flashback scenes are just too slow and make the pacing feel tedious. Speaking of slow, most of the time you have to sneak veeery slowly, there aren't many places you can even walk normally or even slowly. Funnily it's nothing like in the movies. Some minor gripes too, there seem to be AI art on the walls, it's also Amnesia Rebirth all over again with   and it's a generic and boring story. At first it felt kind of cool but when you realize how generic it all is it's just turns to s*it and btw it's too long. There is a lot more little stuff that's annoying as hell, but I don't care enough to list them here. If you like walking sims with instant death, go ahead, but if you want something horror with fun gameplay, play something else for example, Silent Hill 2 Remake, Alien: Isolation etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Love A Quiet Place lore and was excited to play this game. There were very tense moments where even on hard difficulty it felt like I had room to breathe (pun not intended) if I made too much noise. Story felt like it belonged in the universe, even if it was pretty predictable and overly bleak.  On the flipside, there were several times it felt like I had no idea where to go if it were not for the yellow paint. Which, quite literally, marks every point of progress in this game. It's a little obscene, and though you can turn off the paint in the settings it feels like a bandaid for somewhat poor level design. And the loud audio stinger for when you make too much noise was obnoxious. It played way too often and sometimes left me confused if the monster was actually searching for me or just wanting to play me the song of its people. While the slow speed helped with the immersion, there were certainly times I wanted to just run through a level and get to the next point. The game overstayed it's welcome just a wee bit in that regard. Overall, I still enjoyed it for what it was. It definitely oozed atmosphere. The tense 'hide and seek' moments felt unique to this universe since the monsters are on full display, glorious booty and all. If you're looking for an indie-style horror game that's a little slower than your average 'hide/run from monster' simulators and love the Quiet Place universe, give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the A Quiet Place movies, I was really excited to dive into The Road Ahead. However, I initially hoped for a more narrative-driven, decision-making game, like Until Dawn, since I’m usually not a fan of the gameplay style this title employs. But I stayed optimistic, especially since it was developed by an indie studio, and the premise seemed promising.Let’s get the negatives out of the way first. Some levels dragged on too long, making them feel tedious. The moments where you get caught and killed lose their scary impact after the third time since the same animations repeat, which takes away from the tension. I also wish the Death Angels (the creatures) were more unpredictable—they follow predetermined paths, which lessens the suspense. The pacing felt a bit uneven at times, which made some sections frustrating.One mission I particularly disliked involved being in the back of a van, trying to shoot Death Angels with a shotgun. The controls in this section felt clunky and unresponsive, which made it more frustrating than fun.Now, onto what I enjoyed. I really liked the characters, especially Alex and her backstory—I found myself invested in her journey. However, I wish the other characters had been more developed and involved because the ending left me wanting more. While the puzzles were enjoyable (if a bit repetitive), balancing stealth, avoiding the Death Angels, and solving puzzles under pressure made for a thrilling experience.There were some genuinely scary moments too. One standout moment happened during the fourth mission when I accidentally kicked a can, and a Death Angel crashed through the wall of the house like the Kool-Aid Man—it made me scream out loud! I also appreciated that the protagonist has asthma, which added a unique layer to the gameplay. Managing her condition forced me to think more carefully about my surroundings, and it made my decisions feel more impactful.Overall, despite its flaws, A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead lays a solid foundation for future games. I hope we get more entries in this universe because there’s so much untapped potential here. With tighter pacing, better-developed characters, and refined gameplay, the next installment could be truly exceptional.

I do wish there was a bit more interactivity with the environment rather than just going to the yellow painted ledges and quietly opening doors.. It just felt like it was missing something else. Overall this was a good experience and worth the $40 AUD price tag.I give this game a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game does a good job of portraying a story in the Quiet Place with a cast of unique characters and increasingly tense environments. However, the creature AI and story line are lacking wherein for people who do not typically indulge in stealth horror games would likely not enjoy the game in its current state.The game definitely captures the essence that the movies give. While playing I became hyper aware of every small detail and noise I made. Story tugged at the heart strings and majority of the cast of characters were likeable. The story has a variety of levels with unique mechanics and pathways around so it never felt like a drag playing each different level.While the game is good, I hated playing as the main character as I do not know any world where someone needs as many inhalers and pills in such a short frame with no physical labour. The only redeemable quality about her was that  That was the absolute only reason I cared for her and would have been quite happy playing as literally anyone else in the game. The sound system is a fun concept but is just frustrating when it comes to actual game play. You can be moving the absolute slowest you can through an obstacle you cannot avoid and you will still manage to amplify above the atmospheric sound and attract the creatures. This annoyance becomes further amplified when using planks to move around. I think I could breathe on the planks and it'd create enough sound a whole orchestra couldn't achieve. This was enough to PMO but the actual angels themselves were a whole other thing. During periods where they were not physically present, the amount of noise you make did not matter as long as you waited enough time. This is in stark contrast to where you are face to face with them and the slightest noise will make them barrel to your location and baby sit the area for the next 3 years. This would be fine if it wasn't for their massive hit box and chicken winged stance where if you don't have any items to create sound a distance away from you, expect to be clipped by the wings of these beasts. If somehow I was able to make no sound ever and these issues became obsolete because of that, the pathing of the creatures would still be enough to make the game enjoyable because what do you mean the angels have jumped on inaccessible areas for most of the level for it to only jump right onto my ass as I'm about to escape? The randomness is fine and expected as these are wild creatures obviously but it becomes annoying when I die due to it suddenly wanting to tip its toes into some water. I would still recommend this game to anyone who really loves the Quiet Place universe and/or really enjoys tense stealth horror like Alien Isolation but would stop at that. The game really hasn't got much for the player to get invested in for a story game and the gameplay itself is quite infuriating at times. I'd wait for the game to have a few updates hopefully fixing the gameplay elements many are talking about or I'd wait for the game to be on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so early impressions review. I had pretty high expectations for this game, something about the early footage really sold me on it, and the game has surpassed them. It runs solid and doesn't cook my gpu like some UE5 games do. It has a good bit of graphics settings and even maxed out with hardware RT my 7900 xtx has even shut off the fans occasionally. With the hotspot on my gpu being in the 50s a few times and commonly in lower 60s. This card runs hot, especially with UE5 games for some reason, and they cook when using RT as well. So the game is clearly very well optimized. One negative is that it only has frame gen with DLSS. I easily rectified that by installing a FSR3 that worked with no issues; upgrading the upscaler to 3.1 and adding frame gen. Still would be nice just to have it natively though. The game is very Alien Isolation inspired for sure. It totally embraces the world of TQP though and truly feels apart of it so even with the similarities it doesn't come off as a Isolation clone by any means. I've really been impressed with the world building and writing/characters so far and am already invested which I wasn't expecting so that's a big plus. Like I said the gameplay has some alien isolation to it but it also has the physics system of something like Amnesia for when you open and close things or pick up things. I have always loved those mechanics but now they're even more involved because it's all about being quiet. So you have to be super mindful to not slam open stuff or swing doors too fast and make the hinges squeak. So that's super cool to find a way to make those mechanics more than just a novelty. The thing I'm most impressed with is the sound design. They're so well done and really help you feel apart of the world. I'll come back after beating it and update how I feel about the whole thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only roughly about 90 minutes in, about the average runtime for one of the actual movies in the franchise this game draws from. While I'm still in the initial phase of the game, where you just begin to actually encounter a Death Angel proper, I'm given immediate flashbacks to Alien: Isolation's "San Cristobal Medical Facility" whilst trying to escape the dilapidated halls of a hospital. So far, the tension and atmosphere can be cut into with a knife, with my initial impression of the game being extremely favorable. The graphics and environmental detail are fairly impressive. Some noticeable limitations in the animations do not detract from the game visually, and I've encountered few instances of stuttering, if at all. It's a surprisingly well-optimized title, which unfortunately, requires a degree of recognition nowadays. As a fan of the aforementioned Isolation and games like Amnesia: The Bunker, The Road Ahead looks to scratch a very similar survival horror itch that requires more patience, as the meat of the gameplay revolves around extreme stealth and limited combat. Definitely excited to see what the same devs do with the Jurassic Park IP in the upcoming JP: Survival.

name: Contra: Operation Galuga
detailed_description: A new entry in the legendary Contra series is here! Contra: Operation Galuga is a thorough reimagining of the classic run-'n'-gun action game from the '80s, featuring modern graphics and sound, new stages, new enemies and bosses, new play mechanics, an updated weapons system, and explosive co-op combat for up to two players in Story Mode or four players in Arcade Mode! When the Red Falcon terrorist group takes over the Galuga Islands off the coast of New Zealand, elite Contra commandos Bill Rizer and Lance Bean springs into action, initiating an all-out war in which the fate of mankind hangs in the balance! Run, jump, and shoot your way through eight levels using a devastating arsenal - including the spread shot, laser, and homing missiles - now with stackable upgrades and awesome Overload abilities! The intense action is customizable with three difficulty settings plus a variety of additional challenge options. The true Contra legacy begins now! Key Features: •The original run-'n'-gun game is back, reimagined and more action-packed than ever! •Attack aggressively across eight explosive stages! Infiltrate the jungle, ascend the waterfall, speed through an enemy base on a hovercycle, and more! •Multiple playable characters with distinct abilities! •Epic, screen-filling boss battles! •New and fan-favorite weapons, now with stackable upgrades and incredible Overload abilities! •Multiple difficulty options and a wealth of extra content

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty damn good so far, honestly.Been a huge fan of Contra my whole life, but specifically have very fond memories of Contra 4 for a variety of reasons. Contra 4 also happens to have been developed by Wayforward and was a phenomenal entry. This game has a lot of the same feels and vibe as that one did. The 2.5D visuals used feel a little dated, but the Contra run and gun gameplay you know and love is there and that’s all that truly matters. Sound wise everything is satisfying and the soundtrack is more on the orchestral side, but you can also unlock different soundtracks for arcade and challenge mode. Speaking of those modes, there’s plenty of content on offer from what I can see so far. A full fledged story mode with cutscenes, arcade mode which is just classic play until you run out of lives, and a challenge mode with tons of different challenges (speed runs and stuff). There’s also a new perk system where you earn points as you play to spend in a perk shop that give nice little buffs to your character (Spread equipped on level start, Lance having a higher double jump, etc.) so that’s a nice little way to change the game up or give you an upper hand if you’re struggling. Don’t forget to put in the Konami Code for a special shop bonus!This game also runs perfectly on the steam deck out of the box, 60fps, so you can get your Contra fix on the go. All in all, as a fan, I recommend the game so far. If that changes at all the more I play, I’ll be sure to update my review. (Any game that lets me play as Probotector is a good game)Finally we can leave all that crap with Rogue Corps behind..

_childDocuments_.review: Wayforward knows what they're doing because they already made Contra 4. Contra: Operation Galuga on the surface might look like a simple cash in on Contra 1 nostalgia. but mechanically there is quite a bit of new things added to the series.First off character selection there are 10 characters who all vary in degree, Bill and Lance, have the most standard playstyle they have double jumps and Dashing/Air Dashing, but even between the two you can get a character specific perk. Bill's allows him to be in invulnerable durring a Dash, and Lance gets a Higher Double jump. Then you have a character like Stanley Ironside who's playstyle is entirely different, He can't Double Jump or Dash, but he has the Contra 4 Grapple hook to elevate himself higher quickly, and he can Hover. The Probotector Robots have the potential for all 4 movement options since they get double Jump and Dash, and with their two character perks giving them access to the Grapple Hook, and Hover, you only get two perk slots. so those movement options will be at the cost of something else that can give you more fire power, or survivability. Different characters may also very in what weapons they get.The Perk system is there if you want a bit of an edge in gameplay, there are cheaper perks like Start a level with your weapon of choice, or more expensive perks like keeping a weapon after dying, or increasing the amount of hit points you get, or healing a hit point when you overload a weapon (useless if you play with one hit deaths of course)When it comes to weapons the Lv2 upgrades by collecting the same one twice makes a return from Contra 4 and the new feature is Overloading. you can use a weapon (or just it's Lv2 upgrade if you are on an easier difficulty) in exchange for a powerful move. For example Laser lets you slow down the world around you, and you'll be free to deal a big chunk of damage to a boss. Flame gives you a very long lasting Flame wall that stops projectiles, Machine gun gives you invulnerably for a decent amount of time. You can also call in a bonus weapon pod if you fill up the meter. So every weapon drop you see is the opportunity for an overload.The levels enemies and bosses are a re-imagining of Contra 1, it'll be familiar but there is always a twist to keep things fresh, for example the Snow level now take place on a speeding Train moving though the snow top mountains, and the Robot boss is more elaborate, half way though it turns into a homage to a Contra Hard corps boss. This is a Solid Contra game, and it's very much worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I think my biggest issue with this game is that it doesn't adhere to the old philosophy of contra design (something cool or unexpected needs to happen every 3 screens, there's allot of repetitive dead air in this one most likely due to the 4-player mode) and the soundtrack being so forgettable, I really wanna like it but so far as a long time fan who was cautiously excited for something new I kinda dislike how there doesn't seem to be a single original idea in this game at all? Also it uses allot from contra 1-4 in ways that are kinda questionable? Like what if Super C gets remade? All of its ideas got re-used in this one already. Also all the enemies being hodgepodges from the other games without any real thought as to why they are there.Contra 4 had allot of original ideas, and this game kinda just re-uses them down to almost it's whole enemy roster (in terms of enemy behavior) and the whole time I'm thinking "man this game is pretty creatively bankrupt in a way I'm not enjoying"I'm not gonna say the game is bad, it's not, but it's just "passable" and kinda bland.I'll have to replay on arcade mode to see how the game really truly feels but clearing story mode on normal *is not a very good first impression* as a long time fan.Tho, I feel the biggest point that hurt this is the soundtrack being so bland.Shattered soldier and Hard Corps have some AMAZING OSTs, the whole series does even contra 4 was AMAZING in the department, and WF is usually known for their amazing music so idk wtf even happened here? I feel like the music might even be the main culprit to why I feel this harshly about the game, if it had some boppin tunes it might recontextualize the game for me but as is the OST is very uninteresting.Also, don't make a contra game this story focused ever again that's all I have to say about that.I really wish I could reccomend this game, I'm a long time fan of the series who really cares about its legacy titles and while I wasn't expecting much I was still disappointed in baffling and unique ways.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Contra fan since I got the NES version as a kid, it brings back so much fond memories of staying up late playing with my brother. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's the best Contra game in a LONG time. Is it perfect? No, it's not. But it's vastly superior to the more recent iterations that have been tarnishing the IP. I think the negative reviews I've seen are a bit too nitpicky, especially when looking at the games that came before this one. It's awesome seeing Contra done right again, especially in a new way that feels fresh and revitalized. Not to mention, it IS a re-imagining of the original game, so expect to see some memorable things from time to time. Just with better graphics, music, new gameplay elements, and more story. If the Contra series ever meant anything to you, I'd definitely check this out at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, it is one of the best classic sidescrolling run and gun games on the PC. The background story is easy to summarise: Red Falcon, a terrorist organisation, has occupied a remote group of islands and appears to be developing a forbidden weapon there. A special military unit sent there to clear up the situation has gone missing. So the two elite soldiers Bill Rizer and Lance Bean are sent out to stop the terrorists (or whoever is on the islands). They can also rescue the missing soldiers if they are still alive.At the beginning, we can select the difficulty level (easy/normal/difficult). Another setting allows us not to immediately lose a life with every hit, but to be a little more resilient thanks to several hit points. After each game, we receive a few coins - the further we have progressed, the more. We can use these coins to buy small improvements in the main menu, such as an extra hit point or the ability to upgrade our weapons from the start. Not dramatic upgrades, but definitely useful little things. There are a total of 36 such improvement, and we can select two of them per character at the start of each level.We run and shoot, but we are a little more mobile than in the classic Contra games. Double-jumping is one of our abilities right from the start, as is sprinting (dash). We can learn eight more skills in the course of the game. As in part one of the series, we can also lie flat on the ground to avoid the - comparatively slow - approaching enemy projectiles. We can easily shimmy along steel beams. We use the controller to control the game; by pressing RT, we remain in place and can use the stick to change the direction of our fire and fire in all directions. We carry up to two special weapons (there are six in total), which we can switch between at any time in a matter of seconds. There are eight game sections in total. In the second level, we are not running on foot but are travelling on a hoverbike and cannot stop. Supply drops give us new weapons when we collect them. We can also overload (and thus destroy) one of our weapons, which briefly gives us an extra ability. Weapons can be improved in their performance if we pick up an upgrade for them.There is a story mode, arcade mode and a challenge mode. The game can be played alone, although in story mode both elite soldiers are involved in the mission. However, it is even better to play the story mode together with a friend in local two-player mode. Then one controls Bill and one controls Lance. Chaotic, but also incredibly funny. You can play with four people (locally) in arcade mode. Bill and Lance are then joined by two probotectors (soldiers in a combat suit) or other unlocked heroes; there are no conversations or cutscenes in this mode. The challenge mode, on the other hand, offers 30 difficult individual scenarios and is only possible for one player. You can play with an ultra widescreen (21:9) without any problems - but with black bars on the side. Gamepad support on the PC is good - Playstation Dual Shock and X-Box One controllers worked straight away.Contra: Operation Galuga brings the series back to its old strengths, but significantly reduces the previously often inhuman level of difficulty. If you like, you can also set the difficulty level like in the old games (loss of life after a hit, tons of wildly shooting enemies). I am not so skilful and frustration-resistant and have more fun with a slightly lower difficulty level. But you should be careful here - with the difficulty turned down, with checkpoints and endless continues, as a pro you will be too fast in front of the final boss in level 8. The graphics are fantastic - with a resolution of 2560×1440 you simply see more than with the oldies at 300×200... Plus 100 FPS at 100 Hz (on my monitor) and a great soundtrack and voice output. Classic gameplay, modern technology - brilliant. The gameplay is also great fun - finally a really good classic run'n'gun game in the Contra universe again.

_childDocuments_.review: official mission briefing--------------------------------Year: 26XX AD. The Galuga Archipelago off the coast of New Zealand is ground zero for a mysterious meteor shower. Six months later, the Red Falcon terrorist group invades the island, and unusual gravity waves can be detected emanating from the area. The Earth Federation sends in the GX Army for reconnaissance, but contact has been lost. With no other viable options, the Earth Marine Corps dispatches its most elite soldiers - Bill Rizer and Lance Bean of the Contra unit - to investigate and neutralise any potential threats. The conflict that follows turns the once-peaceful island into an all-out warzone where the fate of mankind hangs in the balance.Source : my review--------------the game is fun to play while being more forgiving than the older games. you get a lot of continues. the game unlike previous iterations has difficulty levels, you can play on easy, normal or hard. you can also chose one-hit deaths.  the game offers variety of perks like special weapon retention on death and options to start with a special weapon type to name a few. perks have to be purchased from the perk shop with credits earned from playing the game. additionally the game has a story mode,arcade mode for up to 4 players co-op and a challenge mode. Story mode gives an idea about what is happening while you run and gun where as the arcade mode has pure action without the story. Challenge mode has different challenges set out for you to test your mettle.cons---------Remoteplay doesn't work properly, the second controller isn't detected properly in story mode. It shows keyboard and mouse as second controller in story and arcade mode remoteplay i'd recommend waiting until that is fixed before buying this game.possible solution for remoteplay p2 not working in story mode-------------------------------------------------------------------------------by CoPilotLindy:My friend and I had the same issue but we figured out how to work around the bug:Instead of Story mode, go into Arcade Mode. For whatever reason it'll force the remote player into P3 slot, but that's fine. Both of you select your characters and start Arcade Mode into the first level. Once the level starts, pause and quit out back to the main menu. Go back into Story Mode now and it should just suddenly work with the remote player as P2 (at least it did for us). But heads up that you have to do this every time you restart the game from Steam if you want to continue in story mode. Disappointing this wasn't caught before release, clearly people were going to use remote play to do coop.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game at this point. _childDocuments_.review: I think they mostly hit the sweet spot here--it has a high pick up and play factor, controls are easy to grasp and responsive (wisely, they don't over-egg the pudding), it looks great without calling too much attention to itself or making the action too chaotic to follow, and there's plenty of call-backs for us old fogeys who's been playing Contra for (grumble grumble) years and anti-frustration features for those of us who might have lost a step since our prime.It's just a notch below HARD CORPS: UPRISING in terms of being an ideal "start it up and blast things" kinda game, but I am enjoying it a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Contra: Operation Galuga

_childDocuments_.review: $40 is too much, but on a good sale it's a must-play for anyone who played the originals as a kid. Heck, it's a decent play for anybody new to Contra, but just be aware this game trades heavily in nostalgia, so you will be missing that part of it if you're new.Couch co-op is a huge plus, and it's very forgiving with what controller(s) you use. You will NEED a friend next to you to enjoy this game to the fullest. It's fine solo, but once again, you'll be missing a part.The Normal difficulty seems well-balanced for two players who are generally at least decent at games. Expect 90 to 120min for a story play-through, making this approachable as a have-a-friend-over sort of afternoon. Unlockables, arcade/challenge modes, etc gives some replayability, and the story hints at piles of DLC on the way - of course, I guess we'll see about that.Graphics are great and it runs smooth on low to mid-tier systems, but it's definitely more than a bit "diarrhea Christmas lights." It's not truly a bullet hell style game, but the screen gets pretty busy.Sound design is solid, and the remixed music is decent and familiar.Voice acting is way better than it deserves to be, and adds to the classic campy vibe. An unexpected and pleasant surprise.Again, get it on sale, and play with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Contra: Operation Galuga

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little bit too easy playing arcade and story mode. It feel like playing Hard Corps Uprising on rising mode where you level up to the point that the only challenge is the platforming. However, if you unlock extreme ultra mode. There's a lot of fun to be had. A lot of enemies running front and back of the screen. Bosses have a lot more health so they don't die so fast. Using the weapon switch glitch can help you but will not save you. The only downside to this mode is that it is single player. So, if you are playing with a friend you are basically locked into easy mode. Also the flamethrower is a bane to my existence.

_childDocuments_.review: God blessed video but it didn't bless this mess.This game is a whole lotta MEH.Been here, done this and it's been done a whole lot better. This is coming from a guy who models his entire online persona after the lead character of Contra and yeah... I can't say a damn good thing about this game.It looks like trash, it plays like trash and the music is forgettable... So forgettable in fact that they had to install optional 8-bit Contra and Castlevania tracks as substitutes for the main OST... what a travesty.The only plus side (which is subjective) is that they've made the game more accessible to casuals, which is great if you just wanna run through the game once and be done with it... but it's a total crutch for the long game. There's Ultra difficulty and Extreme Ultra difficulty modes for hard core players but the controls and graphics are so jank, I can't even see this being remotely enjoyable... it's chalk full of bugs and glitches, controls just decide to not work randomly and the level design and enemy placement is a complete disaster.The MSRP is the biggest sin this game commits. The pricing is absolutely absurd for a game that looks like a $5 cell phone app... $54 CAD for this? GTFO of here. I bought it with a -30% discount day 1 from GMG and the price was still $42 CAD after applicable taxes... I can't even understand the logic here, honestly.If you're a die hard Contra fan you're probably going to hate it, if you're a casual gamer who hasn't touched a Contra game since 1989, you might enjoy it for the nostalgia factor. Nothing will ever capture the magic of the first 4 main Contra entries [Contra 1, 2, 3 and Hardcorps]... this is just proof.It's unfortunately a no from me. I would definitely wait for at LEAST a 50% off sale, and even then, the amount of effort and content in this game isn't worth $15... If you can wait around a year or more for it to get a huge discount, I would, you're not missing out on anything... it'll be 15 dollars in no time.I'd rather just play the first 4 Contra games again and forget this even exists. What a bummer.

_childDocuments_.review: (I wouldn't write a review if this game doesn't have those bugs. That means if they fixed the bugs, I woud have deleted this review.)And, sometimes you can't dash or jump when you press the dash or jump button, and sometimes you do a double or triple jump instead of a normal jump.Imbalanced and cheap level and boss fights including too many boring repetitive levels, too much hp for basic enemies and pure and awful RNG with random cheap attacks in boss fights .  In some occasions in boss fights, you must have specific weapons to clear up the boss's bullets otherwise you can't dodge their attacks, and in some other occasions, unless you use invulnerability, you have no way to not take damage or not die. And plus the frequent death bugs, even if I'm lucky and also perform well in levels and boss fights, if I encounter one of those bugs, I have to replay and re-record the game. Also some death bugs like the level 4 beginning one and the level 3 boss one has caused me traumas that I have to remove my headset, close my eyes and cover my ears otherwise if I encounter those bugs, I would feel a severe heart attack. And even if I do so, when I open my eyes and see my character died, I still feel a light to medium heart attack. When doing no-damage runs in this game, it feels like doing labour job in an assembly line while gambling from time to time and you must win all the gambles while not fall asleep in the assembly line, and even if I don't fall asleep and win all the gambles, there is possibility that the machines be broken and then I'm instantly killed by the machines. It's very boring and frustrating. It's not rewarding to spend time on this game and it's also not even satisfying when I completed those no-damage (or no-death without health bar like most other contra genre games)runs. It's too frustrating and I actually don't want to play this game anymore but I have to keep playing it because there are still some things left to complete. _childDocuments_.review: I really do like this game. It gives me that Contra feel I've been missing. The weapons feel great, the controls feel tight, the level design is good. I don't hate it, but compared to how great Hard Corps: Uprising looks, they should've gone with a 2D look as well. I know 2D would've been more time consuming and probably cost more, but still. Again, it's fine, I don't hate it, but I don't like it.- The music. Contra needs to have good music. This game... just doesn't have it. _childDocuments_.review: WayForward's second whack at , and while this is better than whatever  was trying to be, it still doesn't do the long-running franchise proper justice.It does a lot of things right, the controls feel good and the analog 360-degree aiming is nice, but where it drops the ball are the overly long, padded, eventless stages, the non-descript run-of-the-mill soundtrack (that incorporates a recognizable cue every so often) and a general design blandness that doesn't come close to the imaginative setpiece rollercoasters that were  or especially It features 4 players co-op play, but only local, which is disappointing. _childDocuments_.review: A CLASSIC RE-IMAGINED I really enjoyed this contra game as a persona that used to enjoy the older games and getting my ass handed to me time and time again the fun game play was always what kept me coming back to them. i felt this new one had a very good mix of new and old. it also has feature to give players that are not so good at the games a little helping hand while still not making it super easy.i finished the story in one hour twenty nine minutes and racked up 142 deaths lol.the story mode features 8 different stages with a variety of run and gun levels or vehicle based shooter levels and some beautiful locations from lush green jungles to snowy mountains to ancient temples and alien ruins. the story was pretty fun and reminded me of a Saturday morning cartoon with a good voice cast. there's also a nice range of guns and power ups that feature two different stages that will change the way the guns handle my personal favourites being the homing missile and the triple shot gun these weapons also have a overcharge ability which grants the user to blow the weapon up and slow down time for example.the game also features an arcade style mode and a challenge mode which will give players some nice time sinks.there is also a perk shop that can also grant players a helping hand in the levels from extra lives to starting a level with a certain weapon you like i found this a nice feature and was a very big help although earning coins takes awhile. all in all the game is a nice return and way forward should be proud of themselves great level design and power ups help this game shine although the price seems slightly high i higly recomend this on a 20-30% off sale.also want to say thank you to the devs and key mailer for providing me a code for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a Contra veteran, I started playing from the classics, from Contra and Super C on the NES, continuing with Contra 3: The Alien Wars on the SNES, then Contra 4 on the DS, in the Wii Shop I was able to buy and continue with Contra Rebirth, and Contra Hard Corps, and until the release of Contra Anniversary Collection, I was able to play the Arcade Contras, and the GameBoy Operation C, and after playing for more than 100 hours, I can say that Contra : Operation Galuga is one of the best Contra games. If you are a veteran like me, you will see references in each level, small nods to other games, and even several enemies and bosses from multiple games. Plus you can unlock different OSTs from other games of Contra, I chose the OST of Contra 4 since it is my favorite of the entire saga, and if you want even more difficulty, it has a mode where you only have 3 lives without continues, I recommend playing it with an Xbox or PlayStation controller, since With control you can point and shoot in any direction, if you play on a keyboard like me, you will only be able to shoot in 8 directions, which will be complicated in some areas of the game and enemy attacks, it may be a little expensive, but if you are a fan of the Contra saga, I assure you that it will be worth the full price, in addition to supporting the devs, and showing interest in the saga, so as not to have to wait another 7 or 10 years for a new game, I am not one to write reviews, but I love the Contra series, Let's attack aggressively¡~

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long time Contra fan, dating back to playing this game with friends in the NES days. I've experienced the ups and the downs with the series.I got this expecting that I would enjoy it but it wouldn't earn more than a thumbs down for the two main complaints in the other reviews:1. It is overpriced2. It is too shortBut I can't thumbs down the game for that....for a big big reason.What makes Contra so good? I mean to this day, I have no problems going back to play the ones on NES, SNES, and Genesis...whereas there are games that came out recently that I beat and moved on.And that is where it hit me: Contra's strong point has always been its replayability. Back in the NES days it depended on this. No saving, no password...just sit down and beat it from start to end. Plus the NES games were about $50 in 1980s money. So those type of games had to be something yo would want to come back and play over and over.And that is what this one does already. I've done the first level 3 times already, and loved every run through it. Suddenly the 2 hour long/$40 overpriced complaints just don't hold up.I love Alien Wars the most. I doubt this will knock that Contra out of the top spot. I love the first and have way too many memories of it. I doubt this will take that from 2nd place. But 3rd place...this one has a strong chance.Its good, and it will keep you coming back. For that it is worth the price and the length.

_childDocuments_.review: Background:I play Contra games since very beginning . My first Contra experience  was back in 1992 in my first Family Computer import. I was amazed by the game at that time. Review: Contra: Operation Galuga is great tittle and addition to the Contra franchise. It's retain this "Contra" feel into the game and if you like the first four Contra games (Contra, Super C, Alien Wars and Hard Corps) you will definitely  love this one. is very fluid and extremely responsive and is up to the standard from Konami old school shooter. It's plays exactly like in the old school games plus some extras. You can jump, shoot in 8 direction (or 360 degree) , sweep , double jump. You have special Overload weapon ability that will destroy your current special weapon for a one time special effect. Effect depends on the weapon you currently have equipped. Operation Galuga is not very hard game compared to brutally difficult Contra 3 , but is still challenging and you will have hard time beating the game with old school "One hit kill" option enabled. Still is balanced and all the mistakes are accountable to the player not about bad controls, bad camera, glitches or bugs. All the characters from original Contra games are there plus two Probotector which fit into the story nicely . After completing a level you will receive Credits that you can spend in the in-game shop . Will not spoil the fun what you can unlock it's up to you to find out , but its' worth every minute of struggle to earn the credits.  The game provide nice graphics . It's not something that is unseen for today standards though. It's not rich in polygons and the textures are somewhat cartoonish , but still look nice and fit in the Contra universe. The animation of characters is very fluid and detailed. A lot of enemies do crazy animations (big robot stomping on a train, red falcon soldier running with big rocked over his head, giant alien monster trying to eat a spaceship etc) .Overall the graphics, models  and textures do their job perfectly and you never feel something is out place. Decent job. The  music in the game is very good. The music is nice rendition of already familiar tunes from original Contra game but extended and more rich in progression. This is very nice touch and balance between old school nostalgia and today's music standard for games. Sounds are also very solid. Everything fit exactly what you expect to be and never gets old. The only sound FX that for me personally is little bit out of place is machine gun, but this is just me and very lite nit picking. I really enjoy the story in Contra: Operation Galuga. It's not super corny , but also will not win any Oscar . It's a about an artifact that is left from alien race here on , hidden from another alien race. The goal is our heroes to get first to the artifact. It's engaging story, the voice acting is very good. All characters have their own distinct personality - Razor is rough and direct , Lance is more careful , Ariana is sharp minded etc.Contra: Operation Galuga is great game. If you like Contra games you will love this one. My only negative thing about the game is that is too short, but this is because is classic arcade run and gun shooter. The game is just great and you want to play more after the last level. Highly recommended.Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the *Contra* series, I went into *Operation Galuga* with high expectations—and I'm happy to say that it delivers on many fronts. Visually, the game is a feast for fans of the franchise, with impressive 2D side-scrolling graphics that incorporate just the right amount of 3D elements. The dynamic camera angles and shifting terrain in some levels add depth and excitement, keeping the gameplay fresh while staying true to the series' roots.The character models strike a great balance—keeping that classic *Contra* vibe without overcomplicating the details. Lucia is a standout addition to the roster, and her version of the iconic Spreader gun, complete with a charge-up blast wave, is immensely satisfying to use. Ariana brings a fierce and fun energy to the team, while Lance and Bill are a welcome throwback for veterans of the series. I have to admit, the robot character didn’t quite click for me, but that’s more of a personal preference than a knock against the game itself.The story keeps close to *Contra's* established lore, but with some fresh twists that make it feel modern without losing the nostalgic charm. I appreciated how the narrative played out while keeping the action fast-paced and chaotic, which is exactly what you'd expect from the franchise.One feature I really enjoyed was the ability to pick up perks, power-ups, or start levels with specific weapons and bonuses. It adds a strategic layer to the game, giving you a bit more control over how you approach each stage, and it's a nice quality-of-life improvement that fits right in.That said, my main gripe—and this could be more about me than the game itself—is the difficulty. *Operation Galuga* is brutally hard. It’s not unusual for *Contra* games to be challenging, but this one feels particularly intense. I found myself overwhelmed at times, with projectiles and explosions all over the screen, making it tough to distinguish what's happening. The sheer amount of chaos, paired with the complexity of some levels and the number of abilities mapped to the controller, made it hard to keep up. Maybe I’m just older and slower than I used to be, but I had to grind my way through certain sections.Overall, though, *Contra: Operation Galuga* is a fantastic entry in the series. It stays true to its roots while offering just enough modern flair to keep things interesting. Despite the challenge, it's a must-play for fans of the franchise and anyone who enjoys fast-paced, no-nonsense action games. Just be prepared for a tough ride—you might find yourself longing for a save point or two! As a longtime Konami and *Contra* fan, I’d still wholeheartedly recommend this one. It’s classic *Contra* through and through.

_childDocuments_.review: When a sleek, nostalgic title returns in modern times, you often experience disappointment, not that much, but still often. 'Contra: Rogue Corps' wasn't a bad game, but certainly not what I expected from a nostalgic experience in a new guise, but 'Contra: Operation Galuga' makes up for it down to the last detail!So far I played this new Contra title as a complete surprise, full of nostalgic features that match both the gameplay and difficulty level very well with the good old days, even the visual upgrades are completely acceptable and appreciated.So it really feels like a classic Contra title but with the right new contemporary aspects to give Contra a successful makeover.In the game you will also see all the iconic weapons and environments, but also new levels, enemies and bosses and many new challenges.The levels that I have already played through are always a pleasure to continue even with the number of (necessary) replays and I don't get the impression at all that the gameplay becomes monotonous after a short period.Contra: Rogue Corps is, in my opinion, an outstanding 'reboot' of the iconic Contra NES games, one about which I currently cannot think of anything that I consider a negative.

_childDocuments_.review: [[ First Impressions ]]So far i made it to Stage 3, some things to say:- Levels are quite long, probably the longest stages on the franchise, similar or longer than Hard Corps Uprising levels.- There's a Rising style mode like Hard Corps Uprising but more simpler. This system allows you to equip certain abilities that make the character more stronger than default, things like starting with "M", "S", keeping the weapons if the player dies, etc.However it's limited by 2 slots so you can't abuse of the benefits.- Story mode is probably the most expanded in Contra so far and by a lot, fortunately these story segments are mostly before starting the stage and after finishing it.- Difficulty wise.... Stage 1 and 2 are between easy and moderate (by that i mean comparing it to classic Contras like 1,2,3, Hardcorps JP) , depending on your settings.However at Stage 3 the game becomes noticeable more difficult, getting more closer to classic Contra territory.I will probably make a full review after finishing it but so far... Is the game fun? i would say Yes and easily a true Contra game ......... but so far it doesn't blow my mind for many personal reasons (Art direction, some characterizations that i dont agree, tonewise i think it's too soft for Contra, etc).Should you buy it? i can't answer that yet but i did bought it because i didin't want to have the Contra IP abandoned for another 10 years again and the game is fun and well made enough so far for me. it's 6am here so im going to sleep for the moment....i'll be back.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever seen South Park when Cartman gets his own amusement park and cries out "I'm..SOOOOOOOOO...happy"!This is exactly how I am feeling now after spending an hour with Operation Galuga.Native 4K support - Check120 FPS - CheckI am an arcade gamer from way back, I mean that's what I grew up in, and then C64 then Amiga then Mega Drive, you get the picture. These will always be my favourite type of game, always, and in particular I love run n gun games.I have been waiting for a new 2D Contra for a long time, as any other Contra fans have.I am not disappointed.I love that you can upgrade an already picked up weapon to be more powerful.I love power ups and this has plenty.The music works but there's retro options for that too.Controls are tight, no lag detectable, and you can finally double jump in a contra game. YAY!I personally like the graphics, with multiple layers of parallax, and think this is what a modern Contra game *should* look like. It feels like the older console games to me but simply jazzed up with the times.I like the difficulty choices and how you can have a health bar or one hit death.I haven't finished it yet but this is something, and I had a sneak peak at a video and it's only a couple hours long. But for the first time, I actually think this retro inspired game could have been double the length and 4 hours long, especially at the price.I think price is the only nit pic, it should be 39.95 AUD at normal price (say 25 USD) but it is what it is. near 60 AUD is just too much for this kind of game. _childDocuments_.review: Contra is back!This Contra has some flaws:- Bullets/enemies and power ups in red ... having high contrast for things that kill you had been learned in the 80s- Not clear when the enemies can be shoot in the hover bike levels- The 3D doesn't look as nice as the pixel art, but I hope it makes it future proof for higher resolutions- Reuse of enemies/levels of the past Contras is a little bit lazy- The story mode is a total waste of resources, I'd rather have WayForward put all resources in the Arcade modeStill, this is a real, proper Contra. It gets the most important things right:- Pacing, so many wannabe Contras fail at proper pacing of the action- Crisp controls- Methodical shooting with spurts of pure violence- Excellent level design- Always fair/no cheap deaths- It simply is fun and feels awesome to play!- Most importantly: It teaches the young generation that if a problem cannot be solved by violence, you are not using enough of itThere is nothing on Steam that feels/plays like Contra, worth the full price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Contra: Operation Galuga more than I expected.Positives:- Light hearted narrative was nicely done- Weapons all feel different and fun to shoot- Four player coop, and different characters- Challenge mode is a nice bonus, and appreciated extra content- Mini economy system allows for some interesting strategic choices on bonusesNegatives:- No online coop- In-game weapon drop system is kind of annoying, as I accidentally grabbed/switched weapons more than I'd have liked to.I realise the online coop criticism may be unfair, but it really would have added so much more enjoyment to this game, that I ended up beating just playing alone. Would have really given an excuse to get more friends to buy it as well, really feels like a big oversight in 2024 with a game seemingly built for cooperative play.I appreciated that I could play the game on a casual difficulty level, and found that was JUST RIGHT for me in terms of challenge - BUT still wouldn't have minded the Story mode being a bit longer, but I understand some of the game length is meant to come from the difficulty level. But it took me about 2.4~ hours to beat on casual.With everything said, I would recommend this game to any classic Contra fans who are happy to play a side scrolling shooter.

It has a bunch of interesting challenges and will serve to increase your skill so you can go for the coveted one credit clear!Experienced Contra fans: ignore the critics! Galuga is more than worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I love these kinda of games and while the price is high as someone who will replay these types of games over and over again, it's worth it. It's classic good Contra. You can play with HP (like JPN Hard Corps) or one hit and die like what most people are familiar with. There are 10 characters total after unlocking each with their own abilities (Lucia is trash though). You can only unlock 3 of them after you beat story mode and THEN use in game points to unlock them. I personally think the amount of money to unlock them is insane (8000). If you want to grind cash fast, select arcade, no health or perks, select Bill (he is the fastest) run towards the first enemy, die, kill an enemy that spawns in and die on the one dude until you hit a game over for 87 points. This is faster because beating the level will only net you 200 something points and takes 8-10 minutes to beat. Honestly they should just lower the cost.I do hope Wayforward makes another Contra because they once again knocked it out of the park. Highly recommended for run and gun fans (unless you like bad ones like Cuphead)

_childDocuments_.review: A very expensive game for a very lifeless remake ! Non of the original Contra atmosphere and enthusiasm. The first mission, The Jungle is the most resembling. The gameplay is very chaotic. A lot of bullets, enemies spawning from everywhere. You get very few life points and when you finish a level very few credits to upgrade. Also, in the original contra you were not killed in mid-air by thrown grenades and other objects unless on impact. When you upgrade up a weapon, it does not deal much extra damage. When you receive a new weapon from the flying box, most of the times you shoot it accidentally and mid-fight the fire changes automatically and you get hit. The enemies from the original Contra die when shot once (most of the low ones). Now, you have to shoot them multiple times even the lowest enemies and they form a crowd and you lose again. Also, from the original Contra, bigger enemies used to turn orange, red and then die to give you indication on their remaining health. Now you don't know when an enemy is dying. Overall, except for the Jungle mission, it is not a emotional come-back of the original game. Even the soundtrack and mission music could be enhanced to give a more dynamic rock-heavy metal approach. I hope they will correct all of these with an add-on (expansion) at least because i was sincerely looking for the comeback of a childhood perfect game. In the end and having all of the above presented, the game is not worth the expense, i'm sorry to say this.  Even if it has 8 levels and you finish the game under two hours, it did not bring a ounce of enthusiasm (except for the Jungle mission and a couple more). By the way, the voices of the characters are monotonic and not convincing and the story text is not totally but almost totally rubbish :(

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of Contra since my childhood days, grew up on the likes of Contra 3 and Contra Hard Corps. Naturally much like the rest of Konami's flagship franchises Contra had it's name drug through the mud (Looking at you Rogue Corps and your really stupid idea of adding a overheat mechanic) so I was a bit wary of Operation Galuga.Needless to say, this is the most fun I've had in Contra in quite some time.Story who really cares Red Falcon is invading to get an artifact to allow them to open wormholes on Earth and you as a member of Contra are to stop it. Initially you can only play as your standard Bill and Lance but you unlock extra characters to use in Story and Arcade modes as you go. The game is as pure Contra as you can get: Shoot everything, don't get shot and don't screw up your platforming.Bill and Lance come with a double jump and a horizontal dash, but every character has their own unique ability(ies). Up to you to experiment and see which one meshes with you best.It kinda takes a bit from various older Contra games: There's a bit of Contra 1, Contra 3, Hard Corps, Contra 4 (which WayForward also worked on and is also a very enjoyable game) and mixes it all together into a satisfying explosive salad. You may recognize some of the enemies and minibosses from other games in the franchise as you play along.Per tradition you can carry up to two weapons, collecting another of a weapon you already have upgrades it. Getting hit downgrades it back to level 1 while dying removes it entirely. Then there's the Overdrive mechanic.At any time you can hold a button (LT on XBox controller) and this will activate a special ability related to your weapon. This will either remove the weapon or downgrade it if upgraded but the effects are extremely worth it. Ranging from attack drones laying waste to providing an immunity barrier an Overdrive can make a huge difference.You can also unlock perks and upgrades like more health or starting with a weapon guaranteed...or you can not. Galuga is very customizable in how you can play: You can have all these fancy upgrades and a health bar or you can eschew all that and stick with classic Contra rules: One shot, you're dead, no fancy toys, better luck next time, don't eat dirt next go-around. This also rewards you with more Credits to buy characters and BGM sets.This game gets overall very high marks from me but I have a few complaints:-Overdrives are not equal: The Barrier OD is flat out broken, and the Fire OD flat out makes you near immune to certain bosses. I try to have both so then I can literally not die to anything. Meanwhile the Crash OD is both short range and seems pretty ineffective. Really all the attacking ODs are kinda meh: Defense is usually the way to go.-There's too much story in Story Mode: Sorry, as soon as Generic Anime Antagonist shows up and starts carrying on is when I started mashing through dialogue. There's a few funny bits but for the most part it seems like it takes itself way too seriously. Play through Story once and never again. Leading to---Not much content at this time: May be fixed in the future, game is only a day old after all, but for $40 you get Story, Arcade and Challenge. That's your lot and while you can customize it to be as easy or hard as you want it's still the same content in the end. I will say the ending of Story makes me wonder what the future holds.-Lack of visual options: You can change your resolution and that's your lot. Frame drops? Too bad, hope that fixes it because you're changing nothing else. -Stanley Ironside sucks: I just like Stanley's look a whole lot and was excited to play as him. Instead I learn in exchange for one extra HP he gets an awkward hover instead of a double jump and an even more awkward grapple. In addition his weapons are a bit changed, usually for the worse. The Ripple weapon has nothing on the standard laser. My advice: Don't, and when you unlock two certain robotic characters pretend the Hover and Grapple 'upgrades' don't exist.Overall Operation Galuga is a return to form for Contra and I've had a lot of fun playing it. Got to Stage 7 in Arcade and want to 1 CC before moving on. Also need to dabble in Challenge Mode. WayForward really nailed the Contra formula and certainly wouldn't mind them brushing up other franchises like Castlevania. Not perfect of course (Not every game can be Contra 3) but still a very solid offering for any Contra fan. I recommended it.

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews It appears that classic gaming genres that once captivated the younger generation are experiencing a resurgence, filling the gaps left by certain negative aspects of AAA titles. I’m referring to genres like Boomer Shooter, or specifically, the Run-n’-Gun action of Contra.Contra makes a comeback following a huge setback with Contra: Rogue Corps, in an attempt to bring Konami’s legacy into 3D action. Contra: Operation Galuga revisits the cherished Side Scrolling Action, boasting modern graphics and dynamic Point of Views that will surely catch players’ attention.The story mode, albeit brief with around 2 hours of gameplay, features 8 distinct levels, plunging players into the mission of the terrorist group Red Falcon as they strive to dominate the island of Galuga. The primary goal of the Contra group is to dismantle this operation and foil their plans for control over this strategically vital location. Something peculiar is happening on this island near New Zealand, with a noticeable presence of alien beings hell-bent on eradicating all human life.In addition to this gameplay mode, which can be played in a party of up to 2 players, there are extra modes like Challenge mode, offering diverse challenges such as Speedrun, where the objective is to complete the level as swiftly as possible, Horde mode, tasking players to eliminate all enemies, and Arcade mode, supporting up to 4 players. Regrettably, this is solely available in local multiplayer mode. Also, the inclusion of a perk shop allows players to acquire new characters and perks to enhance their runs.Controls work flawlessly, as expected from a WayForward title, renowned for titles like River City Girls and the Shantae series. Throughout level progression, players will encounter the iconic weapon pickups floating above their heads, facilitating confrontations with enemies. Classic attack types are also back, alongside new additions and enhancements, obtainable during the run by collecting the same attack twice. Certain characters possess specific abilities, like a grappling hook or double jump, as well as unique attack types for each weapon.Concerning weapons, activating the mechanical overload of each weapon triggers its specific effect for a brief duration. These effects are mostly defensive, resulting in various shield effects, either around the player or creating a barrier in the direction it was placed.Upon completing a level, players receive credits usable in the Perk Shop. At the start of each level, players can select two perks, ensuring each run offers a slightly different experience. Funny enough, entering the Konami code grants players an achievement and unlocks the 30 lives perk, although it still requires purchase. Nonetheless, it’s an intriguing Easter egg.Operation Galuga’s levels left some room for improvement; some are overly lengthy, checkpoints are often too sparse, and even on normal difficulty, the challenge is notably high. While this might partly be attributed to the player’s skill, it’s worth mentioning. Most levels culminate in enjoyable boss fights and the story segments are also one of the highlights of this experience. Most feature voice acting, with voices well known in the gaming world, for example, Steve Blum from Yakuza, and are presented in comic book-style panels at certain points.Contra: Operation Galuga is highly recommended for both series enthusiasts and newcomers seeking hours of action-packed entertainment. I sincerely hope an online multiplayer mode will be added soon. Not that couch multiplayer is bad, but let’s be honest, it’s much more practical to invite a friend from across the ocean to an online gaming session than to invite them to your living room couch.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Contra and someone who beat all the games from the original on the NES to Shattered Soldier on the PS2, Operation Galuga feels like a natural evolution of the classic Run & Gun formula that we all like, the game follows the events of the original Contra with some expanded lore and some new characters introduced as well as returning ones from other titles, if you are a fan of the franchise you will definitely recognize iconic Contra characters from previous games and even returning bosses from past installments.The game was developed by Wayforward who previously worked on Contra 4 (Which is one of the best games in the franchise in my opinion) so its nice to see a competent developer bring back the classic gameplay and refine it with new mechanics. Among the new features are the different variations and gameplay styles between characters which change the weapons you get to use and movement, the option to tweak the difficulty to play like an original Contra game locking your aim in 8 directions or dying in one hit and in my opinion the best new addition is the Overcharge Mechanic, allowing you to consume your current weapon to gain a massive advantage such as slow-mo ability, an energy shield that absorbs projectiles and even flying drones that follow and protect you for a limited time.With all that being said, the game certainly fails in some aspects too, mainly the artstyle which can go from charming on certain levels to bland generic mobile tier on others, the music is also incredibly boring and forgettable (luckily it can be changed in Arcade mode) and last but not least the levels are sometimes a little too long for their own good specially the bike levels which used to be full of insane scripted events (Contra III riding on missiles anyone?).Would I recommend Contra: Operation Galuga? It depends, if you are a diehard fan of the series then YES absolutely, its a solid entry in the franchise and what this game sets out to do it accomplishes well enough, however, if you don't care much about Contra or this type of games I can recommend it for kids or people looking for a fun couch coop experience, otherwise wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Get ready to travel back in time with Contra: Operation Galuga! This game is like a love letter to the classic run-and-gun action of the 80s and 90s. You play as a tough-as-nails commando, blasting your way through hordes of alien baddies. The graphics are retro-tastic, with pixelated explosions and enemies that look like they jumped straight out of an old-school arcade cabinet.The gameplay is simple but addictive – run, jump, and shoot everything that moves. You'll be dodging bullets, leaping over obstacles, and unleashing all kinds of crazy weapons. And when you team up with a buddy for some couch co-op, things get even more intense. You'll be yelling at each other to watch out for that sneaky alien or to grab that power-up before it disappears.But don't let the cute retro style fool you – this game is tough! You'll die a lot, but that's part of the fun. Each time you get a little further, and when you finally beat that boss or clear that level, it feels like a real accomplishment.

_childDocuments_.review: Contra : Operation GalugaI will be frequently comparing this game to Ghost n Goblins Resurrection by Capcom because I feel there are many similarities.   Like I said about that game, imagine putting two of the defining Contra games (the 1st and Super Contra) into a blender and getting something that feels familar yet fresh and new.  While you don't get a perfect 1 to 1 copy of any prior Contra game, you do get to see many familiar stages and enemies.  And its not just Contra, I felt a lot of Konami nostalgia on here. I was feeling a lot of Super Castlevania on this.  From level design down to the very flame thrower behaving like a controlable chain like Belmont's whip from Super Castlevania. This game has got the classic Konami arcade action, the speed, the explosions, I come up in the 80's with some of the greatest Konami arcade games and this would fit in.Vania Mix - After playing the demo, many of us here at Steam forums were not feeling the music.   I thought it should have been some hard thrash metal or heavy dance to Industrial ebm.  After I got the game, I was given the chance to set the music to something called "Vania Mix".  It didn't dawn on me at first what that was.  But after playing, this is actually really clever.  Konami has taken the OST of Castlevania 1 and Simon's Quest from the NES and seamlessly weaved that into all the games soundtricks. So like when you fight a mini boss...it would play a mini boss theme from those games.   Heck, even one time you hear the character Bill Rizer say "What a damn day to have a curse" lol and then the Simon's Quest night time theme starts playing haha nice touch.  Price -  I was told I was getting the game for like 33 or 34 but it ended up charging my card almost a full 40 bucks. I don't know if that is in error or just some taxes or fees or what.    Like GnG Resurrecton, I am glad Konami did this, and they could be doing this for Castlevania, just a fun action packed arcade style side scroller game shades of Haunted Castle but even more Castlevania.   There is just something about Beat Em Ups and Side Scrollers, and Fighting Games, there is still a lot of appeal there I think. And this might be a new time in gaming, these kind of games.  Retro 2D but with the power and speed of modern equipment.  But most of us agree.....The price should have been 30 bucks and less than that even better.    Because of the price, I give it a 4 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Contra: Operation Galuga:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~The Red Falcon is a terrorist group that has been coordinating strikes all around the globe. They've set up shop on the small Galuga Archipelago. When the archipelago was rained upon by a mass of small meteors, the Earth Federation government noticed the terrorists’ base and didn't hesitate to send their special GX-Army soldiers to destroy the criminal organisation. Everything seemed to go be going to plan until the Federation lost all contact with their soldiers. That was three days ago. The consensus is now clear: the Red Falcon is much tougher than anticipated. To add fuel to the fire, the Federation scientists' satellite networks recently detected a gravity anomaly, and the source of this anomaly started right in the centre of the Galuga Archipelago. Is the Red Falcon on the verge of creating the doomsday gravity super weapon? There is no time to waste. They have to send their last two elite soldiers immediately. Code name Contra: Operation Galuga!  Contra: Operation Galuga is a run-'n'-gun side-scrolling action game developed by WayForward and published by KONAMI on the 12th of March 2024 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS4, PS5, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch.The game consists of three modes of play: Story, Arcade, and Challenge. The story and the arcade modes have eight levels, from average to lengthy. The challenge mode has 30 specific tasks to complete, each with win-and-loss conditions and some with a time limit. You’ll probably start with either the Story or the Arcade mode. First, you have to select the difficulty level from Easy, Normal or Hard, as well as the health level. You can choose the health meter, which gives three health bars per life, or the 1-hit kill, which is self-explanatory. In the Story gameplay, you can choose between two soldiers, Bill Rizer and Lance Bean, for the first two levels. As you progress, you'll unlock another three characters. At the start of each level, you choose your character; they will have three lives to spare throughout the stage. Your goal is straightforward: make your way to the end of the stage as fast as you can, kill as many enemies as possible and beat the boss of each stage. You'll receive credits at the end of each completed level, which you can use at the perks shop to help you on your next playthrough. The Arcade mode is pretty much the same, but you'll be able to select one of the seven characters available as long as you have unlocked them through the story mode. The other difference is that in the Arcade mode, you start with a certain number of lives to get to the last level and boss. The gameplay is fast-paced and frantic, and the controls are super responsive. You can play with a friend on a local share screen or via remote play, and it will probably be super crazy. Playing single-player is also intense, and you must be ready to repeat stages several times before beating them. Out of the eight stages, you'll be running forward in most of them, shooting at incoming enemies and enemies coming from behind. But you'll also be double-jumping, dashing or lying down to avoid incoming projectiles. In a few stages, you'll be on this hovercraft type of bike, and it will be extremely chaotic from the start - it's really fun. There are a few power-ups, and they will come and go as you progress through the stages. You can upgrade them twice but lose the second upgrade if you are hit. If you died and the power-up you were using before your death was on the first upgrade, you'll lose it when you respawn. You can have only two types of power-ups at any given time, and you can swap them by pressing the LB or RB buttons on your gamepad. You can also overload the power-up by pressing the LT button, and depending on the power-up, it can either create a shield for several seconds or activate super-powerful projectiles. Remember that you'll lose the power-up immediately after you overload them. I find overloading power-ups particularly effective when fighting the bosses. You can request a power-up if the shield under the health meter is complete - to charge it up, you only need to keep killing enemies – but you never know which power-ups you're going to get. I also like that you can sharpshoot at the enemies by pressing the RT button. It locks your character on the spot, and you can aim your right stick with precision and shoot the enemies. Some levels have mini-bosses halfway through, and a couple of them are really tough to beat. I don't think I managed to pass one of them the first time - it always took me a couple of shots, the little buggers. I loved the boss fights! They're fun, fast and not that easy to beat at first, but when you get new perks, it’s a different story, and it will probably be time to switch to the hard difficulty. My only issue is that the game kept crashing on the last boss, which annoyed me, especially when I managed to get to the last stage in the arcade mode. Apart from that, no other issues at all.The graphics are stunning. Great soundtrack and sound effects, and the controls are responsive. Full controller support and the game has been translated into 11 languages.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics+	Story, arcade and challenges game modes+	Fast-paced and addictive gameplay+	Three different levels of difficulty+	Great boss fights+	Achievements and trading cardsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	 The game kept crashing on the last boss fightContra: Operation Galuga is an absolute winner! It's fast-paced all the way through, and it's a stunning run-'n'-gun side-scrolling game.8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!
