_childDocuments_.review: + : There’s something about Tiny Terry’s Turbo Trip that just makes you smile. Fun writing that makes you genuinely laugh without really feeling like it’s forcing anything, an enjoyable silly aesthetic that resembles childhood drawings made 3D, and a whimsical protagonist who steals the show. Everything about the game is oozing with casual fun in a way that you really don’t see in many games these days. + : Accompanying the wonderful aesthetic and silly mood of Tiny Terry is a soundtrack composed by Thomas de Waard, and this soundtrack fit the assignment incredibly. Songs like Driving Around Sprankelwater continue to be a brain worm in my head that added to the fun experience of ramming passerby with my space vehicle. A wonderful mixture of instruments and moods for each district makes the entire experience feel all the more distinct, with a ton of variety in the moods Thomas de Waard creates. There are some songs that helped certain scenes (like Terry reading his family’s note) feel really sweet.+ : With over 1,000 junk to find, and several hats, bugs, and unlockable tools to find, Tiny Terry has enough for any Collectathon fan to enjoy. But it’s not an overwhelming or overdesigned adventure – you won’t ever be struggling with misguided systems to collect anything, and even the hidden rewards are relatively straightforward to find. It creates a game that is very casual and relaxing, where you can play at your own pace and feel comfortable.+ : Very quickly, you’re set out on this small island open world to explore as freely as you desire with one goal in mind: go to space. But you have nothing forcing you to do anything – you can run around and steal cars, for example, despite having a car of your own.  And whether it’s plowing through fellow Sprankelwaterians in your car Simpsons Hit-And-Run style, swinging a bat at passerby to collect their money, driving around and collecting items or even participating in any of the minigames available, there is not a single moment in this game that didn’t feel fun. Not an ounce of fat in the game to distract from that fun, either. While this obviously doesn’t have to be true for every single game, it is refreshing to play a game that doesn’t take itself too seriously and allows the player to enjoy themselves (in a way very reminiscent of Nintendo games).~ : I’d really like to emphasize that while the game is shorter, I enjoyed every second and I think there is plenty of room for shorter titles. I spent roughly 4 and a half hours in the game, with all of the encounter quests done and roughly 80% completed. With dedication, you could probably 100% the game within 5-10 hours, depending on your own personal pace. You could probably figure out ways to speedrun the game, or chase global leaderboard supremacy in a few of the minigames, to squeeze out a few more hours. - : I initially had playtime here, but it doesn’t really fit as a con. Truthfully, there wasn’t much I can think of to outline as a con for this game that wouldn’t be misrepresenting the type of game it is. It’s a short, fun, goofy game at heart with no fancy bells and whistles. If you’re not looking for a game like that, you probably know that already from the trailer. I enjoyed Tiny Terry’s Turbo Trip when I played it during a previous Steam Next Fest. It immediately stood out as a unique and charming title, making me pay attention to it once the demo had concluded. Several months later, I can safely say that title 100% came out fantastic. Truthfully, the genre isn’t even something I tend to seek out, but despite that, Tiny Terry’s Turbo Trip had me smiling the entire time I was playing, enjoying the music and the writing and the goofy gameplay. I would highly recommend the game for people who are looking for a short and sweet title to dig into, especially for fans of Collectathon titles. The game is absolutely worth your money. I’m very excited to see what snekflat does next!

_childDocuments_.review: Took a chance on TTTT and fell in love with it.What really surprised me was how great it *felt* to just *do* stuff in this tiny open world. Driving felt great. Smashing into things with turbo felt great. Jumping and (naruto) running felt great.  And hitting objects and people with your pipe felt really, really great. Everything is snappy and crisp and crunchy – like a 3D open world Vlambeer game. The game just *feels* really good to play... and that made me play it a lot more than I expected to. Looking forward to 100%'ing it - not something I would normally ever consider for an open world game like this.I was honestly pretty neutral on the humour and characters at the beginning, but I had so much fun just driving and running around hitting things that I got sucked into caring about this ridiculous little world. If you're iffy on that aspect, honestly just give the gameplay a try and I bet you'll end up enjoying it like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: is a charming "casual exploration" title in the vein of ,  , and . This burgeoning genre centers around open-world exploration in a small, contained, but content-dense hub world. Terry's adventure in particular borrows from driving sims like , and features the trademark odd humor of snekflat's other adventure, .The world of Spranklewater is an excellent hub world of diverse biomes and locations. Each part of the map has some quest or activity to participate in, and each one fleshes out the world nicely. The driving mechanics are delightfully chaotic, and there are plenty of things to collect. The game's main lifeblood comes from the excellent humor and aesthetic. The game has this deadpan, psuedo-realism tone that permeates throughout, with characters speaking like real people in an unreal world. For example, Spranklewater has a famously lax government that doesn't really enforce against crimes... but the only confirmed criminal is a guy who's personal code of ethics is so strong that he can't commit a crime that involves any kind of violence. There's a giant tower in the middle of the city that was commissioned by the mayor, but it lacks any doorways to get in and ended up bankrupting the city. One of Terry's friends has a dad that steals cars for a living, but since the cars are immediately bought by new clients, it's totally legal. The game is legitimately pretty funny, and a large part of the appeal is just existing in this world. Couple this with an incredible soundtrack, some memorable characters, and an excellent laid-back tropical atmosphere, and it looks like  is a recipe for a good time. Unfortunately, I found Terry's gameplay to be pretty boring. Basically every "quest" in the game boils down to collecting an item, and they all end in a currency bonus for upgrading your car. The game ends incredibly quick (just over three hours), and even in that short time I found myself getting really bored of the core gameplay. This is a shame, since there are so many ideas here that just go to waste. I was actually surprised at how many ideas get shut down over the course of the game. Terry gets his car from signing up to be a taxi driver... but there are no missions involving the taxi gameplay at all, which is a crazy waste of potential. You have a melee attack, but it's only used to bust open trash. You have a glider ability, but you never need it to get anywhere in the game, and so on. This stands out in this casual adventure genre, as each game listed in the intro of this review has some kind of gameplay hook that is compelling.  has the climbing mechanics,  has the photography angle, and so on.  being so unambitious is a real shame, and one of the reasons why I ultimately don't recommend it.  had much simpler mechanics and ideas, but continually innovated and challenged the player with new and interesting concepts. Even if the gameplay was just light platforming and shooting, it evolved constantly ovet the course of the game. By comparison,  never pulls out any truly interesting ideas and remains quite uninteresting the entire way through, while actively rejecting anything that could spice it up.This is a pretty big disappointment for me. I loved , so to see that it's followup just isn't exciting is a real big shame. I think that if this game continued to get worked on, it could really shine. All of the pieces are for a compelling and enjoyable sandbox, but rejecting that potential instead of living up to it just doesn't sit right.

_childDocuments_.review: The dev asked in game for a review so.. Main thing is that the trailer looks much more exciting than what the game pans out to be, which is just.. relaxing, really.The Good• Good, bright presentation. Soundtrack is good.• Quirky dialog, well presented story. His uncle is a good character.• Most of the collectibles are easy to find, including the optional ones. No cryptid placements except for one (spoiler: behind the job recruitment place was annoying to get up to)• Short (You can see the credits in two hours. ..Every game is a million hours or live service these days.)• Phone Hint system is great, and adds to the story.• Runs great on deck, if that applies to you!The bad• Terry could stand to be a little more nimble. The jog is okay, but lacking when retreading ground for things you miss. Certain ledges are a pain to get up to. Glider should be cheaper, imo, more on that later.• 'Empty' feeling once you hit the few activities, which are very brief.• Little variety, other you will spend most of your time at the end slowly jogging looking for 'coins.'• Grinding money by the end for the tracker and government debt, dunno if there's much to do other than dig up dirt and deliver stolen cars. Very slow, so I'm not gonna bother. • No replay value (Feels like wasted potential, polished world and smooth presentation wise -- but its over already. No reason to return or goof around in the world, lack of things to do/terry is just kinda slow.)• Laundromat hint system stinks.TLDR; you're going around a single platforming hub for a few fetch quests, but the platforming isn't great. It doesn't feel like an open world game. Price is kind of right though, $15. Buy it for an alright afternoon, movie ticket style.

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky and charming game with a unique art style and a catchy soundtrack, plus more depth than you might expect at first. You can fall in love! Re-enact GTA! So, no, I did not get to go to space in the end :(A pretty good way to spend a rainy afternoon or two, though, despite the nagging feeling that, with a little more work, this game might not just be OK, but actually great...

Makes me nostalgic specifically for the wii era, like the TT Lego games and the My Sims games. I didn't mind, but should still mention the dollar per hour here could be a deterrent for some.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really like this game  to recommend it.It overall felt unfinished.I encountered a log of bugs, some weird performance issues (for a game that looks this visually simple, it runs like hot garbage). The story is barely present.On a more positive note, I liked the fact that it was short (especially because of the lackluster story). I also somewhat liked the humor and the visual style.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely funny game. Short and sweet.A bit sad that there are so many corners of the island that are empty. Like if I jump down a cliff I'd hope for a secret to be there, but that's rarely the case. Also don't get lured into trying to get all the hats, getting enough money to buy everything requires a fair bit of grinding money. Certainly it's strongest suit is the character interactions, all the characters are just silly in their own way. And the comedic timing on most interactions is just great.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game was cute, funny, and pretty easy to get through. I finished all of the quests in a little over six hours. The last achievement - to 100% the game - was a pain in the butt because you have to find every piece of turbo junk in the entire game. It took me about an hour and a half to finish tracking down all the junk. Make sure to buy the junk detector hat when you can if you're after all the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry is an amazing, fun and hilarious concept that is executed perfectly. Visually, this game is one of my favorite things in a long time. The simple, cute, wacky and sometimes absurd designs of the world and its characters are the main highlight for me, it feels like you are playing a cartoon all the time and I think that's INCREDIBLE.The gameplay and animations are also really fun and have a lot of tiny details and interactions (like, if you press the speak button next to an NPC, it will talk back to you or some decorative elements of the city will go back to their place shortly after being knocked over, making tiny jumps, so cool) that show the love and care that have been put in the development. I've been smiling a lot while playing it :)Also, props to the spanish translation and localization of the game, it's really well done and adapts a lot of worlds and concepts perfectly!Long story short: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is the perfect game for you if you like exploration, collectibles, fun, cars and tax evasion.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is a funny adventure with very charming animations and graphics in a living world. The only issue lies within the gameplay: it revolves mainly on searching for hidden junk and bashing stuff around for ~5 bills or selling cars for 28 of them. It becomes repetitive very fast (especially if you're going for 100%, which takes a LOT of $ — one of the objectives require 999) and could use more variety, especially since the map is big enough for stuff like checkpoint races. But as long as you're aware it may take you longer than ideal to do some stuff, the sweet story and goofy concept won't disappoint you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot more than I originally expected.The trailer couldn't properly prepare me for the absurd humor I found myself laughing at over and over again. In some way this game evoked a sense of nostalgia for me, making me feel like a kid again. I got lost in a simple, careless world for a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to release since it got announced and I'm happy to say that it didn't disappoint. The world is very charming and its characters are full of personality. The music is great and it helps to set the intended atmosphere for the game and it also has a very distinguishable art style that just makes the game even more unique. TTTT is not a perfect game, but I loved everything about it and I think it's worth everyone's time, especially if you're into relaxing adventure games like A Short Hike, Lil Gator Game or Tinykin.I just wish snekflat all of the best for their next games and I wish they continue delivering more games with this level of charm, humour and personality, which will always be welcomed. Oh and if you haven't already, please consider checking their previous game (Wuppo). It's a similar game in tone, it has all of the weirdness, randomness and humour of TTTT but in 2D and it is a boss rush puzzle adventure game that has a cute world full of interesting things to do. I recommend giving it a try, it's dirt cheap when it goes on sale and it's another great little hidden gem, don't let the art style hold you back, you will thank me later ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: An other game that manages to make me smile little after I start it and keeps the fun going for a long while.As someone that has played a short hike and Lil Gator Game though, I think this game doesn't do as well in the terms of movement and exploration as the ones I just mentioned, since most movement mechanics are pretty basic. If you have money to spare I recommend playing the aforementioned tittles after Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip as they share a lot of aspects with it and I personally believe they execute what they try to do much better.Also take in mind this game is pretty short, in 6 and 1/2 hours I have already 100%ed the game. There is little replay-ability outside of world-wide rankings and there aren't that many things to mess around with to extend playtime, so if you are short on money and you care about how much you can squeeze out of a game, I believe this will probably be a bit unappealing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. Finished in about 6 hours, although I didn't get all the achievements.Pros:- Nice fully realised art style- Well designed world- Gameplay is a fun mini-metroidvania- Music is outstanding- Clever and Funny writing- SpaceCons:- Maybe a little short, But not bad for the price- Becomes a collectathon towards the end, but not before it's worn out its welcomeOn balance; Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is a really fun, entertaining game that invites you into its sweet, silly, unassuming world. I recommend anyone who's a fan of tightly designed mini open worlds takes a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a more unrealistic, less wholesome version of Lil' Gator Game. That's not a bad thing, honestly. It's not that much less wholesome. The worst is you can wack people, rob them, and break stuff with a pipe. Nobody gets hurt, but it's clearly not as wholesome as just a bunch of kids playing pretend. There's still a nice little moral to the story at the end, though!You play as Terry, a boy who wishes to drive to SPACE!!! The trick is you need a car, but that's done really quickly. The next step is getting enough Turbo Junk to upgrade your new car's turbo. Each costs 150 Turbo Junk. You only need 7 upgrades to finish the game, but there's plenty more to be found.if you've done the math that's 1,050 Turbo Junk to reach the end. So, how do you get it? You'll find a bunch just laying around, but most will come from doing quests. If you check your map, there's a ton of "?" areas on it to be discovered. These are people you can talk to and they'll usually ask for something, if not keep talking. If you fulfill their requests they'll give you a treasure map for a trash can full of Turbo Junk! If you're going for 100% invest in the junk finding hat from the junk shops. Some if the Turbo Junk laying around can be decently hard to spot. If it glows, there's some nearby. If it beeps, walk and try to listen for higher-pitched, faster-paced beeping. There's a few other objectives to get Turbo Junk, but you'll figure it out as you go. Just follow your heart and listen to the wind!If you liked Lil' Gator Game and wanted more, you'll feel right at home with this. If you liked this and are reading the reviews for some reason, the reverse is also true. Go play that game if you enjoyed this one. If you played both, you probably know what I'm talking about and also know I can't help you further.Good Game/10 I liked it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: What a quirky little game. I really dig the 'simple' graphics, colours and overall aesthetic. Also it played really well, platforming was really smooth and fun. It was just enough packed into a neat package, collecting everything didn't feel like a drag at all. The soundtrack was very cheerful, I liked it a lot :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is a humorous and lighthearted game with funny dialogue and fun quests to complete while burning rubber through the many streets and corners of your neighbourhood. While it won't last you very long (my almost-100% playthrough took about five hours), the creativity, laughs, and even wholesome moments make this a turbo trip worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute delight to play from start to finish. The game is relatively short, but its very, very charming. The animations and movement are smooth, the characters distinctive and characteristic and the game over-all is just hilarious, and it ends on a high note, with inspiring (and absolutely hilarious) dialogue.the only real criticism I have is that the camera controls are a bit, that theres no fishing minigame, and that the game is a bit short; although I can forgive it for that, because its more of a big dessert rather than a 7 course meal.Being Dutch, I also thoroughly enjoyed the Dutch names sprinkled everywhere. I bought the game on sale and I can tell you that its worth the full price. The game puts a smile on your face from beginning to end, never ceases to suprise you, staying fresh throughout the entire playthrough. The music direction is phenomenal as is the art direction.an absolute Must-Play, this game gets a 9/10 and a lifetime supply of beach fries from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: The "cozy game" is a hard one for me to look back on. I loved A Short Hike during my initial play-through, but, spent too long getting 100% to have any real affection upon reflection a couple years in retrospect. Games like Smushi Come Home, Lil Gator Game, and Tiny Terry's are designed to be short, sweet, and can be remarkably relaxing and refined experiences.  This idea hinges on the player understanding this and interacting with the game world in an accordant manner. Not taking too long in any one area or pushing the limits of the small, handcrafted world. Finding "the fun" because "the fun" is the main quest. Tiny Terry's feels different than the other games mentioned because instead of having max hangoutable vibes, it goes for a funnier (goofier), more chaotic energy. More The Simpsons: Hit & Run than Animal Crossing. Not that it doesn't contain all the bug collecting and npc chatting associated with the genre, but that those things largely takes a back seat to slapstick chicanery or general tomfoolery. A solid game a little game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Are car accidents really a bad thing? Do your parents still love you if they leave you behind in order to impress rich people? And is the fame of driving your car into space worth abandoning your school grades?Terry's Tiny Turbo Trip isn't afraid to ask the hard questions, but under that absurdist exterior is a lot of heart. From the comical art direction to the upbeat soundtrack, everything works in unison to create a world all its own. As you explore the city of Sprankelwater, you also learn about the titular Tiny Terry himself. While the game never loses its whimsical touch, it explores Terry's relationships and troubles organically through exploration and every day conversation - but TTTT isn't trying to be the next modern epic, it utilizes the freedom of its game genre to build a free-flowing narrative, much like the gameplay, all about exploration.If that's the kind of game you want to experience, I highly recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is a blast! It's gameplay is very reminiscent of games from the PS2 era, but with a unique art style and sense of humor. This game does a great job of taking a world map (which is relatively small by today's standards) and making it feel massive and exciting to explore. It made me feel like a kid again!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game. Exploring this small town full of quirky characters never gets boring, mostly because there's a lot of interactions and gameplay ideas everywhere. Dialogues are genuinely fun. I could see some inspiration from Hit & Run or Zelda there and there, and the structure is a bit similar to A Short Hike if you've played that one, but it's also very much its own thing. Higly recommended if you're looking for a fun and chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun as long as you don't go in expecting too much. I loved Wuppo so I had pretty high expectations going into this game, although they weren't entirely met I still enjoyed the game. It took me a little over 5 hours to do most of the side quests. I got all but two (a secret and 100%) steam achievements, did all of the markers on the map, and got to 80% completion in game. What I was missing was collecting all of the stuff used for upgrading your car (I had already maxed the car out so I didn't feel the need to collect it all).Things I didn't like:The game is basically a bunch of side quests. They're pretty fun, but can feel a little repetitive if you do a lot of them.The game has a lack of structure. This can be good, but it would be nice to have some plot to pull you in while play. At times you get that, but it feels as if something is missing.Things that I liked:- The dialog is amazing. If you liked it in Wuppo then you'll like it here.- The car is pretty fun to drive and platforming feels decent. My one complaint with movement is that Terry is a little bit slow for my liking, but that is more of a personal preference thing.-The art style looks amazing and the framing for a lot of the dialog shots look gorgeous. -There is music from Wuppo sprinkled throughout in addition to some new tracks which are just as good.Overall it's a pretty good game, but don't go into it expecting it to be too similar to Wuppo.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game in just over 4 hours getting 87% of achievements (not the type to 100%, but I enjoyed the game enough to get this far). Very short game but it was a fantastic experience. Big fan of snekflat's humor after playing Wuppo, I was very happy to get more of that here.The game is in the same vein as snekflat's previous game Wuppo, and also games such as A Short Hike and Lil Gator Game. Short, sandbox games where you run around doing little tasks at your own leisure in a charming world full of quirky characters. Add a sprinkle of GTA such as driving around, stealing cars and assaulting civilians and you've got Tiny Terry.Note: The game refused to start so after some digging I had to add -force-d3d11 to the launch options, which worked.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This really is a treat to play, very small yet very fun and dense open world with funny characters and a cute artstyle, only about 4 hours to finish the game and 9-10 hours to 100%, def worth you time if you enjoy something interesting and fun with a p unique artstyle, also ricky sucks (but in a good way)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: TTTT is an open-world adventure game where you run and drive around the town, collect things, talk to people and generally explore. There's some platforming involved as well, but nothing challenging; you can't even lose in any way.It looks good, sounds good, it's charming and funny, and it works despite having been made in Unity. I didn't even encounter a single bug, and I expected a lot of them, seeing how there's an "unstuck" button in the menu.I really can't think of anything negative to say about this game. There's just nothing to not like. I often find games with "exploration" and "relaxing" tags boring, but TTTT is packed with diverse content, has actual gameplay and dialogues are short and to the point (and genuinely funny, which is rare). I enjoyed every second of my ~6 hours with Terry. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This has been an absolute delight of a game! Terry is such a cutie of a character. He's so mellow and just doesn't get it at times (We've all been there). This is such a fun adventure of whacking things (and people) with a pipe) wearing silly hats, flirting badly and eventually going to space. The world is so unique and bouncy! Would definitely recommend this game to friends!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Wuppo, another game by these devs, is one of my favorite games of all time. It's art-style, music, and humor were fantastic and it created an interesting a living world that I have played through multiple times.Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip retains all that from Wuppo (including some fun call backs musically and Easter egg wise), and then expands on it with gameplay that takes inspiration from Simpson's Hit and Run, of all things. I'd also never turn down a 3D collect-a-thon platformer, especially one that is fun to simply wander around to look for stuff. The world Terry lives in really feels alive, with many areas to explore and secrets to find throughout a play-through.Overall I'm glad this game turned out well, especially after Wuppo BFF didn't end up panning out. It's a unique experience that despite being short is full of charm and engaging chaos. I hope the devs will continue to make games as unique and fun as this!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game about a strange little boy that just wants to drive a car into space. The art style, music, writing and overall feel is pure joy and it´s obvious that all people involved in making it put all of their love into it.The game might be a bit on the shorter side, but the journey through it was so consistently great it left me wanting more once the trip was over. I hope we get to see much more of Terry and his world in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this experience, it's everything i was hoping for, just a fun little little sandbox game with a story that goes a little deeper than expected! I almost 100% it just around 5 hours, but there is a collectible achievement that I just don't want to do.I would give it a 7/10 really good for a short amount of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with the game before it was even out. And now that it is out and I've played it for about an hour, I'm even more in love with it! XDMaybe now that this has released, Snekflat will finally finish making Wuppo: Breft Festival (Forever) :PEdit: I have now beaten the game, and I did it with 6 turbo upgrades, instead of the intended required 7. I found that if you drive up the ramp on the tower as high as you can without falling down again, and then activate your turbo, 6 upgrades are just enough to get you to the point where the game ending cutscene begins. I hope they fix this, because when I did that, I was just testing to see how high I could get with the upgrades I had at the time and wasn't ready for it.Even with the small amount of bugs and unintended exploits, this game is fun and charming, and I look forward to 100%ing it! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game so fun and full of life i already knew the game was going to be amazing coming from Knuist & Perzik now snekflat wuppo is one of my favorite indie games and bff is on the top 3 of my most awaited games ever if you played TTTT and liked it but still wanted more give wuppo a chance it has the same charm with a lot more content :3
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: wishlisted when I found out the devs were working on a new game since I loved Wuppo. bought as soon as it released, immediately knew I'd get my money's worth from the first few lines of dialogue. TTTT takes everything I loved about Wuppo and does it even better: cool/charming art style, interesting and silly characters, and hilarious writing (laughed out loud multiple times in my first hour playing).initially wanted to leave a short witty review but this game is so cool I just had to earnestly gush about it a little. will certainly be joining Wuppo in my "replay at least once a year" hall of fame, 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, and oozing with charm from every pore. The art style pulled me in, and the exploration and dialogue left me with an enjoyable overall experience.Gameplay mostly revolves around searching for currency and collectibles in order to progress. Junk is what you'll need to upgrade your car enough to ride the Sky Tower into space, while money is used to buy things to help you progress as well as cool hats. There's a number of marked locations where there's a mini "quest" you can complete to get a lot of Junk as a reward, ranging from a soccer game to paying off the government.Overall, the game is just running around, talking to NPCs to see funny dialogue, and picking up whatever scraps you find along the way through detailed and complex enviroments, which is nice and fun and low stakes. The dialogue is hilarious because every NPC says every line with a 100% straight face, even something as ridiculous as "a car isn't stolen anymore after you've sold it".All that being said, a few problems:1. The camera is kinda booty. There's a handful of closed quarters areas and the camera doesn't really know what to do. Moving it vertically is severely neutered for some reason. There's also a weird jump as the camera suddenly moves after deploying the paraglider.2. I think I had a bug with a certain NPC who's supposed to follow you around and challenge you to bumper cars. I saw him once at the pre-determined location, but then never again. Edit: I did encounter him while trying to find everything for 100%, but not sure what the requirements are.A fun way to spend the afternoon.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing my review after finishing 100% completion. I think the game is really cute and has a lot of charm. It straddles the line between being a chaotic open world collect-a-thon while also remaining pretty wholesome. Terry is a criminal but he has principals. He engages in a lot of debauchery, but the government is pretty laissez-faire. He steals from the government but also helps them pay off their debt. A lot of thought was put into the narrative of the game and I think the effort shows in spades.In terms of gameplay, it is a lot of running/driving around to collect junk to upgrade the car you got for the job you aren't going to work. But not just any junk "turbo junk." Junk so powerful with enough of it you can upgrade your car for space travel. All in all its pretty great. The humor, music, graphic design, and game feel are all very strong. You could probably beat the game in a few hours and I think that's enough of it to be honest. Getting all the turbo junk for 100% completion was a bit annoying but everything else was a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I'd welcome another low-stakes platformer to the cozy game pile, but this one is terribly unremarkable, offering a slew of derivative tasks to engage with. In TTTT you spend time walking into collectibles, purchasing junk with said collectibles, doing menial chores for one-note strangers, and dealing with car-dependent infrastructure. Don't forget about the obligatory shovel, bug net, and paraglider: revolutionary features that have been known to shake the foundation of every game they appear in. The only thing that might set the game apart is the awkward dialogue which consists of short, derpy conversations that are supposed to be a form of humor. Steer clear of this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem, a small open-world collectathon that is greater than the sum of its parts.The gameplay is deliciously physical. The driving is both weighty and effortless. The world is densely packed with things for Terry to kick, smash, run over, and steal. There are loads of NPCs scattered around that always have something interesting to say, and I always looked forward to running into a new one. Everything about the presentation is phenomenal, from the music to the visuals which expertly capture a 2000's era cartoon platformer aesthetic. The writing is very dry and consistently got laughs out of me. What truly impressed me was the story. Terry, as goofy as he may seem, is a fairly deep and well-realized character in his own right, and I found the game's conclusion to be genuinely touching. I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun story about a kid living in a crazy little town without rules. The environments, characters and details bring life to this exploration-driving game. Filled to the brim with jokes, real-talk and unexpected events! A refreshingly short indie title in an age of +100 hour long experiences that mostly don't achieve this level of pure unscheduled FUN.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Played this at WASD London, added it to my wishlist immediately. It's weird, but within about 5 mins of playing it will completely hook you.It's a game about small moments and lovely things happening. It's such a charming little thing, filled with whimsy and joy and constantly makes me laugh out loud.Offers little moments of peace, joy and laughter constantly and for someone like myself who is neuro-diverse, it really does quiet the noisy part of my brain and gives me those little breather moments I need when playing any videogame.This game is a real gem, don't miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a four hour, funny experience with some stylish presentation, go at it. If you really want to play this game though, I'd get it on sale. I personally got it for $12 USD using the Short Hike bundle, because already owning A Short Hike reduced the base price.Ultimately, despite some really great writing, I was disappointed with the moment-to-moment gameplay that connected each character interaction. For a collectathon, none of the collectibles feel intentionally placed or organized. The turbo junk is just placed all over the ground and rooftops, and they are often phasing behind objects in the environment, making them easy to miss. The blueprints, bugs, and mushroom chimes are just placed in the outskirts of town in areas that don't feel finished. I spent a lot of time walking up and down the sides of the highways trying to pick everything up. You primarily collect cash by either meleeing literal dumpsters and garbage bags or digging up the hundreds of dirt mounds strewn about everywhere.The collectible economy is also unbalanced. I can't recommend trying to 100% this game, as the cash you need to collect every hat and item is way higher than the money you'll find completing every quest and digging every hole on the map. From what I can tell, the only real way to gain cash quickly is to grind out a repetitive car theft mission, and that's only if you're able to find the fancy car that randomly spawns on the map. The fancy car doesn't even get you that much cash either. At least 30 minutes of my playtime was spent grinding this mission because I decided to complete the government debt quest before buying the hang glider, which the latter is needed to get a large amount of junk left on the map.I was also disappointed in how the car is implemented into the game itself. Don't get me wrong, I love how the car feels, and I've had a blast driving around town. But other than one pretty simple destruction derby minigame, there aren't a lot of places to really have fun with the car. There are maybe two ramps on the entire map, so don't expect any fun jumps or stunts to send your car flying. Also, the boost just increases your car's movement to a fixed speed. Upgrading the boost doesn't make you go faster, it just increases the time you get to go at this increased fixed speed. After I hit the required boost count needed to beat the game, I couldn't really see a point in upgrading it any further. This game is silly, why not let me launch my car across the map at absurd speeds once I hit the endgame collectibles?Also, the jumping feels janky with the camera. There were a ton of times where I felt like I was just shy of a ledge in ways that felt unpolished instead of intentional.I could nitpick more, but the point is this game really shines with some laugh-out-loud cutscenes, just don't go in expecting the collectathon gameplay to be as addictive as some of the other shortform experiences that have hit steam in the last couple of years. And this isn't to knock the developer, either! I'm genuinely impressed by the polish and production values from this one-man dev team. I could see these mechanics and universe making for an excellent sequel at some point. But at a base asking price of $18 USD with only 3-4 hours of gameplay before you're forced to grind your way to 100%, I wouldn't recommend it at this time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game visually with tons of style, but as others have mentioned the game feels aimless and with no stated goals after getting the car, and with so much text and no auto advance I burnt out pretty quickly on this one.Four things to maybe consider adding in an update:+auto advancing dialogue+rebindable controls (I know Steam offers a workaround but it is a pain)+A toggle maybe for the accelerator? (I have RSI so this is maybe to specific but it would be nice lol)+a stated goal or direction after unlocking the taxi (I'm thinking about other games in this genre? Short Hike and Little gator game -- all of them have an overarching goal/story that helps keep you engaged, especially coming from the Wuppo team, I was kinda expecting something more grand)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I get liking the charm.  I get liking the writing. But I do not get why a game that has controls this awful gets as much love.  The car has the turning radius of a small tectonic plate.  Every &%@&^@% minigame takes you out of the controls you use in the rest of the game (i.e. are comfortable with and used to) and sticks you in isometric perspective.  Almost every edge in the game has an overhang, so if you are standing next to the wall and jump you bump your head rather than go high enough to jump up.  It's just a collection of poor game design decisions that together make me like the game, but hate playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: There is basically no story, and almost no gameplay, it is just a collectible finding simulator. Takes the thing that open world games introduce to ramp up play time and makes a game out of it.Sad because the environment, aesthetic and goofy characters are pretty fun and have a lot of potential.This game is not worth either full price or the current sale value of 14$
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Crazy impressive solo developer (Lars Korendijk) effort! If you like short, tiny, densely packed open world games with quirky characters like A Short Hike, this is an easy sell. The art style is unique and the lop-sided eyes and faces were unforgettably distinct. The animations are superb, and there is so much attention to detail which adds to the comedy. Terry is left home alone because of his lacking school grades while his family is on a luxurious holiday. He's ordered to go to summer school but he decides to do very adult things like get a job, drive cars, dig up junk, make money, and do crimes (without threatening or harming others) in this anarchist city with no laws or police system. He just wants to take his car into space, no biggie. The awkward humour and comedic timing is spot-on, and made me look forward to every cutscene. The writing is fantastic from the memorable characters to the silly logic of this weird world. The progression system of collectibles and money is engaging, and made me binge this game in a few days. I genuinely would get scared whenever Ricky would spawn in the world without warning, because he'll chase you down across the city to get you into a bumper car battle. The platforming was fun throughout, particularly when you get the glider because then you can ride the wind tunnels that take you all across the map, much like when you fully unlock flight in A Short Hike. It's not just quirky and silly side-quests, but there are some darkly comedic and tragic moments, such as Burning Bernie and Terry's dad's financial insecurity and pretending to be rich. It's a very satisfying ending, and this is the best comedy game of 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this game! Instead of creating a super large open world map with lots of empty space and filler, the developer decided to create a small map that is so tightly packed with content that I was never bored while playing it. I love the stylized graphics, the soundtrack, the gameplay, and the super silly plot.Also the dialogue. The dialogue is so damn funny. This game is full of surprises and I would highly recommend it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I can describe this game is an even goofier, more stylised and modern version of Simpson's Hit and Run. The game is small and can be beaten relatively quickly but it makes you want to go that extra mile and do everything it has to offer. It's silly, it's really silly and it has so much charm that you can't help but smile your way through everything.The mini open world was full of things to look for and find and it felt alive and vibrant with vivid colours and a wonderful soundtrack. It may not be anywhere near as large as GTA V or any of the Just Cause games but it doesn't need to be. The map sticks in your brain and it leaves a mark. It's memorable and fun and I had a blast just driving around. In fact I will still probably boot the game up from time to time to just drive around this goofy little island.It reminded me of my time playing Goat Simulator when I was much younger. Just goofing around having fun. The best part is I don't feel guilty for hurting people either! They just fall over and get back up again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: What a short game, but a beautiful (and i gonna admit it, strange) game it is. Its the proof that you don't need good drawing or AAA missions to make good games. Sometime, you only want to wander in a city and do a bunch of useless stuff, and its okay. Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip makes me want to do that: just appreciate the ride, make some strange new friends, have awkward conversations with them, do silly missions on the road. I'm glad to have discovered this game and helped an indie developer doing others games like that. But now, because of the ending, waiting for a DLC (that may never come, but hoping ahah)!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun little collectathon romp. Humor is very dry Gen Z stuff, I was well entertained by it but I can see how some people might not appreciate it. The highlight of the game is the visual and aesthectic style. The way the characters turn in accordance to where your camera is, the goofy physics, the silly hats and characters. Its all very fun to look at and experience. The actual gameplay leaves a litttleeee bit to be desired, there isnt really any interesting platforming, its more about exploring the town and figuring out little puzzles, so don't expect to be challenged. Overall I would say if you like collectathon games and goofy humor, pick this one up on sale and have a nice evening playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a collectathon, take that as you will. It has a surprisingly down to earth and heartfelt story. The game's QoL can be improved with a better UI for the map and the controls for navigating the inventory is also a little weird. The Game and map is pretty small so do not expect too much from this game. It works well has just a small, fun, casual game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is absolutely terryific. I was thoroughly engaged from the moment I first stepped foot into the city of Sprankelwater 'till blasting off into low earth orbit with my little taxi car. I crawled around every nook and cranny and it took me around 8 hours to 100% the game. Collecting all of the turbo junk can be a bit tedious, but it's manageable. I look forward to more games from snekflat.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: A REALLY well put together AA game, inspired by Simpsons Hit and Run.Really nice story and humour! A lot of moments took me off guard, things programmed in just for 1 time gags so everything always felt fresh.Bunch of stuff to do, can wander off and meet new people, leading to new minigames and things to do. Plus extra content to do that doesn't feel tedious if you stick around past story. I've 100% the game with all achievements in 9.5 hours.Unique art style. Might not be everyone's all time favourite style, but feels like a breath of fresh air in a sea of games that look identical!Really is a 3D game that feels nostalgic back to when games genuinely wanted to be fun!Very polished, didnt find any bugs, but if you did, theres an unstuck button in the pause menu.Really worth the money, and id highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun, humor in the game is childisch but in a very good way.You can see there is alot of passion in this project yet there i some things i noticed.I was able to finish the game (1 boost) before i was ment too. I was pretty fast to discover you can glitch into some bulidings from behind.So basically, funny, good game but it misses some details and fine grinding to be a really really good game
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game. A 'pure' game that doesn't waste your time. I'm impressed at the amount of depth they fit into this little city, and the mechanics that snekflat implemented. TTTT is a mini GTA with all the interlocking systems and mini games they've created. It's difficult to create a game with a unique style but snekflat did it, again (wuppo). Fun dialogue.Runs extremely well on Steam Deck. Better even than some 2d games. If you want to occupy 5-10 hours exploring, this is your game. I truly hope snekflat continues to develop games like this cause I feel this was something special.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is all the joyful, funny romp I thought it would be from watching the trailer. Here are the positives: the characters surprised and humored me, my curiosity was rewarded at every turn of a street corner, the music was like a delightful summer vacation day, and I was surprised by the number of minigames. I took 3-4 hours to reach the story ending and 8 hours to find all the collectibles. This compact playtime benefits the game, but Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip did suffer from the typical pacing slow down of all collectathons towards the end. I noticed diminishing returns on my enjoyment from gameplay loop and humor around hour 6, but there are tools in game that kept me from getting too frustrated. tldr: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is a humorous collectathon that wraps up before overstaying its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun open world platformer, reminds me of The Simpsons Hit & Run, but also a little bit of the formula from games like Lil Gator Game, A Short Hike, and Smushi Come Home. It's quite fun to explore and discover, and has fun minigames, my favorite being the Soccer minigame, which I hold the world record of 32 goals at the time of this review. Check this game out!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool little game. It has a simple premise, it is pretty funny and has a catchy soundtrack. The main character’s single-minded focus is adorable, and the way the story develops over time is heartwarming in a dumb, funny way. One complaint I have about the game is that it is too short, with is a good complaint to have. It is worth the price, specially with a discount. I would like to see a sequel for this game, a bigger game with more cities to explore and more roads. Maybe “Teen Terry Turbo Tour”. Where he visits the world. With more activities and more puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastically gremlin-energy chaos and I LOVED it!- The humor tickles my funny bone in just the right way without feeling forced or overdone.- It's very straightforward game play for the most part. I think 100%ing it might be a little difficult due to the controls not always being the most precise, but that's not a bad thing. It fits the chaotic nature of the game just fine.- Sharing fries with the fish took way more of my attention than it should have, but I don't regret it one bit.- SPAAAAAAACE!Overall this was a goofy, fun time with just enough challenge to keep things interesting while not losing the "relaxing" element that makes this title so delightful. If I could play it for the first time again - I absolutely would!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely hilarious and so much fun to play! I explored the demo prior to this as well and loved every minute. There is so much to explore and many collectibles to find, the devs have done a great job of making such a light hearted, silly, cheek-aching game here. The funny dialogue has had the community & I laughing for hours!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is chaotic, but super cute. I love that you can run around and hit people and there's no consequences. I wish there was a bit more instruction, but it's fairly easy to figure it out. The interactions with the townspeople is pretty hilarious. I loved that the credits gave a bit more to the story as well. Definitely worth buying for something short and cute. I hope they make another one!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is peak. Didnt even know i was playing for four hours until i got off. Would play again and run people over. TERRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRY.**edit I beat the game 100%, and i want a sequel. this game was fun to play (minus me trying to find the turbo junk, thank god the dev buffed the hat) and i enjoyed every minute of it.**
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This is game has to be my fave indie game released this year, I had so much fun playing this, I laughed way too much, loved finding little Easter eggs too. I took my time to explore and then complete the main story line, then found out that there is still so much to do. I got one more achievement left and then I will be 100% satisfied
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: The Nephew and Uncle Dynamic in this game is spot on. Worth Every Penny. Fun game to pick up and play for a bit, or sit down and collect all sorts of hats, bugs, and other collectibles. Collect some turbo junk, do some minigames with people that know Terry, find love, stay in contact with your uncle, and do crime! Its completely legal!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I’m 4 hours in, nowhere close to the end (i play games slow) and I love it. The humor is really amazing, and in a small way carries this game a bit, but the art, gameplay, quests, and the whole overall mission of the game is more than enough to keep me going to finish the goal of the game: get to space. I love it thus far, waiting for Tiny Terry’s Turbo Trip 2 lol
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not exactly sure what pulled me in. The nonsense one liners that every character seems to drop, or the whimsical world in which everyone is connected. I could not stop driving my ride around the city streets, zipping through traffic to collect junk. I love the art of every character. Thanks for the Trip Terry
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: i will recommend this game because its a fun short game, but im actually a bit disappointed and heres why.im a big wuppo fan so i thought this one has to be just as good, but in comparison it felt more like a demo/unfinished game, in the sense that theres this nice city/open world which the dev created, but it feels empty in the way that theres not much to do. you do a few quests, and then just collect money/turbojunk for almost no reason besides achievements.for almost 3 hours of content (and im still being generous here), 15€ is a bit steep, would only buy this on sale.i feel like the dev shouldve put this in early access and worked more on it, and put a higher price on it, because its such a shame that such a nice established world has almost no stuff to do in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Fun casual collecathon, would recommend for a tenner.The writing surprised me quite a bit!Might even be a decent game to give to a kiddo.For the devs, would suggest lowering slightly prices or increasing money gained slightly. And for Junk to be easier to track "post-game" And spread the bugs a bit more evenly^^Other than that it's a big ol' duimpje omhoog van mij :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Don’t get me wrong, I love playing the emboldened hero that’s saving the world or stopping a shadowy organization that threatens nuclear apocalypse, but sometimes it’s nice to drive around a cartoony city full of colorful characters as a kid whose only goal is to go to space so he can skip summer school. Tiny Terry’s Turbo Trip works as intended right out of the box and guarantees at least a few hours of leisurely fun. Read the full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly fun and comedic game about Tiny Terry going to space. There were plenty of good jokes thrown in there, and fun side quests to complete. My only gripe about the game is that finding all the turbo trash can be a bit frustrating since you'll be running all over the map, waiting for your hat to beep in the one or two areas you somehow missed (if there was a system on the map to shown a general area that you were missing the turbo trash, this would be greatly appreciated). Highly recommend playing the game, very fun way to kill 7-8 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: adorable!! fun!!! funny!!!! what a wonderful little gamei wish more of the island was jam-packed with little stuff (even just little things like junk or money in hard to reach corners of the map), but this game is a blast otherwise, and will probably continue being a blast as i hopefully go for completion
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: A game that simply puts a smile on your face. You play as Terry, a young....platypus?....whose parents left him to go on vacation while he's supposed to be attending Summer school, being not-so-supervised by his uncle. Instead of attending school, he decides that he wants to get a car and go into outer space, as I'm sure we all want to right now.The game is you going around town meeting with people and completing objectives related to each character you meet which leads to the next objective, etc. There's not much challenge in any of these objectives, but that's a good thing - this is meant to be a fun game, not a frustrating one.If there are two criticisms to be had, it'd be that a few objectives are tedious to complete without a guide (find items hidden throughout the world), and that there's one objective that requires a large amount of cash that, if you're not aware of how to get money quickly, it's a massive grind.Still, $15 for 5 hours of me smiling and having that childlike innocence and wonder feeling is more than worth it. I highly recommend this game to anyone who is capable of playing "kids games" simply to relax and enjoy the silly humor in them.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: this game genuinely might be one of my favorite indie games ive played thus far.to preface i grew up on ps2 games and this is so reminiscent of simpsons hit and runi felt like a kid again sitting on my x-rocker chilling on a summer day driving around the citythank you snekflat for the joy this game has brought me <3ps: peep the soccer minigame leaderboard ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry is a very easy game to get lost into. The characters are goofy, the music very very addictive, the mini missions simple enough but original.You can be as chaotic as you want without any permanent damage to yourself or the people around you.and your main mission is to go to space!! drive cars, steal cars, wack people....or just spend the day catching bugs.i loved the game, it was just the perfect mix of soothing gameplay and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, relaxing, wholesome game with a nice ending with the uncle in the world!. Good game to play on your down time, it was quite funny and goofy in it's setting. As our character goal is to drive a car up a tower to go to space. Easy to complete, finishing challenges from other characters to get "Turbo Junk" to upgrade your car to go faster. Collect items throughout this city and have a ball.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely charming open world 3D platformer. Feels like something special, great work to all involved! I really admire the art direction on this, it feels very cohesive and the characters feel so expressive. I would absolutely love a sequel where Terry ends up in a bigger city, or maybe gets to go on holidays somewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun and funny game.Something chill, silly and simple to play but just be weary that the games camera can sort of make you sick but thankfully the devs listened as they added an FOV slider and the option to stop the bobbing camera.I'd say well worth the money and you can get more hours if you want 100% the game but I am not an achievement hunter, so I tried to do everything I possibly could. As you can see, I just missed out on a few achievements.Overall experience with the game is that I enjoyed it, even though at first I was lost. A quick tip, just talk to all the ? on the map which will then start the missions, then complete the missions, upgrade your car and what ever else.So I do recommend this game at it's price point for a bit of silly fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: A very short (about 2-4 hours depending on many quests you go for) game about exploration and collecting thing, with lots of deadpan humor (the game's premise is essentially a joke that the ending pays off). There is no combat or death (except maybe getting zero on money), not even much platforming.If you want a game to zone out in while collecting do-dads with no time limit or risk, and a fan of Wuppo's humor, this game can work for you. Otherwise, you will get a very short game that might feel pointless if you are expecting more. Is the criticism that I wish there was more to a game a good criticism? Or a sign that it is good quality?
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little game, I had a great time with it. Unfortunately it is way too short, I'd still recommend it because it made me laugh, and it's honestly really nice playing it, but I finished the game in under 4 hours and ended up craving for more.I'd love to see some more content added, maybe a modding scene who knows.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: great game, I just couldn't put it down, 100%'d it in one session. It's a sandbox game with some lite collect-a-thon elements that's a lot like The Simpsons Hit and Run, with a ton of original ideas and immaculate vibes. It made me laugh outloud numerous times. There's even a bit that reminded me of Yakuza Kiwami, where they give you a rival that can approach you on the street if they see you.I really can't think of a flaw in this game that could get in the way of enjoying it, I played it when I wasn't feeling so good, and it really helped. Thank you dev, I'll check out Wuppo next.Pros:+do crime+explore the small-but-detailed open world+funny+lots of interactivitycons:-the driving is almost completely lifted from Simpsons Hit and Run, I know some people don't like how driving handles there, and those people probably won't like how it handles here.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Hilarious and charming game that I enjoyed every second of. The dialog had me wanting to talk to everyone and not miss anything. You can tell so much thought and love went into this game, the ending made me quite emotional as I had grew to adore the world and characters in such a short amount of time. Don't be put-off by the seemingly short play time, as every second is worth it and it is not a game you would regret playing. 10/10 luv u Terry <3
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quirky, cartoon-y game whose gameplay seems to compare with titles like Simpsons: Hit & Run and I mean that in the nicest way. Though the map is rather condensed and simple, the amount of content is not as much as your average story-based game; what there is in map and content is rich and entertaining.I do have to say that the start kicks off on a bit of a awkward footing which gave me pause. You do spend a fair bit of the beginning a bit lost as to what you do and it does feel a bit barren. I expect a fair amount of people to sort of drift off with the lack of direction. But if you just give it a chance, you get...A surprisingly strong premise from such a simple goal that not only always keeps you guessing with what's going to happen next, but also finishes in such a heartwarming way. I mean it about the ending too, the message at the end is what brought me to writing this review. Good job, snekflat. I hope this game brings you a lot of success.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun and it made me laugh. For the price it's a fun night and if you want to 100% everything then it will take a weekend. The music was especially good and added a ton to the charm and quality of the game. I will say for a game about having a car there wasn't a single race in it, I thought that was odd lol. You'll be quickly engrossed into the quirkiness of this game as you explore though, but if you don't like collecting things and not having anything to fight then it probably isn't for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: AAAAWWEEESSSSSOOOOMMMMEEEEEEEEThis game is great, I loved every second of it and it is one of the best money I ever spent on SteamSo much heart put into this game, and it's easy to tellI can't describe with words how much it made me smile!I absolutely adored it from start to endAnd perfect duration!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely love this game so much, it's amazing.First of all, the odd style it has is beyond appealing to see, it's genuine eye candy just watching some of the basic movements and designs. The cars, the characters, the effects, all of it molds together so well to make the game feel so vibrant! It's so goofy and unserious, and it perfectly encapsulates what the game is.Second of all, the writing is very well done. Nothing makes sense and everyone is just okay with it, most games I skim the dialogue as fast as I can but this game has such funny moments that I dare not skip a single line.Third of all, the gameplay is very simple. Collect the doohickeys to get the win. Yet there's still a lot else to interact with and do. All those little side quests really flesh out the game and keep throwing more interesting things at you!The bad? If anything, I'd say it's too short. It only took 7 hours to 100% the game and get all the achievements, but I still say the game's worth it. I'd kill for some DLC, a sequel, anything!I wish the best for the developers and the best for their future!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super unique and an absolute ton of fun! I found myself smiling from ear to ear and laughing out loud while playing the game. You help terry find Turbo junk all over Spranklewater and form NPCs to use to upgrade terry’s car so he can go to space. The map is small but does not feel super small as there are a ton of funny NPCs and secrets to find all over to map. There are also a ton of locations where you can shop for different items to help your traversal of the map or just to look super stylish. Whether you are running around with a pipe in your hand robbing people for some extra coin or driving around town to your next destination its is just an absolute blast. I really love the world building and the stories of characters in Terry’s life.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Goofy lil game. GTA mixed with A Short Hike. I had fun speeding around town and meeting all the silly characters. Although simple I also liked the story and world building. Give it a try if you are a fan of small open world games!My criticisms are: I got 100% after a long slog of searching for every single turbo bit and one too many trips stealing sports cars to sell to that little kid. It turned a 3 hour long game into a 9 hour and mostly not in a good way. Maybe make things cost less or the bits closer to the roads so you can organically pick them up while driving and exploring. I wish I had spent more time in the car because it is fun to drive but none of the missions require you to be in it. Also, the bat and wrench are seemingly not any better than the pipe? What's the point? Maybe make them able to loot more money or do some special action?
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: If GTA and a cartoon show had a baby, this would be it. Not done with it yet, but not a hurry to do so either, it's a nice game to chill with. It's great to have an open world game that isn't huge and mostly empty, or having you do the same thing over and over ad infinitum. Highly recommend it if you like to do your own thing but still have an overarching goal and lots of side quests that don't feel like pointless filler.Only real negatives are the camera can be a bit of mess in interiors and in tight confines and while I'm not done yet, I'm quite far along already, so it will be short. Would love a larger game world and even more NPCs to chat with, more vehicle variety, and just more of this delightful game to play and explore!I hope this does well so we can get a bigger and even better sequel! This is a fun and silly game, a veritable joy to play.Just finished it. The ending is excellent. I did make sure to 100% everything, but could have ended the game much earlier if I hadn't done so. This game has a lot of heart as well as being goofy and enjoyable to play, get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game illicts the same emotions I felt as a child playing the Lego City bonus level from Lego Star Wars The Complete Saga.No stakes, no time limits, the world is moving at your pace and any direction you want to go in, even mindlessly, is the right way to go. Nothing is taken seriously, nothing has repricussions, you're just a silly goofy dude who wants his little car to go faster. In this charming, whimsical world, that's all you need. Pick it up, clear your head. Cleanse you palate of shooting and high octane action. Stop and smell the flowers with Tiny Terry, it'll do you some good!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It's relatively short if trying to complete the main storyline, HOWEVER...It's got a level of humor that hits a different note than anything I've played before. It's clever, and the devs seem like very funny and fun having people that know how to inject enough absurdity and "well, Duh" moments into the game. This is rambling and I'm stoned, but TLDR this ♥♥♥♥ is good as hell and made me laugh out loud at multiple points while playing sober earlier. devs also shout out the player in the credits and the internet which really put a smile on my face.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sensory delight, with adorable characters and art and music, and it's fun to engage with all the zany character on the very small island you have to work with, although it certainly feels bigger than it actually is. It's fun to explore and get around.I think the game kind of bogs itself down with the digging. Not only is the digging animation rather drawn out, you do it an awful lot to dig up money from the ground. It's rather slow and flow-breaking. That, and the actual jumping and running around aren't really cathartic by themselves.That all said, this is a delightful game of the kind I'd love to see more of from indies, stretching the boundaries of what we usually expect from the industry.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast. This is another tiny sandbox game like Lil Gator Game or A Short Hike that really gets you invested and is actually fun to 100%. The dialogue in this game is absurd, the music is catchy as hell, and the characters are charming. I love playing as Terry, but Uncle Grony is the true hero of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: An exquisitely well-crafted and soulful collectathon in the same vein as Banjo-Kazooie with a dash of GTA mixed in.Explore a quirky world full of interesting characters. Engage in hijinx in your pursuit of Turbo junk to upgrade your car. Go to space.It's a short, sweet game which doesn't ask much of the player, doesn't overstay its welcome, and encourages you to explore around every corner to find that next thing that will make you laugh or smile. I particularly enjoyed the use of pregnant pauses in conversations to great comedic effect.Everything in the game is there for a reason. Nothing goes unused, even up until the end and beyond. snekflat has done it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly ridiculous, but great fun with an excellent sense of humour. A game you don't stop smiling at, but with a surprising amount of content for a micro open work indie game. Definitely one for completionists, with loads of collectibles to round up. Runs great on Rog Ally, if that's a thing for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: it's a great game!!! i've been waiting for it and well... IT'S BETTER THAN I THOUGHT IT WOULD BE. so fun to play, explore the world and see wuppo references everywhere!thanks, knuist and perzik (snekflat). i hope that this game will get even more content and maybe more mini games like fishing or flying on a plane!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Loads of personality to everything with the artstyle and sound design. Music is also great.I do wish there were a few quests with more involved objectives. Collecting turbo trash/money gets quite repetitive. Seems like it's either that or a minigame.Ignore my playtime, the game doesn't take that long to complete. I only took that long because I'm the greatest damn orange football player spranklewater has ever seen, and I must use my talent for good.Reasonable price for a great game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip

_childDocuments_.review: List of crimes committed as a child in this game:- Assault & Battery- Grand theft auto- Aiding and abetting a criminal- Petty theft- Felony vandalism- Interrupting a crab raveI had an absolute blast playing this game, despite its cartoony and very childish appeal. I was able to finish the base game in about 3.5 hours. To reach 100% and also just goof around, the next 4 hours were spent  hunting bugs and scrap, or with the game menu & music running in the background while tending to other tasks. Certainly something that you can have fun completing in just one evening, though I doubt its something to ever come back to in the future for a second playthrough. I recommend this just on the merit that it feels reminiscent of late 2000s games, is a good 4-8 hours of gameplay depending on how in-depth you want to get, and its apparent the devs enjoyed building this game. Equally recommended because it was fun to run around as a child and commit the same crimes as I would in GTA :D

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes when life is beating you down... you will want a game that is laidback. Terry is a simple game. There's no combat, no escort missions, or optional racing mode. You collect monies, doodads, and find silly stuff on the map. This game is a smorgasbord of a scavenger hunt with tons of monies and doodads scattered throughout and some of them in very hidden locations.I beat the game in almost five hours and all I had left were a couple of quests. One was to buy the remaining items in the shops and the other to spend a relatively large sum of money. So the game is a little shorter but that might be a relief if you plan to be a completionist for this one.Oh, if you liked Wuppo then you're definitely going to like this game! There are a few Wuppo easter eggs hidden throughout the game :)

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip is a light, sweet short adventure. The highlights are definitely the art style and music which are both very charming, and the dialogue that is lighthearted and fun. I have a couple nitpicks but they're nothing too serious: I kinda wish the fast travel were unlocked a bit earlier, but the map's small so it's not a big issue. I also feel like the movement could be a little more complex - though I acknowledge that's a really personal preference - as I think it would add to the sandbox-y feel of the game. The ending includes a nice message too, even though the game would be fine being just a silly thing. In the end, I thoroughly enjoyed my stay in Sprankelwater. :)
