_childDocuments_.review: tldr It's best consumed as prequel by many reasons aside from lore-related. Some spoilers ahead.All in all, it's a really nice dating sim. There are many fun mechanics, and you're given quite a big house to explore compared to small apartment that D had in his game. Things change between chapters, your goals alter, and you get to play in somewhat different ways and experience different things. All in all, a pretty nice experience.There is a pretty huge difference though - the main focus of the story is no longer the deity itself, but what happens to her and you. While there are quite a lot of dialogues and other lore-related info given to you, allowing major implications and linking them to events of original Sucker for Love (so I'd not be ashamed of calling this game Sucker for Lore for what it's worth), there are fewer interactions between you and deity specifically, so you don't actually develop a romantic relationship between her and you in the same way as it was done before. Maybe you can blame Muu for that tho.First chapter was quite entertaining, sure, but as soon as you get the hang of navigating the house, it really looses its charm, things become much quicker as there's not much of what the game can do to surprise you. There's less variety, less secrets (at least from what I've observed, as this time the process to unlocking final chapter is rather linear compared to original), it gets a bit stale after a while and I still don't understand how S got as pumped as she did. Her motivation feels like a far cry to what D had, despite how absurdly it may sound.Still, despite all, I'd recoomend playing this game. Just for a little bit of fun, or to spice things up for youself before going to play original for the first or second time. Just... if you've already played the original one, don't get your hopes too high up. They're really very different.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember watching Markiplier play First Date which got me into the series and after playing it myself, made me excited for the next game, so after the delay and the waiting game, I was really hyped up when I learned it dropped so suddenly last week, and within 24 hours of it releasing, I bought it, installed it, played it, and beat it to completion. And so, here are my thoughts.It's short. It's short on a lot of things. You might have one more chapter, but it still feels like not enough in the grand scheme of the game.1. Stardust is cute, Rhok'zi is hot, the cultists are unique, but most of the time is you moving through the house and doing the rituals, leaving you very little time to interact with the characters, especially Rhok'zann. If there was more time with her, like in the demo, the relationship would have felt more solid than sped up.2. The dating pool. It's ONLY Rhok'zann, and as much as I love me some Rhok'zi, I was really hoping to get a chance to date the other Eldritch beings like Muu or Auntie Nyan Nyan, but I also understand the focus is supposed to be on this one relationship. Still, it just left me a little disappointed.3. For all the Eldritch abominations and terror the settings can have...I wasn't as afraid of failing, or even of the threats, as I was in the first game. When I died in this one, I got more irritated that I had to traverse the house again to do anything, and while I really love the mechanics of moving through the house, it got very repetitive, which made it less scary.All in all, I do love this series and I want more Sucker for Love games to be made, but I really miss the balance the first game had. The designs, the voice acting, the ambiance and sound work, even the presentation of an old early 90's anime VHS series, it's all great and perfect and I wouldn't change them in the least bit! I just love these cosmic cuties, and I wanna smooch them, so I hope to get a chance to date more of them in the next game!

_childDocuments_.review: Before this I will say that this won't be an entirely positive review, but it'll be a mostly positive one. Also slight spoilers, though I attempted to minimize anything related to the plot.The most credit to give this game is the art. The art is PHE-NOM-IN-AL. It really creates a great atmosphere that is both unsettling and has you always question your surroundings. The character art is also beautiful, even creating slight variety in the non-important characters which is a really nice touch and makes them more personal, especially the five innocent people in the 3rd chapter. It gives them more character, allowing the person to connect to them more. Plus...GOAT MOMMY GRAHHHH!!!Now the gimmiks and functions. I love the door functions, it makes each room you go in uneasy, especially in certain parts of the game where there's a reason to fear opening doors which creates suspense as you're forced to slowly open it. It's a great mechanic to add that suspense not in the form of music or environment. Though it becomes a bit iffy with the last bit. I won't say much about the specifics of it, though just that there is uniqueness and I do love them. My only issue is that they're...long. It doesn't create much suspense and makes it easy. Like the last one lasted a whole THREE out of the seven minutes I had to survive. Only had to do four to survive the whole seven minutes, and there was a repeat of one. I understand giving enough time to do some of them since it's a large area to get through, though some of them are unnecessary.The last thing...is the main character. I played the demo and full version and was able to see the removal of the protagonist's comedic "you're pretty" reply when you first summon Rohx with how they are going to destroy the forest and defeat her. Now, I will say I understand why. Narrative-wise, this was needed to solidify the MC's motives and not just make this someone who will abandon their motives so easily. I merely wanted to point this out is all as I found it interesting. The real issue I have...is that I wouldn't even classify this as a dating game with how the MC acts. I just consider it a normal visual novel of a girl getting wrapped up in a cosmic horror mess, finding compassion and love as she spends reality after reality with Rohx. It's a really sweet story, I'll give it that...though not a dating simulator. Everything just happens by happen-chance and there isn't really...love. I feel like it all just happens in the end and there isn't much build-up, only attempts made by Rohx that get struck down. I get that it's while all this intense stuff is happening, though it just feels like Rohx is making all attempts to love the MC. Of course I don't mean to add make-out scenes or illicit actions, just anything where Stardust would feel any love for Rohx. I get it, the character is ace...but still, it's meant to be a romance game. The end kiss scene was perfect with the MC knowing what it meant, I just wish I saw more awareness prior other than, like, a single moment where she gets all flustered in her head. I enjoyed the comedy of her blissful unawareness...until it just became a habit. Some is good, though not all.Now am I saying the character writing is bad? Absolutely not. Stardust's intentions and actions stuck to her character and it was great to see a game that doesn't have the MC throw away his/her values at the sight of the love interest. I'm just saying I don't believe the MC is fit for the role as much as Darling was in the first game.Though overall, it's a REALLY great game! The characters you meet are nice, Rohx is ho-I mean...a really creative interpretation of the Lovecraftian horror she's based around, Shub Niggurath, and it's a game that provides an immersive story with very world-interactive elements. The main thing I wish I saw here was player agency/control. You get two options at what you want to go down, that's it. That was the issue with the last one as well, so not just this one. You don't get to interact with how the story goes, you just do what the objective tells you and you get the ending you need to. Though at least with the last one you had a bit more...choice in some paths.I just want to say, no shame to the developers. _childDocuments_.review: Sucker For Love: Date to Die For is honestly a pretty good sequel to the first game, it has its great moments but I sadly think it fails to pick up and continue what First Date put down.  First though, I'll start off with what's great about it! The artstyle is honestly stunning and really hits that revamped 90's anime feel that it goes for, it's visually appealing to look at and the character art never fails to either look utterly adorable or terrifying depending on the moment. I also found the voice acting to be particularly amazing, Buck's voice is incredibly cool and menacing from the moment he first speaks, and Rhok'zan's voice is honestly just nice to listen to! The main characters are all great, with each of them being unique in their own way and really standing out (you know it's good when you just want more of them)! The gameplay is pretty solid with a fun fetch quest style loop with some rituals thrown in, and definitely makes use of the larger environment. The game also has great 'general horror' and tension, as I found the roaming around and opening doors mechanics to be quite tense during my playthrough! I do also like the concept of the game's subversion of First Date's premise by focusing more on romance than lust this time round.However, because Date to Die For is a sequel, I couldn't help but feel let down by it missing the heights of First Date. The reason First Date worked so well is that it not only served as an absurdist comedic parody of dating sims by having you date eldritch abominations beyond your comprehension, but also still managed to have a powerful message about the indomitable human spirit along the way. Date to Die For (in order to avoid rehashing the exact same game) instead aims for a Eldritch Horror romantical adventure with a powerful message about the power of love, but this doesn't hit anywhere near as hard because the game isn't actively supporting that message. You barely spend any proper time with Rhok'zan compared to the entities in the first game, which makes the relationship that develops feel kinda forced and underdeveloped. Additionally, everything Darling did in First Date served as a step towards his end goal of smooching the Outer Gods, whereas that isn't the case for Stardust in Date To Die For; something which again hurts the romance that's supposed to be the core focus. The game also seems to have dropped the comedy a lot compared to the first game; First Date had me constantly cracking up, whereas Date to Die For got only a few laughs out of me.Buck is also heavily underutilised as the main antagonist (despite how great he is). I really wish he had more screen-time and a chance to develop further, because he's easily my favourite character by far.  Overall, I'd probably give it an 8/10. Date To Die For is still a worthy game with what it brings to the table, and I definitely recommend you check it out because it is still really fun and terrifying! However, it feels underwhelming in comparison to First Date given the peaks that First Date provided.

The only problem (of you can call it that) is that all of this added quality comes at the expense of the absurdity, the whole game is no longer a joke. The first game you played as a relentlessly horny guy on a mission to kiss an eldritch god at the expense of literally EVERYTHING. It was carried by the absurdity of that concept alone. This game does much more with the horrifying elements that were introduced in the first game but quickly glossed over in service of the humor. But in turn this game also doesn't have those few moments where it snaps back to seriousness and gets across the lovecraftian nature of what you're doing.It's really hard to compare them, but overall I think this game is definitely worth playing, even if I can't decide if I like it more than the first game or not

_childDocuments_.review: A Date to Die for is a great sequel to the first game. The first game was a horror comedy visual novel that leaned into the comedy side, with a tale about a mega horny dude chasing after cute anime-girlified versions of 3 eldritch Lovecraft deities. This game narrows the focus down to a single deity wooed across 4 chapters, which allows for the relationship the be developed more deeply and seriously than any in the first game. The game is also able to use this narrowed romantic interest to develop side characters throughout the chapters. I found them all rather charming, which was helped a lot  by the consistently top tier voice work across the whole game.The game also leans more into the horror side of things compared to the first, with the safety of a single apartment room replaced with a large house the player has to sneak through to gather ritual supplies. The house remains the same across chapters, but the baddies wandering through it and the rituals you have to perform change each chapter. each of the many doors in the house has to be opened manually, which can be used to peek and see if a murderous cultist or monster is behind it. The combination of this door mechanic and the great sound design kept me feeling tense and appropriately unsafe throughout. The game is a fairly short play-through, I was able to achieve the true ending in about 4 hours. Other reviews point to a max of around 6 hours to grab all the endings.All in all, its a great and briskly-paced horror/comedy/romance visual novel with excellent VO, tense horror gameplay, lovely 90's anime visuals, and some very charming characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, Akabaka brings another funny and charming entry into Eldritch Horror Dating Sims. However, I would rate this below the original game in terms of overall enjoyment.This time, there's only one god to woo, "The Black Goat of the Woods" or, if that's too much of a mouthful, Rhok'zan. Auntie Nyan Nyan from the previous game makes an appearance, but she's more of a side character than anything.With only one god to try and smooch, the story is determined by how you handle the particular villain of each chapter and whether you're able to get them to your side or not. The means to do the former are pretty simple to figure out, so it's not like it's a huge puzzle.There are two endings per episode, a Good Ending and True Ending, and in order to unlock the finale, you have to find the latter for each episode. Be sure to dig around during the finale as well in order to find all the secrets!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely. It has all the charm and life of the first game. Really feels like a breathe of fresh air. The writing is clever and light hearted, the characters feel cozy and nice to vibe with. The horror elements really sell me on it. The exploreable 3d environment are really crazy for a visual novel and I feel like this game really pushes boundaries for what a dating sim can be (Which is not a surprise for this series tbh). Couldn't recommend it enough frankly. Its not perfect and I ran into a few bugs but I don't think I've really had a game experience quite like this game. The spray bottle gag is really funny. SO whatever lmaoI just want MORE. I'm excited to see whatever this dev does next :))))))))))))))

_childDocuments_.review:
While investigating the mysterious disappearances plaguing your rural hometown of Sacramen-Cho, you end up kidnapped yourself! Trapped at the murmuring, pulsating, undulating heart of the woods, your only hope for escaping the labyrinthian roots is to turn to the cultists' strange purple spellbook.

Amidst the fanatical scrawlings of madmen and unsettling images of otherworldy abominations, there's a passage describing the method for summoning the All-Mother, The Black Goat of the Woods -- preserver of life. Will you be able to escape? Or will you find your demise at the innumerable hands of The Thousand?

name: qomp2
detailed_description: Control a Pong ball aching to break free of its life stuck between two paddles. Explore a dangerous, minimalist world, armed with simple two button controls: tap a button to change direction diagonally by 45 degrees, and hold down a button to unleash a cathartic dash forward. That’s all you need to solve environmental puzzles and labyrinthine levels. Around each corner is a new challenge that will test your two-button and problem-solving skills. A variety of difficult enemies and bosses help you mark your time as you navigate through 30 levels spread across four worlds. qomp2 effectively captures the essence of the original 1972 Pong and its spiritual successor, the 2021 experimental indie title qomp. Key Features: Cerebral Puzzling: The simple, two button controls belie complex and compelling gameplay. Use your reflexes and think ahead to avoid hazards, flip switches, and bounce your way through 30 tricky levels. Hidden collectibles push you to explore every inch of the minimalist maps. A Surprise around Every Corner: qomp2 constantly delights as new features, mechanics, enemies, traps and hazards are introduced as you progress deeper into the game. Don’t get complacent: As soon as you’ve mastered one aspect of gameplay, another is ready to challenge you. Bosses: Four challenging bosses block your path at the end of each world. You will need to use all your newfound skills to master their attacks and defenses. Don’t worry. Death isn’t the end in an arcade-inspired world. Quick respawn makes sure you’re back in the action in seconds. A Serene Soundscape: A soundtrack of ambient jams gets you in the groove, and helps you keep your cool, as you work your way through the minimalist maze. An Emotional Journey: An enigmatic story of doubt, fear, and self-acceptance, told wordlessly through simple effects and gameplay.

name: Return to Grace
detailed_description: Return to Grace is a first person narrative adventure set in a visually stunning ‘60s retro sci-fi world. You play as space archaeologist Adie Ito, who has unearthed the ancient resting place of an A.I. god and onetime caretaker of the solar system known as Grace. The only inhabitants of the site are fracture variations of the Grace AI. Each with their own quirky personalities and unknown motives. Adie must choose which personalities to build relationships with as she seeks to uncover the secret of why Grace was shut down thousands of years ago. Mystery narrative where player choice affects story branching, clue discovery, character relationships, and the game’s thought-provoking conclusion. Experience a variety of interactions from harrowing balance beam crossings; to hacking ancient computer systems; to operating an unwieldy, flamethrowing jetpack. Explore a wondrous 60’s inspired sci-fi setting. Evening sized game that can be completed in one sitting and replayed for different experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: I only have one subjective criticism for this game and it's not directly related to the quality of the experience, I think the delivery of the story was decent, but the actual plot was very generic. Once again, we have another mystery about a central AI, and while I don't want to say much more than that, it's almost like an instant creative failure - if you doing a game about a sketchy AI, you need more layers to the plot. Not only I knew where it was going the entire time, the dialogue from "Control" was spoiling the twist for about 2 hours. The dialogue for most of the AI personalities was not even that bad, I even had a few laughs out of the "logic" character, you just needed a better motivation for the AI, or another layer to the narrative.The actual walking-simulator gameplay is decent, it's not exactly a high-end visual experience but it does enough variety for an indie game - I know it does not sound like a compliment, but honestly when a lot of these games just drop you on a generic 3D map, I'll take a game with a bit of variety any day. The game attempts to create a lot of immersive experiences, sometimes it works, and sometimes it does not. The amount of effort you would put into locations was fluctuating a lot, not every location was interesting to explore, especially when it comes to the texture and small details, often having no objects in the environment or a visible background.The story takes about 2 to 3 hours at most, there are a few different endings in addition to some of the small choices during the playthrough, so there is a little bit of replay value. There are no difficult puzzles, it's mostly a narrative experience, although you have to do some very basic input sections like walking on a metal beam, nothing hard though. The game does its best to have a cinematic feel to it, sometimes it will make you do things to build some atmosphere and a sense of escapism, but it's not always convincing.The main character is mostly stoic but I enjoyed her enough. The AI in this game has multiple personalities, so even though there are only a few characters in the game, there are multiple sources of voice acting as the AI will adopt new personality traits. I liked most of the dialogue in the game except the "control" character, I wish you handled him with more nuance, he kinda projects his plans too much.(+) As far as walking simulators on Steam go, it's slightly above average in terms of level design, I like all of the UI changes on the hand with the AI, this game does a bit more to build the environment, immersion, and a sense of escapism. It's not a great visual experience overall, but it wasn't bad in my opinion.(+) With the exception of the "control" personality from the AI, I enjoyed the writing and even got a few laughs out of it, I would say the "logic" had the best jokes. Again, the plot was very basic, but most of the dialogue was fine.(+) I thought the voice acting was mostly good, I just didn't like that one specific character because of the writing, but the performances were done well.(+) Multiple endings, a few forks in the story. - the control character projects his motivations too much, it ruined the game for me, and I also think the game didn't go anywhere, I wish you gave him other motivations or perhaps more depth to the narrative. I didn't feel the same way about any other AI in the game, it's really just the red one, in case you didn't understand what red color coding does. - I mean it was decent for an indie game, it still felt like areas were missing a lot of detail, it was very obvious that you just didn't have enough objects to make every part of the game look unique, as well as often hiding backgrounds.I wanted to say more nice things about the game, but the more I think about it, it really was not that impressive overall, if you handled the "control" with a bit more care I think it would work a lot better. There are some nice superficial elements there, and for the most part, I liked the dialogue between the main character and the good* AIs. You took no risk with the narrative, so I am not going to praise another generic AI story. Unfortunately, very solid, but very average walking simulator with a predictable story.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game for the first time. Wow! The atmosphere and wonder that this game creates kept me hooked the entire time. I found myself searching for more exposition at every opportunity. The choices I made really felt important. I could tell that a lot of thought and effort went into the writing. When I had to make those hard choices between having fun with Pal or taking the safer option with Mom, I found myself standing there frozen by my indecisiveness. I felt a connection with them.I definitely recommend this game if you love narrative based story driven games. Lots of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I played the whole game once through Xbox Game Pass. Enjoyed it so much that I bought it here to support the devs, as well as to have access to it if the game ever leaves Game Pass.Before I get started, my TLDR is: if you're into vibes, get this game. There are so much really cool ideas in this game, including mechanics, interactions, and story. But a lot of these ideas aren't developed enough. There are elements of Stanley Parable and Disco Elysium, but not fully wrought out like within those games. And as others echoed, the story is a-OK. Not more nor less than that.But for me, the combination of these elements in a walking-simulator package created an experience that enveloped me. The banter between the AI components, the beautiful world-building, the visceral feeling of pulling, pushing, and pressing things. Everything together created an immersive experience that was satisfying.Again, I really recommend this game. If you are concerned about the length, it's good to wait for sale. But if you want to have a vibey walking-simulator experience to get lost in for a little while, just get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Grace was a cute walking sim.  I enjoyed playing it.  You are trying to find out what happened to an old AI from the past at a lunar station.  Instead of finding endless notes, you discover “pieces” of the AI so you end up exploring with 6 different personalities that talk and help you.  You find audio canisters from people who had stayed there before to help tell the story.  I thought the voice overs were well done and the story interesting and made me want to continue.  There are several choices that can lead to  different endings.  My “explore everything and try to get the ending I was hoping for” gameplay took about 3 hrs.There are puzzles, but they are almost like filler.  They are something to do as you progress and are not challenging.  For me, sometimes that’s okay. I really liked that the game stayed true to being a walking sim.  There are jumps you need to make, but instead of turning it into a platformer, the game just lets you jump when you tell it to.  Thanks for that!I had fun with the game and am up for seeing what a bad ending looks like.  Is it a must play?  Ehhh … I don’t know if I would recommend it that way.  But if you like walking sims with some fun characters and a bit of mystery to the story, I would definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: A cute and touching little game if a bit simplistic, in comparison to say the works of Stanisław Lem. It explores the ramifications and the possibilities of an AI God-like being and its place in human civilization in the far, far future in a 60s retro science fiction style. Hence a bit naive in its simplicity but noble in the theme it explores in regards to a problem humanity will have to content with in the near future to come, for better and worse. Humanity obviously have the wisdom to content with it in theory, but will it be wise enough to make it work in practice, besides the world is a big place and there's quite a few wounded humans and nations out there … and who knows perhaps soon some wounded AI's too. Contemporary thinkers like Deepak Chopra and old jewels from our various wisdom traditions, does paint a potential bright future. So I can just stay complacent right dear reader. Anyway it's a neat little indie game.

Aida was basically Robin from Subnautica Below Zero, just dialed back one or two clicks. Can we not have intelligent conversations in games? They don't need to provide answers to big questions, some of the best things I've ever read or heard were just conversations between intelligent people from different backgrounds and perspectives who were just exploring their mutual ignorance. Noncommittal/nuetralMy god, the decor... so much leather and brass furniture, polished wood and formed concrete everywhere. _childDocuments_.review: This is a funny, sometimes moving story about Adie, an archaeologist in the 39th century, attempting to uncover the fate of the Grace AI on Ganymede 900 years after her "disappearance". This is a fully 3D, puzzle-light "walking simulator" (though I'd prefer to use the term "narrative-focused adventure game"). I completed the game in about 2.5 hours, but don't feel short changed in the slightest. I think the price is perfect. A very enjoyable (and thought-provoking) experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why the game isn't going to appeal to everyone, but I absolutely adored it. First, it's important for players to know what they're getting into so that there aren't misguided expectations. This is mostly a walking sim, and there is very, very little gameplay. The trailer shows a flamethrower, balance beam walking, running and jumping, etc., and those are extremely minimally present. The puzzles are also quite rare and have an auto-solve option (not a bad thing). The game is really about walking through the beautiful environments and soaking the in the dialogue and visual storytelling. I think it's effective and making these things interesting, but, if you're looking for engaging "game-y" gameplay, it's not to be found here. The story isn't terribly complicated, and I think that the "twist" is spelled out far too soon, but I think it really succeeds in building atmosphere and selling an emotional state that resonated with me. A lot of questions and ideas are presented without being directly brought up in dialogue. That won't be to everyone's tastes, but again, it worked for me. Return to Grace is a bit of a niche product that I don't think just anyone should pick up, but those that know they enjoy "walking simulators" and are ok with a game that only takes 2-3 hours will be rewarded with a polished, well made experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Only one serious bug encountered (first time in the garden, none of the interactables were 'live'. Workaround: exit and restart game; no progress was lost). [edit: the devs tell me that this has already been patched. Fast!] Time to play -- 3 hours. I did not hurry, but I also did not dawdle.I like games that make me think -- and I prefer relatively simple puzzles. This fit both of those preferences. Voicing was superb, and artwork was beautiful and apropos. Some light/gentle humor also worked well. The story was interesting, although as a long-term SF reader, the main McGuffin was obvious to me early on. Didn't spoil the story for me, though.It is indeed a walking simulator (and in fact you cannot run, a minor annoyance sometimes), but enough happened during that walk that I was rarely bored -- and only for very short bits, at that.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this over on Game Pass and loved it so much I had to make sure they got a sale as well! The voice acting is impeccable, The way the characters are written and interact with how -you- interact with them and the environment is really special. The two games that come to mind like it are Firewatch and to a less extent Consortium, but even then Return to Grace is unique.The game play is nothing to write home about: basic puzzles, simple QTEs they let provide an option to make "hold to tap" which is wonderful, lots of walking. Some really gorgeous environments. It's also painfully short at 2-3 hours, but I still think it's worth the full $15.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Grace has a lot of good atmosphere, visual design, and music, but it's a frustrating game. Interactions with the environment are controlled with mouse clicks, but they're often unresponsive or need you to get closer to objects even if the prompt is available. Aside from exploring the areas on foot, the only gameplay is some very simple puzzles, one of which you gain the ability to skip, which I used from then on to avoid more damn mouse clicks. At two points, important dialogue was skipped over, I assume due to a glitch. The first time led to progress becoming impossible, and I had to reload back to the beginning of the section because there's no option to save I could find. The second time, I looked out a broken window and watched my AI companion get chucked out through it for some reason. Reloading again, and being faced with the start of a level again, I'm debating whether it's worth finishing.The story and setting very interesting, but it seems like RtG would work better as a movie, not a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: This game is clearly not for me. I found it to be insanely boring and geared to those who enjoy interactive walking simulators with no combat. The story and setting failed to draw me in and the constant banter from the lead female character was distracting. I also experienced constant frame rate drops in 4k resolution using an RTX3080 and i9 processor when entering new areas, most likely due to the Unreal Engine 4 shader compilation stutter. WASD keys also cannot be remapped to the arrow keys because the arrow keys are hard coded for turning. There is also no fov setting and no way to manually save the game. Overall, I did not enjoy my time spent with this game and I therefore cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

Another solid, recent entry in the walking sim genre.Hoping we'll see more content - it's a rich world with a complex future history that could easily be expanded on in additional discoverable narrative-related items or optional events.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice genre piece. Lots of chunky retrofuturist design and blinkenlights, along with stained glass windows and grand iconography.Oddly enough my overall feeling is that it all came across a bit... graceless. Nothing's particularly worth paying attention to, and thankfully, the game never pretends to be a really profound experience. I probably should have been stoned to really get the best experience with the game. All the bickering AI personas would have been funnier that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: I love exploration games and Return To Grace was exactly what I hoped for.   It is a linear walkthrough that allows you freedom to explore beautifully designed environments while guiding you to each next objective.  The story, graphics, and sound effects are very well done.  There were a few areas that had some mild repetition but never to the point that I was weary of it.  Upon finishing the game, I was wishing for a sequel and ready to play it through a second time.  The game is on the easy side, but I liked that as I wanted to enjoy the story and surreal environment and not have to focus on beating bosses or challenging puzzles (there are neither).   I loved it and found it very well worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Well, its a typical "walking-sim". Roaming around, hearing messages, discovering the station and its history. Nice graphics, no technical issues.However, the story is okayish, not really engaging or exciting, nothing innovative or surprising. Actually, rather boring. Maybe, because the game is sooo short. You have not really time to get into the story - as the game is already over as soon as you get into it. It took me about 3h, not more. Thats just not enough. If I had known how short the game is, I probably would have not bought it...So, give a thumbs-up because it is a average, maybe sligthly below average, walking-sim. Neither especially good nor especially bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Walking simulators tend to have a much higher bar for their stories than other forms of gaming. Other games can have a mediocre or even bad story, but with mechanics that remain interesting for its entire length, it can and will be well received. Return to Grace is a walking sim, a first person trip through an abandoned station, in which you seek to understand, and potentially restore, an Ancient AI named Grace. The game is not especially long, but it is still interesting and full of content for its entire runtime. The game's story is excellent, having nothing spoiled for me, I truly did question my choices, and asked what the decisions I was making would cause. Each of the many different AI personalities are interesting to hear, not just in their lines, but their interactions with the player and each other. Control and Logic specifically, the first two AI we are introduced to, remain interesting and funny throughout, even as their specific desires influence how we progress through the game.Although limited, Return to Grace does include "rewards" for exploring areas fully, in the form of lore or messages, which remain an appropriate compensation for players going out of their way even with slower pacing. I must also commend the games puzzles. Return to Grace is not a puzzle game, nor are they particularly difficult. In fact, in most instances, there is the option for your AI companions to give you the answer or outright solve it for you. What the puzzles succeed in is providing another outlet for interaction with the AI, who remain the only real person to person interaction in the game. The only thing this game fails to do is optimize its formula. A walking sim is by definition, basic in terms of player ability. The entire game is completed with essentially the wasd keys and your left mouse button. The story absolutely fits the game, but multiple times I found myself annoyed with the actual interactions. If the player mouses over an intractable object before a relevant voice line is completed or some other event happens which "unlocks" that object, the player has to move the mouse off the object and back in order to activate it, even if the line or event has completed. This is frustrating, because this is not an attempt to bypass any story beats, but merely playing out the game. It adds meaningless extra downtime in a game formula which is already built on providing significant downtime.Some might call that nit-picky, but a walking sim's limited game play should be as streamlined and efficient as possible, especially since many players will already be hesitant with the slow pace of the game. However, despite some minor flaws in game play, I truly believe this game is worth every penny, which is true even after only having played for a little under 3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Impressive narrative game that manages to keep you intrigued despite its short playtime. It's a walking simulator with (very) light puzzle elements, excellent voice acting and a story about AI, human desire and sense of purpose. The graphics are simple, but effectively convey a retro science fiction scenario. Compared to similar games, the world feels a bit more contained, but the story goes deeper and touches on many existential questions. Definitely a recommendation and I look forward to more titles from the team!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Grace

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous environments with some wonderful colour choices. A thoughtful narrative that uses interactivity and player choice to explore themes of artificial intelligence and its intersections with human endeavour. I don't necessarily agree with some of the concepts and ideas explored in this science fiction imagination of human society, but the fact that it has ideas worth engaging with is part of what makes this a solid choice to spend a few hours of your time. This is a rich experience, give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never bought a game with only 2 reviews before (at the time I bought it), so kudos to the devs on the slick storefront presentation (and devs, be glad for the Discovery Queue).I've played the game for maybe 15 minutes so far and it seems well-made, so I'm doing the devs a favor here given the low review count and just leaving my own positive review immediately. I have nearly 7,000 titles ignored on Steam and that isn't a joke - I have high standards for games up-front, especially for a game like this, so I'd say they put some quality work in on this.This is a walking simulator with slightly more mechanics (there's at least a flashlight) and dynamic movement (climbing, jumping and crawling - all available at specific points, but the average walking simulator literally only has walking). It feels like it's going to end up being pretty linear, but I haven't gotten very far so I could be wrong. I can't comment on the plot since I'm not far enough along.Note - it appears to have good controller support and run flawlessly with default settings on Steam Deck (unless there's a crash later on I don't know about), so this may be a good option for people looking to play on one.

_childDocuments_.review:
Return to Grace is a first person narrative adventure set in a visually stunning '60s retro sci-fi world.

You play as space archaeologist Adie Ito, who has unearthed the ancient resting place of an A.I. god and onetime caretaker of the solar system known as Grace.

The only inhabitants of the site are fracture variations of the Grace AI. Each with their own quirky personalities and unknown motives.

Adie must choose which personalities to build relationships with as she seeks to uncover the secret of why Grace was shut down thousands of years ago.

name: Rune Factory 3 Special
detailed_description: Rune Factory 3 Special - Digital Deluxe Edition The Rune Factory 3 Special - Digital Deluxe Edition features the game and the exclusive "Swimsuit Mode" DLC. Enable this mode in the Trophy Room to dress Micah and all marriage candidates in their swimsuits year-round! About the Game Settle down in an idyllic fantasy town as a young adventurer with a monstrous secret in Rune Factory 3, remastered for a new generation. Features brand new to Rune Factory 3 Special include Newlywed Mode, standalone adventures unlocked after marriage to each of the game's 11 eligible bachelorettes and a 'Hell' difficulty level to challenge even veteran players! Whether it's your first visit or you're returning after a long time away, experience the unforgettable story of Rune Factory 3 with improved graphics and redesigned 3D character models. An Adventure Spanning Two Worlds Step into the shoes of Micah, a young man with amnesia and the mysterious ability to transform into a sheep-like monster, as he searches for a way for humans and monsters to coexist. Thrilling Action RPG Combat Master swords, spears, hammers, and even magic to take on powerful monsters. Recruit townsfolk and monsters alike to explore treacherous dungeons. Sow the Seeds of Your New Life Relax after a long day of adventuring with activities including farming, fishing, and more. Discover the many varieties of Magic Seeds, which grow into strange crops that aid in your adventure in fun and exciting ways! Find That Special Someone Meet 11 lovely bachelorettes, the most in series history! Learn more about them through daily conversations and quests, fall in love, then pop the question and get married. Before you know it, you'll have a wonderful family to join in on your adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: is a remake/enhanced port/what have you of  for Nintendo DS. It’s a farming sim RPG, where you farm, combat, and converse with unique residents of Sharance village.I want to mostly focus this review on how well it does as a subsequent significant rerelease of the original DS game. Which, in summary, good enough but could’ve been better.-The game performs better than the DS original, which is an obvious improvement. That version struggled to maintain a consistent framerate around other entities. Modern PCs and Nintendo Switch are up to the task.-The graphics are also obviously improved. And unlike , they are better on a technical side AND artistically. I think the devs took the criticism of simple upscales to heart and made an effort to make them more appealing (granted, upscaling DS assets wouldn’t cut it as much as 3DS ones). The item sprites are redrawn or at least updated enough to be more recognizable and actually look quite good. The models are also greatly improved, the human characters look nice, and monsters, I think for the most part they use the same designs as those from . Only backgrounds seem to remain AI upscaled. Still, I applaud the effort.-You can skip crafting animations, which greatly speeds up the process (especially if you’re someone who tries to brute force a 10% chance item).-The dashing is now mapped to a separate button instead of requiring to double-tap a direction, which is far more convenient.-Upgraded material box and fridge have greatly expanded storage capacity. Great for item hoarders.-You can change language options (text/voice acting) in case you are curious how original Japanese VO sounds like, a feature since .-All additions from the previous “Special” re-release: Newlywed Mode, Another Episode DLC, Hell difficulty, more than 2 save slots.-The English script and voice acting have been completely redone, which is understandable, since the original was published by Natsume and that original work is likely in their basement somewhere, restrained by copyright issues. I heard that that script did have some issues/mistranslations, so this new translation is probably more accurate (they did keep all the old character names like how Chocolat is now Colette). As for the voice acting itself, I honestly think that some of the new voice lines tend to lack exaggerated emotion compared to the originals… but maybe I’m just being nostalgic and find the old VO charming. Of course, you can just change it to Japanese if you wanted. Or don’t. It’s your choice.-This game does NOT include analog control. You’re stuck with d-pad movement even when using a stick, it sounds like a no-brainer change, it’s baffling why it’s not present. The thing is, the original DID have analog control… if you used the touch screen. Highly doubt you did, but it was always there, in the dark corner, saying nothing. They could’ve mapped that analog movement onto a stick, but they didn’t. But even if the original didn’t have it… c’mon, it’s such an obvious missed opportunity.-This game does NOT fix clunky movement that was in the original. You have a slight slip to your movement, like you carry enough forward momentum instead of stopping dead in the tracks, which can make the controls frustrating early on (I had to re-learn this after not playing original game for a long while).-The game does NOT include multiplayer functionality from the original (going through Sharance Mazes (randomized dungeons) with other players). Personally I don't think it's that big a deal, but it would've been neat to try it out with others over the internet, at least for the novelty of it.-The game does NOT adjust stat displays. In the game, stats like vitality, inteligence, etc. are capped at 999... but only visually, they keep progressing beyond that number up to a maximum of unsigned integer - 65 535. Another basic adjustement that this re-release utterly misses.-The game does NOT include more quality of life changes, mostly from the future entries. This is a “brand new” game, released after  and , available on the same platforms, and is a mechanical step backwards. Makes sense if you’re playing originals back to back, not so much here. Some of these include Escape spell being a separate button like in , better item storage (stashing an item makes it take its own slot instead of adding it on top of an existing one, e.g. you stash 2 iron and there’s already a 7 iron stack. Instead of adding on top of that stack, the 2 iron will take its own slot) and “Shipped” indicator for those looking for 100% ship all the items.-Digital Deluxe Edition is legitimately overpriced (it can be argued the base game is overpriced in itself). You pay 10 extra dollars for……………….. a swimsuit toggle. How is this enticing? Sure, it’s a very fan-service-y DLC, however, you didn’t have to pay extra for it when pre-ordering  on Nintendo Switch. That’s right, it was just a small bonus, for fans that haven’t been served in years. It was a nice little bonus, and now it’s whopping TEN DOLLARS??? Are you really going to pay for that? Freak.-Credits don’t include original DS staff, which is really lame. Shouldn’t it be standard to include original credits? They worked hard on the original, y’know. This game isn’t even developed by Hakama, the new crew behind  and  which includes some of the original staff, like the series director, Yoshifumi Hashimoto. It’s by… Three Rings Inc. (and I saw some IREM in there). I think they were handed a checklist of how to make a “Special” re-release, which could explain it’s faithfulness… but I dunno. Just food for thought.Overall, I think this is a solid way to experience the original. It’s accessible, has some new content, great new visuals and a few improvements, but I can’t help but feel disappointed by the missed opportunities for even more improvement, I think it could've been better, as it is, it's faithful to a fault. Of course, it also could’ve been worse, it could’ve been riddled with issues that weren’t there before (say hello to ). That being said... PLEASE, I hope the pontential  and  and those two non-numbered entries almost no one talks about will have better mechanical treatments, or they'll end up being underwhelming re-releases.But, alright, what if you have never played a single Rune Factory game and this is going to be your first? How is it on its own? It’s… pretty good! It’s the first (numbered) entry to introduce fast paced gameplay, and it’s great. The characters are very unique and fun, the writing is, in my opinion, the funniest out of all entries, which makes this game stand out. The music is great, it has some of the most memorable tunes that I remember for a long while after putting the game off. It’s a little lacking in terms of content and its story is short compared to its successors, but it’s still a quality game with a decent about of things to do. Like most fans, I would still recommend  since that game offers much more, but you can’t go wrong with this one. It’s simply a great game.(Edited after 100% completion, added a couple more negative points and edited some other parts)

_childDocuments_.review: I think I'm one of the odd ones out here, but I really like this game better than Rune Factory 4. I have no idea why 4 never clicked with me after trying it multiple times, but this game does. I'm hooked. I was never able to play this as a kid on the DS so I went in blind here and have really been enjoying it. I think maybe I like this one a lot better than the others because of it's simplicity and for some reason the graphics are better than 4 too, even though that one was remastered as well.See, I like farming games but I tend to get bored with them after awhile because the main focus is on well, farming and animals and it's always the same thing over and over again after awhile. I love me some combat and fantasy in games too and this really scratches that itch. I enjoy the balance between the two here. However, the inventory space is rough and the UI is a bit clunky, but it's something I got used to pretty quickly. The story is good too, and I like the relationship building. I enjoy learning more about the characters and really get a kick out of Sofia and Sherman's way of speaking. It throws me off every time even though I know what they mean, lol.I've not experienced any bugs or crashing and it works great on the Steam Deck right out of the box. I prefer to play using a controller because the keys are a bit weird and wonky, but I assume you can rebind them if you wanted to, it's not something I've tried though. _childDocuments_.review: Finally, Stardew Valley delusionists don't have a leg to stand on. This is the pinnacle of Farming Life Sim, at long last on PC.Get lost women, no one can stop me from farming now!I mean, what are the odds I won't find love here either?It's like if Harvest Moon, Zelda and Pokemon was just one game.My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like Harvest Moon with blackjack and hookers.This one is definitely for nostalgia or for all the Raven bros out there.Rune Factory 3 finally got released on Steam. If you like Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon, let me convince you why, in my humble and extremely biased opinion, RF3 is a peak rpg farming sim game. Rune Factory 3 is a 'fantasy harvest moon' with a focus on both farming and action hack and slash combat. Ever wanted Stardew Valley's combat to be smoother? Well boy do I have a game for you! There are a bunch of different weapon types with elemental magic too! The dungeons are fun and the combat is super satistying. At its core, Rune Factory 3 Special maintains the elements of the original fans know and love, but doesn't do a lot to innovate beyond its graphics. I'm LOVING this remaster though. Still the same amazing game, but with way better graphics and better controls. Seeing some of these characters again after so long felt like meeting an old friend as well. The characters and story are so endearing and the amnesia just never gets old!The combat is fun and there is actual depth to the farming with soil quality and crop level. And so much stuff to do. I remember that I tried replaying Stardew Valley a bit after this one and got bored very fast, given the strange day-to-day pacing that game has, specially compared to RF3.It was one of the games I loved the most when I was younger! People complain about the lack of QOL like only being able to take one quest at a time or having to wait a day to get money from selling things, but I personally think it plays into the theme of RF3, which is that you should take it easy. There's always a tomorrow and you don't have to be in such a rush to get everything done. I dislike it when JRPGs force a million quests on you so in a way I like RF3's system better. At the risk of sounding like an old man, it reminds me of a time when games were simpler and had more effort and time put into them, like how the entire world is one big painting! RF3 may seem more simpler compared to the others in the series, but thats what I liked about it! Its much easier in terms of crafting as well. Storywise and character wise are also nice. In fact I think it has the strongest plot of the series and I liked that my farm (and house) was inside a tree! Also each of the bachelorettes is unique and lovable.It does have one of the largest bachelorette casts in the series at 11 candidates, but it also lacks a female protagonist you can play. Dating a bachelorette is much easier to start in RF3 as it's based on doing quests from a bulletin board, which are in turned determined by your friendship level (FP) with the townsfolk. FP also seems to increase faster than in RF5, which is a good thing because getting married is required to unlock the final dungeon in RF3S.Overall Rune Factory 3 Special is a great port of an already great game and I am glad that we are getting more of this series on PC. I loved this game then and I still love it now! It added so many great quality of life features and just felt so good to play. The characters felt more alive than in any Rune Factory or Harvest Moon game before, and the world and story were so cool. Every aspect of this game is great and has many features that they didn’t bring out again fully in the future Rune factory series. Things like perfume, request boards with different requests in it, the various magical seeds, etc. This might actually be my favorite Rune Factory to this day. I'm so happy this game got a re-release like thispersonally, and I urge you if you’re even remotely interested to give it a chance and try it out. I assure you, you won’t regret it.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ A much better port than RF4 Special. The assets all look properly HD this time, and the colors really pop. Everything just looks a LOT better than in RF4 Special. + Great gameplay. Not the best yet, as RF4 takes the crown for that, but RF3 was when Marvelous really ironed out most of the kinks with the RF formula. The franchise truly hit its stride with RF3, and the gameplay is more polished, addicting, and fast paced than both previous entries. + RF3 is my favorite RF game out of them all purely because of the characters. They are all just instant classics - the Pia + Sakuya dynamic duo, Raven and Gaius, Karina, Sofia, and Raven, Colette and Marian, etc... Notice how I listed them all in groups. This is because not only are they all interesting and fun characters on their own, they have amazing chemistry and pre-established relationships with one another. You don't just get to know them as people but also as groups, and this is what makes this community feel so real and alive to me. The requests and story events also put you at the center of this community very quickly, and you instantly hit it off with everyone. In RF4 and 5, it took me a while to begin to like just a few of the characters - not even romantically, mind you, but just as characters. In RF3, it was love at first sight like 5 times in a row. I genuinely looked forward to talking to each character every game day to see what witty remarks or wacky hijinks they had to offer, and that is what makes this game magical. + The pace of this game felt a lot faster than in RF4. You get character events much faster, you build friendship points much faster, and you can finish the entire story within Spring and Summer of year 1. This may be a negative for some, but to me, I liked this. It let me experience the best the game had to offer almost right away. Combat especially feels a lot faster than in RF4. This is because they let you loose with almost all of the rune abilities, magic, and high level weapons literally half an hour into the game, and if you know which ones to get, you come right out of the gate feeling like fantasy John Wick.Cons:- Less QoL improvements compared to RF4. I didn't expect them to actually add any QoL changes in this port, but going back to RF3 from RF4 is a bit rough in places. However, this is a minor complaint compared to how good the characters, gameplay, and atmosphere of this game is. - Newlywed mode is nice, but the Live2D models used in this mode are the stuff of nightmares. What did they do to the girls? Their Live2D movements are so stiff, so unnatural, and so awkward. I'd have vastly preferred that they just kept using the girls' static portraits that we've gotten used to throughout the entirety of the game. Again, this is a short optional mode, so it doesn't really affect the experience of the main game.- The story is... serviceable. RF games aren't really known to have epic, peak fiction stories or anything, but RF3's story felt a bit undercooked. The final leg of the story in particular was shoehorned in and unnecessary. I'd say the real story here are the ones you make with the people of Sharance, as they are the ones that make this game the most fun for me.TLDR: 9/10Depending on who you ask, RF3 is either the 2nd best or the best game in the franchise. To me, it is the best, with RF4 coming in close behind. I played it once as a child, and now, I come back to it as a manchild. I am pleasantly surprised to say that it has aged amazingly, and you should definitely play it to see what makes Rune Factory such an charming and addicting series for weebs and Harvest Moon fans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually speaking, Rune Factory 3 Special got a much better treatment than Rune Factory 4 Special did. This time the UI and 2D sprites also got major resolution improvements (instead of sloppy filters), making for a much, much better experience. It would've been amazing to see the backgrounds get redrawn, but they are not as bad as on RF4S. Overall, this is the best looking isometric Rune Factory game ever.However, just as it goes with most re-releases, it's not perfect. The script and dub cast changes are considerable drawbacks to a lot of people who played the original game, and even for those who didn't, there will be an underlying feeling of not getting the same experience people did back in the day. I'll still give it a recommendation because I think they did a really good job enhancing the graphics. Still, there'd be much more value to it if they added new content/features and kept the original intro, scripts, and dub cast people love.

_childDocuments_.review: A Nostalgic Trip with Some Thorny Thorns! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Rune Factory 3 Special is a game that straddles the line between nostalgia and modern gaming expectations. As a remastered version of a classic Nintendo DS title, it offers a chance for returning players to relive the magic of the past. However, newcomers might find themselves wondering if it's worth diving into this particular entry of the series, especially with the recent release of Rune Factory 4 Special on Steam, which offers a more comprehensive experience.One of the standout features of Rune Factory 3 Special is its charming blend of RPG and life-simulation elements. Players take on the role of Micah, a half-human, half-wooly protagonist, who must navigate a world where humans and monsters coexist. The game offers an engaging mix of farming, combat, and social interactions. The addition of a Hell difficulty level provides a challenging experience for seasoned players, while the Newlywed Mode adds replay value with post-marriage adventures.While the game's core mechanics remain faithful to the original DS version, it does show its age in certain areas. The lack of quality-of-life improvements from later titles in the series, like Rune Factory 4, is a noticeable drawback. The absence of features such as dedicated teleport keybinds and the limited monster barn can be frustrating for those accustomed to the convenience of newer entries.Rune Factory 3 Special seems tailored primarily to a specific audience: those who cherished the original DS version in their youth. For these players, the faithful recreation of mechanics and the nostalgic trip might be worth the higher price point. However, for newcomers, it's hard not to recommend Rune Factory 4 Special, which offers a more polished and comprehensive experience at a lower cost.The dialogue and voice acting changes have been a point of contention among fans. While some appreciate the new direction, others feel it doesn't capture the essence of the original. The departure of certain characters from their original voices can be jarring, affecting the overall immersion.On the technical front, the game performs admirably, with no major issues reported. This is a significant improvement compared to some other ports of the series. However, players might find the keyboard and mouse controls less than optimal, making a gamepad a more desirable choice for gameplay.In conclusion, Rune Factory 3 Special offers a delightful return to a beloved title from the past, complete with all its quirks and charms. Nostalgic players are likely to enjoy the faithful recreation of the original experience, despite some of the technical shortcomings and voice acting changes. However, for those new to the series or seeking a more refined gameplay experience, Rune Factory 4 Special might be the better choice. In the end, Rune Factory 3 Special is a trip down memory lane, with a few thorns that remind us that gaming has come a long way since its original release.Rating : 7/10 for newcomers, 9/10 for returning playersInterested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great story and characters. - I played RF4 first and honestly, I enjoyed this game way more. Farming is more streamlined with you only having to manage  one large farm rather that 5 smaller ones in RF4. Similarly, managing your pets is also more streamlined with only 1 big upgradable monster barn, not 2 barns for each of your 5 barns like in RF4. Graphically, this game also seems more polished, maybe because this is a remaster while RF4 seems to be more of a port.  - Thankfully, this game did not have the god-awful "Town Events" of RF4 and potential love interests give you "requests" based on your relationship level instead.Cons:- Some of the mini-games during the festivals seem unfair. NPCs participating in the games don't really compete against you but already have a per-determined "points" that you need to beat to win.- Not that many bosses. I think RF4 had more that twice the bosses.Overall, 8/10. Enjoyed this much more that RF4. Please remaster Rune Factory 1 & 2 as well. Carmen best girl.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often review games, but this one feels like it's been flying under the radar for most people, and it absolutely deserves more attention, so here's my attempt at spreading positive word of mouth.If you're a Rune Factory fan, you're likely already aware that this game and Rune Factory 4 are widely considered to be the golden children (woolies?) of the franchise. That is for a damn good reason. And if you're not already a Rune Factory fan, I strongly recommend you take a chance and play 3 and/or 4 because they are some of my favorite games of all time. Much like Final Fantasy, each Rune Factory is a self contained story with new characters, and doesn't require you to have played any previous games. So if you enjoy farming games, dating sims, or dungeon delving RPG's, I urge you to play one of these wonderful games, and I guarantee you'll find something to love.While lacking a few of the modernized features that later Rune Factory games added, Rune Factory 3 has plenty of it's own unique aspects that set it apart from other entries, and absolutely earns it's place as one of the best. It may lack some quality of life features like not consuming recipe bread if there are no recipes you can learn, or missing the more refined leveling, crafting, and upgrading systems later games have, but it makes up for that with some quality of life aspects that disappeared in later games, and in my opinion shouldn't have. For instance, access to new seeds is much easier, plants that notoriously take ridiculously long to grow in later games will grow a good bit quicker in this, leveling crafting is much smoother and less of a grind, and using higher level upgrade materials isn't nearly as hard. It also has features that are sorely missed in later games, the best of which, in my opinion, are the magic seeds.Much like any other Rune Factory, the characters in this are loveable, colorful, and full of fun quirks and stories, and it makes choosing a love interest incredibly difficult. Almost 80 hours in, and I still haven't been able to pick between Marian, Pia, and Daria. The story is deeper than most Rune Factory games, with mature themes like racism and prejudice, as well as good lessons like accepting others and letting go of the past. This is the game where combat truly began to shine, and so it's every bit as fun as later games. It's also a fair bit more difficult than other entries, partially due to the slower progression of stat leveling, but it never feels unfair or ridiculous, and various means of upgrading and empowering yourself are always available. The crafting and upgrading systems are fun and in depth, albeit not quite as intricate as later entries. Still, I felt that it was also friendlier and more approachable in this one. Character events also function differently from later entries, and are typically directly tied to requests you take from the request board or mailbox, and as such it's easier to do whatever character events you want thanks to the lack of RNG involved in it. And I should mention that this game has, in my opinion, the prettiest town of any Rune Factory, as well as the most interesting and creative housing.Overall, while this game may suffer a bit from it's age, it still absolutely holds up, and even trumps some aspects of later games, earning it the right to be played just as much as more modern entries. It's great story, loveable characters, unique systems, and ever present addictive farming, fighting, and crafting, makes Rune Factory 3 a must play for any fans of the genre, or fans of the franchise. I'd give it a solid 9 out of 10, and I sincerely hope more people give this gem of a game the chance it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was one of my all-time favorites from my childhood. I've sunk far too many hours in to it, and replayed it plenty of times. It's one of the few games I've actually 100%'d.To try and give it a fair review, I'm comparing it against the original, rather than as a stand alone game on a 1-10, with 5 being equal to the original, 10 being the best example of how a remake should be done, and 1 being so bad, that it's inexcusable.Graphics: 10/10. This is how graphics should be done in a remake. They are gorgeous, they kept the same aesthetic as the original and just made everything better. It really looks like they took their time to try and capture the same feel as the original, but with a much higher quality. Beautifully done.Gameplay: 4/10. Most of the gameplay is unchanged as far as I can tell, the only difference I've noticed is that when picking things up, sometimes your character will pick two of the same item up at once, which sounds like it'd be great and save a bit of time, but it actually causes him to lag or delay a bit before picking up the next item for some reason, and ends up slowing it down. Music: 6/10. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt. It's probably better than the original, but I can't hear a difference.Voices: 1/10. So bad. All of them. It's awful. When I first heard them, I hoped it was just a bug, but no; the voices sound like someone tried to do an impression of the original and then increased the pitch on everyone to make them sound artificially childlike? And what the heck did they do to Daria?! She used to shout "Rainbow!" With such mirth and confidence. Now it sounds like she's trying to seduce it? It's just creepy and uncomfortable. I genuinely wanted to stop playing because the voices were so terrible.Dialogue: 2/10. The whole game feels like they took the original text, and then rewrote it like a kid writing a report without plagiarizing. Everything's changed a little bit, just enough to be noticeable if you've played the original. For the most part that's not bad, it feels weird at times that you've got a transform belt instead of a transform spell? Just like... why? But the reason this rates so low is because they took out all negativity or hostility. Characters' personalities should have good and bad. When people are stressed, they say harsh things, it doesn't make them bad, it's what makes them human, and too many developers remove that humanity, and instead make the characters these always happy never upset dolls. I would understand if it was just removing Sofia threatening to beat you with a rusty hoe, or wanting to 'Drag you out in to the wilds to let the monsters have their way with you. Repeatedly' (Real quote from the original) But they didn't have to take away all the opposite speak shenanigans. They really gutted her, and it's sad. They also changed the option of getting Cologne to Perfume? Do kids not know what cologne is? Did they think that was necessary, or was it to make the game more woke?Overall: 3/10. It's not unplayable, the graphics are beautiful, but that's really the only thing they did right, and I hate to say it because the game isn't terrible, it's just...bad. Worse than the original in too many ways. I regret buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic remaster with splendidly realized character designs and appealing gameplay. The controls are fantastic as is performance on my sometimes-finicky computer. RF3 is very akin to RF4 so far as visual style, a soft pastel color palette and appealing pixel graphics. The characters are expressive and lots of fun to get to know. The dialogue changes that occur from day-to-day and across events through time are impressively numerous though Rune Factory 4 still exceeds in this area. There are very few farming sims that have as large a script as RF4, and RF3 comes close to comparing. Between the three Rune Factory games on Steam I would recommend 4S, 3S, and 5 in that order. All are worthwhile.The combat in 3S is not as friendly as it could be in the beginning. High difficulty and awkward controls. A couple weeks through, I was able to afford some more useful equipment and I'm more comfortable with its systems. The persistent hunt for better gear and RNG are key to success in this area. The dungeon areas are enjoyable and the enemy variety is great.The festivals, collectibles, unique character events, all of these are stand-out features that I enjoy a lot. The fishing mini-game is also fun. There is always something to do and the gameplay loop is rewarding, lots to play toward and all of it feels light and relaxing. Rune Factory 3 is in what I'd consider an upper tier of farming sims out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't powered through to end game yet and in fact hit a stopping point for the story (possibly a timegate) but I figured 20 something hours is probably a fair time to review.I think this is good but doesn't have the quality of life you would expect from later rune factory games. This is a visual upgrade to a ds game, I haven't played the original for a direct comparison, but the models definitely look really good, and the UI is crisp. I think they put more effort into the upgrade than they did with 4, but I feel like they probably didn't touch the core game at all.The characters and town is nice. I think the characters are all charming and have a lot of work put into them, and this is the only one where I was split between like three bachelorettes. On that note, you can only play male and romance the women, so it's a lot more restrictive on the sim life front than the other Rune Factory or Story of Seasons offerings on store, but there is actually a plot reason for this and they have relevance to the story, so I suppose you can view it as quality over quantity, but they still have all the cute boys as villagers so I'm sure a lot of the audience of this game was pretty bummed about it.You cannot immediately grow anything out of season, and item management is a lot more tedious.  I think normal story of seasons games can get a pass for this because they're juggling a lot less, but it kinda gets under my skin in this? There is a metric ton of inventory management in these games. I wish they implemented the tabbed inventory and the ability to pull up the inventory at the shipping bin the same way it is in 4 and 5.Maybe late game will wow me, but I recommend this game on sale. Rune Factory 4 costs less, and much more fully featured in the quality of life, romance and farming aspects. 5 is less and while some consider it a weaker entry, it still retains a lot of the basic quality of life that 4 had, as well as letting you experience it from a more intimate angle. I recommend getting 4 or 5 first if you don't have them.

_childDocuments_.review: RUNE FACTORY 2!!! HUH? 3??? THEY MADE A THIRD ONE????It really is just a remake of Rune Factory 3 with minor differences and additions. The biggest thing you'll notice is the dub has changed (I have been playing with the JP dub which is an interesting experience, wow Minori Chihara as Sofia) and the script has been retranslated by XSEED. They did a decent job with this and the characters are still the same as you remember even if the lines are slightly different: Micah is still a sassypants, everybody is still weird in the head with hints of fruity, and Pia is still Pia. The intro song is also different (despite having the game having the same saving jingle using the same melody) and has a new animation thing to go with it. I liked the old one but having a new one to look at is nice too. This is one of my favorite games ever made to the point that before I started RF3S I was starting to get anxious over whether or not it would be true to the game I love so much from over a decade ago, and I'm happy to say it's still the same game. The charm is there, the characters are still there, the bizarre balance is still there. I can recommend it to both new players and people who played the original.

_childDocuments_.review: The best game I've ever played on NDS.I spent days and nights for years in my childhood on NDS. Out of hundreds of games I played, Rune Factory is one of the six games I remember till this day, and I'd rate RF and Pokémon series my top 2 favourites.My childhood began when I discovered a Harvest Moon game on Gameboy Colour. I'd repeatedly farm from day 1 to just about to finish year 1, then the batteries died and there's no save option in the game. I grew into a fan of Japanese RPG when the NDS generation hits. One day I discovered Rune Factory 1.. farming, collecting, bonding with villagers, building a family, forging weapons, feeding animals, making meals, expanding my home, etc. ALL IN ONE. It's like finally I found my One Piece. The game system & design are dream comes true, there's no need to change anything other than maybe some new designs or small adjustments if they want to release new episode etc.I had only played RF1 on NDS and wasn't aware that they released 2,3,4. Luckily I found RF3 on steam and to my surprise the game feels like home to me but better. I got the deluxe version with no regrets because I'm just a huge fan of RF, but honestly it's not worth it as it only added the swimwear mode which I actually prefer the normal clothing for the villagers. _childDocuments_.review: My favorite of the Rune Factory gamesAs a port of a DS game it works well, all of the functionality was preserved but it's quite bare-bones as ports go with the most notable thing being that the original opening song of the game was changed to a new one so we lost the amazingly haunting song that is "HAPPINESS" by Yazumi Kana (which you should go listen to right now if you never have).This game is a farm-simulator RPG that leans heavily into the RPG aspect with multiple weapons, weapon types, spells and level-ups, you have to engage in combat quite frequently to progress in the farm aspect so it is good to know what to expect. I like this game quite a ways more than Rune Factory 4 (although that one would be the best one to start with if you're new) this one is more compact with a shorter story, incredible characters, amazing soundtrack and smooth gameplay with tons of quality of life features.All in all give this game a chance if you're into real time action RPG's and want to be surprised by how in depth and addictive the farming element is.
