_childDocuments_.review: It's good, certainly better than Disgaea 6, but I feel like you can tell the developers are starting to run low on ideas for how to iterate on the series. Item Reincarnation and Item Properties have some interesting ideas, but Jumbification feels a little superfluous. I think the 3D models look alright, but so far I feel like they haven't really capitalized on the benefits of 3D. There's special cutscenes for each skill and spell, but each one isolates the unit and the target in a special cutscene zone. It feels a bit odd and flow-breaking, especially when it's just a basic Heal spell? With full 3D, the camera could be rotated completely freely on maps, but it's still constrained to fixed 90 degrees of rotation, and very limited zooming in and out. There also don't seem to be any map story cutscenes, even though there's a lot more potential with all assets being in 3D?The pricing for the character DLC is a bit high, but the way people are talking about it, you'd think the developers kicked their dog. Runs great on PC and Steam Deck, and being able to seamlessly transfer your save between the two with Cloud Saves is great.Overall, I don't think this game is better than Disgaea 5 Complete, but I don't think it's that much worse either. If you haven't played Disgaea in a while, why not try this one?EDIT: I'll try and update this review as I play more. The more I play the better I feel about it. There are a lot of extra QOL features that make the game experience feel good.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Disgaea 5. I've played it extensively on the Nintendo Switch and still bought ultimate edition for PC which should be an indicator of the quality of the game. This is more like a sequel to Disgaea 5 than it is to Disgaea 6, many mechanics return such as capturing through base, weapon skills and the largest roster of character classes that a Disgaea game has ever launched with.Skip Disgaea 6 unless you're a hardcore fan and go straight to 7 in my opinion, although 6 had good tactical combat during the story it did not hold up at all post-game, but this one shines gloriously in post-game especially with the new item reincarnation/PvP systems and so on.It should be noted that if this is your first time trying a Disgaea game then you should likely not start with this one as it starts with a high difficulty and all the mechanics that have been refined over the years such as reincarnation and demonic intelligence are in full force here along with new mechanics. If you're looking for a good starting point then I would recommend Disgaea 5, then after playing through that and learning everything coming here.Though, this personally does not detract from mine own rating as I've been with the series since the first game, and to finally have a game focused on the fans & niche of the genre with needing to utilize these mechanics we've been given all these years is great.Item Reincarnation alone as a system is worth the new entry, being able to craft (though through an RNG process) an item and outfit it with tons of properties and increase its power and/or even be able to do things like make edible weapons you can eat in an emergency is amazing and adds new depth/strategy to the game in the long-term if you're not a meta chaser. For someone who plays the game and takes their time, this is by far the best Disgaea, there's tons to do and you'll find yourself absorbed for hundreds or even thousands of hours trying out different combinations of things both old and new.10/10 best SRPG returns, again.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Disgaea 2, D4, D5, D6, the DS port of D1 and vaguely watched play of D3. This game feels like a take of the game play of D5 (which is an amazing thing, trust me.) with a story that is marginally better than D5, to the point of which i'd be okay with saying it's on par with D2. Mechanically, the differences between D5 and D7 here are that instead of overloads you get Jumbility and Hell mode. Jumbility for all units, being effective map wide boosters and AoE hits at the cost of your unit being map-large and unable to special. Hell mode being the reason that story characters are good (when one of the "hell modes" is 3 actions in a turn you know it's pretty crazy.) I never really liked the item world before, as it felt too big and too long but in changing it to short bursts of 30 levels instead of 100 for a legendary it feels much less like a slog (at least for me). Due to item traits, you'll still need a similar amount of attempts on an item to get it "Overpowered" but even then, 30 levels is far more digestible than 100 for someone who has a life. The art-style is... not much better than 6, sadly, but that is the price of going 3d models. They're very chibi compared to the art-style of 5 and before, but that's forgivable when everything else is good.So bullet points:Gameplay: Great! Some of the best in the series.Story: Better. 3rd or 4th best in a 7 piece series. You might like it more than I.Graphics: Meh. 3D isn't nearly as charming as the 2D sprites from before and the 3D isn't exactly impressive either.Should you buy it: If you really like big numbers, love strategy rpgs, and don't mind a little bit of grinding to break everything... Go for it! It's a lot of fun. Maybe you'll get really into it and beat a superboss or two. Maybe you'll stare at the "character design" for hours on end. Maybe you'll just play the story and get a chuckle or two. I believe you're likely to get a lot of good out of this one.

_childDocuments_.review: An extreme improvement over Disgaea 6 in essentially every way.Although the PC port is more or less the same as that game (Very good for general PC port standards, and fantastic for in-house Japanese developer standards), there are some issues with the automatic controller option not displaying the right prompts on PlayStation/Nintendo controllers (Probably because they aren't detecting the controller type through SteamInput and as a result it assumes that an Xbox controller is connected), and some weird framerate related issues on the Steam Deck when zooming or when the Steam overlay/menus/popups appears.There's supersampling, FXAA, and TAA as anti-aliasing options, and from what I see, there's very little visual difference between FXAA and TAA, and TAA still has very noticeable shimmering, which makes me wonder if it's even working. The dynamic resolution scaling and upscaling options don't seem to be temporal in nature (They're using rather basic spatial upscaling), so for those wanting better performance on a high resolution display (So the UI looks crisp and clean), 3D rendering is going to look worse than it should.A bit of a shame that there's already a ton of content cut out to be sold as DLC, because if not for that, based on what I've heard from a bunch of different sources, we'd have another game of the year contender (Outside Baldur's Gate 3, Armored Core 3, and HiFi Rush) simply out of merit of it not being a soulless and busted game release lacking expected features (in 2023) and aiming to milk their players completely dry to appease out of touch shareholders. Very few games have released this year that actually fit that criteria. I will at least give NISA some props on the fact that they didn't put deluxe edition content behind a separate paywall that requires buying the game again (like IdeaFactory has been doing as of the past few game releases). At least then, you can buy the rest of the content on a sale or something if you want the complete edition.I currently can't speak for the localization, whether or not it's accurate and true to the original intent, and if there's content removed or changed, but go into it with expectations that NISA pulled a NISA (If there's anything definite in this world, it's that NISA or Nintendo Treehouse are gonna pull some bollocks like they usually do). At least since the game is on PC, someone can make a content restoration/retranslation patch if need be.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think Disgaea 7 represents an improvement in the series and makes a good entry point for people new to the franchise. It's good, colorful fun with an engaging gameplay loop, decent writing, and enough material to fill out 100+ hours of playtime. I definitely enjoyed Disgaea 7 and would recommend it to anyone who enjoyed previous Disgaea games or has an interest in the series. I bought it at full price near release and I don't regret the purchase at all.However, at the time of this writing I just abandoned a third playthrough of the game with the realization that I'll probably never pick this game back up. This is pretty different from other games in the franchise that I've played numerous times and will play many more times -- including Disgaea 6. Disgaea 7 just has too many mobile-game design elements for me to really enjoy grinding up a decent team of characters. The Disgaea franchise really didn't need gacha, foil cards, RNG-based systems, and more useless collectibles; while cutting back on genre-defining mechanics like the Item World, innocents, and unit towers.The writing has improved since Disgaea 6, stepping away from the "just misguided and misunderstood" themes that started with Disgaea 5 and seemed to be turning the franchise into sappy Circle-of-Friends episodes in a Saturday morning cartoon.  "Bad people do bad things" is a pretty basic and trope-filled method of writing, but at least it's easier to do well than the emotional complexity and nuance that D5 and D6 attempted. Disgaea 7 still shoots for some deeper writing with nuance and complexity but it doesn't plaster its attempts all over the place; so when the more emotional writing fails to land, the work as a whole doesn't suffer.Each Disgaea game comes with a special set of systems or mechanics that set it apart from other games in the series. Disgaea 7 introduces Hell Mode and Jumbification, both of which are fun to play with a few times and then you'll probably forget they're even there. Hell Mode suffers from the same flaw as most, if not all, ultimate-move systems: too good to use on trash mobs, not good enough to matter on bosses. Jumbification, on the other hand, is so good the designers made it a pain and a half to actually use except on certain key levels. This leaves Disgaea 7 in an odd place where it doesn't feel very unique as a Disgaea game.

_childDocuments_.review: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless? A Devilishly Exciting Adventure! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless marks the triumphant return of the beloved Disgaea series, offering fans a blend of demon mischief, tactical RPG gameplay, and quirky humor. In this review, we'll delve into the world of Disgaea 7 and explore the various aspects of the game, from its characters and story to its new gameplay features and overall presentation. While this review will highlight the game's strengths, it will also touch on some of its drawbacks to provide a balanced perspective.The game introduces players to the dual protagonists, Fuji and Pirilika, each hailing from opposing belief systems in the demonic realm of Hinomoto. Fuji embodies the Hinomoto Code of Destruction, while Pirilika idolizes the Bushido code of old. This stark contrast in character beliefs promises to deliver amusing interactions and engaging storytelling. The initial impressions from the early stages suggest that Disgaea 7's humor and oddball characters remain true to the series' legacy.Disgaea 7 retains the core gameplay that fans adore while introducing some exciting new features. Jumbification, for instance, allows characters to temporarily transform into giants, adding a strategic layer to battles. The concept of filling the gauge through ally deaths adds depth to the game's tactics. Hell Mode, another addition, offers powerful attacks, with each character charging it differently, diversifying gameplay strategies.One notable change is the increased difficulty level, a response to feedback from Disgaea 6. While this adjustment may appease long-time fans seeking more challenge, it could potentially alienate newcomers to the series. Additionally, the limitations imposed on auto-battle, requiring a finite resource called Poltergas, might disappoint those who enjoyed its convenience in the previous installment.The hospital, where players can heal and unlock items through a 'gacha' mechanic, adds an element of unpredictability to the game. The absence of microtransactions in this system is commendable and promotes a fair gaming experience. The concept of Item Reincarnation, although not personally experienced, promises intriguing gameplay opportunities by allowing players to transform items into unexpected forms, adding a layer of customization and experimentation.Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless exhibits a 3D art style that some players may not prefer. However, the graphics are clear, with well-designed characters and an easily readable user interface. The audio, particularly the English dub, offers an enjoyable experience, although players who prefer the original Japanese voices might miss that option.In conclusion, Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless offers a promising return to the beloved Disgaea series, with its signature humor and quirky characters intact. The introduction of new gameplay features like Jumbification and Hell Mode keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging. However, the increased difficulty level and limitations on auto-battle may polarize the player base, with some welcoming the challenge and others lamenting the loss of convenience.Despite its potential drawbacks, Disgaea 7 appears to be a worthy addition to the series, blending classic elements with innovative features. Fans of tactical RPGs and longtime Disgaea enthusiasts are likely to find this devilishly exciting adventure a welcome addition to their gaming library. As for newcomers, the game's humor and unique gameplay mechanics might just entice them to join in on the chaotic fun of the Netherworld.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of Disgaea since 1, and absolutely loved 5 when it came out in 2015 (for PS4, at the time). After that, we were all pretty sure that Disgaea was done and 5 was a good farewell. So when 6 happened, I was excited! And it was... unfortunate. In addition to the English release initially only being on Switch (which could barely handle its unpleasant jump to full 3D), it eventually hit PC at a super high price tag. Higher than the one people are upset about with this entry.Disgaea 7 is, thankfully, the first proper Disgaea that's happened in 8 years. They fixed the mistakes of straying too far from the formula in 6, yet brought forward and improved several of the improvements. It's Disgaea, so I've only scratched the surface of something I'll undoubtedly get dozens of hours out of, but here are a few stand outs for me:- The 3D has won me over. I LOVE sprites, and one of the first signs of trouble with 6 for me was that the series was doing away with the awesome high-def sprites of 4, D2, and 5. But, the tech has gotten there, and now animations are properly snappy, fun to look at, and characters are detailed enough to feel closer to anime-level than blocky 3D.- QoL features are everywhere, from removing the Chara World (which was, indeed, unfun after the first 30 runs), to finally adding more dispatch groups to organize your team with.- I thought I was going to stick to Japanese, but the English VO is so excellent I've left it on. Fuji, in particular, is a much more fun protagonist than Captain Emo (sorry Killia). Some characters are still grating, but that's kind of an intentional hallmark of Disgaea at this point (Flonne).- The best music in a Disgaea game to date.- The invention and use of the term "Jumbility", which makes me giggle.So far, the missing elements are few, minor, and personal preference. Things like the lack of magichange (though I'm fully aware it didn't have much use) or the inability to put symbols or special characters when naming someone. There are a couple UI hiccups here and there, and I'm not a huge fan of how the Dark Assembly is presented (it actually seems like renaming senators "Sumo Wrestlers" is a translation issue, as they are, in fact, not wrestling).So, amidst all the pitchforks regarding pricing, I'll say that FOR DISGAEA FANS, this is an absolute blast and worth every penny. And, though I don't really want to jump into the arguments over DLC practices, I will say that the game is well made and fully complete without any of the additional things that, frankly, feel mostly there for long time fans. Hopefully the goodness of the game still pulls through and we have a chance at seeing a Disgaea 8.Also, dood.

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus Christ that price. Between that and Disgaea 6 being a dumpster fire, here's a thumbs down on the house.EDIT: This is getting changed to an extremely begrudging thumbs up.  The 3D models are quite ugly. It was a sad change away from the gorgeous and refined spritework of Disgaea 5, but not nearly as bad as Disgaea 6. The levels still look like a bland mess as they've always done, although the Item World feels like a very small selection of similar rooms.The main characters are extremely skin deep with surface level quirks and nothing else to define them, and plough along an extremely well journeyed road of predictable tropes, although this can comfortably apply to every entry in the series.  The plot is the usual fare of anime nonsense and continues to stray ever further from the genuinely touching tale of Disgaea 1.But all this is par for the course, we are here to GRIND, and grind we do. Mechanically, this is the best Disgaea game in the series, a lofty title I previously attributed to Disgaea 5.  A lot of the pain points of grinding are eased away and time sinks that used to be trivial yet irritating to do repeatedly have settled down.  If thoughts of Chara World fill you with bile and vinegar then you'll be glad to know that's gone.  The auto battle system has been refined and also made into something you need to earn by completing real battles.  There are some misses here though: There are two main Gacha systems which are overwhelmingly influential and irritating in their own way.  Firstly, the hospital prizes have been replaced with a gacha which gives enough money to pay for itself alongside top tier equipment for whatever part of the game you're at, however there is a lot of button mashing to keep pulling it, even though you can pull up to 100 at a time, you'll be pulling it hundreds of thousands of times, because it feeds into most systems in the game: It gives money, experience, permanent stat buffs, great equipment, evilities, mana, you name it, you can gacha it. As soon as you have a functional loop to pull the gacha, you will never need to farm EXP, money or mana in battle againThe second big miss is the Item World.  Sadly, each item now only has 30 floors to their item world, but there is reincarnation for items to do it all again.  Sadly, the reincarnation is a gacha pull, both for what the item turns into, and for the properties the item will get.  If you want a particular property on an item, like warping or multi-hit, you can hope to get lucky or do the same 30 item world levels many dozens or hundreds of times.  This can be automated to a degree, but still a major pain since there is no way to move properties around like innocents, so you can feel the pain of seeing an amazing property on a crummy 3-rank item you'll never use.Subclass maxing is also a very manual progress, it must be changed one at a time per character or you waste the class exp you get.  Hard to believe this system is even still here and harder still to believe that it has avoided any quality of life.The GUI has been polished to a great degree, everything just works really well and with a massive returning cast and a nice selection of old and new characters, it feels great to play and grind up to your perfect item world diving, Carnage Baal slaying team.  For that reason, I give the thumbs up, but with the caveat that the game is painful in a lot of ways.  Painfully shallow characters, painfully predictable cliche story, painfully ugly world and models (the bloom will leave you wondering if you missed some graphics settings) and a very painful price to play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I should preface this with the first time I ever heard about the Disgaea series:Early 2016. LUElinks (it doesn't exist). A request from a well-known, actually diagnosed extreme-end-of-the-spectrum autistic and OCD user: "can anyone recommend me a game? Just finished [this obscure pokemon rom hack]"Cue the first response: "Disgaea 5 came out recently"I could practically see the hodge podge of maniacal grins and actual sweat dripping from various palms among the follow up posts."Bro, that's a death sentence, like actually morally wrong to recommend Disgaea in this instance""XFD do it""Maybe dip your toes into Disgaea 1 or 3 first""brb, drafting the copypasta for literally everyone who'll be asking where he disappeared to"You see, when this guy says he finished Pokemon, he didn't *just* finish pokemon. Completing the Pokedex? Catching every shiny? What are you, some kind of amateur? This guy raised or caught one of every pokemon of , of each gender, storing as many copies as needed to cover every type of pokeball to boot. Let me break that down: a level 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, etc charmander, and for each of those levels, one stored in a pokeball, greatball, duskball.... So if you think THAT'S pretty crazy,  throw in shinys. That's who we were dealing with here, and that's just on the raw pokemon-collection side of things. I dare not speak of how he handled stats, HMs, TMs, and berries.Anyway, yeah, the first response was Disgaea 5. This led to hundreds if not thousands of replies running the gamut of moral/ethical efficacy to surprisingly relevant permutation mathematics as could be applied to this one guy "finishing" Disgaea to practical logistics, like if the organization tools available would be granular enough to actually help him keep track of everything past certain extreme points that even slightly more normal people wouldn't bother caring about.Long story short, we never heard from him again. Ever.As for me, that conversation was compelling enough to give Disgaea PC on steam a download and a few tutorial missions, after which I bounced right off. If memory serves, within the first couple hours, I'd been tasked with throw stacking units to reach the end of a stage without actually moving anyone, units that explode when thrown, and where I kinda peaced out were the different colored panels with different effects that could be manipulated and destroyed - simultaneously if done a certain way - by moving around and hitting these matching- and null-colored prisms on the map. Don't get me wrong, FFT is in my top three games of all time, and I have over 120hrs in more than a couple Fire Emblems, but Disgaea was apparently something else entirely.Fast forward to Disgaea 7. I'd been itching for a good jsrpg after years of Fire Emblem kind of dominating the mainstream spotlight. And..... they actually onboard new players at a good pace time around! (Though, to be fair, I'm comparing against my hazy memories of Disgaea PC.) The tutorials and missions ease you in much more gradually and gently, and you aren't pressured to leverage the more esoteric mechanics until way later, when you're naturally compelled to. The story is completely different from the more serious likes of FFT and even Fire Emblem, but just as heartfelt in its own ways, as wacky as the setting is.So I've come to realize that Disgaea is quite like a similarly well-known yet niche series from the stealth genre: Hitman.They both do things just as well as mainstream games in their genres, but they add on a lot (like, an infinite amount) of ways to approach and play the game for any kind of player seeking something "more" from the genre, however they define it for themselves. Both practically beg players to cheese the ever living crap out of them, but they also give players, should they choose to accept them, actual reasons to leverage mechanics in any combination to make the game as challenging or as easygoing as they're comfortable with.It turns out the kind of player who actually seeks out that experience is somewhat rare. I think most can agree that gamers, generally speaking, are perfectly content with being given some static challenge and being tasked with mastering it. Disgaea (and Hitman) can be approached this way, definitely, but players are also presented with all these knobs and buttons to take the genre to these crazy extremes in all kinds of different directions, and that's where people can get overwhelmed. Disgaea 7, in my experience, presents these options in a very palatable way that encourages players to take things at their own pace.In my 60 hour playthrough so far, I've just completed Chapter 8, which is a little over halfway through the main story, with all my units averaging around lvl50, with the challenge bumped up to 1 star in the cheat shop. I've taken many detours to reincarnate several characters back to level 1, a handful of items reincarnated a couple times just to help with leveling new and reincarnated units, and I tweak mana, experience, and currency gain rates as needed to keep pace with the main story. At one point I tried bumping up the difficulty to 2 stars (out of 20) in the cheat shop and got my butt absolutely kicked in a mission from the previous chapter, so, uh, that's one knob to be explored and leveraged....... out of............. a bunch of them. On top of this even passingly familiar presentation of the srpg genre, I have a "Diablo 2 simulator" running in the background, where I have several NPC parties exploring and completing item worlds for me. I get to check in on them every so often, seeing if they picked up rare items, if they beat bosses, and subdued innocents (these arbitrary units that can live in items and can essentially be "captured" and raised to be slotted into other items to raise their stats) to be collected in my farm.So yes, there's a farm for raising and breeding innocents. Their offspring have higher stat caps than the previous generation, and they can breed to produce different types of innocents.Look, Disgaea has a lot going on, both in and out of the traditional srpg mainstays. You're free to engage in as little or as much of it as you want.I wonder how far along that guy's gotten in his complete categorical compendium of Disgaea 5.

_childDocuments_.review: "Back to form" In short:    The Good - Plays like Disgaea 1 - 5 with some nice new features, but ultimately it's more of the same.  - The graphics department did a good job translating the art style and character sprites into 3D character models. - Even though the plot and characters of this series are a bit too weeby for me, they're not as intolerable as Disgaea 5's roster. Which just felt like having my limbs cut off and being forced to crawl through a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CrunchyRoll convention.     The Bad -- Even compared to the older Disgaea titles, the first 2 chapters feel like a bit of a poorly paced slog. The nice visuals do not tide you over the need to grind early, before the item world is available. Meaning you will replay some really tedious maps over and over before you really start the game.  -- The pricing plan. I know some publishers make it really awkward, but not only is it kinda asking for a lot out of the box, .It means I can't recommend this one to those new to the series yet. Just get Disgaea 4 complete on sale. Then come back if you know you're into the game play loop, and hopefully this is on sale with sensible DLC prices There was a long break between 5 and 6, and when I saw the negative feedback for 6 on release, I skipped it.  For Disgaea fans, this is back on form, it also feels like it wasn't a stripped down port with less features than a previous console release. Skipping 6 means I'm not sure which features make a return from that title, but the Juice Bar and Jumbofication add the right kind of balance between streamlining QoL and just straight up kicking out gameplay. Really happy to see a decent Disgaea title for the first time in close to a decade now. Especially when it seemed like 6 wasn't going to ever be made.

Aggressively naive comes to mind, and holier than thou. But worse is that the story coddles and makes the character somehow always right. Her quirks are NOT endearing.• It's got that garbage Japanese story habit of villains needing to be forgiven no matter what. Everyone's got a sob story that apparently excuses everything they do. Who cares if character x, y, and z massacred 1000s each? Who cares if they killed your family? We should think about how they had it tough maybe, and empathize with him. We can understand them! Who cares if they'll do it again, the main characters can reform them! Killing no-name mobs is fine! But killing the worst who happen to have names is bad! And if if a villain gets killed by someone else, the hero party cries for them. "How dare you!? We were just about to save them!" They shout. This is on full blast this game.• Continues following the recent Marvel trend of immediately undermining any potentially serious moment with a joke. Once you realize this, and see it coming every time, it is grating.• The references to other series are great as usual.Gameplay• NIS horribly misstepped with Disgaea 6--completely misunderstanding why fans love it. Those issues are fixed. But the gameplay has some issues ex: The hospital is easily the best way to max out most major resources. You can do it by playing stages, but it's very lacking, and hard to keep doing when you know better• Innocents are useless now. They took the item-locked unique innocent idea from 5, made it worse, and doubled down on it, HARD.Pricing• Worth noting. More expensive than the equivalent on any console. PC got screwed.• The dlc costs more than the game does. They're reused assets, and some units are REALLY good. The dlc are awkwardly grouped to spread the OP units around so you have to buy everything if you want the best skills. There are dlc units that are so good they are mandatory if you want a shot at winning PVP against anyone who knows what they're doing.All in all a decent entry in the series, but NIS is getting more and more slimy. Wait for a sale unless you're impatient to scratch that Disgaea itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 10/24: Beat the game. More thoughts added to original review belowDo I recommend this Disgaea? No. Is it fun enough for long-time fans of the series? Yes. I hadn't bought 6 after hearing the negative feedback so I can't tell you how much better it got, only that it's far worse than 5.This game's progression is overly streamlined. Disgaea games have to find a balance between (A) Being such a grind that it's boring and no one wants to keep playing, and (B) So streamlined that you can fall asleep and beat the game in 2 hours. I've beat the entire game and most postgame, excluding repeating series boss, Where I think this game went wrong:- Item World is more for character level grinding until you get late game and get the best weapons you can. Improvements on items feels incredibly negligble compared to how much characters level up up until things like Exodus (emblem) or Diamond Edge (Sword). Common items are completely worthless as they only have 10 floors.- Item World having a 10-floor cap on all non-rare items. Common items are trash very quickly as a result. You can enhance the rarity, but it makes more sense to get a really strong female thief (Who doubles stealing %) and grab items from Item World or Martial dimension.- Hospital Gacha gives out WAY too strong of gear way too early.- Only being able to vote for stronger items once per chapter arbitrarily limits players into continuing the story just to buy new stuff. Why not just let the player keep voting for better? I have 500k in the bank, please let me use it.- Item World Research. Disgaea 5 let you send your own party members in, which had a fun negative of losing people while they were out. Now it just sends prinnies automatically. Great.- The Main Base is too big for not having anything extra to do? Disgaea 2 would place new chests around the base per chapter just to give you something to do for walking around. There's nothing in this one.- Assembly Votes are horribly broken for cost vs. reward. You can run a vote that costs 50 Mana, fail, and they may ask for some outrageous payment (One vote was about 860 Million HL). But... At that point in the game, my characters were all strong enough to just fight the court instead. If it's 50 Mana, and my whole team can clear the fight, why bother charging 860 Million HL?- Geo Blocks in this game are boring. There used to be a lot more chaos with them, especially in earlier Disgaea item worlds. I've been through probably 500 floors of the Item world and I've run into 1 Invincible block, 1 warp, and 1 Clone. I've probably seen 90+ floors of a colored floor with "None".- Can't tower attack. Why?- Jumbification is overpowered. Do it late in Item World and you can clear 20-50+ levels pretty quick, and the enemies are slow to respond to it. PLUS you can stack 2 charges of Jumbification.- General Shop sucks. Items are always the same until a vote. So you Vote for Better Items -> Buy all new equipment -> Come back after the next vote. There used to be unique "Shop rolls" where you could just re-enter the store to see if anything new showed up.- The amount of items available doesn't scale well. You drop off really early, and the final story boss has negligible amount of health- Quests that result in a Secret Scroll reward are a disaster of item management. Not only do they give you a repeating, endless supply of mana, but they're annoying to deal with in general; They consistently reappear in the quest list after you use the scroll.- The gap between Story + Post-Game Content is downright malicious. Minimal spoilers, I cleared the final Story boss in one hit. The Post-Game recurring boss, I couldn't even leave the base panel. Whereas it took me 33 hours to beat the core game, one post-game boss will probably take me another hundred to get anywhere close.

_childDocuments_.review: Feel like I can weigh in on Disgaea 7 now that I've cleared postlude, minus carnage baal and have played enough to get a good feel of all the systems in the game.It's certainly better than 6, but that's also not a high bar to clear. More generics, a few of which return from D1 or 3 surprisingly, the story and it's characters I found more entertaining than 6, but opinions may vary. the new Jumbify mechanic adds some new possibilities with strategies, but the AI will usually counter with it the moment you use it as well, and isn't bound by duration like the players is, so you usually have to deal with removing their jumbify effect so it doesn't interfere with your plans.Hell Mode is basically revenge mode but instead of ally kills/deaths charging it each characters hell mode charges differently, personally the charge is slow enough that I ended most fights before it was even an option and there's nothing like D5's Revenge Booster Innocent to help charge you up for a fight.I personally feel like map design is a bit weak this time around, they feel far too large at times, especially with the reworked bonus system usually having a clear within 1-10 turns as the gold item bonus so some times you waste entire turns moving towards enemies, at least before you start getting movement boosting items.Chara world is still gone, but also the rather annoying super reincarnation system from 6 is also gone, with character move/throw/counter boosts coming from bills in the Dark Assembly so slightly less time consuming than either to get those boosts. The Juice bar returns from 6 and and functions much the same as 6 minus the ability to spend exp on class and weapon mastery disappointingly. The Netherhospital also got some new/reworked mechanics added in to it first being the new gacha rewards which is how you gain certain evilities as well as stat extracts with points for this being obtained from getting healed up at the hospital. The curry shop from 5 also returns in a form here in the form of the wickedhancement system, albeit HEAVILY nerfed compared to what you could do with the curry shop the only things you can do are increase 1 to 3 of the 8 main stats for up to 100 battles, no more gaining billions of hp and sp from carnage elixirs sadly.also the item world has some new features in the form of item reincarnation and also downsized the possible length of an item world from 10 for common 20 for Rare and 30 floors for Legendary, while item reincarnation comes into play once you clear all floors of an item, much like normal reincarnation a percentage of the stats carry over into the items new form, now if that item stays the same type or not is another story as the possible items it'll turn into come from what you have registered in the data shop, but you have an option via item enhancement to ensure you get the same base item. Personally I think still prefer how Disgaea 4 handled item maximization personally, but I do like some of the ideas here.If I have some negatives, one is that I miss all weapons having a 3x3 AoE skill, because to the surprise of no one, Martial 4 is a 3x3 map, which means you're stuck using magic, fists or swords for a 3x3 skill for most units. My second issue is the tedium of subclass mastery and the removal of the ability to use the juice shop to max it out, as it stands now once you hit the stride of leveling one subclass up to max in one battle, you then have to back out of map selection, go into the main menu, select your character, tab over to the subclass menu, and manually cycle to the next given that there's almost twice as many classes this time around, I do wish the game either cycled to the next available un-mastered class or let us use the juice bar for maxing classes because the tedium of going through all those menus builds up.All in all Disgaea 7 is certainly better than it's predecessor but not quite as good as 4 or 5 in my opinion, but still a pretty solid entry for the series and is worthy in it's own right.

_childDocuments_.review: A massive step up from the unfinished failure that was Disgaea 6.   Although nowhere near as good as Disgaea 5, Disgaea 7 is in every way a step in the right direction and is certainly an excellent game overall.   The cast is back to classic Disgaea quality, we have an insane number of playable classes, and the overall writing is as silly and charming as ever.The graphics are still a huge downgrade from 5 (it will clearly still take some time before NIS learns how to make 3D as expressive and detailed as their godly 2d), but they are a big step up from 6.   So expect something like an HD 3DS game, and not like a modern 3D title.   But if you can get past the weak visuals there is a lot to love here,It's a shame the DLC is so overpriced though.  That is (rightly) going to turn some people off  from the get go.Regardless, if you love Disgaea or simply want a SRPG with an invader zim like sense of humor then your money will be well spent here.

_childDocuments_.review: Main campaign and early postgame is quite good. Some QoL improvements have been made, while some changes have made things worse. Particularly the final endgame grind for good items, as well as equipping and stat maxing an entire team is incredibly RNG heavy and mind numbingly tedious. You're looking at potentially hundreds of hours of mindless repition to outfit a whole team.Then you take that team to PvP only to find out that it is full of obviously cheated items and units with stats that are mathematically impossible to have on legit gear and units, and so far nothing has been done against them. On top of that there are frequent connection issues. The entire feature is a real mess.If you can't even have the simplest plausibility checks in your game for an online feature, then do not have such a feature in the first place. The game also clearly does not respect your time or sanity. After this many games, they should really be able to do better. As such I cannot recommend this. At least not full price, wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all i love the Disgaea series and i played everything with the exception of Disgaea 3 becouse i sadly never got my hands on it.Disgaea 7 is a good new entry in the series that gets rid of some problems that Disgaea 6 had (in my opinion) like the lack of classes and a overall lackluster roster of generic characters. The whole game also has a lot of things that can make grinding easier if you can figure them out becouse the game will never tell you but the community has a lot of guides and is very open (at least from what i could experience over the years) so thats not a problem.The 3D models are a lot better than what we had in 6 and even though i still like the 2D models a bit more they are beginning to grow on me. The Main Characters though..... oh god no.... i could somehow like the cast from Disgaea 5 they had their charming points but since Disgaea 6 i pretty much hate most of the Characters and its not even the fault of the Characters themself its becouse the story got so bad that it makes the characters worse as well. Nothing has any meaning anymore and yeah i will never forget the 6 maps that are pretty much copy and paste just becouse they had no ideas at what to do this far in to the story anymore. There even is a copy from a character thats really relevant to the story of Disgaea 5 in the story for Disgaea 7 but its just a comedic relieve that you never get to battle or do anything with its like spitting in the face of D5 players that the game is a joke or at least it felt like that to me. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic entry to the Disgaea series and a massive breath of fresh air after the mid game that was Disgaea 6. There's a lot of negative focus on the DLC prices at the moment, but (while annoying) I can understand that they're trying to bring the series back into a profitable state as it's already more of a niche play for many here in the states. No prior experience with the series is necessary to jump into Disgaea 7 and it's story has returned to the silliness of previous entries such as Disgaea 4, which is great. If you're a fan of wacky humor, silly attacks, and HUGE NUMBERS, you'll find yourself at home with this game. Overall, you can expect around 25-30 hours of gameplay if you only focus on the main quest, but the game really shines in all the extra content available meant to completely break the power levels of your team, and with even minimal use of that content, it can double, triple, and beyond the number of hours you spend in Disgaea. The whole point here is to turn your characters into literal gods if you feel like it, and there's equivalent god-tier characters waiting for you in the end game prepared to wreck your team, so look forward to it! I can't recommend this series enough, and I wish more people knew it existed and gave it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Uses some very old character designs; most of the generic classes hold to their designs from past games which are often more than 15 years old. I'm finally getting some good ones in chapter 6, but the game pales in comparison to earlier installments and does not exploit its flexible geopanel and throwing systems.There is once more a pile of systems that end up less interesting than what Disgaea 4 or 5 have on offer. Magichange is gone. Character ranks have gotten simplified to the point that they are finally superfluous - I personally won't miss them. Levelling items has changed again in a fashion that seems interesting but ultimately won't fix the issues it introduces in postgame, i.e. that everything concentrates on a single powerful character with expensive equipment.The plot is competent even if the script has some weak moments. The format resembles an audio drama, having reduced the visual component to a minimum.Graphics ultimately don't look that good. Characters are fine, but every battle skill will bring its own scene and stage which take you out of the action and the context. It makes it difficult to know which of your units are getting attacked during the enemy phase.

_childDocuments_.review: With fun and fresh new mechanics and gameplay throughout, new and returning players will seriously enjoy this Disgaea. Probably on par or better than Disgaea 5.- Disgaea 7 returns to a proper structure and not over-bloated numbers that Disgaea 6 had. Now players can feel more rewarded for the work, grind, and learning they go through during the game story and post-game.- Skill cutscenes are proper again, units can properly re-learn weapon related skills, and there's no over-simplification from the buff/debuff skills. Now there is less confusion and proper team setups across.- The auto-battle has been overhauled and is balanced. No longer it is needed to win, but rather reward. The Auto-battle turns battles into a puzzle where you have to use the D.I (Disgaea AI/Programming) completely - no player assist. The better you pre-plan your units, the better your rewards for auto-completion. Favouring practice, thought processes, and decision making over Disgaea 6s "Just auto everything."- Juice bar is properly done. No need for terrible D-Merit system for post-game characters. Lots more monster and generic units to make. Categorized/better evilty system. Item world properly stripped down for grind. - The soundtrack, story, and voice-acting was far better than what Disgaea 6 displayed. More unique characters with touching moments and great humor along.- The best hospital reward system overhaul. Turning into a reward machine for better items, extracts, and money. Even though they call it "Evil-Gacha," it is all free and rewards are all balanced, you can't reset game for different things. Replacing the ancient Disgaea hospital system was a great choice.- No magichange, but JUMBO. Creating a new, simple, and very fun field mechanic for bosses and yourself. Giving a field bonus for both sides of the field whether it be an extra attack or more damage. JUMBO units creates some devastating combos and effects. Then the jumbofied unit dealing massive AOE damage to clear things on the map or just the need for massive damage.- Item re-incarnation for even more customized equipment. The introduction to Item properties, you can shift unique elements of various equipments over to weapons or other equipment to have some very strong and unique items to use.- Netherworld HUB elements. Now you can re-visit completed maps as if they were at your base. With more maps for interaction with NPCs, more shops to check out, and great side-quest/challenges to try.- More QOL features for class creation, skill transferring, evilty learning, item management, and overall pace of grinding. It's fun and enjoyable on all aspects.- Amazing battles where numbers don't matter. Sure having a super strong party can help, but there are Carnage fights and certain bosses you need to overcome that isn't purely won by grind. Learning of your evilities and enemy evilities will make you re-think your strategy and plan better. Instead of usual power creep in video games that just "Has more HP and more damage."- The less innocent variety. It's all stat based for items. But at least there's no need to be grinding the Item World over and over for that perfect innocent level you need.- Evility scrolls not showing who learned what. Sometimes you need a party with 10 of the same evility. But applying the scroll doesn't show in the menu who's learned what. But it's just an extra click to check anyways.- No ingame engine cutscenes. It's all done on character arts now. All other Disgaea's use their sprites/models for some scenes but it doesn't impact gameplay. - DLC prices for returning characters. NIS for whatever reason split the characters into different packs (more sale I guess) but none of the characters are really needed. Even for post-game.

_childDocuments_.review: As of the writing of this review I was at around 36h of gameplay and had already finished everything the game has to offer (outside of the uber version of the usual suspect) which for old disgaea standards is a really low time.The game itself has a weak story but enjoyable since the plot itself feels a bit redundant but still has the charm of the usual disgaea plotline, the main issue I felt with this one is that they reused a lot of old tropes, boss battles for no reason during the chapters and there is no clear direction for the characters they just seem to be doing stuff until the plot crashes down and they solve the problem and everything is fine.Gameplay wise the new mechanics are a miss for me: Gigantification makes a lot of clutch times a walk in the park since it fills itself during the mode for some reason and recovers the characters as if it just got out of the base panel (this is felt mainly closer to the end game where some battles are a war of attrition) and hell mode I barely used outside of story battles since the resource takes way too much to fill (it felt like a gimped Revenge mode of D5 for the ones who played it). The removal of bonus bar at the end of each stage felt a weird change but it works really well since most of the time during the game it was impossible to fill the 9 stages.Generic classes are still a bit boring, they increased the number of the ones we have available sure but most of them are just gender changes of already existing ones or returning classes from older tittles, and no Majin class isn't back for some reason so this means generic classes will be supports most of the time because there is a clear downside between them and unique characters.The OST is a banger but sadly short, most of the new music is really good but it's so reused during the game that it starts to be annoying, I am not sure of the OST count on other titles but this game felt really repetitive on that aspect.D.I. is back as expected but this time around is actually well implemented, nothing in the game is done assuming you will be using it and you just end up using it for repetitive tasks while you are missing some pieces for fast farming. Item world feels like a downgrade while it's nice that you can get higher tier items way faster the end goal will be waaay slower than any tittle (outside of D6, but that game assumed you were using DI anyway) and I think in order to mitigate this items overall are useless for all the game content, perhaps if you are aiming for ranked that optimization will make a difference.Post game:Without spoiling anything, I really liked what they did to join the "end game" with the main plot line, was really nice to see it and been a while since they done it. No returning characters is kind of a bummer unless...DLC:Yep you get the older character, as DLC with no voice cutscenes and about 1m long cutscenes for each character and those cut scenes feel way too forced. And as usual DLC characters will have most of the best evilities for min-max or making some parts of the game easier (mostly the curve from the start of post game onto late game) do mind, that they are not needed in order to make a smooth progress.  TL;DR:The game is nice if you are a fan of the Disgaea series or are interested in getting into the series since older titles might be a bit too much, as a strategy RPG I think there are better options in the market even inside the series itself. I think the game is worth the release price tag but 100% I don't recommend getting the DLCs at full price

_childDocuments_.review: I’m currently leaving this as “recommended” as of now, but they better fix these issues soon.Translation is atrocious! Whoever was in charge of localization should get fired. Seriously. As well as the person that’s in charge of quality control (if it’s not the same single person, which considering the lack of quality here I wouldn’t be surprised). I’m just going to give two examples, but there are many. These are just two that are the most “in-your-face.” “Lift” isn’t lift in the menu, but “Litt.” I’m not joking. It’s mentioned as “Lift” everywhere else, except in the menu. You know, the big one that’s seen all the time. Yeah. Last example is the DLC “shop” is broken. You can view everything else in the DLC menu no problem (like the “Apply” menu), but the moment you select the DLC “Store” option nothing pops up. Like, nothing at all. You’re dead. Nothing can be done anymore. You can’t exit the menu that doesn’t exist, you can do nothing at all except stare at the blank menu. I have to leave the game and force close it to get out of the “DLC menu.” Like, seriously??Why wasn’t there a “day one patch” like everywhere else? It’s still Disgaea, but better, so that’s why I’m still recommending it, and I’m confident that these things (and the many more that I didn’t mention) will be fixed, but everyone should be warned that these things exist. Especially the DLC lock-out. That’s super strange and annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game is an improvement from Disgaea 5. I skipped 6, due to the price tag and auto-battler design. The new 3D models are a welcome change and I have found it very odd that a lot of fans in the series want to go back to 2D. The game also supports uncapped framerates and runs pretty well, even on Steam Deck or ROG Ally. Playing the game on my ROG Ally at 120fps in bed on a VRR screen is just great.The story is also as zany as ever, even with the samuria/Japan theme, which I don't care for in a game like this. But the combat is fun, the new mechanics are interesting, and the items/classes are just as good as ever. Lastly, on release, the game and DLC are definitely overpriced. Especially for a niche title like this. It didn't bother me too much to purchase them though, as I spent roughly 100 hours in Disgaea 5. I will definitely get my money's worth on this title.

_childDocuments_.review: People need to chill over the dlc pricing.Is the dlc overpriced? Yes, absolutely. But does not having it detract from the game experience? Absolutely not.Disgaea 7 is a great example of learning from a previous entry's mistakes. Everything that made Disgaea 6 poorly received has either been done away with or re-imagined to better fit into the classic Disgaea gameplay. This is absolutely a top 3 Disgaea game for me, and I have none of the dlc. The thing others don't realize is that the dlc is there for longtime fans who like continually seeing their favorite characters in each new game, but at the end of the day it's just additional content. If you don't like how it's priced don't buy it. This is a $60 game that can provide easily over 100 hours of gameplay.It would be really nice for people to not leave pointless negative reviews on the game base page. If you wish to leave one do it on the actual dlc pages so you don't help discourage potential new buyers from one of the better games in the series. I for one would really love to see ports of 3 and D2, and would love it even more if we got a Disgaea 8. So here's hoping it sells well enough to convince NIS the series is still worth porting.Also as a side note I have tested this game on steam deck and it ran well at the highest graphics. The only concern I had is that when I had it installed on a micro sd the load times were atrocious and it would momentarily freeze every time it tried loading a new asset like a special animation. Once I swapped it over to the internal storage (I have a mid-tier deck) this issue completely vanished.Anyway it is bs that we don't at least get Pleinair (the mascot character!) for free.

What's more, even older generics are back too!+ Tons of features to explore.+ The 3D models still retain that Disgaea charm, even if they aren't HD sprites.+ The cast is mostly fun and the story too. Other features like Sightseeing appear to be replacing them, but I still miss the Skits.- A certain shogun of this game. Really putting the Eww in Ewwdo with this one.Extras:~ Easiest Disgaea game to "break", grinding-wise.~ The Demonic Intelligence system reminds me of Carnage Heart.~ Netherworld Sightseeing should be expanded. I love this feature, but I wanted more from it.~ Valvatorez wrote a chapter of this game.Overall, Disgaea 7 is lots of fun.Doesn't surpass Disgaea 5's gameplay or let alone Disgaea 1's story, but it is still a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: We'll get that DLC debacle outta the way. This game originally came out January for Japanese audiences. They didn't have DLC at launch so they slowly rolled them out. It wouldn't be fair to have a "complete edition" when that audience probably payed for each one as they came out especially since not even a year has passed. People like to compare the DLC situation to 5 when that game was out for 3 years before coming to Steam. You can enjoy this game without DLC. It's really only there if you like legacy characters.Aight now for the review. This game is easily one of my favorites in the franchise. The story is leagues better than whatever they were trying to do in 5. Voice acting is especially good, but there we some audio issues when even if you max the voice and event volume they get REALLY quiet.Gameplay is the usual Disgaea gameplay. You like the typical TRPG style they go for then you're fine. The Jumbo mechanic is pretty interesting. Getting huge, buffing your team, and being able to aoe smack anyone on the map is a nice gimmick. The switch to 3D was jarring (I skipped 6 cause it's garbo.) but I understand why they did it. 2d art is expensive as hell and having every character redrawn from 4 different angles would be excessive each entry. The 3D is fine, but the animations lack a lot of fluidity and kick. Like with 2D your brain fills in the gaps while in 3D you see it as it is. They'll hopefully improve it with time. Item World has been made so that you don't need to climb 100 floors. Good.My only qualms with the game is that they don't have the color customizing from 5 and the fact that Asagi isn't in the game RIP. This game I'd give an 8/10, but if they add Asagi then it'll become 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The best Disgaea game yet!Has one of the best, if not the best stories and characters of all disgaea games, Particularly with Pirilika and Fuji who almost always made me smile with how they interacted.Also has the best gameplay of the disgaea games, very reminiscent of Disgaea 5, With lots of evility combos, builds to optimize, and strategies to utilize. Units are much more hardy in this game compared to other disgaea titles, which makes more strategies impactful since you don't instakill everythingThe new mechanics are really fun, but are a bit rough around the edgesJumbify which makes a unit take up one of the four sides of the map is quite fun, which i was surprised by since i thought it would just be a stat buff like in Pokemon. It gives a symmetric effect to allies and enemies for the duration of being big. My favorite being the martial artist which guarantees counters, thereby making units counter eachother until one dies.The main issue with the mechanic is that the attacks are the same regardless of weapons or spellsThe other mechanic is Item Reincarnation, which allows you to make your perfect item with special properties. Like making a gun that pierces like a spear, or a bow that has increased chance to counter like fist weapons. It's very fun, but unfortunantly the item can, not only rank down when reincarnating, but you also aren't guaranteed to get the same type of item. I've even had some times where of the three options, all three were a rank down and a different item type which is very frustrating

_childDocuments_.review: Not the best in the series but also not the worst. Do you like the basic gameplay loop of Disgaea? They you'll like this. Took me 23 hours to beat the story and you will need to grind probably for chapter 4 but definitely 12. Took me another 23 to level up and beat most of carnage. This can be done much faster if you know what you are doing (I didn't). I also never used the auto battle. ConsThe price but on PC we have just been getting the complete editions years after launch. This time we got the same as everyone else. $105 is outrageous especially for the quality of the stuff you are getting. You can just skip half the DLC battles because none of them are voiced and the story is forgettable. But the DLC characters have the best Evilities to min/max your time investment. I am disgusted in myself for spending the money on it.I skipped 6 so this is my first time seeing the 3D models. They 100% don't look as good as past games and you don't get any scenes involving the characters except the anime 2d now. You get use to the models but the massive bloom on them makes them look way worse than they probably are.The item world is fairly useless now. You get almost all your power from class mastery and juice extracts then Evilities. You can spend tons of time grinding out perfect weapons and traps but you can just get millions of base stats way faster not doing any of that. The systems now revolve around the hospital gotcha and the juice bar if you want to do things more efficiently. It also takes forever to get a mastered class so don't be like me and just switch out once you hit 5 stars and just do the 6th much later 1000x faster when you are stronger.I didn't really care for the story and most of the cast of characters. Although I've heard a lot of people say otherwise so YMMV.The demon intelligence (auto battle) is set up horribly. Instead of just beating a stage and just copying what you did you have to map out confusing stuff. Doing the demon shogi is an exercise in frustration so just look up a guide. I want that hour back trying to unlock carnage.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game. If you're here, it's probably because you like / love Disgaea, like me (and 96% of everyone else here). If not, and this is your first NISA / Disgaea game I still recommend it. That being said:I see a lot of griping about the price. Boo-hoo, too expensive - the company isn't doing too well. Player like me would gladly buy ten copies (if they could) just to keep the company afloat for another release. I'm sure NISA knows this, and some people are pissed about it. But not me. I'd buy this game for 200$, And it's not like I make more than minimum wage here.At any rate, if you're a new or returning player - this game is terrific, but it does have a few crashes and glitches that can be troublesome. The devs are actively working to fix everything, so that's a big plus. Quick break down:Hell mode (aka REVENGE from 5) is good, done better even.Jumbification is... okay. I haven't really used it, and I've beaten the super-secret-super-bosses. And yes, if you know who I'm talking about - it's BOSSES this time. Juice bar returns!Stats have been toned down, no more Rakshasa - which will be missed.I give it an 11/10, soft 12/10. If you're a NISA fan, then what the netherworld are you waiting for dood?! Buy ten copies for all your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Most comments made by other people, I share the same sentiment in. Disgaea 7 is a great game and a step up from 6 with a better cast of characters and uses the 3D models to better effect, but it's still worse then previous entries before it in multiple ways. The price tag for the base game and dlc is not worth it currently and I would suggest playing past entries as they cost less and are all currently on Steam. Disgaea 7 costs too much and really doesn't do anything better then the past entries if we were to exclude 6. Most reviews may mention the jump from 2D to 3D hold the game back, and I agree. It's more appealing in the hub world but during combat it looks less impactful and flashy. Past games are more visually appealing with the 2D format then here. Cutscenes, gameplay, and the level of detail in skills are a lot better then anything shown in disgaea 7. The fact each skill can't be on the map and must have it's own background linked into it shows how restrictive the 3D effects are. Other then the developers at NIS themselves, A large portion of the disgaea fanbase doesn't want this direction and would prefer they go back to the roots of disgaea's writing and 2D sprites.The jumbo-gimmick where you become big is not the reason people bought the game and the 'hell gauge' is just a revamped overload from disgaea 5. Jumbo gets pretty old quick and I found myself rarely using it because it hinders performance (Specifically on the switch port). Again, Disgaea 5's overload provides a better formula and is structured a lot better. Everyone needing to fulfill different conditions to activate this makes it tedious. The item world is made shorter but levels increase faster, which I do appreciate as it makes the system less time consuming but in the long run saving time isn't a complaint that most players wanting to minmax would do anyways.The competitive player versus player mode is for bragging rights only and just like the jumbo-gimmick, i kept ignoring it. In concept it sounds fun and Disgaea RPG did it perfectly, but in disgaea 7 it's completely irrelevant to the experience. It's optional and you don't have to do this, but if you choose to play it you get a rank and that's about it. There isn't any meaningful rewards that make it worth your time.It's story is great and i'd say its one of the better entries, but it's cast (although voice acted well) is still lacking on anything to properly get invested in. The characters from past entries returning as dlc, are  butchered in personality. Some examples come from the earlier entries such as the cast from disgaea 2. Adell for example is portrayed incorrectly as it's forced to have a joke overwrite the best and serious aspects of the character. They may have removed the voice problems from disgaea 5 and make replacements that do a better job, but in return the dialogue written for the characters were made worse. Although some characters are portrayed correctly, they are still a far cry from being perfect.  These dlc packs feels like an obligation more then quality, and the fact they are separated to encourage buying all of them is a understandable but still greedy business tactic. Just like the base game it is overpriced, and considering the complete additions from past games has provided ALL of the dlc onto it without an extra cost, this makes it more pricey and having less quality.I think the game is entertaining on it's own, but if you aren't able to afford the game or don't like certain aspects of the story i'd recommend past entries. If you want the best story and writing, go for disgaea 2. if you want the best gameplay, buy Disgaea 5. Disgaea 7 is the newest entry in the series but is not the best. The 3D direction they are going with this game is more restrictive and unpolished. I love the franchise, but the developers are going in the wrong direction to keep people interested. They are ignoring old territory and making new gimmicks that to put it bluntly, no one cares about. Companies tend to innovate games in order to make them more interesting, however these changes often don't work and come off as faults to the game. For Disgaea 8, just copy 5's formula or wrap all of the games from the past into one package. These 3D models, gimmicks, characters, and most importantly gameplay don't stand on it's own. Disgaea 7 isn't a bad game as it sets out what it wants to do, but it's not the first or best disgaea game to play. Play disgaea 7 and then any 2D entry including sprites from the past, you can see how those four details work and how the jump to 3D really hurt the franchise.Don't buy disgaea 7 unless you are ok with spending the money and want to play the newest entry of disgaea. If this is your first disgaea game or you can't spend the large sums of  money, buy disgaea 1-5 instead. Even at a discount, disgaea 7 will always cost more then the past games and the fact it provides less content is really disappointing. I'd only recommend this entry if you want to complete your collection or just want to see the best of the 3D models they have provided. I wouldn't recommend it for any other reason as you can genuinely have a better experience with other games in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played several Disgaea games, and a very large number of turn-based strategy games.  People who have not played one of these before shouldn't be too concerned about the learning curve, as the tutorials are decent, the mechanics are a little different but RPG vets will adapt, and there are guides and forums if you get stuck.  Yes, the Prinny is supposed to explode if you throw it.  Know that you can spend as much or as little time messing around with it as you like:  fans of customization and trying different builds will enjoy the options, but you don't *have* to sink 100+ hours in, multi-class all the characters, or hit New Game+.  Folks who like story will be okay as long as they don't expect the game to take itself too seriously.People who have played Disgaea before will more or less get what they expect--Assembly, Item World, wacky characters that you can cheese to level 9,999, etc.  It starts a little slowly, but the devs don't hold back  and hide the "known features."  I'm not a completionist; fans of the series would be horrified to learn  that I've never bothered to level a character to 9,999 and I fully expect to be stoned due to this admission.  If I'm *not* stoned to death, I expect I'll be at this title for quite awhile.Something that'll apply to everybody:  I'm used to playing these on a console and a gamepad is STRONGLY recommended for your own sanity.  Edit at 200+ hours:  Yep, still fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: I'm like the one guy who misses the bigger numbers of Disgaea 6, but even so, this game is almost better in every other way. _childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't the best Disgaea game, but I personally like it a lot. However, the DLC is priced too high, and there are less mechanics than 5.I like all of the new mechanics, and to be totally honest I don't feel myself missing any mechanics other than Magichange. Item reincarnation is a fun system, and Jumbification isn't as good as Magichange but it is a nice change of pace after Magichange was in literally 4 main series games.I actually like the visual style of this game, the 3D models actually look good and some of the unique attack animations look nice, the facial animations in particular look really nice in my opinion.The DI system also strikes a nice balance between allowing you to idle like Disgaea 6, but also not mandating it, and giving you a lot of fine control over how your units auto battle. Which is nice for the few people that liked the feel of Disgaea 6, but the general game feel resembles Disgaea 5 a lot more, which is a good thing.5 is the best mechanically, and this one's tied with 4 in my opinion, which is in second place. 4 has a better story and more memorable characters, but I didn't find the characters in this game grating, which is better than 3 and 6. If anyone complains about this game's story please remind them 3 and 6 exist, anything's better than petty daddy issues mcgee and his pathetic one-note sidekick.Not that story is a big part of a Disgaea game anyways, it's all about them mechanics. Here's my ranking of the games mechanically:5 > 7 = 4 = 2 = D2 > 1 > 3 = 6.1 is only as low as it is simply by virtue of just not having the mechanics that were introduced later. 1 is by no means a bad game despite it's low ranking there. That being said, I think all of the other PS2-era NIS games are more interesting than Disgaea 1, which is likely due to the fact that Disgaea 1 is shockingly the most straightforward of them.3 and 6, ARE bad mechanically, and I actually dislike 3 more, but 3 did introduce the evility system so I guess it's slightly better. 3 also introduced Magichange, however, it was added to re-releases of Disgaea 2 and works better in that game. Shame Evilities sucked until Disgaea 4.While unlikely, if this game gets re-priced to a similar price to the others, I would recommend this as a great first Disgaea. While 5 is the best, it actually is so mechanically complex that I've met many people new to the series who struggled to get to grips with all of them. Given series fans like me tend to prefer mechanical complexity, well there's a reason we all like 5 so much.This game is more condensed, but everything here is very well done, so I'd still recommend it.If you're new to the series, play this if it's cheaper than 4 or 5 in the future. If not, play this if you've had your fill of 5.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: Feels a bit like a reboot. Way better than 6, good systems, greatly improved performance/visuals, the post-game/real-game feels a bit more accessible. the map stuff is a bit simplified as well.Still all about breaking the game and figuring out how to use the tools you're given to do so. I love them all (although I've only gone deep on a few and have not played Disgaea D2), but I think this takes the place as the new entryway to Disgaea (previously being 5 complete, for me). Hard to explain if you haven't already been there, but if you have, D7 feels great and is an easy rec.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as Disgaea 5, but fixes almost everything wrong with Disgaea 6. _childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: Longtime fan of the Disgaea series.  This entry is certainly better than the dumpster fire that was 6, but doesn't have the depth of 4 or 5.  Some the old mechanics like geo-panels and innocents are present, but feel like throw-aways in this entry.  Missed opportunities.  The new mechanics for jumbofication and hospital gatcha are not too engaging, but neither are they distracting.  The netherworld is well organized and the user interface has several quality of life improvements that make things like inventory and evility management smoother than in previous entries. Overall, 7 is a good game-- neither the best nor the worst in the series.  It probably was meant to be a starter game for a new generation of players.  As long as NIS builds on this base, I'll happily keep buying Disgaea games.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to give this a positive review because of all the bugs, but it was still enjoyable with all the bugs.I have an older computer at this point and the game would grind to a halt for 30-40 seconds to play animations of novice skills like star fire ice etc. The have been patching it at least. Or attempting to fix some of these problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since the D6 fiasco I was worried about the future of the beloved series, but D7 melted away all the worries.It was the best Disgaea experience I've had since 5, and in some aspect - the best since 1. I think the one thing that the first one exceeded this one is the (super) crazy and fun story, along with the really extraordinary main cast, but the cast here isn't full of PHD either and the story is both funny and engaging.Overall, I've had a blast and once again since D5 - got carried away to min-max (without feeling it as a chore) like a good Disgaea game.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: The quality of life improvements added to this game are amazing and now it's easier than ever to "get everything", which is extremely welcome now that I'm an older fan if the series who can't invest 9,999 hours into the game. It has great characters and is quite streamlined. Only thing I didn't like is that the music has been kind of a downgrade. I hope there will be more content coming (Where's Asagi!?) but I doubt it. Still this is worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

Some things I would like to see improved are re-adding non-stat innocents while keeping the item property system, compromising with the auto battle to not make it worthless by needing fuel probably by just cutting the fuel and instead just letting players use it on cleared levels, bring the juice bar back to its former glory because it's such a pain in the butt to raise class mastery and I feel that it sorta encourages just making a single uber character to solve all your issues.The game is pretty great otherwise, and I would highly recommend it. The story is 8/10. Most of the characters are wonderful and while the constant "Do your worst" insertions in the text might be grating, only two characters have such issues in my opinion, the other being Ceefore, who will say "Ready snort FIYAAAAHH" inorganically in an otherwise serious conversation. If you want my rating for story and mechanics compared to other Disgaeas not including 3 since that is the only I haven't played yet (BRING IT TO STEAM NISA).Story: 2, 1, D2, 4, 7, 6, 5Mechanics: 5, D2, 4, 7, 2, 6, 1

_childDocuments_.review: I started this new installment with some reservations, but it quickly became one of my favorite entries in the Disgaea series. _childDocuments_.review: Good but not greatThe story is alright has some good characters. it feels pretty streamlined and not overly insane on unlocking post game stuff. graphically it looks fgine its not going to win any awards in the graphics department which Disgaea games have always looked 10-15 years behind modern graphics. Gameplay is great and if you like SRPGs like FF tactics or shining force this is for you. The DLC practices in this game are horrid and i mean really bad. Disgaea games in the post game part have always had a bunch of characters to unlock. now they have only a few and none of the characters from previous Disgaea games. Those you will have to pay for and its $7 for a three pack which is a rip off. half of these characters should be in the post game. Etna Laharl, and Flonne have always been post game unlocks now you got to shell out an extra $7. I'd heavily advise waiting for the complete edition when its on sale for $20-$30. If the enxt Disgaea game is like this ill be doing that.Also not a lot of classes to unlock. lots of characters have been cut from this. The new Jumbofication ability feels like a novelty i could have done with out. They would have better off keeping turning monsters into weapons or even merging monsters together.The Item world has been changed now to only 30 levels for a Legendary item instead of 100 and yoiu can just blow through them which is nice and not worry about clearing them. you can reincarnate items and run through them again and make them stronger along with  much easier way of adding bonuses. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who's only played Disgaea 1, 2, and 5 this does scratch the itch I get to play a Disgaea game and I pretty much live in the item world now.
