_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal return to form. This is the comedic power trip I always want from Disgaea.Characters are fun, the story is both funny and structured enough to hold my attention no problem. The mechanics feel rock solid, you have many ways to become overpowered for where you are and they can be used or ignored at your discretion. _childDocuments_.review: Better than Disgaea 6 in pretty much every way. I'm still futzing around with min-maxing in the postgame and I'm really enjoying myself. It also runs perfectly on my desktop and on the Steamdeck, however it does suffer some frame loss over time which is corrected by rebooting the Steamdeck.Pros:-Many returning classes-Monster weapons and Mon-Toss are back-Autobattle is limited in a sensible way and now feels like it enriches the gameplay instead of removing it-Items can be reincarnated and now have random passivesCons:-Many returning classes are alternate gender classes, but no celestial host-Not many returning monster classes, only the Horseman is back from Disgaea 5 for example (RIP Bunny)-Innocents other than the main stats and dual stats are removed due to the random passives on items-No map skits like previous games, no animated opening-Overpriced DLC packs for the characters, all of which are only the most popular. No picks like Metallia, Zetta, or characters like Thursday/Jennifer/Gordon.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge upgrade from 6. Happy NIS realized 99,999 was overkill for the levels, where grinding items, abilities, and proficiency should be the main focus.  Not a fan of the $40 DLC which is too much for some evilities and characters; especially compared to 5 being under $50 which included game + DLC. However complaints aside it seems the rough transition from 2D and 3D has passed and they've been able to focus more on the gameplay, adding more units, and story. The fact we now have 3D models for the series, hopes they do some more spinoffs like a Prinny 3(D).Just like many Disgaea, you can bumrush the mainstory and get humbled by the carnage postgame. Then you grind and bumrush again only to get humbled by some superbosses which actually takes some planning even with overpowered stats. Postgame item world grinding and having my units participate in online ranked battles is a nice way to see the fruits of my labor when the final final final superboss isn't enough. You don't need to play the previous entries to fully enjoy this one so it makes it a good entry, since it's very streamlined. If you did enjoy this one and want something similar, I'd recommend 5 which I consider the Pokemon Emerald of Disgaea.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: Major improvement over 6.  Story was good and game play was great as well. While some people may not like the auto battle I think it was handled in a great way.  You can easily farm item reincarnations by doing an auto battle and repeating it 29 times.  This lets you take items that you have  being researched fully researched so you can reincarnate them to get new properties quickly.  The late game grind is pretty simple and quick once you get a few things set up.  So leveling multiple characters is really easy. Overall I really enjoyed this game.

_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like they took what worked from disgaea 6 and threw away everything else. Auto-battle isn't the entire endgame anymore, and the skip feature makes it so even the parts that are are less annoying. Miss the full in-engine cutscenes of older titles, though, the visual novel style doesn't have the same impact in a lot of scenes. Also, the new hospital reward points gacha being limited to 100 pulls at once means a significant portion of the endgame is auto-mashing the confirm button with steaminput or a keyboard macro.Pricey with all the dlc and it feels really important in endgame so wait for a sale if $100 is too much to swallow, but I paid full price and it was pretty worth it in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless

_childDocuments_.review: Disgaea is Diablo for SRPGs, your constantly getting different gear, going through randomly generate and non-generate maps, and just getting stronger everytime you play.Really fun story. I love the huge giant moves you can do with your characters. The story took me about 20 hours to beat, but I still have so much to play. Really good game. Kind of a Diablo SRPG game.Runs amazing on the Steam Deck, and is a perfect steam deck game if you own one. I been playing the game on the Steam Deck without ANY issues. It just runs. I did notice some frame time dips, but its just here and there, nothing to really complain about. All my buttons and triggers work, everything just works. I think Disgaea, the way it is made, makes it the series the best to play on Steam Deck.Everyone complaining about the DLC are being forgetful. Every modern Disgaea game had DLC (that you had to pay extra for). The only difference this time is that they went up in price like every other game. I don't like paying $100 for the whole game so I didn't.I love the new jumbification system, its neat to see your character get super big and powerful and just one taps everything on the level.The item reincarnation system is very nice. I like how the tree is displayed within the item, so it gives you a sense of what the item was in the beginning to the end of the tree. It is RNG, so sometimes you might not get a better "rank" item, but your stats will always go up regardless, so I think the system is still isn't bad.The Online A.I. Battles is a cool neat little feature, but that is basically it. You just take your characters and fight other people's character but its all just auto fights. It doesn't add much to the game, but its nice to have it I guess. You do get rewards of course, but its the least used feature by me at the moment. (other games did have this feature in some way or another)Netherworld Sightseeing is a new feature where you can visit the map you just played on. By using this feature you can get more quests, and do more more fights for XP. It's basically more ways to get XP, nothing here to make the player mad, only happy.They changed the way how the Demonic Intelligence system works. This is basically the system where the A.I. will play for you (aka auto battles/mobile games). You can adjust how the character will play and everything, there is really a lot of settings. I didn't dip too much into the settings, because at default it seems to work just fine. But you do need Poltergas for auto battles. This can be obtain by doing story levels constantly, very easy to obtain honestly. In the beginning of using this feature you'll have to fast foward through the animations, but eventually the dark assembly will allow you to actually just skip through a whole battle like how some mobile games do it for you. A prompt would come up at the end of one auto battle completed, then it will allow you to skip the battle as many times as you would like. I have no issues with auto battling in this game. I think its pretty balance for the most part. You can't use it in the item world, which I don't know if that is a good thing or a bad thing, because you will spend A LOT of time in there.Max character level in this Disgaea game is 9,999.There have been several different releases of Disgaea and this one does still do team attacks, and lifting of characters on your head. But you cannot do any tower attacks that you can find in Disgaea 5. I don't think it hurts Disgaea 7 not including this feature, it just takes some of the level of complexly out of it, and I guess just makes less ways to play.Hell mode this is another character feature that they pretty much had in other games but just called something else. Not much to say about it other than it does make your character stronger and makes you feel awesome kicking enemies's butts.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is after beating the main story. Day 1 DLC is always such a bummer even if it is for characters from past Disgaea games, and I think the pricing of the DLC is a little too much. As of right now, it's basically $90 USD for all the DLC, which is crazy.Other than that, I think this game is a solid one in the series. It's an improvement over Disgaea 6 but still not as good as Disgaea 5. I miss the pixel art from the older games and I understand that 3D models will probably be cheaper, but I feel it's such a downgrade. The 3D models look like something out of the GameCube era, maybe even earlier than that, which was over 20 years ago. The gameplay is fine and I think they have improved on auto-battles from Disgaea 6. The story is alright, it has it's moments where it's funny and everything but overall it's just alright. Basically, if this isn't your first Disgaea game then I recommend it because you know what you're getting into and I feel it is a return to form after what happened with Disgaea 6. But if you are new to the series I'd recommend buying Disgaea 5 Complete and playing that first then coming and buying Disgaea 7 if you like the gameplay loop and enjoy what the games has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got the vibe of Disgaea 5, but with a few years of QoL features added on top. (Workaround: replace the healing skills category logic with your healing skill of choice to make it work, but less flexible)The missions that replace the bonus gauge give you interesting way to treat the battles as puzzles. It makes each battle different from the last, so I feel much less tempted to always use the same base strategy for everything.I play this for the mechanics, which are solid. The plot... it's very tongue in cheek and contains a lot of references to other pop culture and memes, but it's pushed very close to cringe territory. It's an acquired taste.

_childDocuments_.review: Here after completing the main story.This game almost entirely supports ultrawide 21:9 resolution, but only in Borderless mode. There's very specific parts that are in 16:9, but 99% of the time you'll be enjoying 21:9 fully, from menus, to gameplay, even during VN style scenes of which the background art is in ultrawide resolution. This isn't zoomed in either, but actually more to see. 16:9 during VN scenes actually has some fully opaque letterboxing, while 21:9 has half transparent borders on the sides. I think the borders are there just to help you focus on the center, but it'd be nice to have the option to toggle them.The OST is a banger. Don't skip it.I feel DIsgaea as a series started as a niche, full of wacky jokes aimed at a niche audience, and the main story was practically the B-plot. Tie that with a game that demanded you take steps to grind up your characters, and you got something that I think was not for everybody. The series has improved over time, and I think Disgaea 7 is what lies at the end of the majority of that improvement.The main story is the A-plot fully, and all the jokes serve the main plot to help you relate to the characters and their own involvement. The grind still exists, and yet the game lets you get a feel for things and gradually introduces elements to you to make it all work together at just the right pacing, and you feel rewarded for piecing together the elements. At least for the main story, the grind is more of a puzzle for you to put together, and you're rewarded for it tremendously.All the characters are solid. There's not a single character in the main cast that I felt like ignoring, which unfortunately I can't say for some characters in other DIsgaea games. Even many of the side characters I wanted to join my party and see more of their story, and I'm still hoping I'll see them after the main plot.I think most people skipped Disgaea 6, and I certainly did, so this is the first entry for me and many others in the move to 3D characters. The good thing is that it's actually mostly a good thing. You'll maybe feel jaded about the extreme idle sway animations characters have, but once you get used to it the only real drawback is that almost all, if not all, special attacks transition you into another screen entirely in order to perform the attack, which also makes it confusing for attacks which leave characters in a different spot. There don't seem to be many attacks that move characters as it is this time around, and that's probably why. The bright side is costume support in the form of additional "colors," but I'm not sure this feature really exists beyond DLC. Otherwise it feels like a pretty equal give and take. I'm sure there will be many who will miss the 2D characters, but I think it's possibly a correct step to take.

_childDocuments_.review:
The story of Disgaea 7 is set in a Japanese style netherworld called "Hinomoto Netherworld Cluster," which has been taken away its "Bushido" and is in shambles by the hands of demon admiral Opener.

The odd duo of lone samurai named Fuji and a Hinomoto otaku girl named Piririka set out on a journey spanning all of Hinomoto to obtain the legendary weapons known as the "Seven Blades of Origin" in order to defeat the corrupt Oedo Shogunate.

Can Fuji, Pirika, and the odd balls they meet along the way regain the honorable Hinomoto once more...?

Disgaea is a Strategy RPG set in a netherworld where anything goes.

The story progresses by forming an army with the unique allies you meet on your journey, training them, and going on quests to various locations in the netherworld.

Enjoy creating characters and armies of your own concept, and battles where the damage numbers will go into the tens of millions!

name: Football Manager 2024
detailed_description: Reviews About the Game Step into the shoes of a real boss and write your own football story in Football Manager 2024, the most complete edition in the series yet. Whether you’re a manager who likes to build from the bottom or prefers to chase immediate glory, the perfect challenge awaits. The arrival of the new Meiji Yasuda Insurance Ltd J. League licence unlocks J1 League, J2 League, J3 League for the first time ever, giving you the opportunity to explore new horizons in Japan. Wherever you manage, it's up to you to build a team capable of competing with the world's elite. Game Description Continue your relentless journey to the top of the footballing world by using the new ability to import your existing career from Football Manager 2023. Craft a winning tactical approach, incorporating modern football’s most popular systems and cutting-edge positional innovations to deliver victories on the pitch. Master the transfer market, using new ways to shape your side to cultivate a squad capable of achieving your goals. Level up your players on the training field, developing the mentality and teamwork needed to transform contenders into champions. See your tactical vision come to life on Matchdays, with every game elevated by improvements to ball and player movements. NEW FOR THIS SEASON TRUER FOOTBALL MOTION Enhancements to player animations, ball physics and lighting deliver the most immersive Match Engine in Football Manager history. Move to the cutting edge of football by using the new Inverted Full-Back player role, while more intelligent player rotational movements add more fluidity to every highlight. DOMINATE FROM SET PIECES Make an impact at both ends of the pitch with an overhauled Set Piece Creator. Lean on the expertise of brand-new Set Piece Coaches to develop winning routines in every scenario that will help you to outsmart your rivals. BRACE FOR TRANSFER BATTLES Showcase your squad-building skills in our most refined transfer market yet. You’ll face a trickier battle for talent as your rival opposition managers are now more strategic than ever in their recruitment decision-making. NEW AGENTS TO BUILD A DREAM SQUAD Better shape your perfect squad with the introduction of new Intermediaries that will help you offload surplus players for a cut of the final transfer fee. Additional functionality for existing Agents and the debut of TransferRoom, a football marketplace for transfers in real life, gives you more real-world powered tools than ever to build an elite team and dominate the competition. ELEVATE PERFORMANCES WITH TARGETS Motivate your team to achieve more on and off the field by setting them individual Targets. Whether you’re focusing on goals scored in a season or average training performances, challenge your star players and top prospects to maximise their ability. A HOST MORE ADDITIONS Enjoy greater variety in every career with the arrival of two new game modes. Real World mirrors when players actually joined your club. Your World sets club squads and budgets at the day your career starts, meaning that only players who joined before that date will be in your squad, giving you the opportunity to rewrite your team’s transfer window. Elsewhere, you can look to dominate international management and plan for your country's future with a revamped National Pool that gives you a better overview of the talent at your disposal. Match preparation and briefing meetings deliver you winning insights before each fixture. That’s not all though, with many more changes waiting for you to discover in every career. This version contains information that is still under approval process by rights holders and may contain data that does not, at this time, accurately reflect real world data. For context, some club and player assets may be absent during this version.

_childDocuments_.review: Games like Football Manager 2024 leave me wishing there was a 'meh' category for recommendations.The core gameplay loop is great, but SI know and have been exploiting this in order to release the same buggy game year on year with new paint and database updates. Credit where credit is due: the match engine is the best it has ever looked. Player animations are smooth and natural, with matches feeling inherently exciting and watchable. If this is your make or break feature, dive in. Peel back the curtain and you start to notice serious issues, though. There's a certain frantic and madcap character to the engine's offensive qualities. In October of my first season, I beat Spurs (3-1), Man Utd (7-1), West Ham (7-0), Bournemouth (4-0), and Burnley (7-0). The only disappointment was a (2-2) draw away at Newcastle. In short, you can wrack up dizzying wins in this year's FM, and with frequency. Such riotous explosions of goals are fun, but not exactly realistic. On the other hand, defence feels like a roulette of nightmares. Just when a league title seems to be yours, you'll concede to marked players from vastly inferior teams against the run of play and morale in the 96th minute. A lot. Clearly, someone needs to 'git gud' here - the question is, is it me or the match engine?Injuries are also baffling. My newly purchased, supposedly world class goalkeeper was injured 4 times in separate incidents in a single calendar year. This led to a combined 14 weeks on the sidelines. All of these injuries occurred during matches, twice during Top 4 title race matches (versus Man Utd, Man City). Broken Hand, Fractured Wrist, Bruised Shoulder, Fractured Lower Arm. The cause of each of these injuries? Catching the ball. Meanwhile, players who are literally duct-taped together will petulantly demand to keep playing big matches with high intensity tactics, creating injury spirals.Speaking of player interactions, these are also bonkers. My star striker with two Golden Boots in the previous seasons was called up to an international tournament and therefore missed several weeks at the club. They won the tournament and were celebrated as the continent's best striker. After returning, said striker was burnt out and needed to be rested for a couple of matches. The player responded by threatening to leave the club for 'not getting enough game time'. Then they suddenly forgot how to score goals, as supporters in the Social Feed noted, because they were 'unhappy'.It's incidents like these that raise the rather taboo spectre that FM's AI is sometimes actively working against the human player, as opposed to just simulating some facsimile of a real season of professional football. The jury's out on that, but with top-flight football being difficult enough to compete in, it's frustrating to have to slalom around nonsensical AI behaviour too.Logical aberrations aside, performance is good. I haven't experienced a single crash but I've run into my fair share of touchline tablet substitution bugs, and even some grammar issues in in-game dialog. It's a mature product at this point though, and it should run decently on all types of hardware.My observations might make it seem like I hate the game, but really it's quite a nuanced affair. With a game like this, reviews tend to fall into two camps. Those who review the current game as a whole, or those who are looking at the game as the aggregate sum of changes from the predecessor(s). In the first instance, I'd give FM24 a thumbs up - it's a good game and I expect to play many more hours. In the second instance, I am much less enthusiastic. I haven't played FM since FM21, and I still feel there's not enough change here to warrant a full price purchase. This combined with the incomplete J League licensing (despite deceptively being touted as a headline feature), and legacy bugs leave me with no choice but to leave negative feedback. I'm open to revisiting my review if the promised patches change things sufficiently.

Perfect for both newcomers and dedicated managers looking for another season of tactical mastery.

_childDocuments_.review: Without question, the most complete Football Manager in years. _childDocuments_.review: This year’s iteration is the final of the series before the upcoming major overhaul next year. Whilst changes are deemed “small”, they have had significant positive impact on the general feel of the game. The new set-piece routines are also a great plus for anyone that loves getting hands on with tactical set ups (one I am enjoying!).By far a long, long overdue upgrade to the match engine, but the look, feel and visuals around it are a huge step up. Well done. Definitely not perfect nor AAA grade quality, but a big step up from previous years. If you are looking for FIFA level graphics, turn your attention elsewhere, this is a purely management simulator (and still far cleaner than any competitor products in its category).       • Players underlap/overlap appropriately (no more FB running into Wingers)       • Players understand spacing and no longer bunch up in the past       • Ball movement are more realistic (touches, bouces and dribbling)       • The defender shot blocking issues are resolved (less wild blocking, more penetration)       • Movement looks more natural.       • Flow of movement is very fluid       • Feels more realistic.A very long due (more than) incremental match engine upgrade. Not graphics, but actual AI decisions, variable movements and more.       • You can still find out if VAR ruling before its announced by player celebrations (a premature anti-climax)       • Keeper movement looks a little lacklustre/delayed at times, but this is experienced in other football games as well, so I guess it’s a common difficulty.It’s a finally good update to the series. and it only took up to its final iteration. Match engine and tactics to me are a great upgrade, no UI changes. But things feel smoother and more refined.Despite some people stating large issues, I’ve personally not experienced anything on a new FM24 save.       • I've not had any injury issues       • I've not had "50 shots 0 goals" issues       • Game has run completely smooth for me.For those saying the ME is terrible and they can’t seem to score. Instead of blaming the match engine when majority of others are satisfied with it, maybe look into your own tactical structures, training methods, and team cohesion. The silent majority seem to be fine, and I’ve not had any severe ME issues since FM21. The odd bogey team (Bournemouth and damn Solanke for me) does occur, but nonetheless, everything has been a significant step up this year in the ME.Been playing since fm12, and fm24 is the best one since pre-2020.I'm a sucker for FM and have always loved the game and continue buying it. It’s an amazing time killer. Particularly when you don't need to be glued to your screen to play it.Could I have just downloaded a database update from the workshop for FM23? Yes. I could have also done that for FM19,20,21,22. But I love the game and franchise, no matter how much people claims it stagnated. It has killed thousands of hours for me (this doesn't even include the versions before Steam! or the Offline hours I had on previous iterations).

_childDocuments_.review: FM23 was disappointing, with a big promise midway through of a better match engine in the 2025 edition, so no one had any expectations for FM24’s features to be worth a buy - We were wrong.First headline feature, which by all means, is good news for anyone who wished to continue a save for ages. Personally not something I’ll be using much, as I play thousands of hours, and rarely find myself at the end of the cycle, with a save worth continuing over toward the new game. headline feature score in my eyes.By far the best thing, possibly even the best upgrade from one edition to the next, we ever had. It is extremely surprising to see such a big leap forward, within the match engine here in 2024’s edition, but everything from deflections, players movements, lighting, how the different tactical approaches and player instructions is shown within the engine, is far better than ever, and I can’t understate this enough - If you play on an older version of FM, and wonder if 24 is worth it, when 25’s promises a new engine,, as this version is light years better in the match engine already. feature.Goes hand in hand with the Match day experience. The new inverted full backs is a great addition, taking advantage of real life tactics, such as Man City or Tottenhams, that can be replicated to an extent where it is believable to showcase “copies,” that play out how you expect it. In the past, it could sometimes be hard to tell what one instruction did, or how it was shown within the match engine itself. Generally speaking, this is a lot easier to spot now, and by that, also easier to understand both your own tactic, and the opponents. Leading to a more rewarding playstyle if you love to deep dive into comprehensive watching and making tactics. feature.FM23 had a similar headline feature, and I do not believe it was at all improved - Hopefully, AI and everything under the hood will feel better now - Though after many hours in the (cough cough beta) I’m not feeling it. feature - As I’m confused, and don’t see or feel them being smarter.Always nice to see new leagues become playable and licensed. feature.Second biggest and most interesting feature for this edition, long overdue, but finally remade, is the set pieces system. Question is, is it any good? Well, it is better than what we had before, but it is by no means perfect. feature.Half baked? I’m honestly not sure. In theory, I like it, but I’m not sure how these targets, and in theory - reverse promises the players make to us, impact in any real game play, outside of role playing. It seems to have a very small effect on morale, but that is about it, no matter if it is training or in-match targets. feature, but with potential to impact more areas in the future, such as contract negotiations, player time, likelihood of them becoming less upset in the future, etc etc.To me, the third best feature. Both unexpected, works really well as it is, and with potential for custom Date bases from modders being easier to implement too. Using the Real world database, with all the transfers happening when they should, was simply put, excellent to watch in my first early save. feature.A much better match engine than the previous edition. Better performance on the simulation (not a headline feature, but worth a mention for those with potato PC’s) A new set piece system, which the community asked for. New game modes are also something not to be sniffed at for a large amount of the playerbase.I will categorise this release and features, as the best since 2009 with the 3D match engine  … Yes, I would call this the best FM improvement in 15 years, and I don’t think many of us had high expectations. is what I will give the new features.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager 2024 is the latest installment in the long-running management simulation series, and it's another solid entry that will please fans of the genre. This year, Sports Interactive has focused on making the game more accessible to new players, while also adding in a number of new features and improvements for experienced players. One of the biggest changes in this years iteration is the new transfer system. It's now much easier to find and sign players, and you have more control over the negotiations. You can also now set specific targets for your scouts, which will help them find players who fit your style of play.Another new addition is the ability to create your own set pieces. You can now design your own corner kicks, free kicks, and throw-ins, which you can then save and share with other players.Overall, FM24 is a game that will appeal to both new and experienced players. It's packed with new features and improvements, and it's one of the most addictive and engrossing management sims ever made.Here are some of the pros and cons of Football Manager 2024:Pros:More accessible to new playersNew transfer systemAbility to create your own set piecesImproved match engineMore exciting matchesCons:Can be overwhelming for new playersSome of the new features are a bit buggyIf you're a fan of management sims, then you should definitely check out FM24. _childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I can not recommend this game.Sure it works and is fun to play, but I'm starting to see a trend, the same trend FIFA started showing all those years ago.For example; The Squadplanner is completely useless and they show no effort to even fix it."But I can use it? I haven't noticed any issues with it?"If you haven't noticed issues with it, it is because you are not rigorously using shortlists.Whenever you have really huge shortlists the performance of the Squadplanner gets ruined for whatever reason. When you open the Squadplanner, the game slows down to a crawl and in worst case scenarios, the game can even crash if the shortlists are big enough; I've witnessed it myself.This is a bug that has been present since FM23 Beta. Worst part? It was reported on their bug forum way back then and I did my own post in FM24 Beta. But it hasn't been fixed, it's still in the game.Even though they say on the forum that they will look into it, they don't. Hence, the same bad feeling that FIFA started to give me years ago, where it is all about fixing superficial issues, issues that the broadest range of players will encounter.It's the equivalent of a car, they fix the frame so it looks all nice and neat but under the hood there are glaring issues in the engine department that they don't seem to care about fixing, because most players might not even open the hood. Which is why you see constant fixes to the match engine, because all players are exposed to it.I don't know, I think it's a really bad path to be on for this franchise.Despite how many bug reports we do, it doesn't seem to matter unless it is a widely experienced issue or superficial at first glance.There are other issues with the Squadplanner as well, such as that it auto populates, absolutely ruining any usage it might have, since it is used to create plans, but if those plans are constantly altered, then what is the point?They also pushed into it some really important stuff such as the Comparison screen that is important as well as Assistant Reports etc. But forget about using these if you prefer to use shortlists for scouting purposes and to target players for your club. The bigger your shortlists, the less performance all these things get, since they're all under the Squadplanner main category.The game is playable yes, but for how long? Some features aren't working and it looks grim in the future due to negligence. Squadplanner was one of the flagship features of FM23 and it hasn't been fixed since the FM23 Beta.It smells a lot like FIFA and I don't like it.They need to change course and start caring more about the quality of their product, not how many sales they'll get, otherwise history will repeat itself..

_childDocuments_.review: I'm struggling to recommend FM24 this year, and I think it is the weakest iteration of the game in a long time. I've played the game in one format or another since around 2003, with 2007 being the first installation of the game where I really sunk hours into the game, so I am very experienced when it comes to Football Manager. It's always been a fun game and easy to sink hours into, but this year, I can't put my finger on why but it's felt soulless and lacking any real immersion. It's turned into a frustration simulator as no matter how much I master the tactics, morale and structure of the team, results are destined to go against you. Granted this is often the case in football and in previous years. it has been realistically reflected in the game, so I've never been one to really rage at the game when a result or set of results go against me. But this year. it seems that there's no rhyme or reason to anything. If the game wants you to lose, it will force you to lose. You can go on a massive tear in the league and dominate with a squad clearly better than your competitors, but then all of a sudden, your team forgets how to play football and turns into a Sunday league team. Making laughable mistakes, ridiculous choices leading to red cards, and the opposition then turn into prime Barcelona. Again, I've had this happen in previous years but I can understand and accept the logic behind it, and can either rectify it through my own tactics, morale management or just simply ride out a tough period. Now, the player feels obsolete, and I am powerless to prevent totally avoidable losses. I'm looking forward to what they do with the game in FM25, as it feels like they've phoned it in for a few years now.

_childDocuments_.review: Best FM since the last FM. After 20+ years, finally saying goodbye to the 2D match view.Later edit:Ok, played some four hundred hours more or whatever. The small improvements ultimately lose their sparkle and underneath them are the same old inefficiencies, relying on a game engine that's too flawed to offer long term enjoyment. It sucks that many other parts of the game work quite well then.The match engine keeps generating what it's always generated - ludicrous amount of chances/goals in 5 minutes from the start of the match, either side of half-time or around the 90th. The problem is more so how they are generated - I've played with a lower league club and reached the PL, but the blunders I see in the PL, misplaced passes, senseless losses while in possession, other blatant mistakes, make the lower league players seem like the real pros. I mean seriously, the football IQ on display is atrocious. While the occasional nice goal does come about, there's almost no match without amateur blunders required to generate scoring chances.Ultimately, while the new visuals are a definite improvement, there's still so much work to do in this department. I've forced myself to accept that I'm not looking at something that should really replicate a football match, but just be consistent to whatever internal logic the match engine has. I have also been in the PL for two years, but the club won't seriously increase my stadium or build a new one (7k seater), despite having copious amounts of money available.A lot of the systems need an overhaul or to be straight-out removed from the game, because they undermine the experience. From the valuation system of players (good luck selling that 25 million player for more than 1 million most of the time), to the sideline messages (ugh, this moron encouraged us again while we were one-nil up, time to get despondent), to press conferences (seriously, why even bother?), to manager confidence (any player I sell upsets the fans, who barely rated my tenure higher than a B- in spite of five successive promotions).Let's see what the big ME overhaul will bring for next year, but for me, reducing the scope of the game and ensuring better functionality over what remains would be the true step forward.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about the Football Manager series. Over the last 5 years I've invested over 1000 hours but I think I'm just about done with it now. The match engine is much better than in previous years (though not perfect) and it's still "fun" on the whole. However, the series is plagued by issues that take any enjoyment out of the game. I'm going to list a few that have really taken  me out of the series:- Save Corruption. This one is huge. I lost a several hundred hour save and I'm just disheartened about it.- Injury rates. Seem a little odd. I have the the highest rating and number of physios in the league, play a slow tiki-taka ball and I have the most injuries in the league seemingly non stop? How does that work?- Reputation. Horrendous all round. Teams end up with an average age of 30+ because they don't ever play younger players as they aren't generated with the reputation to be seen as valuable. Clubs can buy players way above their station, or not be able to buy players (despite being in the Prem) due to reputation. You can have a player score consistently and never get interacted with by teams or have a player with high reputation get hounded non stop. It's all round horrendous. - Player interactions. The players act completely mental. They'll demand a wage of 900,000 p/w when your team averages around 30,000 p/w, then get offended and demand to leave if you suggest that is madness. Promises are utterly broken, staff interactions and interactoins with players never work out. By far the most visibly frustrating feature. If you like management or simulator games, as I do, then sadly avoid the Football Manager series until these get fixed because they suck the enjoyment out of a game that could otherwise be very good.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager is not for everyone, it is a game that people either really get into or they play it once and never touch it again. I started playing from FM15, almost a decade spent investing time and money into this franchise. As I am writing this I have decided to finally uninstall the game and am finally parting ways with this franchise, I wanted to write this is a warning for anyone who is interested in picking this franchise up. This is not a game, or at least not a game in the traditional sense. I understand that this is technically a 'simulator' and I will get that the FM purists will comment that if you want to play a game go play Fifa. I understand but this is where I would like to put the warning, FM more than anything is a RNG simulator. Zealand once said that playing FM is similar to playing poker where you can do everything right and still lose. When you win it does release that rush of dopamine but I've felt for a while that much like what Zealand says this franchise triggers the same response as gambling in a casino. Unlike most other games it is very easy to get addicted and even through all that anger and frustration you will keep telling yourself 'one more game'. If you are thinking about picking this up, do take this into consideration. No matter who you are, even if you never thought yourself to be someone who would get addicted.. just be careful. Don't start this franchise I would stay away from it..

_childDocuments_.review: I am glad that SI took all the fun out of the game as that saves me hundreds of hours in a year to focus on life. I have not liked any of the versions after FM21 but at least they weren't boring. This one is the worst of the lot. Most of my the matches feel like watching a dead rubber game between Everton and Crystal Palace, while simultaneously watching paint dry. What makes the game boring? Not being able to buy a goal from open play. At this point, my team can only score from corners, in spite of having fairly good strikers and creative midfielders. Halfway through the season, none of my two strikers can score a goal between them. Tried every instruction in the book: direct passing, removing "work ball into box", setting the mentality to attacking, changing the formations, adding "be more expressive". Nothing works. I am playing in the Spanish League with a pretty decent team, and both my strikers are rated as "good" players, so I know it's not the tactics. Basically, if you are not playing with a top level team full of elite players, the game is a slog as your strikers can't score from open play, your midfielders can't create any chances, and your wingers keep hitting the ball into the opposition defenders while crossing. Most of the goals will be from set pieces and the overall balance just isn't there. On top of all this, opposition corners are broken. It's very hard to clear a corner. Even if your player manages to head the ball away, it will in most cases fall to an opposition player who simply passes the ball to any of the numerous opposition players in the box that your defenders have completely forgotten about. Not to mention, the non-sensical decision-making of supposedly good players, where they will cross when shooting would be easier, shoot when crossing would be easier, pass the ball to themselves and then somehow contrive to lose it still, and so on. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished my 1st season with City. Some things I've noticed:1) Wingers or wide players still go for goal regardless of how tight the angles are, rather than square the ball for a tap in.2) Floated crosses are in general ineffectual, due to the attackers preferring to head the ball towards goal resulting in an easy take for the keeper. I'd prefer to see my striker head the ball down for a on rushing attacking midfielder to blast into the net or an player in a better attacking position, but this never happens.3) Players are too sensitive and interactions in my opinion haven't been massively improved. I praised Josko Gvardiol for his recent form and he actually fell out with me! This happens a lot actually and doesn't make any sense, everyone appreciates praise.4) Media still ask irrelevant questions in press conferences and comment on how a player is playing in a new role/position when they've been doing it all season and are natural in that position. 4) Contract demands are out of control, especially for high potential youth players. I've actually got a 15 year old demanding 30k a week. I mean C'mon be real here. IRL Rico Lewis went from 5k to 25k after a season in the 1st team so I expect new gens to be on similar money until they've shown some real potential and featured in the 1st team.5) As above, but 1st team players demanding double salary. Ederson 300k, Rodri 300k, B.Silva 450K per week!!!6) As expected Man United are OP, nothing new there though, they have been for years.... not salty or anything :)7) Average to good player valuations seem excessive. Joelinton for example was valued at 150m.8) Player fatigue in my opinion needs toning down, not by much but it is a little harsh to have half my team "jaded" by October. Keeper injures are an issue for me too. Ederson damaged his knee in Feb and was out for the rest of the season. This, annoyingly was after he signed his new 300k per week contract.9) The "new" set piece creator is just laughable. It's just more U.I on top of U.I and has been unnecessarily over complicated and you still can't create a bloody set piece! Bring back the drag and drop system until you can figure a better way of implementation please!With all that said I do feel S.I have over exaggerated with their pre launch build up. Some of the things they said they would change quite frankly haven't been, but unfortunately there isn't a YouTuber popular enough to criticise the game and it's short comings. If there was someone with a platform who criticised the game then maybe we'd see some genuine changes, but alas they are as usual full of praise and I can't blame them, the game pays their bills after all.  The reality is, if you like FM and have been a fan for many years, then you'll buy this version as well. If however you're new to the franchise.... _childDocuments_.review: Some things really good about this version of FM, which I haven't played since FM19.  The match engine is fairly good, and the UI is nice, easy to use and looks much better.But IMO the game is broken by player interactions and happiness.  It's dumb and doesn't reflect real life at all.  Promises are broken and player unhappiness is broken. E.g. if you don't play a player for a few weeks, they'll be in your office complaining. The options you have in the conversation with them are too restrictive making it more like solving a puzzle than actual human interaction.  And in any case pretty much whatever you do they'll become more unhappy unless you back down.  ONce they're unhappy it then rarely seems to go any way but to them wanting to leave.  Even if you start them every game.  The other issue is that the underlying game is in many ways the same as in 19 - new presentation, but the same logic behind it.  Press interactions are boring - again, restrictive options. Team talks are boring and formulaic.  Plus there are other niggly issues.  For example, as a new manager I can't see the stats of the likes of Jack Grealish, Casemiro and Antony. Very silly to suggest a football person wouldn't know these guys' stats? It's a shame, I came back to FM 24 hoping for a better experience. If you're a new player, yes buy it, but if you're a regular player, I wouldn't buy it any more often than every 3 years.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited until every update was out in the hopes that they may sneak in a match engine tweak with the last data update.  I was wrong, but that was expected.  I've played 9 FMs (09-11, 18-22 and 24), and my goodness, this FM has been the most disappointing and most unenjoyable FM I've ever played.  I did not have fun playing this edition as it felt like an unrealistic arcade rather than a realistic simulation.  It's been so unenjoyable, that I haven't been able to finish a single season.  Normally by April, I'm 3-4 seasons in and have another save going.  Each player plays the game their own way, my issues may be minor or nonexistent to others.Pros- Better animations when watching matches- An attempt was made to add in more statistics, accurate calculation for some is a different matter (ex. OPPDA)Cons- Hyper lethal AI attackers, where the lethality may be inversely proportional to the amount of possession they have.  Less possession for the AI = higher accuracy from the few shots on target the AI may get.- The AI scoring with their first shot on target more often than not, especially if it's during a key highlight- Inability of your team to press the opposition effectively, if at all- Defender's positioning has been an issue since October 20, 2023 (literally 1 day after the early access was released) and has been flagged as a "known issue" by SI for months.  Still no fix more than five months later and SI has moved on.  It will not be fixed for FM 24.- Player interactions and the team mutinies they can spawn- Frequent injuries- The promise system (not specific to just FM 24)- Poor AI team management and team building- Your team's tendency to hit the woodwork... a lot- Bloated game full of features that are not robustly implemented- Lack of communication from SI, outside of "here's a new update, download it now!"Areas where they can begin to improve?- Please stop adding new features before the previous features are made robust or even removed if necessary... please... PLEASE!- Communicate with the users regularly rather than simply telling them that a new release is out and to go download it, before going back to radio silence.  Also, be open and honest.- Overhaul player interactions from scratch- Overhaul, or preferably, completely remove the promise system- Make the in-game editor free with the main game- Have more people and more time for the alpha and beta testing phasesIt's wild to me that they had no intention of patching the match engine after December 11 (the last time the match engine was updated) and told absolutely no one.  Players were making bug reports on the match engine for months after December 11.  People were continuing to report on the day of the last data patch (April 9).  If you're thinking "those bug reports will benefit FM 25."  Great, but I couldn't care any less, I didn't pay for FM 25.  I can't say that I'm interested in FM 25 anymore after seeing how FM 24 was handled.  I think I'm done with the series, if this is the direction SI want to take FM.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Football Manager 2024, or as I like to call it, "The Relationship Tester." You see, while you're trying to build your dream squad and master the transfer market, your significant other might wonder if you're still part of their real-life squad. But hey, the game has it all!First off, let's talk about the new ball physics. It's like watching a game of pinball on a bumpy table. The ball bounces around like it's on a sugar rush, and you're left wondering if you're playing football or dodgeball.But wait, there's more! You can import your career from Football Manager 2023. It's like time travel for football geeks. Who cares about real-life transfers when you can continue your virtual football dynasty?Now, the Set Piece Creator. It's not just a game; it's a masterclass in tactical board games. You can outsmart your opponents with your set-piece wizardry. It's like playing chess, but with corner kicks and throw-ins.And what's this about Intermediaries? They're like the middlemen of the football world, helping you get rid of dead-weight players. It's as if football agents and used car salesmen teamed up to redefine the transfer market.Then there's the Match Engine. It's so immersive that you'll feel like you're watching a real football match. It's like sitting in the stands, but without the overpriced stadium food and that one guy who can't stop shouting at the referee.The two new game modes, Real World and Your World, add a twist to your career. It's like choosing between a real-time strategy game and an alternate history novel.So, Football Manager 2024 isn't just a game; it's a commitment. It's about building your dream squad, dominating from set-pieces, and making sure your partner doesn't trade you for a better player. If you're a football fanatic with some free time and a healthy relationship, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game offers a realistic portrayal of the football world, my journey with it has been marked by a colossal number of injuries, leading me to question the game's mechanics.Despite meticulously managing physios, being the top La Liga physios (5x at 20), and carefully rotating my team to prevent fatigue, I found myself dealing with an astonishing 4 to 6 injured players consistently. It's a perplexing situation that challenges the strategic depth of the game.Another aspect that stood out was the players' temperamental nature. Unlike other titles, players in Football Manager 2024 seem to become discontented far too easily. After just 10 matches, even those designated as fringe players express a desire to be starters, coupled with an insatiable demand for salary increments. It's not uncommon for a player earning 300k per year to suddenly demand a staggering 1.5 to 2 million per year, all because we secured a place in the Conference League. This demand becomes particularly absurd when players who were content with their contracts just 1.5 years before expiration refuse to negotiate or extend their contracts without apparent reason.One striking observation is the apparent bias in the game dynamics against the player. While negotiating with my club, Osasuna, players ask for exorbitant salaries ranging from 3 to 6 million per year, despite the club's average salary being below 2 million per year. Astonishingly, when I opt not to sign these contracts, the players go on to accept significantly lower offers from much weaker teams, ranging from 800k to 1.2 million per year. This discrepancy in negotiation dynamics adds an unwarranted layer of frustration to an otherwise immersive gaming experience.In conclusion, while Football Manager excels in providing a realistic football management simulation, certain aspects, such as injury frequency and player contract negotiations, seem designed to challenge the player rather than enhance the overall gaming experience. It's a delicate balance that could benefit from some fine-tuning to ensure that the challenges presented align with strategic depth rather than creating a sense of imbalance.

You can now set targets to players and I have to admit that this seems great, however I have not yet finished enough of them to check how impactful they are. Oh yeah, one more thing, you can now sell all players you don't want to have when rebuilding a team to Saudi, or at least everyone elses team in the game seems to be, only in mine they are interested, however not buying.Otherwise no change, still 4-2-3-1 gegenpress all day, play ball into box still means they will hoof it from the sidelines by air, you can just keep the "encourage" and "berate" shout and get rid of all the rest as players just start crying. I just read first 5 words of the press question and know what box to click at bcs I played FM23 and they did not even bother to shuffle the reply fields. Also if the press asks me about how great of a start to the career at my club my new signing has and I say "he became one of the key players immediately" maybe the player could at least react well to this? _childDocuments_.review: My main issue with this game is how little it changes over editions, and how the devs just do not fix issues that have been there for multiple years. It's a bit of a joke at this point.Pros:- The match engine is much better this year. It actually looks and plays like real football.Cons:- Interactions/promises are completely broken to the point where most people just avoid them completely if poissible. I had a CB recalled to his club because he "wasn't playing as a central defender" despite him definitely playing there (and in the agreed role) the entire season.- Everything is still based way too much on reputation. It doesn't change dynamically enough either. There should be an overall reputation and a 'current' rep because if I'm taking a team from rock bottom of League One to automatic promotion in one season I should be talk of the town but I barely get a rep boost. It's also just way too slow if you want to grow a team organically.- AI Squadbuilding is still absolutely terrible and SI have said they're happy with how it currently is, which must be a lie. Clubs still focus way too much on rep and sign ageing players or players they do not need, instead of competing for prospects. It's way too easy to hoover up all the best talents for myself because the AI are stupid.- Logic of the game is broken all over. Clubs rejecting offers for players and then selling them for way lower than those offers, players asking for super high wages at one club and accepting 3 times less than that at another similarly rated club, etc..- Spread of talent over the world is not balanced. Lack of full-back newgens still an issue. Dynamic youth rating still not working very well.- Newgen faces look atrocious and have only gotten worse. I know Miles said this is because he wants them to look like the player in game but you can barely even see the player faces in game! It's rubbish and ruins the immersion when half of your youth intake are balding 16 year-olds with vitiligo.

_childDocuments_.review: The best version of Football Manager to date. The match engine is the most realistic its ever been. I would recommend people buy the official in-game editor so they can fix a few stupid problems that pop up with the interactive mechanics off the pitch.  So for example, if a player is unhappy for a dumb/unrealistic reason, the IGE can be used to remove that. Tactically, the game's addition of positional play has been incredible. It's not perfect (nothing is), but it's a huge step in the right direction. Players are more spatially aware, and rotate properly according to their role. One gripe with the match engine is the sheer amount of offsides calls, and VAR interventions. These are minor complaints. Overall 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely the worst iteration of FM I have ever played and I reckon I have about 4500 hours across the last 4 iterations.The 'set piece overhaul' is just a feature that means you never have to touch set pieces ever again. A feature that was supposed to 'overhaul' a mechanic in the game has just turned it into something completely non-interactive and has seriously nerfed set pieces which is something I always used to have fun with.Other than that, there's basically no other new substantial features other than extremely minor additions like the intermediary transfers which are only really helpful when you've given up on getting any money for a player and just want them gone. TransferRoom is completely useless at getting rid of players and the fact that the game has removed the strategic selling of players in this way makes squad building in FM24 really frustrating.Oh and I forgot that they ruined training as well, getting rid of match preparation and specific set piece focuses was an absolutely terrible move. The match boosts you could gain from training was what made it feel so rewarding to keep going back and tweaking and they also added an element of risk reward to the game. Do I want to focus on doing a lot of match boosts at the detriment to my standard training regime? Do I have a lot of youngsters that would benefit from a more intense training schedule rather than focusing on match boosts. Instead, in FM24 I simply can't do anything in training to prepare me for the upcoming matches making it feel completely non-interactive and I just find myself pressing whichever one of the training presets happens to take my fancy.A general theme of FM over the last couple years is the 'stream-lining' of features which actually in reality only results in those features becoming less in depth and thus less interactive and honestly just ruins the immersion of being a Football Manager. Not only has this ruined existing features which I enjoyed in the game (such as scouting and the complete REMOVAL of in-game analysis) but it's also taking away from features we sorely NEED:Why is international management still so barebones? People have been complaining about this for ages! You can't even train or rest your players when you're an international manager! I went into a World Cup final with half my starting eleven on 60% condition because I was unable to rest them after a game like you can in normal club management where it would not be an issue.I HATE FM24 because I'm simply doing LESS in this game. I'm not changing set pieces depending on who I'm facing, I'm not editing my training to match what the opponent could potentially do against me, I'm not making significant changes during matches beyond substitutions because (lastly) the logic of this game and tactics just seems non-sensical.This is just all compounded by the removed features of FM23! The "new and revamped data hub" displays absolutely nothing worthwhile whilst in a game. Why remove things like Assistant Manager feedback? Does a manager not talk to their assistant during a match? I've already touched briefly on scouting but recruitment focuses are crap! In my experience, they rarely come up with gems that you don't already know about and I've just given up and delegated my scouting to my staff, something I never did before FM23 - wouldn't dream of it! One of the most fun late-game goals for me was to fill up my knowledge map and that feeling of building a massive scouting network was amazing, but this was removed too. Why?The last 2/3 years of this franchise have been severely disappointing and has changed things so fundamentally that I'm not even sure if it can get back to the level it once was. They can't just undo the things they've done in the last few games. (scouting will never go back to being as good as it was, set pieces won't be changed for another few years seeing as they've only just touched them recently). What hurts the most is that the negative changes to the game are what has been pushed as "new features" meaning I've spent £40 to play a much worse version of a game I love.

_childDocuments_.review: There's both good and bad in this game. To start with the good - there are absolutely no other football management games that comes close to the complexity and accuracy of the FM series. Now, granted, there isn't a whole lot of competition in this market, but still - if this is the type of game you're looking for, this is your only real option.The bad is just the lack of effort and investment from the developers. This series used to be amazing, with the match engine being fixed on a quick schedule, bugs being ironed out, etc. Nowadays, absolutely nothing gets fixed. The moment 23 went gold, their focus was on 24. The moment 24 went gold, their focus was on 25. For both FM23 and FM24, the match engine has had the same weakness - an absolutely obsession with DMs. Your tactic has 1 DM? You'll be competitive. You have 2 DMs? You'll win the league. You have 3 DMs? Best team in the history of the game. In this genre of games, it wins by default - but that's due to the lack of competition, not from the great work SI is doing.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager 2024: Where Tactical Brilliance Meets Virtual DramaRating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Football Manager 2024 by Sports Interactive continues the tradition of delivering a deeply immersive and strategic football management simulation. As the latest iteration in the long-running series, FM 2024 offers refined gameplay mechanics, enhanced realism, and a plethora of features that cater to both seasoned veterans and newcomers to the world of virtual football management. Here’s why it stands out as a must-play for fans of the sport:Gameplay and Mechanics:FM 2024 excels in its depth of gameplay and attention to detail. As a football manager, you take control of a team of your choice and guide them through the intricacies of modern football management. From scouting and signing players to devising tactical strategies and handling media relations, every decision impacts your team’s performance on and off the pitch. The game’s user interface is intuitive, allowing you to navigate through comprehensive menus and statistical analyses with ease. Whether you prefer a hands-on approach or delegate responsibilities to your coaching staff, FM 2024 offers flexibility and depth in managing your club.Graphics and Sound:While FM 2024 focuses primarily on data and information rather than cutting-edge graphics, the game’s interface is clean, functional, and optimized for managing your team efficiently. The match engine provides realistic simulations of football matches, with player animations and tactical interactions that reflect the strategic decisions you make. Crowd noises and ambient stadium sounds add to the atmosphere during key moments, enhancing the immersion without relying on flashy visuals.Realism and Depth:One of FM 2024’s strengths lies in its commitment to realism and authenticity. The game boasts an extensive database of real-life players, clubs, and competitions, ensuring that you can experience football management at a global level. Player attributes, team dynamics, and in-game events are meticulously modeled, reflecting the unpredictable nature of real-world football. From dealing with player injuries and transfers to managing team morale and tactics, FM 2024 captures the complexities of football management with impressive detail.New Features and Improvements:FM 2024 introduces several new features and improvements that enhance the overall gameplay experience. Enhanced AI for both player and managerial interactions provides more realistic challenges and strategic depth. The revamped scouting system allows you to discover hidden talents and build a squad tailored to your managerial vision. Tactical innovations, such as new formations and set-piece strategies, offer additional avenues for strategic experimentation and customization. These additions contribute to the game’s longevity and replayability, offering fresh challenges with each season.Community and Multiplayer Options:The Football Manager community remains vibrant and active, with forums, fan sites, and online communities where players share tactics, tips, and stories from their managerial careers. _childDocuments_.review: I have been very critical of FM over the last couple of years. Without any real competition it felt like SI was just going through the motions and had allowed the series to stagnate and stop moving forward. It was fast becoming a gloried DLC filled with gimmicks that initially look great but soon fade into the background after a few uses. It was fast becoming a victim of the yearly release cycle. Maximum profit, minimum effort. This resulted / accumulated  in the release of FM23 which was basically a £35 database upgrade with a few superficial gimmicks thrown in. I saw nothing to warrant my money and in my own pointless protest refused to buy it. Roll to this year and I can honestly put my hands up and admit FM24 is a much needed  return to form (of sorts) and at the  least movement in the right direction. I would recommend it. Coming from FM22 the match engine is much improved. (FM23 players may not notice this as much) The way players move, ball physics / deflections, the fluidity of the animations and the variety of goals scored is a huge step up. Its great to see a tactic actually represented in the ME. If you play a slower style of play, your team actually look like they play slower.  While in FM22 every style ended up looking like high tempo gengenpress.  It gives the players more options to stamp there identity on a team. The ME just seems more dynamic and its great to see this represented in the games you're watching. The core game has always been fantastic and FM24 is still addictive as ever but there are also a tonne of small little improvements on top. Having more control of set pieces, the clearer and better breakdown of finances and the ability to set targets to players just to name a few (of many). On paper they are small improvements but unlike the gimmicks of previous versions *cough* Manager Timeline * cough* do actually have meaningful impact on the game and the way you play it. That said the game still has issues. Over the years the series has slowly placed more emphasis on the importance of squad morale. To the point where is borderline Morale Manager -  its massively important.  This becomes a problem when you increase the amount of interactions / variables in the game that can impact Morale negatively. Especially when the player doest have the variety of responses / tools to manage it. For example: You can be plodding along, enjoying life, when BOOM - your 18 year old 5th Choice CentreBack decides you don't have enough depth at..... Centre Back. This can quickly snowball into a whole squad mutiny / team meetings / end of the world scenario and basically the entire squad will go from Perfect Morale to Poor morale and your form collapses....The game is also far too easy again and I didn't notice any improvement in either manager or transfer AI. (I won the PL in my second season with Bournemouth,) The money in the Saudi League only makes this worse as you can easily exploit the crazy fees they will pay. I got 70 million for 1 goal in 10 man - Big Dom Solanke with an AVG of 6.60. In total i sold over 300 Million worth of players to the Saudi League in  two years. Fun in a beta but could make the game quite boring later on. So overall despite these issues the game is much improved and for me at least 100% worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: ⚽ *"Football Manager 2024: The Game That Makes You Believe You Could Manage Real Madrid!"* ⚽As someone who sneaks in gaming sessions between meetings and deadlines (don’t tell my boss 😜), *Football Manager 2024* has become my ultimate escape. This game isn't just a simulation—it's a full-on obsession. If you’ve ever dreamed of managing your favorite club, making tactical masterstrokes, or unearthing the next wonderkid, this is where those dreams come true.**Gameplay**: It’s *Football Manager*, so you know what you’re getting—endless depth, realism, and detail. But *FM 2024* refines that experience to near perfection. The new tactical options give you even more control over your team’s playstyle, and the AI is sharper than ever. Opposing managers will actually adapt to your strategies, forcing you to stay on your toes. This isn’t just football—it’s chess on a pitch.**Transfers & Scouting**: The thrill of scouting and signing that hidden gem never gets old. The transfer system is as deep and intricate as ever, with a level of realism that makes you feel like you’re negotiating in a real boardroom. Whether you’re haggling over a superstar or signing a promising 16-year-old from a remote league, every deal feels significant. Pro tip: Be ready to justify those high wages when the board comes knocking! 😅**Match Engine**: The updated match engine looks and feels fantastic. Player movements are more fluid, the animations are smoother, and the overall presentation has taken a big step forward. Watching your tactical plans unfold on the pitch, whether it’s a perfectly executed counter-attack or a solid defensive setup, is incredibly satisfying. Managing egos, keeping the squad happy, and building morale is just as important as tactics. One wrong move and your star player could be knocking on your door, demanding a transfer. It’s challenging, but that’s what makes it so rewarding.**Addictive Factor**: The “just one more match” syndrome is real. You start a session intending to play for 30 minutes, and suddenly it’s 3 AM, and you’re debating the merits of a 4-3-3 vs. a 4-2-3-1 for your next Champions League tie. If you’ve got responsibilities, *Football Manager 2024* will make them disappear (just like your free time).**Final Thoughts**: *Football Manager 2024* is the pinnacle of sports management simulations. It’s a game that demands your time and attention but rewards you with unmatched satisfaction. Whether you’re taking a non-league club to glory or trying to manage the egos at a top European powerhouse, this game will keep you hooked.👍 **TL;DR**: *Football Manager 2024* is the ultimate test of your footballing brain. Deep, addictive, and endlessly satisfying—this is the closest you’ll get to being in the dugout without leaving your desk. _childDocuments_.review: It's football manager and an upgrade on FM23. I recommend it but its not perfect yet.Big issues with FM still persist. AI makes it way too easy to win everything. They never bid for any of my players and even on the extremely rare chance they do (and its not a youth player) its way below their value. This just allows me to take any team from any division and make them the best team in the world unopposed. For people trying to stay realistic, this is the biggest obstacle. The supposed counter to this issue is Saudi (shouldn't have to rely on them so much but they're a blessing) and the 'hire intermediary'. Hiring the latter can be useful at times but ultimately the value is extremely low most of the time. A club bid £9m for one of my players, I accepted but the player rejected their contract. I checked intermediaries and the highest offer I could get was £1.9m -10%?The second biggest is that you are given too much money. After one season in the premier league, even as a minnow that's recently promoted? Here's a £62m budget.Last big obstacle is that lower prem clubs and high championship clubs will have budgets near £100m. I had a player with a £57m release clause. He rejected Leverkusen and went to Nottingham Forest. Edit: The second after posting this review, a league one club and a ligue 2 club (namely Bordeaux who are in big financial trouble irl) just bid £14.5m for one of my players. Whilst this is his market value there is no way that this player, a POTS winner in a premier league team would, in real life, be sent to a club two leagues below and certainly not for such an incredibly expensive fee. I want to sell him, but to accept these offers ruins the realism aspect.In addition some clubs make extremely unrealistic choices, would be cool if AI actually stuck to their clubs' visions. Some other annoyances are young players asking to be a star player, players wanting a new contract WAY too often and many high potential youth players freezing below 100 PA ensuring their potential is never reached.

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time, in a world where the digital realm and reality often merged, there was a game that stood head and shoulders above the rest. This game wasn't just about playing; it was about living, dreaming, and achieving. This game was Football Manager, a title that didn't just entertain but transformed lives.The Unseen Glory of Football ManagerFootball Manager wasn't just another video game. It was a simulation, a portal into the exhilarating world of football management. Imagine this: you’re not just watching your favorite teams and players anymore; you're in charge of them. You make the calls, you decide the strategies, and every victory is a testament to your genius.The Game That Trains the MindPlaying Football Manager is like attending an elite business school with a focus on sports management. It sharpens your analytical skills, enhances your decision-making capabilities, and teaches you to manage resources effectively. You learn to scout talent, negotiate contracts, and devise tactics that could outsmart the likes of Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp. The joy of seeing your meticulously planned strategies unfold on match day is unparalleled. It's a mental workout that keeps your brain agile and your spirits high.Building Relationships, One Match at a TimeFootball Manager isn't just about managing a team; it's about building relationships. You connect with virtual players, understanding their strengths, weaknesses, and personalities. You become a mentor, a leader, and sometimes, a friend. The emotional investment is real. When your star striker scores a last-minute winner, or your underdog team achieves promotion, the elation is as genuine as any real-life victory.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone always whines about the match engine not changing. Moved from FM18 to FM22 a few years ago and was blown away then, and when I moved from FM22 to FM24, I was blown away even more. My only complaint - and I cannot stress how minor of a complaint this is - is that when I leave the game running for 4 or 5 days, it will have a graphics glitch-out and crash with a "update your drivers" message. But if I just do the most basic of due diligence on my part of saving and re-launching every couple days, it's fine.For vets, the new set piece system is staggering. I can just give it all to my set piece coach. Done. No tinkering with the ancient set piece menus, just do a small wizard and then the set piece coach takes it from there. So easy.The transfer system feels better. I can't just sell guys while in the 5th division of England for three times my annual wage budget anymore, and I can't rig scouting as easily as before. It feels like I genuinely have to work at it to find quality players. My only complaint here is that occasionally, I'll get an obscure guy from Sweden or Argentina in my Scouting Centre when there is zero chance that a club of my stature IRL would target or even know about him.I'm extremely optimistic about the future of FM and think all fans should buy FM24. Even if you won't play, you can use it to port over your FM23 save and then port that one over to FM25. Come on, how many thousands of hours do you get out of this? Throw some cheddar at the guys that make that possible.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been discussed and denied by the developers and fanboys many times but some games and your season in general is scripted to a point. Especially when you and your team are overperforming the game will start pushing back and stacking the odds against you. It can do this in enfuriating and unrealistic ways like injuring all your three of your goalkeepers in one week. Or make your players suddenly think they are in the UFC and produce flying tackles with two legs thus getting red cards and giving away penalties. I play and manage all my games in the match engine and it is very common and clear to see when the game is forcing you into a bad run. Like taking the lead 2-1 and your defender decides it's time to dribble through the center of the park in the 92nd minute while you have his instructions set to take less risk and don't dribble. He loses the ball it's 2-2. You quit. Reload. Same result but with slighlty different drama. I've done several tests reloading a game as much as 9 times. Put in different players. Different tactics. Got a draw 6 times and lost 3 times while my team is on par or even better then the opposition. In most of those games i went 1 or 2-0 up. I don't invite pressure by going on defend. I keep pushing high up and simply drop the tempo, put on waste time, work ball into the box. Players just don't listen. Almost always the match engine will produce your players making a stupid risky pass. Give away a stupid penalty. Your goalskeep will pass it to one of their forwards. And 2 minutes before time your opponent draws with a 30 yard screamer. You look up the player that produced that supershot. Stats say he has a 6 for long range shooting. It's another draw. Do you know what the odds are of that happening that consistently? In FM 100% Protecting a lead is near impossible in these scenarios no matter what you do.So why would the developers do this? Cause the game would be too easy otherwise. The game and the match engine isn't "smart" enough to  counter your management of the team. So if your midtable with Crewe Alexandra in the premier league while the game has calculated you should be fighting for relegation it will start shoe horning some results in. This isn't new. I'm 44 years old and have been playing since Championship Manager 2002 but it's been worse every year. I don't mind losing but i do mind the game giving me the illusion i'm in control while for at least half the season i'm really not. And if you do force me to lose then at least make it look believable.
