_childDocuments_.review: This is the first FM game in about ten years that I have felt able to give a positive review to, and that is purely because of one feature that has been requested for years going back to the days of Domark's Championship Manager on the Amiga. That feature is the ability to import your save(s) from the previous version; that feature alone makes this version worth buying for anyone with significant hours invested in a save from FM23.Getting a new database update each version/year is fine, until you've played a few seasons in your save, as it will have diverged so far from reality that it doesn't matter whether you started with 'real' players or a completely random database of players. Ten seasons in, and most clubs are unrecognisable from the ones that started the game. The enjoyment for most long term players is taking a small team/club and transforming them over a number of seasons, often twenty or more, and watching the rise and fall of players you've brought in and nurtured into superstars. You can now carry on that save from year to year without having to start from scratch each time.The rest of the game is basically the same old story. Tiny improvements, some screens moved around, a couple of changes to the UI here and there, and an up to date database of players and staff. The match engine has got a bigger facelift than normal, and is a lot more fluid and 'feels' realistic for once, however, it still looks like it was made in 2002 using assets from Kevin Thom's Football Manager on the spectrum - but I suppose small steps and all that.Price-wise, again, it's at least twice as expensive as it should be for what you are getting in terms of upgrades. Owners of previous versions should be getting a hefty discount of around 50% for this as it simply isn't worth the money over previous versions. If you do not own any other versions then £40 is reasonable, although £30 would be fair.As I said in last years review, we have zero choice, the game has no realistic competition so if you want to play football manager then you get this whether you like it or not.And the in-game editor is now £6.99, for something which should be included for free. You can buy fan made editors for less than that with more features, although slightly less convenient. People who bought this in early access should get this for free regardless.

Boasting enhancements in player animations, ball physics, and lighting, the Truer Football Motion aims to provide the most realistic Match Engine in the franchise's history. Some appreciate the depth these additions bring to squad management, while others argue that certain changes, such as player interactions and squad dynamics, feel unpolished and unpredictable.A recurring concern is the presence of bugs and the game's reliance on Denuvo DRM, prompting frustration among users. _childDocuments_.review: Overall Rating: 4.5/5 StarsPros:In-Depth Management Simulation: Football Manager 2024 offers an incredibly detailed and realistic management simulation. The depth of player data, tactical options, and team management tasks make it the most comprehensive football management game available.Improved User Interface: The user interface has seen significant improvements, making it more intuitive and user-friendly. Navigating through menus and accessing key features is smoother, enhancing the overall user experience.Enhanced Match Engine: The match engine has been refined to provide more realistic and visually appealing match simulations. Player movements, ball physics, and match events feel more authentic, adding to the immersion.Dynamic Player Development: The dynamic player development system is impressive, allowing you to nurture young talents and see them grow into world-class players. The addition of new training modules and mentoring options enhances this experience.Comprehensive Scouting System: The scouting system is robust, providing a wealth of information on potential signings. The ability to scout players worldwide with detailed reports helps in making informed transfer decisions.Cons:Steep Learning Curve: The game’s depth and complexity can be overwhelming for newcomers. Understanding the intricacies of tactics, training, and player management requires a significant time investment.Time-Consuming: Football Manager 2024 is highly time-consuming. Managing a team through a season, especially with all the detailed options available, demands a lot of time and commitment.Occasional Bugs: While generally well-polished, the game can still have occasional bugs and performance issues. These are usually addressed quickly by the developers, but they can disrupt the gameplay experience.Recommendation: I highly recommend Football Manager 2024 to fans of football and management simulation games. Its unparalleled depth, improved user interface, and realistic match engine make it a standout title in the genre. While the steep learning curve and time commitment might be daunting for some, the rewards of successfully managing a team and achieving glory are immensely satisfying. If you enjoy detailed strategy games and have a passion for football, Football Manager 2024 is a must-play.

This is the first time, I feel I didn't do justice to my money with my day-1 purchase.       First of all, this is a huge complex simulation game. Lots of players, staffs in the game and their interaction, hundreds of matches and it's calculation. There bound to be some bugs happen at release. Unfortunately, this year the bugs were more than doubled. None of them are game-breaking but definitely many of them are immersion breaking.        Some bugs regarding AI managers and clubs decisions, making this game very easy to break. You will not feel challenged enough. AI manager will not make subs, and you can change 5 subs and win the game during last 10-15 mins. AI transfer still very weak, they are buying players but not playing them or playing them in different positions, making the player under-perform. AI players also making stupid decisions during transfer by chosing lesser team with respect to money or competition etc.      Steam doesn't allow number rating, so I cannot say this is a 6 out 10 game. So, officially I selected "recommended" but with some reservations. If you liked older FM, then this game is immersion breaking. If you are a newcomer, this game is easy to exploit, but you won't be challenged enough by AI.       I hope SI fixes this in future. Till then I will go back to FM23.

_childDocuments_.review: Like it, no, I love it!I just don't get most of the negative reviews I've read.  Not one crash in over 450 hours of game play.  The tactics work for me, and the UI is good.My best piece of advice to any purchaser is to get the in-game editor.  It'll help you with smoothing over non-football related issues, such as finances.  As every fan knows, IRL football depends on money, so some wealthy type comes along and buys a team; then all of a sudden, the team buys good players and starts climbing the ranks.  So just simulate real life in the game, by tweaking the finances with the editor.To help with your enjoyment though, don't tweak the player stats.  Let the players develop naturally by your coaching and training.  Take the money woes out of the equation, and focus on improving your coaching and training style.  Also, to get a real sense of achievement, I recommend starting with a team in the bottom tiers.  As you improve your coaching, your team climbs, and you're both happy!This game is more chess than people realize.  As in chess, you have a strategy that you deploy.  However, based on your opponent's response, you have to remain flexible to change tactics along the progression of a match.  And the same applies during the course of a season.  As Bruce Lee famously said, "Be like water, my friend!"

_childDocuments_.review: I've Played a number of different versions of Championship Manager/Football Manager over the years, since the original Championship Manager 3 which was 98-99 season.  You would think by now any problems would have been ironed out.  But no.  Very slow  game play. I'm finding it takes about an hour to play 1 match. What with all the emails, and decision making between games. As  Far too much reading of small text, especially with all the press conferences you have to attend, and that gets very repeptitive.  Rather than trying to provide a fun football game, it tries to replicate running a football team, which isnt fun.  Found i was getting a headache and sore eyes after playing for a couple of evenings.  In 2021 i tried the "Touch" version which is a lot better, as it speeds up a season and allows you to play a match with an auto-result feature.  But this version you have to play each match.  Also new feature since 2021 seems to be a ganging up of the team if you upset one of the influential players. So a player might have 4 years on his contract, has a bigger club wishing to buy him. You refuse, he kicks off and you have a team mutiny on your hands. Don't think that would happen. Too cumbersome. A season is going to take several weeks if you are playing a couple of hours a day. Nah not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a bit dissapointed honestly. All the hype about new AI match engine was wrong in my oppinion. Yes positional play is noticable, but now every opp team plays the same. Every single one, even the last team on the table plays like Man City last season. Gegenpressing almost doesn´t work anymore. Even the last team on the table builds up from the back better than Man City. The so much hyped new Standards/Corners/Throw-ins system is nothing special either. Not impressed at all. Sometimes it is even confusing and unorganized.When it comes to player ratings I can talk about Premier League, which I played this year with Arsenal. All in all it is not bad, but what I have noticed is that Man Utd players are in my oppinion made too good in the game, while Man City players are in my oppinion made too weak. I was surprised to see that when I started the season and it certainly did show later in the season, where Man City gets beaten by every team on the table, while Man Utd dominates the league without losing a single match. I mean really? Harry Maguire? Well accoring to a new fm24 match engine Harry Maguire builds up from the back better than Ruben Dias, Ake, Stones and Akanji, all four together. Harry Maguire! After a while AI adapts to your tactic, which is normal in real life too, teams learn how you play and adapt accordingly, make your life harder ofcourse, it is normal, but for your winning tactic, that got you on the first place in premier league to now suddenly and totaly be dominated by the team in 14th position. I do not think they possess the quality to do that, even if they understand every single detail of your tactic. That is why some matches are easy and others hard. Well in FM24, there are no easy matches anymore. Bayern will destroy Darmstadt 95% of the time, even without a tactic. But in fm24 Darmstadt can build up from the back better than Man City. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game but with some reservation; Let me elaborate I only buy Football Manager every few years and the last one I bought was FM 2015. Every year the latest edition gets a bit more complicated without adding playability to the game. With FM 2015 I managed to get Hearts FC to win the SPL every year and eventually win the Champions League on a regular basis. That was fantasy football and great fun. The only downside was that the 3-D game mechanics weren't entirely convincing with the oft qouted "ice skating on the pitch" in some evidence This version of the game is much more realistic which means it's less fun. I manage The Spartans FC and and managed in something like ten years took the club from the fourth tier of Scottish football all the way up to the top tier. However I spent nearly all my time in the SPL avoiding relegation which was so frustrating I decided to delete that particular game and start again using the youtube tutorials . However this hasn't made much difference despite following all the advice from multiple sources on youtube None of this is helped by needlessly complicated tactics and elements such as keeping the players happy. No matter what I do the players attributes often drop to an alarming level  which is a pity because the game visuals are fairly impressive Sega have made it clear that FM24 will be the last "Traditional version" . I've no idea what this means for the future but I do hope this means the game will be simpler to play. I for one am rather nostalgic for the good old days of Championship Manager where you could play a whole season in a couple of hours .

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an overall improvement over the last few iterations. I bought FM 22 (I have like 450 hours) and it was good, tried FM 23 and it was so-so, it just not feels like a updated version to FM 22. Alas, they announced the switch to a new engine in FM 25 (Unity), therefore, I was not expecting this version to be good. After saw some gameplay and reviews on YouTube, I decided to try and was glad that I gave this game a shot. As a whole package, it improved upon its last iterations quite a bit. The game feels smoother to play, new roles got added, tactics got tweaked, set-piece got a major overhaul and it feels better to actually do set-piece in the tactics than letting the game do it for me cause the whole thing was so bad/tedious in previous games. Another important thing is that the animations for match engine got updated, it just feels so good now to see how the ball move around and how the players handle the ball. The match engine now has the fluidity/feel like actually seeing a football match, whereas in previous iterations it feels like some dots hitting the ball and no physics attach to anything.The game gonna get an engine update next year (FM 25). However, based on my previous experience with engine changes of different games/franchises, the first game on the new engine/toolkit is always the worst one in recent times. Also, looking at the Dev Update, I am not so optimistic about the next game. It feels dumb down in a lot of different ways cause the designed it with the other platforms in mind. It just not feel like a full-fledged FM to me as they removed quite a bit of features and UI got changed makes it looks like a mobile game to me.TLDR I would say get this version cause it gonna be the best FM version for quite a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Introduction:The announcement of Football Manager 25's transition to the Unity engine, while a nod to graphical enhancement, starkly highlights a deeper, more troubling issue: the game's stagnation. As a long-time supporter and critic, I can't help but express profound disappointment in the direction of the series.The Problem of Stagnation and Complacency:Sports Interactive seems to have settled into a comfort zone, lacking the drive for meaningful innovation. This complacency, likely fueled by a lack of competition, has led to a series that feels increasingly out of touch with its player base's desires and the evolving landscape of football management.Demand for Substantial Overhaul:Online Servers and Live Seasons: The game must adopt online servers for real-time season updates. This isn't just a 'nice-to-have'; it's essential for a game purporting to mirror the dynamic world of football.AI Revolution and Tactical Depth: The AI is archaic, the tactical options limited. We need a system that reflects the complexity and diversity of modern football strategies. We are tired of 4-2-3-1 engine busters.Authentic Player Dynamics: Players in the game should embody real personalities, complete with ambitions and complex relationships, influencing team dynamics in profound ways.Interactive Training and Influential Staff: The training and staff mechanics should be more than superficial features; they should be integral to a team's success and play style. I want to hire a staff member because he may have unique methods that align with my play style.Robust Club Management: Managing a club should encompass all facets, including financial and commercial decisions that have tangible impacts. Companies ready to buy in or bid for our clubs investment opportunituiesFUT-Like Mode Innovation: Introducing a FUT-like mode would inject fresh energy into the game, offering a new way to engage with football history and fantasy.Revamped Release Schedule:Beta Launch: Align with the start of the EPL season. 2 Weeks before a match ball is kicked.Post-Transfer Update: Immediately after the summer transfer window.Regular Seasonal Updates: To accurately reflect the unfolding football season.Call to Action for New Developers:The genre is crying out for new voices and fresh perspectives. I urge new developers to step into this space, challenging the status quo and igniting a much-needed revolution in football management simulations.Conclusion:This isn't just a critique; it's a clarion call for radical change. The Football Manager series must undergo a fundamental transformation or risk losing its relevance. As fans, we deserve a game that evolves with us, challenges us, and reflects the beautiful complexity of the sport we love. Sports Interactive, it's time for a true revolution, not just in graphics but in spirit and substance.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Football Manager 2024: Tactical Symphony and Managerial Brilliance UnleashedRating: ★★★★★Introduction:Football Manager 2024, the latest masterpiece from Sports Interactive, transcends the boundaries of traditional sports simulations, offering a deep dive into the intricate world of football management. This detailed review aims to dissect the game's multifaceted features, placing a spotlight on its tactical intricacies that elevate it to the pinnacle of virtual management. Additionally, we'll draw insightful comparisons between the in-game tactical brilliance and the strategic genius of three world-class real-life managers.Realism and Database Depth:FM 2024 kicks off with an unprecedented commitment to realism. The expansive database meticulously replicates the dynamic nature of the footballing world, encapsulating real-world player statistics, transfers, and dynamic events. Whether managing a top-flight club or steering a lower-tier team, the realism injected into the game sets an authentic stage for the managerial journey.Tactical Mastery:At the heart of FM 2024 lies an extraordinary tactical engine that pushes the boundaries of virtual sports management. The revamped tactics creator serves as a playground for managers, offering an unparalleled depth of options. Crafting playing styles, tweaking formations, and assigning player roles become an art form, providing a nuanced and immersive experience. The match engine's refinement contributes to the visual spectacle, mirroring the unpredictability and excitement of real football matches. Watching meticulously planned tactics unfold on the virtual pitch is nothing short of exhilarating.Comparing Tactics to Real-Life Managers:Pep Guardiola (Manchester City):FM 2024 aligns seamlessly with Pep Guardiola's tactical brilliance. The emphasis on possession-based football, fluid movement, and strategic pressing mirrors Guardiola's hallmark philosophy. Managers in the game can meticulously replicate the intricate playing style associated with the Manchester City manager, fostering an environment of control and creativity akin to Guardiola's renowned strategies.Jurgen Klopp (Liverpool):For those enamored with Jurgen Klopp's gegenpressing style, FM 2024 serves as a canvas for emulation. The game captures the essence of Klopp's tactics, encouraging quick transitions, relentless pressing, and a cohesive team approach. Managers can orchestrate their virtual squads to mirror the high-intensity, aggressive play synonymous with the Liverpool manager.Diego Simeone (Atletico Madrid):FM 2024 caters to managers fascinated by Diego Simeone's disciplined and organized style. The ability to set up defensively solid formations, execute effective counter-attacks, and instill a robust team mentality echoes Simeone's tactical pragmatism. The virtual world allows managers to embrace the challenges of creating an organized and resolute team similar to Simeone's Atletico Madrid.Scouting and Recruitment:FM 2024 introduces a revamped scouting system that mirrors real-world player recruitment dynamics. The global scouting network becomes a manager's lens to unearth hidden talents and promising prospects across diverse footballing regions. Negotiations in the transfer market reflect the intricacies of real-world deals, enhancing the satisfaction of securing strategic signings or nurturing young talents.Player Development and Dynamics:The game places a strong emphasis on player development through the revamped development center. Personalized training regimes and mentoring contribute to the individuality of squad members. The dynamics system introduces a new layer, emphasizing the impact of player relationships and team chemistry on and off the field. Managers are tasked with navigating egos, maintaining morale, and fostering a cohesive team environment, mirroring the challenges faced by real-life managers.Media Interaction and Managerial Impact:The media plays a pivotal role in FM 2024, influencing public perception and player morale. Press conferences, interviews, and media interactions add a layer of authenticity, making every managerial decision feel consequential. This aspect of the game parallels the real-world impact of media interactions on a manager's reputation and the overall narrative surrounding a football club.Challenges and Learning Curve:FM 2024's depth is both its greatest strength and a potential barrier for newcomers. The steep learning curve demands dedication to master the intricacies of tactics, scouting, and player management. However, for those willing to invest time and effort, the rewards are substantial. The challenges presented by the game contribute to its longevity, ensuring that each season remains a unique and engaging experience.Conclusion:Football Manager 2024 emerges as a pinnacle in virtual football management simulations, showcasing a tactical symphony that harmonizes with the strategic brilliance of real-life managers. Its commitment to realism, attention to detail, and tactical mastery make it a must-play for football enthusiasts. The comparisons drawn between in-game tactics and the strategies employed by world-class managers demonstrate the game's ability to capture the essence of football strategy. Whether you're a seasoned veteran or a newcomer to the series, FM 2024 provides a dynamic and immersive journey into the heart of football management, solidifying its place as a premier title in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is the third and final edit I'll make since the last main patch has been released (there's another upcoming to finish up the database updates required, but that's all it'll do afaik). If you have FM22 or FM23, don't bother with this one and stick with what you have. Most of the hours I have racked up here are from accidentally leaving the game on while I'm off doing something else, or simming seasons while doing other things to test whether it's worth committing to a long-term save. I keep restarting this game because the AI squad building is so bad that there's no challenge the further along you go (it's no different from FM23). The J-League is not fully licensed either.The AI squad rotations are still so weird too - the managers will rest their best players at Champions League finals, despite them not being injured or fatigued, which...???? Teams also still do the usual 'buy player for around £80m, never use him, then sell him for much less than that' issue that plagued FM23 (and probably the previous FMs too).I'll keep playing until I'm bored of the idea of football management games since there's no way to get a refund. The problem with games like this is that it takes time to start to notice bugs, and certainly much longer than the 10-hour cut-off limit Steam has for refunding games. Aside from that, there's no way I'm getting FM25 because SI has made it clear on their forums that they're happy with how the AI managers and squad-building logic are performing, hence why there was no change in this latest patch (nor were there any changes to the match engine despite a lot of great feedback on how to improve certain aspects on the SI forums).One piece of advice I'll give to anyone when it comes to FM25 - don't take any promises of 'features' at face value, and either wait for evidence of these things or put the onus on SI to demonstrate the changes they've claimed to make before you take them seriously. 'Improved AI Squad Building' shouldn't mean anything unless they can show you how it's been improved. It might even be in SI's best interests to stop promoting features they can't prove exist in the first place.

name: Flashback
detailed_description: You will play as a deliveryman and encounter various characters and events. You need to make your own judgments and choices. After that, your attributes will change according to the outcomes of your choices. When your attributes drop to zero or go too high, you will meet a bad ending or something special. The attributes will change slowly over time to prepare you for the incoming accidents. For example, you can give up the current event and let another personality take your place to handle all the problems for you. In this situation, the current event and changes to your attributes will be interrupted. Quitting an event comes with a price. Your attributes will decline after giving up events but your level will rise instead. Your level may play an essential role on certain occasions and determine the course of events. On Day 30, something will happen and you may reach the end or go back to the first day. Anyway, the fate of the characters depends on your choices.

short_description: Flashback is a strategy game oriented to your choices. You will play the role of a deliveryman and live in a turbulent city for a month. You will meet various characters and experience events, and those characters' fates will cross and they will usher in their own futures based on your choices.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm all for supporting small dev teams or solo devs and I do like what this game is going for. Paying $1 for a short and simple game is fine, and the price is acceptable for what it has to offer. I also wanted to give it enough playtime so I can make a fair review. With that said, I will be talking about what I liked and disliked about it.Starting with what I liked:Although there could be more variety in the music, the tune the game has sounds pretty catchy. Good job to the composer!I also really like the art style, and the CG's are nicely drawn.I also like the idea of being a deliveryman in a city where you cannot predict what you will encounter, and you can choose what you would do in a certain scenario, be it a good or bad situation. Depending on what you encounter and/or what you do, you can lead yourself to different endings, or positively/negatively impact your attributes. You can really do so much with that idea. Now on to the things I dislike. Which is basically about lacking elements:As I have mentioned, the deliveryman in a turbulent city with unknown encounters idea is very interesting. That's mainly what has motivated me to buy this game.I was a little disappointed with the lack of world-building in this game's universe. You aren't really given much information about this city, which doesn't even have a name from what I have experienced.  You don't really have much information about the protagonist or the people living within the city and why they do the things they do. You basically jump in, the game says you're going to a city and you speak with a ship captain to earn yourself a job there. Then afterward, you proceed to randomly generated events and you survive until a certain important scenario appears that can lead you to an ending. It would be nice if there was a lot more depth in this world, because with what it is, it has so much potential to create a very serious and engaging narrative involving the protagonist itself, the characters you encounter in the game, and the city they take place in. Another thing I was pretty disappointed about was how empty everything seemed. What I mean by that is this.Even though you are in a crazy environment you have to live through, and so many characters and scenarios to see, I felt very little attachment to everything. There isn't much reason to care about what is going on in this game when you pretty much just do one thing in one scenario then you jump to the next without any regard on what has been happening before. It's just "If you choose one option or the other, your attributes can go up or down and some text to follow up with it explaining what happened for them to go up or down."That's just about everything I have to list. _________________________________So my main critique about this is the game's lack of world-building. I feel if there was a genuine plot to go on with this idea and the materials used, it could've been a much better experience. I will admit. After playing this, it has gotten me interested to see what the devs have in store for future projects. There's lots of potential and I can clearly see that from their works. _childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying, the game looks to be a part of a much bigger whole. And by that I mean it looks like the game is actually part of a series of different games seemingly connected to each other. And it starts with Sunset Routes (the first game / SR). Who knew that the characters weren't simply numbers and skills on a ship after all?As a standalone game, I agree that it lacks straightforward world-building. Although, you could also say that the game itself is actually part of the world-building for the possible series the dev(s) have in store. Really, while it may work as a sole game, I found myself appreciating the game a lot more because I liked the character designs and endings for the first game and wanted to know more about them. It felt nice to finally see a number of their individual story descriptions, and even their names and little quirks.Beautiful art as always, and music is pretty chill.The gameplay is basically a visual novel with a dice roll (Choice-based Roguelite). This means that sometimes the same choices have a "bad" and a "good" roll, good being subjectively dependent on what stat you need (or want to reduce). However, it also does offer you ways to mitigate the punishment of RNG through game-over buffs, game knowledge (a choice's possible effects) and most notably, the Give Up button. There will be runs that can just stop you altogether (unless you have like... foresight lmao), don't get me wrong; but going through the days is actually more consistent than people may fear.Overall, it's an interesting game with really good amounts of potential it sets up. I know it's pretty hard to gauge how good the future installments will be, but I would still recommend this game for its chill gameplay, aesthetics, addition to the lore of SR, and not to mention, price. I look forward to the next part of this story.

_childDocuments_.review: First up this shouldn't be confused in any way with the famous and popular 1990's adventure platformer, Flashback.  This is not that game and not related to it, despite the conflicting name. Flashback is basically a badly translated E-book stapled to a shallow, often nonsensical "stat survival" game... you know those kinds of games where you start with a set of stats (health, food, sanity, water, whatever, not far off Oregon Trail if you think about it), and you bumble along hitting RNG events which thump one or more of your stats... only rarely boosting some of them.  So you know, just like Oregon trail, really.  In this particular case, instead of dying from dysentry on the way to Oregon, you're fed some badly written E-book stuff along with your stat thumping.  Kind of like if you went through a library, ripped out all the different chapters from a bunch of books and then put them back together in random order.So yeah, it doesn't "work" from either a literary or a gaming perspective, and yet here it is on Steam as a paid product, doing less than what some browser/Flash games are capable of. I guess I should mention the "plot", not that there is one... you're a delivery guy in an Anime style supernatural/cybercity thing and you all your RNG stat thumping comes from various delivery jobs you do... it's tiresome, really.  One important note is that even though this is an amateur project, it does seem to be sincerely and genuinely made.  I couldn't find any flipped assets, plagiarism or any other kind of insincere actions from the developer, but unfortunately genuine intentions alone are not enough to produce a brilliant PC gaming experience.There's an overwhelming amount of mediocre Visual Novel/E-book style cutscenes in this game.  So you'll spend a huge amount of time not playing the game, but clicking through endless lines of poorly written VN text cutscenes because the developers couldn't work out how to relate their narrative through the game mechanics, and decided instead it would be better to compete with reading a book for your time.  We're here to play games, not watch hours of garbage intersituals.On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.To make matters worse, while lazy, low quality pixel "art" has been used, making the game look bad, many elements of the game aren't done with pixelcrap... which accomplishes a couple of things.  First, it shows the developers perhaps could have done better and they knew it, so that's a major screwup.  Secondly, it destroys any hopes the developer had of creating a "retro aesthetic" as their excuse for the lazy pixelart compromise... It looks completely inauthentic from a retro gaming perspective.  Visually, this is a hamfisted mess, a dogs breakfast of bad visuals, and this kind of laziness and poor quality should never be foisted on gamers.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.The game features mostly static, barely animated 2D images, the kind of thing you expect to see in browser/flash games.  While the artwork itself, while mediocre, might be considered passable, the visual presentation here is negligible, it might as well be a slideshow or a Youtube video.  Pac-Man, Space Invaders and Asteroids had more advanced animation and visuals going on than this game does.The developers didn't design the game for modern gaming PCs, as such the display resolution caps out at 1080p, a very low resolution that became mainstream back in 2006 and became obsolete when 4K entered the mainstream in 2014.  The game simply won't look right on modern gaming displays due to this failure on the part of the developers.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Flashback is relatively cheap at $1 USD, but it's not worth it. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  This is also competing with over 11,000 free games available on Steam, many of them far better than this paid product.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me not to recommend Persona 5 Tactica, but for anyone other than Persona die-hards, a recommendation cannot come while the game is at full price.  While costing the same as a main series Persona, Tactica suffers considerably from being a spin-off release.  The story is fitting for a Persona title but lacks the detail of a full entry due to the game being much shorter and having no extended cast, and the gameplay strips out much of a Persona title’s breadth and flexibility, while remaining on the shallow end even for its adopted genre.  This doesn’t make Tactica bad, but it doesn’t justify the same amount of money as a much larger mainline release.First, the story is short by any measure, carried across a meager four bosses.  Only the game’s newcomers see any kind of character development or grow in any way, and while that’s understandable for the game’s small scope, the Phantom Thieves are very much just along for the ride here.  Tactica isn’t about them, and they’re present for two reasons only: to facilitate the main character’s growth, and because fans would riot at the idea of a Persona 5 spinoff without them.  A start to finish run through takes thirty hours or so, which is a lot to dedicate to a single person’s story, while still coming up on the short side in term of total play time (for a Persona title at least).  That play time can be extended via side missions, but these are, for as much as I could stomach of them, “Here’s a map, finish it in one turn.”  Figuring out how to do this isn’t tactical gameplay so much as puzzle solving, and while others’ opinions may vary, it fairly quickly became drudgery for me.  Other than a small handful of conversations in safe rooms, these are your only opportunities for more dialogue and interaction between characters, but the challenges were so tiresome I eventually quit bothering.  Imagine if every bit of optional Persona 5 content was “Kill this shadow in one turn,” and you’ve got the idea.Gameplay as a whole isn’t bad, but with the change in art style they’d have either had to redo every summon or have them stand out awkwardly.  Instead, you have the “sub-persona” system, by which personas are awarded as map loot, and can be assigned to any Phantom Thief, allowing the rest of the cast to use abilities from two (even though only their unique persona ever appears), while by the same token limiting Joker to two.  This might be slightly less painful if not for the fact that every persona has at most two abilities: one inherent, and one inherited during fusion.  As a result, personas largely end up as “stat sticks,” serving to boost your gun damage, melee damage, SP, and HP.  In fact, these are the core stats of personas.  They are essentially your gear.  To make up for this somewhat, each character has three quite small skill trees.  Although this isn’t very Persona-like, it works to add some variety, although certain nodes in everyone’s tree are practically non-choices, as doing without would be painful.Losses from shoehorning Persona into a narrower system aside, Tactica also doesn’t do a particularly good job of making them up with depth of tactical gameplay.  Aside from persona skills, each character can perform a melee attack or shoot a gun.  The importance of staying in (read: adjacent to, more on that in a moment) cover makes melee a very poor choice in most situations: approaching may leave you exposed, attacking may leave you exposed, and not being in cover opens you up to being critically hit.  An attack will move you into the space your target vacated, so it’s possible to get back into cover that way, unless you’re hitting one of the few enemy types where that doesn’t work.  As with the main series Persona games, taking a crit will knock you down and give the attacker a free action, including movement, so this is to be avoided at all costs.  Fortunately, for certain definitions of the word, being “in cover” for this purpose is easier than it ought to be.  As long as you’re next to cover, whether it’s high or low, or actually between you and an attacker or not, you have resistance to attacks.  With melee not being much more damaging than gunfire most of the time, relying on it for any purpose other than knocking enemies out of cover is a waste.  All out attacks do appear in the form of triple threat, in which a character with an extra turn from a crit can form a triangle on the map with the other party members, dealing massive damage to enemies within.  Also, one persona ability (ambush) which Erina has natively allows a bit of depth in opting to shoot enemies as they move in.  Otherwise, there’s just not much here.  Attempts at more exist (knocking an enemy from above into Makoto’s range lets her shoot them in the air for example) but don’t present themselves as opportunities often enough to bother planning around them.The lack of depth largely extends to persona abilities: with cover being the difference between resist or crit and elements being a non-factor, persona abilities aren’t what they were in Persona 5.  There are two main uses in Tactica: hitting an area (which is a frustrating experience, as you cannot freely target the ability and must center it on an enemy, meaning a two by three tile ability that COULD hit two enemies separated by two tiles will not), and moving things out of cover.  Psi/Psio/Mapsi, etc. force targets to move toward the caster, making them arguably the best abilities in the game.  Garu/Garula/Magaru, etc., knock back their targets, potentially out of range, which isn’t ideal, but if they fly into another enemy, both can be made vulnerable.  Any other use of active persona abilities is just not particularly helpful.  In an interesting metaphor for how flat this makes personas feel, they’re found in game as gears with two dimensional images of the persona on them.  Even healing is entirely unnecessary if you’ve taken the right skills from the skill tree.  Against the final boss, and when playing sloppily, I made use of Erina’s flag ability to heal, and main character’s ability to drop a block that heals (reminder: the main character is not Joker!) and didn’t need anything more.  Erina and the main character also have these abilities built in—choosing them or not isn’t necessary.  I was playing on normal and imagine the healing situation changes a lot on merciless, but there’s just not enough tactical depth here to make that an interesting proposition.The game’s four “kingdoms” (palaces, but not) feature four bosses, two and a half of which are gimmick bosses you won’t beat with tactical gameplay.  The first will require narrative intervention, and the second is a matter of navigating from one end of a map to the other, only to be knocked back and be forced to repeat this (with different maps) twice.  The third boss is the only “honest” boss fight in the game, with the final boss also involving a gimmick to prevent damage to your party and deal it to him instead, but at least here the players trigger the gimmick themselves in a way that feels fairly satisfying.Given the depth of existing tactical RPGs, the hugely stripped-down nature of personas and the elemental damage they usually provide, and the diminished scope, Tactica feels like a wasted opportunity in a way other spinoffs like Persona 4: Arena didn’t.  A clear of a fighting game to see a character’s ending doesn’t take that long, and the Persona fighting games were excellent in their genre.  Tactica feels like a slog to get the story, despite how short it is, and while that story is well done, it isn’t worth full price with the game itself in such a middling state.(Edits for typos, grammar, and clarity)

_childDocuments_.review: While I can very much recommend Persona 5 Royal, and even Persona 5 Strikers as a sequel/spin-off, I sadly can't recommend Persona 5 Tactica.Persona 5 Tactica doesn't really capture any of Persona's essence. It's basically just a skin slapped on top of a tactics game. If you love those games, then I think you'll enjoy it. But I think they could've done way more with this game. Persona 5 Strikers wasn't just a Hack 'n Slash game, it implemented way more Persona elements like free-roaming in certain areas, a bigger story, and weaknesses. And I would've loved to see it here as well.I really tried to like this game, even forcing myself to keep playing because I love Persona so much, to try and capture some of that feeling. But that's the reason why I don't like it. Besides the style and the characters, it almost doesn't capture the essence of what makes Persona great. Also, the game is way too expensive for what you're getting. So even if you do like tactics games, get it only while it's on a huge discount. The story doesn't start strong, the enemies variety and the fights are very repetitive, and it really doesn't have a lot to offer.So like I said, I sadly can't recommend Persona 5 Tactica as a Persona fan. Instead, I'm waiting for the upcoming Persona 3 Reload, which I am very excited for.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game because I am a Fire Emblem fan. This game manages to overstay its welcome while also being way too short for 60 dollars. The story is fairly bland and predictable. The gameplay has the promise of being interesting but almost nothing is done with it. The core mechanics are interesting in their own right but the level design doesn't allow it to be as good as it could be. Every mission is the same, you have 2 classes of enemies that show up in every mission and 2 gimmick enemies that sometimes show up. The gameplay becomes a test of whether or not you can get good positioning in order to All-Out Attack and wipe the whole board. This would be fine if maybe 5 of the total 52 missions had this as their main objective but its every non-boss fight mission. Thats another thing that this game has does poorly, bosses. Every boss in this game is a slogfest that comprises 20ish turns of just wailing on the boss while positioning to dodge attacks. This applies to EVERY boss in the game except for 1.  The way personas and persona fusion are implemented in the game is boring. It feels like a chore when you have to wait about 20 seconds for the game to play the animation and then subsequently load the velvet room for you to just fuse 1 or 2 personas and then swap where they are equipped. One of the only character progression mechanics I actually enjoyed was the skill tree with free respecs. The story is nothing to write home for. Once the premise is revealed its predictable until the very end. Unless you are a big persona fan and a bigger tactical RPG fan, don't buy this game, especially not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Very underwhelming and disappointed with this one - I thought this would be a large tactical adventure using Persona's fun system of exploiting enemies' weaknesses. Gone are the intricate fusion mechanics, now in its place is the inheritance of a single skill plus a unique skill, which might not even be that good anyway; fusing a stronger persona barely means anything now, outside of an incremental increase in HP, SP, and damage.There are no more elemental strengths and weaknesses, so spells just do ailments now, but their distinctions barely matter, so there's no smart decision in choosing the right skills to use. The menus are clunky and unintuitive, the shop menu is separate from the Velvet Room menu for some bizarre reason, you can buy weapons from the shop, but only sell them at the Velvet Room, and you can't dismiss personas whilst IN the Velvet Room - You know, the one place in the game where it would make sense for you to free up space for more personas?The story is predictable, and the two new characters aren't interesting whatsoever. If you've played a single persona game before, you'll probably guess the plot of the game within a few hours. The final stretch of the game is just a "fight the bosses again" but this time, it loses the impact because Toshiro had already come to terms with his past.Given how many people in Japan there are, you'd think the Phantom Thieves would be pulled into the psyche of someone for a whacky adventure every other day, but no, it's only when Atlus wants to milk this franchise even further.Don't buy this game at full price, it's not worth it. If you're really curious, wait for the game to drop to £10 or something, but at full price, I'm going to have to give this a hard thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: A boring, bland tactical RPG on which they slapped a Persona 5 skin.As a big Persona 5 fan, I was thrilled to see a new iteration of this game. Striker left me a little yearning but it still delivered something at least correct.This did not.The difficulty is non-existent as well as the game content. The personas ? Luck of the draw, not like they make a big difference. The tactics ? You master the Triple Threat Attack, you beat the game (with a few exceptions). The bosses ? Tedious yet easy. The few "original" mechanics are either overused or underused.Without rushing, while making sure I watch every discussions, try to 3-star every missions, making sure every character is usable, do every side quests, I still manage to finish it quickly (Not necessarily a bad thing considering how uninteresting this game is).Everything that makes Persona 5 Persona 5 is gone. The stylish movements, the astonishing backgrounds, the characters side story, an interesting story with twists, everything 'extra' is missing. It felt like some sort of weird mini-game.It can still be an enjoyable game but wait until it dropped at 1/4 of the price because it's not worth more. Personally, the only good thing I got from this is the fact it made me want to play Persona 5 again. Well, that and the wedding skit.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A bunch of really cool ideas, executed as though the dev team was trying to see how little effort they could get away with while still making bank on Persona 5's brand.The Good:- Positional cover-based combat with mechanics that HEAVILY reward smart plays.- Elemental weaknesses are replaced with interesting status effects, so choosing your party is less about covering bases than planning your strategic approach - shock effects control movement, wind inflicts knockback, etc.- Characters can move freely within their movement range until they perform an action, giving you plenty of opportunities for planning and experimenting with positioning before you commit.- Seriously, this could have been really cool if they went harder in the X-COM direction. A team of sneaky underdogs abusing status effects and cover mechanics to bring down numerically superior foes? When it works, it feels fantastic.The Bad:- Flanking barely matters. Hitting a unit that's completely out of cover gives the attacker a whole-ass extra turn, which feels  but for some reason leaning gently against a wall protects you against that even if there is physically nothing between you and your opponent.- The soundtrack sounds like if someone asked an AI to write tech support on-hold music in the style of Persona 5.- The story is bland, sub-fanfic tier writing.- The game really, really wants you to pay attention to as much story as possible, to the point where you can only skip cutscenes until the point where you need to make a (wholly pointless) dialog choice.- Missions are too short to really get invested in. Considering how uninteresting the story is, it's frustrating that at this point I think my gameplay has been about 40% gameplay, 40% cutscene, 10% load times, and 10% menus.- Personas are boring now. Every character can use an extra one, therefore every character SHOULD use an extra one, therefore you're gonna spend way more time in the Velvet Room, but those sub-personas are significantly less impactful so it's ironically much less beneficial.- All-Out Attacks feel clunky, they often force you to ruin your positioning just to get slightly better attack coverage, and they don't even have the stylish finisher animations.- Enemy AI is terrible. Like... when units can freely reposition until they commit, the enemy shouldn't get bottlenecked, ever. Instead it happens like once a mission.- Seriously, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ story. Persona 5 was fantastic. Even Strikers was pretty good. This one is about the Phantom Thieves getting isekai'd for some reason, but luckily the Velvet Room got isekai'd too, and also they met a totally unrelated politician who also got isekai'd on a different occasion. The story tries to dangle so many plot hooks in front of you but it doesn't actually follow through on enough to make it feel like anything matters.- The whole game pauses if you alt-tab. Including loading screens. Just... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The Ugly:- The art style. It's not just chibi, it's DK Mode.- Joker's silhouettes in the menus have red faces for some reason.- There's a character who doesn't have a persona, she instead has "arts," but the default keybind for it is F so her menu helpfully offers the option to use "FArts" every time she's selected.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off with the positives.Small party size:If you've ever played a strategy rpg before, you've probably played fire emblem. If you have, you'll know what I mean when I say that big party sizes can be a massive pain. Moving 10-13 party members every turn just sucks. Thankfully you only have three party members in this game so turns go by pretty quickly.EXP share:This game has full exp share for the whole game and oh my god it's so good. Atlus PLEASE put this in every persona game from here on in it's like the ONE thing I don't like about strikers.Art style:What you see in the trailers is what you get. A lot of people really hate it but I actually kinda like it....and that's about it. The rest of this review will be dedicated to the major aspects of the game and why they're... not so great.MUSIC:Even if a persona spinoff isn't up to par in the gameplay or story department, I at least expect the music to be good. That said, the music in this game is honestly super disappointing. None of the tracks ever stood out to me as even "good". Even Lyn's vocal tracks sound lackluster to me for some reason. Obviously this is super subjective so before you take my word for it, you should look up some tracks on youtube. If you do, you'll probably see what I mean.GAMEPLAY:This game is easy. Really easy. I played the entire game on the highest difficulty and I only ever lost ONCE. If you've ever played a strategy rpg, you're probably shocked to hear that because srpgs are games of trial and error. This game is just that easy.There are three ways to do damage in this game: melee, guns, and skills. Skills are broken. Skills:- break cover- are AOE- apply a status effect- deal WAY more damage than melee and gunSkills let you avoid the mechanics of the game way too much. Opponent is behind cover? Spam skills. Should you be behind cover? Nah, just use a skill and apply a broken status effect. Damage up close? Skills. Damage from afar? Skills.The only drawback of skills is that they cost SP but there are way too many ways to regenerate SP for that to matter.The main reason why this game is so easy is because you can use skills and the enemies for the most part can't.There's also the horrible AI. The AI of this game often feels like it intentionally goes easy on you whenever you make a fatal mistake (remember I played on the highest difficulty). Even through the braindeadness of this game, none of your mistakes get punished so you truly can just turn your brain off.Ok so the game is easy but does that mean it's not fun? Kinda, yeah. It's ok at first but at a certain point you just get tired of how repetitive it is since you never have to think and the optimal strategy is always the same. This game does NOT benefit from being 30 hours long.There are some other problems, too. Persona fusion is limited and bland. Lack of enemy variety is a big problem (most maps only have two types of enemies). The bosses are really gimmicky but somehow not interesting at all. There's a pointless boss rush at the end of the game that only serves to pad play time. There's not much to like here.STORY:There's nothing to say here, really. I'm not sure why, but Atlus spinoff stories never seem to get anywhere close to the level of entertainment or engagement that I get from mainline persona games. Maybe it's the lack of social links? Maybe it's because there aren't many new characters? I'm not sure, but aside from all of that, this story just isn't that good. The whole story is about one new character's arc and it's really not that interesting so the overall story is kinda boring and flat. Even by persona spinoff standards, this story isn't very good.CONCLUSION:Overall this game just isn't good. Even if you're a P5 superfan (like me), this game isn't worth your money.This is the part where most reviews say it'll be worth it if it goes on sale for $20 or something, but I honestly don't think this game is worth 30 hours of your time no matter how much it costs.

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed it so far. A few things it's not, there is zero walking around town, zero socials, (seemingly) zero minigames, Straight up, it may have the primary P5 team and the title but, this isn't Persona. What it is, is a fun little TRPG. Mind you, your part is only 3 members at a time which is very remarkably small for the genre. This game playfully enters the realm of games such as Shining Force, Fire Emblem, Bahamut Lagoon, Tactics Ogre, Final Fantasy Tactics, Disgaea, Xcom, Banner Saga and Valkyria Chronicles to name a few. In short, I am biased because I have loved this genre since I was a little kid in the early 90s. Some of those titles did have more RPG elements than this does though, which has about none. Story wise, so far anyway, 15 hours in I'd say it's uh, kinda what you might expect out of a Chibi Persona spin off, it's not bad but, it won't be remembered. New Characters seem fine, I'm not personally impressed but, the memes are already flying. The art style very simple but, clean and well made towards their clear goal. In my opinion it looks good but, it all feels pretty darn low budget for the launch price of this title in 2023. The audio, well the music is great as one expects of this series. The VAs, if you're here you probably already know them well, love them or hate them. The graphics options are straight forward and simple, there really just isn't a lot to micro here. I some scenes are locked to 60 but, generally I lock 120fps (my display limit) at 4k resolution with 125% render scale and SMAA. I could probably reduce all that significantly with minimal difference in the final product. My rig:Ryzen 5800X3D3080 12gb32 gb 990 ProNovember 22, 2023 Update: I finished the main story. No technical hiccups on my end. The story I think, was overall enjoyable with a conclusion I found satisfying. It is nothing to write home about but, perfectly serviceable. If you do all the optional quests I will say, the gains from them in total bring down the overal difficulty significantly towards the end. At 34 hours for the main story with me really, dragging my feet and taking my time I can't say it was a whole lot of game for the launch price but, I still have no regrets. The battles were a lot of fun for me which, is completely key as this game is just battles, cut scenes and menus.

_childDocuments_.review: "Oh wow! I love Persona games, and I love tactics games! So this is like Persona 5, but tactics based, right?"Right! With just a few small exceptions. You remember the cast from P5? They're here, but... They're now drawn in the same style as everything in "The Murder of Sonic The Hedgehog". Chibi, for lack of another word. Their personalities are now 1 dimensional cariacatures of themselves. They don't develop more depth as you develop relationships with them. Matter of fact, you don't develop relationships at all really. They're almost parodies of what you might be remembering them as."Huh, that bites. Is there still a vibrant city to explore that's full of neat little things at certain times and almost has a life of it's own? There's gotta be right? And stuff you can only do at certain times of certain days? Right?"Not one bit. No exploring, no calendar or clock keeping time. You got your home base, where you can shop and do other party management stuff and sit thru some visual novel scenes (with those 1 dimensional parody characters mind you) that I presume are the replacement for the relationship building system."Wow...okay... But there's gotta be tons of cool monsters to fight right? Either the set from P5 or the ones from the previous games, right? And ya gotta find and exploit their elemental and status weaknesses, like usual, right?"Counting bosses, I'm pretty positive there are fewer than 20 distinct types of enemies to fight. Maybe fewer than 10 if we don't count bosses. Elements and status effects exist, but aren't meaningful or necessary in any real way. By and large you can ignore them here. It's a tactics based game, but the actual tactical decisions are far simpler than in any of the Persona games. To compare to actual tactics games...the whole thing is probably on par with the difficulty level of Xcom's title screen. "Hrm...Xcom was hard, but the title screen was pretty easy to get through... Oh! I know! There's gotta be a really thought provoking story that touches on many larger concepts like the nature of the mind, subconscious, and self, right? Or maybe offers some intriguing moral/ethical points to mull over?"Nah. At least, nothing you haven't literally already seen in P5, and a decaf watered down version of even that."So...it sounds like it has none of the things that really define the Persona series, and isn't even a very good tactics game."Correct. But except for those things, it's totally a tactics version of P5!If on the other hand, you aren't expecting a tactics version of P5 and just treat this game as something totally unrelated to that series, And aren't expecting the sort of challenging or interesting tactical gameplay you might find in Xcom or Fell Seal or any other real tactics game, and it's on sale for like 10 bucks or so, you might find this one amusing for a while."But wait a minute...you say all that, but it looks like you spent 60 something hours playing this game!"I finished it, hoping it would eventually get better. It didn't really. As for playtime...I've no idea my actual number of hours spent playing, but it's nowhere near what's shown. I've got a habit of leaving games running while I go run errands or cook dinner or do housework or whatever else...and I get distracted easily; especially with games that aren't very good. So don't expect anything close to that for a single playthru, and there's not really any reasons to play more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this, Then a little let down, Then absolutely addicted.I love tactical Rpgs and I love atlus games. In my book this is a match made in heaven. I was let down in the beginning hours, because the first quarter of the game really holds your hand, introducing you to each individual mechanic meticulously one at a time. It was very slow, and taking so long to be able to break the mold and play around with the levels yourself mad the game feel very shallow and one dimensional. From around the 15th level or so though, it really becomes massively engaging, trying to finish runs in as few turns as possible. Some quests even require you to finish in one turn, and i found these to be awesome, blending tactical battles with almost puzzle game mechanics. I was kinda against the whole chibi art style, but honestly it really grew on me after awhile. I still probably would have preferred the original persona 5 art style, but one of the game devs made a good point about this art style was used to increase visibility of the characters on such large maps. Either way its charming and cute and i like it.The story feels a little cartoony at times, and for the most part this game is a lot more light hearted than P5R, but the serious points HIT when they come. This is a surprisingly engaging and rewarding story and you really do feel it by the end. I was begging for that after the credits scene. I really liked the new characters introduced in this game and i hope to see them again. Erina needs to be in the persona 5 fighting game if we ever get it. lolAll in all this is a great game and well worth it for a persona/atlus fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, now that I've 100%'d the game, I can give a review.Long story short, I wouldn't pay full price for this game.  There's not a whole lot of content, you're better off buying a mainline Persona game, you'll get much more gameplay.  But at the same time, the gameplay loop was starting to get repetitive in the end, so maybe it being short is a good thing.My biggest gripe with this game compared to other tactical games, is that there's no building your characters.  Every character has a fixed skill tree, which can be fully unlocked by the end of the game.  That gives you little reason to re-play the game via new game+, except to finish getting achievements.  And on the topic of achievements- the game doesn't give you enough gold.  This becomes super noticeable once you start hunting achievements.  Every achievement costs gold, and I had to replay the game three times to get enough gold to buy them all.

_childDocuments_.review: The plot is an extremely typical fantasy spin off. The Phantom Thieves are dragged away to an unknown world for an unknown reason, to solve the problem of a couple of new unknown characters. Their plight eventually gets interesting, but cliche tropes like amnesia, mind control, and pointless dialog choices, make story lose a lot of impact early on and I found myself skipping a ton of unimportant fluff by the end. There is really only one solution to solving most of the combat encounters: force the enemy out of cover with  skill, hit them for a Once More, and then make as wide an All-Out Attack as you possibly can. All the skills do the same thing and different elements only lead to minor differences in secondary effects; there are no elemental weaknesses and therefore no real incentive to deeply customize your skill builds. This is further reinforced with Tactica's Persona system. Personas can only have 2 skills total, so they mostly boil down to being additional HP and SP for your units to wear. The UI, music, and visuals are all very strong, but only if you're into that. The chibi style is used throughout the game, even during the most serious moments, so the off-proportions can be a deal breaker for some.Aside from that, there are a ton of small issues that eventually tun a minor itch into a serious blemish over the 20+ hour campaign including but not limited to: Why do I buy gear at the shop, but sell them at the velvet room? Why are there two different tabs for looking at quests, but only one actually lets me do them? Why does the game not ask me if I want to equip my newly formed persona when I used my old to make it? Why, during weapon crafting, does the game not ask me if I want to buy a weaker persona instead of using my high leveled one I'm currently using?

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of feels like I'm playing a fanfic everyone knew wouldn't sell well by itself so they slapped the Persona 5 name on it and added the Phantom Thieves as an after thought to get people to buy it.As far as I played into the game, you could have taken the Phantom Thieves out of the story and would have taken less tweaks than adding them into a plot that seemed way too forced and predictable. The Phantom Thieves generally take a backseat in the story, which makes no sense when it's supposed to be about them. Erina even gives Toshiro control over the Rebels and the Thieves -without asking beforehand- just because he had one strategic idea that happened to work out, though he does none of the fighting himself and the Thieves won many missions before that. There's no exploration -like in previous games- what so ever. Half the time I skip over the dialogue due to disinterest, which I found jarring because I was very invested in Royal and Strikers. Joker doesn't even have access to Personas in the same way he used to. He can only use one at a time, so gathering all of them up felt meaningless. Yes, everyone can now have sub-personas, but it was Joker's thing to make him the Trickster and the protagonist, not a background character with no real reason to be included, like he came off as -to me- in this game.   The plot has recycled storytelling from the Persona 5\Royal, which came across as an attempt at eliciting an emotional response from the player as well as trying to build common ground with the Thieves and Toshiro. Instead, it felt like a story that should have either ended before it began or gone through rigorous editing to ensure this game wasn't Persona5\Royal just under a different name with enough tweaks to try hiding it, but didn't due to popularity. The only difference in all three games was the turn-base combat to hack and slash to tactical, otherwise the plot remains generally the same throughout all three games. Beat up palace\jail\kingdom owners until you reach the god born of desires at the end, kick his butt and end the game.  I mean, they had that whole set up with Akechi they could have played off of or brought Sophie back with a new issue needing fixing. Heck, even had them both come back. Anything, instead of releasing a new game that feels more like it was meant as a DLC for Persona5\Royal.

_childDocuments_.review: Atlus is still riding on the Persona 5 train to milk the fans around to world, but is this game worth your time and money ?Story : 5/5At first I wanted to knock off 1 point since the game is ~25 hours long and costs 60 €, but I decided against it since the story is so good.To be honnest the story takes a bit of time to get started, but it knows how to hook you in with good character progression for our 2 new character.It has to right twists and uses our knowledge of the P5 lore to subvert our expectations. I didn't expect to be so hooked but I liked the story a lot and I even shed some tears.The story is a bit "too much" like Persona 5 (rebellion, will power, fighting oppression,..) but you won't see a Frenchie like me complain about thatGameplay : 4/5Another spin-off where Atlus shows us a different way to play with the Phantom Thieves. But unlike the fast paced "beat them all" Persona 5 Strikers, P5T is a tactical turn by turn combat where the caracters move on a grid and try to make sick combos.Just like in Persona 5, you need to knock down you opponent and surround the ennemies for an All-out-Attack. But instead of basic weakness to elements, this time you need to get the ennemies out of cover to knock them down.It makes for quite an addictive gameplay with a lot of satisfying combos to pull off.Music : 5/5Legendary composer Shoji Meguro is working on Metaphor Re:Fantazio so his assistant was put in charge of the music for this opus.Of course Lyn and Lotus Juice are still back with banger songs, wether those are meant to be chill, sad or nervous. The game also uses some songs fromn P5, but very sparsely so it leaves a lot of room for the new songs to shine. My favourites are "Got your Tail" and "Truth or Dare".The musics are not as great as in P5, but it's not like it's a feat that was ever done by anyone so it would be harsh to take down a point for that.Art : 4/5The chibi artstyle takes a bit of time to get used to, but it's not that bad. What's bad are some models that have comically thin arms and huge hands.This style is perfect to do comedy, but kinda hard to create any tension with. You eventually get used to it and the story grips you in anyway, but it makes it hard to take anything seriously during the first few hours.Special mention for the animation which is really good especially for the last boss cutscene that goes hard on the animation level.Overall note : 18/20I liked this game a lot, it knows how to play with my emotions and how to make me feel like a mastermind when doing sick combos.The game is a bit short for a 60 € price tag, so I would suggest to wait for it to drop to 30~40 € during a sale unless you miss the Phantom Thives that much.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels more like a puzzle game rather than a strategy game. The main gameplay loop is attempting to combo the majority of the enemies as efficiently as possible, leading to a great incentive to finish levels as quickly as possible. A low turn count playthrough of the game could be enjoyable, but the game lacks enough depth to warrant the effort in my opinion. As of writing the review, I'm about 1/3rd of the way through the game and fought the first major boss. I'll continue going through it eventually, but finding the motivation is taxing when there are more enjoyable games out there.It's great if you're looking for more Persona, but this is a pretty lackluster standalone experience. As a tactics game, there are much better options out there. Definitely not worth the full $60 price-tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m about 7 hours in to Persona 5 Tactica so this is more like my impression than a review, but my impression is that it’s inconsequential.The gameplay is composed of turn-based tactical missions which only take minutes apiece to complete. You might be tasked with reaching an end goal in a certain number of turns, or destroying an object on the map which has more HP than your standard enemy, or to just clear the board of any opponents. The varied objectives are appreciated, but when coupled with the fact that the enemy AI will sometimes run up against walls turn after turn while you merrily make your way to the goal, the encounters start to feel very samey rather quickly. If you do happen to make a mistake, you can undo your entire turn without penalty – which makes the game approachable, but also entirely too easy even on higher difficulties.The beloved characters from Persona 5 also feel much too similar to one another in gameplay. Rather than exploiting enemy weaknesses with skills they’re vulnerable against, I find myself reaching for Garu magic as much as possible to knock enemies around the board while simultaneously downing them – which sets groups of them up for easy one-mores and devastating all-out attacks. Crucially, every single character can now use sub-Personas, so you can load up Garu magic skills on everyone and toss enemies into little piles that you blow up. It would be funny if it wasn’t so clearly overpowered.Each session of gameplay is bookended with some kind of conversation or story beat with a handful of new characters in tow. The stylized, cartoonish 2D sprites are expressive, but it’s hard to feel like they don’t hold their own against Persona 5 itself, or even the spinoffs like Dancing in Starlight or Strikers. Perhaps it would feel better if the writing was sharper or heavier, but so far, the deep emotions that typically course through the veins of this franchise’s mainline entries are completely absent. Hopefully there will be gravity to the story by the end.There are some redeeming factors to Persona 5 Tactica. The music feels like a collection of demos and b-sides to the original game’s soundtrack, but there are a few catchy standouts. The sidequests that occasionally pop up between story missions present far more of a challenge than anything else in the game and feel more like gripping puzzles than the trivial combat encounters you’re otherwise faced with. Additional rewards can be had for completing objectives beneath a certain number of turns or without incurring any deaths, so those can slightly increase the intensity of any given mission.If you’ve never played Persona 5, steer clear of this game. If you have played it and you’re really, really craving more of the Persona 5 cast even after finishing Royal and Strikers AND Dancing in Starlight, then Tactica might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but definitely did not live up to the expectations. To be clear, I very well knew this was not going to be as grand as P5R. The first two chapters are fun, learning the mechanics (which are well designed and fun), mastering them and some fun story build-up. After that, nothing new happens anymore...The story becomes very predictable and overly stretched out. There is for example 4 different long dialogue sections, which basically each said the same. I always like to listen to all voiced dialogues, but ended up skipping past some, since it didn't add anything anymore.After the first two chapters, combat starts to become repetitive as well, since there's no introduction of any new enemies or mechanics anymore.I wish I could like it more and did enjoy the first parts of the game, but it left me disappointed in the end and therefore I can't recommend it.
