_childDocuments_.review: I've heard some people say that they don't like the art direction of P5T which is fair, it's not for everyone. It's similar in style to Persona Q/Q2 and for a spinoff with this kind of combat system, I think it works really well. P5T doesn't take itself too seriously and the chibi art style adds charm to that. If you vibe with the art style, or even if you don't but are willing to look past it, there's a great game to be had here.The gameplay follows the template set out by games like Xcom but honestly, for me the game that resonates the most with P5T is Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle/Sparks of Hope (fantastic games btw). It almost feels like Atlus set out to put a Persona twist on those very games and I think they managed that to great effect.The story is interesting enough but isn't suited to newcomers to the series. Gameplay wise, I like that each character feels unique in the way their personas interact during battles. It feels like team composition matters and the ability to give an additional persona to each party member, not just Joker, is an interesting change. One of the highlights for me is the challenges. The challenges are essentially scenarios which require problem solving, there's usually one right way to complete the mission and figuring out the correct steps and executing the game plan is satisfying. Plus the rewards completing the challenges gives make it worthwhile as opposed to challenges being stuck on as an extra for no reason.And it goes without saying, the soundtrack goes hard as is the case with every Persona game. When it comes to soundtracks to set the tone and get you vibing, Persona does not miss.That said, one of my main gripes with P5T is the deluxe edition and dlc. I'm not a fan of day one dlc, or sparkly jazzy editions which come bundled with exclusives and extras that make you feel like you are missing out by not buying it. Being a big Persona fan, I caved and got the Digital Deluxe Edition. I have zero interest in the weapon pack or the Persona pack because I don't like dlc which gives me an early game advantage. I like a challenge and to earn my progress so to speak. The reason I picked up the deluxe edition was purely for the Repaint Your Heart dlc. Challenges with Akechi and Kasumi? I'm all over it. But I would argue this could have, and probably should have, been included in the base game, especially at the steep price for a spinoff. The upcoming P3: Reloaded offers various editions with various extras and dlc as well, something I would like Atlus to stop knuckling down on personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Real quick. I liked the game, but unless you're a personahead, this game isn't worth 60 bucks. It's a 40 dollar game.This is a pretty in-depth review after a full merciless playthrough. A quick summary of my thoughts is that the game doesn't put its best foot forward, with the first 10 hours or so spent on maps that are too flat and not enough enemy archetypes. However, once maps start becoming more restrictive and tactical towards the end of chapter 2, where you need to work hard to get into the positions that were just given to you before against brand new enemies that have abilities to control the field, it gets a lot better. The same goes for the story. It takes far too long to get going, and even when it does, your mileage varies heavily based on how much you resonate with the themes it presents. It relies heavily on the ideas it presents being intrinsically sad to get you emotional because it didn't have enough time to set them up properly. That said, I did resonate and I did enjoy the gameplay when it got better, so it's a thumbs up from me. If you want to know more, read ahead.The only gameplay worth talking about is the combat system. The day-to-day gameplay is replaced by conversations, and the persona fusion isn't deep enough in this game to talk about.The combat is another example of Persona 5's gameplay mechanics transferring well to a whole different genre, although in this case, it's a little more apparent that it's not quite the right fit. You'd think it's and XCOM like, but it's more similar to Mario x Rabbids. You have a team of 3 on handcrafted maps that have gimmicks and you need to efficiently kill everybody to fulfill objectives that give extra rewards. Your characters can move so long as they haven't attacked, meaning that they can get into a risky position for an all out attack and move to a safe spot after it's done. Speaking of the AOA...The Persona twist comes in the all out attack. Before I get into that, I need to explain how this game translated the knockdown mechanic from the original game. This game is unlike other grid based tactics game in that it only matters what angle people are attacked from if they're in full cover, which gives them full immunity to one angle of attack.However, being in cover gives people a "resist" status, and as long as people have that, they have resistance to damage. That means that you can be standing flank somebody and not deal full damage. Units that are at a higher elevation will also have resistance against normal attacks against anyone lower than them, though magic will still crit them if they're in the open.If somebody is attacked while they don't have the resist status, then they get crit and knocked down, and the attacker gets one more action. There are numerous ways to remove the status, like melee attack knockbacks, spell knockbacks, or various status effects. The coolest one is the follow-up attack, where you melee an enemy off a cliff to your ally, who crits them and gives the initiator a 1-more. If you're the one that knocked an enemy down, the character that has a 1-more can trigger an all out attack. A triangle is drawn between all three of your characters, and if the knocked down enemy is inside it, you can all out attack everybody within that triangle. The all out attack is the most powerful attack in the game and every single mechanic is balanced around it. Every character can heal when you AOA, so you're incentivized to play aggressively and just heal up with it. On any difficulty except merciless, it will oneshot the normal enemies and severely wound the elite ones (which is why I played through the game on merciless - it was too easy otherwise). It's a cool system that emphasizes efficient movement and there's a constant choice to be made between "Do I want my character in cover, or do I want them standing out in the open for this juicy AOA?". Not all your characters can have a 1-more, so you need to make sure that whatever character you use to set up the others for an AOA is in a good position so as to maximize coverage.Unfortunately, it also means that anybody with low movement or lacking any kind of set-up persona skills is screwed. Normal attacks and even engame magic simply can't match up to you just AOAing half the map. Not all status ailments are made equal, and the characters that specialize in the ones that don't set up are never a good pick. Haru (bless her soul), has the worst movement in the game, so it's hard to mechanically justify using her outside of achievement hunting. The new character, Erina, specializes in the forget status and has the only built in overwatch move, both of which do nothing to set up a 1-more. Even Joker is kinda meh, because his status is "Despair", which lets him run faster and further the next round, something that isn't all that useful next to simply killing the enemy here and now. The sub-persona can cover for them somewhat, but as sub-personas only have two skills in this game, only one of which is inheritable, you can only do so much, especially when the sub-personas are the only source of passive skills like exp+ or multihit damage+.On top of that, the AOA being so movement reliant means that whether an engagement is fun to play through or not is solely through the mission's map. Early on, maps are way, way too simple. They're flat and boring, and there's very few tactical choices to be made outside of "knock them out of cover and AOA". However, the later chapters have way more vertical maps with gimmicks that actually force you to change how you play. Enemies will be up against the edge of the map on a cliff, and you have to work to get to them. There will be elevators with switches that you have to fiddle with to open up a path.Of course, all of that goes out the window when it gets to the boss fights, all of which are extremely underwhelming. There's no strategy outside of buff up with Mataru, get in cover, and deal with whatever gimmick they spawn. It's boring.Side note: the quests in this game are more like puzzles that you have to find the right answer to. They're fun and require more thinking than most fights in the game.Without spoiling too much, it's pretty much just like the Persona Q sub series in that the whole game is just one giant character arc for a character that, while I liked him very much, will probably never appear again in the future. Every other character has pretty much nothing going on for them, they're just there to be a chaotic scooby gang. The character's arc gets a bit too long to get going, and the start of the arc is a little bit too insufferable. However, I really enjoyed the bits where the Phantom Thieves try to help him work his way through his issues. Each Thief uses their respective struggles from the main game to relate to him and share with him how they got through it, which I thought was a great use of the characters. The heavier moments that come really do come, and I enjoyed them when they did. I just wish they were dotted throughout the game more effectively instead of being shoved into the back half.Outside of the story and characters, the worldbuilding is extremely messy, but easily handwaved away by the fact that it's all in the metaverse and metaphorical anyways. And, big spoiler alert, you do kill god in the end. You know, just like every single Persona game.I really thought I wouldn't like the art style, but I was pleasantly surprised. The simpler art style lends itself great to varied extremely dynamic full body poses in the game's conversations that I thought really brought each character out. It blows Royal out of the water in that regard. The vocal tracks of the game are an insane bop, but I really can't remember any of the other tracks even if you put a gun to my head.

_childDocuments_.review: P5T is another solid entry in a long line of Persona spin-offs which is, in my opinion, certainly worth looking into for anyone who seeks something outside of the 100+ hour long experiences that mainline games provide.  First things first, Tactica's gameplay (which does kind of resemble XCOM series) is actually surprisingly good with a lot of room for player creativity thanks to the ability to mix and match different characters with their own unique skills and weapons as well as equipping them with additional personas of your own choice thanks to the Sub Persona system that came straight from Persona Q (which I hope we're going to see on Steam one day) for almost every single level in the game. The important part to point out here is that unlike in PQ, this time around everyone get experience regardless whether they were in the active party or not during the battle, meaning you're not longer encouraged to stick to the same few characters for the optimal play. The story, unfortunately, doesn't really do anything exactly new, repeating a number of tropes we've already seen in previous games. I wouldn't call it outright bad by any means though, as the characters of Erina and Toshiro, their dynamic and development are interesting to observe and overall, there are some engaging and funny moments sprinkled throughout the plot. Another thing worth mentioning is that a lot of people weren't happy with Tactica's artstyle starting with the very day it was announced, and while I wasn't a particular fan of it at first either, after playing the game I have to say that it's grown on me and quite fast too. As for the OST, it definitely made some additions to my playlist for the nearby future, especially with songs like Got Your Tail, Truth or Dare and Inextinguishable. I could go further into some positives and negatives of this game, but quite frankly I doubt that it will have a significant effect on whether someone is going to want to play it or not. The major point of contention, however, is Tactica's default asking price, which is quite steep and perhaps too much so, but with a discount I think it's well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Persona 5 Tactica is a Strategy RPG with a Persona coat of paint on it. If that is what you're after, this certainly delivers you that. The game is good, the combat flows well, and the story is hit and miss. It's worth a pick-up on sale if you're not a fan of both the genre and the franchise, but only one or the other.Story: I'll keep this as spoiler free as possible by censoring the spoilers. This game takes place after defeating  in Persona 5. The DLC, "Paint your Heart" however, does not start at that same point. Instead, that DLC story begins before . This does affect the timing of the two stories, as the DLC technically happens before the main game. Onto the actual plot, then. It's a plot of amnesia and working through repressed trauma. The way it is handled is hit or miss, and starts pretty slowly. It only picks up in the third area, and even then it's only interesting for around 10 hours of gameplay.6/10.Music: Persona 5's music continues to be great. Lyn is doing the vocals in this game, and the music is superb. "Inextinguishable" is the standout track for me personally, though the credits song "Far to you" is also great. Classics like "Beneath the Mask" (though with a lofi remix) and "Aria of the Soul" are back as well. The ambient music during battles or talking scenes can leave a bit to be desired though. The game very much sounds like a Persona 5 game, and that's a great thing. 8.5/10, good soundtrackCharacters: This game introduces 2 new characters to the Phantom Thieves, both early on. Erina and Toshiro. Erina reminds me a great deal of Chie from Persona 4, but no such comparison comes to mind for Toshiro. The game revolves around these two characters and their development, which is handled well. Without spoiling the game, Toshiro goes through a satisfying arc and Erina is handled about as well as she could've been considering her arc.The rest of the cast is the same as Persona 5's. Morgana is still exceptionally annoying, and Futaba will not shut up in battle for 2 seconds. As for the DLC, the 2 missing phantom thieves (Crow and Violet) are the main driving force there.8/10, Persona casts are usually great, this isnt an exception.graphics: Very different art style from what we're used to seeing from Atlus. Instead of the usual anime style, it went far more of a Chibi direction. The thing you'll notice hte most are the character's eyes. It doesn't look bad, but this style also doesn't do it for me personally. It was made to age well, and I think in 5 years it wont look any worse than it does currently.Level designs are good, the visual settings are great as well. The effects from the various skill are well done and there aren't any obvious issues with things not fitting into the style of the game. That being said, more than 6 enemy types would've been appreciated. The game can feel extremely repetitive due to lack of variance in what you're fighting.Graphics 5/10. Meh.Audience: Older teens to adults. There is language, though no F bombs like Strikers had. Nothing flagrantly sexual other than a select few personas, but you rarely see the persona artwork anyway because of how the game itself plays.18+Gameplay: It's a Strategy RPG. cover mechanics, pushes, AOE barrels/abilities, along with the usual SMT buffs, make Persona 5 Tactica play in an intriguing way. The downside to this approach is that Persona skills bypass sightlines, which makes the game laughably easy. There is a one-more system in place like all SMT games, and the gameplay loop is solid enough. Complete stages, fuse personas, make weapons, upgrade skills, do a quest or two, repeat. 7/10, alright.Difficulty: As I said in the gameplay section, this game is laughably easy. Regeneration from All-Out-Attacks, ending the turn behind cover, and various persona traits make it exceptionally difficult to even lose a single party member. Not to mention how overtuned the healing skills are. Play this game at a higher difficulty and it'll feel so much more rewarding.3/10, raise the difficulty.Play Time: About 24 hours. I'll be finishing my 100% of this game shortly, which requires NG+, but a standard run through of the game should take you around 24 hours depending on how much you want to grind.Price: Get it on sale. If it ever drops to about $30, thats the most I'd pay for it if you aren't an ATLUS/Persona/Strategy RPG fan.Bugs: Yeah, he's a persona in the game. Oh, gameplay bugs. None that i encountered, which was great to see. The game could freeze up occasionally, but it never crashed or had an otherwise catastrophic error.10/10.Final Score: 7/10. Only for fans of Persona that also are interested/fans in strategy RPGs. it's a safe skip if you're not truly invested in either. It's nowhere near as good of a spin-off game as Strikers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just okay, and yet this is the first turn based tactics game that I've finished. Despite little experience in the genre I played all but the first couple battles on merciless difficulty and found it way too easy. Enemy variety is very poor with most battles having the same two enemies and your best strategy every fight is to get an "all out attack" by surrounding enemies with three squad members as it deals massive damage to a wide area of enemies for no SP cost. These attacks can be done nearly every turn by stringing together "one more" moves awarded for attacking enemies out of cover, enabling squad member to perform another action as well as resetting their movement. By daisy chaining these together each party member can get into a perfect position to pull off a "all out attack" almost every turn and finishing battles within a couple of moves. Admittedly, pulling these off is fun, and it became a challenge to see how few turns I could clear each battle in, but I feel like the whole system could've been so much better.One thing that helps pulling off these plays feel fun and streess free is how all characters can move around without becoming locked into position until after you take an action. You get three members in your squad, all of which can equip Personas that give bonus HP/SP plus extra active or passive abilities. A couple of missions during the DLC I forgot to equip any persona making the game significantly more challenging. It's possible the game orginally intended for only Joker to equip Persona, and then this was later expanded to everyone with minimal play testing and that's why the game is so easy? Who knows.Each kingdom (this game's version of a dungeon) introduces new environmental mechanics unique to that Kingdom and usually a couple new enemies. Despite this, most missions you'll be fighting the same two enemies repeatedly which quickly feels dull. Boss fights are hit and miss with some using the tactics gameplay in unique ways, and others are disapointing variations of basic enemies and environments.In between battles there's basic visual novel style story telling with generic 2D backdrops instead of the 3D character models common in persona games. This makes sense as there's no hub worlds to explore: equipment purchasing, side quests and so forth are access entirely through menus. There's also optional challenge missions some of which where the most fun battles I had in the game each requiring you to min-max nearly every move, or use your abilities in creative ways you wouldn't think of in normal battles, to finish in a limited number of turns; these kinda felt like puzzles as there's a finite number of ways to complete them yet some people may find these frustrating. Dialogue acompanying the side quests is usally interesting enough but the main story is a little dissapointing.There's no character development done to the original Phantom Thieves crew with the story focusing heavily on two new characters. Unfortunately, I found both of them a little too serious, like Makoto but turned up to eleven; by the end of the story I like them more but it took a little too long to get there. I also found myself missing the big social events to lighten the mood. Fundamentally though, I feel like setting the game after the events of the main game but before Royal / Strikers is a little dull and we already kinda know nothing major can happen. I would've prefered it to be set as a new entry in the timeline after Strikers to see how everyone is getting on 1-2 years after Strikers.Overall, I still enjoyed Tactica but it's perhaps overpriced by 30 to 40 percent and would only recommend to anyone who's played the other two Persona 5 games. The Repaint Your Heart DLC is great and in some ways I prefered the story / new characters here to the main game as well as the two new battle music tracks that are absolute bangers. I was reluctant to use the other DLC for bonus Weapons / Personas until I had unlocked something with comparable stats legitametly. The weapon skins looked cool but where quickly replaced by better ones so would've prefered them as weapon / character skins that leave gameplay unaffected?

(ฅ'ω'ฅ)Persona 5 Tactica marks an adventurous turn for the revered Persona series, intertwining the charm of its universe with the thrill of tactical combat. This game invites players to lead an uprising, assembling a team of heroes from the beloved series. With an all-new story, the game promises a blend of emotional narrative and challenging turn-based battles.The game's strengths are evident in its dynamic combat system, which allows players to utilize Personas and a variety of weapons, adding a layer of depth and strategy. The return of fan-favorite characters and the introduction of new allies and foes enrich the experience, providing both nostalgia and novelty.The music, a signature element of the Persona series, continues to shine here. Fans have lauded the soundtrack as a high point, with familiar tunes and new compositions setting an immersive and engaging tone. Additionally, the early purchase bonuses, including additional Personas, add a tempting incentive for series enthusiasts.However, not all is perfect in the world of Persona 5 Tactica. Some players have encountered technical difficulties, such as game crashes and performance issues, which detract from the overall experience. The use of Denuvo anti-tamper technology has been a point of contention, with some users experiencing problems starting the game.Moreover, the decision to include certain characters and content as paid DLC on day one has raised eyebrows. While these additions are exciting for fans, their placement behind a paywall has sparked discussions about content accessibility and value for money.In conclusion, Persona 5 Tactica is a commendable spin-off that successfully marries the series' narrative depth with strategic gameplay. While it excels in delivering a compelling story and engaging combat, it's not without its technical and content-related shortcomings. For fans of the series and newcomers alike, this game offers a unique experience, though it might be wise to wait for technical issues to be resolved or for a sale. As it stands, Persona 5 Tactica is a bold step in a new direction for the Persona universe, worthy of attention despite its imperfections.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: This game is unfinished. Not in the traditional buggy, unoptimized way, but in a "nothing was balanced or tweaked" way. This game is brain dead, offering no challenge in any way even on the hardest difficulty. A few game mechanics and some incredibly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ai are at fault here. It's insane how some of these things were implemented.Cover is implemented in the weirdest way in P5T. Cover is segmented into half cover and full cover. Half cover basically reduces all damage by like 50%, even if the enemy is shooting you from the side or back. Full cover will nullify damage from the front, and will reduce damage from the side and back by 50%. This makes, ABSOLUTELY, no sense. Having cover reduce damage by 50% regardless of if you're being flanked or not just removes all complexity, positioning, and depth from these kinds of games. The only thing that matters to this game is that you have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wall on one of the four sides of your character, and then you get the benefit of cover. This is the primary reason the game is so brain dead, positioning just doesn't matter in this game. You'll never be meaningfully punished or rewarded for good positioning and flanking.The enemy types are also are very bad for a tactics game. There are like, 5-6 enemy types for the entire game. The musketeer, shotgunner and rifleman are all functionally the same, but with different skins. They have slight stat differences, but nothing that will ever change your strategy or force you to play around. There is the grenadier, who will counter attack once per round any enemy that attacks him in a certain radius.  This enemy is close to being good, but this enemy's ai is some of worst I've seen like ever. He can't benefit from cover, but he seems to have the AI of the basic enemies, so he will regularly seek it out anyway. If you have the high ground on him, he won't seek a way to get to you, and instead just run at the wall of the high ground you're on. I think this is a bug, but for the first 25 levels of the game he just wouldn't melee attack me. He would get in range of my units and just sit there...doing nothing.Drummers are the support enemy, but their heals and buffs are too weak to ever really matter in the game. Bosses are pretty lame, and their AI are almost never designed to utilize their skills.On top of this, the basic enemy types will often still spend a turn shooting you in full cover even though it will do no damage to you. They seem to only flank you if they can do so in one move. Overall, the ai is way too simplistic, and the enemy types have no impact on gameplay. It's just such a shame because the framework for a good game is here. The skills, character mechanics, and progression is all really fun, but all feel meaningless when there isn't any challenge. You'll feel no reason to improve your skills and gear when you'll just obliterate enemies regardless.Most of my other problems with the game have been extensively mentioned in other reviews, the price especially being something you should consider. There's no way I can recommend this game even if it's on sale though. It's just unbelievably brain dead, and that's really ironic for a tactics game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I love Persona 5 beyond anything and I played all the modern Fire Emblems and this sounded like the perfect game for me. I wanted to hang out with mu favorite characters again.Story:In principle I like the story premise. The revolutionary themes are cool and the story of Toshiro definitely has a few very interesting plot points. In practice, however, it just didn’t work for me. The presentation is very barebones and even though I am not an expert it feels like the writing quality is just not even close to the main game. Everything felt more like filler and I ended up clicking away a lot of the talks.Gameplay:The round based tactical gameplay matches the Persona 5 gameplay astoundingly well. The one-more team attacks are all very cool. However, I feel like the personas feel very detached and unnecessary. I think you can perfectly play through the game without ever visiting the velvet room and just use the personas of the characters. The shop for weapons also is just another click to spend the money, but there are no interesting decisions. Overall the difficulty is too low and difficulty settings don’t make the game more complex just more tedious. On a bright side the side quest missions are nice small puzzles. Not really difficult either, but I enjoyed solving them and it feels great to clear an entire map in one move for example. This game had so much potential. Unfortunately it didn’t work for me. Thats why I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a turn-based strategy game developed by Atlus.Yes, the characters loosely refer to events in Persona 5, but more importantly, memos you can view outright spoil certain plot points in that game. Play Persona 5 Royal first. If you like turn-based strategy, chances are you like turn-based RPGs too.This game takes place after Persona 5 but before Strikers. The DLC for this game, Repaint your Heart, takes place during Persona 5 sometime before .No.With that out of the way, onto the review.It's like Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope. For those that haven't played that, your characters can move freely on the map within their reachable range, and won't settle in place until you select an action to perform. It has a cover system, but unlike most other games, cover provides protection even if you attack that unit from behind. Which is weird... but them's the rules.Unique to this tactics game is the ability to knock down enemies to get another action. If an enemy is without cover, or has had their resistance broken through some other action, you can down them with another attack. The unit that downs them gets another action, which  having their movable range updated. This is a really powerful move for getting around fast, and mirrors Persona 5's emphasis on quick battles.As if that wasn't enough, the unit that gets the extra action also gets the ability to activate a "Triple Threat", this game's version of an All-Out Attack. This is incredibly powerful and dare I say overpowered. Just to give you an idea, maps that have conditions like "defeat all enemies within 8 turns" for extra rewards can often be cleared in 2 turns, and the only reason that it isn't 1 turn is because enemy reinforcements usually spawn on the 2nd turn, lol.Like Persona 5, it's one of the easiest games in the genre. All-Out Attacks being what they are along with a pretty generous cover system makes this a cakewalk on Normal difficulty. I recommend Hard for anyone that has even a tiny bit of experience of tactics games. Hard difficulty also has friendly fire, which adds an extra layer to your actions, it's really good.Not much. There are some "reach this area" battles, but most are just "defeat all enemies", which is fine in my opinion. There's much more variety in environment than enemies.Sidequests explore a "carry object to area" victory condition, but it's never used in the main quest.I found bosses pretty boring to be honest, and they tend to drag. Near the end of the game you have to fight all the bosses , with no differences whatsoever. What a waste of time.Pretty self contained. Two new characters, Erina and Toshiro, are introduced and we follow their journey along with the Phantom Thieves. They have pretty good banter too.Like Persona 5 the plot kicks off with a One Piece-tier villain designed to grab your attention and slowly segues into a more serious tone as it goes on.The Phantom Thieves themselves have no character arcs or developments to speak of really, they're mostly just there. Persona 5's cast was always the weakest of the modern Personas (in my humble onion), but still. Don't expect anything other than banter.The dialogue can drag a bit as the characters have to reiterate how much they need to help those poor citizens, or have to denounce the bad guys yet again.Other than that I found the story compelling enough.There are some nice tracks as expected from a Persona game.The hideout has a few themes it goes through that are pretty relaxing,  which is just what you need for a rainy day.There are several tracks for battles.  is the one that will probably grab your attention first, as it's the first one that has Lyn singing. It's not  or anything, but good enough.The DLC has , which contrary to its name has the loudest and stinkiest sound I've heard from a battle theme in a long while, which fits the backstreet alley neon punk theme of that DLC. Also has the rapper from Persona 3, Lotus Juice, in it so that's pretty sick.The Velvet Room theme is back... unfortunately. I've learned to tolerate it, but I will never like it. Speaking of the Velvet Room...This section is mostly a nitpick, so you can skip it if you want, I just had to complain somewhere...A sub section within Music / Sound dedicated to a single character?Yes, because Lavenza has some really annoying voice lines that play  while in the Velvet Room.Linger even 2 seconds on the main screen?Viewing the compendium and selecting a persona to view its abilites because it doesn't display by default?Ok, now I want to see that one.Ok... maybe this one had the abilities I wanted?Oh forget it! I'll just exit out of this whole thing!*back**back**back*I honestly can't believe this. As if the Velvet Room wasn't annoying enough. It's almost funny.This game is around 30 hours. Replayability comes from higher difficulties.There are skill trees for each unit, but they simply aren't interesting enough to experiment with on subsequent playthroughs. Since your units can equip sub-personas, any unit can have any ability you want. Since it's a tactics game with unique units I had hoped to see some more unique abilities a la Triangle Strategy.Despite all the mechanics it still lacks the depths of other turn-based strategy games out there. It's still a good time, and if you're a fan of Persona 5 and want to see more of its cast, you can't go wrong with this really.

_childDocuments_.review: 10 Hours in, I've done about 20 story missions or so I would say.First impression:Everything feels flawless.The animated cutscenes are cool,the rigular Story, showed in a Visual Novel style is handling it's interactions with it characters in one of the most dynamic and expressive way i've seen with a story recounted that way. And on the same note, the way story, combat, and progression feels its extremly well interwoven together.But now what about the most important aspect: The game playTL;DR: Extremly fun and easy to handleTurn based strategy games have seen may froms of iterations troughout the years and for most a lost of the aspects have been set in stones, as they were solid and fun ways to experience those games. In P5T although the core is extremely similar to one of those games, the simple fact that moveing your characters in a free roaming manner on a square grid makes it for a very dynamic approach to strategy. Paired with the fact that most actions require one or two press of a button to activate, makes it so at some point you almost forget it's a strategy game. It's an merge of action and strategy which is very snappy fun and quick. One thing I would say which though is that combat is not "extremely" hard at it's core. The game has a lots of mechanics in place to let you exploit every aspect of its design to its full potential with barely any restrictions. Which is cool, don't get me wrong, right of the bat you feel like a genius master strategist, but it also makes for maps that are fairly easy to clear in very few turns. The game even rewards you with a Sticker Star if you manage to clear some stages in a limted amount of turns, encouraging you to use and abuse all you can. Every second in gemplay is a maximum amount of fun, but in between every maps, there is dialogue. Amazing alive, well written and especialy voice acted dialogue, but still, when you want gameplay, every time it feels like a tease. Short map, a little story, short map, story, menu naviationg to build your personas, short map, etc. What i'm trying to say is that sometimes I would like for some maps to actually take 20 turns to complete, but so far none are like that, which is fine, it's not the type of game, it's no fire emblem, but for what it is, it's extremely fun and whenever a maps ends, i already want more. Which i guess is good for the game.So yeah, Extremely fun and polished experience!

_childDocuments_.review: With reluctance, I can't recommend Persona 5 Tactica.Despite all inevitable comparisons, Tactica isn't that much like XCOM. It's more like a puzzle game blended with baby's first TRPG. You have a small arsenal of tactics at your disposal: cover, gunfire, melee attacks, air follow-ups, 1-More, and the Triple Threat. You and the enemy take turns moving all your units, Fire Emblem-style, around the map. You can shoot at enemies, preferably from cover. Cover reduces or sometimes negates incoming damage. You can use melee attacks to displace enemies from cover, exposing them to more damage. If you hit an enemy with a melee attack from a high altitude and an ally is underneath, that ally can air juggle the enemy with death from below as a follow-up. Hitting an exposed enemy gives you a 1-More, allowing your character to take another action in the same turn. Triangulating your units when you have a 1-More active allows you to perform a Triple Threat, where you blast all enemies within the area of the triangle. You're probably going to spend so much time forming triangles for Triple Threats that this game ought to have been called Persona 5: Triangle Strategy.Though these core tactics work well, they're also comically overpowered once you master them. I've never complained of a game being too easy, but Tactica is too easy. The campaign tries to mix it up with a switch mechanic, where pressing switches opens some doors and closes others, but by the time this is introduced, the campaign is more than half over. Tactica seems more balanced around its 15 side quests, which are brain teasers meant to test your understanding of the game mechanics. Unfortunately for Tactica, I utterly despise brain teasers, so these quests come off as time wasters.Speaking of time wasters, the biggest problem with Tactica by far is the story. The Phantom Thieves are, for whatever reason, sucked into an alternate dimension and have to battle their way back home. Along the way, they encounter a random civilian who also happens to be in the running for Japan's next prime minister. This guy, frustratingly, is the main character, and the Phantom Thieves are reduced to sidekicks in their own game. They spend the entirety of the game trying to get the main character to grow a pair while the plot progressively discards any internal consistency, even to the chagrin of the characters. The whole thing comes to a head when, and I'm not kidding, the god of conservative politics comes down and tries to smite everyone out of fear that the main character is going to embark on a campaign of political reform, and then you awaken a Persona based on Che Guevara.If it wasn't bad enough that the plot's dumb as rocks, the biggest issue is that the game is 60% cutscenes. You'll spend untold hours sitting through the characters' annoying chit-chat about what they just did or what they're about to do. The game constantly barrages you with cutscenes that are 7-9 minutes long, then throws you a level you can complete in half that time. Tactica refuses to let you enjoy the game because there's an ungodly amount of unnecessary babble, and I strongly dislike games that disrespect my time.I debated on giving Tactica a grudging recommendation until I considered one question: would I play this game again? The answer is no, and if I knew then what I know now, I wouldn't have purchased it. Tactica relies on its nominal connection to Persona 5 to sell. It's a criminally short game for a full price purchase, clocking in under 32 hours even with all the mountains of grating dialogue and the 15 side quests, and most of the time I found myself bored or irritated while waiting for the game portion of the game. It's mechanically solid and it has all of the flash and panache of Persona 5 in its style, but its abysmal story, clunky UI (there are two different menus that should be condensed into one but just...aren't), and generally tedious experience did not so much take my heart as it did break my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a very good game for what it is, but if you're expecting a challenging experience akin to Fire Emblem, you're looking in the wrong place. Earning every achievement is (kind of) a drag. NOTES: First Play-Through took 29 Hours (Hard Mode). I completed 94% of the Persona Compendium and earned every possible achievement aside from purchasing 50 weapons.NG+ took about 10 Hours (Merciless, taking advantage of Persona Compendium)ORIGINAL REVIEW: I'll definitely be updating this once I beat the game and once I unlock every achievement, but as of right now this game is actually fantastic.EDIT: In order to earn every achievement, I had to complete two full play-throughs, which let me get very acquainted with the game's story and mechanics. The early game is the worst part, and I felt that the earlier boss fights were dragging and not fun. Later game bosses are significantly more fun, even when you fight certain ones again. Completing the Persona Compendium was the only task I did not enjoy in this game. Side Quests are few in numbers and fun in content, while Hideout Conversations are typically short and sweet, providing a tangible reward for watching through them. The Compendium was just a chore and was the only reason a second play-through was ever required, as New Game+ personas are REQUIRED. Honestly I should've expected this as P5S had similar NG+ bonuses that were required for achievements, but it was still irritating and the least fun part of this game.Overall, this game was super fun and I will definitely be doing a third play-through, as I still have yet to experience Merciless outside of NG+. My first play-through was on hard mode, and I found it to be a bit too easy, but I was expecting that as I am the type of masochist to play Fire Emblem on Lunatic/Maddening for fun. Merciless was still mostly a cakewalk, but I found it more difficult to earn each mission's awards on the first attempt. It was also significantly more punishing to your mistakes, but definitely still on the easier side of SRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 still lives rent free in my head. If I had unlimited time, I'd probably jump back into that game world and just have fun messing around with it. Alas, I do not and I need to play more than just one game. I did give P5 Strikers a shake and... I can't. Musou games just aren't my jam. They feel like lesser Character-Action games (Bayonetta, DMC, etc). I got bored and it now collects digital dust on the Switch. But then I saw Tactica was on the horizon. As a big fan of the rebooted X-COM series thus far, I needed a tactics-game to fill the spot left behind when XCOM 2 updated itself into "broken-mod" territory. After getting this for Xmas in 2023, I gave P5 Tactica a chance. Results were... mixed. It certainly has style and personality befitting a Persona 5 spin-off. The Chibi-Artstyle isn't quite my jam, but I get if we're controlling little dudes on an overhead map, it shouldn't matter. But the menu, music, and story engines were all still working hard, so I can't complain too bad if the art is just a little bit of an adjustment to make. Plot is the scooby gang gets abducted by a new meta-verse "ruler." but instead of their usual fighting style, we're now forced into tactics-based combat for... reasons. I'm not complaining about the combat, but the switch feels rather arbitrary. Most of the gang gets kidnapped except for the protagonist (joker) and the tutorial character (mona). They are rescued by the new character, Erina. While I can't say why, she doesn't get a Persona to bring out in combat, which is somewhat disappointing at first. It sorta pays off in the end, but still feels weird to introduce a new character into Persona without a Persona. It's like making a new X-Man, but they don't have a mutation. After rescuing the gang, you beat the boss only to discover there are more bosses to fight and one of the new characters you meet seems to be connected to all of them. Plots unravel and you fight god again at the end of this one. Not so much a plot twist as it is an unneeded redirect when the first part of the plot is pretty good. I'd say Persona games are at their peak when they're diving into the psychology of a specific character and seeing how their world functions. It becomes less-so when it suddenly becomes a world-ending crisis and god wants to kill us all or something. Plus it feels a bit repetitive when this non-descript amalgamation is more or less just another non-descript amalgamation like in the mainline Persona 5 game. There are puzzle maps you can do to gain XP and get small rewards. Some of these were genuinely fun. Others were exercises in frustration. The game doesn't have a lot of gimmicks and gameplay in combat feels like a slightly more engaging Mario + Rabbids style tactics game. But compared to meatier games, like X-Com, it also feels a little hollow. You still get Persona Fusions and capture them, but they serve a more supporting role and to become stronger weapons when you meet some high-bar requirements to get even remotely good ones. There isn't much of a "S-Link" system, making a lot of the REALLY LONG story beats between missions feel a bit like a drag. I get we're all friends here since this takes place late in the P5 timeline, but game certainly feels weird without it. This game isn't bad, but it definitely doesn't feel committed to the genre of tactics. More like it dipped its toe to see what it might be like. And while the experience isn't bad, I definitely felt like it was missing something most of the time. It wasn't as immersive as Persona 5 Proper, and it wasn't as in-depth as X-COM or Fire Emblem. I think if Persona truly wanted to dive head-first into tactics games, it has the chops to do it. But this was just a small step in that direction with a lot of room to grow into it. I mean, if the Like A Dragon games can become solidly playable turn-based RPGs, then ya'll can manage a Persona Tactics game. I believe in you. As it stands, it's fine. If you like Persona (like me) you'll probably still enjoy it, even with it feeling a little too easy, breezy, and light. But maybe that's what we need is a Persona-Snack before we get Persona 6 or Persona 5 Arena. Or whatever Refantazio Metaphor is supposed to be. But if you're looking for more of the tactics-gameplay, this will probably be underwhelming as hell. But your kids who are just getting into tactics games will probably appreciate this (or something like it) as their first step into the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing introduction to tactics for newcomers to the genre. If you're a longtime fan, I recommend diving straight into merciless. It would've been a good idea to have another difficulty that was even more punishing, but I understand that Tactica is supposed to be a more forgiving experience, and that's not an overall negative. I really loved the triple threat and ailment systems. Persona's "One More" mechanic translates super well into the gameplay, and I find myself hoping for a sequel that amps up the difficulty and uses these ideas to their full potential. If you liked meticulous planning in the original persona 5, I think this spin off will appeal to you far more than strikers, which was okay, but in my opinion, didn't really play to the strengths of the persona formula. My biggest criticism is that the game just isn't long enough! I think another 15-20 hours would've made it worth the full 60, but as of now, only purchase this game on sale. In my opinion, this is a $40 game, and that's not even talking about the DLC. Really rude of them to hold fan favorites hostage $20. The story is serviceable. I think they could've had more writers on this project. Toshiro is a very fun character, and I loved learning about his life, but it really wasn't enough to carry the whole thing. It would've been nice to have more newcomers and villains. It's disappointing that Atlus keeps clinging to the original persona 5 canon; the plot beats added in Royal could be expanded upon in interesting ways. Akechi and Sumi are my favorite persona 5 characters, so it's disappointing to not see them in the main campaign. However, the rest of the phantom thieves are here, and they still have a fun group dynamic. If you like the persona 5 cast, you'll like this game's story. It's very character driven. All in all, this game is a good purchase for people who loved Mario Rabbids, big fans of persona 5, and people looking for a good intro to tactics. I'd wait for it to go on sale, but I really did enjoy my time with the game. It's sad that tactica came out so late into persona 5's lifespan because I think it would've been more appreciated a couple years earlier. Give it a shot if it's less than 40 bucks!

_childDocuments_.review: *When I mention 5, I am referring to Persona 5 Royal, including its extra semester. Not the original P5 release.*Persona 5 Tactica is a somewhat unexpected entry in the P5 franchise - but it's a welcome one. The plot for the main game takes place just after P5 Royal, so think... Maybe mid-to-late Feb to the very beginning of March. The majority of it takes place in the Metaverse, so like Strikers (or Scramble), the social sim aspect is absent. Not a con, though. I like that this and Scramble prioritize plot first and foremost. You can still name Joker and respond as him in various scenarios, of course. He also talks a little bit more in this, which surprised me upon first playing through the game itself. Like P5 and its sequel Strikers, Tactica does touch on pretty intense topics at many points. It gets pretty feelsy, especially towards the tail end of the game itself. The story doesn't hold up as strong as 5, but it's still relatively decent. I absolutely loved Toshiro's development and how it handled those heavy handed topics I mentioned earlier on. I can't really get into specifics because spoilers, but trust me, Toshiro will probably grow on you. So, even with my own praises for the game being mentioned, I will also admit that the game isn't perfect. With each kingdom that passed, you would hear the group say that they are hoping they'll go home after defeating x boss. It would be reasonable to hear this after just beating the main boss of the first kingdom, but it was grating to hear it a second, nay, third time. It's probably a nitpick of mine. I have another piece of criticism towards the game, which is well... How little it was marketed. Persona 5 Tactica in of itself is under-rated in my opinion and I wish more folks were able to get into it. I do understand Persona 5 exhaustion/burn out is a real thing and heck, I'm kind of starting to feel it. I also understand why P3 Reload was prioritized more in comparison as it is a remake of a beloved JRPG from the PS2 era. Not to mention the scope for that game is bigger in comparison to P5T. I just, can't help but wish the marketing was a bit more balanced, because it does feel like Tactica flew under the radar. Jabs at Toshiro regarding his age and being referred to as "old" or "gramps" for that matter. While I'm relieved to see that Ryuji at worst got one scene where he was physically picked on, I do think that some of the needless bullying just got moved onto another character. As of writing this, I have no idea how old Toshiro is as there's not a listed birth year for him let alone a birthdate, but the minimum age in Japan to be a Diet member is 26. So for the sake of this, we can just assume he's around his late 20s to early 30s. He isn't exactly old by any means. This is probably just a nitpick of mine, but felt like I should mention it. I did notice some flaws with the story and I would get into them, but this review is well... Massive already. I'm just going to leave it at that.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but more of a puzzle game than a proper tactics game. Personas are frustratingly dumbed down and enemy variety is lacking. DLC and game don't really warrant $60~70 and is more of a $40 dollar price range game. Everything around the gameplay is pretty good. Art, music, interface. However, the gameplay is about half the game's runtime with the other half being the story.Which while good, is told mostly through textboxes. Not once does a scene play out on the battlefield or in the middle of a combat encounter. Credit where it's due, full art and cutscenes break up the monotony of that fairly reguarly. There's even character portraits drawn for one off gags in some of the optional side conversations which is really cool to see. Lots of the dialogue is voiced and sounds pretty good. However it can be too quiet in comparison to the music in the background. It feels a few levels too quiet in various conversations across both the main game and DLC. Those conversations are pretty good and including the side conversations was a great opportunity for characterization. It felt like the writing team had more freedom than in P5 with what characters were allowed to say, and all the characters had some good dialogue and chances to connect with the new characters. Even if I wish they went more in depth about those connections and had deeper discussions about them.Despite all that the game feels a bit short, like it could've used another section. Overall a solid game but one you should wait to go on sale for.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: So i originally made a meme review since i expected the game to be great. But after playing for a bit, i actually am kind of dissappointed. If i could i would give this game a Mixed rating, since im unsure if i like it or not.I am very conflicted about this game, i want the game to sell well since i love Persona 5 (my fav game of all time) and want to see more games made around it, but at the same time i cant say that the game deserves to do well.Style:Its very rough around the edges and borders on low effort. Most of the game is a visual novel, which can in a way be said about the Original and Strikers, however the 3D Modells and animation atleast make it look believable, but in this game its purely artwork. Which is very dissapointing since it is a full price game (besides the Modells already exist, would it be so hard to give them small animations?).The Visual novel aspect of the game makes it pretty much impossible to really get a feel for the world and places the characters are. You are supposed to be inside massive kingdoms, but do to the style and reused backgrounds, it makes it look like as if you were moving in a small street with like 10 buildings. Marie fails completely to feel like a ruthless leader when you dont even get to see the kingdom or its people in a big way.Unlike P5 and Strikers the menus also dont feel remotely as stylish or snappy and feel very generic.Battle:The combat is beyond boring. Im not the biggest fan of the genre but i have played similar games in the past. And all have been a lot more fun. The combat is insanely basic, and way to easy even on Merciless. The AI is so terrible that they sometimes dont even move or attack you for no reason. All characters also feel pretty much the same, while in P5 and Strikers all members filled a certain role, and felt unique, this game is the exact opposite. Both the guns and melee are interchangeable with on another for all chars. The skills are technically different, but in execution do the same (Deal dmg, do an effect). And since all PT can now equip a side Persona which can give them skills which they never had, it makes them seem even more of the same (Yusuke can get Garu, which would normally be Morgana or Joker only). Hiding behind cover practically makes you invincible and only a few enemies can counter that.Also neither Armor nor Melee weapons can be bought, you can only buy Guns and the Dmg diff is almost non existant. Velvet room has been shafted hard and fusing Personas is boring, and doesnt feel interesting at all since Personas only have 2 abilitys now, and the first one is always locked, so you can influence a single skill. Characters no longer level UP instead there is Skill Tree which is pretty much only "Skill more range, more DMG) very basic.NO ALL OUT ATTACK END SCREEN LIKE ???????Music:Onto the biggest crime. The music sucks, for the most part. Both P5 and Strikers have amazing soundtracks and even the basic songs are really good. In Tactica most songs are so generic and boring that its insulting (i heard someone describe it as chat GPT being task to make a P5 inspired song, and it fits so much).Even inside combat the music is so boring that it becomes insulting. You will occasionally get a vocal track, which are always amazing (especially the DLC, Lotus Juice never misses).But aside from that its just whatever.Persona is knows for having amazing music, so to blunder it this hard should be illegal. Story:The story is fine so far. Im only in Kingdom 2 (Kingdom 2 is already a morbillion times better than 1) so i cant speak much on it. But do to the prior mentioned problem with the visuals, plot poins feel very weird and awkwardly executed, since things just kinda happen and you dont really know where you are or what the situation looks like. There are cutscenes from time to time, which are great but they sadly only highlight the massive problems of the visual novel aspect. Also the PT just kinda exist, this game is Toshiros and Eniras story, and the PT are just kinda there for the ride, which is very much unlike P5 and Strikers. End:Strikers was such a good high effort sequel, and this is the opposite. Its Atlus trying to make money with the most low effort stuff by attaching P5. In a sense its really predatory. The game isnt bad by any means. But if you arent a P5 fan, there is nothing here for you, unlike Strikers which even if you didnt play the Original was good enough to stand on its own legs. Its by no means worth full price, this is a 40 euro title max. Its a glorified visual novel (not even fully voiced with minimal dialogue) with boring shafted gameplay, and whatever music. _childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game, it feels kind of lazy in some parts, but I can't help but like it. Again, cool variation on the gameplay and ok story, even being a better idea of what this game could be, a small side story. but it costs wayy to much for 3 hours of gameplay.All in all, if you are a Persona fan, this is worth it, but if not, get this when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Another one of those moderate reviews that sadly balances out to a negative for me. I'm far from fluent in SRPGs, with Triangle Strategy and Final Fantasy Tactics being the only ones I've played to completion; however, I loved both titles, especially Triangle Strategy, and I'm sad to say Persona 5 Tactica brings very little to the table to differentiate itself from the pack, or for me to recommend it over them. The greatest selling points are seeing the Phantom Thieves again, and the stylish flair in UI that the original Persona 5 was so well known for. But unlike Strikers, another P5 spinoff, the story Tactica has told so far has been akin to a reflavoring of P5 base, while referencing little of the substantial character or team building that Strikers capitalized on. I understand that telling a gripping narrative probably wasn't the developer's guiding star when making this game, but without it, what you're left with is a tactical combat system that feels increasingly banal as the game goes on, relying on strategies that are painfully overtuned in effectiveness. There are also moderately deceptive practices in work with the marketing of the DLC, where it was positioned as adding two fan favorite characters to the game's roster, only for them to be cordoned off to a separate side-adventure until you beat it and the base game in full. Finding that out left a sour taste in my mouth. Ultimately, I don't think P5T is a bad game by any means; it's just a frankly underwhelming one, and absolutely not worth this asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately Tactica falls a bit flat especially up against Strikers; a near perfect spin-off sequel. The good was mostly what we all loved about the base game; the cohesion between the Phantom Thieves is always fantastic and after 100+ hours with them they feel like best friends we are seeing again for the first time in a while. But towards the end of Tactica I found myself not as interested in what they had to say anymore, a surefire sign that I am ready to move on from this cast.Speaking of familiarity, one of the weaker parts of Tactica was it's story. The lack of any overworld to hangout in, a staple of Persona, was such a detriment and the visual novel-esqe dialogue scenes were tough to get invested in. When all was said and done it felt like a rehashing of 5 with many similar plot points (even the final boss was eerily similar in design to that of 5's final boss) and at this stage felt tired. Keeping the whole story as a personal journey for Toshiro was an interesting choice but ultimately felt too drawn out. I would've really liked to see him involved in gameplay much earlier.On that front, gameplay was fun to start but very quickly fell into a familiar rhythm. I played on Hard after seeing reviews mentioning how easy the game was and even then I cake walked through the game. I lost 1 character through 52+ missions and that was in the final battle because I didn't bring heals; I never got close to losing a party member at any other point. The sole challenge was completing the mission in the allotted turns for the bonus and even that never came close. Enemy variety was extremely light which only made combat less interesting and more familiar very quickly. Party members also are largely homogenized due to the ability to equip Personas. All this is to say, it didn't feel like much strategy was at play in a game that used "tactics" in its name.The game isn't bad by any means and definitely has it good moments but mileage will vary. Persona 5 fans might love another opportunity, mostly likely the last, to hangout with this beloved cast of characters but those not attached to the series might find it harder to enjoy.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE after playing the DLC----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I went ahead and played the DLC, and well, now I know why the main game seems so thinly stretched and lacks variety. They pretty clearly cut the game up to resell a scenario as DLC that should have been part of the main story.The DLC took about 5 hrs to finish the campaign on merciless, all in one sitting. It is slightly harder than the main game, but not by much - I only restarted a single battle out of the 15 maps on merciless difficulty. It is actually pretty good taken just on its own tbh. It adds some variety sorely lacking in the main game. For the story it tells, it is a pretty appropriate length. The problem is, the main game is 50 battle telling a story of similar size.Noticing that makes me suspect the original vision for the game was multiple kingdoms, each telling a small story, just like the DLC with Guernica and Luca's story. Then the Toshiro and Erina story would be another kingdom of similar length. Then probably one other kingdom (I am sure we will see that 3rd one soon enough an another $20 DLC). Plus a few maps to get to the final boss, still ending up at about 50 maps.  Each of those kingdoms will have different mechanics, just like the DLC, and maybe even have different phantom thieves featured in each one, joining at the end for one big blow out.  It honestly would have been amazing as I describe it, I would have absolutely loved that version of the game.Instead we get this, where they cut out one of the kingdoms for $20 DLC, save one other kingdom for later release (speculating of course, but mark my words), and then stretch the last kingdom so thin it cannot hold itself up. Just another example of terrible game industry practices. It makes me sad seeing the positive reviews on Steam, because people cannot even recognize when they are being taken anymore, it is just the norm.So my original review conclusions stand after playing the DLC - don't pay full price, and only get it if you love P5 or tactics games enough to ignore a slog of a story and severe lack of variety.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ORIGINAL REVIEWNot at full price. On 1/2 price sale it could be worth it if you either like tactics games or love Persona 5.The writing and story is extremely weak. The characters have conversations where they explain the same thing over and over, or do that annoying anime thing where they do not understand obvious, basic information. The relationships in P5 were so great, it is hard to believe the downgrade in this game. I have never wanted to skip conversations in Persona games, but this one I found myself glancing at my phone as Motoko explained why bad man is bad for the 5th time.The battles are more a puzzle game than tactics. The fights hinge on the one more mechanic, where you use positioning and decisions to have everyone attack at once. It is fun and engaging, but it offers no challenge once you figure it out beyond making a puzzle out of it. I started on merciless, the highest difficulty, and it was laughably easy, especially by mid-way.  And that was not through grinding, I did each fight once and only once.There is a replay option to go back and retry fights you have done to get the full 3 star rating or more money/exp. I got the full 3 stars on my first run through of each one, easily in most cases.  You are rarely in danger of losing even a single character. I did have to restart a couple of the fights, mainly due to not understanding something newly introduced.  The game does introduce some new things in the form of enemy types over the course of the playtime, but it still comes down to finding a way to do a one more attack and getting into a triangle surrounding the enemies. By the end you basically have 5 enemy types, with reskins over and over. Pretty lackluster for a tactics game. You will also be running around with 200+ HP soon enough with enemies doing 20 damage to you...Oh and don't even bother with the DLC, the game is easy enough as-is. I actively avoided using any of the DLC personas until I arrived at creating them naturally through fusion. Otherwise, the DLC gives you access to high level persona right out of the gate, all the way up to something like a level 90! So if you use them before they are naturally available, the game will lose what little challenge it has. The weapons you get in the DLC will be good for a few maps until the normal upgrades outclass them. Again, I avoided using them too, because there is no need to make things even easier than they already were,.Speaking of DLC, the $20(!) DLC is a stand alone piece. It is very confusing at first, because when you start the game you can switch between two different start screens, one with the DLC and one without. It is easy to think the DLC screen integrates it into the game, and should be the one you use, but nope, it is just its own separate thing. Apparently it can be played in either order though, as the DLC is a prequel, though the game does warn you to be familiar with the tutorial mechanics before starting the DLC. I don't know if I will bother with it by now, the game has already worn out its welcome 43 hours in (I am right at the final boss at that point).

_childDocuments_.review: To start: If you're new to the series, P5 in particular, you'll be completely lost and have the main game spoiled for you.Persona meets X-COM. So Strikers as Dynasty Warriors now Persona adds it's charm to X-COM.Pros:- The story is interesting and follows the usual Persona beats well. They have this down to a fine art now and if you're a fan you'll like it.- While not as tragic as the main game there's emotional weight behind the story.- The cast are back with newbie Erina being an excellent addition to the team. - The mechanics work well and they've taken the Mario Rabbits technique, that is to streamline it massively and make it suit the Persona style.- The trademark Persona 5 style and incredible soundtrack are back too.- I adore the chibi art styleCons:- If you're into the slightly madder spin-offs Persona have that play with the wider Persona universe I think you'll be disappointed. At least so far this is tied into the Persona 5 universe alone.- There isn't much depth to the Persona building or stat building mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: It looks like it'll be more tactical than Persona 5, but it's less tactical. They remove a lot of aspects and it really just turns it into a boring, easy game. Your personas only have 2 skills, one inherent and the other learned. So customisation is basically zero. There's no mechanic for recruiting personas, you just get a random selection after beating a mission. There's no normal world sim sections, a huge part of the original game. There are no stealth sections or even just movement and exploration. It's all menus and levels. There are no elemental weaknesses and all characters and abilities work in just about the same way. The story is both extremely slow and constantly interrupting the gameplay. Most of the dialogue is pointless commentary on a situation you already know about. The art is dumbed down significantly and I feel like it's designed to sell funko-pops more than anything else. It's just not appealing and doesn't match the more serious tone the Persona games try to match. It's honestly just really poor. I was playing on the hardest difficulty but it's still way too easy and it just doesn't provide any kind of challenge. There's little to no character growth or interesting skill combinations. The overall story seems fine but basic and it just moves far too slowly. Levels are more like extremely simple puzzles than tactical fights. I like Persona 5 and Strikers but I really can't recommend this one. Especially when it's at such an extortionate price.

_childDocuments_.review: A charming addition to the series that falls short with its core gameplay.I've thoroughly enjoyed the series spinoffs such as Persona Q and Persona 5 Strikers as entries that are compelling to play and also add to the universe in an interesting way (as a crossover event game and as a sequel respectively). Tactica didn't meet my high expectations on those fronts. The story, new characters, art design and music are solid, but the blend and layering of Persona series mechanics with tactical gameplay didn't quite work for me.Ultimately I was able to breeze through the game leveraging "One More" and the occasional "Triple Threat Attack" (All Out Attack equivalent) while not needing to leverage most of the other mechanics presented. There are skill trees, personas, ways to chain attacks, different stage gimmicks and enemies...but in the end most of these ended up being fairly inconsequential or uninteresting. The final section of the game felt padded as well which was a bit disappointing.While I did enjoy the story for what it was, as noted it didn't add to the universe in a particularly interesting way. Nor did the gameplay grab me in the same way that PQ and Strikers did previously. I suppose the missing element there is that both were leveraging other series (Etrian in-house and Musou with Omega Force) and their respective teams expertise. If the intent for these spinoffs is to introduce new types of games to series fans with a Persona skin, Tactica as a standalone falls short for me in making the case for the tactics/strategy genre.If you're a big fan of P5 and its characters, I'd still recommend playing this (perhaps on sale) for another fun adventure with the PT. Otherwise I don't think Tactica adds anything particularly interesting to Persona as a whole and isn't a must play by any means.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to finish this, but I'm really disappointed. The persona system just seems tacked onto an existing basic tactical design, so you can summon demons and equip them to your party members which will usually only give you one more ability that you don't really have the SP to use. The gameplay so far has been defeat/evade a grand collection of three enemy types. You've got your big healthed tank guys, the standard troop and the buffing/magic attacking drummers. The boss fight I've had at this stage differed from this but at the end of it the boss regained all of her health, undoing the work I'd put in,  and I had to wait for RNG to place the objects needed to actually defeat her into the arena. There hasn't been any complexity of story so far and I don't see that changing any time soon. I guess there was some biting commentary on....arranged marriages? I can't believe we've gone from extortion, abuse and then the magnum opus of free will vs paradise that royal gave us to this. The little phantom lemmings annoy the ♥♥♥♥ out of me as well. Maybe the dlc is good but this has caused me to think more cautiously when it comes to P5 sequels.EDIT: After having played more, there is more enemy varieties but the umbrella blockers don't really do anything except present a barrier to you and while the ninja swappers can make the gameplay a little more dynamic, but not by much. I really don't understand why they didn't just use the variety of megaten demons that exist already as an enemy force. The story is a little better I guess. For perspective I'm pushing myself through the game, mostly skipping the very boring visual novel dialogue so I'm not getting the most of it really, but from what I can glean it's all centered around the one guy, who may or may not be punishing himself, I have no idea. _childDocuments_.review: 5.5/10If mixed reviews were still a thing, that is what I would give this game. This is an alright game that borrows heavilly from the modern XCOM-games as well as the Mario+Rabbids-series. The Persona 5-skin is mostly that, a skin strapped on and a system trying to incorporate elements from Persona 5. It does so successfully, most of the time, but otherwise does not offer anything noteworthy. I would NOT recommend this game at full price, it just is not that good. But on a sale it is an alright time, and a nice revisit to the Persona 5-world if you have missed it.Persona 5 Tactica is an isometric turn-based strategy game where you go through levels and defeat enemies and move around a grid in order to complete them. As previously said, it borrows HEAVILY from XCOM: Enemy Unknown and the Mario+Rabbids-series. It focuses a lot on story and presents an alright tale set in the Persona-universe.Each character has their own strengths and weaknesses and you are free to customize your party at almost any time. On lower difficulties, you can probably make due with the craracters you like, but on higher settings, you have to plan carefully, and the game offers a good challenge.I found the story quite boring and predictable, with a lot of the elements repeating to the point where I felt almost no urgency. It just dragged on and I waited for the banter to stop and the game to progress. I cannot really put my finger on what I disliked about it, but safe to say is that I predicted a lot of the twists early on and thus when they actually came it had a smaller impact on me than intended.The combat and strategy-elements are fine, not on XCOM-level but they do the job. I am not sure WHY this game feels a need to exist, really (except to make money, of course), but it does not really fill a niche in the genre, which grinds my gears a bit. The elements incorporated from Persona 5 works, I guess, but feel more in place because they need to be there, rather than being the core focus. This is especially true for the weapon and money-system, where you just buy stronger and stronger guns and little to no strategy goes into choosing a certain weapon for a certain battle. This is especially true once the concept of weapon CRAFTING is introduced, where the weapons DO matter and when you NEED to think strategically. Why are there two methods to acquire weapons, one boring and one "fun"?The music is great, and gives the Persona 5-vibes I want. Nothing bad to say at all.The presentation is fine, with the characters being more "chibi-like" in their artstyles than in Persona 5 or Persona 5 Strikers. It reminds me a lot of Persona Q, which is not a bad thing. It is just different.All in all, I was dissapointed in this game, but it is still an alright game. I recommend purchasing it on a sale for those who love XCOM-style games or those who just want to play everything Persona-related. Oh yea, this probably goes without saying but PLEASE play Persona 5 before this, otherwise nothing will make sense.
