_childDocuments_.review: ( full review with screenshots:  )Persona 5 Tactica is an odd game because of what it isn't. Atlus already had a tactical RPG series in the Devil Survivor games, and those games were already not far from being Persona tactics games. Considering that Persona Q was just Etrian Odyssey rethemed, I'd have expected this to establish a pattern and be Devil Survivor 3 but with Persona 5 characters. Instead, it actually has much more in common with XCOM and is arguably more of a puzzle game than a true strategy RPG. DS2 is still my favorite tactical RPG ever made, so I'm disappointed that this is certainly not DS3, but it's still worth playing. Let's get the strategy vs puzzle game issue out of the way first. Bosses and objects aside, there are only four enemy types in the game, and two of them don't appear until you're well past the halfway point. You can only use three characters per battle, don't get to choose their starting locations, and can only assign them one persona with two possible ability slots. Each character does have a skill tree and a unique elemental affinity, but since many of the skills are shared and there are no elemental weaknesses, most characters don't actually feel very different from any other. The strategic choices you make in other similar games about which units to equip, how to arrange your forces, etc, are largely not present in this game. At the tactical level, the core of the game is the idea that hitting a defenseless enemy gives the attacking character a bonus turn that can also be used to perform an all out attack on every enemy contained in the triangle formed by your three characters. Where most games in this genre are about carefully planning your advance to pick off enemies while taking minimal damage, P5T is about chaining bonus turns to get your characters spread out so that you can do an all out attack on the entire board and wipe everyone out in one move. If there was any doubt about that being the intended way to play, most of the optional sidequests are puzzle battles where you have to accomplish that setup in one turn. So mileage will vary on the gameplay depending on how much you enjoy setting up those attacks. Battles can definitely feel repetitive thanks to the limited number of different enemies and the fact that it's easier to just use the same three characters in every battle and keep their equipment current, but the puzzles do eventually get pretty satisfying. Later areas introduce some dynamic stage elements that allow you to pull off exceptionally long turns if you're careful about your placement and order of operations. Alas, that really is only true of the second half of the game's levels. The first kingdom (which takes up almost the entire first half) just isn't that interesting and spends too much time on trivial tutorial battles that aren't very interesting as either puzzles or tactical battles. Unfortunately, the story follows a similar arc. The first kingdom takes too long to establish anything interesting about its new characters and, presumably to avoid dumping the entire cast of P5 on you at once, comes up with some gimmicks to slowly drip feed you the Phantom Thieves two at a time. It takes far too long to get through this part of the story and, since you already know these characters and they don't play very differently, there's not even much payoff. It gets better and ends well, if never close to the level of regular P5, but I wouldn't blame anyone for not wanting to fight through the underwhelming first area. The last two things I want to mention are the music and how this fits in with the original game and other Persona spinoffs. You probably won't be surprised to find out that the music starts off unremarkable and gets better as the game goes on. That really is the story of this entire game. As for how it fits in, it's supposed to take place some time after the main game and, while it doesn't exactly spoil anything, would be pretty hard to follow if you haven't played P5. The events and characters of Royal are not mentioned in any way, nor are Strikers or the other spinoffs. I think this does a better job of feeling like a part of the P5 story than spinoffs like Dancing or P4 Arena, but it doesn't do anything as interesting as Q did by having the casts of different games join together. --------For more reviews, see

_childDocuments_.review: I was new to the persona series starting with persona 5, so I didn't know exactly what to expect with the spin-offs. I played Strikers, which I found to be surprisingly awesome albeit still not as great as the main title. I was expecting a similar experience with this one, and it got there... kind of. Gameplay:The enemy variety could have been better, and some of the status effects could be more substantial. However, overall it's super fun. Being able to pull of an all-out attack that encompasses huge parts of the arena is unbelievably satisfying. I played on the normal difficulty, which was a bit easy, but I found that to be a strength. It wasn't so much about winning as it was about stringing together moves in smart ways to position enemies the way you want them, using the right abilities, and positioning your own characters to do the max amount of damage in a round. When it all lined up, which was pretty regularly, it felt great.Story (no spoilers): The story is pretty great. However, it takes a while to really hit its stride. The early villains are a little too one-note to be all that interesting, even if their designs are cool. I found myself kind of bored after awhile once the novelty had worn off, but around the midway point, it started getting some character nuance and became a lot more interesting by the last third. There were a few moments where I even got emotional. It would have been better if they'd fleshed out the early stuff better, but the ending stuff, particularly around Toshiro and Erina, was so good that I can excuse it.Worldbuilding/animation:The art style is completely new to persona 5, and for the most part, it nails it. Seeing all the new design elements were great. The majority of the dialogue is conveyed through the use of 2D images of characters in a few different poses against a static background. The sprites are cute, but it comes at the cost of not seeing much of the world. The background and sometimes the clothes change, but there is a level of removal from feeling like it's an actual world, something I missed from seeing the Phantom thieves meeting up in different places. I didn't realize how much that made previous games better, so that aspect was a surprisingly big negative. You get the occasional full 2D portrait to convey a scene (all of which are worthy of using as wallpapers) and sometimes you'll have a fully animated scene in 3D, but both are somewhat sparse until the last half of the game. Pacing:Honestly, pretty bad. There is just way too much time spent in menus. I could have just skipped all the persona fusing, optional dialogue, and sidequest missions, but those make your characters significantly more powerful over time. Not to mention that, at least for me, a lot of the side content of persona games is kind of the fun of it. Do I need to play darts with my friends in Royal? No, but you kind of miss out if you never do. It just could have been implemented better. It felt like after every few fights there was always a good 20-30 minutes of downtime. And that downtime allowed me to think more about the things that were missing than the things that I liked. By the end, I minded less, but again, that was because there was a lot more to be invested in.Music:Do you even need to ask? (It's good)Other points of note:It didn't feel like it was rushed, per se, but it was very evident that corners were cut. The menus are needlessly complex. Additional optional dialogue is pretty flat and mostly just talks about stuff we already knew or could easily guess (although some of it is still good, with the hypothetical marriage scenario being an unbelievably wholesome highlight). Assets are reused towards the end of the game, which I didn't exactly hate, but it did drive home this point. The last kingdom was pretty bare design-wise. The last boss had some interesting mechanics, but it was far too easy to avoid everything he threw at me and just wail on them. There were just a lot of areas that could have been touched up.Conclusion:It might sound like I hate the game. Most of the above is criticisms, after all, but I actually really loved the game. I just really, really wanted to love  ALL of it. It has an amazing core, and moments that I will remember long after I finished. I am hard on it because I knew it could have been incredible, and it was a matter of time and effort rather than design. Adding to this was knowing that there was day-one dlc. It was a really good game that could have been an amazing one.Still, I do recommend it for anyone that's a persona 5 fan because I did like it overall. The beginning is meh, but the novelty of the game mostly carries you through until it gets to the interesting and more emotion-heavy stuff. It doesn't reach the same heights, but it hits enough of the right persona notes to be enjoyable.Paint Your Heart DLC:It's really good. Basically, take all of the good stuff from the base game, trim a lot of the gripes I had, make the world and enemy designs even better, add even cooler music, streamline everything, tied together with a solid story. If you get the base game, just get the dlc. Never got bored, even playing it immediately after the base game. Unfortunately, being so good highlights my gripes about cutting corners from the base game, but it is what it is.

It was also very welcoming to see the sub persona system to return. The artstyle is cute, but personally would have preferred if they used the standard art style seen in Royal and Strikers. Some of them were fine, but the ones where I had to clear the mission in one turn were not fun to play. The game also has a lot of dialogue. Someone could easily beat this game in a couple of afternoons by skipping all the cutscenes. The plot also got very predictable by the second kingdom. _childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Tactica is, at time of writing, the most recent spin off of the Persona series, as well as the most recent game in the series in general. Despite that, I feel as though people will immediately write it off due to it's art style, or because ATLUS is "milking" the series, which is something I think is completely absurd. However, I'll spare the rant about how people treat Persona spin-offs for Reddit, and will instead review this game as a part of the series on it's own merits. Of course, there is going to be some mention of things that occurred in at least Persona 5 itself, as this game is a followup to that game, at least in a way. I can't discuss some elements of the game without at least a single minor spoiler for this game, and mention of the ending of Persona 5, so keep that in mind. Persona 5 has been out in some form for over 5 years at this point, is easily available, AND has the Anime for those who can't play it, so there's really no reason you should be playing Tactica first unless you don't care about that stuff, or you're P5 Veteran.Tactica picks up sometime during the period between Ren (Joker) is released from prison at the very end of Persona 5, but before he goes back to his hometown. Given that the calendar in that game skips a number of days between those two points, regardless of it being the vanilla ending or the Royal ending, it makes sense that something could be slotted in there with no real issue. This is something that the game touches upon, albeit extremely lightly and briefly in the opening hour, so it sort of expects you to know that much of the story so far. It expects you to have this knowledge, because the Phantom Thieves we all know and love don't really grow or change during the events of the story, and are instead just here to support the new characters.Shortly after the Thieves are brought into the mysterious new Metaverse (called "Kingdoms" in game, which is what I'll be calling them for here on out), we meet Erina, an equally mysterious girl leading a Rebel Corps against the dictator Marie (not related to P4's Marie, the name is pronounced differently). She is one of two new characters that are something of a focus for the game, though despite being all over the marketing material, she's the less important of the two major new characters. She's actually charming, but doesn't really have an arc of her own, so to speak. It makes sense once you see why that is later in the story, but I won't get into that. She does sort of grow over the course of the game, but it's less noticeable than the other new characterSpeaking of, the real star of the show is Toshiro Kasukabe, a member of the National Diet (which they still pronounce wrong) that got brought to this new world under unknown circumstances, and he has partial amnesia. The game is more or less his story, as you uncover the truth behind why he's in this world, and how he's connected to the various bosses, among other things. He's introduced within the first hour or so, and your opinion of the game's story will largely depend on how much you like him. Toshiro took a little while to grow on me, but by the end, I was pretty happy with him. He starts as a spineless coward, and he's an adult, so he get a little bit of the Zenkichi (from P5 Strikers) treatment by the Thieves. The story is  him, so your mileage may vary if you don't like him very much.As mentioned above, the Thieves don't really get development, but they are still the characters you remember. I've heard people say they get watered down like the characters are in Persona Q, but not to the same degree... but I don't really see it. They are largely just playing a supporting role, and are the driving force for the gameplay, and not much else. The bosses aren't really much to ride home about either, and are generic jerks that really only exist to facilitate Toshiro's development. They're serviceable.The art style is the other thing that draws comparison to the Persona Q games, but only insofar as basic chibi/cartoony visuals are concerned. I find that the art is more "Panty and Stocking-esc" then Persona Q. As far as how good it is, I tend to think it's pretty good, but I can totally understand if people don't like it. I think it works for the most part. If anything, I just wish the portraits for talking were framed better, because Morgana's just kinda hovering to be mostly above the text box, and I always find that distracting. The game has many CGs in it, and they're all pretty good, with one of them actually changing art style to emphasise the mood, which is nice. There's even a few anime cutscenes in this style, and they look good. Otherwise, it's largely just the same pop-art aesthetics.The voice acting is really solid, but that's to be expected. I played in English, and some of the actors (namely for Erina and Toshiro) don't have any other credits (according to BtVA), so I was actually kind of impressed most of the time, and I could tell the delivery issues that were there likely were due to the voice direction, and less the talent on display.The music is solid, but that's to be expected, it's Persona music. It's admittedly a little weaker than the past few releases, but it's still solid.The gameplay is where this game shines, at least to me. It's a basic XCOM-lite type Tactical RPG, where elevation and cover determine how much damage you take, but with a slight Persona twist. Really, the only thing from Persona that carries over is some status ailments, All Out Attacks (called Triple Threat Attacks in this game), and the One More System, albeit not through exploiting weaknesses. Instead, you're exploiting enemies' lack of cover to score extra hits. It's actually pretty simple. I think the part of the gameplay is actually in the more puzzle-y side of things.What I mean by that is that each Mission (save for bosses) have additional optional challenges that encourage playing optimally. They're largely just "Win in X Amount of Turns," and "Lose No Characters," but there are a few others for select missions. The highlight of this aspect is the side-quests, which are little puzzles where you often have to figure out how to take out an entire arena in 1 turn, or escort an item to the other end of the map in a set number of turns, among other things. These are fun to work out, and test your understanding of the mechanics, even if only a little more than the base missions. Some of them can be headscratchers.The only other element of combat I can think of is the use of switches to raise elevators and open/shut doors. With the elevators, you can manipulate the terrain as a result to score additional attacks by moving them, which is fun.The game features the return of Sub-Personas from Q, but with a twist. Everyone can equip Sub-Personas, not just Joker. They grant 2 additional abilities to the user, and that's it. As a result of this and the lack of Elemental Weaknesses, it's largely just about maximising usefulness outside of harder difficulties, and even then, this game isn't especially hard.Overall, I think if you like Persona spin-offs as much as I do, you're going to have a decent time. If you're expecting something grand, like Strikers, you're going to be disappointed. The game is very clearly rushed in some places, but it's polished, with no issues with crashing or any bugs, at least from what I experienced. If you're unsure about it, I'd wait for a sale, or just play it through Game Pass if you have that. If you just want an excuse to see the Phantom Thieves again, it's a solid time. Overall, I'd still recommend it, but not above playing Strikers.(I'd throw a review of the DLC in too, but I don't have the space, and am probably pushing the character limit as is with this.)

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Tactica is an unique addition to the Persona Franchise, contrary to the belief that we had before it's release that it would be similar to Final Fantasy Tactics or Tactics Ogre, its really different.You have a lot of freedom in the board, you can run with your character here and there (with limited squares), the animations seems fluid, the attacks are really good, its unique.As usual, the soundtrack is amazing!!For a better experience, I recommend turning down the music volume a little bit because for some reason the dub volume of some characters are really low compared to the others, specially Toshiro, there are times when you barely can hear him talking, its not that the music is really loud its his voice volume, you can hear all the other characters lines perfectly but his voice volume is so low sometimes that you can barely hear him (AND ITS NOT HIS WHISPERS, HIS NORMAL VOICE VOLUME TOO!!)(may have subtle spoilers below)I loved the story, for me this game put the Phantom Thief squad to watch what regular people that have no powers, no acess to the metaverse, no Personas would do when facing problems, problems that are really similar. I believe all of them could relate something that the new characters have faced, losing a friend, abusive school member, losing a relative, abusive family and many other problems. It was a really nice touch by Atlus to show that despite having no magic powers, they still faced and solved their problems, showed that it has consequences and that you should be careful, all of this without decreasing the importance of the Phantom Thiefs for society.The different art style was really cool, I loved it. Yusuke expressions always made me laugh, Makoto angry expressions were perfect, it was really cool to see the cast in drawn in a different way, I really liked it.I have only one complaint about the art and animation direction of this game, some cutscenes really needed to be animated, like their entering the doors in the third kingdom, it would made more sense if their entered at least one of them. I really, REALLY HOPE Atlus release an Artbook of this game, I would certainly get one.The DLC was really cool too, Akechi and Joker throwing jokes at each other always made me laugh and seeing Kasumi again is a blessing. Gernica was a good character and I loved her design, specially the one in the Art Report section.I believe it should be more explicit that you CAN USE Akechi and Kasumi in the main story after beating the DLC and that the DLC has no spoilers of the main game story, so people play it before the main story to dont miss out anything.Thanks Atlus for making another great game, it always make me smile to see the gang together again, their conversations and funny moments together,  that last picture of them together in Leblanc gave a feeling that this might be their final game, I hope not but if its, it was a perfect run, 4 amazing rpg games!And thanks to the voice actors, I cant describe it in words how awesome your works is, Erina voice lines felt so touching you could feel her rage, you could feel Futaba anxiety when she was giving tips to Toshiro to a problem she could relate and Yusuke, oh Yusuke, hes such a 8/80, hes either being completely stupid and making you laugh with his crazy way of thinking or hes deadly serious with his I'LL SLICE YOU TO PIECES, Matthew makes Yusuke SO SPECIAL, i LOVE IT.I really recommend this game, 10/10!!

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 5 Tactica is a turn-based strategy game in a mould similar to XCOM or Fire Emblem with some changes that are both good and bad. Generally, I would say that if you like Persona 5 and its characters like I did, then you will enjoy this game well enough to recommend it. My major disappointment as someone who has played Persona 5 Strikers is that they made the same mistake of front loading content at the start of the game. Once you get past the first two worlds, you will see a drop off in the quality of maps, story and world building. It's as if they want to rush you to the end of the game. Below, I have included some basic pros and cons that I think are worth mentioning.

_childDocuments_.review: For a Persona spinoff I've been pleasantly surprised with the game. The voice acting is as good as the original games, the new characters are interesting, and the gameplay is simple but complex enough to be entertaining and challenging. The story so far isn't something to write home about but I'm invested enough in the characters to figure out what happens. The game will best be appreciated by people who played Persona 5, however. If you didn't play and enjoy the original game you will likely not enjoy this one as much unless you get super hyped up by strategy games and chibi anime characters.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial review of this game was extremely positive, but now that I've given some time to think about it, I just don't see the game in that light anymore. I strongly do not recommend this game if you expect it to be as good as the other persona games. Even on the hardest difficulty the games triple threat system is extremely easy to abuse and breaks most of the stages. The story was pretty good up until the 4th dungeon, where the story heavily fell off and the dungeon itself was boring and unoriginal. Trying to 100% the game was also just boring, as it included farming the same stage for 3 hours for experience and money. The dlc was good but I really didn't like how it ended.For the positives I have about the game, it is a good story. While it doesn't hold up at all to the mainline games I can't really fault it for that since it's a spinoff. A lot of negative reviews seem to dislike the art style but I disagree, I like the cartoon style. The music for the game was alright, and I liked the final bosses theme.At best I'd say this game is a 5-6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, but it's overall really short and lacking. It is also baby easy (I played the whole game blind on hard mode with no DLC, never got a party wipe and had 3 KOd party members total). I had fun, but I'm not really sure who this game is for other than fans of persona 5. It's not a challenging tactics game at all, especially once you reach the final area and suddenly you can regen 300+ hp every turn. It's not for people wanting a cool unique story since it's really just about Toshiro's mental state and the phantom thieves live reacting to it. P5T has a cool premise, but ultimately flounders when executing the premise and becomes too easy and too boring by the end of the game, which happens suddenly and abruptly. It's still really fun to chain together way too many 1 more's and wipe the entire map though. I wish the DLC was base game, because it sorely needs more content. I would reccomend waiting for at least 20% off before buying this, since you aren't really missing anything. Best I can do is a 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Persona and you enjoy Tactics games, Persona 5 Tactica is a neat little blend and will be worth your time, especially if you aim to 100% the game. It's sort of like the Mario and Rabids Kingdom Battle game for Switch, but Persona themed instead of Mario. If you haven't dipped your toe into the series, or Persona 5 specifically, it's not something I'd start with, as it does take place after the original Persona 5 ending, though it also doesn't spoil anything from Persona 5. It's a self contained story that kept me interested from beginning to end.The combat had enough variation to keep the game going, though by the end of the story, it was feeling a bit stretched out. I could have done with a couple of less missions overall, as there was about 52 missions and then 15 side quests. A lot of the side quests were simple challenges to try and beat the entire level in a single turn or complete a different objective, which kept it interesting enough. Unlike Persona 5 though, I couldn't see myself replaying levels over and over to get to level cap and fusing every single Persona. If this sounds like something you're interested in still, I think it'd be a solid title at 30-50% off. Depending on if you're going for a full 100% completion, or just clearing the story like I ended up doing.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, as someone who has played all the persona spin-offs this game was actually very refreshing in the ways it plays with the formula. If you've played past persona games a lot of these concepts won't be new but the people making it clearly know that and do interesting things with that in mind (the characters even joke about it), in my opinion. Not every old concept is played with a ton but enough are to make this a game standout, as well as having a good story centered around the new characters. The Phantom Thieves, while not having character arcs of their own, do play a part in the story in nice ways. They exist to help the new characters and I thought it was done well, they aren't completely flanderized and are given more to do then repeat their respective bits. As a persona spin-off, it is one of the better ones if not the best (although I would need it to settle in my mind as I have just beaten it at the time of me writing this).

_childDocuments_.review: Perspective: As you can tell from my profile picture, I am a massive Persona fan. Persona 5 was my first Persona game, and I have played through it 4 times (Twice on vanilla, twice on royal, 3 times on PlayStation, once on PC).When Persona 5 Tactica was first announced, I initially brushed it off as "another P5 cashgrab". But my, as someone who isn't too much into strategy games, I'm glad I gave this game a chance.This game came out literally right as my mock exams ended, and on the day I celebrated my birthday. So, I ended up getting this game.The strategy gameplay is genuinely fun. Mixes the right aspects of Persona and strategy RPGs. The boss fights are also pretty well designed.As for the story, it's actually pretty decent. It follows up and coming politician, soon to be Prime Minister Toshiro, and how he ends up in another world. Eventually, the Phantom Thieves also end up in this world, though this is my complaint with it; it's never really explained why the Phantom Thieves ended up in the Kingdoms. However, the Phantom Thieves meet a girl named Erina, who without spoiling too much, actually has some good character writing behind her. As for Toshiro, he's actually a pretty solidly written character who is funny and has some good character development behind him.However, what really makes this game an 8/10 is hands down the 3rd kingdom. I won't spoil too much of it, because you should experience it for yourself, but it's very emotional, and has some great themes. It's no Royal arc, not even close, but it's still very good.As for my only other complaint, the 4th kingdom is very lame, and the final boss just feels like a copypaste of Yaldabaoth.Overall, I'd reccomend this game
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and well-made tactical rpg. The art style's nice, the animation's great, and the music is also really good. The story's interesting enough for what's basically just tantamount to a really large palace. By large palace, I mean that the game is focused around the characters Toshiro and Erina, with palace referring to Persona 5's dungeons that centered around one particular character's mental palace. I thought that the combat in the game was pretty fun, but I do wish that there were actual elemental weaknesses and stuff. Also, I played through the entire game on the mericless difficulty, and I just outright never lost once, which really just goes to show just how incredibly easy the game is. Some of the side quest missions were semi-puzzles, which I found to be quite fun. I also found that almost every persona ability in the game was kind of just mostly useless, as you'll be killing just about every enemy in the game using the triple threat mechanic. The only enemies that you won't outright eviscerate with the triple threat mechanic, are the bosses, which are decently made, but also just too damn easy.At the end of the day, I think Persona 5 Tactica is a very solid tactical rpg, but it lacks diversity in combat since there are no elemental weaknesses, and almost every combat situation just boils down to figuring out how to best utilize the triple threat mechanic. Hell, the only REAL difference between the characters are their passives and gun hitboxes. Sure, they each have a different type of magic debuff, skill but some of them are mostly useless effects, like despair, and at the end of the day, none of them are really particularly THAT useful in any given situation, since you mainly just use magic as a way to knock enemies out of cover, so you can get a one more, which you'll use to line up a triple threat attack.Shin Megami Tensei Devil Survivor 1 and 2 are both far superior tactical rpgs with better stories and combat. Why am I comparing Devil Survivor 1 and 2 with Persona 5 Tactica? It's because they're both Shin Megami Tensei tactial rpg games by Atlus.I give Persona 5 Tactica an 8/10. It's worth a purchase, in my honest opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Much like Persona 5 Strikers, Tactica should not be your entry point to the Persona series or the Persona 5 family of games...there's little to no character development or exposition among the main cast, and frequent allusions to the team's prior adventure (the game takes place in January/February following the events of Persona 5's vanilla story arc, and - excluding the Repaint Your Heart DLC - ignores the events of Royal's 3rd semester) could leave someone feeling lost if they're not familiar with everything the main cast has been through.But if you're a series veteran itching for another ride with the Phantom Thieves, Tactica translates the Persona formula into an enjoyable turn based tactics experience.  The maps are varied and fun to maneuver and fight in, with lots of elevation changes and obstacles.  The side quests, 15 in all, are like puzzles with basically only one solution, but the main story missions are flexible in how you can win them.  There's a variety of skills, gear, and Personas to use that result in an endless array of combinations for how you approach your battles.  My one quibble is that I would have preferred they keep the original art style instead of the sort of Lanky Chibi style they went with, but that's small potatoes.P5T is a winner.  If you want another adventure with old friends, pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a persona game with a life-sim then this game is not for you, go play strikers.unlike other persona games, this game focuses on the battle system rather than than the out of battle experience.although this game focuses on the battle system it still does a great job at making sure the story is relevant to royal/vanilla and introducing the 2 new characters, Erina and Toshiro. but you should still play it after persona 5/royalNow for the pros and cons of Persona 5 Tactica.so yeah, if you are looking to have a good time and liked persona 5 then this game is for you but i think you should wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike strikers, I don't think this game holds it's own without already being a fan of Persona 5. Also unlike strikers, wanted more of the characters? Good luck. Its heavily centered on the new characters so you'll learn nothing new about any of the dynamics. It's not like I needed more backstory - atlus made it clear its not happening - but the conversations don't add much, with the exception of the imagined weddings, which is actually very fun. I found the early game lovely and that feeling fizzled out quick. Ill update when Im finished + the DLC (hopefully they explain why Akechi is in his Prince outfit and not the black mask) but the game fulfilled its goal I have for all persona spinoffs: Did it make me like a genre I hated? Yes. Its a great tactical game if you love persona, I had my doubts for a genre I hated. Also. the art style gives Yusuke huge hips. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Big persona 4 and 5 fan, and typically the spin-offs to the series is fun too in a different way than the mainline series is fun. This is no exception. I can potentially see how people might react to how too different it is to the mainline game gameplay-wise, but i feel that is essentially what a spin-off to a title is meant to be. Explore new avenues and genres and explore how you can utilize som of the classic mechanics in a different way. I feel like they did a excellent job doing that. Persona 5 battles er usually really quick, so they made the battle encounters in this game also relatively quick compared to most tactics games. Especially if you use your all-out attacks and one-more mechanics efficiently. There is alot of reading and listening to characters talking and hanging out, same as persona 5 also. Which i immensely enjoy, the characters are just so much fun, including the new ones. As usual the voice direction is great and the english voice actors are amazing. Typical Atlus quality. Some issues with audio balancing though sadly, seems like some lines of dialogue are just too low in volume, but it's not that big of an issue. Story was great, of course not as great as persona 5, but it is a spin-off, so it is to be expected. I still enjoyed the story alot.I would say that it was worth the asking price for me personally, but i am a big persona fan, so my enjoyment is very biased. Critically speaking though it is not, it is clear that it is a lower budgeted game, it feels more like an 40 dollar game in my opinion. A great 40 dollar game, but a 40 dollar game nonetheless. So wait for a sale potentially if you are not that big on persona, but if you are, you'll probably don't care and buy it anyway and enjoy it i think. Well, hopefully.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: While it is a little short compared to the other spin-offs from the persona series, I feel that It makes up from that with the story being one of my favorite spin-off stories and adding 2 really lovable characters, with the only two downsides I see is that only the Repaint your Heart DLC is actually worth the price, and that .
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Imma be honest, if it didn't have the moniker of Persona, I probably would ever consider playing this.The game is a simple strategy RPG with an adorably aesthetics, pretty ok gameplay and good music, I think that having a household name like Persona, Atlus is allowed to experiment with other genre within or outside RPG.Would recommend if you like either: SMT/Persona or SRPGs in general (that been said, Give us the dancing game Atlus)
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, although the price is a tad high for what you get (feels more like a $40 game than a $60 game). The tactics combat is simpler than games like Fire Emblem although some of the levels are more puzzle- than combat-focused.In terms of the story it's great to be with the Phantom Thieves and the personalities and attitudes are all there. Erina fits in nicely with the team, and while Toshiro isn't as much fun as Zenkichi (from Persona 5 Strikers) his character acquits himself well.I haven't finished the game or played the DLC yet but will update this review once I have done so.Note: Game was played on the Steam Deck. No issues.|EDIT: Having completed the game and the DLC, I feel like I can still recommend this game with the caveat that I still think it's priced too highly. The DLC was more like a $5-10 DLC than a $20 one, and I still think the game should've been $40.That said, the game is clearly not a "cash grab" on the development team's side. The writers and creators have amply demonstrated their familiarity with the characters and settings and you can tell plenty of care was put into the game's design.Diehard fans of both P5 & Tactics RPGs should pick this up and play it asap. Those just fans of one of those two should probably wait until it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just fun, specially if you like both Persona 5 and games like Xcom (even though it's very much a simplified version of it), although I have to say that cutscenes are really long, and sometimes that ends up with me not being able to play at all for the day. Overall, I'd recommend it after playing Persona 5 Royal, and I still like Strikers more as a spin off for 5.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: A fun P5 spin-off, especially if you have enjoyed games like Fire Emblem or the Mario Kingdom Rabids (which I feel shares the most gameplay similarities with.) The visual style is fun and the voice acting still sounds really good. But the audio mixing in the game does feel off a little sometimes. Like the voicelines being delivered can be very soft, and the music will drown out the delivery of those lines, turning down the music can help but I thought it was a bit weird when I started playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: While personally, I believe Atlus should finally let go of Persona 5 and proceed to Persona 6, this game is still a great pick for those who enjoy the P5 cast.Good points:- the different artstyle is good- the music is still amazing- the changes to how the Personas behave is a breath of fresh air- each of the cast has their own strengths and weaknesses- figuring out how to complete the "finish in 1 turn" optional battles is a nice puzzle- Xcom liteBad points- the DLC (or was it a pre-order bonus?) weapons break the 1st chapter's difficulty progression- standard difficulty is a bit on the easy side- some of the elements inferior to others (Agi is a better knock back option to Garu. Zio halts enemy movement better than Bufu)- movement and range is important, making chars with both low movement and range unnecessarily handicapped.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't meant to be some massive spinoff of the Persona series. But man, this game is massively exceeding my expectations. Love the music, the artstyle is surprisingly charming, and the story, while silly, is actually interesting. This game has been a blast for late night Steam Deck sessions. - Note: Not really a justified price tag but... I don't care.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the actual game is good. Fun gameplay, good writing and character dynamics, and good graphics. Music is a bit more boring than usual, but still nice.The issue is that it crashes. A lot. During a lot of different places, but always in recognizable patterns. Erina's Gun attack, taking a mission with Skull, Noir, and Fox, and anytime Active Support activates. Mostly able to be worked around, but quite problematic.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute love letter to the fans of Persona! Joker and the Phantom Thieves are back and in a new world nonetheless! Aided by Erina, leader of the Rebel Corps, Joker and his friends take down a dictator by the name of Lady Marie! The game is an absolute masterpiece with the amazing new chibi character designs, satisfying combat and gameplay, and funny and entertaining characters and dialogue you expect from a Persona game! Easily one of my new favorite Persona games!!
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: If you love the thieves interacting, then this is a good choice for sure. Although the visuals are more "romantic novel" style the conversations that the gang holds are quite entertaining to me.The gameplay suits my tastes just as well. Compared to Strikers more "hack and slash" oriented fighting Tactica is still strategy oriented which I think will appeal to players of the original game more.Also Erina is the best non phantom thieves character since Zenkichi (extremely biased on this one)
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Persona but it's Fire Emblem. If you were expecting throwing 10+ units onto the field like FE, you're in for a surprise. Combat is three units on the field versus a bunch of enemies. P5T uses the Sub-Persona system from Persona Q but watered down. Sub-Personas in Tactica can only have a total of two skills instead of six. Characters also have skill trees to determine their powers, gaining points to spend by doing quests or having conversations at base. A bit different than FE's Support system.The game also has a cool soundtrack and super cute artstyle! If you wanted to take a bunch of chibis basically into war, this is for you! This game contains spoilers for Persona 5's story. If you want to play this game without getting spoiled, I suggest you play P5 or P5R before playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for Persona and Persona 5 fans. It's fairly easy (so far) compared to other tactical RPGs. But the gameplay is engaging and should appeal to everyone. But one's enjoyment of the game will also be reliant on whether you like the story and storytelling. If you didn't like how Persona 5 went about it, then you won't like it here either. The PC port is great too with decent options and high framerates.It would be irresponsible to not mention that this game comes bundled with the malware known as Denuvo. While I recommend the game, I also don't recommend playing it until the malware is patched out.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty run of the mill tactics game, with enough differentiation that it's engaging. The Persona flare is present, the characters are their usual entertaining selves, while the story doesn't do anything groundbreaking, it's enough to keep you going to experience the amazing gameplay. The unique systems the game has to offer force critical thinking, and the wide array of attacks at your disposal allow for a variety of different approaches to the same encounter. Although, having been playing on Merciless, the difficulty is lacking, and at the very least- inconsistent.Update: The story definitely becomes much more interesting as you continue to engage and are able to learn more about the world, but more importantly, the new characters. The more and more I learned about the dynamic between Erina and Toshiro, the more I wanted to help them out, and as the threads begin to intertwine, it all crescendos into one of the most comprehensive stories in a spin-off. Although the pacing is inconsistent, and the story can be predictable at times, it is engaging enough to satisfy. Alongside the quality tactics experience, it's well worth your money. The boss mechanics are all unique and varied, and the game is a fun experience to 100%
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Another great persona spin-off. Excellent writing, dialogue, and the new characters are all interesting and likable. If you're a persona fan don't write this one off. You can notice the smaller budget in things like environments, but the combat more than makes up for it, and it has the same passion and flair as a mainline persona game.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: This is Persona Tactics, the story is a little weak but and to be honest its a little over priced, but it has a lot of persona 5 charm. Its a cute side story the art is a nice change of pace, the music doesn't miss, and the game play is fun and achieves what it sets out to do. This game is for Persona 5 players and fans of the franchise you wont regret the buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Its really fun so far. Great music, really fun game play with good controls. The game play is straight forward, but it isn't simple so there is fun to be had with strategy and tactics. My only complaint so far is that... there doesn't seem to be a quit game button? The only way I've found to exit the game is to alt+tab out and hit "Stop" in Steam. Which is fine, but it just feels wrong, haha.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin by saying I am a Huge Phantom Thieves fan. Persona 5 Royal is the game that made me fan of the Persona series. Anyways, Persona 5 Tactica is a very fun and interesting game. This version of the Phantom Thieves is very entertaining, the art style of the game is the perfect fit for its game play. Game play is very easy to follow thanks to the tutorials which are not so long that it bores you but also not short enough to leave you with more questions. The story is so much fun and easy to follow EVEN if this is your first Persona game. The soundtrack is a banger as always. I also HIGHLY Recommend the DLC mission, the items are a nice plus but unlike P5R DLC Personas, these are not game breaking easy mode. Since this iteration of Persona game play requires more than just persona strength and more well TACTICS! A must buy indeed either full price or discount TAKE YOU HEART!
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, I am not a big fan of tactica games. I like games like XCOM for sure, but games like Fire Emblem were never my speed. Maybe it is because of the P5 skin, but I have been enjoying it! The game is cheery, the art cute, and it provides a solid challenge (For reference, I am playing on hard right now.) The game itself knows how to explain its features, and found a way to work in the persona system without making it the main focus. Also, the enemy isn't totally brain dead, if you misplace your guys, they will take advantage of it. That being said, it does have some issues. The game is pretty easy, tho that may change, I haven't lost a unit once. I hope it gets harder, but we'll see. I think it is a fun game, and a solid option if you don't like/play tactica like games but wanna either get in or try again.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: Ok while expectations weren't high, this game is worthy of the Persona 5 title, Erina and (in particular) Toshiro are great characters that easily rival Sophie and Zenkichi in terms of depth...But um wheres my P5 remixes Atlas?You are not telling me that you brought back Lyn for one of the last P5 spin offs before P3R gets all the love and didn't remix Last Surprise? OK well maybe it doesn't fit the battle style fair enough...BUT NO RIVERS IN THE DESERT?!? ARE YOU KIDDING ME ATLAS THE STRIKERS HEAVY METAL REMIXES WERE AMAZING YOU PAID LYN TO VOCALISE NEW SONGS BUT NOT A NEW RIVERS IN THE DESERT EXCUUUUUSEEE MEEEEE??? Like what?!? Aria of the soul is obviously back like all the other Modern Persona titles and i'm pretty sure its not a new arrangement so couldn't you of also stuck the original Rivers In The Desert over one of the boss fights? How did you omit such a good song smh. Well at least the new Beneath The Mask goes hard...
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: So, first of all: I love this game so far. It's a new Persona spinoff with new gameplay, a new Story and it's great fun. The story and the music are great and the graphics are too, despite being also something completely new. Some people may not like it, I didn't really like it at first either, but it grew on me extremely fast. It's way more comicy, but so is the entrie game, including the jokes. That makes it less immersive than the other games, but not worse. I mean, it's not even the first time this series tries this, Persona Q and Q2 were very similar in this regard. It also has no open world, the only time you can actively control Joker is during fights. Other than that it's pretty much just a visual novel, but that doesn't bother me. In fact I enjoy this change of pace.Now to the technical stuff: This game runs extremely great. My PC can run that game at highest settings at framerates that are incredibly high and I've not experienced any technical difficulties. The only issues I've experienced so far is that the sound balancing is a bit off in some scenes and that I'm experiencing pretty long loading times, despite my pretty good hardware.And fyi: This game uses Denuvo. Denuvo is trash. It's most likely the cause for my long loading times and most likely is also the reason why the game doesn't run at more FPS and crashes and freezes for some people. I hope they'll remove it at the beginning of the new year and only use it to increase the time needed for hackers to crack the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: having beaten the game due to that unfortunate 15-minute mishap where atlus unlocked the game early I can safely say Persona 5 Tactica is a spin-off with a captivating and canon story worth playing and a Merciless mode which actually poses a challenge that was easy to learn and very satisfying to master
_childDocuments_.name: Persona 5 Tactica

_childDocuments_.review: After a strange incident, the Phantom Thieves wander into a bizarre realm where its citizens are living under tyrannical oppression. Surrounded by a military group named Legionnaires, they find themselves in grave danger until a mysterious revolutionary named Erina rescues them and offers an enticing deal in exchange for their help. What truth lies behind Erina and the deal she offers to the Phantom Thieves? Overthrow your enemies with powerful Personas, an assortment of weapons, and wipe them out with style in this fresh new tactical RPG from the award-winning Persona 5 game.

name: CRYMACHINA
detailed_description: CRYMACHINA Purchase Options About the Game CRYMACHINA is an action RPG where mechanical girls strive to survive in a post-apocalyptic world to become “Real Humans.” But what does it mean to be a “Real Human”? Join the three playable main characters as they fight in fast-paced action RPG combat featuring a myriad of tactics to customize your weapons and challenge your foes. This heartwarming story of love, told by synthetic beings, will pull at the strings of your biological heart. See for yourself whether happy catharsis awaits these mechanical girls as they cry, struggle, and overcome their fate. IntroducePrologue(); In modern times, a strange disease runs rampant. A young girl named Lebel Distel who teeters on the brink of death hears a mysterious voice–”You have been chosen.” Though taken by darkness, Leben awakens to find herself in a dark, post-apocalyptic world and is greeted by an android named Enoa. Leben finds herself in Eden, a structure where machines continue to operate with the goal of creating “Real Humans” to restore humanity. Guided by Enoa, Leben becomes entangled in the battle to become a “Real Human.” IntroduceMainCharacter(); 'Humans get a gold star.' Enoa (voiced by Hikaru Tono) 'Humans are stupid.' Leben Distel (voiced by Risa Tsumugi) “Humans should live in a cool way.” Mikoto Sengiku (voiced by Ruriko Aoki) 'Family makes us human.' Ami Shido (voiced by Minami Takahashi) IntroduceGameplay(); Venture between the battlegrounds of Eden and the safe haven of the Imitation Garden. Within Eden, face exhilarating and cathartic battles against mechanical enemies and discover the unknowns of the dark world. Then return to your base, the Imitation Garden, to relax, customize your weapons, and enjoy lighthearted and heartwarming conversations between the girls. IAskYou (); Be sure to wishlist today and await updates with a warm heart! Steam Version Features 4K Resolution and High Frame Rate Explore Eden in stunning UHD and arbitrarily high frame rates, depending on your hardware. Keyboard and Mouse Control Support The keyboard and mouse can be used to play CRYMACHINA as effectively as with a controller to complement any preferred gameplay set up, from playing at your desk to the flexibility offered by a PC paired with your TV, remote play, or handheld PCs! This release includes precise mouse camera control and the ability to interact with menus using the mouse and keyboard. Additional Graphics Options Advanced graphics settings can be used to optimize your experience for your particular hardware setup! Arbitrary Aspect Ratio: Steam Deck & Ultrawide Support The game scales to various aspect ratios. This has been tested from 21:9 to 4:3, but should also work well on any display in between, including the venerable Steam Deck’s 16:10 display!

_childDocuments_.review: Additional Info:In the late twenty-first century, humanity is on the verge of extinction. Centrifugal Syndrome, an unknown cause sickness, is steadily wiping out the population. At first, we see people vegetating on hospital beds, but following the death of our protagonist, Leben Distel, we find her in an empty chamber, where she is greeted by Enoa. We're now 2000 years after the end of the world in Eden, a space construct, and Leben, like others, has been picked to prove to herself whether she can be human again. Enoa, the benign Deus Ex Machina, develops a digital soul for Leben, one of three digital souls given mechanical life. The first Deus Ex Machina, along with Eden's global order, vanishes just before Leben awakens. Your four protagonists will now set out to defend themselves against the attacking armies, figure out what happened to the other Dei Ex Machina, and gradually improve their humanity, as the amount of humanity in a machine is determined by the number of experience points (ExP spelled E cross P) they have.Most notably, the game is generally text-heavy. Before or after a mission, we convene over a cup of tea to discuss current affairs or get to know each other better. Tea parties are normally necessary, although some are optional, so they must be held if we want to go on missions again. This also earns us EGO points, which I'll go into later. As a result, the optional tea gatherings are worthwhile as well. After you have viewed all of the necessary tea parties, you can choose from a number of predetermined levels or check out alternative coordinates from the notes you collected in previous levels.Once a level is selected you gain ExP by killing enemies, which you can use to level up your characters, EGO points, which you can use to improve your individual stats and Enoa's support in battle, and you can collect Sentiments, which are armor pieces, as well as floating secondary weapons called Auxiliaries. On the field, you'll also find personality data that Enoa can crack for loot, such as new weapons and Auxiliaries, as well as EGO points. It doesn't do anything that no other action RPG has done before, but it does bring enough to the table that you can experiment with different customizations. Unfortunately, the actual combat is where things get stale. It's just a shame how much style and unique animation has gone into what is, admittedly, a rather simple battle system because it quickly becomes button mashing with little diversity and the limited number of enemy types doesn't exactly help either.Now, let's talk about the weapon systems. We have the primary weapon, which is different for each character, as well as head, torso, and waist equipment, and even two supplementary systems. The Auxiliary Systems round out the overall presentation. Shields, Combat, and Interference Weapons are only a handful of the kinds available. Each of these systems is available in varying degrees of rarity, and as a result, they have different status values and gimmicks. What's fantastic is that you have complete control over how the available attack modes are configured. There are also boosters that can only be used once to provide system benefits, such as lowering enemy defenses. This means that each configuration has a different usage factor and that each have a different maximum utilization value per system. If this usage max value is reached, the system enters a cooldown period during which it cannot be used.When you're not in combat, you'll hang out in the Imitation Garden, a safe, digital space where Enoa can engage in casual conversation with the three heroines. These deal with more mature issues such as the fear that your consciousness has been uploaded into a robot body and what that entails, and I enjoy the characters in CRYMACHINA because they are nicely written, even if they are a little clichéd. But, despite everything these people do, I can't help but believe that they don't fit in as well as they could. There's no doubt that the situation in Eden is serious, but while the atmosphere in Imitation Garden can get a little murky depending on where you are in the story, there's never any real lasting conflict between the cast, and if there is, it's already history or it's broken up by too much comedy.It should be noted, however, that everything has been dubbed in Japanese, which is not always a good option because there is a lot of chatting in the middle of numerous battles, and in an action RPG, you don't have time to read subtitles to grasp what's going on. An English dub would have been preferable. The background music is also excellent, with the anime opener and another similar segment in particular sticking out. And that, combined with the highly distinct but outstanding art style, is something you don't see very often. It attempts hard to be a character-driven drama about grief and pain as they relate to the subject of becoming human, but the connections between the characters are superficial. And, while CRYMACHINA's beautiful and amazing character designs stand out, they cannot redeem a game marred by dull, repetitive combat and dreadfully linear dungeons. Nonetheless, I see things in this title that I haven't seen in any other title.CRYMACHINA has a unique environment, fantastic soundtrack, and a really interesting graphic style combined with anime aesthetics that I really enjoyed. Unfortunately, there isn't much else to do with the same old battles, monotonous and straight dungeons, and sometimes clichéd dialogue. You get to know the people, their likes and dislikes, how they interact with one another, and how Eden works. There are some surprise story twists here and there, but everything is fairly straight forward. CRYMACHINA is a decent action RPG/hack'n'slash if you don't mind a lot of reading and the very simple level design.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, An amazing game that's terribly boring when you play it, but makes you emotionally attached reading it.As you MAY have already know, this game's all about four robot lesbians that fight to find themselves and to live. To sum the whole thing up, it's a SoL + Yuri + Romance + Visual Novel + Action RPG + Dungeon Crawler game. Emphasis on Visual Novel, and Yuri. It doesn't get more complicated than that.Most of the game is spent focusing on character building, romance and yuri. The rest is pretty much everything else.The settings is, somewhat similar to Shin Megami Tensei and others, as in "mankind is dead" settings. Except, in this world there is no demon, there's only machine. The story isn't really interesting as it's mostly straightforward for the beginning... until the twist hits. Several times. The game will introduces more characters later for both supporting and antagonist side, but they have no time for any character development at all and they are rushed compare to the main cast. It's such a bad thing, but the game itself is already short enough since the reading part take up more time than the gameplay itself. Which, speaks of gameplay and stage design... Oh my god. This is tedious. The game explains so much you understand so little. You can beat the game, mind you, with the launcher button. This game has the attack that's equivalent to Arc of Obliteration on crack from Dragon's Dogma and it destroys everything and lets you snowball with 15 levels behind. But here's the catch, the level scaling start from 20 and you can't have a low level run. But being low level (just above 20 levels of difference) means enemies give more EXP, which in turn you can exploit the hell out of it to level up everyone. Or how about "every single stage is just a long corridor that you walk to the end",.... It's just a broken mess that you have yet to seen how simple and braindead it is.So what MAKES you interested in this game? It's simple. The main cast, their voice acting, the music and the artstyle. The pacing of the game is too fast, and it feels like they have no intent of hooking you in. But that's fine, because it's merely a plot device for the characters to develop. The entire game's just this way. You couldn't care much about the story even if there's some interesting twists here and there, but you ARE invested in the characters, because they're just that good, and even with the pacing of an average Counter Strike Source bunnyhopper, the character developments don't feel that boring or too rushed (sometimes), and you enjoy it. There's moments that, if it's played out without voice acting it loses its impact completely on the player's feelings as a whole, and it also elevates the interactions between characters. You get to hear, and read and develop a proper connection to the characters as a player who's watching them getting closer as a family and lovers, their stories in previous life and what they think about the world etc, etc... it gives you that emotional push to finish the game. It's one of the game that you couldn't help but to keep playing despise all the garbage jank that stops you from playing because of how repetitive it is. But, due to the fact that it's a visual novel and, there's not much of "visual" parts except cutscenes and some very specific parts of the game, you don't get to see much, once again, it's a shame.The artstyle/graphics is what I would say "unique" among the other anime-style games, because bosses can have really really good designs (if they're not recycled enemies posing as bosses) and character sprites are very expressive. Then the music hits. I have no words to say other than "What did I just listened to and why is it so good". The entire soundtrack, composed by Sakuzyo, as well as vocals done by Hikaru Tono, is just simply phenomenal. I didn't feel like anything sounded repetitive, even the one that plays during the talk scenes in tea party; each one of them is very unique and Jesus Christ dare I say for once an OST with this long range of music type - including dubstep which sucked ass and has died since like 6 years ago - feels like a waste on a game like this. Honestly without the artstyle/graphics, the characters, the voice acting, and the music, I would have not even bothered to play this kusoge.This game could've been great, like really great. I wanted to read more stories of the main cast because of how good they're, yet the story ended so fast I just feel really bad that I'm so invested into stories of these girls' life and their love for each others. The artstyle, being really good but limited by the lack of variety in enemies. The voice acting and the music are without flaws, but because the game's so short, it also makes you want MORE of them. I 100%'d this game in 13 hours. The endgame contents sucks because, its just more tedious gameplay, and you get 12 more tea party stories, but that's it. THAT'S IT. Nothing else. Do I recommend it for the things I listed above to be positive? Yes. Should you buy it? HELL NO. Wait for sale. Don't buy this thing in full price. Even if they're releasing a new DLC that's currently exclusive to Nintendo Switch version, it's just gonna be reskins of the main cast anyways. There you go, another yuri action game that's unfortunate enough to have severe flaws that stop it from being kino.

_childDocuments_.review: Much like its predecessor ,  is a story-driven action RPG with great visuals and flavorful anime characters, and overall a game with lots of emotion and personality. Some say that  is a much-improved version of , but as someone who played through both games one after another, I beg to differ. Each of them has its own strengths and weaknesses, and picking a favorite among those two is rather difficult.The two games have unrelated stories and can be played individually from each other. While ’s story is a personal one (the protagonist journeys through purgatory to find her younger sister's soul and bring her back to life), ’s narrative takes place on a grander scale in a futuristic setting, even if it's not quite a space opera. ’s core message is also deeply impactful: humanity is not given by being born as a , but by having a heart, a soul that loves and protects the ones that it cares for.Two thousand years ago, an unknown disease with a 100% fatality rate and a mysterious cause wiped out more than 20% of the population. Because of resource scarcity, the rest of the population engaged in a war and eventually went extinct. In their last moments, the remaining surviving humans created a gigantic space structure (called "Eden") in hopes of preserving their species. Eden was equipped with eight Dei ex Machina (machine gods): self-evolving, artificial life forms whose only purpose was mankind's resurrection. The game’s storyline starts with the sudden disappearance of the first Deus ex Machina, which leads to a war for control among the other Dei ex Machinas, causing havoc on Eden. To overpower the machines, command them back into order and install peace, a "Real Human" is needed, as to machines humans are gods. For this purpose, the eighth Deus ex Machina (Enoa) revives a young human girl (Leben) by encasing her soul into a synthetic frame, essentially transforming her into a battle machine. The team led by Enoa and otherwise consisting of Leben and two other girls, (Ami and Mikoto) will try to make their way through various virtual areas of the space structure, fixing the corrupted machine code and overwriting it with Enoa’s, while also trying to gather enough ExP for Leben (the “chosen one”) to become a "Real Human".Both games use the same formula of alternating between individual missions and story bits. However, ’s story is much more ample than ’s, covering most of the gameplay. The missions, which in  took 30-45 minutes each, were spawned over several floors with lots of side paths and had dozens of enemies to fight, are now squeezed into very short and linear runs that usually take less than 10 minutes and end in a boss fight. Barely any enemy is encountered and every mission is basically a straight and quick path to the boss, with some of them having an optional micro puzzle that unlocks a high-level miniboss.This 180° turn in the design might have been a response to the complaints about  that the gameplay is too repetitive or boring. Personally, I find this decision to strongly downgrade the fun of the game. While the environments are extremely spacious and beautifully crafted, they’re not meant to be explored. You’re not even expected to spend much time traversing them, because there’s almost no one to fight ( has at least ten times more enemies). The boss fights are rather lengthy, thus most of the “action” part of the game will be spent in the boss room. I love the visual novel aspect of the game and that roughly 75% of the time goes into reading through the story, but during the action parts of the game, my fingers were itching for some quick hack-and-slash action and unfortunately,  failed to fully satisfy this itch. It’s considered a hack-and-slash game, although… there is  hacking and slashing.In each of the missions, you will play as one of the three girls, with you being able to freely pick which one of them to bring into battle only during side missions or in the additional content that you can unlock after the main story ends. Unlike in , where all four playable characters were always available and you were also allowed to switch between them mid-run or even mid-fight, here the main missions are usually locked to a specific character. This means that you will have to equally level up and gear up all three girls to be able to overcome all levels / boss fights, which will require a bit of grinding.In between missions, the girls gather for a tea party in a virtual garden, where they will chit-chat about their progress or plan their further actions. Most of these cutscenes / dialog sequences are mandatory for story progression, but there are some optional ones with some extra dialogues that add flavor to the game and help build up the characters, all of them being fully voiced. The virtual garden also acts like a main hub for the game, allowing you to transform the items collected from missions into pieces of gear (using the same “cry” mechanic from  ), organize your equipment, upgrade combat abilities, consult the encyclopedia of enemies and story concepts, etc.The combat in  retains its simplicity from , which for me is one of the most enjoyable aspects of both games. Your basic melee attack and your ranged attack will fill the damage gauge of the enemies. When it’s filled, you can perform a heavy attack that downs them, followed by a finishing attack on already downed enemies. Rinse and repeat this sequence until the enemy is killed - that’s pretty much all there is to it. You can also dodge attacks by dashing away or sometimes counter them by parrying and additionally make use of three extra abilities (a heal and two damage-increase skills) that can be upgraded with the currency gathered from your runs. The difficulty of the enemies depends heavily on your level: being 2-3 levels lower makes them pretty difficult to kill (requiring lots of attacks) while being 2-3 levels higher can kill regular enemies even with one hit. The bosses hit very hard, and often you can even die after a couple of their hits even if your level matches theirs, and even on the easiest difficulty mode. It’s a game in which you have to constantly dodge the attacks, but fortunately, there’s a pretty clear visual cue that shows you when you're expected to do that. The required reaction times are also very decent, the enemies allow you enough time to dodge their attacks as long as you're not stunned. is more of a Yuri visual novel rather than an action RPG. It’s a decent and enjoyable game, but it won’t scratch that itch of mashing buttons and seeing enemies drop dead. The visuals and the music are top-notch, the story is immersive enough (as long as you enjoy lengthy reads), and the combat is fast, fluid and to some extent effortless. Given that it’s a ~20-hour game, with around five extra hours of grinding for 100% achievement completion, I’d say that the asking price of $60 is rather steep. It’s certainly a game worth playing or wishlisting if you’re into some casual, laid-back hack-and-slash action, but it’s advisable to wait for a sale.You are invited to read  if you want to find out more about it.

_childDocuments_.review: CRYMACHINA is one of those games which seems to have dropped off the radar.  In a nutshell, you're paying for a very well written, story driven game that focuses heavily on it's character interactions and deeper themes within a sci-fi setting. It has fun combat with linear and succinct level design that does a good job invoking atmosphere and imagination but with little substance. It has spectacular art and sound design with a fantastic soundtrack which I went out and bought immediately after finishing. It relies heavily on visual-novel style storytelling but also presents itself with cinematic cutscenes on occasion. Fundamentally this is a compact story driven game, mostly because it doesn't deviate at all from it's core story into endless side quests like most games of today. Expect to finish the core game in 18 hours, although there is still plenty to do in the post-game. A lot of people compare this to Nier;Automata. The combat has some similarities, it's also a game about androids in a post-human world. However CRYMACHINA has a greater focus on character interactions/relationships with one another, tells a completely different type of story with a completely different range of themes, and has a much smaller budget. It can be just as heavy though, and has just as much potential; I was a huge fan of both games and I desperately want a sequel to this one.  As an added bonus, Yuri fans rejoice because this one has plenty to offer here.
