_childDocuments_.review: Tons of fun to play, and very challenging. Expect to die. A lot. Game has a sense of humor that starts to feel snarky after awhile, but I think it gives it a bit more spice. Everything goes at your pace, so it's definitely relaxing and very strategical, though if you try to play it fast, you're probably gonna have a bad time.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Still one of my favorites. The guys at QCF Design know how to make a game and how to interact with the community. I've been following this project since alpha; I have seen the hard work and sweat and love their small team has put into this project. Also: play the alpha. It's free, it's absolutely excellent on it's own, and it's entirely different than Desktop Dungeons as you see it now.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, every hour I play this game I realise more and more how much I love it. The gameplay continues to be compelling even 100 hours in, I still haven't unlocked everything or beaten every challenge and the soundtrack... Oh, the soundtrack. Even if you never buy the game, you should buy the soundtrack!Once I eventually unlock everything I'll probably be sad there isn't more, but it won't stop me from playing whenever I want to fill a few minuites with something fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Should you play Desktop Dungeons?Desktop Dungeons is a rogue-like turn based RPG that plays out perfectly. Definitely a one-of a kind. Honestly, the game is fun, strategic and has received a lot of acclaim and approval from the gaming community. But getting past that, is it really a game you want to play? You start out as a Human Fighter trying to beat dungeons, steal their loot, all for the rightful mission of building your own cities. On the way, you meet fearsome monsters and plots that could end your city..Or fund your wealth. A lot of story-telling is involved, for example, you can even call forth the power of the ancient deities to aid you in your quest, or make a Pact with another to become more resilient. There are a lot of customization and combinations one can try to beat the levels. This game is definitely worth its price. If you doubt my words but still want to give this game a whirl, you can always wait for it to go on sale, then give it a try.Should you play Desktop Dungeons? Yes, you should definitely play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Simple in concept and easy to pick up (even for a 15 min break), but this game offers perhaps the most depth and challenge of any I've seen (and that's saying something!). Requires exceptional calculation and improvisation - a unique and challenging blend that may not be for those faint of heart. You will die - LOTS. But, if you're looking to test your limits in a puzzle-like dungeon crawl, you can't go wrong with Desktop Dungeons!I played the free version of this before picking this up on steam. While very similar in style, this offers a much better campaign, better learning curve, even greater challenges, awards, versatility, polish and so much more.Highly recommended for anyone with masochistic tendancies.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like ROGUE-LIKES? Do you like PUZZLES? Do you like CHEESE?If you answered yes to two or more of the above questions chances are you will enjoy Desktop Dungeons.Each dungeon can be completed within 15-30min, meaning it is perfect for lunch-time playing. Or in between bigger work projects. Or instead of those silly work projects that keep you away from the next dungeon. Who needs a job when you can defeat MONSTERS from your chair? Not this Orkish Warrior. Nuh-uh. No Siree.UPDATE: This game is great if you are unemployed and have time to kill monsters. Do recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this on a Linux Ubuntu 14.04 laptop plugged into the big living room TV.  It goes full screen no problem but the graphics are in 4:3 so it has the black borders on the side.  Some say the game has bad graphics and I am not sure why.  I have seen games with way more pixelation where everyone is talking about how great it is.  To me what matters is, are the graphics pleasing to look at? With this game, I say yes.  It has a nice overall look.It took me awhile to warm up to this, but I love this game.  It is a great turn based strategy gem.  It appears to be a RPG dungeon crawl but it is not.  Dungeons are solitary one floor puzzles.  Each time you start with a level one dude. The money  you earn lets you upgrade your town which gives you more dudes and starting buffs to choose from.  So it is RPG-ish but not much.  It is pretty challenging but totally doable.  Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Great Rogue/Puzzle adventure!More Puzzle than roguelike but attention to detail at it's finest.  Mash strat, stat and items to overcome evil all the while managing your health, mana and survival.  Begins easy but comes on strong and really gives you that 'Atta Boy' feeling when you've completed a new level.  Many ingame achievements such as winning without use of healing or mana pots, using only physical or magical damage, won the round with each of the various classes, etc.I keeps you going that's for sure but the difficulty ramps up the farther you go and unlocking new classes, abilities and powers for your Mage, Thief, Fighter and Priest (to start) which should hold most of the 'genre' to a good long while.I had played the free version for awhile prior to the purchase of the retail so I'm hoping to get more time in it amongst the other dozen or so of things I need to get back too (lol, gamer ADD am right?!) but it's nice to play a round at lunch or while on an important conference call for work (note, please do not impact your work productivity on a game; that's foolish.. OR IS IT?) Regardless, love the idea, design and playability on this one and I hope you do too!~Icky
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good roguelike game but to those gamers that hate any form of rng be warned if your gonna pick it up. You have plenty of options to control your luck and with some simple logic and mathmatical skill you can overcome some bad luck. However sometimes you might not get the clutch item you need, or be short just a few exp for a level up due to unlucky situations. so beware the gods of luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is HARD!  Don't let that put you off - there are a large number of very clever and well thought out puzzles within this game.  Most of these are small and perfectly formed; you can play through in a short space of time.Generally when you fail to complete a dungeon it is because you made a mistake; this can be frustrating but it is immensely satisfying when you do complete it.There is an element of grinding - you need to unlocks gods, classes, races and gear to be able to complete some of the challenges.  You can still have fun without doing the ridiculously hard challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent strategy game with quirky humor to carry you through the first few hours, and by then you'll understand how to use game mechanics to pull off a clutch win in every level. Every 5 minutes. Then you get adventurous and try specific character builds (full mana gnome warlord is hilariously cheesy, to name one) and eventually take on the vicious levels, which are well-designed gauntlets you need to really plan for. The devs did a great job on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Fun roguelike. The mix of beating maps with various different heroes and building up your town and heroes to get stronger works very well. There is no real story, but the individual dungerons each have a bit of story to them. Like most of these types of games, it starts easy but gets progressively harder. Also like most of these games, there came a point when it got too hard for me and I quit. Still recommend it for those who like a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the idea of this game, and I even like the game itself, for the most part, but I cannot recommend it.The learning curve is deceptively shallow until you pass the Easy dungeon. Then, it gets steep quickly.I haven't decided if the problem is the procedurally generated levels (meaning you can't figure out the right path and then execute it properly on the second run, if you didn't manage it the first time), or if the problem is the tricks you can use to beat things beyond your normal abilities (an expectation that once you've encountered an ability, you'll be able to put it in practice like a seasoned rules lawyer).Either way, the Normal dungeons are all too difficult for me, even after several runs at trying to solve them.The result, however, is this: far from being a fun and quirky game you can use to fill ten minutes for a break from your work, it becomes a frustrating problem that has players spending much longer than intended trying to beat a dungeon, any dungeon, before giving up in furstration.Great idea, lousy execution.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive, clever and a lot of fun!But beware, this is NOT a rpg, this is a pure puzzle game!Your goal is to get as much xp as possible in the dungeon, which means fighting monsters which are higher lvl than you. If you succeed in taking down a high lvl monster you get bonus xp. If you pull that off enough times you will have high enough lvl at the end to take on the boss monster.+ nice gameplay concept+ a lot of variation, many classes that play differently, new gods, monsters appearing and so on...+ nice humor+ great extra puzzle mode
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Like most Rogue-likes, it's stupendously difficult. Prepare to die... A lot. I'd say I win about 1 out of every five to ten games I play. It's enjoyable none the less. Extremely enjoyable. It's nice ot have something that you can take out and play for about ten to fifteen minutes while on the train.Do not buy if you're the kind of person who gets stupendously butt-hurt because you lose fairly often, then avoid this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hardcore puzzle/roguelike game. It will stretch your problem-solving and optimization skills to their limits and still find ways to surprise you hours into playing. The combat/leveling system is deep and rewarding, and there is a near-endless amount of content and quests available to keep you going for weeks. I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I expected this to be good. However, I was surprised at how good, and how addictive and fun it is. Normally I play games like this for 20-40 hours and then get bored of them, but I'm at over 100 hours on this and still having lots of fun. Well worth getting. Still haven't finished the "final boss" quest yet, but even when I do, I imagine I'll keep playing it for some time, it has a lot of replayability.If you like strategy/puzzle games, this is a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic gem.  Very surprised this game doesn't have more popularity than it does.  I've never played anything like it before.  Some have called it a puzzle game, which I think is a bit misleading.  It's more an adventure game that requires smarts.  Would definitely recommend it to any indie game lover.Support great stuff, please.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great thinking game that you can play in very quick sessions (dungeons aren't that long) or as long as you want (jas that just one more dungeon! feel). This is one of those games where when you figure out how to beat a dungeon you just feel extremely happy because you are pushing the game mechanics to their limits, you have to play almost perfectly and strangely enough its so satisfying to time the advanced (even basic) techniques to get ahead in the dungeon. Loved the free version (you can still find that), so I had to pick this one up with the more polished graphics, polished mechanis, and small city-upgrading meta game. Well worth the purchase!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily one of my favorite games of all timeFor fans of dungeon crawls, Race and Class drastically changes strategy and play style. For fans of roguelikes, each level has a different layout, but still keeps certain criteria to avoid automatic losses and have unique themes/events in later levelsFor fans of puzzle games, the game becomes incredibly difficult in the later levels and requires careful planningEverything in this game comes together and every piece plays an important part. Easily worth more then $15; you will get your money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: The deep strategy, clever tongue-n-cheek writing, and the challenging difficulty make this game a must play for anyone a fan of fantasy/RPG or puzzle/strategy games. Unlocking all the races and classes is very fun, and trying out new missions and strategies is a real challenge. I laughed aloud more than once, and the illustrations and music are both highly entertaining. Overall, this is a well made game.I will say that, as a new player of puzzle/strategy games, this one is a bit over my head at times. Perhaps I'm just not good enough, but I found myself dying a lot in the later game. And, honestly, I doubt I'll ever "beat" it. It becomes very difficult. But, if you like that challenge, go for it. Deaths aren't cheap; they're earned--easily earned, but earned none the less. No cheap deaths here.All in all, this one was a surprise for me, and I love it. Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: GoodLikes:- innovative game mechanic where unexplored tiles are used as a resource -- uncovering tiles is the primary way to heal and regain mana, but damaged enemies are also healed.  You have to strike a balance between exploring to discover items and enemies, and saving exploration for when you need to regen.- strategic gameplay that is somewhat puzzle-y- has puzzle levels- has daily challenges- a lot of things (classes, enemies, items, upgrades, etc) to unlockDislikes:- once you get the hang of the basic strategy, you pretty much just apply it to every level.  It is still fun, but I wish there were more strategies.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons is one of those games you would not imagine it could be so fun! It has copious amount's of jokes scattered all over the game (even the main enemies are a joke - Freaking Gots, C'mon! LOLz!). I've neglected it a few times because the first impression didn't capture my eye, but as Steam pushed and insisted I've decided to give it a go, and boy... was I wrong in ignoring it... oh yeah! I'd say if you see it on sale  and if you like puzzles, RPG and sarcasm buy it
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game.  Each dungeon is random but you need to kill and pick up items in a certain order or you won't be able to get out.  A bit frustrating but also entertaining.  I highly recommend getting this game but you need to pay attention to the character class and race you picked versus the monstor that you are going up against.  Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: 10 minutes or less? Yeah right... This is definitely NOT a RPG. This is a ressource management system. Not a game. A system. Because a game is supposed to be fun. After many hours, I realised I did NOT enjoy it.When you realise you can't beat the boss because you'r missing 1 HP, you don't learn from your mistakes, because next time it's gonna be completly different (random). You also realise you waisted your time from the begining because you either kill yourself in frustration or exit the dungeon with a few miserable gold pieces.This is nothing more than an elaborate software to learn basic math.Music is beautiful though. At least I still have the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game at this time.  It is -not- pick up and play as mentioned on the page, and dungeons can not be finished in 5-10 minutes unless you are an expert at the game and know all the strategies.  The fact I had to reference a strategy guide during the tutorials repeatedly was a big warning sign.As it stands I've barely made it past getting the banker, and I've spent the last four hours trying and failing to finish any dungeon at all.  The game is beyond difficult.  If you aren't willing to sit down and do some number crunching and brain math, don't waste your time.  This is not a casual, low-input game you can fluff through.  I'm going to try sticking it out a bit, see if maybe something clicks and the game gets easier, but it's getting lower and lower on my priority list and will probably end up in my 'waste of time and money' list.It's a shame, because I enjoyed the premise, and it certainly seemed cool on the surface.  I just didn't realize I was in for Dark Souls the Puzzle Game minus the part where keeping your nose to the grindstone eventually results in progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Game would be much more fun if it wasn't impossible to win. You spend all this time setting up your strategy, carefully exploring for health and mana benefits, but in the end you get your ♥♥♥♥ kicked in by overpowered enemies of your own level, and you are nowhere near level 10. I know what the spells do and how to take advantage of special skills, potions and all of that jazz, but it never helps.You'll just be wasting your time with this game. It's not fun; it's work. Hard, fruitless work. Go ahead, buy and play the game. See if you can get any farther than I have.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: dungeon-crawling with a big focus on utilizing map resources wisely and killing monsters in the most exp-efficient ways. every map is a new puzzle onto itself, not to mention the dozens of class-race combinations and preparations to embark with. this was basically my favorite roguelike a few years ago and now it has loads more content and polish. the free version is still available on their website too to try out.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons is a good game for what it is. I played free variant for a long time, before picking up this  release.The released version adds more of everything, more monsters, spells, classes, quests, rewards ...This version also has upgraded graphic, making everything more charming.Game play is turn based, with monster being stationary (some bosses have blink spell, that moves them unless you counter it.). At the beginning dungeon has fog of war. You reveal parts of dungeon by moving to adjacent square. You want to be carefull how much of a dungeon you reveal, since each square you reveal, recovers some of you health and mana. This is the main way you will recover health and mana. This means that exploring too much too early can leave you unable to heal, later on. On the other hand each square you reveal can have beneficial items, that you might want. This makes unrevealed tiles in dungeon weary important resource.This is a quick game. Once you get used to controls and basic concepts, you can easily complete a dungeon/quest in 5 min. If it will take you longer it will be because you spend time thinking of best move.Game is also paced quite well, so at the beginning you only have access to one class and one race (human fighter.), but you quickly unlock more.With all that said, it is important to remember that this game is a filler game. It's meant to be played in short sessions.If you play it for hours, you will quickly become bored. But playing couple of dungeons every day, while waiting for whatever bigger game you are currently playing to patch itself, it is time well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelike game have always been one of my fav this game is no exception. Desktop Dungeons is pretty a good one at least when you play it for the first hour on "easy level" everything goes smooth and it's been a pleasure. Then after 2 hours the game starts to be rough.You have to think carefully before making a move or you could hardly beat any normal rank levels. constantly hit and run of a higher level monster, think which magic to keep and sacrifice is important and sometimes you need luck to beat one level. It's quite like the tutorial says:" prepare to die a lot."So overview this game is quite good but, like I said this one is difficult, but once you get used to it and can manage to get over most levels the game will become enjoyable.(probably you will devote lots time before make it through...)
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: best lil indie puzzle game ive ran across in awhile, got the free beta version and luvd it so much i wanted to support the devs by buying into their primo versionpart roguelike / part rpg , then mix with a sudoku/puzzle braintwisterits both devious and delightfully arty/funny/mean/witty/sharp/hilariousdeadly goats? nerdy racism? pointed jabs at politics and economics? sadistic gods that reward or destroy the pious at their leisure? ya this game has it all =]
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant game to play for a half hour before work, as a warmup to a more mentally challenging game, or to binge play for 10 hours with a 2 litre botttle of coke and a tub of celebrations. its got a good sense of humour and decent power balancing. I bought full price and would do so again, its a bargain if its on sale!!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the original, you'll definitely like this one as well! Like the original, you need to complete dungeons in order to unlock new classes and races. More or less the same story here, but there are a lot more possibilities and I think also more control over what to unlock first. This is a great game to play over a short break. (Though some of the dungeons may take a while.)It is on special at the time of this reveiw. If it's on special, definitely definitely get it! If not, still get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game since the Beta/almost-ASCII days and loved it immediately. As time went on and they added fun graphics, better mechanics and a game that was more cohesive and gives you some (very loose) direction it's just gone from strength to strength.It's a real brain puzzler, fun and sometimes frustrating - you really have to extend yourself to get passed even some of the normal levels but it's a lot of fun learning!Steam says ~30 hours on this game, Steam - you know nothing! I'm sure that can be tripled with all the pre-Steam iterations of this brilliant fun little game!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite puzzle games. Challenging but rewarding style of game. You will probably get frustrated sometimes but in the course of this you will begin to learn which leads to a great feeling when you finally do overcome the challenges. Wait till it goes on sale though as 15.99 is a steep price for this type of game IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really bad for productivity! In the end its always "i'll stop after i clear 1 more dungeon." and I ended up clearing 2-3 more dungeons before i manage to stop. Its really fun, its easy for starters and hard to master, after 40 hrs of playing i still manage to make newbie mistakes and ended up killing myself when i'm already near the end of the dungoeon. Definitely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I've lost count of how many times I've told myself "That's impossible" playing this game. I've also lost count of how many times I've proven myself wrong. Desktop dungeons is an amazing puzzle/strategy game disguising itself as a dungeon crawler. It's a game for people who enjoy figuring out the minutia of the game's mechanics and using them to squeeze every little extra bonus you can out. As many other reviews have pointed out, it's a great distraction for over a lunch break or when you generally need to kill about 10-15 minutes. The semi-random nature of the dungeons can lead to some runs that are genuinely impossible, but I've rarely felt cheated by it because of the small time investment. Nearly 150 hours in, and having cleared over 90% of the game, and I can still say that there's still plenty of "that's impossible" left in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game. It's a rogue-lite dungeon crawler where you always know exactly how much damage you and the enemy will do, so you always know if hitting something will kill you. This leads to you running to and fro in the dungeon, preying on weak enemies, throwing everything you have at monsters two levels above you for an experience boost. I frequently find myself betraying one god, worshipping another, downing three potions, and killing the big boss to leave myself with a handful of health. Rogue-lite in this case means that you unlock new classes which give huge gameplay changes and new races which give different small buffs that occur only when you trash items.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Marginal thumbs down.  Desktop Dungeons is a decent rogue-like game with puzzle elements.  My main issue that it is a timesink.  It is alright that a game makes you die a lot, but this game give you nothing on death.  Even when you win, the player has to go through dozens of level just to unlock minor upgrades.  Worse, once upgraded, nothing much happens since the game adjusts to your leveling.I wish that the progession was less like a slog, since the gameplay hits a sweet spot.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a hack 'n slash game, it's a puzzle game and boy is it frustrating!!  The exacting combinations needed to win past the first few levels is annoying.  I want to like this game so bad.... it's tough when 15min of work leads to a mear 20gp because I had no way to heal myself for the final battle or the boss was too high level.  Too many options and choices and you'd better hope you pick the right ones.Also becareful using he altars!!  I was geared up and poised to take down the boss, drank a mana potion and WHAM, diety stripped me of all my gear... so much work for nothing.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: People call this a roguelike.  Despite appearances (quests, races, classes, spells, weapons, monsters, potions, etc), it's more like a puzzle game. It's a sequence of single-screen dungeon crawls, each with a different character, starting at level 1.  Dungeons are randomly generated, plus there are some semi-random quest dungeons and completely fixed puzzles.  The game rules are simple enough, but complex strategies emerge.  It's easy to learn and difficult to master, although I have to say mastery would be a little more attainable if there were better in-game documentation.  There is of course a wiki.One last warning: it is addictive.  As in: "Holy crap, is it 4:00 tomorrow morning already?"-class addictive.  Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: OH MY GOODNESS! This game has to be one of my most favorite games i've played for a while. It takes RPG like elements and says "Oh you're good but i'm going to make you better :)"  when you first start it will be a little difficult but don't stop then keep pushing on because this game is a must buy for this year if not in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Tried the free game, was addicted in moments and loved it.  Bought this game yesterday Love it even more.  I can see myself playing this game a lot.  Love how the individual sessions are relatively short but tied together with the kingdom.  I am already just replaying lower level areas for fun even though I haven't unlocked it all.  Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game borrowing some ideas from Roguelikes and RPGs, Desktop Dungeons is a game about killing monsters in as effecient a way as possible, you can level up high enough to kill the final boss.  This may sound like a typical RPG, but it's not.  Each dungeon dive take a few minutes, with gold earned used to add new options for future dungeon dives.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy slot machines? Do you enjoy games of chance? Do you enjoy games that you have very little control over the outcome?Then we've got the game for you. Desktop Dungeons. 95% luck-based gameplay! It's a hoot. Everything is determined by random number generation. The map layout and enemy / item placement factors heavily on whether a dungeon is beatable or not. You can carefully work your way through a dungeon for 30 minutes, just to realize at the end that you don't have enough health and there is no way to recover the health you need to win. This happens most of the time.So if you enjoy gambling and dislike strategy having any influence on whether you win or not, this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly fun and addictive game.  It short it is a procedurally generated micro solo dungeon crawl.   It has basic rpg theme elements of classes and races which set your base skills and character progression.  Add in a layer of equipment and inject a play strategy based upon one's deity of choice and you have a pretty large degree of freedom and replayability.  While the layout and enemy composition change between runs of a given dungeon there are consistent parts.1. a set number of mobs of each level up to 102. a set # of glyphs (spells)3. a set # of skill ups4. a set # of shops5. Undiscovered tiles which restore health and mana when explored6. A set # of potionsLike some gameshows you can retire from the dungeon at any time and keep your winnings thus far.   Which is helpful when it is impossible to defeat the dungon boss and just need to amass gold to improve your town.  A run becomes an optimization problem, in which the player needs to maximize each step and attack to best utilize the resources at their disposal.This game scratches the itch of a turn-based roguelike rpg that can be played in 10 minute chunks.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I haven't played Vicious dungeons, but did 'finish' the game.This is one of the best games I've played in a while. Simple to learn, but there are many aspects you need to master in order to succed.The difficulty curve is great: not to steep, but somehow manages to be engaging all the time.The dungeons are extremly varied, each one having its own little quircks, and requieres that you rethink your approach.As a negative the game resolution sucks:(, which is a shame because the art style is quite charming.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I played and really enjoyed the "coffee break"-length first freeware version of Desktop Dungeons, and was looking forward to see what the full, fleshed out version was going to look like.  The core mechanics are still there - strategic turn-based dungeon crawling that plays out like a puzzle you're trying to solve, maximizing the efficiency of every attack, every move - along with a beatuiful music and graphics upgrade, heaps more of the dry, witty humour, more classes and races, and bit of a story arc/narrative progression through the missions instead of randomly generated encounters. (although it's got those too)It also feels like the difficulty was amped up a bit more, it seems a lot harder to get up to Level 10, so the game isn't as "casual" as the freeware version.  Not that I didn't have to stop and ponder about how to best solve a dungeon in the freeware version, but I find myself doing it a lot more for a lot longer in the full version.  It's not necessarily a complaint, but it feels like a map takes about 20-30 mins to beat, verses the 10-15 mins I felt with the freeware version.All in all an excellent light-hearted puzzle/strategy game with some decent depth and tough choices to make. Recco'd!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a dungeon crawler/roguelike: it is a puzzle game. This must be stated upfront, as I think the only reason you wouldn't like this game is if you expected something different. The other warning is: this game is hard. Ridiculously ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard. You won't beat it 100%. This isn't because of cheap difficulty, though; quite the opposite. The game mechanics have a shocking level of depth to them. Everything is carefully considered in the way it's designed, and the game expects you to have the same level of forethought in order to win. Will decently entertain and challenge you for quite a while before you can progress no further and give up. There's also a good bit of humour in the game, which I liked. The art style isn't too detailed, but it doesn't need to be. It looks pretty good and should be fun if you like challenging puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: A complex simple game concept I played DD off and on when it was still beta years ago. I'm very happy it has finally made a real release on steam. I think DD is best described as a resource dungeon crawler. You do the standard dungeon crawl. Delving into dungeons, slaying monsters, collecting loot, and (hopefully) defeating the boss in order to emerge victorious, but instead of regenerating you resources [hp/mp] these are regenerated by moving to unexplored areas [aka fog of war]. This forces you to think about you next move. Think of ways to stay alive so you can defeat the next monster, gain lvls and equipment, so you can win. There are also a number of classes and races with different abilities. Each class has deferent strengths and weaknesses that you can adapt to your own play style. This coupled with a number of levels/terrains equates to hours of fun. Highly recommended as a good dungeon crawler game for casual player
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly addictive game with a fantastic sense of humor. It combines dungeon crawling with resource gathering and city (kingdom) building in a straightforward, well-balanced and enjoyable way. On the surface it may look like a roguelike, but it's really more like a puzzle game; failing a dungeon doesn't lose you much. Besides, the game provides you with such positive and encouraging messages when you die! Also, goat bosses!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop dungeons is one of those "easy to learn, hard to master" games. You can play one map in a few minutes. However, the difficulty will put most people off in the first few hours. Even following the tutorials and puzzle packs, the power/class comibinations are so mired in minutiae that even on the simplist of maps you will not be able to figure out a winning solution.You will die, often, even after 50+ hours I can barely clear 10% of the maps. Is the game fun, yes. Could it use some fixes, yet. Should you buy it? Yes, if you like a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: While it's certainly a difficult game, the difficulty never felt unfair, and actually makes you feel proud for completing levels in certain ways. The difficulty rises in a way that keeps you coming back for more punishment, and it's a fun game to waste time with as most dungeons can be completed in just a few minutes. If you like challenging strategy games with good replay value, than this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I have actually been pleasantly surprised by this title, almost to the point that I wish I could share the in-game experience with a friend.The gameplay is simple and straightforward, and at times the game can be fairly difficult.  There is a fair amount of depth to some of the combat, and at times players can find themselves in real trouble if they don't properly manage their resources.  Regardless, it is a casual game with low system requirements, and it is deliciously old-school in terms of scope.  There is a long-term objective in building up your kingdom, but in terms of gameplay, your characters are not saved - levels gained in a dungeon are not carried over, though your game progress is.Check it out - the game is fun with just the right amount of nerd appeal for RPG fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been into roguelikes, but Desktop Dungeons is fun.  It streamlines the concept a bit, simplifying it just enough for me to have a good time.  First you choose a race and a class (more of which get unlocked as you play), and move around a small dungeon, killing monsters and grabbing treasure.  Exploring new parts of the map heals you, so you want to make sure you don't over-explore too early.  There aren't a lot of healing potions on each map, so you'll need those unexplored tiles to heal yourself after each fight. I've enjoyed the free "alpha" version for years, but didn't think the full version would be worth the money.  I finally bought it on sale, and so far I think it's been worth it.  The most obvious improvement is the graphics, which are now vibrant and whimsical, but still very simple.  Instead of just starting a dungeon through lifeless menus, the game is now framed with an expanding town.  You can still get into a random dungeon with just a couple of clicks, but you also have the option of completing specific missions that help improve the town and unlock new options.  This version of the game is a bit friendlier than the alpha, with several optional tutorials and practice dungeons to teach you how various things work.  But this user-friendliness doesn't mean it's lost its edge.  It's still a very deadly game of resource management, and I still lose much more often than I win.  But that's what makes it fun. If you've never played the free version, try that first.  That will let you know if you like the gameplay.  Then, if you really enjoy it, buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best games I've purchased. Ever. Desktop Dungeons is like a nicer kid brother of Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup. It offers more expanations, humor, and artistry than the original while still murdering your about a thousand times a day. Every time you think you have the upper hand, you quickly realize that your favorite strategy was amateurish and that it couldn't possibly be viable at higher level play. It isn't quite as intricate as its predecessor, yet DD is more easily enjoyed by a wider audience of gamers. Anyone who loves crunching the numbers and breaking games will get tons of hours from this purchase and the more casual gamer also has much to enjoy from the charming fantasy world created.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the flash version for seriously lengthy amounts of time, I was quite keen on getting the full fledged version. With about 10 hours under my belt, I still have mixed feelings. This game is more of a puzzler than a rogue-like. There is a heavy amount of strategy in the game and multiple ways to accomplish the tasks, but it is not the dungeon delver game that I was hoping it would be.The game is hard, but fair. Any time you die, you'll realise your mistake or you'll wish you were a little luckier in finding the monsters you needed. Many of the puzzles will have you banging your head off the wall as you ponder just going online for the answers, but the game can be beaten normally.I think that my biggest complaint is the lack of depth. As you progress through challenges, the game gets harder, but you don't really get better. The later classes that can be unlocked are just variations of the same character and there is no character advancement whatsoever.I'm on the fence about recommending this game. I got it through the humble bundle and I think that it was a worthy buy for that, but the lack of depth and the one-off nature of missions makes this a no-go at MSRP.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle/RGP game. Pretty addicting because you can keep on going through the same dungeon with different combinations of races and classes and enjoy it everytime. Highly recommended. I got it on sale which made it very worth it for me. Don't know if it's worth $15 but if it hits a sale definitely get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very addictive and quite fun. Every class really does play in its own way (with the later ones being especially distinctive). The various spells are all useful and fun in their own ways (and feel well-balanced). The game provides for several distinct ways of maximizing your experience points, important since leveling up within the limited span of the dungeon is perhaps the single most central game mechanic. Quests, varied dungeons and unlockables just give it that bit of extra structure and keep everything feeling fresh until you realize you lost track of your whole day.The only gripe I have, if it can be called a gripe, is that there's an awful lot of quests that ammount to "beat this same dungeon several times with different characters", all added to your map at once, which can feel slightly grindy and discourages you from the characters you just unlocked.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like a facebook game, a puzzle game, and a roguelike squished together, but the actual dungeon gameplay is very much about being clever with resources. This is a game where exploring the fog of war doesn't have a direct cost - it has a benefit, and misusing that benefit is what has a cost. I like it~
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical but bought it anyway as I'm having to spend a lot of time off my feet at the moment, damn am I happy I went with it though!In short, for the Too Long Didn't Read, it's purely a strategy game and not for the faint hearted. For those who like a brainy challenge however this game is a must, it combines many elements of strategy with a tidy interface and no dithering about. It allows and even encourages you to plan far in advance and won't interfere with these plans - as a result however when it gets hard it really doesn't mess about.It takes a few games to get your head around it but it's very simple to pick up. The outcome of every move is predicted and even an entire fight is easy to plan beforehand with little indicators showing how many attacks it will take with the selected move to take down your opponent and how many he will need to take down you. In this way you can easily see for example that you each need three attacks so if you attack twice and then use a GETINDERE glyph to ensure your attack lands first you will win the encounter.It has found an interesting balance for exploring a dungeon. On one hand you want to find new glyphs and stat boosts but health and mana is regained by exploring so ideally you need to utilise that first, but otherwise it is not punished.Monsters only ever retaliate so braving the unknown is at practically zero risk. Just as long as you set right click to attack to avoid inadvertently killing yourself against a higher level monster.If I were to have any gripes it's the lack of direction the game gives you. Not so much the Minecraft sense in "here's a world go amuse yourself" but more in that it gives you TOO much to do. I currently have about 15 quests, several requiring multiple dungeon runs to complete. Completing one will often generate two more. But monetary rewards are good incentive to upgrade your kingdom to provide more options for starting a dungeon.Overall it's a beautiful game, a true challenge but not in the "haha I instakilled you now do the last half hour again" way. More like an elaborate chess game with increasingly complex challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the alpha from 2010 and I love this version even more. Quick and puzzle-like dungeons are fun to smash through over lunch, each takes about 5-15 minutes. This version adds some much needed balance, variety, and persistence to keep me coming back for more. Also you can play from any* browser by linking your steam account on their site. I can see myself coming back to this game again and again over the coming months.*If your browser of choice supports the Unity web player.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just freakin' glorious.*Especially* with the hard work the Extreme Edition development team is putting into it.Yes, the game isn't as similar to other roguelikes as you might think based on the images; it's more of a resource-management puzzler with some rpg elements than a dungeon crawler. You can be *really* creative with your dungeon crawling if you truly dive deep into the mechanics and figure out the edge cases. If you're not sure if that's your cup of tea, they've left the free alpha up on their main website for plenty of years, and while it's very rough around the edges and not nearly as complex or feature-rich, you'll get a feel for how the game generally works.Link here: Now, this game in its vanilla state already has *tons* of content, especially if you're a completionist, but if you're playing this game in 2020, there's almost no reason not to pick up the officially sanctioned Extreme Edition mod as well. If you wanted to, you could ignore all of the new content and go about your journey as normal, but eventually the new dungeons (almost all of which are much more challenging and unique than vanilla dungeons) and the new classes/items (that you can get at any point) will tickle your fancy and the new mechanics generally push what is possible in this game with its current mechanics without doing something drastically new. Plus the mod developers have a strict "no base game changes" policy (that might eventually change through a second edition of the mod) so you don't have to worry about not getting the vanilla experience on a first playthrough.Try the alpha, and if you like that, you'll absolutely love the full game. And if you dislike the alpha but only for its lack of polish, the full game refines the formula to a T.Anyways, there's one caveat if you're playing this quite old (but wonderful) game in today's world: The mac version doesn't work with Catalina since it's 32-bit. If you *aren't* playing on a newly updated Mac, give this game a try; even if you end up not enjoying the gameplay, it's got a charm that just doesn't disappoint.I've been playing this game on and off since 2011, so if that doesn't tell you something, I don't know what will.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: First time writing a review, but this game deserves it. Very engaging and can be tricky right from the start. The premise is simple, its a puzzle game that brings the rogue-like to its simplest level. It then expands upwards with a great deal of complexity to make a completely different game. If you get stuck early on, don't despair. Take a look at the beginners guide on its wiki site and you should be on your way.If you are a numbers guy/girl, you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!It IS hard. It IS unfair (sometimes at least). But that's not a problem - it's an asset. DD has a high replayability and you will have to do several stages and tasks again and again because of wrong class, race, equippment or just one false klick. But in fact that's the thrill: to master the game you have to play some perfect rounds, know all the tricks and skills and of course you need a bit of luck.That sounds less fun than it actualy is. You got to plan and think a lot, but winning a difficult level will outweigh that. The approximately 10-15 minutes of playtime for each stage (when you survive, otherwise playtime can be much shorter ;) ) are well balanced between a short break and not loosing to much time in case of failure.A nice fact is that you can play DD after buying on Steam not only via Steam, but also via the DD website. A nice amusement if you are not at home and on a PC without Steam and don't need download and install anything. That works for Windows RT tablets too.When playing via website please consider, that Steam acchievments will not be unlocked and it does not count to your playing time. Otherwise I would have several hours more.In the end a good occasionally game you should not take to serious. At any discount a must-buy if you like roguelikes and have a good frustration tolerance. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously though. This game is /hard/. If you like grind your skull against the wall difficult matched with simple to learn controls, straight forward challenges, and great gameplay pick this up. All the difficulty and depth of the game lie in just how creative, careful, and well-thought out your strategy is.And even if you die, a succesful dungeon usually runs 10-15 minutes tops. Its not an issue to restart and go back at it a different way, or with slight changes, or just a info gathering run that doesn't net you anything but forewarning.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Deceptively simple looking game that is actually quite intricate and tricky. The action is comprised of a series of small turn based "dungeons" that takes about 15 mins each. Between dungeons you have the opportunity to improve your kingdom by spending the loot (if any) that you've managed to gather allowing you a greater range of hero classes and bonuses.Gameplay is fun but does get repetetive, however at the price it's worth the risk.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly my favorite rogue-like OR puzzle game. The amount of choices you can make and how those choices affect your chance of success is truly awe-inspiring. As you traverse the game, you can see yourself improving as well as your character classes improving. In order to keep a challenge, they introduce new more difficult enemies as you reach new milestones. It is the kind of game you can lose hundreds of hours in (I know I have probably sank almost 150-200 hours into this one.) I have been playing this game for so long, and I am still not very far. I am just now starting to get to "hard" dungeons, so there is an incredible amount of replayability there.I've been playing this game since it was in its alpha form, back in 2011, and every now and then I still come back to sink in another 10-20 hours (not all at once). To me, it is the Skyrim of rogue-likes/puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This review is for the Desktop Dungeons Soundtrack, though the game is great too and also recommended.This soundtrack is extraordinarily good. I can't stop listening to it while doing random stuff. It sounds like a masterful orchestral composition, but it is just a game's soundtrack, this game's soundtrack, and I think it is just made by two dudes. It is about 107 minutes long, comprised of 25 full length songs. The music has a retro feel to it, often reminding me of tunes from SNES and Playstation RPGs of the nineties. I highly recommend getting this soundtrack, with or without the game. If you enjoy orchestral or nostalgic tunes, are looking for something sort of relaxing and musically involved at the same time, or are a Baranowsky fan, this soundtrack is a must.Edit: And with a quick google query of Grant Kirkhope, the other music guy on the album, I've learned he also did Banjo Kazooie and DK64! Lol.. this is really good stuff here...
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Counting the alpha (Which is still free and an excellent demo of the game) I think Ive clocked the most game time to dollar hours ever on this game. Not really a rogue-like, more of a puzzle game that uses a rogue-like as a framing device, the number of unlockables is absolutely staggering and the game is incredibly deep.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming puzzle game that involves pacing your progress as a character leveling up defeating monsters in a dungeon. Exploring the dungeon (uncovering tiles) is how you mainly restore health. Items, races and classes each have their strengths and weaknesses that change how to progress best. Taking on difficult monsters as early as possible quickly becomes required to defeat dungeons. Defeating dungeons earns you money to unlock more classes, races and items. Try out the free alpha on  but take care not to get addicted to it :P
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This little thing has been sucking up a wholly inordinate amount of my time lately.  It is on its face a little rpg lite type game, where you maneuver a little adventurer around a series of procedurally generated maps looking for loot and baddies to win to level up to face the boss.  That on its own would be cool and fun and a little enjoyable time waster, but there is a second 'meta' level of developing your town between quests to gain access to better starting goodies, more classes, races, etc.Even then, I would have been happy to play on its own, but theres something more devious and hooking (for the right kind of personality) than either of those first two aspects.  When it comes right down to it, the game is quite simply far too hard to enjoyably play on just its face value.  The tutorials begin to show you the true way, which is that really every map is not so much a dungeon to adventure in, as a very cunning and difficult puzzle in the shape of a dungeon.There is absolutely a 'right' way to pass through each little dungeon that maximizes your xp, items, and chances to victory, and it is almost never the straight forwards way of just running around and clicking enemies as you come by them.You want to slow down, pace yourself, calculate each new move, each new click to maximize the value that you can extract from each scenario.  Sure you can fight a bunch of random level 2 or 3 enemies, when you are level 4, and you will win each fight easily.  However if you alter the pacing, and fight one of those level 3 enemies when you are level 2 instead (and have the right mix of skills/stats/items to win) you'll get a serious XP boost for defeating it.  Multiply that out by the 20 or 30 enemies on a map and you can be a whole level or two higher when fighting the final enemy.Each class and race has some little unique twist which lets you change the rules around and re-optimize your approach, and you can mix and match some of the random dungeon attributes (as you level your town up) to maximize your chances with the mix you choose for each map.TLDR?  This game is far deeper than it appears, its much more tactical/strategic than it is a cute little rpg, and the difficulty level absolutely demands you play to the higher level if you want to get through all the various scenarios of the later game dungeons.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I just enjoy this game a little too much its not healthy, Some one take this addicting game from me! PLEASE I don't want to be digging through random trash dungeons trying to get my fix. THIS IS NO LIFE FOR A SELF RESPECTING MALE!Aside the addiction this game is great get it, you'll end up preforming oral favors to completion upon your daily duties just to play it or selling your body whichever works for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great but resolution is HORRIBLE.  It's designed for ! You can't see anything in 1920*1020 unless you use x2 zoom settings then it looks blurry and ugly.Great idea but you don't expect people to design games for 800*600. If you are going to charge people $15 please hire a designer and design it for modern resolutions such as 1920 or at least 1400, 800*600.I really like the game but can't pass the horrible resolution and blurry pictures. Stay away unless your computer and monitor bought in 2001.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: A challenging and rewarding roguelike with funny writing, well-tuned gameplay, and creative mechanics. Really captures the learning curve component of the genre in which you are rewarded for being clever and learning from your mistakes. The short format is fresh and the persistent components like unlockable classes and challenges keep me coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a rogue-like stripped down to the bones. I find it quite fun but I wish that the graphics were higher-res. The low-res scaled up looks pretty blurry. I'd recommend if you are loking for a turn-based rouge-like RPG that can be had in bite-sized chunks.Also, would recommend picking it up on sale for $5 or less unless it just really really hits your game sweet spot. You can get a lot more game with better attention to graphics and UI detail than this in the $15 area.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: rctuth Demighty was a prime example of a Barbarian... was. Unfortunately he could not overcome the heavily armored vampire that was master of the dungeon. Barctuth Demighty bravely ran away with what little loot he had managed to gather. He fared better than those who never return.Desktop Dungeons is an interesting little roguelike in which everything is a carefully managed resource. Gold, inventory, enemies, even unexplored dungeon areas must be handled in a delicate balance as one progresses towards the boss. You will die uncountable times in your quest to learn the nuances of dungeon exploring, but the wit and fun of the game take the edge off the many failed attempts.With 112 different race/class combinations, every randomly generated dungeon brings a new experience for any play style. The dungeons are small enough that a run can take as little as 10 minutes, excellent for the casual gamer who doesn't have hours to spend at the computer.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue-like dungeon crawler. Turn based fun. Surprisingly deep gameplay for what looks like a simple game. Each dungeon is only around 10 minutes long, so you don't have to sit there and grind all day long. At this point, I only have ~1 hour into it, but that is probably the equivalent of 5 different dungeon runs. The authors also have an excellent sense of humor, and clearly don't take themselves too seriously, which I like :)
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the original (which is free download on their site) and enjoyed it...you will LOVE this one. It has all the same mechanics but a bunch more unlocks and additional things like building a town and puzzle packs. The only con I have so far is the graphic options are not my favorite. You do't get resolution sizes but just 1.5x, 2x and its not the sharpest at the biggest size. Otherwise a great game and sure to suck 10min sessions from my life over and over.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: A really clever game, with a ton of depth and strategy. The best description I can think of is that it's an RPG pared down to it's most fundamental elements. The neat thing is the amazing variety of strategies that come out of the basic rule set. The character classes all have a ton of meaningful variety, and to win on the harder levels you really need to be playing to the strengths of the character class you're playing. The religions vastly change the way you play, and will sufficiently punish you if you aren't. And the random elements (items you find, monsters that you encounter, etc.) are guaranteed to keep you on your toes. Although there ends up being a ton of classes and abilities and statuses and items and religions and monsters, the game has a nice meta-structure, where it won't populate elements that it hasn't explained to you yet. Basically, it's a great game and anyone interested should certainly play it.Also, I am not sure if the steam version allows it,  but if you buy it directly from the Desktop Dungeons website, you can play it out of your web browser, which is kind of nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Question yourself, question your sanity, question just how much time you actually have. Question how many runs you can do. Question if you can kill that guy. Question if you just saw a red outline. Question if it's worth checking the wiki. Question whether or not to convert that item. Question whether to explore and regenerate or use your resources.Question yourself, question your sanity.The only thing you shouldn't question is whether or not you should buy this beautifully simplified roguelike, the answer to such a question being a resounding YES
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game since the alpha version and it has been great to see it evolve into the finished product you see today.  This is the kind of game you can shelf for a while and come back to play it for 10 - 30 mins and then shelf again.  The gameplay gets more complex the further you get, to the point that some dungeons might seem impossible to complete, but with the right items, god worship, and stratergy you can beat it. It is definitely isn't your typical rogue-like, but if you enjoy unique puzzles, don't mind a game that's a challenge, or love goats, then buy this game.  It is well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game since it was freeware and loving it all the way!  The game presents a very interesting take on rougelike / RPGs by adding unique leveling, healing, and skill elements which turn it in to a hybrid puzzle game.  The latest verison includes a lot of advancement and unique classes, skills, and upgrades.  It's certainly worth the pricetag just to explore it's unique take on the genre.  My only gripe with it is the graphical scaling; it just doesn't look as good as it should on higher resolution screens.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game since the Alpha. I remember when they started to remake it. I remember pre-ordering, and playing in the limited web browser version. I say limited because it didn't always run smoothly.And it finally is released. I love this game. Have since I first saw it. I'm a proud Alpha turned Beta pre-owner, and will never forget it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: A while ago I played a lot of the earlier, lighter, version of Desktop Dungeons, and had a lot of fun doing so, but even playing that didn't prepare me for the fantastic game that DD has become with hard work and polish.Its essentially a rogue-like puzzler, with an overworld progression that doesn't get reset when you die, but you do have to replay the dungeon you were in when you succumbed to evil.Pace is very good, the game makes sure that you don't end up in an unwinnable situation unless you really, really try hard, and if you do, there's plenty of sidequest you can fall back on, and improve your town and unlock new items, races and classes to improve your chances.Theres even hand-crafted puzzles, that beside being fun and really challenging, teaches you advanced tricks and tips, which you can then use on your next quest into the dungeons around your settlement.Classes and races are varied and play very differently, and the quests are different enough that there aren't just one uber combination thats going to win every dungeon for you.Dungeon runs take somewhere around 15-20 minutes, some faster, some slower, but the game can be played at exactly the pace you like.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice game if you have half an hour to wait on something. Do a little dungeon and come back later for another. I've been playing the old game alot, and I realy like the kingdom part they put in the game lateron. It is an easy game to start, but can get frustratingly hard the more you play. I realy reccomend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I was in the MANvsGAME chat when this was due to be released, and in that chat was Danny Burnowski (Sorry if that is spelt wrong) - One of the amazing music artists of this game.Watching MAN get a sneak peak into the game absolutly drew me to it. The night it was released, I bought it... and glad I did. It's everything you want in a tile based kick up the ass.Amazing game, and the music is delicious.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Just makes you want to keep creating new dungeons. However, be warned. Although it says that this is a casual game, it is not. Complex strategies and deep thinking is required to get you to the end of each dungeon. 10 minutes per dungeon? Sure, but you'd usually never finish it. And yet, it's so addictive that you'd usually play again, with no improvement. I'd seriously recommend this game, whether you'd like to release stress or build up steam. So, if you are thinking of getting it, just get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of hyper-strategic games and sarcastic meta-gaming, this is a must-have. It's also a must-have if you only have enough time for one dungeon run, or don't want to get sucked up into a long game. Regardless! I've been a fan of this game since its alpha stage, and it's come a long way since then.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after watching a few hours of let's plays on various channels, and deciding that it was something I'd be interested in. After buying it and playing fifty plus hours on it, I've finally "finished" the game. But I haven't even touched half of the content yet. This is a game that will keep you coming back again and again, and provide countless hours of content to you. With multiple classes to choose from, 28 dungeons, over a hundred items, and a unique take on the roguelike genre, this game is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: A great game where you get your money's worth. I spent 33 hours on it and still haven't unlocked everything. It may seem difficult at first, but once you get the hang of using the mechanics to your advantage you will be clearing out dungeons in no-time. That doesn't mean the difficulty will rise though, the later levels bring in all sorts of gimmicks to make you think. However  there will be situations where a randomly generated dungeon will prove unsolveable.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I played this since it was a game competition beta. And then i sort of forgot about it. And then i was sent my preorder keys. I am totally blown away. This game has evolved in such an amazing way. This is just the ultra deluxe version of the already awesome time-killer i once played. Excellent graphics. Fantastic Music and sound (i mean *really* fantastic!) and the gameplay has gotten so much smoother. And as a topping, very decent wit has been added. 100 of 100! Perfect! Just how games should be. And i played my first computer game waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaay back in time :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: If your a fan of Rouge-like, Play this.If you like Puzzle games, Play this.If you like Dungeon crawling, Play This.But what ever you do.PLAY THIS GAME!!!!!Found it online a year or so ago and bought into the pre-beta thing. Now they've made some great changes to the interface and gameplay.Activated it on my steam account and CAN'T stop playingReally why aren't you playing this game???
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good , I have noticed some peeps complaining about the price , but all I can say is that I have had more fun with this game than I have had with many full priced titles , the game is hard and addictive , and when I say hard , I mean justone more go hard and it doesn't reall get frustrating. It also has an amazing amount of content and replayability , plus a really nice retro vibe to it too.If your on the fence about this game , then dont be , and if it does go on sale at any time soon grab it immediatley !
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelike meets puzzles while city building and resource management get busy in the corner.  What seems simple at first reveals itself to be complex and layered.  Not to mention very difficult (seriously think dark souls hard).  However the difficulty adds an old school arcade one more go feel.  This game is more addictive than football manager.  If you are balking at 12 quid for it when there is a free version do not worry.  The paid version has so much more content than the free version (city building etc) and is much more refined and well balanced.  The years of refinement really do show when comparing the two versions.  One of the best and unique indie games around.  A must buy.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons has been in beta for a very long time now (well over a year or two!) since it's debut at the IGF in it's free form. Since then, the game has grown massive beyond the inital scope and idea, adding in a story, many new classes, races, monsters, and so much more. The gamepay, however, has remained largely the same: Explore a randomly generated dungeon, fight monsters, collect loot, and defeat the boss. But in true rogue-like fashion, your ability to accomplish this is left up to fate and skill. Each new area you explore has different rules and layouts, with features like gods to pledge your loyalty to or shops to buy needed equipment. You will curse at your computer, you might throw your keyboard and mouse across the room. But the game itself is rewarding when you finally get that perfect run together with that smooth combination of careful planning and a touch of luck, leaving you with a warm feeling and a craving for more. PIck this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons is an interesting game and worth looking into, but it's not quite the 'roguelike-lite' that it advertises itself to be. Each dungeon is one level (occasionally with a sublevel with more treasure or more enemies) and your adventurer always starts fresh at level 1 at the beginning of the dungeon, so there's no characters that carry over from dungeon to dungeon. The most notable difference between this game and other roguelikes is that monsters in dungeons do not move and do not attack until you attack, which causes the game to become more of a puzzle game than a genuine roguelike- the challenge comes not from the monsters themselves but rather budgeting your resources and defeating the monsters in the correct way to give your hero as much power as they need to defeat the boss monster and defeat the dungeon.That's not saying Desktop Dungeons isn't entertaining or worth looking into, though. As far as being a sort of time-waster to play inbetween ordering a pizza or during a break at work or something, it fits perfectly since each dungeon could take at most 15 or 20 minutes to complete. The gameplay suits itself well to playing in short bursts rather than sitting down for long sessions and as such is a perfect fit for the busy gamer looking for a more intricate experience over Bejeweled or games on Facebook or something.That being said, I'm not entirely sure this game is worth the $15 price tag. Maybe wait for it to come on sale for $10 or less, then go ahead and make the dive.One final note: The soundtrack, made by Grant Kirkhope (Banjo-Kazooie, Goldeneye, Perfect Dark) and Danny Baranowsky (Binding of Isaac, Super Meat Boy) is excellent and fits the game well. Makes the dungeon-crawling a lot more thematic and interesting than it would have been otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Dungeons is an incredibly balanced coffee break roguelike puzzler with truly surprising depth. It's a thinking person's Minesweeper with cognitive clutch play that never cheats and always rewards. It's easy to pick up and play, offers plenty of strategic nuances to discover, and makes you feel like a genius every time you defeat a dungeon boss.Desktop Dungeons features a wide array of races and classes to play, spells and equipment to wield, gods to worship and dishonor, and a limitless supply of varied dungeons to conquer. It's witty, whimsical, and has some charming art and an exceptional soundtrack. Well-paced progression will have you coming back again and again. An instant classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Part dungeon delving rogue-like, part puzzling strategic thinkery. Desktop Dungeons does something original with its influences and it it does it in bite-sized chunks that leave you either begging for more or screaming for mercy - right after you clean up the blood and gore left from your previous failed delve off the dungeon wall. It is ruthless in its difficulty, but patient in its desire to teach you to think out you every step - and you will be punished for failure. Succeed and you will be rewarded, for these dungeons are packed with wealth, just as this game is as stuffed with unlockables as a goblin is loot.  Desktop Dungeons does requires some math for success but it might trick you into enjoying it. The sucked me into pushing for just one more dungeon over and over again, but its punishing difficulty did mean I found failure more often than success.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to understand, very hard to master. It's a very simple yet nice rpg/puzzlegame. Tactics and stategy is all that matter, very few luck roll and usually you don't count on them. Graphics is functional, the musics are nice. The game is very dept with a lot of class/race combos that always play differently.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: Has all the elements of a classic rogue-like dungeon crawler game, with the added bonus of missions being finishable in under 20 minutes.-Enough content to last for a hundred hours of thought provoking dungeon crawling.-Short mission-based dungeons allow for easy pick up and put down play.-Will ruin your productivity after 1 playthrough. Procrastination at its best.Hundreds of hours in, and I still come back for the randomized daily missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: I have been in the beta for this game for years now. Hell, I started playing Desktop Dungeons when it was in alpha! It has come a long, long way, and it's now hard to believe that it's finally officially released to the public. This game is a roguelike brimming with content. Enter mini-dungeons to complete quests, unlock more classes, build up your town, gather new equipment, find new dungeons, strategize your efforts... and of course... die a lot! If you like roguelikes, this is a great, great game. You will get addicted, you will get frustrated, and you WILL have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Desktop Dungeons

_childDocuments_.review: This is the hardest game I have ever played. It makes Dark Souls look like Nintendogs. Ryu Hayabusa would not survive one of these dungeons, and in fact would break down in tears. You have a higher chance of beating Battletoads on 2-player mode (with your kid nephew as the 2nd player) than beating this.If you enjoyed the (still free and still available) alpha, then you will enjoy this game. If you found the alpha too hard, you will find this harder.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent puzzle game pretending to be a roguelike. Presents a thoughtful game system, gives you a dozen or so character classes that each surgically break the game system in their own special way, and asks you to exploit the breakage to complete difficult challenges.I love it to death, and you should too.

name: Forgive Me Father 2
detailed_description: Play the first instalment of the franchise About the Game Journey once again into a malevolent world inspired by H.P Lovecraft’s myths where madness awaits on every corner. Embark on a path to salvation as you continue the story of the Priest character from the first installment. How long can you balance on the edge of sanity? Will your sins be forgiven, or your soul consumed by madness? Distinctive dark comic-like visuals Dark hand-drawn graphic design where every frame looks like a page from a comic book is one of the pillars of Forgive Me Father, and the sequel brings a fresh perspective to its unique style with improved sprites, models and atmospheric lighting effects. Prepare to feast your eyes on juicy blood effects and animated gibs flying everywhere! Dive into the madness Defeat Lovecraftian nightmares with a wide range of weapons. Fight hosts of diverse, formidable enemies and beware: each and every one of them evolves into different, ever more evil and twisted forms of themselves - this journey does not get any easier! Gear up and fight Define your own playstyle and assemble the deadliest arsenal with plenty of weapons to choose from, each with even more powerful variations designed to cause absolute mayhem and bring utter destruction upon your foes. Take your pick from devastating shotguns, lethally accurate rifles, explosive launchers, and unleash their full potential. Gain mad skills Overwhelming madness is your best friend and worst enemy at the same time. Let it flow through you, unleash absolute mayhem on your foes and gain extraordinary powers as a reward. Embrace the insanity, use it to fuel your bizarre new abilities, and teach the horrors assaulting your senses to fear YOU! Otherworldly soundtrack Experience the surprisingly fitting combination of strong electric guitar riffs and energetic drums underscoring the dark Lovecraftian atmosphere. Slay hordes of deranged cultists and confront unimaginable ancient evil while listening to the original soundtrack that will make you headbang for hours on end.
