name: Station to Station
detailed_description: Join our Discord! Roadmap About the Game Attention all passengers! We are thrilled to announce the highly anticipated arrival of 'Station to Station' on your PCs! FEATURES A relaxing and peaceful experience Beautiful, colorful voxel art Optional strategic gameplay to earn high scores CONNECT THE WORLD In Station to Station, your world starts small with a handful of rural structures. Place stations and create connections to foster growth and expansion. As you build more connections, your area will grow, transforming into a vibrant, lush environment full of life and color! To keep you on your toes, the game also features engaging puzzle elements, challenging you to optimize routes and solve logistical conundrums. ADMIRE VOXEL-ART VIEWS Hop on board and steam through colorful biomes. Breathe life into the dry desert sands, and transform the untamed mountain terrain. Build and watch your tranquil world come to life with an ever-widening tapestry of flora and fauna! THRIVE For those eager to put their management and planning skills to the test, each level offers optional challenges, stack bonuses, and unique mechanics tied to every biome! Whether you seek relaxation or mental stimulation, 'Station to Station' has something for everyone! GET ON BOARD AND RELAX Follow us, join the community, and choo-choo with the devs. Check the external links to join our Twitter and Discord! Station to Station is inspired by titles, such as Mini Metro, Train Valley, Dorfromantik, Terra Nil and Islanders.

short_description: ‘Station to Station’ is a minimalist & relaxing game about building railway connections. Grab your conductor’s hat and bring the voxel-art world to life through the magic of trains!

_childDocuments_.review: While I've enjoyed the game, it isn't what I thought it was. Everything I'd seen online (short form content) had shown the game to be a city builder where you have to create a train station between towns to generate profit in order to move on to the next area. When in fact it's a level by level / complete XYZ challenge before moving on without really giving you the chance to sink your teeth into any management of any sort.  Fun but not what I thought it was and if I'd have realised, I don't think I'd have gotten it.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful & the puzzle mechanics are engaging.It amazes me that reviews with under 2 hours can be taken with any credibility. Someone tells you that the game doesn't offer X, Y, and Z without even having played the game. It's frustrating how wrong they are. There is difference of opinion and then there is simply lying because you didn't get enough of a dopamine rush within your refund period. It was advertised as a puzzle game that uses a gorgeous voxel graphic, and it delivers on that. To call it a mobile game is disingenuous. What you want in a game like this is for it to be it's own thing. There are train-sims already. There are more train-sims coming out where you can happily turn your map into a dystopian nightmare of efficiency. This is a game that rides the edge between cozy/comfortable & a challenging puzzle game exceptionally well. You'll see me finished the game with 15+ hours played by the end of the week. Putting Baldur's Gate 3 on hold for a bit. Unlike the 1.8hr negative reviews, you can go ahead and comment on mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I am one of the artists for this game and this is my own review for my own game?When I first saw the concept game play I was really sceptical. Was not even sure if this is my kind of game. For the first half a year I wasn't really positive that is will be fun. Though the game evolved over time and became quite a well polished product.What do I think of it now? I think it looks much better than I expected. It's very pretty actually. Gameplay is quite challenging and itches my completionist part of the brain. When the game gets boring there is usually a new mechanic that gets introduced which gives the game a new spin. On a scale from 1/10 I give it a 7.7This is not a managament game, it is a puzzle game. If you expect something else you will be dissapointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: It really is a lovely little game in many ways, but doesn't click as a puzzle experience (yet) for me, From my POV, the puzzle solutions seem very linear and prescriptive. It looks more freeform and creative in approaching solutions than it actually is, at least so far. It's not especially satisfying to finish a puzzle because there was not much room to do it any other way. And it's already a little annoying. The side-challenges turn it into an optimisation task that's a bit of a chore and has you hunting for the one pixel that knocks an extra 1 gold off the price of building the track. This takes up much more of your play time than any decisions you have to make, all of which are pretty obvious - if you have the info, that is. Often an earlier step in a puzzle can mean you have to effectively restart later, so you end up puzzling over the connections and solving it all as many steps up-front as you can manage. You kinda solve it on your mental drawing board, deploy your solution, then get thrown a building you weren't expecting and need to re-do. I've yet to have the satisfaction of an 'A-ha!' moment.Also, this means lots of time staring at an empty, dead, desaturated landscape for a majority of your play time. The bits you connect get coloured in, but then you never need to look at those bits again, the next bit of the puzzle is over in grey land again, and so you never really have any reason to spend time looking at the pretty version you're activating.  And the gfx are occasionally truly lovely to behold when you zoom in and pan around, but it all feels kinda static and lifeless in play. The main playscreen looks less charming than you might expect, most of the time it's going to feel like a zoomed-out Minecraft map sitting in grey space. And it's turned out to be less fun than I had hoped. Levels take a while to play and the trial-and-error puzzles mean harsh reworking is likely. It's made me not want to play it again, because I can see as the levels are getting bigger this is becoming more of an issue, and life's too short to have to redo whole swathes of stuff, y'know? It's weird, it has loads of great ingredients and the devs deserve a lot of credit, you can see it's been created, cooked and delivered with love and charm, but ultimately the flavours don't really work together for me as an enjoyable dish. Maybe that's just my tastes of course. Maybe the puzzles open up and become less prescriptive, with less clairvoyance needed as the game goes on, but I'm struggling to muster the enthusiasm to find out. I don't dislike it, but .... I've loaded it up the last couple times and just hovered over the start button on the map select screen and decided against it. Hoping future updates might expand the framework and offer modes more to my tastes because it's so appealing from the outside but it's just not a game I feel like digging further into at this point to find out if I can fall for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: THIS IS NOT A TRAIN GAME.Okay, so - it's a puzzle game first and foremost, that happens to have a train theme. But I felt compelled to warn that upfront because trains are my father's brand of autism and I know how particular y'all train people can be.This kind of caught me off-guard, since I had seen a teaser for the game in some Not-E3-Anymore showcase in recent years and just thought it looked like a cozy train game with a nice voxel artstyle. What I didn't expect was how addicting the relatively simple mechanic of hooking up stations in a particular order to maximize bonuses would be. The game never exactly feels hard unless you're trying to go for 100% completion, and the main puzzle mechanic doesn't change much throughout the game's duration. What keeps it fresh is the steady introduction of new biomes, each with their own little quirks and special ability cards to play to make you think even more about where to place your stations and railways. Props to the composers for using a progressive soundtrack arrangement that becomes more complex as you progress through a level - gotta be one of my favorite genres.Cute, relaxing, quality. I definitely recommend to puzzle game fans, and tentatively recommend to train fans if they happen to like puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Well.. naahh..This game looked so promising, classic concept, beautiful design, but (for me) completely ruined by some of the gameplay design choices:-you don't see all the buildings from the level start, so you never know, where the future train lines will go.-you can't deconstruct, move, or undo anything after it's connected. You can only save and hope to find the right savegame between all the automatically named files.-there are five autosaves, overwritten every time you place something. Way too few, as you override basically all of them while connecting just three buildings.-no undo button, and no quicksave, which would be incredibly useful in a save/load heavy game like this-this forced you to play the level once just to find out what goes where, memorize all connections and restart to build it properly.If you don't care about aesthetic building and the challenges you'll find a great game. If you want to complete the challenges and achievements it means starting every level just to memorize the layout and then restarting / reloading as often as it takes to micro adjust the tracks and bridges close to pixel perfection to build as cheap as possible.Things that would have to change (for me):-Show the whole level with all buildings right away, so you can plan your tracks-not so linear progression which would allow an undo button. Or any other way to adjust your construction, so you're not forced to restart after every mistake-or unlimited autosaves per level, saved every time when placing anything which can't be changed. And something as simple as a damn screenshot shown when browsing the saves, so you can find the right one right away
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the prettiest and cutest games I’ve ever played. This game is perfect for unwinding to and enjoying the scenery after a long day. The levels are really well designed and the game stays fresh with brand new mechanics and game cards (which provide various bonuses).I love how the extra challenges (in the form of a money challenge for each level, and a unique challenge for each level) are completely optional, so I can just spend my time watching the trains go around the map transporting milk and wheat to the cities instead of worrying about making the most efficient route, though that’s fun too!Overall, It’s clear that the developers put so much love into this game and it’s a blast to play, whether you’re a casual gamer or a hyper-train engineering nerd.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A good example of a game where a long time has been spent making it look nice, and not long enough making an engaging experience. You may enjoy it as a simple calming game to play, but it misses the mark as a puzzle game.I very much dislike the "Stack bonus" system. It encourages you to build connections in the wrong order, which is very unsatisfying. The game should champion creating good connections that allow you to build further good connections. Instead it asks us to build connections that do nothing. This is not a fun puzzle mechanic it's an annoying piece of micromanaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat: This game is a puzzle game. If you come to this looking for a train management game or something similar, you're probably going to be disappointed. Would it be neat to have a train/transport management sim in this kind of style? Absolutely. But Station to Station is not that experience. With that out of the way, let's get to the meat of it. This game is a relaxing, cozy, overall-chill experience with a touch of brain-twisting when it comes to getting the bonus objectives on some levels. Most of the time, the objectives are satisfying to hit and aren't too obnoxious. There are a couple so far that have been a bit frustrating but in my case, it's been a sleep deprivation issue making me less than optimal at solving the puzzle aspects, rather than the structure of the puzzles themselves being bad. I'm trying to pace myself so I don't tear through the entire game in one day. There are generated maps, which I've only kind of explored so far, but there's definitely love present in the handcrafted levels that's enjoyable to experience and I'm already more than a third of the way through them. I have a feeling that I'm going to want more of the handcrafted ones when I reach the end, and I do hope they have an idea for future content at some point. But that's just how I am with all delightful cozy games: I want more. But this game has a lot to offer. Great art and design, great music, and just overall style. There's a delightful reactivity of the world when connections are made and resources are satisfied. It's not just that the landscape gets more lush and filled in with each connection, the music also reacts to your actions. So the game sounds get more depth as well. It's just like, everything in this game is tooled to push that serotonin button in your brain. And I mean, this is a pretty wholesome way to get those kinds of feels. If you like cute art and chill puzzles and TRAINS, then definitely check this game out. I'm excited to see where this studio goes from here (even if it's something other than more of this).Edited to add, after finishing the content that was available at launch, and starting in on the new region added after launch: This game is still real great. I've replayed a lot of previous levels just because I loved them so much. And, though I'm not done yet with the new Gold Rush-inspired biome/levels, I'm really enjoying them, too. The soundtrack and music reactivity just really gets me every time. It's just a great touch to the game and so fun to experience every time. I can't wait to see where this game goes in the future, as well as where this studio goes, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: The main appeal of this game is to recreate the feeling of building an elaborate train set, where you can design the track layout and zoom in to watch the trains rolling around in more detail.But then the game introduces cards and additional objectives, and you realise that this is actually a puzzle game that can get quite challenging at times.You can switch off the puzzle elements and just freeplay the game if you want, but the point is that this game caters for people who want a chill time AND the ones who want something with more depth and/or goals to aim for.One of the best surprises of 2023 so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played in years.It's beautiful, *really* beautiful, voxels don't work everywhere but here they absolutely do and work perfectly.Visuals aside, the game is a joy to play; simple to play but an enjoyable job to master.  Placements of stations, tracks and routes all begin to make sense in the most delightful way, slowly and surely with the perfect amount of level design and tutorial to guide, no, help you to find the best solution.Perhaps that is the defining character of Station to Station, it's gentility.  So often in these games you get through the tutorial, have a few softball levels and then the dragon roars and you're stuck.. I was never stuck and, as a player who's not very good at these things, I appreciated that massively.I had to start over a few times on a few levels but it was never a problem, the gameplay is simple enough that you can lay your groundwork quickly and very soon you're back on track (pun intended) and better than you were.  If all else fails there is a tickbox to continue without monetary concerns, this is gaming gold - use it if you need to and eliminate potential frustration.Special mention goes to the custom levels also.  They're incredibly well tuned and can give as much or as little challenge as you want.  Once I had been through the main levels I spun up a good few custom levels and enjoyed them every bit as much as the designed levels, the engine is *that* good here.Incidentally, probably one of the games I've taken the most screenshots of, it really is that beautiful.  One of my favourite things to do was, at the end of the level, but on photo mode and just zoom around, watching the world I helped create just tick along.An absolute low octane joy, pretty much perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is more in the vein of "Islanders" or perhaps "Dorfromantik", than any kind of model railway building simulator, and that's perfectly fine. Mechanics are very simple but the optional challenges (present in every stage) become more and more difficult to complete. That, coupled with the fact that there is no single way of solving (by connecting all possible profitable routes) any of the levels, makes the game fun to return to time and time again, in short bursts. Visuals make the game look like some kind of coffee table model train diorama, though they are surprisingly heavy on the GPU.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of games like Mini Motorways/Metro and puzzle/cozy games in general, this game was excellent. In addition to the maps visually evolving as you play (one of my favourite aspects of this game), various small details/super fun easter eggs, the gorgeous voxel artwork, and lovely soundtrack, the game play itself has a great balance of relaxing game play and puzzle challenges and presents great replayability due to the Star and Fund challenges within the levels, which you can also choose to simultaneously complete for more of a challenge. The game does a great job of introducing you to the various mechanics, train types, and cards. As well, the different levels have different combinations of these mechanics, train types, and cards, further onto the puzzle aspect of the game.The artbook was breathtaking; it was really magical to learn more about what inspired the team throughout the creative process and the personal touches that went into the game. From learning about all the various elements, such as how big a voxel should be, to the history behind some well-known trains, to architectural considerations, the artbook was wonderful. Overall, it was a fantastic read! If there was a hard copy of this artbook, I'd buy it without hesitation.Game aside, to say the team is highly engaged with the community and works hard to listen to an implement feedback is an understatement. It has been an absolute delight seeing the community's suggestions come to life in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't quite hit right.Has some beautiful voxel design, that you never see because you're fully zoomed out. Seems they designed for some great closeups, but forgot to make it look good from a distance.Game play is a little more frustrating than relaxing. It's hard to plan ahead, or more so, not so fun to have to zoom around and look at what will need to be done in the level and plan how the tracks should be placed in advance. It would be a lot more fun to just place the tracks, but they dangle the star and piggybank challenges in front of you, to feel the pressure to do it perfectly. I suppose i'm just looking for a game more like dorfromantik where you just adapt to your buildings and keep working with what you made. Or unrailed where making a mistake is quite funny and you feel it immediately.Making a mistake, then feeling it 5 minutes later and not being able to change it without totally restarting the level just feels de-motivating.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Train-themed games in any form are probably one of my favorites, but after trying, let's call it, "unofficial demo" for a little bit, I wasn't so sure about this one. The gameplay seemed extremely simple: you just put stations and connect them without much thought, that's it.Eventually I did purchase the game anyway and now, after completing the 100% achievements, I'd say that my first impression didn't change much: you actually do need a little thought, but only to understand how the stacking works. Then you just create two big chains of buildings; one chain gives resources, another chain needs resources. When done with the chains or are close to going bankrupt, connect those chains and boom, the stack is so ridiculously big, that it overlaps the stack interface, gets you a couple of thousand bucks and opens all buildings and cards. This method can be applied for every single map in the game.Therefore, in a nutshell, this is a very low challenge puzzle game that can warm you during cold days. And I mean that literally - for some reason the "state of art" voxel technology used to create this game is melting a 4070Ti, if played on higher than Medium graphic settings.Did I enjoy it? I think yes, to a certain degree. In a way like starting the game every now and then, and completing a level or two. Can I recommend it? If you are looking for a very minimalistic and simple train-themed puzzle game - yes, you'll most likely enjoy this one. If you are looking for some management, there is not much here in this regard.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute and relaxing puzzle game. No time limits or anything like that.Since some people misunderstood the description: It is NOT a settlement builder or anything like that. Its just a puzzle game about connecting different locations with railroads while using as little money as possible to achieve that; with some side-challenges on every map.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: It's very pretty, but there just isn't that much to it, at least not enough for me to keep playing after the first hour. You place stations in front of buildings and connect them. As the game goes on, it introduces more of a puzzle aspect where you need to make sure to connect buildings in the correct order as to not run out of resources. It also adds additional, but simple, mechanics. The trains themselves are for aesthetic purposed only; they might as well be roads or paths. The tracks are just a means for connecting buildings together.I can see it being a fun simple mobile game, but it just wasn't what I expected or was looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for October 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before November 5th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A mix of a Euro-board game with resource management and placement.Station to Station looks like a Railroad manager game, it’s not. The game revolves around building and needs logistic support. Each level starts with a couple of buildings that need to be connected to produce goods. Once that’s done, the game drops more and more of the required buildings that require all their needs to be taken care of. There are a few wonderful systems here, including a stacking bonus. And since the map fills out progressively, you need to consider what additional rail lines will need to be placed. Then there’s two challenges per level, one is different on each level, and another is about maximizing your cash flow. All of this makes the game into a puzzle game more than a management game, but I think the look of the game will make people think about it as something different. There’s not a lot of difficulty, and even when you run into a roadblock, you usually can just restart the level. If you ever get stuck with analysis paralysis, this will probably also cause you some panic, because there are a lot of micro optimizations you can make, even if you don’t need to. Pick this up if you like puzzle games. There is a decent trial-and-error cycle with this game, but with a few attempts, you’ll be able to beat any level, and even when you make those mistakes, they can be obvious in hindsight. This won’t push the limits of players, but is a nice comfortable game, and I love watching the world’s color return when a building was completed. _childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game. Anything to do with trains I'm all about. The Aesthetics are wonderful. The issue I have with this game is that while its primary focus is clearly an aesthetic creation, the mechanics are remarkably dull, an afterthought. It seems the developer created a beautiful engine and then said "How do I make this a game?" The core "challenge" of each level is to connect everything, the puzzle element being that each station has 4 connection nodes, and you need to plan so that you have a node and a path available for any future buildings. This is simple enough. The challenges however, are incongruous with a player's aesthetic motivations- a typical problem in any sort of city building sim. When playing this game, I want to make my rails wind around and follow terrain, but to meet the fund challenges, you just need to make the lines as straight as possible to minimize cost. There's also the stack bonuses which seem to be an answer to this problem, but if I'm being honest, its just a kind of lame mechanic. Instead of having bonuses for the order in which buildings are connected to the network, it would make more sense if there were bonuses for continuous lines, as opposed to points where the sim-trains need to transfer goods. I also subjectively, absolutely hate the cards system. Back to the subject of aesthetics, its unsatisfying to have every station stocked with 4 connection nodes, and generally only utilize 2 or 3 of them, but this design limitation is the central puzzle aspect of the game. So there's a fundamental disconnect there. When I first loaded the game and saw that the stations were designed this way, I assumed I was supposed build lines with dual rights of way, or loops.Additionally, the maps feel very constrained and small. I'm not sure what could be done. Optimistically, I'd hope that the developer released this game as a sort of "proof of concept" for their voxel-train-game engine, and plans to make an actual game with this tech in the future. I would call this game finished, and hope for a sequel with much much bigger maps and completely re-imagined mechanics. Aesthetics 9/10Gameplay 2/10

_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a relaxing puzzle game dealing with train tracks.The visual style is charming and there is calming music.It can also be very satisfying to pull of combos.In each level you need to connect all the buildings, and on top of that most levels have two additional goals: usually one which means you must have X amount of money left at the end, and one with a more varied goal like "only have four bridges" or "get three 4x combos".Overall I like this game, but there are some annoying things. Once something is placed and connected it is locked, and the only way around this is to go back to a checkpoint or to restart the level.Still, this is something you can get used to. It doesn't detract from the overall charm.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, the controls for this game are downright . Every other train sim game needs to take a look at this game to see how track building should be done. Station to Station is very sim-lite but I would love to play a full-blown rail simulator with these controls.I love the art in this game. The puzzle aspect is fun, and it's very intuitive to play. No time limits so you can admire the art.My one complaint is that it could really use a better "undo" feature. Sometimes you place a building and realize later that you blocked yourself and have to revert to a previous checkpoint (sometimes multiple times). Rolling back to previous checkpoints is a bit slow, and sometimes I've had to restart the level completely to fix something.P.S. Once you've solved some of the puzzles, check that box that gives you unlimited money and try building some ridiculous stuff, like corkscrew tracks and unnecessary bridges and routes over mountains. It's a lot of fun for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent puzzle game where you face a series of small premade maps and consider mostly the order of operations to connect hubs so the most possible supply lines connect at the same time for a big "stack bonus". Its railroad themed with cute animals and little cubiod machines/trees in the background, but gameplay mechanics don't try to act like trains, it competes with board games rather than simulators.The game basically offers two difficulties, just finishing the levels which is super accessable and all age friendly, and completing both map specific optional challenges (one is always finish with more than some amount of money, the other could be for example build no bridges, clear no trees, or build less than 2km of rail total), which requires a lot more thinking/planning during play. Ignore the early access, at its current price its worth it for whats already in game, and I have yet to see anything remotely unfinished or to be developed looking/feeling, and it runs well even without high end PC hardware.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous and fun train puzzle game. I'm a sucker for train games and this one was a peach to play. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay challenge is more akin to "connect the dots" than to a puzzle or a management type of game.What bothers me a little is that sometimes you have to replay the level again or revert to a quicksave because you cant move, replace or reconnect the tracks and stations once laid down - for a game that says "relaxing" on the front page, this can be a minor inconvenience that does not make much sense to me..For example:  If you want to complete all the challenges on a difficult level, you have to basically discover and memorise the optimal layout on your first try and replay the level building your stations and tracks in the intended order.For a person that likes trains, the lack of a turntable forces the wagons to disappear and reappear facing the opposite direction - for a game so beautiful and breathtaking this is an ugly solution.If you make every station a turntable, maybe you wouldnt need to rework the whole game just to add them  .

_childDocuments_.review: I seldom write Steam reviews, but I thought I would make an exception for Station to Station.Station to Station is not meant to be facile and simplistic, nor is it meant to be a complicated tycoon simulation or strategy game -- it captures the enchantment of dioramas, the nostalgia of toy trains, the thrill of card stacking, and the satisfaction of strategic connectivity.While the gameplay is relatively straightforward, Station to Station understands the fundamental principles of clean and structured game design -- things that impatient and self-entitled players often fail to appreciate in games today, complaining about anything that requires thought or causes the smallest degree of frustration.There is a kind of touching 'purity' and 'elegance' in Station to Station's design that you rarely find in games anymore, and having nearly completed all the levels and optional challenges, I think it is now one of my all-time favourites.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is a path finding optimisation puzzle game that feels very much like a mobile game. The train theme is basically irrelevant in regards to actual game play. The beautiful graphical presentation is also irrelevant as you will spend almost all the time zoomed out trying to find the best path. There is no real fun in placing a building (station) in a predetermined spot, placing another building in a predetermined spot (station) and drawing a line between the two, in a (pretty much) predetermined spot. I don't even know why they even made the stations a part of the game as you have to place them exactly beside whichever building you need the train to go to. I guess the developers were really trying to push the train theme...By the time I played the 4th scenario, I was already bored and the simplistic game design becomes very apparent...Extremely disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Might be for you if you want a very easy puzzle game, but don't buy this looking for a challenge unless it's discounted. I wish there was a "maybe" option. If you like combo-happy board games, especially pickup and deliver style games, you're going to enjoy the puzzles on offer. But.... once you understand how to optimize your rails for the biggest combo stacks... there is little to no challenge here. I was hoping that the demo (that has been removed since release.... that's a red flag imo) was just a taste of greater challenges to come. What I've found instead is just an endless loop of the same level of challenge that was present in the demo. The developer said that "playtesters claimed a total completion time of 25-30 hours to get all challenges, and 8-10 hours to complete the game normally"....I have a hard time with the former. I've played for 70 minutes, following the basic principles of rails optimized for combo stacks, and grabbed every challenge in the 1st World, along with 2 levels in the 2nd. There are 32 levels total... I've completed over 1/5th of the total content, with challenges... Meaning that unless I were to hit a wall at some point I'm going to finish at about 6 hours *with* challenges. I feel that whether the asking price is going to feel worth your "8-10" hours, will depend entirely on whether you are a *very* specific kind of gamer. I regrettably, am not, despite *wanting to be*. If you asked my gut reaction, it would be to wait for a sale, or until they (hopefully) put the demo back up at some point. I can't recommend it at full price or until you can get a taste of what is on offer... and I can't recommend that you watch videos because there is so little content available that you risk ruining what little challenge exists for yourself entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: To be clear, this is a "no" in consideration of price versus content.The game itself is neat but not special. The only thing that has it going forward, is the visual appeal.Beyond that, its a blant puzzle game where you connect stations with rails and try to do that with the least money spent.Too simplistic for my taste.I didnt expect a Tycoon game and i understand its catering towards puzzle players that want to min max their connections and use of one time abilities, to gain the highest score.To me, that was becoming boring really fast.I wished the game would have gone deeper into complexity, allowing me to do something with the money i saved after a mission (meta upgrades?) or unlock abilities using the stars and thus defining my playthrough, with the possibility to choose different upgrades on my next attempt.The game tries to provide more complexity after you progress. More stuff to connect, complex terrain and such stuff.But it ends up being samey (i played till mid Region 2 as of now).I know where it is heading in terms of gameplay and to me its not holding up my interest a lot.Its a neat game for puzzle fans that want cozey visuals. For 8€ or something in that area, its an ok pick. Still not special or great, but solid at what it does.I personally would rather recommend getting Train Valley. More content, more complexity, still the puzzle experience.However, i understand if thats not for everyone, so Station to Station has its niche.At 18€ however, that niche isnt properly served by it.For 18€ it doesnt go far enough, doesnt provide enough, doesnt give enough incentive to keep playing.Its a blant but solid Arcade game hiding behind good visuals that try to cover up its simplicity, or maybe embrace it, as apparently in todays gamedesign 101 simplicity (aka a lack of choice and decision making) seems a pro rather than a con for some people.Not to me. A game can be simplistic but still complex, this however is just simple.Its also repeating stuff other games have done far better and worthwhile.I guess theres a rush for the Dorfromantik hype, but while Dorfromantik and other games manage to provide a good mixture between simplistic concept and complex decisions, this one only manages to emulate the visual feeling of building (colouring in this case) the world.I wished they worked on this game for a lot more. Early Access would have been a better choice here, as it feels polished but not fleshed out because of above reasons.Personally i would prefer to see modes being added.I could imagine some sort of "endless" mode, where you start a map and connect industries, cities and whatnot and once you are done, you take you money (score) and abilities to the next map thats more difficulty.Then difficulty continuedly grows, maps become larger and so on, until you run out of money.Each successful map would give you a choice to pick a perk that you keep while continueing.That could be fun, as it would increase decision making, complexity and a challenge at the same time.But its unlikely a game like this will ever see something even remotely similar.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, charming, and engaging puzzle-lite game with a beautifully polished voxel atmosphere. At a fundamental level, you want to chain together as many resources through a pipeline (eg: wheat -> flour mill -> bread bakery -> city) to deliver what is needed in one big hit by placing stations at buildings and joining them via rails. Though the order you ideally would want to chain resources together is fundamentally quite simple, every level mixes it up in multiple ways, some of which I'll explain.You manage rail and station cost via an economy. Buildings may be too far or the terrain too unsuitable to join things the same way each time due to cost. Buildings also appear through a level as you earn income - do you chain all the resources you currently can to maximise profit now, or save some for a bigger subsequent chain? Cards granting extra one-off bonuses are also unlocked similarly to buildings, and can be planned for and juggled to maximise profit and minimise costs in different ways.At a base level completing the majority of levels isn't overly difficult. Every level, however, has two challenge conditions on top of the base win condition which incentivise planning and different approaches. One always revolves around minimum amount of leftover profit while the other can be anything from petting ambient animals, not building any bridges, or using up all your cards in a round.On top of all this, there is so much polish and attention to detail. You can slow down your gameplay, zoom in and enjoy the atmosphere. As production ramps up buildings churn to life, farms grow, cities sprawl. Trains toot and chug along, they come to a stop with a hiss at crossings to let other trains pass before starting up again. The environment as a whole is just adorable.As of this review there are 32 official levels, and it took me 14 hours to complete all of them + challenges. I can see it being completed fully in 10 but for less experienced people or those who want slow down over 20 hours is definitely reasonable. I recall the devs said playtests had many people taking around 30 hours. YMMV.For a polished, pretty game with puzzles that are engaging without being taxingly difficult this game is absolutely worth looking at. Take it slow (or don't!), enjoy the aesthetic and ambience, and become the voxel train coordinator you were destined to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this as a more relaxing puzzle-by-train-track game that I'll play while listening to a podcast or in between more intense games.The primary goal in order to complete levels is to transport things or people between stations that allow for things to be built, and those built things are often needed elsewhere. Different buildings get built over time, though you can see the locations of where future buildings will be created once a certain number of needed things get to where they need to go.Voxel visuals & sounds are good, progressive gameplay mechanics while going through levels are well done, and the optional bonus goals can add extra challenge for people who want it.  Just because it is a more relaxing game, that doesn't mean the base gameplay is really easy. Part of the challenge is that once a track is connected, that track and its stations cannot be moved or destroyed. Unless you reload a checkpoint/auto save or a manual save, you have to adapt to your track & station choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A little over an hour in and this scratches the exact itch I hoped it would. It's cute, it's easy (so far), it's trains. I can tell that there's a high skill ceiling to this, where you could get everything lined up perfectly, build continuous loops, etc. but so far you don't *have* to do that, you can just make neat trains.My only note would be that I wish you could remove track once it's been laid. If you misclick, that's it, you have to load from a save.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a "train sim game".. this is more of a "connect the dots game".It is not a bad game. I like the concept, the art style and the vibes. However, why market it as a train sim when it is absolutely not? The train/s are very irrelevant even.The moment I linked a railway to form a loop and the trains did not loop was the moment I knew something was up - this was stage 1. Then stage 3 happened. The game's main mechanic was introduced and it is to connect all stations into a singular railway. No loops allowed. It really ruined my immersion and I just stopped.It's a good looking puzzle game, but they need to change their marketing team.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is an excellently made game. I've played roughly 10 hours in the full version, but I also had the opportunity to playtest beta versions when the game was in development. The team did a wonderful job making a game that is fun and relaxing, while adding enough challenge that the game remained engaging. I encountered no bugs or issues of any sort. The soundtrack adds to the atmosphere and it all comes together to form a truly enjoyable experience. I look forward to any expansions that may be planned (hopefully with Autumn colors).
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This game went from fun to infuriating real quick.There is no undo feature or ability to delete track after it's connected. The only thing you can do is "reload checkpoint" which takes you back to your previous station connection. This will also delete any unconnected stations you preemptively placed, revert the buildings so you have to go through the same animation of them being re-added, oh and it reverts your upgrade cards so they're effectively randomized. Except they're not randomized, some will just outright be removed from the pool.I have a card that lets a rail transport both freight and passengers. It's the last connection I need and everything falls into place. Only my previous connection obstructed the last station connector. No big deal, I'll just use the rather cumbersome reload checkpoint feature. Replace the rail making sure I don't obstruct the station... Oh, have to get my cards. No train; can't make this work without it, reload checkpoint. No train. Repeat this maybe thirty times trying different orders and checkpoints, no dice.This genuinely made me mad. I can't even remember the last time a game actually made me mad. It almost feels malicious by design but I think it's more likely due to incompetence.And sure, I could've just restarted the level and beaten it in the time it took to write this review. You know what I did instead? Uninstall.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station's voxel-art is gorgeous and charming, but unfortunately that's where my enjoyment ended. The puzzles have been repetitive and not terribly interesting - too structured to be relaxing and cozy like Dorfromantik, not complex enough to be puzzling like Minimetro. It's a shame, but the game isn't carried by vibes alone . Feels like this was a beautiful art project in search of a game mechanic, and the latter just didn't live up.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really pretty, but unfortunately that's as far as it goes.The ‘puzzles’ are limited to the fact that you have to - build the cheapest routes and use discounts effectively- delaying rewards for as long as possible to maximise them.Unfortunately, this doesn't fulfil what players of economic simulations would like. Namely that efficient production chains are created. In this game, it is just as good for a good to travel through 4 stations as it is to build a direct connection. One track is as good as the next, as long as it creates a network connection. Literally, in the first level of the second region you're asked to create an "illogical" first connection to maximize your gains (staple bonus). This make sense in the context of this game, but it immediately demotivated me.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A begrudgingly chosen no here. Basically I've played it once, I don't think I will play it again. As other reviews have mentioned the art style is nice and you can zoom right in but there's no real incentive to, and whilst (as the dev points out in other responses) the point isn't to make a nice network it still feels wrong to me to be encouraged to make a bad one. I think this is my train geek speaking, so it's a me problem not a game problem. It was nice to look at and lovely to play whilst I played it (the soundtrack was great). But as I said at the start I probably won't load it up again. Compared to others which I do keep going back to this felt a bit of a let down.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun and relaxing train puzzle game, and it fills that role well. The voxel graphics look lovely and the puzzles are solid. I love the serotonins when I get a big stack bonus.I have a couple of gripes however- The game is not built to help you out with mistakes, there is no undo button. - Though there is a reload from checkpoint button, this is slow and it isn't always clear to when it will take you back. Granular control would help- There is a workaround, namely saving every time you do something, though this is slow and always puts you through a loading screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a relaxing puzzle-lite game about connecting different buildings with tracks and stations. Personally, I felt the puzzle side of the game was rather lacking. While each 'biome' has a slightly different addition to the core mechanics, the game felt relatively the same throughout. I was hoping for an increasing difficulty as the game went on, but it remained a flat experience overall. Some people may enjoy that, but that was not what I was personally looking for.I do not recommend this game if you are looking for an actual puzzle solving experience. However, if you just want a relaxing game with 'puzzle-lite' elements and beautiful voxel art, I'd definitely still recommend picking it up on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a chill building game without having to dig into a complex city builder, and Station to Station has been a complete addiction for a few days. It's gorgeous, the sound design is top-notch, and completing levels is a great mix of building and puzzle. Completing levels is usually fairly easy if you don't totally blow your budget on too many bridges or something, but some of the optional challenges take quite a bit of effort to complete.The card system is a really fun, kind of unexpected addition, and thoughtfully playing your cards to get a discount on bridges or place a luxury passenger train adds some good depth to the puzzle of connecting stations together.Absolute recommend if you want a cozy, train-based puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr buy it, it's greatStation to Station is an amazing game. For me it was (and is) a relaxing experience, you can easily play it with your kids/nieces/nephews. Even if things don't work out, the game looks great, the sound is nice and is overall fun.If you enjoy a good challenge, then that's exactly what the financial and extra challenge are for. And with higher levels the game gets more difficult and takes more brain power. E.g. my brain can't handle the dream levels, but I love all the levels.Buy it, 10/10. Even on full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a brilliant little thing, really. It's like if Thomas the Tank Engine had a baby with SimCity, but without all the disasters and angry residents complaining about property taxes.You're basically playing Railway God, right? Connecting buildings together like some sort of transport matchmaker. "Oh, you're a lonely wheat farm? Let me set you up with this nice mill I know. They're very grain-friendly."Now, here's the clever bit - you want to be a bit sneaky with your connections. Don't just go connecting everything willy-nilly like a desperate speed-dating host. No, no, no. You want to be strategic about it. Connect the unrelated bits first, then BAM! Link it all together at the end for that sweet 20% bonus. It's like getting a discount at the shops, except you're the one who owns all the shops.They've thrown in these little challenges too, but honestly, they're about as challenging as making a cup of tea. Most of the time you'll complete them by accident while just playing normally. And if you don't? Second time's the charm. So there you have it. Station to Station: It's relaxing, it's clever, and it won't make you want to throw your computer out the window. And if that's not a ringing endorsement, I don't know what is.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun little relaxing game. If you like model railroading, then you will also appreciate this title. Although, the main focus is not so much creativity as it is the puzzle solving aspect. The music is top notch and peaceful. I recommend playing this game on a rainy fall day with a cup of hot coco for the full effect.I am hoping that tunnels get added as a mechanic in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: At it's core, this is simply a puzzle game with slow moving trains added for visual appeal.  For something billed as a relaxing experience, it sure has a lot of frustration built in.  You'll find the need to reload or restart fairly often, as the devs decided that once something is built, it's immutable.  Since stations have two platforms, choosing the wrong one early on can be disastrous later.  This is because, the game only shows you your next objective after having completed the current one.  Thus, that next station may need to be connected the platform you've already chosen.  Not sure why the devs thought this would be a "fun" way to play the game.  Humble Bundle is 0/4 so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fairly fun relaxing little game. Very minimalist as the description says. For some reason I thought it was going to be more like a model train simulator where you get to build and set things up so they function together and get to watch some trains go around all the tracks rather than disappearing and reappearing  going the other direction, so its more like a puzzle game than a model train set. Still enjoyable.Edit: Thank you for continuing to update this game! The creative mode is fantastic. My two year old will point at my computer and say choo choo any time he wants to play. He loves watching the trains and its great to ask him where he wants to build the tracks and have him practice some decision making. Also the standard mode has some really fun and challenging twists later on that I am really enjoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice casual game in beautiful voxel art: build railways and connect production sites and cities and fulfill their respective needs. The economy system is pretty simple: it depends on the resource itself at each site and not on how many resources a train can transport – it only depends on existing connections. In the tutorial you quickly learn how this works. Speed does not matter as well: as soon as you connect two sites, the demand is covered immediately. So this game is more about railway organzisation than resource management – the latter is only there for smart planning of your railways.Later on, the maps become more complex and additional (optional) map goals make them more challenging. You get bonus cards for special effects, like cheaper bridges or additional income, that make it easier to hit the additional goals, too. All in all I would say each map takes up to 15 till 30 minutes. You can finish a map without achieving the additional goals, but you can come back later and play the maps again.If this game gets an update, I wish it would be more rewarding to explore the map and click on things. You can zoom in close for some beautiful screenshots, but you can hardly click on the environment to make somehing happen (some things react on mouse click, try it on your own), If you like trains, puzzles and voxel art, this is your game. Recommendation? Yes!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, its very cute and calming at the same time though the puzzles are challenging to get all challenges done in a level. I will sometimes be playing with station placement and accidental place it and my only option is to return to last checkpoint which may delete multiple stations I've put down instead of the one accidental. Love the game and I'm planning on 100% the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Train Valley 1 and 2 I very much enjoyed this game - it's not the same but both are train puzzle games and for some reason I love those! :D Relaxing and just the right amount of challenging without being too difficult or stressful. _childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Too easy, little challenge, even on hard price difficulty level.Not a logistics game...sending goods along a snaking path though every station yields the same amount of money as a short direct connection, so the game ends up mainly being a matter of identifying and making the cheapest connections. And trying to achieve combo chains which essentially priorities you in delaying actually satisfying good demands until you can make one final connection that satisfies all those demands (which seems like a counter-intuitive way to connect stations, but is a consequence of the combo mechanism)The graphics and track layout engine are fantastic, however. (Though one small gripe is I should be able to put a station on an already existing track.)
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Such a relaxing and fun game to play.  Beautiful aesthetic and gorgeous soundtrack. The voxel graphics are really charming. I do wish there was an undo function so I could go back a few steps every now and then or edit my tracks or stations - limited of course, don't want to make it too easy.  Now that there's a creative mode this game is just... *chef's kiss*

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).Station to Station is a casual puzzle game where you need to connect different types of building to each other using stations and train lines. The types of building vary from raw material extraction or agriculture, industry and processing and cities (consumers). An example of a chain is: Wheat Farm > Mill > Bakery > City. In each chapter new buildings and new mechanics are added. The game also has cards that you can spend to get bonuses and discounts on rails and trains.The graphics are voxel based, but since you’re looking at the map from far away most of the time the cubes aren’t very noticeable and the game, despite its simplicity, looks great, and together with the relaxing music the game’s ambience is calm and relaxing.Regarding gameplay, besides connecting the buildings I mentioned before it’s important to make as many connections at the same time to get the biggest reward possible. To do this, you need to connect the buildings that aren’t related first and in the end make a final connection that will connect everything together, like this: Connect the raw material to each other and to the city, then connect the industries to each other and lastly connect them all to the city, this way you’ll get an extra 20% on each item delivered. The more money you get, the faster you’ll unlock new buildings and cards, and with more buildings you can build even bigger chains.The levels also have two special challenges that you need to complete. Personally, I found them easy to complete as the goals set are easy to reach and even surpass by a lot. Most of the time I got at least one of them by playing normally, but even when I failed a second try was enough.  81 Achievements. Around 18 hours, without help but I had to repeat some levels. Easy, the levels are easy to complete.  Easy, to 100% the game you only need to complete the two extra challenges on each level, by the end of the game, the only achievement I missed was petting the dog, you can find it in the . The two custom games that you also need to win are easy to set up and complete.  Station to Station is a casual puzzle game with voxel graphics, a relaxing ambience and puzzles that are fun to solve but not too challenging. In each chapter new mechanics and building are added to prevent the game from becoming monotonous and repetitive and, overall, a good experince for fans of puzzle games..
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy train game, logistics puzzler. Super cute art style. This isn't an operational or corporate sim type train game, it is purely connect the things for points, get enough points to win the level. Each level has three tasks. Connect all the things, Do it with an amount of money left, and complete a special task such as connect everything an industry needs with a single track segment. The constant addition of new mechanics and new industry chains  and new biomes all keep it challenging and engaging throughout. I 100%ed it in about 26 hours. I definitely think it was worth my time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is easily one of the best looking games I've ever played it's absolutely gorgeous, I love the Voxel art design. The detail of every building and map/trains is impressive, the more you zoom in and look around the more little surprises you'll find. The lighting and just how colourful the world is made just riding the trains and admiring the beauty of it all one of my favourite things to do. I was however, disappointed the game is mostly a puzzles game and not really about trains or constructing elaborate railways and cities ect. Once I got over it not being what I expected I discovered I enjoyed the mechanics and thought the difficulty was spot on, they do a great job at providing more challenging optional goals for those wanting more demanding tasks, but also allowing the game to be a cozy non stressful game if you just focus on the main objectives which were pretty easy. I wish there were some customization elements tho, maybe if you could use the extra goals as incentive to unlock different locomotives, themes for buildings ect. Would be nice to be able to decorate and makes things nicer, could still be the puzzle game but also providing more of what I feel like people expected from this game. The music is pleasant but quickly becomes repetitive could use a few more tracks or longer loops. It's a more demanding game on your PC than you might expect but it runs well on my 3080ti/12900k at 1440p but there is some issues with lag while placing down long tracks the frames plummet. The campaign is a decent length and took me about 14-15 hours to finish doing a little more than half the optional goals. The custom game mode is awesome with tons of settings which provides huge replayability. Overall especially for the sale price during the spring sale the quality is very high and even for someone that doesn't particularly love strictly puzzle based games I still really had fun with it. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Its a real cozy puzzle game giving me Islander vibes. The challenge of the puzzle is a medium-low - more on the pleasant experience of figuring the solution out rather than hard boiled puzzle and planning. The score and challenges are rather lenient, affording some flexibility in execution. I've seen some complains about RNG, but its mostly a planning and anticipation. Some levels took a few tries as I realized how the map was gonna play out (objectives are gradually spent) so it takes a bit of caution.If you're looking for a hard challenge, this might not be it. But for solving "just hard enough" puzzles while listening to the beautiful audio and zooning out with the choo choo trains, I give my highest recommendations. Fair warning that the custom mode (procedural generated) does not provide as much satisfaction as the main maps with harder requirements, bonus objectives and tailored placements, so expect around 15 hour total for all maps and objectives
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Understanding what this game is... is key to whether you will like it or not. This is not a game like Train Valley, First stop, transport fever, or any train time management game. This game is all about figuring out how to meet the two challenge goals on each level. Each level is a puzzle with a train station resource flow theme. That said... Being that I love games like what I mentioned before, I wasn't sure if I would like the game or not. But I do! I have to take it a level or two at a sitting, but it's perfect when you aren't in a hurry or doing something else at the same time... like drinking a cup of coffee or eating... etc. It gets my brain going in the morning. And it keeps it going when I'm tired and need to stay awake haha. Great game devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Different from the other train puzzlers on the market, it isn't about optimisation but how big of a combo you can make. Essentially how unoptimised of a track can you make to get everything connected. It's challenging to get all the objectives in a few levels and others are quite easy. One frustration is you don't know what the stations are going to be ahead of time before you unlock them. So I find myself restarting levels often because I wont have enough funds to build around my current railsI'm enjoying it and recommend it to those who enjoy train valley or other train puzzlers with the caveat that its not ocd friendly and its different. And you need to be patient and willing to restart often.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent example of one of those cozy and charming voxel art style logistics puzzle games (which also happens to have a great soundtrack).  In particular here, it's a game about trains and railroads as the player is working to supply all the buildings with the needed raw/refined/finished goods to complete the map.The visuals are fantastic and the animations are quite charming when it comes to watching the railroads and new buildings place down in the world.  Photo mode makes it easy to get nice screenshots of your railroad and the corresponding scenery.The game is very easy to get into and start playing and has a fairly non-invasive tutorial/guide, but can get quite challenging very quickly when it comes to fully clearing each level given the spending and placement related criteria you have to meet (hence the puzzle aspect).
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A nice relaxing puzzle game that gets highly strategic as the game goes on. The atmosphere of the game is great, I love how the level tracks progress and the level beautifies as you build your railways. This is a great choice for anyone who loves strategy puzzle games, especially people who like them artistically presented.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I'm blown away. This is simply fantastic. From the absolutely gorgeous voxel graphics, to the perfectly fine tuned gameplay that has just the perfect amount of challenge, with plenty of secondary objectives to keep things interesting. The attention to detail is amazing, and it shines through that the developers have a passion for the game they're making. Simply outstanding and a strong recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A fun train themed puzzle game, the puzzles aren't too difficult so the game is a fun and calm experience.If you want more of a brain twister there are extra objectives to go for that make the puzzles more interesting.Overall it's a great mix of chill train station connecting with some interesting puzzle decision to make if you want. If you just want to enjoy placing train tracks there is a 'no money' mode so you can just build however you want without worrying about optimizing the track layout.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: one of them cozy puzzle games with trains. if that's enough to sell you, you won't be disappointed. it got me hooked in any case. it's really great at creating a certain vibe as well, what with the voxel graphics and chill soundtrack and all that.that said: limited amount of levels with no workshop support (yet). level challenges vary in quality. some are legitimately challenging and fun, others seem tacked on, and some are downright stupid ("click 4 dromedaries"? really?). some minor bugs but nothing gamebreaking.overall recommend, but maybe wait for a 30-50% sale
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute and cozy game and the tilt-shift aesthetic is really well made, also the music is really calming, even the animations on the different production buildings are very adorable, but now comes the big BUT of this game:It is first and foremost a puzzle game where you have to beat the challenges presented to you, so you can’t just build like you want and to make pretty towns and maps.Nevertheless they added a creative mode now, so you can make pretty maps all day long!

There is a ton of content (infinite content, if you keep generating custom worlds to play through!) and a lot of fun achievements and secondary objectives, and some decently complex puzzles! The soundtrack is superb and it's honestly fantastic to sit back and watch the trains after completing a level. Highly recommend for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game with its challanges, but everything is optional so if you don't wish to complete a challange because it is too much you can still proceed with the next level. I like that it is in a way open-ended but also not as in, there is a creative mode but the main levels are in itself finished. I dislike too open-ended games because I like the feeling of having played through a game so this was enjoyable to me. _childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is a track- laying game with block terrain and items. Some puzzles seem almost impossible, but there will be a solution. Don't be afraid to use cards - they save on costs, and you don't gain anything by having cards in your hand at the end of a map. I found the music soothing and the game engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is not Transport Tycoon Deluxe, because there is no economy simulation. This game plays much more like Dorfromantik. Which is really nice, but might be different from your expectation.You're playing levels in which you're trying to connect points of interest with rails to match the products they produce. The main goal is to find the shortest rails that obstruct the least land to conserve money and allow future rails to be placed without the need of bridges (which are costly). Every connected POI match (like wheat + mill) gets you money once (and only once). Also connecting multiple resources on the same rail network to a consumer POI gets you extra combo money. You're not allowed to run out of money (but theres a no money mode for those who think the money challenge is stressful). When all POIs are connected successfully you get a star rating for the level and play the next level on a completely new map.

The cities grow, the industries accept & provide, and you can custom-design the slopes, the size of the map, when you want the train to climb or descend. And you can watch your grandchild have fun, being just like you.Engineer hat not included.

When I watched Many a True Nerd play this game on YouTube, I was immediately relaxed and excited. I decided to give it a go, and absolutely love it. _childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very atmospheric puzzle game to relax and tune out. The music keeps you in a cozy mood while you gaze at the beautiful scenery and solve the management of your train tracks while taking your time. I love this games asthetic, i love the music and i love that there is no rush, no time limit. Exactly what I expected and wanted after playing the demo.The price is more than fair considering that there will be content added to the already big amount of levels and regions and I'm more than happy to see what more comes next. _childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

Its a great mix of beauty, Musical Wonder, Rewarding Challenges, Planning, Stellar Design and most of all relaxing fun With Trains! It has great progression as you travel along the rails in your journey to the next beautiful biome. Choosing what path to take with your rails as There are so many ways to finish each level making the repeatability a joy every time you revisit this gem of a game.
