_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a puzzle game where you optimize placement of rails, while I expected something more like a management/simulation game. The choices you make don't feel that important. It looks nice, but there's just not that much to it in terms of depth.The puzzle aspect consists of- Choosing the order in which you connect buildings- Finding the cheapest route between stations and whether or not to use bridges- Whether to play cards to further optimize costThe game also seems to be poorly optimized, which is not a deal breaker, just a little disappointing.Maybe pick it up on sale if you're looking for a relaxing, simplistic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful voxel-art puzzle game.  With trains!Now, lookie here:  If you're assuming this has anything whatsoever to do with train simulation, forget it.  This game has nothing to do with train simulation.  It is a pure puzzle/connect the lines game, done with a train motif.  And done wonderfully!Did you read what I said?  Nothing to do with trains!  So don't buy this game and then go complaining it wasn't a deep simulation of trains.  Or had anything to do with trains, other than there being a lot of pretty voxel trains in it.Alright, I think we're clear.  Buy the game immediately!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Very simple train track building game to link up various buildings with materials they need. Played a few hours now and so far I've been very impressed by the simple nature of the game and the ease of controls, It teaches you slowly how to go about things and then spices it up by adding challenges and bonus cards you can use to help complete those challenges if you choose to. The 1st 4 levels have taken me a couple of hours and there are a lot of levels to unlock in the game, a fair few hours play I think judging by my game time per level. Overall though if you like train track building games you can't go wrong with this for the budget money it costs.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, relaxing and very beautiful puzzle game.Over time, the puzzles become more complex, but honestly they still remain very linear. So I would say that the game is not exactly about sitting and trying to solve a single puzzle for hours, it just does not challenge you too much. The game rather provides a great meditative experience and relaxes. Great for a chill evening. It is worth mentioning absolutely gorgeous voxel graphics and quite good relaxing music. Would definitely recommend for a chill gaming session.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely perfect in its simplicity. You can either just relax and enjoy the combination of soothing music, beautiful graphics, and slow pace of gameplay or utilize your brainpower and try your best to accomplish occasionally really tough challenges. I think Station to Station is ideal for every overstimulated mind (just like mine) and has the potential to offer relief from anxiety etc.Much appreciate for reloading checkpoints (btw that wasn't in the demo) and custom mode that can provide you with countless hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I like trains, I like puzzles, voxels. I like puzzles involving trains made with voxels. Just got the game, dunno how big the variety of locomotives is, so far I've seen 4 engines (love the double fairlie), but I love the visual style of the game, and the gameplay is solid and fun. (Hope a creative mode shows up so you can just mess around and make layouts)Sadly not related to the David Bowie album.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played this game for a long time yet (only 1 hour at the time of the review), but so far, I absolutely love it. It is relaxing, the art style is beautiful, and the music blends in so well with the gameplay. What a hit! I would recommend this game to every puzzle and simulation fan out there. If you liked Mini Metro, you will love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A little bit annoying how you can't readjust railroads and stations once you put them down, because when you reload a checkpoint to rebuild and readjust, there's this bug where some buildings lose connection with their stations (which you previously successfully connected) and you then have to restart the whole level to fix said bug. Other than that everything's swell, it's a cozy little puzzle game where you have to strategize the building and connection of your railroads and stations.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen quite a few people complain about a lack of certain railway-related features in Station to Station and compare it to real railway simulators. However, I just think it's an unfair comparison to make in the first place. I see this game as, first and foremost, a puzzle game, with beautiful voxel graphics and trains. I've played through the entire game and I found it enjoyable and fun to plan train routes and connect various industries via stations. Though I would welcome some features proposed by other reviewers for more challenging levels and more options, I love the game in its' current state too, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a puzzle experience. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Eh. Not for me. I love the art style and am always excited to play with trains but this ain't it. The permanence of every action combined with the fact the game reveals locations on the map as you go combine to make for a constant annoyance. You can build out a perfect network and then surprise, there's a farm behind everything you built and you just went bankrupt trying to run it ontop of everything. These forced resets for things there's no way I could have predicted get very old, very fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is not exactly what its presenting in its previews. Its just a puzzle game sort of. Ingame youre not attracted to the "voxel experience". Youre just not looking any deeper into it because youre most of the time fixed in overview. Its not about building beautiful tracks on beautiful landscapes and relaxing while looking at your scenery. you just solve a straight forward puzzle and keep on going to the next level, not caring what you built before. For me its not a real voxel game like teardown or cloudpunk, but sadly just a mediocre puzzle game, nice, but not breathtaking, thats why I cannot recommend it, sry.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: "A relaxing and peaceful experience"No, it isn't. No undo buttons ruins this, the checkpoints are not an acceptable solution. Imagine getting near the end of a level and realizing you've screwed yourself just a few rail placements ago. Too bad, gotta restart the whole level. Might as well watch a guide to get it right the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: It might be my fault of not reading too many reviews and content description; or for focusing on the "Simulation" tag, while ignoring the "Puzzle" one. This is not a railway builder, a simple manager where you lay down tracks in the most picturesque ways, manage your wee company, earning small bucks that allow you to build some more tracks, all while enjoying cosy views (which are undoubtedly very cosy). This is a logic placement game, where you can very easily lock yourself out. In fact... I really I don't want to say it, but the addition of these weird cards made me do it - it is a deluxe mobile game. I can perfectly imagine there are people, who will enjoy their time with it. But it is definitely not for me and definitely not a "Simulation".
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this, but if you're into certain genres I could see some people liking it. This game looks great, but in reality it's just a basic, mediocre puzzle game. There are better train based puzzle games out there. The game is level based and basically boils down to placing stations right next to buildings, then connecting the two. You get tiny little maps where more buildings unlock as you make connections. The problem with this is that you have two or three buildings at the start so you have no choice but to make the single connection or two. With stations having to be very near a building, it severely limits any kind of strategy or choice. The station has to go where it has to go. Then more building open up and it's just rinse and repeat. There's a card mechanic that comes along later which helps with the tedium, but it's still just a bland puzzle game. There is a "custom game" feature, but it boils down to the same game play without the level based part.Granted, I am a little over an hour in, but given what I've played so far, I don't know that I'll play much more of it. I bought this immediately after I saw it in my discovery queue. If I'd have bought it on Steam I'd have refunded it, but I got it on humble instead thanks to my humble choice discount and some money in my humble wallet to save a bit of money. I should have known better. Whenever I impulse buy a game it almost never turns out to be good.I wasn't expecting a tycoon game, but I also wasn't expecting... this. The most fun in the game is just zooming in and watching your trains chug along in the voxel world. But a great art style does not equal a great game, and that's certainly the case here. You could substitute the train aesthetic with... I dunno... waterslides, the buildings with pools and the items with  people and it'd be the same game. Meaning, the train motif is just an artistic choice. The fact that they chose trains has no bearing on the gameplay itself.If you go into it knowing it's a kind of connect the dots puzzle game, and you like that sort of genre, maybe get it on a sale. It's not for me though.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly feel bad giving this a downvote because it's a good game, it's just not my kind of game. It's slow, sleepy, and single-path puzzle driven. If you're looking for a hyper relaxing puzzle experience, this is probably perfect for you. I require something far more in depth to itch my strategic bones. I don't really like puzzle games. The feeling that there's generally only one way to succeed just ruins the creativity to me, unless that puzzle makes me do something surprising and fun (like Portal or Poly Bridge's use of physics). This, to me, is more like putting together an actual puzzle. The maps are set up in a way that guide you toward that one optimal way of designing the routes to get the objectives cleared. Then there's putting the stations down and connecting them in just the right, weird order, to maximize stack bonus and money saved from your cards. It's all very much a bottle-necked design experience. Do it this ONE way or you won't get both bonus objectives. I'm sure later levels will be more open ended, but I want a game to grip me from the beginning and this game just made me feel so tired, but also a bit frustrated by the tedium of placing tracks in just the right way to avoid a bridge and optimize cost.Again, I am not the target market for this, so take my review with a grain of salt. IGN made this seem way more interesting to me than it was. If you relate to what I'm saying, that's the kind of person this is directed to. Not every game is for every person. This game should find it's people.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little train-themed puzzle game with gorgeous graphics and a cosy pastoral vibe. If you enjoyed Mini Metro, you'll love this. It doesn't have a whole bunch of strategic depth, but it is beautiful and relaxing to play.Or at least... I can tell that it would be, as designed. Unfortunately, even on the Steam Deck, it struggles on the very lowest graphics settings. I found it frustrating trying to move the camera or even click on buttons with framerate sometimes in the single digits on large maps. I'm sure it would have been a joy to play on a really beefy system, but it badly needs more optimisation before the rest of us can enjoy it.Also note: This game is designed to be played with a mouse. There are button controls, but they're frustrating and unintuitive. Save your sanity.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of other people, I picked this up from Humble's Monthly Choice (October 2024); Now, initially upon reading the blurb and skimming through the store page, I thought this was going to be a sort of city-builder lite, essentially a comfy version of something like Railroad Tycoon, with lovely little voxel graphics.I was a little surprised and disappointed when I found out that the main gameplay loop is "connect A to B then connect that to C" with some challenges like "have X$ at the end of the stage" and "don't make more than Y metres of track". As for enjoyment of this title, it's going to depend whether you care for the achievements and challenges. For a game that touts itself as comfy and relaxing, spending 10-15+ minutes pouring over the map and fiddling around every time you want to place something, because it might save you $2, only to finish the stage and be $3 short for the "Fund Challenge" can actually be quite aggravating. Another huge annoyance is slapping down a station and trying to connect it up, only to get "bend too tight" and it refusing to place any track, or saying it'll be $300 as it tries to put 4 bridges in a giant circle to make the ends meet. Thankfully, in some scenarios this jank can be an advantage as I cheesed a stage by having a station at a 90* angle up a sheer cliff-face, which then meant I only needed $20 of track. Because of these points though, it is very easy to get to the end of a stage, only to then realise that you're going to have to restart as you've locked yourself out of the challenges due to money or placement, because once something is placed, it cannot be moved or deleted. The "load last checkpoint" will only undo the very last section of track you've placed, so to complete a stage and both associated challenges, you'll likely need to replay the same level several times, or at least load back to a previous save-point multiple times.I'd argue the best way to play, especially in the later stages, is to focus on one challenge at a time, replaying the level again for whichever one you missed.Now, there's a lot of complaints saying that you don't know where buildings will pop up, which makes what I just wrote even more annoying, however, at least in the first 2 areas/biomes, there are giant piles of wood and bricks littered around the map, which will say "Under Construction" when you hover over them. This means that you do actually know where buildings will eventually be, although in most stages it doesn't say what the buildings are or when they will unlock, so the best process is to always leave a spare platform at most stations you place.Overall, the game has the "comfy" aesthetic and soundtrack to it, but the actual gameplay can be quite obnoxious and repetitive, especially when you miss out on a challenge by $2. I definitely wouldn't class some of the stages as "relaxing" either. If you don't care for the challenges or achievements, it could be a chill game to play off and on, but you'll probably only get several hours of play-time out of it before being done with all the stages. I wouldn't personally say I regret picking this as one of my Humble choices, but I certainly wouldn't have ever spent the asking price of £14.99 on it. Even the 50%-off sale price, now I know what the game is about, I'd be very on the fence.If ever there was a moment where I wish Steam had a "Maybe" option, this would be it, but there isn't, so it's a "Not Recommend" from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping there would be more strategy involved in the puzzle solving. But once you hook tracks to stations you've pretty much "solved" the puzzle. The running trains are just a nice visual if you think to slow down to appreciate them. Not much train simulation beyond that except sandbox mode. The unique voxel look is beautiful but mostly lost when zoomed out enough to see the map to play the game as intended.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Game treats you like a child. You are forced to do everything like the game told you to do. Wow you connected 2 buildings? You are such a mastermind. Here are your next 2 buildings. Good luck connecting those two :O Maybe it's going to be better late game, but the beginning of the game is just frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just a bit too slow for me. The animations take too long, if you want to undo your last step, you have to go through a loading screen that resets the music, which takes a bit too long and annoys me. I wanted to achieve 100% on this game so I kept on playing, but it just wasn't much fun.On the bright side, the landscapes are beautiful and, the trails you create fit in and look organic, and there are new buildings and challenges introduced in each region, but nothing ground breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a very charming and sweet little game. The art style is faultless and a joy to look at. However, as others have said, the actual gameplay experience is lacking. The problem is that while the levels look very open and approachable, the actual way you go about solving the puzzles is very prescriptive and linear. This is not like Transport Fever 2 which one could argue is a giant puzzle game of connecting train stations and industries together. Unfortunately, Station to Station is simply not engaging enough (to me) as a puzzle game which looks freeform on the surface. Regardless, as a spectacle, this game is simply lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Besides the fact, that I expected more of a simulation/management game, I tried to like it as a relaxing puzzle game. Sadly, the puzzle mechanics don't work for me.The goal of the puzzles is to connect stations in an optimized way, which means you need to connect as many stations as possible that do not affect each other until you can connect a station that will result in a "combo" of effects to grant bonus income. Also, there are cards that e.g. reduce the costs of tracks or bridges, increase the outcome of a combo,...But the game has three problems for me: 1.) All the levels feel the same, as no new mechanic changes the way you play (at least until world 3 of 5)2.) The cards are drawn random3.) When you start a level you only see a couple of buildings that needs to be connected, when you progress through the level new buildings appear that needs to be integrated. This resulted in restarting a level after the first time that I knew who would appear, so that I could plan my rail network from the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, i'm always happy and proud to see a game from a dutch developer! And more so when its not a crappy game but a good one with some love and quality put into it. I'm only 1.7 hours in (did the first few lvls with my son) and it's already putting a smile on our faces. I hope the undo/correct/move option will get some improvement. Its there now in a crude form with the release. but in my opinion one should be able to delete tracks at all time. I hope (and think)  the game has a bright future and i hope it's gets more updates and additions (trains, maps, buildings).
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: The game looked very promising, with train systems and a visually pleasing voxel design. I was fully prepared to spend the evening going through it until linking stations in ways that trains don't actually travel from source to destination was introduced, and I realised the trains were there just for show...There doesn't seem to be a useful delete or undo button, so I couldn't remove a station that was slightly too far from a town and had to create another one next to it. The only other option was to reset, because the checkpoint included the incorrectly placed station.The visuals are great, but unfortunately the beauty quickly fell apart when this game became purely a train-themed puzzle with no actual train mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like a fun and relaxing game. Sadly feels very frustrating to play.I would love to just take back what i build and place it new if i see a big problem.I hate the Star and Pig challenges. I get that they are making it more complex, but for me they felt like i needed to redo the level until i get them. And redoing a level feels very frustrating, because you still get building after building, even tho you already know where everything will be.I hope i can get back to this game in half a year and they fixed all my complains.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: My negative review comes down to a matter of personal preference. The game is very pretty with a good soundtrack and a nice change of pace from my usual preferences of shooters or RTS. So why don't I recommend it? This strikes me as a mobile game at best. It's really something that belongs on an iPad rather than needing full WASD configuration. The logical paths of resource->production->city made sense to me, and the game was very enjoyable, but I'm not sure this needed to be a PC release.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing puzzle game.Great, unique and really beautiful visuals, decent sounds and audio, lots of levels and challenges to do, and a lot more.The only thing I did not like in the game is the randomness of cards you get when achieving certain fund treshholds. One game, I can make a simple mistake, and see that one card would make my idea work, but I didn't use it, however, after restarting the level, I did not get the same card I needed, making it even more difficult to finish the level. Now, this only happened two times where it truly mattered, but it did feel bad.Also, i did notice an extreme use of my GPU when using higher graphic settings, which was not expected from a game not that graphically heavy, which is something the devs should take a look at in the future.Outside of this, I really have no other problems. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Game is one of those "easy to learn, difficult to master" type scenarios.  If you want to just blow through it and connect the railroads to each other/junction, the game isn't difficult at all.  However there is an art to planning it out and finding the best possible routes to get a max stack bonus and achieve both the $ and Challenge bonuses for each round. I absolutely love it and feel its one of the best casual puzzle games I've ever played.Add in the charming graphics and effects and relaxing soundtrack, this game ticks all the boxes. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a lovely and fun game. It blends super chill ambiance as you ponder how to build your railway empire. I liked how there were different biomes in the campaign and that they are secluded from one another, The graphics are lovely. I love this kind of art style. Music is also pretty good. UI is simple and works, but its not perfect. I have nothing but good things to say about this great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a puzzle game where you are tasked with building railways to connect resources together. This mainly involves optimizing rail/cost ratios, connecting certain places together in a certain order to maximize combos, and using cards that cut costs or give bonus money at certain times. Absolutely nothing wrong with this game but I feel like I got all I'm gonna get out of it by the 7th level.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: There is no main objective other than connecting all the buildings without running out of money. This makes the game super easy if you don't want to go for the optional challenge and the under certain certain budget optional objective with steam achievements being the only reward for completing those. Still pretty fun as a comfort game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cozy/relaxing puzzle game. It's not much of a train sim or management game. It's about finding the optimal path and order to create rails in to hit your goals. Bringing more goods to one location from one track will give you stack bonuses so you really want to organize your map accordingly. My only complaint about it is that you'll unlock new buildings to put stations in as you get more money per map. You will often times end up blocking yourself because you don't know what the next buildings will be. They always appear in the same spots so I feel like you end up playing it once to beat the level and then your hopes of hitting the goals relies on remembering the buildings. You can see the early signs of a construction site where the buildings will appear and hovering your mouse over them will give you a name but then it's up to you to remember what goods it needs and produces. It would be nicer if it would show you everything so you can plan better on your first go around.However, that's more of an issue if you really want to hit all the goals. Simply beating the levels outright is fun on its own. I really enjoyed the game all the way through. It took me about 16 hours to 100% and I loved every minute of it!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this is NOT just a pretty voxel game with trains. Well, it is that, but it is also much more. Station to Station is actually a casual, laid back puzzle game, where you are tasked to crate complex railway connections. It is generally quite easy to beat a level, but if you want more of a challenge, you can try the optional goals, which make you think a lot harder. If you’re not into puzzles, the sandbox mode lets you just build railroads and watch the trains without worrying about anything. It’s super chill and perfect for relaxing.The graphics are super pretty, with colorful voxel art that makes everything look so nice and cozy. The music is also really calming, which adds to the laid-back vibe.It’s not the kind of game for people who want a tough or super complicated experience, but if you just want to chill and have fun, this is a great pick. It’s simple, creative, and really fun to play when you just want to unwind.Recommended at discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful puzzle game. At first I was expecting a train game, but this is more of a connections puzzle with a cute train skin. Still, the ambience is relaxed, the mechanics are clean and work well, and I loved the soundtrack that grows as you make connections. All-in-all, a high quality puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The graphics are cozy, very satisfying, the gameplay is fun, a good mix of puzzle, challenge and strategy, cards give a lot of control about how you want to play it.BUTit made my PC crash to black screen and I needed to restart whole PC. three times. no other game has done this so beware.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of an indie gem here! A relaxing puzzle with music perfectly fit the theme, splendid voxel graphics and puzzles. Puzzles are not too easy and not too hard, just fine to enjoy a game and sometimes challenge your brain.I spent there 30 hours and never ever I met a bug or something that would disapoint or annoy me. Get at full price. It's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly a great game. I am not a fan of cozy/relaxing games and i would have never played this one if not for humble bundle. But i am very happy i did. I think "simulation" is a wrong tag. Puzzle would a better way to describe this. It is not super complex where you need to bust out guides and videos. The in-game tutorial is pretty much sufficient. The combos are very satisfying to pull off but if you want a relaxing experience, you don't even need to understand them to progress. Just happily connect your stations and enjoy the view if you want.It has a gorgeous art style and the music makes feel happy and giddy. It does not have a lot of complexity and bells and whistles, it does a few things and it does them very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just so lovely. The way the map lights up and the music builds on itself as you slowly unravel the puzzles and connect your stations feels amazing every time. The value in here is out of this world as well, with custom map editor and also a random generator to keep playing new levels with plenty of customisation of every possible variable over and over.The only thing that would keep this from being a true A+ for me is how some of the challenge stars for some levels are worded in a way that isn't the easiest to understand, but since levels don't take too long to retry, it's not that big a deal if you misunderstand something and want to try and do another run to optimise.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I am generally repulsed by voxel "art", however, this is one of the few games I have seen use voxels effectively to such a degree that I forget that it is voxels and can appreciate it's beauty. Gameplay is simple but deceptively deep as you go further in the levels. A great vibe game for playing while you are listening to a podcast.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Very cozy and relaxing puzzle game.  Great voxel art too.I do wish there were some harder puzzles, and that more then just the very final one made you put together all the things you'd learned in previous groups of levels.  There's a custom game mode but the random nature makes them pretty hit or miss, and even on the hardest settings they're not that hard.  If you want a real head scratcher puzzle game this probably isn't for you, but for a relaxing time with lovely aesthetics this does the job.Oh, and if the devs see this - make your undo button go back more then the current 4 moves.  You should be able to undo all the way back to level start.  On some of the longer levels you can be forced to restart because you screwed up not noticing where a new element was going to spawn 6 moves later which is frustrating and ruins the otherwise pretty excellent vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting and engaging little puzzle game. Not excessively hard by itself, but all levels include challenges to make them a bit harder. I did not have patience to do them all, but they do make you finish level in unusual way sometimes. Overall, game is much more then i expected from quick glance over store page, worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a puzzle game about how to connect various resources by rail within confines like difficult topography and mission specific goals than a rail building game like railway empire, etc. This is a good thing for me as the other rail building games are way too complicated doing simple things. However, I got bored after one map, but I might go back to it again. 60/100
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Halfway done, 7.5 hours on record, all challenges beaten. So far. Alright, I had to look one up for a bit of help, because I did not understand the challenge requirements (and I still think they're ♥♥♥♥♥, because they require an insane amount of planning ahead if you also want to finish the funding challenge at the same time, which, granted, you don't need to).So, every level consists of you building stations and railroads (duh) to satisfy consumer and production needs. When you've satisfied all needs the level is won. However, there are 2 optional challenges for each level: funding and star. The first one requires you to have a certain amount of money left at the end of the level, the second one challenges you with doing something special, usually, or out of the ordinary, like "collect all loot on the map" or "build a railroad that cuts through exactly 15 trees", and some such.These challenges are what makes the game interesting. Otherwise, it would just be a very zen railroad puzzler. And yes, the game is a puzzle game first and foremost. The graphics are charming, and the basics of an "economy" are there, but your main goal is to use the buildings and cards (cheaper railways, more money for connections, free water bridges, etc.) at your disposal to close to optimal efficiency (there is some leeway, so it's not ultra punishing if you didn't do something perfect). To get the best results, you're not supposed to connect the production chains one at a time, but create a railway network that connects as many as possible at the same time.Example: Instead of building a railway between a wheat farm and a mill to produce flour, and then to a bakery to produce bread, and then to a city to supply this city with bread, you can connect the city to the bakery, then the bakery to the mill, and finally the mill to the wheat farm, i.e. in opposite order. That gives you a "stack" bonus of +20% money per stacked resource. But since cities require more than one resource, there's quite a bit more complexity involved, depending on the level. And since new buildings and cards are unlocked in each level according to the amount of money you've already made, bad early decisions can have a negative cascading effect. Basically, you want to make as much money early on to unlock more options to make even more money. Sometimes this requires replaying a level until you know exactly what you will have available ... and when. But that's ONLY for the challenges. The levels themselves can be beaten super easily without that much forethought.Currently, the game consists of 54 levels. I believe there is room for DLC if the developers so choose at some point in the future. If you're looking for a neat little zen game with cute lego-like optics that ALSO offers you some optional challenge ... and if you like trains, then this is for you. The closest game I can think of would be Train Valley 2 I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a game developed by Galaxy Grove and published by PrismatikaThe game offers some nice graphics, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessStation to Station overall, however, is a fun game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring and tedious if being played for a long time, but is a very good simulation and puzzle game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Very well executed game. The puzzle loop is great, it's not over the top advanced but it still challenges your thinking. There are 3 things to focus on when completing a level which is to get all the buildings connected and then finish the level with a certain amount of money and then there is a bonus task which can be different things. I really enjoyed that every world you played introduced a new element to the puzzles which made all the different worlds unique. There is also an option to create a custom game. Once I was finished with a level I always stopped to admire my work when the trains moved across the world past each other. It made the world feel alive. Oftentimes i stopped to go into photo mode to take some pictures because the graphics are very good in the game. The way the light reflects on surfaces, blur in the distance and realistic shadow casting it's always pretty to take pictures.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I might be a bit biased since I attended a presentation that the developers gave about this game's development 2 years ago, and thus I was so excited to finally play it. All that aside, I love the game A LOT. Such a great mix of relaxation and puzzling. 1000% recommend, I played 3h straight and I would keep going if sleep wasn't important
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Steam locomotive puzzles, beautiful voxel art, pretty music, and tiny little horses that rear when you click on them. Station to Station (not to be confused with the David Bowie album of the same name) is a fun and often difficult puzzle game. You're expected to connect various resources together in the most efficient, profitable manner possible. Every level has a monetary challenge as well as a bonus challenge, but these are purely for your own sense of accomplishment. So long as you connect all of the resources without depleting your funds, you'll progress to the next level. I found this game to be really addictive, and since I bought it at a slight discount, I definitely feel as thought I got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Appearances can be deceiving.Take, for example, Station to Station.You think you are getting a game about trains with a rather unique aesthetic.You would be wrong, for there is absolutely no economic or logistical management in this game.Further investigation might fool you into thinking you are indulging in a rather enjoyable puzzle game with a train skin.Again, you would be wrong.For this is not a game about trains at all.It's a game about making connections under increasingly adverse conditions.It's a game about incorporating new relationships without impacting on those already established.It's a game about life.In an increasingly disconnected world, this is your ticket to training and guidance to a more connected life.You deserve it, your future children, and grandchildren, depend on it.

_childDocuments_.review: <This revue is written by a non-native speaker>Ok, first of all - "Station to Station" is NOT a tycoon game, and I'm fine with it. I have no idea how anyone can look at the store page and think it's a tycoon, but apparently some people did.It's a pretty casual train puzzle, perfect to relax after work. The best analogy I can think of is "Train Valley" - you need to connect the "points of interest" and not get bancrupt. But  this game is much more relaxed because there's no time limitations at all. The trains don't have a specific time to spawn and go, they can't crash, they... mostly a decoration. You chose where to build stations, how to connect them, sometemes you can chose the train itself - basic fright or passanger, or some special train that gives you extra money in specific conditions. The tutorial is easy and intuituive, you won't be wandering "WTF is this thing?" and "how TF do I do this?" - all the mechanics are clear and simple.The graphics - pixelated, but 3D, simplistic, but detailed. There's something very warm and comforting about this style. Everything looks like it was built in Minecraft!Overall: If you like train puzzle games, like "Train Valley" - most likely you will enjoy "Station to Station". And if you liked this game - go check out "Train Valley"!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, Although a little short and i'm not a fan of how dumb the bridges look. The water also looks a little out of place given its not pixilated. The grafics voxel art grafics are well made and enhanced by the beautiful lighting of the game. The music is relaxing and smoothing and the overall feel of the game is a nice joy ride after a long day. A beautiful ride for strategy game enjoyers!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: I was immediately drawn in by the trailer and this game did not let me down! Station to Station has been a relief for me after stressful days.The design is beautiful and it made me so happy to zoom in and see the little buildings do their thing.When you complete each level, you can stay there until you are ready to move on, allowing you to spend a bit more time with the scenery.The music... the music is so good. And as you progress in the level, the music will change a bit, giving you different layers to the same track.It is heartwarming, calming, moving, joyous, I truly love it. Thank you to Paul Aubry for composing such a great soundtrack. It fits perfectly into the world of Station to Station.You start off most levels with just a few buildings in place. Connect them up and more buildings will appear, eventually allowing you to make use of all the buildings in the area. You will have a limited amount of money to do this, but getting from start to  finish on a level is absolutely fine.Along with more buildings being unlocked, cards will also be given to you.There will be new types of cards introduced throughout the game, e.g. cards that allow you to have different trains, blow up rocks, reduce the price on bridges, etc. I think the pacing of these is good, and doesn't overwhelm you with too much information at once. It allows you to strategise and make extra money.Each level (beyond the intro) will have a fund challenge and a star challenge, which can be tricky. These will require you to do a lot of forward planning in order to finish the level with a certain amount of money, or to satisfy a requirement. I've missed quite a lot but will go back to complete them for sure! It felt great when I did complete them, especially both in one go!This game has just been so nice to play and I'm looking forward to the future updates! I think Station to Station will always be a game I can go back to at any time. Thank you, Galaxy Grove!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so satisfying.On one hand, its relaxing. The music and visuals and cozy, and there's no stress because there's no rush and any mistake is easily corrected by loading the last checkpoint or restarting the quick missions. And on the other hand, its still interesting and engaging. I love the frequent little dopamine hits from figuring out each efficient connection, and even better the ones from completing a mission, achieving a bonus objective, or getting a really big stack bonus. And the game never gets old due to the frequent additions of small new mechanics.My only complaints is that its short, and that it could be just a tad more challenging, at least for bonus objectives. But then again, the high quality leaves me with excellent memories and no filler. I'll take quality over quantity myself, so well worth a buy. And besides, maybe the developers will keep adding more? I can only hope.If you're the developers reading this: Congrats on a game well made. _childDocuments_.review: I guess first and foremost I should mention this game is a bit outside of what I typically play, and I still really enjoy it. So this review is for the people like me that ask the question of whether it is really a game for them or not. My gaming profile is primarily turn based strategy and rpgs, with the occasional puzzle game.I find this to be a puzzle game with a fun, low-key vibe, a train theme, and an attractive pixel aesthetic. Doesn't burn the brain, but does provide the challenge of puzzling out the next series of moves and feels rewarding when you hit a solution you like. Simply finishing the levels (connect all the resources) is the basic challenge and something everyone will likely be able to do. Each level also has a specific objective which earns a star and a funding objective for finishing with plenty of money. These are the extras for those that want to try for them.I suspect I will ultimately get 12-15 hours out of the base game with all achievements and that feels like a reasonable value for me. I also enjoy that I can play in smaller chunks of time (30-45 minutes) and come away feeling good about the play session....also, there is apparently a dog you can pet - haven't found it yet, but who doesn't want to pet the dog?EDITFound the dog! _childDocuments_.review: With thanks to the folks at Galaxy Grove and Prismatika, we’re bringing you our full review for Station to Station. As ever, this includes our common-sense parent’s guide, as well as accessibility analysis. If you’re wondering if Station to Station is good, or even just if it’s safe for kids, we’ve got you covered.Our video review is just below, or you can keep reading for our extended written review below. (you can also read with much better formatting in our   Station to Station is a laid-back puzzle-breaking affair. You’ll use stations and rails to join raw materials with industries, and make sure that different produce can get to the cities that need it. It’s a fairly simplistic title, but we’ve found it to be bursting with charm, providing an exceptionally cosy and relaxing title to get a little lost in.Players will look to join these industrial landmarks within six different cozy regions. Each region has five or six scenarios, and while straightforward they do offer increasing challenges as you progress. Station to Station allows strategic thinking, offering puzzle-solvers bonuses for stacking goods. In addition to additional income, stacking will also allow you to hit financial targets for each level.Station to Station also gives various star challenges, with different objectives to unlock the additional achievement. Each scenario will require you to simply join all buildings to form a rail network and ensure goods can move to where needed. These financial and star challenges give completionists a little something extra, without breaking the relaxed and cosy environment for those who prefer a laid-back playthrough.As well as placing stations, rails and bridges (and watching your bank balance), Station to Station also provides single-use cards. These cards can give various help, such as lowering costs for rails, bridges and forest management, or increasing payout for completing connections. It’s important to use each at the right time if you want to get the most out of them, but with a chill nature to the game overall, it’s not vital that you get this right. According to the Family Gaming Database, Station to Station is rated by PEGI at 3 and above, but we have not found a rating for the ESRB at the time of publication. With that said, this one is absolutely family friendly. We’ve not found any concerning elements, and with the ability to turn money requirements off, micro-bandits can build to their heart’s content. It might not be aimed at younger ones, but it’s certainly one which we’re happy for our micro-bandits to get involved with. It is abundantly clear that the folks at Galaxy Grove have worked to make Station to Station as relaxing as possible. This has also meant that it’s also very accessible, and it’s one perfectly suited to players who want or need to take their time. All controls can be fully mapped to whatever you need, and the clear well-contrasted visuals mean easier reading.In addition, players have the option to turn off monetary requirements at any point. This means that you’re free to play not only at a time which suits you, but you are just able to build without limits. While it’s possible to challenge yourself in the title using challenges and stack bonuses, it’s not something that’s required.  Pixel Bandits Level for Station to Station is a . Station to Station doesn’t have the train-management depth of titles such as Railway Empire but it really does nail it as a cosy puzzle adventure. The different biomes don’t have much mechanical impact, but do provide a sense of progression, alongside additional cards and industries.It’s lovely to watch your cities grow as you connect them with additional goods and passengers. In addition, there’s a real sense of achievement after securing particularly lengthy stack chains, when placing your final piece.It’s a nice one to share with the family as well, and our micro-bandits enjoy watching the incredibly cute trains pootling between cities and stations. If you’re looking for a relaxed and exceptionally adorable puzzle title, Station to Station is definitely one to take a look at.

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a nice relaxing change of pace from other transportation strategy games out there. By being more of a puzzle game than an economics simulator you get to think more about planning a whole mini rail network from a high level, rather than worrying about each little % of gradient or minmaxing maintenance costs. And it really is all about , a good forward thinking strategy is the secret to success. No timing, no crazy levels of spatial reasoning, it's all about thinking ahead. New rules are introduced in each world, all of which play into the core mechanic of connecting industries and cities but add more things to consider while building a network. Finishing a level never gets too difficult, but optional objectives (in the form of achievements and money targets) give incentive to do things differently and reward effective use of the game mechanics. It really is quite satisfying to connect everything in just the way the developers intended and watch as the money flows in, fulfilling the level's monetary objective. And thankfully all of the levels are short and digestible, so it's not punishing at all to use one run to figure out the level, then replay and get those achievements.While the graphical style is cute and innocent, it is a bit GPU heavy and there are ways to cause lag (like planning a very long rail line). The voxel models are surprisingly detailed and full of animated bits (apparently it is possible to model outside Stephenson valve gear with a few cubes, who knew), but not enough to warm up a GPU - it seems post processing will gladly eat up all of the GPU. And on the topic of art, the soundtrack is very well made. There's also a bit of dynamic music going on, with buildups that happen as the map is completed. It's another way the game rewards play.I think this game is a nice relaxing and rewarding way to spend a weekend, a good way to take a bit of a break and be a part of something that wants you to have a good time.

Although as my own personal challenge I did play levels so I could try and get both in the one instance.Also to continue your value for money the game has a random level generator as well. I have played only a few levels of it. I can say it's difficulty comes not from the curation but the randomisation of it. So it presents a new level of challenge for each random one created.The achievements are pretty easy to get with only one really "hidden" achievement in the form of the "Pet the Dog". I won't say how you get it. I recommend this game for it's relaxing sound track, easy to watch graphics and puzzle gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely game to chill out to. I played it with my 7 year old and he understood the core premise in no time. Wheat goes to the mill to the bakery and to the city. He loved fooling around with optimising his routes or trying to build the most expensive track he could. Definitely recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: It's little bit like a combination of OpenTTD with a graphical style similar to Minecraft but way more cute. I played the demo a few months ago and have had this on my wishlist ever since. It's great fun little game, there's no pressure to get things done and it's just a case of trying to use the landscape efficiently so you can fit all the tracks in to connect the locations.If you like slow paced puzzlers with cute graphics then you'll probably enjoy this one. I wish the team best of luck and hope it sells well!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Station to Station is a wholesome little puzzle game featuring the cutest Voxel trains I have ever seen!I played the demo months ago and fell in love! Since then I have started playing the main game waiting to unlock the card system and some more difficult puzzles. I was not disappointed as the first region the tutorial area was coming to the end things were already getting difficult and really required me to think about how to complete the missions!I did post this video showing the first region if your unsure if the game is for you
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Cerebral but not overly taxing, a nice relaxing little game. If you play, I'd urge you to sometimes zoom in and just appreciate the the flora, fauna and structures - these little details are easy to miss if you just play the game to win.I think if I keep up the pace I'll possibly clear the main campaign within 6 hours (but the difficult looks like it can ramp up, so this is just an early estimate!), and there are 2 challenges per level to keep you coming back, plus a custom mode.I heartily recommend this if you've had a rough day!
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and calm game to get into! I like the slight minecraft/ Teardown aesthetic and getting to build train tracks and stations is a lot of fun. The instructions are pretty simple and the game is easy to understand and get started playing. I love the music as well and the sound effects when you do something right hit the right spot for encouraging me to keep going :)A fun and casual game that's pretty addicting and a good way to past the time without any real stress or headaches.
_childDocuments_.name: Station to Station

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing and pretty! I adore the voxel style and the combination with depth of field blur gives it a beautiful model train set vibe! name: Mirthwood
detailed_description: Wishlist + Follow! About the Game an enchanting RPG life sim. Fleeing a continent swept with war your arrival in a new land provides a fresh start. Experience an immersive medieval fantasy world sandbox that allows you to choose who you want to be. Manage your own homestead, build a farm, plant and harvest crops, rear animals, and upgrade your facilities to craft items and gear. Build a peaceful life for your family and trade your goods from town to town. Mirthwood features a rich, fully realized world, with gorgeous hand-drawn graphics, immersive sound effects, and an original musical score. Explore an open world comprised of six diverse regions and three distinct towns, with much to discover - and uncover. Battle Storms, Winter, & Disease with survival-lite elements as you progress through a bewitching world. Take up a sword or ready your bow in real-time combat, Mirthwood will pit you against a variety of enemies from Bandits to werewolves. Equip yourself with a collection of weapons, armor, and clothing. Level and specialize your character in your chosen combat class to improve your ability to survive the dangers of Bleakwood. Mirthwood’s ecosystem makes organic stories possible. Face new situations and conditions generated by the living world. Embark on quests, encounter dynamic events across the world and investigate mysteries. Search for Rare & Epic Loot across the world and find new adventures along the way. Meet and befriend (or insult) townsfolk and NPCs across Mirthwood with a new Sims-style interaction system. Establish & Grow a Relationship with any NPC, unlock new social Interactions as your relationships grow, and even uncover quests and tasks. The other denizens of the Free Lands each have their own lives to lead and will go about their days and nights in a fully simulated world.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not let the hours next to my name fool you; I've put just over 80 hours into the playtests over the last two months.  Getting a decent blend of RPG and Open World Survival Craft, can be really tricky, not to mention quite a bit of work.  A TWO PERSON DEV TEAM managed to pull it off--- but oh yeah, it is also a pretty cool farming sim with a deep NPC relationship component.  The fighting is a little simple, but I still find it quite fun (and this is coming from someone who plays Valheim, Enshrouded, and Nightingale- not Stardew Valley).  The devs are ridiculously responsive....like...push a hotfix in the middle of a playtest at a suggestion, responsive.  Any minor things that might be buggy at launch--- I have never had more faith in a game's developers to get it handled quickly.Great game. Great devs.  A really high potential hours/dollars ratio.  Do yourself a favor; give it a shot AND support a small indie studio (Brian and Daron, you guys rock!)
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I give this review a yes because there's a framework here for a great game. The artwork is beautiful, the setting is sublime, and the intent of the developers is well placed. However......This game is not ready, it's not a full release. Most of the systems are not effectively in place, There are stutters every time I'm running around. There is a lot of work that needs to be done to make this what it's supposed to be.Let's talk about the bad first--frame stuttering, while running from one place to another, not a killer but annyoing especially when fighting-no tutorial or guided experience, where can I at least go to get something? The opening quest is so open that it doesn't explain any of the game mechanics, you go to the nearby village and... explore? I'm not opposed to leaving someone to figure it out on their own but systems need to be more intuitive if this is how you leave us.-incomplete/unbalanced systems, why does farming not yield seeds? Why are finished products or produce of less value than seeds, why do I have to buy seeds? why would I waste 2 peas and an onion worth 32 coin on a 23 coin stew when I need to pay 8 coin per seed of onion and 11 per seed of peas? This isn't well thought out and that's just farming. I've read there are bugs in peas and potatoes, which keep growing without seeds, but I haven't seen this yet. everything else is one seed=one plant then buy seeds again. Also hunting should yield meat and pelts not just one or the other.-skills are negligible. I'm not sure what benefit there is to skills but when I do 3 damage with a bow there's not much benefit to 2.5% increases. the only reason to work on skills is to get the cards, and I have NO idea how to activate more cards for use. progression is not intuitive or noticeably effective.-buttonology/UI/UX, I've no issue with the general UI, but using only RMB to exit any menu (not the same button that opened it) is not helpful or intuitive. there should be other ways to open close menus, the TAB wheel is a good idea but it doesn't make sense, and I can't switch between tools and weapons without it. items that can be picked up/stolen/opened/gathered/harvested are not easy to see and I have a 42in monitor. There should be a glow or something that makes items in the wild or barrels stand out more.-interactions with people. Maybe I'm doing it wrong but I have no idea what I'm doing or how to interact with people effectively, I pretty much just talk to them over and over again and go through each option for dialogue, most of which fail miserably, they don't like me and I'm not sure what I'm doing right or wrong.The meh--Combat, it's fun and has some distinct challenge which improves the experience, but it's clunky as hell, poorly explained, and aside from health potions and food, I'm not sure there's really any value to it.The good--art and sound are wonderful, I really enjoy exploring the areas around my farm and towns, meeting hermits in the wild the option of exploring a new world makes this game something interesting.-the world, day night cycles and biome changes are fascinating, it seems there's some lore here, too, I'm interested in digging into.-incomplete systems show great potential, I like hunting, I like farming, and I like doing the quests, they just need to be better fleshed out.-good bones, this game has great bones, it just needs sinews and muscle and flesh.I will continue to play this game, and I hope the devs aren't turned off by the experience, they've built something that has so much potential, I see it as a 6 or 7 out of 10 now, but with upside to be 8 or 9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it an honest try - and now I understand why the developers pushed the game back 2 months. It's just not ready, and is definitely more of an "early access" release than a full release. And the price tag is a tad high for the quality of gameplay. A few suggestions I haven't seen the other negative reviews (and the positive ones that say the game is bad...?):1.) Make leveling skills more impactful. I got to a point where I had most skills at level 5, a decent ways in, and they made little to no difference. A 5% chance to get extra materials? When you can only mine maybe 10 nodes of the resource you need every 2-3 days? 5% damage increase on bows? I do 8 damage max per shot against enemies with over 100 HP, so that won't even show an increase until I can get a bow that does at least 10+ damage per shot.2.) Settings - In a more casual game like this, allowing the user to set specific sound types to different levels is just a basic thing that should be available on an early access release. The music IS good in this game, and I do appreciate it, but - the problem with music in a game like this, is that it gets repetitive really fast when you are playing casually and farming in a specific area. It would be nice to turn it off for a bit if it starts to get repetitive - because it definitely does.3.) Combat Height and HP Sponges - I don't think the combat is necessarily as bad as other people think in the reviews, but the height disparity issue and insane HP pools on enemies turn it into a frustrating slog. The height bug is extremely obvious when using ranged weapons and I can't imagine this was intended by devs - if I am on a hill and the enemy is on a lower terrain, you have to shoot at your "height level", AKA 5 feet above the enemy's head, to actually hit their hitbox and score damage. The same applies in melee combat, and is probably why players seem to think it's worse than I think it is - even a slight difference in height can require the player to aim at the enemy's feet or above their head (even in melee combat) to land a hit. I took to kiting enemies to an area with even ground for a more fun, fair fight - but it's just not possible in all areas.4.) General Direction - this might be an issue caused by some other areas where the game falls short, but I'm not really "working" towards anything. Quests and trackers feel really disjointed and random. I think it would better to have longer term goals set as quests to achieve, and have them tied to NPCs and social development (see next #5 below).5.) NPCs and Social - This is probably the biggest let down of all. The social system seems to have a lot of depth at first, until you realize (quickly) that NPCs are just a set of somewhat random and very general personality types, and not unique characters with any unique dialogue. A fair comparison would be if every Stardew characters still had liked and disliked gifts, but all said the same exact line when receiving a liked/disliked gift. I genuinely do think the idea behind the social approach and interaction menu is neat - with 5 different general types of interactions and 5 different "sub" interactions in each set. And characters with preferred and disliked types of interaction - but it's the ONLY thing that sets them apart.6.) This last is one is obvious per other reviews, but I would remiss to not include it - the bugs. I have had 3 CTDs while fast travelling. Stuck multiple times in terrain and had to quit out and load an earlier save (pretty sure if I hit the save button, it would be game-breaking and I'd permanently be stuck on my save). Enemies have teleported, or just despawned randomly. I've been stunlocked by enemies teleporting and attacking far faster than they should. Game has stuttering and freezing issues on a high end PC regardless of settings.If you are still considering buying this game, please do read through the positive reviews as well. I don't know what is going on there, but it's ridden with reviewers coming to the same conclusion I did (game is not ready/not worth the price tag), but still clicking the thumbs-up button for some reason. The result is that the review level on the surface at the moment is "mostly positive", but most of those "positive" reviews are pretty heavy critiques.

_childDocuments_.review: It probably should have been released as early access, but the devs seem committed to getting the game where it should be. This is definitely that cozy game with a dark twist that you've been looking for. That said, it wouldn't be the worst idea to wait until they finish the social systems before diving in, if those systems are important to you. They are pretty empty right now. I absolutely love the farming/crafting and player progression. The quests are great and the world is really well crafted, with little notes and lore sprinkled about that actually lead to cool discoveries. Combat isn't the most exciting, but it works.Fun game, looking forward to future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited for this game. Ive had it on my wishlist, played the demo, loved the art work, and was looking for a new survival Stardew valley/ valheim esk game.I spent 35 hours and finished it.  I was very thorough too. If I’d have just focused on finishing the game it would have been half that probably. I’m disappointed :(I finished the game yesterday and was so sad that I decided to sleep on it to make sure I had time to reflect on this. Pros-It’s pretty- I really like the art work. Good concepts- it has good potential. There is a multi select “dialogue” system, an economy system of sorts, character progression that you can change daily. All of these things I will touch on in the cons though. Amazing narrator! Added mystery and elegance.Consbuggy- Like so buggy it was almost unplayable at times. Quest finished without me doing anything once haha. I’ll give you more detailed bugs in the cons list. Lagging- it was stuttering and lagging and freezing constantly. I disabled overlays, set it to run as admin, everything I could think of. No fix. I just played through it. I’ve learned to play through lag over the years. It’s an acquired skill :)Crashing- often times the fast travel makes you crash. Not every time but a lot. It’s a fun game to see if you’ll make it. Early access- so nowhere on the store page does it say early access. The release was delayed even so  they had more time to get the game ready. Normally a game will say early access and if this is early access I would defiantly critique accordingly. In several comments players are saying early access in remarks. So if it is in early access that kind of irks me. It should be marked early access. I’m going to put on my tin foil hat here and say this feels intentional. There is a wave of gamers, like me, who are now refusing to buy early access games. I’m sick of it. Because I’m sick of getting excited about something and being disappointed. Like this. So if they are hiding early access to sell the game shame on you. But again it’s not marked early access anywhere, there is no road map or anything else so if it’s not in early access then shame on them too for putting out a game with so many problems. it just sucks. Resources- that is the only reason this took me 35 hours. there is an abundance of late game ore but iron which is tier 2 and 3 is so hard to get. there are so few iron ores and it takes a while too re spawn. defiantly needs too be re balanced i think. calendar year- so i finished this game in the beginning of winter. i thought maybe there is more and i just need to wait until year 2. so i slept until year two. that totally freaked the game out. day one of year two was spring of 16. whatever that was and no it did not open anything else up. i ran around the map just to make sure. World size- who needs fast travel when you can run across the map in 60 seconds anyhow. I didn’t time it but if it’s not a minute it’s close.Story- oh there was a story? Sorta. very shallow and not interesting. Economy system- they tried. There is a stall that you can check on demand and in supply items that changes every so often. It was so buggy I can’t tell you how often. there are times you check it and every in demand product is strawberries and in stock strawberries. Animals- i suppose this could just fall under buggy but...I can’t check on my animals because their little icon box stays on my screen all across the map. A restart will make this go away. So just go fast travel and crash and your chicken icon  will be fixed. Dialogue- what’s the point? Building friendship does not give you quests or benefits. You can’t get married or have kids. There is no special dialogue. Nothing. I like the dialogue game. It’s unique. but it has no purpose.Battle- the hit box is so crazy. You have to hit monsters diagonally. It’s so jankey. I made it work but ugh it was painful.End- let’s just take every monster on the map and put them all in one clearing. A clearing full of 20 werewolves and 15 wraiths and 50 rats. Why not. That seems like a great tedious bs challenge. Honestly that’s just lazy. I killed them but the whole time I was just rolling my eyes. Map- nothing is labeled. Maybe that’s a choice by the team. Idk. But it was annoying. Which camp is named what? You just have to memorize it. No hover over. You can pin one thing but pin is erased on restart. And you crash and have to re start so often there is no point pinning. Skill cards- skill cards are mostly broken and have no effect. Ex: I went with archery as I have to hit everything at a weird diagonal angle so I just found this easier with kiting and shooting. There are two archery skill cards. Both called ranger, both with the same description that arrows now deal poison damage. different pictures. Neither work. There is no poison damage to be seen. You seem to do the same amount of damage with and without those cards. I’ve tried one, then the other, then both. Nada. As far as the cards go they really don’t seem to impact performance at all. It’s weird. I do the same damage w the 5% perk as I do without it as well. I don’t think the cards work at all. I did notice a few coins different with the craftsman card and your hunger does drain ever so much less with the iron stomach. But most of the rest of them I think are broken. Or maybe I needed to restart when I changed cards? Everything takes a restart on this game honestly and I just don’t have that kind of patients or time. Weapons- this is just a gripe I guess BUT there are like 20 or more different swords you can choose from and craft. There are 4 bows. No named or special. I’m nit picking with that but it would be fun to see a special bow as  that’s the only thing that got  me through that game. All and all: This is not a finished product. It’s got to be early access. If it is then maybe it will be great after a while. But it needs a lot of work. Good concepts, pretty game but shallow story unfinished ideas and broken / buggy beyond enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: I eagerly anticipated this game for about 18 months.  Now that it's here I can say the wait was worth it.  Mirthwood combines elements of some of my favorite games and genres and does it in a way that I enjoyed and appreciated. I grew up on Harvest Moon and Legend of Zelda: A Link To The Past. I was happy to see that most of what made those games so beloved was present in Mirthwood.  From the first few moments of gameplay, it becomes clear that this isn't your usual Cozy Farming Sim. No, this is an adventure that will be laden with triumph and heartbreak. Each new twist in the story adds to that sensation and the characters have a way of drawing you into their plight. The landscape itself tells a story and the world is filled with clues and remnants of the tragedy that has befallen the Free Lands. I thoroughly enjoyed exploring the map and finding scraps of paper and letters from people in the world. The bleak and almost hopeless atmosphere only made me want to work harder to save these people.  There are, however, issues with some of the systems and mechanics in the game. To the developers' credit, they have been updating, patching and hotfixing many of the problems that people have reported. For a team of two, they're doing a stellar job. I try to keep in mind that it has taken Stardew Valley 8 years to get to the condition it's in. I am confident and excited to see what the team at Bad Ridge has in store for Mirthwood.  Would I recommend this game? Absolutely! I would add a caveat that players should expect a very different experience than they're used to from a farming sim. It might not be everybody's cup of tea but if they give it an honest chance, they might just develop the taste.  I would give the game, in its current state, a solid 8/10. My rating will go up as new systems and content gets added.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game that I’ve been lucky enough to put many hours into given I was able to playtest. The minute it came available to purchase, I was right there and ready for Mirthwood team to ‘take my money’. Talking of the team, they’re brilliant. Very quick to solve issues during the playtest, and I’m happy to say even a couple of my ideas got implemented - thank you devs! Therefore I have absolute faith the team will continue to deliver and the game you buy today will be even better in the future. That’s not to say there’s not a substantial game at launch. I’ve started a new game a couple of times now and played completely different each time. That’s why Mirthwood is such a gem. Whether you want to be a humble farmer, interior designer (so much fun doing up your little homestead), raring animals or want to go full on bandit, this game lets you live the Mirthwood life you wish. It’s a real joy to play. Part cozy with a bit of grind, great to look at, and yeah, highly recommend.For those wondering if it works on Steamdeck, yes it does. That’s how I’ve been playing with no issues. So happy to support these Indie developers. In fact, for the amount I’ve paid vs time played, I’ve got great bang for my buck.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for 1.5+ years after I saw the first glimpse of it. I followed every little crumb of information to find out if it would really match up to my hopes (and dreams) for this game.And it did. I'm serious if I tell you this might be one of the best games I've ever played, even though it has its flaws.In September I joined the amazing community on Discord. It has been so welcoming, and the way the devs and staff have been communicating AND listening to their audience is beyond my expectations. Everything gets addressed, no question is too much, help is just around the corner if you are in need. Their transparency about the (state of the) game has been really refreshing to see and I really enjoyed being able to participate in the playtests before launch. I've played around 50+ hours in total now (playtests included) and I still have so many things to do, to explore and to read into the lore.At last, a special shout out to the visuals! The colours, imagery, effects – it's a work of art. Even on the lowest settings it's gorgeous to look at. It feels like flipping through a storybook. And thank you devs for including candles at launch, much appreciated lol. ( I play Mirthwood on my MacBook Air M1. It runs really well, although it's not supported I can recommend it when playing through Whisky. I have added a guide to the Discord for whoever wants to try!)

_childDocuments_.review: Buyer beware: this game needs more time to cook. If this were an Early Access title, it would be acceptable, but as a 1.0 release, the quality control isn't there. Too many bugs. Too many controller issues for a store page that boasts "full controller support"  and "your Xbox controller is supported". Steam Early Access is 11 years old at this point. If you want to release a buggy mess, that's your avenue. No one will be upset because you have set clear expectations. 1.0 conveys some modicum of QA and polish. These are not new concepts. This game has a lot of potential, but I feel let down as a consumer.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood was in my wishlist for a long time, so when it got released, it was an instant purchase (I will come back to this later).Let me preface this by saying that I love "cozy" games, farm sims, and life sims in general. I also love when these genres are mixed with darker themes, like Graveyard Keeper for example. With that in mind, Mirthwood looked right up my alley.One of the reasons I bought the game so fast was that it's not an early access. Or at least it's not advertised as such, even though it truly feels like it... the game is unfortunately very badly optimized for what it is. You can't get 60 fps on Steam Deck, and all in all it's a quite demanding game, which is weird to see because my PC just ran Silent Hill 2 and Helldivers 2 with cooler temps and less micro freezes.I had trouble starting my journey: I had to launch the game twice because it glitched during character creation. My character got stuck in front of a closed door (?) and the game froze. I initially thought there was a bug regarding female characters, but nope: women have male voices, which means that my female peasant sounds like a 40-year-old dude.I was impatient to see the social interactions Mirthwood has to offer, but there's not a ton of great dialogues with people in the village. You can speak to them by selecting a topic, but you will only see emojis (like in The Sims) which makes interactions a bit shallow in my opinion, and most people forgettable. I would have appreciated some real lines of dialogue. The option to start conversations also didn't systematically appear, so I had to restart the game as well. Oh, and the combat aspect is quite janky and slow.I guess that's pretty much it. I'm quite disappointed because this game feels like an early EA title, but it's not advertised as such and is sold for 24.50 euros, which is way too pricey in my opinion. That being said, only two people made this game, and it's quite impressive!
