_childDocuments_.review: I've been debating on whether I should leave a review or not, but I decided to just to warn anyone who might be looking at this game for a cozy weekend.I'd like to first preface this review by saying the game has a lot of potential. It's got a beautiful art style, lore scattered throughout the map, and I like the NPC system thus far despite it being pretty shallow. You can run from enemies, not having to fight them if you don't want to (although you will take a few hits if you're stuck in the caves with them), you can hunt for food, and place things wherever you want.However, that's pretty much the extent of the good stuff. Like I said, it has potential - as an early access game. This is NOT  a finished game, and it shouldn't have been released as one. Especially not when its initial release was delaying by 2 additional months with the promise of more fleshed out systems. Half of the systems aren't even in the game yet. There's game breaking bugs and glitches that are in the process of being fixed as they're reported, and the economic balancing in the game is still being worked out.If they'd released Mirthwood as early access, it wouldn't have half of the negative reviews it does now. I would've made this a positive review. But they're lying to their potential customers by releasing it as completed, because it's simply not. The development team is made up by two people, which is extremely impressive. They've made something good, and with time it'll be something amazing. They have an active discord, where they fix up the bugs reported relatively quickly. They're pretty cool. Unfortunately, them being pretty cool doesn't fix their mistake of releasing this game unfinished. If you want to check Mirthwood out, I highly recommend waiting maybe a few more months. Hopefully by then, it'll actually be completed and worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on potential and the fact that the devs are actively making improvements. I like the game, but it does have problems.The game is a lot less cheery than most farming games, which I think is very fitting for the medieval setting. NPCs do have some sort of character which determines what type of social interaction works well and which doesn't. If you get close to them, they will react to you based on the relationship. Your farm is not a safe zone, so when bandits are chasing you, they follow you onto your property. If a bandit chases you into town, NPCs will draw their swords and defend themselves, which might be helpful to you. You can interact with items like campfires, even if they're outside of your property or belong to somebody else.The devs are working on the game the whole time, which is good. Walking and fighting feel a bit weird, even though I can't pinpoint the reason. I can't comment on the alleged false advertising because I never watched the trailers.  I'm not new to the genre and I still have many questions that can be frustrating to figure out. There is a rudimentary tutorial section at the beginning of the game, teaching you how to move, how to fight and how to equip or use items. Afterwards, you are basically on your own to figure everything out. Some sort of ingame encyclopedia or NPCs related to the subject explaining it would really help! Based on my observations, I assume that this might be what happened: This is the devs' first Steam release (not necessarily their first game). They are really passionate about their game and worked hard, but didn't ask more experienced developers for advice. Playtests either didn't take place or the playtesters were too homogenous so that many questions that are being brought up now were simply not raised before release. Because of the lack of advice from more experienced devs, the game got a full release, even though many feel that it should have been EA (and I agree!). The anger and frustration of the players was probably a frustrating and maybe overwhelming situation for the devs.In the end, there is a solid base with many good ideas, but suboptimal execution. The game can and is being improved upon, so I remain hopeful that at some point, the majority of players will be happy. For that reason, I keep the thumbs up. If, however, the game ends up being abandoned in an unfinished state, I will change it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure why this game gets so much love in reviews. It might have been better as a pixel-art game as the style is one of the main problems. For such an emphasis on combat the combat is very boring and frustrating because of the poor interface (have fun jumping forwards into enemies!) Farming is secondary and crafting not that satisfying. Graveyard Keeper is more fun, Stardew Valley a better sim, and Kynseed a better story and combat. 3/5 in hopes post-release dev improves the roughness and balance a LOT.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much exactly what I was expecting.... and then some. _childDocuments_.review: Selecting 'Recommend' because there is no neutral option available. Returned the game but will check for updates in the future.Mirthwood is a title that I was drawn to from the first time I saw a teaser over a year ago. It has a lot going for it, and I genuinely feel that can (and hopefully will) improve over time. Unfortunately, in it's current state it's just not something that I'm willing to invest any significant time into.What's great:- The game is beautiful and looks like unique to anything else that I have played- The soundtrack is spot on, perfect fit for the game's ambiance- Interesting class/profession approach, though some seem much better than othersWhat's rough:- The whole menu and UI system is confusing and defaults to an unreadable size- The UI prioritized aesthetics over function - not much contrast, font choices are pretty but get old- The storage system is a mess. You can only carry so much of different categories of items, which is a lot much confusing than basing it on weight (which also sucks) or inventory slots. If I have room to pick up a new material I should instead be able to use that slot to pick up a mushroom. At minimum, the game does a poor job of explaining how this works. - From what I can tell there is no crafting from materials in containers- Player onboarding/tutorial could really use some work. Had 6-7 quests within the first 10 minutes with no idea what to prioritize, when to sleep, etc.- Everything is a bit clunky. Combat, chopping wood, farming etc. What drove me batty was the fact that you can only swing an axe if you are aiming it at a tree. So if you aren't aligned correctly you click and nothing happens.Overall, the game has a lot of potential but I am disappointed that they delayed release by a month and it still came out like this. Development shouldn't be rushed, but this seems like the extra time was not enough. I've played a lot of these types of games, and Mirthwood did not feel like it was worth investing time into right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely beautiful and intriguing game, but it often stresses me more than I'm comfortable with and I've got slightly mixed feelings for other reasons too. Mirthwood was on my radar and I would have been beyond excited if it weren't for the combat. A dev statement said their goal was letting you avoid it, but I was wary. When I was generously gifted a review copy, I thought I'd give it a try. I found options for "easier combat" and "easier survival" in the settings and chose both, hoping for a chill RPG+ experience in a beautiful world that's not just yet another cutesy farming sim. My first impression was heavy Book of Travels vibes, but with slightly more direction and fewer bugs. The graphics and the music are positively enchanting. Performance is rather amazing considering I've been playing on an almost 10 year old laptop a good bit below minimum specs and it was ok-ish with the lowest settings (EDIT: a bunch of people are very unhappy with performance on Steam Deck though). Finding my way around the game took some time and for some details a LOT of time, too little tutorial especially for farming and tools imo. Exploring would have been very cool if I didn't constantly get attacked (as I said, I was looking for that combat-free experience). I've so far managed to get through the game without equipping a weapon, but it's often been stressful and frustrating. It is possible that part of it is due to lag on my poor old laptop, but there's also just the sheer amount of bandits, wolves and various other aggressives. Often I end up picking up another "follower" or 3 while trying to run away. EDIT : If you miss all your health points, you're respawned nearby with some of your health back up and your inventory untouched, so that's pretty forgiving. Farming probably would have been a better and more profitable experience if I'd figured out earlier how to properly prepare the soil. Watering actually has the best system I've come across, always found that a pita in other games. You can't collect or "produce" your own seeds though, so that's tedious. There's a decent amount of decorations and extra stuff to customise your house, and they are in the same pleasant style as the rest of the game. The inventory system is restrictive and upgrades are grindy. Crafting seems very grindy, unless I'm missing something again. I did miss info on how to upgrade your tools, but even now that I've finally figured it out I need a large amount of iron to upgrade my basic tools, but for mining iron ore I need... the upgraded iron pickaxe?? Sooo I'm hoping they'll reconsider that, or in case I got something wrong that there'll be more of a tutorial. I didn't manage to get my villager friendships to move even the tiniest bit, so I'm wondering if they're bugged. I didn't try super hard though because clicking on symbols to get a plus or minus and some general theme of the conversation isn't all that interesting. On the plus side, there are some NPCs with quest-related dialogues that are actually meaningful and well-written. There's a good amount of world-building and lore spread across items and quests. I got a couple of bugs, some that seem to have broken side quests. Nothing dramatic or game-breaking so far (unless the lack of any friendship progress is a bug and you're really into that kind of thing). I didn't check out hunting and fishing because I don't enjoy stuff like that. So far that's worked out fine, though maybe it's a reason why I'm struggling a bit with money. A big heads up that this game only auto-saves after sleeping. It does NOT save when you exit to the main menu. There's a manual save at least, but only a single save slot. No idea how that's still a thing in 2024 tbh. So I've got a lot of issues with this game. Which is why I stopped playing, right? Nope. Every time I close the game, I can't stop thinking about it. * * * If you like chill and story-driven games, check out my curator . You're also welcome to join the .

_childDocuments_.review: Im sorry, I was so excited for this game, but its nowhere near ready. To label this as a full release feels like a complete bait and switch.Where to begin.The Skills:Skill upgrades offering 2.5% increase to stats is so minuscule a player will never see any visual improvement to damage. This is coupled with skill cards that will offer choices such as "5% more defense against enemies" vs "Take less damage". How is a player supposed to make an informed decision based on that information?The grind: Gather everything. Especially basic wood. It sounds ridiculous considering were in a forest, but wood becomes so scarce because you will NEVER be able to chop anything bigger than the saplings. Even all the way to gold axe. If anything some of the tools seem to feel worse as you upgrade them. With the copper watering can I consistently was able to water a 2x2 crop square. Upon upgrading to the steel can I was suddenly having trouble hitting that 2x2 square. The visiual targeting definitely didnt get bigger.The Bugs:Throughout gameplay I consistently had moments where the game would freeze for a split second, drop fps to 1 then quickly recover. It didn't make it unplayable, but was very annoying.Fast travel would quite often begin crashing the game. When attempting to go from A>B game crashes. Upon reload A>B would Crash again. Perhaps A>C will also crash, but A>D might not after which fast travel works again. Another exercise in complete frustration. This despite using the load button, not continue as apparently this was also causing issues somehow.The final bug that killed the game for me. At one point you are tasked with gathering 4 key items to open a door. I proceeded to place the first one in the door when I first obtained it so I wouldn't lose it. At some point during gameplay this key item was then deleted and upon returning with the final 3 I discovered my save was now bricked. Its safe to say Ill never see the end of the game as a result, unless a fix is implemented.The Missing:The marketplace shows trade routes, tax rates, town coffers, item requisitions. These are all seemingly not implemented at this stage in the game.  I may also be one of the few people having conversation progress reset, but not once during my 21 hours of playing has charisma leveled even once. Seemingly, its not implemented.I could also be wrong, but I could swear during the demo it was heavily implied wed be able to repair the meadery. If I'm remembering this correctly there is no longer any trace of this being a thing in game. I'm hesitant to even include it in this review cause at this point I feel like I'm totally misremembering this part from the demo from earlier this year.There's so many possible key bindings just missing. Its like PC gaming was an afterthought on a game, that as far as I can tell, has only released on PC. You cannot use number keys to select tools. You must use a radial menu, select the tool slot, then tap E till you get the tool you need. Additionally there's no separate equipment slots for ranged and melee weapons, only active tool/weapon. This means as you loot new weapons and try to quickly switch to you legendary runeblade, but looted a rusted copper sword earlier, you'll suddenly be left wondering why you're hitting for no damage. This is because the game almost inexplicably DEFAULTS to the worst weapon in your inventory.Finally:The game has good bones. It could turn into something really great, but while I'm not the biggest fan of the early access system this game should either not have been put up for sale yet or been enrolled in the early access program. To call this a 1.0 is a bit far fetched for me and that's coming from someone that really likes the art style and general design idea for the game.Definitely hold off on purchasing for now in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's gutting for me to write a negative review, I was so excited for Mirthwood!Unfortunately, the more I played, the more I realized it should've been an Early Access release, and had  another year in development. None of the content currently available feels fully fleshed out or polished.It has been UNBELIEVABLY buggy for me. Not talking about little things either, no, quests are broken, storage was broken, animals are broken, placement is broken. There's no point in investing in Livestock. Animals refuse to eat the food. I couldn't get them to eat Hay or Animal Food, and now they refuse to produce anything because they're starving.Inventory is abysmal. It doesn't matter how many free slots you have, you can only carry a certain # of items per category. Say you start off with 4 max Materials you can carry at once: Wood, Stone, Copper Ore, Leather. You can't carry any more than that at a time without upgrading using 8 Feathers (which you find scattered around the map). Although that might not seem like an issue, it becomes frustrating very quickly, as this is a game where every resource counts, as the grind to get them AND the storage to keep them is ridiculous. I ended up dropping my items in (organized) piles spread throughout my farm. Thankfully, dropped items don't despawn.Morality makes no sense. You lose Morality when you pick 'Evil' choices or Steal. If you open a chest that doesn't belong to you, you lose 5 points of Morality. Even if you don't actually steal the item, opening it and looking is -5. Often times you'll accidentally steal something nearby when trying to talk to a NPC. -5. I just finished a quest where I freed a woman FROM A CAGE, and it gave me +5, the same # of Morality points when I accidently open a crate with an Onion in it. I couldn't tell you what the point of this is, besides the exact same remark from NPCs about how I'm untrustworthy. Same goes for affiliation equipment, some clothes are Criminal, Nobility, Peasant, etc. But I don't think this serves a purpose either.NPCs themselves are bland, boring, sooo lifeless. I've come across perhaps two, maybe three NPCs I was interested in befriending, but of course they can't be, for whatever reason, they're not generic like the rest of the citizens. It's a guessing game when I speak to them. Cards are cool, course, reminds me of Fable or The Sims, but none of it means anything. Even if you decide on a specific NPC to befriend, it takes FOREVER to level them up, and the process of doing that is the exact same thing over and over. It's such a bummer, I don't bother with it at all now.I don't understand the Skill Cards at all, I only have a single active slot unlocked, despite having unlocked 15+ cards to use. Thought maybe it was like Fo76 where you can easily switch them in and out, but no, it locks that card in place when activated, forcing you to wait 1 in-game day before you're able to change it. I can only ever view all of my cards when I browse through the separate Skill categories, as the All section only shows 12, when I know I have more than that to choose from. Skills are forgettable, nothing special there, just small percentage boosts towards more damage, accuracy, chance, gain rate, etc. It's so miniscule, +2.5%, +5%, that's it. No thought put into making any of this interesting, or even fun, which is so sad, because the combat desperately needs it. Combat is terrible. It's the absolute bare minimum. You have Sword and Bow. You can use both, but you're better off picking one and sticking to it, so it levels up faster. Engaging in fights isn't fun, it's frustrating and tedious. Movement and controls are clunky, but not in the  way, in the  way. Attacking with sword is moving left and right. Sometimes when swinging, you'll see it hit, but it doesn't do damage. There's a blocking mechanic, but blocking when the indicator pops up, has input lag resulting in an unsuccessful block. Same with dodge. Switching to Bow was my best decision, as you can use it while on horseback, and it's been a lot easier to tolerate. Sadly, there's still a multitude of issues. Creatures will often phase through objects and unless on horseback, you can't distance yourself enough to break their chase. Unlike NPCs, enemies stand still, not moving around or interacting in any way, . Why is a pack of wolves chasing me alongside a lone bandit? It doesn't feel believable. You'll do mostly creature killing, but at least their loot is reasonable. A pelt, meat, if you kill a bear, you might loot a fish, makes sense, right? So how come when I kill a man fully decked out, head to toe, in steel armor, all he drops for me is a Red Apple?Decorating.. not at all worth the frustration. What you're able to build/buy for your home is like 10% of what's used everywhere else.  Homes in villages are decorated beautifully, so it hurts to know your home couldn't never look even a fraction like that. Items I've placed often go invisible or disappear completely. Once you repair the stairs, you get three rooms on a second floor to decorate, except the furniture you place up there will still be visible when you're outside of the house. Also I placed three chests upstairs, and they disappeared completely. So.. maybe keep your chests on the first floor. For now. Number of resources required to change the floor and walls is INSANE. No matter the room, the options don't change, so why do I have to spend the same # of resources for each room? It honestly feels like most of my time was spent grinding for Wood. You can place dirt or stone paths, just make sure they're where you want because once you use the Eraser, you can't place anything else. Paths don't prevent resource respawn, so grass, stones, trunks, logs still spawn on them. Actually, these natural resources spawn everywhere, even in pre-built structures, like the Mill or Chicken Coop.Night time is unbelievably dark. I can't see anything. A lantern or even a brightness slider would help with this.Quests are a MESS. Doing things out of the game's (very lacking) direction, breaks things so easily. I'm thankful I thought to keep backups of my saves, as there's no way to restore an old one, so if something is broken, you're SOL until it's patched.Story is so uninteresting, even quest givers are boring, their lines completely flat. VA of the narrator is excellent, but that's the best you're going to get.Mirthwood is NOWHERE NEAR a Sandbox, an ImmSimm, or even a Farming Sim. Farming is one of its many unpolished features, but game's completable without ever touching it. I believe it would've been a lot more enjoyable if it didn't try to be a jack of all trades, instead sticking to what makes it great, exploration. I enjoyed traveling around, discovering notes, scenes of environmental storytelling. Soundtrack is magnificent, creature sounds terrifying, and the aesthetic gorgeous, but sadly, that's not enough for me to recommend at its current state.

I'm very disappointed to see a publisher release a game in this state.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm worried no one will read this review cuz it'll be lost amongst all the others but here I go anyway.So the game gets a thumbs up, of course. The game is actually pretty good. Now it's not how farming sim games or life sim games typically work, here it's a lot more in-depth I think. Overall the whole thing is really well thought out. There are relationships, dialogue and conversation mechanics. A morality system. The classic survival things like health,hunger and stamina meters. You can upgrade and clean up your farmstead and even build new buildings on it like barns and chicken coops. You can explore this massive map which graces you with fast travel and at it's heart it's a farming sim game but in medieval times.There's a LOT about this game that I really like. I like the realism, I like the in-depth nature of it's gameplay components and other functions. And I like the massive open world like feeling you have while playing it along with all the stuff you can find and explore.What I DON'T like is the combat. It's really janky and kinda awkward. The actual using of tools is also a bit awkward and clumsy. Why after your person finishes chopping a tree do they have to wait 3 seconds to continue chopping to get rid of the stump? I find this confusing and unnecessary. Also the game has a bit of a questionable stability. It froze on me once, dropped frames on me several times, and I also experienced frequent sound glitches/bugs. So it's not perfect, it needs a bit of ironing out. However if you were looking for the next farming sim or life sim game, this is a pretty good one and I highly recommend, which is why I'm giving it a thumbs up.However, if you'd like a more in-depth look at the game then I encourage you to check out the review on my YouTube Channel (link below).Otherwise, thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

But i just cant as is.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a very pretty and cozy game. Music and ambient sound is great and immersive (other than a single sfx in the forest that I find weird haha).The combat is very simple and easily 'exploited' playing vertically, since so far only you can attack in that direction with the bow.Farming and house decor worked just fine. Didn't spend too much time other than fixing the house, putting some furniture and planting 3 or 4 type of crops. All worked well.There was a weird bug that happened on a nearly fixed time basis, where it looked like some process is called on a update or tick function that kinda froze the world for a few ms. Happened a lot yesterday, not so much today. Might have been fixed? Not sure.edit: UI bug that was introduced in a patch is already fixed!edit: lots of bugs have been fixed in the last week. so far they are doing a good job and it seems to have a good future if we keep getting this treatmentedit: relationship reset was fixed as well, but not with the loss of current progressWith my main problems being fixed I can now safely recommend the game as being a fun experience.But I'd still warn you that the game feels like some features aren't complete yet (and there are roadmaps for them). So, in the end, it feels more like an EA and I'd prefer it was tagged like that. But for my own experience it already delivers a decent product that is worth that price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit* Just avoid this game, it is just plain DUMB.- Story is meh- Quests are wack a mole on the map- Worst combat ever implemented in a game- Farming is lame- Conversations are pointless- Progression is a pain from copper to iron - total slog- Map is small, can get across the entire map in under 10 minutes. you just run back and forth constantly.I wanted to like it due to the medieval theme and the art style.. Art is top notch, but everything else implemented was an after thought.Cool idea, poor!!! implementation! all the mechanics and quests are sub par. Just pass on this..........................................................................................................................................Unique game for sure! I will change my review to positive if some issues are addressed.* Combat is super clunky, Splattercat addressed this in the demo when it first released and hardly any effort was placed in it. For a game that has a lot of combat, I don't see why it was ignored.- Add a target lock, reason is that the way you lunge with your swings is pretty bad and the enemies hit box is at their feet. If you're attacking from top to bottom, good chance you will miss.* Controller Support - this is a poor implementation that's currently in game. Text menu's should show what button is for next and for skip. During conversations, the emote options should have a underline on the highlighted option. I state this because the highlight of the card is barely enhanced over the unselected options.* Combat - Reduce the enemy dodge count, really annoying to have the enemy just constantly jumping back every time you swing.Overall, I'm really impressed with the graphics and novelty of the game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to stick to the things that are most prevalent:GORGEOUS - This game is one of the prettiest I've played, period. The art direction and the effort put into the art are very impressiveWell tuned Systems - I've only scratched the surface of most of them. This is not your Stardew Valley though. The way this game demands you satisfy hunger and engage with it's world does not leave you feeling cozy. It has you feeling satisfied that you are doing well without feeling like you can just float through every day.Average Combat - Not great, not terrible, but it's so prevelant that it doesn't feel the average that it is doesn't feel great.Immaculate Vibes - It's going for mystery and wonder without being so magical that you are bored of the mundane. And it hits that mark very well.Engaged Developer: The team is actively listening to feedback and making changes to make the experience good for everyone. Which is good because...**THIS HAS BEEN FIXED, WITHIN A DAY OR TWO OF THE REVIEW** Poorly Optimized: The developer is working on this, but the long and short is that the game doesn't run very good. That sucks. They have different ways to mitigate it on their wiki and Discord. Still, it's got performance problems and you can tell. **THIS HAS BEEN FIXED, WITHIN A DAY OR TWO OF THE REVIEW**Overall: Updated to 8/10 from 7/10, as they resolved the performance issues! - This is a good game. It's worth the money they're charging, and it's going to be worth it and more by the time they polish out the performance bugs. In the meantime, if it looks like your kind of game, it probably is. This game delivers on the promise it sets out to fulfill.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game.It's style, it's deliberate, relaxed pace and even it's combat system which seems to be something of an acquired taste to some. That said, I have a high tolerance for jankiness and, brother, this game's got some jank.As much as I'm genuinely enjoying this game, I'd be remiss to tell people to pick it up as it is. With some pretty glaring technical issues, inconsistent balancing in game progression and some frankly baffling design choices, this is 100% an early access game by any other name and should have had months of EA development and ironing out of these issues. We can argue the morality of releasing an unfinished product as a completed work, but I feel I've seen far more egregious examples from much larger and established developers, but it's not to be ignored entirely.That being the case, why the positive review? I think it has the foundation of a really great game and I can't say the framework built here is "bad" per se. The core gameplay is great and none of the present problems with the game wouldn't be worked out with a little more time.If you can tolerate a bumpy ride while the developers figure some of these things out, you could do a lot worse than what's already here.For everyone else, I say wishlist it and keep an eye on it; with a little time and work, this could potentially be a classic in the making.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a couple of hours into the game, did a couple of quests, farmed a little, went hunting, forged new weapons and restored the house to it's former glory.That's basicaly it. While the graphics are quite nice and everything works fine (well a few crashes here and there), gameplay wise there's not much there. It's just bland, tedious, boring even. I did stuff for people and pretty mucgh found every settlement there is. And now...now what? Sure I need to "find some stuff" but that's just another dungeon crawl, kiting things with my trusty bow, not getting hit even once. So, does it get better over time or is that it? Where is the promissed freedom? What am I supposed to do with all that money I've got after I bought everything I actually want? What's with the NPCs? Do they ever do something important? Don't get me wrong, I like the atmosphere in this game and I like how it looks (really reminds me of "Wildermyth", one of my personal favorites) but besides the grind for resources, there doesn't seem to be anything to it. The combat is bad. Like REALLY bad. The crafting is...well it exists. The interactions with NPCs are not worth mentioning and the story is there but it hides in the bushes. Gameplay wise, the story is pretty much optional.Problem is that with an optional story and no really good alternative game mechanics, this whole thing feels rather bland. Boring. I can't have any meaningfull interaction with the NPCs, the fights are grindy and not worth it, the farming feels like a sidequest and gathering is just a grind. As of now I have the feeling that the game doesn't know what it actually wants to be or where it wants to go. This is (officially) not an early access game but it clearly feels like one and I have no idea wether this is going somewhere or not.As of now I would give this at least six months to either be refined into something that is actually good or become another DOA title.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is okay, adventuring around is alright, the art style is pretty good. [Map is decorated with a bunch of chests, containers, barrels, shields and swords that you cannot use, open, interact with, anything] Which is not fun....Combat is okay, nothing special, zero dopamine hits. You can swing, hard swing, parry/block and roll. The enemy almost always gets out of your range and makes it difficult to hit them. No special effects, no dmg or crit notifiers, just basic sword swinging at each other at a slow pace. No different animations for a miss or crit. Game needs Special effects when you crit, or something. Different animation needed for when you miss an opponent.  It is early access, I would wait to buy it though. I would say buy the game after Quality Of Life is implemented, some optimization needed to reduce random lag when moving around on map also.I am on the fence about recommending the game or not. It uses a morality system that makes zero sense and loot system is really really poor.  Okay cool, if you want to be a bad guy and have low morality that's fine, although Stealing an apple from a chest and automatically losing morality is a poor use of a morality system though.  [Very few chests and containers can actually be opened. 3/4 of containers in town that can be opened, you HAVE to steal from them if you want the small amount of items within. Literally losing morality for stealing an apple or a bad quality hat in a chest. The chests only contain 1 or 2 items at max and you lose morality with NO ONE AROUND.  The loot system is almost non existent.There is no other choice. You either loot it and instantly lose morality even if NO ONE IS AROUND AND NO ONE SEE's or hears you. You instantly lose the morality just because....Maybe if I was stealing an expensive sword AND someone saw me okay....but no one is around and you automatically lose morality. No 50% chance to lose morality or a sneaking/stealth skill to prevent people from hearing or seeing you loot the crate with 1 ITEM in it.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  [which is quite disappointing BTW, 1 item in a chest?! That I am now losing morality over automatically and the item happens to be an apple, but wait I can't even loot the apple because I have 3 food items already and can't have more than 3 food items or whatever small limit is is].  I lost 10 morality for killing a DUDE, but I lose 5 morality for stealing an apple from a CHEST where there is NO witness.  SMH. These are probably the worst crates I have opened in any game tbh.Bruh, quality of life massively needed. It's not like this is an MMORPG and crates or enemies dropping armor and weapons would ruin the economy. This is literally a single player game with a terrible loot system. If you want to play as good, then you lose out and can't loot the chest. There is no stealth system, or lockpick system to even have a chance to loot it without losing morality, you just auto lose morality. Game needs optimization as it will lag in certain spots. It is around once a minute, but enough to notice when you are traveling around every couple minutes. You can only hold a couple food items before it says you can't hold more food items. I have 3 apples and 3 honey and I can't make 3 honey apples because there is no more room for food apparently......BRUH, weird poor choice.I just killed a rabbit with a bow. I can pick up it's hide, but I can't pick up the rabbit meat....................just get rid of this dumb can't hold more food. Loot system is pure garbage. I killed an assassin in a heated battle. The assassin is in full plate armor and has 2 daggers and ONLY drops an apple..... what is this garbage literally. FULL Chests only contain 1 or 2 items and most of the time it is always one or two things of food. I did find one ranger hat, the rest has been all food though. Enemies have only dropped food.  Have a chance to drop a lockpick? You could then use the lockpick on chests you have to steal from and would have a chance not to get caught, instead of AUTOMATICALLY getting caught with morality when stealing from any chest, when no one is near you. For the love of god have a chance to drop armor/ weps/ enchants, scrolls to enchant, shards to buy special items or make special items....Some not useless would be great. If you have a couple food items, you can't even loot said apple that I worked so hard for....loot system needs to change now. A chance to drop more than 1 item.   Have some special effects that make different melee weapons attack differently.  Have variations in and random enchants and random dmg types on weapons. Some variety?For decoration they put chests, barrels and crates all over, there are swords and shields on the ground and they are just props taking up space on the screen, you can't pick any up. You can pick up like 2 swords in half the map, out of hundreds. You can loot 1/50 chests or containers present, which is not fun and makes it confusing to what LITTLE you can actually interact and open, which isn't much.

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to hold off reviewing until at least 1 hr into game. I’ve tried this game on steam deck & Asus Rog Ally. The key issues preventing any resemblance of an enjoyable experience are:1) The game is barely 30FPS on steam deck with graphics settings having nil impact. The gamepad controls isn’t detected at main menu requires manual tap on screen or mapping mouse to trackpad 2) the steam deck also feels more laggy once in-game akin to streaming gamepass on it mobile on bad 4G network.3) menu settings changed during game didn’t seem to sync over after exit to menu instead resetting to default. The menu options are very basic so it’s not biggest issue4) On rog ally performance is also an issue  barely achieving 30~40FPS @ 30W turbo mode at 1080p! With AFMF I get 60~70FPS with 70+ ms latency added from AFMF but without AFMF I’d have to run this game same as steam deck capped at 30FPS… That sounds pretty ridiculous right? Clearly there’s some major optimisation issues… But yes technically I can run this game on Ally @ 720p and get near 60FPS not stable… Black Myth Wukong magnitudes more ambitious than this game can run on Ally @ 1080P medium settings 40FPS on same TDP with no FG…Also gamepad controls are bad. Starting with the mouse cursor stuck on screen. Which you can only move to edge of screen but ever so slightly see it protruding from the edge. To move the cursor to the edge you have to manually toggle mouse only on your ally ACSE or use your finger on screen. This is clear indication of the devs not optimising properly for controller but claiming ‘full controller support’ on store page.5) The controller mapping is not functional. For example the sprint button can only be enabled by holding down rather then option for toggle… But it’s not clear if it character is sprinting or normal pace due to bad animation differences. The sprinting also doesn’t trigger reliably more like hit and miss. I swear it almost looks like your character starts sprinting then immediately resumes normal pace. I’ve tried holding down sprint and toggle neither offers reliable feedback…There’s distinct sense of bare minimum thought or bad effort poorly tested put into controller support. But the worst part/non functional part is sprinting seems to only trigger sometimes (not to do with stamina), and doesn’t seem to trigger at all for certain directions when running downwards towards bottom of screen for some reason. So imagine in game your character can run left, right, up but not down using controller???Also encountered a bug where if you map sprint to RT button, it also triggers attack (x button) everytime you press RT to sprint. Only workaround is using RT button as block so block takes precedence over attack but a weird glitch regardless.6) navigate to skills menu etc and it’s barely readable even holding the rog ally in front of my face at 1080p native. You can appreciate how much worse on steam deck…7) Touched on before but it’s hard to actually differentiate often if your character is running or just normal pace.8) on Rog Ally returning to game main menu doesn’t detect controller input unless you move the left stick left right multiple times which is janky af….9) The game can’t save via menu so the first 50+ mins I spent with limited exploration and trying to overcome game issues/bugs means when I exit to main menu everything resets progress wise to zero.

_childDocuments_.review: Today, you venture into the swamp.  Your goal is to grab iron, to forge to steel, to make a bow that can kill the monsters living there in a reasonable timeframe, to stay longer in the swamps and grab more iron.  You walk through sunny woods dotted with Witcheresque Slavic depression p*rn, such as two duelists who vied for a lady's affection and apparently killed each other at the same time, and a family lost to suicide and tuberculosis.  You run into your closest neighbor, a generic thief who frequently respawns and attempts to murder you.  You kite him for 2 minutes with your bow and take a health potion from his corpse.  You reach your first lode of iron.  A nearby rat charges you.  You nock and fire arrows at a rate that would make Legolas Greenleaf nod appreciatively.  The rat desyncs to the left.  The rat desyncs to the right.  Half of them miss.  The rat is undeterred and closes the distance.  It has decided one of you must die today.  You kite backwards and continue to turn the rat into a pincushion.  You reach the town.  Residents draw wooden swords and surround the rat, beating it to death.  Given that they're medieval libertarians, this is a commendable display of unity.  It drops no loot.  You turn to the noblewoman next to you and try to crack a joke.  For no clear reason, she is disgusted and insults your honor.  Dusk has fallen.  You begin the trek back to your cottage.  Tomorrow, you venture into the swamp...In all seriousness, this game has some potential but it's just not a finished product worth asking price.  The combat system is underbaked as described (melee is similarly tedious but less effective) and any semblance of a story is background overshadowed by the equipment upgrade process, which is both important and a slog.  Inventory space is constrained and the skill tree really isn't flashy.  The character system isn't bad, but it has no real dialogue outside of quests and isn't a draw.  Relationship gains are glacially slow.  Secondary quests are mostly fetch quests with a little kill mixed in.  Part of the problem might be the sandbox nature of the game, but it needs more depth both mechanically and thematically to be worthwhile.  I also was beset by performance issues.On the upside, the artstyle is cute and I really did feel like a peasant hovering above starving initially.  The devs aren't done implementing features into this game.  If fancy home decor was more expensive, healthbars more sane and tools cheaper then the game might progress more smoothly.  Unfortunately, there still needs to be at least a more satisfying gameplay loop overall.  I'll likely give it another chance after more work is done.Overall conclusion: soft no

_childDocuments_.review: I do like the game, and I will continue to play it! However, it still FEELS like an early access title, despite not being tagged as such. I'd have no problem recommending Mirthwood if it were labeled EA, but I can't in good conscience say it's a solid full release. Those who avoid EA titles attempting to avoid the issues below may feel especially disappointed.The social mechanics are broken, or so unbalanced that they might as well be. Festivals, marriage, and babies are planned for later updates. Some players are/were encountering critical bugs and performance issues, although patches are being released. The in-game economy and resources could use some fine tuning.All of these issues are understandable and easy to forgive for EA, but for those hoping for a "finished" game implied by a full 1.0 release, I'd recommend wishlisting and waiting for now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential and with a bit of tuning it would be really good, but for now I cannot recommend it... which is a shame, but I'll list some of my issues in the hour I plaid it:>Combat is clunky, not terribly so, but definitely feel like it can be exploited>Crafting and trade menus are tiny, as in I cannot see what it says unless I click on it and bring up individual item, coupled with a text colour which seems to blend in with the background means I am constantly shoving my face 1 inch away from the screen to read>Enemies follow you home, which is not something I hate actually, why should my home be safe? However, they do not return to their start points, which means I shook a monster off my tail, only to have it stand on the main road and catch me again as I'm walking home.>NPCs could really use some kind of portrait system which a few variations (neutral, happy, sad, angry, etc.) to make them really pop and feel alive, rather than just the in-game faces which while nice to look at, does not really attach myself to them.Again, I think this game has real potential and I want it to succeed, but until its been fine-tuned and less clunky I don't think I can recommend it... _childDocuments_.review: There are times when you come across a game and you know immediately that is going to be special.For me it's Mirthwood.I'd honestly been struggling finding a game lately, it all just seems to be the same; grind a tier, move up, rinse and repeat.Sometimes the true joy in a game is the stuff that doesn't always register as a "win" for you as the PC and can be as simple as playing, enjoying the rain beat down on your IG house while you cook yourself food and putter around fixing decorations.Mirthwood gives me a world that is living, a place to call my own and the chance to mark my place in the world.Can't ask for much more tbhThe graphics are simple but stylish, the music is great, the sound effects are perfect.Combat isn't crazy detailed but if you're expecting Souls-iike vs Legend of Zelda you know you're already setting yourself up for disappointment.I will say this though, in comparisons for combat in open world survival games this is better than a lot that are out there.I see this as the time of game where you can either get into the minutiae or blaze past it and have a good time either way.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not fun. It takes forever to really get any amount of money.           Many crafting recipes also end in a net loss, or only marginal gain.The limited seed store inventory means you can only grow a very limited number of crops at once.There does not seem to be any interface to track animals, nor is there one to track acquaintances.Assigning an animal to a shelter can only be done if you can find the animal and open its detail screen on the bottom of the UI.The game gravely stutters every time it loads an adjoining area.The bonuses for leveling up a skill are pitiful.          2.5% bonus melee damage on a 7 damage weapon adds 0 damage.The perks you can assign are uninformative, telling you nothing specific about what they do.Animals (chickens for certain) get stuck to the bottom UI and their Feed command gets stuck as well.There does not seem to be a point to socializing. NPCs have no dialogue and just hang around a few places in town all the time, regardless of time of day.          Quest giving NPCs have dialog, but only in reference to their quest.           A painter has dialog about the area.Harvesting large numbers of crops is a chore, featuring a relatively long wait between animations and mashing the interact button (holding to interact with multiple crops doesn't work in my experience).Melee combat is annoying, you only attack to the left or right, but enemies can be anywhere in a 360 degree angle around you. Granted, they also, can only attack to the left or right.Ranged combat is lame, you can attack in 360 degrees and kite enemies, but enemies tend to be spongy and encounters become tedious.Save your money for now, wait and see if it gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game.  The artwork is very good, the overall art style is interesting, it's immediately clear that talented people put a lot of work into this.  But the game immediately hits me with a few big issues within just the first hour.  I've booted it up several times now and I keep running into issues that remove any desire I have to play:1) The UI/UX is pretty bad.  Talking to people sucks, conversation trees involve asking about a topic and then going back to the main topic where you have to read the previous thing they said again. Yes you can press the continue button to skip but this is also how you move to the next topic, and so it's quite possible to accidentally skip something.  There also doesn't seem to be a keyboard shortcut to skip though dialogue.The menu and options are extremely barebones and not all keys can be rebound.  There are numerous other small complaints I have, but they can be summed up as just most of the UI feeling extremely clunky.  Some keys are used for certain tasks regardless of rebinding which means I don't feel I can rebind ANY - when I first played IIRC I rebound something to an unused key (F i think?) and it turned out that it was used for mocking people (and this use can't be rebound) so I had to rebind it again (or risk constantly losing reputation with townsfolk on accident)Based on the many social interaction options that were immediately available in the first town (after the intro sequence) it seems like social interaction is intended to be a core part of the game, but I find myself actively opposed to engaging with it given how clunky it all is.1b) Less important, but during character creation there are several choices where it is unclear whether they have any gameplay impact, and the ones where there is a stated gameplay impact it is unclear what that specific impact amounts to.  This can be fine, but these also don't show up in any of the menus as far as I can tell, so it's unclear if this is all just flavortext.  It's possible these are listed somewhere but if so, then file this under "unintuitive UI"2) Combat is extremely unpolished, slow, plodding, clunky, and yet also uninteresting.  Rolling is always forward, and backsteps are always backward, but this (and attacks) are based on the direction you face which changes only when moving (not with the mouse).  Animations (attacks, rolls, backsteps)  can't be canceled and have comparably long windups and cooldowns.  This results in a methodical and slow combat style where e.g. you can't backstep while blocking, and can't easily switch between attacking and dodging.  There does seem to be some input buffering but it's... not great?  I don't know how to articulate it unlike some of my other complaints, but I definitely feel like attacking after backstepping, or backstepping after attacking doesn't feel great.  Changing direction is extra annoying because it doesn't work while in animations.  If you start attacking right, then hold left and keep attacking, you will keep attacking right over and over even though you are holding left.  You have to stop attacking (or dodging or whatever) wait until the animation finishes, then press left, then you can start attacking again.  This all creates a very slow, methodical combat style - which can be done well - but the optimal strategy, at least so far, nonetheless seems to be to mostly spam attacks with the occasional block or dodge.  A lot of enemies so far seem to just rush me (though the tutorial enemies felt more methodical, so perhaps there's more of that later).  I also think it just isn't done well here.  I like souls games (and even they allow animation canceling) and I like mount & blade.  This doesn't feel calculated, it just feels bad.All of this feel worse because:3) YOU CAN ONLY ATTACK LEFT AND RIGHT.  I'm putting this as a separate point because it's a huge problem.  Enemies are not limited by this (or at least they're better at switching direction) and one of the early combat encounters (after the intro and a thief right by the initial town that felt pretty strong for the area) takes place against several enemies in a vertical hallway.  Yes, you can kite them back to a horizontal hallway, and yes attacks can damage enemies diagonally below or above you, but it just feels really unpleasant and unintuitive.  Why can't I attack downwards?  I don't expect an extra set of animations, it's fine if my character is looking left/right but the attack hitbox is up/down... which is what the enemies do.This is, of course, followed by an encounter with a much stronger enemy... in a vertical hallway facing upward.  (technically the enemy is to the side in room at the end, but unless you play very aggressively and are okay taking hits from an enemy that can kill you very quickly, you'll need to back up into the hallway - or if you want to try rolling around it, which is unpleasant giving how clunky changing direction can be)To be clear, attack hitboxes can hit enemies sort of below/above you, but if you attack left and the enemy is slightly right of down it won't hit.  This is exacerbated by how hard it is to switch directions.4) Just as a separate point, pausing is inconsistent.  I don't even know how this happens but pausing while enemies are in certain animations just... doesn't pause.  I'm not 100% sure if the game just fails to pause or if just that enemy stays unpaused, but it's a pretty big bug to have on release after multiple patches (this bug is present as of V1.0.24f on Nov 17th).6) the intro is on the long side and, as far as I can tell, adds nothing to the game.  Mirthwood feels like a game where they really want you to care about the plot instead of just setting you free in the world.  There's an intro where you're introduced to your family before immediately leaving.  This includes a combat tutorial and a morality choice, but honestly the entire thing could be replaced with a few sentences in a text box.  This is followed by a horse ride and the title drop which is... fine.  I like the ride through the lands.  I probably wouldn't dislike the intro as much except that:5a) I accidentally hit a key (f4? based on reading some patch notes, it looks like this is an unstuck key?  It's not labeled in game and is, like most things, not rebindable) and got teleported to a void for a bit, then eventually teleported back to the start of a section where I had to run to the boat again.5b) it's very railroaded, then it's followed by a horse ride, then you get to your land which is at this time full of invisible walls and then when you finally are set free (I think) there's a quest to meet someone at a tavern in a town (which - side note- has another, closer, more prominent tavern which is a bit confusing) and then after that there's just enough time to figure out how to collect some wood and stone before you need to sleep.  I assumed this is where the game really sets you free (you can go do whatever but it feels like the story implies you shouldn't) but after sleeping I got a letter telling me to meet someone at a ruin, which is followed by a dungeon with the aforementioned clunky combat.Now I could just wander off, but either:A) The story is very important (hence the lengthy intro) and there could be consequences (can quests be failed? is there a timer?  maybe I get really important items or features that unlock).  If this is true, consider giving the player some time to get settled and play the game.B) The story isn't that important and I can just ignore it.  If this is true then don't waste my time with the intro and all of this immediate exposition.  Drip feed the exposition over time instead of frontloading SO MUCH.Anyway I've hit the character limit but in short: This game seems promising but there are a lot of problems.  I'm not refunding but I don't feel I can recommend it at this time. This feels like an early access release, not a finished game.

_childDocuments_.review: The theme of this review is "which would be fine...if it were in Early Access."From the short notice delay to the present fun but somewhat buggy state of the game, to the shifts and sometime vague elements of the roadmaps, to the features to be added (not meaning DLC here) there at least appears to be a lot to recommend Mirthwood as an Early Access title. At present, there are a lot of bugs and frankly quite a bit of either unimplemented features or features yet to be added. Take socializing. At present you can 'do' social interactions, but they have little to no effect and no consequence. The devs have communicated on discord and reddit that work on this is ongoing but as a feature it isn't really implemented yet. If I look at the two previous roadmaps the devs realeased, things like marriage, funerals, and children shift a bit in the way they are described (e.g. Original Roadmap = marriage and dedicated ceremony, players can have children - they age, players can play as them if their characters die, and abilities pass through DNA for Q1 2025 vs. 2nd Roadmap = Marriage Improvements, children/legacy system for Q1 2025). This is, at best, quite vague. Trade routes are also 'in' the game but do not seem to actually effect prices, resources, or item availability. Features and functionalities which are presently in the game but not implemented or working are something that would be fine,  Mirthwood were in Early Access. But it isn't.There are many things in Mirthwood as it stands that point to clear love and attention as well as thoughtfulness on the devs' part - for example, you can move containers without losing their contents, the skill development system allows for prioritization and customization while still allowing you to switch things up without needing to reclass or fundamentally respec a character, etc. Although these are clearly markers of a thoughtful approach to how the game will include and encourage customization and personalization, at present things like bugs, ingredient requirement-to-resource availability, and a variety of questlines either interrupt/disrupt gameplay or cause a confusing amount of discordant grind. Not just fine tuning, but revamping and bug squashing to a pronounced degree are needed in a number of areas. Which would be fine  Mirthwood was in Early Access.The combat is subjective. Some will love it as it is, others will find it fairly simplistic or frustrating (for keyboard players, shift = sprint and shift = heavy attack) - it needs adjusting both for hit boxes (run away from enemies, arm a bow, and aim for the 'bottom' of any enemy), etc. Which would be fine  Mirthwood was in Early Access.I cannot recommend this game at present because it is an Early Access game that is not in Early Access. I would recommend this game in a heartbeat if it were early access with clarity on its present state and not simply "check our discord" from the devs. At present the game is definitely playable, already visually and audibly distinct in lovely ways, and can be enjoyable - but the things that look to set Mirthwood apart are, at present, not really functional or integrated into the game. That is, other games do what Mirthwood can do right now, but better, and what Mirthwood is planning to do looks wonderful but isn't actually functional right now. Which would be fine  Mirthwood was in Early Access.I'd be thrilled to update and change this to a Recommend once/if the state of the game changes.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m conflicted on how to rate this one. The game’s strengths lie in its hand-drawn art, atmospheric music, and its distinct, open world. Features like crafting, farming, and trading add depth to the simulation aspect, while the Sims-inspired social system introduces a layer of relationship-building.However, Mirthwood struggles to fully deliver on its promises. Bugs are prevalent, ranging from game crashes during fast travel to terrain glitches that have trapped my character, forcing restarts. Combat is unbalanced, with spongy enemies and awkward hit detection, particularly on uneven terrain. The social system, while conceptually strong, lacks depth, reducing NPCs to generic templates with repetitive dialogue rather than unique characters. It’s also hard to build positive relationships, as there is no way of telling how to respond to a NPCs “dialogue.” Progression systems also feel unimpactful, as leveling up offers minimal noticeable benefits. It also seems, at least in my game, that combat (melee and ranged) are not leveling at all. There is also an issue with farm progression, as iron is needed for almost everything and it’s very limited on spawn rate in my game. Where it does occur (the swamp, mostly), enemies spawn and I spend more time fighting creatures than collecting iron. If I wanted to play The Witcher, I’d play The Witcher, which has a better story and gameplay. I just want to collect iron so I can upgrade my farm. While the game shows potential, its current state feels more like an early access build than a polished release. Players looking for a smooth and rewarding experience might find Mirthwood frustrating rather than enjoyable. Until the developers address these shortcomings and improve the game’s overall stability and depth, I cannot recommend Mirthwood in its current form.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I've enjoyed playing this, it feels unfinished. It's very atmospheric and cosy.I see a lot of thumbs up reviews are commonly saying 'it shows promise ' or 'there is a good framework here'. While those statements are true, that's not a finished game is it? If you're releasing a game at full price, it shouldnt 'show promise', it should be delivered in full on the date you've decided to release it on.I feel it's unfinished for a few reasons:- the dialogue resets to the initial phrase after each option is selected- There are very limited clothing and armour options.- Copper is almost irrelevant unless you're selling Copper weapons for money. You can just skip straight to Iron with little effort.- very limited cooking options, to the point where it's hardly worth producing some ingredients - Social interactions and choices dont seem to have any consequences.- Trade routes, also don't seem to have any impact on goods or prices.- Combat feels more like luck than skill- Herbalism feels irrelevant, you can't grow herbs, so you need to go out looking for them, which usually involves combat, but you take more damage as a herbalist?! - Not well optimised for the more simplistic graphical aesthetic.Overall it probably should have been released as early access, as it doesn't feel finished, so the price should come down until its more of a full game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood is DIFFERENT!  If you're TIRED of the same sugary sweet farming and life sims and want a game with dark undertones and a bit of spicy combat but with a warm ambiance and homestead creation, then Mirthwood just might be your cozy jam this winter. Here are my first-impressions after 8 hours of playtest and full release gameplay:LIKES-Medieval Setting & lore/mystery -Choosing Character's origin/social class/background that adds positive and negative Traits-Beautiful Soundtrack & Hand-drawn Art -Mix of Genres (Open-World Survival, Farming/Life Sim, RPG)-Combat & Survival Difficulty Settings-Sandbox style Exploration-"Sims" style NPC Interactions-Crafting a cozy farm & homestead-Looting (and Stealing)-Works on Steam Deck on launch day! (at 60fps, reduced graphics)-Controller Support-Multiplayer & Marriage/Family on the RoadmapCOULD BE IMPROVED-Ability to move Camera & hide HUD for screenshots-Occasional FPS Stutters (running at 120FPS @3440x1440p/120Hz, high settings, 4070Ti Super)-Combat & Tools feel a bit clunky: bow difficult to aim left on controller, fishing much easier on KB/M-Choices of character's traits doesn't feel overly significant (I chose to be an introverted peasant farmer but don't see NPCs reacting to these choices?)TL/DR:For around $20, I'm VERY pleased with the cozy yet dark exploration, survival, farming, homesteading, and social interaction of Mirthwood.  Sure, the game could use a bit of optimization and smoothing of mechanics, but it's a pretty darn good full release, especially for a small developer team. Mirthwood is the perfect cold weather game to curl up with on the couch on these dark fall and winter evenings for an enchanting, suspenseful fantasy adventure that can be as cozy or action-packed as your mood desires.    Disclaimer: I was NOT provided with a free copy of Mirthwood and purchased it with my own funds.  My views are honest and unsponsored.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite ready yet. It seems like it could become something pretty cool, but right now it is clunky to the point that I needed to request a refund. I've added it back to my wishlist and I'll check in sometime down the road to see if it has improved.Example problems:- The mouse scroll wheel moves menus an almost microscopic amount. I unlocked my scroll wheel and spun it as fast as it would go. It still took me about 10 seconds to scroll down past *one single item* in the shop.- Looting items from boxes and enemies requires you to click on a specific portion of the item. There is no indicator to tell you this. The majority of the loot box is entirely unresponsive and you need to click around until you find the spot that lets you actually interact with the item.- Doors will often duplicate themselves when you open them. This will result in a sort of fan of doors swinging open all at the same time.- The very first quest in the game requires you to pick 3 mushrooms and 3 herbs. They are the only 3 mushrooms and herbs in existence and if you click on them in your inventory at all you will automatically eat them.- The second quest in the game tells you to head North to go home. If you're like me, you'll spend 15 minutes heading towards the top of the screen before you finally decide to snoop around to the left of the screen. I guess left is North in this game, because that's where you'll find your house.- Weapons do not need to touch your character to deal damage. Additionally, your weapon hitting an enemy does not necessarily mean that you will damage them.- The morality system is extraordinarily basic, but also somehow entirely counter-intuitive. Early in the game, you will find a man who is about to be executed by soldiers for being a deserter. His crime was that he chased an enemy soldier to prevent them from poisoning the water supply. If you spare his life, you will take a hit to your morality. If you execute him for deserting (even though he was actively engaging the enemy) you will gain a boost to morality.- Crops are seasonal. That much makes sense. Unfortunately, in this game you can't plant peas and carrots in spring. That was strange news to me as someone who grows his own peas and carrots. Both of those can be planted before the frosts end and they will thrive.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so desperate to like this game. The art style is gorgeous, the blend of adventuring and homesteading should theoretically be exactly my kind of game but it's just not there yet. My biggest gripe is the combat system which makes me want to pull my hair out as characters slide past each other almost comically in an attempt to fight one another being stuck in long overdrawn animations facing the wrong direction. The AI seems to have a vendetta against you as on multiple occasions in attempts to avoid the clunky combat I've ended up being chased by wolves, boars, bandits, wraiths, werewolves, and thieves who have inexplicably decided to put aside their differences and hunt me down exclusively. I've even baited them into a town of villagers who all took out their swords to attack the creatures only for the small hoard of monsters I've accrued to continue to chase me ignoring the village militia who are hacking them down. The farming system is lackluster with only a few crop types per season which for me meant no real incentive to delve deeply.Quests tend to be very bland with little to no variety or story behind them. Either "Gather these ingredients" or "go to x location and kill x creature" with little reward.The skill upgrade system gave me no incentive to progress further with laughable stat upgrades like "+2.5% extra melee damage" or "crops grow 2.5% faster" providing no noticeable change in gameplay. The system of dynamic relationships with townsfolk was a massive draw to me however it seems to be nothing more than a long exaggerated grind pressing a limited number of categorised talk options. I don't really know if there's any more depth than random choice or if their mood affects their actions because there isn't a tutorial for the mechanic. Finally performance seems inconsistent across the board with smooth performance once minute to crashes and frame drops the next with seemingly no cause.I know it was delayed once but the whole game feels like it needed more time in the oven. I'll be waiting for future updates but at the moment there's no way I can recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had well over 100 hours in beta testing for this game!  The two developers Brian & Daron (and their assistants and mods) were and still are quite active and responsive in the Discord (I totally recommend you join the awesome vibe there), and have overhauled many parts of the game for launch. It's crazy what they've accomplished in a short amount of time--and there's a ton more to come. They've been transparent about what launch would be like, and the following months/year after.  So anyone who is nitpicking should probably pop in the Discord and read in the news channel! Of course, Mirthwood's vibe isn't for everyone. It's not a complicated combat game, nor is it extreme farming or a massively hugemongous world (yet!). You don't have a messy action bar clogging your screen.  What it is--a beautifully hand-drawn creation, very fairy-medieval style, with attention to very specific lovely details--the world really is alive!  The soundtracks and environmental sound effects are fantastic and relaxing, too.  The conversations you'll have with NPCs are entertaining and I'm super excited about how that mechanic will evolve.While it is inspired by other sim life games, I feel it stands on its own with its unique style.  You have your own space to be creative (or not!), you can be a wandering adventurer (or not), you can have relationships with NPCs (or not...tho marriage/family mechanics are coming next year!), you can be a humble farmer, a Royal thief, a Noble socialite, or a variety of other characters...or...just play organically and see what your life in Mirthwood becomes. What you choose as your race, class and profession all affect how you experience the world. You can play in the open world/sandbox, follow the main quest, or both. It's up to you.  There are TONS of little mini-lore-stories all over the world, too. Some funny...some sad...and some that I hope pop up again later as more quests so we can immerse ourselves even more in the Freelands.Yes, as others have mentioned, there are mechanics that need more adjusting and polishing (again, see the Discord!) and the devs have shared their plans; but they are also looking for the gamers' input. So before you leave a review, be aware of where it is currently in development and play plenty of hours yourself as well as doing your research in the Discord for help if needed--jump in there and give your feedback.  If a game in this state is not for you, it's simple--don't buy it. lol.I enjoy supporting the small indie developers and love the personal interaction.  It's fun to be a part of an evolving game which has also been a labor of love and passion.  Yes, there are things that I personally think could make the game better, but don't we feel like that with all games?  With Mirthwood, we have the opportunity to give that feedback directly and have it be heard almost immediately. I have absolutely enjoyed every minute of playing, even during the bug-busting beta. There have been no deal breakers with me with this game! I love it!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do but there is a lot that needs to be fixed before I can recommend it for the price tag. 1: the game is not optimized at all. Combat is clunky and often you get hit when the enemy is nowhere near you. Also, certain areas of the game stutter hard. I am playing on a 4090, this little game should not stutter at all, ever. 2: the grind is cranked up to 20 out of 10. it's so far turned up that you can tell this is an artificial extension of game play by the devs to make this a 20-30 hour game when there is only 5 hours of content. The resources do not regenerate fast enough and when they do, it's random, which forcing you to run around an entire area hoping to find more than one node of whatever resource you're looking for. Example, you need 10 Iron bars to upgrade ONE SINGLE TOOL. But on a good day (in game) you will only get 14 iron ore. it takes 5 iron ores to make 1 iron bar. Then if you want to upgrade a tool to steel, it takes 2 iron bars and five charcoal to make a single steel bar. I literally grinded iron ore for two irl hours and only got 47. 3: the NPCs in this game suck. Flat out. They have zero personality to them. and the relationship building system in the game is atrocious and had to be thought up by a four year old because my six year old could have done a better job. 4: every single quest in this game sucks. There is not one quest, to include the main quest line, that grabs your attention and makes you WANT to do that quest. Oh, and you can't read most quests before you accept them. Walk up to a yellow exclamation point and the only option is "accept". This game has the bones of what could be a good, solid, game. But right now, its far off the mark and the devs need to put in some work to get this game in a good state if they ever hope to continue making games. Right now, do not buy this game, save your money and go elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Beautiful soundtrack. This was one of THE most anticipated games for me in recent times. The trailer had me hooked. I loved the art style, from the hand drawn and painted look to the gorgeously detailed and crafted environments. It seemed to be grounded in an old medieval time but had elements of pagan magicks and creepy mystery. I was hooked. And now that the game is finally out, I would say it was worth the wait.It's such a wonderful blend of cozy farm sim mixed with rpg adventure. I'm spending my time hopping from gathering materials, to building up my homestead, to vanquishing bandits and monsters alike. There's a perk card system that clearly has taken inspiration from Fallout 76 (another one of my favorite games), equip-able weapons and armor, and skill sets that get more boosts the more you use them. I'm having such a good time exploring the island, uncovering little storylets hidden throughout, and wondering where the game's going to take me next.Earlier I mentioned the soundtrack. This game's sound design is amazing. The musical pieces are beautiful, comprised of haunting and sweet harp pieces and gentle soft vocals. This paired alongside the wind, rain, and other nature sounds do such a good job at helping immerse you in this land and make you feel right at home.The combat is a little clunky, but once you get used to the 2Dish / 3Dish control, it's not too bad. Not overly complicated, but still require some basic finesse to make it so you don't get clobbered. I really don't mind it because, as a whole, it mixes just fine with everything else here. There's some socializing that can be done with the various villagers, although I haven't messed around with it too much. I typically play into a full hermetic lifestyle in these games so all the NPC's will know of me is the back of my cloak as I'm running past em to my next adventure. But! That being said, it's got fun 'Sims-esque' conversation prompts. You don't specifically say much, but I like to use my imagination to fill in the specifics of what they're saying to each other. You can be nice, you can be mean, you can be silly, you can flirt. Roleplaying is key in this game.Mirthwood is a real gem. It's made by (I believe) a team of just 2 people (I hope I'm correct in saying that). They really put their heart into this game and it shows. From me to the development team, thank you so much for creating this delightfully intriguing game.  I only have a handful of hours in the game already, but I hope to have many more.Support this game. Give it a try. Don't go in with any expectations and I think you'll be pleasantly surprised and rewarded.
