_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood is a charming but otherwise unsatisfying game.The art style is appealing and has the look of old-era fairytale storybooks. Other than that, the game plays pretty much like any game in this genre. You are given a giant plot of land and told to go have fun. If you've played Stardew Valley or anything like it, you already know exactly the kind of gameplay loop you're in for. Like other farming/adventure RPGs, you'll spend your time between improving your home, clearing land, gathering resources, building crafting tables and exploring the world around you to complete quests. The first days of play are enjoyable enough because it's still new. As time goes on, the grind and repetition quickly drain the life out of the game.You'll be given a set of copper tools early on. In order to upgrade these, you'll have to build a furnace to smelt metal, buy an upgrade kit from town and then have enough metal bars. The issue, is that iron, one of the most crucially vital resources in the entire game, is somehow incredibly difficult to find consistently. This will effectively create a bottleneck in your ability to progress, because a huge number of things you will need require large amounts of iron. It takes 5 iron ore to make a bar, and each iron node can sometimes drop as little as 2 iron. When you have 5 primary tools, it takes a lot of iron. For reference, in 33 hours of play I still had a copper hoe, scythe and watering can because iron is just that rare and there are more important things to craft.Next, is the combat which is just awful in every way. It's not engaging, it's not fun and it's incredibly tedious. You don't learn new abilities or attacks, and every single enemy constantly spams their disengage. These things would be minor annoyances if not for the fact that every enemy has at least 2x the HP that they should have. Rats, the most ubiquitous RPG enemy of all time have something like 30 HP. In the early game, when you're probably using a rusty sword, you'll be dealing between 5 and 7 damage per hit. In Mirthwood, beating a rat to death with a slab of rusty metal takes way too long. Somehow, even worse than that is that rats do insane damage for what they are. Prior to giving up, I was wearing brigandine and an Elven great helm and they would still bite me for 5 HP. How can I possibly be well-geared and still find a rat dangerous?Progression is empty. You'll level various skills by using them, but the growth rate is absolutely glacial. I had to kill 10-20 enemies with a sword before I got my first skill-up in Melee. Then there's the card system. Every 3 levels or so in a skill nets you skill cards. You have 5 slots for these, 4 of which need to be purchased through a vendor. Each skill has 5 cards (plus bonuses from shrines) and there are 6 skills. Being forced to choose which weak perk you'll use instead of having all of them active is bad design. None of the cards is particularly valuable, so forcing this kind of choice limits the power of your character, and therefore the fun of the game. Each level up in a skill comes with a relevant stat increase, but it's so minor as to be completely negligible.As you'll see from any review I've done within this genre, I am a glutton for punishment. The grind is initially fine because you're still seeing new things within the game. However, I finally decided that enough was enough. There's not enough "good" in Mirthwood to continue chugging along. The game could be so much more, but there are way too many poor design decisions that really hold the game back. Buy on sale, if at all.

_childDocuments_.review: After near 18 hours into this game I think I am able to let you guys know what I think. _childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood is a game with a charming art style that that follows the farming sim genre and is similar to games such as Stardrew Valley or Coral Island, although fails to really innovate in any way to make it stand out from its competitors beyond its art style and setting. Much of Mirthwood is pretty bog standard or the genre, and if you've played one you'll feel right at home here in Mirthwood. There in lies the problem however, it doesn't really do anything different and in fact does a lot of things worse. For instance the NPCs; most of these games have a whole town of characters you can usually interact with, romance, be friends with, and so on, usually having distinct personalities and dialogue to engage with. This games doesn't have that at all, none of the npcs have dialogue outside of quests, instead you interact with them similar to how you interact with characters in the Sims series, and so there's really nothing to distinguish one npc from the other nor is there really any feeling of connection to those NPCs. There's no dialogue, it's just things like "Click chat" "Click gossip" and then get a little plus or minus for the NPC's reaction. This makes most NPCs just feel like pixels on my screen rather than people I can talk to and interact with. There is also the problem of the combat. This is probably the only area this game tries to innovate over its competitors in the genre in that it at least tries to make a more interesting combat system especially since this game has more of an rpg setting in which you can explore and fight bandits and monsters and the like. However the combat is terrible for a multitude of reasons. The first reason is that it's really easy to cheese, most combats can be won by just back peddling and stabbing once and then back peddling again. However if you engage with the combat the way the devs intended, it's just not good either, it's very cumbersome and unresponsive. There are two dodge buttons, space bar dodges backwards, and then V does a dodge roll towards the enemy. However the game forces your character to look towards an enemy when you're close enough, meaning that if you step a little too far away while avoiding attacks, your character will turn around and face the wrong way, meaning if you use one of these dodge keys, it'll go in the wrong direction. I think it really would have helped if they were on one key and dodged where ever your mouse was or whatever way your were walking, instead of this really cumbersome system. Blocking is also unresponsive and slow, and range of weapons is really misleading. You would think your longsword would have more reach than a bandit with a dinky knife but in this game the guy with the knife both has more reach, and attacks faster than you. Monsters are much the same, you'll think you have reach advantage but then the monsters will leap or lunge as part of their attack giving them considerable range, and because blocking is so slow and cumbersome, it can often result in your taking unexpected hits. This all together just makes the combat feel really cumbersome to engage with although I at least respect that they tried to make it more engaging than other games.Picking up quests in this also just isn't really engaging, you'll spot a yellow exclamation mark and you can interact with them to accept quests, but instead of bringing up a page with the quest information and having an accept button, it'll just accept the quest without telling you what it is until you open up your quest log. I've also noticed this game uses AI art here and there like the title screen, which is really disappointing considering that most of the game is hand drawn and is really charming and I hope the AI art is just placeholder art. It's just a lot of small details like these that bring down the enjoyment of the game, on the surface it's very charming, I like the art style and the medieval setting, but it just feels cumbersome in most aspects of the game and a down right downgrade in others when compared to other games in the genre. I'd definitely wait for this game to get a few patches in before buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: sorry for the long spew, my first review actually. there's a lot of bugs and clunkiness. the day cycle wasn't synced with the clock in the bottom left. the clock is split into 3 times, it would be night time when the clock showed day, evening during midnight, and day during the night. and when it was raining my crops were not watered, probably due to the weather also not being synced, causing me to also lose crops. How is the very basics of this type of game, nonfunctional?Combat is just running around with a bow until the enemy is dead, since if you try to use the sword you are pretty much guaranteed to get hit way too many times. And all but the later swords do about the same damage as the bow, make that make sense.. Also you have to deal with being occasionally glitched frozen after being hit, having to sheath your weapon to fix the bug so that you can move or do anything again. And the amount of times I go to switch weapons or tools, only to accidentally eat/drink an item I was planning on selling is ridiculous. this game is in no way controller supported, a bare bones afterthought it seems, since I have to still use mouse/keyboard to do some things, and heaven forbid you accidentally leave the mouse cursor somewhere on the screen, it will cause the inventory screen to freak out. The resource grind is crazy, having to wait for a very limited resource to respawn, scattered around specific locations, while each craftable item requires quite a hefty chunk of those materials. Your chests have to be right next to your crafting stations or it wont register they exist, so even that convenience is pretty much nonexistent.I never felt any appeal to the relationship aspect, seemed like they took inspiration from the sims mechanics tbh, didn't interest me in the slightest. As well as the quests, they just throw random quests at you with no heads up, storytelling, just here ya go, ya can go do this, i guess.It does have campsites, which act like other smaller home bases you can fast travel to and from, which was nice. Credit where credit is due lol. but dang, I wanted to enjoy this game but waay too much clunkiness and bugs really threw me off it

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of thoughts about Mirthwood, and while it's definitely not perfect, I really enjoyed it (a lot more than most Stardew-inspired games), and, despite its rough edges, I would definitely recommend it to fans of the genre. It has a bit of that secret sauce that really kept me engaged and having fun, that I haven't found in many other games recently.I've put around 19 hours into the game, and just finished the main storyline, without putting a ton of time into side activities. Narratively, Mirthwood is a bit of a mixed bag for me. It obviously has a lot of thought and love put into it, but I felt like the story was too grand for what the game is actually capable of conveying.  There are found notes and books that reveal some of the world's lore, and while I enjoyed reading them, I didn't feel that it was ultimately enough to give a full understanding of who I'm supposed to be, where I am, or . In a similar vein, you choose a background ranging from peasant to royalty when you first make your character, and it does frame this as a choice with gameplay buffs and debuffs, but I expected it to also have more of a narrative consequence. Even if you choose to be royal, you start out in a shabby peasant's house in a village with your family, and I didn't notice any difference in the way NPCs reacted to me because of my supposed nobility. The dialogue system as well is a bit awkward. With NPCs that have real dialogue, certain options are questions that return to a hub, while other options have the 'exit conversation' choice hidden inside of them, or progress the conversation without any clear indication. It also always replays the first chunk of NPC dialogue after each response to a question, which makes it read a bit strangely, and there are, on rare occasions, stage directions written into the dialogue. Sometimes the dialogue is inside quotations, other times it's not. It's nothing terrible, but just a lot of little things that would benefit from a bit of polish. All in all though, the writing quality itself is better than a lot of what I've seen in other similar games, especially in the notes and books, but the overarching story is underdeveloped and dialogue loses a bit of its potential to how densely it's packed into each paragraph, and how awkwardly it's often presented.Also, for anyone considering buying, know that the romance system is not at all like Stardew. Most NPCs have no real dialogue or personality beyond some assigned traits. Interacting with them is based on choosing topics, and reading Rimworld-style little blurbs about what they said. This can increase or decrease friendship or romance ratings with the different little guys you meet around the world, and not to say this is a bad thing, it has its charms, but it's definitely not a character-based dating sim in the way that other farming games often are.In terms of gameplay, like a lot of people have mentioned, the combat is a bit clunky, but I found it fun enough to try figuring out. Honestly though, I did spend basically the entire game running circles around enemies with a bow and arrow, chipping them down very, very slowly. Decorating your house and farm is fun, but ultimately, actually farming isn't really necessary for progression through the story in any way, beyond the first quest that forces you to learn how to farm.  I wish it had been more solidly tied into the main story, or any quests, since now that I've finished pretty much every quest available, I don't have a ton of reason to go back and engage with that mechanic since there's no real goal left to work toward.The exploration itself I found to be a ton of fun though. The map is big, but you run decently fast, have a lot of fast-travel options, and the world is well designed so there's almost always something cool and rewarding to find in the wilderness. Even if it's just an environmental storytelling skeleton with a note and an apple in a bag, there is always something, never just a huge expanse of emptiness. The crafting system is also pretty simple. It's always pretty clear what you need to do to advance, and where you need to get those materials. Iron and steel are a bit of a grind to get, but wood, stone etc are easy to come by in large quantities. It's enough work to progress that it feels like a satisfying task without ever feeling insurmountable or like a total slog to get through.The art stye is obviously super charming, the music is great, the vibes are impeccable, etc. The game is a fun experience, well worth the price as it is now, and the devs have put out consistent updates since release to address bugs and quality of life stuff. I hope they'll keep working on it, maybe flesh out the story a bit more, refine the dialogue system, and fully realize all of the potential that's here.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:*Active and Dedicated Developers: The two-person development team is impressively responsive, pushing out timely patches and updates based on player feedback.*Beautiful Art Style and Atmosphere: The gothic aesthetic and immersive environment are stunning, reminiscent of The Witcher 3’s White Orchard.*Freedom of Play: You can pursue your interests at your own pace. Whether it’s farming, crafting, fishing, winemaking, questing, or even building a reputation as the town’s infamous thief, the choice is entirely yours.*Exploration: Discover treasure chests, ruins, towns, and locations with hints of lore. The scattered notes revealing the scene or location's backstory add a wonderful depth to the experience..*Fast Travel: Signposts at camps allow for convenient fast travel across the map, making exploration easier.Cons:*Resource Gathering and Crafting Grind: Some mechanics, like gathering iron ore or managing crafting ratios, can feel overly grindy. Thankfully, the developers are actively tweaking these systems based on community input.*Bugs and Glitches: Technical issues are still present, but the developers are consistently addressing them with frequent updates.*Combat Challenges: Combat feels clunky and can be challenging, especially with low-tier gear early on. Frequent enemy encounters during exploration can be frustrating, but upgrading to a bow early or adjusting difficulty settings in the menu can help.*Limited Tutorials: The lack of in-depth guidance may leave new players struggling to figure out some mechanics through trial and error.Verdict:I wholeheartedly recommend Mirthwood, but with the caveat that it’s still a work in progress. If you prefer a polished experience, you may want to wait and follow the developer updates on Discord or other platforms. However, if you’re okay with a few bugs and enjoy being part of a growing game, you’ll find countless hours of enjoyment in this eerie yet beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: They had me at 'hello' when I saw this game pass by in the store.When it finally came out, I hesitated to buy it because of quite some negative reviews.But a couple of days later, after some patches had come out (nothing more frustrating than bugged quests), I gave it a go anyway because I was so in love with the visuals of this game.So I started on 11/11/24, could complete every quest I found and have all achievements now.The sceneries and sounds are just amazing, in every season. Explorers are not only rewarded for finding those feathers, items or outfits and special stones... No, they get rewarded with nice little details in the scenes too.So, you have are the quests, the exploration, being a thief or a good person, books and notes, the farming, fishing, mining, tool upgrading, crafting, decorating and killing... I did not really focus on a single thing, not on farming and especially not on charisma. I only spent an afternoon purely on maxing that out - for the achievement as in the game itself, I didn't notice any benefit so far but maybe maxing some friendships will open some doors :)At first, I thought everything was so expensive but when you run around a lot and slaughter some werewolves and thieves on the way, you make already some decent budget from that.But yes, I did some farming, out of fear at first because I had bought a chicken and it wasn't until I noticed I could not buy animal feed and thought it was going to die (my expensive chicken, haha) I panicked, spent all my money on seeds and sold some crops to buy that mill blueprint. Oof, I made it. My chicken is still happily running around and even has a nice coop and friend now.I really enjoyed this game and had no issues except from 3 crashes during a teleport and the fact that this afternoon I had to restart as suddenly I did not get to see all chat options anymore.  I was getting some lag sometimes when going over to another scene but it’s just a second or three and I’m sure they are going to fix that too.That’s all concerning my issues, for 54 hours of playtime.I only had a couple of djeezes in the very beginning when shooting with the bow for the first time but I got the hand of it very quickly and even maxed out archery before melee as the bow comes in pretty handy but after all, I got hooked to my best sword. And yes, that was weird too at first but hey, practice makes perfect, no?Apart from the charisma, nothing really felt like a chore.The fishing game is one I haven’t seen before and I can imagine on a controller it’s indeed probably hard but on PC, it’s no biggy.For now, I did not notice a big advantage for upgrading the farming tools but then again, I had a maximum of 60-70 plants at a time which was quite manageable with the copper tools.Voilà, that's it.If a DLC comes out, I'll definitely buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: first time writing a review! saw this youtuber play this game and decided to give it a try. i really wasnt expecting much but i've been pretty impressed so far. i thought this was going to be like any other cozy farming sim, but there is so much more depth to this game with its lore scattered throughout its lands. personally, i've enjoyed adventuring and discovering the secrets this world has so far. one thing that has surprisingly grown on me is the combat. at first, i wasn't a fan. i've seen others have some words abt it, not sure if its buggy or just me having terrible reaction speed LOL but regardless, its way more engaging/interactive than other farming sims and has been a fun challenge to work thru. Mirthwood is not quite like other well known farming sims I've played in a refreshing way. with that being said, it's only fair to mention that this game still has a lot of kinks to smooth out. the dev seem to be pretty transparent and very hardworking and have been pumping out patches to address as many concerns as possible from what i've seen in the last few days. the hardwork hasn't gone unnoticed, keep up the great work! if this game interests you, but the issues you've seen in other reviews are worrisome, wishlist this game and come back to give it a try. i think you'd really be missing out on a fun, unique farming sim if you don't. otherwise!!!! if you're cool with a WIP then please try it and stay along for the ride. this game has so much potential and im so excited to see what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really should have gone into Early Access, because it is clearly not finished. The devs have a good roadmap of upcoming features, but it's not totally finished. With that being said, it is still a good and fun game with a lot of promise to be better. The Good-Art Style. The visual style is really interesting. I do not like pixel art games like Stardew Valley, I just don't have the nostalgia goggles for it. This is a nice middle ground between pixel art and 3D animation.-The Sleep Cycle. Yes, you do need to sleep. No, you do not need to sleep at night. You can sleep any time of day, as often as you want. And there are little camps scattered all over you can sleep at so you don't need to return to your farm.-The Farming is Optional. You don't have to farm, and if you go off adventuring for a few days there's no loss of crops. If you have plants in the ground and don't water them they just don't grow until they get watered again. -The Story. I like the overall story of the game. I had completed what there is so far, and I hope that more gets added. The Bad-Some Controls. Not every control is bad, but a lot of it is not great. The heavy attack and sprint keys are, as a default, the same option. Most keybindings you can change, but early on it's not very easy.- The Fishing. Sorry, I hate the fishing mini game. The wedge moves too fast and the mouse too slow. And there's not much of a tutorial for it, so you're just struggling to figure it out.-Material Availability/Use. Different materials are not very well balanced. Iron is in super high demand but is not very common. Same with regular wood. The devs have made some of this better, but it's not well balanced yet.The Ugly-Poor optimization. The game, at least last I knew, loaded the entire world map at once. That causes lots of lag and issues. The devs seem to be working on that though. But for now it is as bit slow and takes up a lot of power.-Buggy. Right now, the game is prone to lots of bugs. Furniture in my second floor will not show up when I am in the house, but will show up when I am outside. It's very odd to see a bed just floating in the air. Some things load in inaccessible areas. People will respawn in areas they can't leave. Thankfully, these are being addressed and are getting fewer by the update.What I Wish the Game Had-An NPC directory. Names, class, affiliation, where they live, and your relationship status shown on a menu you can scroll through and search. Currently you can only view that when next to an NPC.-NPC Locator. In a similar vein, it would be great to be able to mark where an NPC is on the map for quests and relationship building. Sometimes I have a quest to speak to Person, but I cannot remember where Person lives.In summary; it has some good aspects, a few issues, and the promise of more content in the future. 8/10. I enjoy it, it has some issues, but many are being addressed as they crop up so it's better than a lot of games that get no changes after release.

_childDocuments_.review: My time I spent on the game has been really fun and I enjoyed this game immensely, but there is certainly room for improvement. Lots of bugs, (which have not really gotten in my way at all, and the devs are regularly patching them) but there is the framework of a game that, in the future I think could rival Stardew Valley. Some systems such as notoriety and morality do not really have much of a purpose yet, but I can see something being made for them to be more of a mechanic. Example being, morality changing the character's appearance, having morality/fame locked quests, or just having the NPC's react more to you. Speaking of the NPC's there is not much of a point to making friends or romancing them so far. It'd be interesting if it took a fable approach and have you be able to have NPC's follow you to places, or hire them as body guards.The homestead is really cool, and the camps. It would be neat if you could go further than it just being personal property/farm, and you could expand them into small settlements that NPCs could move into, build homes for them and decorate them and pay taxes to you from as a "landlord" type of thing. Amount and rarity of decorations in homes increasing how much they pay you on tax day.To close out, there's alot that needs fixing, but this game has absolutely MASSIVE potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if Skyrim and Stardew Valley had a baby. I find that I keep being drawn back to it. I like that there are quests in addition to the farming/crafting cycle. In 20 hours, my game has crashed 3 times, which is not too bad. I like the autosave and fast travel feature. I wish lumber and iron were a little more plentiful, I'm having a hard time really getting my farm up and running, ending up with stacks of crops that I'm slowly feeding into crafting items, which takes a little too long considering the running around I have to do in order to quest. I think the balance needs a little fine-tuning there.The main quest line is very interesting so far. I don't like that with the side quests, there's no turn-in for them, I don't have a sense of closure, it's just over. The morality and renown bonus doesn't give a sense of closure, because I don't know what happened, for example, with the farm after I killed those wolves in the cave for them. I suppose they just went back to business as usual? The art style is gorgeous. I love the attention to detail, even the scroll bar has a beautiful pattern on it.I did notice that there aren't any female thieves, bandits, or wanderers, which seems like an oversight. This is a beautiful game with the potential to appeal to both male and female gamers (Stardew Valley appeals to both as well), so I think this should be corrected.I think the only thing I really don't like is the fishing mechanic. It's both difficult and time-consuming, especially when I have a lot of other things to do in game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was one of the people waiting for launch day and counting down the hours until it unlocked. Was so excited for this game, and it has such an incredible foundation to work from. I love the underlying story so far but I do have some feedback. Things I Love:- The narrator is exceptional and really creates a vibe.- The visuals of course are stunning- The sound design is great and immersive- The expectations of the character player and what you do in the game is awesome- The environment as a whole is very well made and planed outThings I dont love- The fighting mechanic is just, not great. _childDocuments_.review: This game is almost really good, but everything falls a bit short.First the game is buggy as heck right now. I spent 15 minutes trying to figure out how to interact with a hammer in a tree (it's part of a quest). There was one tiiiiiny spot I could stand and the interact would flash for a nanosecond. In the main quest line I was told to go get an artifact from a dungeon. I did not find the artifact but the quest changed to go talk to the questgiver anyway and it started moving me to the next step of the quest.Combat is clunky and unfun. Being unable to swing your sword toward the top or bottom of your screen means enemies can approach you from some weirdly invincible direction. The bow can shoot up and down though! And you have infinite arrows which makes cheesing with it really easy, but really boring. Hunting was fun for a bit until I realized how low the drop rate on meat was from animals. You kill an entire deer and 4/5 times there is no meat on it. You need some kind of wholesale deer slaughter to get any decent amount of resources.Seeds grow quickly, which is kind of nice, but farming takes a huge amount of time because of bad interfacing, and the seeds are weirdly expensive. Also having to go and buy recipes for every single food you want to learn to cook is really annoying.And everything takes too many resources. You'd think early, staple items like chests and a furnace would be quick and easy to get. Nope! You have to hit dozens of rocks to get enough for a furnace, and keeping it running with wood is a pain in the butt. Chests are similarly ridiculously resource intensive, making everything feel far too grindy. Lastly, NPC are about as boring as you can get. They have no actual dialogue and all interactions is some kind of Sims-like system. There are screens to track what each townsperson likes but moving relationships is basically just clicking buttons repeatedly and watching little icons over their heads. Unlike life sims like Stardew, the townspeople are incredibly generic and boring in pretty much every way. Each is very one-dimensional as well in that they like one thing and you just spam that over and over to make them like you. Also, they constantly walk away in the middle of conversations! How rude!I didn't even get into the framerate drops and lagging, as well as other bugs like weirdly small menus. There's plenty more.There is the bones of a really interesting game in here, but everything feels half-baked. More frustrating than fun right now and nothing gives any sense of accomplishment. Hopefully this will get patched up at some point because it could be fun. Sadly, right now it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for something that's very free form, encourages your imagination with an immersive, lived-in world with Fable vibes that lets you do pretty much whatever you want, this is for you. You'll probably have a great time like I am. Yes, there are performance hiccups, and definite need for improvement in some areas, but overall, I found it didn't detract enough from my personal enjoyment of the game.Things I love so far:- Art style: Very charming, cozy, grim.- Music: It's been very fitting so far, and most times, I don't even notice it while I'm busy doing things, but when I do, it's great.Gameplay: Keeping in mind, I've barely scratched the surface, but I really like the idea I can farm, adventure/explore, craft, socialize, it just feels really nice being thrown right into the world, allowed to do whatever I want essentially right away. The quests have also been so far, one of them caught me off guard and hit me in the feels a bit when stumbling across an abandoned home. Some of the other quests are pretty straightforward and easy but I enjoy that personally, mixing those in. Overall, I feel there's plenty of content here in terms of quests, homesteading, exploring, crafting.Social aspects: Technically, it's a part of gameplay, but I put it as its own thing because it feels like its own thing in the game. Socializing with NPCs feels simple, but fun. It's like the Sims in a lot of way, and the fact you can wander about in to town and elsewhere, seeing others who may like you or even hate you, is really immersive to me.Combat: Honestly, probably the weakest part of the game for me. It's not outright terrible or anything, it's just passable, but I'll explain that below.The two main things I'd like to see improvement on so far:- General performance fixes: This needs the most attention right now for sure. The framerate can be pretty all over the place. I will say though, they've been trying to put out patches, and very quickly too, so hopefully this gets solved.UPDATE: For me at least, almost all my performance issues have been fixed and addressed. Amazing job devs, thanks!- Slightly snappier combat: It doesn't need an overhaul or anything, but I feel like it could be tweaked to be a little quicker/more responsive. To be more specific, I think the parry button needs to activate much quicker. I think it'd feel great if right when you're prompted to counter, and do click it, it activates similar to the Arkham/Mordor games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really special mix of a lot of the games that I love and some that I feel that I should've. Here's what it keeps reminding me of (in great ways):The Witcher series: The lore and setting just give me that same rich fantasy feelStardew Valley: Never got into this one...Think it was too much plot, but all the life-sim and farming stuffTerraria/Starbound: The satisfying crafting, mining, and exploration systemsThe Sims: The broad NPC relationships that make you actually care about townspeopleThe visuals really stand out - I love the hand-drawn feel with those great 3D touches (especially the water!). The menus are great. The quest title cards are great. So much going on here detail and love in this game already. I suck at the sword mechanic, but honestly enjoy combat. Kiting with the bow is pretty easy...maybe too easy? Most of my experiences have been with 1-2 opponents (excepting rats) and none have had projectiles of their own yet, so that will probably change my opinion.Crafting and homestead progression are rewarding so far.The main con is it gets a bit jaggy when moving quickly out of an area, but it's not enough enough to really effect game play. The game froze on me once in 10 hours. Will this be a 300+ hour game? Not sure, but I'll easily get 40 out of it and hopefully see this game continue to open up.

_childDocuments_.review: Definately i wont recommend this game at its current state.I appreaciate the effort and good work, the game has potential. First of all the game crashes randomly and you lose your all progress including the looted items, farmed items and completed quests. There is no autosave or quicksave if something goes wrong (by going wrong i mean losing progress because of crashes and etc.). The combat is very clunky, i thought i would get used to it, but i couldnt. Pros: Artwork, atmosphere, music and sounds, a good approach to this genre.Cons: Game stutters occasionally, quests are generally very straight forward and few in numbers, being stuck hurts especially during combat, very few and clumsy inventory management (there should be more and mixed slots or encumberence system), poorly designed map (easy to get lost and points of interests dont have name indicators on them), fishing mini game is not so fun, looting random crates and slain monsters are generally not so rewarding (i guess developpers wants players to lean on crafting rather than looting), levelling up certain skills only give very small bonus which doesnt have a significant impact on the game. Resource nodes not very easy to come by (i guess developpers did this intentionally so that the content cant be finished very quickly, otherwise people will get bored this time)Long story short this is an early access game with a potential. Needs lots of QoL and stability improvements. I was very excited about this game. Havent refunded just to support developpers for their good work, hoping they will improve the game much more in the near future.

You talk to random npcs who drop quests on you and it's all piled together and your'e just confused on where to start. What's worse is most quests I have completed, the rewards have been underwhelming. I think some quests I've received no reward. Maybe that's a glitch but would it matter, as the reward would probably be underwhelming. My last few hours of this game I started to really form an opinion that I do not like this game. Why? IRON!!! You need an iron pickaxe to harvest iron ore!!! I don't understand that because you have to craft the iron pickaxe yourself. So you have to found iron ore scattered around the map. Not harvest but finding it iron random spots like untop of a tables in an npcs house or on a bandit or OR you have to buy it. Which is also frustrating because the amount you can buy is limited to what the store has in stock. The store that happens to be far away from your house. Not only that but you need to then melt the iron ore into iron bars. 3 or 5 iron ore to 1 iron bar. In almost 5 hours of gaming I have only managed to find 12 iron ore. I need 10 iron bars for each tool I need. It is so stupid. I've never played a game where I needed material A to harvest material A. So i give up. I'm not going to run around the map scouring for materials I cannot harvest but NEED to progress in this game. SO i cannot recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: I loved the demo, but somehow, even after delaying release, the "finished" game is a mess and lacks the depth that the demo and advertising promise. I get that it's a small team, and that is commendable, but it feels like they've promised more than they can possibly deliver given the current state of the game. There are a number of systems, but they are all very shallow and underdeveloped. You can farm or not, it won't change anything in any meaningful way. You can fight or flee, again it won't actually affect the world or the outcome of anything you do in any major way. There is no depth or richness to the choices you make about your character. It's all very surface level stuff. Even the story itself is also quite bland and lethargic. Things just sort of happen, I never felt compelled into action in any way. The mysterious stranger is unnecessarily cryptic. Please, just tell me why I should care. It's so odd to escape a terrible raid and just be given a horse, a house and handful of random quests.An interesting idea in a timeless setting. Beautiful art design, although there are some contrast and saturation issues where things look washed out and can be a bit hard on the eyes. Overall, it's a nice framework for a really deep and engaging game, but there are far better options in the same genre, that offer many more hours of gameplay, for around the same or less cost.I hope they switch it to Early Access and continue development, but I do not want to play a game that doesn't deliver what it advertises itself to be.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a mix of many game types which I believe makes it unique. When I want to cleanup my house, build a garden or some storage, cook, or chat in the local town, I can do that. When I want to go questing, build up my skills, find new gear, I can do that. I don't feel that the game has forced me to play it a specific way, really allowing me to spend my time how I want. I can't think of a large studio release in recent days that has worked this hard, provided this much flexibility in game play, and has made me enjoy solo gaming. I was planning on waiting for a review until I was further in, but I discovered pretty quickly that I enjoy it enough to recommend it. A big shout-out to the whole team. _childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, the game is very unpolished and will need quite a bit of time to refine many systems/bugs, and therefore I would not recommend buying it now. While the art style is interesting, I don't feel it is bringing anything new to genre. As many have said, the combat is very clunky, with the biggest issue being the lack of north/south animations. The skill system with cards also feels like a downgrade from a lot of other titles in the genre, with many of the bonuses being way too small to notice. I have spent a lot of time investing in the social mechanics in the game, but my biggest issue thus far is that there is no menu to track relationships with NPCs, you have to find them and get close to them and click a little box to see what your status is with them.

_childDocuments_.review: This "Not Recommended" is VERY conditional, as it, if this game looks good to you, you might very well like it. For me, there were a couple things that really made me not have a good time. First of all, the couple quests I had at the start were not very intuitive. "Find blah blah blah", but no mention of where to look at all, so I ran around for 20 minutes with no progress before giving up. Maybe that gets better later.The second thing I disliked was the fishing "minigame". I put that in quotes, because it isn't much of a game. You have to move an arrow to keep it inside of a green area that moves around in circles without much notice. The thing is, the progress bar for catching the fish, while the arrow is in the green area, is super slow, which means you spend over a minute trying to catch this fish. You'll probably catch it, it's pretty forgiving, but it will take so much time and the fish isn't worth anything, so it's a terrible waste of time. It isn't fun, and fishing in games like this, if they have them, should be fun. At least, as far as I'm concerned. Anyway, the reality is that there is probably lots to love about this game. It's got a "Mostly Positive" rating, because most of the people who play it like it. I'm on of the few that didn't enjoy my time with it, and my rating is based on a very small amount of playtime, which should absolutely be considered. So, yep, I sadly don't recommend this game, not if the issues I mentioned sound like things that would also kill your ability to enjoy the game.

My specific complaint about combat is there are dodge and roll mechanics but none of it feels smooth. The keybindings for combat are kind of awkward and also your character seems to get stuck facing a certain direction or being unable to move until after a long animation plays. I have a gaming mouse and just wanted to set up buttons for dodge, roll, heavy attack, and block, but you can't do that. Hopefully it'll be addressed in a future update. =)  I think the game is still super fun even with awkward combat. Also, I wish talking to the villagers was a little more fleshed out. At the very least, I'd like to know what my relationship score is with them. I've been flirting with a townsperson for awhile and our conversations usually go well, but I'm not really sure what the purpose of talking to the townspeople is. It hasn't unlocked anything so far but maybe I'm just missing something or haven't raised my relationships high enough yet to notice anything. _childDocuments_.review: I have been loving playing the game so far, i love the art style and the story. But listen, 1. The fishing is atrocious. The ball fills up so incredibly slowly that i've just gotten so frustrated with it, that i don't bother with it anymore. I hate that it's so bad. 2. The map is kinda useless, nothing is labelled and not all quests have indicators that show where you are supposed to go, or where the people you are looking for are. I shouldn't have to constantly search up online to figure out where the people i'm looking for are or where i'm supposed to go.3. The combat is janky, but i'm janky at combat so it does mostly work out ok for me, but the character doesn't respond quick enough. For example, i'd be fighting and the enemy would jump to behind me and i'd be pressing the button to turn around, and instead of turning around, they'd start walking backwards while hitting forwards.. annoying.4. Lastly, the wood situation is abysmal. Most of the trees are decoration and can not be cut down and the ones that can be, are only in a small area including your own land. And you better hope you don't cut down the stumps or you'll be waiting for SEASONS for them to actually grow back. Some don't look like they are growing back at all. This so incredibly frustrating, considering that everything takes a ridiculous amount of wood to craft, i don't understand why the wood is so very scarce.Despite these issues, i am really enjoying playing. And would love to see the things i've mentioned improved upon. It has the potential to be a fantastic game, in my opinion. There is just a few little things that let it down a bit at the moment.

I have been recommending this game to my friends for a bit now, I have used analogies to express this game to them from  to . And I have heard people refer to it as  and yes we can make those, but honestly this game is Mirthwood. It is its own unique self, it has its own identity image and mechanics, from fighting mini-game to management of resources to live and prosper (and more importantly customise your base and sell goods at town :D).  If you are burned by dev teams who make good games but bad moral choices, by unfinished games with lots of plans but no chance to follow though or repetitive life SIMs that have so much promise but fell short then give it a chance because it's not one of those,

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try sum up my impressions, in short...The game (exe) maybe has potential, but to be honest, what this game is really lacking is "the game". Many developers nowadays seem to forget what a "game" means and why games like Terraria or 7 Days to Die are so successful. A game means that you as a player are expecting "rules", say per most RPG or Survival, and and get rewarded by either playing the game by rules or finding ways to get better are playing by the rules or exploiting them by a minor degree to gain an edge. The player should be allowed several "paths" to advance the game and the game should be balanced so that investing into either of those paths is generally equal in fun, progression speed or gains.The problem with the game is that there is no real progression and reward for progression and different pats you can take are not balanced. With combat not being interesting and crafting not balanced there is not much when you sum it all up. Basically the (single) dev spent too much time making the game.exe and too little making a game, and that didn't even pan out so well.In addition, the game is released under 60 FPS on a PC that plays Skyrim at 120 FPS capped, and periodic "hiccups" that impact your experience. This is almost top-down with side-scroller elements that played on Amiga 500 in 1992 with less than 1 MegaBYTE of RAM and graphic performance of today's scientific calculator.While I do appreciate the fact that a single developer did this game, if you try hard on your exam but don't score, you still don't get a passing grade. I hope that the game improves in the future, but at this point I cannot recommend the game, but I hope that my purchase can help the developer with making some money and hiring more people that can help make a game out of this exe.

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, I give a thumbs down at first because I don't understand the gameplay. Usually, I change my mind later after getting into the game - realizing it was my fault. Not the developers.In Mirthwood, it's the other way round: I was excited at first, because the graphics, music and story was so authentic and captivating. But after playing a while, I see the flaws: game-breaking bugs, and some kind of helpless feeling what to do next. In many open world games, there is this long list of what to try, explore, craft and what to do next. In Mirthwood, as big as its potential may be, I kinda have to look for a way to keep myself busy. There is no real reason to go big in farming, there is no real reason to go adventuring, there is no real reason to craft.Yet.I still believe in Mirthwood - one day it might even be a worthy successor to games like Stardew Valley. But this day is not today.

_childDocuments_.review: Has the bones of an interesting game, but isn't a fun game in itself right now. Wait at least a year or two before even considering purchasing it.I'm fairly disappointed. I watched the trailer a while back. I loved the art style and the idea of a social simulation to fiddle with. Bought the game pretty much the hour it came out.It's clear that a lot of love was put into the art and music for the game. Sadly the same can't be said of its design or its technical aspects.The game stutters quite a lot. Probably while loading assets as I move from one part of the map to another. The display settings don't seem to work unless I go back to the main menu and reload my save, and even then I'm not sure. There's a 15-20 minutes-ish prologue with nowhere to save until it's done. Once it's done, the game doesn't autosave for you, or encourage you to create a save yourself. I ended up losing two characters and about an hour's worth of time because of this.Enemies chase you across the map, and if you die to them, they stand rooted to the spot they were in when they killed you, and you respawn somewhere close to them. The combat is finicky, it's up to the toss of a coin whether you take a swing where you mean to. Enemies have two kinds of attacks, weak attacks which can be blocked and strong ones which can't, with neither telegraphed well enough to respond to reliably.The art style is charming, but there's a fair degree of visual clutter, and it's hard to spot what is interactable through what isn't. To further muddy things up, the same assets are used as props and interactive objects (see the bard in the tavern, for example, or any number of crates and pots).The social sim... on the face of it the concept is cool. Mechanically, to get someone to like you, you initiate a conversation with them, and click through two menus again and again until one of you gets bored. Hopefully you, because you're a living, breathing, thinking human with little time for needless tedium.More time should have been spent prototyping the systems advertised as features, with proper art and music coming in only much, much later. As it stands, it feels like the devs started ambitious, but realized too late that they'd bitten off more than they could chew.I hope it gets better. I think they've got something that, with time and polish, could be fun. For the moment though, cool art, half baked features, and the meta-story of two hard working devs is all you'll get for your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Some minor bugs were experienced, such as assets not loading in while fast-traveling or NPCs stuck communicating with each other until reloading. I hope that future updates will add an improved quest marking system, as I found myself lost on several quests. Outside of that, this will be a game that I see myself playing for a long time. The shining light in Mirthwood is the freedom it offers the player. A solid sandbox experience, combined with a cozy, farming, and life sim, all packaged in a hand-drawn pop-up book style.I made most of my money crafting alcohol and preserving jam while hunting and fighting mythical swamp monsters with a hardwood bow. I am hooked on Mirthwood. Most importantly I’m looking forward to experiencing all this game has to offer and the future multiplayer update. You will gladly devote all your free time to this game, grinding and farming for resources for hours on end without even realizing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Held back on a review for quite a while, but I think I'm at a point where I can comfortably give an opinion.I'm about to head into the second season, but I feel like I've got the basics and whatnot down, so.The game definitely has a ton of potential. Apart from the absolutely charming art style, which definitely adds into the medieval feel, the music, ambience and immersion is definitely there. That being said, there are bugs and performance issues - but after seeing how active the devs are and how responsive their team in the Discord is, I have no doubts that they will polish the game based on community feedback. Beta-branch updates are being pushed out multiple times a day and feedback is thoughoutly discussed.The game itself is in a very enjoyable state, imo. Apart from some stuttering here and there, I haven't run into any big bugs whatsoever so far, might just be lucky, but it's enough for me to happily continue playing without really "chasing a goal", like you often do in these games.The game just throws you into the free lands and goes "alright, off you go to live the life YOU want to live". Be it as a thief, a farmer, looking after your lifestock, adventuring or just mining, it's all quite viable. Money takes a while to make, which is a nice change compared to planting 58943 blueberries in stardew and being set for the next 3 years. It makes you work for your upgrades, quests are vague and don't hold your hand and guide you to the exact spot - it encourages you to explore, to pay attention, converse, pick up little letters and books strewn around - but in a way that it's still comfortable enough to play without looking things up. It's such a breath of fresh air that I can only highly recommend the game!! If you're fine with some stuttering and apparent lil bugs, please pick it up. If not and you'd prefer to wait until it's a little more polished, I'd say give the devs a few more weeks and it should be at a good state if you'd prefer that. <3

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good.  The game just released into Early Access on November 6th.There are some bugs, but none of them so far have been game-breaking, otherwise this would be a negative review.  After 22 hours of game play, I just experienced my first game crash as a result of a fast travel request from one location to another.  I have used the fast travel process frequently with no issues until now.  The game has a semi-casual feel to it, and is more relaxing than most RPG's.  I suspect part of that credit goes to the music score which has a lighthearted and easy-going vibe to it.  Lot's of quests, and so far at least none of them have been broken.Graphics are good, though there is a pretty regular graphics stutter that locks up the game for a second or so.  It has not cause a crash as of yet, nor has it interrupted or hindered combat.Combat is simple and straight forward.  As the game has almost full controller support, I find that to be the predominant way I play, including combat.  That said, any resource harvesting that requires using a tool (wood axe, pickaxe, hoe, scythe, watering can) can only be accomplished with the mouse (and keyboard for moving the character from resource node to resource node).  Same goes for fishing.  I suspect this is an oversight and will be remedied at some point.  I've gotten used to switching back and forth when harvesting.There is a whole social interaction between the PC and NPC's that I've not spent much time pursuing, so I'm not going to go into very much detail of it for this review.Some game decisions, such as stealing, impact a sliding scale reputation for your character (good versus bad), and NPC's interact with the PC accordingly.  A bad reputation can be reversed, at least partially, by making small donations at shrines that are found throughout the world.  Completing quests also positively impacts reputation.For being in Early Access, the game is doing just fine and I consider it enjoyable.  I can't envision there being much of a personal desire to replay the game after I complete it the first time (which is pretty normal for me with almost all games), but that said, I suspect I'm a long ways away from finishing the game.  I think the game is currently on sale for $22 US.  There are a ton of playable hours in the game, so for the amount of entertainment it's providing, I see that as a well spent $22.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood appears to be a medieval sandbox that is part RPG and Life Sim with a morality feature that measures the player's propensity for Good and Evil (i.e. stealing -  vibes anyone?).  Essentially you can manage a homestead like in  within a setting like  minus the construction grind and town building, while emphasizing combat a bit more thanks to a grim starting narrative like you see in .Granted at 2 hours played I may have only scratched the surface of what's in store for me later on in the game, but what I see right now has not disappointed and has me excited to see how deep it goes as I continue my playthrough.Only real suggestion I have so far is a recommendation to simplify the inventory slot management.  Once I realized that the player typically gathers 4x more "food" items than any other item or resource type, it became very quickly apparent that I'd gather more total resources per harvesting run if every current inventory slot could hold anything rather than how it's split between types right now.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's a fun, unfinished game that was slightly more expensive than it should have been, but still worth a buy.It's essentially a Stardew Valley clone with a little extra enhancement to combat. You start off with normal farming stuff and get a basic weapon to explore with. You can mine resources to upgrade your equipment and can grow food / fish to handle hunger and make money.The exploration part of the game was well done and felt rewarding with hidden equipment recipes, side stories, and random boss enemies. The farming was about what you'd expect as was the mining and crafting. Main story was similar to Stardew Valley as well centering around contributing resources to 4 nodes.You start in the spring season and I completed all the game content before the end of fall. There's no reason to maintain the farm once you get enough money to upgrade your equipment as there's no end game surrounding farming and I didn't even get into the advanced buildings and animal husbandry. You don't even contribute crops to the 4 nodes.The main story moves pretty fast once you finish these 4 nodes and after that, the game just ends with no other real objective.it's obvious this game is unfinished with the shallow mechanics and features. On top of what I've already mentioned, there's an entire zone locked off from the player and relationships with NPCs are absolutely meaningless. You don't even have actual conversations with them like in Stardew Valley. Interacting with NPCs was clearly an afterthought. My only real complaint is the game isn't done.  The bones are there for a really great experience but it just needs more time. I still argue that the game is worth the price paid if you've already played Stardew Valley and want a fresh take on the idea...just don't expect the same depth.

_childDocuments_.review: When I adjusted my expectations for this game, I started to enjoy it a lot more. I was expecting something more story heavy and quest driven which it is not. There are quests, but they mostly seem to build renown which I’m still not sure what the point is.When I started playing this more like a sim game and a base builder, I started enjoying it much more.It was released as a complete game, which it does not feel like. It should be early access because it still feels very clunky. A lot of the negativity around it is because of that. But for real, the game is $25 bucks. Do I think I got my moneys worth for $25? Yes. I’ve been enjoying it as I get the hang of it.It definitely does not hold your hand. I’ve had to look up a lot of stuff online, but luckily a lot has been posted about it. The art style and the premise are amazing. I think it’s a unique concept and I look forward to what they will be adding to the game in the future. I really wish it had just been released as early access because I think people’s expectations of the game would’ve been better aligned. I also hope they will continue to improve the experience for the steam deck. Even with their recommended settings posted to discord set, it feels clunky and laggy at times. The performance can drive me nuts and I’m not a person who is usually bothered by that. I also don’t love the combat on the steam deck. With easier combat and easier survival turned on, I find it difficult. I know this review might sound like a lot of complaints, but I really do recommend this game. It’s enjoyable. I just wish if they were going to release it as full access, the experience would’ve aligned more with that and I would like others to have clearer expectations then I had.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an impressive game. The graphics are beautiful and evoke a fairy tale setting which reminds me a lot of Wildermyth (another good one if you haven't played it). The combat is rather simplistic and may not appeal to some people. I myself was starting to dread another fight kiting wolves/werewolves with a bow because they hit too hard. But level up your sword and you will be carving through them easily. The winter's blade sword and plate armor I had towards the end of the game made all fights trivial. The campaign took me a little over 20 hours. The game offers a fairly deep farming and building system, but I didn't spend much time doing those activities. I didn't build most of the available buildings and didn't purchase any animals. If those systems appeal to you then you will definitely get more time out of this game than my 20 hours. I would recommend this one to anyone who enjoys a fairly relaxing rpg romp that offers a decent story and great exploration. I was discovering new things all the way to the end, including the standing stone mechanic that I figured out too late to really engage with. I enjoyed this one enough to keep my eyes open for any future DLCs or projects from this studio. And I might even do a 2nd run through at some point. Solid 8/10 in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood is a gem for anyone seeking a tranquil yet engaging gaming experience. From the moment you step into its beautifully hand-drawn world, you're immersed in an environment that's as visually stunning as it is calming. The artistry behind the graphics is truly a standout feature, giving the game a unique, almost storybook-like charm.The gameplay strikes a perfect balance between relaxation and action. While the overall tone is laid-back, the combat offers a surprising level of satisfaction. It's easy to pick up and enjoy, yet nuanced enough to feel rewarding. This duality ensures the game appeals to a broad audience, whether you're here for the exploration or the thrill of battle.Mirthwood is more than just a game; it's an experience. Its combination of aesthetic beauty and smooth mechanics makes it a must-try for those who appreciate a creative, calming escape with just the right touch of excitement. I cant wait to see what else this TWO developer team has stored for the future!

_childDocuments_.review: At 10 Hours:Combat is definitely a learning curve, but it's still interesting. Learning the ins and outs of the game without seeking videos and spoilers is proving a nice challenge. The farming sim aspects are becoming clearer, though it still feels generally more like an adventure game than a farming game. The world is harsh and challenging. No enemies are level scaled, giving some more of those Morrowind feelings. You have to earn your place in certain places. Excellent.At 4.9 Hours:It's been a really long time since a game immediately drew me in like this. It's gritty, dark and yet somehow peaceful. I think a lot of that peaceful feeling has to do with how much you're required to use your own brain to get through it. You get what you need, but no one is holding your hand. You have to do it yourself. I'm delightfully reminded of Morrowind, if Morrowind had more of an Oblivion setting.This game is clearly a labor of love. I feel like I can feel the love of the developers for gaming itself in every piece of their creation, from the artwork to the music (THE MUSIC) to the map which gradually fills itself in as you go. I know people make games to make money (we need it in this world, obviously) but sometimes it feels like devs just try to churn out a game to make a buck and I don't get any of those feelings here.I've seen a lot of people complaining about combat. I'm enjoying it. You have to actually do it instead of just button mashing. It takes strategy, but overall I found it intuitive and enjoyable. So far. After several more hours, every single encounter taking that much effort may get old. We'll see.Obviously I've only been playing 4.9 hours and I will update my review as I play longer. So far Mirthwood is one of the best things I've played in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood is, for me, mostly a mixed bag. It hits all of my wants for a game - simple but likable graphics, a fairly easy to grasp interface, the framework for crafting and farming and all that. The narration is incongruously excellent for the indie nature, and I wish there was more. I like the questlines and the incremental gear upgrades - there's a lot to like here.But there are also cautions I would put out there - this is, I think, a two-person dev team, and while they're trying to respond to the suddenly large playerbase, they can't do so with great agility. In my mind, this should have been a well-polished early access title, rather than a often-janky full release. Here are the issues that I've come across that you should be aware of:- Unity will crash with some regularity. There aren't multiple saves, so sometimes the autosave will put you in a dangerous position of crash looping- Second floors are hazardous. If you save there and load in, feels like there's a 50% chance you'll fall through the floor into the shadowed first floor, and your only option to fix that I've found is to bump around in the dark until you find the stairs to bring you back up to the second floor- Combat is, as yet, unrefined. Archery will seem OP for about half the game, at which point melee decisively overtakes it. Most of the time, the dodge instincts of AI will mean you can swing wildly and stay safe, as they'll constantly be jumping away- Social interactions, which appear to be an important aspect of the game, seem not to work at all. Long conversations have changed my standing with people not at all, despite me saying the right (or even the wrong) things- Renown and morality have almost no effect on the game that I've seen, except for what people may say when they see you. There's one morality exception, if you decide to go dark, but other than that, no effect- Wood is shockingly rare for how prevalent it is as a building material. You're in a forest, surrounded by trees, but there are only two specific tree models you can ever chop down, and they're not particularly common- Trade routes/commerce quests seem also broken - there will be swings in prices of goods, but they're not extreme, and repairing the trade routes doesn't seem to do anything- The end of the game is...well, it's tacked on. The main quest builds through this good guy v bad guy story, gathering arcane items from deep dungeons and otherworlds, and it's to ultimately unlock a final dungeon that...I mean, get ready to mash them buttons. There's no secret new type of enemy, just a metric ton of the ones you've already seen- Then! The epilogue quest - SO ANTICLIMACTIC- So many locked doors! So much content I can't access! A mysterious canyon that's clearly for the future, but outside even that, businesses and utilities like mills are inaccessible - why?I very much hope that the devs iron out the rumpled spots, because this is iron worth striking. But unless you're a hardcore fan of the format already, you may want to give it a few months.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood: A Dark and Whimsical AdventureMirthwood is not just a game; it's an immersive experience that has completely captivated me. From the moment I stepped into its enchanting world, I knew I had found something truly special.The game's difficulty curve is well balanced, challenging players without being overwhelming. It rewards patience, strategy, and skillful resource management. The building and decorating mechanics are incredibly satisfying, allowing players to customize their homes and surroundings to their heart's content. The grind is far from tedious; it's a journey towards long-term rewards that keep you engaged and motivated.Mirthwood's farming system is a delightful blend of simplicity and depth. It's a truly satisfying experience to tend to your crops, watch them grow, and reap the rewards of your labor. The sense of accomplishment is palpable as you transform a overgrown and neglected patch of land into a thriving farm. It's a great way to relax and unwind, and it's also a valuable source of income and resources. The economic system is a brilliant touch. The joy of carefully managing your currency, and making strategic purchases is truly addictive. Exploration is a delight, with hidden secrets, stunning landscapes, and captivating quests around every corner.The art style simply breathtaking, it is a perfect blend of dark themes, with whimsy. Every pixel is a masterpiece, from the eerie forests to the quaint villages. The sound design complements the visuals perfectly, creating an atmosphere that can be both enchanting and unsettling.The social system is another standout feature. The characters in Mirthwood, though simple, feel memorable. Building friendships with characters like the Inn Keeper Clifford made me feel like a new guy in town, but as our bond grew, I felt more and more like I belonged. This added depth and richness to the world.The developers deserve immense praise for their dedication to their community. Their active presence on Discord and their tireless efforts to fix bugs and improve the game are truly commendable.Mirthwood is the finest game I've played in a long time, easily able to bring me back to the days of Fable's release. It's a masterpiece that blends challenging gameplay, immersive world-building, and a relaxing farming sim into an unforgettable experience. If you're looking for a game that will captivate you for countless hours, look no further than Mirthwood.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 40 hours playing the game and finishing just about all the quests and campaigns (that are available atm) I have to say it is a pretty fun game.The art style of the game is a new take for me but, overall a pretty fun game. Do I have a few things to say about it? Yeah several. For one, this game should have been released as Early Access not as a full release. Why? from the first day there have been bugs with either, audio, graphical, mechanical (teleportation and or wardrobe issues but luckily they have been fixed so far). Felt almost like I was testing the game while playing the campaign but, the team behind it has been really good about releasing updates pretty quickly after people report the issues.The farming mechanics honestly aren't the best? They also hold no value really in the game. Like yeah you could spend time setting up your farm but besides farming Flax for a few things, there is no benefit in growing crops (unless you want to make meals that heal some but you could just make use of health potions, takes less time to make and the flora grows pretty quickly to obtain the necessary ingredients to make em) Cooking just raw meats like venison, boar and any type of fish does well enough to satisfy hunger. If anything fishing is the best way to get pretty good amounts of food to store in your inventory. Though the fishing mini-game is really annoying but, you get the hang of it after a while.The social interactions with NPC's honestly give no benefit. I've spent a few hours trying to max  a certain NPC and it gets me nowhere or rewards nothing besides leveling up your skill on it.And as for skills, they have honestly very little to no effect. I haven't noticed any changes from equipping the skill to it being unequipped. (Skills that give bonus foraging or wood or more ore) Hardly noticeable even with the skill branch maxed out. Same for any combat related skill, I hardly see a difference even with Branch Bonuses.There are still quite a few areas that are blocked (because they haven't added them yet or aren't finished) which is what gives the vibe that this game is Early Access and unfinished. Over all a fun game but the game just needs a lot of fine running and re-balancing of both economic systems and monster spawns. (once you get to the end of the campaign you'll know why)But I got my moneys worth, 40 hours for a 22 dollar game? The game is fun with a lot of space for growth. Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. I think it’ll grow over time and develop into its own. But for now, it’s not there. I agree this should have launched as an Early Access title. And honestly, I more than likely wouldn’t have purchased it if it was tagged as so. But so far the game in endearing. The graphics are pleasant, and the farming/crafting is on point. The npc interactions seem shallow and insubstantial. Granted I haven’t delved too much into relationships, as I’m more focused on the farming, but it doesn’t seem overly worthwhile to talk to anyone. I love exploring the woods and finding things. The one thing I’m not overly fond of, and not to sound too much like a broken record, is of course the combat. I’ve been attacked by bandits and thieves so far. The bandits are a pain, but manageable. The hit and run strategy works for them. The thieves however are much much harder and I’ve had to run to the village for back up each time. Not exactly the most optimized, and I get the feeling that it wasn’t the most developed part of the game when it was released. I hope it gets better. Other than game play, the UI is difficult to navigate on a controller. Half the time I don’t know what I’m selecting or it is unknown if it’s actually responding to my moving the d-pad/joy stick. The text is a little small, especially when I’m playing on my Steam Deck at a lower resolution, even with the in game UI scaler all the way up. All in all, it’s got a few kinks to work out, but I think this could be a really great game. It’s definitely an EA title, even if it doesn’t say it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood shows a great deal of promise.  It feels like a passion project with old school influences.  While it certainly has some rough edges right after release, as far as I can see, the dev team is actively watching for feedback, taking it graciously, and will hopefully act on it.  That said, I think a lot of the criticism is unbalanced.I've played far enough to feel I have "broken through" to the main game, where it has become fun and rewarding.  The early game was a slog for me, but I don't think it has to be.  My sense is that the game is trying to give you a great deal of freedom in a slightly harsh, mid-magic, dark fantasy world.  My main challenge was in the expectation/tone setting:  the prologue tries to teach a little of everything, and makes it seem fairly simple to take on seasoned soldiers in combat.Then the prologue ends.  Combat is much harder.   Exploration is often combat bounded -- while you CAN run, you don't "feel" like you should have to after earlier victories.  The Farm Sim aspect is very slow to start, so you want to go find resources to make it faster, leading to a difficult early phase trying to get your equipment upgrades to make the core loop fast enough to be rewarding.It does make it very rewarding when you break through.  I enjoy the early desperation of being an exile in a new land, I enjoy the investment in slowly growing.  The game just seems to draw you away from the "Stardew Valley" experience that I was drawn to.  The early quests for homesteading are few and they lean towards tutorial rather than advancing the game, so you can walk out with some cosmetic upgrades that don't help mechanically when you're desperate for progress.  Combat isn't excellent.  It'd be tolerable if it were a minor entertainment to distract from the main game loop, but there aren't many alternatives to drive progress other than exploration-and-combat.  The quest system also takes the game in this direction.  Other games have quests for delivering crops, etc.  This seems mostly traditional RPG, in the sense of 'carry this from A to B' or 'go to A and kill B.'  That creates a distraction towards combat, which again, doesn't seem to be the design intent.Once I got past the desire to "seek approval from the game" by completing quests and went radically apathetic to society, it became a lot of fun.  Slowly growing my little farm and learning what works was great.   Many people have complained about the farming mechanics, for instance.  My main concern is the lack of information available to the player to make a decent decision.  For example, I've seen some complaints about wheat (buy a seed for X, sell the crop for X+1, very slow progress).  Other crops sports multiple harvests per season, or gain great value through crafting (jams, fermenting, aging, etc.)  As I'm learning these dynamics, its rewarding to grow my empire.In the end, that's it.   If you embrace the plight of your character (e.g., you're more than average, but still dead broke in the Dark Ages), then simply overcoming that challenge is enough.  Building a noble house from the agrarian roots, then into husbandry, then as a noble warrior.... that can be great.  The game just doesn't do a great job of setting those expectations up front, so the early game feels confusing and punitively slow.  Settle in.  Have some coffee.  It'll pay off.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Can't believe only 2 people made it, there's so much detail. I play on the Rog Ally and this game has been great to jump into and take anywhere. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential; it's fun and intriguing to play. Unfortunately, I have to give it a negative review (since there's no neutral option on Steam) due to the current bugs and frequent stuttering issues. Once the developers have had a chance to polish it further, I’d be happy to update my review to a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice alternative for everyone who finds cozy games a little too cozy (meaning, too cute, unrealistic or, ultimately, boring). This game has everything you need (farming, crafting, animal husbandry, orchads, foraging, mining, community, romances, etc.) but there's several major differences:- It offers tons of side quests that help you pass the time between all your farm chores, so you're never really out of things to do.- It has a main quest, that I haven't yet finished but which seems rather original for this kind of game. - it is grim, and you don't have to be nice to everyone. You can actually become a thief if you want. - The world is dangerous and you have to rather quickly invest in a weapon and armor if you want to stand a chance outside your village.All of the above, together with beautiful graphics, make this game special within the genre. There are little things/bugs that need fixing or polish (e.g. the dialogue tree could use a rework to flow better, right now it's clanky and unpleasant to play through), so don't expect everything to work perfectly smoothly from the start (you kind of see small budget in some of the game mechanics), but it is, nonetheless, a game worth recommending.
