_childDocuments_.review: Only a few hours spent on it so far but I can already tell this may become one of my favorites further on, along improvements and fixes. Huge fan of life sim & rpg this game gets me both in one title. It has a feeling of a few of my all time favs: stardew, fable, the witcher. That being said, i play on deck and controls cant be set properly and some actions are impossible. Also, the ingame tool to report bugs or comment is not working properly on deck (not able to type anything). There is a few gameplay bugs here and there (unfeedable chiken as example and unable to rotate furniture), but seeing how devs are responsive, I think most of them will get fixed with a little bit of patience. Only hope it can be tweeked for better playability on deck!!! For now I'll try it on my computer to see the difference on gameplay as it has an incredible potential !!!

_childDocuments_.review: My friends jokingly call it my "Elder Scrolls Stardew game," but there really isn't a better way to describe it. I get to run around basically looking like the Black Knight from Monty Python just shooting everything with an insanely overpowered bow and stabbing them with a super cool sword while also taking care of chickens and growing so so many grapes for a wine empire. This tiny developer team is pushing new updates every other day in response to Discord feedback, and I can't wait to see what else we get.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend, very impressed so far and imagine I will continue to be.Imagine Stardew Valley, except rather darker and gritter, with quests and were wokves and wraiths... and a little more of a challenge, which is very welcome. And bigger. The map is huge, which I wasn't expecting - with lots of little secrets to uncover it seems!The art style and sound track are both gorgeous, and playing the game is a pleasure - even just running around and taking it all in. The combat music is epic though, so make sure you get into a scuffle or two.The game play is great, I'm finding it smooth. There's more to keep in mind than a true "cosy game", but that just makes it better and way more satisfying. As a big cosy game lover, I still consider this one, except... much, much better.You can either focus on your farm or go adventuring killing monsters and doing quests, or both. I recommend both, it's super fun.There have been a few bugs and issues upon release, but the devs seem extremely committed to getting everything sorted. They have been very communicative and obviously hard at work.I hope this game goes as far as it can, additional content, DLC, the whole shebang. It could be one of the greats.Cannot recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Rpg and farm sim games this hits that sweet spot for both of my favorite genres. Very much like stardew but the graphics style and mechanics makes it stand out as its own thing. Throw in a good sense of exploration and questing and its a recipe for a classic. The devs are awesome and are constantly updating and fixing bugs while moving forward to release more content for the game. 9/10, one of my favorites in years.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.It is new and a buggy,  there are many things to adjust, but also so many things to love.I like the graphics - nice change to all the pixel clones (dont get me wrong I played over 400 hours Stardew Valley, but this is a nice change.)I like the slightly creepy atmosphere, the earie feeling you get..I like that you can make youe own choices.I like the story, though I'm afraid it will be over way too soon. And esspecially - the game doesn't hold your hand. You have to think for yourself, to look around for quest locations. I'm so thick of games that dumb you up and show you all the names and dots on the screen where you have to go. Like you are a blind idiot. So, thank you developers! Please don't make it easier. just give us more wood and iron, and more decorations! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: While the game still has some minor bugs and QoL issues, for it's price point it is 100% worth it. If you are a Harvest Moon/Stardew Valley fan you will find a lot to love. The lore is diverse and seems to have some deep parts to expand on for future DLC and updates. The art and music is also fantastic and the game is easy on the eyes to watch and play!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings fellow Farmers, Adventurers, and Wanderers!If you love to farm, if you love to craft, if you love to just wander and explore the lands.  Or just be the delightful little loot goblin that you may be. WELL, I have the game for you!There's mystery all around, as you meander through the beautiful lush trees, plains, and several other kind of locations!You'll make friends, you'll make enemies! You'll have to choose your path - Are you good? Are you evil? Are you somewhere in between, perhaps? Everyone, including yourself come from varied backgrounds. This will change how you interact with the people you meet on your travels, as well as where your farm resides. If you'd rather go loot and quest, you can! Don't feel that you're tied down to your farm, farm only if it interests you!You may also stay at your farm if it so pleases you. There are plenty of adventures to be had at home, as well as on the road! You customize your looks, your home, your adventure! Choose wisely, my friends. "Home isn't where you're from, it's where you find light when all grows dark."I wish you luck on your journeys, my friends. Happy Adventuring ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I got hooked on this game since I saw the demo back in Summer. The demo was not enough and it went on the top of my wishlist. I love the art style, the storyline, and the controls. TBH I lamented when they pushed back the release date, but after the first playtest I realized with the Devs that it wasn't ready yet, and what they did release has been amazing. These two guys are working tirelessly to get all the little annoying bugs to bring us a wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, this game does have it's share of general indie game roughness. Yet, in spite of that, this game is addicting and highly enjoyable. Also, the duo dev team are pushing out updates nearly daily to fix the issues as they arise. Any issue I've encountered never dimmed the love I have for this game. Most of said issues are fixed within 24 hours of being brought to light on the Mirthwood discord which is a thriving community of helpful and kind people.This game is like Stardew Valley and Skyrim had a baby; which is a combination I didn't know I needed until I played Mirthwood. <3So excited for the future of Mirthwood and the team behind it!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game since the demo and playtest. While it has had some growing pains, it is to be expected from a small developer. So far, they have done an exceptional job of listening to their community and consistently improving.If you get this game near to when I am writing this, I heavily recommend joining the discord, its super helpful for figuring out any confusing mechanics and they have an area for bug reporting which is consistently monitored and responded to.I know it is growing but the game play is already a blast. You can go a couple directions in play style for this. A friend of mine is barely at his home base and is out killing and hunting, meanwhile I have dived into farming and have built an aged wine empire. This game balances feeling cozy with exciting combat elements. I am excited to see the social elements grow and can't wait for co-op to be introduced
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I have been eagerly awaiting Mirthwood and the world is gorgeous, the art style is very unique and I enjoy it ( reminds me of a storybook which is fitting). The world is alive with secrets, everywhere you can roam and find notes of things that happened ( For example: You can find a man stabbed to a tree and you can find a note on the ground that tells you what happened to him= and you're given a choice to bury them or take their sword.) You see animals who died recently or decomposing, you can find thieves, and monsters. The world is very much moving and I love it. I would love to see more friendly npcs going about their lives like hunting or walking outside of villages. I feel that while this game does market itself as cozy and soft game it isn't and that's a good thing. People called this 2d skryrim and it does feel like that, I would like for the devs to lean this way. The game doesn't have to be marketed just for people of the cozy genre this has the makings of a very good open world. Some cons is that in its current state the prologue is very buggy and while you can get through it, it will def hurt any first time buyers and they'll want a refund. The game can be a bit buggy still but the devs are constantly working on it and are very quick to fix things, Overall I love the game and I am rooting so hard for it. Keep investing in this game please.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy, open-world simulation game with RPG elements (skills, combat, character creation). After an eventful introduction to the game you are presented with your own farmland, complete with a cottage and room to grow. I really enjoy the medieval setting as well as the beautiful hand-drawn graphics, which I think adds a lot to the cozy feeling of the game. The game features a social system akin to The Sims where you can interact with the denizens of the world by choosing specific social interactions (joke, flirt, chat and so on). The game had some bugs when it launched but from what I can tell the developers are highly communicative and have released several smaller patches to iron out the worst bugs quickly. I recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! Amazing game! It's like stardew but with more RPG elements. The artwork is incredible and the game, oh so cozy. You can quest, explore, farm, romance, have babies and more! Yes, there are bugs but please understand this is not triple A game, this is two guys in the back of a van. Idk about the van part, but give them a break! I really hope the roadmap works out and they get multiplayer because I want to farm with my BF!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun lil mixture of things like Stardew Valley, Graveyard Keeper, and similar like games. The art style is quirky and unique, and the story is pretty interesting to. However this game is far from polished.Its 100% playable, and I do recommend, but in 13 hours I've encountered 5 reoccurring bugs. 3 Minor, 2 Major. Most of them require exiting out to the main menu and reloading to temporarily fix. I'm certain there are more bugs that I have yet to find, but regardless of that, I have been enjoying the game.tldr: Little buggy for now, but incredible potential
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Fun mechanics, once you get your graphic settings figured out there is no lag (took me like 5 tries though). The story and fighting mechanics are super enjoyable and so far I've just had a blast managing my farm. Still not sure what the point of the campsites are though other than just fast travel points.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review even though I haven't played many hours yet because I want to say how much I love this game! Let me say, I DO NOT like Stardew, but Mirthwood feels like it does everything better than Stardew. I have seen reviews saying people don't like the combat, but in my opinion the combat fits the medieval fantasy setting well. It's slow and calculated instead of fast paced. BEAUTIFUL art! It feels like a genuine old-school RPG with how you start with nothing and make a name for yourself with surviving and trading. There's A LOT of quests. NO weapon durability. SAVE at anytime. Chat with townsfolk, customize your house, farm, forage, hunt, fish, mine, lumberjack, keep animals, etc!*ALSO* There are two options toggle-able in the menu - EASIER COMBAT & EASIER SURVIVAL - For those of you that want an easier approach!Overall Game in my opinion?9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Well 25 hours in, I really enjoy it. This probably should of been a EA release, given the level of bugs that need squashed and polish that needs. . .uh . . ..polished. . . still. It's good for a farming sim. Their "simulated world" idea seems unimplimented and overly ambitions for what they're actually capable of delivering. Combat is a simple system that exists. The skill feel like the need more "oomph", to really give them that "stardew skill/lifestyle" choice they're going for. IGN would give this a 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Booktok gals - this one is for you! Do you like being of an elf lineage discovering new lands on horse back AND being able to farm and romance/form relationships with NPCs? The game isn't completely polished, as other folks have mentioned, but the very small development team (of literally two people) know this and are continuously working on patches and updates. Even without everything being 1000% perfect, it's still a true joy to play. 10/10 recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the exploration, crafting, and building up your home. I look forward to finding out more of the story (cause I've been basically running around doing side quests and gathering resources) and future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing new farming sim that ticks a lot of boxes. An interesting evil / good alignment system, mysterious atmosphere and creatures, a vibrant village and economy to interact with, and a lot of great quality of life mechanics (such as crafting will use items in nearby containers without having to manually get them out). A solid 8/10 and expect that to rise as they add more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game to play, yes it does have some bugs but overall its not something to deter from. i like how the game just lets you go after the intro. There's really no hand holding on anything which i like. combat it alright, it need's more to it but hopefully they add more stuff to that the farming side is which i love sure it can be grindy for some things but its something i can enjoy doing for hours from raising crops, to making gear, making wine and rising farm animals, there's a lot to learn in the game im still finding things as i explore the wilds i recommend it, but i do notice stuff missing or not showing up but i do know the devs are updating  the game, but try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some bugs still, but the developers are on it! They are super responsive and open to feedback. But this definitely has an "early access" feel to it, though it's not labeled that way. It's got SO much potential though, and I'm excited to see it continue to grow. It's definitely playable!! I think that some people might not want to pay more than $20 for a game that isn't polished yet, so that's why I'm warning y'all. With how fast they're working, I bet it will be significantly smoother by December (2024).What I like about it:- 3rd person POV without feeling Cartoonish (refreshing!!)- cozy vibes but with mystery and some spook (lite spook)- it doesn't hold your hand. you gotta figure out some mechanics on your own. I'm still a bit puzzled by the social interactions honestly but maybe that's just par for the course lol- fishing is the perfect difficulty level imo- combat doesn't feel too hard. I think some people don't like that, but I appreciate it. I try to game for enjoyment, not to feel stressed or frustrated.What I don't love:- very very early on I was worried about running out of food with no way to get it without like starving for a day (if you run into this, don't fret!). It was also not clear at first what seeds could be planted in what season (they fixed that), or how long the seasons are.- confusion about morality. so far it seems the only way to earn morality is to donate to the church ?? It's giving ~Catholic indulgences~. I'm early in the game and often not sober when I play games so I very well could just be stupid :)- Also confused sometimes if "harvesting" stuff on other people's property is stealing or reduces morality? I don't think it is, because it does give the option to Steal sometimes, but I'm confused as to why sometimes it's theft and sometimes not (it's not like I have a relationship with any NPCs and it's not always public land)- There is very little difference, if any, between a crate/chest/barrel/loot/tool that you can interact with and one that you can't. In some way there's a degree of better Immersion that way, but I don't think I like that mechanic. You'll see what I mean when you play it. There will be a sword and shield just laying on the ground but you can't pick it up because it's just background??I don't see Mirthwood becoming one of those games I play over and over for hundreds of hours but I can see myself comfortably spending 50ish hours in this game minimum. Still seems like a decent deal for the price of entertainment per hour, etc. :) And again, I think this thing will keep growing!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: it was absolutely worth the wait, i'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys farming sims. i only have two complaints:1. as other people have said, it does a poor job of explaining itself. there is the bare minimum of guidance and no tutorials, and quests are sometimes unclear. it would be a lot more helpful to have quests marked on the map2. npc's take too long to talk to each other. i wanted to talk to an npc but she was talking to another one from morning till night and i was just stuck there waiting on her. npc's should chat for way less time with each other than with pc
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: A soft recommend. Feels more like an Early Access title. Positives - Art style and concept are amazing. Refreshing take on farming simulators with fun RPG elements. I really like the social element of the game.Negatives - Game can be buggy, combat needs some polish and the game stutters at times.Looking forward to seeing how this game develops over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Great Concept, input response could be a little better, combat is a little tougher than expected for a more casual game, and the survival aspect is a little more hardcore than expected as well. There are settings to make it easier in the options, but for the type of player they're really aiming at it's a little tough for a casual gamer. The loot system needs to be Buffed for sure, I do not appreciate getting an apple for fighting a pretty formidable foe. I'm sure they're already looking into this because loot in the demo was way better. All in all it's an awesome little world to be dropped into. I waited a good 3 months for this game and i'm very happy to be able to recommend this game to anyone looking to escape for a little while.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice top down rpg that feels really easy to pick up and play but it doesn't feel like a knock off of other games like it. You get started with a very nice prologue that teaches you the basics but it doesn't last too long before it shucks you off into the world to explore, fight, and craft. The character creation is also simple but doesn't feel plain either. There are multiple different creation options for your character, different areas you can start from, and a good amount of classes to choose from so replay value is there. Overall its a nice game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I've been excited to play this game since seeing it at PAX West 2023. I bought it on day one and have loved seeing how active the TWO devs are. It's still a little buggy, but they are very responsive in the discord and are pushing patches daily. I'm enjoying exploring the world greatly and can't wait to progress the storyline
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes a game comes along that is so atmospherically captivating, you know you are playing something special. What this game lacks in polish it makes up for in charm, intrigue and a uniquely immersive experience. I've only played 10 hours so far, but this is already one of my favourite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Not great, not terrible... it's grand.I find the combat to be a bit boring. The exploration aspects remind me of Bethesda stuff - can be rewarding, but likely will get your ass opened and handed back to you, meaning that the better option is to take the game boringly slow. Definitely not for the impatient gamer. I can see that this game is taking an interesting direction, but for now, after playing for a few hours, I think I'll give this game a rest until some improvements and optimisations are made. If you like Valheim, Skyrim, Gothic, or Stardew Valley you'll probably dig it.6/10 for me
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished my first play through and I have to say this game is amazing if you're someone like me who loves playing all aspects of a game. I've gotten all achievements except three, one for maxing all skills and two that I'll get on my morally good play through. I always do an "evil run" through first so my next, main save where I complete everything and go crazy with building / decor is my "good run"Combat is challenging but not impossible (can sometimes be cheesed by using your environment to get enemies wedged places or luring them to town) forcing you to put emphasis on crafting and collecting recipes from merchants which keeps me traveling and exploring always wondering what each vendor has, what I might find if I open some container off the path.Resources feel like a struggle the whole way right now because so much requires iron and wood all at the same time but the dev's have been listening and making adjustments. These resources to respawn every few days and as you learn routes for collecting them it becomes a lot easier to farm, but you'll feel it just starting before you learn the map.The decor is lovely and comes in multiple styles and if you fund it with farming it is very easy to afford anything you want. As you unlock different material swatches for the rooms walls and floors in your house they save and can be freely swapped between which was a nice surprise.So far you can breed multiple types of animals and it doesn't look like they die if unhappy which is good because the stable is currently not working which was a little worrying after I bought a Unicorn but my faithful steed has been fine without one.All in all I think this game has a great vibe, great potential, and I'll be adding it to my favorites and starting my next play through soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: YO! I am an OG gamer. Really!  I am 53 and my first console was an Atari 5200. So yeah, OG!Anywho, it has been yeeeears since a game challenged me as this one is. I admit that I was apprehensive when I learned that it was 'dark'. I don't care for scary games. However, for this game, I will put my big girl shorts on. The developers did not make it easy and I am here for it. I thought that I was going to be able to open the map and find hints. NOPE! You will have to use the old noggin which keeps us all young in mind.If there is a Challenging Game of the Year award, Mirthwood wins hands down.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Cosy lil game. Reminds me a lot of my most treasured games from growing up. It’s definitely inspired by fable, the humour and the relationship you can build with the npc’s is heavily inspired by fable and I’m all for it! The overall art style and the way it plays reminds me of stardew valley. And I at times project zomboid. The soundtrack is beautiful I love medieval type music and this hits the spot. I’m addicted. Just wish I had more time to play it!!Don’t get me wrong it definitely feels like an early access game but the developers are quick to put out fixes and updates and it’s only been a few days since release. Give them some support and buy it. You won’t regret it
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: While the game has some things to improve (melee combat, especially), It ticks so many boxes for me:- The visual style is great.- I like the world and the lore a lot!- It is a good platform for solo roleplay. Your character doesn't seem to have too many narrative restrictions.- It's surprisingly relaxing and doesn't feel grindy at all (like some similar games).
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I played the demo and really enjoyed it and played the full game when it was released on Nov. 6 and it was even better! I like the medieval theme and general life-sim components, but something that stood out to me was the combat. I think the way combat works could use some improvements, but overall I like the way Mirthwood does combat when compared with similar games. The developers seem super responsive to user needs and have implemented patches since release to address minor issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: ive been absolutely obsessed with playing this game! I consider myself a cozy gamer and this absolutely fits into that category! I can tell by the amount of details that everything was done meticulously and with a lot of care! I would like to see more options for decor and seeds for farming, I know its still early but i cant wait for families and romance options!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into RPGs that give off those Skyrimesque vibes and you love that nostalgic GameBoy Sims feel, this game is seriously a hidden treasure you should check out! I’ve been super excited for its release ever since I first stumbled upon it a few months back, and I gotta say, it totally lives up to the buzz. It’s a really charming 2D RPG that hit me right in the feels with all that nostalgia. Just picture a fun mix of the classic GameBoy Sims style mashed up with the open-world vibe of Skyrim—it’s such a blast! That said, I've run into some crashes while playing, which can be a little annoying. Plus, on a personal note, I really wish there were more voices for the characters. There’s just a lot of reading, and it kinda breaks the immersive flow of the game for me. But what really shines is the commitment from the two-person dev team behind this project. You can totally sense their love for the game and the community, especially when you hop on their Discord channel. If you want a fresh take on RPGs with a nice nostalgic touch, definitely give this game a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up yesterday knowing nothing about it and I'm so glad I did! Knowing that it's made by a smaller studio it's important to remember how much work it takes to make these titles. It's not 100% perfect but I couldn't tell you a game I've played in the last decade that has been perfect at launch. With all of that being said it's a solid game with a lot of room for growth. I'm looking forward to the planned updates that have been announced and can't wait to see what else there is to discover!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: The vibe of this game is just fantastic. The visuals is just right up my alley!The combat is rather simple but in a good phase where you need to be tactical.The farm sim part does it job good enough and there are touches like not having to reseed after harvesting that I personally like.The perk system is a great idea and gives the game some depth. Reminds me of the card system in Fallout 76.There is a cooldown for changing perks so you can not just exploit it on the go.The devs have been pumping out fixes and some times they push out several fixes a day, which is amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say that the game isn't perfect, it needs a few tweaks here and there. That being said however, I think this is my new favorite game. It's easy to get immersed in the world and want to explore (normally this is hard for me), I love that the animals reproduce when you have male & female on your farm (this makes their gold cost totally worth it), I'm actually excited to see what else I can do in the game and can't wait for DEV updates.I would like to see chests having higher rewards as well as killing monsters/bandits etc. I also think there needs to be a couple updates with how much wood,stone and ore you receive as I have harvested almost everything on my farm and now am struggling to get enough for 1 animal stall. I think it would also be beneficial to have a relationships panel somewhere as I am loosing track with how many people there are (I love how many people its just hard to keep track of my relationships). Id also love to see even more animal variation (maybe I haven't gotten far enough yet).Overall the game is very good for just coming out! I'm excited to see what the DEVs have in store as I think this could be HUGE competition to Stardew Valley and other games like it!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so, I've been apprehensive about the game, especially since the delay in release. I'm actually glad they delayed the release; when I started it on the release date, it was clunky AF. I can't imagine what would have happened if it released in September, it would have been tragic. Anyways, the game is great, the devs (small team) have patched some of the problems, with more work to come. I appreciate the no-hand-holding style of play, have fun farming, mining, battling, etc. I'm looking forward to some more depth such as; NPC interactions, more buildings, refined combat, map improvements. The map needs more detail and the ability for the player to zoom in on areas or to mark waypoints. It would be interesting to have the ability to map 'permanent waypoints' that the player can save and title with a name of their own. Anyways, I'm glad I've downloaded it, even if it needs some refining. Recommend, 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: He's only mostly dead, which means he's slightly alive. The game has it's issues but is a very charming take on the typical farming sim we've been seeing. Opening sequence has this cutsey little papercraft style only for you to see someone impaled on screen moments later. It's refreshingly dingy compared to the hyper colorful worlds of Stardew and Mistria, but not so dark that it's not still cute and quirky in it's own ways. But it does have it's set of issues- a bit buggy here and there with the AI pathing, lagging, and the way the settings work is just weird. You have to basically refresh the game to make your screen size change. A few quests get a bit stuck until you pick something up or repeat an action to make them take, but it's nothing game breaking in my 4 hours of play so far. Nothing that is so far out of field it shouldn't be tolerable or unexpected from a smaller game dev. I'm sure they'll get to it. The combat is... something. The fishing minigame is also something. They're challenging in their own right and I am interested in seeing how it changes as I progress.I will say one thing that kinda got me was the lack of tutorials. You are balls to the walls on literally everything. Click and find out what happens, and don't be a wuss about it. Also the NPCs? Npcs may find your attire cute, funny, or repulsive and react in kind. Certain dealers only work with you if you're good/evil and it's an interesting experience to see what causes that to flux. I will continue playing and see where it goes.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: For everyone who loved everything about Stardew Valley EXCEPT the farming part, this is the game for you (although I love SDV and the farming in it). For an early access, this thing is robust right out of the gate but this is in essence an adventure game. Think Link to the Past that also has farming, crafting, and minor yet addictive base maintenance mechanics. Bugs and sometimes a crash or two but I looked past all that because it's SO fun. Can't wait for new updates/patches to hit this thing.Also it runs good on Steam Deck even though it's not verified just yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: So I've put quite a bit of time into this game. I am still learning but the framework is intriguing. The quest/map indicators I'm still getting sorted out but the main story and other stories are quite interesting. Truthfully I'm having so much fun exploring.11/12/24 updateThis game is wonderful. The developers actively interact with you on their discord and have been patching daily since release. I'm not sure which I love more the story of the game or the experience with their team.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this game not knowing what to expect, and honestly would have been happy if it had just been a cute medieval farming sim with some RPG elements. But it is so much more than that! The world is well realized and exploration is an absolute joy! Farming, crafting, and combat are engaging without being tedious or getting bogged down in minutiae. Great game that scratches that exploration, open world, life-sim itch in a fresh and fun way!! Highly recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the game so far!A comforting mix of Skyrim vibes, Echos of the Plum Grove, and seamless decorating! It has Sims like social interactions, which I actually really like with the card actions you choose. People react to you too! It all meshes pretty well, but I could see some refining details that could be used, or some quality of life improvements.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I have put in a VERY limited amount of time but.... for a game put together by a two dev team this is really impressive. Graphics: loveStory/Dialogue: decent/GoodMechanics: goodCombat: FineCompared to a lot of other RPS/SIMs that are generally overpriced and stale, this is a breath of fresh air and great bang for your buck.... But by far the most impressive feat is the insanely fast response time by the devs to fix issues and the fantastic discord discussion page to take feedback/suggestions. I can not stress this second part enough as in an age where it feels like big game dev's are not listing to their audience, these guys are breaking their backs to make fixes and improvements in real time. Bravo to the Devs for putting together a fantastic game and now community! if you have the spare cash definitely check this game out and support these guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Currently cannot play. Game destroying bug that hard crashes my computer when in stat menu or inventory with controller and joy to key that turns buttons to keystrokes. Has 0 controller capabilities and freezes when swapping menus. Fix this or you're game toast. cant even speak on any part of the game if I am unable to play it. 0 out of 10 if it lock up this fast. Fix it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Very happy with the game so far, incredibly cozy at times and thrilling at others.Theres something special about setting up your homestead, planting your crops and clearing your lawn before going out on an adventure exploring the land and killing beasts.Some performance-hickups and non-gamebreaking bugs on Steam Deck and there seems to be need for optimizations overall but the devs appear incredibly passionate and attentive to feedback. Patches are rolling out regularly and it feels like the game is getting more polished by the second.We could have something very special on our hands here and with the roadmap we've gotten from the developers, the future looks very exiting also.Recommended ✅
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps should have been released in early access, but for a two person dev team this is highly impressive. For the price tag, it is well worth getting lost in the beauty of Mirthwood. The art style paints a story-book fantasy world, with a fantastic balance of intrigue and cosiness, from solving mysteries to making soup. Like such soup, some patience is required, as this game has some stuttering/bugs, but so far nothing I have encountered has been groundbreaking. Overall however from my first 5 hours, I am highly impressed with the unique charm of this title and look forward to many more soups to come, oh and multiplayer, whenever that may be!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good lovely art style and overall game play but it feels unfinished. When fighting a bandit when you spent ages beating them only to get say some bread when looting...when you can easily take their armour, sword or even the shield makes no sense whatsoever. Health potions are not easily found and relies on you making them which will take time and a lot of patience. You will be grinding a lot in this game and I mean getting lot of wood or stone your mouse (if you are playing keyboard/mouse) will not forgive you with the amount of clicks you need to make. Back to the looting system which for me is a big problem...you do so much work and get very very little back. You see things lying around and nobody about and it says you are stealing the item but how can you be caught when no-one sees you? The game also does lag a lot at times but its not a major problem.You would think I would not like the game with these things going wrong but it has a lot of potential and its a lovely game but needs to correct these things to make it feel more finished. Also yes as many people have mentioned the tutorial...well their really isnt one....you are lot of the time on your own.I would still recommend this though...but maybe not buy it just yet...until a few patches.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is rough around the edges now. It's going to be expanded, and it's going to be polished. Even given the current concerns, though, I have been enjoying it. I enjoy a game that lets me wander at my own pace and generally enjoy things, and Mirthwood is very good at that. I love the art style. Combat is clunky right now, for sure, but it isn't so bad that I don't want to play the game. I would like to see more clarity on how to advance skills and on the rate of xp gain in each skill, and I'd definitely like a clear intro to the social system.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game so far. It is a nice little relaxing game to pass the time with and grind. Being able to just make your own adventure is the biggest appeal. Has a couple of bugs right now that need to be fixed. Horses not being able to be assigned to stable and not being able to rotate items. I am sure that when these are fixed, I will be on designing my farm.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! The art is beautiful. Most of the gameplay is pretty farming and crafting and harvesting. I still haven't really got the hang of chatting with NPC's but they make great back up against big nasties early game that you can't handle yourself. Initially I wasn't in love with the archery system, but I'm getting the hang of it and doing a lot better taking on enemies without my NPC back up. This game does not hold your hand. I'm still having a hard time finding where to go for some quests, but that's also part of the charm. You have to really explore and look around and *pay attention*. I think they've struck a nice balance.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game to play casually sitting back and enjoying the story of a good isometric RPG. Pleasant artwork and music make for a great beginning. The narration gives the feel of a good story being told. During the prologue, you are asked to gather items to make for your family dinner. You are faced with your first hard choice. I suspect this game has many choices that affect your story. You make dinner and awake to your village burned to the ground and your family telling you to get on a boat and leave. I still don't know why they kicked you off the continent.  so far It is fun interacting with NPCs and leveling up your Charisma stat. The conversation is a mini game all in itself with each NPC interaction. It's fun and simple learning it. You have many stats that are directly affected by your choices. Your  is always in question as there are many items to steal in the first town. There is also a  scale that measures your popularity and influence. Lots of exploring to do and you only see whats on screen. No looking ahead of your position or zooming. During the Prologue you get a taste of  and it is what you would expect of a 2D ISO RPG. Combat does allow for dodge rolls, juking, blocking and parrying which is more than most titles will give.   This is where I found frustration. The UI is attractive and the menus initially do not appear too overwhelming. I prefer gamepads in games like this and the store page lists support but it is very flawed. The game struggles when switching from M&K to gamepad and back. You ask why is there switching? Because some screens (the skill screen specifically) show information that is cut off at the bottom expecting you to scroll up to read it all. The game does not interpret this on the controller. In fact most times when scrolling in needed, the controller just fails and you have to exit that menu and come back in. This happens when looting especially. Usually you can use the D-pad to navigate but not the case. A real issue is the highlighted option is sometimes difficult to see believe it or not. Using a controller make the highlight disappear altogether at times.  I will update this review after I play a little M&K. I hope the gameplay issues get resolved in future updates as this title can be a fun one to play through. I believe it is priced due to content but who gives a s*** about content is I am not having fun playing it. Wait for a better sale price and after more updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 10 hours in and really enjoying it! Has elements of Valheim that I really enjoy, crop growing and tending, mining, crafting, weapon building, etc, really allows for a varied experience. Combat is fun and the enemies are perfect for your current level, not too hard but still takes some skill to overcome. The dev team is quick to respond to little issues and are really quick to post updates - kudos to them. Really looking forward to seeing how the game progresses!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I am disappointed by the bugs and how unpolished it was on release, however there is no denying that the game is beautiful, made with love and has huge potential. I really hope the developers fix all the issues promptly. So far I've had good eight hours of fun with this game, with occasional problems caused by bugs. One of them was game-breaking and I had to start from the beggining, fortunately this happened very early on in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games lately that has held my attention and actually been fun. I look forward to playing it and thats just been really rare these last few years (why do most games suck so bad now??). I don't get why some people are having issues with it though, it stutters every once in a while when I'm running across the map but it's not bad at all for me and hardly ever happens and I'm running it on the highest settings. Also, so many games are rushed out lately but this one feels like a finished game, I've had zero bugs or complaints.Anyway, if you like Minecraft, Harvest Moon, and Stardew Valley, you'll definitely enjoy this. I recommend it to anyone who's into those types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Just found out this is a two person team, which gives me hope that this is a passion project and will receive many updates in the future. It feels a little empty, but I believe that will change.UPDATE: It is still going good so far, the biggest issue that I am noticing is that the melee combat feels very unresponsive. It just doesn't feel very good to use. There are times where I come out of a roll and try to attack only for it to attack facing away from the enemies. After attack or roll, there are brief pauses that don't feel smooth. It makes melee combat harder than it should be and not very fun. The ranged weapons don't really have this issue though.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I WANT to like this game. I tried to play it. I ran around and fought some stuff but then I had no idea of where to go or what to do. I looked up a video online and finally found some tools. I thought, "Alright! I'm gonna chop some trees!" .... I couldn't use the tools I found. I really tried to play it but I couldn't even anything. It's pretty though.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game! Yes, it has some bugs, but the devs are working hard to fix them (it's just a team of 2 people, give them a break). It seriously doesn't hold your hand, you're on your own for a lot of things, but it's kind of a nice change. It has fast travel, great crafting, farm animals, combat, quests, and the art style is just amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood is overall a great edition to the farming life sim genre. I really like the art style and the different ways you can play by selecting your profession and background create more opportunity for new runs and repeatability.  My biggest complaint would be the combat, it's just boring and if you have the patience you can easily kite everything and just kill it with a bow
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: It's addicting! Reminds me of playing Story of seasons:friends of mineral town on GBA 20 years ago. Beautiful art style. It's more casual on farming but quit intensive when fight against enemies,the music is too scary! (I was calmer when playing Sekiro: shadow die twice) .Need little bit more guides and instructions. It really took me a while to figure out how to do fishing and how to feed chickens( Need build a mill to ground wheat to make chicken food, DO NOT USE HAY or it will keep showing"miss chicken food"). There are a coupe of bugs but nothing serious. I love this game, definitely worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I quite like this game, it does have a lot of nice things going for it. Art is deffo one of the biggest. Faces look bit weird tho. Maybe it's those tin tin eyes that don't quite blend with the realism of everything else.Combat is weird. But once you get bow, you stand a chance! As long as you figure out where the hitbox is. Social system is interesting, even if I don't quite get it yet. Maybe everyone just likes to be scared, insulted and complained to. Oh and this game stutters sometimes more than me when I'm put on a spot to say something clever,
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: This project can be come a GEM.Done by 2 headed team it feels and plays already quite solid but still needs some baking.Check out my Testplay Day 01 - Day 20+: Here are my major points: - interaction with the npcs is fun using that interaction tools but they conversation has no real meaning other than just pushing points to get you to like, there is no real bonding happening nor a cool story behind talking with them- cooking interface is meh, having to search every time WHAT you can cook while scrolling through what you cant- the combat feels wanky and could use target locking so you dont dodge roll into the wrong direction / give upward downwards and diagonal attack angles as well- boss fights fell extremely underwhelming no special phases and attack patterns + the very underwhelming loot drop or giving you something usefulAnd some other small odds and end.At this state I give it a solid 5/10 and would say it is an average experience BUT IT CAN BECOME A GEM... *fingers crossed for some strong patches*
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: the game i've been waiting for since 4 month ago. a farming sim game with a survival and adventorous element make this game a perfect one.but i think the game still need a polish a little bit more since a perormance bug in the game (probably because of my old gen PC),the farming mechanic in this game is simple yet satisfying, and the farm size is a quite big for you to create your own dream farm.ithe game still not perfect in a matter of performance, but i can understand since they only 2 man devleoper making this awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo back when it was first released and I also played the beta test version - so I knew what I was getting into when buying this game.  I've greatly enjoyed my time playing all versions of this game.  I'm currently only in summer on my playthrough, but I look forward to seeing the different seasons.  The graphics in this game are gorgeous.  The exploring is fun.  The crafting feels rewarding.  The combat is serviceable; nothing special.  Farming is nice and simple.  I've not done much with the socializing as I picked rat catcher as my profession.  I look forward to progressing with the main story as I haven't focused much on it yet. Overall a very fun game that I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing for about 6 hours and I'm really enjoying it. The progression seems pretty well balanced. More difficult monsters and enemies spawn farther from your first camp. Finding ore to upgrade tools and craft better weapons is a pain. There is no was to create map markers. There are markers for most areas of interest but caves aren't marked and I forget where they are. It has some stuttering issues and I've crashed a few times. Maybe it's time to update my GPU. "It can it run Mirthwood" will be the new flex. I'm on a 4090 BTW.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: First I played the demo and was not totally sold on it. Then they opened up the playtest and I gave it a shot. I could not stop playing. Even with the bugs, I found it very enjoyable and I loved that the team was so responsive.Now the game is out and I still have not stopped playing it when I have downtime. I will agree that the combat system is not the best in my opinion, but once I started using the bow instead, I found the game a lot better. I love the day/night cycle does not impact your play experience. I find the art beautiful. I'm not totally sold on the dialogue and chat aspect, but it's growing on me. I think this game is just very different from a lot of games that released lately. I think if you like the idea of survival, but also farming/crafting and selling, this may be worth a try. This game has SO much possibility.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo version and bought the game on release day.  I really like it so far and I am always amazed to see what even a small team can do. It is a game you can enjoy in your own pace, you can have challenges and adventure, but a peacefull quiet time spending doodeling as well. You can feel the heartblood of this project. I'm really looking forward experiencing the progress of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically leave reviews but I'm so impressed that this was done by a 2 person team. I feel inclined! This is a great game. I hope I'm not wrong in saying this feels very similar to Stardew Valley so if you're a fan dive into this one.There are of course some bugs but like I said earlier, this is a 2 person team. They appear to be very active with the community and are doing their best to update as frequently as possible. My best advice for anyone stuck making this decision is to join their discord. It's a very active discord from what I can tell. I do wish this game had some coop. My girlfriend is highly interested and I think it would be very fun to work on our medieval farm together. BUT to my understanding this is something they are working on. This gets me stoked for the future of this game!Very cool to be a part of a growing game, especially from the very beginning. I wish you two the best of luck! I got your backs if you need any testers!
_childDocuments_.name: Mirthwood

_childDocuments_.review: Mirthwood is an open world  life sim, survival, crafting, farming, exploration etc game that manages to balance all of its elements extremely well. You truly can just focus on the parts of the game you want to play, and play the game your way. The game's systems are well designed and the game play loops are very entertaining and addictive, when it's time to quit playing, good luck - it has that "one more thing" factor big time. If you think at all this is the kind of game that might appeal to you, you are probably correct - get it! And join the discord too because the game also has a cool community.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good survival crafter viewed from  isometric perspective, kinda like don't starve. _childDocuments_.review: Great little game, I just completed it and am thoroughly glad I got it.  Yes, it may have some bugs, but seriously, this game is made by two people.  It's not like it's being made by a huge company and then filled with game breaking bugs, like Cyberpunk, lol.  The bugs are MINOR in comparison.  Those who are complaining about this game just have nothing better to do with themselves.   As for the game, it's not unlike Stardew Valley and others of the genre, but definitely is different than those.  It is a game that takes place in the medieval time period with a twist of fantasy.  Good story(ies) are found within, some actually quite sad.  The graphics are pleasing, as is the music, and overall ambiance, and I LOVE the narrator's voice.  I really appreciate that the game had a demo, otherwise, I may have considered it as just another farming type game, thank you.  Good job to the developers so far, and I can't wait to see how this game progresses.

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird to like a game but only have criticisms for it. There is every kind of game mechanic but they all lack depth. I'm hoping they will be fleshed out over time but right now the game is nothing ground breaking and my enjoyment of it is mostly carried by it's setting and art style.My biggest concern is the  . There are no long term goals that you are really rewarded for pursuing. There is a community center type system but other than that the main things to grind for can easily be ignored. There are too many things immediately available to you. From the beginning you can explore the whole map. All other farm plots have no cost once they are discovered. You can use the starter gear and the equipment you find until you have the resources to craft the best weapons and armor, but you'll never really need them since you will have explored everything by then. Money is mostly spent on buying farm animals and buildings, which are just ways of making more money. It's just not very engaging.Second point I want to make is about the social system, which feels fundamentally flawed. It doesn't have the flair and intricacies of the system it's modeled after. These NPCs have no charm or overt personalities and feel completely lifeless. I like that they tried it but I don't think it works in a game that's doesn't revolve completely around it. I'm not sure how they could fix this without uprooting the entire thing. I didn't want to bring up Stardew since it's so unfair but I think socializing was simple and effective and could be an improvement over the current system.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has really good potential. And what's the deal with the market?).I'm still enjoying it all, especially the exploring and homesteading parts. The art is lovely and I don't mind the 2d effects some people are struggling with. _childDocuments_.review: Rating 6/10Why?I personally feel the creators should have waited longer to fine tune stuff before releasing. It's a good game, thus far, but really grindy and some stuff doesn't make sense. E.g. an iron axe cannot cut down trees but can chop down tree stumps. Also, a lot of players like me want generational/legacy gaming- get married, have a family, die and pass it on..  but this is still under development for next year. So this feels more like an early access game than a fully developed game.The good:Love the graphics and the quests involved. I enjoy the way you can farm, but not really worry about farming and explore the map of the world.I also like the fact that there are bandits and thieves which you need to run away from or overcome. You also can sleep at inns, or in certain campsites while on your travels.The bad:The draw in for this game for me was "choose who you want to be". And then there's images of different characters, one with a bow, another with a heart on his chest, a guy with a shovel and a sword, an assassin type and an artist.For the life of me, I still can't figure out how not to be the guy with the shovel and a sword. I was hoping you could choose to be a woodcutter, a herbalist, a blacksmith etc... but it's not the case at all.Another thing is combat control is one of my major peeves. The character at (many) times refuses to face the enemy and even when I'm pressing the key,  they'll still face the wrong direction and this ticks me off royally. And, in as much as I love the bandits and  thieves concept, they pop up too frequently for a game where I just want to build up my little farm (Well I really wanted to be a herbalist, but farming was the default).The inconsistency of crafting is also annoying to me. I gather materials, go to the workbench and voila, without blinking it's in my inventory. Whereas I need to smelt iron, it takes a couple of hours. I'd rather see them be busy crafting on the workbench rather than it just pop up. Same with rebuilding the house. It annoyed me that it was suddenly built after the materials were gathered. I wish there was more to it, e.g. build up the kitchen first and a toilet then build the next room you choose. Heck, even get the woodcutter dude to come help you build and have actual actions for building rather than it popping up and ready.I also don't understand why there is no friendship page interface, nor names of the towns I visited on the map. Anddd... even though I've greeted them and we chat a little, some still say "You're a new face."The Ugly:For some reason, there is no option to adjust the ambient music. There is only one master volume under settings and nothing for voice, nature sounds, etc. If I put this low, everything goes low. I have to play it with the sound off which I dislike since I enjoy the nature and voice sounds.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine this: You, a bottle of brandy, red g-string, a mink coat, and smooth jazz on the radio. A level of coziness seldom seen. This is what it's like when you play Mirthwood in the area around your farmstead. Now imagine that the door of your cozy abode swings open and a pack of vicious wolves come flying through your living room; a veritable tornado of fangs and claws. You spring to your feet as the mink coat falls from your shoulders revealing your now brandy-covered glistening form. You have just enough time to arm yourself with a glass shard from the now broken brandy bottle. You spring forward, make-shift weapon in hand, and strike out violently at all those who would disturb your coziness. This is what it feels like when you're outside of the area around your farmstead.All of this to say: It's a good game and you should probably try it.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game so far. I play on an Asus ROG Ally. The cheapest version. Giving the game a thumbs up because I think it great and will continue to be great. But, sadly, I can't play anymore. I made it through the tutorial fine on High setting, shadows off, with between 30-40 frames. Which coming from decades of console and poor person PCs is fine by me. Honestly 25 up is acceptable if annoying sometimes. Sacrifices and all that. The sad part now. First real day of the game and it was raining, even when I lowered the settings to the lowest option I only made it roughly 50 steps from my front door before the game froze so hard I had to do a hard reset. _childDocuments_.review: More like mixed.It's very rough for the moment (to be fair, it seems like some time in early-access would have been necessary) but the devs are active and the game is interesting. The best strategy is to kite everything with your bow. Most creatures will simply follow you, taking hits after hit, the TTK is insane. If the enemy has too much health, i just drag it to the village and let the NPCs do my job.Melee fighting could be interesting but enemies dodge constantly which is really annoying and there is some kind of lock to the enemy happening, which is annoying too and render the roll useless (you always end up facing the wrong direction after a roll). _childDocuments_.review: I have to say that I love what I've experienced so far, there is definitely charm to this game. The customization is freeing and cozy while the exploration leaves you wanting to explore even more depths of this world. But that being said there are some clunky bits to this game as well and I do not see anyone mentioning them. Here are the clunky bits I came across in the game:-Bug where sound is not heard when chopping trees when in town-Bug where path-making does not work after using "path eraser" tool-Bug where if you "jester" at an NPC and pull up their info after, the info pops up anytime you try to jester from then on-Be careful with keybinds as if you change one it might break something else with no mention of it since you cannot change all keybinds for every action-Bug where if you have enough money for an object you still might not be able to buy it, unless you restart your game-Menu looks unpolished and pop up menu when interacting in the world starts off incredibly small and hard to see until you change the display in the settings-HUD is bad and if you use a consumable from the inventory there is no way to see how much it healed you since the inventory menu is in the way, it should show all 3 stats in inventory menu if you plan to use consumables from that menu to see how it affects you.-HUD is bad and when someone gives you something from a mission there's no way to see that you got it unless you check your inventory later to find it (if you skip dialogue like me, this is a problem because you might forget where or when you got something in your inventory)-Some other things I probably forgot about...Overall I rate this as a solid and fun experience. Although I will say that the bugs can make it a little unpleasant at times, especially when you have to restart your game 10 times in a play through just to get something so small to work. None of these bugs are really game-breaking I would say, as you can carry on for the most part without restarting your game, but it is still annoying enough to proceed through the game with broken assets/elements.

name: SLUDGE LIFE 2
detailed_description: Big Mud is missing! Everyone's favourite rapping frog has vanished, and his closest homie Ghost (that's you) is on a mission to find him. SLUDGE LIFE 2 whisks you away to Ciggy City Suites, a luxurious multi-floor hotel heaving with secrets, gadgets, gags, peculiar characters, and ugly corporate architecture to makeover with your spray can. SPRAY TO WIN A hundred tag spots are hidden around the Ciggy City Suites and surrounding area, including some so well hidden we almost feel bad about it. Hunt them down, spray them, and let the soulless GLUG corporation know what's what. MEET AND GREET There are three times more NPCs in SLUDGE LIFE 2 than in the original game, which means even more citizens, fellow taggers, corporate stooges, and other assorted oddballs to meet and interact with as you explore a truly weird and wonderful open world. TOOLED UP New items? We got 'em! With the Double Js you can double jump and sprint, while the Portable Launcher lets you throw yourself dramatically into the air. There are more, but we don't want to spoil the surprise. Oh, and all the items from the original are back too. SOUND OFF SLUDGE LIFE 2 features a bunch of new music too — including five killer new tracks from Big Mud himself. Explore the island, find the hidden master tapes, and bless your headphones with fresh beats and rhymes from the most amphibious rapper in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: NGL, me and Sludge Life 2 nearly came to blows when, right outta the gate, Dog Lover was set to "No". But y'know what, we got past that, and now we're sludgy as ever. What is this game? Bro, I WISH I KNEW. It's a first person exploration game, it's a convo collection, it's a rap manager simulator, it's a spraypaint extravaganza... but summarising the experience of Sludge Life is like trying to ask Big Mud to not drop bars. Ain't happenin'.Did you like the first? You'll like this. Did you hate the first? You won't like this. It's weird, it's funny, it's obscure, there's plenty to do, and at this price, complaining makes you one of those weirdos that doesn't dust their apartment enough.First 5 mins of the game, I solved an immediate and pretty funny puzzle, found a dude poopin', tripped balls for a solid 20s, and took a pic of a dog. I want nothing more from any game.

I enjoyed the game and didn't mind paying full price to support the developers, but if you are on the edge, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Great follow-up to a fantastic game. It's more streamlined than the first one and improves on several features. _childDocuments_.review: For a sequel to a game that didn't really need a sequel, I was pleasantly surprised by how much fun I had.  We got a new map with both new and returning characters as well as new tools to help us navigate the SLUDGE. It has the same humor as the first game so you'll probably get a good chuckle here and there. Not to mention how immaculate the vibes are. In a nutshell, if you enjoyed the first game, you'll probably enjoy this one just as much.
_childDocuments_.name: SLUDGE LIFE 2

_childDocuments_.review: Sludge life 2 is an amazing follow up to the first sludge life game, Althogh you dont need to play it for plot or mechanics reasons. I would recommend playing it first then coming to the 2nd game. This game like the first, was beyond fun to play through and hunt everything down. Unlike the first one, the map is massive. When playing and i hit the boundary of Cig City i thought, ok this is map size, seems like first one. Then you leave and its like wow. Is this still a indy company?  The items in this game build off the first game and have some new ones as well. The glider is back same with warper, but they have so much more uses now, With the map being a lot more horizontal vs vertical, quickly teleporting to the top to re-drop was well thought out. The NPC's in this game are amazing, You will come across unique rooms filled with interesting characters with one off dialog's that will either leave you questioning everything or laughing your butt off. The movement in this game was a bit frustrating at times trying to parkour tight spaces but became much easier with the boots item. The price for amount of content in the game was completely worth it. Highly recommend to anyone that thinks the trailer looks fun.
_childDocuments_.name: SLUDGE LIFE 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the first one and wanted more, here you go! If you never played Sludge Life I recommend trying the first one since both of these games are identical and essentially the same thing which to me was not a bad thing because I enjoy Sludge Life for the more relaxed gaming and vibe experience. The new map was neat! I liked the references they made to their other games as well since I played and beat them all. I liked the new location to explore although to be honest I prefer the first games map a little more, this one felt like it went for more of verticality while the first game went more for a spread out space.I also felt like the dialogues this time around were a little less and shorter? The first game I believe characters  had more things to say which I think for a short game like this is important since you focus on all the experiences you get but regardless both games still had the funny and wacky dialogues.I also feel like the art for the tags was more creative in the first game but the big co-op murals were still pretty sick. It's really nice to be able to see new taggers and some familiar faces as well.Now the new items were nice! The double jump is a really nice addition but at the same time, the first game made you think a little more on how to approach an area to reach places you needed to tag which is appreciated since tagging spots act like puzzles, so that was sort of missing from this game since its so much easier to climb things, I still had to think for like 3 spots but overall I think they should of made it a little more thought provoking. one last thing, Overall I still enjoyed my experience, this one definitely has more things to collects and see. I always enjoy the laid back chill vibe experience that you get from playing Sludge Life and the world they created with it and this game delivers on that.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game and consequently I liked this one too. But this time the experience was different, it didn't have the same impact. There isn't much newer stuff and this game on overall felt the samey. Don't get me wrong, it's still a good game, it just feels pointless. The first game felt more organic...The endings of the first game for instance felt more substantial and meaningful, I won't go into details, but the new endings they're nice, but they're mostly just pandering for the old fans. They're awesome and everything but it feels kinda random.And if this game is supposed to be bigger, that's not what my experience was. There were more interesting stuff on the first game than this one, and to be really honest, I don't think this game was really worth the time. Now that I think about it, I'll leave a negative review, this is more of the same but smaller and not as well crafted. I would leave a mixed review if there was an option, as though my experience was not bad, but I don't think I would be bothered to play this game if I knew what it was, a remix.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a bit of a sophomore slump since this game feels more like DLC than a standalone sequel. It takes the original map of SLUDGE LIFE and makes it less dense, less interesting, less challenging, less funny, and overall less engaging. Giving the player more items is nice in theory, sure, but they take away all the challenge of the first game (). After getting  right off the bat, there were never any tags or areas that I had a hard time reaching.  While I had a hard time putting the original down, I have a hard time picking this one up, and I feel like I overpaid at 50% off.
_childDocuments_.name: SLUDGE LIFE 2

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the advertising this isn't any bigger or "denser" than the first game.  If anything there are less gags and interesting things to stumble on. The opening zone is interesting, but outside of this it's a considerably less interesting remix of the original with much less verticality and fewer ways to creatively traverse the environment. The new items don't really add much to the experience.It's more of the same, but without the fresh feeling of the original, closer to a DLC than a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: SLUDGE LIFE 2

_childDocuments_.review: Nice walking sim. Having played the first game few years ago, SLUDGE LIFE 2 feels familiar. There’s no real story or specific goal in this game, except to explore the city, enjoy hilarious and ridiculous small talks, discover fun and weird sights, and spray graffiti. Smoking is a central theme in the game—everyone from children to cats, dogs, baby birds, and even crabs can smoke.You’ll have access to various tools like double-jumper shoes and trampolines to help you reach difficulty areas. It took me around 3.5 hours to explore most of the content, including the polluted areas, but if you’re aiming for 100% achievements, it should take about 5 hours.Overall, I recommend this game for its quirky and unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: SLUDGE LIFE 2

_childDocuments_.review: Another round of running about, tagging walls, eating slugs, learning about the world, and encountering unusual strangers.Sludge Life 2 comes across as more of an episodic sequel, meaning that it sorta slides into the existing story and there doesn’t appear to be much innovation on the original’s strengths or gameplay. I’d say the primary difference is the change in structure from a series of islands to one big central area with regions of interest on its outskirts. That said, Sludge Life 2 still nails that sense of organic, open-ended, interest-driven exploration in a bleak, polluted, corporate-controller world. Once again, it's cool how all sorts of small environmental narratives tie into each other all around the map. It really makes the hotel/island feel like a part of one ongoing world. Give the game a try, although Sludge Life 1 does appear to be required reading for a lot of the sequel’s context.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the first part, I enjoyed the full SLUDGE LIFE 2 Demo and SLUDGE LIFE 2.I was really looking forward to this game. However, I was expecting a bigger map and more characters (although there were new taggers and more characters and there were references to the first part).Few new things were added:- Jjs - sneakers that allow you to run faster when you press Shift and allow you to do a double jump- BUB-O - helmet, which is needed only once, in order to pass one of the endings- NECROSHROOM - just like the helmet, you only need it once to pass the same ending for which you need the helmet- MINILAUNCHER - the thing that throws you high up, appears ONLY at the very end, and therefore doesn't make much sense.They've added new taggers that you can do graffiti combos with.The map didn't seem very big, I got through the game 3-4 hours faster than the first part. They also added a mini-game called GATO MAGO, which was shown in the demo version of sludge life 2.I liked the story itself, but honestly, it wasn't enough. The game seemed to be about the same length as the first part.Funny new mechanics that make, surprise just a couple of pieces.After passing remain ambiguous emotions, like everything liked, and like and added little new. I can't say that I definitely recommend this part of the game to everyone, but if you're a fan of the first part and you are satisfied with everything I wrote above - then buy it.I also noticed that the translation into Russian is not correct everywhere, there are a couple of comments (if we can somehow fix it, I'm willing to help with that).Thanks a lot to the developers for their work, I will look forward to SLUDGE LIFE 3 and hope, that all our wishes will be taken into account and there will be a bigger map with even more jokes and different mechanics.I'll be happy if the STEAM will have animated profile backgrounds with BUG MUD and the rest of the characters in high quality.Where animated backgrounds?(

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so first of all shout-out to my bro for gifting this game to me. You the G Victor.Now for a short review to this game: Absolutely pick it up. You don't need to have played the old game to understand what is going on because you wouldn't get it even if you play the first one.I would recommend playing the Demo (Big Mud Sessions) to get the premise of the game before-hand.A lot of improvements over the first game. The endings are even better and well thought of this time around. The game actually provides a story and a choice to choose your (your character's) fate. Overall: Great game. Short one but very trippy and chill. 9/10This ends the short review now I shall be delving deep into the hidden themes that I came across playing the game and a lot of plot points that people either missed or didn't care for. A lot of spoilers so read at your own discression.In Depth Analysis:So I've said it many times, Sludge Life has a very deep plot that is overshadowed by the gameplay and characters. Themes of consumerism and capitalism, corporatism and evil business tactics could already be seen in the first game but themes of rebellion, righteous terrorism, cultism and isolation could be seen in the this entry. This game turns away the vague and seemingly random endings and puts you in a better place in the social and financial scale from the last game. More of it is explained in The Big Mud Sessions.The biggest noticeable change is the location you spawn in every time you enter the game. It is no more a dump made inside of a container but a well built hotel room. Ghost (your character) is now rich and well known, so much so that he has to physically block his hotel door to not let any fans enter. They are actually there for his business partner Big Mud though. Big Mud is missing though and your job is to find him so you can record a music video. A noticeable change from the past is that Ciggy (famous cigarette brand) has now been revived and is doing well. So much so that they have their own resort built to accommodate rich people. This has made a rebellion strike as the resort is built in complete isolation form the rest of the sludge island. Creating a barrier between the rich and the poor. One character enraged because of this is Uzzi (your friend from the past game). He was jailed and then escaped and plans to destroy the shiny Ciggy ball. The symbol of wealth for the company. There is the choice you make now either to find Big Mud and continue your life of riches and leisure or to become a known terrorist.A third choice comes up of destroying the island as the last game. This time you become a monster yourself and sink the whole island in the sludge.A statement of Consumer vs Capitalist comes up during the game portrayed through the imagery of the time when it was the most rampant, during 80s-90s. The main themes of Vandalism and rebellion also seems to be of that time.To make a conclusion, Sludge Life 2 is a great sequel to an already great, cosy and trippy experience of a game. This adds upon those visually, aesthetically and overall narrative-wise. A 9/10 is well deserved for this short, sweet and obscure little game.
