_childDocuments_.review: "My mother always said, 'Don't let your mouth start a fight your butt can't finish.'" Amen brother, amen.Sludge Life 2 is just an insanely charming sequel to the first game. It doesn't feel necessary, but revisiting this ciggy-obsessed world is just a joy so it doesn't rub me the wrong way, personally. There are all sorts of silly conversations to be had, secrets to discover, and a tone that really isn't captured in games nowadays outside of the indie sphere. It heavily reminds me of the "punk" attitude of the Jet Set Radio games with some very "out there" humor, and obviously some poop jokes here and there. But they feel more clever than the humor of something like the Borderlands series and fit within its aloof world. The movement upgrades so far are nice for pulling off risky platforming moves that usually lead to a worthwhile secret or tag spot. It isn't the tightest first person platforming I've experienced, but I've only ventured out a bit and have the glider and JJs. I have a feeling with the whole suite of movement tools the game will hit a stride. Performance wise on the Steam Deck with it's default settings I was getting around 30-40fps. When I turned on map optimization and lowered some shadows and view distance settings, it seemed to hover in the Deck's sweet spot around 40-45fps. That might disappoint some since it's not the most intense looking game, but for me locking the refresh rate to 40 has made it fine, much better than 30. I do recommend turning off the VHS filter on the Deck though (and PC if the game hurts your eyes, I'm still debating on which mode I like more). On the PC with a 3080, 5800X3D, and 16GB of RAM, all settings up to max, the performance seems fine, but has weird moments and FPS drops that are a little jarring. It will go from a smooth 144, to around 60 when looking at certain busy scenes with cascading lights and shadows. I might be trippin' on this, but the mouse camera movement also doesn't feel like "raw input" for me. It feels like it has a sort of delay. On the Deck, with sticks, I didn't feel this, but I suck on sticks. One thing I will mention about playing on controller is that the menus feel rather unintuitive on the sticks, changing simple settings could be improved there!This is definitely a zen out, get stoned, and vibe with an imaginative world and its bonkers inhabitants type of game. It's an Adult Swim cartoon in game-form. If that's your thing then grab some ciggies and get to findin' our boi Big Mud.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Goofy Ahh-some Vandalism Adventure in Sludge Life 2!Review:Oh boy, let me tell ya, Sludge Life 2 is one heck of a trip! If you thought the first Sludge Life was gnarly, well, hold onto your short kings, because this sequel takes the sus factor and cranks it up to 11. It's like stepping into an opium aesthetic dreamscape, but with spray cans and a whole lotta mischief!First things first, the open world in Sludge Life 2 is bigger than a conspiracy theory rabbit hole. Seriously, it's so huge and weird, it's like the developers tapped into some cosmic force of absurdity. Only in Ohio, my friends! Every corner you turn, there's a new secret to uncover, a weirdo to encounter, or an epic gamer moment waiting to happen.The vandalism-centric gameplay is where the game truly shines. Tagging spots and leaving your mark has never felt so satisfying. It's like a beautiful dance of rebellion and expression, where you can give a virtual middle finger to the cranky idiots that inhabit this polluted island. Tallyhoe, my fellow vandal!The game's humor is off the charts. The dialogue is chock-full of irony, irony about irony, and ironic takes on post-ironic speech that will leave you chuckling like a kid ciggy. The quirky characters you meet along the way will have you saying "zoinks" more times than you can count. Trust me, the writing in this game is as sharp as a smoker gang's wit.The visuals are a sight to behold. The grimy art style is so vivid and unique that it's like someone blended a psychedelic trip with a graffiti artist's wildest dreams. The world is bathed in vibrant colors and bizarre scenery that will keep you hooked for hours. Sludge Life 2 truly embraces its own goofy ahh-filled identity.However, it's worth noting that Sludge Life 2 may not be everyone's cup of tea. If you're looking for a traditional gameplay experience with a linear narrative, this might not be your jam. But if you're ready to dive headfirst into a surreal, vandalistic wonderland, then grab your spray cans and get ready for a wild ride.In conclusion, Sludge Life 2 is a unique gem in the gaming world. It's a game that celebrates rebellion, humor, and the joy of exploration. Whether you're a fan of the original or just curious about this wild universe, give it a go and immerse yourself in the glorious chaos. Stay weird, my friends!

Level design is definitely a downgrade; effectively a tower attached to a micro version of the town from the first , but without most of the creative puzzle solving to work your way into every nook and cranny. You don't even need the warper this time.Narratively speaking,  is more of the same: anarchic ethos in a post-capitalist toxic wasteland, but to a lesser depth, and where it might have shone with a commentary on sociopolitical hypocrisy (Big Mud sold out, etc.), there is nothing—an unfinished footnote of a forgotten plot line going absolutely nowhere.Don't get me wrong, this is still a decent enough addition to the  canon, albeit one shallower in gameplay and characterization, with the look and feel we all came to love, but a true sequel it is not.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is awesome. It's literally just as good as the first one! I don't have the original fully completed here on Steam (yet), since I got it for free on Epic Games and 100%-ed it there, but it did inspire me to get this one. I HAVE NO WORDS. Usually, with sequels you expect something ten times better or ten times worse. This right here isn't the case. I LOVE HOW THEY CAPTURED THE MAGIC OF THE ORIGINAL AGAIN. It's just such A JOY to go around and explore every nook and cranny of this world that the developers filled with interesting things. Every NPC has something interesting to say and they all feel unique to one another. You can see how the world is being effected by pollution, addiction and greed and how everyone in it wants to live their life and has their own quirks. And now that we're talking about the world, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ THIS MAP MAN. It's exactly like the first game, and no, it's not the same map, it's completely different, I mean that it has this unique trait to it, which I can only explain like this: Once you start to understand where things are and how the entire map is structured, you notice that it's not THAT big, still big, but not THAT big, although what makes it seem HUGE is the amount of detail put into every single little spot. And I mean EVERY. SINGLE. LITTLE. SPOT. THEY DIDN'T HALF ASS ♥♥♥♥ WITH THIS MAP, every crack in the walls, every literal piece of ♥♥♥♥, the placements of every NPC, every room, every building, every place, every hidden location (many more than one), every animal... it's all worth exploring! As I said, they captured the magic of the original. My favorite part of this game is, after getting everything - all the endings, the items, finding all the secrets, talking to every NPC and overall exploring the whole map, before closing the game for the final time, going to your pictures on your computer and looking at each one. TAKE PICTURES GUYS! Take pictures of things you find interesting throughout your playthrough. Going back and remembering your journey is the best part. I recommend not looking at walktroughs or playtroughs for this game before playing it. It's all about experiencing this world, the locations, the people and the way it develops. So in conclusion: amazing map, amazing characters, amazing lore, amazing endings, amazing callbacks to the original, AMAZING SEQUEL.

_childDocuments_.review: Sludge Life is a series of games where you live your life in the backdrop of a world covered in the waste byproduct of a society only looking to consume and party and maintain the structures for consuming and partying. You can blast cigs and meet strange people and also there's an objective that you have to follow to 'finish the game', but the most important thing is blasting cigs and meeting strange people.It's a short game - if you know what you're doing and are dead set on finding an ending so you can just toss this game away and go back to playing Counter-Strike, you could reasonably beat this within an hour. But doing so would be a waste of all you get to see within this game - the parts where Sludge Life really shines are the parts where you're just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around, seeing what's behind that corner, and finding out that there is indeed, a crab that smokes cigs. For this reason, this is a game where I recommend 100%ing achievements. It doesn't take that long and at the end you'll have given cigarettes to children to smoke.It's four hours long, but this and the first Sludge Life (which is also a solid four if you do all achievements) are the perfect ways to spend something like a long plane ride or road trip with a Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent exploration in a grimy and colorful world that is built around careful obfuscation, spatial awareness and open world platforming that all come together for an experience that stands well next to its predecessor. You jump, double jump, climb and glide over and across crumbling infrastructure in an endless sea of pollution away from any signs of landmass. A gigantic chalice-shaped upper class hotel sits in the center of this slice of grimy heaven, towering above everything and bringing some much-appreciated vertical "oomph" to the Sludge, trading the sprawl of Sludge Life 1 for dizzying heights. The haze obscures everything, and it was a bit of a surprise learning more about the world I woke up with a hangover in. While only a few characters get names in this world, I felt a lot of excitement finding characters I recognized from the first game and seeing how their lives are doing now, plus some new folk to expand the community. The continuation of the "story" from the first game was surprising to me. Sludge Life 1 and 2 are both worlds stuck in time, stagnant and caked-on, unable to change. However, it's clear how much *has* changed between the first and second game, and seeing that story progress the way it did in the time gap was pretty shocking (No spoilers from me, but...you might be surprised finding out what happened if you're as intimately familiar with the first game as I am). This game too finds ways to make it feel like the world is moving more than before. It's not just a moment in time any longer: you'll see new opportunities arise, and old friends standing by your side. It's a bit like a snowglobe, except full of gross slime and needing you to shake it around.Sludge Life 1 is kind of necessary to play in order to play this game, but I recommend it simply because of how different the two games' worlds are, as well as the narrative payoffs between the two. Heck, play this one first and then the first game if you want, or go back and play the first game then this one. I personally don't think it matters too too much, but you will miss some of the new movement options given to the player in this game. Also, there's a reason this is the "2". so me saying "eh, the first and second games aren't that different" feels both incorrect and reductive. There's good reasons to play both of these games.If there are any negative things I have to say for this game, they're small complaints. I miss the map, though I like the in-game reason why there isn't a map now. Also, by the time I got the game's "final tool", I really didn't feel like I needed it at that point. That's really it though! Some load times were longer than expected? Nothing really bad for me though. Extremely good game, will likely pick it back up in a few months to reconnect with this little grimy snowglobe waiting for me to shake things up again.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave a cigarette to a baby bird and took a picture of it to 100% the game.Sludge Life 2, apparently pronounced "Sludge Life Twice" because that makes sense, is the unexpected but very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ welcome sequel to one of my favorite video games ever. And wouldn't you know it, this sequel is killer. The layout of the world was probably a downgrade over the first, but the grander presentation more than makes up for that. This game has so much backbone it's insane. The way this game stacks up against so many bigger games in terms of its world structure and writing and absolute brevity in its approach to politics is inspiring. It's not perfect, obviously. I mentioned the world layout, but on top of that the game still fails to do what I wanted most out of the first game: Expand on the characters more. The game centers around Big Mud and Uzzi but neither really get the service they deserve. And the taggers, outside of Dolo, feel almost entirely like set dressings - even more than the original. The characters are so FUN. Seriously! So why can't we have more of them? I want my interactions with Peep to go beyond two lines. And Dolo only stood out because of the very personal relationship at play for her. Regardless, this game is MORE of the first game. Not, like, more of it. MORE of it. It's [almost] exactly what I wanted. I love this game and I want a Peep plush.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping for a bit more content than 5 hours, but probably the only parkour game I actually think is fun.  Once you know the ropes it is never a frustrating or stress inducing ordeal.  You basically feel powerful in the brain for figuring out how to get up there, without feeling like at any moment your progress could be wrecked by a fall to your death, needing to start all over.  Death is instant re-spawn with meaningless financial debt.  Everything is so responsive that it never feels too unpredictable or janky in terms of whether you will make the jump.  It more that you found the way to do it.   Most importantly it's immersive in an I'd love to hang out there kind of way.  I wish the npc characters had a bit more function than just making a quick random comment.

_childDocuments_.review: If you could see my face when i saw the steam update in my library from sludge life; "Sludge life 2 annoucement". Listen,on top of everything this godly year has given us video game wise, This is just extra icing on the cake. The first game was a great sweet short time,so for such a small but cool experience,hearing a sequel is going to materialize out of nowhere was unbelivably dope. So months later,while other game were annouced to boost the prestige of this year,the game finally release...It's excatly what you expect.Again,It's a short game. Again,it's style is still untouched and as refreshing as before. Again,100 grafitti spot. Again,cat's butthole. Basically,everything that was there is still there.But some png you talk to clearly elude on the previous event in the first game and really feels like things followed up from the first to the second (Before you asked,all three endings are cannon somehow,they're all refered to in text). + there is technically new objects to use and explore the map but one of the two that actually change gameplay can only be unlocked once you do get the ending from finding all 100 tag spot. The other one is a double jump you find in the very building you start at. The biggest difference being,obviously,the map. Way more vertical then the previous one. admittedly,it'll depend from person to person,but on one hand i really dig the the hotel area and exploring it any way one could,but the area below,which is more horizontal like the first game feels really short and cramped. And although there are some spot that are as note worthy as the first one,but a lot of it a l shape rectangle with 5 room and two tag spot tops. What the game asks for you however to complete it would justify you checking out this game.Still as the first one. The sequel is cool,short,sweet,fun,and that's it. It's definetly consistent between the two,and the first one is still one of my favourite game i've played  in recent memory. This game is definetly worth playing if you like game and can accept one not being 10 hours long. You owe it to yourself to play this for yourself. A year like this isn't happening twice in a row. Better get a mouthful a game from now before we go back to lesser year.

_childDocuments_.review: As great as the first, maybe a little shorter than the first? I think comparing the two is natural and makes sense since this is a direct sequel. My biggest issue with this one is that the narrative seems far less cohesive than the first. Though, if you look at this one as a direct continuation of the story (more like an add on than a distinct game) it makes much more sense. name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines
detailed_description: MORE FROM US About the Game FEATURES 🪝 Pure platforming bliss - Fast-paced swinging action meets a whole host of fresh abilities, such as magnetic panels and fire-dashing, all coming together as a tight, fun platforming romp! 🌎 New worlds - Journey across dimensions in an epic quest to save... everything! Each unique world is bustling with vibrant, eye-catching pixel art and bubbling with personality! 🐶 Gameplay galore - Sail across the cosmos to explore multiple worlds filled with tons of levels. Hidden collectibles, secret areas, memorable boss battles, bonus levels, time trials, and more to sink those canines into 🎵 Exhilarating soundtrack - Jazz Mickle's catchy, killer soundtrack will have Grapple Dogs' beats stuck in your head forever, with level-by-level jams that are sure to get that tail waggin'! TWO DOGS ARE BETTER THAN ONE More dogs = more action! Mysterious newcomer Luna joins the adventure, with her weaponry adding exciting new gameplay features to the fray. Alternate between playing as the swingin' hero Pablo and the shoot-first-ask-questions-later anti-hero Luna. THE RETURN OF PABLO The pettable, adventurous, acrobatic pup Pablo returns, with his trusty grappling hook allowing him to zip across levels and worlds throughout the cosmos, completing tricky challenges and platforming tests, along with new powers and new friends. SWING YOUR OWN WAY Hone your grappling skills - or your gun-blasting prowess - with optional collectibles for those who love extra challenge. Try your speedrunning might with the Time Trial modes and race against the world(s) to prove who's the real top dog.

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed the game 100% and it's time to update my review. All of the following is just my opinion.This review is mostly about how the game compares to its predecessor. The original Grapple Dog is one of my favorite games ever (I've 100%ed it twice already), so I started its sequel with very high expectations. While I was a bit let down in some ways, I still enjoyed Cosmic Canines and recommend it, though ultimately I preferred the first game.The sequel does improve on Grapple Dog in a number of ways. The music is overall significantly better, not that the first game's music was bad. There's less overuse of voice samples and more atmospheric tracks, which combine nicely with some of the new moody stage themes. Worlds have been restructured to alternate between several different stage/music themes throughout the world, so you don't have to listen to the same track for five levels in a row this time.Boss battles are more interesting and challenging overall. Fun new power-ups have been added. The stakes and spectacle are increased, and the already great artwork seems even better this time. And the opening logo screens can thankfully be skipped, a much needed change.Cosmic Canines also retains a lot that made the first game great. Level design is solid, gameplay and movement mechanics are expertly designed and very satisfying, and there's decent challenge to be had. Characters and NPCs for the most part are interesting and charming, though perhaps not quite as much as in the first game. Lore and world-building are once again surprisingly (for this type of game) deep and engaging. Every aspect of the game is polished to a sheen. There's a generous amount of levels, and the fun time trial mode was thankfully kept.So why do I like the first one more? A few reasons, mostly having to do with changes made to the gameplay and level structure. My opinions in this regard are perhaps unusual, and you might personally find some or all of these things to be improvements.The addition of Luna as a playable character is a miss for me. Her gameplay is focused on shooting and dashing (she can grapple too, but it's not as important for her), but I don't feel it works as well as Pablo's focus on bopping and grappling. Aiming with the right thumbstick means you have to remove your thumb from the face buttons, which can occasionally be awkward. Enemies take way too many shots to defeat with her default peashooter, slowing things down significantly unless you just dash past them. Firing downward drastically reduces your descent in air, and with some special guns it even boosts you higher. Combining that with upward-slanting mid-air dashes (which you can repeat around seven times before having to touch ground again) gives you nearly unlimited horizontal air movement, which you can exploit to trivialize some of the level design. You can even use the dashes and gun hovering to jankily climb a vertical wall, but it's slow and tedious—which would be fine if it were never actually needed, but 100%ing the game does require it (more on that later).Admittedly, like the other game and movement mechanics, the shooting and dashing does feel satisfying, and in some levels you get much more powerful special guns that one-shot enemies, significantly improving the experience. But I like Pablo's gameplay better nonetheless, so the first game being 100% Pablo is a big win in its favor for me.Pablo's gameplay has also been changed up, in some ways that I like or don't mind (like Pablo's ground pound super-jump and the tweaked grapple swinging), but also in some ways that I dislike. His Mario-esque sprint meter has been removed in favor of always being at a sprint. I thought that gameplay mechanic from the first game was pretty satisfying, so it's a bit disappointing to see it removed here. Pablo now has a punch attack, which is fun and a nice addition to his combat repertoire—but spamming punch moves Pablo faster than sprinting, which I don't think is ideal. It doesn't come up often since there's not usually long stretches of horizontal ground where this would matter, but still. I think a fun compromise would be to allow Pablo to chain punches as long as each punch hits something (an enemy or a box), sort of like how rolling works in the DKC SNES games. Also, the mid-air movement mechanics have been totally redone, with horizontal momentum arrested when you're not actively holding left or right. I actually liked the original momentum-focused air control that people complained about.Level structure has been reworked with some changes I wasn't thrilled about. The first game had a really nice level structure: find five gems and collect at least most of the fruit to unlock two more. It was a Yoshi's Island-like collectathon that served to nicely incentivize exploring the level while also not being as tedious, because unlike with red coins, you would never be punished just for missing one fruit or one small batch of fruit. This made collecting the fruit compelling and an important part of level completion. And with the only other secrets being gems, if you happened to miss one the first time you went through a level, any already collected gems before and/or after the one you missed served as guideposts to tell you which part of the area to look in and when you had gone too far. As a result, 100% completion was never tiresome for me.By contrast, the sequel shakes that up. Fruit are now a currency used to unlock customization options and don't count towards level completion, making them less compelling to collect. There are now only three gems per level, and in place of the other two, there are two new different hidden "collectibles," one being a treasure chest containing a grapple cosmetic and the other being a hidden duck band to find. The problem is that there's no guideposts anymore telling you which part of the level contains the latter two like there would be if they were still gems. They could be anywhere, so you have to scour the whole level again if you miss them. I usually had no problem finding the grapple chest on my first go of the level, but the duck bands are often  obscurely hidden, and often required the aforementioned tedious wall-climbing in Luna levels, with no way of knowing exactly  wall you need to climb. The music does start to fade as you get close to the band, which sometimes helps you find them, but other times they're so far off the beaten path that it doesn't help at all.Also, there seems to be a diminished emphasis on grappling compared to the first game, sometimes significantly so. Grappling was the best part of the first, so having it take a backseat in favor of other gimmicks in the sequel (even though those gimmicks are fun) isn't what I was hoping for. And there's an overuse of "collect all the keys/break all the targets before you can proceed" sections within levels, with one level even having two in a row with a short linear segment dividing them.The first game also had a bit more charm to it. It's still here, just not as much. The NPCs in the first had more fun interactions and dialogue. The ability to explore the boat has been removed, a sad omission, though somewhat made up for via increased presence of team members within levels. Luna also just isn't very likeable as a character for me; though she does get a bit better as the game goes on, she's often humorless and mean-spirited. Understandable given her background, but just not as enjoyable as Pablo's characterization and interactions. On the plus side, NUL is now a team member and he's great, my favorite besides Pablo.I enjoyed my time with the game. The first may be better to me, but this one is still good, and I think I'm in the minority in believing Grapple Dog to be the superior game. Regardless, if you liked the first, you'll almost certainly like this one too.

_childDocuments_.review: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines is an awesome challenging platformer that has 1 missable achievement. It has accessibility features to make the game easier, like an infinite amount of jumps and no damage from monsters/bosses.  11h+ 3/10 with accibility options, 9/10 without accesibility options 1 You don't need a guide No Yes, defeating the end boss without buying any health upgrade is missable No No Yes, you have to get the gold medal in the time trials for every level and challenge No No No, you can play with the accessibility options on and still unlock all the achievements NoIn Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines you play as one of 2 dogs and will move around in the levels by jumping and slinging around with your grappling hook. You don’t have to have played the first game to enjoy the second one. There are just a few throwbacks to the first game. However, it has quite a lot of improvements over the first game. Using your grappling hook is a bit easier and there is a second character with a different skill set. The level determines if you will play as Grappling Dog or Luna.I loved the variation in the different levels and weird challenges. Also, there was a big variation in the aesthetics of the levels. The game also comes with a bunch of QoL features, the most noticeable one for me is the option to jump into a level from the level menu section in which you can also see what you're still missing in each level and then instantly jump to that level. no worries about getting to that different area of the game and finding the right level. Shopping also happens from a menu and not having to physically move toward a shop. Next to normal platformer levels, there are also short challenges. You open up those levels by using fruits you collect through the levels. You can also use this currency to buy more health (warning this locks you out of an achievement), different color clothes, or a different-looking grappling hook.Speaking about the achievements. There are achievements for completing all the levels. Find all the gems and find a hidden band in each normal platformer level. There are also achievements for buying all the cosmetics. There is 1 achievement for beating the end boss without any health upgrade. There is an accessibility option to not lose health, which makes this achievement so much easier but without it, this seems really challenging.Another achievement requires you to get the gold medal on each level. This is also really challenging if you don’t use the accessibility options. However, another accessibility option there is is infinite jumping. This makes these challenges so much more doable but can still be a challenge. I think you need this ability in most levels to find the band, as it seems in 95% of the cases very high somewhere in the level, but in a few levels, it is very low in the level.And last but not least there is an achievement for having the game on progress at 100%. This includes all bands, gold medals, gems but also all the different cosmetics. If you don’t have enough fruit to buy it all when you finish the rest: I recommend the monkey level in the second world. Above the first checkpoint, there are 18 fruits. After collecting those you can restart from that checkpoint and they are there again. To earn those fruits you will have to complete the level, so don't leave the level after farming those but just complete it. I give Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines 4 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.  Solid sequel.  The introduction of a second playable character isn't a total miss.  It's mildly frustrating to adjust between them because one has an air dash and the other doesn't. I'd prefer the game just honed in on one character, preferably Pablo.Also I feel they've dumbed the difficulty down a bit.  I know a lot of people complained the original was difficult, but  I disagree, I think had a perfect level of difficulty.  The gold medal times in this one are way too easy.  I'm making multiple mistakes in runs and clearing gold medal times by 30+ seconds sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first Grapple Dog game about a month ago, and was really excited to see the new one coming out so soon. It did everything I wanted out of a sequel to the game and then some, easily making it both an awesome follow-up and...probably just one of my favorite games of all time now?Things I love:Minor complaints that shouldn't be a dealbreaker, but I still feel are worth pointing out:Overall, please buy this game. If you saw the any single moment of platforming in the trailers that looked really satisfying to pull off, I promise it feels even more satisfying when you're actually doing it. The game had me constantly stopping and saying "oh  yeah that felt cool", all while being in a super charming package with a cool sense of style from top to bottom. Even the small negatives I had with the game weren't anywhere near close enough to stop me from feeling like I wanted to do every single challenge the game had to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: calling it now its gonna hit overwhelmingly positive within 2 weeks. _childDocuments_.review: A first look: At first, I was a little afraid. While I do like most platformers… I’m not the biggest fan or good at grapple hook stuff. I swear I still have an old trauma from the Rayman days on PS—a little different but also a little the same, no? Or at least to me. But I digress. This isn’t about that game but about this game. I admit that I’m super happy I accepted my creator's copy in the end and just gave it a shot despite feeling way out of my comfort zone because all it took was the tutorial to win me over and sucker me in big time, even to the point that I immediately picked up the first Grapple Dog game after recording and then continue playing a bit more.So far, the cutscenes are gorgeously good. The characters are lovely. My first few levels were so much fun, and I’m super excited to see the other levels and keep going. The music is a banger too. I love that there are collectables and even a wardrobe! So much to collect… I hope I find it all because I want it all. This includes the little secret nooks I sometimes find. Yeah! I see you! Or, uh, at least some. I may have missed some,… probably.I'm obsessed with how speedy the ship is and most likely spend too much time just zooming around with it for the sake of the fun of it.I'm not a fan of the time trial events, but I can skip them. Luckily, no one can force me to participate those, but I see how some people might find them a fun challenge.I am, however, a huge fan of the accessibility options! As someone who isn’t so skilled with the grapple hook and is a little worried it might get too challenging at some point, it's nice to have that reassurance that I can flick them on whenever I want/need them. That gives me the opportunity to finish the game and story, unlike some other games. I think that’s very lovely and, above all, thoughtful. Since it really sucks to come a long way only not to be able to see the ending and toss it aside for an unknown time or forever.I know I’m still early in the game, but I already wanted to show my support for this little gem. I hope it helps give it visibility so more people check it out. I didn’t think it would be for me either, and look at me now being all like, woah. Sometimes, going out of your comfort zone can be worth it, eh? I’ll be returning to it soon, right after playing out my other game. I won’t forget about this one.And I would very much like to close off by saying that the pet button is everything. Everything!Luna’s face, though, when you pet her… I howled!Who’s a good boi? -vs- My first time-trial attempt didn’t go so well, lol.

_childDocuments_.review: One of those rare sequels that's simultaneously so massively improved that it retroactively makes the kind-of-solid original feel like a tech demo, and so independent that it's easy to recommend to just play it  said original.Pretty much everything that could've made someone fall off or dismiss the first Grapple Dog is entirely mitigated here. They were rewritten entirely from scratch and feel fantastic here, alongside a new movement option and some really nice quality of life. It's been pretty much entirely smoothed out while still maintaining a good difficulty level - Challenge spikes that the original plopped in the middle of the game are now placed much more appropriately.  Songs are on average twice as long, and there are nearly twice as many. And all of them are bangers.  This is a space adventure, so pretty much every area feels much more unique, on top of having almost double the thematic variety in general. While the number of in-level collectibles has been kept largely the same, they've been split across different categories, with only one type being required for progress, and you no longer have to worry about collecting all of the fruit for extras. On top of the second (arguably even more fun) character Luna, they each have multiple different powerups that add a lot of extra spice to the gameplay.Even things nobody complained about, like the art direction, have been so heavily improved that it makes looking at the original feel wrong.This is among the biggest leaps from the original game to a sequel I've ever seen. An easy recommendation even to those that never touched the original or fell off it. There's no necessary story or anything stuck in that game, just jump into this one....Though I do wish that the Dash/Punch and Pablo's ground pound could be assigned to different buttons so my muscle memory from playing as Luna can't get in the way of midair control. That alone might elevate the game to an all-timer for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: A superb sequel to a hugely overlooked masterful platformer, Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canynes is more of the smooth platforming goodness from the original game, with sugar on top.Luna, the new character, feels significantly different enough from Pablo to justify her existence (in fact, she might be a bit OP even, in comparison to Pablo) and her gunplay is surprisingly fun.More of this please!
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this as a sequel to Grapple Dog, though there are some aspects that may be a bit more polarising to fans of the first game I loved them personally.The pacing is much improved from the first game, it feels like they took the themed level approach from the first game and just scattered them throughout the story, which really helps reduce the tedium of going through a world with the same theme throughout with the same song playing throughout. Instead you'll get a few levels per world that draw from a few different themes to add a nice bit of variety.The addition of a 2nd playable character Luna is something that I think comes down to personal taste, I enjoyed just having a character with a gun I could shoot (though the mechanics can be a bit broken at times, I enjoyed it), the main downsides is the aiming can be a bit clunky while you're trying to move and I often found myself trying to use Luna's dash as Pablo and ground pounded to my death, but overall I didn't find these too much of an issue for me personally.I enjoyed the move to make the berries an actual currency to buy skins rather than another thing to collect to progress (Previously they were required to get medals and you had to hunt down a majority of them) They can be ignored if you don't want the cosmetics, though I collected them pretty thoroughly throughout the game and didn't die that much, I still needed about an hour of "grinding" to get everything, so I kinda wish the prices were adjusted a bit towards the higher end.I liked the collectibles in this game, they didn't feel too difficult to locate outside of one collectable (Duck Bands) which seemed to be deliberately hard to locate and get to, which really made me experiment and learn new quirks and movement mechanics which I really enjoyed learning (And it was amusing to realise that the devs knew some of the particularly broken bits of movement tech and just left it in the game and designed some secrets around it)I like the movement, the new character and the music so overall this was a very enjoyable experience that I ended up just beating 100% in under 24 hours, where as the original game took a similar amount of time to complete but I kept needing to take a break from it due to the pacing.Highly recommend this game whether you've played the original or not. The writing still has a lot of heart and charm, and it was a joy to 100% outside of the final hour of berry grinding.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions: More of what made the first game great, but now there's a cool goth girl dog with guns.The attention to subtle world building in Grapple Dog immediately is paid off with another great intro sequence full of fantastic artwork and neat writing. There seem to be some great polish features that were not present in the original, such as a menu-based stage selection that allows jumping back into an earlier level much more quickly.I will say that I'm struggling a bit with controlling the new character Luna. I tend to prefer playing First/Third Person Shooters with M+KB, so I'm struggling to juggle shooting and movement with the two thumbsticks (I realize this might be more of an issue for me than most others). You CAN play with M+KB here, and even configure the controls (though not the menu navigation, unfortunately), but even that is taking some getting used to due to only having recently finished the first game with the controller. Also, you can't use a mouse when controlling Pablo (I get that he doesn't need to aim, but I'd still enjoy being able to use mouse clicks to grapple or dash).Regardless, I'm having a great time already, and I'm very glad there's another Grapple Dog game out!-- UPDATE: I ended up changing the controller layout so that Jump is on LT, Shoot is on RT, Grapple is on A, and Dash is on B. This ends up working well for me - I can aim while jumping and shooting at the same time. If anyone else is struggling with the default layout and would prefer using a controller over M+KB, I recommend giving this option a shot!With that issue out of the way, I'm fully back to enjoying the hell out of this. Fantastic variety in the level artwork and music so far, and more funny writing in little NPCs you encounter. Also - extra hidden collectibles to look for in the level, and less pressure to collect every piece of fruit (I still kinda do lol, personally I wouldn't have minded this still being tracked).Genuinely a fantastic game and sequel so far, looking forward to seeing the rest of it.-- UPDATE 2: 100%'d it! Again, great game. One thing I did still wanna point out - if anyone felt like the Time Trials were too difficult in the first game - they're a lot more generous this time. Still felt like a good challenge, but significantly easier in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect example of how to do a sequel. All of the original mechanics and movement quirks of Grapple Dog still exist with a lot of new welcomed additions. There is a new fully playable character with a unique moveset, completely new per character power-ups, and even small additions such as cosmetics for both the characters and the grappling hook. It's a shame that it doesn't seem to be selling well on PC based purely on reviews.

_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: After a good first episode, Pablo and his friends are back around in Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines, with newcomer Luna joining the party for a fantastic sequel!While Pablo keeps a relatively similar gameplay as in the first Grapple Dogs, Luna's gameplay is slightly different: she gets a grappling hook as well, but also a gun! Think of her as the Shadow the Hedgehog of Pablo, but with a good gun gameplay this time.With these two characters, this game offers a great deal of platforming, with its fair share of exploration to find gems, hidden chests and even some cool-looking duck band. The boss fights are also a strong point of this game, as they manage to be interesting and challenging without overstaying their welcome.Besides Luna, the main addition of this second opus is the new elemental mechanic: once again, for fans of a certain blue hedgehog, they can remind you of Wisps in that you have to pick them up in a stage and use their abilities until you reach the end of the stage. And they make for a lot of fun level-design!The soundtrack is still as bouncy as ever, and I'd say the story is better written this time around.Overall, the game is super fun to play with lots of replay value to get the best time possible in the time attack version of each level and finding every hidden stuff.Truly an awesome platformer that I would recommend to anyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful gem (pun intended) of platforming game design!I played the original a while ago and was immediately drawn in by the charming visuals and grapple mechanic.  The original fell a bit short in my eyes, but was still great.Cosmic Canines is everything great about the original polished to perfection.No mechanic outstays its welcome, the continuous story makes my heart warm, and they added Shadow the Hedgehog to this one which is always a plus.The levels are shorter, more focused, the annoying fruit-collecting mechanic is gone replaced with a neat shop instead.  Everything about this game begs to be 100%'d, so I'm definitely going to do that in time.  Whereas I felt beat down in the first one for trying anything but the recommended path, this game lets you infinitely gain height, rocket jump, do stupid punch-grapple-slide-bounce combos that conserve momentum - it's just a fantastic experience on both casual and speedrun sides.Check it out if you haven't, please!The dev did a wonderful job and you're really missing out if you haven't played this!The game's also really short so it's not a tedious timesink, every challenge / level actually makes me REALLY want more! (a positive thing)All in all, one of the best games I've played this year ^-^
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: This will be updated when I complete the game.I was a pretty outspoken fan of the first Grapple Dog, and I treated the game a bit like a joke, because I found it to be surprisingly well constructed, especially in level design.  This stood in harsh contrast to what I expected, so I was pleasantly surprised to say they least.When I heard about the sequel, I immediately knew I was all in.  The game... DOES deliver.  So far I've really enjoyed the new game.  The new mechanics are really fun.  Although, I find all the new dashing and traversal powers to muddy the simplicity and actual GRAPPLING from the first game.  For this reason I actually look forward to Pablo's (original grapple dog) stages more so then the new character Luna, even though Pablo gets a lot of new abilities.  I think some of the greatest stages in both games are the challenge stages, which I would love to see a lot more of, when things feel a little more "bite-Sizeable," the game really sings.  I also appreciate the hidden band secrets, but I feel the elimination of fruit completion for a "finishing" of a stage was an odd choice, as it feels like exploration to find the fruits is WAY less rewarding.So far, I really do enjoy the game, and the physics upgrade is MASSIVE to really enjoying the platforming.This comes HIGHLY recommended, especially for the price point they released at.Tons of character, great style, top design, and has tight and intuitive platforming.Give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: About halfway through the game so far, would recommend to fans of the first. Pablo's stages are great fun, the momentum gameplay's back just as great as before, and the new gimmick power-ups are nice to play with, the grass sword is loads of fun.The new character Luna? I love her. I love how they updated Pablo's design to really sell the Sonic/Shadow pairing the two of them have, and she's got this great sourpuss personality. I reckon she'd be annoying if you couldn't read the tropes and see she was going to develop. Also, her opening lines of Pablo: "Nice name!" Luna: "Thanks, I chose it myself" - perfect. No notes. Fantastic if I'm reading the implication right.So now it's clear that I love Luna - I just wish I didn't have to play as her. The run-gun stages with her are very annoying to control, since you have to aim with the thumbstick and that takes your thumb away from the buttons - the ones you need to use to dash and jump and everything else. I found her easier to use when I changed the fire button to left trigger instead of right, but no amount of remapping can change that the (definitely intentional) game-breaking platform skipping you can do with her (aim down & airdash over and over and over) is kind of weird. It can trivialise levels and otherwise doesn't feel as satisfying as it should. I think she's kind of a miss gameplay-wise - again, I *love* Luna as a character and I'm so glad she's here, I just wish her gimmick wasn't the guns. (Yes I know the guns are also for the aims of the Sonic/Shadow parallels but that's just my take)The graphics remain vibrant and imaginative, the new dimensions you explore are fascinating (though I felt a little weird about how in this whole multiverse thing the Frogs universe gets so much focus; if it's about how many universes there are, why repeat so many levels?), the music's nice, and I'm definitely going to buy the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines is a fun and challenging grapple game where you have to fight your way through levels collecting crystals, bashing / shooting off enemies till you reach the end of the level. Each level is designed nicely and has lots of platforming, grappling and lots of secrets to find.The music was very engaging especially in the boss fights which were really enjoyable. The sequel introduces the new character Luna which was very fun to fight with.Most of the dialogues put a smile on my face which will give it a plus.Unique style game with overall rating of 10/10. Really recommended to any platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on launch and made it a point to get nearly all of the main game collectibles without any form of hesitation. It took me two days to beat the main campaign and I cannot wait to do the time trials as well as general clean up on my first save.As for the proper review - Mechanically, it's an improvement from the foundation of the first Grapple Dog in almost every regard. The controls are still tight and while the physics can at times become unwieldy, it's something you get used to.My only issue is with newcomer - Luna. Her defaults might cause some issue for those. I personally remap the shooter to RB and weapon swap to RT to allow greater comfort on my Xbox controller. You might have better mileage with the defaults or not. But at least you can experiment with the generous remapping options.The story is a bit tad bit more complex than the first game. At least in terms of steaks. My only issue with it was I felt I never got to spend as much time with the characters as I did in the last game. Especially with lack of being able to enter the boat between worlds, which was one of my favorite bits of flavor. Not a huge loss but still - It says something when my biggest issue with the story is that I wish there was more of it to enjoy.Grapple Dogs: CC is a wonderful slice of platforming which I will no doubt revisit time and time again. As well as recommend to others.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off really strong. Goes from head scratchingly easy to kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but pretty enjoyably difficulty right at the end of the game. Weird bugs and jank I didn’t expect either. Not as good as the first one but ok. If I have the first a 9 I would give this a 7. Some levels are so easy they feel like they are just there for padding, all the way at the end of the game too. Eh maybe a 6. Pretty disappointed, loved the first.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: The loved the first game and I love this game as much if not more than it. I like the changes made to Pablo's gameplay like the removal of the run meter, and the abilities he can get during levels. I like Luna's twin stick adaptation of the gameplay and found her to be equally as fun.The level design is great and varied in terms of themes and objectives, sometimes it's a straightforward get to endpoint or sometimes it's a collectathon. The challenge levels each world has for each character is fun.Honestly my only problem is that I've experienced a few crashes on the High Winds level, I'm not sure if it's because of dashing completely through the wind or if it's because I have keyboard and mouse binded for Luna levels. There also a glitch with Pablo's vine ability where it can clip through walls, which can zip Pablo somewhere else Sonic 3 style. It has resulted in some level restarts or in one case a game restart because it froze the game.I love this game so much, it's definitely one of my favorite titles I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Pablo is back and better than ever! And now with a gun-wielding team mate! It's still packed with charm like last time. The music is great, absolutely my jam. Sort of Jazz Jackrabbit-style music, if that makes any sense. The new challenges with the new team mate Luna are really fun. The movement feels even more fluid than last time. Just the first couple of dimensions have been really fun and creative so far. Highly recommend this game, especially if you liked the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: I think I need to play Grapple Dogs 1. I had a lot of fun then the levels started to get really long and grindy with finding the gems to unlock more levels and finding 20 keys to open a door. Definitely worth trying but the grind started leaving me conflicted. I love Pablo's gameplay (this game has a 50/50 split playtime for each character) a lot more that's why I'm saying I should try the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: After an hour of playtime I can say that this game is pretty good so far. It would be cool to see features like Pablo being able to grapple by left clicking. I do like the new additions such as a new playable character even if they are playable for a selected level. But the new hook skins and items you can buy and the shop makes collecting things more rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: A lot like the first game, but everything better. They toned down the challenge a bit, which I think is welcome since the first one could be pretty frustrating at times, and there's a new playable character which for me was a genius addition. The new character brings an intensely different gameplay style more akin to a run n'gun, but still keeping the grappling and wall jumping mechanics, it's pretty cool! If you liked the first, it's an obvious buy. If you didn't like some things about the first, I strongly suggest you give it a try! And if you didn't play the first, it's better if you do since the story follows up from there, but honestly it's no big deal if you wish to start from this one and play the previous later
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: If you did not like the first game, still give this a try!Cannot believe how good this game is. Honestly, I bought the first game and it did nothing for me. It was cute looking, I played it for about an hour, and was like “nope, mid!” But this game is so much better in every way. The movement is better, the level design is better, the extra abilities and the girl dog with the gun are so much fun. There are some minor nitpicks I have (the bosses suck!), but overall this is a very good game that I can see myself 100 percenting soon.  Tragedy that this game is not bigger.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: A charming platformer with a great sense of motion to it. It's not the most complicated game, but it's got a good sense of progression while constantly introducing new things throughout the game. Music is solid, a lot of collectibles and unlockables to make exploring feel rewarding and only minimal jank. I did play through it with a keyboard only for the new shooter character and despite very much not being recommended, a good 90% of the game felt as fluid as possible even with the "sub-optimal" choice taken, so let that be a testament to how good the game feels.The only real downsides are that you can easily lock yourself out of one achievement and need to do an entire bonus run for it potentially and that there are some minor bugs that can throw you off the groove.Just like the first game, the writing is charming and silly for those who want a nice lighthearted adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: grapple: yesdogs: yescosmic canines: arguably soseems good to meOn a more serious note though, this game is great! The pixel art is stellar, the gameplay is somewhat simple yet satisfying and fun, and the music and sheer amount of polish makes it a very well rounded experience. I highly recommend giving it a shot. Best wishes to the developer and their future endeavors!
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Really good sequel and one of the best platformers around.A fantastic sequel from start to end. They geniunely managed to improve almost every aspect of the first game. Surprisingly, it felt a little less climatic and epic compared to the original. But not by much. And everything else is SO MUCH better! Pablo himself feels as great as ever and Luna took some getting used to, however, once you do, it is great run`n`gun action. The themes are also more creative, taking a lot of ideas from the prequel`s climax. Moreover, Jazz continues to grace us with an outstanding, funky swing soundtrack. The writing is again sharp (if not sharper!) and hilarious. With the improved grapics and cutscenes, it almost f feels like a cartoon. If you are looking a classic platformer that soars with flying colours, literally, check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Grapple Dog 2: Electric (Earth,  & Fire) Dog-awoo!Pablo's back with a brand new adventure but all the same satisfying grappling, swinging, and jumping action! Now complete with a new set of [level-specific] power-ups, Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canine gives Pablo an extra layer of movement and attack to speed through these new fantastically designed levels. There's also a fun new playable grapple dog, Luna, who joins the adventure and controls fairly similarly with the exception of her dash and equipped gun. Her runnin'-and-gunnin' is an incredibly fitting addition the game and while it has a slower rhythm, it brings a new unique depth to the platforming mastery that has you carefully aiming to eliminate enemies or knock over levers midair as you swing or dash between points.Overall if you enjoyed Grapple Dog, I highly recommend Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines! Also while I played the first game on keyboard and mouse, I do suggest playing this one with a controller!
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Great 2D platformer! A lot of content, customisation, and a really fun moveset!I really like playing as 2 different characters but I do find the run and gun gameplay a bit more awkward than the simple platforming, I think combining platforming with twin-stick shooting is just a hard square to circle (as someone who has made a 2D platformer twin-stick shooter I can understand).The art is beautiful, the level themes are really creative and numerous, and the first two power-ups Pablo can get are a highlight!Highly recommend, this game is mega underrated!
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the first Grapple Dog game which was one of the most charming and fluid indie platformers I've played in recent years. When I first heard about the sequel which featured an additional dog and now they were in space, it seemed like a joke; But this game is no joke (although it does have a delightful sense of humour).This second entry in the Grapple Dog series manages to deliver more of the fun, fast paced platforming which made the first game so successful, with the addition of a multitude of new weapons and gameplay mechanics which keep it fresh and engaging. The addition of the new playable character 'Luna' adds some welcome variety to the game with her play style being similar enough to Pablo's to not break the flow of the game, but her combat focus gives her levels and boss fights a distinct flavour. Her self seriousness and too-cool-for-school attitude makes her the perfect contrast to Pablo's empty headed positivity (think Sonic vs Shadow).Also if you like cosmetic items this game has you covered. With dozens of outfits and grappling hooks for each character you can change your wardrobe every level and never run out of options. I've only completed the first two worlds but I'd say that so far the game is heaps of fun, and does everything you'd want from a sequel and more.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: General Review:Overall Rating: 8/10Notes: Great game, just needs a bit more polish.- - - - - - - - - -Yet Again, just like the previous game, this one gives me enough drive to write another review. And also like the last game, this one delivers a splendid experience.Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines, like Grapple Dog before it, is a platforming game focused on grapple hook swinging gameplay, with plenty of obstacles and treasures to surmount using your agility and reflexes. Once again, the controls feel very responsive, with only one caveat that I’ll discuss later. Moving in tandem with the controls, the levels expertly weave your movesets and abilities into fun platforming levels, with mechanics and gimmicks new and returning. I especially liked the environments of the levels this time around, and seeing how these mechanics mesh with their respective, quirky worlds.Now for the new stuff. Pablo’s been more refined this time around, ditching the previously cumbersome run meter in exchange for a quick dash punch. This not only makes Pablo’s movement more snappy and consistent, but gives him better ground speed and more options to deal with foes on the ground. A much welcomed change. More than that, we have a new playstyle: Luna. Pablo’s partner on this mission. Her gameplay focuses less on running through enemies, and instead choosing to gun them down instead. She can dash over and through obstacles, and with her signature sidearm, she can give enemies a face full of bullet shots while gliding in the air. And lastly, both characters get equipped with level specific power ups. From a grass hookshot, to a fireball dash, and even an electric shotgun, the new powerups spice up the level design in interesting ways.Now we come to the awkward parts. Unlike the last game, there aren’t really much in terms of “difficulty spikes”, but there is a new overarching problem with the game: Luna’s flow. Unlike her partner, Pablo, Luna has less momentum to her gameplay. Having to shoot enemies down in situations that Pablo would have just bopped them on the head and be done with it slows the pace of the game down a bit. Not to mention, Luna’s unique kit of bullet gliding and dashes gives her kit some…unusually high mobility. While Pablo’s movement is usually tied to the whim of the stage design, Luna’s movement stares the stage in the face and sticks it’s tongue out at it while flying over it. Not that freedom isn’t appreciated, far from it. It is actually very nice. But it does have the unfortunate side effect of cheesing some of the early to mid game level design a bit. This combination of problems makes Luna feel like a less agile, floaty version of Pablo, which doesn’t really evoke the same feel as Pablo’s Levels or the previous game, to a bit of a detriment if you ask me. Also the previously mentioned control issue comes up in her levels occasionally, where her targeting reticle is sometimes hard to control while it’s not auto locked on something. Not a game breaking problem, but it is something to mention.With those quips aside, I’m thankful to see this game be made. The first game was already fantastic, and to see a sequel that improves on the formula and add it’s own spin on it is very endearing, and I hope to see more of where this series goes in the future. I hope this series continues to evolve and change in impressive ways, and until then, I heavily recommend you give this game and the previous game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great balance between a fairly straight forward grappling-hook focused platformer with some fun power-ups and likeable characters, and an incredible speed game when you get comfortable with the mechanics. Manages to have a whole lot of mechanical complexity while never forcing anyone looking for something a bit more casual to do anything too difficult. If you like 2D platformers for just about any reason you will find something to like here.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Grapple Dog is a platformer game that stands out, it really has this "you are a pinball" feeling when moving around your character. Plus, the sequel really adds plenty mechanics, all unique and fun to experiment the limits of.Really enjoyed the first one already, but Cosmic Canines now really got me hooked on the 100% road.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Cosmic Canines improves on the form and fun of the first game and brings a slew of exciting features that make the experience truly wonderful. New faces, new abilities, character customization, GUNS... and a whole lot of grappling. With an absolute banger soundtrack that tops the original, you'll be bobbing your head as you swing and shoot through beautiful environments and nasty enemies. In case you're hesitant to trust that Cosmic Canines can live up to its predecessor, the original charm is as strong as ever here, and your momentum (literally and figuratively) just keeps building as you work your way through the story. Don't let anything slow you down: get this today and thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: Grappledogs: Cosmic Canines Steam ReviewThe original Grapple Dog was released 2 years ago and soon became a classic, thanks to its eye-popping visuals and great gameplay. Its sequel aims to deliver more of that; you are in the right place to find out how. Has Joseph Gribbin and his crew pulled off another great game? A massive thanks to Dead Good Media and Super Rare Games for the review copy, and to you for watching this video.StoryThe story starts with a recap of the first game and how its events triggered the awakening of a greater threat, which will affect the multiverse. Pablo swings back into action. However this time, he’s not alone. Another gun-toting grapple dog named Luna is eager to defeat Vyr and restore peace once and for all. The shattered AllKrystal must be recovered from Vyr’s Generals.Luna has her vendetta against the multidimensional invaders and as the story progresses, you’ll learn what makes her so cold towards others. GameplayGrapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines is a 2D platformer that heavily emphasises collecting items scattered through the levels. The main items to collect are keys needed to open the passage to the world boss and gain the AllKrystall shard. As with similar games, some collectables come in the form of fruit. These are used as currency to buy cosmetics, upgrades, and even unlock bonus levels on the map. The game plays well thanks to its tight mechanics and clever level design. Both dogs share similar traits such as wall-grabbing and kicking and their trusty grapple hooks. Pablo can punch and bounce off enemies, as he could in his previous instalment. Some levels will have him using power-ups that add an extra level of complexity to the mix. Luna is more geared for offensive and lateral traversal. She can dash midair which negates any damage and can also use her gun to defeat enemies and shoot switches. Her power-ups come in the form of different ammo load-outs. These new mechanics help invigorate an already great platformer, further enhancing the experience. It also means that the developer has been able to explore the physics-based gameplay in new ways, rather than just relying on the titular grappling hook alone. These power-ups live in specific stages and are essential to reach the end. You could argue that having them as permanent unlockables would enhance the experience further. However, they make the whole experience feel like an old-school classic. Think Donkey Kong Country levels with one of your animal friends in it. For example. Those unique aids gave the levels some personality and uniqueness. Plus there is A LOT here for platformer fans!Levels come in different variations; standard ones and time-attack versions where a task must be completed as quickly as possible. The latter tests your skills and talent. Hi-score junkies will be glad to know that standard levels can be replayed as a timed trial too.After collecting enough keys, the world boss level can be challenged. These battles were varied and not too difficult. I found Destion challenging, but I needed to git gud fast.My only issue was a single soft lock that required a game reboot. It was recently released and a patch can fix any initial problems. Overall, this is a well-balanced platformer.Visuals, Audio and PresentationGrapple Dog’s iconic visuals return, combining flat colours with thick outlines and geometry. The dog duo will traverse dense forests full of giants to futuristic cities where monkeys drive flying vehicles. The clever use of parallax in the background gives the game its visual depth, but it also the little details in the foreground that bring the world to life. The little birds that fly away on approach, or the eye-catching billboard that helps build the worlds that Pablo and Luna are trying to save.  Several NPCs can interact within a stage, and although they offered small talk at best, it added to the humour and fleshed out some of the game’s characters. Don’t skip them entirely, though, some conversations may provide useful information. My favourite levels were the noir-inspired Catsablanca. Deprived of colour, these 1920’s-styled stages full of cats felt like playing on a Gameboy Pocket, so it was nostalgic on two levels.If this isn’t your thing, try out the rainbow stages that marry music and visuals via a metronome. Objects in the foreground are white, including your dog, and the beat switches platforms around.None of this would be possible without the great soundtrack. Some sweet tunes will catch you bopping along to its Jet Set Radio-esque tunes whilst swinging around levels. The fusion of jazz and scratching is sublime. Make sure you download the soundtrack, will level a link below.The overall presentation oozes tonnes of love and attention to detail. The level intros were particularly a nice touch. Conclusion		£11.99 €13.99 $14.39 $18.79CAD $21.20AUS this is with the added 20% discount until 26th September.Grappledogs: Cosmic Canines is exactly what we hope to see in a sequel. It keeps some of the best parts of the first game and adds more to the formula whilst balancing difficulty and gameplay, which can be a tough thing to do. Medallion Games seemed to have spent the last two years wisely in brewing a platformer that offers fun and challenging gameplay. This sits up there with the great games that inspired it and is an essential pick-up for fans of the genre. I am particularly looking forward to the Super Rare Games physical announcement.9/10 Grapple these Dogs Now!+ Brilliant Presentation+ Replay Value+ Sublime Soundtrack- Minor Tech issues that need patching

_childDocuments_.review: Another solid platformer, and fun to see the characters from the first game continue on.  Grapple Dogs is cute, colorful, and Luna's different playstyle adds a lot of variety to the platforming challenges.  I'm not sure if it's a little easier than the first game or just coming into this with a feel for the controls from last time made the difference, though it does feel like the timers on the time trial stages are a little more generous.  Either way it's a fun time and I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: (FYI I'm one of the playtesters in the credits)Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines is a great example of a game taking all issues of its first entry and improving on it in every way possible. The art, level design and elemental powers are fantastic, the bosses and music a big improvement over the first game, and I was surprised by how much content there is for those aiming for 100% completion. Aside from a few minor bugs along the way that damper the experience a bit, I can't recommend this game enough.And yes, you can pet the dog.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: The original Grapple Dog is one of the best platformers of the last few years and this is somehow leaps and bounds ahead of it. If you skipped that one, Cosmic Canines does a great job getting you up to speed and doesn't let up from there. It is absurdly polished, rich in level and ability variety and dazzles with genuine spectacle sometimes as well. It has platforming fundamentals down, with great controls, but doesn't feel backwards looking or referencial, giving it a confidence that few other games of it's kind have. Indie platformers aren't exactly a novelty, but games of this quality absolutely are. If you like the look of Grapple Dogs even a little, you'll be treating yourself WELL by picking it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Easy recommendation, grapple mechanic still feels very good (intuitive but deep, lots of ways to play with release timing and slack to get different trajectories). Luna was more fun than I expected. Has a pretty unique look with a great Hideki Naganuma inspired soundtrack. It probably won't take you too long to get all the crystals but I personally will probably get all of the time trial medals eventually because I like playing it that much.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: this game is Even Better then i Expected it was going to be! defenentaly better then the original grapple dog and it alsow has really cool and creative levels! for example there is cool music levels where instead of it being donkey kong style, with the entire level being shadows it has white vibrant and colorfull music levels! and i thought that was pretty cool! good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was a nice surprise and this one expands on it in significant way. More environnement, additional power for pablo, and a second half with Luna that add run and gun element to the mix. It all works quite well, retain the charm of the original, play real well and is just fun as a whole. highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Grapple Dogs: Cosmic Canines

_childDocuments_.review: Swing, jump, and blast through dimensions in the follow-up to the critically-acclaimed 2D action-platformer Grapple Dog. Zip between action-packed worlds as Pablo and Luna team up to save the cosmos in their own unique ways.

name: Empire of the Ants
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Experience Empire of the Ants like never before with the Digital Deluxe Edition. This exclusive package offers players a deeper dive into the world of ants with a 3-day early access, a digital artbook, stunning HD wallpapers, and an immersive soundtrack. About the Game Knights in chitin armor: fight for your Queen, the Federation... our Empire Experience an immersive journey and defend your lands through tactical and strategic battles in an epic, microscopic world. Play as 103,683rd, an ant of the warrior caste with an inquisitive mind: explore the Federation and fight for it, conquering new territories. Exploring, strategizing, and forging alliances with the local wildlife will be crucial to emerge victorious from the many challenges lying ahead. _childDocuments_.review: There is fun to be had here. Graphically, it's beautiful. The animations are great. The gameplay overall is fun. It's got a pretty good level of tactics and strategy. And, with the amount of time I've had so far, no bugs, glitches, or crashes. Simply, I like the game and I feel comfortable with the asking price.*Disclaimer: The following is my own personal opinion and I hope the devs see and read this and hopefully implement some of my desired features.*The game is basically an RTS top-down point and click strategy game that was turned into a 3rd person game. It has more in common with Empires of the Undergrowth. I say this because, unfortunately, you are nothing but a commander of sorts. Initially, I thought the game would be a type of RPG ant-roleplaying game, with a lot of inspiration from the Sim Ant game from 1991. Sadly, you (as an ant) cannot forage resources or battle enemies. You cannot freely enter your colony's ant hill and dig or excavate your underground city of tunnels. Your only purpose is to roam and command legions of ants and ally insects. You, yourself, cannot help gather food and resources or engage in combat. I really wish this wasn't the case and really hope the devs can patch this in.

_childDocuments_.review: As an ant game lover, I really can't give this game a thumbs down... but I'm still disappointed that it's not the same RTS style as "Empire of the Ants" from 2000 or "Empires of the Undergrowth" or even "SimAnt", where you actually take part in building a colony: gathering food, nursing brood, engaging in combat, etc. In this game, you play more like a scout and commander, with everything taking place above ground, which kind of loses that true ant colony vibe. There's no attacking the enemy queen in her protected lair…So yes, I am a bit disappointed.
