_childDocuments_.review: Empire of the ants is a third-person RTS based on a novel of the same name. The game puts you in the role of a commander ant that can traverse the battlefield and order units around in order to win wars for your federation.Given the more grounded perspective, the gameplay sits somewhere in the middle of the spectrum in terms of RTS complexity, which I found really enjoyable.You can only control a handful of units at a time. The basic three unit types are warriors, workers and gunners, all of which beat each other in a rock, paper, scissors-like manner. However, given your charming ant pheromones, you can also utilize other species as special units, like beetles that can aggro multiple other units at once, or aphids that heal your nearby troops.The main way to shift victory into your hands is by capturing nests around the landscape. These can then house upgrades for your army, defences for the nest itself, or even grant you active abilities that you can use to buff your units during battle, or fast travel around the map. Nests have a finite number of chambers that can be used to create these upgrades, and each nest can only create and be the home of one unit. This means that you need to expand your territory quickly, and be thoughtful about how and where you create different upgrades.The story mode was much more engaging than I expected. There are no signs of humans aside from occasional leftover objects like footballs. You are left to your devices as a meager ant, trying to win a war for your federation. There are short snippets of dialogue in between missions that tell a tale of intrigue and drama. I never would've expected to be invested in peace treaties between ants and termites, but I really was!This is very much helped by the lovely execution of feeling like a tiny ant in this vast world. Shallow amounts of flooding are clearly detrimental to your tiny bodies, and all of it is accentuated by the gorgeous art direction and graphical fidelity of the game, as well as the wonderful soundtrack and sound effects. All of this really brings the ant fantasy to life.Interestingly, the singleplayer mode has a number of different types of missions for different play styles, and you don't have to do them all, allowing you to experience the parts of the game you enjoy the most. Aside from the strategic combat encounters, there are also missions that purely have you explore, or traverse the level, which I also found quite enjoyable.Currently, the multiplayer modes only allow for 1v1 or 3FFA, but I think it'd be really cool to see some sort of team modes as well.As for my gripes with the game, I found that sometimes I was stuck watching fights go on for a while with not much to do. Perhaps it's maybe because I'm not the best at RTS games and so don't multi-task as much as I could. Although it was always fun to watch my warrior ants yeet ladybugs into orbit, so I can't complain too much.Additionally, some of the UI can get a bit confusing at times. I love the intuitive and almost diagetic base building UI, but distinguishing between friendly, enemy and allied units is not as clear as it should be in the chaos of combat.However, overall I really love the charm and attention to detail the game brings. It is really a lovely atmosphere and experience to play, and although the game is maybe more simple than a traditional RTS, I think the way everything is balanced is very thoughtful and results in really rewarding gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard review to write because I absolutely appreciate the devs for giving this concept life. However where the game falls short for me is the complete lack of colony management and having conversational dialogue between Ants to move the "story" forward which is extremely immersion breaking when set against realistic graphics.For some odd reason in the back of my mind I had hoped it would have been a modern version of Sim Ant from SNES. A game where you could start a colony from scratch with a single queen and grow it into a sizable nest before the colony got so big that war with the red ants was unavoidable. This just seems to focus on rock-paper-scissor instance wars that you enter by running around talking to different Ants. At the end of the day the game is beautiful and it's my fault for having high expectations. If they ever incorporate colony management in the future then this game will hands down be an unquestionable winner, but until then I can't really recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give it a neutral rating in its actual state but since there is none I have to give it a thumbs down. Its recommended on sale around 20-30 bucks no questions asked but its not worth the 39,99 or 49,99 for the digital deluxe edition because there are too much things bugging (haha!) me.The graphics and music are beautiful! I am now through the whole story campain with ~15 hrs played. Its fun to run around as ant, jumping from leaves to leaves (yeah you heard right, you can and have to jump in the story when things turn into a plattformer for some missions) and just gazing at the landscapes. Maybe you asked yourself "♥♥♥♥♥, normal ants jumping??!!11" Ah, I see you are an ant nerd! Don´t expect to much realism from the game, you will be disappointed in the details. But if you always wanted to ride a mantis while commanding armies of ants towards other ants then keep reading. Thats the kind of game to expect and it looks damn good! :)That beeing said I got the feeling alot that the devs cared more about the visualisation then other stuff. There are a few mission types during the story campain. I would describe them as skirmish, scouting, hunting and plattforming. Whilst the devs tried to put variety to those missions, the feel very repetitive after a while.Same goes with me for the combat. Its supposed to be an RTS but it feels like playing Overlord or Bannerlords with ants.You are limited to a maximum of 7 legions, with 3 basic types of units (melee, gunner, worker), one of three superpredators and one of three support units. While I had a fun watching the battles the combat didnt suck me into it wanting more. I was also disappointed that your ant character cant doing anything besides giving orders, building stuff and buff troops. There is no way to interact with the enemy yourself. Even if you get "attacked" there is only a health bar depleting. No enemy is interacting with you at any time... maybe this was lazy development or it was because of the multiplayer part of the game to not get stucked colliding or beeing surrounded by troops. I dont know but its not immersive at all.Other stuff that annoyed me was at one point at the story you gotta fight against black ants. In the cutscene you gotta see that they are colored black but ingame you are just fighting against the same model of ants as yours. That and other stuff seemed just lazy for me.One can also only hope no one with arachnophobie is playing this game. I dont think they will make it through the story...So in short I regret to buy the digital deluxe edition for the head up start. I wanted to support the devs because its an ant game but in retrospective a little discount would have been the right way to go for myself.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, yes, it's a visually stunning game, much thanks to the UE5, and their photorealistic scans.Now that thats out of the way:RTS: It's so barebones that any RTS fans would get frustrated at how few options you have. The ants also don't move like you anyone would expect ants to move, they basically move in a circle formation, and just attack whatever circle bugs they need to fight and just the edge of the circle starts fighting the edge of the other circle. It's extremely simplistic programming here, and it really shows.You also are limited to one type of worker ants (they can double as a melee ant if needed), melee ants, and ranged ants. That's it. You can upgrade those to "veteran" or "elite" versions, but visually they don't change. And you can only have a set amount of "legions" (which is one circle, if you refer to what I said earlier), which is less than 10 if I remember correctly.You do have some other unique unit types you can add in there, but they're not really that relevant. It's a "healer" type of bug, and a "tank\taunt" type of bug, I'm sure you get some more unique types of bugs as you move along the story, but I didn't really care enough to bother getting past my refund time to find out what a snail would be like to ride in battle. You can't even have any sort of organization, or grouping, you either command ONE circle, or ALL the circles. And this includes your worker ants, which are supposed to be gathering resources (which there are only 2 of: food and wood). And instead of being a "top down" camera god, you're one of the ants running alongside them. Can you do anything other than "buff" your units? Nope. Can you fight? Nope. your ant is just a glorified camera that can jump.So anyone who's every played RTS games can agree that this game's RTS aspect is aligned with what you would expect from a mobile game RTS... But even those are getting more advanced than this.And what about the rest? Well, the rest is like I said mediocre. You're allowed to "explore" the map they've made, and you have some minigames like "catch 3 fireflies", which is just walk on them and they disappear, and other collection and discoveries, like circling a football, or some other stuff that just gives you a journal entry you can read.There's a story in there as well, about ants fleeing a flood and so on, but anything that isn't you battling something is just added on top as sprinkles. You really feel that they didn't really put much depth into that either. And you have about 25hours of the story mode, which is mainly doing one battle after the other.Pricing a glorified tech demo about ants at 40€ is ridiculous. Had it been at 20€, I'd be less critical of it, but you get WAY more depth in a 10 year old RTS game for 20€ than you do from this game. This game just looks pretty.You can't even crawl into the ant nest. Seriously. At certain points you'll have a cutscene where you enter the nest and after a loading screen with a video looping of you walking, you'll end up in a chat room with the queen, where you get told what to do, and then you automatically leave and you're on the surface again. Wanna go back in and check what else is in the hive? Nope, black wall blocks the entrance. You're an ant, in an ant colony, and you can't even enter the main base of operations.Wait until a sale puts it at\below 20€, then you'll feel a lot better with the visual nature tour you got, with some RTS elements in there. 40€ is extremely overpriced.
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews because I usually don’t care enough, but I’m making an exception for this. No other game comes close to what this could have been. Visually, it’s amazing. The perspective of being an ant is outstanding, and you can lose yourself just wandering around looking at stuff. But once the novelty wears off, you’re left with painfully barebones gameplay.If I were five, this would be awesome. But for anyone who wants depth, this game doesn’t deliver.Now, if it had the visuals and perspective it does, combined with the depth of Empires of the Undergrowth and RTS mechanics like Mount & Blade: Bannerlord? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, that would be next-level. Sadly, I doubt it’ll go that way—it probably wasn’t the devs’ vision—but damn, that’s the ant game I dream of.I hope the devs see this and think about what this game could be. If they push it in that direction, I’d buy it again in a heartbeat. Until then, I can’t recommend it for anyone who expects real depth from a $50 game.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who adores ants, I was eagerly awaiting this game for months and even bought it on pre-order. Unfortunately, I ended up returning it, as I couldn’t justify spending $40 on something that fell so short of my expectations. I get that it’s a fresh release and updates will likely come, but the game feels so superficial—literally! You can’t even go inside the ant nests beyond cut-scenes, which is such a missed opportunity for depth and immersion.As a landscape designer, I was really excited about the detailed and atmospheric ecology shown in the preview. This was about the only positive aspect for me. The gameplay itself felt really dull, and it seemed like little effort was spent consulting with entomologists or even researching ant behavior. One of the early mechanics is learning how to jump, which is odd, given that ants aren’t known for jumping. There’s also a species-collection mechanic where you add entries to a diary, but it feels more like a checklist than an immersive experience. For anyone interested in myrmecology, I’d recommend Empires of the Undergrowth over this game—while it might not be as aesthetic, it’s far more engaging and educational.

are the chosen ant number 340433244524, and you go around doing some missions given to you by the queen they are all told with very high importance but in the end what you actually do is jump onto _childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this is a story driven game based off of the book with the same name and vaguely similar to the 2000's version of the game. Don't expect a city builder, expect a campaign similar to starcraft.Gameplay is 7/10 | Units are easy to control and fights could be harder IMO. The units run off of a rock paper scissors style system. Controlling 103,683 when she is upside down is a bit difficult, as the game does not invert your controls for you, but that's a minor gripe. Upgrades and economy could be a bit more complex but as this is more story driven I personally don't mind.Art style/visuals/graphics are 10/10 | Hands down the best looking game I've ever played. Photo-realistic is the word that comes to mind. The sense of scale is amazing and it makes you feel truly tiny.Soundtrack is a 10/10 | Mathieu, Mark, You both outdid yourselves here. Buying the Deluxe edition just for the soundtrack was well worth it. You've perfectly composed a documentary style orchestra and I'm glad you both are on my radar now.You like ants? Buy this game. I'd argue it should be 60$ but for 20+ hours of gameplay it is well worth the price. I only wish the game had a built in map editor so that you could make your own PvP/PvE maps. THAT would make this game timeless IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep it simple for those wanting to know if this is worth it:- It's worth the price- 16 hours of content at a decent pace (100% missions and story)- Visually outstanding- There's multiplayer but none for the story- The story does have some loose ends but isn't bad- There is a good variety in units, so you're not forced into one playstyle- The missions are surprisingly not the same all throughout. Some are hunting missions (solo), some are stealth missions (solo), escort missions, strategy missions, defence missions...etc- The audio is like butter perfectly coated over a slice of toast. There are brief moments of odd silence without music during some missions but it's nothing too jarring If you like ants and want some delicious insect eye-candy, grab this. You won't regret it

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game. The world is beautiful, walking around like an ant in a tiny yet large world was great. That being said i feel there is so much wasted potential in this. As a big fan of empire of the undergrowth I may be coming at this with a bias. I had hoped for some epic fights against behemoths. For example  one mission in empire of the undergrowth has you battle a giant american bull frog and after its defeat your nest gets swarmed with amphibians looking to move in after the top predators defeat. something along those lines  would of been amazing. I understand the game is loosely based on the book by the same name but when creating a game about ants you have the possibility to make anything a threat and create any story. The mission with the preying mantis was a good example, actually i expected the enemy to come out with its own giant insect so my mantis could fight with it. I was disappointed at thatAnyways games great, i had no interest in the multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: - Graphics  are amazing.- Multiplayer seems very basic. Not very thought provoking when it comes to unit movement and resource management.-  If you happen to be involved in the first "war" started on the map (in 3 FFA) it is very easy for the person not involved in that engagement to mop up the scraps after it is over and claim a swift victory. - I feel the game could benefit greatly with a Co-op campaign and increased player limit in PvP. - Hopefully the devlopers will continue to refine this game, it has great potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing Happens.I was a little irked when it dawned on me I wouldn't be in some massive garden exploring or something but running around little maps with loading screens in between things. Then I realised I couldn't go into the nest unless prompted to but it was just a cut scene. ' Ok' I thought, but its beautiful and probably good in other ways. _childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: Massively disappointing. I had such high hopes for this game, and it was a giant let down. It LOOKS amazing, I do really enjoy just wandering around the environment as an ant, and everything looks really cool. HOWEVER, the game play is absurdly basic, there is no colony mechanics. I was really hoping to have an open world, survival type colony sim, but as an ant, instead I got... idk a really bland extraction type game kinda. A mission starts, you load into a new area, and complete an objective. You cant leave a space or the screen greys out. You cant wander the interior of the nest, or construct new tunnels or rooms. Its all surface level. Game has SOOOOO much potential but falls flat. Maybe they can use the same engine and pull of Empire of Ants 2 that has the depth needed to engage but this is a massive miss imo. Do not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: The negative reviews are made in good faith. The game is beautiful and just misses the mark. The mechanics are nice, the physics are fun and only slightly embellished. The cut scenes are short and minimalist but fit the game and story. You cannot build and manage a colony, total miss. Empire of the Undergrowth looks far worse and is a much better game. Who knows what updates will bring but for now, go play Undergrowth. Costs far less and has a ton of better and more satisfying content. I am not unhappy that I purchased the game because I like supporting non AAA games but I also cannot recommend the game with such an unsatisfying game play/story dynamic.
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  Looks great, great fun.  Love ant games.HOWEVER, the sole purpose for this thumbs down is the structure of the campaign.  NO SPOILERS.  This campaign, time and time again, builds up to a big thing that is going to happen.  You do your missions, you talk to all the ants around, you uncover story and intrigue, and then that big thing that you were looking forward to just takes place in "memory pheromones."  So you read a little bit on screen about what happened.  And every time you're left like, "Well GEE I sure would have liked to actually PLAY through that or see that level design or actually DO some story stuff."  This just leaves the story as a glorified tutorial of sorts where you play the same kinds of missions over and over.  You do get better.  You do learn more about how to play.  But the best STORY parts of the STORY are nothing but disappointing reading.  Like yo, come on.  I don't plan to go play this online and pvp people.  VERY few of your customer base is planning to do that (this is not going to have a thriving multiplayer community, I waited for 5 minutes looking for an online match, found none, and gave up).  We're here for a good solo experience.  And while this is fun to play, it gets quite repetitive, the RTS gets jumbled and hard to discern what is going on, and the BEST story parts are nothing but "sit still and read what happened" instead of actually playing through it.  There are about 3 times that has happened so far, and this last one made me pause the game and actually write this review, because the whole story was leading up to it and I got so slapped in the face with the fact that I didn't take part in what was happening that I just had to come warn anyone that is going to get this for the singleplayer experience.  Anyways, grab it on sale.  Have some mindless fun with being an ant and stuff.  But DUDE did this fall flat on its face on HUGE climactic story points that had SO much potential to be unique levels and experiences to play through.  And that, in my humble opinion, warrants a thumbs down since I (and most all others) are going to be in this for the solo experience.  I'm just sad, man.  What a wasted opportunity for some of these big moments
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: Not really the game I was expecting, alot of features missing that I would have thought to be standard in games by now - like being able to do coop with friends vs ai. Massively love ants, and was expecting at the very least some kind of research put into it so that the ants you can control would at least be native to the same regions.The game is quite fun, don't get me wrong, its a fun little RTS that's pretty basic to the grips of, visually amazing, and puts an emphasis on expansion to be able to succeed in campaign and multiplayer. That being said, I'm very surprised there was nothing involving the interior of the nest - aside a couple cutscenes where you don't even get to explore the interior. I like the idea of controlling the colony from the pov of one of the ants, quite a fresh take on it and I think it works really well. I'm not overly impressed with the game, as it seems most of the work has been put into the way it looks, and it's made some other aspects of the game suffer - such as unit variation, nest building, maybe even a persistent colony nest that you can actively help to grow and progress the way you think is best. Still gonna play it quite a bit, and look forward to any updates and what they might add :)
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning graphics and very well animated while still performing quite well. Engaging story. Still giving this a thumbs down because of the misleading description and demo. _childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: I only play pvp. Currently Gold V. I've been pleasently surprisingly to find this game is deep and polished rts gameplay wise.This game is about hard counters, timing, positioning, and resource management / decision making.Rock Paper Scissors unit balancingEconomy Vs Defense SpendingHigh Travel Time makes unit positioning and timing attacking very significantThe close camera makes vantage points very important to commanding effectively in addition to upgrades and abilities to gather intelYou choose which support, super unit, starting unit, and which four spells you can make in each matchThe impact of your choices can change depending on which map you playThe initial balance seems to be that beetle super units with the snail support unit is just extremely strong. I would call it op as it makes units practically unkillable.That said there are many strategies that seem viable in my experience so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game but there's some things that make me go crazy. Timed missions. They're beyond stressful making this unenjoyable. _childDocuments_.name: Empire of the Ants

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game wasn't the ant sim i was hoping for the game play is still quite fun  and extremely immersive . I can see why people aren't happy with the finished product but id still give it a try if you are open to ant style games to have a new twist on the genre .Pros:(for me). I enjoyed spending time on collectables . Visuals are extremely well made and are stunning at the worst. Runs very well wast upholding said graphics. Easy style of combat to get used too . Lots of game play story wise (so far). Online combat is fun. Different from other ant games. Nice to control more than antsCons:(for me). Feels like there should be more game play for the price the game is set at. Wish there was a little more diversity . The drowning speed although not major can be annoying at times . _childDocuments_.review: I actually love the game. but I cant recommend the game for now. this game needs difficulty setting / options.I feel the game difficulty set to easy in early game, and turns to very hard when you get in mid game. in mid game, you have to at least do a mission once to scout the area and remember the locations. you have to pick legions, build structures correctly; and your timing should be very precise. because you have "no room for error". one single mistake could lead you to fail. the spawning rate of the enemy's legions sometimes feels too fast. even they have fewer nests (base), they can spawn faster-stronger legion than yours.if you are a hardcore gamer, you can try it out.if you are more casual and you want to enjoy the beautiful graphic of the ant's world, better stay away from this game (at least for now until the dev give difficulty setting)

_childDocuments_.review: The game has great potential, but gameplay is severely lacking. I was going through the story and figured the guided part was the tutorial, but it never stopped. I was expecting an Ant version of "Human Odyssey," but I then got a "fixed to the rails" storyline that deviates not one bit. I was excited to be thrust into the world of ants, but instead, I was locked into a ride that is equally as thrilling and linear as Disney's "It's  a small world after all" kiddie ride. I love the concept, but if you want to have a game that blows people away, then you need to take some open world and gameplay hints from Ancestors: Humankind Odyssey. The fortunate thing is there is much room for improvement, it's not a lost cause. I would recommend purchase when on sale in the hopes of a future addition of an open world sand box style survival. Visually stunning and detailed as far as graphically, which is certainly not for nothing. I bought it not on sale(unfortunately) but because the gameplay footage was amazing, I thought I was about to dive into this massive Ant filled world, instead I should have jumped into the reviews and descriptions. The story mode is just a glorified Tela Novela for ants, like real ants,so you can imagine how interesting that would be to a human. 😬 I have not played the multi-player (which I appreciate the addition of) but we all know the average game has multi-player on a less detail oriented experience in lieu of playing with a larger community or co-op-ing. I will definitely check it out. But research people, if you care about you dollar. 🤷🏼‍♂️🦅🇺🇲

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all over the place. Some levels you can build units. Other levels you are locked with pre-existing units. Sometimes you build defenses around your ant hills, sometimes you can't. Sometimes you can use powers, sometimes you can't. Some levels have radar to find things, those same level the radar stops working when you get near an object. It's like the developers designed a level and thought it was too easy. So they picked a random thing to change on the level to make it harder.There is zero consistency from level to level. If you love games where the developers put in arbitrary limits on you in the name if difficulty, this game is for you. However if you like your games to have set rules that are uniform throughout the game then this game is not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely gorgeous game about ants. If you're familiar with the Overlord and Pikmin games, the gameplay is like that, where you control your main lil' ant, and then have legions (groups) of others you can command to move around and fight etc, and it works on a hard counter system, like rock-paper-scissors. Worker ants beat gunners, gunners beat soldiers, soldiers beat workers etc.During battle, your ant doesn't actively partake, but you can get powers to use to help your legions out.Movement is for the most part perfect fine, but when it comes to tight spaces and intersecting areas (like branches), it can get a little finicky and difficult to have it go the way you want, especially notable on super rough terrain. If you move slowly it's not a huge issue, but if you use the sprint, you'll often find yourself flung off into the sunset.As hilarious as it is to accidentally fling yourself into the water again, it can be a bit annoying if you're trying to get somewhere fast.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is riddled with bugs!And now, information about the campaign for the wary consumer, from someone who has actually played the game to completion. Spoilers ahead for the types of missions present in the game.36 total missions, across 5 chapters. and 4 mission categories.2 "Traversal" missions, where the mission is entirely composed of semi-difficult platforming, with frequent checkpoints and quick re-spawns. These serve mostly as exposition for the game's story, and contain no RTS elements at all.Exploration missions contain no RTS elements at all. There are 9 "Exploration" missions, of which-- 1 is a tutorial platforming stage introducing you to the movement controls-- 3 are "Hunt" missions where you must kill a certain amount of insects by jumping on them in a large area with no minimap-- 3 are "Find Object" missions where you must find a certain amount of friendly insects and interact with them (two of these are timed, but the insects are always in the same places) in a large area with no minimap-- 2 are "Stealth" missions where you must scan a certain amount of objects, legions, and nests and then escape, but there is no punishment for dyingTactic missions contain RTS elements, but some of them remove your ability to build legions or upgrades. There are 13 "Tactic" missions, of which-- 6 are "Wave Defense" missions where you defend your nests or legions from waves of enemies with the legions provided-- 4 are "Eliminate" missions where you must kill a legion, nest, headquarters, or neutral camp with the legions provided-- 2 are "Gather Resources" missions where you must get a certain amount of resources within the time limit-- 1 is an "Escort" mission where you lead a friend to the end of the map while being attacked from all sides by enemy legionsStrategic missions contain only RTS elements, and never restrict the type of upgrades or legions you can make. For most of them, you can also choose which super-unit and support unit you want before the mission starts. There are 12 "Strategic" missions, of which-- 7 are "1v1" missions where you fight one enemy-- 3 are "1v1v1" missions where you fight two enemies that will not or cannot come to one another's aid, or else actively fight one another.-- 2 are "1v2" missions where you fight two enemy AIs at once (neither mission is required to beat the game, and they are substantially harder than any other missions)

_childDocuments_.review: This game comes close to getting a good review from me, but it falls short in one particular fashion that makes all the beneficial elements non-valid.The good:It's a good game for ant style enjoyers, it has fun dialogue, there's a variety of mission types, and the combat, while very simple is fairly enjoyable for any RTS fans, the world -looks- fantastic, (Absolutely a con if you don't have a high end computer, it will run like steam fried ass).The bad:The controls are quite possibly the single worst I have had on any game, you control your RTS elements by running around on the ground level. So, seeing what is happening is very crucial to doing that. So you'd expect the movement to be the most ironed out situation, even more so with an ant wherein you are supposedly highly mobile and able to climb everything.Wrong. Your ant has severe epilepsy and -WILL- start spinning around at randomly because you encountered a small stick, equally, your ant does not handle like an ant if you use the sprint, (Which is needed due to the high pace of the missions), it will instead handle like a rally car with all the suspension removed, you will spend more time in the air, then moving forward. You are literally slower sprinting in some situations than you are walking at a snails pace. Equally, there are collectable butterflies and beetles on certain levels that for the completion, you need to collect. However, the butterflies are erratic and will fly away, this would be fine and would present a challenge if it were not for my ant developing a panic attack and flying sideways away from the direction I jumped in due to divine intervention. Three times I managed to sneak up on the butterfly, and three times did my ant defy the laws of physics and sail off to the side. The lack of mobility renders every other feature of the game incredibly frustrating, at best. If they fix the mobility, the game would be good, perhaps, but seeing as I highly suspect they will -not- fix the mobility, do not buy it. Fortunately, I received the game for free, this is fantastic, as I would rather tap dance on lego then pay this much money for this game. To recap:The RTS: Made jarring by the movement.The exploration missions: Made jarring by the movement.The army commanding: Made jarring by the movement.The collection missions: Made jarring by the movement.A lot of these represent a simple fix, time will tell if they consider it.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually amazing game and runs great! Game play loop is pretty good and the combat animations are AMAZING, very well done. The story is actually pretty good so far, the talking between the ants feels like some kind of fantasy and actually makes we want to go out and read the books, and there are some clever eggs when you find them.Where it kinda lacks are things that have been said already, your ant can't participate in the combat but you are pretty much support and deal out buffs. This isn't a colony management game or anything but if that is your bag then Empires of the Undergrowth is your game (which is also amazing.) When the workers are gathering food it would be nice to see the food item dwindle down even if its just an animation. The units you get move in groups and not very ant like, but since it is an rts that might make sense. There are also times where I feel like there are too many units per legion and clutter up the field a bit. I really would love to see the PC ant be able to do some melee combat and have some underground colony areas though.There is also some jank with the camera at times which makes precision jumping difficult to calculate during certain story missions but that is the only real gripe I have with the platforming sections other than some missions have specific mechanics only for that mission and sometimes they don't feel all the way fleshed out.Multiplayer is actually pretty great, its fast pace and there is 1v1 AI skirmish as well.All in all, this and Empires make two great games for Ant lovers.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve really been enjoying this game! It's worth noting that the game is inspired by Bernard Werber’s Ants book series. The main ant character in the books participates in both battles and exploration missions, which is why this game doesn’t fit the mold of a pure RTS.The game is absolutely stunning. The visuals are incredibly well-done and add so much to the immersive experience. Personally, I’m quite happy with it. The atmosphere of the books is well captured, and it brings back memories of my teenage years when I was a big Werber fan. I particularly enjoy the strategic and battle missions—once you get familiar with the building dynamics, it’s an absolute blast. However, I tend to lose interest during the exploration missions. That’s just my personal preference; I’m sure others might feel the opposite.One thing that truly impressed me is the game’s stability—I haven’t encountered a single bug since I started playing, which is quite rare these days.It’s not a fully open-world game where your ant can explore the depths of the woods, nor is it a traditional RTS. Instead, it strikes a unique balance between the two genres. That said, if the developers were to release a DLC or a patch allowing you to manage an entire colony or explore a sprawling anthill, it would be the ultimate addition to this experience.Initially, the only downside for me was that the game didn’t support my widescreen display. Thankfully, this issue has since been resolved with a patch.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of the Ants takes players on an unexpected journey into the insect world, blending RTS mechanics with a third-person perspective to create a truly unique gaming experience. Based on the novel of the same name, this game offers a campaign filled with intrigue, tactical combat, and a surprising level of depth for what is essentially a story-driven strategy game. While the game excels in certain areas, it does leave a few key features wanting.At its core, Empire of the Ants is an RTS with a twist. You are not managing a sprawling ant colony or directly controlling every aspect of your army like in traditional RTS games. Instead, you play as a single commander ant, tasked with overseeing and directing your forces on the battlefield. The rock-paper-scissors combat system keeps things accessible but strategic, as you deploy units—warriors, workers, and gunners—that counter each other’s strengths and weaknesses.The real fun comes from the ability to recruit and utilize various insect species, such as beetles and aphids, who add unique abilities to your army. Beetles can aggro multiple enemies at once, while aphids provide healing to nearby ants. These special units introduce a fun layer of complexity, allowing you to craft diverse strategies for every encounter.The game leans heavily on territory control, with nests serving as both a means to expand your army and unlock powerful upgrades. This gives a real sense of progression as you capture and defend new areas, but it can also lead to a somewhat repetitive pattern of "capture and upgrade" that, depending on your preferences, might feel like it's lacking in variation. The limited number of units you can control at once means you're always actively engaged, but some players may find themselves wishing for a little more complexity in the larger strategic management.Where Empire of the Ants truly shines is in its visual and atmospheric design. The game boasts some of the most impressive graphics in recent RTS titles, with a photo-realistic art style that captures the scale of being an ant in a vast, hostile world. Every blade of grass feels like a towering tree, every drop of water a dangerous flood. The attention to detail is staggering, with environmental elements like flooding or the constant threat of predators always keeping you on edge. The sense of scale is unlike anything I’ve experienced in a game, making you truly feel like a small, vulnerable creature in a sprawling world of giants.The soundtrack complements this atmosphere beautifully. A sweeping, orchestral score punctuates moments of triumph and tension, creating an emotional undercurrent that elevates the experience. The sound design is similarly top-notch, with the buzz of wings, the crunch of enemies underfoot, and the subtle hum of ant pheromones all contributing to a sense of immersion.The story in Empire of the Ants is more engaging than I expected. Between missions, short dialogue snippets reveal the political and social struggles of the ant world, from peace talks with termites to the internal power struggles of your federation. While this may not sound exciting on paper, the game does a wonderful job of making these small moments feel significant. The absence of human influence in the world, save for some scattered objects like footballs, allows the game to build a completely immersive insect kingdom. You’ll find yourself invested in the fate of these tiny creatures, which is a testament to the game’s world-building.Combat in Empire of the Ants is fun, but at times it feels a bit limited. While the game offers some engaging tactical opportunities, especially with the inclusion of special units, the overall strategy doesn’t evolve much throughout the campaign. You’ll often find yourself repeating the same patterns of capturing nests, deploying units, and battling enemies. The game could have benefited from more varied combat mechanics or a greater variety of unit types to keep things fresh.There’s also an issue with pacing at times. Watching battles unfold can be exciting, especially when your warriors send enemy ants flying through the air, but it can also lead to long stretches of inaction where you're left watching the outcome play out without much to do. For players who thrive on constant engagement, this may be a bit of a drawback.The user interface (UI) can feel a bit clunky at times, especially during the chaos of battle. It’s not always easy to distinguish between friend, foe, and allied units, which can be frustrating in larger skirmishes. The base-building UI is intuitive and almost organic in design, but the overall clarity could use some refinement. Similarly, some players may find the camera control a bit awkward when navigating the environment as an ant. While it’s not a major issue, it does detract from the otherwise fluid experience.Ultimately, Empire of the Ants is a game that’s easy to recommend for fans of RTS titles who want something a little different. The unique perspective, gorgeous visuals, and captivating world-building make it a standout in the genre. However, its simplicity in terms of strategy and gameplay may not appeal to those seeking a deeper or more complex experience. Despite a few UI issues and occasional pacing problems, Empire of the Ants delivers a fun, engaging, and surprisingly emotional adventure in the tiny world of ants. If you’re looking for an immersive RTS with a fresh twist, this game is well worth the crawl through its many battles.Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: After a bit of solo play and two multiplayer games, this is definitely one of my favorites of the year, and I’m eager to keep going. I highly recommend this game for the refreshing experience it offers and the unique approach of a third-person “accessible” RTS that works well with a controller, though it’s very playable on a keyboard depending on the setup you prefer.In more detail: the game is visually stunning, showcasing nature beautifully, and it runs smoothly. I think we’ll get used to this kind of standard with Unreal Engine 5, but it’s still impressive. Content-wise, there’s a single-player campaign where you play as a scout ant (apparently following Bernard Werber's book, which I haven’t read) that combines “adventure/exploration” missions with more “tactical/strategic” ones. The game’s appeal for me lies in the latter aspect, which works really well in multiplayer. Anyway, it seems like there’s a fair amount of content between the solo campaign and multiplayer modes.You choose your starter, support unit, and predator unit. A small downside is that the support unit doesn’t seem very useful (except maybe for the rhino beetles, but not really for the others). On the other hand, predator units are truly the backbone of your setup. I’ve tried 1v1 but haven’t tested 1v1v1 (which doesn’t appeal to me as much). You spawn with two nests, your starter unit, and you need to quickly get your economy going by capturing and upgrading nests (resource production, new units, powers, new info, etc.) – a good knowledge of the maps seems essential. So far, it’s hard to tell if a defensive or aggressive meta will emerge, but one thing’s for sure: you can’t mess up your economy and need to unlock unit upgrades quickly. Looking forward to seeing the depth of the gameplay over time and the variety of maps. Games go by quickly and are intense – and it’s hard to recover if you start off poorly. Even though it’s a casual RTS, it’s not very forgiving of mistakes! So, it’s actually more challenging than I expected in multiplayer – which some will love, and others might not.Overall, I’m really enjoying it so far, and I think it’ll keep me hooked for quite a few more hours. The game seems to deliver on its scope and does what it intends well, at a fair price. That said, I hope for a big focus on multiplayer in future updates: new units or factions, perhaps making the scout ant more impactful (in combat, affecting the economy, not sure how), the option to play with more than three players and in teams, maybe on larger maps with different game modes, etc. The solo campaign is nice, but there’s potential here for a great multiplayer and competitive game if updates come quickly and the developers provide a transparent roadmap.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of the Ants is a wonderful little game, especially if you or your kids love ants. But its also relatively shallow. While it takes full advantage Unreal Engine 5 to deliver some very realistic visuals ultimately the game often feels fairly flat especially in its exploration missions and ultimately never manages to hit the peaks that you would hope.Ovear all it's a fun game that looks great but i'm left wishing there was more meat on the bone.Absolutely gorgeous and lifelike visuals that shows off what Unreal Engine 5 when used properly and optimised efficiently so it doesn't stress your system. First up the game runs flawlessly for me.I play at 4K with DLSS set to Auto and fps locked to 60 with all settings turned up to Max. Not a single issue with performance and my system runs at about 75% max load with out excessive fan noise which is really impressive for an UE5 game especially at 4K.I can reduce the upscaling and push my system load up to 88% / 95% but i don't like the excessive load especially when DLSS delivers such a nice image and auto allows the engine to keep my frames where i want them.The power of  Nanite on full display here. The complex details of the ground really stand out and are a critical feature given that you are spending all your time as an ant so close to objects.  Nanite allows for these really complex meshes to be delivered to the renderer without taxing the system and without any noticable popin of lower LOD. The texture / surfacing work is also really nicely done. Everything looks or feels just as you would expect and all of this is topped off by some very good sound design. When you walk over different surfaces the game audio responds correctly just adding to the tactile nature of the world.The insect models also look gorgeous. They are nicely detailed and the shading is incredibly lifelike. Given that we are in this tiny world things like subsurface light scattering through some of the creatures bodies or various plants is a key part of getting things to feel natural. Not sure if the game is leaning heavily on GI for its lighting but it all feels very natural. Shadddows are detailed and soften off in a reaslitic way. It all looks really really good.Gameplay feels like a 3rd person adventure game mixed with some very light RTS type action. Its not your typical overly hardcore micromanagement style or RTS. You are an ant that roams around the battlefield and commands various groups through interaction. Selecting a specific group is done easily with keyboard or mouse wheel, then you aim with right click and then left click to confirm where you want to send them or what you want them to attack or gather.Different classes of Ant will do different tasks. Some mele attack. Others have ranged attacks. Others are specifically for gathering resources food. There are also some shallow base building mechanics that allow you to choose which troops to create or what defences to build up around your base.You are the commander ant telling your various legions what to do. You find a high perch for a good vantage point and then command directly from the battlefield instead of from the typical RTS top down view. The game starts off with a few tutorial missions to introduce you to the movement mechanics and then the commanding mechanics. There is also a little bit of platforming as well as some absolutely terribly designed 'find this thing' missions which really suck. They are poorly designed and ultimately dull to play through. I'd love to have seen the devs take more advantage of the gorgeous world they crafted and give us way more interesting exploration missions. It plays like a fairly chill game to play if you love ants. You get to look at some beautiful visuals. The music is peaceful and relaxing. The game doesn't feel overly taxing yet provides a decent enough challenge and generally feels satisfying once you complete a mission. Some later strategy missions take a few attempts to get right. Mostly because of timers. I never found them frustrating though. I always wanted to figure out what i needed to do differently to be more efficient.Outside of the strategy mechanics everything else feels like a massive missed opportunity. Unreal Engine 5 does all the heavy lifting for the visuals combined with some top notch environment and creature work but you can't play this and not wonder how much better this wold have been with some more development time into the adventure game outside of the RTS missions. I really thought that there would be far more to the hub areas and that you could build up your own nest / base and do some fun exploration. The game tells you about various creatures like spiders being dangerous, yet when you encounter them in exploration they look incredible but do nothing.Still recommending because if you are looking at the game then you almost certainly love the visuals and think that ants are just awesome but be aware that outside of the fun RTS / Strategy modes the game does feel a bit flat in places and the adventure / exploration missions are ridiculously half baked.10/10 for art direction / graphics 7/10 for gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: This game is innovative and interesting. I am excited to watch it develop and expand.For potential buyers:PROS1. Creative and unique campaign experience includes RTS battles, platforming missions, and some interesting cat and mouse style missions. Overall the variety is good and pacing keeps you hooked2. Soundtrack and visual style is top tier. The music is whimsical and sets the tone very well for the game. This pairs incredibly well with the scale of the environment and throughout each mission I felt a sense of child-like excitement for what comes next. This is especially true with the scouting missions.3. RTS skirmish modes are fleshed out with 10+ maps and allows AI to be tuned for how you like to play. Skirmish play has been incredibly fun for learning how to play and experiencing all that the game has to offer for PVP.CONS1. Unit variety is inherently low. The main units function similar to rock/paper/scissors where one type has advantage over another. This makes optimizing combat very easy, as you can quickly identify what types enemies have and send the counter unit in that direction. However, this quickly makes stalemate after stalemate in longer matches. Once fully upgraded all the unit types have a ton of health, and will often take 30+ seconds to resolve combat in a one on one battle. When both players are maxed out and have the same unit composition the game will soft lock as both players cannot make any advantage over the other. [Yes, there are special units and commander abilities, but these do not turn the tide of battle when the other player has them too]2. Pacing is very inconsistent. The ant you control has a super fast sprint [that can be upgraded pretty early] which makes scouting the map quick and pretty easy. The units that you control don't sprint, and have a base movement speed slower than the player walk speed. This is very likely balanced by the developers to prevent the game from going too fast, but in late game the unit speed is painfully slow. There are special units that help with this [rhino beetles act like unit carriers] but you can only have one special unit in your roster at a time.3. Difficulty scaling [This plays into the pacing issues above] is all over the place. There are several units in this game that are mechanically superior to a fault. If you chose the snail as your special unit, you are in for a slow tank to creep from base to base. If you select the hornets, you have access to the only flying offensive unit that can only be attacked by one unit type. Select the rhino beetle and its like you're playing an entirely different game. In late game the most difficult part of combat is replacing your armies as they are defeated. You have to keep units constantly in battle to hold the line and hold your opponents back. The rhino beetles can carry two armies of any type and can move near 5x faster than any ground unit [and can only be attacked by the one ranged unit type when in flight]. There is a distinct advantage to having flying units, as the only way to really counter them is with the one ranged unit type. Once your opponent builds those to counter your flying units, you build soldiers [that have a huge advantage over the ranged ones] and smash your opponent as they helplessly try to rebuild. Overall: This is an incredible game that is worth trying out. I see this game developing into a really unique RTS that will stand out in the genre. I have concerns with the balancing, but that will be polished as the developers recieve feedback. If you like platforming adventure games and don't have any experience with RTS games, this might be a good one to try. The combat mechanics are very simple to understand and quick to master.RTS 6/10PLATFORMER 8/10OVERALL 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: For this review I will be looking at the game from a mechanical perspective, not a story perspective, because when it comes to online games for me, I prefer game-play over story because in an online game, you're never playing it for the single player campaign unless you're new and need to familiarize yourself with the game. I'll be going through each unit type, and then onto the powers, giving my opinion on each one.Starting Troops - LegionsThe starting troops, consisting of Gunners, Warriors, and Worker Ants. These three are counter each other like Rock, Paper, Scissors, and they get their job done. They have three tiers, however, the perks unlock at Tier 3, and you'll most likely be at Tier 2 for majority of a multiplayer match unless it's really drawn out. So some perks for Tier 2 would be nice considering you'll likely be in Tier 2 for majority of an online match.Support Troops - LegionsSupport Troops, in my personal opinion, the worse unit in the game. I played 5-10 multiplayer online matches and I have only seen 1 person use them minus me, and I immediately ditched it after realizing how garbage they are. I don't mind that they take increased damage from all units, I don't mind that you can only have one support battalion, I don't even care that they're only tier 1. But what I do mind is how weak they are, You are going to have a much better time investing in a Starting Troop or a Super Predator. Just do anything to make them more viable, because as it, you can remove them from the game and I guarantee nobody would notice or care.Super Predators - LegionsSuper Predators, the complete opposite of Support Troops, they are crazy stupid. Being the Tier 2 unlockable units, they are like the Support Troops where you can only have one battalion. The only difference is that once you unlock them, you most certainly win the game unless your opponent has a Super Predator and vice verse. If I had to rank them, #3 would be Hornets, #2 would be Dor Beetles, and #1 would be Rose Chafers. Out of all Super Predators, Dor Beetles and Hornets are the most balanced in my personal opinion, with the Hornets being the weaker of the two. As for the Rose Chafers... You have any Gunners, you can't utilize them as Rose Chafers are IMMUNE to any acid attacks which include the Gunners. Super Predators as a whole are decently balanced, I would nerf the Rose Chafer so it can take damage from acid attacks and in turn, doesn't shut down Gunners. Not a huge nerf, maybe like a 70% resistance.Pheromones - PowersNow for the fun part of the game, Pheromones. In general, they're balanced and they serve their purpose. The only one I would buff are the Gnat Spies. For all of the powers, they have a use, some more than other, but especially with Gnat Spies, as soon as you get Tier 2 and 3 of Cartography, you have a deadweight power that's useless. At least the Burrows power can cut down on the travel time you'd have to make, even though it's smarter to just run and replace Burrows with an actual useful Pheromone. Out of the Powers in the game, the top 3 that I've seen and in my personal opinion is Shielding Spore, Raging Pheromone, and Reinforcement Call. Everything else is alright, and the two that really need the help are Burrows and Gnat Spies.For my final judgement, I would give it a 8/10. It's alright and has a good foundation if the devs want to continue to update and support it. And I want them too, it's a really cool concept which has massive potential and I really want to see this game do well. The pricing does drag it down a little bit, it should be at maximum a 25 dollar game so I would wait until it's on sale. I hope the devs will listen to the communities' feedback and take it to heart and improve this game because I don't want this game, with tons of potential, to rot away after a month.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly its a very fun game. It has a lot of repetition in it, however what RTS doesn't. I find the battles fun to watch from ants cutting one another to pieces, Beatles flinging one another across the map, and last but not least the Apache helicopters of the bug world wasps. The game play overall is interesting but as noted repetitive though I don't mind this at all as it still makes it fun. The game sprinkles in missions for you to carry out with your single ant to aid in that category however. The economy side of the game is simple and easy to learn, but can be challenging to manage. Having to decide what upgrades to go for and so forth gives it a challenge outside the battles. You are presented with strategic choices and have the ability to play like a turtle or an absolute blitz tactic. I find defensive strategies tend to be stronger and over time to win out if you can manage to survive blitzing players in pvp. The unit diversity is surprisingly good for an ant game, the ability to recruit other bugs really diversifies the overall tactics and strategies you can employ. I do find the overall unit count to be a bit low and would prefer slightly larger battles as the current size really limits overall tactical choices for no other reason than game mechanics. On the same note I do find the unit system a bit frustrating for pvp for the simple fact that it is hard to field the appropriate counters to your opponents units for only one reason and that is units are tied to territories. So in order to build a counter to say wasps are gunners you have to have a territory with no legion in it, however if you have no gunners built you have to destroy a legion building and replace it with a gunners legion and then wait around 4 to 6 minutes for the legion to be raised. This can result in you losing a pvp match from a single mistake in particular if your enemy fields wasps and you have no gunners you are certain to lose the game, especially if you have not had time to construct proper defenses for you nests yet. I don't find these to be inherently negative components of the game but rather periodically frustrating. I respect the design and can see what the devs envisioned however this tiny part of the game is slightly unappealing for the simple fact that single mechanic makes the game difficult to play flexibly. Other than that one aspect I find the game to be very fun, however if your looking for a successor to sim ant this isn't it, this is not a colony sim. In fact you have very small interactions with the colony, this is more focused on the struggles of an ant kingdom and your small part in it out in the world away from the colony. You are just the leader of a very small contingent in what seems to be a very large ant realm. I enjoy this aspect of the game and feel like it was a good choice for the overall design, as it fills a niche within the "ant world" game that I have not seen done before. If you are looking for a relaxed strategy game, with beautiful maps and environments, and with a decent story that diversifies the game play about ants this is for you. If you are looking for a hardcore colony simulator about building an ant colony from the ground up this is not that. I rate the game 8/10 and I believe the game delivers in every aspect it advertises and meets all my expectations in a nicely presented bug free game about bugs.

Take part in the exodus of a doomed and lost colony. Play as the Ant Savior, whose mission is to lead its "people" and rebuild a home, protect them, make them prosper and conquer new territories through different seasons.

Based on Bernard Werber's best-seller, Empire of the Ants will offer a strategic experience close to the iconic books series.

Experience immersive adventures and defend your lands through tactical and strategic battles in a microscopic world of epic proportions.

Exploration, strategy, combat skills, but most of all, the local wildlife alliance will be necessary in order to emerge victorious from the many challenges that await you.

name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors
detailed_description: A self-remaster of the 1994 spinoff to Taito's 1987 arcade classic, The NinjaWarriors, with The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors, Tengo Project have taken the original console beat 'em up and reimagined it, adding extra moves & combos, 2 new characters, 2 player co-op, fluid, even more hand animated pixel art and an amped up soundscape to boot! Select one of five android ninjas, each with their own unique ninjutsu techniques, and take the battle to Banglar's army alone, or with a ninja partner, as part of Mulk's revolutionary force! Maintaining the original's 16-bit style, Return of the Warriors expands its playfield from 4:3 to a wide 16:9, adding heavily redrawn backgrounds, even more fluidly animated characters and explosive pyrotechnics. The enhanced music comes courtesy of a new, arranged soundtrack, alongside unlockable soundtracks from the 16-bit console original, and arcade version, by Zuntata. Multiple difficulties provide challenge for even the most seasoned ninja, and Time Attack allows you to compete against on the leaderboards against the fastest masters of ninjutsu in the world! Features A 16-bit classic, reborn in full, 16:9 wide screen glory! Lovingly redrawn, pixel art graphics and smoother animation! 8 stages, 2 difficulties, 2 play modes and multiple unlockables! 5 ninjas with multiple techniques allow for 5 separate play styles! Punch, kick, slash, juggle, throw, crush and combo your foes! 2 player couch coop for ninja nunchaku action! Select from Arcade, Again or a new arranged soundtrack! About TENGO PROJECT NatsumeAtari's ultra-skilled game-smiths were responsible for bringing titles like Pocky & Rocky Reshrined , WILD GUNS Reloaded and more to consoles in the 90s and now they're back, better than ever, bringing Technostacy to modern gamers!

short_description: Alluring audio! Pixel art perfection! Beat-em up beauty! Discover how hard a 32,000kg ninja hits with The Ninja Saviours!

_childDocuments_.review: Tengo Project is one of the best developers out there right now, and in my opinion, The Ninja Saviors is their best game so far. It's also one of the best beat 'em ups ever made. I'd highly recommend it to any fan of the genre, or anyone looking to get into it because although it's unorthodox, it's pretty easy to pick up. The trailer does a good job of showing you what you'll get, but you'll find five totally unique characters to choose from (including a giant mecha), eight stages that are just the right length (it's not too long like some other modern beat 'em ups), two good soundtracks, and some of the best pixel art in the business today. What else could you need?The one knock against this game (and Tengo's other releases) is its lack of online play. As far as I know, you can get around this by using Parsec, but I've never tried that myself. Personally I don't care, but I know this can be a big negative to a lot of people.I played this when it originally came out on the PS4 and bought it again just to have on my PC & Steam Deck. So my play time is low right now, but I know the game fairly well. I just ran through it once and the PC version seems perfectly fine to me, for what it's worth. You can check out full clears with every character on my YouTube channel if you're interested in seeing more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, one of the best 2D action games of all time comes to Steam.Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors a.k.a. Ninja Warriors Once Again is a remake of a SNES game, with remade art assets, extra characters, new moves, arranged OST and improved combat mechanics. It is a 2D beat'em up that plays in a single, linear plane unlike games like Final Fight that let you move up and down the screen. This, among other things, allows the game to focus a bit more on projectile dodging and evading attacks via crouching and jumping in a more natural way than a traditional beat'em up.Another difference with the usual games in the genre is that, while there are enemies with high endurance that can take multiple hits (against which you can make use of the newly introduced juggle combo system), there's also a constant stream of simple mob enemies that are constantly harassing you, but go down in a single hit, which makes the game feel more intense and fast paced than everyone being able to take multiple hits.There's three default characters, all with their strengths and weaknesses, with the balanced Kunoichi, the fast Kamaitachi and the heavy hitting grappler Ninja, and once you beat the game on Normal and Hard difficulties you can unlock Yaksha, a ninja girl with stretchy arms, and Raiden, a massive, towering mech who is extremely slow but hits like a nuclear weapon. Every character is their own world, with their own mobility, special attacks, grabs and such, which greatly enhances replayability since every one of them is such a different experience.Besides these characters, you can also unlock a hard mode and the classic arcade Ninja Warriors' OST, which includes fan favorite theme Daddy Mulk.  All in all, this is a great choice for anyone interested in classic, arcade-style 2D action, with unmatched pixel art visuals, excellent OST and deceptively simple gameplay that lends to skillful play once you master it. The game requires some effort to beat, but there's infinite continues, which makes it approachable for everyone. Don't hesitate to buy it if you are even remotely interested in the genre, and want to support these high-effort, gorgeous pixel art games from developer Tengo Project.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Game kicks ass. Natsume is on fire with these remasters!Ive never played a bmup with such emphasis on crowd-control and it's awesome. Movement and combos are very slick and precise. My only complaint is the hitbox on the final boss which can feel like a total crapshoot. Also no way Yaksha only weighs 50kg walking around with that bakery.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a beat-em-up where you control a forklift. It controls different than anything else you have handled, and to do simple things is much more difficult... but the immense power, precision, and technical variety you have at your fingertips once you understand this is a forklift and not a sports car is unmatched. It takes a LOT of getting used to and nothing else plays like it as everyone else wants to be a sports car and not a forklift, but there's a very good reason why there's a forklift in every single factory and an equally good reason why this game has stuck around for so long.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the everloving $%^* out of this game way back on the SNES, and to have it pop up on steam with updated everything, it's definitely hit the nostalgia button hard. The controls are butter smooth, the new attacks are a nice addition, and taking advantage of the iframes in attacks is still a go to way to get through crowded areas. Already on the 5th stage and the only, literal only complaint I have is that Ninja can't grapple the first boss and any time that dude shows up later. In the original, you could grapple stun that dude for a quick kill so kinda sad that will affect any speedruns of this, but that aside, the updated graphics, music, and controls are fantastic. Pick this up if you like side scrolling beat-em-ups!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Tengo Project is really keeping the "old school" flame alive!The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors is yet another revival done right. It takes the already awesome SNES title, and improves things on every level.The combat is fast and fluid, the pixel art graphics are improved (and in widescreen) and look lovely, and the arranged soundtrack sounds great.The cast of 5 characters (2 of them brand new, and unlockable) all play differently enough to make each playthrough a different experience, and you will need to adapt your strategies depending on the character used.To top things off, there's 2 awesome alternative soundtracks to unlock (the one from Zuntata for the original Arcade game, and the soundtrack from the SNES version), which adds further variety of options for replaying the game.Personally, I had a blast replaying the game with the new characters, while listening to the 1987 arcade game soundtrack by Zuntata. It doesn't get much better than this!All in all, this is a must for fans of the genre, and a loving revival of this classic franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: As there is no way to play the original Ninja Warriors TAITO arcade on Steam/Steamdeck (only way these days is emulation or Arcade Archives on consoles), i finally pulled the trigger on this one.While i'm a massive fan of these guys' work on Pocky and Rocky (kikikaikai) and Shadow of the Ninja Reborn, this one feels (like the SNES version honestly) somehow a downgrade in terms of atmosphere from the original arcade.Mind you this game is still a a very fun game: much more mechanics and diversity than the original, hence reccommending it, but not necessarily an alternative to the arcade.Still masterfully executed work and beautiful pixel art, but the game itself being some sort of spinoff / home market adaptation,  doesn't convey the spirit of the original, at all.The difference in gameplay between the 2 in that this new version plays more like a(vastly improved) 2d restricted Final Fight Beat 'em' up 90's style, while the original arcade feels more like a  melee run and gun 80's style , still pretty unique though.From the music to the simpler and faster gameplay, every action and hit was deliberate, impactful; much less enemies on screen than this one and no massive murder moves: you really felt in control of unstoppable, precise, emotionless ninja terminators loosing skin parts when hit with firearms and moving like creepy robots.The arcade has a somewhat dramatic tone, feels darker and in general has a completely different vibe than this one.Playing it for the first time in the arcades at the time, with the 3 massive CRT screens setup was absolutely mind blowing.The soundtrack was full-on cybernetic vibes: beautiful compositions ... the tracks in this one , in comparison, feel a bit generic and uninspired.Fortunately you can still unlock the original Arcade soundtrack composed by Zuntata beating the game on normal and enable it in the options.Get Saviours for sure, it's a beautiful game, but please play the 1987's TAITO arcade if you want to experience what the real Ninja Warrios was all about.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best 2D beat 'em up games is finally on Steam.Great playable characters variety, each with their own unique gameplay and moveset. Combat feels godlike due to the perfect mix between the options avaiable to your character, enemy variety and frame data balancing each action with the right amount of power, risk and reward.There are unlockable characters, soundtracks, hard mode and time attack to add replay value, but the super polished and fun gameplay does the heavy lifting here.Presentation is also amazing with top tier 2D pixel art and a kickass soundtrack.Tengo Project means quality, if you're into beat 'em ups, this one is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you are into beat em ups. Not too long but pretty challenging. 5 characters, 3 to start, and 2 are unlockable. They all have their own playstyles and quirks. For example the scythe ninja has a very fast crouch-walk, whereas the heavy grappler Haggar-esque archetype has rocket shoes he can use to boost back and forth. Each character has a bunch of special moves, and in a rare display of big-brain in this genre, they can all block by holding the attack button. Took me about two hours to beat the game on normal. I can definitely see myself going back to beat the game on hard after I unlock the next character. Your first playthrough on normal unlocks hard, a new character, AND new music. The music is great, the SFX are great, and the attacks all feel good. This game would have been totally at home in arcades around 1992-1993. If you like beat em ups and enjoyed other recent genre greats like Fight N' Rage, Shredder's Revenge, or Streets of Rage 4, give this one a go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the greatest beat em ups of all time (if not THE greatest) back on the SNES, and this remake expands it to be even more of a masterpiece then it already was.The presence of blocking, grappling, and incredibly well designed movesets on each character not only makes the game play more like a thoughtful fighting game than most traditional beat-em-ups, but gives you so many incredibly cool options for every situation that you can almost play it like a SSStylish proto dmc character action game. Combine that with tricky enemy AI and some amazing boss fights, and you have a real desert island masterpiece of 2d close combat action gaming that never gets old.I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: I just found out this game came on steam from a YT video. The joy on my face just can't be explained. I played this game on SNES when i was 6-7 years old and it was AMAZING! I just finished playing it and to my surprise they added things that the original did not have which im grateful for because it adds that extra awesome to an already great classic beat em up game. The added improvements in this remaster is so nice. My only gripe is that its over too quick :( Here's hoping they do a sequel! This is one of my favorite games of all time. I have so many awesome memories playing the original on normal mode, hard mode & making up my own BS story as a kid lol. Ninja Saviors / Ninja Warriors will forever have a special place in my heart. P.S: Plays well on steam deck =)

_childDocuments_.review: Only one of the greatest SNES beat 'em up games ever created. If you know, then you know. ;)This is essentially a remastered / remade version of the SNES cartridge. It falls in the same camp as the Wild Guns remaster where the developers improved game play and added in new characters.New Stuff:It has deep and fun game play mechanics, they seem complicated at first but they're actually very simple, it's just a matter of you knowing what to do in certain situations and having good reflexes.The game has an amazing soundtrack! One of the best for that era. It's just a fun game all around and it can be considered casual or hardcore depending on how you play it. If you're going for a no death run, this game is torture. If you're looking to just finish it alone or with a friend, you have infinite attempts at it so just have fun and get practicing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: A reimagining of a classic from the SNES era. Keeps what made the classic great, while adding two new characters, and mechanics. Not that the story was a big draw, but it would have been nice if they added a couple of cutscenes.  The deal breaker for me which turned it from recommend is the fact that in order to beat the game and unlock the new characters you have to beat it all in one sitting. There is no way to save your run and come back to it latter.
