_childDocuments_.review: Having invested a lot of time in this game, if you see this on sale for about 5 dollars, I could recommend getting it.This game is primarily designed around speed running.  The fatal flaw of all of the Tengo Project games is that I think they never quite live up to their potential save for the fidelity upgrade.  In terms of gameplay loop, this game focuses on timing the player.  So, speed running/Time Attack.The problem with this is that the enemy behaviors and combat are both an upgrade, while simultaneously a massive DOWNGRADE from the SNES original, which is baffling.  Specifically, enemies can just stall out with zero manipulations or methods to create consistency.  As with most Tengo Project games, sans Pocky and Rocky, there's just a baffling amount of RNG that was inserted into the game.I have multiple top times in this game's stage time attack, but doing a whole run is just hilariously awful because there's just so many questionable decisions.  If a boss blocks?  Your run is over.  If an enemy chooses to go airborne when you approach them on wake up?  Your run is over.  If the enemy stalls, back pedals and hangs off screen?  Your run is over.Enemies are allowed to be degenerate in this aspect.  They will react perfectly to the player, but the player has no real way with most characters, save probably NINJA, to counteract this awful type of design.  You reset over and over, but for ANYTHING.  Enemies just do not cooperate and I don't think the designers understand, let alone thought about "What are you testing the player for?"In the Super Nintendo game that Ninja Saviors functions as a remake for, enemy attacks had distinct high and low properties, same with the player.  The player now has no such recourse, if enemies block then they block perfectly, most enemy attacks will hit the player whether they are crouching or standing.  Because Ninja Saviors' foundational design is based on being a purely 2D scrolling beat em up, with no Z-Axis, this is very baffling.  Enemies ABSOLUTELY have high and low attacks, however.  They can strike at your legs and hit you with "lows" like sweeps or standing low slashes to your legs. Hence, why I say "questionable" or baffling.  Why isn't the player allowed to do this?  Why does the player have no way to utilize this style of combat on enemies, while enemies are allowed to attack the player, wake up with complete invincibility and go airborne.  This affects concepts like grouping, okizeme or attack enemies while they rise.  Computer opponents have MASSIVE considerations and favorable properties that will drain huge swaths of time as the player is forced to watch them escape and otherwise sit off screen or stall.Stalling.  In a time attack/speed running game, is a show of incompetence.  There's no real way to put it otherwise, the enemy behavior in this game is sub-standard.  Another aspect that multiplies this flaw is that enemies are also allowed to sit on the borders of the screen constantly out of range of the player.  This just serves to punish the player for things that make zero sense.  That they might, oh no, strategically group enemies or utilize the play space to go faster is instead coded or designed as if that's a terrible thing.  Why put a timer on the screen and time the player if ultimately the designers made decisions that show that the game isn't actually willing to make this sporting?  Whether you're playing casually or for the speed running aspect, this just makes it so engaging with enemies lacks a feeling of fun because the play this creates just utterly non-interactive.  You have to hope the game cooperates and just keep resetting/retrying for swaths of arbitrary reasons.  As a licensed property, I would actually say the original Ninja Warriors succeeds at being a well themed title, where you're a literal Ninja Terminator that unceremoniously slits the final boss' throat.  This is the other direction that Ninja Saviors/Ninja Warriors Once Again just cannot live up to.  This game trades in that type of theme and flavor for a game that emphasizes dynamic combat... but because enemies behave so degenerately, the player ultimately has to ask themselves if playing through a game that doesn't nearly match the narrative of the game it is following in the foot steps of is worth it.There are no multiple endings, the final boss is a completely underwhelming, arbitrary fight.  The game is really faithful to being a higher spec 16-bit game, but its ultimate flaw is that it just does not justify its design decisions in any direction, be it scenario or just being about speed running.  Speed runs are contingent on consistency, and I would still say that an enjoyable action game should not leave the player feeling helpless/infuriated when everything comes down to something the player just has no direct control over.  Do not get this game unless it's on a major discount if you're the type of person who loves consumer protection.  If you're not afraid of playing an unfortunately mediocre game that is held back by one glaring flaw (enemy behavior, which ultimately affects anything you do) this isn't necessarily the worst game out there, but it absolutely has a fatal flaw that unravels what it has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the original, but I've loved pretty much all of Tengo Project's other remasters.As always, great music and amazing pixel artEnough difficulty without feeling to crushing, but it definitely took me a bit of experimenting to get used to the moves your character can do.A bit of a twist to the normal beat 'em up formula that made it a joy to play though. _childDocuments_.review: Utterly perfect and what all remasters should strive to be likecoming from someone who played the hell out of the original snes game not only does it have ways to expand combos, you can even burn meter to do special moves besides just the full screen bombthe extra aspect ratio really ups the challenge because enemies are further away you really need to utilize blocking and avoiding certain attacks. The small claw guys will hit you if you don't avoid their forward dash and enemies with guns need to be ducked or blocked until you reach themit's just so well put together.

_childDocuments_.review: Ninja Warriors was originally released 30 years for the now legendary Super Nintendo videogame console. Ninja Saviors pays homage to the above mentioned, including the original soundtrack (finish the game to unlock "Arcade" soundtrack) and the three main characters, plus a couple of powerful new additions that unlock each time you finish the game. Sadly, there is no other way of unlocking them, so at least you will have to play the whole game twice. Character moves have been upgraded, with special jump attacks, and finishing moves (not like in Mortal Kombat) Bosses have also been updated, but if you were playing the original so long ago, you won't have any problems playing this Sequel-ish. However, the game is too short. 7 stages, plus one final Boss stage, and that's it. True to what most Beat 'em ups were all about, you just try to get to the end of the stage by beating as many enemies as you can, which may have been nice back then, but now it feels a bit boresome once you're on stage 3 or 4. I'm not sure this game has a meaningful replay value. Once you unlock the 2 new characters there's isn't anything interesting left to do. There are no secret stages, no character upgrades, and the multiplayer option is just to play local with friends. Although there is a Time Rush mode that activates when you finish the game the first time, it still is a local game option, not online. For being an upgrade, it feels lacking in that department. Old farts like me, will probably play it twice to get the hidden characters and then forget about it. A DLC, or an update with more playable stuff, would expand the life of the game.Overall, a good game, but one you won't play long.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: a game so good I bought it twice, steam and switch. one of my favorite beat em ups, what a wonderful retouching of a great game. the music is absolutely fantastic, the animations are the work of a team that has been doing this for 30 years and been together the entire time and it shows. the characters are all unique and fun to clear the game with, and the new unlockable characters even more so with the screen filling Raiden that needs his own command to turn around. I still come back to it to try to beat my times and enjoy the story (its really simple but hey I like it)
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: I love this dev (Natsume), but this game is...Graphics are really good, the music does it's job.There's some problems with the control of the character. You would expect that a game that focuses on speedrunning would have dynamic characters, but in this game you can't run at all. Some characters have throws or attacks that make them move foward faster, but that's not something that should take the place of simple running imo.There's way too much RNG. Bosses can simply decide to defend half of your hits or take everything. Enemies can stand outside of the screen for what feels like an eternity and will only return if you step back a little and let them slowly walk back to the screen, which is a overall major time wasting thing. So much of that is outside of the player's control, but all of that ruins any speedrun by pure chance and that's unacceptable for a game where the focus is speedrunning lmao.Because the speedrun aspect is lost, the game is dead after you do a 1CC as there's no reason to speedrun this game.The final boss in this game is probably the most annoying final boss in a game I've seen in a LONG while. Nothing about it is interesting. It's just a spam of stage enemies and you having to throw these stage enemies at the glass while some lasers pop around.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: I've prayed before that this remake would make it to steam and I am so happy it did. As a fan of the Super Nintendo game, I can say this is the near definitive way to play the game. It looks beautiful, you can have both the new and original OST, and it plays damn well. One of my favourite beat em ups easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Normal skill is a bit harder than the SNES version, especially the giant boss of act 1, and the final boss of the game.  I did a normal playthrough swapping between Ninja and Kunoichi, Ninja is a powerhouse and Kunoichi imo has the easiest way to defeat the final boss... at least in the SNES version.  Great game for fans of cyborg ninjas though and a nicely updated classic, hoping to try out multiplayer sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Games wicked solid. Never played the SNES version? No problem, I hadn't either. A beat em up on a straight horizontal plane, no eight directional movement. Think of a platformer with beat em up combat (games got zero platforming though). Got your default combo, a grab, your jump and specials. 3 button control scheme, combats easy to grasp but hard to master. Moves are based on the direction you're holding and given you're on a single plane you have to have the right strats down to deal with a heavy group. Graphics are amazing, some of the best pixel art I've seen. Musics awesome, and upon completing the game you unlock the arcade and SNES renditions to play in-game. Also two unlockable characters, and each character plays extremely differently. Not much to do after a playthrough admittedly- can replay as the other characters, do hard mode or load up co-op. I'd like to try co-op but my friends choose to play ♥♥♥♥ instead of having a good time. Don't take from their example, get this game and have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Ninja Saviors is fun remake of Natsumi's classic side-scrolling Beat 'em up. The pixel art has been redrawn and reanimated at high fidelity for a very appealing presentation. Each of the five Ninjas has their very own unique play style and combos which really makes it feel like you're playing a whole new game each time. All the moves are listed in the options and are easy to do with no complex fighting game inputs. Some of these moves capitalize on chaos, such as a multi hit combo that hits enemies behind you, turning being sandwiched into something positive. Personally I would start with Ninja (the big guy) as I felt he was very fitting for people learning the ropes.The game unlocks a hard mode when you beat the final stage and you get a time attack option for each stage you clear. Each boss has badass design with unique patterns and playstyles, many of which give off 80's yakuza or martial arts film vibes.If you like Beat 'em ups, fast paced moment-to-moment gameplay and replayability, I recommend Ninja Saviors as well as Natsumi's other titles on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you,Natsume! For bring this over on steam. I waited since it's 2019 release for this to be brought over to Steam. The ninja saviors : return of the warriors is a remaster of the Super NES title "The Ninja Warriors" (Ninja Warriors Again in Japan) which itself is the sequel to the 1987 arcade title also called "The Ninja Warriors". This is a side scrolling beat em up which adds quite a few things from the Super NES original. Wide screen BloodMultiplayer Extra characters, moves and animations Play the original first then come back to this and you'll see what they added here was all for the better. The Super NES version of this game is great. Just lacked multiplayer, it's here and the music has been reworked and I like it more than the original super NES score, but that score was also good.  To make a long review short. If you enjoyed the Super NES release or like beat 'em ups then buy this game. you'll regret not doing so!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna recommend, but just barely. Like an actual 5.5/10 sort of situation.I was a huge fan of the arcade original with the slick designs, animation, and that slamming soundtrack. I never had the chance to try this sequel on the SNES, but I was pretty hyped to see it here with extra characters.So, what you get is fairly straight forward. A minimal nihilistic storyline, some bad ass ninja androids kicking the crap out of an entire army and some creative design decisions that make all of them play a bit differently. No real bells or whistles beyond unlocking the original soundtrack after a playthrough and the new characters Yaksha and Raiden.This isn't a long game, but the stages can feel dragged out and monotonous, don't expect too much variation or surprises. Your general gameplay goal is crowd controlling swarms of enemies through stages with your slow-as-hell ninja. They have some slight maneuvarability in their skill sets, but most of them are annoyingly sluggish. Enemies range from one hit wimps to being pain sponges, but this also depends somewhat on which ninja you play as. Bosses are pretty challenging, but sometimes it feels like it's for all the wrong reasons.Which brings me to my rating. Hit detection is pretty jank both for and against. There just doesn't seem to be much rhyme or reason half the time with how and when strikes connect. There are moves that have invincibility frames but others are more questionably. You'll eat hits that don't really make sense, like getting knocked out of the air by an enemy's crouching attack. You can block, but it's clumsily implemented as 'hold attack after attacking' and slows you even further. Really, offense is the best and often only defense here.Bosses are particularly weird with their hit boxes, making some fights more challenging than they should be, but again, this also depends on what ninja you're using... some just aren't suited to fighting certain bosses.The difficulty is on the high side, in my opinion. You can get better at this with practice, certainly. But there's going to be that inconsistency factor over your play throughs creeping in. There's also a strange design choice of being forced to replay through a hall of enemies before retrying certain bosses, but not others. This gets irritating and more than a little boring when you're stuck on a boss fight and need to practice it further. The final boss just... sucks. It's a tight room with auto lasers going off, unending swarms, and your only way to win is to throw enemies past the glass where the boss is hiding, despite that you can visibly reach him. So, it's the Def Jam Vendetta final boss all over again for those who know. It's doable, but very tedious and aggravating since you have a slow ninja and roughly only one, maybe two of your throwing attacks will have any chance to work. And of course, a hallway of enemies awaits you if you want to rechallenge. Bleh. I know it's supposed to be a final boss challenge, but it's not much fun to keep doing when half the character roster can't throw enemies effectively.But hey, I'm expecting too much here. This is a very old fashioned style SNES era title and the dry challenge shows under what is otherwise a very cool aesthetic of android ninjas. It's a remaster with some modestly nice additions and I'll admit I wish there was more meat on the bone, because I do like it. Gameplay issues and erratic hit boxes, however, prevent me from loving this old school game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Great beat 'em up it's a shame you have to complete the game to unlock Yaksha the animation of her breast in the trailer is amazing. I think the game is too expensive and too difficult. The throw in the last mission does not work on purpose so that you cannot complete it in less than 2 hours and get your money back.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent beat em up, I really love the chunky sprites of the huge enemies, everything is so detailed and well animated in this beautiful pixel art, really wish there was more games with this level of quality. Not only that, the soundtrack is pretty good too. The controls are a bit awkward at firsts, but it becomes a pretty addicting game of trying to survive through waves of enemies and beat everything as fasts as possible. The length of one play-through is around 1 hour, so it's a bit long for an arcade game, but it is still a pretty enjoyable game to do in one sitting and try to do better scores, specially when there is 5 characters to choose from, each one with pretty unique play styles.I'm not an expert on beat em ups, but this one sure a really good one, visually amazing and addicting gameplay that makes you want to improve to get better times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: The 2 player co-op and 2 new characters are appreciated but I was hoping this would have various gameplay improvements. It has almost every flaw the Super Famicom game had. The visuals and audio are obviously improved but it's still a flawed beat-em-up that takes under an hour to beat with very little additional content and very few improvements. It's a shame as there's lots of obvious changes that could've made it so much better. The Super Famicom game had lots potential to improve upon.Misc:-The time trials feel pointless in a game where there's a massive amount of randomness.-They unfortunately made it so you can't grab the big masculine robot enemies anymore which makes them less fun to fight.-There's some strange sexualization in this remake with Kunoichi having larger bouncier breasts, the female swordstress enemies' breasts swinging from side to side in a really awkward way, and the new character Yaksha being a 5'1'' character with ridiculously large breasts. That stuff just feels out of place when the original wasn't like that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors has gorgeous pixel work.  I like how each playable character feels pretty different, and I like the sound design.But man, do I hate Ninja Saviors.  I don't understand what the developer was trying to accomplish with this game, and frankly, I can't find the fun at all.  The game play is on a completely flat 2D plane.  You cannot move in and out of the environment, nor are there any upper or lower levels to jump to/from.  There isn't even any variation, like slopes, or things you have to jump over or anything at all.  You cannot dash (one character sort of can but its awkward), you just slowly walk right through every level.  Fodder enemies come at you from both sides as you move through the level.  Due to the lack of any sort of terrain variation or 3D movement, there is very little difference in each enemy and how they attack.  Sure, they may look different, or have a different weapon, but their options, like mine, are extremely limited.  Yes, even though they took care to outfit each character with a wide variety of different and unique moves, they all seem pointless.  I don't seem to need to use any of them to plow through the level, though they do at least make things a little less monotonous.  But this is what I mean about not being able to figure out what the devs were trying to do.  Why would you give me all these moves, almost like its a fighting game, yet the movement and especially the blocking options make it impossible for me to play like a fighting game.  I am flabbergasted by the blocking especially.  To block, you need to hold down the main attack button.  This is insane.  Lets say I am fighting the level one boss (again, stunning pixel work).  He is a rather large man that throws these huge uppercuts at you.  If I see one coming, I can't move back out of the way it time, you don't move fast enough.  If I try and block, I throw out an attack first, and get hit!?!?  It's just not fun.   I played the first four levels, and more recently booted it up and tried all three characters, in case one of them clicked better for me.  They didn't.  I don't like playing this game and I don't think I am going to again.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: If you remember the mid-1980s classic "The Ninja Warriors" from arcades, this is a sequel of sorts. It's a good game with extra variety in gampelay and additional characters, but there is only one reason why I give it thumbs down, but it's a very big one-the game is way too difficult. If you like being potentially frustrated to no end by boss battles, get it. If not, you probably want to stay away. Find the original console game if you can and play that first before going for this one, especially if you're playing alone (it's prob easier with local co-op).
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous game with some balance issues. Its fine most of the time, but some of the bosses are just infuriating. Specifically Jubei (zips around the arena with lightning speed doing random things) and Banglar (you have to throw enemies from very specific spots to hit his pod while dodging a barrage of environmental hazards).Its a fun experience with tons of replayability, but these two bosses almost ruin it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: The Ninja Saviors Return of the Warriors is one of my favorite beatem ups and I am a huge fan of the beatem genre.This is a 2D plane scroller (not a belt scroller). There are 5 playable characters. Most beatem ups are really fast paced, but while I wouldn't call The Ninja Saviors "slow" it is slower than your average beatem up; you need to be a little more careful and intentional rather than being super fast.For newbies, you might want to know that there are a lot of moves where you have to do compound inputs to do. For example, in midair as Kunoichi if you hold down and press attack she will do a double jump sword slash attack; also if you are crouched and you press jump she will do a thrusting attack rather than jumping; so if you are struggling then you might be making the game harder than it need be by not using your full move set.I love the graphics and sound effects of this game. I just find it really satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time when I was a boy playing in the arcades, I first played the 1988original arcade game "The Ninja Warriors". and there were 2 playable ninjas; the pinkKunoichi like in this game, and the Ninja in the classic was a male version of the pink one,but in blue & minus the long ponytail. the arcade was long, hard & brutal...I only got as faras level 2. But then when I got "The Ninja Warriors: Again" on the ZSnes emulator, it waswhole new experience, but the story, plot, main enemy & objective were still the same: assassinate Banglar.but the SNES version had 3 characters this time: the Kunoichi, a cyborg ninja in blue with nunchucks& a bladed, skeleton ninja called Kamaitachi. TBH, that game was way better in terms of gameplay, music,enemies, bosses & the playable characters themselves.But now, this version of the SNES classic just makes playing all over again all the more worth it,especially with 2 new playable characters; a towering behemoth called Raiden, and a cute shortstackninja girl with extendable arms called Yaksha. plus this remastered version of the SNES classic has 3 typesof the game's BGM: Remastered, OG Arcade & OG SNES. also, 2 difficulty modes...and each have time attackmodes whenever you complete each level.So, if you're after something refreshing but also nostalgic this summer, get this game.I strongly recommend buying it if you're a fan of this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: I wish more games from the SNES era got this treatment!This is Ninja Warriors in all its glory, and so much care went into improving it it's insane. The already excellent controls are somehow more responsive and more slick, with some new special moves!The graphics are amazing. The sprite animations are smoother, and scenary and landscape are now much bigger and more detailed.This is excellent, that's how you remaster a classic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Old school pick up and play but with some decent strategy to the characters. Tough at first but doesn't take too long to get the hang of things. I don't like how in two-player mode the life bar is shared, makes it tough to play with the kids, but it's better than having no two player mode at all.Great graphics, good sound, tight controls. Recommended for single player old school brawler fans, especially those that like the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Beautiful design. Characters are interesting and cool looking. Fast action and fun to play. Old school retro feel is super fun and you can even give it a CRT effect.Cons: Crashes a lot. And not just the game, it crashes the whole PC. Bad character balancing where two characters cant even jump so you cant avoid ground bombs, and one cant even grab which is a huge mechanic in the game. In fact, if you just keep grabbing the game is Super Easy mode. The giants are annoying to fight, but that's just personal preference.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: The Ninja Warriors was my favorite beat'em up when I was a kid. I remember I used to rent it from the local video-games store (the guy wouldn't sell it, since it was more profitable to milk every penny from game thirsty boys like me) and it was painful to arrive to late at the store on a Friday and  see it in the hands of another kid.Now I can play it again with a nice new design, very beautiful colors and awesome new features: the original characters have new moves, you can play each stage in time mode and there are two new characters - one of them feels like you are controling a boss instead of a normal player character.The game runs smoothly, great music and it's as much fun as playing it from an SNES. I woul only suggest the developer s to implement a score system or a game mode devoted for scoring - I know the game itself is based on the time you take to finish it, but a scoring system would be great to have as well.Freaking nice game, worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: instantly fun, it's pick up and play, it supports fightsticks, and uses accurate button prompts to the controller of your choice (presumable, I haven't tried using a switch controller because I'm not that much of a masochist.) it's a good port of an already great game, and my only complaint is that it's developed by Natsume Atari, who are kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but this? surprisingly good.

_childDocuments_.review: The Ninja Warriors was one of the best beat em ups on the SNES and this remake makes it ones of the best I've played.An excellent side scrolling beat em up with good art, mechanics, animations and a well made remake that adds a lot to the game. The remake includes different music options to use, a larger playing field with updated backgrounds, two new characters for a total of five, new moves for each character, uses both the Kunoichi and Monkey enemies that were in different region versions of the original game, and adds a two player mode. Each of the five characters plays in a very unique way with very different focuses to their playstyle and how they move, with one of the new characters being the largest character I've seen available in a beat em up that can transform between two different modes and who is so large that they use a button combination just to turn around. One of the few beat em ups to both include an option to block and being even rarer among games by having it be both useful and responsive and holding block allows you to still move around and gives access to quick dodges that can avoid or block attacks and put you behind or closer to enemies. A fairly rapidly recharging battery meter allows you to perform a screen wide damaging bomb attack to deplete the full charge or to use a portion of it for a special move unique to each character either done from a stance or by altering the final blow of a combo, taking a harder hit that knocks you down will drain your battery back to nothing giving even more incentive to block and dodge.There is both a normal and hard mode with the hard mode changing up enemy numbers and variety and the game unlimited continues that start you at a stage checkpoint with the option to change character. Three problems I had come form of there being no ability to save or continue from where you left off so you need to finish in one sitting or keep the game left on (though beaten stages can be replayed by themselves and it is not a long game so this isn't too much of an issue), there is no ability to rebind block to a button instead of holding attack which I've always found an awkward way to block (though this might be the only game I've played to use that method while still being responsive), and enemies love moving off screen and just staying there frequently backing away to leave the screen or trying to attack while out of sight.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! The characters all play really differently, the enemy design is interesting, "normal" mode was a bit of a challenge at first but I'm getting better at it as I play. Uncomplicated -- if you like ninjas and robots (and you wanna play as a robot ninja) to do some morally uncomplicated violence where you topple an evil dystopian regime (...) -- get in there.Music is great, moves feel really satisfying to do. If you think you would like this kind of thing, you probably will.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid and addicting beat them up, the achievements is tough but really exciting to obtain.They really nailed this remake, from the graphics and the music everything became much-much better, especially Kunoichi, she really got a pair of massive  if you know what I mean ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)The additional characters are pretty cool too! Raiden and Yaksha, I mean *cough* *cough*  Yaksha （￣︶￣）↗
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: This is an update of the original SNES game, and as a massive fan of that, I have to say that this game is better in pretty much every way. The graphics, control, sound, and challenge are all vastly improved culminating in what is quite possibly the best single plane beat 'em up ever made. If you love beat 'em ups, you really can't miss this one. God bless NatsumeAtari.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a remaster of my favorite beat-em-up genre in the SNES. the remake remains faithful to the original while also adding several improvements such as new moves, new characters and game modes. How they handled the remake is also great too. At quick glance, it feels like the original but in reality they added alot of things in the low that you would not notice until you do a side-by-side comparison.The thing I like about this game (especially the original) is the simplicity of the game mechanics. The movement is fluid and the inputs to do special moves just feels right. It is amazing how this game helds up well with the modern beat-em-up standards. The game is not difficult by all means but what makes the game attractive to me atleast is the not overly difficult gameplay, correct set of special moves each character has to make the game fun, does not feel grindy and tedious and actually is one of those games that you want to challenge yourself and beat it as fast as possible.The original three (Konoichi, Ninja and Kamaitachi) had their own perks that makes you want to replay the game, and now with 2 more additional characters, this becomes more interesting to play with.So for those that were not fortunate enough to play the original back in the SNES era, why pick this game?  A remaster of a beat-em-up game whose mechanics stood the test of time. Can be played by 2 players (Was originally a solo player game), highly replayable and speedrunner friendly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun to play and to replay. I'm playing the SNES version sometimes too. It haves some good improvements, feels like the definitive edition. The first boss is harder than before but anyway you can just run from it and use the super move. Anyway, is fun and is worth playing, alone and co-op. 10/10 game in music, gameplay and having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, glad I picked it up. I had this for a moment back in the day, but didn't really give it a chance. Glad I came back to it after all these years!!Found out this game had moves that I didn't know about back in the day. SMH... I really should have gave this game a better chance back in the day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: FINALLY ON STEAM!! Been waiting for this to make it to Steam like the other Natsume game remakes (Wild Guns and Pocky & Rocky). Super fun remake of a classic beat'em up from the SNES. The combat has a surprising amount of depth, not on the level of SoR4, but still lots of ways to combo skills and attacks. The soundtrack is great and has various versions that are unlockable and the devs added 2 new characters to also be unlocked (who are really fun to play also). If you enjoy a good brawler I highly recommend this game, especially if you are one to do 1cc clears of games. Well worth the asking price!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Primarily played this on my Switch, but I'm definitely happy this game has finally made its way to PC. Though there isn't anything special or new for the PC market (outside of the typical resolution changes), it's still a great game to play regardless of what system you're enjoying it on. Definitely liked it enough to double dip and support the release. Hopefully, the next Tengo Project title won't have a three year long absence from the PC. Considering how quickly Pocky and Rocky got released on the PC, I'd imagine this shouldn't be as much of an issue going forward.High recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Remake of the '94 SNES original, featuring improved graphics and additional content.Should you, somehow, be a huge fan of the original, you'll be quite pleased with this.The problem is that this is a very shallow type of game; walk, punch, walk, punch punch. There's a bit more to it than that, but really not all that much. Each character plays quite differently, so at least there's that.Speaking of characters, this version features two new ones; but you'll only get them after finishing the game, and not even the prospect of using a original character makes finishing this more than once even remotely palatable.To my surprise, this is getting great reviews otherwise. I suppose my attention span and tolerance for mediocre games must be far lower than the average Steam user.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: If you've thoroughly enjoyed this game on the SNES and haven't played any other version since, then this nostalgia bomb hits HARD. Those extra achievements, Co-op, HD widescreen, 3 soundtracks, 2 new characters to unlock, and a few new moves certainly boosted replayability. Thanks to a friend, I was grinning from ear to ear all the way past my first playthrough. ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Beat 'em ups out there and I don't say this lightly. It was great on the SNES and it's even better here.It's a single lane Beat 'em up so no need to worry about aiming, instead the depth of the game goes into the mechanics of the character. With 5 different playable character, each plays very differently from each other.It's a great game to speedrun or just try to get good at it since it's also pretty short but that's not a bad thing.The pixel art is beautiful, the music is great and the gameplay is tight and perfect, there's nothing wrong with this game exceeeept the lack of online coop. Hopefully it'll get patched in the future. Besides, it's made by the original team of devs so the soul is intact.Worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome beat 'em up game. Each character has different playstyle and all fun to use. They added 2 new characters with this port/remaster which is super cool and Raiden is especially my favorite of the 2. A hulking giant that towers over everything in the game really make you feel like you're controlling a boss.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I had 8 mins on steam. HOWEVER, I can say for retro gamers and people whom are interested in retro games, This is fun. Taking the best version of Ninjawarriors, the SNES version, and expanding on it with added characters is awesome. I have the collectors edition (via strictly limited) so I had this on switch before but, I double dipped for PC. worth. 9/10. Just zoomers or super casuals may say it sucks cuz they can't handle the game and that is definitely a skill issue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest beat em ups ever made! Absolutely fantastic game. Looks beautiful, sounds amazing, plays brilliantly. It may not seem the most intuitive game at first, but keep at it, and you'll soon feel like way overpowered out there. I've played this a lot on PS4 and happy for it to finally come to PC. Buy it! You won't regret it!Check out my 1CC for tips and strats for a sub 2500 second run and get that Mad Murder Machine achievement
_childDocuments_.name: The Ninja Saviors: Return of the Warriors

_childDocuments_.review: In TAITO’s latest arcade action title you’ll slip into the role of one of five android ninjas and brawl your way through waves of enemy hordes in a dystopian future. Over a total of eight levels, you’ll take on the tyrant Banglar and his henchmen either alone or - for the first time in the history of the series - with a friend. So settle into a night on the couch with your friends, and reminisce about the golden era of 90s co-op game evenings you know and love.

name: Taiko no Tatsujin: Rhythm Festival
detailed_description: The Setlist Edition The Setlist Edition includes: - Taiko no Tatsujin: Rhythm Festival - Anime Songs Collection - Pops Collection - Vocaloid™ Songs Collection About the Game Welcome to Omiko City, where everyone’s favorite Taiko elements come together in one place! Together with Don-chan, meet your new friend, Kumo-kyun and aim to become a Taiko Master! Taiko Mode Drum along to the rhythm of your favorite songs and aim to play them from start to finish! Select from 4 difficulty modes. 76 songs across multiple genres such as Anime, VOCALOID™, Game Music, and Pop are available in the game! Songs include Gurenge, My Neighbor Totoro - Ending Theme Song, Charles, MEGALOVANIA, Into The Night, Feel Special and many more! Have fun playing casually with another player or compete for the highest score! You can also use Improvement Support to help you improve your drumming skills! 3 types of party games for 1-4 players are available. - Great Drum Toy War Play along to songs and deploy toys to push back your opponent's toys and aim for victory! - Don-chan Band Work as a group of 4 to perform successful concerts! - Run! Ninja Dojo Become a ninja and race with up to 4 other players! Overcome multiple obstacles as you compete for 1st place! Online Matches - Online Ranked Match Challenge players from all over the world and aim for the top ranks! - Room Match Play casually with friends and players from around the world in Taiko Mode and Great Drum Toy War! Have fun playing Taiko solo, or together with friends! Taiko Music Pass - Join the Taiko Music Pass to access over 700 additional songs! New songs are added every month! - Some songs are also sold individually. *Another edition of this product is available. Please take care to avoid duplicate purchases. *Taiko Mode and Great Drum Toy War can be played by up to 2 players. Don-chan Band and Run! Ninja Dojo can be played by up to 4 players. Each player needs 1 controller. *This game is compatible with the Taiko no Tatsujin Drum Controller for Xbox Series X|S, Windows PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh BROTHER, we are SO BACK, and FINALLY freed from console and osu! jail.Pros:+ Visuals are unsurprisingly eye-catching, cartoony, vibrant and outright gorgeous+ Performance is REALLY good; uncapped FPS and no stutter.+ literally less than 3 GB of space; even with grandpa-wifi, you can get playing almost immediately.+ Even compared to most rhythm games, the replayability is INSANE.+ Very easy to pick up for new players of the franchise and genre, very difficult for veteran players of the franchise and/or genre who seek a greater challenge. The simplicity of the base gameplay mechanics is genius, welcoming but also adds surprisingly insane amounts of depth.Mixed:+- The song list is some of the most diverse in Taiko history, heavily laid back by a MASSIVE premium, which is listed on the cons.+- The Taiko Pass: While it offers many songs for a surprisingly cheap-per-month pricing, the game relies and promotes this aspect of the game way too heavily, to the point where I feel this game should have gone free-to-play.Cons:- This game costs a MASSIVE premium: The base game is $50. You then have to pay a 1 to 3 month sub for MOST the music, and if you are so dedicated to this game that you want to play harder songs, REALISTICALLY, you need to THEN pay ANOTHER premium for a drum controller, a HitBox (which I personally think is cheating and thus GA-d myself from using), etc. Yes, you only need to pay $5 for 1 month or $10 for 3 months and the game offers a first-time discount for the sub. Yes, I understand there is a TON of music and licensing for said music costs a LOT of money. HOWEVER, I feel I speak for the rest of Taiko and the rhythm community as a whole when I say that this game is better off having MASSIVE LOADS of DLC that we can buy then KEEP rather than buy a monthly sub for an already-premium game. The worst part is, you can't buy most of these songs from the Taiko Pass separately, so if your sub runs out and/or if you can't afford a sub at some point, you're ♥♥♥♥ out of luck from practicing your favorite songs.- Cache download: I get that you don't NEED the cache download to access the base game's songs and the Setlist edition's DLC, alongside the fact that the game DOES need to go online and download data to give players the most up-to-date setlist for the Taiko Pass, but Cache/Pre-installs in gaming has become a practice in modern gaming that has understandably, and deservingly, been frowned upon. (*COUGH* Call of Duty games, FINAL FANTASY XVI, Monster Hunter Wilds beta as examples)Do not get me wrong, to say I am beyond ecstatic to FINALLY have an OFFICIAL Taiko game come to Steam is a MASSIVE UNDERSTATEMENT, but I think this game's very steep premium, from the game's price tag itself to the fact that there are paid DLC and a subscription on TOP, to the fact that the most dedicated players' difficulty's songs require a 3rd party controller for optimal play, makes this game a hard-sell for people who simply want to play a fun arcade-style rhythm game, which is SADLY a MAJORITY of any game's playerbase.To the beginners who are interested in trying this game, I encourage you guys to try out the demo or download osu! and trying out that game's Taiko mode. If you have decided to buy this game, don't be afraid to try out easier difficulties or songs first. I'm not implying that you HAVE to pay a premium to enjoy this game. I'm saying, however, that this is sadly the most OPTIMAL way to play for the most dedicated experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Poor base song setlist for $50, and you won't even have permanent access to much of the library unless if you pay $100+ more in DLC, about 99% of which is not high-level/endgame content for serious players.Somehow a new bug has appeared in-game where notes appear in front of sliders instead of behind sliders, completely opposite to what arcade taiko does. Offset in this game wildly varies due to poor optimization and frame drops. For western players playing at their normal hours, ranked mode is dead past A rank due to a lack of players. This hurts because ranked mode is the only way to potentially access songs locked behind the game's music pass, which other reviewers have rightly roasted for locking licensed songs behind a monthly subscription, potentially stripping away content from the player. A lot of endgame content is behind this music pass, so a huge timesink is involved for players wishing to grind to S rank and have a slight chance of playing a 10* without spending more than the $50 for this game.Controller has an inherent advantage over keyboard due to having 4 keybinds for 'don' compared to keyboard's 2 keybinds, as well as a more conducive layout for button spamming, so drumrolls will almost always win lower ranked matches.Almost all of the menus in this game are cluttered beyond belief. The offset settings are buried behind about 5 layers of menus, and will not automatically save if you try to test new settings, for an example of the menu frustration you will inevitably face when trying to optimize this game.This game is fine if you're completely new, but this game is a toxic experience for those who have stuck with the series for long enough to enjoy endgame content.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice version of Taiko. If you've played one Taiko, you've played them all. But, this game has some goodies. First of all - training mode, where you can train on parts of the songs. It also shows how you did in different sections of the songs, so you don't even have to remember in which sections of the song you did worse. Oh, and it has saved replay of your best run, with marked notes that you pressed too early or too late. Very useful stuff.The basic rhythm mode ditches marking of favourite songs, and instead you can have 5 playlists, each with up to 100 songs. I think it's less useful than favoruite songs, as you can't filter by genre and favourites, etc. You also have to download songs from your DLCs and songs from Taiko Pass one by one, which is very tiresome. But since you have to be online all the time to use Taiko Pass, you can just... download them as you play them.And now, Taiko Pass, is a point of contention for many. I was originally baffled by the idea. But the subscription of the pass for 1 month costs the same as 3 songs that you can keep "forever". And you get access to ~700-800 of songs. That said, they still offer regular DLCs at the same pace as they always did, so you can decide how you spent your money.The base game has 70+ songs, which sounds like a lot, but I feel like divide between genres is worse than usually. There's very little Anime and Pop songs, even classics barely exist. About half of the songs are in Namco originals section. If you're like me, and don't like most Namco Originals, you'll feel like the base has too little songs.Finally, the game comes with 3 party modes. Which are fun, but also all have big issues.The toy war is most fun when you have toys and can build your own toy box. The thing is, you need to go trough lengthy toy war story mode to unlock toys, and they unlock at snail's pace. There is no other way to get the toys. And the story mode can only be done solo, so you can't really play this mode as party game unless you farm it first.The orchestra mode is pretty fun, but there's few songs available. Furthermore this also comes with a story mode. And it's very strange. The orchestra mode is only fun with 3 other players, and it's completely infuriating and un-fun with CPU. So you'd want to do story mode with friends... but the story mode comes with VERY LONG cutscenes, so are you expecting 4 people to watch it, instead of playing the game? We've skipped everything, but what's the point...Finally there's ninja mode, which is the most party-mode of them all. You just jump in and play songs. This one has one major issue of requiring everyone to play at the same difficulty level. In Orchestra mode each player can select a line with different difficulty, in Toy Box war both players can choose appropriate difficulty, but here, everyone is equalized to one level. This means that the matches become very predictable if skill level of players partying is vastly different.Finally, there's an issue of guests in party mode. I switch, I assume, each player could choose their own account, and everyone played with their names, and Taiko customizations. On Steam, you don't get to choose accounts for other players - they all join as guests, with default Taiko outfit, and are just named Guests. People should be able to enter their own names, and customize their Taikos, to make the party more fun. One other issue is the "season pass" style progression. When you play offline modes you charge "level ups". When you have 5 level ups the game will prompt you to go back to the main menu to collect them. If you're in the middle of the party you don't want to do it, so you'll probably ignore it. But if you launch the game while you have some levels stored you'll be forced into the "season pass". The season pass ignores fields with story mode, and the story mode forces you into songs. So if you turn the game because you want a session of your favourite song you might be forced to play something else. It's only irritating for first 10 hours or so, after that you'll unlock all of the story mode, and you won't be doing it ever again. The pass goes for many, many, many more levels, and it's not time limited or tied to online, so it becomes just fun "you unlock new things" stuff.You can also play online, and in addition to customizing your character, you can set typical online stuff, like badges and quotes. I don't really do online, so that's as much as I can tell about it. The toy war mode surely makes more sense online, as everyone can use their own toys.Another minor inconvenience is inferiority to the Switch version. We get less songs (mostly lack of Pokemon songs, because Nintendo doesn't want to promote their products to people on PC, I guess), but we also missed on Nijisanji collab. We still can play the songs, but we can't unlock mini-characters. Those were only available until September 24th, and this game released on November on PC. In total we lack around 15 songs on the pass, and it would be nice if Namco added some PC-only songs to offset the difference. Why not give us ending songs from Portal or something?One of the best things about the PC version is support for high refresh rate screens. The additional clarity of the scrolling notes is really welcome!At the core of it, Taiko no Tatsujin is mostly about the Rhythm section. And that is as strong as always. No different than other Taiko games. But if it's not broken, don't fix it. I mean, if none of the party modes and online existed, I would still give this thumbs up. Finally having the thing on Steam is great. The amount of content is huge (with the pass, or if you pay up for many DLCs). It's fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Rhythm games are generally expensive. But if you think about it, licensing and distributing songs, especially songs that are as well known and popular as the ones that Taiko offers, is EXPENSIVE. The reason Guitar Hero and Rockband died out in the west is because they couldn't convince their consumers to help pay for more licensing. The reason Japanese rhythm games haven't hit markets outside of Japan is much the same reason: no one here wants to pay more for more charts.Other community-charted rhythm games are actually distributing through piracy. To keep things above board, moderators have to reject charts if the chart contains a song from an artist or studio that's likely to send a cease and desist. All the other songs on there either have express permission from the artist, the artist doesn't care and is chill, or the artist doesn't actually have the capital to legally fight the piracy (Also why the songs on those all feel like obtuse selections).If you want to get into rhythm games, you have to know that. Another note, yes, a lot of these songs are covers. That's mainly caused by copyright. If the song is original, Bandai can own the right to both the composition and the performance. But if it's, say, an anime opening, the performance is usually protected by a studio and Japanese copyright law. Some of these covers deviate more from the originals than others. I can't tell a difference in Idol, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Bling-Bang-Bang-Born sounds so different it's disorienting. If that's a dealbreaker for you, then keep that in mind.  (For the record, Guitar Hero and Rockband is also all covers.)About the game itself, it's deceptively simple, but it has a lot more grit behind it than you'd expect. Despite being a game that could get away with being called a two button rhythm game, the patterns and strings of notes can leave you reeling. You have to get some muscle memory before you can clear songs on harder difficulties.As for gripes that I have about this game...having to download DLC songs one at a time, not really having the option to pay more to have DLC songs permanently (I'm just super adverse to subscriptions, even if they're actually better for my wallet than buying all songs as DLC), only being able to assign 1 keyboard key to each drum hitzone...Still, I'm glad that I can play a Taiko game without pirating it through something like Osu!taiko. Bandai does a really good job with their franchise, and they definitely deserve my money. This game is genuinely the best taiko experience you can have in the west...unless you're one of those lucky ♥♥♥♥♥ that has a Round 1 near you. Tch.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is nice, almost exceptional. It's everything around it that's problematic. The world is beautiful, but the world building is so incredibly awful. Beautiful vistas are ruined by giant inflatable balloons floating around in the sky. Exploration is trivialised by a character calling you and telling you when there's something interesting nearby, with a big pop up on your map to further spoil the fun of it. The racing aspect is great but it's getting to a part when you're finally done being forced to sit through introductory cutscenes that is such an aggravating process I wouldn't blame anyone for refunding this in under 20 minutes. I shudder to think that every new player is going to be force-fed the same bland Ubisoft gruel that I had to suffer.This is a simulated world built for simulated Gen-Z adrenaline junkies. Specifically a boomer's idea of a Gen-Z adrenaline junkie. Every single character in this game is annoying and embarrassing, there is not a single redeemable personality present. I press pause and there's my guy acting like a man-child using his skis as pretend machine guns like Rambo, or using his snowboard as a pretend bazooka, and doing the weirdest poses on post-game screens. My character behaves like the kind of person I'd be instantly annoyed with the moment they came into my vicinity. All of the cosmetics I've seen are terrible. Again, a boomer's idea of what they think Gen-Z will consider fashionable. It's the "letting your child choose their outfit for a school day" but as a whole fashion style mixed with overbearing product and brand placements.1. In the home base there's a chalk board that references Thinking Foot, that old rage comic.2. They use a cover of Gangsta's Paradise  How dare they not use Weird Al's version?3. Everything Brett says. Every single word. No exceptions. His entire script is full of dialogue that will make your chocolate starfish pucker up with cringe. "ThIs'Ll pUt tHe PiCkLEs In YOuR buRgER. "As I've said, you'll not start enjoying this game until you're a bit further along. That's not just because of the forced cutscenes, it's also because you will start out with gear that is categorically worse than end game gear by a whole lot. Turning, acceleration and breaking will all feel so incredibly sluggish until you get something halfway decent. I don't know why they keep the better content until you're 8 hours in, you'd think that's what they'd want to start out with, so I won't blame you for quitting if you do give it a try. In every race you're going to be many valuable seconds behind your peers just because you're new, not because you're bad.You'll be able to unlock the snow racing, snow tricks, bike racing, bike tricks and flying careers for free, but the BMX career will cost extra, and I'm sure so will every career released afterwards too. You'll not find any missed opportunity for monetisation in this game. The cosmetic shop pulls the age old FOMO shtick by not showing you the entire cosmetic store at once. There is a handy dandy feature that lets you almost instantly get back up if you fall, and lets you rewind your last movements if you've made a mistake. However, I hoped they would've added an instant respawn button taking you to the last checkpoint since rewinding is so incredibly punishing. There are also some bugs causing you to lose races over a matter of seconds, such as getting stuck on props in the environment, and visual bugs such as . There is also no way to reverse on any of your equipment, so you're going to have to rewind instead, which is annoying. Also the costs that are attached to this thing are disgusting.Good gameplay, everything else is intolerable.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been burnt out from gaming for years, I couldn't play games for more than 10 minutes before getting bored.Riders Republic changed that forever.I've played this game today for 13 hours in one session. Let me tell you why:This game is all about progression, levelling up, and getting better gear.The fact that, no matter if you get first or last place, you will make progress, regardless of your difficulty setting or gear level.I had so much fun riding down hills, doing tricks on the snow board, doing impossible 1440s and so on.There's literally so much you can do, from bikes, paragliding to even funny and weird gear like a pizza bike or a giraffe costume.It's an amazing experience overall, even with the weird visual glitches.I WOULD easily give this game a 11/10But unfortunately, it's far from being a perfect or well thought out game.Here are my complaints about the game:Almost everything like clothing, even careers (sport modes) requires real money, and it's not cheap.I bought the standard edition of this game for 15 euros. After playing for hours and having fun, I decided to get the most of this game, like the bmx career, by buying 2.3k worth of republic tokens (real money currency). The bmx career costs 2k tokens to unlock, that's around 20 bucks. If that's not crazy enough, wait until you see the price of single items and outfit bundles, 900 to 2k tokens, that's around 10-20 euros, it's a ridiculous price! And it needs to be reduced to something reasonable.  But don't worry there are also items on the shop that can be acquired from in-game earned bucks, but there are 2 two problems: 1. There's not much to see on the shop for bucks. 2. They're also very expensive, keep in mind i've been playing for 13 hours, have almost 500 stars and around 50k bucks, and items cost 20k bucks, seriously???Thank you for reading my review this far.In conclusion, this is an awesome game, but unfortunately the prices of items make the standard edition not worth it, so don't make my mistake and buy the 30 euro/dollars edition of this game, unless you don't plan to play this for long.

_childDocuments_.review: Riders Republic is a good game in spite of itself.There's an unskippable 45 minute long tutorial. Every single line of dialogue is atrocious. The music selection is pretty limited. Everything interesting for the character customization is locked behind a paywall. The trick system is straight up bad.If you crank the dialogue volume down to zero and get past the tutorial, you'll find a game with an incredible sense of speed and an absurd amount of ways to ride. Ride bikes downhill. Take a ski jump. Use a jetpack to soar through the sky. All of this can be done in one continuous run, as the game lets you swap equipment while playing. I've flown my jetpack at breakneck speeds towards a ramp, swapped to a bike, and before landing the jump, switched over to a big wheeled tricycle, because why not?There's an absolutely ludicrous amount of routes to ride, and every 30 minutes, a 64 player event can be joined that is utter chaos in the best ways.Pick it up on sale. Some of the equipment is DLC, and you'll have a better time if you pick some of it up. Also, skateboards are coming soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously, absolute worst tutorial ever. For that alone the game deserves to not be recommended. Tutorial, rushing it as fast as you possibly can, is 40mins. And filled with low quality video's, and voiced by a bunch "Cool" and "Radical" individuals attempting to hype up the game.Who ever designed the map to slowly go to every new event that's become available to you after you unlock them, in a row, and unskippable, should be fired. I ended up Alt-F4'ing after sitting there for 3 straight minutes watching the map uncontrollably go to each new event one at a time. First 45mins of this game was more then enough. Not even worth the sale price at 75% off. Feels like a downgraded Steep game, where they attempted to tie in features of The Crew 2, but instead filled with a bunch of simulated characters to pretend to be real players, when it's practically 98% ai's riding around. The funniest part is they are all on paths, and if you sit still for more then a minute, which your forced to on several occasions, you can very quickly tell the game isn't full of people, it's full of ai. With the worst tutorial, clunky UI, and bad controls.It's honestly Steep, but made slightly worse in all areas, and filled with gimmicks. Go look at the 2 videos on the steam store page, and ask yourself, how much of it is actual gameplay, and how much of it is random showoff crap to try and get your attention. I feel ashamed purchasing this.EDIT: Others weren't joking about Micro-Transactions. I started up the game again here to give it another go, and pretty much everything, including various events, have to be purchased with micro-transactions. _childDocuments_.review: I did not think the reviews here talking about how bad the tutorial is were serious but I promise you, it's one of the worst tutorials I've ever played. It's way too long, throws too much at you at once, and never lets you take a break to actually go enjoy the game until you complete it all the way through. It is UNBEARABLY LONG and tedious with the worst dialog of all time. I legitimately almost refunded it because it was that bad and I am NOT the kind of person to do such a thing. If you did refund, I do not blame you.That said, if you made it through that agonizing process, you'll find an excellent game. I LOVED this game's predecessor, Steep. Played it here on PC and even more on PS4, completing every event on the latter. This game really steps up what that game already did pretty well in my opinion. Switching between sports seamlessly is really neat to experiment with and it makes the map effortless to move around in. The map is HUGE and full of both bots and real players anywhere you go; giving the ridge a real sense of life to it. There's a Zen Mode where you can explore the map without any events so you can simply just vibe while taking in the gorgeous landscapes. It's a beautiful world to just take in when you're not thrashing every inch of it with your sick tricks. The base game has plenty to keep you busy, but I'm really enjoying the DLC content so far. The BMX and Hoverboards are a blast to tool around with and give me Tony Hawk and Dave Mirra/Matt Hoffman vibes for sure.Snowboarding and skiing are back with a different trick system which is both hit and miss for me personally. It is nice that they let you switch out control schemes on the fly at any point (even mid race!) and they even included the old Steep controls as well. It really takes a minute to get used to the controls, but it did click for me eventually. Wing suits and Rocket suits are back too and still fun to use. I will say the Rocket suit events are incredibly hard at times and even borderline unfair in some cases, so be prepared to redo them a ton of times. Wing suits got a bit of a rework and they handle more arcadey but in a very positive way by letting you gain some altitude to keep a line going via the boost button. It does take some of the danger of wing suiting that made it so satisfying and dangerous in Steep, but overall it's a welcome addition.The downsides in this game basically boil down to a classic answer: Ubisoft. They'll nickel and dime you as always and the Ubi launcher is horrific. The DLC is, again, pretty fun, but it's not really cool to lock new sports behind a paywall. If you're going to add new sports, everyone should be able to use them. It's a scummy tactic that is anti player, plain and simple. I've experienced some stability issues where I've clipped through halfpipes and had plenty of bugs happen in my time, but never anything completely game breaking. It's caused me to have to restart events, but that's about as bad as its gotten. Usually a bug just makes me chuckle and it's fixed by just resetting my character. It still sucks, but polish is rare in AAA games unfortunately.This game is FUN at the end of the day. It's a blast once you're able to access it. It's a wonderful sequel to Steep I've always wanted personally and it seems like there's plenty of content on the horizon still to come. Even if the people on the map are bots, it's really cool to see this active and thriving world as you're exploring it. Having someone do a flip over me on their snowboard while I'm in a bike race never gets old, and seeing active races in real time going on in the distance gives the world a little more vitality that other open world games lack nowadays. Worth picking up on sale, especially the deluxe edition with the extra DLC sports if you're interested.

_childDocuments_.review: Riders Republic is a wild ride through the great outdoors that takes extreme sports gaming to a whole new level. After sinking hours into this adrenaline-packed adventure, I can confidently say that Ubisoft's open-world sports playground has carved a special place in my gaming heart.Graphics and Visuals (9/10):From the moment you set foot in the massive map of Riders Republic, you're greeted with stunning vistas, from the snow-covered peaks of Bryce Canyon to the lush forests of Mammoth Mountain. The attention to detail in the environment is impressive, and the game truly captures the beauty of various national parks. While it occasionally stumbles with minor graphical glitches, the overall visual experience is breathtaking.Gameplay (8/10):Riders Republic offers an exhilarating variety of extreme sports, including downhill biking, snowboarding, skiing, wingsuit flying, and more. The controls are accessible yet offer depth for those looking to master each sport. The sheer range of activities ensures there's never a dull moment, and the freedom to seamlessly switch between them is a fantastic feature. The bike and board physics feel authentic, and nailing a tricky stunt is immensely satisfying.World Exploration (10/10):Exploration is at the core of Riders Republic's charm. The open-world map is an absolute joy to traverse, offering diverse landscapes and terrain. You can race down mountainsides, explore dense forests, and soar through the skies, all in one seamless experience. The social hub of the Riders Ridge brings the online community together, fostering a sense of camaraderie among players.Multiplayer (9/10):The multiplayer aspect of Riders Republic truly shines. The Mass Races, featuring up to 64 players, are chaotic and immensely fun. Whether you're competing in downhill races or trick competitions, the multiplayer mode keeps the excitement levels sky-high. The game's seamless transition between solo and multiplayer activities is a testament to its design.Soundtrack (7/10):While Riders Republic features a decent soundtrack, it doesn't quite reach the heights of some other open-world games. The music is enjoyable but not particularly memorable. However, the sound design during races and stunts immerses you in the action, making up for any musical shortcomings.Customization and Progression (8/10):The game offers a wide range of customization options for your rider's appearance, gear, and equipment. The progression system is satisfying, with various challenges and events providing a steady stream of rewards. However, some may find the grind for certain items a bit demanding, especially if they're aiming for a particular look or equipment loadout.Conclusion:Riders Republic is a high-octane love letter to extreme sports and the great outdoors. Its stunning visuals, thrilling gameplay, and expansive open world make it an enticing addition to the sports gaming genre. While it does have a few minor imperfections, they are easily overshadowed by the sheer fun and excitement that this game delivers. Whether you're carving down a mountainside, soaring through the sky, or racing against dozens of other players, Riders Republic offers an unforgettable gaming experience that's well worth the investment. It's an outdoor playground that's sure to keep you hooked for hours on end.

_childDocuments_.review: - The chaos and mayhem of the mass races is a key selling feature of the game and they absolutely RULE!- Game lets you try all of the year 1 pass toys like the rocket skis as well as the bmx bikes and skateboards for free in both some of the rotating weekly LIVE challenges, and some of those creators' custom events which is appreciated and helps players decide on what toys they wanna buy for the freeroam.- Game will constantly populate the open world with short-life ghosts of players that make the world feel quite alive, it's quite the clever illusion and probably the first time I've seen a game try emulating world life of this scale, it's basically the next best thing you could ask for in an open world multiplayer game after, you know, the actual other players. (Which is especially awesome in my case if you read the last point in this review)- The sense of progression with the account star system is fantastic, even if you login for 5 mins and grind some rails and that's it, you'll still get a star or 2. While mass races and weekly challenges are the best sources of stars, it's ultimately just an account playtime indicator which serves its purpose well. For reference, I've played for about 50 hours and my account has over 2000 stars. I've seen some flashy-looking dudes with hundreds of thousands of stars. Seasonal progression and rewards are also pretty neat with best-stat gear or exclusive seasonal cosmetics.- Game is an absolute content creator's paradise! Between the ability to completely hide the HUD, the excellent photo mode and all of its settings, and more recently with the skateboard expansion, the replay mode? Capturing memorable moments here is super easy. All of the listed features are not new unique inventions by any stretch, but a lot of games choose to include them when they don't need to, or get how much flexibility to allow the player all wrong. This game has JUST the perfect amount of options without feeling too little or too many.- Cosmetics and emotes are not too stingy if you don't spend and play those weekly challenges, but I would have preferred a bit more generosity on that front. It's kinda annoying that not only is the game NOT free, where the cosmetics only cash shop is an acceptable trade-off for monetization, but it's also not even cheap, and on top of that it still expects you to spend some cash if I want to get me some outfits with cloth physics or neon/animated shirts and masks? Pretty greedy from ubisoft if you ask me.- I need a grappling hook/swinging mechanic, or short-range teleport. The game's greatest strength is its traversal and it's kind of criminal that I have all of these extreme sports available, but not a more unique/engaging way to encourage switching between them other than literally navigating terrain made for other sports. Perhaps that could be a great idea for a future expansion or 2 for the game.- I also need a custom decal system that allows me to customize and paint our skateboards/snowboards/hoverboards/etc, or at least a gear transmog system that lets me copy the appearance of any of the unlocked skateboards/skis/rocketwings/etc to whatever I have equipped. The curse of choosing between good stats and good looks should long have been a thing of the past by this day and age of gaming, Ubisoft. Where it not for the good range of available cosmetics for your character, this would have been a MAJOR problem given that the game is all about YOUR STYLE, but thankfully this is just a minor personal inconvenience for me.- I also don't understand why the game feels the need to be always online. There is a literal zen mode in the main menu which is basically solo mode. And this isn't a seriously competitive game where cheating is of any concern. Again, you will understand my frustration with this a little better if you read the last point in this review. I am basically always playing this game solo all the time anyway. This is a foundation that absolutely deserves immortalization in some form or another, it tries some wild ideas and it actually nails some of them quite well for some really fun times. I truly hope Ubisoft will include an offline patch that allows playing the game without internet at the end of the line.- As a very chill game this is overall a little expensive, I would ultimately recommend buying either the skate or complete edition and ONLY when they're on sale. With that out of the way, this is the game I play in between my other big time-sinks and greatly enjoy the variety to this day. It doesn't NAIL any particular sport to the point of skating being more fun than a standalone skateboarding game, for example, or skiing/snowboarding being better than SSX/etc, (and I really hate the occasional jank of bike racing controls Ubisoft, please fix that ♥♥♥♥ asap), but it gets the core aspects of all of these sports right. And in the end, that's what truly matters as you fly/skate/glide/ski/bike across the chasms/mountains/canyons/forests/parks/snow. More content is planned for the next season including the new longboard and the custom event editor, so the game will continue to thrive for a time, I suspect.- (Very specific and niche complaint which will likely not apply to you) Apparently, connecting to this game from Egypt causes ISP throttling problems which means I am not able enjoy any of the actual multiplayer aspects of the game (including the mass races), without using a VPN, and this sucks. Ubisoft doesn't give two ♥♥♥♥♥ about trying to change their servers' required ports for access so Egyptian buyers be warned on this one.
