_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this game to hit steam because this is absolutely my kind of game. I love bike sports and other non-engine sports, especially when they're open world and open ended. I got it instantly upon release and I was only able to get a half an hour in before deciding to refund it.There is explicitly one reason that convinced me to refund it and it's the absolutely unbearable controls. It feels like the game won't let you play it, or that your bike is sifting through a thick layer of viscous goo. It expects you to hold the left stick full in either direction for turns, which will cause it to slowly accelerate into turning until it viscerally snaps into a full turn. If you try and compensate for that by turning the other way, you have to hope there's enough time for the turn acceleration to catch up otherwise you're SOL. Outside of turning you just have very little control over any of the sports and everything feels so forced and clunky.You have the option to 'drift' by holding left trigger to increase your turn speed, which it does, so much so that it's incredibly difficult to control. It does count as a form of breaking still, though, so it will slow you down significantly. Your options are either don't turn enough or turn far too much and lose a lot of speed in the process. I'd say tweak the games control settings but there really aren't any, not any that matter anyway.If you're coming to this game as a more casual racing game player you're probably more likely to enjoy it, but coming to this after playing many racing games (and REALLY loving Descenders), this game just takes so much control away from the player that it's not remotely fun or satisfying for me. I love any genre of racing game from arcade to full on sim but these are easily the worst controls I've ever experienced. It feels like I'm fighting someone who's actively trying to counter my every input, or multiply it, like I had given a little sibling a second controller and they're trying their best to make the game as unplayable as possible.Feel free to try it on your own and form your own opinion, refunding is always an option, I seem to be in the minority. --- I played the game more to give it another chance while I waited for the refund process to complete. I was welcomed back with the most tediously designed UI interaction and gameplay I've experienced in awhile. Throughout the intro, every possible chance the game gets it will make you sit and wait for nothing while simultaneously treating you like you've never even seen a videogame in your life. This is  an intro issue, though.I keep coming back to it while the refund continues to process but I just can't do it. It's  to being something I'd absolutely love, but it just feels so restricting. It feels like, to me, Ubisoft took their railroaded, handholding intros and made an entire game from the concept, and unfortunately the genre they went for is one that greatly benefits from player freedom.For the people spamming Jester awards on every negative review, thanks for the points lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my edited version:I have played this game for many hours now, and my opinion of it has only improved over time. It is an incredibly addictive game that you can easily hop in and out of for both short and long play sessions.THE INTRO: The intro can be as short as a couple hours or as long as 20 hours depending on how quickly you progress. As a casual player, I'm not even sure what specifically constitutes the "intro" other than unlocking all the sports, which does take a while. For some, the zen mode where you freely ride alone may be the most enjoyable.  CONTROLS: The controls have a learning curve and took me a while to get used to. They are a mix of SSX and Tony Hawk. I originally hated the controls and repeatedly changed them to find a better setup. What ultimately helped was mapping all the tricks to the D-pad and the original D-pad controls to the letter buttons. This helped me understand how the tricks actually work by directing your rider left, right, up and down. Once I grasped that, I switched back to the default controls, and the letter mappings made more sense. This method may not work for everyone but helped me tremendously. MULTIPLAYER: Playing with friends can be frustrating at first but is enjoyable. You can ride together in the open world and challenge each other. Finding each other initially is difficult, so I recommend turning on the visible line in the accessibility settings which draws a line between players within 20 feet of each other. This is especially helpful when you're still learning how to control your rider. One thing you can't do in multiplayer is complete tasks together. Like to progress through the actual game you have to play every track solo and finish it at least once alone. You can always challenge friends and build your own track, but it would be very nice if I could somehow do some of the actual missions along with my friend if I've already completed them. Would be fun to watch or to be able to do it along with a friend while we both unlock things independently. Something like that? Just kinda sucks to kinda always bounce in and out of social groups. The multiplayer battle modes are fun, but I haven't really explored them much. There really is a lot going on in this game, which is why the intro is so long. It kind of needs to be.DIFFICULTY: The difficulty is customizable. Easy settings are highly recommended for the first couple of hours as you get used to the speed and controls. The difficulty provides a real thrill once you progress to the pro levels. A small mistake at high speeds can end a race in an instant, which can be panic-inducing but feels extremely rewarding when you succeed. Reseting your rider after a crash is immediate, but the falls can be jarring enough that I often leave my rider lying on the ground for a few moments.  MAP/GRAPHICS: The map and graphics are gorgeous, similar to Red Dead Redemption's landscape and variety. Instead of riding horses, you can use almost anything else to navigate the terrain, and more options will likely be added. The changing time of day and weather enhances the evolving feel of the game.SOUND DESIGN: The sound design is fantastic. I love hearing the skis on the snow, the wind, and ambient nature sounds. While there is a lot of good music, especially 90s alternative rock, I prefer using Spotify to play my own playlists. The ability to incorporate custom Spotify playlists into games would be amazing.As others have noted in their reviews, the annoyingness of the radio DJs and announcers have that weird overly happy vibe as if I'm being talked to like I'm a 10-year-old who thinks hoverboards are totally rad. I see why they did it. It's a fun and playful game that you shouldn't take too seriously. However, I just wish it was a bit more for adults in some ways while retaining litterally everything else other than the Voice Overs. *I used AI to edit/clarify points made in my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Riders Republic promises an exhilarating experience by combining a wide range of extreme sports into a single, sprawling open world. Developed by Ubisoft Annecy, the game offers a vibrant playground filled with high-octane action and a plethora of activities. Despite its ambitious scope and energetic gameplay, Riders Republic is not without its issues, which may affect its overall appeal.One of the game’s strongest points is its broad selection of extreme sports. Riders Republic includes everything from mountain biking and snowboarding to wingsuiting and skiing. This variety ensures that players have numerous options to explore and enjoy, catering to a wide range of interests and playstyles.The open world in Riders Republic is vast and visually impressive. The game features a diverse landscape, including mountains, valleys, and desert regions, each designed to accommodate the different sports. The expansive environment provides a sense of freedom and adventure, encouraging exploration and discovery.Riders Republic excels in its multiplayer mode, featuring large-scale events that can accommodate up to 64 players. These chaotic and competitive events are a highlight, offering a thrilling and dynamic experience as players compete in massive races and challenges. The multiplayer mode adds a layer of excitement and replayability to the game.The game offers a range of customization options for characters and gear. Players can personalize their outfits, equipment, and vehicles, allowing for a unique and individualized experience. This level of customization enhances the personal connection players have with their in-game avatars.One of the major drawbacks of Riders Republic is its technical performance. Players have reported various issues, including frame rate drops, graphical glitches, and occasional crashes. These technical problems can disrupt the immersive experience and detract from the overall enjoyment of the game.Despite its diverse sports and activities, the gameplay can become repetitive over time. The core mechanics, while enjoyable, do not evolve significantly throughout the game. This lack of variety in the gameplay loop may lead to a sense of monotony, particularly for players seeking more depth and innovation.The progression system in Riders Republic can feel somewhat shallow. While there are opportunities to unlock new gear and upgrades, the overall progression lacks depth and complexity. The rewards and advancements may not feel particularly impactful, leading to a less satisfying sense of accomplishment.While the multiplayer events are a highlight, the single-player content is relatively sparse. The game’s focus on multiplayer and large-scale events means that solo players may find the single-player experience lacking in terms of depth and engagement. This can make the game feel less rewarding for those who prefer solo play. delivers an exciting and visually impressive action sports experience with its diverse sports options, expansive open world, and thrilling multiplayer events. The customization features and large-scale races add to the game’s appeal, making it an engaging choice for fans of extreme sports.However, technical issues, repetitive gameplay elements, a shallow progression system, and limited single-player content may detract from the overall experience. Despite these flaws, Riders Republic remains a fun and adrenaline-pumping game, particularly if you enjoy multiplayer competition and exploring a vast, dynamic world. Just be prepared for a game that may have its share of rough edges and technical hurdles.

_childDocuments_.review: Riding High with Riders Republic: Where the Mountain Roams and Laughter Explodes!Oh, Riders Republic, you quirky devil of a game! Prepare for a wild ride, both on and off the slopes, as this cornucopia of craziness combines extreme sports, hilarious shenanigans, and outrageous fun like no other. Strap in your seatbelts (or don't, I mean, who needs 'em?) as we navigate this wacky world that will have you rolling on the floor with laughter!First things first, get ready to look at your character—uh, your alter ego—with an equal mix of adoration and uncontrollable giggles. The customization options in this game are off the charts. From perfectly coiffed hairdos that defy gravity to outfits that scream "Wow, I paid a lot to look like this," you'll definitely be the talk of the Republic. And who can resist the allure of racing down the mountain while dressed as a giant avocado, or better yet, Santa Claus on a unicycle? Bring it on!Now, onto the gameplay that'll make you question your life choices. Hold on tight as you hurtle down a variety of landscapes, including snowy mountains, sandy deserts, and yes, even the cityscape. But don't think these races are your typical serious business—oh no, Riders Republic encourages you to break all the rules and unleash your inner prankster. Launch yourself off cliffs into unsuspecting fellow riders, take an unexpected shortcut through a poultry farm (that's right, chickens included), or even knock someone over so expertly, they'll think they just got hit by a drunk snowman. Just remember, folks, it's not about winning—it's about making everyone cry with laughter!Now, let's talk about the multiplayer mode. Strap it up and prepare yourself for the craziest party on virtual wheels. Join a crew of adrenaline junkies from around the world, laughing, joking, and occasionally crying together as you hilariously sabotage each other's attempts to reach the finish line. The truly beautiful thing here is that even when you're in last place, it somehow feels like a win because the pure joy and ridiculousness of the game eclipse any semblance of competitiveness. It's like a group therapy session, where the only medicine is laughter!And can we take a moment to appreciate the bonkers events featured in Riders Republic? Whether it's a twisted game of "Capture the Llama" or a "Wing Suit Watermelon Challenge" (yes, you read that right), you'll be left questioning the sanity of the game developers with a massive grin plastered across your face. There's never a dull moment in these wild events, and if you're looking for something that will keep your friends entertained while simultaneously questioning your taste in games, look no further!In conclusion, if you're seeking a game that combines extreme sports, outrageousness, and an endless supply of belly laughs, Riders Republic has got your back (and your sides). Unleash your inner daredevil, embrace the chaos, and prepare to be thoroughly entertained. Just make sure you have some spare pants nearby because you might just laugh them right off!

_childDocuments_.review: I had multiple paragraphs written about all the issues I have with Rider's Republic, why I have low expectations for AAA games in general and how this one in particular still managed to let me down, and so on.But nobody wants to read another wall of text from an overtired idiot as he nitpicks a bunch of tiny annoyances and the industry at large. I'll stick to the big one. Well, the biggest big one.The biggest issue with Rider's Republic is the camera and lack of camera adjustment. The first of the third-person cameras moves around a bit but spends most of its time too close and too low directly behind your character's back, making it difficult or impossible to see directly in front of you. The second one is thankfully zoomed out a bit, but it's even lower and off to the side so now it's hard to judge exactly where you're facing beyond having just a general idea. Some games do the second "off-to-the-side" camera angle pretty well but this isn't one of them. I'm sure it's great for low-speed flatland tricks on a skateboard but not for anything else. And as I mentioned earlier you can't adjust this. There are no options to adjust the distance or height of the cameras at all. Why not? That alone is enough for me to  recommend against picking up Rider's Republic, even on a good sale. If you're not convinced, a quick Google search can show you a wide range of camera complaints. I'm surprised it's not better reflected in the reviews here. Anyway, thanks for reading. Overtired idiot, out.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I can not recommend this game in it's current state, This is unacceptable for a game that is charging people 60-120$ with no sale. I am going to list some of the major issues i have with this game.The game can become hard locked at times putting you in either an infinite load screen or locking you into a screen where you would push enter to start the match but nothing happens, this has happened to me 4 times now over just a few hours. The game also has crashing issues as well, seems to happen at random. Server stability is not good at all! every time a player joins in on the game world you are in it causes a pretty bad lag/freeze spike to occur, if you have cross play on like most people normally would to have more players around the stutters/lag/freeze spikes are constant due to many people constantly leaving/joining the game world. I found that turning cross play off is necessary if you would like to cut down on the freeze/lag/stutters by like 80%. Obviously the down side to this is there will not be nearly as many people in your world, but hey i think it is worth it purely for better stability server wise. The other issue i have with the game even though it is not game breaking it looks god awful! i mean i don't know what happen here but holy hell it is bad! textures always fail to load in on time so you are always seeing unfinished textures along with many visual bugs that occur, as far as i am aware i do not believe the console version of this game had any of these issues according to what i found of the internet. Now i want to talk about how bad the controls are for keyboard and mouse users like myself, it is bad i mean really bad, it almost makes me wounder how much they tested before they decided to launch this game on PC. There are even tricks that you just can not do with a keyboard at all, like a nose manual on a bike or a wheelie, the game tells you push s or w SLOWLY to do said trick, how the F do you push a key on a KEYBOARD SLOWLY? yeah anyway point proven. Not everyone owns a compatible controller like myself, and no i am not going to go spend 60+ $ on a controller that i will rarely ever use. The other issue that i just recently started running into is the random disconnects from the game serves that occur, you can be in the middle of a race/competition and then all the sudden you get disconnected from the server for no reason at all. I am honestly so confused why people are giving this game a thumbs up in it's current state, the game feels like a half baked product, i mean seriously i have played early access games that are much more stable/visually better than this game. If you are willing to still play this game despite it's issues then i would say pick it up well it has a deep sale like i did, thankfully i only lost out on 30$ instead of 120$ for the ultimate edition. I will list my PC specs below for the people reading this thinking it is my computer being a potato. I forgot to add that almost everything in this game seems to be a pay with real life money to unlock. (like the bmx bikes)My PC Specs: GPU 3080 CPU ryzen 7 7800X3D Ram 32gigs DDR5

_childDocuments_.review: Are you tired of reality being all "gravity this" and "physics that"? Well, strap in, folks, because Riders Republic is where gravity decides to take a vacation and chaos grabs the steering wheel!Picture this: You're zooming down a mountain on a bike, and suddenly you're like, "Nah, forget the bike, let's snowboard!" Then, out of nowhere, someone zooms past you on a rocket-powered wingsuit yelling, "Catch me if you can!" I mean, who needs to make sense when you can do snowboard tricks off a cliff one second and then BASE jump into a massive canyon the next?This game is like a wild rollercoaster ride where the coaster is made of extreme sports and the safety instructions are just a wink and a nod. Want to race against 50 other players? Sure thing! Want to pull off a backflip while riding a bicycle off a ramp? Absolutely! Want to howl like a banshee as you soar through the air in a squirrel suit? You got it, buddy!And the best part? You can customize your character to be as serious or as absurd as you want. Want to ride down a mountain dressed as a unicorn with a snorkel? Why not? Want to race against a person who looks like they stepped out of a sci-fi movie while you're dressed as a giant hotdog? Go for it!Sure, there are moments when you'll crash and burn spectacularly, but honestly, it's worth it just to see your character ragdoll across the landscape like a clumsy acrobat. The crashes are just another way the game says, "Hey, let's laugh at ourselves and try that again!"Riders Republic is a glorious, chaotic carnival of extreme sports where the only rule is: there are no rules! So, grab your gear, prepare for the unexpected, and get ready to redefine the laws of physics in the most hysterical way possible.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has battled with depression, I understand the need for an escape that can provide a glimmer of happiness and respite from the struggles of everyday life. In my search for a game that could lift my spirits, I discovered Rider Republic on Steam, and it turned out to be a surprisingly therapeutic experience that offered a much-needed reprieve from the depths of despair.Rider Republic's vibrant and immersive world provided a welcome diversion from the weight of depression. From the moment I stepped into its expansive open-world environment, I was immediately captivated by the game's visually stunning landscapes and lively atmosphere. The vibrant colors, breathtaking vistas, and energetic soundtracks all worked together to create a sense of joy and freedom that had been absent from my life.The game's wide range of activities and challenges became a valuable outlet for my emotions. Whether I was racing down mountains, pulling off exhilarating tricks on a BMX bike, or soaring through the air in a wingsuit, the sheer thrill of these experiences acted as a counterbalance to the weight I carried. Each triumph and accomplishment within the game provided a much-needed boost to my self-esteem, reminding me that I still had the capacity for joy and success.Rider Republic's gameplay mechanics were a crucial aspect of its therapeutic value. The intuitive controls and responsive character movements allowed me to focus on the sheer enjoyment of the moment. Whether I was embarking on solo adventures or engaging in multiplayer events, the game's seamless mechanics made it easy to lose myself in the experience, temporarily setting aside the struggles of depression and embracing the thrill of the ride.Moreover, Rider Republic's emphasis on freedom and exploration resonated deeply with me. In a world where depression can feel suffocating and limiting, the game's open-world environment provided a sense of liberation. I was able to choose my own path, set my own goals, and embrace a virtual world where the possibilities seemed endless. This sense of autonomy and agency helped me regain a sense of control, even if it was confined to the virtual realm.Furthermore, Rider Republic's multiplayer mode fostered a sense of connection and camaraderie. Engaging with other players in events and competitions allowed me to experience a sense of community, even from the comfort of my own solitude. The shared experiences and friendly interactions served as a reminder that I was not alone in my struggles and that there were others out there facing similar challenges.In conclusion, Rider Republic proved to be a therapeutic escape for me as someone battling depression. Its vibrant world, thrilling activities, and emphasis on freedom and joy offered a respite from the darkness, allowing me to find moments of happiness and accomplishment. While it may not provide a permanent solution to the challenges of depression, the game's ability to provide temporary relief and a sense of empowerment was invaluable. For anyone seeking a game that can lift their spirits and provide a therapeutic escape, Rider Republic is a captivating choice worth exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: GameplayThe game hosts various challenges you can tackle in about a dozen designated event types, snowboarding and skiing, mountain biking, flying with rocket wing and wingsuit, the DLC skateboarder and BMX as well as the toys. A lot of fun and varied ways to traverse this beautifully made map. If you haven't guessed yet; freeroam is easily my favorite aspect of this game.You can also participate in races called events against CPUs, winning these will get you exp for the relevant career. Leveling your career up will reward you either with better gear or bucks you can spend on outfits. These outfits are on weekly rotation. While tastes are subjective I think there's plenty of good outfits you can earn for free. You can also earn gear and outfits from completing sponsor challenges.Beyond this there's a lot more activities you can participate in like online Mass Races and Trick Battles. There's also Daily Sponsor Challenges, Weekly Challenges and Weekly Shop Rotations making you almost never run out of reasons to play even after finishing the main game.DownsidesThe game opens up with a tutorial and cutscenes, you'll quickly notice this game is a little cringeworthy, but that only makes up a tiny percentage of your playtime. The dialogue in general is a little cringeworthy, but again it only makes up a small percentage of your total playtime. The music isn't really good in my opinion, different strokes for different folks I guess. You can disable the ingame music, still use the other sound effects while playing your own music in the background.Events are in my opinion the weakest part of this game, because it's an open world game it has to confine you to the intended area and route somehow. Basically keeping you from taking shortcuts during races or earning trick points in unintended locations. Their less than elegant solution is to put checkpoints every 30 feet. If you miss a checkpoint during a race you can kiss your victory goodbye. While an alternative solution is hard to come by, at least make the checkpoints less frustrating to deal with, I've lost tons of races just because I missed and arbitrarily sized checkpoint.There's also little incentive to try if you can't make it into the top 3 as 4th till 12th (last) get the same rewards. I know it's supposed to reflect medals in real life, but from a gameplay perspective it makes little sense not to just make it more incremental. However once you have your gear you can mostly avoid events in the bulk of your playtime.MonetizationThis is basically an MMO so it should be considered a live service game and should be treated as such. Premium outfits shouldn't be considered any more or less taboo in this than other live service games like ESO or Warframe. Doing so is kind of a double standard. This is a game that gets regular updates and DLC. The developers need to be paid to get us that content.I preface this because the game seems to catch a lot of flack for selling outfits for real money exclusively, However compared to other monetization schemes Riders is arguably one of the healthiest ones. I'd argue it's a really good example of how monetization should be done.They're confident enough you'll enjoy the DLC items, they let you playtest them for free so you can make an educated decision whether you want to buy them or not. There are no lootboxes or fomo items as about half the seasonal Premium outfits can be bought outside their featured week and there's no pay-to-win at all. Even the bought currency isn't purposefully inconvenient as the incremental amounts you can buy are usually exactly what you need for a set number of outfits.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game and I love it.  I love the game-play, the challenges, the huge open world and seeing the thousands of other players around me enjoying multiple sports in real-time.  The immersive environment and multiplayer events are intense, fun and nothing short of magical.  I've been excited about RR for quite a while and was excited to finally buy and play it.  There are two words why I am giving this game a negative review - Ubisoft Connect.  As an adult who balances work, kids, wife, life etc. There is precious little time that I actually have to play games.  This is especially true for games that I like, but are inappropriate for my young children.  When a game comes out like RR that I feel I can play with my children, I get really excited to bring them into this hobby.  When my young son wakes me up early on a Saturday morning and I recommend to play a few video games, I want the game to work.  Ubisoft's madding system of negotiating multiple admin screens, dual security verification, email confirmation, internet errors, rinse and repeat, makes me just not want to play, let alone purchase any Ubisoft product in the future.  I hope that Ubisoft can figure this out.  I stopped playing Farcry 5 about a year ago due to this exact same issue.  Compounded with an poor customer service experience, I nearly wrote off Ubisoft games at that time.  Coupled with this continued experience now with RR, I will think very hard before ever purchasing another game from Ubisoft again.

_childDocuments_.review: ### Riders Republic - Review**Rating:** ★★★★☆ (4/5)**Introduction:**"Riders Republic" is an expansive outdoor sports game developed by Ubisoft Annecy, offering a vibrant open world for players to explore through various extreme sports. Released in 2021, it combines biking, snowboarding, skiing, and wingsuit flying in a lively environment that encourages both competition and exploration. Here’s a detailed look at what makes "Riders Republic" an exciting experience, as well as some areas that could be improved.---**Gameplay Mechanics:**- **Variety of Sports:** The game features an impressive range of extreme sports, allowing players to switch between biking, snowboarding, skiing, and wingsuit flying seamlessly. Each sport has its own mechanics and style, catering to different player preferences.- **Dynamic Open World:** Set in a massive open world that includes iconic national parks like Yosemite and Zion, the game encourages exploration. Players can traverse diverse terrains, from mountains to valleys, with various challenges and events scattered throughout.---**Visuals and Sound Design:**- **Stunning Graphics:** "Riders Republic" boasts vibrant graphics and a colorful art style that brings the outdoor environments to life. The level of detail in the landscapes enhances immersion and showcases the beauty of the different terrains.- **Audio Experience:** The sound design features a lively soundtrack and immersive sound effects, with the sounds of nature and sports adding to the overall atmosphere. The commentary during events adds a competitive edge to the experience.---**Multiplayer Experience:**- **Social and Competitive Play:** The game excels in its multiplayer options, allowing players to team up or compete against each other in various challenges. The massive multiplayer modes create a lively and dynamic experience, with events that can accommodate a large number of players.- **Events and Challenges:** Regular events, including time trials and races, keep the gameplay fresh. Players can also create and share custom challenges, enhancing community engagement.---**Critiques:**- **Learning Curve:** While the controls are generally intuitive, mastering the nuances of each sport can take time. New players may find the variety overwhelming initially, and a more structured tutorial could help ease the transition.- **Repetitive Challenges:** Some players may find that the challenges can become repetitive over time. More variety in events and game modes could enhance long-term engagement.---**Conclusion:**"Riders Republic" is a thrilling and engaging game that successfully captures the spirit of extreme sports in a beautiful open world. With its variety of sports, dynamic multiplayer modes, and stunning visuals, it offers an exciting experience for both casual gamers and hardcore sports enthusiasts.If you're looking for a game that allows for exploration, competition, and a taste of adrenaline-pumping action, "Riders Republic" is highly recommended. Its vibrant world and engaging gameplay make it a standout title in the extreme sports genre.**Overall Recommendation:** A must-try for fans of extreme sports and anyone seeking a fun, social gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I played quite a bit of Steep and was excited for Rider's Republic since it was announced and was very excited at the potential for another Steep-like game! After its announcement I didn't hear anything about it, but when I found out it was on sale I picked it up for $20, and honestly I don't think I would have paid more for it. I'll talk about it from a Steep fan POV as well as a regular player POV.In relation to Steep it's an okay Steep successor; it has similar features (like session markers, custom race content, etc) that Steep fans will like and the gameplay is roughly similar to Steep but with new sports and gear to use. There's a noticable absence of the Bone Collector progression and instead seems to focus you more on 'getting good' instead of crashing in fun ways, which is a little disappointing.However, comparisons to Steep aside I think even for a general audience there's a lot of UX and game design decisions feels either a little sloppy or strangely directionless, and its microtransaction economy is one of the worst I've seen in a Ubisoft title to date.UX: When dropping into the game it immediately puts you into a race scenario, and you can tell they wanted to get you directly into the action. But after that begins a series of forced introductory cutscenes and missions that took me about 1.5 hours to complete. Some cutscenes I could skip through, while others (like video call or ones that play when you unlock new content on the map) force me to sit through them even when I'm not interested. Generally speaking it feels like the directors couldn't decide if they wanted the player to get in on the action right away or onboard them slowly, and it ends up falling flat on its butt on both fronts.Gameplay: Some mechanics just feel sloppy or purposeless.For example there's a 'rewind' mechanic like Forza that lets you rewind your progress at any time to a previous state in the race. The game seems to tout this as a thing you should be using, but I've found it to be very intrustive. Firstly, it resets you facing forward, even if you were turning, which has the possibility of sending you careening in a different direction from your rewinded point. It also doesn't preview your momentum very well, which can make it hard to know if you should be breaking, gliding or accelerating at your restored point. It also doesn't stop the timer during some race types, which makes the prospect of using it instead of just restarting the race pointless if you're on any difficult aside from the easiest one.There's also swarms of AI riding around the world, and following them can show you where major paths and courses are in the open world. It's a neat technical feature at a glance - some of them just jump around in place or mimic the behaviour of players randomly goofing off. However you'll soon notice that they phase in and out of existence at the start and end of their lines like some kind of Matrix glitch, and if you stand in place you'll see that they're all actually the same characters repeating the exact same action over and over on a short loop. What makes them extremely unbearable is that there's some sources and challenges that require pinpoint precision which become 1000x harder when you have a swarm of 12 AI jumping around and flying this way and that in front of your screen. There's no option to turn them off, they add little, and get old very quickly.Realization: What was nice about Steep was that generally the 'realization' and justification for the world was pretty minimal. You were just a person on a mountain doing sports and events. For some reason the direction here decided it needed to double-down on rationalizing this premise - like some Ubisoft Executive looked at the premise and complained that it 'didn't make enough sense' or something - and it hurts the game so much.Now there's a cast of characters who all talk with dialog and "cool" lingo written as though a 45 year old man tried to imagine how a 15 year old talks (bless the writers, I can only imagine finding 100 different ways to write dialog basically just telling you to "Go play [x] event" or "You did a good job" would be such a pain in the butt).The world itself is also full of branded tie-ins, which I understand is standard for Sports Games but feels out of place here - most Fast Travel points have a Ford F-150 in front of them framed perfectly in camera when you travel to them (which you'll be doing a lot) while CLIF is featured in the main HUB and Prada has a line of in-game events you can complete. It just feels aggressively integrated for even a sports title.I personally thought the art direction in previews looked cool at the time, but after playing for a while it felt really aimless. The world is a...eco-tech-neon-punk 'rider's paradise' but it's really difficult to nail down what the 'look' its going for even is. Players are given clothing items to either look like a regular joe or a character straight out of Fortnite. It's whiplash inducing and generally a look that feels like Ubisoft Direction generally just didn't have a solid vision for what the game's world should look like at all and it really shows. Maybe some Executive looked at Watch Dogs Legion and said 'idk make it like that I guess'.World: The mountains, forests, canyons outside of the manmade stuff is pretty, however I find that unless you're travelling on the more level defined paths in the world it's easy to bump into stuff and feel like you're in the wrong place. I found Steep was much more forgiving when it comes to exploration and 'carving out' your own path in the world, but here if you go the wrong way it's much more likely to feel like you're *going the wrong way*Economy: This is the most painful part to me. I understand games are expensive to make and am typically skeptical when people complain about game pricing, but I do think Rider's Republic is one of the weirder monetization schemes out there.It's a premium game you pay full price (~$75) for, but its in-game economy is structured like an MMO. Most gear like bikes and skis are earned through events which is nice, but I noticed I played 5 hours and had no new cosmetics and a ton of 'Bucks' to spend. Steep rewarded cosmetics fairly regularly, so I was surprised I hadn't got anything new and decided to check out the in-game shop.I checked the in-game shop and noticed that I could afford exactly 1 outfit from the shop with my in-game money, but the selection was really limited. There was maybe 16 items in total and out of those 16 maybe 11 of them were premium-currency only. I looked some stuff up online and learned that not only is this normal, the shop also cycles content *weekly*, so if you don't like anything in the shop that week you better be ready to come back next week and try again.It's an arbitrary restriction that you can tell they lifted from F2P MMO models to enforce user retention and get people coming back with their friends again and again, but I need to reiterate that this is a paid game that costs $80 regularly. I don't think I'd play this on a *weekly* basis, especially not just to see what's in the store, and since I already paid for the game I'm doubtful I'd every buy the premium currency. This cosmetic store would be fine as an optional side-thing for die-hard fans, but as a casual player it's crazy that I now have tons of money in-game, nothing to spend it on and no cosmetics I feel like buying - it seems like a massive failure in the economy's design. I hesitate to call things 'greedy' but it really does feel like it's overstepping goodwill here.TL;DR It's a fine (maybe a little worse) successor to Steep that has gameplay annoyances which compound into larger issues, hostile economy design and what feels like sloppy direction on what could have been a much cooler idea.

_childDocuments_.review: Yo, dudes and dudettes, hold on to your surfboards 'cause I gotta tell you about this gnarly video game I've been shredding lately called Riders Republic. It's like, the most epic gaming adventure you can have without leaving your bean bag!Okay, so the game is set in this futuristic California, where all the bros and babes have formed their own rad republics. You get to be this sick rider, cruising around on your neon hoverboard, dodging palm trees and jumping over beach volleyball nets. It's like a wild mix of Tony Hawk and Tron, but on a whole new level, bro!The story is like, totally righteous. You're part of this super cool crew that's all about bringing the stoke back to the republics. You gotta complete all these gnarly missions to unite the factions and take down the boss dudes who are trying to ruin everyone's good vibes. Talk about a righteous adventure!The graphics, man, they're straight-up trippy. The sunsets over Malibu are so vivid, they'll make your eyes pop. And the characters, oh boy! You got this dude with a handlebar mustache, all about the retro vibes, and this chick with rainbow hair, spreading love and positivity like a human disco ball. The game designers totally nailed the California vibes, bro!Now, the controls take a bit of getting used to, like finding your balance on a shaky surfboard. But once you get the hang of it, you'll be pulling off tricks that'll make even the pros jealous. Plus, you can customize your board and gear with all kinds of rad stickers and neon paint jobs. Gotta look fly while saving the republics, right?But here's the real kicker, my dudes: the soundtrack! It's like they took all the best tunes from the '80s and mixed 'em up with some futuristic beats. Picture this: you're grinding on a rail, doing flips, and jamming out to some sick synthwave. It's like time-traveling to the ultimate beach party, bro!Overall, Riders Republic is the ultimate game for all you California dreamers out there. It's got the sun, the sand, the sick tricks, and a righteous mission to save the republics. So grab your shades, twist one for ya boy, start up the game, and get ready to ride into a totally tubular gaming adventure that'll leave you stoked for days, dude! Cowabunga! 🤙*Disclaimer: Review written by ChatGPT. I've been busy.

_childDocuments_.review: While Steep was a great game (100% on it) I really waited for this game because I love DH IRL.This game was a total disappointment. Its overly complicated UI makes you feel lost all the time. Finding stuff is nauseating and the whole freedom and joy of exploration that was the soul of Steep is lost here..In steep there was constant urge to do better and trying again was motivating. Here you finish a race and be glad it's over. shut down the game and maybe return after you forget how painful it was.Controlling is more clunky and less fluid. There are always some tiny obstacles that suddenly lock you into place not letting you go. The whole experience feels not fun at all.And what I find the biggest failure of all: You unlock gear and get your favorite equipment but there's no point in using it because all equipment has stats so you're forced tyo use the "best" stats making the actual equipment irrelevant.In Steep they were cosmetics so you could use any equipment and truly be "you". Here you are forced to use equipment some idiot chose to rank better stealing the decision from you. For example Burton Custom is ranked 803 pts while Nitro Santoku is 900 pts. IRL both are great boards but if you think Custom is Mikkel Bangs choice for Natural Selection Tour and Ben Ferguson has Custom os Hometown Hero no one rides Santoku. Jared Elston had Team Pro. Hailey Langland had Karma. Yet someone decided Santoku is better board here and if you want to use Custom you're putting yourself in disadvantage.For DH bikes Cube Two15 is right there at the pinnacle with SC V10 but somehow GT Fury is worse?And bikes that the very best Rampage riders ride are not elite bikes? Like Norco Shore, YT Tues, Canyon Sender, Transition TR11, Devinci, Hyper, Commencal.... No, but someone decided Cube of all bikes is the best your money can buy and is the dream bike of all humanity.This game is a mess and not fun to play. If you like wintersports, play Steep instead or SSX. Or anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the Complete Edition at a 50% discount (which technically equals to full price for this game if y'ask me) and it's not a bad purchase honestly. Kinda complex for an onboarding experience, not to mention there are a lot of sports to figure out at the same time. I have grown to like a lot about this game, pros outweighing cons but lets talk about it:Pros:- Competes with dedicated indy games and gives them a run for their money, while being an all-in-one solution (looking at Skating, BMX and Snowboarding/skiing, Downhill games) - Cool open world exploration with jetpacks, wingsuit, paragliders etc. Not to mention you can bike, skii and skateboard around too, almost seamlessly switching sports on the fly.- Lots of various terrain, plenty of decent tracks but honestly even just freestyling down a path can lead to plenty of replayability as it's almost never duplicatable.- Music choice is excellent (Ugly Duckling, Black Thought, People Under The Stairs!) for a game trying to be the Fortnite of extreme sports this is as good as it gets.- Day/Night cycle, you can pick your time as well from the map.- Community is alive, compared to many of the extreme sports games it's great. Compared to the most popular games, it's on the lower side. Like 50-100+ people playing on my server at a time from what I've seen.- Multiplayer features work well, rare lag when more than 20 people are in the middle of your player during a 60 man race.Cons: - Customization is honestly not that great, despite the large amount of choices. You either like something or you don't, no color changes, no different looks (like Skate 3 where you can choose hat tilt, shirt tucks etc.. not even hoodie on/off toggle)- There are only a few faces to choose from for either sex and they are all cheeks apart from 1. Hairstyles are also lacking, not to mention beanies cut out hair completely (to avoid awkward clipping obv but that should have been addressed differently)- Requires the Ubi launcher which only works in Beta and you gotta hit cancel three times on the open prompt before it actually starts up. Not the hugest hassle but it's more of an assle. heh- Requires online connection at all times (the offline mode doesn't work when their server is out)- The gear itself is cosmetically locked (there's no transmorphing it either) so if you want the best performing gear, bike, board w/e you are stuck playing a single item or two for the rest of endgame. Not even griptape for the skateboards, wheel color, etc... LOCKED.- Mod support is made near impossible (still zero mods to this day) due to Ubi making their code extra saucy and trying to make some extra money on the cooler looking (in their opinion) gear which is made only obtainable by real cash. P.S. I'm gonna need a LONGBOARD FUNKIE for the Skateboard career.P.P.S. PETITION to add AGGRESSIVE INLINE make it into the game! Ubi you already have a rollerblading game besides that the rest of the trick animations can be reused from the ski stuff - i.e. super low barrier to entry and you have untapped profit potential here as there hasn't been a good inline game since the Aggressive Inline on the PS2!

_childDocuments_.review: Chilli con carne recipeif you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding Chilli con carne recipe you've come to the right place,Ingredients1 large onion1 red pepper2 garlic cloves1 tbsp oil1 heaped tsp hot chilli powder (or 1 level tbsp if you only have mild)1 tsp paprika1 tsp ground cumin500g lean minced beef1 beef stock cube400g can chopped tomatoes½ tsp dried marjoram1 tsp sugar (or add a thumbnail-sized piece of dark chocolate along with the beans instead, see tip)2 tbsp tomato purée410g can red kidney beansplain boiled long grain rice, to servesoured cream, to serveDirectionsSTEP 1Prepare your vegetables. Chop 1 large onion into small dice, about 5mm square. The easiest way to do this is to cut the onion in half from root to tip, peel it and slice each half into thick matchsticks lengthways, not quite cutting all the way to the root end so they are still held together. Slice across the matchsticks into neat dice.STEP 2Cut 1 red pepper in half lengthways, remove stalk and wash the seeds away, then chop. Peel and finely chop 2 garlic cloves.STEP 3Start cooking. Put your pan on the hob over a medium heat. Add 1 tbsp oil and leave it for 1-2 minutes until hot (a little longer for an electric hob).STEP 4Add the onion and cook, stirring fairly frequently, for about 5 minutes, or until the onion is soft, squidgy and slightly translucent.STEP 5Tip in the garlic, red pepper, 1 heaped tsp hot chilli powder or 1 level tbsp mild chilli powder, 1 tsp paprika and 1 tsp ground cumin.STEP 6Give it a good stir, then leave it to cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.STEP 7Brown 500g lean minced beef. Turn the heat up a bit, add the meat to the pan and break it up with your spoon or spatula. The mix should sizzle a bit when you add the mince.STEP 8Keep stirring and prodding for at least 5 minutes, until all the mince is in uniform, mince-sized lumps and there are no more pink bits. Make sure you keep the heat hot enough for the meat to fry and become brown, rather than just stew.STEP 9Make the sauce. Crumble 1 beef stock cube into 300ml hot water. Pour this into the pan with the mince mixture.info.This great chilli recipe has to be one of the best dishes to serve to friends for a casual get-together. An easy sharing favourite that uses up storecupboard ingredients.it's also freezable

_childDocuments_.review: Riders Republic is the perfect adaptation of Steep that fits every mood of every week through your highest-highs & lowest-lows, presents extreme but fun challenges while also leaving you some mind space for yourself, has good progression with a fun experience which helps you push the limit, but also rewards well enough to keep you going for that 'Legendary' Status.Steep also has it's breaking points and both share a lot of the same. However they're both entirely different games.I grew up playing Sports and most games in the Sports genre, and Riders Republic has turned out to be exactly as expected.Of course - it's not as realistic as something else, or it doesn't have the best mechanics of all time, or best-graphics or  yada-yada-yada. But that's exactly what this game stands for - it doesn't need to have every best thing in the world in order to be the best. It only needs a set of things to work cohesively to achieve what it's trying to be. In fact it's not even trying to be the best and that's exactly what makes it that much more special.Riders Republic is one of the best and most fun sports games I've ever played, alongside the old Tony Hawk Pro-Skater & American Wasteland which also had an undeniable fun unique Multiplayer experience. Games like these demonstrate that games deserve to be experienced to be understood and to never be compared.This one's for the people that learn from the game, cause it'll have you doing things like you're trying to die.9.9999/10 - just because the game controls break when you hit pause in the middle of the race. But Steep doesn't exactly even pause - it just puts you back in the starting position soon as you hit pause.I really wanted to hold off on the review until the Legendary Status but ong, this a game changer for your worst days.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to pretend this game is perfect (right now I'm enjoying a very fun audio bug that persists across reinstalls that makes the audio cut out random sound effects and music at random intervals, and also there is some other weird stuff but i haven't experienced anything game breaking, mostly just funny character model glitches), but I would be lying if I said that I didn't love this game. I had this game on Epic for a decently long time (for those with another version, all dlc transfers over, even if you buy the cheapest pack, as long as you use the same ubisoft account), so my hours don't match how much I like the game, but it's just fun. Racing feels dynamic and satisfying to master. Learning how to do complex trick combos was one of the best feelings I have had playing any game ever. The world hides fun little secrets while looking great, and even the "boring" areas aren't all that boring if you decide to make a custom race or trick challenge. Mass races are also another highlight, pitting you against 1-59 other players in a race to first. It's chaotic and a good time.Unfortunately some sports are locked behind dlc packs, but if you wait for a sale even the most expensive pack that includes everything is pretty cheap (for example, the steam 2024 summer sale had the complete version available for 30 USD), so it isn't that bad. IMO, the extra sports are worth it when on sale for a good price. When it comes to costumes though, most costumes will cost you more then they are worth. Don't think you can buy the clothes with special effects without giving up a bit too much cash. The free currency isn't useless though, having some pretty decent clothing options and being easy to get. Don't know where else to mention this, but the game has a free battlepass system, which can give you very competent gear and goodies, making it by far my favorite battlepass in any paid game.I have a lot to say, but that's only because I love this game and want to see it be the best it can be. IMO, it's already significantly better than it was at launch. I understand that some may be skeptical, this being an ubisoft game and all, and while it does feature some annoying ubisoft garbage, when you get past that, you are left with an amazing and memorable game. I recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: it's a good game, tons of variety and hours upon hours of content. Yes it's good.I would recommend the game but like there's a huge caveat that's the DLC being really egregious however by in large the game mechanics are super fun. There's a ton of variety not just in event types but different sports all together with completely unique play styles as well. Visually I've had moments when I see some of the scenery and think this is such a breathtaking game, and it really breaths a lot of life into it with the players just free-roaming around like crazy. Like really there are some spots that have easily over 500 players (either online at the moment and/or ghost of them) and it's really surreal and insane to see. There really isn't any other extreme sports game like this at the moment, maybe one bicycle game that comes to mind is descender and I enjoyed that quite a bit as well, don't want to disrespect it, I love that game but despite all the ♥♥♥♥ people throw at them, this is Ubisoft. If we were objective here, it has way more polish, you can instantly tell at a glance it's a triple A game and on a league of it's own. If you like these kinds of games, I'm very sure you'll find at least one activity you enjoy doing.Now the bad part, the in-game stores and the constant DLC releases with new types of sports, yearly passes, etc such a bummer for me though. I really want to have more hands on experience with the skateboard, longboard, hoverboard, etc but all of those are locked behind a DLC pack I don't own. I managed to try them a bit via some events that allow you to participate as a sort of demo and they feel alright, but obviously you're constrained to that event and can't free roam with it. I understand that development time has an inherit cost but for a game I bought a complete pack for 60€ having to pay 40€ for a skate pack and an additional 20€ for a year 3 pass is really steep (no pun intended). Not to mention cosmetics. Cosmetics for your character are almost all locked behind a shop and/or really long progression grinds with things like sponsorship where even if you finish your sponsorship contracts (which take 21 days mind you, essentially a full month as they are time gated), you only get 4-8 pieces of clothing from that brand. I mean I'm sure they could had done a bit more, at the very least give different color waves like if you unlocked a Vans pair of shoes from their sponsorship give us all the shoe colors. Having more than 4-5 purchasing options on the store at a given time and even giving you cosmetics as you level up from different career paths would had gone a long way. I have like 30.000$ but inflation in rider's ridge is tough man, I can barely afford a top with that and that's if I'm lucky to go to the store and find one I like cause there's usually only a couple options and if it's not what you like well sucks to suck dude. Despite all that, I don't play for cosmetics, you're not forced to buy any DLC you don't like, they are so confident in their DLC they even make events or even go to the trick school to just play around with them where you can try the new vehicles/gears/sports before you purchase so I can't knock them for it, if anything they are very transparent with what you get and you get to try it which is more than what a lot of companies would do. This game will definitely give you tons and tons of hours of entertainment. If anything I've considered stopping myself from playing not because I don't enjoy the game, but because I can be hooked for hours straight on end.

_childDocuments_.review: Rider's Republic takes all the arcadey aspects of other extreme sports game and mashes it all into one fun and variety filed experience. If you're looking for an realistic skii or mountain biking game, don't come to this game. But, I believe that the most fun you can have in an extreme sports game is the arcadey aspects of it. The bikes and skiis/snowboards feel very good to use (I haven't tried the skateboards.) It's a nice game to just hop into and ride around and have fun with. The bikes are some of the best I've seen in a game of this sort; you have control over most things, there's a decently high skill ceiling, and all the animations, hud effects, and sound effects all feel great. The snow sports are good, but if you're coming from a game such as steep it's not going to feel quite as smooth. Turning and overall movement doesn't feel like you're on snow, it's all very sensitive and you can very quickly make huge turns. But, beyond the actual game mechanics, the mass races, trick events, and other activities are all decently fun. The trick contests are simple, but enjoyable. The mass races are what really stand out in my opinion. They're on a huge scale and the feeling of winning a mass race is amazing.It's not all good, though. A lot of the game is locked behind a paywall. BMX, for example, which is one of the best sports in the game imo, is largely locked behind a pay wall, and this is true for many other sports. It's very frustrating not to be able to access events for certain sports, but the areas for those sports are at least free for everyone. This monetization can very easily drive you away if you're more focused on the events though. But, if you're like me and just like a game to ride around in, listen to music, and chill, this game is great. Although I would argue nothing beats Steep in that aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're at the point of reading reviews to try to decide whether or not to buy this game, I'm assuming you find yourself in the same dilemma I found myself in: Should I buy Descenders or Rider's Republic? I wanted a downhill biking game and it was such a hard decision. Well, luckily I own both, so I can compare them side by side so you don't have to. I'll just copy+paste my review on both so you can compare the two without purchasing both. (Or, heck, DO buy them both. They're both EXCELLENT games in their own regard, with each of them having unique things that make them 'stand out' from the other.)So without further ado, Descenders vs Rider's Republic.Q. Which one 'feels' more like biking? Which feels more natural?A. Hands down, Descenders. I don't know what it is, but I've never played a biking game where the riding just felt absolutely natural and 'right.' Don't get me wrong, the riding in RR is still great, but there's something about the flow of D that makes it feel like you're actually riding a bike. (Also, RR, despite being loads of fun, can feel a little glitchy at times.. and occasionally, if my Steam Deck lags a little, my rider will come to a dead stop in a heartbeat... which is somewhat problematic in a game all about maintaining high speeds.) In D you will feel the trails, feel the speed, feel the jumps. It feels right.Q. Which has more to do in the game?A. Hands down RR. I'll speak a little more about D in a bit, but let's be real here: RR has bikes, skis/snowboards, wing-suits and more (and skating if you buy the DLC's). There are all kinds of side quests in RR, different types of races, all kinds of goals and achievements... It is an open-world setting, and that world is filled with things to do. In contrast, while the levels in Descenders are large, the only kind of 'open world,' so to speak, are the lobbies and the multiplayer arenas (where you can't gain Rep).That's not to say there's nothing to do in D. You can mess around in the lobby with other players, you can go on adventurous rides, conquer boss jumps, and pull off great stunts. You can go play in the multiplayer worlds. There's plenty to do - it's just not filled to the brim with content like RR.However - it needs to be said that sometimes quality vs quantity is a thing. Maybe more on that next.Q. Which has more VARIETY?A. That's right - although RR has a TON of stuff to do, it HAS to be pointed out that Descenders' levels are procedurally-generated, so each time you go on a ride your paths will be different. Now, it's not so different that you'll feel like you're in a different world every time.. but the paths ARE different enough that it will absolutely keep you on your toes. You can't attempt to 'memorize' the paths like you can with RR. You'll ABSOLUTELY have to establish some real flow in D.Q. Which has better graphics?A. This one is VERY hard. While RR is an enormous game filled to the brim with details, there's something extremely beautiful about D as well. Both of them have highly detailed worlds, and each one has their own 'feel' to them. Descenders makes you feel like you're in this lonely, far-away natural world, while Rider's Republic makes you feel like you've gone on vacation to a huge park of sorts filled to the brim with people. The 'world' seems to flow a little more naturally in D, while the cuts between biomes in RR can sometimes feel a little abrupt. I don't know if there's a clear winner on graphics - despite RR having way more assets, the simple beauty of D has its own stunning appeal. I think this one will just be a matter of opinion for each player.Also has to be said that it can take a bit of a beast to run RR at full settings. My Steam Deck seems to be able to handle most graphics-intensive games fairly well, but I actually had to turn down the settings on RR just a little because I was losing FPS and it was getting glitchy.Q. Which has more multi-player/better function?A. Probably RR, although the multi-player in D still adds a lot of fun. In D you can ride around with others in the lobby, go to multiplayer worlds full of random stuff, and encounter other players out on the trails. Far as I'm aware, that's about it. Out on the trails you're not really racing others, but it's still cool to encounter them.Meanwhile, in RR, there are 'mass races' with 50+ other players (although I'm pretty sure there are plenty of players who are able to cheat), you can challenge others, etc. So yes, there's a lot more competition in RR. It's also a little more seamless in RR - in D, players have a tendency to 'glitch' and fly all over the place. Both are fun, but if multi-player competition is extremely important to you, probably RR.Q. Which has more 'stuff' to get?A. No clue. I have LOADS AND LOADS of 'stuff' in D. Bikes, accessories, shirts, pants, helmets, it seems like there is just no end of customization stuff to get in D. Meanwhile, in RR, I have plenty of 'stuff' like bikes, skis, snowboards, wingsuits, and all kinds of garbage... but very little in the way of clothes and accessories. Crappily,  it seems that if you want clothes or things like that, you've got to actually purchase (like, with real money) in-game currency to spend. I have no desire to spend money on clothes. That stuff should be won by playing, just like in D. Seems greedy of RR. One difference is that in D, the different 'bikes' are mainly just skins, whereas the different gear in RR actually have their own performance stats. So this is again a matter of opinion - if you like things to be fair and be more about skill, you'd prefer D, where everyone's bikes are on a more equal playing field... if you want to have the 'fastest gear around,' then I guess RR.But remember, again, there are TONS of things to be had in D, and a lot of stuff in RR that is locked behind a paywall. It will be up to you to decide how you want to play it.Q. Better music/sounds?A. No clear winner. I don't usually like in-game music so I often turn music in games off, but in both of these games I leave it on. The music in D gives you more of that 'I'm riding with determination in some far-off and lonely world,' while the music in RR tends to give more of that 'woo-hoo, I'm riding like crazy in this adrenaline-junky world filled with people.' Each on has their own appeal.For the sound effects, I prefer the ones in D. Once again, they just feel more natural. (Despite being a somewhat smaller production, there's actually a lot about D that just feels more 'natural.')Q. Which has a better 'reputation' system?A. IDK. Each one has a 'reputation' system where you can show off your skill in the game... It's REP in D, and 'stars' in RR. I'll say that the rep of other players is a lot more visible in RR. You of course earn rep and stars by doing well in the game.Q. Which one has more daily/seasonal events?A. RR. D has a 'daily run' which can be a lot of fun, but I hear that a lot of folks are able to cheat and get billions of points or whatever. (But then again, from some of the races I've done on RR, I am almost certain there's cheating there as well.) Meanwhile, there are always a ton of on-going events in RR.Q. Is there a clear winner between the two?A. Not for me. I play both. When I feel like playing with a ton of variety or against other players, I'll switch over to RR. When I want an experience that feels just about as natural as it can get, I switch over to D. When I want to try to earn the fastest/best gear, I'll play RR... when I want to win an enormous variety of customization, I'll play D. When I want a more open world 'free play' style I'll play RR.. when I just want to go through procedurally generated series of levels I'll play D. I really do believe that each game has its own unique strengths and weaknesses.Q. Worth full price?A. Wait for a sale if you can. But for either one, they're both fantastic, so it wouldn't be the end of the world to buy at full price.

I started with T and C surf factory and Skate or Die.  Love THPS, Skate, Skater XL, and Session. This is a great arcade skate game. Gameplay is most similar to Skate, but with better animations.  Not quite as good as Skate in its depth and freedom of expression, but close.  Contrary to other reviews you CAN choose from different landing options; assisted, auto, and manual. If you are curious and hungry for an arcade skate game to play while EA finishes Skate 4, check out some gameplay on YouTube. Too many driving and extreme sports games have adopted this style and I really have a hard time believing anyone actually enjoys it.

_childDocuments_.review: Would like to have a "meh" option.Its a fun game for sure. The biggest problem with Riders Republic is in how it somehow downgraded in comparison to Steep. Sure you now have a lot of more sports that are not just snow-sports. But the controls feel subpar in direct comparison. This is especially bad for the snow-sport-disciplines as Steep was feeling much better. I dont quite understand, why they would downgrade from their already existing systems from the predecessor. But thats how it is.The progression system is absolutely flawed, as you have actual loot that differs in its stats. You dont feel like achieving something, because most of the time the loot is just pure useless clutter which you will also never use in the future because of the loot quality differences. This also means you have to play the game for a solid 50 hours+ to actually have the best items and be able to compete on the leaderboards. Its not even guaranteed to get a good item just by playing the carreer, which means you might have to grind endless hours just to get a lucky drop in the lootbox system. This is beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up in my opinion.In Steep there was only cosmetic changes, which was good, because it ultimately means the only thing holding you back was your own lack of skill. Riders Republic is completely different. You will never compete before investing into the game at least 50-80 hours. You could say its the longest tutorial a video game has ever done.I cannot say anything bad about the price, because what you get for around 40$ is a lot. I can understand the pain when you buy everything without a discount tho. Because literally everything is hidden behind a paywall. Wanna Skateboard? Go buy it. Wanna ride the snow-mobile? Go buy it. Steep was not different in that regards, but the paywall was not as big.The whole presentation is made for 10 year olds and feels like playing Forza Horizon. In comparison to steep this is bad as well. Its not so much about the vastness of the nature and about exploring good lines. It also lost a big chunk of realism. Sure, Steep wasnt a very realistic game, but Riders Republic is even more far away from that point. Prepare to do 999999 degree flips while landing on a rail after a 500m jump.Why do I still recommend it? As I said, I would like a "meh" option. But there is no other extreme-sports game out there which even comes close to this game. It has a huge map, and the different activities are fun. There is a lot to like. This game shines in downhill biking and bmx. It feels like it was made for that.But if you only buy this game to play a Steep successor - you will be disappointed. I have warned you.If you only want a realistic snowboard game, buy Shredders. If you want a Skateboard Game, better wait for Skate 4. If you want a good ski-game, yeah no, I feel you.

_childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERS!RECENT CRITERION:I can confirm that Steam Deck support is well done and playable. My only issue is that I'd like to be able to play offline on Steam Deck which is not currently supported. I don't care if I don't progress in levels playing offline, but I'd like to have the option. I rarely ran into game breaking bugs like freezing or stutter. SOUNDTRACK:9/10 Matches the theme of the game, but gets repetitive like all games. Just use your own music once you re over the OST.GAME PLAY:10/10 for this genre. The sheer number of toys you can use and the size of the map are insane. Then you have around 20-30+ missions for each "toy?" that add countless hours of progression. It's the perfect laid back Xtreme sport game that you can pick up whenever you're interested. I'd recommend increasing your trick difficulty so you have some challenge landing things rather than being assisted by the game.CRITICISM:Paywalls ofc. You have to pay for a few campaigns like BMX separately. You also have to buy skateboarding and/or the campaign for sb separately. The skateboard DLC feels like it pays homage to Skate 3, but since it's a small part of the game there are only a few skate parks right now. Some of the DLC toys are a ton of fun, but some of them are pretty uninteresting too. OVERALL:If you're a fan of the genre then this is a must have. If you want a new skate game then this can quench your thirst temporarily. I know I'll be coming back to this game based on how fun the free roam is. It's got great graphics and atmosphere that bring me back to hit the slopes again and again.

name: ANONYMOUS;CODE
detailed_description: This is the latest work by STEINS;GATE creator Chiyomaru Shikura, in collaboration with returning staff from the Science Adventure Series. 2037. Nakano, Tokyo. Pollon Takaoka and his best friend Cross Yumikawa make a living as a pro hackers wherever they can; wherever hasn't been affected by the 'Sad Morning' disaster that occurred February 6th, 2036. One day, Pollon declares he is going to 'elope,' despite the fact that he is single. However, he meets a mysterious girl called Momo in a place no one is supposed to be... Suddenly, mysterious assailants appear and chase after Momo. During the escape, Pollon receives the 'Save & Load' app which allows him to save data and start over just like a video game. Little does he realize this is only the beginning... The mysterious, genius hacker 'Cicada 3301' who organizes a series of 'Quests' that seem impossible to solve. The 'Gaia Institute' that reactivated the earth simulation which was supposed to be frozen. The thugs from Vatican's '513 Holy Office,' working behind the scenes... Pollon is thrown into numerous plots as a result of his encounter with Momo, and faces a major event that shakes the world. What truth awaits you when you use hacking, saving, and loading? Hack the myriad branches of reality and 'load' the ending that saves the world! This is the story of the hackers who will rewrite the future. About the gameplay ANONYMOUS;CODE is a visual novel where cooperation between you, the Player, and Pollon is the key to success. Advise Pollon on when to Save and Load. Your choices and Pollon's actions determine the outcome of the story. Use the Hacking Trigger, an interactive scenario-branching system. Instead of a conventional story system, the Player uses their own judgment and the Hacking Trigger command to help Pollon decide when to Load and change the future. Controller Support: Developer's Recommended Configuration This game has partial controller support, the developer recommends the Gamepad template.

_childDocuments_.review: Full review: Pros:Cons:Originally released in 2022 in Japan, ANONYMOUS;CODE is the latest and most ambitious entry in Science Adventure series overall. Series newcomers may begin with this title, but should go in with an open mind. While still plenty enjoyable standalone, ANONYMOUS;CODE's world and mechanics will be better appreciated by fans who have experienced other SciADV titles before it.2037, Nakano. The Sad Morning has long passed, but its scars still haunt; a sore reminder of the tragedy. Millions were displaced or killed when spaceborne satellites simultaneously fired on the world in 2036, an earthly calamity spurred by wholly digital circumstances—namely, the Year 2036 Problem.And yet, life goes on. For Pollon Takaoka, our young, dropout protagonist, this means making a living to survive in the aftermath, using the only skillset he’s got that’ll give him an edge: hacking. Make no mistake, though—Pollon is no malicious black hat. Together with his hacker pal and right-hand man, Cross, he’s formed a two-man team he calls “Nakano Symphonies.” Their creed: to help anyone who’s in need, no matter when.Not long after the story begins, Pollon encounters a mysterious, catsuit-clad girl named Momo who’s clearly in need of help—somehow or another, she’s gotten the country’s military and the Vatican on her tail, desperate to capture her and whisk her away. So of course, where any reasonable person would falter, Pollon, foolhardy and justice-driven to a fault, swears to help her no matter the cost.ANONYMOUS;CODE is fast, fun, and frantic. It’s got the classic Science Adventure formula, seamlessly weaving enthralling storytelling with fantastical sci-fi setpieces and lovable, down-to-earth characters. Hayashi Naotaka and Ayano Suehiro have delivered a tight, bulletproof narrative that promises to deliver exactly what it does: a powerful rollercoaster ride of action, emotion, and high-speed adventure. And for the more seasoned SciADV fans, there are layers upon layers of hidden meaning to uncover throughout the narrative.The protagonist duo, Pollon and Momo, are a joy to follow. Their actions and their motives are selfishlessly selfless—you'll always be rooting for them to succeed as they fight to save the world. Their character arcs are carefully crafted and full of emotional highs and lows—sometimes even bringing a tear to the eye.While somewhat accessible to newcomers and STEINS;GATE-only fans, keep an open mind as you play—not everything you see will make complete sense, because ANONYMOUS;CODE is greatly contextualized by the SciADV series entries that came before it. Many of these games are already conveniently available in English on Steam. It's never a bad time to start the binge. Check out  for more info.The implications ANONYMOUS;CODE has for the rest of the SciADV series is startling. This is both the end and the beginning; SciADV fans will  want to miss this story.ANONYMOUS;CODE features stunning and varied graphics, a strong English localization, a knockout English dub, and an unforgettable soundtrack. After seven years of development, it's been well worth the wait. Players should rest assured that this entry is a gem amongst gems, packed with love and attention to detail.Like ROBOTICS;NOTES before it, ANONYMOUS;CODE aims to evolve the static feel that visual novel characters can have by introducing animated character sprites. As characters speak and think, they will react accordingly: leaning in close, widening their eyes, moving to and fro, and so on.In its most tense, action-packed, or visual scenes, ANONYMOUS;CODE will interrupt its regular visual novel flow to introduce the Manga Trigger: aka, scenes depicted in manga format, complete with its own unique artstyle and sense of motion.ANONYMOUS;CODE’s English script is confident and passionate, a definite step up from previous, more lackluster series localizations. This is further strengthened by an on-point English dub performance, which feels true to the game's vibe, sometimes even surpassing the Japanese track.The soundtrack gets full marks: it’s got a wide range of memorable pieces, subtle and exciting, gradual and breakneck. The way certain tracks blend into each other with increasing tempo and presence is absolute genius.Some issues do bear mentioning, however:ANONYMOUS;CODE's Digital Deluxe Edition features a full-fledged guidebook and complete soundtrack. This is a great addition for the more passionate fans who'd like a deeper dive into the world of ANONYMOUS;CODE.The SciADV series is back, and it’s better than ever. ANONYMOUS;CODE is, in pretty much every respect, one of the best Science Adventure games, if not one of the best sci-fi visual novels on the market right now. It simply succeeds where it must, and its successes are sublime.I don’t think anyone knows where the series is going to go from here, but one thing’s for sure: this is a step up and a step forward. The future of SciADV looks exciting, and we can’t wait to see more of what it has in store for us.
