_childDocuments_.review: Anonymous;Code has an incredible presentation and a beautiful soundtrack. A full english dub is unheard of in this medium and it is appreciated, I very much enjoyed that aspect. However, we've been aware of this title since at least 2015 and its quality in terms of story and characters leaves a lot to be desired. I really did want to like it, but I only partially do.As someone very familiar with most other SciADVs, the experience feels like a collage of many of the other adventures. As a result, the structure ends up being not all that original, with some exceptions. This is however not really the core issue- The events seem to play out in such a way to maximize the encounters with scientific concepts rather than configuring themselves to create a coherent emotionally meaningful experience. A good chunk of the adventure is spent resolving meaningless artificial problems which serve as nothing more than setup. And even then, these problems end up holding no bearing on anything.  What ends up being the actual antagonistic force is lacking an understandable motivation. The length of the adventure is far too short, and while this is not in itself an issue it does indicate a problem which is the limited exploitability of the save and load mechanic to lead to different outcomes. Taking Chaos;Head Noah as reference, it is in my eyes elevated and redeemed by its routes. Sena's route for example is well... exemplary, giving huge insights into both the world and the character. Its frankly more interesting than even the main route itself. The lack of such routes in A;C hurts the character development and world-building considerably. This leads to factors other than perhaps Asuma, Nonno, and Bambi feeling either too conventional, like caricatures, rehashes, or just underdeveloped. Just as an example, Liddie manages to be all of those at once. She's nothing more than a vessel for scientific exposition with all the depth of a Bill Nye episode without the entertainment. And that might actually be giving her far too much credit.As for the ending, At its most fundamental level the adventure feels like a simplified truncated version of Steins;Gate with a coat of sci-fi paint which is more style than substance.With all this stated, I still think this experience is decent. The pacing undeniably fun and frantic. Despite that, I don't think I would recommend it to anybody other than those already invested in SciADV. It might have better luck with an anime adaptation that takes advantage of the fast pacing to at least deliver an entertaining action packed interpretation of the events, akin to Occultic;Nine yet probably superior. Unfortunately, it will inevitably end up being intellectually shallow much like what it would be based on. I hope to be tasked with observing a more interesting set of factors next time. The meta science parameter is certainly very interesting though.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: ANONYMOUS;CODE is a love letter to any long-time fan of the Science Adventure series, especially the theorists out there. And more than anything, it feels like a thematic sequel to the STEINS;GATE sub-series.If you’re not super invested in the Science Adventure series’s lore, this may not be the most appealing game for you. And if you’re looking for a more emotional game akin to the CHAOS; entries, STEINS;GATE, or ROBOTICS;NOTES, you might not like ANONYMOUS;CODE much either. But if you care about the series’ overarching storyline and all the unanswered questions that have piled up since the release of CHAOS;HEAD, you’ll find yourself with one of the craziest experiences you’ll ever go through.10/10 — best SciADV entry so farFull review:

_childDocuments_.review: Everything on display here is just kinda underwhelming.The save/load gimmick caused the plot to lose all sense of danger or suspense. As a result there are no real sacrifices made in the plot. The mechanic itself is annoying in practice, as you're expected to know exactly what line of dialogue to activate the load at. I found myself stuck a few times because it's just too contrived. In terms of variety, only one of the "bad choice" endings were interesting.The world here does not feel grounded much at all. I understand in the context of this VN it might make sense to have people breaking the laws of physics or having superpowers, but again it's hard to take it seriously when people are just teleporting around like it's some superhero comic. There is no limit to how ridiculous the powers get in this VN. Even then, the save/load power renders everything pointless in the end. If this was a pure hacking story with real consequences and a believable amount of fictional powers, it would have been much better in my opinion. Meeting agents sounded like it was going to be a threat, but you soon realize how comical they are. There is no sense of looming threat at all here, something steins;gate did much better.I found a large number of the characters obnoxious, and i never ended up liking the MC or the main chick. Cross and the detective were one of the better characters. There is a lot of fourth wall breaking here if you're into that, i just found it not much of value when the main story left much to be desired. In general, i think they tried too hard to jam so many different elements into one story here that it just falls flat altogether. Compared to steins;gate, chaos;head, or even robotics;notes, this story does not feel like it has focus. And if i had to pick between this and robotics notes, i'd say i enjoyed the latter more.The audio mixing in this game is seriously bugged out. Sometimes the character voices are too loud, other times too quiet. To make things worse, my game kept going into a black screen crash and at the very end i had to look up the (very abrupt) ending on youtube.In terms of overall enjoyment, i think it's a decent novel if you want a quick story to go through. It's definitely not the best work in the science adventure series as far as i'm concerned though.

_childDocuments_.review: Mfs at SciAdv cooked yet again.Don't come in expecting Steins;Gate or a multiple route long psychological thriller like the Chaos; games, this one is way shorter (~20h) and linear (only 1 normal ending, 1 true ending and game overs if you make a bad decision). You'll get instead 20h of non stop action, from the first second you launch the game to the end credits there is always something happening without a single second of filler or slice of life. The most SciAdv entry out of all the SciAdv entries that will use, reference & answer almost everything that haven't been explained yet in the previous games (and also introduce even more complex concepts for the future entries), that's why having read all the previous VNs is very recommended.Recommended only to the hardcore fans who have read everything and whose soul & wallet are bound to the SciAdv deity, you'll have an excellent time as always with this entry.

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILERS FOR THE ENTIRE SCIENCE ADVENTURE SERIES BELOW)For reference, I played on PS5.I do not like Anonymous;Code, in fact, I actively dislike it. I hate to say that as such a huge fan of SciADV, but I really, really, do not like Anonymous;Code.This so called "culmination of the Science Adventure series" was nothing more than a disappointment, and it pains me to know that. It miserably fails to live up to the quality standard of every other mainline SciADV entry. The only other entry in this series that I dislike is Steins;Gate 0, which is not mainline, and I've only seen the anime adaptation. I didn't like the way that it handled the cast of Steins;Gate, but I loved some of its ideas and could see how much potential that story could've had if it was in the hands of more competent writers who understood the material it was a spin off of. However, I refrain from truly disliking it until I've completed the visual novel, in the hopes that it may redeem a story that I otherwise did not enjoy. Anonymous;Code has no excuse. Just like Steins;Gate 0, it is another watered down rehash of the SciADV team's most popular entry, and once again, it misses the mark. If I had to pick between Steins;Gate 0 and Anonymous;Code for which Non-Steins;Gate I thought was better, it would be 0 with no hesitation.To adhere to the character limit, I'll be skipping over positives. There aren't many to speak of anyway.Starting off, the sprites here are bad. Seriously bad. They look like baby's first flash animation character design. They have this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 2.5D artstyle that seems like it's trying to blend together the 2D sprites of Steins;Gate and the Chaos; games with the 3D models of Robotics;Notes, but doesn't commit to either, and comes out looking terrible. Every body part of the characters is independently animated, making them look like they were pulled out of a gacha game. I legit could not stop thinking about this the entire game. They look terrible. How bad they look is made especially apparent with the CGs and Manga Triggers, which change the artstyle completely and look a thousand times better. The difference is night and day. The best example I can think of is this, In this case, the sprites look simplistic and bad, and the CG makes those same characters look great. The baked lighting and extra detail of the CG makes the characters look more in line with the sprites in Chaos;Child, and they just look so much better.Think of this story as a shonen. It follows a teenage hacker named Takaoka Pollon, who meets a strange girl name Aizaki Momo, and they embark on a dangerous journey to save the world!!!! Lose interest yet?If I wanted a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ shonen like 95% of anime and manga out there, believe me, SciADV would be the last place I would look. It takes place in a futuristic cyberpunk setting (ooohhhhh) where people have superpowers and super high-tech technology!! This is a far cry from what I've come to expect from the grounded, realistic settings of the Science Adventure series. Remember how Steins;Gate (original) never showed you SERN's dystopia in 2036? Yeah, there was a reason for that.The characters here are equally as bad. They're less characters and more so caricatures. Pollon is a boring ass protagonist. He's an "anon with a bright future who can't stand idly by when someone's in need!!" What's with the cringy ass writing?!? Pollon has the power to "Save and Load" like in a video game. It's overpowered as ♥♥♥♥. Takumi and Takuru were , Okabe had Reading Steiner, Kaito was mostly ordinary other than Slo-Mo (which he couldn't activate on command) and Yuta could use . Pollon's Saving and Loading is basically a constantly available Time-Leap Machine, meaning he essentially has Reading Steiner and can time leap whenever and wherever. His ability is so strong that any and all sense of the danger felt in Steins;Gate is completely absent. . Momo, the heroine of this game, is booorrrinnggg. Compared to Rimi, Kurisu, Akiho, Serika, or even Ryoka with her ridiculously huge tits, Momo is just a total nothing character.The story here is really boring. I was checked out about half way through and just couldn't wait to be done. This is the shortest SciADV entry I've played thus far and it's the only one I couldn't be bothered to 100%. Not to mention it has enough religious undertones to make even Hideo Kojima weep.Onto my biggest problem with Anonymous;Code, and one that I feel impacts the entire Science Adventure series as a whole, and for the worse. To me, it seems like Chiyomaru Shikura and the Science Adventure team failed with Anonymous;Code to realize just how important these stories are to some people. My love for this series started with Steins;Gate, but it's become much more than that over time. I'm more emotionally attached to these stories than I am some of my distant relatives. To see the decade and a half history of this fantastic series trampled by the most underwhelming game in it hurts me in a way that words just can't describe. So for that, I'm afraid that I just cannot recommend Anonymous;Code.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the series, I'd say it's a must-play. Very important to the overall plot and worldbuilding.But I wish it wasn't.None of the characters are particularly interesting - only three really get developed, and they're sadly fairly generic - and the main gameplay mechanic is basically trial and error.And even those really important plot things almost make the rest of the SciAdv series pointless. I recommend it (in my words) only because I'm sure it'll be required reading for everything that comes after.This game went through years of development hell, and, frankly, it shows. I know the team can do better, and I really hope that, now that this is out, they can focus on making the next entry really great.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as it pains me to say this as an absolute lover of the sciADV series, unfortunately I cannot recommend Anonymous;Code. And the worst part of it, is that it's not even for the game itself, but because of what Spike Chunsoft did with this game's launch regarding the pricing of it.For starters, no matter how much I think about it, there's nothing that justify this game's 60USD full price (54 with launch discount). To my surprise, some people around here were saying the "VN is supposed to be priced like that", but they clearly don't know sh*t. There's just no way this is normal, and it's simple as that. So you're telling me a 20-hour VN cost the same 60USD as Baldur's Gate 3? What exactly went through in your minds when setting this price up? The "awesome" and never-seen-before English dub that about 5 people will choose instead of the original voice-acting in japanese? The art style? The game's mechanics? The OST? I mean, whatever reason they chose, if you have decent common sense, you know that this is not even close to justify the price of it.Up next, let's talk about regional pricing. I live in Brazil, and for some reason someone decided that both Brazil and Mexico should now pay for the sins of the entire human race when launching A;C, so they went ahead and came up with the brilliant idea to not add regional pricing for this game here and there. You know what this means, right? This means we are LITERALLY paying 60USD converted 100% directly into our currency (270BRL with the launch discount, and 300BRL for the full price). Just for comparison again - and for the sake of my sanity - please, read what I'm about to write now calmly and let that sink in: This is not Valve's doing, by the way. In case you didn't knew, publishers/developers can manually decide the price from each region based on Steam's recommended regional pricing. So the question is, why they opted Brazil and Mexico out of this? Was it a rookie mistake from the new intern they're having trouble paying? Or it's really just the mindset culture from Brazil and Mexico that can guarantee sales at those numbers because they're so confident that the people here and there are so passionate about things they will do anything to get what they want? Either way, I think we can agree that this is both very sad and disappointing to the VN industry as a whole.And yes, I feel both regret and shame that I still bought the d*mn game at this price here, because unfortunately my love for sciADV series speak louder than reasoning.Shame on you, Spike Chunsoft.

_childDocuments_.review: ANONYMOUS;CODE - A Cyberpunk Adventure with Highs and Lows! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)In the world of visual novels, few names carry the weight and anticipation that Chiyomaru Shikura's works do. As a fan of the Science Adventure Series, I couldn't help but dive headfirst into the enigmatic realm of ANONYMOUS;CODE, a game that promises to deliver a unique hacking experience while also wrestling with complex narratives and cyberpunk aesthetics.The first thing that strikes you about ANONYMOUS;CODE is its visually stunning presentation. The user interface and graphical elements are nothing short of breathtaking, immersing players in a cyber-future-techno world that's both sleek and captivating. Coupled with an outstanding soundtrack, featuring compositions by Takeshi ♥♥♥, the game successfully crafts an engaging atmosphere that draws you into its story.The narrative of ANONYMOUS;CODE is a rollercoaster ride through a dystopian Tokyo in the year 2037. Our protagonist, Pollon Takaoka, stumbles upon a mysterious girl named Momo, setting off a series of events that shake the world. The plot unfolds with breakneck pacing, keeping players on the edge of their seats with a frenetic and captivating storyline. It's an engaging sci-fi narrative that manages to justify its rapid progression.However, there are mixed aspects to consider. Character development, while not underdeveloped, falls short in terms of engagement. Some characters feel like mere vessels for scientific exposition rather than fully fleshed-out individuals. Pollon himself, though a capable protagonist, doesn't quite reach the unique depths of Shikura's previous creations.One of the elephants in the room is the game's length and price. At a hefty $60, ANONYMOUS;CODE offers a relatively short plot, taking me around 16 hours to reach the true ending. This might deter potential players looking for more content for their money. It also raises questions about the depth and value of the save and load mechanic, which doesn't seem to lead to as many different outcomes as one might hope.The biggest letdown, however, is the antagonist's motivation, which remains unclear and unconvincing. This lack of a compelling driving force for the plot's central conflict leaves a noticeable void in the narrative.In summary, ANONYMOUS;CODE is a visually stunning and engaging cyberpunk adventure that, despite its shortcomings, holds its own in the world of visual novels. It's a must-play for fans of the Science Adventure Series, but the steep price tag may deter newcomers. While it falls short in character development and offers less content than expected, the fast-paced narrative and the unique save and load mechanic make it a worthwhile addition to the genre. However, if you're not already invested in SciADV, it might be best to wait for a price drop before jumping into this cybernetic world. Here's to hoping for an Anonymous;Code Elite (Steins;Gate Elite) that addresses some of these issues and truly fulfills its potential.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually 'playing' novels and whatnot, but I'm a big fan of Stein's Gate, and seeing as to how this was written by the same author (and plays in the same universe) I figured I might as well give it a go.Buuuuut, maybe trying to compare it to a full fledged 2 season anime set up expectations the game couldn't possibly cash in on:The story of Anonymous;Code isn't bad. But it's also not great. The characters are nicely detailed and flow well with each other, but they're also extremely predictable and cliche'd. The core storyline is kind of interesting, but a big failure is the fact that all major plot twists are kind of obvious even before the game starts dropping the obvious hints. It also fails on capturing the nuanced complexity that was Stein's Gate, and in the end tries to capture not with creativity or ingenious mindgames, but simply by stacking stakes upon stakes and escalating the story into the absurd.Voice acting is arguably top notch, and the graphics aren't something that's supposed to be factored in for a visual novel (but are pretty decent nontheless).So, at that stage the game would probably be at a middling positive review, so what's the catch:The game utterly, abyssimally, fails at it's control scheme. Knowing little about visual novels, I booted it up, and essentially was taught (by the game) that it's mostly just a linear story, which has several dead-ends that you need to circumvent by pressing one single button at a specific point in the scene, to 'remind' the protagonist of his special ability he generally uses all by himself.This leads to mostly just hours upon hours of passing through conversations and text walls with no real gameplay, occasionally reloading a particular chapter to repeatedly hit the button on every line of text because it's sometimes hard to figure out why the game devs made that specific line the only one you can interact with.Then you come to Chapter 10 (no spoilers, dont worry), and get stuck because even redoing the entire chapter, not a single line of text can be button'd successfully. You then check a guide and ONLY THERE learn that the game also has an entirely different gameplay mechanic for you to affect the story... that the game never once explains to you, and which (on PC) is bound to M1 together with 'progress text', which (given the amount of text you would have to 'click' through) you quickly learn to do with a button press (A, S, D or SPACE) instead. Meaning by the time you get the ability to specifically affect the game with M1, you won't be using your mouse and (as me) maybe miss the game mechanic entirely.That was OBNOXIOUSLY frustrating, because it means, 10 hours in, with most of the story done, you realize you played the game wrong in it's entirety. All because the game's control scheme is a mess.I would love to have given this game a positive review, and I might have still done so, regardless of the control issues, if the story had been up to par with Stein's Gate... but that's just not the case, so I'll have to disrecommend it.Maybe wait for an anime adaptation, or if you still resolve to get the game, do yourself a favor and check on a spoiler-free basic guide first, to get the full experience.Overall, a 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm less than an hour into this so far, so I can't really speak to the quality of the story so far. My only real complaint from that perspective is that while controllers are supported, there's no in-game screen telling you the controller bindings.The other thing I'll say is that the localization seems on-point. They went through the effort of dubbing it (and dubbing it well, I might add), which I imagine was no small feat, so I was hoping there was some real effort put into this release and I'm not disappointed so far. The text under the logo in most Science Adventure VNs is usually completely garbled nonsense English, but here it's actually comprehensible. If you like other VNs in this series this is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most interesting concepts in all of SciADV so far, but not enough time is given to really let these concepts breathe, and for all of their implications to take hold. Compare this to something like Steins;Gate and the Chaos; sub series, and while those games are more limited in their scope, adequate time is dedicated to their mechanics, impact on the characters, etc. So far, the 'neo' SciADV works (Anonymous;Code, Occultic;Nine) both have this problem of breakneck pace, and a substantial lack of atmosphere and presence in the world for the reader (Observer?) results. There are moments where we get a sense of how these revelations and scifi concepts are affecting the characters, see Oz's breakdown in Chapter 9 as a good example, but these moments are few and far between, and, due to the pacing issues, our protagonist's struggles are nothing more than minor hiccups, where in the past, we would've stewed in Takumi or Okabe's despair and mania for an uncomfortably long time. A lack of significant low points results in a cheap pay-off when the protagonist finally does overcome the forces set against him, similar moments in other SciAdv games are some of the best in their genre, but here, it seems like naught but a pale imitation.The implications for the future of the series, as well as the re contextualization of the past, are great, but honestly, I feel as if the characters are mere vehicles for that lore. If I was to sum it up, Anonymous;Code is the anti-Chaos;Child in the SciAdv series, where Chaos;Child lacked in innovative sci-fi compared to past entries, Anonymous;Code had in spades; but where Chaos;Child made you cry, Anonymous;Code made you click faster to get to the important stuff.Still good, and the technical elements were really some of the best I've seen thus far in a visual novel.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you love real world Lore woven into a game, this game is an absolute treasure trove~♥I'm only starting chapter 4 of this game, and I AM IN LOVE~♥ The countless references to real events and terms and even quantum science and theories and internet conspiracies, has had me scouring the internet looking up related things and the accuracy of the information is pretty good making it even more fun~♥. I feel like this game was made for people like me who enjoy these kinds of things~ This game has me looking up information and learning new things, and the best part is, some of the references I actually knew about since I grew up in the 90's. I haven't had this level of Easter Egg Hunt like fun since the first Assassins Creed game came out and I used my silly Spy Books to decode all kinds of hidden things in the AC game, morse code, various kinds of Ciphers, hell I had even learned to read and write with a Pigpen Cipher thanks to those books, and that helped me decode all kinds of hidden messages in the Assassins Creed game. What's more fun, is the fact the characters in this game, often resort to doing the same things I am doing while playing the game, looking up information online to confirm it and gain a better understanding of the topic at hand. This has also helped me understand what's going on in game even better too. I have been greatly enjoying this game from the get go. When I bought it I was expecting it to be a Save & Load Power Junkies Fantasy, but I wasn't expecting to actually spend a lot of my time actually studying topics online, which has been half the fun thus far!~♥ Granted most this information goes in one ear and out the other for me, but I have had a lot of fun looking it up and reading stuff about them. When studying the Double Slit experiment I realized I'd even come across something similar in regards to how light works in narrow spaces, when I was in my mother's bathroom of all places and saw the light coming in from the crack between the door and the frame created a strange dark and expanding rainbow effect as the door closed and the bathroom light was off, the dark rainbow grew up till the point the light got cut off entirely which was why it fascinated me at the time. Not sure it's totally relevant but it came across my mind while I was reading up on the Double Slit experiment. I don't know how far I really am into the game yet, but I'm certain there's gonna be tons more I can learn out side of the game, from events going on in the game that reference real world things. Some of the fun interesting things I read up on are: the Year 2000 problem and Year 2038 Problem, John Titor, Esperanto (this one I knew about cause I watched Danny Phantom a Lot, it's the language Wulf speaks), Three Secrets of Fátima (funny how the name Fatima keeps coming up a lot lately in my life, Shadow Frost Witch anyone ;) lol), Cicada 3301, and the Double Slit experiment, are all things I've studied up on since they all came up in game, I've been absolutely loving this game thus far~TLDR: THIS GAME MAKES ME SMARTER!! lol

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid entry in the Sci-Adv series with lots of neat little nods and references to the previous games for the most observant. The story is pretty fun and very action packed from the get-go, featuring a colourful cast of characters trying to save the day while dealing with some pseudo-scientific shenanigans along the way (although I do feel like they might've overdone it a little bit in the later chapters, even by Sci-Adv standards).I found the visual presentation to be fantastic, with the novel sequences switching to a comic-book format for the more intense scenes and generally switching things up from time to time to keep things fresh. That said though, some of the pseudo-animated 2D sprites can look pretty goofy sometimes (with the characters' hair bouncing halfway across the screen at times if you skip the dialogue too fast, among other minor things), but overall it didn't distract too much from the core experience.The "Save And Load" mechanic is also pretty neat and very reminiscent of Steins;Gate's Reading Steiner, while still putting its own spin on things. However, I felt like some of the trigger points were a little too precise for my liking, meaning that you could easily miss your chance to Load back in time even though you technically shouldn't. Luckily though those moments were few and far between and it's usually pretty easy to tell when you can (and/or should) jump back in time in order to progress through the story (some of the optional scenes however do require some out-of-the-box thinking to reach though, which is a nice touch IMO).All in all, I had a fun time with it, and I can't wait to see what else the Sci-Adv universe has in store. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: No spoilers in this review.First, I'll say that I really enjoyed this experience. I am a huge SciADV fan and have been for almost a decade. It's a series very close to my heart and as such some of my opinions will be skewed by this fact, some skewed overly positive and some skewed overly negatively.- The characters are really good. There's a lot of charm in the personification of the cast through their voices, art, and animations throughout the VN. Everyone has a role to play and none of the characters feel like they're stepping on the toes of the others through their part of the plot. I personally got attached and invested in almost every recurring character.- The worldbuilding is campy, but in a charming way. The technology on display, the input methods the characters use to interface with said technology, and a lot of the "I am a hacker therefore I can hack into things easily" trope is very kitschy but its unapologetic representation kind of makes it overflow into being cool. - The main gameplay is conceptually very solid and engaging.- The plotline of the adventure is engaging, with earned high-stakes and some incredibly memorable moments. While not playing the game (usually between chapters), I was inspired to think and ponder ideas/story beats presented in the plot, which good VNs should always strive to achieve. - The art is gorgeous. There are some things that could be polished. One of the earlier-appearing militarized characters has his mouth animation looking quite...unfortunately unpolished. But besides those hiccups, I really love the art style they went with here even though it doesn't hold a candle of the non-Elite S;G art in my opinion. Some scenes are illustrated in manga panel style and I wish there were more of these, as they are a special treat whenever they come up.- The music is really good and sets the tone very well. While not quite as striking as Steins;Gate music, it is easily some of the best in its genre and I plan to enjoy the soundtrack even after finishing the game.- Not enough breathing room between major story plots beats. There is an immense amount of story whiplash in this game. There will be a scene with a huge revelation or event, and the game just kind of moves on and drags you with it. Particular moments have characters in peril that don't really give you enough time to let it linger on your tongue.This problem also extends to lore implications, as there will be info dumps that don't give the player time to really let things sink in. I won't go into detail in the interest of keeping it spoiler-free but there were several times I had to open the log and reread conversations a few times because it felt like enormous exposition was given in such a quick and rapid-fire way.- While conceptually cool, the main game mechanic is very obtuse to use naturally. You basically need a guide if you want to see every CG and optional scene. S;G struggles with this too, but a lot of its choices come from your cell phone literally ringing or pinging you for attention. - There are a lot of times where the log feature (pretty standard in visual novels) just straight up does not work. You can hit the button and it beeps at you as if to tell you "yep, button received" and it just does not give you a log of what you just read. This is very frustrating. This was likely done because of the way they tried to make the text that the player sees be in-universe in a way, but I don't think that concept was worth sacrificing the ability to reread dialogue that just happened.I'm not sure how I feel about the ending. As a standalone end to THIS TITLE, it's satisfying and a good way to cap off the adventure. But this game was pitched as the pinnacle of what SciADV was building to and I don't see it that way at all.On the wider SciADV community you'll find a lot of people talking about how this game changes/recontextualizes/ruins the entire series and I don't agree. There's evidence in the text to suggest that this is the case, but also enough evidence to suggest that it isn't. There are a number of theoretical flame wars and arguments one could make to argue one perspective or another but I don't think we'll really know until the eventual release of Steins;??? (or, at the very least, Steins;Gate Reboot in 2025). That being the case, this game can't really be what the whole series was building to, then.For now, I'll say that it's my opinion that while the ending has huge implications it doesn't have the immense collateral effect that some people insist it does.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing. The game starts strong, and it is the complete opposite of the previous Science Adventure games in terms of pacing- it's FAST. Honestly, I enjoyed it, and found it funny how parts that would normally be slice-of-life scenes are just skipped over entirely to continue the game's fast pacing. The game only really stops to explain scientific concepts, and these explanations make good use of the comic segments to help illustrate everything. There are very few slice-of-life scenes, too.This pacing also works against it, however, as there are too many characters inserted into the story who simply don't have much time to shine or be developed in any meaningful way. The motivation of one of the major antagonist groups isn't explained very well and there's a lot of interpretation that has to occur to figure out what it *might* be.The game's action is really, really crazy when compared to previous entries of the Science Adventure series. These parts, the game does well, and it's probably what it does best.However, the game runs out of gas towards the end. It feels like after the first ending everything is just phoned in and underwhelming. Plot points are suddenly resolved off-screen too many times with incredible ease, robbing the game of some seriously needed character moments for an underdeveloped cast. I didn't mind the characters, but I felt that they were underdeveloped, some underused. For example, the MC's best friend, Cross, doesn't really get any development at all, and his whole character is one-note at best. Other characters, like the Cyber Force Dolls trio, did not have enough to do. Only one of those three gets any sort of development and backstory at all, but even then, it's minimal at best.I played with the Japanese Dub. They did a great job, and some of the VA's obviously had a lot of fun with their lines.Now, in regards to this game's position in the Science Adventure series...This is the game's weakest aspect. It uses the entire existence of  as a crutch to the point of absurdity. Aside from that, references to past games are essentially relegated to cameos, some which are really easy to miss if you're not paying full attention as it can literally be gone from the screen in an instant. The game basically leaves you blueballed in regards to this, to an insane degree, which simply left me annoyed.Many concepts are alluded to from past games, and new ones in this game as well, but the game never goes far enough to actually commit to anything. I'm sad to say that if you're coming into this after reading Chaos;Head Noah in particular, expecting "you know what"... don't expect much.When I finished the previous Science Adventure games, I felt like I had just experienced something amazing and was awestruck.When I finished Anonymous;Code, I felt confused. The way the game ends is so abrupt that I had to check to make sure I didn't miss a route, or an ending, or SOMETHING.And really, because of that, I simply can't recommend this game.To end this review on a positive note... Rosario's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hot.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not particularly long, but a must play in my opinion. If you like Steins;Gate, then it's definitely a must play. Personally having the hacker concept and the tagline "Hack into God" was enough to get my attention. However, after playing the game, I can safely say that the writers cooked real hard and it is a great addition to the SciAdv series.Why I consider this game to be a must play isn't because of the way they wrote and weaved all the science fiction aspects to such a degree, but because this game may be the last good one in the SciAdv series. Reading this made me feel like I was experiencing Steins;Gate all over again for the first time, and sadly they might not be able to pull it off ever again so I think this game should be enjoyed regardless of it's shortcomings.The trigger system isn't very obvious to when it should be used, and can cause some frustration (especially when used at a wrong time). A tip would be to trigger whenever there's kind of a question asked by the main character, something like a rhetorical question or when he's questioning himself too. But generally most players wouldn't have much issues getting to the end of the game and when stuck, a spoiler free walkthrough would easily help (highly recommended after finishing the game too, since some scenes are very easy to miss).Overall, I didn't have much issues with the trigger system (a few hiccups here and there) and I was pretty immersed and locked-in throughout the game. I bought the game during a sale and I kind of regret it, if you can afford it and love the SciAdv series I think it deserves full price ♥ and since it's a pretty short game (20 hours ish) make sure you finish it!~

_childDocuments_.review: I originally left a positive review when finishing Anonymous;Code, but after having a few months to let it sink in, I have to change it to a negative one. When I finished, I was enthralled by the climatic, action fueled ending. However, I found myself disappointed with the underdeveloped characters and themes. Fast forward to the present and the climax has worn off. Sci;Adv has always been great for its characters and themes, and like I stated, those things are massively underdeveloped. This work did not fit the quality standard entries had set before. You are not paying $60 USD (or whatever price may be equivalent in your country) for a well constructed story but a crappy shonen that just looks nice. This does make me worry for how the series will go forward, but the hopeful part of me wants to blame it on A;C's ridiculously long development time. Hopeful part of me also hopes someday we A;C gets a C;H Noah like rerelease that adds onto the story (character routes and more scenes within common route) as it could salvage the work. But for now, this is just painfully forgettable.If you have any interest in buying this, I assume you are a fan of the Sci;Adv series and will be following future entires. This will likely be required material for understanding of the overarching plot, so you'll have to get to it someday. But with all my complaints, I'd wait as long as you can for a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Anonymous;Code's biggest problem is that it is criminally short. Depending on reading speed, the true ending can be reached in 20-30 hours, and I would only say 30 if you Auto mode the entire VN. It is all gas, very few brakes from the start - if you are not a fan of games in SciAdv due to their slower pace, this actually may be the game for you. I did find being tossed into the thick of things a nice change but as the game continued, I found that this did not allow me to get attached to the cast in any significant way or feel invested in the story.I genuinely liked the entire cast personality wise, however almost all conversation in this game is plot related. Not every VN needs to have a massively long build-up period rivaling Steins;Gate to create an emotional attachment to a cast, but A;C leaves far too little breathing room for me to really care about anyone. If this was intended as a plot-centric VN (as opposed to character centric like the rest of SciAdv), the story would have to have been something that glued my eyes to the screen for all 20 hours in order for me to forgo cast attachment. It was not. The story is solid throughout, never boring or outright bad, but is nowhere near as memorable as Steins or even Chaos;Head/Child.Other aspects of the game- English cast was great, overall HUD is busy yet works wonders in immersing you into the year 2037. Character portraits are thoroughly animated (not CG models), can look a bit uncanny at first, but now I think I prefer it this way. Presentation wise, this is a culmination of the preceding 14 years of SciAdv, raising the bar greatly for these kinds of VNs. OST got some good bass. Steins;Gate is not required reading, but A;C's core science concepts are more easily digestible if you have played/watched Steins.The primary "gameplay" feature of A;C, is best experienced for yourself blind, its damn cool and is unique in its integration to the story when compared to other methods of interactivity in the series. Like the other games, though, the gameplay is more for flair, a topping if you will, and the magic of it was gone by the halfway point.So most of A;C can be considered "decent" to "good", with too few moments of peak, and far too much hacker action movie - for me, at least. I feel this VN has been intentionally made to not "play" like the rest of SciAdv and not follow the same emotional high and lows; there's nothing egregiously wrong with the overall product that make it unreadable, I believe the shortcomings I perceive are a result of design. I'd say to SciAdv fans, alter your expectations, and I'd encourage those who didn't vibe with Steins/ the rest of the series to give this one a shot. Most importantly, if immersing yourself in a character drama driven plot is what you look for in a VN, you're going to be left wanting for more all throughout this far-too-short science adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Can you hack into God? If you are a hacker where is God to hack into? And even if you find God, how do you know what God is? Such concepts are explored in this new chapter in the sci;Adv series from the Mages studio.As a Sci;Adv series A;C it stands true to its core values. It weaves its narrative using a lot of deep scientific concepts intermingled with sci-fi tropes, conspiracy theories and of course conspiracy facts that require a reread (or two) after finishing it to appreciate it in full. And an adventure it certainly is. It has quite a fast pace with little down time and very short time to catch your breath, jumping from part to part seamlessly.A;C is very much an attempt to recreate the magic of S;G. There is a very loose connection with S;G 0 that is finally revealed after the bad ending but not one I was hoping for. In fact, I am quite confused as to what timeline the events take place. Or which world layer? Fate lines anyone? Confused yet? In fact could A;C be the Steins;??? we never got. To avoid confusion this is NOT a time travel story.Some of the mechanics of the game are similar to S;G. Rinse & repeat (saving and loading on this occasion) is used again and again as a means to predict the future and influence the past to progress the present. Occasionally, it becomes tiring because the mechanic is not explicitly explained. But then again fans of the Sci;Adv series will know by now that this is very much the case with all games to date.Where A;C fails to elevate itself to cult status (in my opinion) is character development (or lack thereof). The story is too short (27-30 hours long) to allow for that. Was it budget problems that necessitated an expedited production? We will not know. What we do know is that the reading time is less than half compared to C;H and S;G. And that shows towards the end. Pollon (the MC) is a normal character which is a first for SciAdv. He is like a white knight wishing to help people and aims to save the world. More of a caricature of a shonen manga story than the charismatic Okabe Rintaro or the neurotic Takumi Nishijou. He is part of a gang of hackers. We never learn much about his beliefs, his worries, his secret thoughts; we just get a small glimpse to his past. This could have been explored much more if there was such a will.The heroine (Momo) is also uni-dimensional, which is again a missed chance before of her backstory. This is hardly explored further with only a glimpse of emotional tingles towards the end that nicely wraps around the beginning of the story. Again a similar trope to S;G.The supportive cast is easily forgettable and some irritating (see the Cyber Force Dolls trio and the forced kawai Nanoko). Similarly to the two MCs they do not have a backstory and even what we get is hardly interesting to justify their existence beyond a filler cast.The lack of inner monologues is what distinguishes this VN compared to other SciAdv novels, and in particular C;H, S;G and S;G0. All the cast is mostly talking to each other and we hardly see what they are really thinking of the extraordinaire situations they find themselves in. There is hardly any slice of life content, and that may be a good thing (see R;N). What we needed was double the story time.In fact it is the villains that get more attention this time around and become the more interesting characters that add spice to the main dish.The visuals, presentation and artwork though are exceptional. I liked the manga panels action sequences as it was a refreshing idea. I do not particularly like the MC artwork (Pollon) but this may be a personal taste (green hair anyone?). Many of the characters look and feel alive and in my opinion watching/reading it feels almost like watching a semi-anime. In some cases though artwork remain static though despite major developments in the story.The music delivered by Takeshi ♥♥♥ is divine again and it is easily recognisable as it has all his signature elements. Makes sure you purchase the soundtrack of 52 songs if you purchase the game. It is so worth it ! Despite how many tracks are there though during action sequences the same 2 tracks are used again and again. This became tiring after a while.The plot though is amazing and this is where Chiyomaru and his writing staff shine. In fact it is the most mature, complex and interesting of all Sci;Adv series. There are elements in the story that are part of Internet lore (I realised Cicada 3301 is a real story similarly to John Titor’s story previously), history, religion and conspiracies. Like a great architect Chiyomaru uses all these elements to tell a story that will compel the curious reader to explore further all these elements. It is almost like A;C acts as a pivot for rewarding its readers’ curiosity.If only...if only we knew more about the protagonists this could easily surpass C;H or S;G/ S;G 0. As it was delivered I'd probably give it a 7 (I use my own scale with 7 being. "Really good. Misses elements of excellence. Anyone can still enjoy that"). I believe what may have happened is that the studio had a small budget due to the financial problems it had run into and it really excelled with what it had. I would recommend this VN to anyone who enjoys a good sci-fi story whether they are new or old into the Sci;Adv series. And it would be so easy to produce a spectacular anime based on this source material. The models are already there, the artwork is there. They would not need updating and because of its fast pace it would suit anime fans if the story would not overwhelm them with scientific content. What we would hope is a 24 episode run that incorporate character development and a back story.Whether you wait until the game is discounted (criticism over the short duration and full price was voiced at its release) or you support the studio buying it now at its full price hoping that they will continue churning out amazing stories is down to you, the reader. After all you are God, aren't' you?

_childDocuments_.review: The culmination of the entire Science Adventure Series. Unlike other entries you're thrown right into the thick of it, making it very well-paced.  If you're coming from steins;gate (anime or VN), DO NOT PLAY this until you finish the other mainline games (Chaos;Head Noah, Robotics;Notes, Occultic;Nine anime). This game takes key elements from those stories and uses them in new ways, so having previous knowledge will greatly improve your enjoyment.The ending of this game and the themes it questions you with will make you reflect on not just this game, but all other SciADV games as a whole. And perhaps...your own reality as well. Who's eyes are those eyes?

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much a 'streamlined' version of the SciAdv formula - for better and for worse!The pacing is /much/ quicker than the others, and gets into the action much faster, which was refreshing! But this did come at the expense of side-character development and fun slice of life scenes, which made me a little sad, as that's a big part of what I like about this series.It also makes some of the leaps the plot takes feel a little sudden/contrived, in a way that would probably have been easier to hide if they were drip-feeding info rather than constantly throwing it at you.That aside, there's a lot of good stuff here - very likeable cast, some of the best presentation/style I've seen in a VN, a great translation/dub (finally), almost zero Anime Pervert ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (you did it chiyomaru, only took you 16 years)Probably my least favourite in the series, but I still enjoyed it a lot, and it has me excited for the next game - if Mages can combine the good parts of Anonymous;Code with the slow-burn/character-focused writing of the rest of the series, OOH BABY

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one. I, first of all, think this game is really good and even without the rest of the Sci-Adv series a great stand-alone game. Music is top notch as always (Takeshi ♥♥♥ my love you did awesome). I find it cool that this game even has an english voice over (sticked to the japanese one but I just find it cool lol) and also it's just a very high quality visual novel. There is always something going on on the screen thanks to BMI, the characters move and switch between sprites fluently and the CGs sometimes is also moving. The overall quality is really good! I think however that too little focus was put on the individual characters. One of the things which I enjoyed most about the Sci-Adv are the complex characters as well as their developements, and the only characters who had any developement are the two protagonist as well as . The game is very fast paced which doesn't leave much time for character building scenes and the characters aren't bad, they're just not as developed as they could've been / as good as the characters from previous Sci-Adv games. Like I said the game is fast paced and that is a good thing and a bad thing. In this game you don't get bored because the next cool thing happens immediatly after the previous and the game itself jumps into action right away. Because of its fast pacing it is a bit shorter than previous Sci-Adv games but I wouldn't say it's generally short.Also the main mechanic of this game, the load and saving mechanic, is cool but also could've been much much better. The way it works is like this: In the game you will get an game over if you just keep reading, but you can interfere. When it seems like the right time, you can show Pollon the save and load screen to show him that he should load a previous save data which he created. This will make him jump into the past and literally load the world and he can redo whatever he was doing and avoid a game over. However it isn't always exactly clear when you should load. Oftentimes you can only load when a certain text box is shown on the screen and not before or after that. This will cause you to mash the load button when you think you should load, which is annoying and throws you out of action. My conclusion however is this: This game is great! Like I said, it has its flaws, but that doesn't mean it's a bad game. The entire game, from start to finish, is captivating and because you can interact with Pollon you feel more linked to the world. The entire time you root for Pollon and Momo, try to solve the mysteries which are presented and, because it's the culmination of Sci-Adv, are sure to see recurring things. It's really a good (and also even without a CoZ patch) well translated game and it definitely is worth buying, especially if you're a Sci-Adv fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This wasn't my favorite SciAdv game, but it was pretty good. I was nervous about the English dub, being the first game in the series to get one, but the voice acting was really good and the translation was miles ahead of the previous games. I might be in the minority, but I also appreciate that this was shorter than some of the others in the series, which sometimes have not-so-great pacing and drag on at times.The music and art are phenomenal (Game Over is one of my favorite songs from the series), although in some of the CGs the art style is different enough that it was kind of jarring. I loved the (minor spoiler)  It's a small, simple thing, but I enjoyed it immensely. The story didn't blow me away, but was decent enough. I'm mostly indifferent towards the characters, and some of the ones I felt I wanted to like (especially Bambi) just didn't really get enough attention. If you're a fan of the SciAdv series, you definitely need to give this a go though. The impact and implications this has on the overall story/world of SciAdv is incredible.I would say if you're a fan of Steins;Gate / the SciAdv series as a whole, this is a decent and satisfying addition to the story, though I would definitely recommend getting through all of the previous entries first. If you've never touched the series before, this probably isn't the best place to start, but it's a good game nonetheless. Get it on sale.

All missions support online co-op play for up to four players. Take control of four different soldier classes and fight alongside real EDF members from across the country.

_childDocuments_.review: It's EDF as we know it... a but too literally in my opinion. Not a lot of new stuff, not a lot of new vehicles and weapons, at least not in the first 20 hours i played as Ranger. Except for the new enemy times (who are good at least) haven't seen anything new from EDF5 yet. Even the music and menus are the same as EDF5 as soon as you're finished with the "Prologue"... this is extremely lazy.There are some cool new stuff, like Ranger Backpacks and Air Ranger drones.... but everything that was broken with EDF 5 is still broken here. And every bad design decision, is copy pasted in this "Sequel". Examples: - Bad PC port with no settings- Unusable Free Bikes who just crash you if you hit a pebble (At least it can turn now)- Your camera goes inside the ranger's arse if you decide to sprint-  The Ranger sprint which is so useless, dodge rolling is faster and lets you see in front of you while you do it- Unusable helicopters due to them not having any controls an being too slow to react to anythingAnd not to spoil anything too much, but this game, is too literally, too much like EDF5.Setting as not recommended, as this should have been a 30-40$ game for how little it did to evolve from EDF5. It's still fun, but i already have EDF 5 so buying 6 feels like i just paid for a 80$ expansion pack that adds nothing but new enemies and 3-4 quality of life features.Edit after 20 hours: Yeah this is EDF 5 with some sprinkled new enemies from time to time. No new vehicles, no new weapons, all the stuff that was in the marketing is a facade and you can't even use the new post apocalyptic vehicles. I wish i had access to the same acid EDF fans take to cope because this feels like a scam and should have cost 30$.Edit after 30 hours: Finally saw some truly original and amazing new content! It lasted 2 missions, then back to EDF5. Still no new weapons, vehicles.... never even unlocked the new wasteland variants

_childDocuments_.review: I knew very little about EDF in general, starting off with EDF 5 and learning how it all felt and how the game was played, it didn't take long for me to really get into the game and all of its hectic battles with insane weaponry at your disposal.EDF 6 provided exactly what I wanted. The story was pretty neat overall and unique, but I'm not going to get into details about it due to spoilers. The only main issue is multiplayer. The fact that it uses EPIC servers for multiplayer was the WORST idea ever! Can't tell you how many times D-sync happens when I'm playing this online with friends, seeing them shooting either at a wall or the floor, but they're targeting enemies straight in front of us. It causes friendly fire pretty often as well and when you're playing through it on Inferno, there's nothing worse than killing a teammate who isn't anywhere in your line of sight, but on their screen, you're aiming right at them.I still recommend the game, of course. It's a ton of fun with friends if you want some wild action shooter to play and plenty of missions to go through as well as weapons to unlock and level up. If you can deal with the D-sync that is the EPIC multiplayer servers they use, I'm sure you'll be fine and will have plenty of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The Haruhi Season 2 of EDF. Ultimately this feels like too little too late with some decisions that soured the first impressions. If you're familiar with the overhaul mods for Dark Souls 3 and similar, this feels like a more professional version of that. Its too much retreaded ground to really feel like a sequel. Certainly not in the way the transition from 4 to 5 was. Story wise this is a sequel, but the whole thing feels like an accessory to 5. After 5 years, 60$ price tag, and a whole lot of recycling it just feels kinda weak. Then throw in EOS drama which I'm assuming is the culprit for all the desync online. Its a fun game, there is a lot of content, but its in an awkward spot where I can't really recommend you jump in on this one if you haven't played the others since you'll be missing a lot of the gimmick with the whole time loop thing. But if you've played 5 its a little too much recycle. As far as gameplay changes go, its a mixed bag. I think the backpack slot for ranger makes total sense and should have been there since the start. 2 weapons and a grenade/utility slot just makes sense. Wingdiver..... its good on paper, how they balanced it in practice though is a mess. The weapons from 5 that have been moved to the backpack slot feel kinda weak/ very situational. And the new ones like the spear and saber are so ridiculously overpowered that it honestly feels like a waste of time using your regular weapons most of the time. Wingdivers main gimmick since 4 has been high risk high damage suicide bomber type of gameplay where they put themselves in a precarious situation to take out a transport ship or spawner, needing to manage energy to be able to fly away after doing the hit; all with super low health. Well now, with the spear that is on a short CD and doesn't cost energy, wingdiver can takeout multiple high value targets with basically no risk or energy management. Airraider: this one is controversial, I ended up putting the most playtime into AR with edf5, and really enjoyed how flexible the class was. Much of AR's core identity is taxed and stripped away in 6 in favor of the new drones. These were fun at first but I eventually came around to not liking them. They succeed in making AR much more lethal at close range and personal protection but it honestly just feels spammy and non committal which is not at all what I enjoy about AR from 5. The drones will come off CD as soon as they return, so if you are sending them to targets only 20m away they come off CD instantly just about and you basically are just spamming whatever is available on your weapon deck. Airstrikes and vehicle calldowns have had their cost significantly increased to the point that you will struggle to get a single vehicle called in and maybe one more by the end of the last wave of a mission. The biggest thing for me though, is all the support equipment is now in the backpack slot which seems like a good thing until you realize you can no longer play support raider with multiple pylons and turrets. Turrets have been taken away and given to ranger now. So yes, no more super depth crawlers yoked out with a power post. defense post, and flamer turrets attached to it. No more power post and bunker for aerial enemy missions. It sucksFencer I haven't played yet but it seems like they made out pretty good this time. Weapon balancing in general continues to be bad, many weapons are straight up unusable. Homing weapons still have wayyy too much of a tax put on their damage/energy draw, the plasma cannons for wingdiver are a joke there are basically only 3 good ones in the list due to damage/energy ratio. The missions have some of the same issues that 5 did where it doesn't feel like there is much of a momentum or leading up to something. Enemies will be introduced then not really be followed up in a meaningful way for a long time after. The game is strained between edf5 enemies and the new ones in 6, the whole timeloop remix thing isn't done as well as it could have been. Some missions are literally a copy of 5, overall the mission list is bloated and overlong. Especially since you need to beat the game to access hardest/inferno difficulties. The new enemies are pretty fun, they are largely well done remixes of existing edf5 enemies. I did find myself starting to long for killing just basic bugs again, the androids just don't quite feel as enjoyable for some reason. Though I do like watching the fast androids swing around the buildings. On a technical level, these games are really starting to strain the asking price. There are some graphical improvements over 5 but they are very minor and the novelty of many enemies on screen can only go so far especially when we are all rocking better hardware by 2024. Muddy textures, bad lighting, no FOV slider, no uncapped framerate. Its just a bit unacceptable this day and age for a full retail asking price plus DLC. Also at the time of writing it is still a pain to get a full inferno lobby going. A mix of low playerbase, low playerbase at high levels perhaps, and a schism between those who want to use autoloot cheat mods and those that don't. So all in all I found myself losing momentum with it, it was a bit long in the tooth to finish the game and the aforementioned issues compounded with problems trying to get inferno groups going and my desire to play is kind of grinding to a halt. I'll definitely not reach the playtime I have in edf5. So I'm still giving this a recommended, but I would grab it on a sale. If you're a first time player I would say probably get 5 first. Its hard to fully recommend this to first time players or players of previous games, its an odd one.

_childDocuments_.review: Whether or not someone wants to make an Epic Games Store account, it's absolutely unacceptable for a company to lie about this hard requirement until 6 hours *after* release. That's bad enough, but SANDLOT / D3PUBLISHER are still obscuring the truth here. At time of writing the store page states "Requires 3rd-Party Account: Epic Online Services (required for online play)" which isn't the whole picture. If you have the installation of EpicOnlineServices blocked or have it disabled under Windows services, the game will not even launch (Giving an error asking you to verify game integrity). You have about 20 or fewer truly new levels, and honestly everything is copy and pasted.The changes, especially to the Air Raider with drones, are really awesome - I wish the drones could lock on like missiles if you held down the attack button, and only shot a target beacon with a tap, but that's just me.The story is confusing at first, but two things to know:1.  There is a time loop caused by the invaders which is actually not bad writing.  The loop is used to explain ALL games in the EDF series and why each are slightly different from each other, how the Primer (main enemy) is able to seemingly predict the moves by the EDF and conjure counter technology seemingly almost instantly without apparent manufacturing time, etc.2.  Once you complete Mission 137 you will get annoying popups that really don't tell you what to do.  I thought it was an error at first.  You must go BACK through all your completed missions and find 6 new missions that have "???" instead of a mission number.  Complete those and you can go to Mission 138 (which is actually more like Mission 144).That being said, there are like 3 maps used for the dreary future, you keep going to it over and over, and after each "final fight" with the Ring (the time ship) which resets the loop you get to play a few EDF 5 missions.There are a few new missions once you fix the time loop after making things go in the humans' favor, as well.Most weapons now have quicker reloads and larger magazines, and you will need it - there is a Mother monsters on level 3, and one level that has like 20 Erginus, 10 Archelus, and 3 single-headed Ghidorah knockoffs (I will let you see for yourself).  No joke - bring vehicles!And remember the EDF 5 early mission where you escape the base and like 30 pylons hit the ground, and the mission ends?  Not this time - you get to fight them all AND THE SUMMONS.It's doable in single player, but you will likely run into times where you have to grind specific levels for certain equipment to survive.  And of course armor.And now... screw Epic, and screw lying trash companies that participate in underhanded tactics.  EDF 6 isn't even ON the Epic Store, so it is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that Epicwarez were included in this game for crossplay purposes.  You still can't connect to people on Playstations (thaaanks, Sony), and the bottom line is that Epic most likely paid D3 (now owned by Bandai Namco) under the table to stealth-install their scraping software to get Steam users.  AGAIN!And D3/Bandai Namco sold their souls.THAT is why people are pissed - there was ONE announcement that Epicwarez would be on EDF6, ON THE EPIC STORE DEV BLOG.  Nothing, NOTHING on D3's page, Sandlot's page, or the Steam page UNTIL HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON JUNE 25TH.It was PURPOSEFULLY hidden, and there is NOT ONE SINGLE GOOD REASON for Epicwarez to be installed with this.Moreover the gameplay is now unstable even in singleplayer, and co-op is simply not permitted unless you have an Epic account.  Did I mention that crossplay actually doesn't need an Epic account to function?  You can switch it off when you make a game IF you truly are using Epicwarez to enable Crossplay.Which D3/Bandai Namco/Sandlot has made PAINFULLY clear that THEY ARE NOT AND IT IS ALL LYING ON THEIR PART.For further reading, look up Helldivers 2...And full disclosure - I haven't refunded the game, YET, but only because of their comment that Epic would be removed.  It damn well better be, or they can kiss my friends and siblings' money goodbye as I have told them to wait on purchasing.We can always go back to EDF 5!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it a 6.5/10.   But if this is your very first EDF game? It could be an 8.5-9/10.The game leaves me not entirely satisfied, but also, not entirely disappointed.  No, that doesn't make things even-steven.First thing that left a stink in the air around the game is that sneaky and dishonest move with Epic - everyone knows what I'm talking about, so I won't say more.Now for the rest of the game. I played 4.1, 5 and Iron Rain.My favorite experience was 4.1 BUT I lost my EDF virginity to that one, so I suspect its a nostalgia-biased thing.With my experience playing all these games, I would compare EDF 6 with 5.  Takes a lot of the missions! And also most of its enemies. Speaking of which,  a lot of the   enemy designs are, unfortunately, silly looking.  Not cool, or self-aware cheese like some 40-50s space adventure movie.  Just plain dumb.   I'll sound very shallow here, but the new enemy designs make it hard to play the game. So damn goofy.  I seriously miss the Hectors <3 And then mob-masses.  They really toned down the ant swarms besides a select few missions... I'm not sure about the weapon list.  So many weapons.  So many crappy weapons.  So many crappy weapons that you already had in previous EDF games.  You'll find your few favorites (that you used for EDF 4.1/5) and use them for the entirety of the game; with the exception of a couple for mission-specific needs. They have tons of info-background for each weapon, but you still don't know exactly what it does, how it works, or how it looks (the blast-effect).  A pop up, looping clip, of the gun being used would be helpful! (A training room where you can easily access and swap all your available weapons would be even better! )....And then once you find the specific gun you like, you sorta want to level it up!  But that's in the hands of random rolls. Which brings me to this..!  Imagine having a point system where you   your upgrade, per-weapon.   Again, allowing for different builds:    You could even redistribute these points whenever you want.  Sorry, I'm just day-dreaming at this point. Maybe I was spoiled with other games, maybe it was just Iron Rain - but over a decade of the franchise and we can still only change our armor/uniform colors?    Come on, maaan!  Do better.  Even changing my GUN color would be fun. Ok, here's my idea: Give out reward points with missions that allow you to shop around and buy unique goodies.Another day-dreaming idea? To have an actual "physical" lobby, where you could visit weapon shops, armor shops and cosmetic shops, etc.  Give a face to the random voices we hear over our coms.  Could help us maybe care a little for the soldiers we fight with, and human race we fight for, or something.  We appreciated, and miss, Maeve! it has it's jankiness; might be part of its charm, honestly.  But I would love it if the radar would have a North indicator - strategizing with your party would be a lot easier.. Your radar map gives you an idea of where things are, but only more specifically if you're near the subject.  But , my party members, I would  to know their distance! having a "Player 2 -  1450m" would be   Then I know I'm safe to use my mega blasty pewpews.  Or if I'm KO'ed, My team mates can quickly chose who will run over to revive me - dude that's 50m away, or 500m away - hmmmmm!   Other option would be to simply have them identified as "Low-Medium-Long"  of that makes things easier? Sorry, sorry, day-dreaming again.For the story, more of the same, but with a bit of a twist - an annoying one. Time travel. You will  your Air-Raider on these "going to the past" mission.  I feel your pain.The thick cheesiness of the story, the randos lines are sometimes chef's kiss - so horrible they are!  Not so great when the random soldiers run across your very explosive shot-RIP.  I miss the EDF chant from 4.1 It was the best.... My true feeling?  6 years passed and they gave us a very   polished copy/paste of EDF 5.

_childDocuments_.review: First of the epic requirement has been removed.The game is fun and insane as always with it's B movie story and voice acting. Some missions are repeated but because of story reasons have a twist with ambushes or different enemies.There is also a few new enemies that also have variants, a new end boss and new gear. First of every class except fencer has a new backpack equipment slot. This let's the air raider  have a guard drone, the usual bunker or life vendors without sacrificing a weapon slot. The ranger now has the turrets of the air raider or grenades in that slot and some of the wing divers more situational weapons have been moved here. This allows you to take more niche things that previously were not good enough for a weapon slot. Also they get a new saber weapon in that slot that is excellent to cover when you are in emergency mode as they recharge separate to the other things.THe Air raider had the most changes overall as he now also has drone version of his airstrikes that aren't as powerfull but can be used alot more often and are avaibable even when the air strikes aren't avaiable (underground and another mission type I won't spoil). They are a bit underwhelming as most people playing Air raider play it for the big booms they can dish out but for me they were a lot of fun and allow air raider to be more usefull for caves.Overall there were some QoL changes like online and offline mode being synced for gear and missions. No need to grind both modes.So in the end it isn't anything that revolutionary but fans of the series will feel right at home with some nice changes and new missions and enemies. The epic stuff was unfortunate and probably more done out of ignorance from the devs than any malicious intent. So if you want a fun game with lots of missions and lot's of op weapons that can be played with 4 players give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: The good : I'm a fan of edf and so far am having a lot of fun inside it. The changes to the classes feel like nice tweaks and a slight improvement over 5. The story is time travel based and there are a lot of levels to get through (more then edf5) but this also means returning to older edf 5 maps with a twist which gives of nostalgia vibes but keeps stuff fresh. The new enemies are fun and spice stuff up.The game looks a bit better then 5, explosions are lovely as ever and less laggy and the buildings crumble in a nice way. So far story and voice acting wise, on par with the rest of the series, like a cheesy sci-fi audio drama one is a part off when playing. The other nice change is that progress in the campaign is no longer seperated between offline and online, but shared.The bad stuff :- epic store launcher needed and whenever a achievement triggers on epic one loses control, quickly alt-tab from and back to the game to regain control.- if the lobby player crashes and the mouse does not wish to show itself, alt-tab, select the x on the game, then the mouse shows itself again.- When an air raider summons a vehicle the whole game gets a hickup for all in multiplayer (even the enemies, whole game freezes for a second then continues)So far am enjoying it, shame they had to add that epic launcher required as that soured quite a few people on the game. If on the fence about it wait for a bit for a price off, it is good fun both solo and with friends.Regarding the dlc : edf always had dlc, all dlc except for the mission packs (that still need to come out) are just cosmetic and can be disregarded, even low level they do not help out as one quickly levels away from the dlc items and as such they are there if you want to give the company a bit more cash. The bonus mission packs always add more challenging levels with a few more weapons and are for those die-hards that are not content enough with the original missions on hardest or inferno level.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve been along for the ride with the previous games in this series, buckle up—because this one’s like an all-you-can-eat buffet of everything you’ve seen before, but with extra toppings. It’s got the same delicious flavor, just more of it, so don’t expect any radical changes to the recipe.The enemy variety in this game is like a monster mash party where everyone’s invited. There are so many different types of baddies that it’s impossible to get bored. It’s like they took a zoo, mixed it with a nightmare, and threw it all at you. Every time you think you’ve seen it all, the game slaps you with something new, like it’s saying, “Oh, you thought you were safe? Guess again!”Speaking of slapping things around, the weapon variety here is massive. You’ve got everything from peashooters to god-tier cannons. But, let’s be real, some of these weapons are about as useful as a chocolate teapot. Sure, it’s fun to mess around with them, but when the going gets tough, you’ll be ditching those underpowered duds faster than you can say, “Why is this even in the game?”Now, let’s talk about the vehicles. Remember how cool the AirDiver and Ranger used to be? Well, now they feel like they’ve been through the spin cycle one too many times. They’ve been nerfed so hard that their main purpose seems to be playing the role of a glorified punching bag. Need something tanky to soak up some hits? Great, hop in. Need to actually get stuff done? Better start running because these bad boys are about as useful as a bicycle in a swimming pool.Multiplayer is where things get... interesting. Picture this: you’re lining up a perfect shot on an enemy 500 meters away, feeling like a tactical genius. Suddenly, your brother, who was standing next to you a second ago, gets blown to bits. Turns out, on his screen, he was 500 meters away, right in the blast zone. Who knew teleportation was a thing? Apparently, Epic Online Services did, because the synchronization here is about as accurate as a broken compass. It’s like playing a game of Marco Polo where everyone’s blindfolded and in different pools.As for the story, there’s a twist that I’m not going to spoil, but let’s just say it’s like the cherry on top of this chaotic sundae. It adds a nice layer of depth, or at least a moment where you go, “Wait, what just happened?”In the end, I still recommend the game, mostly because I like to watch things explode. It’s playable in multiplayer, even if the synchronization sometimes turns it into a comedy of errors. And yeah, it’s a bit pricey, but if you’re into this kind of madness, you’ll definitely get your money’s worth. Just don’t expect perfection, and maybe keep a spare controller handy for when things get really out of sync.
