_childDocuments_.review: Having finished this game, playing every mission with friends, this game is not worth it and it's entirely down to the poor quality of the netcode. This game is pretty much identical to EDF 5 with a lot of quality of life improvements, and if it ended there it'd be a clear improvement in most ways that matter. The dialogue and story is bad, the levels are often less interesting, and the mission selection is extremely recycled, but none of that matters much in an EDF game. Enemy variety is good, actually, there's a lot going on and it changes things up constantly through the game, and the weapons themselves are also better in a lot of ways, most things actually felt worth trying, but none of the good outweighs the single bad aspect.The Epic online system makes the whole game fall apart and it's not the login requirement that a lot of reviews mention. The netcode and syncing between players may as well not exist, it takes seconds to get desynced from other players in a mission, and since it was perfect in previous games and terrible here it looks like it's entirely down to Epic being tied in. Your character model and ragdolls will never be where they should be compared to other players, you'll see other players teleport across the map, run into walls, or shoot in random directions, so there's zero feeling of the people you play with actually having any impact or even being present a lot of the time, and prepare to get shot by teammates who just can't see you directly in front of them.The entire reason I find EDF fun is because it's a silly game to play with friends, so if you can't reliably see your friends doing things, show off stuff to them, or even see the same things in the same place as them, enemies and loot crates included, you may as well be playing alone or with total strangers half the time.Other super popular big games use the Epic online service without any trouble so I don't know why it's so bad in this game, but with a game where the only real way to play is with other people it's an unambiguous recommendation to avoid regardless of any other improvements made.Also it's a long one. _childDocuments_.review: Allow me to start off; there are some rough patches in this game. It's by no means the Magna Carta of games, but that doesn't detract from the fact that it's a tried and true formula; made even better with this release. Desync issues on indoor levels are present, there's some unreasonable difficulty spikes, and some weapons/tools just don't click right. However, moving past those nitpicked gripes, I've never had more fun in an EDF title.I see a lot of clowns rushing to review-bomb the game over the almost non-existent Epic Games integration. I see even more clowns rushing to complain about every single tweak made to the individual classes. The bottom-line is; the class-changes are barely noticeable, and with the insane gear you get not even mid-way through the game, the classes feel even better than they did in previous titles.I myself have always been a Fencer main through 4.1, 5, and now 6. The only significant change from 5 is the *slightest* reduction in boost/jump speed and distance. As an offset to this though; without any slots; the fencer can now do two consecutive movements. Pair this with the boost/jump upgrades, the Fencer can literally fly further than ever before. Gatling guns, cannons, the whole lot; are just miles more engaging and satisfying to use.I can't speak heavily about other classes, but my friend; an air-raider main, has had similar results. Minor nerfs paired with greatly increased power in other aspects. I'm disappointed to see just how many negative reviews are flooding this game. These devs have launched another fantastic game, hindered by a wave of Redditor-Troglodytes with ill-intent. There's a reason the Japanese are weary about western-audiences, and this game is a great example of it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDF: Extraordinarily Dysfunctional Fiasco!!!Wow, just wow. EDF has really outdone itself this time. The game, in its current state, is like... a trash bin with rotting fish sitting at the bottom for over 3 weeks in 115°F weather! As someone who has played every single EDF game, I can confidently say this one is in spectacularly bad shape at launch.Let's address the elephant in the room, the Epic Game Multiplayer requirement... this wasn't in other EDF titles but for some reason, it is now. To also add, this requirement wasn't listed on the product page when purchased but after 6 hours of the game being released... it magically appeared. Okay, let's dive in to the other issues....First off, the tutorial. I hope you enjoy slow, unskippable dialogue because that's what you'll get. Want to understand the controls? Too bad! There's no real control menu and if you find it, it's not neatly laid out. Everything is everywhere, much like the developers’ sense of direction when making this game's menu and options.Graphical options? Forget about it. You can’t change them in-game, and the options outside the game are abysmal. Ultra-wide support? Missing, of course. But don’t worry, they added a letterbox option so you can enjoy those lovely black bars on the left and right. Want to fix the scaling issue? Just un-toggle it and stretch the resolution of your monitor. Brilliant, right?Oh, and here’s the best part: A GAMER "not the dev" on the discussion board used a hex editor to add proper ultra-wide support. Imagine that! A random player fixed what the developers couldn’t be bothered to. Now it runs perfectly, which is hilarious and depressing all at once. It really look someone not paid by the game to fix that in a matter of minutes.Oh... 60fps... locked! I'll let you think of a random rant in your head...In summary, if you’re a masochist who enjoys subpar gaming experiences, this is the game for you. Otherwise, steer clear unless you want to feel like you’re sifting through a garbage bin on a scorching summer day. Or, until they can clean up the mess.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: 10/3/24So I know a lot of people have changed their opinion on the game given the new patch removed the Epic Games requirement (not really an issue for me, I thought)... Oddly enough I'm going to go ahead and change mine to a thumbs up to because while it isn't in any patch notes I've read, the game hasn't crashed on me once since this latest update. I don't know if this was related to the Epic situation or not, but at this point, I think I can give it the ol' "cautious thumbs up". I stand by a few of my minor gripes, but they ARE minor, and the game is just generally pretty fun, if you like the formula. Old review preserved, since most of this didn't change:I really want to be able to give this game a good review (and to be clear this is a JUST BARELY can't recommend for temporary issues), because it's got a really interesting story that kind of explains the entire EDF series in a really clever way. There's also some kinda nice little improvements to loadouts, in that there's now a separate slot on most loadouts for a one-button grenade, beam saber, ZE-GUN, etc. Also, the gameplay is pretty fun, if largely unchanged from prior iterations...While most people are complaining about the Epic sign in issue (one which, to be clear, I can understand both sides on), my biggest issue is that the game has serious stability issues, often CTD-ing once an hour or so. Usually this happens at the end of a mission, and as EDF is kinda known for lack of checkpointing or save progress within missions, if this happens you're SoL. Add to that some real performance issues with load time, texture pop-in, and some really odd design choices (like a tutorial mission you'll have to replay multiple times throughout the game), and it feels like a bit of a step back for the series. If EDF is traditionally a "Solid 7 out of 10" game, this one sadly feels closer to a 5.5/10 as released. Honestly it feels like an "Insect Armageddon" or "Iron Rain" game, not an EDF proper title.To be clear, it's still a pretty fun game, when it works. There isn't anything revolutionary here, but if you liked 4.1 and 5, it's more of the same. Also worth note is that this game should really be called EDF 5.5, as it pretty much requires you to have played EDF 5 to make sense of the story (even if you do have to get 30-50 missions in before it really makes sense). I'll likely re-visit this if they manage to fix some of the performance/stability issues, but for now it's frustrating enough to warrant a "stay away" warning to newcomers. Anyone really into the series is probably going to disregard this anyway, and they'll find it a mildly frustrating, somewhat disappointing return of a nonetheless well loved friend, and though I WISH they'd taken the extra time to fix it up before release, it's still an OK game (just not for most people).

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:- without posting spoilers, I can confidently say this is hands down the best EDF story I've seen.- more missions than the last game, meaning there're more scenarios for you to test your loadouts.- new enemy types this time around not only looked cooler, but also behaves a lot smarter too.- NPC allies in general have become more useful.- most classes (keyword here being 'most') got many Quality of life changes. You'll quickly find yourself right at home with most of the classes you main, along with the new weapons that were introduced, as well making some of the weapons that are previous unplayable in 5 much more enjoyable.  I'll get to this later.CONS:- lemme just get the most obvious out of the way: Desync will plague your online experience. you can get revived when your teammate is across the map, and ppl can friendly fire each other even when you're like 50 feet apart of each other. In other words, this problem forces you into accepting that ally positioning simply don't matter in this game.- The year is 2024, and this game somehow regressed into giving pointless cutscene missions where you just stand there and listen to NPCs talk, completely breaking the pacing of the game and downgrading the quality of mission flow compared to 5. It wouldn't have been so bad if you're not also being forced to walk around at the speed of NPC & not being able to shoot things.- The new universal feature, vault, where your character can jump onto/over things if you're just barely touching the edge on paper should be a welcoming addition. In practice, it only benefits Ranger & Air Raider. Vaulting is detrimental to Wing Divers due to the fact you spend on average the same amount as you would with a dash. Yes, you need to spend your precious energy on this mediocre move with slow animation. Oh, and as WD you also can't vault if you're charging your weapon.Vaulting is also detrimental to Fencer for the sole reason that you lose all momentum if you do this, mainly from the signature dash-boost. AIR RAIDER:I'm making a separate section on this topic just from the sheer oversight & nerfs this class got; it's almost like Air Raider as a class got put on an sacrificial altar for the improvements of other classes. Where do I even start- Nothing is more ironic to describe a class that strongly "assist allies" than making the decision to limit his supporting tools to only his singular backpack tool. In EDF5, you have the full liberty of being a buff-slut by using all 3 of your main weapon slots of heal/defense/offense zones or guns. Add to the fact you can also go full brick-slut by taking all 3 weapons slots for total bunker-down, and it's not hard to see why AR got shafted so hard.- Air Raider's airstrikes, gunship attacks, and vehicles/mechs has nearly tripled in cost. Unless RNG blesses you with maxed upgrades, you will find yourself struggling to use them effectively. - Air Raider lost access to the stationary turrets. Yes, in this game, one of AR's iconic weapon series, and also one of the strongest tools for defense & offense, has now been completely deleted and handed over to Ranger in favour of the new series called drones.- While the drones themselves have generally good stats for you to work with, they all unfortunately lack severely in the Quality of LIfe department. For starters, your mini "airstrike" drone runs doesn't let you pinpoint the location you want to like airstrikes. If you want to aim further, you'd need actively turn your camera to look up and then fire. Then you've got problems of drones having collision hitbox themselves, which often makes them stuck in buildings, sometimes forcing you to wait half a match just to be able to use it again. Even in cave missions, where drones are supposed to shine the brightest, can still end up getting stuck and unable to fire in the proper direction you want them to.- The sheer amount of anti-Air Raider design in this game is simply boggling. Ranging from missions in devastation timeline where you straight up can only use drones because of "story reasons" is a huge spit in the face for AR mains. Then there're the new enemy types like shielded anchors that covers their entire top, to fully armoured foes that only reveal their weakness at the front in certain times, and you'll see why AR struggles so much at getting thru missions.(Yes, I am aware you can cheese the shock drone and hit anchors thru the shield.) (No, that does not make AR any more fun to use.)All in all, this game still took a step in the right direction, but with such blaring & questionable choices, EDF6 has left me with quite the bitter-sweet feeling.

You have been warned.Over 140 missions makes it hard to pick out the few that are legitimately bad and take that with the typical level of wing diver salt not because the missions are actually bad but that the WD's kit doesn't have the best answers to the enemies in mission. As it stands all characters have some mission or another that they absolutely cannot do without help (or significant grinding, more on this later) and some missions in which they excel so strongly that any other character seems underwhelming because you just soloed the mission with no damage and a 0 level set of weapons.Bullet points:Graphics. Boost pylons still exist, but you can only bring one type, as they're now in the backpack slot.On the other hand, Air Raider has now received drone type weapons, which function as miniature versions of his calldowns. these make him much more survivable, should enemies get close. _childDocuments_.review: Thrilling and bombastic action that could have been even better with some editing.So the core of Earth Defence Force remains as absorbing as it has since Global Defence Force, the second game on the series that laid down the template. You face off increasingly interesting enemy designs in massive cityscapes, with your strategic options slowly increasing as the game unfolds. There are over a thousand unique weapons spread across four classes, and the enemy and crowd placement means you're often incentivised to make the most of what you have, especially in co-op where the balancing is fine tuned to near perfection for a group of players going through anew.How EDF6 advances things is in one significant fundamental: The physics. The implementation of Havok is the best it's ever been in the series. Character movement feels more nuanced, building destruction is more robust, enabling new strategic options. The improved physics pave way to some incredible new enemy designs. There are a whole family of Androids that exhibit what looks like procedural animation as they walk around the rubble, and blasting these metal foes to bits is never less than fun. Each new class of android ups the ante in unexpected ways. The grenadiers blow themselves up, causing chain reactions, while my favorite are the diamond-shaped ones which swing around urban environments - it's like taking on Spider-Man, except there are hundreds of them on screen at once. Utter madness! The kruul - these multi-legged monsters who brandish guns and shields - also benefit from the more nuanced physics.Taking on missions is as fun as ever, then, and when the game is at its very best it feels peerless. Yet EDF6's campaign is probably the most rocky the series has seen. The game sends you through multiple time loops, which on paper is a great way to reuse levels with a twist. But upping the mission count from 110 to 150 has clearly had tradeoffs - it certainly feels like there are a greater proportion of uneventful missions here, and the flow of the game is certainly different...but not necessarily better. Where in previous games the action would continue to ramp up until proceedings reach a beautiful crescendo, EDF6 is a lot more rocky, with excitement being momentarily taken away from you as you'll continually follow up a banger of a level with a few mindless ones. It also doesn't help that many levels are lifted from EDFs 4 and 5, either.I'll let other reviews address the technical side of things since there's nothing I can add there that hasn't already been brought up. So in short, the core of the game remains fantastic, and the best its ever been, but the campaign is certainly inconsistent to say the least, and it lets things down to a degree. Sandlot could have knocked it out the park with some much needed editing.

_childDocuments_.review: Base Game Review: The game is essentially 5 but with more content and gameplay variety.  To truly enjoy the game you have to forget about the campaign and simply focus on your characters armor and weapon progression.  At 70 percent completion the armor and weapon limit is removed which makes endgame content easier to do.  So far I have played every character, but have mostly focused on Ranger and Wingdiver.  The easiest way to get to 70 percent is to realize that if you complete a campaign at a specific level it gives you 5 percent completion.  If you play the campaign through on Hard on one character it clears Easy and Normal, which sets you at 15 percent completion.  So the quickest and easiest way to get to 70 percent is to complete the game 4 times on Hard with each character which puts you at 60 percent.  Then you can choose your two favorite classes and beat each of them on Hardest or beat one Hardest and Inferno on the same class.The way that I look at the game is that its sort of like a minimalist action RPG.  The missions are basically dungeons and the boxes you pick up during the match are loot.  Bosses and higher tier enemies drop more loot.  Once you have enough of your weapons upgraded and a significant amount of armor you can essentially outlevel low level content and move onto the next difficulty tier.When you look at the game like this it seems a bit more interesting than simply killing bugs over and over again.   Each character class functions completely differently and is akin to a class in an MMORPG.For example, Wing Diver is essentially a Mage.  High damage but very low armor rating.  Her abilities function very similar to magic, with powerful energy beams.  She is able to conjure up various methods to evade danger and shield herself.Air Raider is akin to a Warlock, capable of summoning massive elemental damage like fire and explosives as well as various vehicles that simply poof out of nowhere.  A lot of his abilities revolve around drones that he can order to attack targets, much like a summoner's pet.  They are also capable of dropping pillars that heal other players, much like a healing totem.Fencer is the tank warrior class.  Capable of doing a lot of damage and can use a shield, able to hold their own in close quarters combat and use various kinds of swords and hammers.  A skilled Fencer can tank and hold aggro on enemies while the other classes scope out the situation and deliver ranged damage.Ranger is more agile than the Air Raider and not as tough as the Fencer.  Their weapons are more conventional and their combat style is similar to the Fencer but they are not as good at tanking as they lack a lot of defensive abilities.  They can however use various weapons and tools that can heal themselves or other players, which makes them function a bit as a Paladin, able to hold their own in combat but also able to support the team with healing.When I started seeing the game like this and turned off most of the sound effects, the game is fun to just grind while watching a movie on a second monitor.  Intense gameplay but relaxed enough to play casually.  The real enjoyment I get out of the game is seeing my character get stronger.  Its a bit like Dragon Ball Z or something, seeing my characters power level increase and using their skills and abilities to help carry low level players.  Its a rewarding experience when you keep your team alive and know that they couldn't have won without you.  The teamwork and skill to beat some of the endgame content is pretty intense.  For instance, despite the game seeming like a nonstop fragfest where you simply aim and shoot hundreds of bugs, on higher difficulties MMO strategies such as kiting and pulling specific enemies becomes paramount.  Resurrecting dead players is also incredibly important.  You cannot simply rush in and expect to aggro everything in sight immediately like Leroy Jenkins and expect to survive.  Every class truly provides a different gameplay style and has an important role on the team.Definitely worth the buy, despite the aging graphics engine and the excessive price.  The gameplay loop is addicting and as of writing there are a ton of people playing so it is easy to fill a match, so long as you are playing on Hard, Hardest or Inferno.Also, I highly recommend picking up the Lootmaster mod from Nexus.  I was initially against the idea but after beating the game multiple times, I felt like I earned the right to add it.  Its a very simple installation.  Just drag and drop into the base directory.  Even if you want to play completely legit you are still going to be forced to use autoloot when randoms join who generally never ask if you want it enabled.  If they are using a trainer they can turn it on and off but its a bit cumbersome compared to Lootmaster.  You don't realize how much time, effort and stress is removed when you add autoloot.  Its almost impossible to beat end level content when everyone is trying to pick up armor crates.  So autoloot provides a huge advantage in several ways.  Mission Pack 1 Review:I didn't have high expectations for this DLC.  I assumed it would just be more of the same, just empty shooting galleries with the same enemies and no story.  But to my surprise the game actually fills in some details in the story and has a proper ending.  It comes with 19 missions but the first and last missions are basically filler.  If you have already played a significant amount of the base game the unlocks for Hard mode aren't that great.  But if you beat the game on Hardest or Inferno the rewards are actually really good, especially if you have the armor and weapon cap unlocked from having 70 percent progress in the base game.  This DLC has its own completion progress so in order to unlock the cap you need to beat the game a minimum of 6 times (hard, hard, hard, hard, hardest, hardest).  The enemy variety in this is actually really interesting and it requires a lot of skill and proper timing to complete some of the arenas.  If one of your teammates fall, you are almost guaranteed to fail the mission but sometimes highly skilled players can prevent a wipe at the last second.  The most interesting addition are the giant pillbugs but the machine gun bees and taser spiders are pretty neat too.  I wish they would branch out to other insects but this developer doesn't like to innovate, essentially releasing the same game over over.  But miraculously the game is incredibly fun and is one of the best games I have played in years.  I have already sunk a ton of hours into this and plan to 100 percent the base game and both Mission Packs.Additional DLC Review:I can't give this content a proper review because all sources point to the fact that its a total waste of money.  From what I can tell they are low level luxury items that would be phased out by higher level gear within a few missions.  This is content that should have just been in the game or cut entirely.  Or at least put together into one package that made sense.  Would have been nice to get it included with the pre-order package but this company loves to nickle and dime the community to death.  So it is best to avoid the random DLC garbage and stick with the base game and Mission Pack 1 and 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-More bugs and clankas to shoot-A lot of weapons to utilize-Intern acquiredCons:-The English translations (some of the chat prompts especially) seem to not be done properly or are unfinished. Noticed it when I tried to start singing and the lines didn't actually match up. It's not a huge deal, but it bugs me (pun not intended)-The tutorial is way too long and the first few missions aren't all that special. Upon coming to this realization you will realize that you spent almost 3+ hours on what are essentially tutorial levels and now you can't get a refund as you've exceeded Steam's 2 hour refund window.-Constant crashing that some believe is tied to AMD cards, but there does not seem to be any real link to that as the game still crashes with Nvidia and Intel cards as well. Seems crashing is more or less random if anything.Fixes for Some Crashes:-For whatever reason there is a crash associated with Epic Online Services, it's a pretty simple fix: This PC>Program(x86)>Epic Games> Epic Online Services>managedArtifacts>98bsomethingsomething> Rename "EOSOverlayRenderer-Win64" to something else such as "frick you EOS"-For crashes that may be associated with AMD chipsets and some Nvidia cards you will need to install dxvk gplasync and its config files which can be found on EDF's official discord server in a pinned message. You will need to use an application such as WinRar to properly extract the 64 bit version of the files. Be sure to run the game in windowed mode with anti-aliasing off and any other graphics settings to the bare minimum and then exit the game to save those settings. Those files can then simply be dragged and dropped into the game's installation folder (where the executable itself is located). I would use Notepad++ to double check the config file to ensure it has the correct values.Summary:The game is still fun when it works, but I am not a fan of the CTDs and stutters that happen quite often regardless of the hardware you are running. Even with the community "fixes" that are available they are either hit or miss which is why I would recommend holding off on buying this bad port until after the game's stability has been resolved. If you want to play an EDF game and have fun then go play the other games since those ports are actually stable

_childDocuments_.review: I love the EDF series, it's a lot of fun to play with friends and has a lot of replayability as evidenced by my hundreds of hours in previous titles on steam alone.  Having said that, this was a $15 effort at best set at full price.   If the developer had announced a graphical upgrade patch to EDF 5, and put it out for free, this is likely what it would have looked like.  Even then, levels are lifted wholesale from previous games and tossed in here with no changes to voice acting, graphics, enemies, etc.This is a franchise that I don't ask a lot from.  Give me new levels and interesting setups, maybe a few new enemies, and maybe just maybe some new weapons and I am happy.  They failed to deliver most of what I think is a basic request.The largest change in the game is found in the Air Raider, trading their mostly air-based attack sets for a mix of air-based and drone-based attacks.  This was, as stated, to provide air raiders more choices in underground levels.  Just one problem, a lot of the drones DON'T WORK in underground levels as they often get caught on terrain, making them worse than not usable, but simply overwhelmingly frustrating and useless.  Then, as a bonus slap across the face, the Air Raider air-based arsenal is not usable in what seems to be about 30% of the above ground levels as well, and where air raiders shined brightest (against teleportation anchors) has been taken away except when you are playing copy-paste levels from old games where the original teleportation anchors still exist.New enemies stutter-move inconsistently through the maps making targeting unreliable in a frustrating way.The vast majority of the weapons are recycled and still suffer from the same nonsensical upgrade system wherein a weapon stat may be maxxed out at, lets say 4 stars (for instance accuracy B), but have 7 stars of progress, so when upgrades for a weapon are obtained, it can be truly useless for no good reason.  Poor stepping within an upgrade path is one thing, but purely useless bounds is just poor quality.The levels give even less information about what will be encountered than before, unless you use a guide or memorize the levels you will spend a lot of time bringing useless weapons only to die and have to reconfigure.  A bit of good:A rework of all classes was performed with mostly solid upgrades to how each class functions apart from the air raider.Graphics were updated for the newly created maps (20-30%?) and they look great!Some new versions of old enemies were created and are fantastic (shock spiders, new red ants)Don't give lazy developers money, especially AAA money, for a very lazy, and very poor version of a great franchise.  Buy EDF 4.1, or 5.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean if you hate the idea of making an Epic account because Tim Sweeney killed your dog or something, I'm not gonna change your mind. Though it should be noted you don't need to get the EGS app if that's your big concern, you can literally just make a throwaway account on a random email if you want and that'll fulfill the requirement to play online. Or you can wait for D3/Sandlot to do the supposed removal of the epic account requirementOkay, now those of us who are here for the actual game and not the drama?It's more EDF. What does this mean? Solo or co-op third person shooting with an insane amount of enemies most of the time, ridiculously large sense of scale and destruction that you can't really find anywhere else, with a focus on arcadey fun over more complex third person co-op shooters like Helldivers. But you still have to play smart to an extent: Consider what weapons work best for the mission and opposition you're facing. Consider what enemy groups to engage and when during a mission if they aren't aggroed from the start. And with a certain type of jank EDF is known for that somehow ends up being charming thanks to the Havok physics engine. It won't win any awards for graphic fidelity, but in exchange for that you get numbers, destruction, and a sense of massive scale you won't find anywhere else. Four playable classes all with their own distinct method of killing bugs, robots, and humans-Sorry, I mean aliens that look like humans. Kill enemies, loot the battlefield for new weapons, wash rinse and repeat until you stand on the hundreds of thousands of dead enemies you went through to reach the end of the game.Much like 5 was a huge step forward for the game after 4.1, 6 is yet another huge step forward after 5. We have...-Tons of new enemy types that shake up the formula in new ways. Remember how Frogs and Grays changed things up in EDF5 due to behaving more like actual soldiers, using cover and flanking you? Well, EDF6 went on steroids with this idea with tons of new enemy types that bring new mechanics to the table.-Somehow an even bigger campaign than EDF5 now totaling *146 missions!* Seriously, it's huge. Nevermind DLC2 will have a whopping *40* missions this time around, compared to the 15 or so from DLC2 in 5. This is without a doubt the biggest EDF yet.-Significant improvements to all classes, with 3 of them now getting offhand slots for things like grenades, deployable turrets, and all kinds of brand new toys too, this means you get to bring even more destruction with you into a mission than ever before.-The Air Raider (tactical/engineer/support) now has a crapton of new Drones that make him much more viable both solo and in group play. He's the best he's ever been, even if you can't use airstrikes for a chunk of the campaign due to plot reasons. But don't worry, his new army of drones is just as deadly.-An actual plotline beyond "Oh noes, Aliens." You thought Doomslayer's been through some stuff? Wait till you see what Storm-1's been through...tldr? Shoot bugs (and other things) solo or with friends. Get loot. Repeat for over 140 missions and then do it again on a higher difficulty for even better loot. Not a fan of the graphics cause they look like they're too old or outdated? Buddy, if you tried to do in Helldivers what EDF6 does, your computer would spontaneously combust. You don't come for graphics, you come for the sheer insanity of how much goes on at any given time.There's a reason EDF has become my favorite co-op shooter as of late, and 6 just keeps it going.

Imagine a bullet flying toward you from the front, hitting you, and you're shoved to the right, or the left and a bit forward, or whatever, depending on where the ball intersects with you during that physics tick.Shield enemies that negate entire categories of weapons. who are still massive bullet sponges with the shields frozen in place, often moving their bodies around in a circle like a goofy carnival game.Drones that twitch around at the slightest provocation that makes shooting them a roll of the dice unless you're using an explosive.Level recycling like I've never seen before. It's unreal. A story about aliens using time travel to invade earth as anime NATO fights them off becomes tiresome, and I don't even know how you could do that on purpose. The B-movie scifi dialogue from earlier installments has taken a bizarre turn for the dour.It's not all bad, there's fun to be found. I'm at 36 hours, and will probably play more, But you'd be better off with EDF 5.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DROverall, I loved EDF 6 and highly recommend it to long-time fans of the series and newbies alike. Sandlot has announced that they are in the process of removing the EPIC sign-in requirement for online play.Finally finished my first playthrough of this game and I had a great time through all it! EDF 6 delivers on the same great arcade-style gameplay as its predecessors with several quality-of-life improvements to each of the 4 playable classes. The dialogue and characters are just as goofy and campy as ever, but the story had several interesting twists that keep you engaged throughout the game's insane 140+ missions. It's a shame that this game got so many negative reviews due to the EPIC Games sign in requirement for online play. As a long time fan of the series, I can confidently say that this is the best EDF game that I've played. It has loads of memorable and challenging missions, and all the new enemy types that were added are interesting and have cool (albeit goofy) designs.I played through the game doing mainly local coop with my roommate, so I can't speak to the quality of online play in this installment, but the devs have announced that they are in the process of removing the EPIC requirement for online multiplayer mode. I suspect that the game's ratings will skyrocket once they square that away.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I'd like to say ignore the negative reviews, the game is being review bombed and these reviews don't reflect the quality of the game at all.I'll address the reason for the review bombing by others later in my review however I could not in good conscious give this game a negative review as that would be disingenuous.EDF6 is the follow up of EDF5 the two games make up a self contained story and while I do recommend that newcomers play EDF5 first it isn't necessary to enjoy EDF6.The EDF franchise is best described as every old B Movie blended together into a videogame, it's cheesy, it's over the top, and it's downright hilarious at times.You'll find yourself facing off against huge hordes of giant bugs, giant robots and kaiju, and an assortment of huge alien creatures each with their own combat style and strategy to defeat them.There are 4 classes to play as. Ranger: your standard soldier, he's the most well rounded and the best class for beginners.Wing Diver: An all female unit that uses jetpacks and energy weapons, her weapons rely on the same energy meter as her jetpack so mastering her can be tricky, she is also a class cannon, she has the lowest starting health but packs a huge punch.Air Raider: A "support" class who's ability to call in air strikes, vehicles, and weaponised drones makes him feel more like a one man army than a support class.Fencer: The Fencer is a walking tank, slow but tough and packs a lot of firepower, unlike other classes who can only bring two weapons with them the Fencer can carry up to four and wields two weapons at a time, he is the hardest class to master but becomes death incarnate once you do.During the course of the game you'll fight ridiculously huge armies of enemies in almost fully destructable environments, if you see a building you can probably destroy it providing you have an explosive weapon.As you kill enemies they'll drop boxes, collecting these boxes will grant you one of three things.Armour boxes: These Red boxes will increase your total maximum health "armour" by roughly one point for each one you collect so you're always getting stronger just by playing.Weapon boxes: These Green boxes will grant you a new weapon/vehicle/air strike/equipment item or level up something you already have, there are hundreds of weapons and such to unlock.Health boxes: These White boxes will restore your health, they come in two sizes a small and a large.What's new in EDF6?EDF6 introduces a lot of new enemies but also gives each class a bit of an improvement, Ranger, Air Raider, and Wing Diver all now have a backpack slot that let's them carry an extra bit of equipment such as a grenade, sentry turret, defense drone, or energy shield, these new items make the already addictive gameplay loop and frantic combat even better!Missions: The game features roughly 140+ missions not counting DLC missions, these can be play solo, in splitscreen co-op with a buddy, or in four player online co-op, this is where the issue regarding the review bombing comes into play.EDF6 is the first game in the franchise to be released on Epic Store and as such it requires that you make and link an Epic account in order to play online, this was likely done for the sake of crossplay.As most people know Steam users including myself hate having to link additional accounts in order to play the game online, this is made worse by the fact that D3 never mentioned anything about this prior to release and it isn't listed anywhere in the Steam page for the game.I was pretty mad when I first found out as my main concern was that this would render the online unplayable on Steam Deck, however after making an account and linking it (which took about 5 seconds) I was pleased to find the online works as well as it ever has.While I understand the frustration I think the review bombing of what is otherwise the most fun game of 2024 is a bit ridiculous and over the top, I'm mentioning the Epic account issue in my review because it does need addressing but I feel I'd be doing a disservice to my fellow gamers if I left a negative review and potentially caused someone to miss out on such a phenomenal game, especially since the series is already very niche.EDF6 is absolutely the most fun the franchise has ever been and for a franchise that tends to be more fun than half of the games on the market that's really saying something, the new weapons are a blast to use and the new enemies are a blast to... well blast.I cannot recommend this game and that franchise in general enough!EDF! EDF!TLDR: If you love having fun buy EDF6 unless taking 5 seconds to link an Epic account so you can play online is a deal breaker for you.UPDATE: D3 have heard the feedback regarding the linking of Epic accounts and are working to remove that requirement from the game.I expect everyone who left a negative review for that reason alone to do the right thing and change your review to positive.

_childDocuments_.review: I love EDF to bits.Having said that, the producer's attitude towards this release deserves a thumbs down. I am going to skip over the Epic store gadget inclusion because everyone has mentioned it and honestly it is not a big issue for me.But what has to be mentioned is the horrible desync this game has in multiplayer. Just so you get an idea, it is exactly as if your game copied the inputs the other player is doing in his game, but in your pc. This means that if at any point they are not copied to perfection, their character will remain stuck in some corner for the rest of the game. The game does not make any effort to recheck if the client and host positions match (unless they get on a vehicle or die and are revived). This is beyond immersion breaking, makes cooperation in hard difficulties impossible, and makes the extremely punishing friendly fire a common occurrence. These desyncs issues happen to everyone I have heard of, and internet quality does not matter. I play with my partner, who is literally touching elbows with me, connected to the same high quality router. In any other game this equals a LAN quality experience.These issues are not present in EDF 4.1 nor 5. You would expect the producer to have mentioned the problem and to be working on a fix, but after more than a month from release, there are no news nor patch. It's like they ported the game, launched it, and then deleted it from their computers.Some players in the community have gotten in contact with customer support, and they just get the typical "verify integrity and if that doesn't work maybe reinstall Windows" speak.So yeah, If you ask me, don't give them your money and just go play edf 4.1 with cheat engine to get pretty much all the quality of life they have added over the two entries. It is a flawless and great experience.This game is otherwise amazing, once you take out the problems I have talked about. It is the same but a bit better, and for once I was actually invested in the story, which is told in a pretty cool way.If you are not a fervent fan of the EDF games who already bought this one on day one for 60 bucks, wait for a sale AND for a fix. Otherwise really just get EDF 4.1, if you haven't played it, you are not missing anything at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I finished the game and started the inferno grind and I can say that its still a good EDF game, my gripes with the game do kind of stay but nearing the end you do start the proper EDF feeling, the enemy I hated also weren't the only enemy through the game. Still, only pick this up if you're a big EDF fan, otherwise wait until a sale.Let me start this by saying I am a long time fan of EDF, my first being 2017 on the 360. I've played through every EDF and their spin-offs, including IR, IA, WB, and even the portable and Wing Diver games. The main line EDFs are all amazing, and that's what hurts 6 the most.6 relies a lot on the previous game to convey its story with time shenanigans, a first really as the other main-line games only really redo the story or reference it like how 2017 (3) and 2025 (4.1) did. However this is really to an odd way of story in a game that doesn't really focus on story. This leads into a lot of issues with 6 compared to the others.First off and the most obvious, the Epic Games account stuff. On one hand, I already have one and didn't have an issue with it. On the other though, they waited until the 11th hour to even let anyone know it was a thing and even the explanation as to why does not address the why in the first place. Its another issue of Epic Games not really meshing well with Steam.Second is server, disconnections for a lot of people for every 3-5 missions. I haven't encountered the issue in private rooms but in public lobbies its almost consistent. Also, de-sync is horrible, almost every time a teammate goes down, you have a solid 30 seconds of them just standing there at full health before they teleport to where they ragdolled. A lot of time you think you can shoot past a teammate or a friendly vehicle and you'll instead just shoot them despite them being 30 feet to your left. I even had a mission where the enemies were all dead on my friends game but in my game they were still alive. This has been the worst is has been for PC online play. Sometimes 5 would de-sync in one mission, 4.1 had the memory leak in the multiplayer equipment menu, 6 is just borked.Third is a personal complaint that I know I share with some, but its new enemies. Most are welcome as they change up the pace and flow of enemy encounters. However there is one that absolutely ruins the fun and balance and thats the Krull. Not only are their weapons hard to avoid, even at lower difficulties, but its those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shields they have. Large shielded enemies are not foreign to the series, 4.1 had shielded Hectors and you can shoot their exposed weapons or limbs. 5 had armored Cosmonauts that took a lot of damage but never regenerated that armor. Shield Bearers don't have weapons. Krull get the most OP and annoying things that all large enemies get in the series, accurate ragdoll weapons, ability to shoot in weird ways to negate cover but the one that ruins the fun of fighting them are their shields. They have these decently sized round shields that can cover their whole body/head. Thats not too bad, but they get the ability to essentially do the Ultra-Instinct meme and use their shields to intercept almost every attack at it with pinpoint precision. While funny to see it block every single bullet that an AC-130's chain gun fires at it, it makes fighting them boring and infuriating. The only way to stop their shield is to shoot it until it overloads, however when it overloads it just stays where the Krull had is last and it can still block bullets. God forbid you fight the ones that have two shields along with two guns or if multiple Krull stack up and use their shields for each other.Fourth is the voice mixing. The new voices and characters are weak, and not in the cheesy B-grade Sci-Fi that we have come to love about EDF. The mixing is poor, even with the dialog volume maxed out and all others lowered I can still barely make out any of the words said. Sadly this also applies to the main character/ NPC that is with you for almost the entire game. Also, that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is a whiny little ♥♥♥♥♥ who needs to shut up about his damn wife and help me shoot a damn bug or two. Voice mixing is also very odd because when you get to the missions based in the past, they sound great and keep the EDF charm.Fifth is the story. I know story isn't really a big thing in EDF and this is more of a personal gripe but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it confusing. Still, the game plays well, there are lots of important changes that differentiate it from 5 that are felt in the first few missions even too. EDF's story exists as an excuse to shoot more bugs. Yes it's campy and fun, but it's not revolutionary and it's not gonna change much between games.YES it uses Epic multiplayer servers, but they function well enough from my experiences. It seems easier to avoid friendly-firing them this time through, but I'm not sure why.If all you want is more "big cool gun go brrrrrrr' and shooty-bang-bang horde multiplayer, this game will give you it. _childDocuments_.review: Giving this game a bad review kind of sucks. The game has quite a bit of charm and there's a lot of things to like about it, but unfortunately the further I got in, the more I just kept thinking "Man, I wish this was made by a developer who knew what the hell they were doing". There's some great new enemies that are unfortunately ruined by either horrible beefed up counterparts or just poor implementation. Androids are one of the first to come to mind. They're pretty fun, goofy enemies, and killing them is satisfying. Hell, even the suicide bomber androids are pretty fun to fight and taking them down with a massive chain reaction of explosions is great. What's not fun is dealing with their big brother counter parts, the big androids, which are obnoxious projectile spamming bullet sponge enemies that they spawn in DROVES. Oh and if that's not enough, there's quite a few missions where they spawn from teleportation anchors so you're stuck trying to slog your way through or around these tanky enemies until you can reach the teleportation anchors they spawn from (oh and the ones they tend to spawn from are the shielded teleportation anchors that you need to get right under to attack). Then you've got the Kruuls. These things have potential to be fun. Basically they're squid aliens that carry one or two shields that block your attacks until you deplete them at which point they can't move the shield leaving the rest of their body vulnerable so you can either focus on disarming them (by disarming I of course mean blow their tentacles off) or going for their heads. In moderate numbers, they're actually pretty fun to fight and satisfying to take down. The problem is that Sandlot doesn't understand fun so they throw them at you in massive waves making fighting them an absolute nightmare. It's a perfect example of misusing a great enemy. They should be handled as big bois, that you fight in groups of three or four, alternatively one or two complemented by cannon fodder hordes or teams of colonists. When the game DOES do that, fighting them is fun. When the game throws them at you in massive crowds of 30 or, it just turns into an obnoxious and frustrating slog.Then there's the missions. Sandlot likes to boast about the number of missions but ultimately that means nothing. Quality over quantity. Sandlot desperately needs to learn that. If the number of terrible missions outnumbers the number of actually fun missions, that's a huge problem. What also sucks about the missions in this case is that Sandlot decided it'd be a great idea to make this one more "story focused". By story focused I mean quite a few missions where you're stuck in place or following NPCs around slowly until the mission actually starts. Honestly it just gives me the impression Sandlot is out of touch with their playerbase. Here's an example. The mission after Kruuls are first introduced is essentially a beat for beat repeat of the mission in ED5 right after colonists are introduced. In ED5 the mission opens up with the squad ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and then Sarge talking about their weaknesses. In EDF5 you don't have to listen to that. You can just say "Ok see you have fun" and take off on your own to go kill those aliens that look just like humans while the sarge rambles about how the aliens have eyes and ears which means they can see and hear just like humans.  That's what people want out of an EDF mission: to jump right into it screaming "WAAAUUUGH! EDF! EDF! EDF!! EDF!!". In the EDF6 counterpart however, you're stuck in place at the beginning of the mission unable to move until some mopey grunt finishes his doom and gloom monologue and another soldier runs over to tell you there's survivors who need rescue. It's counter intuitive to what people like about the EDF series. Worse still, this is the mission where you're fighting kruuls for the first time proper so unless you spoiled yourself with a walkthrough, you might find yourself restarting the mission a few times to tweak your loadout to something suitable for them, meaning each time you've got to sit through that dialogue. There's more than a few missions like that. Here's another example of how bad it can get at times. At the beginning of the second loop, you have to sit through the scientist dude's dialogue, then follow him (walking slowly I might add), to the briefing room where you have to sit through more of his dialogue, then walk over to a designated spot to listen to the captain's briefing, and then the mission begins proper. Towards the end of that mission an enemy somehow got stuck in a wall and I couldn't proceed. I had to restart the mission and sit through that ALL OVER AGAIN.It sucks to leave this game a bad review because I genuinely enjoyed EDF5 and had high hopes for this one. I had hopes that Sandlot would take some valuable lessons from EDF5 about what made it fun and where it could be improved. Unfortunately that just doesn't seem to be the case.

_childDocuments_.review: It's odd to say, but perhaps the most remarkable thing about Earth Defense Force 6 is the writing. The series has always gone for a campy, B-movie vibe - and that certainly hasn't changed here - but a stronger narrative direction helps keeps things fresh even among repurposed content from EDF5. Gameplay also gets a strong shakeup with the introduction of the equipment pack. Items like grenades, mines and turrets no longer take up a weapon slot, allowing you to effectively bring three weapons on missions. It seems like a small change, but it does add welcome wrinkles to the flow of EDF combat. As you no longer need to swap to them, grenades can now be used to cover yourself while you're reloading without cancelling the reload itself. There are also weapons that support partial reloads, like manually loaded shotguns, allowing you to reload early without having to wait the full duration an empty reload would take. Personally, I think this is the best EDF game in ages. 4.1 and 5 were still very enjoyable, but I didn't feel the urge to do multiple playthroughs like I had with previous entries. With 6, I immediately started a second playthrough after watching the credits, and I expect that won't be the last. The only thing I have yet to do is play multiplayer, as unlike the last few games EDF6 currently requires an Epic Games Account to access online play. D3 has said they're going to change this in an upcoming update, but as far as I'm aware that has yet to happen. I don't mind the game using EOS for crossplay, but I'd prefer not to have a superfluous account requirement on top of that.

_childDocuments_.review: My bar for quality on EDF games is very low. The cheesey voice acting, out-of-date graphics, and wonky physics and game mechanics always seemed charming, offering something you couldn't get in any other game. It doesn't feel charming anymore. This is the first game of the series that feels lazy. Most of the assets are reused from previous games in the series. There are enemies that are new, and there are changes to classes that feel new, but you are still using the same weapons with the same models, fighting the same enemies from the last game. You sometimes even play through the same levels, beat for beat, with the same spawn points, ally placements, and even voice acting. During the game, you end up playing the same levels multiple times, It makes sense with the "story", but it feels lazy. There is something wrong with the localization of this game. It is extremely difficult to piece together the actual story through the poorly voice acted and translated dialog. This game also contains multiple sections of the game where you can do nothing but wait while NPCs rattle off dialog, fire off ineffectual attacks, or simple walk around while you can do nothing but wait. It's even worse with the random crashes, causing you to replay the same levels over and over, listen to the terrible dialog, waiting until the level actually lets you play the game, only for it to crash yet again. This game really isn't worth it. You can play EDF 5 or 4 and have a better experience, and you won't miss any of the new features of this game. This feels like it should be a $15 DLC of EDF 5, not a standalone game stretched to last for 150 missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Why did the Primers attack earth and mankind? How does humanity live on even if it's decimated to 10% of the whole population? And where do the giant insects even come from in the first place?All these questions nobody ever asked and the answers are all here, beyond the red sky, beyond EDF 6.Sandlot put a great deal of effort in the story of EDF 6. _childDocuments_.review: Let's get this out of the way, requiring EGS and an account MP despite having said NOTHING about it pre release is an idiotic decision. Plenty of other games have cross store play without requiring a separate account. Otherwise aside from that this is the SAME JANK Sandlot has been doing for a few decades now, flat out REFUSING to learn anything from the improvements, QOL features and actual gameplay changes that Yukes and Vicious Cycle brought to the table with IA, IR and WB. Least of all to say the  they made on a visual and performance level.While this is the best performing version of EDF Vanilla yet, it still is constantly dropping frames with what I honestly almost expect is because perhaps their frame limiter is targeting 59.94hz instead of 60.xxx (Or you know leaving it arbitrary). According to DXVK's development EDF 4 and 5 those games constantly were turning Vsync on and off on frame presentation Dynamic vsync is still present here where it will occasionally show torn frames like in those games, but not nearly as severe. Pick those engineer's brains, because you would have to actually try HARD to get IA, IR and WB to drop any frames or stutter at all. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, ignore the negative reviews about literally nothing. My short and sweet I'd give it an 8/10. The same awesome EDF gameplay from past titles with slight changes to class balance and the addition of a new utility equipment slot. Maps are great, although some are a little too similar to EDF 5. Same classic EDF story and voice acting. Graphics are modestly improved, gore is great, diverse enemy types, and many different ways to play. I wholly recommend it, my detailed review is below.I'm going to spend a bit talking about the negative reviews, which are literally just "Muh it has epic", so skip ahead for the real review. That aside lets talk about the game. So steam seems to be a bit confused as it thinks I've only played about an hour at the time of writing this, but I've done much more. The game is basically a revamped version of past titles. The gameplay is the same with only slight alterations. The biggest change is the addition of a new utility equipment slot that lets you use a variety of tools and items to modify your play style a bit. They re-balanced the Air Raider a to make them more functional outside of the support role so you can actually contribute in combat directly instead of just staying on the outskirts calling in support, although this play style is still possible. Ranger, Fencer, and Wing Diver remain mostly the same but with some new ways to play due to the new utility equipment.For those of you who've played EDF in the past all I can say is its more of the same, so if you liked any EDF game, aside from Iron Rain, you'll like this. For newcomers EDF 6 is basically an action oriented third person shooter with class based mechanics. Think Helldivers but class-based and with linear missions rather than random maps; there are over 150 of these levels in the base game alone with dozens more added by mission packs. Most maps are massive and almost everything is destructible. You can literally level entire city blocks by the time a mission is done. Maps are varied with everything from urban to open fields.There are four classes with distinct mechanics and gameplay. The Ranger is your basic shooter with an array of weapons and high ground based mobility, functioning in the straight forward get in the fight and light things up role. Air Raider is more of a support class and can do things like call in air strikes, heal people with equipment, and more. Both the ranger and air raider can call in vehicles like tanks, apcs, mecha, and helicopters to pilot. The Wing Diver is a glass cannon that can fly; they are high speed, high damage, but low health with exotic energy weapons. The Fencer is literally a walking tank who wields heavy weapons like artillery pieces, mini guns, and a slew of other things. There is a high range of difficulty options ranging from extremely easy to borderline impossible. This game is versatile in how you can play it. If you prefer just running and gunning you can set it at a moderate difficulty and all do your own thing. If you want a more teamwork oriented experience set the difficulty a bit higher and take your time with each objective. The game can be played solo or with up to four friends.The game has a campy plot and like the other games is the perfect blend of serious, satirical, and outright comedic. The graphics are the same as past titles in a lot of ways, but definitely better overall. The gameplay is smooth and clean, I have not had any bugs as of yet. Music and sound design is excellent for the budget.All in all the game is great. My only real critique is that some levels are samey compared to past titles due to the premise of the plot. I won't spoil anything but let's just say that you'll recognize a handful of the levels if you played EDF 5. A lot of people say this franchise is so bad it's good, i just say it's good and leave it at that. 8/10 would buy again.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the Epic Online Services issue for multiplayer, EDF 6 is pretty much exactly what I expected it to be: a sequel to EDF 5 that tries to fix some of the problems (Rangers being generally useless unless they're packing two sniper rifles, Air Raider being useless during any mission where there's a roof) that EDF 5 had. That said, it does have its share of annoyances, primarily that the game takes the same approach that 5 did and makes you go through an extended tutorial segment that isn't fun to sit through and yet has to be sat through on all four classes for completion.I'll start by talking about what Sandlot fixed - each class now has a "backpack" slot, meaning that a lot of the support-type weapons no one ever used unless they were grinding Inferno in 4.1 can be carried around for free. They also re-balanced the Ranger and Air Raider: the Ranger's weapons were generally made a bit better outside of the mandatory sniper rifles, and Air Raider now has drones that allow him to perform air strikes underground instead of sitting around putting up health restores and summoning the crawler robot that had no health and ran out of ammo way too fast.There are still a lot of issues, however. Chief among these is the Epic Online Services requirement - a requirement that only exists because of the PS4 and PS5. There's really no excuse for it: a lot of games use Epic Online Services in a way that you never really see it - if you've played Elden Ring, that uses EOS but you never see it because it creates a dummy account for you and automatically installs and uninstalls EOS with it. For some reason, Sandlot chose to half-ass the implementation and requires an install of the standalone EOS client, which makes people think you need an Epic Game Store account to play. You do not need an EGS account: you can make a dummy account in the same exact way that Elden Ring does automatically, it's just a manual process. EOS is also notoriously hard to get rid of, which isn't great when the entire Epic Game Store has been accused of being a data-thieving botnet.Other issues I ran into were mostly specific to the Air Raider. A lot of the new drone attacks have really deceptive AOEs that I wish would be clarified - early in the game, you get a mortar drone that actually has a MUCH wider AOE than the targeting icon suggests, but you also get a machine gun strafing run that is smaller than the targeting icon by a bit and is kind of annoying to aim. If they got rid of the mandatory EOS install and made it like Elden Ring, I think I wouldn't have a problem with this game since it doesn't do anything wrong that EDF 5 didn't already do wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: So after cooling down a bit, manually disabling communication with epic servers in my hosts file out of spite, playing some more and reading about the latest notice by developers about the Epic Games situation, I will now adapt my review.The Epic Games Services stuff is shady, but apparently tied to their engine choice. I tried to research the kind of data collected and shared by these services and could not find much except for an evaluation from a "common sense privacy program". Look it up, it's quite interesting. Anyway, I found my way to deal with this situation and like I wrote in the original review, I would have refunded the game if I loved the series any less.As a background, I have been following the EDF series since "Insect Armageddon", played 4.1 on PC and 5 on PS4. On the latter, I have reached 60% total completion... which means completing every single mission with every class on at least hard difficulty. So you know I don't mind the grind. I revel in grinding certain missions on inferno with special setups on the edge of my seat to farm overpowered weapons and absolutely flatten the invaders in the lower difficulties later. That moment when you unlock some new and insane weapon or vehicle you haven't seen before... yeah, that's the spot.But now to the actual game review. To make it short, I felt right at home. If you played EDF 5, you know what to expect. There are a few minor improvements in graphics, textures and maybe size of the maps, but that doesn't matter much. I have only played singleplayer in hard difficulty up to now and it feels right. Challenging, but doable with the right equipment choices and tactics. The Air Raider's (best class) new drone weapons are extremely cool and the support drones defending the player are a really useful addition. I haven't played the other classes much yet. Ranger and Wingdiver also had new support equipment, I don't know about the Fencer, but all in all it seems like they have improved upon some of the classes weaknesses from the previous games, resulting in an even better combat flow and more strategic options. And I think the enemies seem to act a bit more intelligently than those in older games ever did.In my opinion it's the best EDF so far if you can look past the Epic Games Services situation.

Also before you start your first mission go into settings and switch the camera from Type 2 to Type 1 (type 1 is the traditional EDF camera setting).Earth Defense Force 6: Live. Die. Repeat. Terror from the Deep didn't start strong for me. The post-apocalyptic tone wasn't doing it for me however a certain "thing" happens and suddenly everything clicked. I was hooked. I felt more invested in the story here than in any other EDF title for this reason. Some players aren't a fan of the dialogue here however I enjoyed it still. The sergeant grew on me. With that said holy cow this game is long even compared to the other EDF games. I finished it on hard as a ranger and it took me over 45 hours. Not a bad thing just be prepared. Gameplay wise it's a continuation of EDF 5 with further improvements. The extra equipment you can use on top of the usual arsenal is a welcome addition especially some the gear the Air Raider now gets. The new enemies have a perfect mix of being fun/annoying so you'll gladly want to blow them up. In my 55 hours of playing at this time it crashed on me twice. Other than that I haven't noticed any technical issues that are deal breakers and I have a mid tier machine. EDF 6 isn't perfect but for me once it gets going it's the best game in the series. It's still hard for me to stop playing. Despite it's long length I'm already doing another playthrough as the fencer on hard and loving every second of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill bugs, aliens, and eldritch horrors from the ocean depths. Fight a dragon that fights the way a dragon should. Pilot a 12 story robot and punch Godzilla in the face. Collect insane weapons and blow up entire cities using everything from standard grenade launchers to orbital laser cannons. All this, and bad voice acting, too! This series has been one of my favorites since I played EDF 4.1. It's bloody fantastic. If you can imagine a cheesed-out kaiju movie with tons and tons of ridiculous weaponry, frenetic run-and-gun action blended with team tactics, and an AI that will kick your ass completely off if you don't play smart, you'd have EDF. And the 6th one is, despite a few changes I don't quite understand or agree with, the best one so far. It's not big on plot. EDF has never really been about the story. The graphics are questionable, until you realize that this is one of those games that just isn't about the graphics, either. As previously stated, it's about teaming up with 3 of your buds and kicking the green/purple/brown/blue/wtf is that color crap out of all sorts of heinous invaders. I have about 58 hours in at the time of this writing and still haven't found all of the weapons. There are HUNDREDS of them, and while some are just more powerful revamps, a lot of the end-game stuff is so powerful that it can level a city block in a single shot. I'm talking tactical nuclear artillery, and at least one case. If you've never played an EDF game, this is a good place to start. Punishing and difficult, but not impossible. And damn, is it fun! Only cons I can call out: collecting drops as you're fighting is a silly mechanic, but there are mods on Nexus to take care of that for you. Some enemies can attack through walls and buildings, which is annoying, but not impossible to defend against. That's about it. Anyone who has read my other reviews knows I can tear a game apart, but I just don't see many game-breaking issues with EDF 6. There are also all kinds of mods on Nexus and other places, so if you get tired of the game, you can change it up. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Its a good turn brain off and shoot game, toss on a podcast/playlist if the writing/performance isn't your thing. Great for putting tons of hours 100% it. 7/10 (Good)Took me of the time of this review to beat the game once on the "hard" difficulty with ranger as a solo with a collection mod, I'm relatively new to EDF (only beat edf 5 once before this) so your time varies. This is a good turn off the brain and shoot game, especially if your into 100% it, as completing the campaign once granted me 15% game completion achievement. *an epic account is required to play online*The story is pretty good, the voice acting and humour is very cheesy but it doesn't take away from the gameplay as you will be knee deep in monster blood and climbing on the corpses of your enemies to blow up more in a constant stream of destruction. Performance wise I crashed probably 8+ times throughout my playthough. The graphical settings are underwhelming but if you played edf 5 you know what to expect.The replayablily is high as theres tons of weapons per class and plenty of missions to keep it fresh, if playing solo I do recommend a mod or (the die-hards are gonna cringe on this) cheats that would auto collect loot boxes. The one I use is called lootmaster on nexus mods. It auto collects loot boxes only when you finish the mission and doesn't collect any additional payout if you fail. The whole "just leave one monster left and run around and collect the boxes" argument doesn't sit right with me as its just padding and if you want to play harder missions later on the grind is real. The game in my opinion doesn't respect your time by doing this, if you only have a few hours a week to play games, those 5+min at the end of every mission really adds up.Story: 7/10  Charming cheesy B-movie plot and writing/performance.Gameplay: 8/10 Lots of shooting, lots of enemies, lots of destruction.Graphics: 5.5/10 looks like a ps3 game, essentially no in game graphical settings.Performance: 6.5/10 had more crashes then expected but the game is pretty fast booting up again.side note: Turning off vsync through nivida panel makes the game load way faster if you can swing it, I personally didn't as I think the engines physics or something is effected by framerate? pretty anecdotal as I didn't do this for more then one or two missions.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is insanely hard but the more you play the easier it gets, I’ve been playing the best online co op EDF series for decades, the more you play the more armour is added to all classes and armour level is carried over to consecutive playthroughs giving this game infinite replay ability, putting several hundred hours into this game is extremely satisfying when you have over 10000 armour (you start the game with 150 armour)for each class making completing missions easier,(still insanely hard but fun)It has a good community who will help new players even though it might not look like it at first to brand new players who can’t be revived immediately due to revive mechanics *(look for lobbies with armour limit lock off/weapon limit lock off)!*These locks are only online so look for lobbies with limit unlocks off to use your best weapons in the mission, these hosts have 70%+ completion rate if they have limit locks off and are the key to quick progression if you’re lucky get the best weapons in the game right away if they change to inferno!Playing offline on hard is good for getting completion above 70% if you want the ability to turn online limits off as host or for getting armour when starting out on a new save!there are no armour or weapon limits offline so when starting a new save it’s good to get high level weapons online through an experienced host(always look for lobbies with limits off before joining any games) even though if you only have a couple of hundred armour!When you can’t find a host with no limits you can quickly fly through missions on hard offline with overpowered weapons collecting armour/weapon drops as you go!Search for a host with 70%+ completion rate after each offline mission you complete, you’ll get armour quicker this way rather than just refreshing the search settings until you find a hard lobby with limit locks off online The level of weapons dropped depends on mission and difficulty levels, collecting the same weapons multiple time upgrade them so a weapon is usually poor when you first find it but could be brilliant fully upgraded, this adds even more replay ability!Campaign missions are up to weapon level 100 drops DLC1 missions are weapon level 100-106 dropsDLC2 missions are weapon level 106-117dropsSome high level campaign weapons under 100 can be unlocked/upgraded in the dlcDlc1 weapons can’t be found in the dlc2 campaign missions and vise versa!The dlc missions and weapons when fully upgraded are well worth the purchase if you like the game and think you’ll put many hours into it!I can help any player who messages me asking for help, just ask especially if you have just purchased the Game or dlc, I can get you the highest level weapons right away but you might have to stay downed for a bit if you’re just starting out, once you get some inferno weapons I can host no limit hard for quick armour and%It’s very satisfying for long term players to  help brand new players unlock high level weapons and collect armour so don’t quit if you keep getting killed and not revived as you will still get weapons and armour you and your teammates collect when the mission end!*****this is important to understand as in this situation , a host will probably change to inferno to get a new player better weapons if they only have the weapons and armour you start the game with!You can’t join or host hardest or inferno difficulty lobbies until you complete the campaign on any difficulty unless a friend invites you or the host changes to inferno once you’re in!Completing hard missions completes easy and normal simultaneously, hardest and inferno only complete themselves if a host changes to inferno this could put you off the game for good when you first start playing as teammates sometimes might have no choice but to leave a player with less than 500 armour downed for several minutes to complete the mission getting you the really good weapons even if you didn’t collect any!when you revive a downed teammate you lose half your armour!Reviving players regardless of armour level for example your total armour is 60000, revive someone and it drops to 30000, revive another it drops to 15000 and so on, this adds another great dimension to the game when health pick ups are in short supply!So if you only have low armour and end up in an inferno lobby don’t quit if teammates have high armour level and don’t revive you, they just mathematically can’t without failing the mission, some players with tens of thousands of armour can easily complete most inferno mission solo when everyone else is downed but risk failing the mission if they revive everyone when no health pick ups or healing equipment nearby so be patient as the higher the difficulty and mission level the more armour rewarded and higher level weapons awarded even if you spend several minutes downed, once you have good weapons and start gaming armour it won’t be an issue be patient and you’ll get lots of very nice weapons for being down most the mission!If you want the highest level weapons in the game as soon as you buy the game before farming armour then be prepared to spend most of the mission downed relying on players with tens of thousands of armour to collect weapons and revive you when possible!I’ve played for over 500 hours and probably 500 more!EDF,EDF!
