_childDocuments_.review: CON: - ENGLISH VOICESWhile they still have some zingers of lines the audio feels like a soulless copy of EDF 5. It would have been funny if they used the same audio files for a few chapters and I would have been okay if they did. But playing through it feels like they fed the audio from EDF 5 into an AI and told it to make something. - EPIC GAMESI've read it from others here, and there are others who are willing to explain it better than I will, so to summarize. If I buy a game on steam I shouldn't need to have an EPIC GAMES ACCOUNT in order to play it with my people! It's okay if it's an option but it should not be mandatory. - DRAGONS!!!!!!!It's petty but way back in EDF 4 we got to fight literal dragons, it was fun and activated the mental fantasy of fighting getting to fight a dragon... However in 5 and 6 they appear to have lost the rights to them and it makes me sad. But I will restate here: This is a me thing. - AIR RAIDER THEFTThe Air Raider is a support class whose whole schtick is calling in things and vehicles. In EDF 5 they took many of the cool vehicles and gave it to the Ranger. Do I care? A little, it feels like they are continuously trying to make the Air Raider Ranger adjacent instead of the special little homicide radio that it is. I'm okay with the Ranger having the ability to call in vehicles but I think the cool ones should be reserved for the one who specializes in calling things in. - UNSKIPABLE CUTSCENESSome scenes in the game require you to wait here walk(not run) over there wait even more and either walk(not run) somewhere else or wait for NPC to reach the designated continuation area. My point is it takes to long and unless you are forced to play the mission it's better to skip it. - SINGAnother petty thing and not something I would put much weight on but I miss "THE EDF DEPLOYS", it was fun and I would activate my NPC horde and sing with them.   "To save our mother Earth from any alien attack"   "From vicious giant insects who have once again come back"   "We'll unleash all our forces, we won't cut them any slack"   "The EDF deploys!"PRO: - EQUIPMENT LAYOUTI main a Wing Diver so I will be using them as a basis:  Special Weapons have been moved to a separate slot limiting you to only one. With what gear I have gotten it's fun deciding if a Spear or a Saber is more viable for the mission. I haven't gotten all the weapons(YET) so I won't speak much on that.  - THE MOST ACCURATE REPRESENTATION OF THE MILITARY [Spoiler?]It is one scene in episode one. It takes place after EDF 5 where you kill Alien Buddha and you and your buddies(Why would you play this game alone?(Exception: Grinding)) are sent to a unit that is undermanned and I kid you not! You are in the back corner of the formation in a group ♥♥♥♥ talking everything going on as the Platoon Leader rips into everyone else and ignores you. - BUILDINGS? WHAT BUILDINGS?Do you have line of sight? NO? Bring explosives and remove that direction! Line of sight given. - CHARACTER SYNERGYWhile I have gripes over the Rangers continuous theft from the Air Raider but by and large I believe the different classes have the ability so support each other to compensate for any deficiencies they may have.

There's also a few new weapons, such as the Air Raiders being sort of a drone fleet master now.  It's the best and latest game in the series, no doubt about it.Why so many negative reviews?  Some people are very riled about the fact you currently need the Epic Games store DRM to access it, and the developers made a colossal blunder not mentioning it on the store page on day one. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: Ehhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh..... I'm going to have to taper this review down to a do not recommend. Someone needs to remind Sandlot that they created a video game, which means that success needs to be achievable without instilling masochism. The developers clearly have a significant amount of work to do before the game is playable in an enjoyable sense.  Are the explosions there? Yes. Are the classes exactly the same? Technically, no. The Air Raider uses drones now.... that's literally the only thing that's new. Are there new levels? ...not really. This is basically all EDF's mashed together in an HD remake. The plot is quite interesting, but you're not going to see too many new features. So few, in fact, you probably won't be able to tell the difference between the previous game and this one.Biggest issue to note: Game balance is horrendously awful. Higher-tier end-game weapons are nearly impossible to farm because of how poorly balanced the game is. Discussions across the board are literally only about how to glitch your way through a wall or get the enemy AI pathing stuck in a way that lets you shoot them, not you. There's literally no other way to play the end-game material without tens if not hundreds of hours of repetitive lower-level farming just to get your health up so you can somehow survive the hoards later on to get the final gear. This issue completely takes away from the game, it's not enjoyable anymore because of how rediculously grindy the end of the game is; which is really unfortunate.I'll probably keep playing with my friends for a bit, but our interest is dying pretty quickly because of this horrible balance. How can the devs fix it? Maybe higher drop rates and dropping enemy health just a bit might help.  Or, scale the hoards to the player count. The balance is probably insanely simple, and there's tons of ways to do it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is disregarding the EGS issue. I personally hate EGS and have a bad history with their lackluster account security. If you have an issue with EGS, take that into consideration on if you want the game or not.Devs are currently looking into an alternative after feedback. I practically only play this game couch co-op these days so it doesn't effect me past having some Epic Games online services stuff installed before I launched the game. I also do honestly trust Sandlot, over the years they've been great. Im not upset over their "lack of communication" because they're eastern japanese developers and I'm in a western english audience, this wont float for everyone but they'll have to do more than just that to lose my trust. They definitely seem to care about the backlash and I hope its fixed. So the rest of the review is solely about the game outside of that issue. Again, if that's an issue for you, I'm not telling you to ignore it. I've been planning a sleepover weekend with my nephew for over a year to play this together so I wasnt going to let that ruin it for him and I dont regret it.This game absolutely slaps. I was kind of worried about the setting seeming boring but MAN was I wrong. Some enemies seemed dorky and I wasnt sure I was going to like them, I love them. I've been playing this with my nephew and we call the little android guys nerds. The big androids dorks. They waddle around and look anxious all the time with big heads. It exceeded my highest expectations so far.CLASSES have all been improved as is usually the case. Ranger has a special item slot added, so you can have decoys/grenades/special throwables or bombs there, 2 weapons and either an armor upgrade or vehicle callin. Motorcycles can be used in underground levels which is nice to help them get around faster.Wing Divers have a special weapon slot as well, which does not put a drain on their energy system. These range from "traps" which are little laser beams you can put out which just shoot in a line for a long period of time, getting enemies stuck in their "Get hit" animation. You can put an energy sword in that slot. You can throw out a shield that blocks projectiles. You can launch little homing bolts at nearby enemies. You can toss energy grenades. You can throw out orbs that shoot randomly nearby, you can throw lightning storms, you can throw out an orb that shoots a MASSIVE damage beam after a short delay. That ones my favorite. When I got the glow spear, I realized I could kill practically everything if I could keep them still with a laser, throw it out and then dash away. It feels so badass to pull off. I'm excited to see what insane tools I get late game.Air Raider has... without spoiling, limitations at various stages of the game. Sometimes you cant call in big vehicles, sometimes you cant call in gunship fire. So you have new drone weaponry. Its plays similar to having a gunship like before but little drones go out and shoot the target or suicide bomb things. They're pretty neat, but I've found my favorite strategy with them is to just have swarms of little machine gun drones. You shoot all your beacons on a big enemy and they get peppered to death. It feels like playing a diablo 2 necromancer. I keep being surprised by a lot of the weapon innovation in this. Different styles of drones, some hover around you, some chase enemies down, some attack your beacon. Some you send on bombing runs. The classics still exist, you also have a 3 weapons and a special slot + your vehicle call in. Special slot for the drones that float around you, buff beacons, drones you just activate and it'll go hunt things down. Another class I'm excited to see what all the various options we get are. I'm about 50% through the game on normal right now so things are just starting to get a bit crazy in terms of what weapons you find.The fencer, I havent spent much time on but has the 4 weapon slots, 2 special slots for augmenting your movement/boosts and whatnot. It feels good and it seems like there will be some fun special augments but its just hard to farm weapons for every class so quickly. I did take him for a spin when I got 2 different leg exoskeletons and stacked their movespeed, it was quite funny seeing my legs move so quickly when running down hill.STORY has actually been quite interesting so far. Usually its just b-movie comedy but this time around I'm kinda looking forward to whats happening. Its going somewhere. Without spoiling what happens, the scale of the war picks up quickly. It doesnt just keep having you fight ants for a super long time before any new enemies come out. Escalation happens regularly. A few times you'll have kind of a "this is to tell more story" mission where not much really happens. But elite enemies are introduced kind of quickly this time. Like I said I'm only 50% through the game and I'm already fighting the special versions of most enemies and the escalation just keeps being pumped into the game.MUSIC has actually been quite surprisingly good as well. The EDF 5 mission  select is still there, but depending on certain stages of the story the music in the menu changes. They grew on me a lot, I found the in mission music to be really great in a few stages as well.OVERALL this game is the same as the previous sequels. Its just the last game but better. 5 felt like a natural upgrade from 4..  6 feels like... I'd almost say twice as good as the last. The pacing is better. The weapons are getting crazy faster. Its not 40 levels of ants, you get a lot of variety and new technology and enemies keep being thrown at you.To spoil as little as I can, you even get to relive some of the highlights of 5 over again with all the new mechanics and weapons. And I really didnt mind replaying copy and pasted missions because again, its only the highlights of EDF5. It kind of helped highlight how much more fun this is than 5, having all the new mechanics in an old games mission.This game far exceeds 5. Cant wait for the mission expansion packs. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal game.  The story is actually great this time around and retroactively makes the entire series better and more interesting. At that point there was a massive ahah moment and I fell in love with the story big time.As for gameplay, big improvements in both enemy variants and class balance.  Ranger and wing diver got a backpack slot, in both cases this pushes them to the front of the pack.  The air raider got drones and the fencer has more default dashes and jumps.  The air raider can't use air strikes or all of their vehicles for all missions but this doesn't really make that big of a difference as they really were best at instant killing huge swarms of enemies on large field missions in order grind high level gear.Every 30 missions or so the game revamps all the enemies and missions become layered with tons of varied enemies.  The only thing I personally took issue with was the EGS account requirement and it's not a real account.  It's like a dummy account that only requires your DOB.  It's annoying because achievements shut off mouse and keyboard achievements when they pop up but they are pretty rare so it's not that big of a deal.  Anyway, if you like EDF and can deal with EOS and a dummy Epic games account, it's an awesome game.One final thing to mention, medals for solo and online are one and the same in this version.  As such, if you beat a mission on hard solo it applies to online for completion percentage.  This is nice because if you manage to join someone and get inferno weapons, you can take them into hard mode and just steam roll everything which is nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Following the removal of the epic account linking requirement, via an automatically set up 'dummy' account, this review has been flipped. While at time of writing (10/3/2024) the game still coughs up an error when launched with EOS removed, it does function without it for single player and multiplayer. (only crossplay being EOS dependent)This being fixed, EDF 6 is EDF 5+++ (and modders have literally ported all of EDF 5 into it.) in terms of plot and mechanics. There are some minor gameplay changes I disliked. (Air Raider losing turrets to Ranger) but a couple of positive changes I do like as well. (The auto reloading weapons, Air Raider's new drone attacks making it more viable underground/without support elements.) Because of the modders work, EDF 6 is a viable alternative to EDF 5 if you just want the entire story in one place and with slightly adjusted balance. That said, EDF 5 runs on Steam's multiplayer servers, so while it lacks crossplay it's not going to complain each time you open it up about EOS being missing.On the whole and considering a patch (or a mod) can disable the complaint popup easily, EDF 6 is a solid recommendation from me. Truly over the top weapons, insane scope of combat and goofy B movie storytelling fully willing to take it's farce seriously. It's a small step forward to a better EDF, and for those who did play EDF 5 and recall the campaign's plot points, 6 has more impact and ends with more of a triumphant feeling of finally wrecking their efforts for good.original review below:(Was) Unlisted requirement and install of Epic Online Services, a known mal/spyware issue. While I already have it on my computer so it doesn't concern me as a risk, this is a deceptive business practice. Additionally, an epic account (linked to your steam account) is required for online play with or without crossplay. While a 'dummy' account will be setup if you don't have one to link, it's still an external tie to your steam account leading through a security risk 'service' that you were never told ahead of time would be installed. (Which is a definition of malware, software you were not informed would be installed and run. It autoruns on startup of your computer by default.) The  game can't even be played single player if you block EOS from running on your computer.This makes the game quality itself irrelevant to most people, hence my ability to review it with 6 minutes of (non) playtime. Just long enough to confirm the above information.

_childDocuments_.review: The EDF 6 gameplay is no doubt excellent as expected. The addition of backpack slot means you can bring utility equipment without sacrificing firepower. The throwable equipment got a major improvement, they now have much better handling. The missions are much more fast-paced. No more spending 2-3 missions showcasing a new enemy type. The game will be throwing kitchen sinks at your team, and you are expected to overcome the challenge. There are some critiques that missions are just EDF 5 rerun, but in actuality those missions are more like the same missions with an interesting twist (no spoiler).Overall the game is great, but there are LOTS of technical issues that need to be addressed:-Since EDF 6 runs on Epic server for "crossplay reason", there are rampant desync issues which were non-existent in previous EDF titles. For instance, teammates may appear to shooting at the ground aimlessly. In some cases, you might witness your teammates falling off a ledge or phasing through buildings, but they are actually not.  While these issues are not necessary game-breaking, they are highly noticeable to the point where the desync issues are disruptive/ nuisance. - For some unknown dumb reason, you lose keyboard/ controller input for 5-8 seconds whenever Epic achievement popup happens. If you happen to earn any achievements while fending off the bug swarms, congratulations you are now dead.-The worst of all, there are rampant crashes. Although players' experience may vary, these crashes are both chronic / random in nature. The crashes wouldn't be a big issue if it weren't for the fact that EDF still refuses to introduce RECONNECT feature. For a 2024 (technically 2022) game with hiked price tag, it is an outright embarrassment at this point. Imagine sweating yourself in a long difficult mission just to crash right near the end, receiving nothing and have to do all that over? That's just a combination for bad gameplay experience.Until the dev addresses these technical issues especially the crashes, I would not recommend this game to anyone at the current game state.

_childDocuments_.review: Earth Defense Force 6 is likely the best one I've played so far, (I've played 4.1, 5, Iron Rain and WB.) and I will explain why.-----[OVERVIEW]-----There is one thing to get out of the way, and that is EOS or "Epic Online Service" which at this point in time is currently required to use to play online in EDF6. This is because it allows cross-play between steam and epic users. It is likely a turn off for many people, however I found that it was very unintrusive, you don't need Epic Games Store, or Launcher, which is good. Supposedly it also allows crossplay between PS5 and PS4.But most people are concerned about Epic being intrusive and stealing data (which yes, is a worry!) However the good thing is that by using EOS like this, EOS will only be able to see what is *PUBLICLY AVAILABLE* on your account. If you do not have an Epic account, it will simply prompt you upon joining multiplayer to make an account, you only need to put in a Date of Birth, and it will tie your Steam account to a brand new Epic account. They won't even require an email, nor do they know what email you used for the Steam account, so it is very unintrusive.EDF 6 is very much like EDF 5 in feel, but many things in the game have been vastly improved such as enemy variety, mission variety, amount of enemies, amount of weapons, etc. If I were to introduce someone to EDF this is the game I would do it with.I will also note that I am CURRENTLY on Mission 33 "Winged Legion"-----[GAMEPLAY]-----EDF 6 has made many improvements to all classes which are highly noticeable and change a lot of their kits for the better. The changes made to each class makes solo play far easier and enjoyable, along with allowing you to make even better builds. This has made gameplay across the board far more enjoyable. We will go over each class and I will note changes that I personally feel in the game, or the most important ones.--[RANGER]--The backpack slot is IMMENSELY useful, alongside various weapons just feeling better. I no longer feel like I need to run Shotgun + Sniper or Shotgun + Rocket Launcher or GL for the entire game now, which is a HUGE improvement.Let's talk more about that backpack slot though. It is just amazing. It allows you to use grenades, turrets, claymores, bombs, etc, which has made Ranger feel a lot more cohesive and better. No longer do you have to sacrifice using something potentially more viable for a more niche solution. Personally I very much enjoy the fire grenades, as they provide very good uses, but find myself using claymores and even stationary bombs sometimes.The various weapons that ranger get also feel good across the board, along with the vehicles and other support utilities he has. Overall it is a massive increase in enjoyment for ranger and I love playing him so far.--[FENCER]--I also absolutely love Fencer in this game! You get stock 2 forward and jump boosts, which helps a lot in the early game and also allows you more freedom with loadouts, no longer do you have to use dash boosters and jump boosters to get more mobillity, which I felt like was required in EDF 5, especially for my type of playstyle.Aside from that, melee and ranged both feel very good in this game so far, I particularly like the power blade, especially since it has a jump boost which allows you to use another melee to have forward jump boosts (which increase your speed a lot.)I am also enjoying the various ranged weapons a lot, particularly the mortars having aiming lasers and markers for where they will hit are amazing! The gatling gun changes also make them feel a lot better, with them firing immediately and ramping up over time. Overall Fencer feels amazing and I actually main him the most. Especially in solo play.--[WING DIVER]--I am also loving Wing Diver's new backpack slot. Those superweapons and more niche weapons that you couldn't really use in 4.1 and 5 now have an amazing use as a utility! The new spears, sabers, and shields also feel very good, along with the various grenades.As of the moment I do not feel very much changes with a lot of her weapons, although that isn't bad as they feel good, however I do notice a decently large change in her cores, I have to be a fair bit more conservative with my flight and weapon use, although again that isn't bad, it just means you have to play a little more carefully.Overall Wing Diver feels pretty good.--[AIR RAIDER]--This one is controversial, and for good reason.Air Raider got a LOT of changes in this game. He now has drones that allow him to use strikes in missions that he couldn't, he also now has 1 support slot which means that you can no longer stack a guard and power post on a vehicle to have vehicle centric gameplay, but to be completely honest, I always preferred strikes more and only in niche situations would I use PP + GP for vehicles. STRIKES! That is what Air Raider is most known for, the large, flashy, high damage air strikes, whether it be spritefall, cannons, bombs, etc. Most of them were nerfed, particularly things that require reloads now take 2-3x as long, going to 30+ second cooldowns and even larger sometimes, but I do not think these are bad changes. People will complain and say that Air Raider got GUTTED by these changes and is a WORTHLESS CLASS when compared to the rest because the large strikes were nerfed a tad, but they still do a large amount of damage and can completely wipe out enemies, however you can no longer brain-dead spam strikes until the entire screen is nuked. Which is why I think it is good, you now have to use your brain more and play more strategically.Drones, which are a new addition are very welcome. They give the air raider a very reliable (and viable, despite what other people say,) response to opponents. They might not do the most damage, but they are very fast and spammable because they are not on a reload or a credit system, it is on a system where you send the drone out, they do the strike, and it comes back. The drones feel absolutely amazing and I love them.Vehicles! Again, with the strikes people will complain that vehicles feel terrible and they got "ABSOLUTELY GUTTED AND ARE WORTHLESS NOW!!!!" but to be completely honest, vehicles in this game are still perfectly viable and are just fine. Sure, some vehicles may feel like they don't have a lot of ammo, but the point of a vehicle in my opinion is to not stay in it the entire match, unless it is a particularly large one. If we are talking about a blacker, helicopter, or other light vehicles, you were not supposed to stay in it the entire mission and farm kills, they are more of a utility thing that grants you a lot of mobility and has the benefit of guns attached. They feel amazing in this game so far.-----[ENEMIES!]-----Enemies in this game have a lot more variety and a lot of the big hitters from previous games come out far, far faster which is a little scary and very VERY fun. There have been a lot of moments where I was genuinely surprised they had an enemy that was considered a boss enemy very early in the game, I will not spoil much, which is why the enemy review will be pretty small, but overall it feels a lot better than in previous games.-----[Mission Design]-----The mission design in EDF 6 is fairly similar to the ones of EDF 4.1 and 5, except for the ruined missions at the start. Aside from that I am enjoying it so far, of course this may change based on me getting further into the game.-----[Story]-----So far I haven't been able to piece the story together very well but it has been highly interesting to listen to the dialogues of various NPCs. Compared to 4.1 and 5 there is much more things in it so far.So far, I am enjoying this game a lot and hope more people can also enjoy it. I have also had no performance issues and enjoy the small graphic increases. I would definitely recommend getting this game and playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is not a review bombing because of Epic. Is this game fun? Yes! will i play it probably over 100 hours? Very most likely! but do i think it is worth this price? Definitely not... EDF 6 is (in my opinion) exactly the same as EDF 5, but with a few new enemies, guns and way more issues. I havent played that much yet and definitely havent got through even half the missions, but the glitches, horrible D-sync in online coop and the disgusting disreguard of details (either its for a "joke" or not) is, in my opinion, unnacceptable for such a high priced game. I think people would be better of with getting EDF 5 with less issues than this one.Issues noted: - The constant massive D-sync in coop, which can easily cause friendly fire because you simply dont really know where your allies are. - The Epic achievements who completely lock your cam for a few seconds and you cant aim at all - Enemies glitching and teleporting everywhere in online coop, even when you are the host. - The subtitles/text bubbles being completely wrong (some peoples says its intentional as a "joke" but i just think its very bad) - A very big part of it is entirely copy-pasted from EDF 5 (same weapons, same map, same enemies, same spawn waves, ect.) - they made the first mission a "tutorial" which is infinitely worse than in EDF 5 and made it mandatory online too instead of only offline like in EDF 5 (you are just stuck in unskippable cutscenes and talking for 10 mins and if you arent the host, you dont even get to shoot your weapons in the target shooting part)Once again, the game itself is really fun and i definitely will play it alot, but i think this is extremely overpriced for such an "unrefined" game in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Regarding the Epic Games account requirement, I was wary at first since I bought this to play with my friends online, but it turned out to be a non-issue.There is a popup the first time you log in to online Multiplayer (but not single-player or local Co op) that requests you log into epic.  However if you don't have an account you can sign in with your Steam account instead with one button press. You don't even have to give Epic a username or e-mail.So far I haven't been asked for anything Epic related a second time so I think it's just a one and done thing.As for the game itself, it's pretty much just EDF 5 again but the action ramps up way faster. You're fighting mother monsters in the first few missions.I typically play fencer, and the only issue I have seen so far is some wonky hit boxes using blasthole spears against frogs. It works fine on every other monster but sometimes passes through frogs.Other than that the game is great.Edit after finishing game: After completing the whole game co op with a buddy, I can gladly recommend this game. Sure, it contains a lot of what was in EDF 5, but they are constantly changing things from mission to mission and you are always on your toes.  The story is as incoherent as ever, but if you pay attention, you just might understand what the heck is going on by the final mission. Of course no one is here for the story in EDF. We want bugs and robots in the thousands to kill and EDF6 delivers that in spades.If you're just looking for more EDF, especially with the intention of playing co op with a buddy or two, this is an easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Soo, to my understanding a majority of the negative reviews are based on the requirements of the 3rd party account and the lack of that being stated during advertising and frankly, yes that's BS. You never should require a 3rd party account for anything you purchase on Steam and I stand by that line of thinking. However, that sentiment has nothing to do with the game or game play to which I frankly find myself enjoying very much. To my understanding this is also not really an entirely "new" entry into the EDF series seeing as how other reviews have mentioned it encompasses the previous entries' missions in it. So with that in mind, EDF veterans will probably want to wait for a sale but an EDF noob such as myself has immensely enjoyed all 147 missions and after roughly 40 hours of play time I find myself still booting it up after work because It's very well made. Polished with network features that don't suck and disconnect every 2 seconds. It's very refreshing to play a "new" release that functions at launch. (new in quotes because I get that it's been live in Japan for some time so this isn't really new but locally translated)The 4 classes all kick ass in their own ways and are satisfying with a very diverse roster of equipment to cater to different missions and play styles. Enemy variety is very spaced out as well with the re skins only popping up late in the game and not very prevalent on top of that. In fact I was shocked at how many new enemy types I was running into in the late game. As soon as I thought I had seen the whole bag of tricks there was something new. Difficulty feels fair and is usually your fault for not packing the proper weaponry or equipment to deal with the threats you'll be facing. So yea, I have no complaints as far as the gameplay is concerned. It's very much a turn off your brain and shoot the alien monsters for hours on end type game and I find that extremely enjoyable. Especially with no sweaty PvP to have to find a meta build to deal with.The 3rd party account requirement really does kinda sour the whole experience. If it wasn't for that ONE thing I would sing the praises from the heavens. Though as it stands that's just something that you, the consumer, will have to decide if you're willing to deal with or not. In closing, Wing Diver is life.

_childDocuments_.review: How I wish Steam had a "neutral" review score. I just... can't recommend this game. Not at full price. Not even if you are a die-hard EDF fan. Look, without too many spoilers there is an in-lore/universe reason why we end up replaying a *ton* of EDF 5. Far too much of it. But that's not a good excuse for recycling old content in a full-priced release. I could almost forgive it, if *so much* of this game didn't feel like padding. The denizens of the EDF 6 world have about two brain cells to share. The dialogue is atrocious. The songs are insanely bad. If the developers are going to recycle so much from the previous entry, why mess with the songs? Who thought any of that was a good idea?That doesn't even get into how bad, at least in my opinion, many of the new enemies feel barebones or like reskins of others. So few are actually enjoyable to fight. Even fewer have interesting mechanics that don't get horrendously unfun the further into the story you get. I just finished mission 123 and holy hell was that horrendous game design. There are so many instances throughout the game where you just wish you could force the game developers into a small room and prevent them from leaving until they can prove they actually playtested their game without cheats. I'm not saying the MK II/III drone missions and the underground hive missions are impossible, just that they're not balanced to any real degree, or even fun to play through. That doesn't even cover how terrible the ally NPC AI or health are. Literal corpses would serve as more effective and helpful meat shields.Is the gameplay fun? Absolutely, at least when you're not dealing with the above-mentioned missions. Is the co-op fun? Yes, at least when people aren't crashing or desyncs occur. Are the weapons cool? Yes, at least the ones that didn't get removed from certain classes. It's like every positive I have has to come with a caveat. EDF 6 needed more time in the oven. And a better game design team to give it a second pass.Please try and get this game on a sale. Even if you're a long-time fan. It's not a bad game. I just don't think it's worth $60.

_childDocuments_.review: Comment:EDF 6 is definitely not intended as an upgrade to EDF 5, as much as it's trying to be more of the game a lot of people came to love... EDF with some modifications and new weapons.The First Major issue:The first 13 missions are designed as a sort of story focused/tutorial to the game, which I can definitely see why it could push people to refund, these missions felt like they relied heavily on multiplayer to make them fun, the story section of these was very jumpy mission to mission.To get past these missions will long push you over your refund period, which really isn't the best design.When does the game get good:Outside of that once you get past mission 13 you can start using vehicles and better/fun weapons that will result in both the Aliens and your demise. There have been some great additions I've seen so far, whoever was thinking up the newer weapon designs had some fun.Commentary:The commentary is about the same, as EDF 5 was, quirky and funny where it counts while also having some side comments to give a perspective of the current situation of the world around you. Overall I enjoy it, however around half of it doesn't make sense in the first 13 missions, mainly the comments on civilians as there are no civilians around during these missions. Not sure if they were originally intended to exist in these missions or not.Epic Games:The choice to use Unreal Engine/Epic's multiplayer infrastructure was an interesting choice, forcing people to have an account with it without informing the player base even when it's well known Epic has burnt a lot of bridges with the PC market was definitely not an informed decision to make. Epic's multiple attempts to try and forcibly pull players to use their market and infra even when their Epic Game store front runs horribly has caused this divide. Bugs:The only bugs I've seen so far outside of the need for netcode improvements, is enemies shots going through small terrain obstacles, and the (wing diver and air raider) shields that are supposed to block them every now and then making using cover worthless on higher difficulties with low max health (This happens relatively consistently). Some times dying instantly as if being hit by a explosion with no explosion nearby (only had this once), so there is definitely some issues even when playing solo online.Conclusion:I do recommend getting EDF 6 if you enjoyed 5, if you didn't enjoy 5, you aren't going to enjoy 6.This game is plain and simple more EDF fun for a group of friend to play. It's a lot of chaotic fun.The game's first 13 missions should be played with friends if you want to enjoy them, otherwise find some time where your bored and go through them.Make sure to turn off notifications on Epic's social, as any notification will make you lose control of the game for a few seconds

I'll still give it a positive review though since lots of the new enemies are interesting and fun to fight. Boiled down, the pros of the game are:-Cool new enemies-Cool new toys to play with-Some missions have interesting twists on them if you played EDF 5.-Really good soundtrack-The story is pretty interesting in some partsMixed parts:-While many of the QoL improvements among the classes are nice, still really hoping this game would have much more considering it is the sixth iteration of the main games.-Cons:-Lot's of re-used missions from EDF 5 and voice lines that get annoying. _childDocuments_.review: SECOND UPDATE:  Devs have finally made good on their promise to remove the requirement of an EGS account to play online, it's now optional.  As stated, I will change my review back to positive.  I'll be updating the end of it to include my experiences of the game since then.UPDATE:  Devs / publishers looking into the EGS aspect to change it if possible.  If it is changed to at least be unobtrusive (not need a separate account for it) then I will change my review to positive, but not until then.First and foremost:This game requires an Epic Games Store (EGS) account to play Multiplayer and requires Epic Online Services (EOS) to be installed to play the offline single-player campaign.  This was NOT announced or present on their store page until AFTER release.  This right now is the only reason I am rating this negatively.I really like this game.  It's EDF as you'd expect - a direct sequel to EDF 5, where you continue to play as Storm-1, the hero of the Earth who defeated the alien supreme commander.  5 years pass and you start off with a rookie squad cleaning up some remnants of the invaders.Many systems are carried over from 5 - armor is applied in some smaller amounts to other classes you don't play as, and you can unlock and upgrade some weapons for those other non-played classes in missions.I haven't had a chance to play much, but the biggest disappointment (other than the aforementioned EGS fiasco) is the opening level is again slow and unengaging.  Most EDF games throw you into the fray from the get-go - a horde of bugs after maybe 30 seconds of exposition at most.  EDF 5 had you go through an actual mini-tutorial, followed by a lot of running around while they do plot setup in a sense, with maybe 30 bugs through the whole mission.  6 continues this approach with a long, drawn-out walk through corridors, listening to a captain demean his green recruits, and then run off to practice some shooting before "oh no, aliens again!"  The first few missions also start relatively slow - you start with the frog men and fight maybe 20 in each mission before you finally get to bugs around mission 3.Overall, it is a good recommendation - but the score is negative due to the EGS incident.  If you want EDF without EGS, pick up 4.1, 5, or Iron Rain.UPDATED REVIEW:  So, I've finished the game's stoy, and it is incredibly awesome.  You won't need to have played 5 for it, but like all good games playing it makes it about 100% more epic, as you go back to that game's earliest moments and do something amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like EDF, you already know and have been keeping up on this for the last couple years in Japan, it good 👍If you don't know EDF, it's old sci-fi B-horror movies and Kaiju films mashed together in a class based coop shooter that emphasizes enemy count and giving the player a ton of interesting weapons to blow everything (and themselves) up with- with a gratuitous amount of overly cheesy voice acting to love.It is one of those series that has some everlasting jank that long time fans struggle to notice but new players may furrow a brow at, if a weird control default here and a repetitive mission there are deal breakers from the get go then I understand.But if you are willing to give the game an inch, it will give you a gameplay experience that's hooked so many of us over the years.There's just nothing else out there that really comes close to what EDF accomplishes- it aims for a specific flavor and it NAILS it.There's plenty more to say but little reason to say much of it:I recommend EDF 6.I also recommend 4.1 and 5 for anyone looking to try at a discounted price (4.1 is like 20 bucks default as of typing and both go on sale from time to time).The series is a very iterative one where sequels are less major shake ups and are more "A step up" each time, usually focusing on new QOL, more mission variety and ideas tested, and adjusting the balance / weapon identity of the 4 classes a touch between entries.So basically, 6 is the most QOL filled one and has the latest collection of "new ideas" but if you were to try 4.1 or 5 you would definitely "get the idea" of what EDF is just fine and (hopefully) have a blast :)EDF! _childDocuments_.review: I have a deep love for the Earth Defense Force series, but as much as it pains me to say, this latest installment, Earth Defense Force 6, falls short in many ways. As expected, the story remains lackluster with cringeworthy voice acting, but that's not why we play these games. Essentially, this game is almost identical to EDF 4 and 5, with only a few minor quality-of-life improvements. Unfortunately, the developers didn't put much effort into the PC port. There are only three graphics settings available, and unlike the previous installment, widescreen support is missing, which is disappointing. (Letterbox does not count with the stretched to fit screen.)Despite these flaws, the core essence of the game remains intact—blowing up hordes of bugs with friends. I don't have strong feelings about the Epic Games Services like some others do, but I can't recommend this game at full price if you already own and enjoy EDF 4 and 5. It’s essentially the same experience. If you have money to spare and are looking for more of the same fun, then go ahead, but be prepared for a sense of déjà vu, as many of the levels and lines feel recycled.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a fan of edf5, or least found it fun, you will enjoy this one too. It's everything that made edf5 great, and then some. They made some great improvements to the overall gameplay and graphics, and it is a brand new story. It is not just "edf5 but bells and whistles". This is its own game and exactly what I expect a sequel to be. A new story, and the game is everything I liked from before while addressing all the problems I had. If you never played edf5, you'll be really confused and won't get the full experience. It expects you played the game before it. The game itself is still a blast, especially with some buddies, as it has an online pve mode (a bit of a rarity these days). Just expect to be very lost.Edf6 is absolutely NOT just "edf5" again. While it uses some of the same missions (which is for story related reasons), most of it is completely new, or altered content. The graphics are improved from 5. The 60 fps thing is lame, but that's typical of Japanese pc games. I don't really have an opinion over Epic as they're fixing it, other than i believe it is causing desyncing issues online, but nothing that renders it unplayable for us so far. Also mission 1 is just dreadful, devs please change it. If you enjoyed 5, I absolutely recommend 6. If you were eh on 5, you might still enjoy 6 as while it's got the same beats, it fixes some of the issues from 5 too. If you never played edf before, 6 is a super fun game to play with friends, just expect to have no idea what's going on in the story because it's a direct continuation of 5. I personally believe I already got my money's worth, it's been a treat for me and my friends, and we still got an insane amount of content to go.8/10, it has some small issues and the Epic integration was unnecessary, but the game is an absolute blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm three hours in. I hate spending full price on video games... but I can't resist EDF, it's impossible. I waited as long as I could for a sale but I can wait no longer.It's worth it. This is definitely the best one yet, and I don't understand the criticism of it being "not much different than EDF5". None of the Sandlot EDF games are much different from each other and you know what you're getting into when you click "purchase".  That's part of their charm.I've been playing since 2006 with Earth Defense Force 2017 on 360 (18 years ago...my god. Zoomers, enjoy your time in this mortal realm for it only speeds up the closer you are to death) and this is the most "refined" experience yet, with all the jank perfection you came for. If you never played EDF games before, maybe wait for a sale. If you have played EDF before, you won't regret spending 60 bucks on this as EDF6 is as good or better than 4.1 and 5. For those who haven't played an EDF before, it's impossible not to have fun with this game. You kill waves of giant monsters and unlock new weapons, that's the entire loop.Finally, I want to say the dialogue is incredible. You would assume with the cult audience these games have built over the last 18 years that they would start becoming self aware and the dialogue would suffer, but it's still earnestly b-movie glorious and will have you smirking at worst and LOLing at best.My only criticism is that we can't unlock the framerate over 60 on PC, and the continued lack of graphics settings on this PC version... but it runs very well so I can't complain too much.Looking forward to EDF 7! You rock Sandlot, keep being you.

_childDocuments_.review: \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/   \/.... First and foremost, yes, when the game came out, they didn't mention anywhere on Steam about the fact that for someone to play the game, they would need an Epic Game Account. They fixed it after a couple hours of being out, but I understand that some people felt like, because it wasn't published on release, the game should receive a bad review, and personally I don't have an opinion. I get the idea that having to authenticate twice might be bad; if you get locked out of one account, you get locked out of playing the game you paid for, and I get that. But I feel like, to some, they have a bad taste in their mouth due to having a previous history of that happening to them. I never had that happen to myself, and I can imagine if that did happen, I would be pissed..... Some people think that a game that was originally released in Japan in 2022 and then publically released in 2024 on July 25 deserves better graphics, and personally, I can look past the fact that EDF 6 looks the same as EDF 5, and some people will say that EDF 6 looks worse, but that's simply a lie. EDF as a series isn't about high-quality graphics; it's about killing a bunch of enemies and how many enemies you can fit on the screen at the same time. It's a simple concept.  .... To skip the bullsh*t, get the game on sale. If you want to continue reading, feel free. To fallow my previous point, people feel like 60$US (80$CAN) is too much. And I'll be honest, it is a bit expensive for basically a remaster of previous titles, while also being more polished and has more missions. Personally, this feels like a 40$US (60$CAN) game. .... Let's get right into it, all perivous games, we're locked at 60fps. The framerate is locked at 60 fps, and to some, that's bad, and I get it. When you constantly play at 120 fps, you can definitely feel a difference; it almost feels laggy without the lag. And as of right now, there isn't a fix or patch, so if you don't like 60 fps, don't get this game. For most, if not all, of the EDF franchise, the FPS is locked at 60 fps, so if you want to play EDF in any way (4.1, 5, or 6), you'll need to get over that obstacle.  .... Probably the simplest argument *Wrong*. The game, to some, will feel repetitive. Not just the fighting, but the fact that you're fighting the same enemies. I guess that's an argument. Some people are going to bring up previous entries and completely skim over the fact that almost every element that isn't in EDF 6 was DLC and not base game, so expecting DLC content in future games is a bit of a stretch. But besides that, wanting new enemies in your new game is a valid point, but EDF 6 does have new enemies. To continue, EDF 6 has almost the same amount of enemies combined comparatively to both EDF 5 and EDF 4.1 (EDF 5 and 4.1 = 54 enemies / EDF 6 = 45). It also has the most missions of any EDF game in the franchise, with a total of 147 missions, not even counting DLC. And I know a lot of you are going to bring up the fact that some of the missions are reused content, and personally, I don't care; it makes sense . If you're going to complain, do so by complaining about the story, if anything, because that's a genuine argument.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing EDF for a long time now, and I can say, without question, that EDF 6 is the biggest jump in quality between previous games, and in my opinion is currently the best EDF available. At first, I was worried about the Epic integration, as I did not have an account and am generally wary of their business practices, but all I had to do to access the online multiplayer and create a steam-linked account was put in my birthday. IMO, if all Epic is doing is supporting online servers, not requiring me to get their launcher or even verify an email it's no real bother, even though I can absolutely understand the hesitation.As far as gameplay goes, once again, EDF 6 is in my opinion the greatest in the series. More so than any of the other titles, each type of weapon is viable and the balancing feels great, allowing for much more player choice in designing loadouts. I'm sure any other longtime fencers can think to when they discovered dash canceling and realized most of their arsenal was hardly viable, but I found myself using shields, dual melee weapons, and many other weapons and weapon types that in previous games I felt I just couldn't make work. The improvements and balancing extends to the other classes as well, as I've played a few missions on each of them now, and they all offer unique and fun new ways to eviscerate alien invaders.Graphics aren't normally something an EDF fan can rave about. The game does essentially look just like the previous game, perhaps with some lighting improvements, new enemy designs and more impressive setpieces, but the big improvement in this installment is in the level design. The ruined city map the game starts in is practically an order of magnitude more detailed than previous games' maps, pockmarked with craters exposing underground pipes and filled with half crumbling and destroyed buildings. It truly finally feels like seeing the city in the aftermath of destroying it for a whole game :)The translations and story of EDF has alway come off as kinda corny or like a satire lost in translation, bu this game actually seems like it has a plot and i am surprised to find myself really engaged with it as the game does a really good job of making you ask questions (some of them being age old EDF questions ive been asking myself, such as the confusing timelines and irregularities between games), and I genuinely can't wait to get to the bottom of it. The voice acting is pretty much par for course, barring a couple absolutely egregious takes for the EDF infantry song. That one actually really disappointed me, as small of a gripe it is in the face of everything great about the game.To sum up my thoughts on EDF 6, where the other games in line felt more like large updates, this game is the first in the series to feel like an actual sequel. To a longtime fan such as myself its almost like water in a desert and I have never been happier with how EDF plays and feels. It disappoints me to see the amount of discontent around the Epic integration as in this case it is very inobtrusive and isn't coercing the playerbase into switching platforms. My only hope is that the controversy is eventually resolved and more people can join me in enjoying my favorite installment of one of my longtime favorite game series.

detailed_description: Think you and your bestie can take on any challenge together? We’d like to see you try! This new bite-sized standalone We Were Here experience will really put your friend ship to the test. To prove that your friend ship can overcome anything, you will need to take on several puzzling challenges. It’s all about Communication , Teamwork … and Trust . Talk together, work together, and most of all, believe in your friend. The two of you are alone at sea when pursuing a distress call leads you to a deserted island, where you encounter a mysterious boat ride in an abandoned amusement park. This is a voyage you won’t forget, with puzzles that take two to solve. The state of your friendship will directly affect the state of your friend-ship! Be aware, this is an actual test as you’ll be graded on how well you solve these puzzles! Will friendship truly last forever? Or is this friend- ship sinking to the bottom of the ocean? We Were Here ‘Expedition’ Series From the makers of the renowned We Were Here Series comes the bite-sized We Were Here Expeditions! _childDocuments_.review: Total Mayhem Games returns with "We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip," the latest installment in their beloved co-op adventure series. While building upon the foundations of its predecessors, this entry introduces significant changes and promises to be the first in a series of shorter games. Despite the shorter playtime, "The FriendShip" delivers an entertaining and rewarding experience for two players, with improved graphics and refined gameplay mechanics.Familiar fans of the "We Were Here" franchise will find themselves right at home, but newcomers need not worry as prior knowledge is not a requirement. The game follows two explorers, clad in arctic expedition attire as seen in previous entries, as they embark on a new journey. This time, the setting shifts from the eerie subterranean castles to a pirate-themed amusement park situated in icy waters. Gone is the previous storyline involving the Jester and the King, replaced by a charismatic yet judgmental pirate captain who communicates through mechanized wooden cutouts scattered throughout the park. The captain's objective is to assess the duo's ability to collaborate effectively, hinting at a greater task they must undertake in the future.The game begins with an intense cutscene of the explorers navigating stormy waters to track a signal. Upon arriving at the island hosting the amusement park, players are tasked with solving a puzzle to gain entry, serving as a tutorial for the game's controls – standard for free-roaming first-person 3D titles. "The FriendShip" consists of three trials, each designed to test communication, teamwork, and trust.Each trial presents a unique challenge. Notably, players are not obligated to complete entire puzzles to progress through the game, a refreshing departure from previous entries. For instance, the first trial separates players into different rooms, requiring them to describe the pose of a wooden puppet within a time limit. Players must communicate effectively to press the correct button based on their descriptions. This sequence can be repeated up to fifteen times, with the timer decreasing with each iteration. While this might sound repetitive, each round lasts only a few seconds, allowing the entire sequence to be completed in minutes. Importantly, players who struggle with timed puzzles need not worry, as only the initial puzzle must be finished. Subsequent failures, intentional or not, bring the puzzle to a close. Based on the number of completed puzzles, teams receive bronze, silver, or gold tickets from a dispensing machine. Players can then choose whether to proceed or reattempt the puzzle for a better score, catering to both puzzle enthusiasts and those looking to advance.When ready to move on, players insert their ticket into a machine, upgrading their amusement park boat with cosmetic enhancements. The game tallies the results of each challenge, offering a summary screen at the end.In addition to the timed puppet puzzle, "The FriendShip" features two major sequences. One involves players separated by a wall, each with a game board on their side and a selection of tiles. Placing tiles on the boards scores points, but players must decipher the connection between the boards, emphasizing teamwork and communication. The game intensifies as players take turns placing tiles and forming color groups. Points determine the ticket quality – bronze, silver, or gold. Here, players can replay the mini-game for a higher score.The third sequence is a trust exercise. One player oversees an obstacle course while the other navigates it, hallucinated by a gas. The navigator relies on the overseer's guidance to tackle increasingly challenging obstacles. This trial stands out as a test of clear communication to overcome hazards. The course evolves from simple wooden paths to moving platforms, with hallucinations adding complexity. Players must trust the overseer's directions entirely, as they can't distinguish real paths from illusions. As the course progresses, the navigator's vision becomes increasingly distorted, making teamwork essential. Successfully completing this section is an achievement in cooperative play.Visually, "The FriendShip" represents a notable step up in the "We Were Here" series. Character models, especially for the two protagonists, boast higher polygon counts, and textures have improved. Details like stitching on gloves and intricate mechanical devices add depth to the environment. A central canal connecting puzzle areas resembles a Disney ride, providing aesthetic appeal. While the default graphics settings are set to their lowest, increasing them enhances the game's visual richness.However, the default field of view remains problematic, causing screen stretching at the edges. Players can adjust this setting to mitigate the distortion. The new setting and storyline provide a fresh perspective, moving away from the previous tale of the Jester and the King. The captain's character is effectively voiced, evoking a mix of joy, smugness, and foreboding.Audio design complements the environment, with steampunk-inspired sounds and splashing water during boat rides. The instrumental music adds a melodic backdrop without overpowering player communication.The game allows players to communicate via in-game radios, with one player holding a button to speak through their microphone. While only one player can talk at a time, third-party chat applications provide more flexibility for conversation. Effective communication is essential to the game's success."We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip" offers a promising start to a new series within the franchise. Despite its shorter length, it provides a satisfying and enjoyable experience, with the option to bypass puzzles when desired. The diversity among the three major puzzle sections keeps the gameplay fresh without feeling repetitive. The introduction of a new narrative makes this entry accessible to both newcomers and longtime fans. Whether new or returning, team up with a friend and embark on this exciting co-op adventure through a pirate-themed amusement park.

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here: The Friendship stands out for its innovative cooperative puzzle-solving gameplay, requiring players to rely heavily on communication and teamwork. The game's unique approach to co-op play offers an engaging and memorable experience that differs from typical multiplayer games.The setting is immersive and atmospheric, enhancing the sense of adventure and mystery as players navigate through the game. This setting, combined with an engaging narrative that unfolds through gameplay, makes for a compelling experience.The game's design strongly emphasizes teamwork and communication, which is both a pro and a con. For players who enjoy working closely with others, this can be highly rewarding. However, for those who prefer solo play or have difficulty with constant communication, this aspect might be less appealing.One downside is the limited replay value. Once the puzzles are solved, the game may offer little incentive to replay, as the solutions become known. Additionally, some players might find the puzzle difficulty uneven, which could lead to moments of frustration or confusion.In conclusion, We Were Here: The Friendship is an excellent choice for players seeking a unique co-op experience that challenges both their problem-solving skills and their ability to work as a team. The game's immersive environment and narrative add depth to the puzzle-solving mechanics. However, its reliance on player communication and uneven puzzle difficulty may not appeal to all players, and its replay value is limited. Despite these drawbacks, the game offers a distinct and memorable experience in the realm of cooperative gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions: The Friendship is a two person co-op puzzle game where you must work with a friend to escape an abandoned amusement park. There are three different puzzle rooms that must be solved via communication with your partner. Overall, I found this title to be the best of the entire series, which is somewhat amusing given it was free for a weekend and of the titles listed for a price, it's the cheapest. It is relatively short (comparable to the first title in the series, which is/has been always free to play). Whereas other titles in this series feature much less clear puzzles, each puzzle in this game was more obvious. Now, you might think that takes away some of the fun, but I found it didn't. Instead, it allows you to focus on solving the puzzle as opposed to trying to figure out what the puzzle even is to begin with. One playthrough took ~2 hours and a second playthrough for achievements (getting the max score for each puzzle) took another ~2 hours (mostly due to some RNG in the second puzzle). If a co-op puzzle game sounds like something you'd enjoy, I'd recommend this game. That said, I definitely recommend playing the original as it is free and will give you a good sense of the type of gameplay you'll be getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: The world is at a standstill: Do we fear the impending doom of unstable modern-day capitalistic empires built upon lies, deceit and economic influence far beyond our wildest imagination? Or do we fear ourselves and the prospect of changing not because we want but because it is required for us to change in order to survive society as it presents itself nowadays? We were here but at what cost? The friendships we made were the expeditions that taught us lessons, lessons that will cease to exist once we're gone. As modern philosopher and artist Sergio Giavanni Kitchens says, in one of his masterpieces: "Crank up the foreign, I swerve. Keep me a stick if they purge.". You may ask yourself "f*ck you mean" but at the end of the day you can't change the fact that sometimes it do be like that, you just gotta crank that foreign. A poem for ages to come, that's for sure.Regarding The Game: my man came out with a 10 minutes diss but got his a*s bullied in two verses. Truly iconic.Regarding the game: We Were Here Expeditions: The Friendship is that one little game that you are thankful you got for free but at the same time, maybe 3.99€ (for people outside Europe, that's 3.99 epsilons or how we like to call it - 3.99 "the European Union will be the downfall of Europe but at least we got some cool laws to bully Apple into using USB-C") is not that much. It's a rather short game (2 hours, give or take) with puzzles less challenging than the ones from previous iterations but enjoyable nonetheless. A sweet, short experience that you'll find quite fun to go along with your depression. It's.... quite ironic that I got it for free but it seems more polished than We Were Here Forever for which I paid 12.30 €uropean Unions. It is a lot shorter and the puzzles are far easier but it runs like a game, not like a Middle East peace conference.Overall score: 6/10, I would've preferred to have it just a bit longer, just like my schlong.To anyone reading this: Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year! _childDocuments_.review: A decent entry in the We Were Here Franchise, especially for its low price. There are three puzzles total, with significantly differing levels of difficulty if you're going for a perfect run. Puzzles 1 and 3 were fantastic, with 3 being the most interesting and fun/entertaining to complete. However, the second puzzle is an absolute nightmare if you aim for a gold ticket as it's entirely reliant on good RNG - in a puzzle with 4 varying elements, half of which must be explained to the other. It's not a bad puzzle in theory, just very unfair with the rolls as it really does come down to the last two random elements you get. You get one "bad" hand of which you can discard, but even that's not enough.It's odd because in reality you could probably speedrun this game in less than an hour with good communications and very good luck if you don't care for optimal or seamless objectives. Therefore the game somewhat expects you to go for gold, and unnecessarily gate-keeps your progress with the second puzzle. I'd recommend the other ones in the series over this one personally.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played We Were Here, you'll already know what to expect: a range of puzzles designed to strain your patience and communication skills and test your ability to work with another person, especially under pressure. If you've been craving the type of experience that makes you want to beat your game partner with a shoe and feel a true sense of accomplishment for describing a doll well enough, have I got the series for you. The FriendShip delivers exactly what you would expect from the original, namely engrossing puzzles in an immersive atmosphere (this one is an abandoned amusement park), for you to enjoy when you feel like listening to your partner yell about you timing their jump badly for the 24th time in a row. The enjoyability largely depends on your attitudes. If you both take it too seriously it is likely to end in tears but if you make it fun it'll be the good kind of frustrating, like being asked to open a box with nail clippers but finding candy inside. I can't understate how much of a treasure these games are for a long distance relationship. They are actually good communication and teamwork exercises and if you don't kill each other at the end you will most likely understand each other in a slightly deeper manner. My only quibble is that it is quite short, only offering 3 puzzle rounds, but as you can see by my gametime you can get sucked in far longer than would seem to make sense. The selection of co-op games is rather limited and vary wildly in quality, if you're looking for something actually good give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: You probably heard this before, but: If there was a Neutral Steam rating, that's how I would rate this one.I really liked all the games so far and brought all of them, because they are fun, challenging, and have that just the right kind of "Amusment Park Haunted House" atmosphere. And while this one started strong, my feelings turned sour pretty quickly.Let's start with the positives: Still a pretty nicely stylized game. It's cheap for it's length, even now that the "free to grab" period is over. The sole voice actor in it did a pretty good job. It's a nice afternoon/evening co-op experience if you don't farm for golden tickets.(Minor spoilers incoming)However, I still think this is the weakest entry in the "We Were Here" franchise unfortunatly. There are 3 big puzzles in it, and - apart from the first one - the rest kind of feel like those were the ones recycled from the cutting room floor of other games of the series.The first: "Communication" is logical and straightforward once you get what is going on and is a nice, classic 'We Were Here' puzzle. Fantastic start.The second however, the "Board game puzzle", is when things take a downhill turn. Granted, we took longer than usual with my friend since some of the puzzle rules were not clear at first, but oh boy, why is this darn puzzle soooo luck based? This is completly unfitting for the series. The core idea is good, but the RNG can kill an attempt when going for the golden ticket.The 3rd is the worst puzzle so far, because it has something that is entirely unfitting for this franchise: Platforming/Jumping puzzles. Let's be honest: the movement is not these games' strong suit, and the jumping mechanic was probably put in for the players to goof around a bit. It's tempting to create a puzzle with it, but this game is no puzzle platformer. Combine that with lag delay and awful collison detection and you got yourself a bad time. And if you fail in the middle of the puzzle when going for gold? Not only you have to start again, but there is a delay while you reset the puzzle, wasting several seconds of your time, which is just so freakin' frustrating after the third or forth attempt.Not to mention that the last section, which requires one player to lead another through an invisible maze, that has very little to no clear "landmarks" you can shout at your co-op partner, making this puzzle one of the most frustrating timed sections yet.And this is specific to us, maybe it was a slightly corrupted save file after a patch, but the worst part was that after we decided to give up on the gold in the last puzzle and just finish the game, the game didn't register our previous gold tickets and gave us 0 points on previous challenges - which is not even possible! Unless you abuse a bug, I don't think it's even possible to not have at least some points when leaving a dock. That sure left a terrible taste in my mouth after we suffered through the last two puzzles.Overall, I still recommend it, because going for full gold is entirely optional and you can finish the game with partial success in one sitting, and the ending doesn't change (apart from your ranking) but I still don't recommend to 100% this game as it was a frustrating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions: The Friendship is probably one of my favorites in the franchise, the WHH Franchise already consisted of incredibly fun co-op puzzle games that really made you question the intelligence of the friends you decide to play it with, and the Friendship does just that with a new twist. While it is a very short game, its makes up for it with the score system which encourages you and your partner to get the best score possible on all 3 tests to make sure you escape with the best ship and as "Perfect Partners". It was really fun trying to master them with my friend and I'm excited to see what Total Mayhem does in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting little experience, and could serve as a good, low-cost entry point to cooperative puzzle games (especially those made by Total Mayhem). While the original  could also fill this niche (since it was free), Total Mayhem have gained a lot of design skill since 2017.We liked the amusement park setting of the game, the graphical style, and especially the modifications made to your "ship" following the completion of each of the game's three challenges (these were hysterical, especially if you performed "poorly" in the preceding challenge). The first and third challenges were adequate, involving quick pattern recogntion/communication and the navigation of a boardwalk. However, we thought that the second challenge was brilliant. As we began to figure out what was transpiring on either side of the wall, I actually exclaimed "this is fun!" Unfortunately, doing well still feels a bit subject to chance (are the most useful colored pieces available when you need them?), but we tried this puzzle over and over to try and improve our score. We nailed the first puzzle quickly and gave up on the third after we'd done just enough to earn a bronze ranking (since it didn't really pull us in).If you tend to like cooperative puzzle games, I imagine you'll find something to like here. I like the idea of , and look forward to seeing if there are other shorter and more focused experiences Total Mayhem have in store for us.

_childDocuments_.review: Funny thing, a few days before the surprising release of a new We Were Here Game i thought about how much I wished for a new one. Maybe should try wishing for other stuff, definiatly onto something there. On top the made this for free for sometime which a dream move.We Were Here Expeditions: The Friendship can be taken as short entertaining one shot. Its shorter and in length easily compared to the first game. However this game is not trying to be big new story entry. The game opens with cool reference to the other games, without trying to hard to be sequel. Instead of fighting a big bad jester we are stranded on an abandon theme park. Wouldnt it be great to risk our life to trial our Friendship in three challenges in aged and worn theme park ? Yes ? Then this is the right game for you. You decide to enter the Friendship which is coop ride where you need to build you ship by completing a set of task. All task are set arround lesson a pirate crew has to learn before setting sail. Each challenge has a scoreboard awarding you with either bronce, silver or golden ship parts. Great thing you can retry the Challenge at anytime before progression to the next one. Additionally the challenges are not forcing you to pick a side. We Were Here usually devides the players without the ability to switch places. In Expeditions this is not the case. The first Challenges trials both players by switiching up roles every now and then. The second is little more traditionally made however there are "windows" where you can look at the miserable job your partner does. The third however leaves the roles open enough for you to decide. The third puzzle is the best and if you think you partner is not perfoming as good as you could you can change positions. This time I wanna critize something. The playthrough is releativly fresh so I do remember two things that I disliked. First me and my play buddy had some lags and freezing cutscenes. Something that I presumes get fixed in no time. The thing that bothered me the most is this forced retake animations. Everything is done with tickets. When you complete a game you are awarded a ticket which grants one of the three upgrade or is a red retry ticket. In any case you wanna retry you need to feed to munching machine. If you, like us, wanna get the golden ticket you find yourself retrying serveral times. Forcing you to wait till the animiations finished playing. For the first 5-10 attempts its not that bad after 15 or more it gets annoying. For the other four games I talked about the lesson teached and hopefully learned. This time however they are part of the games narrative so I leave this for you to discover. I hope we got to see more games from Total Mayhem within the We Were Here Series. To this point I think all them are great and my timed well spend.

_childDocuments_.review: Another fantastic bite sized entry to the series. TL;DR - 9/10 - Takes the classic duo puzzling formula and offers a bite sized adventure for you to enjoy.For those that aren't familiar, the We Were Here games involves you and a friend/loved one/stranger splitting up and solving puzzles that interact and change based on the other persons inputs. This requires you to relay information constantly and normally against a timer of some kind to keep the pressure up. This makes for some exciting (and sometimes frustrating) moments and it's really satisfying when the end credits roll. This game takes that formula and offers a smaller adventure which was a joy to play. _childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆ – PLAYSTYLE★★★★☆ – ART★★★★☆ – MUSIC/SOUNDS★★★★★ – DOABLE ACHIEVEMENTSWe Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip, the latest addition to the We Were Here franchise, is a delightful new release. Currently free to play for its first month after launch, it offers a short but enjoyable gaming experience. Completing the game took us around 1.5 hours.This game is a test of communication, teamwork, and trust between you and a friend, presenting you with three challenging puzzles. Your performance results in a rank, ranging from bronze to gold (or failure). You can use your tickets to upgrade your boat and continue the journey. Or you can choose to shred them and try the puzzle again for a better rank. While the game provides in-game walkie-talkies, my friend and I opted for Discord voice communication, so I cannot confirm the effectiveness of the in-game voice feature.Initially, the puzzles seemed somewhat perplexing, requiring a bit of trial and error to grasp fully. However, through effective teamwork and communication, we managed to achieve gold on all the puzzles in the second playthrough. Since both players see different parts of the puzzles, playing the game with the two different characters can offer a fresh experience. My friend and I found the puzzles to be challenging and enjoyable.Visually, the game is impressive, especially considering it's currently free. The music and sound effects further enhance the overall experience.For the achievement hunters, the achievements are very easy to obtain. Most of them you will get simply by playing. The hardest ones are getting the puzzles on gold rank, but once you grasp how the puzzles work those are also pretty easy.In summary, We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is a short yet engaging cooperative puzzle game. It tests your ability to work together effectively and offers an enjoyable experience, making it well worth the playthrough.
