_childDocuments_.review: Like its predecessors, We Were Here Expeditions is a first-person puzzler with online coop for two players.  The puzzles in this one have much more of a "mini-game" feel than the previous ones.  Each of the three puzzles can be beaten with a "bronze", "silver", or "gold" rating.The first puzzle, like many of their previous puzzles, involves communicating symbols over the mic.  Unlike puzzles in their previous games, this one has a time limit.  There's three increasingly-difficult sections with separate time-limits.  You're almost guaranteed to fail your first attempt, meaning you'll have to do the entire thing over multiple times if you want the gold.  Unfortunately when we beat the gold challenge, the "success" and "failure" sounds played at the same time and we were only awarded silver.  We did it again, and the same thing happened again. It seems to just be completely broken.The second puzzle is a board game.  While it is unique and I enjoyed it, it has a heavy randomness element, which is a terrible idea for a puzzle game. Even if your strategy is perfect, you might still be denied a gold due to bad RNG, which is what happened to us.The third puzzle is one of those mazes where nasty surprises await.  When you fail, you need to start from the beginning.  What this ultimately means is doing the maze over and over and  until you've mastered all the tricks.  One of the tricks was completely broken and led to us continuously falling through the floor (yes, the real floor) when we shouldn't have.In this game, the developers experimented with new ideas, which is great.  Unfortunately, none of them work.  Even if they weren't buggy messes, the core ideas are just not fun. This is by far the worst game of the series that I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: "It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness... that is the second puzzle of 'The Friendship'" - Captain Picard, Star Trek TNG. Finished the title with all gold, perfect ending. Wouldn't recommend solely based on the second puzzle. It's RNG, and no matter how much you and your partner plan moves out ahead, it's entirely possible for the game to just decide you cannot win. It happened several times, and was so egregious that we needed a single red column to spawn and it didn't give us it for three rounds in a row forcing us to lose that run. It turned a one hour game into a four hour game. Not worth your time fighting the random aspect of that puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I have some things to say about this game. 1. It started off pretty okay. It was fun to look around and see all the visuals. The first round was fine, but I do not think that it is intuitive. Firstly, the hints freaking suck. What kind of hint is "Hint, it takes time to wait for the next hint??" How does that help me with the game? Not only does it waste a hint, but it also gives me no hints. Second round, Is a nightmare. Not only is it timed for failure, but it does not save once you get past the first, so everytime you have to START ALL OVER. For the pattern type games it makes sense if the patterns are incorrect, but for this one I feel like the timed pattern + plus panicky descriptions of the symbols between friends is so unnecessarily stressful! I'm like, bruh. This is literally round two?? We haven't even gotten half way through the game and we're already struggling?? I feel like the second round of puzzles should have a little more time, the third round, omg. HOW, I have 0.3 seconds to process every single symbol my partner describes before the time ends and it's two windows not just 1! LIKE WHAT?! I would say that our communication has improved. Our bond over hating this game has conquered all. Please. Do not charge for this game, I'm glad this was free because I would not pay a dollar for the emotional damage this game has caused my friend and I. Thankyou for the Pre-Therapy boat scene before round 2. It was much needed.

_childDocuments_.review: If We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip was going to remain free, I probably wouldn’t both writing a review. It sounds like they’re planning to make this game cost money in a few days, so I thought I would share my experience with potential purchasers.This game consists of 3 mini games that you do with a friend. You must work together to solve the challenges as you are separated and see different things. It took under 1 hour for me and a friend to beat all 3. The first challenge is very simple and consists of you and a friend matching symbols. The second puzzle was the hardest one taking up probably half our playtime. After solving it, we still have absolutely no clue what we did. Neither of us understood the puzzle at all, we just did random things until it said we beat it. If it had taken much longer, we probably would have given up there. The third puzzle is one where one player guides the other through an obstacle course type thing that the player running it cannot see. It was pretty neat, but did not take long to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: The friendship is exactly what you are going to lose playing this ill designed game.The game consist of 3 trials. Without spoiling anything:- the 1st one is designed properly. You understand what is happening and the tutorial is good enough. You might not understand the time pressure at first, but restarting this trial is not tedious at all.- the 2nd trial is a overcomplicated puzzle, which tutorial is inexistant. You will ultimately succeed, but the game forces you to finish your attempt despite knowing the outcome is already bad.- the 3rd one is the worst of all. This is mostly a platforming trial with many mini challenges where communication is key. The tutorial for the main concept of that trial is innexistant, so you might first not understand what you need to do as the observer, and on the top of that, you will not understand why the observer is key in that trial. Actually, you might not even understand that you are an actual observer. The timings are too tight to feel fair for both players on the second mini challenge. And while this trial is about communication, you will restart it so often that the non-observer player will end up learning by heart what to do, and the communication is reduced to strict minimum. Oh, and the best is that if you have a disconnection, you are frozen... Did I mention the tight timmings?I would really not recommend this episode, and after playing two of them I believe I wouldn't continue the "We were here" series.For the record, I have played both games with a person I have excellent communication, with whom I have solved countless IRL and virtual escapes rooms.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game for any price other than free as most of the puzzles are either boring or frustrating and seem to be designed to waste the players time. The first puzzle requiring 15 correct answers of the same things without any real increase in difficulty is a horrible start to the game followed by a puzzle that is primarily rng that took us multiple attempts not due to lack of skill but the game refusing to give us one of the three colours until it was too late, I get that this is supposed to promote replayability in the game but this puzzle the way it is just isn't enjoyable when one player just cant get any colours to get the gold ticket being refused the gold by the game itself and not by player skill is not exactly fun when the game is promoted as a puzzle game. The last puzzle has a real big problem with latency as despite hosting a party i still had a 300 ping making the octopus zone completely annoying to get through as i had to jump from a VERY specific spot while walking in order to delay my landing long enough to actually land on the platforms and not fall through them making the entire last "puzzle" a horrible experience, if you play this game and see on the menu that you have higher than 150 ping i just would not recommend playing this game. Overall this game is an ok free experience if you enjoy time wasters and live close enough to the servers to make the last challenge fair.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, fairly short teamwork based puzzle game to enjoy with a friend. There are 3 games in total, and you can challenge yourselves by trying to achieve a gold ticket in all of them. Each game was well designed and fun, and required good teamwork. We found the second one was pretty challenging. Easily worth the £1.42 I payed for it.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions: The Friendship is a very enjoyable puzzle game made for two. The puzzles are challenging to figure out at first, but are very much doable once you’ve figured them out. Teamwork is very much required as you are very dependent on your partner, but with some proper communication you will certainly get there. The walkie talkies work alright, although for clarity reasons I did prefer to be on a call rather than use the walkie talkies. There are only three puzzles, but for the price they are definitely worth it. I personally got the game for free in its launch week. It definitely interested me in the other games of the We Were Here franchise, so I’ll keep an eye out for any sales.

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐ 10/10 - A Perfect Co-Op Experience!"We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip" is a fantastic co-op puzzle adventure that truly shines when played with a friend. The game’s emphasis on communication and teamwork makes it a unique and rewarding experience. Each puzzle requires both players to work together and trust each other to solve complex challenges, creating moments of real collaboration.The art style is charming, and the atmosphere is both lighthearted and immersive. It’s great to see a game that doesn’t rely on combat or intense action but instead focuses on strengthening bonds through fun and tricky puzzles. The variety of the puzzles is refreshing, and each one feels satisfying to complete, especially when you and your partner finally crack the solution together.Whether you’re playing with a close friend or someone new, The FriendShip is an awesome way to test your teamwork and communication skills in a fun and laid-back environment. Plus, the shorter length makes it perfect for an evening of gaming without feeling overwhelming.Highly recommended for anyone looking to share a thoughtful and enjoyable puzzle-solving adventure. Grab a friend, hop aboard, and set sail for an unforgettable experience! ⚓

_childDocuments_.review: In comparison to the other titles from the We Were Here series, this title decided to focus on 3 great puzzles rather than a lengthy and boring snoozefest of a story with a variety of puzzles sprinkled in. And it paid off. Two of the puzzles were phenomenal while one was average. $4 is a perfect price for this title, I wouldn't even buy it on sale. It is more like the first title (We Were Here from 2017) where the game focused more on great puzzles and not bad story telling like the later games were (such as We Were Here Forever). _childDocuments_.review: Very small nice experience, maybe around 2 hours.Issue I had was that the game detected incorrect region and ping was abysmal. So it didn't run nicely and I was getting a lot of disconnects before I changed it.Probably due to Total Mayhem Games being a small studio - the level of polish is sometimes lacking. I had some audio issues and had to switch to Discord, it's also not playable with unstable connection. There were points where interacting with items felt tricky.This game is set as a narrow experience, so there isn't much wiggle room or sandbox elements. Which I would consider a plus for focused coop.The ideas for puzzles are just endless and I don't understand where team gets inspiration! That is to say puzzles are excellent. I'd consider them a benchmark for that genre.Maybe something I'd like to see are puzzles of higher difficulty, as I already went through all games in series and got maybe a bit too good with communication and puzzle solving. So I don't feel as much accomplishment.

_childDocuments_.review: Co-op games are always fun and this game is no exception. It was very fun solving puzzles, communicating under pressure and just laughing over the trial and error of each level. The game features a scoring system on each level which allows you to pass levels with a score from bronze to silver to gold. This is very helpful for people who are just getting into the series but also does not require you to waste any more time than you should just to pass the level. Obviously, for the players who want the challenge, they could always go for a perfect score. There are also hints for each level so you don't have to stress too much if you want to finish the game quickly. The levels were creative and challenging also very fun to play through. I had a blast playing the game, but i did have some issues. One thing i see most people complain about is the level with tiles. I usually don't ever use hints for these series, but that level still has me questioning how exactly things worked. The hints weren't even that useful and I didn't want to open a tutorial or anything so we just freestyle'd the level until we got a good enough score to pass. I was not a fan of that level since there were so many stuff i did not understand.Another thing that was annoying was the server ping. _childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is a cooperative escape room puzzle game developed by Total Mayhem Games. It's another entry in the We Were Here series. In this part, we focus on repairing the ship in order to escape from the abandoned amusement park. The developers offered the game for free for a limited time, so I was able to claim it at no cost.The core of the game lies in its cooperative gameplay. Players control separate characters, unable to see each other directly. Escape requires constant communication via walkie-talkie, describing their surroundings and collaborating on solutions. This mechanic is consistent with previous games in the WWH series.While it may not be groundbreaking graphically, there's nothing to complain about. The graphics are pleasing to the eye, effectively capturing the atmosphere of the setting, and the level design is very well executed.Since communication relies heavily on walkie-talkie use, clear and well-crafted audio is essential. The game delivers, with crisp voice transmission, good environmental sounds and pleasant music.We have exposition and justification for our actions, but the story has never been the main focus of these games, and the same is true here. However, that's okay for the game.Solving puzzles with a friend brings a huge level of satisfaction and is extremely fun. While the core story can be completed in a single sitting, the game offers some replayability. We can replay challenges to achieve better results. While a bronze ticket is enough to pass, in good company, attempts to obtain a gold ticket are never dull.

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions is a shorter standalone We Were Here experience where you play co-op with 1 other friend using communication to solve puzzles to make it through to the end.When this released it was free to everyone so I picked it up to play with a friend. This is my first We Were Here game and I will gladly say this got me to buy and try out the other games as I really did enjoy playing this.The game is split into 4 main areas; the entrance area which introduces you to the puzzles of the game as well as 3 main puzzle areas where you spend the most of your time in. Once you reach the first puzzle area you are split from your partner and left to work out what to do in order to solve the puzzles.Once you reach the first puzzle you realise rather quickly that you and your partner are seeing similar yet different versions of the same things, this is where the communication of these games comes in. The 2nd puzzle is similar but there are ways to guide each other to the correct solution. The final puzzle is my favourite and the most different from the others where you have to guide your partner through an obstacle course where they can't see the obstacles, such a neat idea that I haven't seen before.The puzzles also feature a score giving a bronze, silver and gold rank, these are great if you want to test your puzzle skills or if you care about the achievements.The achievements just require you to complete the game and get a gold rank in each puzzle, if you get less than gold rank just shred your completion ticket and re-do the puzzle, if you move on to the next puzzle without a gold ticket you will have to go through the game to get to that point again to get gold rank. . You have the ability to create a public lobby or play with a random. Crossplay is supported. Tonnes of languages supported. Rebindable keyboard mouse and gamepad controls.Short and cheap standalone We Were Here experience where you play co-op using communication to solve puzzles. Game is Co-op only but you can create a lobby to play with random players. 3 main puzzle rooms to solve. Neat and unique puzzle ideas. Score based ranks on puzzle completion. All achievements can be completed in around an 1 hour.

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip Review**Rating: 7.5/10****Overview:**We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is like a trust fall exercise wrapped in a puzzle game, where you and your friend are constantly asking, "Are we still friends after this?" It’s a co-op adventure that tests not just your puzzle-solving skills, but also your patience and communication.**Pros:**1. **Friendship Test:** This game is the ultimate friendship test. If you can survive these puzzles without wanting to strangle each other, you’re probably best friends for life¹.2. **Humorous Dialogue:** The game’s slightly maniacal narrator loves to remind you that communication is key, often in the most hilariously condescending way possible².3. **Charming Graphics:** The cartoonish visuals and pirate-themed adventure make it feel like you’re on a whimsical, albeit slightly perilous, amusement park ride².**Cons:**1. **Short Playtime:** With only a few hours of gameplay, it’s like a fun-sized candy bar – enjoyable but leaves you wanting more⁴.2. **Repetitive Challenges:** Some puzzles can feel a bit repetitive, like you’re stuck in a never-ending escape room with your overly enthusiastic friend².3. **Limited Replayability:** Once you’ve solved the puzzles, there’s not much incentive to go back unless you want to relive the chaos⁴.**Conclusion:**We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is a delightful, if brief, co-op puzzle game that’s perfect for testing the strength of your friendships. It’s filled with humor, charm, and just enough frustration to keep things interesting. Just remember, in the world of The FriendShip, communication is key – and so is not throwing your controller at your friend.

_childDocuments_.review: Consists of 3 puzzles:Puzzle 1 was fun as me and my friend came up with funny names for the symbols we had to tell each other within a time limit.Puzzle 2 is absolutely horrible and is essentially RNG math.Puzzle 3 was also fun due to guiding my friend, (and later myself when replaying it) through an invisible/imaginary course.I claimed the game for free back when it launched, and for $4 it is not a bad price, just make sure you enjoy cooperative puzzle games that judges your friendship.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: What a truly BEAUTIFUL series of games. I picked up the bundle after seeing We Were Here was free and what a ride we've just been on playing through all five games together. Not only is each game truly fun and engaging, but it's been amazing to see how the team have progressed and developed over time (seeing better menus, richer worlds, more complex puzzles etc). I am now almost left mourning the loss of these games in my life. I truly hope this team continues to develop future titles and I will keep a close eye on anything they develop in future! TLDR; HIGHLY, HIGHLY RECOMMEND the entire series.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: General: it's what you would expect from the WWH series. It's a great coop game with an escape room premise. Pros:- puzzles are well designed that tested the 3 categories appropriately.    - 1st puzzle was a typical WWH game that tested communication well.    - 2nd puzzle was unique. Takes a while to figure out but once you have, it's arguably my favourite puzzle of the 3.    - 3rd puzzle was also a typical WWH with some unique, fun gimmicks. - music and sfx were good, as always, as expected. - the puzzles are forgiving as you have room for error and you can shred your tickets for retries. - cross-platform playing is also always a plus. - environmental and setting design was thorough and the colours were pleasing. Cons: - no skippable cutscenes or chapter select, only a minor nuisance. - no borderless settings which is always a shame but a minor con. - wished there was more functionality and usage with the torches but not a big deal anyways. Overall, a fantastic game for cheap (either free on launch or a couple bucks now). I knew this game would be good going in and coming out of it, I am satisfied with how well-produced and well-designed it is.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice and well thought out puzzles. In contrast to other parts of the series, both player are engaged and have fun things to do all the time. Especcially enjoyed getting all gold tickets, which i think also gives you the most value out of the game.Yes its a little short, but pretty cheap and very enjoyable nontheless.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Short but when it just comes down to the design of the puzzles it has to be my favourite we were here. Yes its short but every of the three stages is designed really well and shows the essence of we were here. No long breaks, no unnecessary complex stages. Just pure coop fun. And for the little money definetly worth it
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Played this with a couple of different friends now and each experience was uniquely fun in its own way. The puzzles do vary some between playthrus, and you can also switch sides and play on the other side of the track for your second run, plus the whole experience can be very different depending on who you play with, so there is decent replayability for a smallish game, That being said, it really really matters who you choose to play this with! You will definitely learn some things about your partner by the end of the ride lolJust remember: communication, collaboration, and TRUST!!! Enjoy :)
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking to spend some time in a puzzle game with a friend and have a really good time, this is the perfect game for you.Pros:+ Beautiful Graphics+ Fun puzzles+ Challenging puzzlesCons:- Short, But a good start if someone is looking at the "We Were Here Series"SummaryVery good puzzle game, buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun! My husband and I have played all of the We Were Here games and this one was shorter, but very pleasant. We particularly loved the second puzzle. We had a hard time figuring it out, but once we did it was very satisfying to solve. Somehow this game blends a mix of easy and fun with very complicated puzzles. Really excellent date night.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: My friend and I recently had the pleasure of experiencing something truly special, and I couldn't wait to share our enthusiasm. From the moment we started, it was clear that this was going to be an unforgettable adventure, and we were hooked until the very end. Our mission? To secure those elusive golden tickets.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: You can easily "beat" the game in under 2 hours, as there's only really three puzzles in there. The second one (tile puzzle) takes a bit to figure out, so to 100% it and get a perfect rating for the playthrough, you're going to need two attempts.Neat game, maybe a bit short for full price (as there's little replayability). but definitely worth it if you can get it one sale!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: It is an excellent game, I love the aesthetic and how it simulates a theme park attraction like the ones at Disney World and the like. Better played with a friend or relative or significant other, it can be played with randoms, of course, but I believe it will be more difficult with strangers. I played with a cousin and we had a blast. It's short, took us 4 hours and 2 sessions to pass it, but that was also because we wanted to 100 % the game, so it took us several tries to get gold in each section, if you don't care about that, you can complete the game way quicker, so keep that in mind. Despite being a short game, I still recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Me and a friend got it for free and played it. It was really sweet and the riddles were interesting but not to hard. The problem is, there are only three riddles and we played the second and the third for various times. In the end we played about 90 minutes and because it was for free it was sweet. But for 4 euros its not really much
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Short but incredibly sweet! I've played all the games within the We Were Here franchise and can honestly say that this little ditty has contained some of my favourite content thus far. I do love all the games, but The FriendShip in particular leaves me wanting more...or at least a recreation of it's content at a real life theme park!Great stuff TMG! Keep it up
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a video game, people expect it to rot your brain but you actually put some thinking and teamwork and this game has improved my friendship with online and real life people. I have played all the other game and i would say this one is the best out of all of them. Big thumbs up and reccomendation

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to expect from this standalone game at the beginning but I have loved all games from the We Were Here series so it went without saying that I was going to continue the journey with my friend. While it was short, it was a lot of fun and we really enjoyed the puzzles as well as the theme. I already look forward to the next entry in the series <3
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice game. Always loved puzzle games - this is one of the best I ever played. The puzzles are more graphical, than for examplein the pilot version of We Were There. The game feels much more lighter because of that, and I really recommend it.Althought there are some small downsides. As in the pilot version of the game, there are some textures you can get stuck in. There are also some rendering issues, where the location can suddenly just dissapear and stop rendering. Or for example: once I wasn’t able to sit in the boat, but my friend did, and I was left behind, we had to restart the session.The game is also not long, on first try you should beat it in around 2 hours, but according to the price and the quality of the game - the price is well deserved.Also, as I think, the game is also well optimised, it should run even on a very old machine without a lot of lag. I tested it on a i5 5th gen, and GT720M GPU, and it did really great. I certainly recommend this game, I enjoyed it so much and it is really interesting and exciting.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: The We Were Here series is a great set of co-op puzzle games, and Expeditions: The FriendShip is a cute short game that is a great in-between game while we wait for the next full entry into the series.  The game is very cheap and very short, so it's great for those who want to try out the series without committing a lot of time and money, and it's story is self-contained, so it's not like new players need to know 4 games worth of story to understand what's going on.  This a great game to play with a friend for a night, and if you enjoy it, there's a bunch more games to enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet introduction to the "We Were Here" series. I got this when it was free to keep. For the very short length, it should have stayed free considering it's about an hour in length.Considering the other "We Were Here" games are very cheap, I would not purchase this for anything more than $1. There's a loose story across the whole games and you don't need to play this one first. Get it if it's cheap or free and you're itching for more "We Were Here."
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all the "We Were Here" games so far and this is definitely one of my favorites!Contradicting to all of the other games, this is definitely less scary (even though it's not about that in the other games)!Had a lot of fun with my friend and (even though I got it, when it was free) it's definitely worth it for the price!We finished it in 2 hours but you can beat it faster (but won't get a good score probably) or take even longer if you wanna 5-star all the games.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Shortest game in the franchise (around 3 hours at "worst") but surely the most "cruel", your "friendship" will be put in real danger.If you played the previous chapters you already know what are you getting into, if not then here a short recap:The "We Were Here" franchise is a first person coop only franchise based on resolving puzzles, you and the other players will be separate most of the time and have to talk over the voice chat to resolve some puzzles.If you can clear this game without insulting each others over some of the puzzles (expecially the last one) then there's not much that can ruin your bond, and i'm not even kidding.An actual good social game but not the best chapter in this franchise, worth the purchase but only if you have someone trustworthy to play with or just for some sane hours of pure rage with your now ex-friends.In case try out the first chapter "We Were Here" just to learn the basis, if you don't like that i doubt you will like this game either.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is an enchanting cooperative adventure that seamlessly blends puzzles, communication, and teamwork into an unforgettable experience. The game not only challenges your intellect with its clever puzzles but also tests the strength of your collaboration as you and your friend work together to unravel mysteries and unlock the next chapter of your journey. The whimsical and atmospheric environments create a captivating backdrop, immersing players in a world of discovery and camaraderie. With its unique approach to cooperative gameplay and engaging narrative, The FriendShip is a delightful voyage that highlights the magic that happens when collaboration and puzzle-solving come together in perfect harmony. Grab a friend, set sail, and get ready for an expedition full of surprises and shared triumphs!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the new function of trying the puzzles multiple times within the same savegame if you want to improve your result. For this the link to the achievements are better than in the other older "We were here" games, where you had to start a new savegame to get all achievements.All in all a very good game, only a little bit too short. Therefore i hope there will be a longer "We were here" game in the future with this new function like in this game version.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Overall okay side game of the main series. 1st puzzle was cool. We unfortunately had to stop after the 2nd puzzle due to it having too much RNG. If you're someone who doesn't like puzzles with more than one solution, this probably wouldn't be the game for you. Despite it, I think this is still a good game to try out, as well as the main series. As a mildly colorblind person, I very much appreciate all the little touches to make it colorblind-friendly!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Another good entry in the We were here series.It is a bit different than the previous ones. I prefer the gameplay of We were here forever over this entry's gameplay. The main issue being, that there are basically three mini games and that is all. It has less of the Escape game feeling than the other entries. It still has it's charm and the sound design is great. But there is no reason to play the other side of the puzzles except for one.It was enjoyable and it is not too long.It took a friend of mine and me about 6 hours to get all achievements.I do recommend playing this with a friend and maybe with an open mic. The game offers a voice communication option but just use what you use in other circumstances unless you play this with a stranger.The one major issue I had was, that during the two major cutscenes (intro, outro) the cutscene got really weird and started to not play smoothly. Same was true for the sound. No idea what was going on. It was 100% reproducible for me and my friend. Same issue on two separate PCs using Windows and Linux. The machines are about two years apart in age.All in all a good game being kept from being a great game by my own preference and one "bug".Score: 7/9
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a beautiful Art-Style, tense but rewarding mini games and a blast to play with someone you love. perfect example of less is more within this genre as everything was polished and well executed with an obvious amount of care and time put into each crafted level, game and voice acting. truly loved playing this with my girlfriend and has something for everyone, from friends in it for a laugh or achievement hunter like her and I. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty short and also comparitivaly easier than the 2nd and 3rd game of the series. It only has 3 puzzles/games, which are all not especially hard, but still quite fun!Me and my friend needed a bit to understand how the second minigame works, and during the third minigame we had some problems with motion sickness as well as jumping across the moving platforms due to the timing of them, but it didn't really diminish our fun of the game!I'd recommend it for sure! It's very fun and the end-text after the adventure is very fun as well! :D
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed and would highly recommend all of the games in the We Were Here series, but this one in particular felt positively refreshing. In my opinion, all of the puzzles in this particular game were good. The other games in the series usually have one or two puzzles that aren't really my thing, and that's fine, but there wasn't a single puzzle in this game that I didn't like. The game is a bit short, yes, but it was also free for a limited time when I got it, and the current price (3,99€) isn't bad either. Overall, I would highly recommend this game as well as the other games in the WWH series. Great puzzle games and great co-op games.

_childDocuments_.review: The stunning atmosphere and wonderful soundtrack known for the WWHE-Series comes alive again in WWHE: The FriendShip! It takes a second to understand what and how each puzzle works in your favor and how you need to communicate with your friend to get through the challenges, but the game is worth to play through at minimum twice if not three times to truly experience all of it's glory.Tiny spoiler through gripe:Second puzzle was a headache though, the information can be misinterpreted on the tiles side as the shapes being the valuable thing not them lighting up. There are three activities which are best described as: Describe symbols and emotions; Advocate for your side of a puzzle board; and follow instructions on an invisible obstacle course.Highly recommend for any two folks interested in a cooperative game that will develop more intimate communication between the two
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed all of the We Were Are series but this was certainly a more fun relaxed experience, big bonus is it didn't make my friend hate my stupidity as much lol. Not having to be perfect at the puzzle and having it feel like a mini game is way more encouraging to replay and not give up as easily.

I would highly recommend this game to fans of the originals and to people who are new to this series.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Another game in series and as usually, it rocks. It is beautiful to see how developers go further with ideas and design with each new game. Simple music background.Beside few bugs throughout the game (we reached full score in each category and final scoring told us worst mates and 0 points in every category, in the third riddle it didnt count one lighthouse for us eventhough we switched on all of them, ...) we didnt bump into any problems with performance. I got the game for free after release, but it is absolutely worth it's sell price. The price is pretty low - the game is also pretty short. Three riddles overall. In 5 hours of playtime we went through the game twice (once to find out how the riddles work, to go through the plot and second to reach the highest score) Definitely recommended. :)
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute blast to play with my wife, we've played every We Were Here and this was a nice little snippet in that same universe! Each game's puzzles are always enjoyable and this one is no exception. We played through 4 times, once all the way through and then three more times to get each ship. Definitely worth checking out, especially if you're a fan of the series!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: "We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip" is an exhilarating journey that truly embodies the essence of teamwork and collaboration. The game beautifully challenges players to communicate effectively, strategize, and rely on each other's strengths to solve intricate puzzles. The immersive experience is a testament to the power of cooperation, fostering a thrilling and memorable adventure the strengthens bonds and leaves players feeling accomplished.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I recently played "We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip," and I have to say, it left me wanting more in the best way possible. The collaboration and puzzle-solving aspects are just as engaging as ever, making it a standout in the cooperative gaming genre. I found myself immersed in the world and the challenges presented, and I couldn't help but wish for a longer adventure. The puzzles were cleverly designed, and the teamwork required added a unique twist that kept me on the edgeOverall, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game, especially playing it with my girlfriend. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys cooperative puzzle-solving games. If only it were a bit longer, I'd be even happier!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is like being thrown into a co-op escape room, except your partner speaks in riddles and forgot how to communicate. The puzzles? Fun, but the real challenge is not losing your mind when your "friend" can’t tell left from right. I had a mate when I started the game, but by the end? Let’s just say… I’m in the market for a new one.It’s a great game if you’re into teamwork and screaming at each other over puzzles you swear are broken.Randy Rating: 4/5 — Entertaining, but don’t be surprised if you end up a solo player by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: game suxbut for real, first puzzle was fun. Second puzzle was one of those RNG mobile games where you cant beat it in the 10 moves they give you so you have to buy more moves, yet you cant do that here. Third puzzle requires fast precision movement in a p2p connection making it frustrating due to how the game is made, and you fall through things due to desync. 1/3 on puzzle design sorry guys.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, and a lot of fun! I love that it allows you to switch player roles for each puzzle, rather than choosing just one at the beginning of the game. It let us feel out which player was better at which role on a per-puzzle basis, and also alleviated boredom when we were stuck, since we could switch places to keep things fresh. I really appreciate that it autosaves after each puzzle, since my game partner and I had limited periods each day to play. The ability to replay individual levels to get a better score, or just play to pass them, was also a nice touch; it meant that we could replay just the levels we wanted to, without having to totally restart the game. Overall, the puzzles are nice and complex, requiring both thought and action without being obtuse. It took us a while to figure each solution out, and once we'd done so, it took skill to get the higher scores.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Played as a couple, blitzed the first room then got stumped at the 2nd but refused to continue until we gold starred it - after finally understanding all the parts involved, several retries and cursing the RNG, we got it (ironically now i kind of want to play that kind of tile puzzle more) and of course the last room was full of laughs. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to first game of this series this is very bad. You play three easy minigames with your friend and then wait for anoying voice and long cutscenes. Even story was meh. Started out cool and mysterious abandoned park, but turned out to be casual joyride without real ending or reason why you do the things you do.

_childDocuments_.review: Took about 2 hours and 20 minutes to beat with all puzzles completed with the highest possible score. Took a few attempts since the communication can be tricky and required to solve them. It is crucial to use the walkie talkie and also fun because not both players can talk at the same time. _childDocuments_.review: Played with friend and was a good bit of fun trying to figure out the puzzles. The second puzzle is a little hot garbage to me at least as it was pure RNG and there wasn't really any great way to figure out how to maximise everything. Basically for the second one, good RNG = GG. For the others it was a fun adventure, the whole setting and area was great, good music to set the tone for it, puzzles overall were great / fun and required actual communication and teamwork. Unfortunately for me, it was a little on the short end, but for this price I would say that's reasonable. If you don't have much time to game and want to try something fun with a friend in the weekend, pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: A Co-op Adventure Like No Other - Definitely worth a go with your partner or best mate!Introduction:"We Were Here: Expeditions: FriendShip" is a co-op puzzle adventure game that takes teamwork and communication to a whole new level. Developed by Total Mayhem Games, this game builds upon the successful "We Were Here" series and offers an immersive, brain-teasing experience that challenges players to solve intricate puzzles by working together. In this review, we will explore what makes "We Were Here: Expeditions: FriendShip" a unique and engaging co-op adventure.Gameplay (10/10):The core of "We Were Here: Expeditions: FriendShip" revolves around communication and collaboration. Players assume the roles of two characters who are separated in a mysterious castle and must rely on walkie-talkies to share information and solve puzzles. The game's puzzles are complex, diverse, and require both players to be in constant contact. The need for clear and effective communication is at the forefront, making this game an excellent test of teamwork.Graphics and Sound (9/10):The game features atmospheric graphics that set the stage for an eerie, mysterious castle. The lighting and shadows create an immersive environment that draws players into the game's world. The sound design is top-notch, with eerie and ambient music adding to the suspense and immersion. The walkie-talkie effect on the in-game communication adds authenticity and a unique dimension to the game play.Story line (8/10):While "We Were Here: Expeditions: FriendShip" doesn't focus heavily on narrative, it offers an intriguing backstory that unfolds as players progress through the castle. The narrative is somewhat secondary to the puzzle-solving, but it provides a layer of depth to the overall experience. Exploring the mysteries behind the castle's history adds to the game's appeal.Replay Value (9/10):The game's replay value is substantial due to the cooperative nature of play. You'll likely find yourself wanting to swap roles and go through the game again as the other character, which can offer a fresh perspective on puzzles and an entirely new experience. Additionally, the game's puzzles are challenging enough to warrant multiple playthroughs as you sharpen your communication skills and attempt to complete the game more efficiently.Pros:1. Unique and challenging cooperative game play.2. Excellent use of communication as a central mechanic.3. Atmospheric graphics and sound design.4. High replay value.5. Perfect for couples and friends looking for a co-op adventure.Cons:1. The game's puzzles may be too challenging for some players.2. The storyline takes a backseat to the puzzles.Conclusion (Overall Rating: 9/10):"We Were Here: Expeditions: FriendShip" is an exceptional co-op puzzle adventure that shines due to its emphasis on effective communication and teamwork. It provides a perfect platform for couples, friends, or significant others to challenge their problem-solving abilities and relationship dynamics. The game's immersive world, intricate puzzles, and eerie ambience make it an unforgettable co-op experience. For those seeking a unique and rewarding gaming adventure, "We Were Here: Expeditions: FriendShip" is a must-play. So grab your walkie-talkie, partner up, and embark on a cooperative journey you won't soon forget.

_childDocuments_.review: A short mini-entry to the We Were Here series.  You are graded on how thoroughly / perfectly you complete the puzzles, receiving a Bronze, Silver or Gold ticket.  You only need Bronzes to progress, it's your choice to challenge yourselves to get Silvers or Golds.  This gives it some extra replayability, and a separate skill floor and skill ceiling (something I can't recall seeing often in puzzle games).My friend and I found it plenty of fun for the small price.  A first-time run can be finished in under an hour if you don't care to perfect all the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little game that makes me think of a puzzle room at a fair with "Test Your Friendship!" written overtop.  This absolutely requires two people, with mics.  I came to this straight from "We Were Here," so I was quite happy to see how the devs have honed their craft over the years.  It's certainly less buggy; unlike the former, I didn't find any game-breaking bugs requiring a restart, although there was a little bit of jankiness to it.  The in-game comms had a tendency to just not broadcast whenever it felt we didn't appreciate it enough; my partner theorized it was whenever we both pressed the broadcast button too close together, but I'm not sure on that front.  They have added a light to signal that the other person is trying to broadcast, so that's nice (and we would rapidly strobe each other if we saw that the other person was broadcasting silence, so they could start again and hopefully fix the problem).The puzzles are fantastic.  There are three puzzle rooms that keep with We Were Here's style thus far: both players have different parts of the same puzzle in front of them, time to communicate to figure out what the whole is and how to proceed.  The lobby screen lets you switch roles, but that only determines what your walkie-talkie looks like and the color of your parka.  Your actual roles are determined at the very start of the game by who lets who through a hole in a fence, but even then only the second puzzle is dictated by that.  The first switches your roles around, and the third is another case of who lets who into the hallway.The biggest difference I noticed when coming straight from the first We Were Here was the vanishing of the light horror aspects of the first game.  There's no proper death, and while I spent the entire game waiting for the animatronic lady to start cackling madly and try to kill us, it never comes.  I think I've just been traumatized by the entire rest of gaming.  The closest it came to horror was an unfortunate accidental picking of roles in the third puzzle, but that was entirely my own situation.  I'm thalassaphobic (big fish monster scary) and my role spent most of that puzzle dangling over a shark tank.I got this while it was free, but I think I'd still have been feeling good about this even if I'd bought it at full price.  Happily recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: A condensed down version of the more prominent We Were Here games. This one feels like it belongs in the same series though. It’s still what I’d consider a pretty hardcore cooperative experience, all about communicating different viewpoints and pieces of information. Ultimately, it’s about understanding how all the pieces fit together; celebrating both the victories and defeats along the way. It’s very thinky, and incentivizes repeat tries to try to earn top scores.You basically get three different challenges here. I really love the second one: an abstract board game where each player plays the same game, but following a different set of rules. It’s mind bending at first glance, but actually really well balanced and designed.Recommended if you enjoy co-op games, have a friend, and don’t mind a bite-sized adventure that’ll last you an hour or two.

But in that section with the nausea effect, my partner and I suffered. We had to keep switching off and taking breaks. After we completed it, I remained nauseous for *hours* even though I don't normally suffer from video game motion sickness. I should also mentioned that I streamed this game, and my chat *also* suffered. Everyone felt sick and it sucked. I beg the devs to lessen the nausea effect in a future patch.

_childDocuments_.review: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is an absolute gem of a game that takes cooperative gameplay to a whole new level. I had the pleasure of embarking on this thrilling journey with a friend, and it left us both in awe of its unique challenges, immersive storytelling, and the powerful bond it forged between us.The game's premise is simple yet brilliantly executed. Players are separated in a mysterious and visually stunning environment, each equipped with a walkie-talkie to communicate and solve puzzles. The catch? You and your partner are the only ones who can help each other progress, making teamwork and communication absolutely essential.The puzzles in The FriendShip are ingeniously designed, and each one presents a fresh and mind-bending challenge. From deciphering cryptic symbols to coordinating actions across different locations, the game keeps you engaged and thinking critically throughout. It's a true test of collaboration and problem-solving, and every solved puzzle is immensely satisfying.What sets We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip apart is its captivating storyline. As you progress, you unravel the mysteries of the environment and uncover a rich narrative that keeps you guessing and eager to discover more. The immersive world-building and attention to detail are remarkable, making each step of the journey feel meaningful and significant.The visuals in the game are absolutely stunning. The atmospheric environments, intricate set pieces, and hauntingly beautiful landscapes create a sense of wonder and intrigue that draws you in from the moment you start playing. The attention to detail in the design of the game world is nothing short of breathtaking.The game's audio design deserves special mention as well. The haunting and atmospheric soundtrack adds depth to the experience, creating an eerie and immersive ambiance that enhances the sense of mystery and adventure.What truly elevates We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is the way it fosters cooperation and communication. Playing with a friend is an incredibly bonding experience, as you learn to trust each other's instincts and problem-solving skills. The game encourages open communication and collaboration, and it's a joy to see how your teamwork evolves over the course of the adventure.In conclusion, We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is a masterfully crafted cooperative adventure that excels in every aspect. From its mind-bending puzzles to its captivating narrative, stunning visuals, and immersive audio, it offers a gaming experience that is both intellectually stimulating and emotionally rewarding. If you're looking for a game that challenges your wits and strengthens your connection with a friend, The FriendShip is an absolute must-play. It's an unforgettable journey that you'll be talking about long after the adventure ends.

_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: The We Were Here series has been amazing since its first release in 2017, and We Were Here Expeditions: The Friendship is no exception! If you enjoy co-op puzzle games then pick this one up, because it's super fun (and free for a bit!!). We played through twice, switching sides the second time, and were able to get all achievements with minimal grinding. I can't wait to see more from these devs as they expand the We Were Here series -- well done!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Every great duo has a third to help and spice things up in the puzzle room. At least that's what my wife and her boyfriend tell me. It's a great time on the friendSHIP and took twice as long as the original. Makes me consider buying the 2-4th games in the series. You know, for the friends and the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: The game was so fun! it was way better then the first game. I played it with my best friend and we laughed and had great moments togheter, The first minigame was easy, we got silver. The second minigame was very confusing at start, but after 2 tries we understood, if you understand it its complicated but easy, we got silver again. The third one was easy till the last challenge, we did it many tries because we wanted golden, and it was fun, we needed for that challenge one hour, but it got never boring! The end "video" was really buggy with the voice, i liked the QR Code you can scan to see how well you did. 5/5 Stars, i hope we get more free games like this! :)
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game content just had a few issues with the game where the ticket sometimes wouldn't go in the the retry and would glitch the game so we had to restart it. This was our first issue our second issue was it would randomly pop up a player has disconnected and then disappear, our third and final problem was the audio was very glitchy
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Super casual game. My brother and I beat this one in about an hour and half of playtime. We have previously played all of the games when they released, minus the first one. I actually remember beating the first one in one night, and then googling when the next one came out, and saw it came out about a week later. These are really enjoyable games with someone you have a decent understanding of how the play / think. Could not recommend these games with a S/O or a close friend enough. Very much so waiting on any future installments in the franchise. Cheers to the Total Mayhem team.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit short, just three levels, but I got it for free therefore I can't say much about it. The levels are actually good, they remind me of the first We Were Here game, which takes time to understand how things work but not very annoying due to over-complication like the later ones. My friend and I enjoyed this game.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adorable game that is very fun and truly challenges a friendship. It is easy to screw each other over, but the most fun I had was trying to perfect each part. It has very re-playable mini games that truly capture the feel of the game. I had a great time playing it and definitely will replay it with more friends!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Love it!As the whole We Were Here series, this was an awesome game to play.It was an unexpected and short game, but got almost everything WWH games offers to make you play with pleasure.And a smart choice making it short, giving a taste of what kind of game WWH is to attract more people to play the other ones (that i hardly recommend)Basically, it was a really nice surprise! As a big fan, i really enjoy it and am already waiting for more to come.(hopefullly)
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: very mid, theres 3 puzzles that are really close to impossible to fail if youre fine with bronze instead of gold (you can still complete the game after 3 bronzes) it takes like 2 fails and you realize whats going on because they dont emphasize anything. as soon as you realize what the puzzle actually is, you immediately solve it
