_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: How is the best in the series free?!...I mean besides it being short.  This one has challenges that can be completed through 3 different score thresholds, which is a fantastic change that I would love to see in all future games in the series.  Honestly, wouldn't mind at all if the next games were more short episodic outings like this one too.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend! Fun and short (1-3hrs) co-op puzzle game with heavy emphasis on communication. The models and art are cute, and the puzzles are not too difficult. You can choose to min-max the levels and get the highest award or speedrun to the end with the minimum passing score. One suggestion is to use a different method of voice communication than the walkie talkie provided in game because at least for me, there was a 0.5-1 second delay which made it more difficult to complete the timed obstacles.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I love the We Were Here series! This short puzzler is sooo cute to play with a friend. The puzzles are fun while still being challenging. I also loveee the fact that you can retry the puzzle to obtain maximum score. But whichever you may chose... to 100% the puzzle or to go along with whatever score you did best at... you are still rewarded with cool upgrades for your ship! Go ahead and challenge yourself to 100% the game and unlock all achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: "We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip" is a delightful cooperative puzzle game with 2-3 hours of gameplay that truly shines in its ability to foster teamwork. The puzzles are top-notch, requiring players to collaborate closely with their partner, making for a highly engaging experience. The game's standout moment is its second stage, which adds an unexpected twist and elevates the gameplay to a new level. What's even more surprising is that this exceptional game is available for free, making it a must-play for anyone who enjoys cooperative gaming.In summary, "The FriendShip" is a fantastic puzzle-solving adventure that guarantees a great time for you and your partner. Its challenging puzzles and surprising second stage elevate the experience, and the fact that it's free makes it even more impressive. Don't miss out on this gem from the developer – it's one of the best cooperative games out there.Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: - fairly simple levels but actually challenging if you want to get the best score- small game size and fairly low pc requirements- no friends? the game searches for another guy  so you two can play together :) (playing with friends is still better for easier communication ) - for some reason the game keep putting me in the wrong region to find teammates (might be a bug)- no, there's really not much to complain, it's just fun =)a really fun game to play with friends (brain cells are required), and I have really enjoyed this game. Overall 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I bought all We Were Here games, and I think this one should be free (or very cheap) based on its overall quality.The first puzzle was simple and was usually seen in We were here series. It was not sth new. But I kinda liked it. The second puzzle was "interesting" but I'm not sure if I liked it because you have to be lucky to get the piece you need. The first two puzzles, as I mentioned, were ok. BUT, I really don't like the third puzzle. And I hope that developers will try to avoid this kind of design later. I think We were here series should not adopt "simultaneous" movement design in the game. For the octopus stage and the two planks with ropes keep moving up and down, they require good network connection, good device, good nervous system, and good movement design in games. And not everyone has them. Also, if you fall, you'll need to restart from the beginning. Please don't learn from Getting over it with Bennett Foddy (Just kidding but seriously plz don't make it like that
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip is a fantastic game that offers players engaging puzzles and adventures. It is developed by Total Mayhem Games and is the latest addition to the We Were Here series. Players must work together to solve puzzles and progress through the game. The game supports cross-play, allowing PC and console users to play together.Reviews of the game are positive. For instance, GameWatcher describes the game as “a pleasing taster without being a waste of time, a great introduction to social games without the pressure of eight-player ability fuelled mayhem, and an enjoyable adventure for experienced thinkers and friends alike” . GameFAQs also speaks highly of the game, calling it “a pleasant palate cleanser, an excellent introduction to social games without the pressure of eight-player ability fueled mayhem, and a pleasant adventure for experienced thinkers and friends”
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best We were here games imo, especially for being free atm. There are three challenges you have to complete, one about communication, one about teamwork and one about trust. It first takes some time until you fully understand what exactly you are supposed to do but eventually the "rules" become clearer. The second challenge is a kind of boardgame that is a bit confusing at first but once you know the objective it's a ton of fun. You need a bit of luck to get the highest score but other than that the puzzles are just well done!We played the game twice because in our first go we didn't realise that we could restart the puzzles by shredding the bronze/ silver ticket and got 2.5 hours of playtime out of it.Can absolutely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I had such a good time doing this with my best friend, even the hard parts were more invigorating than frustrating in the long run.  The second puzzle is really hard to get a grasp on the rules and I wish that there was a quicker way to reset it while you are feeling things out, but by the end I really enjoyed it and think that it would be an interesting puzzle mini game concept on its own.I love puzzle games and my best friend usually does not, but we had a really fun time together and have the bestest strongest friendship.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Very short but creative and fun challenges that test your communication abilities mostly. There were some server issues while playing and laggy audio at the very end of the game, but nothing major. All in all, can recommend it to anyone who loves escape rooms or just wants to yell at each other for like 2-3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent!A really nice little adventure with a lovely atmosphere. Based in a sort of haunted carnival type setting this has got 3 very nice co-op puzzles for you and a buddy to take on. A short run-time but this was very generously given away free so there's no way I'm going to object to that. Really good game, really good game series, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Unlike the other We Were Here games (which I also love), this game gives you different scores for each puzzle and gives you your time, which gives the game much more replayability since you can go back and try to do better or faster at the puzzles. This series has been a great way to have fun with my gf when she's away for college, I highly recommend this game! I cannot wait for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game and experiencing it with my friend i would say that i am happy that i spend the time with him and i would HIGHLY recommend choosing to play with a friend if you have one, also the game is free so ehh.... go play it.      (Also, me and my pal got a silver boat on first playthough, i would put a spoiler on this text but i have no idea how to do that)
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Actually, I would have payed the game if necessary. Its a game about communication and friendship, which demands you to win 3 challenges while you are with a close friend of your and must complete the challenges by talking and coming to an conclusion of what you should do. If your and your partner really like puzzle games, you should try this one.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't even know this was coming out! Found it totally random. Very glad I did. Love the whole series and this was an awesome addition. Can't believe it was free. Puzzles were so creative. If you like co-op puzzle games, definitely try it. If you're a fan of the series, then the decision to play or not is a no brainer. Big thank you to Total Mayhem for this!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: There is truly no other game like the We Were Here (WWH) series. I've never had so many  while playing a game, and this expansion is no different. From start to finish, every game in the series tests not just your puzzle-solving skills, but also your communication and connection with your co-op partner. Each challenge pushes you and your partner to work together in ways that can only strengthen your bond—whether that means you’re laughing at a hilarious miscommunication or screaming as the clock ticks down on a time-sensitive puzzle.This series has my . The emotional rollercoaster you experience with your friend is like no other. Every session of We Were Here is filled with memorable moments that leave a lasting impression. You’ll go from moments of intense concentration and puzzle-solving to lighthearted banter and moments of pure joy. The co-op gameplay isn't just a feature—it's the core of what makes this series so special. If you're looking for a game that will  in the best way possible, this is it.For those who’ve never played the series before, We Were Here: The Friendship is a fantastic introduction. It offers a  experience that eases you into the mechanics of the series without overwhelming you. The puzzles are as engaging as ever, but what really stands out is the emotional connection you’ll build with your partner as you navigate the game’s challenges together. If you’re new to the We Were Here universe, you’re in for a treat.A big  to the devs for crafting yet another unforgettable experience. With each new expansion, this series continues to grow in its ability to entertain, engage, and connect players in ways that few games can.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Fun side game from the main series, defiantly worth it if you have a friend and are looking for a short game to play together. Not sure if they give you this for beating the game or beating it perfectly but they did provide a 35% off coupon for We Were Here Together: Forever after finishing the game Hoping to see more content whether that's from more side games or mainline games
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to previos games.Gets little bit of repetitive if you try to get max results, but not too much.Don't have to kill each other in the end?! I don't know if it was a glitch, but we get 0 out of everything in the end. Maybe it happens if you don't use in-game radio? Or maybe if connection interrupts for a couple of milliseconds? I don't know.Not bad for a free game.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved every game in the series, and I enjoyed the absolute hell out of this one as well. The puzzles were super fun, and not too hard to figure out. The only time we had an issue was with the rng of the second puzzle. All in all, I'd give it a 9.5/10, because even though it took a while to get good rng with the 2nd puzzle, we enjoyed retrying it anyway. I can't wait for more puzzles in the future! :)
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: My partner and I have played all of the We Were Here series, and this little game took us back to what we loved when we first played We Were Here Too. Great puzzles with asymmetric information, with the focus being on communication. In The FriendShip, the "story" is mostly an endearing backdrop that, importantly, doesn't get in the way of the puzzles. I find the more spooky and mysterious backdrop more engaging personally, but was highly grateful to return to having the story as a background element/set-dressing. Whether that set-dressing is fun and playful or a bit eerie, as long as the puzzles are great, I'll always be happy to play!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun albeit short co-op experience, it consists of 3 minigames. Each can be beat with a gold, silver or bronze rating and focus on either collaborative quickfire communication, puzzle solving and spatial coordination. Visuals are very polished, with some pretty nice lighting. The music is also both somber and whimsical, I actually really enjoyed the atmosphere.At the current asking price (free) this is an absolute steal. The game took us around 4hs to 100% with plenty of restarts so do consider the bang for your buck when this ceases being free.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: The final 'trust' area was a bit too long for my liking, so when you failed the later challenges it took a really long time to get back to where you were, I ended up just skipping it and leaving with a silver star because I didnt want to do the build up again.other than that a really cute game, I already bought and played We Were Here Forever but if you didnt, the 35% discount is worth it! I would have paid for this game tbh even though it was short. A cute puzzle game, good fun
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: For free, it's great and as long as it's not too costly when it's no longer free. There's no replay value from games like this (unless maybe years down the line once you forget the solutions). The puzzles are fun, but short. Most of the game is waiting for animations to finish, a problem previous games also had with long intervals between actually doing the fun part. Only suffered from some small de-sync issues. If they could get more puzzles and less waiting around the series would be really good, but at the moment there's still just a lot of filler. The production value was good though, even if it was a little too drawn out for my liking!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, fun to play, especially to replay second mini-game (mostly because it's interesting and re-playable), but, this isn't going to be fun for people with small patience, because you have to re-play some levels A LOT to get gold tickets. But overall, this game is nice both from game design side, and as a game itself (+ it's good because it's free, and gives you a look on We Were Here game series before buying other games).
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I am glad Total Mayhem published another game from this awsome franchise We Were Here. Really like the idea of going for some side story from the main series of games. Really like the character designes and the puzzles were amazing and challenging. I also liked the idea of bronze, silver and golden tickets depending how you and your partner did in the minigames. I think it is great for players, who do not want to do some parts of puzzles or it is hard for them so they can skip some parts. The graphics are looking the same as in We Were Here Forever which I think is awsome. The soundtrack in this game is fabulous! The main theme of this game is one of the most beautiful soundtracks I have ever heard! I hope the amazing team Total Mayhem will do another games from the franchise We Were Here.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: This game differs from the other we were here games. But in a good way. So basically this game tests you and determines if you are ready to play the whole series of the games. This game is way shorter than the other ones. Its maybe as long as the first We Were Here. Whether you are a fan of the WWH series like me or a new commer, this game wont let you down. Prepare for yelling at your partner and getting yelled at by your partner when confusion reaches its limits. Prepare you the biggest trust fall in your life even tho its in a video game. Prepare for your brain to be fried by simple yet so tough puzzles. Check out the other games as well if you want more challange, story and of course beatiful moments with your partner where you swear to kill each other.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Played all their games before. This was a fantastic little edition, especially for free (free until mid October). Would have been happy paying £5/£10 for this. Played it with my consistent duo partner and we got full marks on all trials. Took two hours but none of the puzzles were "headache puzzles" which was lovely they were all really interactive and execution related whilst still being very clever. Well done again team and we look forward to playing the next game. I would love to see a proper built up story around these characters, like an adventurers guild or something of the such. Maybe takes them to different places/regions/times. Maybe they reunite or rescue those lost in the castle at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect introduction to the We Were Here series. I recommend playing this one first before any of the others and please play with actual friends and not the randoms, It'll mean so much more to you. The puzzles are fun to solve and get you and your coop partner either scratching heads or laughing at each other. Please don't feel guilty retrying the puzzles to understand how they work!Design wise, there were a couple of bugs near the end that caused a a few resets, small things like restarting a level would bug it out and you'd have to restart the whole game to fix it because you couldn't continue, or the levels would unfortunately bug out and sometimes missed assets or were glitching you through things, but those were easily overlooked and forgotten about while playing.Just to conclude I am pretty biased since me and my LDR fiance played all the We Were Here games before this one and the little jingle that plays in between the puzzles got me tearing up over how meaningful the games were.. Otherwise, loved the graphics the sound design and overall game!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: played this with my girlfriend and it was the most fun we've had on a game together since It Takes Two! definitely recommend it! only issue is that for the octopus mini-game you have to sprint jump to land on the different platforms, otherwise its amazing and I recommend it to everyone who wants to yell at some friends for a few hours!
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie...the physics in the 3rd level, the octopus side, the collisions a bit bad designed? I jump towards the right area but still fall because the platform did not catch up the speed, personally if this is "intentional" design...1 question for the devs..did u try the octopus part...i mean this game is juz a mini game to let you have an idea of their main game so...yea expect some unpolished side but the octopus part can be fixed quite easily i would say as I study game design so yea, you wan to play wif your frens sure but do know some part are extremely hard not as a design but as a unpolished part
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool addition to the We Were Here series. My brother and I beat it in 1h 50m for all gold; The second of the three major puzzles is a bit RNG though. If you liked any other We Were Here game or just want to see if the series is something for you and your friend or partner, i highly recommend trying Expeditions: The FriendShip! :)
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: The WWH series is one of my top favorites to play, and I would recommend playing each one if you have a good friend to play through em with. The puzzles were nice and the puzzles that had timers are always stressful in a fun way. I wish it was a bit longer (there's just not enough asymmetrical puzzle co-op games!) but I can't really complain with this being free for the first month. It's so worth giving it a shot, and the rest of the series if anyone comes across this game and hasn't played the series yet. The devs truly have something special with these games
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: My sister and I were big fans of the series and had no idea this existed until earlier this evening when a different game we intended to play wasn't working. How fortunate were we to stumble upon it a mere three days after release!The presentation is as top-notch as the best parts of Forever, and if one isn't stubbornly insistent on earning all the gold tickets (as we of course were), then it is probably a light one-hour affair and a fun ride.If you do try to get all the gold tickets though you might find that the jumping sections can be a bit fiddly and the very last exercise is quite stressful. It took *us* a lot of attempts anyway.Regardless, the ending is delightful and, for once, . We loved it. Keep making things like this please.

_childDocuments_.review: Game looked promising, and was free, what's there to lose?Initially I was not able to play the game due to a bug. However, an update pushed by the developers fixed the issue.This is a relatively short game, with only three 'main puzzles'. However, the puzzles are very well thought out and quite enjoyable. In particular the second puzzle really shines, and might be my favorite puzzle in the entire 'we were here' series thus far (second being 'the forge' in we were here forever). We had a blast solving it.There is so much to like, that it is easier to address the few negatives that there are. Essentially there are three minor criticisms that I have with the game.1) The game is quite heavy on resources. It even pins my quite modern GPU at 100% in the main menu.2) Some puzzles are very latency dependent, especially the third puzzle. If there is more lag between partners, it is much harder to give feedback and adjust.3) It can be quite tedious to redo most of the puzzle. This feedback again primarily affects the third puzzle. I feel it would feel less tedious if lighthouse switches stayed on, and there were shortcuts that opened up. Then again, the way it is now forces you to perfect the other elements of the puzzle, so I respect the conscious choice as well.Having to run back, wait for the ticket to be spit out, having to recycle it, and then running back to the start could definitely be shorter though.All in all, highly recommended, and even if it were a few euros it would be easily worth it. If this game and We were here forever indicate the level of polish for their future games, I am very excited to see what is coming next.
_childDocuments_.name: We Were Here Expeditions: The FriendShip

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little bitesized We Were Here experience. Great for those that have been thinking about investing into the series to get a taste of the complex puzzles and put their friendship to the test! Even as experienced WWH explorers, my friend and I still found these puzzles to be a fun and satisfying challenge. We both especially liked the concept of the second challenge and got stuck on that one for a hot minute.Overall, if this is your first time dipping your toes into WWH, it's a fun and short experience that will put you and your friend to the test. If you can handle this short adventure then you will really enjoy the rest of the series. For those that have already played WWH, this is a fun little sidequest which is hopefully a sign of things to come for another major release!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a great first experience of the series. The setup is somewhat straightforward, with quick tutorials, and each of the puzzles tested a different aspect of cooperative gameplay. I appreciated the fact that success could range from "basically competent" to full mastery of the challenge; for players who don't particularly enjoy one challenge or have struggles completing it, it is nice to be able to move on fairly quickly if necessary.The setting could have been more compelling, and the runtime is a bit padded with on-rails segments, but that doesn't detract from very good puzzle design. I think the game would be slightly improved with faster puzzle resets, but this was only seriously annoying on the last challenge. My only advice would be to play this with someone who: 1) Can have in-person or quality voice calls, 2) Can connect with low-to-moderate latency, and 3) is at a close skill level to oneself, as you won't know the challenges until you actually start, and you mostly can't switch which player works on which side of a puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: Even without playing any of the previous games, this is a wonderful start on learning and getting familiar with puzzle games! It's super fun and they smoothed out some of the gameplay elements. There is a chance to finish puzzles on a lower challenge level and higher challenge levels, which I think is a nice touch for people who are new. For the most fun experience I would recommend going for the gold-levels, as they give the most victorious feelings when you do pass them. Big props for the game developers for including the repeatability of the puzzles. The codes and pieces change, so you can't remember the order or anything. You will have to understand the puzzle and apply it every time. Wonderful, and definitely the previous 4 games have led me to a Legendary Friendship with my friend ;) Even if I had to pay for the game, I would've said the same - as all their previous work honestly has paid off to make this amazing. The only small detail we noticed is that in the last level you can get stuck weirdly after jumping off some platforms - or you can pushed off by some moving objects (don't want to spoil too much). Nothing else was buggy or weird. Freaking amazing!

The threshold to pass a level should be at a standard and then a bonus for going beyond that for the max score. Overall, my experience was an 8/10. loved it and can’t wait for DLC levels

name: Creatures of Ava
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Creatures of Ava: Deluxe Edition includes: Creatures of Ava Creatures of Ava: Artbook & Original Soundtrack Creatures of Ava: Deluxe Backpack Trinkets Set Creatures of Ava: WDC Charity Backpack Trinkets Set About the Game Features: Join a young nature explorer, Vic, on her expedition to planet Ava Explore 4 distinct and colorful ecosystems bustling with life Tame over 20 wild creatures with the music of a special flute Meet the naam, Ava’s inhabitants, and learn their unique customs Save the planet’s inhabitants from an infection called “the withering” Help Vic solve the secrets of Ava and her own troubled past Can you save a life? Welcome to Creatures of Ava, a unique creature-saver game inviting you to explore a world brimming with wild beings. Instilling joy and wonder, they provide a unique bond that enables you to utilize their skills for traversing the planet and solving environmental challenges. Once peaceful creatures, they now succumb to an unknown infection driving them to behave aggressively, which makes your mission to save them an urgent necessity. Exploration-driven Gameplay The gameplay encourages curiosity-driven exploration of its distinct ecosystems—such as the colorful Nari jungle or mysterious Mâruba swamp—creating an interconnected world. With non-aggressive combat mechanics designed for healing rather than defeating and indigenous Flute melodies that you play to tame creatures, the game further highlights the creature-saver nature of the experience. Meaningful Narrative Step into the shoes of Vic, a 22-year-old nature adventurer as she navigates through the immersive expedition alongside Tabitha, a composed and astute researcher. Together, you confront the recurring infection—called “the withering” by the local race of Naam—threatening Ava’s inhabitants. The game's narrative, co-created by Rhianna Pratchett, is a journey of wonder and mystery but also discovery, leading to the revelation of the planet's captivating secrets. Saving Through Understanding Creatures of Ava is a game featuring a dense, populated world of rich ecosystems filled with creatures that play a vital role in the planet’s natural balance. It goes beyond traditional creature-related genres, offering a deeper understanding and connection with the things you’ll encounter on Ava. Once you come to understand the true meaning of the infection, you will be challenged to step out of the human-centric point of view and learn about the real toll it takes to preserve the primal beauty at the very roots of Ava. After all, can you save something you don't understand?

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's just me, but I don't really want to fight or kill things. At least I don't anymore. The world is just too full of violence. I am so happy to have found this game. Welcome to a world where you get to explore, learn, and pet creatures. You are here to save them but in the end I think you really learn to save yourself. Fixing the problems and learning from the people and creatures of the planet feels so much better than just blasting zombies or pwning newbies at respawn points. If you are looking for a colorful game with whimsy and heart, then this is the game for you. And did I mention you get to HUG/PET all the creatures you find?

_childDocuments_.review: Encountered several gamebreaking bugs and oversights. The biggest one is one that everyone can run into easily:If you teleport all creatures of one species away from an area (fulfill the Rescue Robot's quota), no more creatures of that species will spawn in that area. That means if you have obstacles to clear, paths that require a Creature to explore, etc, you can no longer do those, and you will have areas that you will be permanently be unable to access for the remainder of the game. If there's creatures that you need for the Rescue Robot, key items, quest items, STORY ITEMS, etc, tough luck, you can't progress. And if there's a story item or something you need to interact with for story progression- you're just screwed and your game progression is locked forever. (NOTE: According to the devs- story items can't get stuck behind areas like this, but I've been told by other players on steam discussions that they can't do some quests because of it- so while we know Creatures/Key Upgrade Items/etc can get stuck, we're not entirely clear on the story/quest items yet)I attempted to get support on Steam Discussions, and several players were having the same bug with no way to fix it or around it. We tried many solutions: Reloading the game, area, completing quests- in hopes that creatures respawned- No dice. We tried bringing in creatures from other areas, but a wall blocks them off from leaving their original areas.I'm extremely disappointed. The demo had me so hyped, I literally set my alarm clock for this game's release to buy and play it the moment it came out. Seems I had too much faith in the game devs.To the dev response: Telling us to load an old save if we haven't noticed an area we didn't explore is not a solution, especially for the people in my Discussions thread who said they didn't notice it until hours later. We're not "rushing to teleport". The game TELLS us to teleport creatures away, we are literally trying to complete objectives that the game tells us to do.It's insane that this is intentional by design.EDIT 2: Refund request submitted. It's clear the dev has no immediate plans to change this, despite the unhappy players.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I was delighted at the start of this game (the animation art in the intro is GORGEOUS, the unique designs of the creatures, the mechanic of the flute to rescue the adorable lil guys), my experience was tainted by the fact you cannot return to an area once you've played through that section of the story. Whilst it allows you to tick the area off and put it to the back of your mind, it makes it incredibly frustrating when you realise there are incredibly missable things that are now locked behind a second playthrough. Honestly, I could only recommend this game if you wanted to play it as a stress-free, casual playthrough. Unless you go in with knowledge beforehand of the 100% requirements, you'll find yourself most likely having to completely restart if you don't enter with a guide. The Secret Hall requirement was completely missed for me since I didn't know about it until I was in the final area :(With minimal spoilers, you can use creatures to overcome obstacles like bridges or plant barriers, however once you rescue the creatures in that area there is no way to get to optional areas that are locked behind these obstacles. I also found that I was unable to meet the requirement for using certain creatures abilities (mostly the last area - apparently said creature can dig which I thought I could use to get my final 2 "ability" uses, however I couldn't find any locations and no longer had walls/columns to knock down), OR missing an image of an infected creature which are no longer able to be accessed because I had already rescued  them all. At the beginning, and whilst playing through the second area, I was really enjoying myself and wanted to 100% a game which is rare, but after a while I realised I would have to replay the ENTIRE game just because I missed 3 things - 1 infected image, 2 wind chimes & 1 creature ability requirement. HOWEVER: I have seen a recent post by a developer discussing updates in order to bring back creatures once you've rescued them all (unsure of whether they'll be infected or not), but unless there is some sort of sandbox mode where we can return to these creatures, it won't help the sour taste left in my mouth.I do genuinely adore this game, and would have probably liked my experience so much more if I stuck to my initial casual approach to playing it <3 That being said, I will stalk updates and posts in hopes that I can fix my review soon!!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like this game.I don't like games that remind me how easy it is to get attached to characters made out of pixels and voxels. I always end up disappointing myself with that attachment, which slowly grows only to leave me with a huge void in my heart by the end of the game.I don't like Creatures of Ava because I can't say "I wish it was longer." The gameplay is well-balanced; no chapter felt forced, and there was never a moment where I thought, "I wish this was shorter." The length of the game was perfect. I don't like this game because I'll never be able to play it for the first time again and experience that same positive impression of how one of the main gameplay elements—the camera—was designed. A long time ago, Beyond Good and Evil left a similar impression on me and I would risk saying that Creatures did the same good job in that matter. And finally, I don't like this game because, throughout my entire journey with Vic and Nimar, I managed to forget about everything else, only to be reminded of the everyday world with double the force once the main story ended.Creatures of Ava is a unique experience that will offer anyone willing to embark on a journey through Ava the pleasure of a well-developed story, characters, and the developer's passion, which can be felt at every corner. I don't like this game only because saying "I like it" is simply not enough.

_childDocuments_.review: In  explore and help heal the beautiful world of Ava while you befriend strange creatures and meet interesting people. You play as the main character, Vic, a researcher who arrives on the planet Ava with hopes of saving its inhabitants and wildlife from a planet-wide disease called the withering. There are four main biomes you will explore as you traverse that are each filled with their own flora and fauna.Use your camera to take photos of artifacts and people to flesh out the lore of the world and uncover the secret to the withering. Besides your trusty camera you also obtain a magic staff with various upgrades and a magical flute along the way. This game does have combat but encounters are not bloody or deadly. You do not kill any creatures but cleanse them of the disease using a magical staff. Once cleansed they can be befriended by using a magical flute given to you early in the game. , if you're not as musically inclined like myself. So combat relies more on dodging, jumping and evading than attacking outright while you use your staff to cleanse the creatures. Photography is important in this game, so take lots of pictures of creatures, plants and the people that you meet. There is an index called Avapedia that will catalog your finds as you take photos. The Avapedia will also tell you the research objectives you need to complete for each creature alongside the photos you’ve taken of them. This game does have a variety of puzzles to solve as you go along. Nothing too daunting. You can temporarily tame creatures and inhabit them, using their abilities to advance in a quest. Or you can use the upgrades and magical skills of your staff to solve puzzles like the temporary power of levitation. This game does auto-save at certain points but you can manually save at any time. I would recommend doing this periodically and especially before shutting down. Then when you jump back into the game you just have to hit continue and you spawn right where you saved last. I learned this the hard way so posting a warning so you don't mess up the way I did. When you reach any campfire move your ingredients collected to the campfire storage. They are all connected as a shared stash. You only have so much inventory space and each biome has their own plants. So think of the campfire as extended inventory. Truth be told even the campfire could use more slots. I missed out on collecting samples of every plant to turn in for a quest that requires a plant of each kind from each biome. The kicker, . So your locked out and so is your chance of getting those plants again!This game has lots of settings so each user can tweak their experience. The graphical settings are vast with display options, upscaling options and graphic settings such as motion blur, foliage, shadow and many more individual settings. There are also audio settings, accessibility settings such as subtitles, UI text scaling, game difficulty settings and settings for the in-game camera and flute guide. Controls can be changed (at least with keyboard and mouse). I never tested a controller however the game page does state that this game is mostly playable with a controller. Ava and its inhabitants are gorgeous. Overflowing with a vibrant palette of colours ranging from bright oranges, pinks, blues and more to create a world you want to explore. I can honestly say it is one of the most beautifully crafted games I have played, from the world to the creatures. And you can pet almost every creature in the game once you befriend them. The soundtrack to this game is relaxing and soothing. The music you play with your flute while trying to befriend the creatures is pleasing to the ear. Ambient sounds are fantastic in this game, from the blowing of the wind, to the water splashing or creatures making their unique sounds. Sound and music were certainly an important part in the crafting of this game and you can feel that as you become immersed into the world of Ava. There are also parts with some voice acting that is very well done, cut scenes or meeting important characters at various parts in the game. I wish this game had a dedicated photo mode. The in-game camera is okay but limited in size and frame. This game is too beautiful not to have a stand alone photo mode with filters, frames and poses you can do with the main character. Also adding in animals to your photos would be nice. If you’ve ever played Kena you’ll understand what a wonderfully designed photo-mode can bring to the game. This game deserves that same treatment. I really enjoy this game. Running around and jumping feels good. Taking photos, befriending the creatures or inhabiting one temporarily is interesting and unique. Each creature has its own quirks, sounds and movements.Learning to connect with the creatures by listening and learning each type of creature's own song in order to befriend them really leaves a sense of connecting with each of them. Music really is the language of Ava, the creatures, the plants and the people. Truly a beautiful game with a great narrative and adorable beasties to befriend and hug. 💖

_childDocuments_.review: Around 20h 3/10 1 Not yet, I hope someone will make a nice map with where to find all the collectibles. No Yes, but for the most part, the game will warn you about that.  No No No No No No, you can play on the story difficulty NoOhh Creatures of Ava, you're so beautiful and wholesome! I fell in love with the world-building and creatures already through the trailers and you didn't disappoint in-game <3. Also, the main character looks so good, and the creatures... I'm so happy that there is a "pet" button (And even an achievement tied to petting them all)In Creatures of Ava, you're playing as Vic (Aka StrongLeg and many other variations) who goes to the planet of Ava to save the creatures before the withering takes over. Your landing is suboptimal, but it is a nice way to get to know one of the local inhabitants who will introduce you to the others. From there on out you'll be on a mission to gather enough of each species to make sure they are not lost. To be able to do that and traverse the terrain, you'll have to solve lots of puzzles to clean up small parts of the map. Creatures of Ava is such a beautiful game. The world is huge and will keep you busy for around 15 hours, or more if you also go for 100%. Collectibles can be hidden very well with how big and detailed the world is, but it is just stunning! I also love the designs for all the different animals. Some designs will surprise you if you free them from the withering, but they are all so cute. Another highlight of Creatures of Ava is the music, so fitting and wonderful. and you're playing so many nice songs on your flute while herding the creatures to the safe spot to teleport them to the Ark. I love the story of Creatures of Ava. You're kinda an obnoxious human being who doesn't take the time to understand the world, however, that kinda is the point and will be addressed during the game. The game does such a good job of helping you understand more and more of Ava and telling you the story. I'm also thankful for a map and knowing where to go next. You'll also unlock teleporters along your journey. and what took me a few hours to realize... you don't have to teleport from portal to portal, you can teleport from anywhere on the map toward a teleporter. Which is so nice! During my playthrough, I have encountered some bugs. Mostly creatures get stuck in walls/terrain but gladly if you leave the zone and come back, they are reset back to their original spot. And sometimes the button to talk to people didn't work. I had this very badly by one specific sidequest, but after hopping around the NPC from all different angles, at one point it finally triggered. And the last one is that I'm missing one co-op action for the bird in the first area. I'm unsure if I did do the action with another creature and now missing just one point for that, or if it is a bug. I have wandered around the grassland for hours to find a spot to trigger it, but haven't found it anywhere. This feels weird because for most of the creatures you have way more opportunities to do the co-op ability than is needed to 100% that entry in the Avapedia.Creatures of Ava has a wide variety of different types of achievements. Most of them are for just completing everything and finding everything. There are also ones that do something with combat, like linkin 5 enemies together with your beam attack, or getting multiple status effects at once. And there are also achievements for finding all the collectibles. For the most part, the game does a great job warning you when you'll move past a point of no return and that you should finish specific things if you want to before moving on. However, a few things seem to fall through the grapevines and can still be missed. As mentioned above, I missed early on one co-op action which means that I couldn't 100% all the creatures in the game. This made me think I would never had a chance to 100% the game in that playthrough and I did ignore the later messages about the points of no return. I can say now, that the one with the bird I still missed. A little later at the end of the second area, I thought I found another bug because one of the required actions I couldn't do, but this was on purpose. The game doesn't make it clear but you can pet it later on in the game. I hope someone will be able to make a nice guide where to find all the hidden things, I would love to replay the game with a guide at hand to 100% Creatures of Ava as it is such a wonderful game! I give Creatures of Ava 4 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Creatures of Ava is a chill and relaxing action-adventure game, or it would have been if it weren't for some poor design decisions and bugs.The game looks great, and the writing is very good too, CoA is almost worth playing just for the story and characters. Since it's a casual action-adventure, there just have to be goofy exchanges with a cast of goofy characters :), and CoA does that trope really well.Unfortunately we can't do much with the creatures, and there's not much to do in the open world in general. We can control the creatures only inside a small area, and mostly we just use a creature to open a passage. It's disappointing and rather inconvenient that we don't get any transportation means.The "combat" isn't very enjoyable. The movement and the camera behavior during fights are rather awkward, especially since it's necessary to keep aiming all the time. The animations for the creatures aren't smooth at all, so it's hard to follow the creatures' movements.There are only two buttons for spells, so I have to constantly juggle the assigned spells. Aiming is inconsistent, I never know whether or not my spell will connect with the target.I think some of the design decisions in CoA are very wrong for a casual action-adventure: a limited inventory size and, at the same time, too many different kinds of potions and flowers; environmental hazards everywhere, with Vic taking damage and getting status ailments from everything; attacks which look like they should be avoidable by jumping or standing on a platform but aren't.All that is made worse by the bugs (or some strange oversights). In addition to the inventory size being quite small, the inventory gets automatically rearranged all the time, ruining my manually created layout. The creatures not just move slowly and tend to get lost when they should be following Vic and to scatter immediately if Vic gets into a fight, they also constantly get stuck on the environment. The game doesn't autosave after actions such as unlocking skills, so I have to redo quite a lot of things if I get killed.I almost gave up playing at some point because of a number of small but frustrating things. I'm glad I didn't, because I wouldn't have seen the T.A. otherwise, but still, the game could have been so much more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: === SUMMARYCreatures of Ava has its flaws, but it's still a very good time. The core gameplay loop is surprisingly well designed, and the story is competently told. Where a lot of games fail to make you feel invested in the setting, Creatures of Ava takes the time and quest space to build stories in its world, giving you the breathing room to get invested in the people and creatures in it. Some minor bugs and quality of life issues can annoy me sometimes, but all around I was satisfied with the really fun combat system and satisfying exploration mechanics/rewards, all wrapped up in a story that actually bothered to make me care about it.=== GAMEPLAYGameplay-wise, I was pleasantly surprised by how good movement and "combat" felt. Movement-wise, the game is fluid and I never felt bothered by the controls or how Vic moves. However, the game could do itself a favor and get out of the player's way sometimes. You'll deal with some uncancellable animations such as petting creatures and clambering over obstacles. While annoying, they don't cause a big issue.The combat is rather unique. When you find an infected creature, you have to maintain an energy beam connection to that creature by holding a button. However, each creature has its own move set that it uses to throw you around, damage you, and inflict status effects on you. Combined with four player spells (used in combat and exploration), this works out to be a really fun loop that, while not very challenging, is still remarkably engaging.Outside of combat, the player is expected to explore the world and use the special abilities of the creatures they cure to solve small navigation puzzles through a possession mechanic. The puzzles very rarely make you stop to think; it's usually as simple as finding a nearby creature, possessing it, and using its ability on a glowing object. However, this is still fun for a time. And as I mentioned before, the spells you have are consistently used in exploration, not just combat. That's honestly a good achievement design-wise.=== PROBLEMSThe biggest cons of the game are perhaps two-fold. The first is that the main gameplay starts to overstay its welcome after a bit. However, it was only soon after I started to feel burnt out that the game eased up and changed up the formula a bit to streamline the final region. That was a good decision on the designers' side and it mitigated this complaint.The second issue is the bugs. There are a number of them littered about, but I'm happy to say none of them significantly hampered the experience. The bugs were things like music cutting in or out at incorrect moments or the in-game encyclopedia constantly adding exclamation marks to NPC entries every time I spoke with one, despite the entry not updating. There were some hitbox problems where creatures (or I) would get stuck on terraing. All around, only minor annoyances. The core of the game was relatively well polished, it could have just done with another pass to fix some things and add quality of life features.Despite these flaws, I really enjoyed my time with the game. If you're looking for a good exploration experience with a relatively well-written story, Creatures of Ava is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Creatures of Ava features Vic, a scientist working for an intergalactic corporation. Her mission is to save the dying planet Ava from a little-known and rapidly spreading infection called “the Withering” by evacuating as much of the planet's fauna as possible before they are all consumed by this virus. The game at first seems cute, fun, and very positive.Unfortunately, as the story progresses, you slowly realize that it is not all that happy and you are assailed by a sense of sadness that culminates in a depressive ending that makes you wonder to yourself how lousy people we really are. What begins as a wholesome mission to save a planet evolves into something grander as human ignorance and blinding empathy are slowly swept away through understanding the cultures of the Naam and Ava. Throughout the story, the construction of the overall message of the game is subtle. In fact, it plays well with the way we, as human beings, tend to think that our generosity is the only way. We view our altruism as what is best. It is only at the last minute that it is revealed how horrible human beings can be, especially when it comes to governments or mega-organizations that use members' altruism for their own goals, that all is revealed. In the same vein, the final revelation of what is happening to the planet is fantastic and makes us realize that we humans need to listen more before we act. We tend to stick our noses in places we have no right to because we think we are helping. This is well demonstrated in Vic's interactions with the Naam, the natives of Ava. They do not seem interested in this withering away. They see it as a celebration while still not being sure what is going on. Each type of person Vic interacts with has different feelings about humans because of past experiences. Some are for the best, many are ambivalent, and some actively hate us because of what others have done before. Vic, however, does not care. She is just there to help! She is not like other humans. Vic just wants to save the Naam and collect different species from their natural habitats to give them a second chance. It is only when she really listens after a "wake-up call" that everything clicks. And this is something you may have read numerous times before about how a person has meddled or intervened to “just help” but made situations much, much worse. Creatures of Ava, even with many edges, conveys an impactful message.

_childDocuments_.review: is a cute and colorful creature-collector with four distinct biomes, over 20 tamable life forms, and interesting Metroidvania-esque level designs. It also packs a lot more narrative punch than I was originally expecting, given its cuddly critters and relaxing, flute-heavy soundtrack.    You’ll play as Victoria Hamilton, a naive yet empathetic young explorer sent to planet Ava on a conservation rescue mission to save Ava’s myriad organisms from “the Withering,” a mysterious ailment that corrupts all it touches. Or so you’re led to believe by your employer, the Aleph Corporation, and lab partner/love interest(?), Tabitha.  After a bumpy landing on Ava and a traumatic flashback about her parents, Vic encounters the indigenous and genderless Naam people (or "the Breads” as my naan-obsessed wife kept calling them). Half-offended and half-amused by Vic’s offer to teleport them off planet to escape the Withering, the quirky Breads I mean  nonetheless give Vic a flute and teach her the songs of each ecosystem—Grassland, Jungle, Swamp, and Dune—allowing her to tame and then control the planet’s interesting and surprisingly cuddly creatures.   That is, assuming Vic can de-Wither them first. Using an ancient Ghost Busters-copyrighted vacuum staff granted to her by Nim’ar—a strange Naam with a stranger past—Vic gains the ability to de-corrupt each Withered creature, then use them to traverse Ava’s treacherous biomes. At the end of each biome, you’ll face a puzzle and/or boss, then reach a shrine that effectively levels up your staff, giving it a new ability and a new means of bypassing Ava’s many environmental puzzles and hazards. In this sense,  functions a bit like a “gear-gated” Metroidvania, and I was impressed by each biome’s looping, interconnected level design that changes as the Withering progresses. Before moving on to the next ecosystem, however, Vic will need to complete the current ecosystem’s creature-saving quota set by the Aleph Corporation. Now, as a passionate hater of all things fetch quest, I was originally worried by both this requirement and the fairly generic side quests thrown my way by the Naam. However, there are tons of little mobile teleporter bots scattered about each ecosystem, and the game’s flute-tamer minigame is pretty forgiving, meaning you’ll never have too hard a time rounding up animals like Snow White... er, Snow Black?  Alas, not every bug in Ava is cuddly. I encountered a number of weird game breakers that necessitated reloads—luckily, the game has an auto-save function, but it’s a bit random when it triggers, so remember to manually save every now and then. Hopefully, the pre-release build I received last week has since received some significant polish.  But even with the occasional bug,  is still a charming little creature collector with thoughtful narrative themes, decent albeit infrequent voice acting, and genuine character development. For $25 and about 20 hours of playtime, I think  presents above-average value, so I’ll give it an aggregate MEGA score of 3.53/5 (full scoring breakdown from "Plot" to "Sound" available in the video review) and am happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: In general, this game is fun, its combat design is imaginitive, and it is a beautiful game. The designers should be very proud of their overall implementation of a "nonviolent" combat and exploration themes.However, the "rescue the animals" overall objective shows a lack of foresight and (this may be intentional, I'm only 4 hours in) contrary to the theming. Rather than removing a certain number of animals from the map, your success seems to remove virtually *all* animals from the map. This can cause at least one error where the game softlocks because you "rescued" the animal you needed to progress, and can otherwise interfere with certain completionism objectives that rely on an animal being on the map. Forgot to pet a species of animal before rescuing them? So far, the only way I've seen to resolve it is to roll back to a previous save.Additionally, the world is so.. quiet, when I'm done. I don't hear the birds, I don't hear the songs. Maybe this is an intentional part of the theming where eventually it's revealed that we were wrong all along, but the world feels deathly quiet as a result of my success.

_childDocuments_.review: Creatures of Ava is an action-adventure game that mixes exploration with the collection of alien creatures. You play as Vic, a researcher who has been sent along with her partner Tabitha to save all the creatures from the planet of Ava before an infection called “The Withering” consumes it. From the first minutes of gameplay you will see how beautiful and colorful this world is. It’s populated not only by cute and colorful creatures, but also by ancient inhabitants who call themselves Na’am.The story takes place through four open-world regions, each one with distinctive quests, biomes and fauna variety. Although the main quest always suggests some form of emergency, you can take it slow, enjoy the beauty of Ava and help the locals with their problems. While the story is decent enough for this type of “creatures hunting” game, most of it is spoiled right at the beginning. Despite discovering new alien life forms, including the Na’am population, Vic’s reaction is often too quiet and unimpressed, as if she has seen them before. The Na’am have hosted other humans in the past and learned their language, but what are the chances that they’ve learned exactly the same language as Vic (in my case, English) and practiced it for over 20 years? Maybe I’m just overthinking it, but minor inconsistencies like these didn’t allow me to fully enjoy the story, which is also quite predictable for someone who has played other similar sci-fi games (like The Gunk).The game’s main objective is to extract a sufficient number of different creatures in each region in order to continue the story. First, you will go through a tutorial that covers all the gameplay aspects and grants you a magical staff known as Nafitar; this is your main non-violent weapon that you can only use to cure creatures from the infection and unlock new areas by destroying parts of the infection. Not all creatures are infected, but those who are have become aggressive and will attack while you try to cure them from a distance, so all you have to do is dodge and launch a beam from your magical staff until their health bar is fully depleted. While combat is generally simple and easy, also due to the generous amount of health potions you can craft and carry, it can also be very annoying. During combat the camera will automatically lock on the creature you are curing, but when there are more creatures around you it will be impossible to know when they attack because they are often off-screen. You need to pay attention to the sound they make, but it’s still difficult to avoid incoming attacks from multiple directions. An option for manually moving the camera during combat would have been greatly appreciated (and will hopefully be implemented).After you have found some friendly creatures (or cured them if infected) you need to communicate by using a special flute and repeating the same music notes you see on the top of the creature’s head. It’s a short mini-game that you will have to repeat often to bring creatures on your side and lead them to the nearest bot that will teleport them to the Ark. Once you have rescued the minimum number of creatures in the area, you can still continue rescuing more but there won’t be any extra reward other than experience points; these can be used to unlock more abilities for Vic and the Nafitar, but they do not revolutionize the experience. You can use your camera to take pictures of creatures like in Pokémon Snap, but if feels optional and you should only do it if you want to complete the archive. Additionally, once you have tamed a creature, you can use their abilities to solve environmental puzzles, uncover treasures, destroy barriers and more. The animations, while controlling creatures, are still a bit rough unfortunately. Overall, the mix of these different mechanics isn’t perfect and certainly lacks depth, but it works pretty well with the level design. There is of course some repetition because you basically do the same thing in each area, with combat lacking depth and the flute mini-game quickly becoming boring.Artistically speaking, the game looks very pretty, but also a bit generic. I have seen this sort of art style in other games (especially this color palette), so it didn’t surprise me except for a few wonderful views. The performance on PC is great and the game also supports Unreal Engine 5 new Lumen technology, which adds realistic lighting and reflections, but also has a big impact on the frame rate. In the pre-release version I played (without any day one patches applied), there were a few minor bugs, and a sudden crash during the arrival of Tabitha damaged my save file and blocked the progression of the main quest. Fortunately, you can manually save at any time and there are plenty of autosaves too, so I just reloaded the most recent one to fix it.  I think that Creatures of Ava is primarily aimed at a young audience who love cozy and peaceful games, with a great focus on rescuing creatures rather than fighting them to death. The colorful planet of Ava is beautiful and certainly offers a lot to explore, but the story won’t satisfy sci-fi enthusiasts and the game mechanics are too simple to offer a challenging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Before writing this review I really thought hard about what to write for it. It was a hard choice between recommending the game and not recommending it, because this game is absolutely beautiful and really fun to play. That's really disheartening. When I play a game like this, I want to take my time to explore, and instead it feels like I'm being rushed to do something extremely frustrating and time consuming if I want to get all achievements, which I may have already locked myself out of from the first biome, due to no creature respawning/being able to use creature abilities. It still says I'm missing an Ohol ability and an infected Kraj, but I've rescued all the species in the grassland...I'm at the point where if I had wanted to, I wouldn't be able to get a refund if I tried, so while I recommend the game- or at least the demo if that's still available- I caution new players to really think about things before they buy to play. There is a surprising amount of miss-able content and while I personally haven't run into anything storywise yet, I'm cautious myself going forward.I'm sorry developers, but your responses to other reviews like this is extremely disheartening and I hope that something changes soon to allow other players to get the opportunity to enjoy your wonderful game.~ D.C.

_childDocuments_.review: YES, YES 100% YES.This game is a perfect storm of everything I love from every game I've enjoyed in the last few years. The open world exploration reminds me of Slime Rancher, with its colorful flora and free-roaming fauna. Speaking of fauna, the mechanic where you can control a creature and swap to other creatures at will is a very fun mechanic, and one of the things I loved about Lost Ember. Then you've got your Metroid Prime vibes, what with slowly ascending and lowering circular platforms to get to new levels, and coming back to certain areas once you have the right abilities. And that's just a few of the similarities worth mentioning. You could also argue that the Astaris bare similar resemblance to the Chozo from Metroid, being bird-like and leaving behind ruins and ancient messages. It really feels like Creatures of Ava enjoys making nods to other known and lesser known games, and it's very endearing.It feels like this was perfectly crafted to appeal to me, and I'm so glad I took a chance on it. I played it blind, taking my time, and then looked up a guide to get the final easter egg. I'm completing my saga with the game by writing this review and letting you know you should absolutely play this! It has a very meaningful story and wonderful characters and dialogue, and you're sure to have a blast.

I haven't found anything I dislike or that I would change.It's a Save the Planet Creature Collector, and the musical mini games are creative and fun - but not challenging, which is fine by me. I'm not sure why this game hasn't picked up more traction in the cozy game community yet but I hope it does. I don't think it'll win game of the year simply because I'm not sure that it has quite that much depth, and the game feels fresh and cozy but not exactly groundbreaking - but that's okay for a cozy comfort game to play when you don't want to get sucked into hundreds of hours of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone would ask me what I like most about the world Ava, I couldn't decide. I absolutely adore the cheeky, sportive main with her vivid mimic and gestures, the way she dotes  and fawns on any creature - not fast enough to escape -  she can pet. I still melt at her shriek "It's so fluffy, I'm gonna dieeee". Whoever designed Vic did a great job, she is very alive to me, same for her snarky replies and enthusiasm. I completely disagree with anyone considering her ugly and I really love her voice!Apart from Vic I can't recall how often I stood still and turned around slowly to take in the beautiful world with all its details - ran over to a spot or got out the camera to zoom into something that interested me. Kudos to those who designed this world with a plethora of imagination, creativity and love for details. I'm in the 2nd biome atm and really have difficulties focussing on the quests or map directions because I look around so much.Do I love the creatures? You bet! Do I pet? Ofc, I do, the animations of rolling over and showing their bellies is too cute to miss out. And here again, such an imaginative way to design otherworldly creatures who can aid Vic by clawing, shrieking, singing, burying etc etc. I only capture the questwise absolute minimum of animals, as I suspect the Corporation to not  build a bio arc out of selflessness and sincerely hope, they will be released back to their natural habitat. It's great fun for me to learn their taming tunes on the flute.The Naam, the race living with Ava, in Ava, on Ava. I'm a big fan of the chief and his distrust against humans - and I often nod or smile in self-recognition when the Naam comment on human behaviour and thus show how ridiculous humans can be, be it in a game or in RL.A huge compliment on the music in this game, been humming the grassland main theme a lot and often stood still to listen. I think this will be one of the rare occasions where I plan to buy the soundtrack.So, yes, I wholeheartedly recommend this game  to gamers who want to immerse into a wonderful world -  like to tame/pet/help animals - are interested in a fascinating story.

_childDocuments_.review: Update (18/08/2024): My original review remains below for transparency. I'm willing to recommend Creatures of Ava with the caveats discussed below. I managed to finish the game (despite almost being thwarted by game breaking bugs), immensely enjoyed the ending and found it very poignant. However, I was still unable to achieve 100% due to some poor design choices and aforementioned bugs, which soured the experience in the end. Unfortunately, I am unable to recommend Creatures of Ava at this time. There is no doubt that the game is incredibly impressive for a sophomore title from an independent studio. The game is distinctly AA, but has an AAA sheen. The storyline is sweet, fairly predictable and Avataresque - but I have been enjoying it. Voice acting outside of cutscenes would have been appreciated, and it is a shame that some of the more significant emotional beats were not voiced. The graphics are not overly technically impressive, but the art is gorgeous - I was particular enamoured by the designs of the eponymous Creatures of Ava, by the Naam, and by the beautiful environments. The animations are less impressive, but the creatures all have a distinct personality and it is novel to observe them through the camera whilst hiding in long grass. The gameplay is a marriage between Beyond Good and Evil, Pokémon Snap and classic Legend of Zelda. It didn't set my world alight, but what is here is competent and congruous with the storyline - it feels like every game mechanic ties into the xenoanthropology/xenobiology and conservation hook. The open world is compact and pleasant to explore, and the biomes are distinct. Exploring the grasslands is very different to exploring the jungle, and so on - the way the zones are built has a pleasant "loop" and there are even shades of Dark Souls in how opening a shortcut can drop you into an earlier location by surprise. Overall, the game feels much more than the sum of its parts. Regardless of the above, the game simply lacks polish. The most egregious is the following: all fans of Pokémon and Pokémon Snap understand that filling out the Pokédex is the ultimate goal, and Creatures of Ava has its own Pokédex in the form of the "Avapedia", which completing 100% was made impossible five hours in when I used one creature to lower a bridge, rather than another, arbitrarily. As there are no other bridges I can use the creature on, I cannot trigger its "co-op ability" and therefore complete the Avapedia. The creature is there, I can use the ability, but because it isn't used on an interactable object, it doesn't register. In addition, the conceit of the game is "rescuing" creatures using rescue bots scattered about the open world, and so it is possible to lock yourself out of Avapedia completion (or even entire areas of the open world and collectibles) if you rescue creatures ahead of methodically completing the Avapedia. The game does not warn you that creatures will not respawn when rescued, and so you cannot avoid this without being aware of the issue. The animals are almost constantly clipping into each other when roaming the world, which breaks immersion and makes getting a good photograph for the Avapedia an exercise in frustration. The animals (and occasionally your player character) become stuck in geometry (the former more often) - thankfully, this was always resolve via reloading a save. In addition, entire zones of the open world are locked out as the story progresses, meaning that if you don't get 100% completion of these zones before progressing the storyline, you miss out completely - including on permanent character upgrades. In the developer's defence, this is telegraphed quite clearly before you finish a zone. I am currently unable to finish the rescue quest for a zone and therefore progress the storyline, because a rescue bot has disappeared completely from the world and does not return on reloading the game. I can see on Steam Discussions that other players have been impacted by this gamebreaking bug, and I am incredibly disappointed to experience what feels like a final insult from this game. I have raised my concerns about the issues with 100% completion, however this was dismissed by the developer with a copy-paste response that failed to recognise the specifics of my situation in the game. I have also now raised the gamebreaking bug caused by the disappearing rescue bot, but do not have much hope of a fix given their attitude towards raised concerns. This game could be fantastic, but I have to recommend that you stay away until further patches and polish arrive. I'm sure that if the developers do fix these issues, this game will be on hidden gems lists in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews Video: Creatures of Ava is a family-friendly experience and therefore, comfortable. Who hasn’t spent hours searching for adorable creatures in vibrant, joyful worlds, with the aim of collecting them? In Creatures of Ava, the premise is similar, although the main objective is a bit different. This is an experience that overflows with affection, carrying a touching story that shows players the importance of bonds between individuals, understanding different ideologies, and finally, the cycle of life and its self-regeneration.As expected, the player will fill the screen as the main character of this adventure, taking on the role of Victoria Hamilton, an environmental scientist working for an intergalactic organization. “Vic” and her team’s mission is to save the vibrant planet Ava from an infection called “The Withering.” To do so, it’s necessary to evacuate all of its fauna and flora to a sort of Noah’s Ark before everything becomes corrupted. The game is marked by solving small puzzles, entirely connected to using the various creatures available in each region. There will be moments of reflection in their resolution, but also moments of action, where confronting creatures will be inevitable to free them from the infection that plagues the entire planet.Creatures of Ava is primarily a story-driven adventure. However, its gameplay is perfectly connected with the plot, creating a magical and highly immersive tale. After landing on the strange planet of Ava, Vic finds a sort of staff with a magical aura called the Nafitar, which she uses to heal creatures infected by “The Withering.” After freeing them from this malicious control, Vic will have the opportunity to enchant them by playing their specific melody. Each creature will have a pair of abilities that make them distinct from the others and will help the player in various tasks, such as pushing heavy stone pieces, jumping on sticky platforms, or opening paths for ground traversal to other areas.The combat itself is easy to understand. It involves using the Nafitar to fire a beam of light that envelops the creatures in a healing aura, eventually freeing them from the infection. However, not everything is simple, as some creatures are easier to heal than others. Even so, Vic can trap several creatures in her beam at once, creating a fascinating game of control and positioning. If she takes damage, the beam will be interrupted, and the player will have to repeat the healing process.In addition to the creatures, the inhabitants of Ava who can communicate with humans, the Naam, a race with owl-like human traits, carry the heavy burden of their history. The narrative is told through side quests where the player helps each individual resolve their conflict, which culminates in a better understanding of their mission. Each Naam, whether a tribe mentor or not, quickly becomes a memorable and impactful character for the player. Each personality trait is conveyed through the dialogue, creating a fun and exciting atmosphere, set against a backdrop of cozy colors like green, purple, and pink.One negative aspect I have to point out is the pacing. After nearly 15 hours of gameplay and a lot of side content, I found myself in the final area, only interested in completing the main mission, largely due to the frankly tedious side quests that require a lot of walking to complete. Yes, there are fast travel points, but even so. The world, though limited, gives the feeling of an open world, and while there aren’t any relics to collect, it’s possible to upgrade the character, such as increasing the number of items that can be placed in Vic’s backpack or extending her health bar. Another downside was its performance, as in certain areas, there are noticeable frame drops, which is inconvenient.In summary, Creatures of Ava presents itself as a delightful experience with some interesting story twists that culminate in a heavy ending. Its inspiration from Nintendo titles is quite evident, but its dedication to memorable characters and a cozy atmosphere gives it all the tools to stand out from other titles in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Creature of Ava is a visually stunning adventure that draws you into its lush, vibrant ecosystems. The bond you create with the creatures is one of the game's highlights, especially through the ability to tame, pet, and help them recover from 'the withering.' Vic’s journey adds emotional depth to the exploration, with her past unraveling as you progress through the game. The mix of puzzle-solving, creature-taming, and environmental challenges keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging. Overall, Creature of Ava offers an unforgettable blend of exploration, heartwarming interactions, and a beautifully crafted world that’s a joy to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Creatures of Ava is a good adventure game for casual player. The platforming, the puzzle are easy to understand. the non violent battle mechanism feels fresh to this type of game. The visual is veryy eye-catchyAlso i like the story very much, i love the twist, and you guys successfully delivered some good messages based on the relationship between human and Ava's people especially when they try to solve a big problem in the Ava with their own way and perspective.
