_childDocuments_.review: Creatures of Ava has everything you want in a cozy game, beautiful music, gorgeous art, adorable animals and much much more. This story driven open world game has you saving the animals of Ava talking with the people and exploring the ruins of the humans who came here before.Check out my curator page for more cozy recs!
_childDocuments_.name: Creatures of Ava

_childDocuments_.review: Creatures of Ava is a really enjoyable game that offers a different perspective on exploration and discovery. It is also coming in for a lot of unfair criticism simply due to the protagonist being a female POC, which is absolute nonsense. I would urge anyone to read the content of the negative reviews for the game and decide whether each is an objective opinion (some of which there are) or subjective prejudice.This game casts you as someone attempting to save the world of Ava from "The Withering" - a corrupted plant growth that appears to be taking over the world, and it is your job to catalogue the flora and fauna of the world while saving enough of the animal life to "save" Ava. I don't know what that means yet - I've only just completed the first of four biomes - but I've enjoyed my experience so far. The graphics are fantastic, the game is largely non-violent, with "combat" taking the form of trying to cleanse corrupted creatures by absorbing the negative energy possessing them using a rod you discover early in the game. It has a little clunkiness to it, and there is an ongoing issue with collectables and secrets becoming inaccessible since "saved" animals don't repopulate, and you need to use their special abilities to access certain areas. That said, the devs are aware of this, and it is a very friendly and enjoyable game, and I am looking forward to discovering more of the world that has been created here. Story-wise, it might be a little thin, but the discovery element has proved to be very engaging so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Creatures of Ava

_childDocuments_.review: A first look:I haven’t been able to play as much as I wanted yet, but with the weekend around the corner I’ll have more time to jump in.So far it has been a blast tbh, the creatures are beautiful, the planet Ava is breathtaking, the Naam are… well they’re the Naam; they’re special for sure and my dialogue/story far with them really made me laugh a few times. Because I don’t want to spoil it I’ll keep it vague and just say how I love “being one” with Ava. more proper review will come eventually, but I deff already wanted to give my two cents and just a thumbs up for support. I really like this game so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Creatures of Ava is a thoroughly enjoyable adventure with fun platforming and puzzling with a dash of adorable creatures and humorous interactions. While it does have its flaw, they are quickly forgotten when you're busy giving your newly-tamed friend a proper belly rub as Vic squeals in delight. _childDocuments_.review: "Creatures of Ava" is an enchanting blend of exploration, creature collecting, and world-building set in the lush, vibrant world of Ava. The game invites players to embark on a journey filled with discovery, where the primary objective is to collect, nurture, and battle a variety of unique and imaginative creatures. The visuals of  are stunning, with a beautifully designed environment that feels both fantastical and organicThe story of "Creatures of Ava" is a heartwarming tale of friendship, adventure, and discovery. While the plot isn’t groundbreaking, it is well-written and full of memorable characters. The game’s narrative does a good job of keeping the player engaged, with plenty of side quests and lore to uncover. The soundtrack of  is both soothing and immersive, perfectly complementing the game’s whimsical atmosphere. Truly recommend this game if you are into platforming, puzzles, and "combat," while gathering cute creatures.

This game has personally touched me in so many ways and will most likely be in my top games I played in 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Overall: 9/10 GameThe overall story and notion is, I would say, pretty good. The storyline is clean, and the "Combat" is very easy to learn, but challenging at the same time. Well worth a playthrough, even if you watch some games between. Only thing is it isn't really optimized neatly, and forces you to start out with ultra settings on, so if you have a lower end pc and need it to run properly, look to adjust settings early if on PC>In-Depth:Storyline - 10/10The story underneath is one that takes you for a bit of a stumble. Even though you feel like you know, and how it leads you at the end (and may seem overly obvious), you still kind of get hit with a left hook at the end. Very much a beautiful story to learn from and to guide you through possible difficult times.Artwork - 9/10Extremely vibrant and different in just about every where, the stark difference of the Withered areas and the calm areas creates amazing dynamics. I really really liked the contrast, and it helped feed into the storyline extremely well.Controls - 7/10The controls were extremely simple, and the abilities were easy to learn. However, in terms of accessibility, it seemed a bit off. Mainly, turning off rumble is a key for me, as the rumble causes some arthritis pain to flare up, so I had to swap to keyboard & mouse. Also, the snapping of the staff was difficult to hit properly, as some of the hitboxes on creatures was slightly off. Very minor things though.Overall, I loved it. Hope you all play it as well!

_childDocuments_.review: I just started playing the game, and I'm absolutely loving it! The premise of rescuing creatures on a foreign planet while cleansing its corruption is both engaging and heartwarming. The world is a visual treat, with vibrant, stylized art that feels alive with color and creativity. Exploring the planet is pure joy, and the ability to take pictures of the creatures adds a delightful layer of interaction. But what I love the most is playing the flute. You can actually play the flute!!Highly recommend this gem to anyone looking for a beautiful and immersive adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: Creatures of Ava

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge collecting player, love Ooblets, Slime Rancher, you name it... Creatures of Ava was highly anticipated for me, and I was not let down! Beginning story is well drawn, and farther in has a lot of deeper meaning attached. Game Mechanics are a lot more fun when having to dodge and work around infected creatures to tame, compared with other games that are simply feed to collect. I love that there is a skill tree involved, and that you develop more as you immerse yourself in the game play. I usually wait longer into playing a game to leave a review, but this game has been so much fun I figured I needed to do one right away. All in all, highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Creatures of Ava

_childDocuments_.review: Such a nice creature collector game! The world is absolutely stunning, the creature designs beautiful and silly, where each creature has their own little quirk. And yes, you can pet them all! What got me most in the game is the music. It fits the game pretty perfectly and adds to the biomes that you visit. And the story/stories being told have caught me by surprise as well. I wasn't expecting to be moved as much as I had been. Thinking this was just a silly game to which you can relax to. Oh boy was I wrong. The longer you play, the more you are captivated by the story. I've read through some of the other reviews on here and some of them talk about this 'bug' where you have to collect some creatures and they will go away for the rest of the game. Which will result in you not getting some of the collectibles. Well, that's not a bug. That's literally part of the game and people not exploring enough before they do the main objective. It's part of the game! And it's literally an exploration game. So go explore, see the world and all that before you do what your stupid corporate job tells you to do. Other than that, the only real bug-like thing I've encountered is that some creatures get stuck on an ant or something. Or they get stuck in the walls, because they can't move all of a sudden anymore when I order them to follow me. But that's easily fixed by going back and forth between the lands.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the demo and I've really enjoyed the full game so far too. The world and creatures are so pretty and vibrant, the characters have made me smile, and I'm looking forward to exploring more of Ava. I'm about 15% through according to the game, at 2.6 hours played, but I like to take my time. I've had zero problems playing with an xbox controller. It might not be a super long or meaty narrative game, as per some other reviews, but it's been a joy to explore!

_childDocuments_.review:
Welcome to Creatures of Ava, a unique creature-saver game inviting you to explore a world brimming with wild beings. Instilling joy and wonder, they provide a unique bond that enables you to utilize their skills for traversing the planet and solving environmental challenges. Once peaceful creatures, they now succumb to an unknown infection driving them to behave aggressively, which makes your mission to save them an urgent necessity.

Step into the shoes of Vic, a 22-year-old nature adventurer as she navigates through the immersive expedition alongside Tabitha, a composed and astute researcher. Together, you confront the recurring infection - called "the withering" by the local race of Naam - threatening Ava's inhabitants.

The game's narrative, co-created by Rhianna Pratchett, is a journey of wonder and mystery but also discovery, leading to the revelation of the planet's captivating secrets.

Show off your map-making skills and see how your creations stack up against those of others. name: FAIRY TAIL: DUNGEONS
detailed_description: Fairy Tail: Dungeons sets the characters of the Fairy Tail series exploring a dungeon using only a limited number of moves and a strategically built deck of skill cards to take down foes as they make for the deepest depths. Features an All-new Story One day, Natsu and Happy discover a mysterious door has suddenly appeared below the guild. Inside, they find a strange, expansive dungeon that saps all intruders of their powers. With no means to defend themselves, the two seem doomed until an Exceed called Labi comes to their aid. Once they hear about Labi's missing friend, Natsu and Happy decide to head for the deepest depths themselves. Labyrinth (Solo Dungeon) Use the cards in your deck to attack, defend, cast magic, and more. Power up your deck further with cards won in battle or found in treasure chests. Use cards in a specific order to activate Magic Chains for punishing amounts of damage. Explore the solo dungeon and unlock powerful skills before your lantern goes out. If you're lucky, you might even run into fellow guild members who can join up with you! Even if you fall in battle, the points you earn exploring will unlock amulets which will aid in future runs through the dungeon. Don't let defeat stop you. Try and try again! Characters Each character has their own fighting style and fortes. Natsu, a balanced all-rounder. Lucy, who calls on her unique celestial spirits to wreak havoc on the battlefield. Gray, who uses diverse molding magic to gain tactical advantage, and many more! Discover how to use each effectively and earn the upper hand in battle. Labyrinth Depths (Team Dungeon) Form a team with 3 characters you've trained in the solo dungeon, and dive deep into the depths. Find tomes inside to power up your team's stats. Don't miss out on the final boss—an original character illustrated by Fairy Tail creator Hiro Mashima himself! Music Features a soundtrack produced by Secret of Mana composer Hiroki Kikuta. The world of Fairy Tail comes alive through Celtic-inspired sounds that add a vibrant backdrop to the battles and story scenes. short_description: Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a deck-building rogue-lite featuring characters from the Fairy Tail series. Collect Magic Cards based on moves from the series to build your own unique deck and take down powerful monsters as you head for the dungeon depths!

_childDocuments_.review: Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a rogue-lite deckbuilder. You can easily play the game without knowing anything about fairy tail (like me) and still get the story. Sure, I imagine it could help to know the characters, back story, etc. but it seems like I still get what's going on. Every run consists of three labyrinths. You have around 10 moves to make on the map till you fight the boss. There are normal battles, elite battles, a campfire, a shop, events, and lacrima. Lacrima is used to upgrade your character's abilities which are stored in a tome. After every run, you can save up your tome (up to four per character actually) to get into the next labyrinth with a saved tome. The game's battle mechanic is best described as Easy to learn, and hard to master. It's as simple as it could be. You get 4 cards per turn, can redraw one time for 5HP loss, and play up to three cards (every card costs mana and you have three to start out with). It really gets strategic when thinking about combinations, countering bosses, doing magic chains, etc. Some of these words sound complicated. Fear not. The tutorial is really good. They will literally explain everything to you in a short period of time. It's a short but detailed tutorial + there's a menu explaining keywords, etc. if you even need that. The game is a rogue-lite and there's progression to be made. First off, you unlock new labyrinths, forwarding the story and increasing the difficulty. There's a resource called "LumYou also unlocks amulets and stuff, so there's that. The meta progression is really engaging since it progresses the whole game and you'll be able to fight with two or even three characters at the same time, allowing for even more strategic depth. + engaging thanks to the meta progression+ impactful animations. I very much like them since they feel more alive and fun attacking with special attacks that even look hurtful. + easy to learn, hard to master. Even if you're not into deckbuilder but you're into the series: you can easily play and like this game. And if you're not into the series but love deckbuilders, this is for you, too. It can get really strategic in battles. + good music. Most of the time when playing deckbuilders I just mute the game and listen to music, but I do in fact like it in this game. + good performance. I did not have any problems playing the game on my desktop as well as on my laptop. I have not tried to play on my Steam deck yet. +- some boss battles can take quite a bit of time. This is neutral since some people like it and some don't. Personally, the "long" fights did not feel draining because I was already much into the fights at this point but I can imagine some people disliking this. It also depends on your strategy and how much you're willing to take (as in: how much HP loss) for battles to get longer. - I would like to unlock even more things like cards.- basic story. I did not need that really. - harder difficulties are missing. Don't get me wrong, I did NOT play through the whole game yet so maybe it's something I don't need in the end, or it's unlocked later, but I can imagine hardcore deckbuilding fans wanting even more of a challenge (Tho I don't think the game is easy and look at how many deckbuilders I've played). Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a highly addictive and strategic rogue-lite deckbuilder. It's easy to learn but hard to master. Even if you're not into the series but into deckbuilders, you'll easily grasp the basic story and love the battles as well as the progression. The animations add to the fun since they are impactful, short, and still fun to watch.There's plenty of stuff to like and I'm honest: I never thought this game would be so good since I thought it would be a short cash grab - but it's definitely not!You should definitely get it!
_childDocuments_.name: FAIRY TAIL: DUNGEONS

_childDocuments_.review: A short and cozy roguelike deckbuilder set in the Fairy Tail universe. There are five characters you can play being Natsu, Lucy, Gray, Erza, and Wendy. There isn’t much of a story, but the pixel art animations are adorable. I’ve had no issues playing on the Steam Deck and the overall experience has been pretty cozy, albeit somewhat lacking.Although each character has a unique kit, it is frankly rare to make full use of them due to how short each playthrough is. There are 3 labyrinths, but only the first one allows you to modify your skills and cards. A lot of luck is needed for your build to shine, but without it, the combat can be overwhelmingly slow-paced and unsatisfying. There are amulets late in the game that can help finalize your build, but I feel too much time is needed to get there and most players would’ve had their fun by then.It took about 3 hours for me to complete the game. There was a lot of replay value though and I experimented further with different builds, amulets, and party compositions for the later labyrinths. For those interested in getting all achievements, it would take about 12-18 hours depending on your luck. The game may be lacking in content but I enjoyed what it had to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun roguelike deckbuilder with a good variety and selection of characters from the Fairy Tail main cast in which all of them have quite different gameplay styles/strategies to build towards as you advance through the dungeon plus you also find other members from the guild even if it's just to generate some basic interactions/side-story details and sometimes give you some items or cards in which you can call them up during battle for an attack or special skill.So overall up until now I'm really looking forward to keep exploring the game and seeing which other of these characters, items and unlocks are available to find as you progress plus the depth of the tactics that you will need to use on the end level.The visuals are great with the use of pixel art with some nice effects, plus all of it accompanying with music that although it's not directly taken from the show it's still in the same style and vein that fits perfectly the game (think of Uilleann bagpipes).Overall major credit to the developers for a great use of the Fairy Tail IP in something that shows passion and makes justice to it rather than just being a quick cash grab and also for the tireless push on so many updates and quick fixes since the release of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: + Nice to see Indie developer working on a major IP officially--- A big minus for me: Lack of Fairy Tale themed music, current music is not bad but totally lacked the Fairy Tail oomph. Would be nice if they let us use custom music....+ Many great design concepts...- but ruined by a rigid combo system that does not gel well for RNG-heavy roguelite, which broke the synergy for a potential good design (more below)- English translation of names and skills does not align to Anime/Manga.  Lucy's keys/skills feel MTLed.- Very grindy to unlock anything and everything, including abilities-- Extra, Extra grindy: expectation is you keep running the labyrinth (first half of game) for each char multiple times until you can RNG a good skill compendium, which you can then use for the second half of the game-- Currently, Erza is crashing the game in deeper dungeon.- No access to library during game play, hard to keep track of what's what and what you are missing.++ Well Priced for an IP title.  Games are way overpriced these days and this is not one of them, which is my main reason for picking this up.The labyrinth portion of the game (1st half) let you grow each character individually and learn skills (good idea). Skills are learned based on RNG card drops.  The skill pool is also RNG and you can re-randomize the unused portion with a "Mazefruit" (nothing wrong so far).  However, we are given very limited # of turns on each floor to power up...  1) Combo skills locked behind RNG skill grid (no issue by itself but...)2) RNG on skills so you might not get the required skills for the combo you are able to RNG unlock3) Higher tier skills cost 2 or 3 energy to use.  Your default energy is 3... so making those 4 points combo unusable by default.  You also need to get lucky on a RNG card mod to lower cost on one of the cards. The crux is the current combo system can be unwieldy unless RNG god favors you.  Roguelite is not an excuse to turn this into an exercise of frustration in the 2nd part of the game. This is just poor executionDev needs to rework the combo system to make it more relevant for RNG nature of the game. Or if they want to keep the current fixed skill combination, the skill grid is not the right place for it.Unfortunately there are more - than + at this point in time, so I would not recommend it until they optimize game play and fix the crashing bugs (or Erza smacking down on the devs :P)

_childDocuments_.review: Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a game that does the Fairy Tail series proud in a lot of ways, it has a lot of focus on that sweet sweet teamwork and power of friendship, really showing off all the people they know throughout the series and enemies too, even down to the attacks and sprites used they all are a fantastic nod to the series and look great, it still has a few balancing issues for characters but nothing that makes it unbeatable and it still has room for great updates and fixes in the future dood!Okay the usual big review! So the premise of the game is quite fun and ties in nicely with the card theme of this game, you start off as Natsu and happy who get pulled into a portal accidentally via an X-seed? Called Labi, something big is coming and he needs your help to find his friend and stop it but while you're here you find you have lost your powers!? How do we cope!? With the help of Cana! The wizard who uses card magic of course! How convenient and super appropriate dood.The game consists of three places, I won't spoil what the other two are specifically or how they work other than you start with 1 character and build up to three, this is out of five currently playable characters who you unlock as you get to each part of the dungeons I mentioned dood.The main gameplay consists of the first dungeon, here you play as one of the five characters and build up what's called a tome, in this tome you have a set of basic cards and an initial two spells that work as a chain spell that comes from your characters amulet (I will talk more about those in a little) and a page that has a bunch of slots you can open for various skills ranging from damage increases to specific spells, more health, more chain spell links and a smattering of other rather useful skills that are randomised each run no less dood!As you go through the dungeon you can land on seven specific things, first off typically as you start you will land on Lacrima shards, these are your currency, you can use this at the second thing you can land on, the shop! Who is also along with a certain enemy type a reference to Rave master which brought a smile to my face ^-^ the third thing of which you can also use lacrima on is at the camp, here you can rest for 30% healed, talk to Labi for three free items or the best option in my opinion the enchant option! This let's you add effects to your cards, this can include lowering the mana cost (of which can be up to three cost which is as much mana as you can naturally carry) increasing damage, boosting buff or debuff effects, all kinds of nice things and you even get a re-roll at an ever increasing price each retry of lacrima dood!Now for the other half of what you can land on, first off treasure! These contain a set of three spells, you can only choose one but having three to choose from let's you vary your spells more which is nice and on harder difficulties (yes those exist eventually and you'll want to do them) they can luckily get found with free enchantments! Now that's saving some money assuming you don't get lucky and what ya want first try, secondly are events! There are quite a few that can happen, I won't spoil any of them, save the fun of them but suffice to say a lot are RNG % chance stuff that can really benefit you dood.And finally the last two icons are the enemies! they come in two flavours, Grape purple or strawberry red, the former being little enemies that after the fight will give you maybe a little bit of Lacrima or an item but a guaranteed small health boost! So don't ignore them too much but as for the latter? The red enemies are tougher fights, near the end of a run they are even full fledged bosses which is frankly insane but for beating them you net a higher health boost, usually a free spell card and either a decent item or more lacrima, as long as you play well there's honestly very little reason not to fight them! It's all gains which you will need dood!The first section consists of what I'll call three floors, you equip up to two amulets (one really as the first is a must and gives you your only two first spells, the rest are defence and melee card) which you can unlock via just playing and have various effects and off you go, you have ten turns and then you get a boss! Until you hit the final floors boss and finish things off for that run, at which point your tome is saved for reasons dood!I haven't really talked about battle yet have I? So how it goes down, you use the cards and skills you collect, upgrade and buy to take on a bunch of enemies, you have a few kinds of cards, you have normal attack cards, these are basically just punches, usually one of which has a decent unique effect to it, the rest are just weak but do have a very specific use to them too, then you have spells, these are typically a good deal stronger, they can hit one enemy or multiple, some have special effects to them such as debuffs to damage or defence amount, (which works in a unique way in this, I'll get to that) you also can burn or do extra damage over time from various effects, they are quite diverse and can hit multiple team members too in buffs case and finally you have defence cards, these give you a shield of sorts this mitigates the exact amount of damage it raises it by for that turn, by next turn it's halved, simple, elegant, can save you from taking any damage early on, handy dood!That's not it though, we will talk about what makes bosses well...bosses in this XD as well as one more card mechanic, so of course they have the typical high health and damage but they also have the ability to do a variety of unique attacks along with the usual defence and attacks, some can attack twice even!! Still the thing that truly makes them stand out besides some unique effects and attacks are their conditions, by which I mean they will charge up and the game will say "do 50 damage to the boss in 2 turns!" Or the more important one perform a chain spell, this is the mechanic I was talking about, two spells will be chained and for using them in the link order the second card will do a substantial amount more damage, it's a fun little mechanic, maybe a bit too important at times, oh also you can redraw up to four cards for some of your health which can make a big difference dood.Annnnd that's it really! I hope the dev/s for this do more, there's a lot of love there and the game itself is a blast so having more to actually do and vary up the gameplay a bit would be nice but as far as indie games go they did a stellar job and are either fans or did some great research, either way I highly appreciated my time with the game and hope you all do too if this review made you buy it! Thanks for reading dood! ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: I must say, I think the game is pretty cool on a base level. The pixel sprites and animations are great, and the music is really good but there's not enough, you hear the same 2/3 tracks on loop constantly.I'm not hugely experienced with Rogue-lite deck builders, I have something like 12 hours in Slay the Spire so I certainly know enough that huge inspiration has been pulled from that game, *EDIT: THE FOLLOWING COMPLAINTS HAVE BEEN ADDRESSED, READ BELOW* but I really feel like the deck building it's self needs more ways to consistently get where you want it to go.The same can be said about the skill tree which in my opinion needs a complete overhaul. It needs to be more consistently good, the whole thing is bloated with garbage that is useless for the deck build and "Magic Chains" you're currently focusing on in your run, that you have to waste your points on before you can unlock anything that actually helps your build. There is an option to seek out a "Maze Fruit" which can re-roll your skill tree offering a minor chance to give you a better tree for your deck, but to get one you're wasting precious discards and enchantments just to TRY finding one from your hooded cat companion at rest spots.Overall, fantastic indie game for the price but on a deeper level needs the systems and balance reworked a bit. It's too much of a struggle to find your build, resulting in finding your entertainment.*EDIT: These devs actually rule. The issues I highlighted in the game have been thought over and addressed by the team in the version 1.1.0 update, below is an excerpt from the patch notes.[Improvements & New Features]- New Skills AddedAdded a new "Magic Chain" that allows a free combination of selections.With this update, existing Magic Chains will no longer appear outside the center of the skill grid determined by the amulet.The new Magic Chain will always appear evenly when unlocking skills one space away from the center.Added skills that activate through the use of Wizard Summon Cards or when Extra Attacks are triggered.- Enchantment ImprovementsAdded a feature to reroll effects by consuming Lacrima.- Magic Card AdjustmentsExtensive balance adjustments and new effects added, mainly to Magic Cards with MP costs of 2 and 3, expanding build options and reducing reliance on RNG.

_childDocuments_.review: Super cheap roguelike deckbuilder that's got 5 unique characters (both design- and gameplay-wise) you can play as either solo or as a party of 3 (a single encounter requires a party of 2, but that's pretty much an afterthought).The enemies are a bit sameish, leading to many encounters playing at the same, but the playable character are interesting enough to pilot to cover the price of admission.- Unlike in most other roguelike deckbuilders where you control multiple characters, like Roguebook, here you draw four cards for each character separately (with an option to mulligan every turn at the cost of some HP) and they all have their own mana, so you really feel like your entire team is contributing equally.- As an adaptation, this game is also a huge win, depicting the characters from the anime/manga faithfully. And I say this as someone who had the Fairy Tail OST playing on his wedding while cutting the wedding cake. Huge fan!- While I have only tried 3/5 playable characters as I beat the game on first try, their decks all felt quite unique, so I'm confident the same will hold true for the remaining 2 characters.- The game is super cheep. It's so cheap, even at full price, that it's honestly more than worth the price of admission for any roguelike fan. - The enemies leave a lot the be desired. There's an okay amount of enemy variety, especially for a game at this price, but they all feel sameish. And I don't mean visually, I mean you can approach every combat encounter the same way, because all enemies are essentially HP sponges that act in almost identical ways. In this regard, the game is a far cry from Roguebook (which I keep comparing it to because they're both roguelikes where you control multiple characters).- It's super easy. I have unlocked an extra difficulty that I've yet to try out, but I would have preferred having more of a challenge for the first 3 hours of gameplay.- The deckbuilding is a bit weird. Unlike in Roguebook, where each character has a deck that can support several strategies (Sharra has daggers, build, power/multiattack, and that's just what I can remember off the top of my head), very few cards in Fairy Tail Dungones actually synergize with other cards on their own. The only examples I can think of are a couple of Grey cards that get extra damage depending on how much Shield you have. Instead, each character has several two-card combos that then give extra effects, but to unlock them, you don't just have to draw both cards on the same turn (already a tough sell), you also have to unlock that specific combo in a randomized skill tree. All of this is to say that, while there are a lot of cool cards, there aren't really many (or any) clever card combinations that you can use to break the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game if you like Fairy Tail or deck builders. I love the many references, the simple gameplay, and the beautiful pixel graphics. If you just like this type of game and not fairy tail in particular, get ready for a breath of fresh air with the many unique concepts packed into this game!Tons of replayability and a good paced advancement system!My one complaint is the way you spend lacrima to level up; instead of a skill tree, you have a bunch of cards that are face down until you pick something next to them. The cards get randomized every attempt, so even with many playthroughs of experience you can't build your skills to match whatever deck you've cobbled together unless incredible RNG says so.*Edit - apparently the maze fruit re-rolls the cards except what you've already picked, so that alleviates this issue a good bit. Wording should be clearer.. my friends and I all thought it was a re-spec consumable to redo your choices.**Edit2 - The more you play, the better it gets! Don't want to spoil too much, but there are several modes you unlock with plenty of replayability even after completing all the steam achievements. Hope to see more from these guys, maybe some DLC packs or just a good ol sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sleeper beast of a card game. To be fair I love card game fighters like this. The animations are crisp and fluid, the dungeon layouts are fun and familiar but compelling.The game even has a very smart and intuitive battle system that gives each character a good amount of complexity. Being able to randomly pick up a game this well made for such an affordable price out of nowhere feels almost like I am robbing the developer. Definitely a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very fun. Time melts away. I don't know anything about the anime, but the style is cool and the characters seem fine. Gameplay is basically:1. Bring one character into a dungeon. Customize their cards and perks as you work towards the boss, and keep a saved copy of the character if you beat the boss.2. Beat a boss using two saved copies of characters that beat the first dungeon to unlock...3. A three person dungeon, using copies of three characters who beat the first dungeon. When you get done that, you can beat each dungeon on 3 different difficulties. As you unlock things and manage to win on higher difficulties you can generate stronger characters from the first dungeon. Eventually you'll beat the third dungeon and then its slightly hidden secret boss. After that you unlock a true roguelike infinite dungeon mode with random builds, party members, etc. I haven't played too much of it yet, but I did complete the game otherwise. Highly recommend for the money.

_childDocuments_.review: "Where Stunning Sprite Art Meets Synergized Combat."Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a fantastic addition to the roguelike card game genre, bringing enough unique elements to stand out from the crowd while still satisfying the familiar cravings that fans of the genre enjoy. One of the game's strongest aspects is its combat system, which feels incredibly smooth and rewarding. When you manage to string together combos and hit that perfect 'zynergy' (synergy), it creates a dynamic flow that’s deeply satisfying. The gameplay feels fresh and exciting, and it keeps you engaged with each battle.The sprite-based art direction deserves special mention as well. The character designs, animations, and visual effects are stunning and feel like they leap off the screen. There’s something almost magical about how the game looks and moves, and it adds an extra layer of immersion that’s hard to ignore. Every attack and ability is accentuated by these fantastic visuals, which is definitely one of the game’s standout features.That being said, there are a few minor issues that hold the game back from being truly exceptional. The pacing can sometimes feel uneven, which may limit the game’s long-term replayability. After a while, the flow can become a bit predictable, and while the combat is engaging, it could benefit from more variety or faster progression.Also, I would highly recommend that the developers include an option to fully skip the story and cutscenes from the menu. While the narrative and cutscenes are interesting on the first playthrough, having to sit through them repeatedly can become a bit of a chore. Being able to skip these sequences entirely would make subsequent playthroughs much more enjoyable for players focused on the core gameplay.Overall, Fairy Tail: Dungeons is a visually stunning, deeply engaging roguelike card game with some truly satisfying combat mechanics. If you're looking for something that hits all the right notes but also offers a fresh take on the genre, this is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: I like what this game tries to be, even though it's not flawless. First off, breaking the game into segments the way they did really feels unique and is fun to interact with. In practice it goes like this: do solo runs with a chosen character, and when you win you save the deck and traits you made it through with; when you have two/three characters built up you challenge a deeper dungeon with the final boss. Feels great to put together a team on your own merit. First con though, it doesn't nail making it always feel like it was your smart decisions. I fell flat on my face trying to win on base difficulty with Wendy 3 times before I got an extremely lucky run that turned her into an encounter gobbling monster in the first 3 turns thanks to random events giving me good traits and extra mana/turn. You should have more granular control over things like this, though honestly it feels pretty great to get that good run, it just feels less controllable than other games like Slay the Spire or Monster Train. Second, I also like the idea of the skill trees... in practice they fall a bit short, because they are randomized per run AND because you don't keep the unlocks between runs. I would tend to agree with some of the other reviews that say reworking it a tad to be a little more incremental and letting progress roll over between runs regardless of failure would make that system run more smoothly. And last gripe being some cards and card effects feel lackluster. Basic attacks really suck outside of a specific buff other cards can roll that lets them trigger automatically from your draw pile with no mana cost. Having more control over what buffs your cards get would work in favor of crafting a run just the way you want instead of praying for luck especially on higher difficulties. All in all, that's a lot of negatives I listed, but to be honest they don't keep the game from being overly frustrating or fun as long as you don't mind it being a little grindy if you really want a great deck to form for your characters. Overall I'd give it a strong 7 or light 8 out of 10. Oh and... please add more characters. I'd pay for expansions of other guilds being playable.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game... Not amazing either, but still recommended, but barely (only the cheap price keeps it in the recommendeds as well as me liking the characters, not that there is much story, interactions or anything at all of any substance going on)...Some characters are rather weak and start with a lot of garbage cards.... seriously, Most of Lucy's basic attack cards are abysmal compared to other characters (her Lucy Kick is just a dud when you pull that one, and you only have 4 card hands with the cards you don't use wasting a spot)... Erza isn't much better, getting a LOT of basic attack cards to act as clutter (Lucy and Erza always need to spend most of their time at camps removing cards... Gray is way better with that aspect) and her main combo leads to an AOE which is just mediocre when facing the real challenge: the bosses. And more often than not they are alone, meaning AOE is not great at all.Haven't tried Wendy yet, but out of the 4 I tried, Gray was really good, Natsu was okay and Lucy and Erza were terrible needing great RNG with the skill book (the skills you can pick in the skill book are also rng as far as I can tell), skill gain and card draws to do just as well as Gray and Natsu can do but with just passable RNGLast time I read Fairy Tail was many years ago, and it's making me want to read it all over again (even considering the bad arcs), so I guess there is that too if you are a fan of Fairy Tail. If you are not a fan then avoid this gamePS: the "cool" combo attacks don't look any different when you chain them, maybe a little more flashing but that's it, no change in the animation. So while chaining attacks is cool, the increase in damage and slight increase in flashing and shaking is all you really get.Also the cheap price makes sense, and again the price is the main reason why I recommend this. If it were closer to 20 euros/dollars I would probably turn that thumb down.EDIT: before some people think I just don't know how to play and so don't appreciate Lucy or Erza, I unlocked the achievement "chain master" (activating magic chain, or the combos, 50 times) at 12.3% before I unlocked the achievements "Item Master" (obtaining 15 different items, which you get rather easily early on) at 41.5% and "Sealed Portal Challenger" (progressing the story a bit) at 35.3%. I got that Chain Master achievement within about the first hour of playing... Because I know how to build decks and how to play hands to get the cards I want... In one of my first runs I managed a build where I could chain multiple combos in a row, flowing from one right into another (that, I will be honest, was quite satisfying to pull off and was really really strong).All this to say that the starter decks for Erza and Lucy feel terribleEDIT 2: game is pretty short, already finished it and now it just unlocks difficulties and it's a grind to unlock other amulets and the likes... Only problem is they only let you take 2 amulets, which is boring since it just means there are some that are plain worthless to take. Also, having played more, I can say Wendy also suffers from garbage starter cards with similar terrible basic attack cards like lucy. No idea if it's because the characters are a bit weaker in the series or due to sexism and women should be weaker by default (let's not hide ourselves from the fact that a lot of japanese anime and manga are pretty sexist, and I say that as a person that strongly dislikes modern woke) but this weakness sucks for game balance.Also some characters are way more situational then others. Like Gray and Natsu can just wreck since they aren't situational at all, with gray being able to block and debuff the target's attack while doing some damage and Natsu can do good damage... Meanwhile a lot of Lucy's cards are expensive for what they do damage wise and give situational debuffs like "if the tagert's next attack is support then there is a 60% (if i remember correctly) chance to interrupt", but that sucks (and i'm not even sure it worked once for me) against bosses since it never interrupts them, and surprise surprise it builds you up to face 2 very powerful bosses back to back in the last "chapter". All in all it would have needed a bit more attention to those kinds of details, but for the price I suppose it's fine. You don't go to McDonalds expecting really good food for the price they ask (though man has it become expensive for what it is... Shouldn't these fast food chains be reminded of their place? why do people so easily pay so much for such garbage... Okay, I know why, laziness and complacency).

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the sprite work in this game is really amazing (I think my only issue is Lucy's hair in her portrait being more green than blonde but that's a nitpick)Next, animations are also great, while some make the attacks look a little too weak (Wendy's Sky Dragon Roar comes to mind), a lot of them do like nice and bring the attacks from the series to life in a good way.Enemy variety is where I might have to be a little negative again. The pool of enemies you encounter is a bit weak and does lead to very samey encounters, especially on repeat runs. That being said, the enemies that are here do require enough strategy to make each encounter not boring. Since the name of the game is taking as little damage as possible during each encounterI see heavy inspiration from other deck building tbrpg's such as Slay the Spire, but unfortunately the one thing that's missing is build variety. While there are 5 characters to pick from, their builds are sort of set in stone. And your goal is to acquire the proper cards to make the character really shine in your party, rather than making a unique build. And that unfortunately makes some cards just strictly better versions of other cards. And in higher difficulties if you don't get said good cards you're sort of screwed.While the build variety isn't there. I do like the other ways you can express your characters. The enchant system and lacrima skills are fun to have around. And truthfully I wish Slay the spire also had a small pool of randomly chosen upgrades to cards rather than just rigid upgrades, like this game does. Something I wish was different about the lacrima system though is the first skill you get. Rather than it always being the same, I wish it was something you chose on the grid (having all of the skills chosen from the pool visible) and then everything being reshuffled, with the 4 adjacent skills to your chosen skill being kept where they are.Lastly, I may sound a tad greedy, but I do hope this game will be supported for a long time, with the developer taking into consideration all of the suggestions and criticism. Since we have something that's on the verge of being a truly great game. And if willing, I would not be opposed to paid dlc in the future in the form of extra characters to play as. I came in blind and was really hoping that Gajeel and Juvia would be extra characters you could unlock as well. But as the party stands now, the main 5 characters a good starting point if the plan is to add more characters in the future.All of that long winded reviewing to say I would absolutely recommend this game to fans of Fairy Tail, since it's easy enough to pick up and play since the deck building is easy enough to get a handle on quickly. And for fans of deck builders, since there is some depth here with the extra systems in place. Between the party system, lacrima skills, and enchants.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, the game is incredibly unbalanced. When you get one upgrade, that upgrades Lucy's prayer from healing 4 to healing 5, and then have to fight a boss that one shot me at 37 health with no crit? On floor 2? That's literally not even fair. During my 2 hours, I got 6 runs in. 1 Natsu, 1 Gray, 4 Lucy. Lucy makes the most sense for me, and got me the farthest. The farthest being the boss of floor 2. Sometimes it's Mono Bird! Who's "hit with 6 cards or more" thing is bugged and never worked, even when I managed to use items and hit him for 8 cards! Meaning I always got hit with the big finisher attack! How great and awesome!I never got my "step foot in the labrynith" achievement, but I don't care about the bugs on the Steam achievements. I care about the game physically being unfun to play. Steam told me this would be like Inscryption. Except, in Inscryption Chapter 1, losing gives you rewards still. You can still easily get back to where you were and learn something from it. Chapter 2? Absolutely no downside to losing! You can try again and again with various methods. Chapter 3? A mix! You only lose your money and your spot. If you've already cleared the area of encounters, then you have nothing to worry about and just get to try again.But FT Dungeons? Has none of that. Everything you do gets reset, you keep nothing. You can't even go back after losing and collect say a pouch of the lacrima you had last round. There is no incentive to losing other than the "points system" which give you useless items or lore. I do not want to talk to Blue Pegasus members in the Labyrinth, I want a way to get past floor 2. When there's no incentive to losing and every incentive to winning in a game like this, it makes players more frustrated when you powercreep your literal tutorial levels.I'm not one to criticize without offering solutions. So 1. Give more healing items. Even with a bag full of them+Polyuscia's medicine, I die constantly due to just getting flat overpowered. 2. Give more ways to upgrade your cards. When you have a run that's expected to go super far and then you get 0 ways to upgrade things except the campfire at the end of a floor, which usually you HAVE to use for healing or just die immediately on the next floor, then there's no point in contnuing that run. Hell, without a reliable way to upgrade things then you have no use going past floor 1 at all. Because you will get crushed.3. Rearrange some of the decks. I get that the whole point is that you have to explore to get more magic, but when Gray literally spawns with 2 cards and the rest are basic attacks that everyone has? It's just pathetic. And if you can't get chests to spawn or don't have enough fuel to even get to them, then you're stuck at a boss with almost nothing!4. Keep the Book of Remembrance through all runs. Starting a run with +2 to say Lucy's Virgo Stardress is not going to kill replayability. It will help players who get far return to where they were and will help players who are struggling to get further actually manage to play your game.I want to love this game. I want to keep playing this game. Fairy Tail has a special place in my heart and it genuinely upsets me to see something I looked forward to buying be so ♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for all Fairy Tail fans and fans of this genre!+ Story (even if short) fits FT very well and doesn't leave u needing/wanting more+ Very very very nice magic/attack variety+ Magic and attacks are totally matching the anime/manga and this was done very well (amazed by all skill by each char specially Natsu and Lucy's)+ Nice rouge like card battle turn based combat mix, its super fun! (think old school jrpg like Chrono trigger, breath of fire or early FF but instead of the defaults "attack, defend, magic, item" u get 4 cards and play/mix match them)+ Multiple difficulties can be unlocked (harder dif = better rewards/items u get in the run)+- "Only" 5 chars (main ones obv), its great but would have been epic to be able to be able to fully play as Gajeel and few other chars (still not a con tho)+ Side chars that u meet in game (even if not playable/fully playable)+ Tutorial is very nice + u can always check "help" in case ur unsure or forgot how something fully works-+ A bit grindy in the term that u have to beat the first labyrinth multiple times til ur happy with ur loadout (also u can only enter with 1 char at a time), also higher rank rewards are rly a must have and sometimes its a bit of a pain to grind to get them (luckily game is rly fun and its never 2 grindy so u don't need to waste 50+h to unlock important things in game)+ Challenging after the "first" area/labyrinth+ "Secret final boss" and "Secret" mods unlockable after beating himOverall very fun game obv dedicated to FT fans. Everything was done so well and true to the manga/anime ♥PS Fans of the genre that never saw/watched/read Fairy Tail will like it as well :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Fairy Tail - great. If you're not into Fairy Tail (like me) - also great! It's a very solid roguelite deckbuilder and every run feels fresh.There are a lot of decisions to make, both before and during a run. Which of the 5 characters to play? Which starting relics to pick? Speaking of relics: If you like certain playstyles/builds, you can use certain relics to begin your run with a specific combo.During exploration, you choose the route you want to go, while pondering on the skills and cards your deck needs the most.During battle, playing a single wrong card at the wrong time can (on higher difficulties) be pretty devastating. You HAVE to strategize. And strategizing you can! Each turn of combat, you may (at the cost of life) mulligan the cards of your choice. Or rather, every card you decided NOT to keep gets discarded and replaced.However, they are only discarded that way. Not automatically at the end of your turn, like in most RLDBs. Which gives the player agency and the feeling of being in control of your destiny. One of the more frustrating experiences in other RLDBs is when I draw block cards when the enemy doesn't attack, or attack cards when the enemy does attack. Here it's different.Also, if you like progression systems, then this game's a treat. There is soo much stuff to unlock! Characters, relics, spells, game modes, etc.The game's only downsides are repetitive music (which I personally don't mind), some questionable balance choices and a few bugs here and there. I have to commend the devs though, because they fix said bugs quickly and regularly.If you still have doubts, try the demo!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a great writer or reviewer, my attention span for writing is short, which makes it hard for me to focus and i always go all over the place.But maybe this will help?Its a solid fun game. Its a turn based card game.I enjoy rougealike games alot, but most of them are the same (this one included) but the different is the theme and characters.The fact that it has characters from an anime that i know, makes it more fun.I have thought about it before, how someone should make a rougealike with characters from an anime, but when i thought about it, i wanted Naruto or Bleach.The use of cards made it more fun, (i have usually only played those were you walking around picking up power ups and combine them to better power up. So for me, this was a change.The game works very simple.You have a lantern that gives you 10 turns, each time your character moves, its a turn,And for each turn you can interact with, monsters, events, shop, chest or money.Lab1This is where you bring your characters one at the time, to try to get the best deck possibly in 3 stages, the bosses for each stage may change.And there are different ways to get the stuff you need (cards, boost, items)Either you fight monsters, walking in to an event (which may give you "money, enchant or boost), get chests or buy from a tent with "money" you get from fight, chest, or on the map.There is also an fireplace, were you can either rest for hp, enchant cards, or get stuff by talking to a character.When you finish, you save your deck in one of four slots for that character.Lab2This is where you bring two characters with saved decks.Thats all i will say.Lab3 is a combination of Lab1 and Lab2.But you can no longer power up or add to your deck.Instead you get overall boost tombs that can power up specific characters or overall help with healing and such.Or you just stack up on items.Everytime you finish a lab, your overall level goes up, for each level you unlock new stuff.New event characters, or held items that you can start with.Overall its a fun experience for the price you pay, which is worth it.Don't know if this is it or they will add more, but more would be fun.It was a bit strange with the enemies to begin witih, but i got over it pretty quick.I would like to see the same thing with other animes, but i think that some wouldnt work with these made up enemie types.Naruto already have a bunch of ninjas they can use (main or background characters), and Bleach has alot of different types of enemies to use.Maybe the devs can make this happen?I would be all in, if so.I hope this helped someone to decide, and if so, i hope your as satisfied as i was.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a pretty simple card dungeon crawler / roguelike deckbuilder kinda game with Fairy Tail characters and a short story. Took me 4-ish hours to complete the basic story of it. You have a relatively simple game to pick up and learn, different characters with their own specific archetype / deck style and dungeon crawling through floors with all kinds of items, pickups and fights. After your 'stamina'/lantern runs out you get a boss, you gotta do 3 of these floors first to get a "tome" which basically saves the deck you cleared with on a slot for later. After doing this for 2 characters you can challenge a bit of a harder boss without spoilers, after that you unlock a "deeper labyrinth" which requires 3 of these tomes (so essentially the game expects you to clear with Natsu, Lucy and Gray for starters). Deeper levels are same concept as the first layer, only that you have 3 characters to use at once. Clear all those floors and after a double boss gauntlet you get the credit rolls. There's a difficulty unlock that I haven't tried yet after, there's a lot more cards and other unlockables left to clear. If you only want to clear story, 4-ish hours for most people. If you wanna do everything, you'll probably get a little more out of it. Keeping this as a fun side game, I'd say it's worth it if you like either this genre of games or the Fairy Tail franchise. You can play this while waiting for Fairy Tail 2 game to hit the shelves. 11€ on the opening offer, about 14€ without sale. Neither are a bad price, people that think this is too much are probably salty. Just know what you're getting into beforehand tbh.Overal: Decent game, short story that could've been better, detail / love for the franchise and characters is great (small stuff like all the different moves and having actual different characteristics, for Lucy for example you see the spirit of every celestial key you collect on the victory screens which I thought was genuinely nice, all the celestial outfits are cards, a lot of Erza's armors are covered, etc.) Music still great, details and combat are good overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eyeing this game for a while and after playing it for a bit, it's quite interesting. It's not the best of the genre and i felt like it has stuff that lacks oomph like sound effects, animations, and sprite expression, but it's still quite a simple and fun game for its price. Moves are character accurate, sprite work for characters are good looking, and the gameplay repetition is what you'd expect for a rogueliteIn an era where most anime games are either gacha or arena fighter, Fairy Tail making RPGs and Roguelite is quite a fun welcome. It made me remember the old era of anime games where they try making weird stuff and sometimes it sticks, this game certainly sticks. If this is where FT's video game is going i think it's going to be fun

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is brilliant.It's a nice little card game rogue-like with lovely animations (As a Fairy Tail fan I smiled with glee seeing all the magic in motion). Balance seems very reasonable as I was able to make very steady progress and have unlocked but not yet played higher difficulties so there's definitely room for more difficulty. Starts simple and has a nice flow with building a deck that suits a character and then bringing multiple of them together to make a team. Reasonable amount of unlocks to get and a story that is fit for purpose and is entertaining enough to set the scene for the game.I really only have praise for a release like this, with a reasonable price, faithful pixel art style and a fair difficulty and amount of content. A demo being available is just the cherry on the top for good developer practises all around.
_childDocuments_.name: FAIRY TAIL: DUNGEONS

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very decent and enjoyable game for the price point, especially if you are a fan of fairy tail. A few things that do not quite hit the mark though, skills pretty much do the same thing, with a few exceptions on enchantments, activating magic combos should have more effects than just increased damage. For example, why does Erzas adamantine armor combo just do more damage? It would be far more interesting if you were rewarded in different ways for achieving a combo. Perhaps for pulling off one of the defense type you could gain a buff that decreases all damage you take whilst reflecting damage back to attackers. Or you could store damage and in a few turns unleash a massive attack for freeThe re-play value doesn't quite hit for me either. Not having ways of increasing Mana in between rounds beside an item is just not fun especially when you only get 3 a turn and most cards cost 2+ should just be more ways ti add max mana or reduce card cost through combosAll in all, if the devs made the effort to tweak a lot of the power buffs and abilities to make it more variable i would happily throw more money at the game as it definitely deserves the love on both sides of the business
_childDocuments_.name: FAIRY TAIL: DUNGEONS

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo quite a bit and really liked it, the full game is really nice and I absolutely love the pixel art and the beautiful animations of the attacks. The runs are fun and the characters that I've unlocked so far are nice and have each their own gameplay (might update on that when I have more hours) ! In this game the characters use cards as in any deckbuilder to attack or cast buffs/debuffs. A point I enjoyed a lot are combos between attacks, which will boost the damage of the attacks. In the dungeon while you advance you can either run into : a small fight, a big fight (more mobs/tougher mobs), getting money, getting cards or a campfire to rest/upgrade your deck. You explore the dungeon for a set amount of moves then you have the boss fight and can proceed to the next floor if you're still alive. At the end of a run in the first level (if you didn't die) you get to keep the deck you used to use it again later, if you don't like it you have 4 slots to try and get a better deck by redoing a run (Once you got the deck you keep it even if you die after). The dungeons are nice and the difficulty curve is (for my level) correct. To sum it up, it is a really nice roguelite game even without knowing Fairy Tail (even though knowing it makes the story and character's interactions more interesting) and it is fully worth the current price (11 euros / 12 dollars). I wholeheartedly recommend this game if you like fairy tail, roguelites, or even better, both.

name: Cat Quest III
detailed_description: Get whiskered away on a hearty catventure in Cat Quest III, the third installment in the award-winning Cat Quest series! Play as a swashbuckling purrivateer in this 2.5D open-world action RPG set in a fantastical pirate-themed world – the Purribean - an archipelago swarming with Pi-rats searching for the Northern Star - a long-lost mythical treasure. Alongside your trusty spirit companion, set sail through the Purribean in your very own ship! But beware, the seas are dangerous, and a meow-tiny is nigh as the hordes of Pi-rats under the order of the Pirate King hunt you down… RETURN OF THE CAT The cutest action RPG you know and love returns for a colorful adventure filled with furr-iously fun gameplay! Delve into a paw-geous new world with varied dungeons and biomes to explore, and encounter fierce battles with the newly refined combat system featuring tighter attack combos and weapon swapping. Playable in either solo or local co-op! SAIL THROUGH THE PURRIBEAN For the furr-st time in the series, sail the seas and battle in your very own ship! Explore the waters on your ship, seamlessly zip to shore, and traverse the land on paw to hunt booty in the paw-esome pirate world - the Purribean! There's treasures galore to be found, including new weapons, like the blunderpuss, furr-ocious spells, gla-meow-rous costumes, and more! X MARKS THE SPOT Embark on your very own treasure hunt and craft your own story with complete furr-eedom! Choose to explore the deepest corners of the Purribean at your leisure, or say ahoy to a quirky cast of characters and aid them in their quests along the way, in any order! The meow-steries of the Northern Star reach far and wide, and it’s up to you to investigate, gather clues and uncover the many secrets of the Purribean. This (cat’s) tale is yours to make, so weigh anchor and let’s go!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes you are reading this correctly. I played cat quest 3 for 18.6 hours straight the day it launched. Im not sure anyone who didnt have a pre-release copy can beat my time. I 100% the game 3 times in a row, and I have a lot to say about it, so lets dive in.Short answer, this game is genuinely incredible. its everything cat quest 2 wished it was, fully realized.Long answer, this game is the best in the series, and is one of my favorite idie games of all time, but has a few things it could touch up on.First off, the composer of the ost is genuinely so incredibly talented. I can only think of like two games off the top of my head that I've played with better music(celeste and bravely devault) It takes the best parts of the previous games and perfectly weaves them in with the pirate theming of this game, and they are all wayy to catchy. i will be hearing these songs in my dreams for weeks im sure.The visuals of the game are stunning, I wish I had an oled monitor to properly enjoy them, but alas. I dont need to go in depth here, yall can compare to the previous games and see the impressive step up yourselves. shoutout to the starting cutscene for a new profile looking stunning.As far as gameplay goes, there is a lot to unpack. Almost all of it is generally very very positive, but there are some things that did get worse/I have some issues with.My biggest issue is that some bosses have attacks where they cannot be hit for upwards of 10 seconds at a time, or severly restrict the loadout you can use against them, or both. the wizards in particular were frustrating and not all that fun, ESPECIALLY when stuck in the infinity tower, where 10 seconds makes a big difference. Id like to request that all of the boss wizards be removed from the tower or the ai changed to not do the hover out of reach attacks. the feeling of watching the time slip away on a solid run is kind of crushing, and it doesnt have to be that way. as a side note the first seeker is kind of irritating in that it railroads you into ranged, and i find the boss to be much more fun when in the tower and I can smack it with my claws. On the other hand, some bosses are very very well designed. All three captains and dracatula are very fun to fight, with meowtallika being especially cool with the atmosphere and attack patterns. Unfortunately the spells the player uses can heavily block telegraphs in the 2d fights, but I enjoy many of the 2d fights enough that it doesnt bother me(other than the wizards). The ship battles are in my opinion somewhat unremarkable, either you can beat them or you cant. losing your boat is sometimes a little too punishing, but if you do get away, its too easy to repair and return to the fight against a weakened boss. id like for ship bosses to heal their health if you lose agro and repair your ship. i do like that heal can heal the ship as well, its a nice touch.probably the biggest improvement gameplay wise over the last game is balancing. in the last two games, balancing is basically non existant, with like 1-2 sets of armor being objectively way better than all other options with 0 competition. looking at you old master set. this game has stronger options and weaker options, and while i used the same build for all 3 playthroughs, there are a lot of cool build ideas that are viable, its not dominated by op sets that break the game. I hope when mew game rolls around they dont release some wack op crap that breaks the somewhat decent balance they have. Gold hat is very overtuned atm, would like to see a nerf at some point, preferably in the next week before the speedruning gets going.The side quests and dungeons are also much better this time around, with less in number and a greater emphasis on making them interesting. I see a lot of people talking about how this game is so much shorter than cq2, and while it is a smaller game, its more tightly packed and the quality of each piece is much better. I have no issues with the length, and think it is worth its full price. I did kind of wish for a little more trinkets and spells tho, there arent a lot of trinkets that buff guns, which i feel is a missed opportunity.speaking of guns, i think they are a great addition, but one of them is notably wayyy better than the others, which kind of takes away build freedom, especially for the tower. _childDocuments_.review: What another awesome installment. you can play this without playing any of the prequels. Keep an eye out for the point of no return and finish everything before entering that door. ~10 hours to completion.  Around 10 hours 3/10 1 will help you find missing gear, but for the most part you don't need a guide at all. No Kinda, if you go through the ending you can't go back, but the game will warn you about that. No No No No No No, you can play on the story difficulty and still unlock all the achievements NoI love the Cat Quest series so much and this third installment is so awesome! I loved moving around with my ship, shooting canon balls at enemies, and finding all the hidden secrets. One thing The Gentlebros (the developers) do so well within this series is that everything is there for a reason... A specific text blob when doing an action, mist, patterns with shells, it all is there for a good reason! In Cat Quest III you are on an adventure to find the Northern Star. You start on a small island and will do your first dungeon over there, but then the world of Cat Quest 3 is all yours. And you might not be able to fight every enemy just yet, there is always a save point around the corner, so trying out and seeing how far you can come doesn't hurt at all. The most amazing thing are all the (little) secrets, there are just so many. You will constantly have the feeling you explored something special, or you have an idea of what to do next. However, the second best thing by far is that your cat will change looks by what you decide to wear. The gear has special abilities so you don't want to choose them all by looks, but it is just nice to see the armor change. By the end, my cat was wearing a very ugly head, but it had such nice stats. Of course, we can't furrrget all the cat puns. How have they already filled 3 games full with cat puns without boring us? That is just a skill on its own! I only have 2 small complaints. the first one is that I would have loved to see a quest log. You can kinda see the quests on the map, but I would have loved just a short list to remind me what I'm working on. And the second thing is the white screen. Sometimes when loading ( for example at the start of the game) the screen turns totally white. This kinda hurt my eyes. I wish it was a black screen instead of a white screen. Both things are quite minor. The achievements in Cat Quest 3 are for completing just everything. Get every bounty reward, find every item in the game, and complete a lot of side quests. After you finish the game you can't go back into your save file, so finish everything before entering that specific chamber... the game will give you one warning about this, so make sure you don't skip text so you don't miss this. For the rest... just keep exploring and be curious about why something is there! I missed a few items when I thought had explored everything. Gladly there is a guide where you can see all the items listed and then click on it to find out how to get it. I give Cat Quest III 4.5 out of 5 stars and I hope we will see many more Cat Quest sequels!

_childDocuments_.review: Cat Quest 3 is great, but it is WAY shorter than I expected. There seem to be much fewer side quests than Cat Quest 2, and the main quest is significantly shorter. I finished it in one 5ish hour sitting (I plan on continuing to 100%), and in that time I finished the main quest without really realizing it, and I finished a bunch of side quests as well. The charm and core of Cat Quest is in this one, but a lot of things were changed and many of those changes are side grades at best.First, the map and the boat: The boat is a fun new mechanic and the fights with it were fun, even if they were very simplistic. However, the boat is also quite fast, and I'm not sure if the map is actually smaller than Cat Quest 2, but it certainly feels that way. Certain UI elements like seeing dungeon level and enemy level, especially on the map screen, are missing in this game, so it's easy to stumble on an area or enemy that is way higher level and not notice until you either get one shot, or hit a bunch of times and realize you've done little damage.Then the changes to weapons: You can now wield both melee and range at the same time, which is a great addition, and in addition to the returning wands, there are a few different types of guns that are fun to play with if you aren't into the type advantages.The changes to the magic spells were worse *for me* but that is likely just my opinion. There were a couple returning spells from Cat Quest 2, but there were a bunch more that were changed in some way. I think these were a decent way to mix up the spells overall, but I ended up just sticking with a single spell instead of using 4 that I liked (which is what I did in Cat Quest 2).Finally, there's the dungeons and the difficulty: I made the mistake of playing on easy. It was VERY easy, and while it was fun to feel overpowered against certain enemies, it made other enemies and fights trivial. There were fewer dungeons than in Cat Quest 2, and about half of them are 2D instead of the usual 2.5D, which IMO is worse for both fighting and traversal.Overall, it's a good game, but it is 2-3x shorter than Cat Quest 2 and doesn't offer the same variety, and it is much more expensive. This is one of those "I wish I could give a maybe" or "buy it at a discount" types of games. It's good, but it doesn't cross the line to be great.
