_childDocuments_.review: There is a cat, it has a quest, and this is the third time we've been through this so .. story checks out. If you're a fan of the series I absolutely recommend buying this, if you're new to the franchise or not sure about buying this one then consider it's about seven to ten hours of unique content for the price of a movie ticket, and if you're looking for grind/builds/complexity then just keep on looking elsewhere.Definitely a fun game that I recommend for anyone looking to play something light-hearted. There are a few challenges to overcome, but the difficulty isn't very high; most content only requires a few tries at most to work your way through even under the intended level. The world is very open and content can be approached in any order (which is how I played three-quarters of the game without having the only healing spell), but as is typical for the series this game uses level-gating to keep players from wandering too far away from the intended sequence of play.Thankfully grinding isn't really a core mechanic of this entry, with plenty of experience and in-game currency flowing in from doing just about anything. However, I have seen some a bit disappointed that the lack of grind makes the game feel shorter than the previous entry in the series. Having taken just a hair over twelve and a half hours to complete the game twice, I can understand their perspective; but personally, I don't miss the tedious grinding in special grinding dungeons to engage with endgame content. I really enjoyed the natural and easy flow of progress through this game without having to stop and grind out character and item levels needed to advance. You should keep this in mind when making your purchasing decision, however.Of course, there are some issues with the game... First, lots of the items provided are either not good, copies of another item with minor variations, just a gimmick, or all of the above. Second, nothing can hit an enemy flying higher than head height; not firearms, not seeking spells--nothing. Third, a lot of the sidequests are just "take item X from A to B" livened only by some in-game humor. (Well, when said humor actually lands.) Fourth (and maybe this one is just me), in a game with a pirate-themed adventure you search for buried treasure exactly once.The game does a lot to establish character meowtivations, but doesn't do much world-building at all. Where are these islands? Who built all this stuff, and how? If there are no non-pirates, who do the pirates plunder? How does the spell shop stay in business, is it trading with the mage pi-rats? Don't worry about it, and just accept it is what it is--I guess. Your companion's references to the Pirate's Code are interesting until he refers to #6 twice as two different things, then it just feels like some silly filler text that doesn't really matter or relate to anything. This feels a bit odd compared to the previous titles that put quite a bit of effort into establishing the lore of their respective worlds.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the absolute peak of the Cat Quest series.I played through Cat Quest 1 and 2 several times. To start, I've only been into about 5 hours of this game at the time of this review, but I need to say, I think GentleBros took everything that worked well from the first two games and then built on top of that for this game.This is Cat Quest as you know it. Funny cat pun dialogue, cat sound-effects and all, but this is the first time in the entire series where I actually am invested into the overall story. The overall theme of pirates is awesome, and to be honest, the ship battles are actually fun and engaging as well. The map is beautiful as well, it's just a culmination of what made Cat Quest 1 and 2 good, and they took all of that, and made it all even better somehow.Even though I'm just 5 hours in, I NEED to address the very few negative reviews that exist at the moment. If this game indeed has less content than Cat Quest 2, I'm not even bothered by that. Cat Quest 2 has SO many "go on the other side of the map, kill (x), then come back, then go on the other side of the map again, talk to (x), then come back," etc etc etc, side quests. Those quests definitely took up time, yes, but they were extremely shallow side quests. In all honesty, that was the worst part about Cat Quest 2. So far, 5 hours in, there's nothing like that in Cat Quest 3. And to add, my friend and I have barely scratched the surface in this game 5 hours in, as we're both 100%'ers who like to do everything! And this game is cheap in general, so already I got my money's worth. Anyways...:The art direction is a 10/10 as well. An absolute upgrade over the last two installments, the extra shading, shadows/lighting, are absolutely beautiful. I don't think they changed engines or anything, but they seem to be pushing Cat Quest to its maximum. Cat Quest 3 is an absolute state-of-the-art game in terms of art direction.That all being said, I need to highlight the single negative I have with the game. The camera is a bit of a lower point-of-view from the previous games, so you'll have to get used to that. I wish they kept the same camera angle, it's just lower now than the first two games. But within an hour or two of gameplay, you WILL get used to the new camera angle. I just don't understand why they didn't keep the same camera angle from the previous two installments. At the end of the day, if you are a fan of Cat Quest, definitely pick this game up,--you WILL get used to the new camera angle, trust me!The fact that there's the Steam "Play Together" option makes sure you can play co-op with a friend who doesn't even own the game themselves, that is an absolute BOON to this game's playability--I'm playing with a friend who does not own this game, yet we are able to play remotely through the Steam "Play Together" feature--look into it if you have no idea what I'm talking about, it allows for local co-op when even if your friend does not own the game. Shift-Tab, send that friend a "Play-Together" invite, and they will be able to join LOCALLY on your own PC for co-op, without even owning this game. I bet that's gonna blow your mind if you had no idea that feature existed on Steam!So, getting back into it: I recommend Cat Quest 3 to anyone who is a fan of the previous games, or even anyone who is a fan of cats and cat puns in general, and is looking for an amazing game to play, with or without a friend. Especially those who enjoy top-down action games on top of that.THIS IS IMPORTANT FOR NEW PLAYERS: if you are one of those people who hasn't ever touched Cat Quest, you do NOT need need to play Cat Quest 1 or 2 to understand what's going on in this game--this is in an entirely different timeline/universe/etc, there is no lore that you need to care about if you are considering picking this game up. You can play Cat Quest 3 with impunity, and I would recommend you to do so.TL;DR: 10/10 artstyle. 9/10 gameplay. 10/10 sound effects (cat noises), but also 9/10 music direction. Also, you don't need to play the first 2 games. You will like this if you enjoy cats in any manner. You will also SUPER like this if you like 2.5D action adventure games. Also, you can play with a friend even if they don't own the game through Steam's Play-Together feature.Have fun, Cat-venturers! I pawlieve in you!!

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game from the first one all the way to this third installment and I have to say that it has improved so much! The graphics is so beautiful with its lighting and water effects. The new mobs were really cute too, and some of them gave me maplestory nostalgia.Some negatives would be the new boat mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: Don't think I've played the previous games in this series, but this one really caught my eye. Played the demo and I was instantly sold! If you want a cozy little 2.5D RPG to play.I would say the game is more worth $10 instead of almost $20 because I've been playing all day and I think the game is pretty short, and as I've seen some people mention the game has a good bit less substance than the previous game, I really would have liked to at least sink at least 20 hours into this, but at the rate I'm going I'll probably finish everything in about 15, and that might even be pushing it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is practically Purr-fect in every meow'ing way. Its whimsy, it's fun, it's Cat-Purrates & Pi-Rats. There's literally nothing about this game that there isn't to love. Is it a little hard combat wise, sure, but it's not Dark Souls levels of difficult. Who doesn't want to spend endless hours roaming the maps of the Purr-ibean on a little ship and fighting whatever foes come your way? If you love Cat Quest 1, this will be your new best friend. (I didn't mind 2 but it wasn't a snip on 1.) You can sail solo if that's your jam, or play local co-op and sail the seven seas with friends. Idk why you'd want to, but the option is there. I have waited long for this game, and truly, it did not disappoint. <3 Cats, D&D-style campaign, Pirates and Whimsy. If you hate this, you hate fun. XD

_childDocuments_.review: Among the three Cat Quest games  so far, Cat Quest III in a way is the best. Cat Quest III is akin to playing One Piece Manga in cat mode. You get to hunt down different pirate captains and hunt down the one big treasure. All the dungeons are also unique unlike CQ 1 and 2. It is a small open world to play around with. The game play is more polished and there are also ship battles as well. The only complaint is that it is really way too short for the amount of money the developers are charging. If you rush through the main story, it will probably takes you 6 hours or so. I took around 9 hours and that is cause i was just exploring around, playing around with most of the side quests. The problem with Cat Quest III that it is way too short for the amount of $$$ the developers are charging. The whole map size and contents should have been at least 3 times more. Main quest should run up to 16 hours at least. Unless you don't mind the length of the game, i would recommend getting the game at 60% discount. Though game is fantastic, it is just way too short. Before you can finish your first purr, game is over.PS : This is the first time i pre-ordered the CQ series game. Don't think i will do that again as i felt shortchanged by the length of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Even without the save file error that wipes everything, I cannot recommend this game. There are still too many errors, bugs and oversights to accept in a full priced game. They added a new camera angle, but there are game modes where the new angle makes hides the buttons the game is asking you to press because the commands are covered by other on screen graphics. The referee pathing is still poor, and they will walk all the way around the two wrestlers in a pin, from one side to another. Teams/factions entrances are still not coded properly, to where you don't get a full team entrance. The Universe mode is essentially exactly the same as last year, and still does not have a "blank" template option so you can build your own company from the ground up. Instead you have to unselect and delete tons of things and even then, the records and histories page still shows WWE wrestlers and records.The Showcase mode is a total mess. The game will give you multiple sentences worth of information while the game is going. And, half the time the controls it tells you to do are incomplete and you have to pause the game to find out exactly what buttons you need to press. I understand you want the players to perform specific moves to push the story of the match forward, but I should not have to pause the game, read the objectives and then attempt to do said objectives 10 to 20 times a match. I did not spend time with MyGM, so I have nothing positive or negative to say about it. MyRise was really hard to get through, and as such I spent about an hour or so total in that mode. It's a mess of a mode, the dialogue/writing is nonsensical, the version of the WWE they present here is nothing like the product you see on TV and the menu/UI is just awful. I understand wanting to have a "social media" element to the game, but it feels like it was written by someone who is really out of touch with todays social media.I see people saying "if you liked 2K23, you'll like 2K24". Which is correct, but only because it's the same game as last year. They need to figure out how to solve all the bugs, glitches, errors that occur constantly. They need to figure out how to present their game modes with respect to the people playing this game and value their time.Overall score 6/10EDIT - Requested and received a refund. Thank you Steam, the customer support is excellent!

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, :It's a decent game - if you like wrestling/fighting games and you haven't bought a WWE game in a while, you may get worth out of it for the roster update. That said, I'm not particularly happy about forking over over £100 for the Wrestlemania edition for them to release a further edition this week which requires  outlay of money and frankly, it smacks of a total lack of respect for the consumer of the product and lazy cash grabs.There's plenty of depth with the MyRise, MyFaction, Universe mode and so on and as always, there's plenty of creative options for you to try with making your own superstar, entrance, victory and so on; as ever, there's a wealth of downloadable content from other creators also. I've played for around 40hrs in total and have pretty much kept most of my time playing the MyRISE content, so there's definitely a lot of value in terms of time you can spend on the game modes.Regarding that, the MyRISE content I've played through so far has been fun and hearing the superstars voiced by their real-life counterparts is good, though some definitely seem to have put in a better performance than others! It would be nice if there were a couple more overarching storylines per gender (male are tied to the "Dark Horse" story, while female are given the "Cap" story) and having not played through fully, I don't know if this happens, but it'd be great if some of the other characters you play alongside (Psycho Sally, Carly Prime et al) get unlocked for play on completion.Graphics are reasonable enough, they don't feel like a massive upgrade from the last game I played (2K22); more negatively, there's some "uncanny valley" moments with some of the models and the input doesn't feel as responsive to me as previous editions of WWE games I've played.I've had numerous instances of my character stood doing nothing after pressing an input which can be really frustrating as the normally fluid gameplay takes a hit; or the collision detection to determine your character being located either at a weapon, or climbing ropes is shoddy at times. In my opinion, the entire reversal system and collision detection is still no better than the Smackdown vs RAW editions when Yuke's were the developers. If anything, I'd say it's considerably worse than games that are over a decade old.I am running a relatively high end PC that vastly outstrips the minimum and recommended system requirements: for context, an AMD Ryzen 7800X3D CPU, GeForce RTX 4070 Ti Super GFX Card with 32GB DDR5 SDRAM and the game breaks constantly.The "help" from 2K Games suggests that the "Graphics Device Removed" error suggests my PC is not capable of playing the game and it must be below minimum requirements. So, this is to show that this quite simply not the case at all.The game will crash randomly on the loading screen, or during saving your CAW, or during a match with a "Graphics Device Removed" error - the last one of which actually corrupted my steam folder, making it unreadable along with every other game in the folder. Thankfully, I've been able to repair the hard drive and subsequently my Steam folder has been saved, but is that really the sort of expectation we should have as consumers? [EDIT - I've actually had another one that fully crashed my PC. I'm not sure I want to even attempt to play this any longer as I genuinely fear it will break my system. For reference, I have played Cyberpunk on full Ultra settings from start to finish, as well as WoW, F1 and others for long periods and never had anywhere close to an issue, the problems are entirely down to this game and unique to it.]I don't pay the best part of £110 for a game (40 Years of Wrestlemania edition) for it to be completely riddled with bugs, memory leaks, incompatibility issues and the like. That's a huge outlay to spend for any person for a game and I honestly feel cheated by the developers for the money spent, considering how many game-breaking problems there are.I want to like the game as at its heart, it's still the same as the old SvR titles but updated to the current day, which is what I love; but it's incredibly frustrating that I've had to repair the game twice already following crashes. I've tried to start in compatibility mode to allow it to get past the loading screen, disable every single overlay including the steam overlay to prevent random crashes and it STILL manages to not work properly. Unfortunately, it seems that a lot of other annual titles suffer the exact same sort of issues with code being sloppily built on top of ancient code (see F1, FIFA, Football Manager, etc)If I had less than 2h played, I'd refund it. So, I can't in good conscience recommend this game to anyone. I certainly won't be buying any more editions going forward, or at least until there's a serious change in quality control from 2K and Visual Concepts.This is the first time in nearly 20 years of owning Steam that I have felt compelled to write a review about how genuinely poor a game is. That should give you enough of an idea of how bitterly disappointed I am in it.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is mostly the same as previous editions, with 6 main modes:- MyRise : Two custom stories, one for male custom wrestlers, one for females.    - For males, it's fine ? I don't like how they keep handing you titles and then stripping them off you after one match.   - For females, I really like the story but I havn't played too much of it after the first 3h ish.- Showcase: You do a lot of wrestlemania matches to unlock wrestlers / arenas. It's fine, but it feels like a chore. I hate how they often censor a lot of things in the IRL footage (referees face, old wwe logos, fans, t-shirts...), this really takes the interest out of having archive footage if half of it is blurred. There's also no commentary and you're left with a boring music. ALSO, there's currently a gamebreaking crash in the orton vs rollins match. This is UNACCEPTABLE.- MyGM : a gameboard type mode, where you book cards and manage a roster. It's really fun, but the main issue is that this edition introduced a new metric, a wrestler level, that after a few seasons make every wrestlers wayyyyy too expensive to hire in the draft and you can't have a full roster early. This is offset after a few weeks with the upgrades of your logistics but  the scouting mechanic also feels too restrictive, i wish there was an option to search by "any ring level"  - MyFaction : the ranked / competitive / microtransaction mode : not a fan. I don't play these games for pvp, but it's innoffensive enough I guess.- MyUniverse : A sandbox mode, where you can do many things. It's fun to simulate entire years and see who ends as champion and the Wrestlemania cards the computer generates.- Play: basic matches, nothing bad to say.My verdict, a fun game, especially if you like wrestling, but ruined by minor inconveniences and crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but beware of bugs.  I have had a lot of fun with this game so far. Created wrestlers look much better this time around and some interesting gameplay mechanics have been added, but it seems some items that were available in CAW  before are missing now. ALSO.....This game has lots of bugs. Each update seems to introduce new bugs where the game was perfectly fine before.  I can't speak for the online play as I don't really do that but I have had issues where my universe mode just seems to become corrupted. I find myself unable to even open the Create a Wrestler section of the game. This resulted in me having to start the game over, which makes me want to quit playing. Lots of time was spent tweaking each created wrestler I had, which was about 10. That hardly seems enough to cause data corruption.There's also laziness with the Universe mode, lots of cool things can be introduced to make better rivaries and storylines but most seem to be the same from the previous year. It's nice seeing the new match types, but I feel too large of a focus is on My Faction. There is some fun to be had there, but it is clear they want you to spend money. I understand the desire to make money, but the main focus should be on making the game as solid as can be and taking care of bugs THEN worrying about locker codes and all that.I also feel that lot of time is spent policing the wrong things. People who create wrestlers have content taken down while people who share and create inappropriate items (nudity) seem free to do as they please. Overall, the game is fun for me, but the bugs that keep piling up makes me want to quit.

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to endorse this because I played it over ten hours and did not find any game breaking glitches or crashes. But then, i exited it and came back a day later. All my save game data in every mode was missing. So it lost my progress, all the hard work I put into Universe Mode, MyRise, GM Mode, at the Reliving WrestleMania section. I have two different carefully-created superstars I was playing. Losing all that progress makes the game not worth it. Too bad I bought the most expensive edition at $120, and played too long to get the refund.Update :Soon as they patch one thing, others pop up. I’ve been continuing to play this game because I paid for it. This is the first time I ever played all the modes in a WWE2K game. Now although I did find things to like in them, there were bugs in every mode.Sometimes the ref is standing in the way which keeps me from seeing the action which means I can’t control what I’m supposed to do. There are objectives that have to be completed that the player cannot control and until you do get through them, you cannot go forward in that mode of the game without restarting the whole thing. One I ran into requires that I whip a guy into a particular corner then grab him while he’s standing. Okay. But it turns out I’m too strong when I send him in. _childDocuments_.review: AbsolutelyTLDR: 2 single player stories, 1 GM mode, A load of wrestlers, A LOT of moves, (Seriously there's a lot) multiple different game types and an online mode.Detailed review: So first, I would like to point out the sheer eye sore of the amount of moves there are to choose from, I'm not joking, there's so many moves half of them I'm not even sure are real.The single player is very well thought out but you have to remember it is infact a story, not the type of story you would find in previous games where you can just flat out goldberg it and win every match.Now I've only played one of the stories (Male) which ends in a bitter sweet fashion but I won't go too much into detail with that, however clocking in 18 hours already just playing the 1 story mode when there's still one to go is pretty impressive.There is a combo system, while it's very basic it's still fun to be able to feel like you're actually doing something more active than spamming one button. Everything feels impactful, really impactful, if you want the best experience I highly suggest turning the AI to high difficulty+Now for the cons, (We have to be honest) The online, it's pretty dog tier connection wise, you're gonna be VERY lucky if you happen to get a match with a decent connection.The crashing, there are pretty frequent crashes on this game, I've got a pretty decent rig and I'm still noticing some frame drops, and within the first hour of playing I ran into a bug that forces me to delete a folder inside the main games folder just to make it play properly which seems a bit weird to me.With everything said, if I knew this game was going to be as good as it was I would've bought this game at full price without any remorse.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played most of the WWE games in recent years (that are on steam still), ups and downs here and there, clocking in about 200h in each, (2k17, 2k20, 2k22, 2k23) playing the game random matches, story etc... making characters, streaming AI only to friends to watch the stupid stuff happen.This years game, contrary to the reviews runs so much smoother than previous years games, maybe I missed the initial launch scuff and crashes, or i got lucky.I have not done everything in this game yet, so i don't have an opinion on everything so far, will probably have to come back and update.What most people probably want to see though Pro's and Con'sPROS:Runs smoother, loads into matches a lot quicker than it use to, doesn't stutter as much or at all in character creation when moving between different clothing options.Looks a lot nicer, even compared to last years game, and Im pretty sure its the same engine still.The amount of matches is nice, the new addition of special referee (which hasn't been seen since the MUCH earlier games is a welcome comeback) Casket and ambulance matches, these are ok but definitely not the best (slight con AI is super aggressive when trying to "put them away" and it takes a lot of effort, i normally play on legend, but still currently on normal and they REALLY don't want to lose the match when you go into the mini game) Gauntlet/Gauntlet eliminator/Gauntlet turmoil are probably the highlight of the new matches. Can do 4/5/6/8/10/20/30 versions of these.Gauntlet is 1v1 and when someone loses, winner stays on next person comes in. Winner is who pins the last person.Gauntlet eliminator, starts as a 1v1 and people get added like a royal rumble till the ring fills, timer stops and waits for someone to get eliminated, person comes in about 30sec - 1min, but you aren't restricted to the ring you can go in and out of it.Gauntlet turmoil, you ever just hate that one person and want to punish them, this is the match, it takes handicap matches and says "suffer." This match is 1v3/4/5/7/9/19/29, One person verses an entire team, best of luck to the one man.That's the new stuff.Some older matches got "new" stuff backstage brawl now has 2v2 and fatal 4 way modes, and a new area you can go into.Multiple ring announcers, adds a nice feel, can choose which one you want for the match, this doesn't really matter if you don't watch the entrances though.Lots of referee choices too this time, some being generic ref 1-4 and some being the actual ref's from WWE, male and female.Wrestlers now have the ability to THROW weapons at each other which is just funny. My first time witnessing this, Wrestler one downs Wrestler two, goes outside the ring, gets a chair from under the ring, as he's coming back in Wrestler two gets up, Wrestler one just throws it at him from across the ring hitting him in the face, and he hits the floor.Random but the blood is better, on the Wrestler, and the fact it actually drips on the floor like the old games.CONS:My first gripe, which probably shouldn't be this but, some of the caged matches... don't fade the caged wall facing the camera enough? If that makes sense, its basically too obstructive blocks too much vision, and your attention gets grabbed by the wall too much, so you can't see the fight too well, im not sure why its like that in this game, because it was never an issue with the previous one'sThe match types that do this are, Hell in a cell, elimination chamber. Im honestly not sure why these two do this, i double checked for hell in a cell if it was to do with having more than 2 wrestlers in the cell, it was not.Steel cage and War games are completely fine, they don't have the issue, the cage wall fades fine (checked if more than 2 for Steel cage would be an issue, it isn't, just seems to be a hell in a cell issue.)The AI, which should be the first gripe, but its not that often it does this, however its slightly irritating. They will just zone out sometimes and just stand there if its more than a 1v1 until someone comes to smack them.This could be seen as an issue for others, which it kind of is, but its sometimes funny. If they down someone in the ring, the person still stood up will sometimes go out the ring "for a quick walk" then come back in.(This is from purely AI only matches from what I've seen, they don't do this if you are actually playing someone)During pins they won't interrupt them sometimes, they will just stand there and let the match end even if they could have prevented it, I've noticed that being a thing with some of the previous games, Im not sure if its a bug with the AI or its so matches can actually end because if they were smart they could stop the match from ending every time.PERSONAL CONS:Obviously this happens, contracts and such but certain people not being in from previous or older games, so certain moves sometimes aren't in, but the big thing being music and entrances, messes with making characters, i get it i do, but gripe none the less.Why is there still not opposite gender fighting, it sometimes happens in IRL wrestling for a short moment, older games allowed you to have Men Vs Women matches, and to top it off the AEW game (not sure if its actually any good though) allows Men to fight Women.Yes there's mixed gender 2v2 matches, but its not the same, if the opposite gender hits one and other, match is over because of DQ, that's not the case with IRL WWE. (all the time with IRL anyway)OVERALL:Yeah I like the game, it runs better than previous years games, character creation is better, new matches are good, some do need polish, would be good to see more of the older games matches in which they slowly seem to be adding, would be nice to see special ref being allowed for more matches than normal 1v1, and game does have its WWE jank still, but its nothing game breaking from what I've seen.Will come back to edit if something majorly changes.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:Improvements: The gameplay has seen some fine-tuning, with smoother animations and more responsive controls compared to its predecessors. The addition of new moves and improved physics adds a layer of realism and excitement to matches.MyGM Mode: This mode has been expanded with more options for customization and control over show logistics, which has been well-received by those who enjoy the managerial aspects of WWE.Graphics and Presentation:Visuals: The graphics continue to impress, with detailed character models and enhanced arenas that capture the look and feel of WWE broadcasts. Lighting and crowd animations have also received updates for a more immersive experience.Presentation: The presentation remains strong, with updated commentary and improved broadcast elements that contribute to a more authentic WWE atmosphere.Roster and Customization:Roster: The game features a robust roster, including current superstars, legends, and some new faces. However, some fans have noted the absence of certain popular wrestlers, which can be a downside for those hoping for a more comprehensive lineup.Customization: Customization options are extensive, allowing players to create and tweak wrestlers, arenas, and belts. The addition of new customization features adds depth, though some users have pointed out occasional glitches in the creation suite.Modes and Features:MyRise: This mode, where players can guide their own wrestler through a career, has been improved with more storylines and choices, but some feel it still lacks depth compared to other career modes in sports games.Online Features: The online multiplayer component has been stable, with fewer connection issues reported compared to previous releases. However, balancing issues in matches have been a recurring concern.Overall Impressions:WWE 2K24 is seen as a solid step forward from WWE 2K23, with notable improvements in gameplay, graphics, and features. However, it still has some room for growth, particularly in roster updates and some of the deeper gameplay modes. Fans of the series will likely find it a worthwhile addition, but it might not revolutionize the experience for those who are new to the franchise.If you're a fan of WWE games, this one is definitely worth checking out, but it’s good to keep expectations in check regarding some of the ongoing issues and missing features.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the WWE games for what they are and invest a chunk of time most years. 2K24 is very much an incremental update to 2K23. There's not a great deal of anything "new" here, besides a few match types (for which I personally have little interest).There has been some amendments to the divisive MyFaction mode, which I believe to be for the better. Specifically, in 2K23, you worked through repetitive 4v4 match-ups to progress the namesake mode, whereas this year, you progress via a gauntlet style system. That said, some re-balancing is required to the "grind" of said mode. It now costs significantly more MyFaction tokens to unlock new cards, presumably to arbitrarily prolong the lifespan of the mode. I expect I'll get bored far sooner.The Showcase mode this year revolves around "40 Years of Wrestlemania", allowing you to work through specifically chosen Mania matches from over the years. For me, the key word here is work... The showcase mode is becoming a chore in it's current format and could benefit from a revamp. The stop-start nature of the mode, splicing archive footage into match-ups is tedious and acts to pull me out of the moment. It may be a little more work, but I feel that the mode would benefit from said moments being rendered in-game.The core gameplay is enjoyable for the most part, specifically in one-on-one match ups. For me, as is the case most years, the game falls apart in anything outside of a 1v1 match. The AI is abysmal...absolutely shocking and infuriating. The AI has for many years now prioritised poorly e.g. targeting the player controlled character in a multi man ladder match, despite the fact that I am stunned outside the ring, whilst happily allowing another AI character to steal a victory.Graphically, the game is decent but doesn't push or take advantage of PC hardware. The character models are mostly good but there's room for improvement visually. Specifically, hair is still a problem (as it has been for years). Also, the arenas and crowd are becoming increasingly outdated visually. There is a stark visual difference between character models and backgrounds that could benefit from some attention.I would summarise by saying that if you enjoyed 2K23, you'll likely enjoy this game. That said, if like me you are beginning to grow tired of the format, maybe skip this year and see whether we get any fundamental changes in 2K25 (unlikely)...My hope is that the developers take a step back to further improve what is here, rather than introducing new match types. Lets get the AI in a good place first and foremost. Then maybe turn attention to some of the more troublesome match-types such as Royal Rumble which could benefit from a complete revamp.

_childDocuments_.review: This is now the third consecutive year I have been playing WWE 2K, and 2024 may be the best version of WWE2K. With the resurgence of 2K coming back after a much-needed break in WWE2K22, they blended the best parts of action arcade gameplay with a wrestling simulator, creating a fantastic gameplay experience for WWE that I have played since the old Smackdown vs Raw days of the early to late 2000s. WWE2K24 showcases Wrestlemania history from the beginning, showcasing some fantastic matches as we go through the history of the WWE. However, while this is an excellent showcase mode this year, this exact showcase had been shown before, and that was during THQs last outing with “WWE2K14.” While we have cutting-edge graphics, I found the 2K14 version better as it promoted some stellar matchups that were questionably missing in this latest showcase. However, after leaving the showcase mode, we have many game modes that players can get lost in. Since becoming an annual player, I have been obsessed with the “My Faction” game mode. If you can keep up and stay on top of the weekly towers and love grinding for digital cards, it can be a genuine blast and a grind. I don't mind, as I love the gameplay of this series, and getting a wrestler I love with an excellent ranking feels incredible. When it all boils down to what matters the most about this game, which is the wrestlers, the graphics, and the gameplay, it is all here, and I love playing matches off the cuff and seeing some of my favorite wrestlers come down the walkway in their best-looking graphics to date. If I were to ask for anything more from 2K, I would love something to make this game feel more alive. I remember playing the Smackdown vs Raw campaigns all year back in the day, and in this game, there just is not a drive for me to do that, so I resort to grinding My Faction, exhibitions, and DLC releases to keep me locked in throughout the year.

_childDocuments_.review: The last wrestling game I purchased before WWE 2K24 was WWE '13. It has been over a decade, so what is my impression of the latest rendition? I regret my purchase. The issues with the game are manifold: From complicated controls, missing wrestlers, and server disconnections to half-baked game modes and gameplay that lacks player agency.For some unbeknownst reason, someone considered it a good idea to make every signature and finish a two-button combination. Doing this in a one-on-one match is one thing, attempting this in a match with multiple wrestlers is a nightmare, especially if the signature or finish additionally requires directional input, is performed as a springboard move, etc.Furthermore, any action in the game locks both the AI and the player into unnecessarily long-winded animations, and if you cannot guess (you read that correctly) the correct reversal button, you are in for what appears a never-ending beatdown in favour of the AI. On the other hand, if you instantly reverse the overly aggressive AI's first charge at you (all AI opponents charge at me the moment the bell rings), you can dominate them as long as you do not attempt to pull off the same move multiple times in a row. Anything cool you may try to do, such as setting up a table and a ladder in order to perform a move from the ladder through the table, will be quickly undone by the AI. If the AI does not do it on purpose, any of the many animation glitches will do it.Showcase mode is exactly what the name says, a showcase. You are led through a museum and have no agency other than attempting to recreate the match perfectly according to the game's objectives. Equally hilariously as annoyingly, the AI will reverse the move you are supposed to perform over and over. If you fail any given objective, you need to start over. Yeah, it is as much of a chore as it sounds.MyFaction is so horrible that I do not even know where to begin. I paid money for the ability to choose a certain starter pack. Well, the game's inputs were all messed up, so the game chose, against my will and any ability to stop it, the pack I wanted the least. Selecting a starter pack cannot be undone. You will be stuck with it. So now I am stuck with a bunch of low quality cards I did not even choose myself. Worse, however, is the fact that when I was finally making some progress, the server said, 'Wait! Are you... are you making progress? Are you actually about to have some fun? Time to pull the plug!' And a disconnection from the server means, your run ends. The cards I unlocked and purchased? Gone. The progress on the run? Gone. I gave it another try today, but the three-on-three and four-on-four matches in which the AI interrupts every pin unless you take EVERYONE out first killed the rest of my motivation.For all kinds of political and legal reasons, many WWE legends (wrestlers or otherwise) are missing from the game. Some of them work for other companies, some are currently facing legally relevant allegations. The problem is that you cannot recreate some of the most iconic matches in WWE history without these legends.I am probably going to play some matches in exhibition since I already own the game, yet for anyone who does not own the game yet, hold on to your money, wait for next year's game, and wait for the reviews before you get it. In brief, I do not recommend this game.Edit:I have played around with the exhibition mode for some time, and my frustrations with the game have become cemented more than before. Most match types, especially on higher difficulty settings, are an exercise in frustration. While I win nine out of ten matches, it is never a satisfactory victory because of all the issues I mentioned in my original review.Furthermore, Universe mode was more fun a decade ago. Yes, seriously. Once more, I can only emphasize my original recommendation: DO NOT PURCHASE THIS GAME. I wish I could say otherwise, but I cannot in all good conscience.

_childDocuments_.review: WWE2K24 is another step in the right direction with improvements that should have been implemented about a decade ago. But it's got a lot of issues. Also, lots of price gouging by 2K, especially with the bs DLC. It's overly expensive but it does play very well. While I recommend this game, it's certainly not a value.For all of my gripes, the character models do look very good this year. The roster is a good size and features current wrestlers and past legends. The gameplay, while not to the fun level that the old Yukes SD games were, is a good mix of arcade and simulation. Big props for being able for actually being able to switch the camera view. The biggest thing holding the game back though is its insane price tag. If you actually want to get the real, full game experience, you will be spending WELL over $100. That is bloody insane! It's also not cool that 2K has a standard version of the game that will leave the player without much of the content. It's a typical scumbag corporate move that the video game industry needs to change. Speaking of which, you'll have to endure multiple patches if you buy these games new. I don't pre-order games any longer for a good reason.If you're like me and you still like pro wrestling, there is certainly fun to be had with WWE 2K24 but I can't recommend it because of the issues I mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr If you've never played a wrestling video game before, this should be your first stop!I've only gotten into wrestling recently, so I may not know  there is to know about WWE 2K and the history of this industry, but my word is it a heck of a lot of fun. Yes, the showcase mode is just objective city, but you can just put it on Easy difficulty and grind it out within three to four hours. And again, it's  for a complete and utter noob like myself.Where I ] lose myself is the Create a Superstar feature. I currently have about twelve hours in this game, and about ten of those hours was JUST going through all the customization options for the MALE superstar alone. The model sculpting, the ENORMOUS selection of clothes, the VAST roster of moves, and even creating an entrance, victory, custom championship., arenas, signs, etc. All of this is just a sliver of what this game has to offer, and I have yet to really jump in to all of it. Not to mention the return of special guest referees, casket matches, ambulance matches, create a custom referee, stuff that should never have been removed since the Smackdown vs Raw days, yada yada yada.Yeah yeah, certain character reskins being locked into MyFaction (this game's version of Madden Ultimate Team) is pretty trash, but we should come to expect it from AAA and AAAA game studios in current year.And yes, the removal of two very controversial names this year (Vince McMahon and Brock Lesnar) is a hot topic, but there are also other names that are not in this game that were also in WWE 2K23, those being Edge, Dolph Ziggler, Goldberg, Elias, just to name a few. But if that's reason enough to make you not want to buy this game, you're not missing much.I will continue to update this review as I continue to go through the other modes on my own schedule. But currently, with 12.1 hours logged, as a very casual, laid-back WWE experience, it really does live up to the hype, and bides my time until Wrestlemania XL.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the exact same game as WWE 2k22 (I skipped 2k23).Graphics are identical, gameplay is identical, it's WWE 2k22 with an updated roster.It's slop but I'm playing it anyway because I'm a sucker just like you who bought this game and likes WWE.I did a long-winded review on WWE 2k22, my tl;dr problem with it is that the collision sucks and is gamebreaking; it's ridiculously easy to "miss" moves that hit a wrestler just because they were slightly out of position or in the middle of doing a stupid "ow i'm hurt" animation that lasts 4 seconds.I pine for the WWE Gamecube games, where collision was ridiculous; in a six man match, you could do a (Claudio Castagnoli-style) Giant Swing in the middle of the ring and use one man to knock every other man down like bowling pins.  It wasn't very realistic but it was fun as hell.  No other WWE game has come close to replicating this experience.But that's not why I'm negatively reviewing it; I'm reviewing it negative because as mentioned above, the collision sucks.  It's worse than any other WWE game I've played and I've played WWE 13, WWE 2k16, Smackdown vs Raw 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011.  All those games had better collision than this one.Anyway there's some new features in 2k24 over 2k22, including some new problems.  Here are the new problems:- Stamina.  There's way too little of it.  I love that they made it so your weakened wrestler occasionally stays down after doing a big slam late in a match instead of instantly springing to their feet, but they went too hard on the stamina overall because unless I am playing as turbo-charged lvl 99 Roman Reigns or Cody Rhodes, my wrestler is completely out of stamina just from running from one corner of the ring to the other, and it regenerates way too slow.- Showcase mode cinematics.  I love the switching back and forth between in-game and real life footage, been done since WWE 2k16, probably earlier.  Unfortunately they went too hard with this.  There's literally some showcase matches where you are just watching the actual match longer than you are playing the match.  Shawn Michaels vs Kurt Angle at Wrestlemania 21 was one of the worst offenders, with maybe half the match passing by just in cinematic.Also, I get the censorship is necessary due to copyrights and such, blurring out the WWF logo and blurring out Donald Trump's face in the Randy Savage vs Hulk Hogan match (true story), but what the hell is going on when they are blurring out the faces of referees, Howard Finkel, random people in the crowd, random T shirts in the crowd, even other wrestlers who are either still in the company or departed on good terms?The Randy Orton vs Seth Rollins 2015 match features interference from The Authority's goon squad Joey Mercury and Jaime Noble (J&J Security).  They are fully rendered in-game, have their faces and everything.  They look like the real people.  So why are the actual Mercury and Noble blurred in the real match footage?You're a multibillion dollar company now thanks to McMahon being sleazy and then selling to Endeavor to try to sleaze his way back into power.  Stop being cheap a-holes and cut some royalty checks or don't give us real match footage that's half-visible.EDIT:  Another thing; the MyRise story (for women at least) sucks.  WWE 2k22's MyRise story was largely aimless, moving from one cluster of nonsense to another, but at least it was entertaining with the option to be obnoxious and irritating, largely via picking fights on faux-twitter with other superstars.Here, your character has their own specific backstory and personality that you have no input into, and they are dumb as a rock and thick as a brick all in one.  There's no option during the storylines to pick or say something that deviates from the painfully badly written storyline options, almost all of which seem to involve you embarrassing yourself (the Rhea Ripley questline) or being easily manipulated by blatant idiots (such as Alfie the agent).And there's not even any real variety in terms of stuff to do.  "Missions" amount to "Do some damage to opponent" and then win the match.  Very rarely are there opportunities to see the story actually change from you losing, as you'll be forced to redo the mission until you win.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of wrestling like I am, these games with always scratch an its for more. But sadly the cracks on the series are beginning to show once again on WWE2K24. The game is plagued with crashes and freezing for many players as well as a few noticeable bugs that sadly are still around after several years of these games. It makes WWE2K24 feel like flashy shovel-ware like many yearly sports games unfortunately. To be clear, the game LOOKS GREAT! Wrestlers are very well designed, moves both look and sound appropriately impactful, and the general atmosphere captures the WWE Experience. But the My Rise feels dated at this point. While I enjoy the story of being a new wrestler coming in from the indies and pushing their way into the WWE scene, The locker room conversations with WWE wrestlers feels flat and un-interesting. Their dialog is very generic and some speak in audibly disinterested tones that don't reflect their on screen personality. Another issue is the bizarre game balance or lack of balance for that matter. Take SUBMISSION MOVES for example. Normally the minigame is pretty straight forward in WWE games. You beat your opponent down and when they are weak, you hit them with a submission move to get them to tap out. The minigame has you quickly smash specific buttons in order to overpower them. So whats the issue? Well in WWE2K24 the AI by default can press buttons in the minigame FAR FAR FAR faster than the player to the point where it is legitimately impossible to beat them. Its so bad that even with your opponent fully beat down, all body parts on their health bar red, stunned from a finisher, and out of stamina THEY WILL STILL PRESS THE BUTTONS SO FAST YOU THE PLAYER CANT KEEP UP! For me specifically I had to google how to beat the 2K24 AI so I could continue story mode only to find full forums of players also stuck in submission story missions. For those wondering there is an advanced option on the main menu where you can turn down the AIs button strengths and turn yours all the way up. You effectively have to cheat at the game to win the submission mini game by making the AI's buttons ineffective.This is a shame though because there are some good re-balances made from previous entries that I really like. For example the AI cant "reversal spam" you anymore. Now reversals are just timing based. You no longer have a set amount of them and can just do them whenever. GREAT! GOOD JOB! FANTASTIC! Another problem is the return of boring GENERIC items for custom characters. Yes those bland outfits and entrance songs that would never see the light of day on modern WWE are back again. Who can forget such classic songs as "Bubbles 1" and "Western 2". Or the outdated necklace model that seems to hover above your character's chest? Maybe you want a hat that causes all your character's hair to flatten out on the sides of their head.This wouldn't be such a big deal, if it wasn't for the fact that WWE WRESTLERS LOOK GREAT! Their intro and victory music is made by real bands that create such an energetic mood with professionally designed outfits that look amazing! The quality between WWE products and the generic character creation items are night and day to the point where its just better to copy professional WWE stars pants or entrance themes. Some people do make cool things with the limited toys we get to play with, but personally I hate that we are in 2024 going on 2025 and I know the next WWE Game will just copy and paste the same tired old create a character items.  All together, This game doesn't meet the mark it should be shooting for. Its just another forgettable WWE game. Copy and pasted, stale, lacking creativity. Do I like it? Eh, its a WWE game. I'm a wrestling fan so Ill probably play it more. But I can't see myself getting invested or buying any DLC. See you next year when we hopefully get something to be excited about.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version:This is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and a complete cashgrab!Do not buy this, except you are a quicktime fanatic!Long Review:I loved the WWE-Games back in the day. This had mostly positive reviews, so i wanted to give it a try. I hoped for a Game that i can enjoy with my frinds on the couch and recreate some iconic matches together. That is the reason why i bought the Wrestlemania Version, so i dont have to unlock everthing. But lets go for it bit by bit:Gameplay: The controls are so unintuitive, that you have to play all the tutorials for 30 minutes or you cant even get a grab done right. Why does it have to be so complex? That doesn't add anything to the expierience an everything feels kind of sluggish. And even if you know how to steer your Spaceship of a character model, every 2nd move gets countered by the AI, no matter if they have stamina left or not. Thats extremely frustrating and you don't get cineastic matches but endless counterfests. For you to counter an attack, you have to press Y most of the time, but sometimes its A, B or X all of a sudden. And you have to be quick to do it at the right time. Sometimes you have to hit it before the move happens, sometimes in the middle of it. If you like really fast QTEs, this is for you, else invest your money otherwise. The Camera is placed so near to the ring, that sometimes you cant see if you hit with an attack or not. The AI gets up much faster so even if you counter something, most of the time the enemy hits you to the ground right away, without anything can be done about it. MyFaction-Mode:Of course there is another way to milk the cashcow and its a collectible Cardgame called MyFaction. The big issue here is, that this gamemode unlocks some of the playable Characters in Exibition-Mode. Either you pay more money on top of the 100 bucks of the Wrestlemania Edition or a good amount of chacters stay locked.And even if you cash in another time, its still gambling if you hit the right cards. Thats a shame!Showcase-Mode:Could have been a nice feature, but the tasks you have to do need so much time because everything gets countered. Even the finishers are countered so you have to build up again and again to complete it correctly. And if you misplay one single thing, you lose the match and have to start all over again. In my case, the progress wasn't saved correctly twice, so i had to do the Rude vs Warrior and Warrior vs Hogan Match 3 times now. Some tasks are not recognized even if done correctly (Loaded finisher in Rude vs Warrior for example). Content:As a long time WWE Fan it broke my heart when i wanted to recreate the 3 Way TLC Match with the Dudley Boyz, The Hardys and Christian and Edge. No Hardy Boys, no Edge. So many Superstars of the Franchise, even some Hall of Famers are just missing. You can recreate them in the Editor, but that needs time and isnt the same. But good for you if you are a Cena Fan, there are 7 or 8 Versions of him to play at least.... There is also no Workshop, so no Community Charakters can be downloaded. The Match-Types are all there, so at least thats something positive to say. Graphics: The main Characters look good and the moves do, too. But what about the rest? All the Arenas look exactly the same. The Entrance-Areas, the Ramps, the fireworks, the lighting, eveything looks like from a 15 year old game. That crushes all immersion for me. But if you have to release a Game every year, these parts seem to be to much to ask about. Conclusion: They tried so hard to develop a Simulation, that everything thats fun about WWE is completly taken out of the Game. Even if you buy the premium product, you still have to pay for a slot machine game to unlock every single character. The graphics are ok but the level of detail totally sucks. Many Superstars are missing and others have 6 versions of them. The Showcase mode is to clunky to have fun with. I think this was my last game of the Franchise. _childDocuments_.review: Have been playing wrestling games since the early PS2 era and I've got to say that every release since WWE 2K22 has offered more and more with each passing year!Special Referee matches are finally back after a decade, as well as the addition of an Ambulance match, and a Casket match. We also see the return of MyRise, Showcase Mode, MyFaction, GM Mode & Universe Mode. All of the aforementioned game modes have received updates and additions that further increase replayability for hours and hours of fun!Overall, I've sunk nearly 25 hours into this game, which will probably multiply by 6 for the remainder of the year until the next release! These negative reviews regarding issues migrating progress for those who pre-ordered are blown out of proportion. Players were warned that if they continue that they'll lose their progress, all I did was update the game, backup my save, and then reload when the immediate patch was installed with no issues.If I were to knit-pick issues, they'd be the following: Collision with certain grapples and moves are clunky at times, the reversal prompts are mis-timed at times especially when mid-animation, and the AI can't seem to stop doing running attacks despite me turning them down in the sliders. All of the aforementioned issues are small and trivial and were either present to some degree in previous titles, or will be subsequently patched in future.To conclude, I LOVE this game, would highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: 2k20 was abysmal and as a result, I skipped several entries after that, and have decided to give this version a shot.  I'm happy to say it is a return to form for the series.  The roster is absolutely loaded with today's stars.  My one gripe is that the majority of Legends are locked in Showcase mode, and this year the accelerator does not unlock them.You must progress through Showcase mode to unlock classic stars and arenas.  I initially was excited for this mode, but after playing the first few matches, it grew old very quickly.  First, you're given a dozen plus mini-objectives during a match and failure for the match to play out as it historically did results in not unlocking everything.  For example, playing Hogan versus Andre, I was given the objective to put Andre in a corner and attack him.  However, all my irish whips kept sending him in to the ropes.  Eventually, I gave up and just decided to win the match normally.  This meant that famous spots such as the bodyslam never played out and as a result, I unlocked Hogan but not Andre.Further, as the matches progress, they seamlessly transition from gameplay to archival footage with Corey Graves serving as narrator.  This sounds cool, in theory, and in the first playthrough of a match it is.  However, if you fail some objectives, like I did, that means replaying the match.  Which means sitting through all the footage again.  It just makes progression through Showcase a slog.  The alternative, is purchasing the 40 Years of Wrestlemania upgrade.  This will unlock all the Legend superstars but *not* classic arenas.  There's a ton of classic Wrestlemania venues in the game, but you're going to have to play through all of Showcase to get them.With all that being said, that was really my only disappointment.  There are a great many more modes to play -- MyFaction, Rise, Universe, My GM, and so on.  As said before, the roster is absolutely stacked, which is what I was most excited about.  WWE at this point in time has a tremendous amount of talent under their umbrella, and the vast majority of them are here in the base game.Overall, I recommend the game.  The gameplay is fun, the large selection of modes means there's something for just about everyone.  Showcase, which I felt was a big selling point for me prior to making the purchase, is cool exactly 1 time.  But it is aggravating that Legends who were readily accessible in years past -- Razor Ramon, Diesel, Stone Cold, Bret Hart, etc, are all locked behind progression through Showcase.  But I guess that's how they get you to drop the extra $20 for the upgrade so you can have them right away.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: So, they fixed one of the bugs mentioned at long last in the recent update. However, I'm keeping the review as Not Recommended due to MyFaction being the way it is and even worse than it was in 2K23 in terms of greed, Universe Mode breaking every year for everyone(I only really play Universe Mode to earn the Achievements and then abandon it, and that's only on home console, anyway), and how nonsensical the Persona Card system is, especially with the ones that were only available for a limited time on top of a couple only being obtainable via a freaking action figure. Ntm Persona Cards on their own are on average worth 50 USD in VC.Edit: I'm changing my rating to Not Recommended, cause there are bugs and problems with the game that haven't been fixed for months, especially one that messes up move collision, usually after connecting with a diving grounded attack or a running grounded attack. According to my email, I first reported the bug in **MAY**. Then there's a bug relating to custom entrances where Cody's pyro, if selected as the first pyro, will go off during the 2nd pyro. THAT HAS BEEN IN THERE SINCE LAUNCH!!!But hey, at least you get to spend 4000 dollars more on VC just to get an exclusive model that's just the 8th version of The Undertaker with nothing else actually different to it, right? Cause CLEARLY that's where the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ priority lies with 2K!!!Avoid this and avoid every other future entry. The ship has sailed and it exploded from a horseshoecrab.Original review below:It truly is amazing how something can be good if a company actually tries, and it's hilarious that, as much as I like it, AEW Fight freaking Forever was the one that resulted in them giving a ♥♥♥♥.Like, the game has a few features ripped right out of Fight Forever in 5 signatures and 5 finishers, blood all over the mat, and even the ramp camera(even if that was a feature in older WWE games, but still), what more do you need to accept that FF pushed 2K to try this year other than to get that stick out of your ass?With that said, the 5 sig/fin thing feels like they missed the point of why it worked in FF, as you could straight up do sig/fin combos such as, say, the Running V-Trigger 4 into a back grapple finisher such as the One Winged Angel. Here, there aren't any combos you can make work that way, sadly. On the plus side, moves that fit perfectly as finishers and signatures, such as Seth Rollins' 2 different Superplex combos, can be set as signatures without compromising any other moves. AND the Super Finisher option allows a wrestler to have a move that is that immensely impactful from them, and a couple even get to use them after they were primarily regular moves from them in the games prior, such as the Spiral Tap from AJ Styles and the Package Piledriver from Kevin Owens.I haven't played the Ambulance match, but I've played the Casket match, and the tapping with the minigames(not so much pinfall related imho) really is an issue. I get changing the button to keep me on my toes, but for submissions I feel it doesn't work that well as it did with Breaking Point Submissions, and even after I hit a finisher and throw them into the casket, they still manage to resist quite a bit from the closing of said casket.I did not beat MyRise yet, but I feel like outside of a few promos in front of a crowd, the voice actor for The Dark Horse wasn't given proper voice direction, which can admittedly be said about a lot of voice lines in the games as a whole.Universe Mode seemed fine for me, but I got my PS5 Trophies and hadn't touched it since, so I can only go by what everyone else has said about the recent patch, once again, completely breaking Universe mode.Persona cards are a neat way to actually have MyFaction playable wrestlers in other modes, but not only did they decided to NOT make the MyRise Originals into Persona Cards, but only 6 wrestlers seem to be unlockable as such, with 3 of them being either limited time only, linked to DLC, or linked to a 25 dollar action figure while also being on a time limit. I like having a complete roster in my games, but that last part is especially scummy. 2K has also said that other Persona Cards can be attained through pieces known as Oddities, but I haven't heard a single thing about that since that was stated almost two months ago.I don't care about the GM mode, so I don't know if they added anything new or not, nor if they fixed anything or not.Showcase Mode I feel is a bit overhated, even though some criticisms such as a lack of commentary, censored faces, and DUBBING OVER HOWARD FINKEL OF ALL PEOPLE are all valid. I think the one match that worked without commentary in that was Cena vs Wyatt at Mania 36, but that's only cause of the type of match it was. RIP Bray Wyatt.All in all, I'd....get this on a sale, if you haven't yet already. They added a ton of new and returning features and actually gave a ♥♥♥♥, but not enough of a ♥♥♥♥ to listen to the Quality Assurance team.More companies should listen to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ QA team.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is anything but user friendly, A lot of glitches in Universe Mode make keeping your divisions consistent a pain, and the fact that there are divisions at all is maddening. But the game itself is fun, the creation suites are the best we've ever had, and you can have a wealth of fun by just watching a Universe Mode play out. I recommend this game but only hesitantly because, well...Let's go over the negatives first:- Combos and combo enders have no place in a wrestling game, - It takes nearly 45 minutes to set up taunts when creating a wrestler - we don't need a taunt for every position possible and there are some options that my wrestler would never use. - move set creation needs a search option - I don't want to scroll through 200 moves in the B section just to get to Brainbuster 2. - Way too much randomness in the random universe set ups, there should be some sort of artificial intelligence that at least partially influences what occurs, when you aren't playing the matches. I'm not saying it needs a heavy influence, but Kane being the manager for CHASE U happening when they have no connections or allegiances makes zero sense. Also, the old smackdown games had no problem with this, AND still gave us procedurally generated storylines, with actual interactions, promos, and cutscenes, why can't we have this now? That was almost thirty years ago.- In connection to that Universe mode should be realistic while also presenting us with generated storylines and interactions. I remember on Smackdown Just Bring it (Which was two console generations ago) I would get back stage interactions with completely random superstars that lead to rivalries, alliances, and even relationships. Now I have to set EVERYTHING up myself or nothing happens at all, and there still are no actual in character interactions. That was 30 years ago, no excuse to not have it now. Breathe some life into Universe mode, make it feel alive.- MATCH TABLES are a TERRIBLE IDEA, just let matches happen based on rivalry, I shouldn't have to do this for every show.- Let me copy my shows to other days of the week and edit them accordingly, I have 307 wrestlers and 6 divisions under no circumstances should I have to redo ALL OF THAT just because I want the same roster for two shows. Like I said, this game is not USER FRIENDLY, and that is its biggest fault.- GET RID OF DIVISIONS. I shouldn't have to choose if I want Eddie Guerrero to be World Champion or Tag Team Champion, he should be able to do both or either, and I shouldn't have to influence that. The divisions make NO SENSE, the old games understood this, THAT WAS ALMOST 30 YEARS AGO. the game should be able to tell who should be going after each title, we shouldn't have to determine divisions.- The graphics and animations feel like they haven't advanced at all since Smackdown vs RAW 2007, do you guys know what hair looks like?- Soundtrack is the smallest and the worst ever.- I'm not going to play your card game to unlock stuff. Just not going to do it.Pros:- Other than the Combos, the gameplay is great, hitting finishing moves and super finishers feels REALLY good.- AI is much better than it has probably ever been, though in ladder matches it does seem to have issues.- All of the creation suites are just fantastic, creating your own signs, logos, arenas, entrances, entrance videos, championship belts, custom match types (that you can actually assign to Universe Mode). They're all just great. Make it so that we can make cruiserweight championships include light heavyweights and make it so that we can have championship belts specifically tied to match types (like hardcore matches or cage matches, and CUSTOM MATCH TYPES (DEAR GOD PLEASE)) and you've nailed it.- They brought back the ramp camera, been waiting for this for many years. What's the point in having a cool titantron if you only see it during entrances. Love the Ramp Cam.I know that the cons far outweigh the pros, in number, but the creation suites being as good as they are go a long way for me. the game really is fun to play and watch, and I get emotionally invested in watching my personal wrestler hit their finisher while their own body is fully red, only to get a two count. Come'on man you can do it!But there are a lot of problems with this game that there are simply no excuses for. Universe mode should feel like you are in a never ending WWE career. It should be dynamic, there should be interactions and relationships, and rivalries and allegiances caused by dynamic action, cutscenes and promos. and they can all just be procedurally generated. The old Smackdown games did this with no issue, and it made everything so much more alive.You are going to spend a lifetime creating your perfect wrestler, arena and title belt, and you will have a lot of fun playing with those things. I just wish there was more life.

_childDocuments_.review: WWE 2K games have not had the best reputation, especially after the recent disaster of WWE 2K20 and WWE 2K Battleground. WWE 2K24 is a delightful change of pace bringing back fan favorite match types and heavily focusing on the opinion of the fans. It includes returning match types including the Casket Match, the Gauntlet match, the Ambulance match, and the Guest Referee match. Along with the return of these match types they have also included new match features including throwing weapons, and the return of standing on the announce table. These simple features are welcomed as WWE 2K has been notorious for leaving beloved match types and features out for more useless features such as extra weapons and better graphics. This edition of the WWE 2K series also welcomes: Blood splatters on the ring, new camera settings, better selling, super finishers, create a sign, new paybacks, new weapons, real referees, new creation suite, first ever boxer playable in the form of muhammed ali, face paint fading, create a referee, spectator mode, and the trading blows feature. This bevy of new features is a refreshing change of pace for the WWE series and marks the start of WWE 2K fully listening to the fans when creating a yearly installment of their game. As much as I love to praise this game, there cannot be a WWE game without negatives. Recently, there has been a controversy of "persona cards" in the MYFACTION mode of the game. These cards are locked behind certain requirements of unlocking cards. Players have reported spending upwards of $400 for an amethyst "The Rock" card in MYFACTION. This has caused a lot of people to be upset with 2K for including deluxe editions of the game but still encouraging players to spend a lot of money for certain unlockables. Another negative aspect with WWE 2K24 is the neglect of the X Rated Content being uploaded to the community creations tab. WWE 2K has been very adamant on punishing creators for uploading modded characters but have been called out for neglecting mature content being uploaded which is against their community guidelines.Overall, WWE 2K24 is worth buying if you are a fan of the WWE games usually. But if you are a fan of the more arcade style games it might be a better use of your money to wait for a discount on the game. But WWE 2K24 is a good change of pace for the series.

_childDocuments_.review: ***READ BEFORE MAKING A DECISION TO BUY***I don't really know where to start with this game and 2K as a whole.For 7 years now, I have accumulated information, data or instances related to the online side of the game that shows that the same disconnection issues that have plagued the game year after year are still ever present in this game and have gone without a fix for 7 YEARS. During covid, I made contact with the likes of Bryce Yang and in August 2020 I had a conference call with Bryce and two other members that were on the dev team to try and put forward issues that needed to be addressed when it comes to the online side of this game and I put forward a bunch of stuff, one being the desync between players when playing online and this was ultimately fixed for the most part. Moving on, I had showed them evidence related to disconnections in the game and how they're solely as a result of 2K not wanting to pay out for the use of dedicated servers and instead think it's acceptable just to cheap out and stick the online side of the game, including the community creations onto terrible P2P servers. While trying to gain successful matches online using CAFs, you will 99% of the time be meet with "lobby warning", in game disconnection or a crash to desktop and this is a direct result of the abysmal P2P servers they're using, because once any tiny shred of data related to a CAF drops out then that is it, it leads to a disconnection, lobby warning, match warning and then it disconnects everyone in the match. These are issues that have been present in the game for 7 long years without a fix, now couple these poor P2P servers with people using wifi or playing with a poor connection and you can almost bet your house on it that it is going to disconnect. Disconnections will also still occur  during matches using regular wrestlers and this can also be pinned on P2P servers not providing any connection stability between the players, so if one persons connection isn't up to it, then it'll just lead to a disconnect or the player dropping out and it is really know surprise to me that this game isn't cross platform because the dev team can't even get community creations the online side of the game to work seamlessly.I put in 100s of hours playing, trying to play and testing for bugs, glitches etc and forwarded them in detail to the likes of Al Stavola, Bryce Yang and eventually Phil Dixon the CEO. After weeks of having pretty good communications with them, they eventually fell silent and decided not to bother replying to my emails which tells me everything I need to know about 2K as a company, a company that is happy take peoples money for a game that isn't even fit to be released!Having studied the coding related to the online side of the game, it has become pretty apparent that they are just rehashing and reusing the same old coding year after year, whilst still having the absolute balls to take your money.2K aren't bothered about listening to the average player, the average wrestling fan, but instead invite yes men youtubers to their HQ to play the game, a bunch of shills who will put out videos saying what 2K want to hear and pushing forward a whole load of lies about this game to the gullible fans of the community just so that they don't lose their streaming deal or their 2K perks.I HIGHLY ADVISE AGAINST EVER PRE-ORDERING ANY FUTURE 2K WWE GAMES AND INSTEAD WAITING FOR IT'S RELEASE AND READING REAL REVIEWS, NOT REVIEWS STUCK OUT BY PHONEY YOUTUBER SHILLS ON THE 2K PAY ROLL.
