_childDocuments_.review: This is a review for MyGM mode only because that is the only mode I play, so please bear that in mind. If you're a fan of MyGM, this year is absolutely worth a purchase eventually, but you can certainly justify a buy right based on what's new this year. They've made a few significant changes to the formula, mostly for the good, but there are some remaining flaws and along with some newly created ones I'll discuss. Pros:-New Wrestler level up system. Now instead of fumbling in the dark trying to discover a wrestler's favorite match type you can have up to 2 favorite matches that you get from leveling up which is amazing. You also get the ability to select an alternate class, which can be very handy. There's also small perks sprinkled in, but overall this makes the game much better, but...(see cons)-Special Guest Referee is a welcome new match type that has a place. Also they got rid of submission matches ending rivalries, so it can be used normally.-There's a new scouting system that you have to use to sign free agents. On the plus side, you can sign free agents for any length you can afford. 1 week all the way to end of season. This is a much needed and welcome change. However, the actual scouting...(see cons)-They redid the building/stadium upgrade system so now you can upgrade whenever you want. Your still going to want to do the stadium capacity first, so that's still kinda overpowered, but hey, it's better now with the freedom-The balanced the GMs but...(see cons)-They added ECW as a brand but...(see cons)-They added trading, but...(see cons)Cons:-New match types are welcome, but Casket, Ambulance, and Last Man Standing (LMS) matches really suck. Why? Well the loser of a Casket match leaves the show, meaning your out a wrestler which makes this a very niche match type and not worth it because you can get the same results from other match types without the extreme negatives and cost. Ambulance and LMS matches leave at least 1 wrestler injured guaranteed. Ambulance is far longer though. Again, same complaints with Casket that they aren't really worth using. I could see it if you like playing matches yourself and want some variety though.-Another issue is that they implemented an (optional) unlock system for match types which I overall like, however, with Casket, LMS, and Ambulance taking a couple seasons to unlock, wrestlers that start with them as their favorite match type can't even use them for a while. Overall, you can overcome this and probably ignore it, but it's a bit annoying being very sub optimal.-The other issue with the new match types is that wrestlers favorite match types are random every run. So basically, in my opinion, you want to avoid wrestlers in the opening draft that have -Rivalries can ONLY end during PPE (PPV) which is really frustrating. I'm not sure why they ditched the old system where rivalries can end naturally whenever (or let the player choose), but it makes the game easier because...-Using stale rivalries has no negatives, just like in prior year's entries. I'm not sure why the game tells you a rivalry is stale if you get the same high ratings out of it. If it's a bug, it's here the 3rd year in a row and they've fixed other bugs quickly. I think this may be strangely intentional, but not well explained.-Wrestlers still complain about losing in an event everyone knows is fixed. Why?-Still some wonkiness with events overlapping when they shouldn't that should be easily fixable by the devs. For example, a wrestler should never be mad at me if they're injured and I have no possible way to complete their quest. I can see an exploit, but just extend the deadline to a week or two after they come back. A lot of this weirdness could be limited if the devs limit 1 quest/event per wrestler at a time. Very simple fix.-Balance is still off. Money accrual and wrestler pay scale well, but for some reason, the amount you get in the draft stays the same. They really need to give you an extra million a year for each subsequent draft because the wrestler cost really goes to the money. Granted you're rolling in so much money by season 3 you can sign people back (if they show up available), but money gain still feels way too high on the last 2 stadiums.-I think wrestler stamina still recovers too slow OR you don't get a big enough roster at start. Personally, I would like to be able to do fun match types more often, but you really can't if you want to have your stars available when you need them.-The AI, even on extreme (the highest difficulty) is still not to hard to beat. Those hoping for a challenge this year, sorry to disappoint you. The AI also sometimes hoards money when it's behind. It needs to be programmed that hoarding cash does little for it's chances at winning. Even overspending would be better than sitting on cash.-Xavier Woods is still in his same OP form as a GM. The other GMs are closer now, but his power to steal a wrestler permanently is still very much a "cheat code" (what it's called in game). It can swing 700k to over a million in value to you each season which is far higher than other GMs. I like the idea, it just needs to be toned down somehow, like giving the other GM some kind of compensation. I want to use him, but I can't because he's too OP in my humble opinion.-ECW has no woman's titles. Maybe this is historically accurate, but can we please just give an option to the player to include these for balance and fun. As it stands the ECW brand is there as a way to handicap yourself or if your some kind masochist. -Still no hardcore titles or title creation in MyGM-Trading is ruined by the AI trying to pawn off wrestlers that have low morale, are injured, low stamina or have niche use cases to the player. I get the AI won't be able to get the last thing, but you can program the AI to avoid offering hurt, angry, low stamina wrestlers. You also can't counteroffer a trade the AI offers you. Basically, after each PPE (PPV) the player can do up to 4 trade attempts, along with the player. The one saving grace is occasionally the AI will offer an interesting trade. The AI seems to be pretty belligerent to anything the player offers, but that might have been because I was in first place.-They limited all powers cards to 1 per week of a given type. There are certain types I believe you should be able to use more than one of that type a week because the benefits are small or not immediate. Still some tweaking to do there.-Soundtrack is awful. They really lowered the music budget this year. I mean, I end up turning it off regardless because there's so few tracks, but they really cheaped out. No Metallica this time guys (or anyone recognizeable). The genres are all over the place too. How about some medleys of wresters intro themes or something? What about something orchestral? Whatever this music is, it's terrible this year (they even put in the Taco Bell song ffs).-Still no "skip all" button for the AI matches. I get this is programmed for human players, but for offline, please, for the love of all that is holy, let us skip through the AI matches in ONE BUTTON PRESS please. It's at least 9 per week right now, plus seconds loading the next AI's matches. It adds ups, I'm telling you. This should've been in the game last year.You might think with all these cons that this mode isn't worth your time, but to the dev's credit it's deeper than ever and I hope we get some patches to tweak this mode into being even more fun. And that's the key, this mode is fun if you love business sim style games like me. Check it out when it's on sale.P.S. Controller support doesn't work in MyRise during matches for some reason, but works fine in MyGM and exhibition. Must be a bug.

_childDocuments_.review: Right now I absolutely cannot encourage anyone to buy this game. If you are considering it, stop, read this post, then consider again.1) The BIGGEST issue first: the bugs. The game is choc-ful of them. In fact, there have been more bugs added to the game from 2K23 to 2K24 than actual pieces of content. That's right. They revamped MyFaction (which no one likes), changed up MyGM (which is feature deficient, and half-baked), and added a few match types. Oh, and they added blood smearing on the ring. You know what else they did?-   Completely broke custom wrestlers, making several aspects of customization straight up reset at random. Also, while you're customizing there's a completely random chance that your game just... crashes to desktop (customizations don't autosave so you just lose all your progress).-   Broke Create An Entrance, creating several instances in which pyrotechnics become permanently disabled (only way to fix it is to completely reset your progress on the entrance), and titantrons are reset to default smackdown screens (with no way to change them).-   Broke several moves such as the "Perfect 10 Punches" which completely softlock the game if there are only 2 competitors. Yep.-   Broke perspective adjustments, making AI vs AI spectator matches nearly unwatchable when doing matches like Hell in a Cell. The cell NO LONGER becomes transparent, so you're just staring at a piece of metal half the time. Same thing with Tag Team matches. If the fighters go to the right of the ring? You're just staring squarely into one of the wrestlers backs, with the MOST important section of the screen blocked. This is ONLY an issue for AI vs AI matches (which a lot of people love hosting), but not an issue in PvAI or PvP.-   Broke the Community Creations tab. Wanna upload something with a custom name, or text? Go ahead, but if you have any random words that the moderation system deems inappropriate seemingly at random (in my case, the word ECON for some reason), it'll just crash your game to desktop.-   Broke the Community Creations UPLOAD system. Yep. You wanna upload a character with text on them that ISN'T deemed inappropriate? That's great. The text will disappear for anyone downloading them though... not custom images you put on the character, JUST the text. Oh yeah, and your moveset might get reset, or your signs, or your stats, etc etc. Literally nothing that you upload is guaranteed to be saved. It seems to just delete your work at random.==2) The game visually is a mix of amazing, and absolute abysmal garbage:-   The lighting? Pretty good.-   The arenas? Great!-   The models? Terrible. Female models have a mix of fine looking, and disgusting mannequin features. Male models are either muscular, slightly fat, obese, or skinny... but all skinny models have concave chests as though they've been flattened like a pancake. On a side note, I've seen better ambient crowds in games from the early 2010s, the crowd in 2K24 looks worse than the crowd at the arena in Oblivion.-   The textures? Trash. There's plenty of good looking things in the game, but why are SO MANY of the pieces of clothing marked recolorable if the team making them couldn't be bothered to properly define the bounds in which the color will change? Change a red piece to black, and watch as the forgotten pixels of red create a nasty looking crust around it.-   The animations? A mixture of great, and bad. Tons of animations look super cool! Too bad they're mixed in with animations that are half the framerate, robotic, and seemingly not changed since the PS2 era.==3) What about what they didn't do though? Let's see:-   They didn't fix AI in Hell in a Cell. They still wander around the outside of the ring cluelessly, and often just get stuck... unable to continue the match until you take control of one and jostle them around.-   They didn't fix the multitude of clothing issues. Plenty of clothing pieces are still extremely poorly modeled, poorly textured, or broken completely. Several pieces have jutting, stretching polygons, and some pieces have actively gotten worse (such as one of the trench coats, which has had the fur texture turn into... cubes).-   They didn't fix the AI. At all. It's still utterly, and inexcusably unintelligent. The AI will routinely decide to do the worst possible thing they can in whatever situation they are in. Randomly slow walking around the ring, and allowing themselves to be counted out. Picking up weapons just to throw them on the ground. Using extremely long taunts knowing the enemy will be able to attack them. They're just... terrible. It makes fighting them unfun, and watching them even less so.-   They didn't attempt to improve the MyGM mode (the mode everyone I know actually plays the game for). You know how cool match run-ins are? Yeah me too. They're in the game! Not in MyGM though. Why can match run-ins happen randomly when in play mode, but when you schedule them to happen in MyGM you HAVE to simulate the match, meaning you cannot watch the run in happen? What about 3v3 tags? No? Maybe first blood matches? No? What about GM interference? Nope. 2K... you have all the resources for the scenes involved in these match modifiers from Universe mode... just carry them over to MyGM.==Alright, review over. I don't need to explain any of those points any further, I'm sure you get what I'm saying.TL;DR? Don't buy the game. If you absolutely must, then wait a few months. They're charging 60 dollars for a game they've delivered to you stuck together with duct-tape, and bobby pins. Skyrims bugs were charming, 2K24's bugs are not.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this writing I have over 25 hours of playtime experiencing what MyRise, Showcase, Universe Mode and the 4 new match types in exhibition have to offer. And I am pleased to give WWE 2K24 a massive thumbs down because this uncooked disappointment is nowhere near the standard that WWE 2K should be striving for.Let’s start off with one of the main selling points about WWE 2K24 – the celebration of the past 39 years of Wrestlemania showcasing the best matches narrated by Byron Saxton. There are 21 matches in total (plus the bonus match at the end) with 11 matches from the Ruthless/Attitude Era and 10 from the Modern era respectively. And like the past two WWE 2K games everything is objective based, which means be ready to do repeat objectives that demand you to do them in a specific location. This mode overall is nothing more than a boring hand-held tutorial that forces you to obey instructions rather than having fun. Every time a cutscene happened mid-match I was constantly asking myself “Is that the end of the match” because I wanted nothing more than to be done with this so-called celebration of Wrestlemania.This year’s MyRise mode features a women’s (Unleashed) and men’s (Undisputed) that tells quite good original stories like you being a famous independent wrestler who repeatedly turned down WWE contract offers in the past because she wanted to stay creatively free but ends up signing with WWE anyway, or winning the Universal Championship vacated by Roman Reigns who got bored of being an undefeated champion to go to Hollywood. During this mode you can unlock wrestlers who appear only in MyRise, but the catch is they only appear in MyFaction as MyFaction cards. Speaking of MyFaction, there’s about 5 or so wrestler slots saved for alt attires locked in your roster so if you’re like me and don’t want to make a 2K account, you’ll always have “?????” shoved in your face as a locked wrestler and there’s nothing you can do to remove them. And don’t expect to get the MyRise characters through community creations because a 2K account is mandatory to access the downloads – crossplay or not.In some ways this mode has seen improvements but it’s also seen some new bugs that makes me want to stay away until 2K gets working on them and fixes it. I like how they’ve improved the rivalry system so you can now see which rivalry option your opponent has taken and now you can target whichever opponent you want in a multi-man match with your rivalry action. The wrestler management system in wrestler-mode has is now easier to access letting you start and end a rivalry, compete for or defend a championship within one menu.  The bad is that it’s plagued with bugs. Half of the time the game forgets my customized global settings so my hold input for minigame reverts back to button mashing. Not to mention the crashes you’ll regular encounter.- Several visual bugs with pinning animations and performing moves and reversals. - Constant crashes trying to load literally anything outside of loading screens for example the next wrestler in a Royal Rumble, a piece of clothing or winning a match.- Brain dead AI that has referees counts rope breaks way to early and doesn't confirm a submission victory when they SEE A WRESTLER TAP OUT. Some CPU wrestlers glitch on one spot and try to hit springboard dives far away from the opponent that doesn't even hit.  - Randomly but temporarily deleting moves and clothing assets from the game files.- Universe mode doesn't remember your global settings for other modes and reverts to default settings. The mode also puts incorrect match rules like enabling DQs and count outs in a triple threat match when they're supposed to be off.Folks, just keep playing WWE 2K23. This year's instalment is another 2K20 where bugs and crashes plagues too much of the gameplay to actually enjoy. Final verdict: 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: This year's WWE2K game is out and it's actually better than its predecessor, which was already more than solid.Of course, it's not particularly difficult to get better, considering the low points the series has had in the past.The graphics are solid, but I wasn't expecting any great leaps from its predecessor.As usual, the big superstars like Cody Rhodes look a lot better and more realistic than their real-life counterparts.Hair was and still is a big problem with 2k.Short hair is still good to look at, but as soon as we look at the longer hair, it sometimes makes you feel funny in your stomach.The play of lights is all the better for it, whether it's the lights at the entrance or the audience pulling out their smartphones and taking pictures during a finisher, it looks great.The sound of the game is also still very good, here too you can't expect any major improvements on last year, but who does?If you want the best experience, turn off the commentators anyway and commentate on the action on the screen yourself!The music selection has some hits, but if I have to listen to "Genesis by Grimes" again, I'll forget myself!Universe mode and GM mode continue to work well.Here, too, the right ingredients had already been found in the last offshoot of the series and these were simply refined further.The selection of superstars is excellent, with 200 wrestlers available for you to play.Yes, it feels like there are 10 Undertakers, John Cena and the usual suspects. But you can still expect a good 140 unique wrestlers.In addition, you can still create your own superstars in CAW (Create a Wrestler), which has remained pretty much the same.You can also create your own arenas, shows, championships and videos.This year you also have the possibility to assign your own posters to your wrestlers which you have to upload to WWE2K beforehand.That's great, but tell me 2K... what about the possibility to create your own moves like back then? Create a Finisher was a hit!Forget the Showcase Mode.They've made it even more annoying than last year's.Instruction after instruction. There's no fun in the game.It's much more of a "movie" that you re-enact and as badly as possible.You have more action when you play games like Until Dawn, Life is Strange or something like that.But if you want to unlock the characters and arenas, there's no getting around it.I recommend: set the game to easy and give in to boredom for half an hour.Do this exactly 3-4 times and you should be through.MyFaction has been revised, there are now also extra "Persona" cards, which also unlock skins/characters for the Maingame.So you unlock Sheamus from 2009 right at the beginning.That was a very nice decision by 2K!That's exactly what we wanted!Let's see how it continues in the coming weeks and months with such "Persona" cards.Because I haven't found more than Sheamus in my playing time so far.Otherwise there are Proving Grounds, Weekly Towers, Ranked Battles and the so-called Faction Wars.The Faction Wars have been reworked.You now make your way to the boss units.This means that you start with a 1 vs. 1 match, for example, and once you have completed this you receive a reward.Then you can move one space further, but you have to decide whether to go up or down.There is a chest at the top and 3 question marks at the bottom?Let's go to the question marks... oh! I can choose whether one of my wrestlers is healed or whether I want 200 credits.You collect these credits during your run and can then use them to get cards in the Faction Wars store.There's a changing range of cards and, for example, you can also buy boss units that you've already defeated.Stars such as Stone Cold Steve Austin, John Cena, Undertaker, The Rock... and all in at least Ruby quality.It's a fun mode... at least in terms of the general idea!But the fights are still not exciting enough.The boss fights are again 4 vs. 4 matches which sometimes only last 1-2 minutes.2K have you ever played the mode yourself? It's just not really fun in the long run.Just having an idea is not enough, you have to implement it in a way that makes it fun!Oh, and it's even better when you lose your progress from a run because the game suddenly crashes... and believe me, that happens more often than you can or want to accept.Because the technical state of the game is modest, at least on the PC here on Steam.Sometimes the characters, even your own, simply freeze and you can't do anything, neither taunts nor moves... nothing.Then after 10-15 seconds the game realizes that something is wrong and it continues.The AI of the opponents this year sometimes seems more stupid to me than in previous years?I don't know, on Legendary it was fine from time to time, but it still tries to pin after every suplex... what's going on?And this problem that sometimes you can't do anything doesn't just happen 1-2 times every few hours, no.Assume 2-4 times per match depending on what kind of match it is.And today, on release day, Early Access players got the rude awakening that they would lose their score and access to the DLCs."If you click on yes, you will lose your data", I click on "no", the game decides otherwise and everything is gone.2K.. You want at least 60$, if not 100$ or 120$ dollars for a game that you bring out every year again and only adjust small things and give some characters a small visual update, which is already outdated in 2024 anyway.These are things that you can still accept as a hardcore fan (like all sports game fans, right NBA, NFL, FIFA people?).But the fact that your game has such technical problems is a disgrace!As I said, the game CAN be fun.But if you're really interested in buying a new WWE game, wait a few more weeks until some updates have come out.You don't want to spend your money on something that kills your progress AND/OR massively disrupts the flow of the game with bugs like "you can't move your character", "you want to punch? then please wait 10-15 seconds".Just wait before you buy WWE2K24.If you still have the predecessor, play it until then and prepare yourself for exciting storylines!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game after release so I can’t complain about my pre-launch data being wiped. Not a problem I experienced so my opinion isn’t colored in that light. Short answer: great game. Would recommend.Long answer: I haven’t played a wrestling game since the Wrestlemania line of games for the GameCube. Long time. So after getting back into wrestling I picked up 2k24(mainly because I’m a Cody mark). I’m absolutely loving the game. MyGM mode has held up most of my time but I’ve gotten a lot of gameplay time out of it.  The wrestlers look amazing, even being forced to use fsr1 it still looks good and high fidelity with minimal “sizzling”.  The in match game play is fun and quick to pick up, even after a tutorial run I feel like had I skipped it I would have picked it up easy.  HUGE roster, the thing that always made or broke a wrestling game in the past for me was the depth of the roster. Over 100 people last I read up on it and plenty of recognizable faces, and some wildcard pulls that I haven’t thought of in years (dude love, Jim the anvil etc) Still have a lot of game to play so haven’t even scratched the surface of it. Cons:I don’t like being limited to 60 frames, even intros are hard set to 30. The latter im settled with though. Lack of option settings. If I turn down the music to 0 ALL music is set to 0. So I can’t just set menu volume to 0 and have the wrestlers walk out to their music, no, it’s either suffer the soundtrack or have everyone walk out in silence. Pray they change that.Can’t run the game at native resolution. You’re forced to use an upscale,  fsr1 or linear upscaling. Just gives the feeling that pc was an afterthought. Glad the game doesn’t run bad on pc. But you can notice some roughness around the edges and sizzling.

I swear the people complaining about bugs, glitches, and performance have to be trying to play on decade old rigs they've never upgraded. This happens with every new Steam release of a next or modern gen game, the people giving bad reviews because they keep trying to play on potatoes and then have a ton of issues, but they'll always claim they have a top end PC. This practice seems to be more prevalent for wrestling fans..... every year we get the same complaints and every year I wonder how they keep having issues. I have a mid range PC. 10th gen i9, 32gb of DDR4, 2070, SSD. And I'm running this game with everything on max in ultra wide 4k without a single issue. Not one frame drop, not one bug, not one glitch. _childDocuments_.review: After playing this I cannot recommend this to anyone, and playing it has made the decision to never again purchase another WWE2K game a very clear choice. There is good and bad, but for this review I'll point out what I felt made this a never again decision.The Women's MyRise is just awful. Not only do you just do random matches that really make you feel like you're not on a quality journey focused on you and an actual wrestling career, but a part of those is them forcing you to be someone you may not, but in my case did not, want to be. A part of the journey and through most of the series they turn you into a person that you'd despise in real life, and honestly do everything to avoid. So most of the series I spent hating myself (my character), and the comment Regal makes at the very beginning is so appropriate when he says, ever feel like you're not in control of the thing you're supposed to be in control of? Congratulations creators! You succeeded. Not only was I not in control of 'who' my character was, there was no professional career path that I could actually respect, just a lot of random things that were very disconnected. I get the concept of feel free to experiment, but you should be able to pick a path that aligns with the type of wrestler (person) you want to be; Good, Neutral, or the Evil that you force on us, which I do everything in life to avoid people just like this.I don't want to give too much away, but then after all that chaos of crap you then finally give us the one thing we sought after, a title match. But then you just immediately end the game. At no point do I feel like this is a respectful journey, nor do I feel like this is a rise and a career that we get to enjoy, not just getting there, but also after we get there. In my opinion, you fail greatly in the Women's MyRise.I don't normally play the men's side but I did try it out a match or two just to see if there was a difference, and there really was. You start immediately in a more serious career thread. To be fair I don't really know how this plays out I just stopped and uninstalled the game.As much as I enjoy these types of silly games, I'm at the point where I expect more from them that you never deliver so I am done with your brand and giving you money for this kind of "turn me into a bully with absolutely no career, but a lot of randomness," crap.Another thing that I do not enjoy is the punching back and forth circles. I could never figure those out at all. Most of the time it was a real struggle to even do normal moves on opponents. Overall there are some things better than WWE2k22 but not a lot. And, the things they did right with WWE2K22, which I still felt were lacking in the career journey, they completely removed or changed for the worse. This is just my opinion of my experiences. I do wish these were better developed. But as they are, I cannot recommend them, nor continue to buy them.

_childDocuments_.review: Long version:I have to defend this game as it got bombed with negative reviews. Don't get scared by them. There was a bug at full release for all players that had early access, the game could not be played, but if you pressed a wrong button in the menu all your progess was lost, this is why there are so many negative reviews. Bug was fixed about 20 hours later.I have spent 1/3 of my life in the last 6 days on this game and I absolutely love it! WWE 2k23 was already the best WWE Wrestling game ever for me; I spent 100+ hours in that game. WWE 2k24 changed nothing of everything that was already good and just made other stuff better and listened to the community. New Match types (Casket, ambulance, special guest ref, gauntlet mainly new), Tag Team partners are allowed to enter just once to interrupt the cover until they get tagged in and out again. Showcase was very nice and entertaining, not too easy, not too complicated. I personally have not played MyFaction as it just looks like a "we need a FIFA pay-to-win mode in our game to earn more money" game mode. People say it got better than last year, still not interested for me. The other modes, MyGM, Universe, MyRise, are all great. The only thing I hate is sadly online. The servers are just very bad, and in almost every match, you get a random disconnect and the message, "all players have been replaced by AI, do you want to continue?" This problem existed in 2k23 already and sadly is still in the game. You don't need much to make online matches fun, but one fundamentally important thing is that you don't get random disconnects all the time. If they fix this, online is great as well, although it's all very simple (no mute option for your mic, etc.). Like online is just held on the simplest version of playing games online, but that is okay, as long as the servers are good and you don't get disconnects all the time. People who pay attention will notice the small details like Rey Mysterio going now into the second rope when running into the ropes and more small details like this which show how much love was put into this game. Loading times are so much quicker, almost non-existent, just when browsing in Community creations, there is still some time to load.Overall best WWE Game ever existed for me, 8/10, 9/10 if online would be working well, and there is always room for improvement I think like special guest referee not just for 1vs1, but also for multi-man matches e.g. or fixing minor bugs. _childDocuments_.review: I recently picked up WWE 2K24, and let me tell you, it’s a mixed bag. The graphics are decent, and the character models look great, but everything else feels like a step backward. The gameplay is clunky and often unresponsive, making matches frustrating instead of fun. The controls seem overly complicated for no reason, and I find myself button-mashing just to keep up.The MyCareer mode is another letdown. The storylines are predictable and lack the depth that fans like me crave. Plus, the progression system feels like a grind, and the rewards often aren't worth the effort. I expected a more engaging experience after the previous titles.And don’t get me started on the bugs! I've encountered glitches that have caused me to lose matches, which is beyond annoying. It seems like the developers rushed this one out without ironing out the kinks.Despite all this, I can’t help but keep playing! There’s just something addictive about creating my own wrestler and watching them rise through the ranks, even if the journey is frustrating. The nostalgia of WWE keeps pulling me back in, and I have to admit, I still enjoy the thrill of landing a finisher (when the game lets me). So, while WWE 2K24 has its fair share of problems, I’ll still be playing—just with a little more patience and a lot more hope for the next installment.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: After some slider tweaks, this is now my new favorite wrestling game, taking the spot from 2k19. The core in-ring gameplay is the best it has ever been in the hands of VC, and all the little changes add up to something much greater. It doesn't translate to video. Just play it.Long version:My first wrestling game memories are playing WWF Warzone and Attitude. Then onto the AKI N64 games, and further into the Smackdown series on the PSX. I've been playing the Smackdown games since the first entry, though I always prefered the N64 AKI titles. I took a brief hiatus from the series after SvR 2011 and picked it up again with 2k19 here on Steam.When I came back with 2k19 my mind was blown. No more grapples, no more silly spots jumping from the Smackdown fist only for them to get up two seconds later (I always hated that as a kid...spots don't mean anything if they don't do damage)--I loved it. My new favorite wrestling game. I kept up with the series through every entry afterwards. I bought the bomb that was 2k20, though I didn't get it until after most of the bugs had been fixed. Then they took a break, and hit us with 2k22. I liked 2k22. I didn't love it, but it was fun. The new style was a lot more arcadey, but that's what people like so I just tried to have fun with it. 2k23 was more of the same. I expected 2k24 to continue that trend, but I was very wrong.After watching tons of gameplay videos I thought I knew what I was getting into. I jacked up the difficulty to Legend like I always do, and went into a match. I got my butt handed to me. "Why does this feel so different? It didn't LOOK that different from the videos," I thought.The AI has been turned up a notch. They are more aggressive and slightly smarter. They actually use their finishers, and tend to do more moves and sequences that make sense as opposed to the previous titles. Is it perfect? No, but it's a lot better.Everything feels heavier, and just a hair slower--in a good way. I feel like I am actually beating the hell out of someone. There's weight to the movement, and a smoothness to the animation that wasn't there previously.I'm having banger after banger of a match, and it's amazing. I haven't felt this way about the in-ring gameplay of a wrestling game since I was a kid. It can be brutal, bloody, dramatic--all the best parts of great wrestling stories and matches.Thanks to the "tag debuff" limit on breaking up pins, I can finally play tag matches for the first time in several years. The selling is better. Matches feel like they have some drama and life to them. The blood is better. The animations are better. The irish whip system is better than it has ever been, with reversals as well as the ability to kind of "queue up" a rebound move early, meaning headbutting the CPU is a lot less frequent than it used to be. Everything about the in-ring experience is so much better, and actually so unexpected, that it sells the game alone for me personally. They put in serious work and polish, and I love it. This is the perfect mix between sim and arcade style. All I need now are rope break 5-counts, crawling to the ropes during submissions, and chain wrestling. But honestly I'm having so much fun, I don't even care about that stuff either.Showcase was meh. Some awkward moments and silent bits where there should be narration to fill the gap. Some of the objectives are very time consuming, let alone some of the longer cutscenes.I'm only a few hours into MyRise, but it seems more entertaining for me so far than last year. I'd call it an improvement.Haven't played Universe Mode or MyGM yet. I'm assuming not much has changed with the former, and I'm no expert on the latter.Technically speaking, the load times on my NVME are super quick. Quickest they've been in the series recently across the board from what I can tell. I had one crash to desktop when trying to delete a CC CAW, but that was before the first patch. No other issues on my end.I didn't cover everything the game has to offer, but for me the most important part is in the ring, and I think they've knocked it out of the park. It's a 9/10 for me, and my new favorite wrestling title.

_childDocuments_.review: I was one of the unfortunate souls who bought the $120 forty years of WrestleMania edition and then proceeded to have their data erased when the game came out. And I'll admit... that's gotta be the biggest problem I've had with this game, and they did resolve it. And, as you can see by my playtime, I'm rather pleased about thatIt has since been about a week since it happened, and I haven't had the game crash, let alone delete all my data. And beyond all of that, this really feels like an improvement over 2K23. Technically, things are mostly the same, but there's additional bits and bobs added for both variety and QoL reasons. On of my absolute favorites to mention would be the reversal prompt is now able to tell you if your input was too early or too late. On top of that, thanks to the WrestleMania Showcase mode, certain legends like Ricky Steamboat and Ravishing Rick Rude are back on the game's roster, as well as a huge array of alternate versions of stars from different eras that DO have different stats. Maybe they could've had one or two less versions of Cena, but they also have four or five different versions of Bray Wyatt, so it does feel like they were listening to the crowd as much as their wallets. OH! And let's not forget having the ability to have CASKET matches, AMBULANCE matches, GAUNTLET MATCHES OF VARIOUS TYPES! You can have special referee matches, No Holds Barred, falls count anywhere, an entire Royal Rumble. They've really made selecting a match feel like it's 2006 again with all the options, and you can make your own preset of rules to save and select to use.If I had to give one genuine worry about this game, it would actually be the MyRise story mode, specifically the male side in Undisputed. Don't get me wrong, I adore the idea of letting the player become the Universal Champion and prove themselves and all that... but that does bring up the question of what the hell the story would be for a 2K25? I'm sure someone will think of something good. Personally, I'd like it if we got a MyRise mode that took place in a past generation of wrestling with past legends as main points of the story, but that will only happen in my hallucinogenic dreams. Outside of that, though, the biggest takeaways from the game are common lag issues some folks have, most of which are fixable, and the aforementioned botchamania with the early access players' save data, which they have fixed and seemingly fixed well.I would absolutely say this game is worth market price if you loved 2K23, so long as you know how similar the games are to one another. However, I do think this one has enough different and interesting about it to warrant a separate purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I play this for the Universe Mode. It's one of the best wrestling sims out there.  This game and an excel spreadsheet and you can run an unending and ever-changing wrestling promotion and it's very fun to do. The game itself is excellent.  I have run into a few small release glitches, nothing game-breaking. The game play is, as always, a lot of fun.What I don't like is that several wrestlers are locked behind playing other modes of the game. The Showcase mode is interesting and I do like the history and videos. But having to complete a bunch of different tasks in a single match  play through (they DO reset) to unlock everything under one match, is just terrible game design.  Just as an example, in the triple threat match between Rousey, Flair, and Lynch, you have to complete 16 tasks to unlock everything. 16!  Furthest I have made it is 10; by that time everyone is completely drained of stamina and there's no point in going further because any cover is a win and if it's not you, you've lost everything. 10 out of 16. What did it unlock? The arena.  That's it.  It reeks of Pay To Win and that's just a bad look.   Beyond that, the game itself is solid and enjoyable. 7 to 8 out of 10 as is right now, ignoring the above issue. In the end, I just bought the Wrestlemania DLC and got all the added showcase wrestlers. So it all works out in the end, if you're not willing to try and grind impossible content.

_childDocuments_.review: Potentially the best WWE game there has ever been. Here are some reasons why, and please note that these views are strictly my own.:What a trip down memory lane, for someone who has watched WWE since 1999, I absolutely loved it. Reliving some of the most iconic moments at WM in a new way. The cutscenes/videos were great. There are things I wish were included that weren't, but understand not everything could be done for various reasons. Example, :Faction Wars has been reworked into a ladder system with choices. Stages with stage bosses, the 4v4 match and a journey before you reach it. The journey has different avenues that you chose and can lead you into various different match types, 1v1s, 2v2s, 3v3s and 4v4s. Each fights impact on the superstar remains onto the next. There are rewards throughout the ladder, with currency, sideplates, armour, health, and even the potential to swap a card from your team with one of the random superstars picked from your collection. If you beat a boss, their card unlocks in the marketplace where you get to spend your earned currency doing these ladders on rotated, permanent and unlocked boss cards.:New additions have been made to this ever growing gamemode that has become a fast favourite of mine, the way contracts are handled has been changed, there is trading between brands, scouting, new managers, and superstar data is presented in a new helpful way.Additionally:The day one DLC mismatch issue is fixed and has been from day one. It also didn't delete your saved data, it gave you a warning message saying there was a "mismatch" with a question "do you want to erase your data?". You then had to actively click yes. As a heads up, you can still manually delete your data from the settings menu under the "deletion utility" section.

_childDocuments_.review: The high spike of negative rewards is because a lot of people unfortunately lost their progression from early-access when the game officially came out.  Thankfully I was asleep then at work so I never experienced any data loss but it sucks for those who did.As for the game it is another continuation of the success story started from 2K22 - just like any annual sports franchise you need to make a decision if you are okay with very small but meaningful quality of life changes, the very high price for essentially the complete edition (the 40 year version is 160 Canadian + tax) or if its okay to wait for a sale or skip a year or two.  I dont like factoring price into the review as price is subjective and it can fluctuate over time.The game is an improvement over 2K23 if that helpsI do have a laundry list of ideas that I want to see in ASAP, things dating back to the PS2 days of 2K wrestling like meaningful decisions in matches depending on if you're a heel or face.  We used to be able to do cocky pins, holding onto rope break pins or submissions for example to get momentum up if we were a heel for example.  Right now for a very long time since the Xbox One / PS4 versions of 2K every match regardless if you're heel or face is the same outside of crowd reactions.  We need to bring this kind of interactivity and immersion back in matches.We also need a much better story/universe mode.  I really miss the days, again in the PS2 era, where you can walk around back stage and actually live the life of a WWE superstar.  I really do appreciate the MyRise mode but it really cant keep being a static conversation with borderline poor voice acting from the wrestlers.  The lack of immersion missing from these kinds of things to say the least is really disappointing.So yeah, overall its a good game - MyFaction is a joke and a waste of time.  I legit tried it for about an hour and I cannot stand anymore of it let alone ever would consider putting actual real money into it.  The grind is outrageous too - you need to play endless amount of matches just to make enough for a basic junk back that has garbage in it.I know this "review" is a mess but I just wanted to write something up to counter balance all the negative/mixed stuff even though my review wont even count towards it because I bought it from GMG - hopefully it can just get viability to prospective buyers

_childDocuments_.review: £104.99 I paid for this. I played 15 hours and felt so bored by the experience. At least 2 of those hours I had just been streaming the AI playing the Royal Rumble while I was AFK.The "story" is awfully bland. It's about 3% story (half of which are voiced by characters that don't even exist).Dragon Age can get Kate MulgrewMass Effect can get Seth GreenDeath Stranding can get Norman ReedusElder Scrolls can get Sean Bean and Patrick StewartFallout can get Liam Neeson And Cyber Punk can get Keanu ReevesBut WWE2k24, they get a few wrestlers to do voiceovers, but then create a bunch of persona's to fill the cast, making it an even more unauthentic experience.The MyFaction mode seems fun at first, then the enormity of the challenges seem absurd. _childDocuments_.review: Great game hampered by crappy shortsighted business decisions, console centric design, and bugs. The game itself, pretty solid. A ton of wrestlers included, fun gameplay, nice presentation. Looks sharp, plays well. But at least for me a huge draw, at least initially, was the CREATIVE aspect. I really enjoy getting creative, making a ton of custom wrestlers, and inserting my favorite film/tv/horror characters into the game, and checking out others wrestlers as well. It seemed like it gives you a ton of tools to do this, and does, but then SEVERELY hamstrings it needlessly.For instance, yeah, it would be a lot of fun to download other peoples cool creations. Only one problem... roughly %75 percent of them use some piece of gear, intro, or move that is either PAYWALL LOCKED behind DLC, or more frustratingly, locked simply because you HAVEN'T UNLOCKED IT IN GAME YET. So guess what? You can't download it, AT ALL. Even without those parts. Nope. What a POOR DECISIONWhich brings me to my 2nd point. You'd only be able to download a handful anyway because the game LIMITS YOU TO 100 COMMUNITY CREATIONS TOTAL. And that includes your own, so you hit that cap fast! Why is this even a thing on PC? We typically have WAY more space than on consoles. Why are you limiting us? This wouldn't be a problem if if was remotely open or modder friendly, because we could download as many as we wanted and save it wherever we wanted, but it isn't. Which brings me to my final issue...They are the complete opposite of mod friendly. They act like they are big supporters of "Community Creations" but then have the whole system closed off and MICROMANAGED into oblivion. Wanna use a custom texture? Cool. Well, just go to their website, sign up for a mandatory account, and only for the platform you own it on (gee, wouldn't want a PC player to be able to share with a ps5 player TOO easilly) then upload it to your account, THEN go to that account in game, upload it to your online account, then RE-UPLOAD it again to be able to share. Why all this convoluted nonsense? Let us save as many wrestlers to wherever we want, let us worry about space, and if I want a custom texture, face or piece of music let me drag a drop it to a friggin folder. YOU DO NOT NEED TO BE INVOLVED EVERY STEP OF THE WAY (with extra steps thrown in needlessly just for extra micrmanaging)Even their profanity filter is micromanaged to the point of being broken. I tried writing a description for one wrestler and said "... she joined a local wrestling league as soon as she could". Prohibited words used. I was like "huh?", then looked at what they asterisked out. Apparently their awesome filter read "aS Soon AS She could" and decided I was writing the word "ASS" twice. Yeah...awesome work 2kAnyway, keeping us from downloading creations because we haven't "unlocked" arbitrarily gated gear is ridiculous, as is your low limit on creations, and putting such a strangehold on the process of uploading and downloading is asinine and is why I refunded

It's literally called my rise, yet there is absolutely no character building, your either instantly world champion with mediocre story lines or even worse if you choose to play the other option which clearly sells you on starting in a indie business and you work your way up. NOPE! I think you play one or two matches and then your straight to WWE and for the vast majority of the story you do play as the character you've spent ages making.Oh and there's no option to loose a match, you know to build a rivalry or story line, nope just replay the match until you win.It's a shame that a lot of old features like creating your own Finisher from scratch haven't made a come back.The controls:Barely changed, really easy to pick up, takes a bit of learning to figure a few things out like lifting and dragging your opponent around.Graphics:Graphics are okay, nothing ground braking but its kind of what you expect.Would I recommend buying the game?No not really, not unless its on sale for dirt cheap. I certainly wont be buying 2k25 when it comes out, I'll probably wait until its that's on sale. Plus the weekly updates are killing me, 9gb this week for what? "Fixing Bugs" doesn't appear they very good at it if its this often. I think the updates are for the stupid Myfaction thing that no ones likes. Please for the love of god stop trying to ram this down our throats.

_childDocuments_.review: (A quick addendum to this: not everyone's save data got deleted, that was just what the initial impression everyone had. When the "DLC not detected" message came up, you could either continue into the game which WOULD DELETE YOUR SAVE or you could close the game. I didn't continue so my save data was not deleted. I'm leaving the original context for the review here so people can see it and also understand why the reactions are the way that they are, but I didn't have my save wiped and neither did anyone else who didn't hit "yes" at the DLC error screen.)I got the 40 Years of Wrestlemania edition and have playing since the initial Early Access launch with no problems, but now all of a sudden I can't boot the game up anymore because it no longer detects some of the DLC I had installed. Will not recommend until the problem is fixed, will update as needed.UPDATE: Not only has the problem not been solved, but it has gotten worse. All save data for Early Access players has been COMPLETELY WIPED. The game is also literally unplayable because the Nightmare Family DLC has been removed, and the game cannot detect it and will not open properly without detecting it. This means that IMMEDIATELY AT LAUNCH, THE ENTIRE EARLY ACCESS PLAYERBASE HAS HAD ALL OF THEIR SAVE DATA DELETED AND HAS BEEN COMPLETELY LOCKED OUT OF THE GAME.Don't buy this game. Do not give 2K a single cent of your money until every known issue has been resolved. Do not reward the "fire and forget" of yearly release company's for yet ANOTHER COMPLETELY DISASTROUS LAUNCH.Do yourself a favor, go play Smackdown vs. Raw instead. Plenty of places to find the game, go do that instead of even thinking of buying another defective 2K piece of garbage.UPDATE 2: So, they fixed the DLC issue, and for the most part the game seems fine again. However, it's worth noting this is 2K, and more bugs are bound to happen. For that reason alone as well as the blatant carelessness with the launch, I can't recommend the game at full price at least. However, it's a competent enough and fun wrestling game definitely worth keeping an eye on for when it goes on sale.UPDATE 3: The creator mode does nothing to protect creators. It mutes all commentary and entrance music, but you will still automatically be flagged for footage used in cutscenes/Showcase mode/MyRISE mode. Not even the full footage, if the platform you're streaming to detects even a few seconds of the live action cutscene, your stream will be flagged. Be warned.

name: Hot Lap Racing
detailed_description: Hot Lap Racing offers a thrilling ''simcade'' racing experience driven by an in-house physics engine built exclusively for the game. Explore the dynamic history of motorsport, spanning from GT to Formula 1, and engage in competitive races against friends or online opponents! Experience 15+ licensed and custom tracks, with more than 70 different layouts! Tracks include Zolder, Salzburgring, Kuwait Motor Town, Jarama, Laquais, Navarra, Oschersleben, Gingerman Raceway, and more! Choose from a diverse range of more than 50 cars from various motorsport classes and eras, such as Formula 1 cars from the 60s to modern endurance cars. Cars include the Peugeot 9X8, Alpine A110 GT4, Alfa Romeo 155 DTM, Brabham BT24, Formula Extreme (a car created by the community), Ligier JS P320, Renault R5 Turbo 3E and more… Challenge real champions from the history of motorsports! Many ways to play! Career: Embark on your journey as a young driver and strive to reach the pinnacle of motorsports. Master a wide range of iconic cars on legendary tracks and compete against some of the greatest drivers of all time. Hot Lap Mode: Race and improve your lap times with each attempt. Different motorsports categories in one game: Endurance, Single-Seater, GT, Electrical, or Production. Train yourself in each class and discover everything across eras and classes while driving! Your view matters: With camera angles set in the Rear, Far Rear, Hood, Bumper, and Cockpit, you can choose your way to race! Online & Offline Multiplayer: Race to be the first to cross the finish line! Play up to 4 friends locally, or up to 12 online!

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've played far enough to do one Championship at Tier 4, I feel I've seen enough to give a more actual kind of review of sorts. And unfortunately, I have a lot more bad news than I would have hoped.So from the original rundown, I mention the lack of Controller Vibration and Calibration being big problems. And these turn out to be pretty important given that the game's handling feels very strange. On the racing scale, I would like to say it feels much more Arcade than Sim, but at the same time there are cars that will just suddenly snap into a spin which doesn't feel arcade at all. In particular, the V10 F1 car in T4 has a massive likelihood to trip over any kerb you look at even slightly funny.But that's not even the biggest problem this game has. It's the AI. If you thought Forza 8's launch AI was bad for punting you about, it's *nothing* compared to this. The AI effectively drives like you don't exist (or anyone else on track for that matter), and just surviving a push through the field from P12 to P1 is incredibly difficult. Oftentimes, you'll go into a corner at optimum pace only for an AI to absolutely smash into your side and send you completely outside track limits or, just as likely, into a race-ending spin.This is made worse by the Career's scoring system. It's a letter-based grade that goes up to S-rank, with a forced cap of A+ if you have the Racing Line enabled. But the way the points system is set up is that you lose points for every off-track excursion you make, regardless of if it was your fault at all (as well as penalties for crashing significantly into another car, for cheating and for skipping the race altogether). And if you thought about using the Reset to Track button to recover from a mistake, it takes so long to actually Reset the car that there's no point in ever using it.The only surefire way to max the odds of you being able to get the top rank, you basically either have to Qualify for every race you do and try to land Pole, or figure out how to survive Lap 1 without losing too much time to the race leaders. And another huge problem in this regard is the complete lack of Restart option in the Pause Menu. If you screw up a race, you have to Quit to the Main Menu and reload in. And doing this means you'll have to do Qualifying all over again if you want to start from somewhere other than the back.This all culminated in the last race with the V10s, in the not-Monaco street track called Riviera, being what can only be described as an utter calamity. Attempting to do anything with that race without Qualifying on Pole is a lost cause. The AI is so incapable of driving in a pack that it is highly likely that after Turn 1, you will either be greeted with cars literally being sent into the air, or the road to be blocked by someone having been sent spinning. And even if you do get past some of them, you're just as likely to then get punted from behind before you escape the narrow starting sector onto the runway strip. And even if you survive all that, you have to avoid hitting any of the numerous kerbs throughout the track or you'll also find yourself quickly facing the wrong way.As it currently stands, I cannot recommend anyone to pick this game up in its launch spec. Which is gravely unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: Offensively inoffensive.It's a cute little game, has an interesting track and car list, it's clearly made for Switch looking at the UI and asset quality, etc, etc... But those aren't the problem.The driving is just not fun, they clearly went for an arcade driving style but it's overbearingly "arcade". You can just throw the cars into the turns without braking or throttle control, the steering is extremely slow and unresponsive (and obviously can't do anything about it), the chase camera is insanely floaty and motion sickness inducing (another thing that you can't do anything about)... It's just not a pleasant experience.I like arcade racing games, but it's still possible to provide a driving experience that isn't overbearing for the masses and still makes sense to racing game fans. NFS, GRID, DiRT, GTA, and other games have done this in the past, you don't need to have this overly wacky driving style that just feels completely disconnected from my inputs.If you like the modern clunky arcade racers we have these days, you may like this. If you're more of a fan of the older arcade handling styles of the early and mid 2000s, you probably will find this too janky.

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with all of the other mixed/negative reviews about the pricing of the game. It definitely feels overpriced in comparison to the content in the game. However if this game was on a sale I would highly reccomend it to anyone looking to pick up a new couch racer that you can play locally with your friends as the genre as a whole seems to be on a decline which is sad to see. I spent a few hours with 3 other friends trying out the local multiplayer mode and we had a great time. The car and track selection is varied however there are a ton of French tracks (not a complaint, just pointing it out) We raced everything from the electric cars to the open wheelers and overall it was a great experience. A small complaint would be the AI feel like they are blind when it comes to racing next to you or they completely move out of the way like they're under blue flags. There was still some moments of proper racing and maybe I just needed to up the difficulty to max as the medium difficulty felt too weak to me and my friends. When speaking about the solo mode, please please please allow me to up the difficulty as the start of the game has just been a long winded, boring, sunday drive. I understand having a dynamic difficulty but please allow us to change this to have a challenge from the start. Otherwise its a pretty standard, championship based campaign mode you would find in a multitude of other racing games, Grid legends comes to mind when comparing the campaigns.  The cars as a whole feel good, each vehicle feels unique and comes with its own pros and cons. The physics are basic, but I feel that it helps reach a wider variety of players from different skill levels. you can really throw the car around and brake really late. Overall - a solid game that would definitley be worth adding to your library, maybe wait for a sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: Yea, Hot Lap Racing isn’t good…-Handling feels overall good. When turning off traction control, you can get some noticeable oversteer and sliding. It feels like GRID Legends, but if it was gripper. Arcady, but decently fun.-Great selection of cars and tracks. The fact that this game has some licensed cars & tracks is pretty insane for being a smaller dev team / publisher.-Online multiplayer and 4 player splitscreen is great to see.-The menu artstyle and design is pretty nice.-Graphically, this is extremely ugly looking. I understand this was made for Switch in mind, but the fact that this game *actually* looks worse than PS2 games at ultra settings is an achievement. Like, instead of some going for some cool stylization that might have helped with performance on the Switch, we get realism puke. Literally the leaves on the trees are badly compressed pictures!-The third person camera is terrible. It's way too stiff, which makes the turning feel awkward. It's also stiff at higher speeds as well, with no camera shake or FOV increase. This means the sense of speed is really bad. I guess they wanted to go with the third person cameras seen in sim/simcades, but considering this is an arcade track racer (despite their ‘simcade’ claims), the camera should be more dynamic.-Sound design is just not there. It's incredibly basic, with things like crash or skid sounds either being really low or completely non-existent.-The AI kinda sucks (I’m playing on medium). When they are off by themselves, they drive fine. However, if they are in a pack, they crash into each other, drive off the track, and crash into stuff. The first few minutes of a race are an absolute disaster.-No damage model. Like, your car doesn’t even get scratches.-There is no MPH option. Rather minor, but pretty annoying nonetheless.While the dev team seems passionate about motorsports, their game is just really lackluster. I  be able to barely recommend Hot Lap Racing if it was cheaper, but for $30? Absolutely no way. This is one you should avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: As of today i cant recommend the game, its too expensive for a game that needed more polish before launch:-AI is terrible, brakes too early, slow some times and it has truck like physics, your cant affect them while they can move you like you were 10000kg lighter, wich usually ends up in you spinning around and losing the race or having to come back from last(so short races are ruined).-Automatic transmission is terribly slow because upshifts work alright while downshifts dont, so youll be at a great disadvantage entering corners because you dont have engine braking(tried doing some test but from the steam deck is kind of hard to get right, so take this with a grain of salt).-Car handling is not realistic not arcade, more like, kinda unconfortable but not super bad.-Translation to spanish could be better.-Steam Deck performance could be improved.But not everything is bad, the game has lots of potential and i think most of the problems could be "easily" fixed in a few patches(will update acordingly):-Music is great-Jarama Circuit <3-Lots of different cars to choose-Fun game "story mode"In cases like this i would refund the game, but i think that a few patches and some loves from de devs to get the problems fixed and find the perfect balance between "sim" and "cade" would make this game a really fun one to play. So if you are the dev reading it, keep it up! i know theres real potential in your game, just take the feedback from the reviews.As some suggestions for more content i would love to see:-Karts(got this idea while trying to race formulas on drift track).-New tracks(not necesary to be licensed).-More driver(and maybe car) personalization.-Old junk cars(everyone likes old bmw or civics hehe)Anyway those are my suggestions and might not fit in your creative vision of the game(wich isnt bad for me).I wish soon i can update this to a recommended one :)

_childDocuments_.review: Good-Driving school, while not amazing, is something that vast majority of games do not have;-Career mode*General structure is rather typical, however there is an option to switch between different disciplines at any point.*There's also a licensing system, which supposed to control player's progression throughout the career depending on his racing performance and behavioral discipline;*In addition, there is an underlying objective - collecting/winning parts for a car which will be used in final races;-Content is interesting, plenty of obscure tracks and cars.Bad-AI is really bad at this stage. Hard to believe it has passed gameplay testing;-The price is quite steep for what the game actually is/or the state it is in;-Option to restart career races is missing, which is likely by design, and possibly would not even be a problem if AI would not be this bad;-No day/night cycle or weather changes. Other-Car handling resemble GRID's - while I'd like more sim like behavior, it is a matter of preference.

When Sonic the Hedgehog becomes the game's victim, everyone is off to get to the bottom of things. However, something feels a bit off - is this really an innocent game or is something more sinister afoot? Join the colorful cast of the Sonic the Hedgehog series in an exciting new adventure! New & familiar faces Interrogate some of your favorite characters as you figure out what happened to Sonic. Play as a new character who is starting their first day working on the Mirage Express, and meet the kind Conductor who is finally retiring from his long run with the train! All aboard! Immerse yourself in the sights and sounds of the Mirage Express, featuring fully hand-drawn landscapes and characters. Canon or Headcanon? You know what they say: everything is canon*. *This is not a Sonic Team title, but we strongly believe in the power of headcanon!

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming, easy going and... oddly touching game that I feel like Sonic really needed at this time. Seeing these characters not on a big, world-saving adventure for once but just hanging out and enjoying a good party was so cool to me, and it reminded me why I love them so much.I'm not quite experienced with these visual novel mystery games, so I don't know if the gameplay did anything new or interesting, but the idea of keeping it a secret from the player whether it's *actually* a game or not was really clever, and it kept me intrigued all the way through.The presentation of this game is *godly*, everything looks so colorful, the character portraits' coloring going outside of their outlines made it have a hand painted feel to it, that just looks so good with these brightly colored vibeo game characters. I really hope they can get the artists for this game for future projects too, they deserve a massive award honestlyI was gonna detail how good the character writing was, how the added fan service was mostly in backgrounds so it wasn't potentially distracting to someone unfamiliar with those older titles, and just how suprisingly *great* and varied the music was, but this game is free and only takes 2 hours to complete, so I rather save that text space and just tell everyone who's reading this to just: PLAY IT!10/10, the most fun sonic experience in a long, long time
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming and well-put together game (honestly I would've paid for it - but I could see the short 2 hr runtime being an issue for some), the art is beautiful, the characters are well-written (even Shadow!), the gameplay segments work fantastically to break stuff up (and the accessibility settings!!), and I loved following this story through to the end. God bless SEGA, somehow making a silly April Fools joke into a geniunely good little visual novel.

_childDocuments_.review: This is so much better than it has any right to be. Think  and  with a special zone thrown in there.The plot feels like it could be a comic mini-series. The humor is leagues better than what we were getting pre-. The art looks like it belongs in a graphic novel. The music sounds like it's (purposely) straight out of a visual novel made in RPG Maker. There are callbacks everywhere, and characters (like in ) actually act like themselves. A ton of love was put into this. Now I want a spinoff series.Also, Knuckles has his hat.Who'd-a thunk one of the best  games in recent years would be an April Fools' Day visual novel?
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: That was extremely good for a free mystery visual novel with 1 minigame. The minigame was used extremely well, although I had some gripes with it personally. For a lane-switching-based game, I really wish the square Sonic was on was highlighted (the shadow wasn't good enough for me to tell where I was, especially when it shrunk while jumping). Or, if not highlighting the squares, I wish it was a proper lane-switching game, because I got really sick of losing rings because I was 1 pixel too far into the wrong lane when I thought I was in the correct one. There also seemed to be a speed increase proportionate to amount of rings gotten, which I didn't notice until the end of the game after Sonic pointed it out. I couldn't tell the speed was increasing until I realized everything was really blurry, so I kept making bad jumps because I didn't realize the pacing of the jumps was changing. Kind of reminds me of playing Robot Unicorn Attack, way back in the day, except way less obvious that things were speeding up, and the depth perception in an isometric view is pretty difficult to judge.But, I did everything without the assist mode and I felt comforted knowing I could use the assist options to make the minigame more bearable at any time - I just couldn't let go of my pride, personally, so I didn't use it. Given the gripes I have with the minigame's design, having options like that is incredibly valuable, especially since let's be honest - we're all here to solve a murder of a famous IP character!The art was beautiful, and the writing was so fun. The game went on a lot longer than I expected, so I had to take a break after the first 5 hours, but I was actually glad the rest of the game had a different pacing than the first half (yet kind of disappointed at the same time, I wanted to keep playing - but it IS a free April Fool's day game after all). I loved all the little memey jokes I could participate in. Although, sad days for any players named Amy in the real world - you're gonna have to pick a different name for your character!Speaking of the player character, I'm gonna be losing sleep at night trying to figure out what they are... A fox? A dog? A ferret? A hyena? The world may never know...
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is a fun little visual novel game in the Sonic universe (anything is canon) and it shows a new style of game that I personally hope they bring back more. The characters were fun and the story was engaging, the references were surefire hits for a longtime fan like myself but are easy enough for others to see quickly if they've played a few Sonic games. The THINK minigame was fun and provided challenge and the story wraps up nicely as a fun special presentation for the Sonic universe. I would recommend this to any Sonic fan looking for a quick to pick up adventure with Sonic and his pals.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely horrible runner in isometry. Animated character sprite does not represent your hitbox, your shadow does. Blue goblin also can't change movement direction fast enough, but rings in diagonal formation make it seem as if you could get them all. It also has visual novel part which is very linear. You can't lose or make bad lasting decisions, you always get endless chances. Pixel hunting for interactable items is peak gameplay here.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing experience that I can't recommend enough! It's free, so you don't lose anything but time by trying it. The writing is a delight, and it's just fun to see these characters again. It feels like many of the characters in this game (Espio and Vector, and Blaze come to mind in particular) haven't had prominent roles in a sonic game in a really long time. I hope the success of this game encourages SEGA to do more with these characters. Even when the games aren't perfect, Sonic's strongest aspect is its characters, and this game encapsulates that perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I'm kinda speechless. The writing and story and well-paced and well-written (although I kinda skimmed through some of it towards the end, but that's probably because I was streaming the game on Twitch for way too long and I was hangry), I love the platforming sections and how they make a visual novel feel like an actual Sonic game (especially towards the end when they get more difficult), the difficulty curve is nice and I love how satisfying putting all the pieces of the mystery together is. They did not need to go THIS hard for a Sonic game on April Fool's day and I seriously hope they don't pull a Nintendo and take this game off Steam like a week later. This game deserves to be played and preserved as an odd little piece in Sonic's history
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: A game clearly made by people who adore the character cast of Sonic the Hedgehog, no over reliance on the most recent caricatures each character's personality usually ends up being. If you're looking to see your favorite characters just goofing around, this quick pick up is totally worth your time. I'd even say the final THINK segment was challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm lost for words.So much to say, but can't give spoilers.This game is amazing, and one of my favorite Sonic (themed) games ever.Sure, it's not a traditional Sonic game in any sense, but the game really shines by it's writing, and character exploration. _childDocuments_.review: This game is worth it only for Sonic fans.The story and characters weren't interesting and the dialogues were a slog.It's a story that works for a kindergartener and an adult, but will please neither, because it's too much reading for a kid and not enough complexity for someone above the age of 13.I guess if you are a Sonic fan and know the characters, then you will love it, but for me there was nothing that would grab my attention.The action stages have a terrible motion blur to them and after about an hour started to make me sick (both physically and mentally honestly).It wasn't that bad most of the game, but at the final stage my head started to hurt.I enjoyed the art direction and of course it's nice that it's free, but the only thing that kept me going was the fact that everyone kept saying "Let's finish this!" for half the playtime, and I thought I would only have to play another 10 minutes...When I saw the trailer, I thought it would be full of self-referential/4th wall breaking humour and a bit of a more mature tone to it, but I just got a kid's game about Sonic.

_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Plenty of companies do meme premises for April Fools, but this is one of the few that is an honest delight. The idea of a Sonic VN is absurd, but here it's done as a showcase for characterization and fan service, ending with a surprising amount of pathos for both the story and the fans who like these characters. Add that with some platforming that gets a bit tricky and not sadistic, and you've got a fun package.The main issue is the actual mystery, being pretty straightforward. But even that flaw is overshadowed by the game's love for the source material, even referencing Sonic Unleashed of all things. If you love Sonic's cast, this game does too and that's more than can be said for most Sonic titles.  This is a game made with love and I would honestly pay for another Sonic game in this format.
