_childDocuments_.review: "The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog" is very enjoyable and even if played purely as a mystery doesn't feel cheap. It follows the standard rules of mystery in that enough information is given you can come to logical conclusions, and while it's definitely more fun if you have a history with the series Tails ends up giving you enough context you don't feel left out if you don't. The fact you can modify the "Think" minigame for whatever difficulty level you choose is a nice inclusion also as having played it with 0 changes I can safely say some people will find it trying to nab enough rings while also time movement just right. I would recommend it, as for the price of free it goes above and beyond to the point it highlights how charming the Sonic cast really is when they're given the opportunity.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic the Hedgehog is dead for real and I miss him every day. I ship the conductor and the train and believe that his wife was also a bird powering a robot. If you have any questions about the lore it is answered here, mostly about the nation of Spagonia. As a plus, you get to see half a portrait of Professor Pickle, and the Gamer Hat from Sonic Forces.The ability to name your sonic is also nice, and adds a sense of depth and realism to this hyperrealistic game. In fact, at points my eyes went crossed because of how mind boggling the effects were in the thinking games. Truly a puzzler for the ages. I do wish that our character sonic did not have a physical body, for it is annoying and has no pants. Only the goodest sonics have pants, for some reason. I did enjoy the twists, even though I saw them coming for I am a hyperintelligent hedgehog, myself. Oh that reminds me, Silver isn't in this or even mentioned, which saddens me greatly.Anyway, This game took about two hours, which is way too long for a sonic game, because you are meant to go fast. I wish the ingame settings let you turn up the speed to more. Also also, I expected to win back my money that I lost in the slot machines. Honestly a bit of a soft lock as you need currency to get the good ending, and money to procure goods and services in the supermarket levels. But at least thanks to my hyperintelligence, as mentioned beforehand, I was (and still am) smart enough to overcome this bit of mechanical coding tomfoolery, and bested this meager program with my brain and also large muscles. In the end, I won. Sonic and the others somehow survived and had a nice time even though Sonic did in fact die. PRO-TIP: If you do manage to beat this slow game, do NOT pick the spaceship ending, because everyone in this universe has already been to space. They even had an entire game about several planets being a combined theme park. Dr Ivo "Eggman" Robotnik is absolutely smart enough to run legitimate business ventures, which is a major plot hole. I enjoyed the side story in the comic where he operated as a repairman with a loving daughter and hilltop community.Overall, this product FAILS to mention the previous space encounters run by Sonic and etc., and that is a LARGE failure in my eyes, as a train running through space has vastly more potential for higher stakes than a measly mobius-bound one. Brings the whole thing down an entire letter grade for me, could have easily be fixed by replacing Amy Rose with Shade the Echidna, the superior love interest for Sonic and Knuckles and Shadow to combat one another over. Once and for all, the characterization was very in-tune, except for Eggman's lack of candor when it came to attempting to vanquish his belovedly hated enemy, Sonic and co. as he never has EVER missed the chance, especially when he drove the large robot beetle in Africa when Sonic was a werewolf, or should I say Hogwolf, which is the *correct* syntax of what Sonic became in that title. But I digress, this game is everything a Sonic the Hedgehog visual novel has always wanted to be: Charming (Like the bee, haha, who disappointingly did not get a major cameo in this, but did, in fact, likely receive a tease for an upcoming musical title game, which I am very much looking foreward to with baited breath. as are my large fanbase.), Attractive, delightful, pleasing, likeable, enjoyable, very in-character (except for Sonic losing, which he is legally NOT ALLOWED to do, please patch in the proper method of storytelling which omits any mentions of loss on everyone's favorite blueman, as is the morally correct thing to do.) as well as advertising new menu options for the Sonic redditbase, which in my opinion as a chef are sorely needed in this modern day and age.I'm not exactly sure how to rate this game in the end, as I never actually completed it, in that I feel empty and hollow when I look back on this experience. Perhaps I missed a slot machine payout or a trash can reward. Maybe Sonic was replaced by a perfected duplicate who you could have identified at the beginning, saving you much time. This seems likely in retrospect, but I do not simply have the time to go back and investigate (ha ha do you get it because it is a mystery and investigators are involved in mysteries.).Overall, nice game, lacking in combat mechanics, and could have been released exclusively on Nintendo Switch and Wii U or 3DS. Quite enthralling and betwisting, and motivational in the darkest aspect that Sonic and friend have ever accomplished. The voice acting was good, but I couldn't find the option to turn it up and my speakers are very poor, so I could only catch small glimpses of it through my Let's Plays of Sonic & The Black Night on my phone in my lap. Which is also an amazing game, would highly recommend, 100/100%.Final Score: 80%/100, enjoyable and zealous. Please enjoy it, but beware the long runtime may make you forsake your refund. I received this title for free due to my existing connections and reputations. Please understand that even though I WAS sponsored that I did NOT allow it to affect my reviewing prowess.Have a nice day, and blast off at Sonic the Hedgehog Speeds.-Signing off, theCheese0fd00m

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so somehow this year managed to have not one, but TWO sudden really cool games just totally shadow-dropped. I'm really surprised this is free, considering how greedy Sega was with the Legacy Collection, lol. It's certainly better off as free though, since it's just a short visual novel. I had a great time with it though. All the characterizations are on-point. The player character is a bit annoying at times, and it definitely gets a bit corny, but overall the writing was totally solid. I was also surprised how often the humor landed well. The short sections of more "traditional" gameplay are also surprisingly pretty challenging at times, but not frustratingly so at all. If you're a Sonic fan then this is totally worth the time. Really awesome li'l surprise release here. Also the art and music is pretty great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a verily thrilling side journey in the world of Sonic the Hedgehog. The designs and artwork were eye-candy, the music was truly a delight to listen to, and the jokes and dialogue were excellent. The only gripe I have about this game, without spoiling it, was the slight repetitiveness of the DreamGear mechanic. I cannot comment on the DreamGear sequence difficulties, as I refused to indulge in Assist Mode out of dignity. Nonetheless, a charming and memorable adventure without all the big stakes and flashy action.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: "The Murder of..." is a delightful surprise of a visual novel, surpassing all expectations for an April Fools freebie. This gem of a game deftly weaves players into the murder mystery alongside a colorful cast of characters, including Espio and Shadow, who are given a chance to shine with some fun writing. The quality of writing, art direction, and gameplay segments are top-notch, making it hard to believe this game is free. While it may not offer traditional Sonic gameplay, it stays true to the characters' personalities and history. SEGA clearly knows these characters inside and out, and that's what keeps Sonic fans coming back for more. For fans of Danganronpa, this game has clear inspirations, making it the perfect evening entertainment for anyone who loves a creatively written dinner party. Don't miss out on this captivating experience!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This was a charming little experience, and even coming from someone who never plays VN-type games, it was absolutely worth the hour or two it takes. They had no reason to go so far for an April Fools' joke, but I'm really happy they did.If you haven't played it and you like Sonic, do yourself a favour. Take a seat, make a drink or something, and give it a chance. If you love the characters, you'll love this little story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly charming 2 hour visual novel, and probably one of the best Sonic games to date. I loved the characters just as much here as I did whenever they showed up in past Sonic media. The story was pretty engaging with plenty of twists and turns expected of the mystery genre. And the small amounts of gameplay they put in fit perfectly with the story aspects and didn't feel bad at all  In short, a delightful game to play whether you're a fan of Sonic or not, and was worth the playthrough. I would love if Sega published more unique games like this
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of point-and-click adventure games, as well as murder mysteries, this was an absolute joy. The amount of effort and love poured into this project is very radiant! _childDocuments_.review: SPOILER ALERT! If you have not completed the game, I don't recommend reading this review. With that out of the way...---For a silly little April Fools' joke, this game is surprisingly deep and very fun. It's astonishing they took the time and effort to make this! It's really cool being able to see all the different rooms and interrogate with everyone, you really get to see their personalities shine, like how Espio tries to act all calm while answering, or Shadow gives you the stink eye a lot, or the Chao Egg heist with Rouge and Blaze. The interactions with the train are very enjoyable. I found it funny how disappointed my character was when the trash bins didn't have any clues lol. As for the Dream Gear and endgame stages, they remind me a lot of the Genesis games, which, basically every Sonic game does, but it's nice to see anyways. The ones at the end are also surprisingly challenging, with the abundance of robot arms and the train always shooting bullets at you. It was very satisfying to complete this! I was definitely expecting this to be on the short side, and it was, but considering that, they managed to cram a whole lot of story into this (though, it is a visual novel, so they kinda have to.) Also the scene with Eggman at the end had me in laughing tears, "let's go dad" XD... All in all this was a very great game and I would recommend.

And without those frustrations, this was a lovely game otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a charming experience, and it's very obvious there was a lot of passion put into this little project, despite the fact that his was an April Fools project. The plot isn't anything "too" ambitious, but it is much more than I was expecting it to be. The plot is probably fairly predictable, and there are some occasional silly "cringe" jokes, but they aren't really a problem at all. The puzzles are fairly basic, but they are fine and get the job done. You occasionally have to play these mini games where you have to dodge obstacles whilst collecting rings to solve a puzzle (a similar thing is done in Danganronpa). These can actually be pretty challenging. took me several tries on the last few stages.This games biggest strength is definitely the characters writing/characterization. These characters probably have not been represented this well since Sonic Battle. Their personalities really gave me early 00's vibes. It was honestly pretty strange to see them written like this after years and years of whatever god awful characterization they've been given in the main games. The lack of voice acting probably helped a lot though. I would love to see some more future games like this. From what I understand, this game was created by a group of fans. Seeing as the game is actually... "good", that doesn't surprise me.8.5/10 better than Frontiers.

_childDocuments_.review: I know my reviews for games can be long and intricate...but F*ck man, this game is too cute and charming.For Free game, The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog has a lot of effort put into it for being such a simple April Fools Point & Click game. With Sonic and the Gang celebrating Amy's Birthday, she wants to throw a Murder Mystery Party on this train she rented, but things turn for the worst where Sonic the hedgehog did get murdered...or did he?What can I say the writing is charming, the characterization of the Characters and the roles they play in this mystery party is cute, there's just really nothing to complain about...although if I did have one thing against this game is that the murderer is the same person, I would've like it if there were multiple playthroughs were a different character did the deed and you solve it with real logic and deductive reasoning, but this game is made for young audiences so I understand why they didn't.Still, Free and a fun time for a few hours. These fun little side games are what I always wanted from Sega while we wait for the next mainline Sonic games.More of this, please!

_childDocuments_.review: While  is an enjoyable enough hour or so, this is a case of the concept for a game being better than the actual game. It seems like an -alike featuring Sonic characters, but, in practice, it's much simpler than that; there are comparatively few player choices, and most of them are "but thou must" affairs where it just cycles briefly around until you pick the correct prompt, with no possible branching and no consequences for making an incorrect choice. Tails and the player proceed in a straight line through the train, always completely exploring one room before moving to the next, and interviewing all the characters consecutively.Whereas  gives the player a mountain of evidence and creates its challenge by expecting you to present the correct pieces at the correct times, here there is very little evidence, no control of when to present it, and no penalty for presenting the wrong piece. Instead, the challenge comes from the "think" levels, which play out as isometric platform stages reminiscent of a simplified  with Sonic running automatically and the player guiding him left and right to collect rings and jump over obstacles and pits. These stages are reasonably fun for what they are, though they seem an odd core mechanic for a visual novel; the options contain a large number of difficulty modifiers, so they can be reduced all the way down to impossible-to-lose if needed, though they are the *only* element of challenge in the entire game.The art is fantastic, capturing a good sense of Sonic the Hedgehog as costume drama, though it is entirely static; the only animation in the game is in the "think" stages. The music is perfectly acceptable, and the script, while it does a good job of being fun and capturing the sonic spirit, is badly in need of another editing pass. There is a vast infestation of "singular they" illiteracy, often in places where it makes absolutely no sense, and not even consistently -- there are a few (correct) instances of "he" that apparently slipped by the political correctors. There are also a number of other flaws and typos, including the use of apostrophes to form plural nouns, that suggest that more attention was paid to political shibboleths than to the English language.Overall,  is definitely worth a play for anybody who is amused by Sonic and likes visual novels. It's cute and fun, and it doesn't cost anything. It does leave me with an odd desire for a proper, full-fat Sonic-themed  knockoff, though, which is something I never expected to want.

_childDocuments_.review: TOP 10 HOTTEST SONIC CHARACTERSSonic the Hedgehog. One of the greatest and most attractive characters ever thought up. He can run at sound speed, take out enemies in a flash, and best of all, he's blue colored and knows how to handle the females. Speaking of females, the Sonic universe might also be classified as "Hot Chick Heaven" because there's such a mess of very beautiful and tough women that it will make you love the franchise even more! And since Valentine's Day is around the corner, I've been inspired to make a top 10 list of the most beautiful female Sonic characters. Grab yourself a snack and a glass of orange juice, and try not to reach through the screen because HERE WE GO!10: Try this question on for size. Who chases and hugs Sonic all the time and wields a powerful hammer? Why it's Amy Rose of course! Though more of a cutie than a hottie, you can't deny the fact that she's still attractive. Two things that make her attractive are the fact that she wears a dress, and when have you ever seen 3 big, very smooth arcs of hair sticking out of a person's forehead? I haven't! So once again, Amy Rose is lovely; that is until she goes berserk and starts hitting stuff with her hammer.Who's at number 9? It's this alien plant girl from a distant planet. Cosmo, from Sonic X. She arrived on the character's planet to deliver a message saying that the galaxy was under attack by a force called the Metarex. She doesn't do much except tell people to stop fighting and focus on the real matter at hand. The real reason she lands at the #9 is that she becomes Miles "Tails" Prower's sweetheart, something Tails needed for a long while.Numero Ocho. Cream the Rabbit's mother, Vanilla. She's attractive and the size of an average human mother. What really surprises me about her is that the leader of Team Chaotix, Vector the Crocodile, falls in love with her. Kinda silly, don't you think? She's another character that doesn't do much, but in a season 3 episode of Sonic X, she helps Chris Thorndyke get into space to fight the Metarex along with Sonic and friends.What number's next? Seven, of course. Wave the Swallow from Sonic Riders. People always root for the good guys, but sometimes, the bad guys steal the show. Her mechanical IQ is equal to Tails. She also happens to be the smartest member of the Babylon Rogues. I wonder why she isn't the leader. Like Jet the Hawk and Storm the Albatross, her specialty is riding the air-boards called "Extreme Gear". With two very long and smooth feathers extending from her head to her calves and droopy eyes, Wave will rock your socks. If only we could see her take wing.Numero Six. Tikal the Echidna from Sonic Adventure 1. Named after an ancient Mayan city of the same name, Tikal is the daughter of Chief Pachacamac. She's yet another character that hardly does a thing except beg her father to stop being so greedy. She also traps herself inside the Master Emerald so that the water god Chaos doesn't reign terror upon the land. When you're the daughter of a person in the highest power, you need to look your best and Tikal delivers perfectly. That's why she's #6.Number #1, #2, #3, #4, #5! Ah-Ah-Ahhh! Mina Mongoose from the Sonic Archie comics. How could you go wrong with a girl that looks like this? She can run nearly as fast as Sonic and she went from being a Freedom Fighter to being a popstar singer. Next to Princess Sally she looks more humanoid than the other characters. Who could top someone who has long mauve hair?This female standing at number 4: Blaze the Cat. One word: Pyrokinesis. How would you like to have that superpower? I mean Blaze could play around in the Himalayas for hours and she would be perfectly fine! Also, 45 degree ponytail makes her look like a Native American. I really like the fact that her love interest is the telekinetic hedgehog Silver. The combination of mind-moving and fire superpowers make these two a reliable couple. But what really lands Blaze in the #4 spot is that her attitudes apparently more different from the other females.Next up is #3. What's better than having a female with cascading quills? How about a female with cascading quills and hair? Julie-Su the Echidna, another Archie comic exclusive has that feature. She's smart, knows exactly what to do as a freedom fighter, and even trained Amy once. She's also the girl of Knuckles' dreams. Heh, lucky him. Her older self in the series Mobius: X Years Later is just downright hot! Just look at that long ponytail! Now we're talkin'!1, 2, button my shoe! Princess Sally Acorn. There's a lot to say about this character. She's the heir to the throne, Sonic's first official romance, the only character that used to not wear clothes, brave and athletic, the most humanoid character, and is like a mother to Tails. In the TV show, Sonic SatAM, one Freedom Fighter, the cowardly Antoine constantly tries to woo Sally, but doesn't succeed because... he's a coward! The Princess is also a semi-perfect example of an excellent love interest, although there were a couple of times when she really snapped and acted like a lunatic; in the comics, that is. But overall, Sally Acorn really stands out amongst the slew of females not just because she's Sonic's first official love interest, or because she's the only one who didn't wear clothes, but because in the comics, she grew very long hair, and married Sonic in the future, becoming the Queen.So, you've seen a pyrokinetic Cat, a swallow, two gorgeous echidnas, and even a princess! Who could possibly top those kinds of females? Well, get ready folks; this is the #1 hottest Sonic the Hedgehog female character. Rouge the Bat. If anybody denies it, how dare you? This woman can fly, she's as strong as Knuckles, and is a femme fatale, seducing other characters into getting what she wants. Instead of having one love interest, she has two! Knuckles, and Shadow the Hedgehog. Being a treasure thief, she's only interested in one object set; jewels, especially the Chaos Emeralds. There actually have been situations where Rouge's cleavage has been exposed, but it eventually got censored. What a price to pay. I think the best part about this beauty is that she wears three different outfits unlike the other female characters. And who wouldn't want to fly across the landscape, be as strong as Shawn Johnson, and flirt with any male, anytime, anywhere. These three traits make Rouge the Bat triumph over all of the Sonic the Hedgehog females. My hat goes off to you Sonic Team USA. You oughta be proud.There ya have it folks. Those were the hottest female chicks in the Sonic universe. I hope you enjoyed it, happy Valentine's Day, and I'll see you later. HERE WE GO!

_childDocuments_.review: This game truly kicked ass! It's not your typical Sonic game, but that's exactly what makes it stand out. The character moments are excellent, with each interaction feeling more dynamic and engaging.The story is a legitimate mystery that kept me guessing until the very end. It's not quite an Agatha Christie or Arthur Conan Doyle novel, but it legitimately had me guessing until the last character interaction (no spoilers) but it all came together very well, It's not the greatest mystery story ever by any means, but you can tell this team worked allot harder on it than allot of television production teams work on some of theirs. I half expected Knuckles to start saying, "The butler did it!" lolThe platforming sections are top-notch, reminiscent of  (if it was an auto scroller... and also good) The precision and creativity required reminded me of Sonic games can be capable of when care and craft are put into them, but with the added depth of a whodunit. It's as if Sonic and Tails teamed up with Hercule Poirot to solve the case of the missing Chaos Emeralds!In short, this game is an almost masterpiece (Only thing that could improve it is Achievements), for a free game, you'd be a buffoon to not add it to your library. The blend of high-speed action, compelling mystery, and character-driven storytelling make it a must-play. 10/10, would play it again faster than Sonic can say "Gotta Go Fast!!!"

_childDocuments_.review: A  murder mystery-themed visual novel released as an April Fool's joke that's way more polished and fun than it probably should be. If that description alone doesn't already pique your interest, there's not much else I can say to convince you. Just pick it up and try it for yourself next time you've got about two hours to kill.  is a visual novel that follows the cast of the  series in a pretend murder mystery party on a highly advanced train called the Mirage Express. You play as a new member of the train staff and are tasked with keeping everyone safe and happy; but when Sonic turns up "dead", you're suddenly thrown headfirst into the game and need to help detective Tails uncover who's responsible. Never in my life did I expect a game like this to ever come out, let alone have it be legitimately good on nearly all fronts.Most of the gameplay is just talking to suspects and clicking around the screen to find clues in each area, but you also get to play a "runner" style minigame as part of the interrogation process (don't ask). You have these linear isometric levels that feel like they were pulled out of of , and you need to collect a certain amount of rings before reaching the end of the level in order to progress with your interrogation. They're not too tough if you're familiar with  games already, but there's an Assist Mode that lets you slow down the game speed, reduce the ring requirement, and even disable damage/pitfalls so almost anyone can still beat it without issue. I say "almost" because there's one issue it doesn't address that I didn't personally experience myself, but have seen other reviews mention: , so play with caution if you're prone to either or both of those.Other than that, it does everything else very well. The visuals are charming, the soundtrack is great (though that one's par for the course for a  game), the characterization of the main cast makes them entertaining without flanderizing them, there's a bunch of little Easter eggs for long-time series fans, the corny humor got some genuine laughs out of me, and the whole story kinda feels like a Saturday morning cartoon in all the right ways. It only takes about two hours to beat, and it was two hours of my evening well spent if you ask me.

_childDocuments_.review: The Murder of Sonic the Hedeghog comes completely out of nowhere and gives fans (and curious outsiders) a piece of Sonic media that is a nearly perfect experience.The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is free which gives it so many points towards recommendation that any of my usual criticism and complaints are barely a drop in the bucket. Conveniently enough, said criticism and complaints are - in fact - super minor. TMoStH (or I'll just call it Murder going forward...) is a stellar piece of visual novel fanservice made by actual fans and if you are a fan of the Sonic series, you really should give it some of your time.Murder's strongest points are both in production value and writing. Being a visual novel, these are both certainly necessities - but not usually what Sonic is known for. That said, if you are a Sonic fan, we've entered a sort of renaissance where fans of the series have had more opportunities to create artistic and written entries for the blue blur. The IDW comics are very well received and I'd make the argument that - as far as characterization is concerned - this game is the peak. The developers understand perfectly what makes the world of modern Sonic interesting. They also know how to write some of the best versions of these characters too - especially if you're a fan of the favorite edgelord Shadow. But millage may vary there.And if that last paragraph feels like another language to you, good news! This game is also totally for you too. Though it helps if you have a background in some of the modern Sonic games, it isn't necessary at all. Al you really need to know are: these are a group of heroic friends who are coming together to celebrate the birthday of an outgoing birthday girl. This game is very outsider friendly. Well... mostly.The weakest part of the game - something that veterans to Sonic games probably won't find too challenging - are the THINK segments. The puzzles where you gather evidence and present it are extremely barebones (there's no penalty for wrong answers, and you have very little options for what you can present). So to shore this up a tad, they added quick platforming segments where you move a little Sonic through an Endless Runner styled sequence. Which is very similar to how a number of Sonic games run their Chaos Emerald obtaining bonus stages. Failing these puts you back at the start of the segments, but they run only about two minutes at most. They gradually increase in difficulty, but overall they aren't too bad. Plus, there are accessibility options if you want to make them easier to the point of outright ignoring them. Truthfully, they're fine and not a hindrance to the game. I was never at a point where I didn't want to do them. They're just not super fun to do.Any complaints I have face the firing squad of two major elements:1) This game isn't very long (1 1/2 to 2 hours, I just voice acted it with my partner hence the double length) and is chock full of enough funny emotional writing to make all of it a joy to experience.2) IT'S COMPLETELY FREE.Murder knows what it's doing. Just enjoy a lighthearted ride. Maybe feel some emotions too. Make sure you save when you get to the Casino car so you can choose every option for that section. It's worth the trip.(P.S. I swear the writing team must have written Phoenix Wright fanfic in the past. The PC feels exactly like what you'd get if you took Phoenix Wright, made him a Mobian, made him a waiter, and removed the gender. Seriously.)

_childDocuments_.review: ******SPOILERS AHEAD********First of all, I've never left a review of a steam game before, if that tells you anything. This game had no right being as brilliant as it was. Everything from the art, to the dialogue,  to the story were all top tier. Truly the best thing SEGA has put out in a hot minute. I went into this fully expecting some shameless display of pop culture references, unfunny meta humor. and other various Sonic twitter account BS, but what I found instead was a surprisingly genuine celebration of Sonic, his friends, and the universe they inhabit. The mystery wasn't obvious, and the multiple twists and turns genuinely kept me on the edge of my seat. I was almost certain that Shadow did it, then when I learned that it wasn't him, I naturally suspected Espio due to the way that the clues lined up, and I was partially right, but the twist at the end with the train itself being a highly intelligent badnik caught me off guard, and was completely unexpected. the very end of the game, after the train was defeated was extremely emotional and actually BROUGHT ME TO TEARS, REAL ACTUAL TEARS!!! and that, to me, is the best April Fool's joke of them all. I highly recommend this game, and give it a genuine 10/10. I'm very excited for what Sonic Team has coming down the pipeline. We made it boys, we're finally out of the Dark Age of Sonic the Hedgehog.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute blast to play. If anything, this is probably one of the best Sonic Games to be released in the modern era (2010-now) Over the years we have had some great games, like Mania, Generations, and Frontiers (maybe), but overall, this game just has so many beats. _childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite Sonic games of all time! To see a visual novel dropped out of the blue that explores everything I love about this series and always dreamed of seeing in an official game but never got to prior is unreal, MAJOR props to all involved! The scenes with Rouge and Blaze felt plucked right out of a story I would've written around them, it felt almost tailor made to my interests in this franchise in that way. _childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly pleasantly surprised. Usually when there's an April Fool's gag around a visual novel, it's making fun of dating sims and not actually real - but this is neither of those things!For people who follow sonic_hedgehog and read the comics religiously, this one's a no-brainer. Play it, enjoy it, leave a review yourself so the bosses of the people who made the game get to see it's being received well. :) As someone who really can't stand the North American social media presence of Sonic the Hedgehog and who only mostly kinda enjoys the comics, even I found things to like, so if you're like me... maybe give it a shot yourself?This visual novel's main secret weapon is that it really does seem like the people who made it legitimately bought into it. There's no "haha, visual novels are dumb" vibe to be found, just a pretty cute (if a bit linear and surface-level) visual novel that has a pretty good shot at putting a smile on the face of even a fairly-jaded Sonic fan.I'm saving my one name-drop for the person who contributed my favorite part of the game, the art - Min Ho Kim, who I know for having done some solid cover artwork for the comics, puts in excellent work in this visual novel with each character. Everyone's so expressive, there's an air of fun with the 'play-pretend' scenario they all find themselves in, and it all fits together perfectly.The "DreamGear" mini game is cute at first blush, but it gets very tedious at the climax. Helpfully, there are assist tools that lower the difficulty in very impressively-modular ways, which I give unreserved kudos for. Personally, I wish the game could've simply had a reasonable difficulty level from start to finish like it mostly had until the finish, but now I know for any replay I do of this that I'll need to turn some of those assist settings on. Even at its worst, it doesn't manage to ruin the good the rest of the visual novel does.This is easily the best April Fool's thing I've seen in my adult life, as it mainly seems to just use the occasion to get away with existing at all. Should you play it if you love Sonic? Obviously, it's free and it's got everything you could want. Should you play it if you just kinda like Sonic? Sure! It's got enough charm to justify itself towards the end even if you're a casual fan, or a fan who's pulled away from Sonic over the years for any number of reasons.Well-done to everyone involved, I'm glad I gave this one a shot. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best Sonic game I've ever played. (S2 and S3&K being the only contenders, IMO. They're great games, but S2 is a little lacking in polish, and I always had difficulty with S3&K's Flying Battery Zone, so I'm being serious.) I appreciate the wide references to Sonic lore. The action sequences are a legitimate challenge (tho easy to retry, and handicap is available) and a ludonarrative vehicle. The humor, both in the story-writing and dialogue, are good; had me laughing out loud at times. The art is both uniquely styled and fantastic. The story is everything I ever wanted from a Sonic game, minus perhaps a little grandiosity. If the game had cost money, I could imagine one might expect deeper problem-solving, but this is very generous for a free game. Actually, I am really tired of point-and-click adventures, but this one was neither boring, nor ridiculous, nor too perplexing. The characters are all likable (which is a good thing, even in spite of the murder mystery confrontations and conflicting agendas). Given how well it accomplishes its scope, I honestly don't think I could recommend another Sonic game more highly.Just one little gripe, though: the word "alibi's", as used in the game, should not have an apostrophe. That could be patched up, right?I would be excited if the team behind this would keep making Sonic games.

_childDocuments_.review: For a free game that came out of nowhere, this was pretty damn good. A visual novel/point & click adventure with real-time ring collecting minigames intersperced throughout. Fans of Sonic will get a kick out of it, as there's some tasteful references here and there, and it's nice to see some of these characters get more to do than usual. This game also serves as a redemption of sorts for Sonic's social media team. I've had my gripes with them in the past, and how they'd cynically spew self-deprecating jokes at the expense of a franchise that, at the time, still wasn't putting out games good enough to warrant the meta-humour. Here, however, that same team (excluding the members who've since left) have been allowed the creative freedom to make a blummin' game, short though it may be. It feels just as official as any Sonic Team-developed game (in some ways, I'd even say it eclipses Sonic Team's recent output). The murder mystery was fun, and while the plot took a predictable turn towards the end, it didn't interfere with the actual murder game the player got to take part in. The artwork and character designs are great, the music was catchy, the THINK sections complimented the VN gameplay by keeping things fresh and making the game worth playing rather than watching (since player agency is one of the most important components of a visual novel), and it gave Sonic's other characters a chance to share the spotlight again. The best part is, it's free. Short but sweet, doesn't outstay its welcome, and doesn't leave me wanting. You can tell the people making this game genuinely do care about Sonic as a series, and it was great to see them put that passion to use in an interactive space. Definitely worth a play through, and I hope we get more surprises like this later down the road. Speaking of surprises, Fang's back in the next Sonic game, and I couldn't be happier.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an engaging time, for a free April Fool's game. Probably would've been better if you were allowed to actually make your arguments instead of being made to play the clunky "THINK" runner sections (there are *reasons* why we don't have too many isometric platformers these days...), but the story and character writing make up for it. I was pleasantly surprised by some of the twists within.If you play this, I recommend using the Assist Mode settings. The challenge of avoiding obstacles and collecting rings with an oddly-controlling character on a fast-moving checkerboard won't meaningfully contribute to your enjoyment of this title - and stubbornly persevering your way through them without Assist Mode (like I did) isn't a satisfying experience, no matter how familiar you are with Sonic. The rest of this experience is too good to spend more time than you need to on an unrelated game style that other titles do better.

_childDocuments_.review: The "Sonic is dead" aspect is obviously the main thing that's supposed to reel you in (and it works). You go in, expecting a quick 20-minute-ish April Fools laugh, but... It turns out to be more than a simple joke. It's a genuinely nice little story. It's clear a lot of love was put into this visual novel. It's chock-full of fun details and references to Sonic's other adventures. Of course, being a visual novel, the main focus is the story and characters.We have some new characters exclusive to this story - the conductor, the protagonist, and... the train. I'll only cover the protagonist here.They're your typical relatably socially awkward protagonist, but... The writers turn that up to an 11, to the point of absurdity. I personally really love that, but some may find that annoying. At many points the game got me thinking "me too, buddy" at their internal monologues and funny antics. And as for the already-existing characters... I think their characterisation was really good! Honestly, I don't have much to say here.The plot was great, in my opinion! The mystery is not very complex or hard to figure out, but the game doesn't treat you like you're incapable of solving it yourself, which is something even big commercial games struggle with. Going along and solving the mystery is really fun!Apart from the main, "intellectual" side, there's also the sonic special stage-style "THINK!" minigames. They're alright, they're a fun distraction from the reading. And if you just do not care for them, or find them frustrating, you can tweak almost every difficulty aspect in the accessibility options, which is fantastic, in my opinion. I personally did play through each one of them, because they were a nice little challenge.It's a quick play/read: I finished it in 4-5 hours, according to Steam; in one sitting. It is a fun one, though! If you're a Sonic fan, I think you'll enjoy this, if you're not, I think there's some enjoyment to be had here too - the narrative is from the perspective of a character who has heard of Sonic and his friends in passing, they are pretty much celebrities to them. This game's a treat, and was obviously made with a lot of love for these characters and the franchise. It's awesome that SEGA let the team make something like this, and release it for free.

And it was mostly fun, if formulaic.The main gameplay is a typical click on the clues then make the deduction style mystery, but in order to have your character get the inspiration to proceed, you have to play a short platform runner game level.  The characters are fun (I can't say if they're true to the other games/ media) and the plot makes good enough sense (in a cartoony way) to be satisfying.  Older folks (like me) will spot issues and plot holes, but for youngsters it would be fine.Personally, the bit I didn't like was the arcade game sections, which just didn't seem a good way of simulating a detective's thinking... but it's a Sonic game, so I suppose it had to be there.So overall, I'm not the target audience for this, but I still had fun.  As a point and click game player, it didn't really make me want to go out and start playing Sonic games, but I could imagine a Sonic player trying this as a first introduction to P&C and really enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ (5/5)I recently had the pleasure of immersing myself in the captivating world of "The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog," and I must say, it exceeded all my expectations. As a lifelong fan of Sonic and a lover of thrilling mysteries, this unique combination of elements was an absolute delight.First and foremost, the storytelling was exceptional. The narrative took unexpected twists and turns, keeping me engaged and eager to uncover the truth behind Sonic's tragic demise. The author skillfully crafted a complex web of intrigue, weaving together a tapestry of suspense, emotion, and nostalgia. I found myself completely absorbed in the tale, unable to put the book down until I had unraveled the secrets it held.The characters were brilliantly portrayed, staying true to the beloved Sonic universe while introducing depth and complexity to their personalities. Each had their own motivations, secrets, and vulnerabilities, making them feel like real individuals grappling with the weight of the investigation. From Sonic's friends and allies to his most notorious foes, every character added a layer of intrigue to the overall plot.The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog seamlessly combined elements of mystery, action, and a touch of humor. It expertly captured the essence of the Sonic franchise, paying homage to its iconic gameplay and lore. The integration of familiar locations and references created an immersive experience that made me feel like I was a part of the Sonic universe, eagerly assisting in the quest for justice.The pacing was spot-on, keeping me on the edge of my seat throughout the entire book. The author skillfully balanced moments of tension and introspection, offering both adrenaline-pumping action sequences and quieter, reflective moments that allowed me to connect with the characters on a deeper level. The murder mystery aspect was ingeniously constructed, with clues scattered strategically, challenging me to piece together the puzzle and uncover the truth.Furthermore, "The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog" managed to evoke a range of emotions. It allowed me to grieve Sonic's loss, yet also celebrate his life and the impact he had on those around him. The story explored themes of friendship, loyalty, and the enduring power of hope, reminding us why we fell in love with Sonic in the first place.In conclusion, "The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog" is an outstanding work that manages to capture the essence of the beloved Sonic franchise while delivering a thrilling and emotionally resonant murder mystery. It is a testament to the author's skill and understanding of the source material. If you're a fan of Sonic or simply enjoy a well-crafted mystery, I wholeheartedly recommend diving into this engrossing tale. Prepare yourself for a rollercoaster of emotions and an unforgettable adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is divided into two alternating segments: visual novel segments with evidence selection, and runner segments with a collection threshold.In the visual novel segments, you play as a generic sonic universe character whom you name, and you interact with the sonic characters as you work to solve mysteries. I found this segment really fun, since it shows a new but familiar side to all the characters you already know. It's written humorously but there's genuine mystery and intrigue, although it unfortunately doesn't get very deep.In the runner segments, you collect rings while avoiding hazards that reduce your ring total, and can't progress until you beat the "level" by finishing with enough rings. Most of the levels of this minigames are simple and can be completed in a few tries or less, but a small portion of them can take dozens of tries without any assist options on. Unless you're the prideful type, I highly recommend turning down the ring requirement as soon as this minigame becomes frustrating. I didn't, and now I wish I was the culprit.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes this is real, yes it’s official and… oh my god its actually kind of good? Because despite a lot of warranted skepticism I’m sure most have towards the increasingly popular ‘advertisement game’ subgenre of the visual novel-sphere, I think “The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog” contains a key ingredient that betrays its release date: sincerity.Despite the fact that the premise, framing, and April Foolishness suggest this should be one big meme filled joke: it actually isn’t. Low stakes and silly as it may be, The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog takes itself just seriously enough to get to the other side of its 2 hours to deliver a heartwarming story within the bounds of a gameplay-lite visual novel… and its well worth the single sitting it asks of you.Sonic is dead, at least in the context of a themed murder mystery game aboard the Mirage Express, setting of our story and location of Amy’s birthday party. You play as an earnest young railway employee but otherwise blank slate through which to view sonic and his friends, as well as partake in the whodunnit-ness.Because there’s been a murder, and how much of it is part of the game and how much of it is real is an ever burning question as you go from cart to cart performing your intense deliberations and information gathering.Or not so intense, to be honest. Because above all else The Murder of Sonic is light and fluffyy…and asks very little of you from a reading comprehension or sleuthing standpoint.Detective tails runs point and leads you towards most of the right answers. Decisions and scenarios are all compartmentalized into individual train carriages, split into information gathering and alibi pressing sections respectively.But between inventory resets between each carriage that keep relevant clues to a minimum, and obvious verbal queues from Tails that signal once you’ve collected everything you need in your cart… you’ve got a game that’s pretty actionless even by the standards of the genre.The one exception to that rule is the kind of hilarious visualization of making mental breakthroughs…which is a simple ring collecting minigame justified by it answering the question “what would sonic do.”The true reason to play is unsurprisingly the writing, earnest writing that resonated with me a whole lot more than it’s ironic dating sim peers. Because The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is as much about comfy vibes among friends as it is whodunnit.Each of the themed carriages is a small 10 minute exploration into the characters that inhabit it, seeing if their alibi lines up to their murder mystery role and also getting a chance to see their  reaction to Amy’s birthday and whatever present they may have brought.As expected its also filled with in-jokes and easter eggs galore that cement it as a treat for existing sonic fans rather than something to draw in new folks.But I think where I was most impressed was where the story and characters played with the very ‘murder mystery on a train’ premise. As you’d expect there are twists and turns and they deliver in ways that are well written, hilarious, and very appropriately sonic.This game does escalate into an excellent final act; and its carried by some heartwarming and realistic woes for our characters. In addition to being Amy’s birthday party, its also coincidentally the retirement day for the games original character: the train conductor, and the trains crew simultaneously treating the day as a send-off retirement party for him is the source of some thoughtful and unexpected moments… moments that made me consciously thankful that this game wasn’t just the joke it so easily could have been.Love em our hate em, these super short brand-advertising free-to-play visual novels are a part of our industry…and I think “The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog” is not only one of the best ones, but proof that they don’t have to lean into their parody excessively to be successful…, and can use the genres storytelling emphasis to deliver writing that’s character focused, real, and sincere if not the next big save the world story.I hate the term that something was ‘better than it had any right to be’, I feel like it can be a little dismissive to the studios and genres that thrive with lower stakes… but if there’s anywhere that phrase is appropriate I think it would be an April Fools game. Make no mistakes about what The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is: there’s no mechanical or puzzle solving depth to be found here despite its detective premise, anything that can be considered ‘gameplay’ is explicitly simple with no way to fail because they want you to finish this. Its linear and on rails in hopes that you don’t get stuck and quit out of frustration; it redirects all of its focus towards the novel of its visual novel and its a focus that’s not misplaced.  Its a fun premise with a well written story that doesn’t overstay its welcome; and it lacks the sort of diminutive smarmy tone that this free-IP visual novels usually have: giving the story and characters a chance utterly real when they want to be.With a short 2 hour run time and an entry fee of 0 dollars, I think you’d be a fool not to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, I think a younger audience will enjoy it quite a lot. I didn't like the ring-game runner, but I understand it's a game featuring sonic. I just wish you could skip all of them up until the final boss. Sonic doesn't actually die, but I'm glad this game's plot does not follow some cliche trope. I was sort of expecting some Agatha Christie Murder on the Orient Express kind of ordeal, but thankfully it's not like that. The dialogue and the story elements are fun enough and fits the sonic universe.This is more of a visual novel than a point and click or who-done-it. Most the time you are given two to three options, and the answer is obvious. I figured out every solution at the same moment the problem was presented, they are all immediately obvious without any sense of subtlety. I figured out who the murderer was almost immediately, mostly since he was acting unusual and his alibi didn't hold up. I figured out the "twist" of the story well ahead of time too. Again, the game isn't subtle at all, and I assume that is very intentional as this would be an excellent beginner's point & click.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little April fools game. If you're a fan of the sonic series, it's a nice microcosm of all the characters and its fun to walk through their personalities. The dream-gear minigame was also surprisingly well-balanced; I found myself just barely clearing the end levels with maximum focus in a try or two (though you can try as many times you need). It was fun.I don't know how much I liked the self-created character. I think if the game was just through tail's POV it would have been better.Recommend if you're into sonic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: the only downside is that i can't get a achievement for using the slot machine 150 times. it'd be hilarious to be gambling away only to randomly see a achievement come up called "gambling your sanity away" or something like that.but other than that. this is probably the greatest sonic game of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite amazing for a free game it takes about 3 hours to complete its amazing what you can discuss and figure out the last few lvls with the ring collecting is a bit hard but can be adjusted in the setting! TY to the creators of this game ans SEGA i'm hoping to see another story line to add to this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like one of the IDW Sonic comics brought to life, and that's a great thing imo.The art, the writing, the references (which heck, there's at least one character detail that originated from the Twitter Takeovers)... Everything about this is a love letter to these wonderful characters, and they are portrayed flawlessly. (Not to mention the fact that it's an Ace Attorney-esque mystery game, AND a play on the classic "murder on a train" narrative, both of which I adore.I hope we get more Sonic content like this down the line. These are great characters, and these past few years have finally put them in the right hands.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining, it can make you busy for around 3 hours. NICE STORY but the gameplay wasn't that good. Like there is no variety in the gameplay. like its a loop, look for clue, interrogate them, Run and Think. But the last minutes of the game was fun. And it was a chance for rage quit at the end of the game XD
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good!  I normally expect most companies to kind of haphazardly stumble into visual novels on April Fools, take some kind of jab at visual novels or the readers and then exit the scene, but this was respectful to the viewers and it was an adorable read!  Had a lot of fun reading it and the mini game was enjoyable! Hope this team gets a chance to put together more visual novels in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little adventure.  Has story driven point and click gameplay interleaved by an isomorphic 3d style sonic game that seems very simplistic at the start, but gets more interesting throughout.  It looks a lot better as a whole than I imagined it could be when I was just getting started.  Fun little one and done, no regrets at the time I spent playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow this free-to-play April fools day joke is one of the best Sonic games I've ever played. That might sound a little over the top but the characterisation of the cast has never felt more realised. I hope Sega hires Headcannon staff to write for upcoming games or even make a full blown RPG, it cant be worse than their last attempt. Also the gameplay is pretty good, not mind-blowing or anything but still pretty fun, around the quality of something like Helltaker, though it can be a bit of a sensory overload near the end.I dont know why you're reading this, its free, just try it for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: So fun! And free! And the characters are so well written! Must-play for fans of the Sonic IDW comics, and a strong recommendation for Ace Attorney fans and the like. I can think of plenty worse First Sonic Games, so maybe this might give you the bug. Great accessibility options for the action-y parts. Play with some friends and make them voice their favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: It's quick (gotta go fast), silly, and a fun challenge - I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys Sonic games and Knives Out/Clue whodunits. I found out AFTER beating the game that there were settings to make the challenges more feasible, so with those settings in mind it's easily accessible to those who want to just have fun with the story as much as it is to experienced fans who want to grind out a few tough courses after rummaging through trash cans for clues.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This might be my favorite Sonic game. The art is phenomenal. The focus on the story and characters is super great, and they're all expressed in wonderfully fun and funny ways. I laughed a lot. The peeks at the world of Sonic are cool and constructive. It picks the right things to focus on.I have a feeling that you, personally, will enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: I like the cute art, the humor, the characters were entertaining...  yeah, this was pretty fun, especially for a free game. It even got a couple real good laughs out of me - not even counting the April Fools YouTube video. And good on SEGA for supporting this. They're support of fans and fan projects always warms my heart~ So, good job all around!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: The references to past games, the clarifications to the world of Sonic, the interactions between these characters we barely see anymore; this is easily one of the best Sonic games as of recent (which is honestly kind of :dirtytp:).Something I will say however is having to replay the whole game to see certain scenes or art within. If this is ever touched again, may I recommend an art book that is unlocked upon beating the story? Overall, I loved this and can confidently say it is probably my favourite visual novel ever. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ A.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to this game for getting me into the sonic franchise I guess. "we sega have heard all of your feedback, and we've decided to take this character in an all new direction: we ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ killed him" instantly sold. Now that I've started looking into this franchise I feel somewhat enlightened. Dear god, there's more of him than I ever could have imagined. There was not one, not two, but THREE animated sonic series in the 1990s all made by the same studio. There is three movies, two live action and one animated I THINK and I'm not even sure. There was yet another animated series on cartoon network with 104 episodes dear god an I've just finished watching half of them. There is apparently like over 200 sonic games. And the worst part. The worst part of all of this is. Sonic was everywhere in my life this entire time.My first sonic game was sonic 06 on the ps3 when I was the weeest of lads. I remember my older sister handing me the controller and playing as shadow trying to kill the dog thing that you rail grinded on and then held on to the horn of. I thought sonic 06 was what a good game looked like at the time. I watched sonic x on hulu and vividly remember thinking the subbed version was spanish because I didn't know there were more than two languages and I remember the theme song being a BANGER. I used to stay up at night watching sonic comic dubs on my mom's laptop when I visited her. My grandma had sonic underground on vhs and I watched it but I have little to no recollection of it. My little sister gave me a sonic sticker two years ago and it sits in my sticker collection otherwise entirely comprised of madoka magica stickers as I type. I play project diva and project sekai and the characters have sonic costumes because the project diva franchise is made by sega. I hadn't realized how blind to sonic I was until now. He was everywhere. Anyways the murder of sonic the hedgehog was pretty cool. The art's fantastic, I like the desaturated colors the characters have because it doesn't feel too typical of sonic, and the texture on the backgrounds is cool. It all just looks really really nice generally. The special stages were a good difficulty, they weren't frustrating nor boring and I felt like they added a lot to the game. The game was very well written, I really liked seeing how the characters interacted and the twists were pretty good. I'd give this game a E for Existential dread at the realization of how everywhere a character can be
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This game is real. And it's actually good. Not what I was expecting.It's a short visual novel with cute art, lines that made me laugh out loud, and occasionally frustrating 2.5D auto-runner stages thrown in for spice. Very much worth checking out if you have any warm feelings at all for Sonic and friends.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: It's games such as these that remind me of my general stance about video games. Games don't need to have the most cutting edge graphics or Cloth Physics or Fish AI or what have you. What matters the most is if you have fun while playing it! When games are fun, that's worth more!This game was such a fun time from start to finish! For Free! That's the crazy part! For Free! I would PAY if it meant more Visual Novel Sonic games, just games that have Sonic and friends written well (since it's a novel that should be the focus) interacting with one another as they get up to an assortment of hi-jinx!No meta humour, no making fun of the brand or anything of the sort! As a Sonic fan, I am Very pleased with this game, and I hope we get more like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I didn't believe I would like the game at first.  I love visual novels and mystery, but having the Sonic and Friends characters in the visual novel made me question it slightly.  After playing it, I enjoyed this game.  I wasn't a fan of some of the fights, but assist mode was a huge lifesaver for when I needed difficulty to be lowered slightly.  I really recommend this game to people who like visual novels and enjoy games like Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Now, according to Steam, I only played this for 4.7hrs, but I have it on record that it was longer. I thought it'd be a cute game to play, maybe an hour or two, so I recorded it to show to my friends. An hour in, and I realized it was very reminiscent  of the old Sonic games I grew up on. Two hours and I noticed it was getting more challenging. Three hours and I wanted to quit, but I knew if I did, I wouldn't be able to force myself to continue later on. So I pushed onward. Four hours in, and I think you can hear my soul starting to leave my body (although every level I beat still gave me serotonin). 5½ hours in, and I discovered there was a setting to make the levels easier. So I lowered the difficulty by making the ring count half the original required amount. I finished the game at a little over six hours. Why did I continue to play despite everything? I wanted to know who murdered Sonic the Hedgehog, of course.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best virtual novel I've ever played. I was not expecting the ending to turn out the way it did, though I had a hunch or two. The graphics are beautifully done, and the story is pretty rich. While the game play sometimes seemed frustrating (especially the parts where Sonic has to pick up rings), the deducing of clues and suspects was very much enjoyable, and there was quite a lot to look through. Even though it seems to be kinda self-evident at times, there were some points that I actually tried to figure out what needed to be done before making choices (even though there really is no "losing" this game). My hope is that SEGA comes out with another free title, but even if they don't, I enjoyed this one! Hopefully, he'd spin right into another game like this one! Thanks, SEGA! 😎
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Amy: ...Sonic.This can't be real!Eggman: Do not worry. Soon the hedgehog will become part of the Planet's energy.All that is left for me is to go North. The 'Promised Land' waits for me over the snowy fields.There, I will become a new being by uniting with the Planet. As will this hedgehog...Amy: ...Shut up.The cycle of nature and your stupid plan don't mean a thing.Sonic is gone.Sonic will no longer talk, no longer laugh, cry...or get angry...What about us? What are WE supposed to do?What about my pain?My fingers are tingling. My mouth is dry.My eyes are burning!Eggman: What are you saying? Are you trying to tell me you have feelings too?Amy: Of course! Who do you think I am!?Eggman: Ha, ha, ha...Stop acting as if you were sad.There's no need to act as though you're angry either.Because, Amy. You are...Eggman: Because, you are...a puppet.Amy: I'm...a puppet?
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: For a free April Fool's joke release, there's a surprising amount of effort put into this game. The artwork is great, as is the soundtrack, and the story itself, while brief, is a charming bit of fanservice with lots of neat little references to past Sonic games and media. The accessibility toggles for the THINK platforming minigame are much appreciated, and the game doesn't punish you for picking the wrong dialogue options. It's a pretty chill experience.That being said, it would have been nice to have a text log to review the last few bits of dialogue you've seen at any given point.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't offer much as an investigative game (it's no Ace Attorney, much simpler) but overall a very pleasant experience. The art style is fantastic!!! Huge kudos to the art team! Assist mode settings for platforming sequences are a very nice and thoughtful touch. Crazy production quality for a free game. Fine to play even for a person not too familiar with the Sonic universe (like me).
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Short & free April's Fools special game, how sweety is that! First things first, I wanna talk 'bout gameplay. Yeah, this is a visual novel so that means there's no much "gameplay" in it, you're definitely right but I genuinely surprised how smooth is this. Every simple piece is like oil in a pan you know. And actually there's a "gameplay" section and that is "thinking like sonic" minigames. They're fine and a necessary addition in my opinion. Concept is similiar to Sonic 2 special stages which I hate it but this works aight. Another thing is OST which is so damn cool. Specially interrogation and final battle themes.Let's continue with story and for me, it's way predictable from the start. Even the fact that  situation. I know this is a April's Fools game and that was their mindset while writing story but I expected a little stronger, like a slap in my face. Because this is a different kind of Sonic game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: The entire game feels like we went back to the OG style of writing for the characters, and I absolutely love it. Shadow being a loner that still cares, Tails feeling confident enough to take on things on his own (even taking on his own sidekick in us), Knuckles being a competitive hothead but not just outright 1 IQ, Vector and Espio both getting some spotlight after some time.The game specific characters also felt naturally fit for the game, and the dream game for us was a fun way of still having us "go fast", just with collecting coins as the priority. Special mention for the final screen because my god, that got a good chuckle out of me while also being adorable and making me happy about a certain character that showed up there.Overall, even for an April Fool's game, this is a really great Sonic the Hedgehog entry.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: The Sonic franchise has one of the best casts of all time and I hope this game is an indication that we'll perhaps see a few more games in this style that let us really dig into these characters and their interpersonal relationships. It plays like a simplified version of phoenix wright, but the art style is incredibly good and I'd love to see a follow up will full voice acting. Props to the team that made this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: While it's a pretty short game, it's very well written and filled with charm, but I guess that's what the best of the fans and SEGA can do for the fans. Overall it's an excellent game and, if you like Sonic and/or murder mystery games, I'd highly recommend checking it out. (And no, I'm definitely not being hijacked by Eggman to say this.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, funny, funky little romp full of cheeky jokes and delightful storytelling for Sonic fans old and new. One word of caution: those prone to photosensitivity may have a hard time with the ring-catching minigames. By the ending, I could feel my eyeballs tingling because of those checkers! Otherwise, excellently engaging. Short, sweet, and definitely made with love by people who truly enjoy the Sonic franchise and all its quirks. Happy April Fools Day!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: For the low, low price of absolutely free, you get:- A hand-drawn Sonic VN;- A lighthearted and wholesome story;- Memorable and funny dialogue;- A plot-twist that's worth the price of entry;- The first time freaking  has gotten some screentime since Sonic Rush Adventure;- No sour notes whatsoever;- An April Fool's joke that's the best thing I've seen in one heck of a long time;- And LET'S GO DADWhy haven't you played this yet?
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game was adorable.  The character designs, the emoting in the illustrations, the UI design, the writing, even the sound design, overall very cute.  Maybe not for gameplay, but for story and aesthetic purposes, I might use this as an introduction to the Sonic IP for friends of mine who know next to nothing about it.Not much in the way of criticisms.  The ending choices for you character and total lack of a wrap up for them were anti-climactic to the point where I wish it had just ended on Eggman choosing rubber duckies.  It also would've been nice to have a comic of the heist plan being executed after having gone through all the set-up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: To me, this is honestly a perfect game in my opinion. People will not take it seriously because its an April Fools joke, but I cannot think of a single think I did like about the game. It kept me captivated from start to finish with amazing dialogue, beautiful artwork, pleasant music, and a surprisingly intense and fun finale that made me want the Think mini-game as its own separate little infinite runner. Over all, it gets a 10/10 from me as a long time Sonic fan. This is an instant favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: What a surprise game. This is without a doubt my favorite April fools ever.A solid murder mystery with some nice twists. Almost like reading a Sonic comic. The characters felt really full of personality,and It was very engaging working through the game.Clues and finding them felt very rewarding, and made sense were to use. I loved the implementation of a mini game for the thinking part. I'll admit it was a little challenging, but not overly so.The music was really a delight to listen to and the art, and pixel art was spot on. Even better is the fact that this was released for free. I would definitely be interested in more Sonic games like this, especially a franchise! I'd have to buy them all based on this gem here!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute and dumb, in a good way.I'm sort of ambivalent on the genre mix. On the one hand, as a silly cute VN, the action gameplay spiced it up... but also some of those little endless runner style levels towards the end got a little frustrating. Still, a cute and funny little story, and it's free, so why not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely fun game. It really caught me off guard with the story. The devs and writers didn't need to go as hard ad they did, not above and beyond, but it went deeper with the story than I thought. It is a good game and i highly recommend it. And no one can say it's not worth it because it's literally free.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This is mostly a short, simple detective game, and it's a lot of fun and very charming. It's spoiled only by the compulsory Sonic-like sections where you have to do a Sonic run to collect rings. In particular the ending has a very long sequence of having to do much longer, much trickier sequences. But you can turn the difficulty way, way down in multiple ways for those bits.Given that it's free, if you like detective games there's no reason not to pick this up. It only takes a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: I think Sega has officially won April Fool's Day for the foreseeable future. You get about 4 to 5 hours of content depending on how fast you read and how thorough you are, which is a shocking amount for the low low price of nothing. My only minor complaints was that Sega, being the memelords that they are, missed a few really golden opportunities to really ham it up; and that the whole thing dragged out a bit longer than it probably should've. Still, I had fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: The game was released on April Fool's day because nobody wants to see Sonic get murdered, but the game is not a joke, it's a real visual novel game with a built-in easy mini-game (which can be set even easier in settings).The tone is light and humorous, each character very colorfully unique. It's a detective story with drama, in fact a lot of dramatic potential which unfortunately, by the game being very brief and focused on humor, the deep dramatic potential ends up sidelined.Maybe you'll walk out remembering the value of fitting in a group of virtuous friends, how loving others is something under your control, how work ethic helps give meaning to the smallest task, but also bring the danger of perfectionism, all in under a 2 hour package. Highly worth it, I've played much longer RPG games with less dramatic impact.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved me, in my moment of need, it gave me a spark of light. Hope some might say, it saved me from a never ending downward spiral into depression, it cured my cancer, it even fixed my marriage and family status. I am now a happy boy, who lives a normal life, thanks to this game. Thanks to it, I was able to kick start my life again, with no issues, this game, is the epitome of perfection, the definition of amazing, it should win game of the year award, just for this. Sega, you are the best company to ever exist. My humble gratitude, and yeah. Keep in mind, this game will fix everything, every one of your problems.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite on par with Pheonix Wright, aka a game you need to pay for, and the gameplay that isn't point and click is a little dissonant to the good part, That being said, it is free, the art is second to NONE and I could frame it, Plus it gives excellent characterization to some of our favorite characters. even though it was a bit of a gag game, I unironically love it to pieces and would in fact pay for a full blown sonic point and click adventure, there is a lot to love and a lot that can be expanded on. You should give it a try, easy 2 hours of easy reading, fun art, and good times, for free! you don't get that value anywhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the best games I've played this year. Super charming little VN, super well written and clearly done by the most passionate of fans. Stuff like this is what I wanna see out of Sonic, all the characters present get fantastic moments for their personalities to shine through and if you're a fan of any of these characters, it's seriously fantastic. 10/10 best April Fools' Day (observed) thing I've ever seen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: I am reminded of the Nintendo 3ds game Detective Pikachu. _childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: for a free game, this is such an entertaining story to play through. very impressed with the love and effort put into this game, genuinely loved everything about it. the art style, the characterization, the storytelling, such a breath of fresh air for the sonic franchise. it makes me really happy and glad to see them slowly begin to break their boundaries with sonic games after so many years of the same kind of gameplay over and over. please keep doing this, i would do anything to see more sonic games like this that go outside of their comfort zone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog
