Overall, it's a very good game, especially for free.Expect to spend under 5 hrs to beat it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, short Sonic murder mystery! It walks you through the entire train (where it takes place) and the incident of Sonic's death. While this is happening, you actively solve mysteries and play a little minigame (that may or may not be holding me back from completion) that can be fun for ideas. Overall, good pacing, amazing art and game play, I give it either a 8.7/10 or 5 sonic costumes out of 3 echidnas
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this game is incredible. As my introduction to visual novels, this was a very fun experience with an unexpected twist and a highly relatable protagonist. I still can't believe that Amy listens to true crime podcasts. On a serious note tho the gameplay sections can make you a bit dizzy. 8/10 search every trash can you see
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing fan game!I was able to complete it in a few hours but don't let that discourage you, it was still amazing. It's a great window into the activities of the Sonic crew when not in the middle pursuit of Dr. Eggman's plot. It still has some twists and turns and keeps you on your toes for the game's lore. The details and artwork are also so amazing, Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic April Fools game. Props to whoever was in charge of the artwork, very fun. It's hard to give a score for a game like this. Overall a fun experience for $0.00, it did what it set out to do. The game itself was very linear, which was a bit disappointing given the variety of text options and decisions.0/10 no Monokuma
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game that allowed me "kinda" hanging out with Tails, my favorite Sonic character.Never played visual novels tho, but I'm aware of genre, tho, in this one its more like simple point and click quest, with very little inventory and small locations. _childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a fun little point-and-click visual novel, with a murder mystery game aboard the Mirage Express to celebrate Amy Rose's birthday. You must tracked down clues, assess the alibis and figured out which of the passengers is Sonic’s murderer. Seriously, for a free April Fools' Day joke game I didn’t expect it be a real game, let alone to see that it’s actually quality work.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: The minigame trips you out since it's isometric viewed. It takes the fun out of the game in general bc you're too busy raging out to proceed to the next level. Personal opinion, minigames should be optional, not required, in a visual novel. The artwork is cute, along with the story, but the minigame is what made me uninstall before completing the game as a whole. (Mind you, I'm at the very end, so the minigame gets alot harder.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games on steam, but this was a fantastic little story for any Sonic the Hedgehog fan! Features a robust cast of Sonic characters and has a charming little story that you could reasonably complete in about two hours or so. Even has some difficulty sliders if you find the mandatory minigames a bit too difficult!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This game came to me at the end of a really long week, and it was exactly what I needed. I had a ton of fun with this, and its perfect for anyone who knows about Sonic to pick up and complete in a couple of hours. I had a lot of fun with this, and it makes me wish more game franchises would do small things like this for their community.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard about there being some game called The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog, and that it was developed by SEGA, and that it was being shadowdropped (for free!) right before April Fools Day, I expected a short, 10-20 minute joke game.I did not, ever, expect to be actually engaged with the story and dialogue almost instantly and for the entire duration of my 3+ hours with this game. It's not going to win any awards for most well-written narrative or gripping gameplay or level design, but to say this exceeded my expectations is a gross understatement. The art captures a wonderful variety of expressions for Sonic and friends, and they're all characterized so well and with so much charm in their dialogue. I doubt I'll play through it again, but I'm very happy to have experienced it once. For anyone who likes Sonic or, especially, its cast of characters, I absolutely recommend this little romp.My only criticism is that segments where you collect Rings can get very difficult at the end of the game. There are options for the Assist Mode, which is fantastic, but, near as I could tell, enabling or disabling the Assist Mode is no longer possible once you've started the endgame. Other than that, this was a really great time. Thank you to everyone who worked on this mini gem of a game, and for all the passion and work and time that was clearly put into it.(Also escape room-themed sequel next time, maybe??)

_childDocuments_.review: My time as a Sonic "fan", per se, has come and gone. I simply have come to accept that what I saw in it when I became attached isn't what it aspired to be, or what any of its other fans saw in it.That being said, I still find myself peeking at new stuff about the blue blur. This is definitely a reminder that there is some heart still in the series.__As far as gameplay goes, it's just an ordinary visual novel. At that, it's a visual novel whose choices mostly don't matter. Either there's only one "right" answer and you're just asked to click again if you got it wrong; or, there's just two same answers to one question that I'm pretty sure don't actually make a difference.There is a little 'game' in this, though. An angle-down running game where Sonic is controlled to collect rings and dodge obstacles to get to a light bulb. It's moderately fun for something so casual. Don't expect too much from it.The story is linear. Even only having played once I can tell the story only goes one way- no different "murderer" every time, or such- which is a shame, because replay value should be the core of most gaming experiences. However, considering this is a free April Fool's Day release, I guess that'd be a bit much.__As far as characterization and story goes, if you're a paranoid stickler for Sonic character personalities like I used to be, definitely keep in mind this is just a non-canon side-piece, just in case "Sonic's just a game franchise about a blue fast cartoon hedgehog" doesn't cut it.I can say that most of this characterization, I would have eaten up if this had come out in, say, "2011".  Sega has long sat on their characters in a way that put their interesting designs and personality buzzwords in the hands of underpaid Japanese writers scribbling something simple and toddler-minded in half a day so they can get back to watching their cruel game shows. "The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog" actually gives these characters a chance to just be observably themselves in an interesting way, corroborating what we know about them (for those of us who do) while offering fresh new angles and scenarios.I will say I wish this was applied more evenly. Two characters I especially would have loved to see more from, Blaze and Rouge, only majorly interact in the introductory scene and in the *one* scenario that we meet them in afterward (Wherein Blaze devolves to something I had thought beneath her, but, again, this VN is non-canon), after which they pretty much never say anything. Still, at least Rouge and Blaze get more chance to express themselves here than they've gotten in most of the Sonic franchise, so it's still a win.___The protagonist, unfortunately, is annoying and difficult to like, outside of brief moments. Pretty much like any, or almost any VN protagonist I've ever met, in fact. Like all those VN protags - heck, like an outright fanfiction character (minus being more powerful than Shadow and born in the heart of Black Doom's mom's secret lab while bedding every other character in the franchise) - he just goes along with everything, makes a bunch of interjections that he doesn't have the guts to actually act on, and just gets invited into the action without any reasonable option to stay more at a distance. With this annoying protagonist, a lot of the would-be enjoyable quirky, Monty-Python-ish humor in this is lost. They should've just made Tails himself the protagonist with us making *his* decisions. Then it would make more sense why he can't refuse some requests, and there'd be no middle man between us and this new take on the characters.____It's still free, a notable time waster, and a chance to see Sonic characters say something other than "hur dur, power of frienship, stop Eggman!" I recommend it to any Sonic fan who doesn't want to take anything seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is a sprawling tale of loyalty, conviction, and the price of infamy, chronicling the inevitable collapse of a motley crew of Wild West holdouts kicking against the slow march of civilisation and industrialisation. Set in SEGA’s most authentic and lived-in open world ever, there are so many things to do, so many people to meet, and so many places to explore it’s giddily overwhelming. The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog isn’t just SEGA’s greatest achievement to date; it’s a game so lacking in compromise it’s tough to know where best to start discussing it.So let’s start at the beginning: It’s 1899 and American outlaws are an endangered species. Sonic and his gang are on the run after a botched heist in the growing town of Blackwater and they’ve retreated high into the mountains where an atrocious blizzard is covering their escape. We slip into the spurs of Tails, an exceedingly cool and capable outlaw who was found by Sonic as a boy and raised on the wrong side of the law, and settle in for a roughly 60-hour story.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is the art an absolute treat to look at every step of the way, but the genuine love and care put into the script is constantly self-evident. The POV character is honestly a delight, they only add good things to the experience and I'm a little sad that we probably won't see more of them after this game. (I named them Cherry!)The auto-runner sections get surprisingly difficult at times, but luckily there are assist features for anyone who struggles with quick reaction times, so if you're just here for the visual novel aspect, you should still be able to get through it. And the sections themselves are pretty fun, I wish there was an endless mode where you could dodge randomly-generated obstacles.This is a game that knows exactly what it wants to be and pulls it off perfectly (even with a few grammatical mistakes here and there). It's a short, sweet love letter to the cast of the series, with a lot of great humor that had me laughing the whole way through. Definitely try it out for yourself if you're curious!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is only an April Fools joke in its marketing.  In reality, The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is a pretty sincere "professional fan project" made by the Sonic social media team. If you liked Sonic Frontier's approach to characterization, you'll like how this game does it too (of course adjusted for the more lighthearted premise). The dialogue is charming, the story actually as a shape to it, and the gameplay sections which occur while you're interrogating people are fun, Bonus-Stage-style challenges which require a little skill. Is it the most polished experience? No. But it's free, and I don't regret spending my Friday night with Sonic and pals.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10Surprisingly, pretty good of a game for what it is. There is missing features for a visual novel like Logs and such, but for the simplicity of the story, it wasn't really mandatory. I expected basically nothing from this game, and while the majority of the time I did feel like was fine, it does get pretty good and explains why some of the gameplay decisions they made, especially the platforming mechanic for thinking pays off.Story/ CharactersPretty cliche of a murder mystery, and while I didn't figure out at first cause I had a pretty ass theory, it was pretty easy to understand why they were the one who murdered sonic. The story does take a twist and turn, but it still keeps it the sonic way if that makes sense. Easily the best story out of any sonic game that I have played so far, and it pulls off what it wants really well. The characters as well are pretty interesting, but not very deep which is to be expected of sonic characters. They were still very entertaining to talk to and figure out their alibis, even how simple their reasons were. Tails accompanies you throughout the whole way and he is just a treat to be with, and most of the other characters were interesting enough, but of course, not enough to deep dive into who they are which is fine.GameplayVisual novel with very simple and straightforward path. There isn't punishment for choosing wrong, and it is pretty easy to figure out what to do and the mystery the game throws at you. No voice acting but that didn't bother me, and of course no log, but never really had to use past knowledge of dialogue to figure out if they are lying or not so it wasn't that big of a deal. One thing I did not like was when you are forced to try to figure out evidence, the game uses a pseudo 2d platforming segment to basically collect coins and reach the end as it through spikes and other crap at you. It does get repetitive towards the end, and it made me wish there was a minigame that allowed me to figure out the alibi, but again, simple mystery so I usually figured it out before the minigame even started. The minigame does make sense at the end why they decided on it, but other minigames would had been nice if they do choose to expand on this (which I expect they won't but thats fine).MusicPretty solid, and some good music here and there. A ton of the music does sound a bit generic, but it works and I never felt like the music was too overbearing or was troubling me. Not going to be adding any of the songs to any of my playlists, but still overall pretty good.Last Positives/ Nitpicks-No Log, but simple enough story to forgive-a bit too long during the murder mystery, especially when I knew what was going on before I even finished interrogating them-Not exactly a sonic fan, but was still worth playing through, and its FREE.- MFs forgot I was there right when we left the train like damn :(ConclusionSurprisingly, pretty good of a game. Of course its simple what it does and repetitive at times for the minigame, but is easily worth the playthrough, especially if you are a sonic fan. Best sonic story I've heard, but that isn't saying much for how bad Sonic stories usually are, if they even exist.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The murder of Sonic The Hedgehog:Before anything I should mention that this game is not anything like the other games. It is much more story focused and shorter. I would compare it to the Persona games before comparing it to the other Sonic games. So if you're not a big fan of those then that is just a heads up.This game is a short but epic "conclusion" to the huge trilogy know as the Sonic games. The game follows you, the main character who just started working at a train station, the train station only does events and this event is a murder mystery, that is because it is Amy's birthday. The game opens with a lot of dialogue that would roughly take about 10-15 to read through if you don't skip through it all like most people do. However after all that you you collect the tickets of all the people who attended the birthday. Just to name a few, Monty, Knuckles, Tails, Amy, and Sonic of course.                                                                                      The Start:Warning, the rest of this review will be spoilers of the main story so to avoid any spoilers please click off and download this game. You'd be doing yourself a favor.Everyone gets their roles. Tails and Amy are both detectives and so they have to wait and hour for everyone else. (Don't ask me why I have no idea) After the hour passes however, the train starts to go really, really, really, fast and then they Tails, Amy and you all pass out. When you wake up you are all in this closet. Amy woke up before you and tails and you have to investigate her. This is also were the DreamGear mechanic is introduced. The DreamGear is kind of like you're playing a sonic game. You have to collect a certain amount of rings, every time there is a new DreamGear you need 5 more rings so each time it is harder and harder. (I WILL FINISH LATER)

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly the only Sonic game I have ever played, and while I know it is clearly a departure from the norm for this series, I found this to be an enjoyable little experience. I don't really know how these characters normally behave outside of this setting, but they seem to have charming personalities, and the art style is pretty cute. The sections played on the player character's qualify as just enough of a "game" to elevate the experience beyond reading a free online webcomic. Speaking of the price, I am genuinely impressed with the quality of this product, especially considering that it was intended as a free April Fool's Day joke. In all honesty, this could have been released on any day of the year, and it would be just as good. While I wouldn't pay a full price for this game, especially considering how the visual novel genre, and especially the mystery subgenre has hardly any replay value, I can't disagree that this isn't worth at least some time and money. It's a good little distraction that I'm sure people who can actually connect to the characters involved from memory will probably enjoy for a little bit.

_childDocuments_.review: First, as a April fools games. Let me say this for the 2 hours of game-play. I felt excited and played this through to the end without a break. I really enjoyed the detective mystery story mixed with the retro game-play. When, the story was rolling it felt refreshing. An I really do hope future games take inspiration from this mini game.  From what little is here . The characters felt in character. The rules they played in the detective drama. _childDocuments_.review: Quaint but enjoyable. It's definitely more clever than it first lets on in the opening scenes. [MINOR SPOILERS] For a bite-sized freebie offered as an April Fool's joke, I was pleasantly surprised at how good it was. It's not gonna blow your mind or anything, but it's pleasant the whole way through.You get a little isometric Special Stage every time you present a piece of evidence, sort of in the spirit of Danganronpa. Some of the other reviews were complaining about it (while - go figure - other reviews were complaining it wasn't JUST the minigame and found the reading bits boring, which... dude, it's a ), but I actually found it pretty fun. Most of the complaints about the "THINK!" segments were that they were too difficult, so if you run into that same issue, you should know  you can use to make them essentially run on autopilot. For my part, I actually thought they were almost boringly easy at first before ramping up to enjoyably engaging by the end, even if I only failed three times in the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is a free-to-play point-and-click murder mystery visual novel which combines classic Sonic the Hedgehog gameplay with crime investigation gameplay akin to popular murder mystery games like Ace Attorney and Danganronpa. This game was developed especially for this year's April Fool's Day following the success of the recently released Sonic Frontiers.The premise of this game is simple: Amy Rose has invited Sonic, Tails, Knuckles and their friends to participate in a murder mystery train ride for her birthday party, much akin to classic whodunits like Murder on the Orient Express. However, as all the participants get into character with their respective roles, including Sonic who happens to be this game's victim, little do they know that someone on the train has actually attacked him!You play as an ordinary, mild-mannered butler whom you can name however you wish. Your mission is to guide your protagonist through their investigation of the attack on Sonic by gathering clues and testimony, questioning suspects and ultimately proving who the culprit is.While this game tends to play like a typical point-and-click visual novel with humorous and witty dialogue as you click on everything in sight, there are certain segments throughout the game which play like the special stages in Sonic the Hedgehog 2 on the Sega Genesis in which you must collect as many rings as instructed before you reach the goal. And, like with most special stages in Sonic games, they get increasingly difficult all the way to the end. In fact, there's a pretty epic payoff in the endgame after you've identified the culprit who attacked Sonic.Personally, my favourite aspect of this game is the amazingly polished audiovisual presentation. Both the graphics and the music look and sound so fresh, refined and akin to the main Sonic games that you'd almost forget that you're practically playing a licensed indie Sonic game.The character portraits really capture the likeness of the characters and breathe new life onto them, especially Tails, Amy, Espio and, most importantly, Shadow. Furthermore, the hilarious character dialogue and small environmental details shows a few sides to the characters that long-time Sonic fans may have never seen before.My only complaints are that this game would've been perfect if the dialogue was proofread and, more importantly, fully voiced. There were a few rare occasions when I spotted a few spelling and/or grammar errors in the text.Furthermore, I couldn't help but wonder how much more enjoyable this game would be if it had the current Sonic voice cast dub all the characters, including our butler protagonist. Considering the fact that the butler was given an androgynous design, I believe a talented non-binary voice actor like Casey Mongillo would've been the perfect voice for them.Mind you, this is still a free-to-play visual novel made for April Fool's Day so I suppose you get what you pay for, with or without money. Having said that, I wouldn't mind paying up to £20 for a fully-voiced version of this game: "The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog Plus" perhaps?All in all, as short and sweet as this free-to-play April Fool's game is, I'd definitely recommend it not only to Sonic the Hedgehog fans but also to fans of point-and-click adventure games like Gabriel Knight and Laura Bow as well as murder mystery visual novels like Ace Attorney and Danganronpa! If you like any of the above, you'll love this game!P.S. In case you were wondering, I named my butler protagonist "Wilder". If possible, I'd love to find out what their canon name is as well as their species.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I nominated this for the 'sit back and relax' category in Steam Awards, I'll update this with a more serious review than my previous joke entry.Adventure Era Sonic fan here who bailed after 2006. This is a visual novel focusing on the side cast of Sonic, and to me, they all feel right in a way that they haven't for over 15 years. This game still manages to feel like a Sonic game even though Sonic is only around for a little bit at the start, and that side cast is a big part of why.The mystery isn't too hard to figure out, so the focus is on the cast and the shenanigans they get up too. It's a lot of fun. There is a minigame where you do some platforming to collect enough rings to make a deduction and move the story forward, but it's pretty easy. You can also try again as many times as you like, so there's no punishment for failing.It's a fun game that doesn't ask too much of you, and, more importantly, it might just be the only Sonic game I've played that is good all the way through with no 'if's or 'but's attached. That's why it got my nomination.

_childDocuments_.review: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog. What an interesting concept. I love a good whodunnit kind of game, so of course this piqued my curiosity.Since the game isn't exactly very long (two hours apparently, depending on how "good" you are), there isn't a whole lot to say. Still, I'll go over some pros and cons.Pros:-I love the art style. Having the characters don role-specific outfits was a clever touch and helped sell the "murder mystery" vibe.-I enjoyed the good humour. I like proper silly humour and this game has some of that.-The story is written well enough, at least the murder mystery part. Threw me off, that's for sure.-I find the music to be pretty good too. I don't know if they were all remixes of Sonic themes or if there was some original music, but I liked it ^^Cons:-I hate those infuriating linerunner segments. I get they wanted to make the game more Sonic-y (and longer), but I felt like it didn't fit in with the game at all. If one needs to play a silly minigame to validate their thinking, they should get out of the thinking game. Or stick to chess, logically.-While I liked the murder mystery part of the story, the ending segments were.. less good. A bit tacked on for Sonic reasons.-Talking to the passengers on the train is fun, but not really necessary, aside from the interrogation parts. It would have been more fun if just chatting with the Sonic crew was a bigger part of the game, in my opinion.-WHERE WAS CREAM?! >: | I know she was mentioned once, but I feel like she should have been on the train too.. Maybe as Amy's assistant or something?Would I recommend this game? Yeah! For a Free To Play April Fools prank this works perfectly fine! If you like a good whodunnit, enjoy spending time with the Sonic crew and like a game in the Sonic universe that is not Sonic-centered, pick this up and play it on a rainy afternoon. Or a sunny morning :P

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has NEVER played a Sonic Game and has only seen the first Sonic movie and some footage from Sonic Unleashed, this has to be one of the most fun game I've played in a bit.For being dropped on April fool's, not only did this turn out to be real, this game really has you engaged and charmed with the characters and the story.First, really love the art style, it's really soft even when some of the characters have bright colors. I love the costumes the characters had, it really went well with their designs!The protagonist, despite being an animal for you to insert yourself, has a personality that really stands out, with some goofy dialogue and even timid thoughts to themself.I applaud you for making the protag non-binary (or not establishing a gender at all), as this way, everyone can insert themself to their liking and give more representation to others!Even as someone who doesn't know much about Sonic, the game really establishes well ever characters personality, you can easily follow along fine even if you don't know the series, and if you do, then you get to see a bunch of references from said series, which I love.The twist and ending also had me surprised, I really wasn't expecting it! Massive props to the team and creators for this beautiful game!I highly recommend this game to someone who loves visual novel murder mysteries, Sonic fan or not, you are in for a fun ride.

_childDocuments_.review: This was actually fantastic. The main thing is that the writing is good with not too much silly stuff thrown in there. It feels like this is a genuine side story in the Sonic universe and not just a throw away joke game, and I enjoyed myself the whole way through. The game isn't very long (probably around an hour or so) but it has a lot of charm. Very nice artwork and surprisingly good music, but if you look at the credits it makes sense. I thought this was going to be a small throwaway title especially since it's obviously an April fools joke, but I'm happy to say it's not.If I had any downsides it's that there is no punishment for offering the wrong evidence. Even if it was some sort of funny dialogue, or just a health system like in Phoenix Wright. This is mostly just a visual novel for the most part, and while that's fine some punishment would make it more fun for me personally. The non story parts are similar to old style Sonic Special stages which is great, but having the last few be full screen is kind of disorienting for me as a user with a large screen. Lastly the absence of any sound effect for when the text scrolls across makes the game more quiet than it should be. Other than that I have no complaints, and would have kept playing this game for hours if it din't end.I would love to see this kind of gameplay expanded in the Sonic universe. There's so many stories that could be told and this brought me back to the days of the old wacky Sonic cartoon. On top of all that I'm pretty sure there's a reference (hidden or not) to pretty much every game in the Sonic game hidden somewhere in here... and that makes me happy.Side note: Allow us to play those stages in some sort of score attack mode, and Sonic x Phoenix Wright when?

_childDocuments_.review: The story is simple but very cute.  The mysteries are not at all challenging, but figuring them out is still fun. There's really just the one problem. This is a visual novel, right?  Then why the hell does it have dozens of unskippable platforming sections?  They're hard as nails, too. Not what I want from a VN, SEGA. Like, I know it's technically a Sonic game, but this really wasn't necessary.  Most of The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is simple point-n-click gameplay that any casual player, like say, your Grandma, could play.  Except you could never recommend this game to her, because the shockingly difficult portions requiring arcade reflexes form an unnecessary barrier to entry for inexperienced players.  The game is a visual novel, not a platformer.  Putting mandatory platforming in a VN is just bad game design.  The whole thing feels confused, like they didn't know what audience they were even aiming for.  SEGA has been in this business a long time, you'd really think they'd know better.  Oh wait, what am I saying?  This is SEGA we're talking about here.  Their track record clearly demonstrates they wouldn't know a thing about good game design if it bit them on the ass.  Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: What I expected: Haha funny sonic is dead game look he's doing the family guy death pose.What I got: an emotional story about greed, selfishness, self-doubt, and trying to keep a positive outlook even in the harshest of times.WARNING! Spoilers ahead.What can I even say?For an April Fools day joke, this doesn't feel like a joke but moreso a message for those down on their luck.The gameplay itself is akin to a visual novel, with an "infinite runner" minigame constantly thrown at you. The VN aspects are admittedly a little bit bland as almost no choice changes any outcome, though for an april fools joke I'll let it slide. The runner sections however, are genuinely fun. At first I thought they were all gonna be either tedious or boring, but I ended up finding myself replaying them a bit just to try and see if I could hold onto more rings then I did last time.7.5/10 for Gameplay.The story at first seems goofy and silly, but then takes a turn. The game explores how one can feel that they aren't worth much, or how everything bad that's happened feels like it's their fault. For a moment my heart genuinely sunk, because, as a person, I have been in a dark place like that before. The story shows that there is always a better outcome, you just have to run and work for it. I didn't expect to have such a heavy message in this game. There's also the whole part of the story with the train not wanting to let go of the conductor, someone whose been with him for MANY years, and how one can turn selfish and greedy just because they don't want to lose that close pal of theirs.10/10 for storyArt and VisualsFrom the glorious art style to the pixel art of the minigames, everything is stylized and amazing. There's even a lot of hidden easter eggs within the environment, some that you'd have to keep an eye out for. Such as references to other sega titles (unfortunately none referencing Jet Set Radio), to even lads like Ian Jr. Yes, I saw him, in various places, Ian if you're reading this I AM coming for you, start running. In the runner sections, the art is flashy but not too much to the point you can't tell what's going on, with everything having a distinct look to tell you what's going to happen and give you some good reaction time.10/10 for artMusic? It's a sega game, I don't even have to explain it at this point. But I will.It has that cheesy generic visual novel soundtrack vibe, albeit with a more sonic style to it, as well as actually being tolerable to listen to on loop. Don't even get me started on the runner sections track, or the final boss track either, those are bangers.10/10 for musicOverall rating:37.5/40Good job.Also, if I don't see the conductor or Barry appear in the next sonic game, I'm not buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what I would genuinely call "Peak fiction". The characters are written in a compelling and fun way true to depictions in other Sonic media and their character portraits were all expressive and well-made. The story is well-paced and moving. The twists and turns it took as the game progressed were original and unexpected. Even the main character is funny and interesting. The thinking minigames were difficult but not too much- even if you do find it too hard, there are settings to adjust for it- and segmented the game so it didn't get too boring. Not that it was boring for a second, because the game's story almost- and I am not joking- it almost made me *cry*, that's how emotional it got me.Did I think that the Sonic murder mystery game would be one of the best games I ever played? No.Was it? Yes, no doubt about it.Would I recommend it? Absolutely.Would I play it again despite already having played through the whole story? Yes! Because the whole thing, the minigame, the character interactions, the art, *everything* made this whole game enjoyable.tl;dr: this game is peak fiction from the art-style and gameplay to the story and characters. It almost made me cry, play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow...I was convinced this was a joke. Yet when I went on Steam immediately upon learning that it was out now for free and that it was indeed not a joke, I was more than pleasantly surprised. I think visual novels are making an impact on the gaming community and seeing something with this level of charm, yet keeping with a simplicity of execution, its like a tasty hors d'oeuvre, one that I didn't know I wanted but was glad I ate.I love the music, the lighthearted silliness of it all, and the fact that Sega was willing to take a risk and showcase something that I can legitimately feel the heart, passion, and love that went into this. Not sure the entire story behind who developed it, but it feels like the labor of love of one person in the best way possible.I know a lot of folks love to give the good and bad in their reviews of games, and thats fine and dandy, but all that really matters in the end is whether or not its worth playing, and I would definitely say this one is. I'd love to see more of this kind of stuff from Sega and other companies, lets take risks again, lets try something new every once in a while, and more importantly, lets acknowledge that a game doesn't have to be a trillion dollar budget project with droves of designers, testers, writers, composers, and all that to be good, its just gotta have some heart.

_childDocuments_.review: A half-decent Sonic game might be the realest April Fool's joke of all time; this Murder on the Orient Express variant, told primarily through the form of a visual novel/point-and-click adventure game with some classic Sonic platforming elements comes as a pleasant surprise in both its form and execution, and while it's more bite-sized fun without a real mystery behind it, it's an actual, enjoyable entry into the Sonic franchise.There's a train, a birthday party, and a "murder" - there's pretty much all the necessary context. The writing is pretty tongue-in-cheek across the board, with characters taking some slightly less serious versions of themselves than one might see, but that's all the stretching of Sonic mainstays we're getting; anyone expecting a more serious story or ingenious storytelling is going to be rapidly disappointed. Across its less than two hour runtime, the player will "interview" suspects, click glowing objects around the room, and play a mental minigame reminiscent of Genesis style "3D" Sonic games. It's without a ton of challenge as an overall package when it comes to the story o the gameplay.But, there's still enjoyment to be had seeing some of the characters act in ways they might normally not; anyone expecting a deep mystery is opt to be disappointed, as the initial "murder" takes up the first 2/3 of the run time, with a last, highly predictable villain taking up the final act. I did enjoy the ramping up of difficulty for the platforming sections, giving a "boss fight" feel to the end of the game. As far as I can see, there are no real extra paths or content to The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog, making one's experience tailored to how fast they can read and the accuracy of their shifted jumps. it ends happily and predictably.The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog is fun for what it is, and actually one of the better Sonic titles of the last few years, as sad as that is to say. It adds a fun little meta-take on some Sonic elements, and while it's brief, it ain't no joke.Better than Sonic Frontiers.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly enjoyed this far more than I thought I was going to. Easy recommend. With Sonic out of the picture, this short visual novel mystery really brings forward, flexes and gives the limelight to some of the series' more sadly under-utilised cast of characters, characters that people have really grown fond of over the years. Blaze and Rouge roping Detective Tails and the steward into performing a heist was just so fun start to finish.The characters are charming and well written. The visual presentation is just on-point (some of the character art here is really superb), the music is far better than it should've been for this short April-fools game.Lastly the mystery itself keeps its cards close to its chest until the closing moments, and when the villain finally reveals itself it ends off on such a bittersweet but happy ending for the conductor, his train and all of the characters aboard. SEGA could really be onto something here. I hope they allow the people that made this to make another Sonic visual novel game, maybe with a grander scope and some extra 'oomph behind it.  ♪(´▽｀)

_childDocuments_.review: Do not let the fact that this is an April Fool's bit fool YOU. This is a good game. If you don't mind story-based games (with a bit of action in the form of a fun "thinking" minigame) and just want to spend an afternoon having a good time, you should try this. You can expect 2 hours of gameplay, as seen by my "hours played" stat, representing someone of average skill playing the game. Exploring almost everything and failing a handful of times. You play from the perspective of an insert civilian character you can name (I think they're a raccoon due to the various references to trash cans that are empty [Like a certain YouTuber's soul]). You're a staff member on a train helping tails solve a murder mystery for Amy's birthday. The plot somehow does a lot with what they have, working extremely efficiently. Genuinely enjoyed it and connected with the self-insert character more than I do in most games. Just the few silly dialogue options gave him a lot of personality, while still fitting into the world. Not a punching bag for comedy but also not a Mary Sue. This is Sonic writing at it's strongest, the whole gang together interacting in wholesome, casual, and believable ways. Like a #AskSonic takeover on Twitter. The game was short (but sweet) and longer than expected for a free game. I probably would've paid 5-10 bucks for it, and only that little because of it's length not it's quality. I genuinely hope the stories of future Sonic games take inspiration from this, even though it's not a Sonic Team game.P.S.The Knuckles level was the first early skill check while learning the "thinking" mini-game. Don't argue with knuckles, he's got hands in the intellectual argument game.

_childDocuments_.review: A free april’s fools game set in the “Sonic universe” that has rave reviews on steam and promises the death of its main protagonist? Honestly, the weird mix of an Agatha Christie-style murder mystery visual novel featuring a bunch of furries of various recognition is on paper quite a blast! Call me intrigued.. You play as (insert name here), a character that is blatantly inserted as a glorified extra heavily infected with a huge dose of fanfictionities (common sympthoms include: constant swooning over main characters, shallow breath, dreamy eyes..) into a drug laced birthday party with Tail’s and friends onboard a wacky talking train. The party quickly turns into a slaughter as a bunch of kids turn up and blatantly throw themselves into a woodchipper.. Well, not really, but we get a mild twist at the beginning and start LARPing with Tail’s in order to find out who murdered Sonic the Hedgehog.. ..and this is where I feel that the story could have been so much more! We get a hint of something great that never truly blooms, but then again as it is a “free joke game” it is hard to be picky. The gameplay however is a bit lacking, this game is basically all story and no game, and the story is quite middling.. The fact that you have to play a really annoying mini-game to actually assemble your meager and unfulfilling clues are at best uninspiring and at worst a quite invasive thing in my otherwise quite enjoyable mystery plot. The environments are quite lovely and I like the various set pieces even if the interactable objects were quite dislocated in my runthrough, might be me, might be a feature.. In short this is the very definition of not great, not terrible.. And the fact that it is the highest rated Sonic game on Steam is a bit of a meme in itself.. For 2 hours of free entertainment it might be allright for a hardcore fan of Tail, or maybe to a closet furry such as myself, but then again there are other way better free furry games on steam so..

_childDocuments_.review: I copped this game just because I saw it was free, and got way more than I bargained for. The artstyle is really nice and descriptive, the puzzles weren't overly difficult, and the writing and gameplay were both fantastic. I'm neither a big fan of the Sonic games nor visual novels, and even I can tell that this was less of an April Fool's joke and more of a genuine love letter to SEGA's flagship franchise. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Sonic the Hedgehog, you won't want to miss out on The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog! I don't really want to give too much away, but if you approach it as a harmless little distraction, you're going to have a great time with it! And it's free, so you really don't have anything to lose by getting it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Played this with a group of friends in the call, this was an amazing experience. It definitely gave me some Bakano/Danganronpa vibes at times with the tone of the mystery, with some pretty tongue in cheek humor. Shout out to my friends voicing the chars with me in our play through. Took us 4 hours to go through the game reading every single line out loud. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good for a free game. You literally cannot lose out. Even if you don't like it you don't lose a dime. If you like Sonic the hedgehog you will probably enjoy this. If you enjoyed Ace Attorney's mechanics you will probably be a little disappointed since it's not 1:1 the same, but it's fairly close. Ultimately it was still fun for me personally and I recommend trying it if you're curious, you might just get 2-3 hours of enjoyment out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Not only it was the most well done and elaborated April Fool's joke ever done, but it's so charming, unique and refreshing for the Sonic franchise. Seeing them being goofy, funny and do any normal activities besides the usual quarrels with Eggman or darker tones we usually see in the media (type of Slice of Life aesthetic), it feels so good and adorable. I had a great time, and I even felt even more in love with Sonic with this Visual Novel! I hope we get to see more of these type of games in the future ;v;
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly surprised by the amount of effort that went into a free April Fools game.  The writing, music, and art is great, and the mixture of Ace Attorney-lite with some isometric Sonic gameplay all worked together better than I expected.  I'm not too familiar with the entirety of the Sonic cast, but I did enjoy how they seem more fleshed out compared to other Sonic games that I've played (maybe due to the visual novel approach).  Overall, I had a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. _childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting combination of basic detective flash game mechanics with a visual novel. My issue with it is the forced arcade game sections, which should be skippable. They add little to nothing to the game, and make for annoying padding. If you aren't into those, I highly recommend going to the settings and enabling Invincibility (something that I only remembered after wasting way more time than I should've). As a visual novel, the game has nice art, a good soundtrack and fun writing, especially for a free game. I'd like to see a sequel, as long as they add "Previous/Next" options for dialogue (like Ren'Py games have) and a way to skip the minigame(s) entirely.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and i personally love all the mystery behind every word it offers. I was so happy to see that my suspicions were correct and i personally didn't expect such an ending but Sage being included just lightly made me smile so brightly.. Overall i think it's a great game if you are looking for something to do for a few hours!10/10 Would definitely play again!! :3

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing and I had a good time.The detective aspect of the game is well paced. Some larger suspicious events are introduced early on that leave you wondering how things fit together while you're solving the smaller, more immediate questions and verifying alibis.There are some cute sections with fun banter between characters and consistently nice art throughout the game.Mystery-wise there were several plausible suspects at the end (at least by my reasoning) but if you pay attention you should be able to piece together the mystery behind The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog.The ending pleasantly surprised me. Game definitely tries to go out on a high note and for me it succeeded.Did have issues playing on steamdeck with all the interactable objects appearing twice, slightly offset but unsure if this is a common issue as I did not see any other mentions of it. Hence played on pc instead.Also, the trash bin dialogue was delightful. Only beaten for me by the Casino section.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: As a Sonic fan, as much as I had a few moments of dying from the inside being reminded about what represents the "Meta Era" with its tone—the 'unfunny' jokes, whatever you make of it—this game was certainly a breath of fresh air after much I had to tolerate with seeing the criticisms bombarding Forces—and the whole "Meta Era" in general, as a result (I may hate it as well, but I could not tolerate constant negativity towards a game series' failure in evolution)—and seeing the fruits of developer-incompetency labour unveil. I still do not particularly like Shadow being reduced to not being social towards other characters despite not having a reason to, and some of the other weird things like Espio's 'ninjutsu' abilities unrelated to ninjutsu, even though it is a cute detail for a character; or Rogue's sudden kleptomania that is somehow connected to her being a thief despite simply being obsessed over JEWELS since Adventure 2 which was about two decades ago (Shadow was included there too, you know, and a better character than most!).Despite all that I say, it is definitely the most meme-worthy modern Sonic game after a long time—the positive kind, I mean—excusing the visual-novel direction, by an extent. You would already have seen the reviews before seeing mine, and that was because I could not bring myself or was too lazy to type an extensive review about this game. Oops.You might say that I should have thought something shorter then, but it would not have capture my true thoughts for my experience with this game, and my passion for this series among some others I see potential for and/or actually killing it within the industry.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: It was released as April Fools but it's an actual Visual Novel, through and through.It's Among Us and Phoenix Wright (Ace Attorney) at the same time (minus the trial day part)But with Sonic chars instead.Sonic is dead, and someone in the train did it.You collect clues, you talk to people, you interrogate them to prove their alibi and even shove evidence right in their face Ace Attorney style.But wait you gotta "collect your thoughts" after choosing the correct evidence. And how you do that? Of course, Special Stage esque mini games! They are easy at first and get harder as you go.There's an option in the option menu where you can make the special stages easier in a variety of different ways.There's no health bar. If you ♥♥♥♥ up, you try again. Both in picking wrong evidence and in failing the minigames.So unless you're a late Gen Z full of ADHD down to your bones, you will get it by just trying over and over.There is seemingly no "missable" content, apart from a few easter eggs if you name yourself a specific name, there's a guide on steam already stating all of them:That's it. Only recommend if you really like investigative visual novels or if you really really like Sonic. Or both.It's NOT QUITE a Sonic game. More of a Visual Novel Sonic themed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: april fools aside, it's a great game, actually worth playing, some of the think sections are a bit frustrating due to sonic not being able to jump instantly after landing, but there's a bunch of options to make those easier if you just want to enjoy the story. it's free, highly recommend spending the 2 hours to play it. the art style is awesome too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to legions of loyal fans, this lovely licensed leap through a locomotive laced with lethal lamentations of its guests likely will lure you in with its charm, humor, premise and of course, other words that start with L. A letter this game just refuses to take, instead constantly reaching for, and eventually taking, the W. If you haven't played The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog, give it a shot, especially if you're a long-time Sonic fan. It's a fun 2-hour romp you can experience for free, and is some of the best Sonic content we've gotten in a very long time.

_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: The mini-games don't really connotatively relate to the detective work you're performing (only feeling appropriate to me during the end segment).The mystery involves elements that aren't ever clarified, and solving it takes a backseat after a certain point.On the flip side, the art direction is really cute, and I happen to like that quite a lot. Not to mention how surprisingly neat the dynamics between the very archetypal characters here felt to me.Overall, I had an okay experience while playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing this game and oh my gosh! This game is honestly way better than it has any right to be, especially for an April Fools joke! Admittedly, the game-play is rather simple, but it's the surprisingly good writing, the beautiful artwork, and the memorable music that makes you want to keep playing it (and it's only 2 hours long, so that certainly helps)! Seriously, I cannot believe that this is an "official" Sonic game that was made by Sonic fans, released on April Fools Day, and is better than a lot of the main-line Sonic games! What a world we live in. So, yeah, 9/10. Would definitely recommend! Oh, yeah, and it's free!

_childDocuments_.review: People are comparing this to EDF, which isn't an unfair comparison, same publisher and all, but it has even more jank with none of the charm.Fewer maps that have less detail between them than you'll find on any one map from Earth Defense Force 4.1.The best, most fun feature, building your own Mechs, is done entirely through keyboard, from placing parts to cycling through menus. And there are more menu controls than they've allotted space for, so you can't even see what they all are.Yeah, you could play this with a controller, but there's no UI for the controls. All of the prompts and controls are for keyboard and mouse regardless. At least it's that way for Xbox controllers, maybe Dualshock users got luckier since this released on PS5.Earth Defense Force benefits a lot from it's cheesy B-movie English VA, and I could forgive the lack of English VA here, but even the text translation seems hastily done, and when it comes to directions or controls it's detrimental.The combat and is unwieldy and there isn't even a basic jump, you'll do a boost jump even if you only wanted to move a little. Others have pointed out the controller deadzone aiming applies to keyboard and mouse, but it bears repeating.The engine is extremely bare bones. No ragdolls, no debris, mechs all seem to have the same mass on the field. Enemy mechs vanish when destroyed, no flying parts, wreckage, or even a death animation. Buildings don't so much as get destroyed as they do deleted, with a flat texture on the ground in their place. Battles seem smaller scale in general, you'll only have a few mechs on your side at most. There's no visible stagger or knockback on enemy mechs either. They can get stunned and arms and weapons can break off sometimes, but they don't slow down or recoil to getting hit.Earth Defense Force 2025, released 10 years ago on the Xbox 360 and PS3, had all of these features.All of this I could look past if it was maybe $30, but it's $50 for the basic edition with 40 or so missions. That sounds like a lot, but roughly 20% of the game is locked behind the $65 EDF edition since it includes 10 more missions.People recommending this are saying that people unfairly expected it to be as good as Armored Core 6. The only comparison I can make between them is that you effectively get all of the content for AC6 for $5 cheaper than it costs to get all the content for this.Keep in mind, this is not a game developed by Sandlot, who developed every mainline Earth Defense Force game. Instead, it was developed by their publisher D3.There wasn't really any deception about that from what I could tell, but just know this isn't a reflection on the actual EDF team.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do wish I could be writing a positive review in place of this. There are some incredibly good aspects of this game. The mech building system is more in depth and with better results than I've seen in anything since Break Arts 2. Furthermore, unlike Break Arts, even the very skeleton and body layout of your mech is modular. Your arms can have arms, your head can BE legs. There's honestly very little extra to wish for in that department, save for something I'll mention later.However it's really brought down by everything else. The plot is slow and with no surprises, the core movement systems and weapon management on your side are barely adequate (but adequate nonetheless) and those are probably the better aspects. The maps are absolutely barren and simple with little of meaning or interactivity present in them. Enemy units have pretty simple AI, and while their body types (constructed with the same wacky construction as your own mechs) do vary their attacks innately, a lot of mechanics like damage type resistances can't be interacted with properly because they are basically invisible, and swapping mechs takes longer than a firefight does. NPCs frequently allude to minibosses spawning, and I'd actually be really hyped to fight a miniboss with high health and locational damage and relatively few ads, but it doesn't really work that way until very late in the game.The controls are very jank, particularly outside combat and in menus, and reflective of a clumsy port from console. There's only 50 missions and almost all of them are forgettable, with nothing much special in them. The missions of the EDF DLC are of a generally much better quality and even they aren't great.All of this would be totally forgivable for me, except that instead of charging $20 - $30 for a hobby project from D3 devs, it's priced as if it was a full A-game.I feel like it could have been excellent with a bit of extra time in the oven to sort out the things that well, every *other* mech game on steam seems to have done well.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet EDF-esque mech power fantasy game that can appease that small itch you have for both customizing a mech and blowing stuff up. A lot of the negative reviews here seem to point to it being clunky, but it isn't as bad as others may have stated and you can easily either edit the options or get used to the handling or even both, and that's coming from someone who finished and still enjoying the game. Sadly the MP aspect got hampered by the negative reviews, but hey, you can play this with your friends or in offline SP.Now, this game isn't perfect by any means, but it's a fun game for mecha customization enthusiasts and especially in multiplayer if you have people to play with. Remember that this isn't AC and isn't developed by triple A studios, so play it not for the realism, but for the power fantasy, the customization, and the shenanigans you can have with your friends, if you even have any. Just like any other game out there, this game has it's own pros and cons so I'll be giving mine as per my experience finishing the game.Pros:- it's a mecha power fantasy, blowing stuff up is always fun- it has a lot of customization. While having weight as a limiting stat, the game still allows you to go full ham with a lot of weapons. Just slap a lot of guns, missiles, cannons, bazookas, armor parts anywhere on your mech (*cough "crotch cannons")- Three tiers of part sizes, allowing you to create a small nimble unit or a very large tanky and slow unit, or just a mech for the memes- Parts level up in this game, so grinding stages will always be worth it, and specific parts with the same SIZE and QUALITY share the same part level. (ie. If you have a level 50 of a certain assault rifle, all copies of that specific assault rifle are level 50 as well)- Accessories aren't just accessories, they have a point in terms of defense, they get destroyed when they get damaged enough and can protect your main parts.- You can use up to 5 mechs you've built in one mission, incentivizing you to make a lot, and you can either switch to them or deploy them once your current one gets destroyed. Note that you can't use two at the same time, because only you can pilot the mechs you make, even in multiplayer.- Singleplayer mode is offline (this should not even be here, but with many games requiring you to go online even in SP, this is a Pro that a dwindling number games have)Cons:- Getting your leg or torso destroyed results in the destruction of your mech, which is understandable, but still frustrating when most attacks are focused on both.- The ally NPC AI is what I would say the clunkiest part of the game, since like EDF's NPCs, your allies will always follow and group to you, but while it's the same in this game, both you and your ally NPCs take damage when you bump into each other... and there have been many times that I accidentally kill them because they group too close to my M-sized tank, and that's not me going out of my way to crush them, just them having a death wish sticking close to my oversized treads.- MELEE is very risky since it is an EDF-esque game after all, meaning, you WILL get swarmed but small and large robots alike, and they most likely will have the weapons to tear you to shreds, especially cannon fire. And it is not as visually-appealing to look at compared to raining things with bullets, so if you'd rather play a mecha game with visually-appealing melee, this probably isn't your game.- Terrain graphics may not be that great, but when you've played EDF, you should be used to repetitive maps. - Some occasional boosters glitches when using tank treads on uneven terrain causing you to be unable to lift off which usually happens on M or L-sized mechs in mountain stagesThings to remember that aren't necessarily a pro/con per se:- This game mostly lacks any sort of wide area AoE explosions. As an EDF enjoyer, this might come off as a con, but considering this game's enemies has a much more frequent reliance on missiles, you probably don't want it to have AoE in this game. You can equip a lot of missiles yourself, sure, but remember the enemies also have them in spades, and missiles aren't long range in this game so you can't just sit in the back while spamming it. So personally, while I am kind of sad with the lack of AoE explosions, it would also likely get very frustrating if all those missiles thrown at me have AoE.- This game CAN be played in melee even in the highest difficulties, but again, just like EDF, it requires a lot of skill, and booster timing, because when you run out of boost in the middle of a group, you're not getting out of that. So it's really up to you if you're willing to suffer that frustration for the memes.- This game is a grind, but at least it's not weapon RNG grind. I can understand that not everyone likes to grind.- You'll be spending as much time or even more in customization than in the map (which is fairly common in games that offer a lot of customization). Personally this is my favorite part, since any time I obtain a nice part or weapon, I directly go to the hangar to equip it.- This game has limited ammo weapons (except for melee, obviously). Yes, unlike EDF's infinite ammo weapons (save for AR and some unreloadable Fencer gears) where you are only hampered by reload time, you actually run out of ammo in this one. This encourages you to use the "critical" function to allow separately shooting weapons that have a low ammo count such as a certain tank cannon series of weapon in the game.Conclusion:So all in all, it's a fun game to play with friends if you have an ounce of patience to get to know the game yourself, and it's very enjoyable just playing with friends while showing off the absurd monstrosities you made. For those who enjoy mecha customization for the funsies, this game will scratch that itch for you, and for those players who are heavily spoiled by triple A games or those expecting this one to be like AC, you probably won't enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get this out of the way first: Yeah, the game's port is kind of jank. They had a number of patches to help fix the controls, and I didn't even start the game until after those patches, but the control still isn't good. It's not unbearable, but it's still got acceleration and a small dead zone, even with the variable speed option turned off.That said, the game's fun, if a bit too simple.The draw of the game is obvious: It lets you customize the hell out of mecha. It lets you go pretty wild, with the only restriction pretty much being that your mech has to have legs. Otherwise, the game will let you do pretty much anything, including things that make no physical sense, such as jamming parts into each other (which is helpful it you want to "combine" parts to make different shapes) or having parts not really attached to anything. This is fun.That said, a major problem is that the game's gameplay systems are overly simplistic. There's only a few attack buttons, and you don't get to assign which weapons are assigned to which. So, if you have a bazooka, a beam rifle, an SMG, a Gatling gun, flamethrower: all of those are assigned to one button. Doesn't matter that they have different ranges and projectile speeds. They're all assigned to the same main attack button, and the only thing you can do to change this is assign a  weapon (not even  a group of weapons) to the "critical attack" button. Similarly, all homing weapons are assigned to one button, and all melee weapons are assigned to one button.Furthermore, along with weapons all being assigned to single buttons, you have limited ammunition for each weapon. Wanted to save the 30 shots you have on your big cannons? Too bad! You can't do it. They all shoot with the SMGs you've also got equipped that have thousands of rounds. No saving your big weapons for big enemies for you! Well, aside from a single one you can, as said, assign to the critical attack slot.Anyway, the gameplay pretty much comes down to circle strafing while holding down fire. There's pretty much nothing else to do because the game's systems are too simplistic and restrictive. D3  should have looked at the way games like MechWarrior handle this, and allowed you to specify weapon groups, to allow you to have different weapons sets for different situations on single mechs that you specifically use tactically, rather than just vomitting ALL of your fire all the time. It is what it is though.Still a good time to take your customized machine out for a spin to blow things up, but it's not particularly anything special.Going back to the customization: It's actually not as user-friendly as it should be. The UI is actually pretty bad. You've got a whole lot of parts you're going to collect and sift through, so you would expect there to be good filtering and sorting options, but there isn't. There are some sorting options, such as by level, by acquisition, by size, by quantity, and by category, but you can't even sort alphabetically. This makes finding specific parts you want a pain.Beyond finding the parts you want, placing them isn't as easy as it should be either. Each main part of your mech (legs, torso, arms, head) has nodes on it. Each of these nodes can be used as an anchor point for accessories or additional weapons. This is a pretty good system, that allows you to sort of graft armor plates and weapons to limbs and have them move around with those limbs. The problem is that selecting those nodes can be a total pain, when you've got a lot of them. Remember how I said the port is kind of jank? You can't click on them. You have to try to directionally select them with your movement controls, which can turn into a challenge to get it to actually highlight the node you want. It's still usable, but it's not a smooth experience.To illustrate how challenging that might be, here's one of my units:The sheer number of nodes means that I spend a fair amount of time fiddling with the camera (arrow keys) and movement keys (wasd) to try to select the right node. That said, this image also illustrates how free-form the building is. Four arms, an underslung Gatling gun. shoulder-mounted gatlings, arm-mounted cannons, floating homing lasers, a chest cannon, two rifles, two SMGs. I doubt you'd be able to put something like this together in any other mech game.In any case, if you're here, you're here for the relatively free-form mech building. If you're not in love with the idea of customizing the hell out of your own mecha, then this game isn't for you. If you feel a deep craving to make your own mecha monstrosities though, then this game does indeed deliver on that front. Just, don't expect much else, at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not "EDF but with mechs," despite what most of the positive reviews claim.As someone who loves weird, janky, niche games, and especially loves mecha stuff, this just isn't worth the ridiculously high price. And it might be hard to recommend for a lower one too.Regular gameplay is too dull and repetitive. People comparing it to EDF, and saying "oh the naysayers just went into this expecting Armored Core!" aren't being honest. EDF is arcadey and fun, with tons of janky low budget charm. This is just kind of bland and cheap, with barely any feedback when shooting enemies. Where EDF enemies go flying, ragdoll, and get blasted into a million pieces when you shoot them, every enemy (or piece of an enemy) in this game simply vanishes with a small explosion once its hp hits 0. Also, the story is told in the same was an EDF game, but with no dub, so it's impossible to pay attention to during gameplay. And what little story there is doesn't seem very interesting, even by the standards of this kind of game.That's not to say it's ridiculous to compare this to EDF. Some presentation is similar (but worse), buildings can be destroyed (this also doesn't feel as good as in EDF), the little pilot you can play as when you exit your mech is reminiscent of EDF character designs, and you spend the majority of the game fighting hordes of enemies. But the overall feel completely lacks the fun and charm of those games. This is barely a step above shovelware in a lot of areas, as much as I hate to say it.Customization is cool though! I'd love to get into it more, but you have to play a lot to get the really cool stuff (as you should, but I'm going to be refunding this so I didn't get to do much with it). It's also fun to collect new parts by defeating enemies, or capturing them, a feature the game VERY poorly explains (so much so that I only knew it existed because someone told me).As for technical issues: the game has Switch controller icons in the menus and vibration settings, but seemingly no actual way to play with a controller? Insane. Whether this was just a weird bug I experienced and not a universal issue, the game needs a lot more polish and a MUCH lower price. Even if this game was good, I'm getting real sick of weird, niche games that should be $15-20 being sold for the same price as AAA titles. It's like the publishers WANT them to fail. Nobody who isn't a Weirdo is going to take a risk on something like this for that price. But again, in this instance, they'd be right not to since the game isn't actually that good, unfortunately!

_childDocuments_.review: The most important aspects of any mech game is the feedback and feel of your mech. The feedback being your weapons firing and hitting a target, which includes it effect, the sound of it firing and hitting the target, and the destruction your weapon can bring.The feel is it's weight, the speed, the sound design of it moving. Either it's large 'stompy' sound effects before boosting across the ground, or feeling it's weight as you glide some over the air. This game lacks both in those departments. Having played EDF5 and plenty of mech games like Battletech, Mechwarrior, Armored Core Verdict Day, Armored Core 6, and even games like Ace Combat 7 and Project Wingman, they get what it feels like to use a machine built for war. Guns fire, missiles launch, bullets flying, enemies exploding and screaming. This game should have been a hit, but it swung and missed hard. The enemies don't react when you hit them like with EDF's insects with partials and them recoiling back, they get hit, take the damage, kneel a little if any, and just explode unceremoniously. And the explosion isn't glorious like in Ace Combat or Mechwarrior, it feels more like an obligatory explosion to hide the enemy despawning as it dies. In short; Feedback is horrible to the point of nonexistance. But the mech designing is neat at least, but why can't I bind different weapons to different keys, so instead of rifles and shotguns and bazookas being separate they're all bound together.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely not recommended at full price or even anything outside of a 75% sale. An unbelievable rip-off. - Four or five maps that would have been dated over 15 years ago, with most being flat planes that have breakable boxes-masquerading-as-buildings whacked down.- 50 missions that take a few minutes each (40 main + 10 sidestory), and pretty much zero variety in gameplay. Every mission is just 'defeat this wave of enemies.' I think there might have been 'protect this building' as an objective at a point, but the mission played out exactly the same as all the rest.- EDF's bad visuals are in service of putting tons of monsters on screen at the same time, and CWW doesn't have that excuse. It just looks bad. Which would be fine if it was putting dozens of mechs on screen at once, but it doesn't.- The game's main draw, the fact that you have almost endless customization of your mech, doesn't actually mean as much as you'd hope. The only movement that matters is boosting and jet-boosting. There's no power core to build around. The only thing that's a limiting capacity is your weight limit. Sure, it's amusing the first time you strap a mining drill to the roof of a car and jet around insta-gibbing enemies, but when you then make a legged mech, or a hover mech, with a mining drill and realize that nothing really changes at all about your gameplay, you'll realize how shallow the building really is.I adore EDF and how D3 handles that property, and I was hoping that they would deliver something of the same entertainment value with this after the trailers, but it really feels like I got taken for a ride. EDF these days regularly has, like, over a hundred missions in just the base campaign alone, and CWW's missions were made with a FRACTION of the effort and yet still only offers a fraction of the amount, with a fraction of the maps, with a fraction of the gameplay, for a FULL price tag.Avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: CUSTOM MECH WARS

_childDocuments_.review: Its no Armored Core...but its not trying to be. Its not EDF and its not really making any bones about it outside of a generally rather self-serious but silly mood. You don't a D3 game expecting superb quality, you play a D3 game expecting some craziness and fun. I got that in spades.If you want to build some insane mechs with more freedom than almost any game on the market (At least  barring Breakarts which is you should also check out) then this is it and its darn fun. D3 is basically a Kusoge developer and that's their bread and butter. This is pretty nice though.Combat is can be pretty frantic and showy, and on higher difficulties actually pretty difficult. The voice actors  put in work (especially the Special AI which are a treat). Its not the most good looking game, but it looks good enough. The music is serviceable with a couple standouts, and the story? Well its a reason to kill a bunch of robots. Its simple. Much of the game is D3 fare, simple.The Mech Building is why you get this and its top notch and the freedom to make what you want to make is limited mostly by you and your tolerance for working with a somewhat finicky builder. If you have plenty of patience though you can make some wild stuff and there is quite a lot of thoughtfulness as well if you want to head into the higher difficulties. Its not mindless, but it can be pretty silly or really cool. Its up to you. Multiplayer is also frankly insane and if you don't have some friends to play it with....get some. The game is what is advertised.....a mech builder. Lean back, relax, customize, and have some fun.My only complaints are really geometry sometimes getting in the way, and the vehicle leg controls are uh....special. Good buy. will spend hours trying to make random anime units.
