_childDocuments_.review: I love Pinball FX, there really is no competition to this type of thing. There has always been an idea that since pinball is such a physical and tactile game that it wouldn't translate well to digital, and Zen Studios has proven that wrong. The latency is limited by sensors and the speed of electricity, much like a real life pinball cabinet. Sure playing on a mouse/keyboard or controller is going to have less charm than a full-sized cabinet. But they offer a multi-monitor cabinet mode in game and you can BUILD a real cabinet to play this in! Plus each table only costs the equivalent of a few plays on the IRL table. The tables are fantastic, the gameplay is fantastic, and this is only the launch, they have a huge road map for more.A lot of users are tweaked that they bought content in the previous game that came out 6 years ago and they didn't get all that content transferred over to the new game for free. Some users are upset that the developer tried to set up an in-game currency payment system during beta. These users don't care that each table was rebuilt with a new physics core for the new engine or that Zen has to repay for the new licenses. These users don't care that the in-game currency would allow them to play their tables on any platform/console they own and allowed users to mix and match tables instead of buying bulk packs filled with tables they don't want. In short the developer has to cater to the market and the market sucks. These users are so cheap and shortsighted that the developer has made concessions which have made for a typical e-commerce system instead of making this a greater venture. In beta testing, there were bugs that had cost me money. The developer was quick to respond to these bugs, restored my credit and more. The developer let beta users transfer their tables on to whatever console they wanted and they didn't have to. The developer Zen Studios have proved to me, a nobody user, multiple times they care more about the user experience than about money. There is something amazing about that and I am grateful for the incredible game they put out. Zen, please follow your heart and make the best game you can. Ignore the vocal minority!

Nobody is forcing you to buy the DLC tables, AND all the remastered tables are the same price as FX3's version, so if you don't have either, you can just get one of them. Also, in terms of "money grubbing" well, if you bought anything on Epic the company gave away copies of it for any other platform of your choice. I, obviously chose steam. Now onto the product.Pinball FX is a wonderful platform to play pinball on. I got back into pinball because of this game. Sure I played like 3 hours of FX3, but when I found out about FX I jumped ship quickly and never looked back. If you just play this game for the free tables, you'll still have a great time. The rotating free events let you try out a variety of tables every week and the two free tables that everyone gets, Wild West and Sorcerer's Lair are great, and SL is still one of my favourites despite buying a number of DLC tables. The game is constantly getting content updates, and it's up to you if you want to pay for them or not. Finally, my one real complaint is the Pinball Pass. It just doesn't make any sense monetarily. _childDocuments_.review: PROTIP: If you're coming in completely fresh, save this game for a day where you want to play nothing but pinball. You get a 24 hour pass on all the tables when you first boot up the game, enough time to try out all the tables in a no-life cram session.As someone who is just really starting to get into pinball, it's upsetting to see a good game get review bombed because their dlc didn't transfer over to a new game... I don't know of any other game that is getting that much flack for something that no other game or genre is expected to do. It seems the only reason they're getting trashed this time is because when they went from FX2 to FX3 the tables transferred over, but they decided not to do it for their newest offeringI just really want to iterate for the people acting like this is the most horrible and unethical thing a game company can do:-I've never seen another game where people expected the DLC from one installment to transfer over to another.-The previous installment is still available, nothing has been taken away from people who bought tables on FX3. Everything from FX3 is still available to purchase. If you have a problem with re-buying tables on the latest installment, then *don't*. You're not missing anything, and if you own a lot of tables you more than likely are an enthusiast who is using an external launcher to sort your tables anyway, so I seriously have no idea why these people don't just ignore the tables they have and buy just the new tables.-This is a niche genre with a much smaller audience appeal, and not only that, but tables cost money to not only license, but to RENEW the licenses. It's not like Zen Studios bought some kind of "forever" license from Williams or something where they never have to pay a cent to keep selling these tables... so why would the people who purchased dlc on older versions think their version would last forever too? I would think these enthusiasts would realize this and want to support the developer of one of the very few pinball games on the market be able to make enough of a profit to license more tables, but I guess not.-EDIT: Just realized there is a 6 year gap between FX3 and FX. I thought with all of this hub-bub Zen studios was pulling an Activision and making a new game every year or some bullcrap... Holy crap, the people complaining about a new version being made and tables not transferring over are beyond ridiculous.And for anyone who thinks the DLC is pretty pricey, that was my first reaction too... but then I thought about how much an actual table costs, and saw how shoddy some older games were, and thought about their cost at the time of release... and with all that in mind,  the prices are reasonable. Better yet, they go on sale pretty often, and the sale price is great (typically 65% off). Just started getting the sale tables this year, and with about $60 invested I have close to half the DLC on both FX3 and FX. Go back to the early 2000s and see what $60 gets you in virtual pinball (not counting free user-made content of course :p)EDIT: Wanted to make a note about lag. If you're playing on a *real* low end PC and/or digital pinball table, you might have issues and would be better off checking out FX3 if you have issues playing any tables on FX. (I think Legends Pinball for instance might have issues running it, can't really find system specs for that one anywhere but it seems the cheapest and most popular). If you're on a mid-end pc or better, you shouldn't have any issues. I'm on a high end pc with a 2nd monitor in portrait mode, and it runs flawlessly.As far as the actual game goes, I started with FX and typically enjoy it more than FX3, but that said, the physics and the look is definitely different. There are some tables that are more visible and play better on FX3 than FX, so it's not like FX is a complete upgrade and FX3 is obsolete. If you're new and looking to save a few bucks while completing your collection, you can ignore the FX3 tables and not be missing too much (outside of the ones that haven't been ported to FX of course)... that said, as someone who came in fresh on FX I prefer to just buy the FX3/FX legacy bundles while the sales are going so I can get both versions. Also, whenever Pinball FX has a weekly deal, Pinball FX 3 will usually have different tables on sale, so it is worth checking out both stores to get discounts on the legacy packs that apply to both games if you're trying to expand your collection both as quickly and cheaply as possible, even if you are only interested in one version's games (both FX-only and FX3-only players can take advantage of this), as the legacy pack pricing is essentially the same as the solo pricing if you own neither.For newbies wanting to "collect them all" while ignoring duplicates for FX3, here is a list of tables (thanks to Emuser in the FX3 review section) that haven't been ported to FX yet:*Zen Classics Pack: El Dorado, Shaman, Tesla, V12*Sci-Fi Pack: Earth Defense, Mars, Paranormal*Fox Animation (Balls of Glory Pack): Family Guy, Bob's Burgers, Archer, American Dad*Aliens Vs Pinball: Aliens, Alien vs Predator, Alien Isolation*Bethesda Pinball: Skyrim, Doom, Fallout*Valve: Portal Pinball*Telltale Games: The Walking Dead

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:I bought the full Williams back catalog during the sale, now making it that I've purchased Funhouse like 5 times if you count that I bought TPA on mobile and steam, and I bought PFX3 on PC and Switch (read below, I'm a sucker, don't be like me). The lighting and physics changes have bumped it up a notch from a "no meh" to a "yes meh". I play these games all the time, I have a ton of hours on PFX3. I like it ok, but the UI issues are still a pain (one more, if you resize the window to be a vertical top down, it resets back when you go to the table selection, a thing that PFX3 had right, c'mon guys!) I could say its unoptimized like some other reviews because I hear every single fan on my desktop at maximum when this game goes and I'm concerned it's going to fly away, but I don't know enough about optimization to make that call.The pro physics on the Williams games have grown on me, and the "feel" is better, though there's still some cases where you can predict to 98% accuracy what the ball is going to do, because its done that every other time (trust me, this doesn't happen IRL). The lighting looks great, and it uses RTX now, which I've been told is good by marketing. The ports over are very clearly done with a lot of care, in particular I like seeing how the pop bumpers work, they just look right. There's still some weird glitches and things that someone like me doesn't like (Addams Family it consistently does the snap snap with the flippers at the conclusion of the first ball, on a real table this is set to be randomized to happen very rarely so it surprises you. This is such a minor nitpick you shouldn't read this review.)Anyway please Zen, please steal that Stern contract away from zombie Farsight so you can carry over some of their pretty cool new stuff. Or whoever. Lets start to see pins from this century be remade with the same eye for detail you've demonstrated here. Meh plus.ORIGINAL REVIEW:Setting aside the repurchasing DLC issue, which, at least when a pack is on sale and combined with a legacy bundle it feels like a reasonable price, it's an overall meh of an upgrade.Some of the lighting improvements are neat and look good, and are definitively a step up over previous iterations of Pinball FX (having played it since its first iteration). The UI feels a bit kludgy and slow and it feels like a step back from the general cleanilness of PFX3. For example, if you have something selected (e.g. "owned games") and you wrap up the game you were playing, it drops you back in the menu without that filter on. A small thing yes, but this was in early access for a while and is the fourth iteration of a game, this should be much more straightforward! I'm largely playing the Williams games, and overall they're good enough. The more "realistic" physics settings give the ball a bit too much weight in my opinion having played some of the games recently, but maybe you can chalk that up to them trying to simulate a fresh out of the box feeling for these, which obviously I can't access since all these games are 30+ years old.While there's a small handful of "new" to digital release games, the vast majority of their Williams games are ones that were first covered in The Pinball Arcade 10 years ago, which means that I've now been dumb enough to buy the same table several times across multiple platforms. That's more my fault being a sucker though. What I would appreciate is if we finally left the 80s-90s and got more recent licenses from Stern, Jersey Jack or whomever else. People love the 90s games, but it might be time to move on. The Zen originals are and have been largely meh to fine. Most of them have very similar rule sets and scoring that lack a lot of the strategy and depth of contemporary real life pinball machines. As said its a meh. I can't really recommend this to anyone that owns a bunch of PFX3 games unless they're a sucker like me. If you don't have PFX3 or The Pinball Arcade and you want pretty good recreations of beloved Williams/Bally games from the late eighties to mid nineties, sure go get it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is coming from someone who has no history with Pinball or Pinball FX3!I'm happy to see this finally make its debut on Steam (after a year of Epic Games exclusivity)! As a newbie to the Pinball scene, I'd say this is a nice entry. You get a few free tables to start with and then can purchase more tables as DLC; this business model of free game + DLCs makes sense as I doubt they could encase every licensed DLC within a single (reasonable) price, and still make it profitable.The big elephant in the room is that previously, players could transfer their DLCs from Pinball FX2 to Pinball FX3 for free, as those two games ran on the same engine, and thus, there was basically no labour involved to move assets from one entry to another. The problem here is that this title makes the jump to the Unreal Engine, and thus, porting the older tables to this newer game required the devs to do manual work. As such, they're now charging again for these tables, whereas loyal fans are conditioned to expect to be able to transfer their previously purchased tables for free, as they have been able to before. This isn't a problem for new players, but again, fans who have purchased tables before are disappointed.As an outsider looking in, I can understand the frustration; it can be debated whether the graphics were even improved, and thus, whether it worth jumping to a new engine or not in the first place. People don't want to pay for what's essentially same thing twice. On the other hand, I've seen multiple players act as though they MUST purchase the new DLCs. It's not like you're losing access to the tables you purchased 5+ years ago, those are still accessible in the phenomenal Pinball FX3, thankfully. I think expecting DLCs to be transferable isn't necessarily the norm in the gaming industry, so it's unfortunate that Zen Studios have put themselves in this situation where it's expected of them now. The DLC bundles that offer a discount for those who already own the tables from older games are a nice middle-ground, but not one everyone is satisfied with. I'm not sure what an alternative could be.I also think the optimization / performance of this game is a bit questionable. I have to play on lowest settings at 720p to reach 60 FPS on my Steam Deck, which is a bit of a bummer. Perhaps this can be ironed out down the line via updates.As for the game itself, it's Pinball! Lots of tables to checkout, with flashy effects and addictive sound design. I think if you're a newcomer, you'll really enjoy this game (provided you're willing to purchase / rent tables), but if you're a long-time fan, you may only have interest in this game's exclusive tables, and otherwise, you'll likely want to stick to FX3. If previous DLCs were transferable, I'm sure this game would have a much better review score. That's the biggest contention point.

_childDocuments_.review: What's good is pretty good. What's bad is really bad.If you don't have a nearby arcade and aren't willing to mess with hobbyist simulators, FX is the best way to try a lot of great tables. Zen's originals are joyless slogs, with sluggish physics, bad theming, and boring layouts—but their Williams recreations, a solid back-catalog of 80s and 90s pinball, look great and shoot largely well. If you're new to pinball, FX's 1-day trial might hook you on some great games!Unfortunately, FX is also full of rough edges. Every table sounds louder or quieter than the last, balls can bounce or clip out of capture states, mechanical sounds go haywire in certain spots, some tables have ruleset mistakes, and Zen is constantly trying to shove worthless live-service nonsense in your face. Williams alphanumerics are in a particularly rough state: , , and  are some of my favorite tables, and here they sound like a record player inside of a washing machine, all mangled SFX and fluttering pitch.But all of that comes second to the input lag. I run FX at a locked 120FPS, and my PC easily crushes the recommended specs, but the flipper response is substantially slower than other sims. My Steam Deck fares even worse; despite a comfortable 40FPS, the flippers respond so sluggishly that it's not even worth the effort. These tables look great, and I really appreciate that Zen's made them more accessible than ever—but they're simply more fun to play with other software.And that's the crux of it. If you've never played IRL or on other sims, FX is probably a passable introduction to a wonderful hobby. But considering the asking price, it's frustrating that FX is less functional than free hobbyist software—and often less functional than Zen's own FX3!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't bother if you're playing on Steam Deck. The performance is horrendous, the deck gets extremely hot and experiences frame drops and input lag on the lowest settings. The developer has said it is not officially supported on Steam Deck so I guess Pinball FX3 is the only option for now unless the devs change their mind and I don't fancy investing in tables on an old unsupported platform.Update 2024-01-30:The game actually improved in performance later into last year to the point where it was playable on Steam Deck when configured correctly (although still not officially verified). Unfortunately the update released on 8 December 2023 has introduced unacceptable flipper delay. According to my testing with high speed video recording, I measured the average flipper delay (time from pressing the controller button to the flipper beginning to move) at 66.7ms (4 frames @ 60fps) in the old version and 133.3ms (8 frames @ 60fps) in the latest version.This flipper delay is too high for a quick reflex game like pinball. It was acceptable in the previous version @ 66.6ms but you can really feel the delay in the new version @ 133.3ms.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play FX2 on 360 and skipped FX3, so I'm not one of those that are bothered by the fact they had to rebuild their collection. I also bought everything when it was on sale, which helped a lot.As for the new iteration itself, it's pretty solid. Maybe a little heavy in terms of performance, but hey, we got Ray Tracing.There's now a subscription called Pinball Pass for those not wanting to purchase any tables. Personally, I see zero value in it. It's just a rental, and it doesn't even include everything. Just wait for a sale and get any table you want forever.Owning tables also helps with Event mode (a seasonal thing that unlocks cosmetics based on how many event points you have). Free challenges can be accessed by anyone and award one point, whereas Premium challenges award two points and are only available to table owners and Pass holders. I don't think there's anything wrong with having this sort of pay-to-win mechanic, since it's not really a free-to-play game. While you do get three tables for free, all the others are merely free-to-try. That means Pinball FX(4) is very much a paid game that comes with a free trial.Speaking of free trial, the moment you boot into the game for the first time, you automatically activate a 24-hour Pinball Pass that is exclusive to new players, allowing you to fully experience the vast majority of tables (and their rewards) for free. Use this to figure out which of the tables you actually enjoy before making a purchase.As for Tournament mode, I haven't played it.I am not a competitive player, which means I get absolutely no satisfaction from beating other people's scores. All that matters to me is my personal average (on top of just having a good time). I can tell you that it's possible to create custom tourneys using your own set of rules though.Do I recommend FX4?Well, it's hard to say no to 3 free tables. Install size is 30+ GB though.If you're thinking of getting FX3 instead, do be aware that that game is no longer being updated with new tables.There is also no cross-buy. Any table you buy over there, you will have to repurchase in FX(4).So yeah, unless you're already on FX3, I recommend going with FX(4) instead.It's not perfect, but neither is FX3. At least FX(4) is still being worked on, so there's hope for better optimization and more QoL improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Pinball FX (PFX) is technically Pinball FX 4, a modernisation of Pinball FX 3 (FX3), built this time in Unreal Engine 4. It includes 3 free tables and dozens of paid tables, split between Zen original designs and classic Bally/Williams arcade simulations. There is also a sister product ("Pinball M") which provides "mature" (horror, blood) themed pinball tables, containing 1 free table, and licensed original designs.At its initial (Steam) release, this was a NO recommendation.Firstly, the Steam release was delayed by a year due to exclusivity on Epic Games Store, despite FX3 already being on Steam for some years. Secondly, it wasn't entirely clear why we needed a new major version: performance wasn't great and the UI was inferior to its predecessor. Loading times were (and are) inexplicably long. The supposed "remastering" looked mostly like more of the same. Zen even managed to "remaster" the same bugs without substantially improving tables or addressing old issues.Oh, and customers had to re-buy their tables... But since then Zen has improved the product somewhat. Performance is better and some quality of life changes have been added. Importantly, they've provided deep discounts on almost all tables through weekly and seasonal sales. There's a LOT of value here.The long loading times remain however, and the UI is still somewhat janky.Late 2023 verdict: recommended, with the expectation that Zen will continue to improve PFX.

Wish they'd release them on FX3 too.I was waiting with my review because I wanted to give this game a chance and cool down a bit. It's probably a good game for new players that didn't own any previous titles from ZEN. But in my opinion it's more bad than good, especially for the older community!

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise, still the best digital pinball without question.  Business model-wise, the transition to Unreal engine was not the best but far from the disaster others seem to think.  For starters, the subscription model is not required, it's just one option.  You can buy the tables outright like previous FX entries if you want, so it's nice to have the choice between the two approaches.Second if you have FX3 tables on Steam, you can of course just continue to play FX3.  But there is a "Legacy Bundle" for all of the old tables if you own the FX3 version which contains both FX3 and FX versions with a 50% discount.  So since you already have the FX3 version, you pay for just the new one at a 50% discount.Yes it sucks they don't give them to you for free, but also understandable as they had to expend time and resources to port them over to a completely different engine.  A 50% discount for the new versions is reasonable IMO and you can of course wait for sales for a further discount (they were already part of the past summer sale).All told, yeah there were some bumps with the migration to the new engine but it's not the total disaster some people seem to think IMO.  And since launching the new version, the Williams license has also brought us Addams Family, Twilight Zone, and now Star Trek TNG which are absolutely incredible classic tables, in addition to all the ones FX3 has.  I'd still recommend this new Pinball FX, especially if you're new to the platform and don't have money invested in the previous version.

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been an easy win.  A new version with a ton of new tables, The fans of PInball FX 3 would have ushered in a new era of pinball and everyone would be happy to play PInball.  Zen Studios are usually on the top of their game when it comes to pinball, while a little more arcade like physics that only enhances the experience, and produces a better game.But this has been mishandled.  First this was released first on Epic.  That wouldn't be so bad, Epic helped make this, sure it gets first dibs on it.  But for a year,  PInball FX 3 has languished with almost no content outside of a few tables, while this got updated.  Well eventually it would come to steam, great.Now it arrives and people who have supported Zen since Pinball FX2, over ten years get.... a day of free pinball, and the ability to buy ALL the tables again.   Literally every table you owned on Pinball FX3 is not honored here, and they want you to buy them again.   The SAME table that you already owned need to be repurchased at the same price if you want to move it here.  But let's give Zen a chance to respond here. "But don't worry we'll give you those games for half price if you own them already*"   Ehh not great, but... sounds ok.    WAit what's the asterisk there mean?   "Well we can't just give you a deal on the tables, that's not fair."   Sounds fair to me, but ok how does this work."   "You get them at half price if there's a bundle offered, but not every game will have a bundle"  Wait what?   "And the bundles aren't on the main page but hey, it's half price."    But that's still half as much as I already spent... and buying those tables at full price the first time was hefty, you have 380 dollars of DLC even at half price that's 190 dollars.  "I know isn't it great!!!!  You can pay us even more."    Yeah, I don't know about that. "Well don't worry we have a new pinball pass"... Ok, what's that?  "It's a way to play all the tables for free*" ... what's that little asterisk there... "Oh well it's not all the tables... just some of the tables.  But that's great".... Uhhhh ok, this doesn't sound great, but it says in game currency, so you can earn your way to play the tables?   "Nope!"   Well ok, how much is it?   "15 bucks a month!"  Wait what?  that's a price of a brand new set of tables..  "Maybe you want to do a year long subscription."  Maybe.....  " 100 dollars..."  That's too much "You're right! 99.99 dollars" Seriously you guys.... "Yup but this way you don't get to keep it..."   That's not a good deal then .  "What do you mean?  OH and better news you can purchase in game currency in different amounts to help confuse you so you might spend more or feel the need to keep buying them."   Wait that's ALSO not a good thing.  "Of course it is.. it means you spend more money and own nothing.  It's a great thing for us."Ugh well tell me what else you have.   "What do you think about... Events that don't feel like they have a strong purpose.."   Well what's the point of them.  "You can earn Collectibles from our season mode.   You get progressive items over time."  Uhhh that's just a battle pass.  "YEah but you don't have to pay for it."  Well that's good.  "You just have to pay for the tables to earn the tokens."  Ugh.. . "And since it's timed content, we get FOMO to keep you playing."  Seriously... what....   "And FOMOmeans you pay more and play more, but not the modes you like the modes we select."  Please stop talking.   "Don't worry the collectables are cosmetic, they don't affect anything, they're just so you can decorate the starting room, you know the place you never really look."  You're not helping yourself.  "Wait we got one more thing I'm sure you're going to love."   I don't know why I'm doing this to myself, but sure, let's give it one more shot...   "PREMIUM COLLECTIBLES ONLY PURCHASABLE BY IN-GAME CURRENCY!" ....  "You there... you there buddy?"Let's summarize this... You need to repurchase the tables you already own, the discount is only 50 percent off and that's ONLY if they choose to offer it, There's FOMO mechanics to keep you playing, if you don't own a table, you're just grinding the three free tables if they offer it.  Same problem with tournaments if you don't own the table. A Pinball pass which is just pure greed, a premium collectibles, in game currency made to be confusing, and this game was released on Epic first for a year And yet this STILL might have worked, but here's the sad truth, the tables feel almost exactly the same as they did on Pinball FX3, so there's no way I can recommend this game in good conscious.  Even if you don't own Pinball FX 3, you might think you can just start collecting tables here...  But  what happens when they decide to make another sequel and all your purchases go away yet again.   The bad news is the studio I respected and felt dealt with their fans honorably is now gone.  But the good news is I don't have to sit here and be reminded of how far they've fallen every time I boot up their game. I'm sorry Zen Studios there's too much here that makes me distrust you.  Pinball pass, Season mode...  I'm off to get my pinball fix elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Very short summation for most people: If you have not bought anything from Zen before and also like Pinball, this will be a great buy for at least a couple of years, just don't try to collect them all because less than a decade later they will expect you to spend another few hundred dollars to get the exact same things again if you want to use their "updated" version. Nah, just ends up they moved to a new engine. I played their own their own game Adventureland on Pinball FX 3, and then played it on the new game to see the differences. If you didn't take a screen shot, most players would think it's the same thing.-- Changed review rating based on developer feedback, saying they have Legacy bundles. While I'm not exactly thrilled about just 50% off, it's better than the 33% I originally read about. That means I can get the ones I really care about and just wait for a super sale on the ones that are just "meh." So here's the part where I get annoyed. I just bought their Indiana Jones table less than a year ago for $15. Now they want me to buy the exact same table again for the same price. I have all 99 tables before that bought as well because I love playing pinball. Their statement was "well, hopefully we'll wait a while and then give people who have already bought this the option to buy it again at 33% off."  Maybe I would find that understandable if it were a $60 game and I just had to pay $40 rather than the full amount and got all my boards back. Just make sure to keep an eye on your g-card temps when using this version (i recommend MSI afterburner, been using it for decade's, lets you see cpu/gpu temps and control gpu fan speed). The only con id say about this version that i experience is that the game will sometime's reset what i have the nudge control set to, back to default which is annoying and happens every so often (i like to play with right ctrl set as my middle nudge). Other then that the game runs perfectly fine for me.Thumbs up from me, has provided me with lots of fun, moments where i yelled BS, cried no no no, and raised my hands up in victory from getting a score in the top 100 or higher. Definitely fun to be had here in my opinion.Oh and one last little timbit of info. This version (pinball FX) and pinball M are the one's zen is still releasing new pinball table's for. _childDocuments_.review: My Love/Hate relationship with Zen has really been all over the map lately, but they finally have FX running really well on my older hardware and finally got rid of a weird lag / frame pacing issue that has been plaguing the game since release.I use my PC to run "OTG" mode through my Legends 4KP which has been flawless with FX3 but FX just wasn't right. Not sure if AtGames changes fixed it in the hardware or if Zen just made it run better, but I can finally enjoy all the newer tables. Even the plunger works fluidly now. Glad I no longer have to resort to playing the still horribly optimized native versions of the tables you can run on the 4KP. Because they both are running on the same engine I'm hoping this means those native tables will finally run lag free soon. Anyway good job Zen on optimizing the PC version after I was starting to lose hope.As a reward I'm picking up some new tables that are conveniently on sale rn :)Anyone who was struggling with it on modest hardware (I run a vanilla 2080 with an ancient amd proc) you should try it again after the overhaul. Could be surprised how it runs now.The old "bittter pill" review:Im going to give Zen a pity recommend here. I too got burned amassing tables across different platforms and versions that dont unlock anything here but maybe a discount. I get that remastering these tables is not a free endeavor for the developers but the business model used so far has taught us all an important lesson that has likely hurt their image greatly. We know that any money we drop now on content can considered lost when the next version comes out and we are expected to "upgrade" to the new "experience".They almost had a great idea with the pinball pass, but their execution left everyone feeling duped. With a proper license model you would have rights to whatever tables you had purchased previously whether console or PC with the option to upgrade each license for a nominal fee to use newly remastered editions of the game. The new FX product would then contain the engines of FX3 and FX Update, and have common presentation and controls models for both. FX would evolve instead of having iterative updates. Players who arent ready to update to the latest versions wont feel pressured, and those who want to keep pace with new and remastered tables have the option to do so.Anyway I feel bad for the team at Zen as likely the team members recently let go likely had no say in the monetization strategy the company went with. Im hoping they are working on a new strategy to win back people who feel left behind with the way things are now. I am a pinhead and a junkie for everything digital pinball. I even pre-purchased the new physical table coming from AtGames in partnership with Zen. I wish the studio well, but I can relate to having management at complete odds with the realities of the world today and know how hard it can be to course correct.That said, about the new product:It seems to be all about the gloss while missing many no brainer functions like remappable controls and digital to analog support for the plunger. Its also much more demanding hardware wise and forced me to upgrade to a RTX 2080 vanilla to get 2K @165hz. Sadly 165hz is not supported in their framerate lock so have to run at 144hz.Once you have all your settings optimized it runs rather well. Low latency setting for Nvidia cards and turning off all vsync, relying on gsync helps with flipper lag and feel. I run in cab mode, portrait with separate backglass monitor and can finally say its almost as good as with FX3.The tables themselves are really gorgeous, but the sound improvements really should be mentioned as well with much better samples and booming sounds like in Twilight Zone captured perfectly. I have only repurchased a few of my favorite Williams tables here and the vast majority of my library will likely remain in FX3 only unless they go on a massive sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played many different pinball programs and I've found the zen pinball FX series to be the easiest to install and play with the most tables to choose from. Programs like Visual Pinball and others take time to adjust settings and get things right for a less captivating experience, while other games like pinball arcade couldn't keep the licenses. Keep in mind when I play I'm only interested in tables that exist physically, and I just couldn't get into the original tables, no matter how much I enjoy Star Wars and Marvel. The table layouts just don't feel natural to me and it rubs me the wrong way. Now I'm most likely just nit-picking and I'm sure many customers get lots of hours of play from them so I'm probably the outlier. I already owned most of the Williams tables on Pinball FX3. It was a blow to hear that we would have to re-buy tables, but I'm not surprised that it happened. Regardless, I jumped in full boat and bought all the Williams tables, reading that the devs would be adding additional tables as time went on, for which I have not been disappointed thus far. I've been happy to pick up Addams Family, Bride of Pinbot, and more. The graphics are a bit off compared to FX3, which worked flawlessly without any adjustments on my end. Most important thing I can bring to point is that if the flippers seem laggy or feel weak when you use them, turn the v-sync option off in video settings. You may need to tinker with settings to make everything look the best you can, but overall I'm satisfied with FX. As long as they keep classic Williams tables coming I'll continue to collect them. Wish they could grab some iconic Stern tables as well, but from what I can tell that can easily turn into a nightmare and I'd rather go without than to have the licensing issues that other devs have run into. My only solid gripe with the game is they spent so much time working on the menus that It takes extra time just to get into a game and when you finish you can't just jump back into the next one. I can fully understand people not wanting to re-buy tables, but if you're new, definitely download the game and give the free trials a play.

_childDocuments_.review: I have little issue with the game itself, if it would work. But for the life of me I can't get it to work under a very common version of Linux, in combination with an Intel Arc, even though it should work on Steam Deck (which runs SteamOS, which is based on Linux) and the Arc-drivers have been updated a lot and are even implemented into the version of Linux I use natively now.What happens is, with some versions of Proton, like the latest and Experimental I believe, the game will launch, but not a single table will launch once and it will just freeze immediately as soon as you hit "start", with the image freezing on the menu's showroom. - I got way further with a Radeon-GPU from 2018 (the Arc I use now is from 2023), where tables would launch and play and stay relatively stable, though still crashed the game the same way perhaps 1 out of 3 to 5 times.Also, now it will give an error from the Unreal Engine with older versions of Proton, which it didn't before (with the older Radeon).Why is it so hard to get this game to run when, on my main computer (this one is for a Pinball-cabinet), which has the same chipset, a newer but similar CPU, a Radeon-GPU, and runs Linux as well, can run just about any game, even ones that are way more complex, as well as PinballFX without a problem??It's absolutely baffling to me. - Maybe it's an Unreal thing and/or just slight deviations between the two computers, but I just can't believe that this game is the most problematic out of the hundreds I've played through Linux and Proton. It just straight-up refuses on multiple distros and clean installs. - I've built this computer for just pinball-games and the major one won't run... I'm disappointed and at a loss...Edit: I should mention, I've also tried GloriousEggroll, but while there is a slight progression, in that it will actually go to the loading-screen upon selecting a table, it will start lagging/freezing there and at some point just stop, then crash to some "LowLeverError"-prompt.What's more, while it finally shows the little video-previews of the tables when selecting them, which it doesn't without GE (but instead show one of those "test-screens" with the colored bars, probably because there's an issue with connecting the video-files), it will also freeze quickly when just browsing a little, which it didn't even do without GE.I did see some people getting this game to work using GE, but perhaps it needs more configuring that I don't know about.

_childDocuments_.review: It's always disappointing to come across a product that fails to meet expectations, and unfortunately, Pinball FX, which was released today on Steam after one year of being exclusive to Epic, is one such game. The main reason for my disappointment is the exorbitant price tag for each individual table, especially considering that this is a game that was released over a year ago.To put things into perspective, Pinball FX received a lot of money from Epic to give them exclusivity in 2022, and now, in 2023, when the game finally arrives on Steam, its tables are being sold at an exorbitant price point that is simply not worth it.It's clear that the developers are trying to take advantage of the hype surrounding the game, but it's a disrespectful move towards the loyal fans who have been eagerly awaiting the official release (you know what I mean).Overall, Pinball FX falls short in several critical areas, making it difficult to recommend to players who are looking for an affordable and enjoyable pinball gaming experience. While the game has some redeeming qualities, such as its initial free download and some interesting table designs, the lack of appreciation for loyal customers and the high cost of additional tables is a major drawback that should not be overlooked. As such, players would be better off sticking with Pinball FX3, which offers a more solid experience at a much lower cost.
_childDocuments_.name: Pinball FX

_childDocuments_.review: After a bumpy birth, Pinball FX's debut on steam is off to a strong start. The Williams tables especially are of high quality. Great physics, great graphics, and integrated cabinet mode. They play exceedingly well, and I look forward to future releases. There are more improvements to be made, but it's off to a great start.Initially a 1-year exclusive on another platform, tables were only purchasable in-game with tickets, The benefit of this was ostensibly cross-platform play, but the downside is that players would have been locked into the developers eco-system. Over the course of a year, and a lot of negative feedback, the developer changed their approach to allow direct-DLC purchases after it debuted on steam as they had on previous iterations of their pinball games. Players that purchased tables on other platforms were given a 1-time form to fill out to transfer tables to a single platform of their choice. Likewise, steam will detect if you own a table on Pinball FX3 and give users a 50% off credit to purchase the license for Pinball FX.

_childDocuments_.review: [EDIT:  Why did no one complain about having to re-buy Civilization when Civ 2-6 came out?  What about all the Dooms?  What about all the upgraded graphics versions of older classics that end up not being as good as the original?  Why don't people complain that they should get all that free again too? FX is a new engine and when they upgrade old tables to it it is because people love those tables and wants to see them look (and play) their best.   You don't want to pay up?  Fine.  Why pound the company with negative reviews that do not reflect the quality of the product?  You are punishing them for improving their products because they satisfied your pinball addiction in the past.  Krazy.]I have and liked all the PinballFX games and many many of the tables.   I do regularly upgrade my gaming machine so the hardware needed for Pinball FX was not a big leap for me.. already had it.  Re-buying favorite old tables... hard pill to swallow buy swallow it I did.  Now I don't think about it.  I will not be buying their new "mature" collection of games through Zen's new Pinball M game... which, I assume, is a Pinball FX copy that allows some control of content for kids access.. kids want pinball.. buy em FX and not M.Here are the recommended specs for Pinball M and, I assume, Pinball FX.. and, I assume, to run at 1080p.  I suppose you'd need some work to guess what specs you need for 1440 or 4K.  Raytracing is probably not worth it... get the frame rate up because things move fast.  DLS could help (you run game a, say, 1080 and video card upscales in hardware to your monitor's resolution... not sure about AMD's "dls".16GB ramRequires a 64-bit processor and operating systemProcessor: Intel Core i7-7700K or Ryzen 5 1600Graphics: Nvidia 2060 RTX or AMD RX 5600 XTI like it.   To do it on a budget.. read reviews for the best tables and buy them in collections when they go on sale.  Sales seem pretty frequent.  For instance, this week they have a couple tables for less than $4 ea.  That's not bad... if its a good table that you will play.   I am not a fan of subscriptions but if I was the owner of Zen or its CEO, I'd love subscriptions.  You have a regular monthly income (within some range of new subscribers and those who drop) and you can know what you have to spend on talent and new IP for new table creation.  Make your payroll.  I have seen people complain about having to re-buy their tables.  I wonder if they have considered what work is needed to move the already developed table under FX2 or FX3 to FX.  There is a lot of work to do.  It is a newer engine what new capabilities.. new physics.  It make look similar.. it may play similar.. it will sound similar... but what you are paying for is a newly "enhanced" version.Even if you do not want to do that I don't see why you have to give a bad review to Pinball FX.   Would you rather Zen run with a skeleton staff that occasionally adds a new game and hopes you will buy it?  Forever at the whim of what they can sell?  If you want a company that takes pinball simulation seriously and delivers a good product.. you have to make it economically feasible for them to do it... help them stay in business and enable them to bring us new tables like South Park ($10 - I have to say I may wait for that one to go on sale.. I can wait months for that.. or just pay the $10 now).I like Pinball FX.  I think the pricing is fair.  Opinions vary.

_childDocuments_.review: As a pinball fan, and owner of TPA (The Pinball Arcade), and FX3, here is a fairly in depth comparison. While I certainly enjoyed FX3 with its unique tables and creations, there is no question many were incredibly easy with the floaty physics of the balls. Tables like Doom, while very fun, were almost impossible to lose. When it came to the reproductions of classic tables such as Williams, it usually fell short of TPA by a margin. The physics always felt off, and while it made for a fun pinball game, it fell quite short of a pinball simulation. This new Pinball FX claims improved physics and graphics, not to mention Ray Tracing, which can be hard for some hardware, though it runs pretty smoothly on my laptop and its 2080 Super. So what is best?Since this is a selling point, I compared all three for feel, but to avoid falling into personal biases, I brought up actual video recordings on YouTube and used them as a reference. Frankly, FX is the winner here, and it shows up in the reactions of the ball, but also small things like falling through the hole in a slide on Arabian Nights. TPA is not far behind in some tables but not all. Curiously, TPA actually has some off-flippers and angles of flippers on some tables. I had no idea of this until observing the genuine video footage. So a win for FX overall. TPA seems to have a lighter incline on all the tables so it is hard to know exactly, and I always found TPA very solid overall.This is going to come as a surprise but while FX has the potential to be the clear best, its graphics and lighting need serious tweaking. The table lights (using  to compare) are overly bright, creating exaggerated shadows. Some tables have outright wrong colors such as Arabian Nights. The lights near the bumpers are white instead of the actual yellow, as well as those around the table. The overall result is a much colder color scheme than the real table. What about Ray Tracing? Frankly, it is a serious disappointment as implemented for now. Side-by-side screenshots with it on and off show that the only visible result is a sharp increase in contrast, so darker areas are darker, effectively making the lights brighter by comparison. However, multi-point shadows and reflections and light bouncing is non-existent. So all you really get with RT is a darker table with deeper shadows. At least with the simulated Williams tables.In terms of simulated tables of old, TPA has an overwhelming edge still, with many many classics such as Firepower I and II, High Speed, and others, but TPA is a dead end, and WYSISWYG. FX is clearly very much alive not only for original creations (I had a hoot with the Snoopy table), but new classics are also being added. I read another user complaining about a mistaken magnet in Addams, but I have not tried it and cannot comment.Much like its predecessor, FX has a ton of added effects, such as flying scores, special effects and more. These can all be tailored to taste so that your game experience, if using a classic table, will not be distracted by these. However, they are a nice touch, no arguments.This is a very personal thing, so I will refrain from passing judgement. If you had tables from FX3, then you get them at 50% off here. I don't know what the cost in the US is, as I live in Brazil, but the average for the tables or bundles has been between $3-6. YMMV.Right now, it stands as the best overall pinball experience for new tables and pure physics, but there are definitely areas to improve such as fixing the RT so it actually does more than deepen shadows, as well as fix the colors of lights and the general brightness of them. This is the only serious complaint I have, but it detracts from the overall impression. 4/5 for now, but should the above be handled, then I will gladly rectify this to a 5/5.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing lighting with HDR and Raytracing and most tables just look better all around. We now have proper portrait mode and all new tables will only be available in the new platform and not FX3. Zen actually communicated this very clearly many times, but I guess not everyone got the message. Devs have to eat, too.Yes, there are inconsistencies in that some Williams tables like Black Rose have a highly spammable center broadside shot (not present in FX3 where it is a lot harder to hit) and many Williams tables play easier than they did in FX3 (and I would argue easier than real life as well). There are exceptions though, Space Station is still hard as is Dr. Dude and Whitewater. We still need custom cameras and multiplayer Battle Royale mode added as promised and we need VR (due to come out this year) but we are well on our way folks. Ignore the haters and grab this game! And hey, you have three free-to-play tables including Fish Tales, so what have you got to lose? Free one day Pinball Pass as well so you can play everything and see what is worth it to you. Another hit against the haters!

_childDocuments_.review: I was an early adopter of Pinball FX on Epic during early access and on Steam since the Steam release. Unlike some reviews you might read here, I have a legitimate 500 hours of active playtime across Epic Games and Steam platforms. While I have over 1000 hours on Pinball FX3, this is not the focus of this review. Here’s what you can expect for the first 24 hours after you install the game:For FREE, you get fully unlocked versions of Williams Fish Tales, a western-themed table called Wild West Rampage, and the fan-favorite Sorcerer’s Lair. Complete the tutorial and get a FULL DAY of UNLIMITED ACCESS to ALL TABLES except for Marvel. This is a taste of the Pinball Pass subscription service (which is 100% optional - you can still buy packs of tables and own them outright).Play the 25 new Williams and Zen Orginal tables added since Pinball FX was released on Epic Games early access.Try out the Events that let you experience a range of tables for FREE in different play modes. Often, this is a full three-ball gameplay experience, just like if you owned the table.Because you completed the tutorial and got the Pinball Pass for 24 hours, you get access to premium Events. Even if you come from Pinball FX3 and are unsure whether rebuying the tables is worth the investment, you can still have a lot of fun with Pinball FX after the free Pinball Pass expires. Play an ever-changing selection of pinball in different game modes for free each day. And you don’t have to pay a single cent to do it if you don’t mind being fed tables to play rather than being able to choose what you play.What have you got to lose?Here are some extra points you might not be aware of if you are new to Pinball FX on Epic or Steam.This is a longer read, but it will hopefully give you some counter-arguments to consider when you browse the other perspectives about the game.Why can’t I buy tables outright instead of subscribing to Pinball Pass?Despite what some say in their reviews, you don't have to subscribe to the Pinball Pass. Every table is available to buy outright on the platform of your choice. If you own tables on Pinball FX3, you will get a huge discount on those legacy tables you already own.The studio still participates in Steam events, where they apply steep discounts to table packs so you can build up your library when your budget allows.Start with your favorites and then mop up the rest as they come on sale! On the subject of having to rebuy tables you might already own in FX3, it may seem the studio is making a blatant cash grab at face value. But if you’ve been along for the ride since Early Access, like me, you can see why they somehow had to cover the immense cost of retooling.Many license holders (very big entertainment companies) need to get paid, and bringing all the tables to the new engine wasn't an easy feat. It took a lot of development hours to do it. They've even redesigned the ball and flipper physics for all the older tables to make them behave more like real pinball machines.Letting tables transfer to the new game for free again after all these years simply wasn't an option. Why did they have to upgrade to Unreal?The earlier engine in Pinball FX3 (the PX Engine) was limiting what the devs could do with the game and what platforms they could release the game on without having to do heaps of custom work.The studio needed to port all their tables to UE4 to remain relevant and ready for the future. The devs confirmed that the PX engine was becoming a nightmare for new projects such as the Williams tables with alphanumeric displays.The move to Unreal Engine 4 unlocks heaps of possibilities for the studio. For example, the move made it possible to have LCD scoreboards with video content in the game. These work like those on modern Stern, Spooky, Jersey Jack, and Chicago Pinball machines. A handful of new tables in the game already have them; it is quite the visual upgrade. You won't see a dot-matrix display (DMD) again in any new Zen Original. The Unreal Engine allows the game to access Ray Tracing, HDR, SDR, and DLSS. SDR and DLSS are technologies that let you render the game in a lower resolution and then upscale it depending on the specs of your GPU.You get a performance boost with barely any quality loss. SDR is available on AMD and Nvidia cards. These upscaling technologies can be very helpful if you have an earlier Nvidia or AMD card that doesn't support DLSS. There's also Nvidia Reflex as an option in the settings, which allows for incredibly low input delay. Since I've been using Nvidia Reflex, my scores have increased exponentially. It makes the game feel incredibly responsive, making it easier to hit your shots.Events keep you coming backThe events in the game are new to Pinball FX, and they offer a very competitive and entertaining experience. They offer limited attempts on a selection of tables, so you can’t overplay, and it keeps competition fairer. The collectibles and trophies you get for doing well in events that you can place in your game room, profile banner, and tournament room are a nice extra. You also get profile customization rewards like banners and backgrounds as you play through the Event seasons. There are some really entertaining new modes that you can play in both single-player (for owned tables) and Events. For example, the 200 flips challenge mode is very exciting to see if you can get a super jackpot or even beat a wizard mode within 200 flips. It challenges you as a player to change your play style to achieve different goals.SummaryBy the end of 2023, the total number of new releases should be at 25 tables. The tables include a selection of Zen unlicensed and licensed themes and several Williams tables. I have been over the moon with the Williams releases this year. They all play realistically, and are some of the best real world tables ever created by Bally and Williams. It is true that a couple of tables still have some bugs, but the team has been fixing them as they patch and update the game regularly. And they don’t seem to be slowing down.

When I first got my hands on this product masquerading as a game I was disappointing that I had to buy the DLC again (especially after already having made the jump from Switch FX3 to Steam FX3), even moreso when I found out my favourite zen original from FX3 hadn't even made the cut yet. _childDocuments_.review: Really bad input lag and occasional stutters in both menus and game. The graphics are somehow darker and look worse than FX3 in some parts. The whole experience maybe besides the physics feels a step down from FX3. I understand the company needs to make money and can't give out the tables you already own for free on each platform but that's only justified if the platform is actually better not worse. The only thing I like so far about the new FX is the soothing menu music that actually quells my dissapointment.I commend Zen for being able to port the tables to UE4 and kept the looks and physics consistent but the Unreal Engine has inherent issues besides presenting pretty graphics and this game suffers from them too.A few improvements I would like to see are...- Less input latency.- Ability to set the render scale to 200% so I can have smoother graphics without blurry post processing anti-aliasing.- FPS limit being a slider you can set from like 30-240 or something.- Improve the looks and smoothness of the menus. They look bad and stutter right now.- Reduce overall stutters during gameplay, camera movement and animations.- Improve sound and positioning. Some tables sound pretty bad and the volume is all over the place.
_childDocuments_.name: Pinball FX

_childDocuments_.review: For good electronic Pinball, Zen Studio's really your only option. The problem is the company knows this and has decided to rip off the player base. Unlike the original FX series your purchased tables aren't going to make the jump here unless you pay for them again - so if you already own FX3, just stick with that. The graphics and physics are no better in this new FX. On top of that the download size is huge because you need to front-load all of the tables for DEMO advertisement. No, trials are no longer optional like in FX3. You also can't set the view of the boards for sections like launch bumpers leading to guesswork if the default overhead is obscured or the text is small. The best they'll let you do is set a pan up/zoom out or pan down/zoom in once, before you start the game which becomes your view for the whole game. Overall, this is a downgrade from what they've had in the past and shows just how much they no longer care about their fans. Best advice would be to back up your copy of FX3 before they take that away and you lose your money already spent on tables for good.

_childDocuments_.review: Asking users to re-buy tables is ZEN's problem not ours. I get the tables have to be redone and that is not free, but couldn't there have been a way to give a one time discount coupon (via Steam) on previously owned tables? I understand they moved engines because it's easier to make tables in the new engine. Okay, but does allowing users to assign custom button or controller inputs really hard? My virtual machines are set up to use the Dpad for nudge. You can not change that in the controller menu. It has to be the R or L stick. I would recommend Pinball FX 3 if you're a Virtual Pinball enthusiast. You have options for inputs. Better yet Zaccaria Pinball is incredible for CAB and VR Pinball fans. 1 game does it all with unlimited customisation when it comes to controller inputs.Until the controller customisation can be 100% customizable, it's a no from me.

These buttons make one or more flippers go up or down.Could someone please explain to me, how the devs managed to screw this up? I play this on a Steam Deck and the input lag costs me most balls. _childDocuments_.review: Here it is : If you are a prior player of the other titles in the series and Zen's business model irks you, then you will not like this game. If, on the other hand, you give eff-all about the money and are only concerned with how good the game actually is, then you will love it. 3 Hour Update : It's still Pinball. It's still fine. It's still pricey for those who care. I don't care. Am I a bad person? Prolly. I own many of the FX3 tables. But there are tables that only appear in FX, so I'll buy those. It's that simple. I know people have a right to complain about getting humped in the wallet. But a negative review based solely on that aspect is biased and says nothing about the game itself. FX is great.

With the latest Pinball FX, though, it's end of the road for me. My mid-range gaming/pinball PC runs most games just fine at medium or better settings, but this game is simply unplayable even at the lowest graphics settings. _childDocuments_.review: Do I like Pinball FX3 more? Yes, but I still recommend this game. If you are new to the series or pinball, I'd recommend Pinball FX over FX3 because it now comes with 3 free tables.  Pinball FX is the flagship game Zen is moving forward with, so it wouldn't make sense for a newcomer to start the series with the older FX3.If you are a returning veteran from Pinball FX3 and have gripes about having to re-purchase tables, well then only purchase the new offerings. There are plenty of other things here to complain about.I agree that is a little lame that you have to repurchase tables if you want to play them in FX, but Zen is not a non-profit. To me the value of this game is in it's new tables, so I don't see this as the pinball equivalent of dropping $$ on a  yearly EA sports game just to get a roster update.   The FX/FX3 bundles are a partial answer to the re-purchasing tables gripes. However, those are a very specific consumer case. It seems like they were only targeted to players who still play FX3, but haven't yet purchased certain tables.  For that player base, it is a value add. I was in that category, so it helped pull me into the new FX. I have no plans to re-purchase any of the remaining tables that did not transfer.My gripes:(Performance)I have a pretty decent rig, but most of my steam library is on external HDDs. I noticed some performance issues in Pinball FX (2023) where frames seem to drop. That is a no-no for a game that is all about precision timing. If you can't predict the path of the ball because it seemed to freeze and then warp a few frames ahead. Maybe just a hiccup. I tweaked some settings to try and avoid it.Not a deal breaker immediately, but definitely a concern I want to be confident my setting tweaks have resolved before I go buying a lot of new tables here. (still intermittent at the moment)(Install Size)Pinball FX3 is 100 tables at ~7Gb. Pinball FX in 120 tables and ~36GB.Pinball FX may have better textures and higher polygon models, and perhaps an “improved” engine.I did a comparison between FX3 and the new FX for the Sorcerer's Lair table.  I could tell there was a significantly higher poly count on the Sorcerer, but depending on your table view preferences and settings, the improvements may not be very noticeable. However, the slower loading times are.(Interface)I feel like they went for sleek and sexy style.  It just doesn't vibe well with me.(Achievements) It doesn't have per-table achievement with the exclusion of some new tables.  They all need achievements.  There are "table rewards" which offer unlockable display items. These are effectively the old table achievements, but they aren't tracked by steam.(Physics)I'm sure it is more real now, but it makes gameplay feel inconsistent.  I think this is just something I need to get used to.  Shots I expected to hit 100% on FX3 tables are now much more difficult in FX.

_childDocuments_.review: This title is very controversial so a bit more investigation was needed and alternate view from the dominating 'why are we paying AGAIN for the tables'. For me start situation is indeed 'Why pay?', so i installed to check what else is there and ignored the ones i owned, except the free tables just to compare and setup video best as i could. Regarding that: Frame rates and steady game play may not be perfect right out of the box. Had to adjust settings a bit lower as stuttering was seen. I got a 2060. Not the worst card out there but then on the other hand a game like this should not require the top cards out there. As for tables themselves they look great. Physics engine is different and older tables look sharp and nice. Albeit will stress your gear so dont even think about playing this on too old hardware. Disk size? Old FX3 that is chock full of tables at 7.3gb. This one is 33.9gb. As for reasons to buy or not buy: - 'We want free/90% discounted tables if we own it before' : This is a major point but looking at FX it is obvious this is not going to happen. Just look at FX rise historically: Started with Tesla and V12 and those basic tables sold cheap. That was then, no licensing fees and a hunger to become a name. Then came those Zen originals that really started the upswing: Pasha, Biolab, Rome, Castlestorm etc followed by the early tide of licensed Marvel games and Star Wars and people begged for more. Well they got some but for some reason many still expect this stuff to be as cheap as the early stuff is. It won't. Licensing in the corporate world goes like flipping a coin -> Heads: You win. Pay me. Tails: You lose, Pay me anyway. - 'For me the series ends here' being said in the forums. It is a valid claim for some. Tempting for me too to say that. But no. New players will NOT be enticed to play a Tesla or V12 table in 2023 - The competition is out there now so this means a race to get the attention. Debatable if this is the right choice but still... - So to whom is this meant for?  New players. Not old ones. Some of the old ones may even be defecting to the competitors so not concentrating on them is a probable business strategy here. Remains to be seen if there is enough of those newbies to bring enough money to get out from the red.  I can see myself buying some of the stuff here making strategic picks here and there using their 'coin' system which in the store translates to approx same pricing as before (expensive). My FX3 tables have not been cheap lately either so i can't be too angry here about hiding the cost behind a coin system. We are not talking here full blown 'surprise mechanics' at least not yet so i'll let it slide...  So... buy according to what tickles your the most. Zen is betting the farm on new people. They must. Enjoy the ride or don't is what i'd say in the end as it seems they really don't have much choice here. I don't know their numbers but from my own corporate world experience i can imagine they are taking some serious risk here. But logical risk as well as staying put and hoping iterative, yet-again-licensed Star Wars packs in FX3 may not be going to be making the difference many hope for. To me the huge number of these tables is a indication of the underlying issue: Get maximum benefit from the license fees and pump it to the max. Regarding SW they sure have done just that. I wish them well in their trials and i hope this turns out all right in the end. It would be a shame if FX dies down as just another game that is incomplete, disliked but with a fully functional store front that is so common now.  Ok thats all. Thx for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Pinball FX

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my review for FX3 still applies to this new version, I like how zen does pinball    At the time of writing there are already 26 tables that are not available in fx3, I absolutely recommend buying at least those 26, & any subsequent new releases, this is currently the best, active pinball sim available, no pinball collection is complete without it.Many of the negative reviews are part of a trolling campaign, rather than honest assessment of the game itself. The performance of the new engine badly needs further optimisation, it is currently very taxing on the system, for what is a significant, but not huge, improvement in visual fidelity (43" 4k screen in portrait/pinball mode), if you're using a smaller screen in landscape, you may struggle to notice much visual improvement over pfx3.For most people, I don't think that improvement on its own is enough to warrant buying tables that you already own, but I like to support the few pinball sims that are available, so for that reason, I will, over time, be buying them all.If you are looking at buying some tables that you already own in fx3, just be sure to choose the "legacy bundle" option, for a 50% discount, & keep an eye out for the regular sales for a bigger discount. Edit: I have completed my collection using that strategy & paid on average $1 (USD) per table, a fair & reasonable deal.As for my experience with graphics settings, after a year of tweaking here & there to arrive at what works best for my system, I have maxed my settings out as I normally would, which results in some flipper lag, then adjusted the "Render scale" setting down until lag is eliminated.For most of the beta I didn't achieve better than 70%, currently my default is 90%, most tables most of the time are fine at 100%, but sometimes, during busy multiballs, I have detected a little lag, making 90% a safe default, hopefully they will continue to improve it further.No matter what I try, I cannot use ray tracing without also having flipper lag, even lowering other graphics settings way down does not eliminate that lag, the only option is to leave it turned off.Currently I only play bought tables in classic mode, so this review does not cover the various game modes, pinball pass, etc.CYA on the leaderboards :)EDIT July '23: A recent update seems to have solved "most" of my performance issues, I'm now on max settings + ray tracing, working great, looking great, & without noticeable lag. still very taxing on the system though, even just idling in the menu will have the fans busy, that's annoying :|EDIT Nov '23: Having just upgraded to current gen hardware (i5-13400F, rtx 4070) I no longer have any performance issues, even running a 43" 4k 120hz screen in portrait/pinball mode. It's performing beautifully at max settings inc. ray tracing, temps are staying low, fans remain quiet, cool 8)
_childDocuments_.name: Pinball FX

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously people are salty that FX3 purchases do not completely roll over to FX, but they have implemented Legacy Packs for those that owned tables in FX3, you can get those same table bundles for new FX for half price.  You have to be careful when reviewing the store pages so that you can take advantage of a Legacy bundle whenever possible.  Williams Vols 1-6, Universal, Jurassic Park, several Star Wars packs, and some Zen tables will have legacy packs whenever visiting their pages on the store page if they exist in both FX3 and new FX.  These will also stack with sales, so during a sale you can make a killing getting Legacy Bundles dirt cheap.  There are currently ~40 tables exclusive to new FX at this time, and while there are some pricey tables definitely and I understand the reservations some may have spending $10+ for one table, but you have to understand the niche market here and the real life component of pinball.  Look up the price of any remotely popular or in demand pinball table and things may start to look different.  My views as a newer pinball player starting in mid-February 2024 may be skewed since I obviously do not have context for development history behind this franchise, but the reason for some of the things people complain about is partly in due to the change to a new game engine to futureproof things more easily later on and so that there aren't as many hands-on constant tweaks needed like there used to be.In short, new FX is the main platform going forward and where you should get unowned tables now instead of FX3, make sure to use Legacy Bundles and sales prices combined whenever possible to get the best deals if you don't feel like shelling out money earlier.
_childDocuments_.name: Pinball FX

_childDocuments_.review: Two pieces of background that are important to potential buyers: 1. I was never a fan of pinball. My buddy took me to this $10-play-all-day-arcade (with a bar in it) and I ended up playing this pinball game called 'Monster Bash'. I was hooked at 35 years-old! 2. I never played Pinball Fx3, before playing this. So I get how a lot of reviews are upset that they couldn't take their tables to an entirely new game for forever, but that literally never affected me, because this is my first game in the series.So, with those two important bits explained...I absolutely love this game. There are three main table types, and understanding this took me a while (because I was never a pinball fan remember).1st type are simulations of actual real life tables. These are tables that exist in the real world, and that's why when you Google "best pinball tables" some of these lists will have tables from this video game on them. These are often the Williams tables, but not always as other tables like Addams Family, Indiana Jones etc are real-world remakes.There are two Williams brand tables that I highly recommend, as I think they are ALMOST must have, Medieval Madness (found in the Williams pack 1 DLC), which most people will include in their top #1 or #2 tables of all-time... and the second is Monster Bash (found in the Williams monster pack), which most people include in their top #10 of all-time. I personally think this table is the most fun pinball machine I have ever played on. And the simulated version on Pinball FX is very close to me playing this machine at my local arcade. I cannot recommend enough that you at least TRY these tables in the trial mode.The second and third types of tables are licensed and unlicensed zen originals made for their video game platforms only. These tables don't exist in the real world, but that doesn't mean that they aren't a good time. I have only played a few of these... and like most pinball tables, they are hit and miss. I prefer 'long' tables, and some of these can feel a bit short in how they play. They also have some really great features because they are 100% digital... meaning that they can do cool stuff that you simply can't do on a real world table, like disintegrate a ball and have it teleport. Overall... I am a huge fan of this game. I think it works great. I think it looks great. I like that I bought the Williams Series 1 Legacy bundle at $10, and it gave me the tables on FX3, so if I want to go back and play that for tables that haven't been remade in the new engine, I can. I like that this game is free, and that I can snag up only the tables I want, instead of spending $60 for a package of stuff I'll never play. I like this game a lot. 10/10 would absolutely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Pinball FX

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy Zen Pinball. I've played a lot of Pinball FX3 on Playstation over the years. When I logged on this weekend and saw that there was a Zen sale on, I got sucked in again. I wound up buying a lot of tables I already have on PFX3 just because of the sale. No regrets. I also like a lot of the new tables. Plus, the fact that I got a day pass to try tables after doing the tutorial was really nice. I've had no issues with the game running on my machine, it looks, sounds and plays great. I haven't played real pinball in decades, so the physics aren't a problem for me. I've also had no input lag at all. But then, I use a wired keyboard, so there shouldn't be lag with that setup. It's just a lot of fun to play.The only thing I don't like about this game are the distracting animation effects. I turned off the floating numbers, but some of the tables have animated effects that aren't there when you play real pinball. I was playing a Jurassic Park table earlier and I had a ball out because a helicopter flew directly over my flippers as the ball was going through, so I couldn't see where the ball was to hit it. Other than minor annoyances like that, I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 14. August 2023: over the last months, I had the opportunity to play a lot of real life pinball and one of them was "The Machine - Bride of Pinbot", a classic from the 90s. Nice about this pinball is that it is also available here in Pinball FX (4). So, after playing extensively both real life and on my PC, I am really disappointed. The Pinball FX version of this table has nothing in common with the real machine's physics. The ball is too light, the reflections too harsh and the bumpers too soft. All in all, the computer version is much easier to play than the real one, and it also lacks the level of difficulty that gives you the satisfaction, when mastering a difficult ball.I don't understand why Zen Studios is not focusing more on the physics on the tables after 16 years of development. Graphics and Audio are great but the physics simply sucks.
