_childDocuments_.review: Dokapon Kingdom is a classic friendship ruining experience that feels like Mario Party on steroids with the mini games replaced by RPG mechanics, a class system, and a huge world map to explore instead of a small game board. You'll level up, fight monsters to free towns, meet random NPCs who will either aid or hinder your quest, back stab your friends, and so much more along the way. I've played on the PS2, Wii, and gladly picked this up on Steam to continue the tradition within my friend group.This is also best experienced as a multiplayer game with friends. Story mode is quite basic and really just acts as a gated experienced to the world map and random events that occur as a means to learn the game. The King provides updates and gives out quests to complete each chapter. Multiplayer is best experienced in the standard mode where the whole map is open from the start and you're at the mercy of the RNG gods, your own wits, and how well you can play your friends in a race to acquire as much wealth as possible. However the $50 price tag is a tough pill to swallow with this being a fairly straight forward port with the only new frills added being online multiplayer which is a welcome change but at $50 you'd hope to see a little more done than keyboard prompts being added in and basic graphical options. $35 is a stretch but $20 feels like a no brainer purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: While I thoroughly love and approve supporting Dokapon Kingdom due to this being a longtime favorite for me, I would also just be careful for those who are looking into it to know a few extra things!1. This game is NOT lying when they call it a friendship destroyer. You need to be careful of who you play this with, as it's very easy to get caught up in the emotions of the game.2. Unfortunately, despite this game having a port on the Switch as well, it is NOT able to do crossplay. I don't know if that plans on being changed ever, but it does hurt a little bit.3. The keymapping is a little difficult to get used to for keyboard, since the usual controls I'd consider for this game seem to be kind of blocked off by being unchangeable menu commands?4. As much as I love Dokapon Kingdom, I really do want to see something new and exciting for this game besides the same game ported again and again.However...I still adore this game, I think it's got a lot to it and I've just simply run the hours and content of this game dry in my dozens of playthroughs that I've had and will continue to have. And I still really want to play it with friends! That's why I still 100% recommend it, especially if you've never played it before!

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game! But, get it on sale.Dokapon is one of the coolest board games (in theory) I've ever played. It's literally an RPG you play as a board game- and yes, that is as intensive as it sounds. Turns only take like 30 seconds each but I've run games well into the 1000+ turns so expect to put down several hours to finish a game! Thankfully, the data saves to everyone's game, so it's easily spread throughout multiple sessions. It's definitely a bit slow paced and repedetive- but if you don't mind that in a board game, this one is truly something new and fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Dokapon is a simple easy to play party game that encourages infighting and bothering each other.  Its incredibly solid but VERY long.  A full story mode game might take 30 hours.  This is not a mario party.Its combat is just stat based rock paper scissors.  A grandmother could make sense of it.Remote play (which allows one player to own the game and for others to play without purchase) is actually almost non-functional.  Continually freezes and always plays at less than 1 frame a secondRegular multiplayer works fine but still sometimes unsyncs and causes the last save to be reloaded.  It saves at the top of the turn order which is maybe two minutes away.  The rolls are determined in advance so if you have to quit because of a crash, each player can take their turns identically with all the RNG intact.  If they're honorable that is, since you know the results at that point, you can metagame.Game is absolutely overpriced, it should be about 20-30$ at absolute maximumFun game, works best when everyone is figuring the game out at the same timeSingle player is a little overwhelming.  The computers even on normal difficulty tend to know exactly what to do.  if youre new to dokapon, play with weak computer controlled opponents, trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: ------ Remote Play Together works on all platforms with no issues whatsoever. -----------------It works even on Linux with no problems. If you have any problems using Remote Play Together on Linux with DK:C, it's because you don't know how to use Linux.Also, there have been some graphical changes to Connect. Some have called this censorship. As a leotard, stocking, and tube top enjoyer, I call it titillation.Now with that unpleasantness out of the way,This game is a very solid port of the traditional Dokapon Kingdom, brought to Steam and given a matchmaking service for online play. That being said, this is a combination of a board game and a RPG rolled together. If you like, imagine Monopoly meets Dragon Quest. This means that if you're going to play a story game, you will tank a LOT of hours and days into a full story campaign playthrough. As such, you're not very likely to just find a group of random players out of the blue for the full campaign without first off setting up a board game session with your friends outside of DK:C's matchmaking service itself.If you don't have any friends to play with, single player is still a fun option and you can even control all four players just by yourself if you don't want the AI to do that (Sneaky AI just shamelessly cheats), but I'd recommend joining the "Dokapon Server" discord... er. Server. There's usually people willing to either Remote Play Together if you don't own it, or to schedule a long campaign together. The discord's been active before Connect came out to help people do longterm playthroughs online, so it's probably your best bet for finding a player or three if you don't already know anyone. Please observe and follow server rules as you join.When you go to fire up a game, there's three modes:Story Mode: Long-term RPG campaign mode. The game is broken down into a series of chapters and plays out a lighthearted story that doesn't take itself too seriously. Each chapter has you taking out usually 3 boss monsters that take over a random city in a continent, then the goal of the chapter makes itself known. All while this is going on, mayhem generally ensues even if players don't attack each other due to random events.Normal Mode: There's no "chapters", no story, and you play for as many weeks as you like. This means there's no border guards to keep you in check, you can happily wander into a level 50 area at level 1 if you really want. This mode makes for a nice one-off session with friends that you can start and have a clear winner for the whole game by the night's end.Battle Royale: Three usually short game modes that challenge your knowledge of Dokapon. Players get to pick their starting level.Town Race - One town gets picked at random. The first player that liberates this town wins the game. Usually a short game, but if the king picks an endgame town, good luck.Kill Race - PVP match. First player to score a random number of kills on players wins. Given how lethal the combat is, this tends to be the fastest game mode.Shopping Race - The king demands a random item. The first to get it to the king wins. Like town race, if you start at a low level, this can take some time if the king picks something incredibly off the beaten path. There's shops in ridiculously dangerous locales with equally ludicrous prices. Good luck.Pick what mode suits the free time of you and your friends.Complete any of the above modes and you'll unlock the Gallery. This is your "100% the game" option. Anything any player in the game acquires, be it local items, gear, hairstyles, jobs, or monsters fought? All of it will get logged here for you to view the full details of, usually with a little lore blurb. If you're a completionist, there's a LOT for you to unlock here that will keep you busy for hundreds of hours of gameplay. And the more friends you play with, the faster you'll unlock this all. There's no steam achievements for 100% gallery, but you have steam achievements to defeat Comacho, and the robo-assassin, so the one helps the other. If you know what those names mean? I'm so sorry.You may notice I haven't described any of the combat and RPG mechanics in the game yet. It's turn-based and who goes first is done via a card shuffle. You pick one of four defensive options on defense, and one of four offensive options on offense. No, I won't explain anything more than this. It'd be like explaining how to break a REALLY good Dragon Quest game's class, combat and leveling system right out of the gate. It's amazing fun to figure this out with your friends and I refuse to cheat you of that joy.Closing thoughts. Due to the RPG nature of the game, the Gallery mode, Steam achievements, Remote Play Together, and ability to have an infinite number of save files as I have SSD space, the game is easily worth the $50 asking price even as a single player game. I will admit - begrudgingly - that this is still just old Dokapon Kingdom with no new gameplay added in and a $30 asking price would have been more sensible, but counterpoint - the game is 100% free if a friend or even total stranger wants to Remote Play Together with you and owns the game. You'll even be helping them with their gallery collection and steam achievements too. Win-Win. At the very least, wishlist the game. If you see it on sale for $30 or less, this is a must-buy. If you're a streamer, this is an insanely good party game to play for your audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Dokapon Kingdom: Connect - A Chaotic Quest for Wealth and Glory! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)In a realm where coins reign supreme and treachery lurks at every turn, Dokapon Kingdom: Connect reinvigorates the classic RPG party game experience, blending strategic gameplay with unpredictable twists. Set in a land beset by sudden monster attacks that have sent its economy into a tailspin, this game beckons players to embark on a captivating journey for riches, revenge, and, of course, the coveted Princess' hand in marriage and the throne. Originally gracing the PlayStation®2 and Nintendo Wii, this revamped edition brings back the charm of the hybrid board game and RPG, while introducing thrilling online multiplayer features that elevate the competition to a global scale.The heart of Dokapon Kingdom: Connect lies in its marriage of role-playing and board game mechanics. The game seamlessly merges elements from both genres, inviting players to spin the roulette of fate and conquer their adversaries. As the realm's bravest warriors, gamers face off in a contest that encompasses multiple modes, from the core Normal mode to the engaging Story, Shopping Race, Kill Race, and Town Race variants. These modes paint the landscape for the grand adventure that unfolds, spanning the vast kingdom's seven continents. In a true test of strategy, each mode pushes players to contemplate their moves carefully, exploiting their skills and items to outsmart foes.What sets Dokapon Kingdom: Connect apart from its predecessors is the thrilling addition of online play. Friends can become frenemies as they engage in virtual battles across geographical borders, further intensifying the competition. This innovative feature enables players to hold grudges and seek vengeance on a global scale, as they maneuver through the perilous landscape of alliances and betrayals. It's in these moments that Dokapon Kingdom: Connect transcends mere gameplay, creating lasting memories and forging new rivalries.Dokapon Kingdom: Connect boasts an impressive arsenal of 11 job classes that players can choose to shape their character's journey. Whether you opt for the valiant Warrior, the spellbinding Magician, or any of the other diverse classes, each choice influences your tactics and approach. The depth of character customization is enhanced by the acquisition of experience points, leveling up your character and enabling the purchase or even pilfering of items that can be wielded to strategic advantage.Visually, Dokapon Kingdom: Connect retains the whimsical art style that has been a hallmark of the franchise. The game's graphics complement its lighthearted yet competitive nature, immersing players in a world where peril and plunder intermingle. Accompanied by a lively soundtrack, the game succeeds in creating an atmosphere that is both engaging and entertaining, capturing the essence of the fantastical realm.In conclusion, Dokapon Kingdom: Connect is a tour de force that successfully melds RPG elements with board game dynamics, resulting in a gaming experience that is as exhilarating as it is unpredictable. Its fusion of modes, each with their distinct challenges and rewards, ensures that players will find themselves enthralled by its replayability. The addition of online multiplayer breathes new life into the franchise, turning friends into rivals and transforming the quest for fortune and fame into a global spectacle. Whether you're drawn to the strategic depth of its gameplay or the joy of scheming against your closest companions, Dokapon Kingdom: Connect promises a memorable and captivating journey through a realm where anything goes and riches await those daring enough to seize them.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: The game that is frustrating and cut-throat. It has it's charm and addictive gameplay, but man is it too brutal and rng based. It has great qualities and some really not so good ones. This is the gameplay aspect and not the port/remapping stuff that others talk about. The many things I dislike about this game:- You will always fight someone on the same spot even if you don't want to. Being forced to fight is not fun.  - Strike is bs, especially when a weak enemy can still one shot you if you decide to not counter it (even though you want to defend sometimes since they can still deal some damage). There does make it so players aren't just steamrolling the lower enemies, but it's still bs most of the time.- The whole can't stop on a specific spot like the castle, shops, etc. You can end up in a loop of never being able to land on the spot you want. Either that or optimize your route which is just a headache to figure out sometimes.- Thief is fun to play as, absolutely frustrating and not fun to play against. Having your items stolen by a thief passing by you means you cannot hold onto items, unless you want to risk it getting stolen from you. Even if it's not broken, it ruins the general experience.- Dying is not fun. Spend 3/7 days (or 2 or less depending on if you get the angels or w/e) doing nothing is boring. Trading off fun for balance.- Darkling. Last place gets op buff for some time, to balance out 1st place players and stuff. Causes chaos which can be very frustrating.Do I have fun with this game? Yes. Is it under a mountain of frustrating mechanics and rng bs? Absolutely. If they tweaked it and added more settings that you can change (like better cpu settings, enemy stats, event % chances, varying objectives, etc.), this would be more than just "the game that you play to ruin friendships/use to torture yourself/others". It's easily the most like/hate game ever. If you have friends that you want to ruin your friendship with, buy this game on sale (like 50% off or something). It is not worth at full price, not by a long shot. I feel it's a 6/10 at the moment, 8/10 if they add more stuff to it.I seriously hope they update the game (which is unlikely) OR make a sequel that fixes the problems of this game and make it more fun and less bs (the more likely to happen, unless they get poor sales).

_childDocuments_.review: It's the classic Dokapon Kingdom. Pretty much just a higher def version of the PS2 version of the game, with some minor tweaks here and there to clean up some bugs and stuff. Honestly if you liked the original, this is a good buy!Price - It's on sale right now so it's not horrible. I would say 29.99 would be the ideal price, given the game is basically a high def port. Multiplayer - Online play requires each player to own the game obviously. Local/Couch play works perfect, and remote couch play is also working fine. If you are unable to assign multiple players, make sure all players are using a controller, and launch through BPM. You can also just use something like parsec to pull players in as well, either way it works great.Graphics - I'd call them "classic" Nothing has been changed, just updated to look good on modern monitors. Compared to the Switch version the quality is a bit higher on PC as well so it looks great on a 4k monitor/TVAudio - Take off your headset when you launch. Audio control options are garbage like most games, and the lowest setting is still loud on a good headset. Audio quality is literally the same as the old versions, same catchy tunes and quips.Controls - Use a controller. KB/M controls suck and can't be rebound. Honestly using a PS2 style controller feels more natural than an XBOX controller. To the complaints - Yes, its a port. you were aware of that already. Yes it's high price, but at least it's not 7 bucks like most games. Seriously, if you like this type of game, this is THE game.

_childDocuments_.review: Dokapon Kingdom: Connect is a game I've played both on the Switch port and PC, and was honoured to be given a pre-release key by the lovely people at Idea Factory. However, my opinion was not changed by this. I've also played it with friends through use of a "magic Wii" and Parsec. (If you know, you know.) I'm also working on a video review that'll go more in-depth than I do here. So please take what I say with a grain of salt.The game can be played with up to four players. Unlike games like Mario Party, you can play with two characters, three or four. The AI is optional, but there are times where you swear the AI cheats. Speaking from experience, they rarely seem to fail. But seeing the AI cast get countered is always glorious to watch. The three starting Jobs also have combinations that unlock others. First mastery, regardless of Job, gets you Cleric. Mastering Warrior and Magician? You unlock Spellsword. Each class also has a fun trait to them. I'll list the starting three below.Warrior: At the start of your turn, there is a chance for your ATK Stat to be raised by 50% for a week (7 Turn Rotations) but your weapon bonus does not count.Magician: You can cast two spells per turn instead of one but you still can't cast when using an item.Thief: You steal an item from each player you pass. Even landing on their space but moving from the tile you started on does not steal.Each turn, you can use an item or cast a spell before you spin the spinner to see how many spaces you can move, if you can at all. The spinner contains the numbers 0 through 6. If 0, you don't move at all. This also happens if you are paralysed. The types of tiles, I'll explain below. Though the game also tells you at the start of Story Mode.Empty Space: Landing on these'll result in one of two things happening. Either a fight'll break out against an enemy that can be found in that area type on the continent or a random event. These events can be good or bad. If you can't afford them, some events will show up. I'll go over some of them here.Mitch Digger: This delightful mole will try to improve towns by drilling wells. His cost is 32g * the income of the town. If you succeed, the town value is doubled, and sometimes, it can even be all your towns in that continent!Doctor Exiles: This won't be affected if you can't afford it, it'll still happen. In Kingdom, he'll give you a check-up that costs (2500g * Week). If you're not at full health, or have a status effect, that'll be 5000g instead of 2500g. Expect him to put you in debt. I call him the "American Healthcare System NPC".Gutz: While not a badass swordsman, he IS an absolute badass in another way. While his services cost an upfront of 3000g * week, he'll try make you a weapon. If he succeeds, it's possibly better than what you have, but it can also be worse.Weber: The curse chests in Paper Mario as a character. Unless you have the Whispers of Dark Revenge, you do NOT want to see Weber. There are three cursed items. The "Big Bug", which eats your items (It can eat cursed items, if you have other non-cursed items), the Blackmail (It kills you when it activates, but you can pay half your cash to send it to another living player) or Nitroglycerin. If you get attacked or hit by field magic, it has a chance to explode. It'll leave you at 1hp, but this can be useful as a pseudo-deathblock if it explodes when an attack would otherwise kill you.We have your typical gaming affair of a story mode, a free-roaming Normal mode with a turn limit (Set it to 999, that's basically never running out, since you would have to intentionally try play 6993 whole turn rotations) or a Battle Royale mode. I ain't talking no Fortnite, but there are versions of this, with three different criteria. Being the first person to save a town, get enough kills or bring the King certain items. Outside of Battle Royale, the winner is the one with the most Total Value when the game ends. Yes, my fellow gamers, this is a game about capitalism. There is no turn limit in Story Mode, since the turn timer just freezes if it tries to pass 999. The only exception is the Week Counter in the weekly results which resets.In conclusion, this game is a real fun experience to me and the surprising depth you can get by looking at jobs and planning a path through them is actually quite surprising for a Wii/PS2 game! This game was a faithful remaster and the added online play is a huge plus. No need for apps like Parsec if your friends own it. If not, Parsec is still just as good option as with a "magic Wii". Just expect a LOT of arguments, even if you make it clear that anything goes. This game didn't get the rep of "The game that ruins friendships" for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: You could of told me a few years back that Dokapon Kingdom would be getting a PC port on Steam and I'd of said ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥... but here we are. If you're looking for a party game that will take 40ish hours to complete, that has all the unfairness of Mario Party, and Monopoly in the body of a turn based RPG, a game that will either build you up to be the storybook hero, or spit on your face at your lowest lows, a game that will test the strengths of your friendships and could potentially even lose you some, then I would highly recommend this.This game, I've gotten more friends addicted to this game than I have fingers on my hands, by playing them through Dolphin. As for this game there really there aren't many changes I could find, and most of them were kind of unnecessary or just bad. Ze Plague is now Monkey Plague, some of the female outfits got overhauls, I've heard events are a lot more common, and item drops are a lot more rare, CPUs are even more sweaty than the original, Darkling is even stronger, your character name is now based on your steam name which will bug out if you have an accent letter, or cut off if its too long, when ever you change someones name by pranking them you cannot decide what that name (which really sucks because I liked using that on my friends and would give them very personalized names they'd hate), and the King screams "You" at you every time its your turn which gets pretty annoying. The good changes are pretty sparse, but in my opinion make it worth playing this over the original. The UI being upscaled which is a lot better on the eyes. Having built in online play, which was the key selling point of this game. Spinner rolls in the original use to follow a random number generator that it would generate based on every player's movement, now its based on when you push the button with some variables. Achievements being in the game is a nice touch as well, none of them are too hard to get, but some require a bit of luck.

_childDocuments_.review: Dokapon Kingdom: Connect is a wonderful port of the Switch port of the PS2 game.The controls are smooth, and the game plays wonderfully.Up to four players (or AI) travel the kingdom fighting monsters, gaining equipment, and most importantly... making money. Spin the spinner to see how far you can move, and pick a direction. There's no set path, you can explore where you want, but the further away from the castle you get, the harder the enemies are. Land on battle spaces to fight monsters (or other players) or get random events. Land on item spots to play a roulette to get something hopefully good, hit up stores to buy new gear, liberate towns from monsters to get a safe harbour and source of income.It's a wonderful RPG board game where you fight to free the kingdom, and often screw over your friends. There's various classes in the game. You start with three, and as you master them you unlock new ones. Each class has it's own specific features and abilities as well as stat growth.As you level up and get better gear, you can clear out stronger enemies and liberate more areas.When a player is in last place for long enough, they will hear whispers of revenge. If they then hit a special spot on the map, they can become the Darkling. A super powered villain that gains XP from stealing towns from other players and is handed a set of overpowered gear to let them harass any players they come across. It's a great way to flip the tables and pull yourself ahead.This is a wonderful game to play solo or hotseat with friends or online.Just remember that the tagline for the game is the "friendship destroying game". ;)

_childDocuments_.review: mario party, fantasy life, and monopoly have been turned into a chimera, akin to chardee macdennis. no more mini games, no more sense, and holy hell can a full campaign be long and arduous. i have yet to get past the first continent, but i think i get the gist of it at this point. go spinner crazy, murder for profit and more profit, mercilessly ♥♥♥♥ the other players, and invest, invest, invest. there is so much going on and at the same time it can feel so simplistic, even janky and broken, that any sense of comfort you sink into can be ripped out from under you with one NPC or sometimes accidental choice by another player. might as well call this the 2016 economic collapse simulator for how fair this can feel. honestly, it's a shame this wasn't a rebuild akin to the *Advance Wars* re-release and remake, because this game is truly one of a kind and pretty amazing with the right people to play with. honestly the state it's been sold in is atrocious given what consumers expect, to the degree it almost feels like a prank. same ugly models and weirdly Harvest Moon music, no new modes and very little additions to speak of. thankfully we only had to buy one copy and we can use steam connect so we don't have to spend the amount of a full priced game for what is essentially a port of a wii game. i think i would vastly prefer a sequel or spiritual successor to this, but other multiplayer games tend to suck ass in comparison to a game 1/3 my own age, so what are you gonna do?

_childDocuments_.review: If you play on PC, just know that it's a VASTLY lesser game than the console version. Buy the PC game.On the plus side, the physicality of the game, and the strategy required to win, is greatly improved from the last game.  Team play is more emphasized, as it should be (I was wondering how they'd make Jokic a more dominant player, as he was pretty weak in '23).  However, this comes at a cost: I'm not sure if this is also a nerf from the PC game, but having an 80 dunk, and the defender behind you, moving slower, means you're about to inexplicably miss a layup from 2 feet.  I don't even try to dunk now unless there are no defenders, it's a completely losing play (maybe 20% success, and I'm being generous).  I'm not even sure the PC version has all  the animations it should to ensure smooth gameplay; this mind-boggling *extreme* difficulty in finishing (75 layup, superstar difficulty, layup timing off) makes no sense, is supremely frustrating, and of course, only applies to you, the player.  [Edit: even after starting a dunk animation - 85 rated - if the defender who is completely behind you can touch you, you will then stop dunking and transition to an awkward layup that always misses - horribly, infuriatingly broken]Micro-transactions suck, the PC version is completely inferior, and the game devs are amazing, but apparently don't have anywhere near enough time for anything but console.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr – PLEASE DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!  These points are ordered by most to least annoying, but please don’t let the order of my personal gripes with the game make you think that this game could possibly be worth your money.  Please do not buy this game.  It is bad.1.	Constant Crashes – I have a decent computer, and it runs games fairly well.  I can play games like Baldur's Gate and Hell Let Loose (far more demanding games) without any issue.  I can barely get through two games of NBA 2K24 before the game crashes, and I have tried almost everything.  This is my biggest gripe with the game and the reason that I am writing this review, because despite the game being extremely bad every single year, at least in past years I could actually play the game.  In 2K24, I can barely even start playing it before it crashes, even though I can play much more graphically intense games without issue.  2.	Rampant Cheating – Please don’t think that I or anyone else is understating the amount and level of cheating that goes on in this game.  In past years of 2K on PC there has been the same level of cheating, and this year is no different, even though some of us hoped that it would be. When I say cheating is rampant, I mean rampant.  Every second game that you play online in 2K will have someone cheating.  2K has never, and in all likelihood will never, do anything about these cheaters.  They are blatant, and they are everywhere.   The players who are cheating are not hiding, they’re not covert, they do not bother to even attempt to hide that they’re cheating, because they know for a fact that they will not be punished for it.3.	Next Gen and Removed Features – If you know anything about 2K on PC, you will know that 2K has never given PC players the “next gen” version of the game that PS5 and Xbox players get.  2K gives PC players the “current gen” version of the game, which is a completely different game.  Let me be clear, the next gen and current gen versions of the game are two completely different games. I don’t mean that the graphics are different, I mean nearly everything from top to bottom is different.  The current gen version of the game is always embarrassingly bad compared to the next gen version, but the amount of effort that 2K has put into the current gen version of the game has been steadily getting worse and worse over the years, and is exceptionally bad this year.  Just as a small example of things getting worse over time, in 2K22 there was a game room with a cool prize wheel (and a bunch of other mini games around it) that you could spin every day to get a fun little reward for your character like clothing, power-ups, and other things.  In 2K24, it’s literally a signpost in the ground that says “DAILY PRIZE” on it.  You click it, and receive your reward.  This is the definition of low effort, and it is embarrassingly bad.  I know this might sound like it’s not a big deal if you haven’t experienced it, but so much of the game is like this and it’s jarring when you see it.If that example was too small for you, we can talk about the complete lack of a story line in 2K24 on current gen.  In past years, although it was less immersive than the next gen story line, there was still a story line that you could take part in on current gen (although that experience had also been steadily eroded for quite some time).  In 2K24, you are instantly in the starting line up on your team, there is no story at all, shoe deal on game three.  Truthfully, the story lines in 2K were always lame and you would probably skip large portions of it, but sometimes there were some decent memes that came out of how ridiculous it was, and there was the (very) rare piece of dialogue that was actually funny or interesting.  Regardless of how lame the story line was though, it’s just another piece of the game that has been stripped away, and for what?  What did we get instead of the story line?  Did the developers spend more time on making the actual basketball aspect of the game better?  Possibly, but I seriously doubt it.That’s all I can think of for now.  If you made it this far, thank you for reading.  I’m sure there’s more I could type out, but I think I’ve covered the worst parts of the game (in my opinion) well enough.  I never write Steam reviews unless I really can’t stand a game and the way it treats its players, or I really love it and want to let others know about it.Please do not buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are even thinking about buying this game, DON'T. I bought it on sale for $8 and I would have rather bought 8 dollar menu burgers from McDonalds. Here is a breakdown:The game is essentially just a roster update from all of the previous games. There has been nothing new added whatsoever. The game is also incredibly buggy, here are just a few:Sometimes when I try and load a game, my screen goes black like it's trying to load the "Pre-Game Show" but it gets stuck at 70%, and I'm forced to force quit the game. IF the game does load, sometimes the referee will just throw the ball way into the air and the ball never comes down, and the players are just stuck in the jump ball circle, and I'm forced to quit the game. IF I am able to get passed the buggy jump ball, I can play for a solid 3 minutes before, all of a sudden, no one can pass. I can't pass, the CPU can't pass, the referees can't pass. No one. The player does the animation for passing, and the ball will leave their hands, just for it to teleport straight back to the passer, whichever player has the ball has to shoot. If you manage to make a shot, then it becomes a turnover spree, because the inbounder will try and pass, but the ball will teleport back to them while they're still out of bounds and they will get an out of bounds turnover. If the referee has the ball and tries to pass the an inbounder, free throw shooter, etc, the same thing will happen to them, resulting in, you guessed it, a force quit. If you are one of the lucky few to be able to load into 2 games in a row, the second game you play will be played against the right players, but on the wrong teams. That's hard to explain so here's and example. If I start a MyLeague as the Bucks, and I play against the Pacers for my first game, then against the Heat in my second game, I will play as the Bucks, but the Heat will still be Heat players, but in Pacers uniforms, in Indiana's arena. I really only ever play sports games because, well, I really enjoy sports, and love anything franchise mode related. I don't need the game to be great, usually not even good. i just need it to be playable, which this game has failed to do. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE don't make the mistake I made by purchasing this game, 2K should pay you to play it. P.S. The first 40hrs of playtime, this game ran great for me, as in, no bugs, good frames, it was what I was hoping it'd be. My PC fits all of the recommended specs, so not sure what happened, but I can't find a fix for it online.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin with this one...Man, back in the days, coming from NBA Live from uh.. some other big gaming publisher, I discovered the NBA 2k series back in 2006 and it was...a revelation. Miles ahead already back then in terms of both presentation and gameplay.I've kept in touch over the years until NBA 2k16. After that, I merely watched the yearly trainwreck unfold on social media when thousands, no millions of people again flocked around the yearly NBA 2k Update.The core of the game is still there. The animations are mostly good, the gameplay is mostly solid, apart from when it's not. Overall, on the court, you still can't find a better virtual Basketball experience to this day.Maybe that's part of the problem.Lack of competition makes things stale. Uninspired. Atriously bad. Oh my god, so bad.I've always loved the idea of playing my own character and getting a feeling for how an NBA career might feel like. My go-to fantasy was always: Simon Jordan, a nephew of the great His Airness. Same family name, huge burden. He understands the implications and he's not a copy of the original, he's a great player in his own right. No, he grows into one.This is what I am looking for, by the way, Visual Concepts, if you are reading this. The journey, the growth from a talented rookie with clear weaknesses, into a hall of fame candidate.What are you giving me here?The weirdest, pointless, annoying, mood-killing cut-scenes I have ever had to endure in any game. They're so bad, you can hardly even meme on them.My player, young Mister Jordan is already in some big fancy apartment somewhere, clearly a millionaire. Surrounded by an annoying manager, girlfriend and social media lady."That's why your fans hate you probably, lol", my rival Shep tells me. I didn't ask btw. No idea why this douche is my rival at all, why he seems like he is about to stab me on the way to the lockerroom. Or why my player first shrugs it off with a coolness, until my "rival" says: "ha, the sun even shines on a dog's ass sometime!" - and oh boy, suddenly my character gives him a look that should kill him, but sadly doesn't.What the ♥♥♥♥ am I watching? Skip.I play my first game. My player has an average rating of 70. Not great, not terrible. I somehow shoot 70 % from mid-range, but I don't know why. There is very little shot-feedback. Clearly, a step back. Let alone the fact that I am being benched for most of the 4th quarter despite having scored the most points on my team.After the game, the season is supposed to start! Yay!Except, no, first, I am being invited to a special club, of which only the best players can be a part of. Clearly, that's me... Mister draftpick number 18! This is where I can satisfy all my shopping needs!...My dudes, I just want to play Basketball and have a succesful season. What is this? Metabook?Disgusted, I try to upgrade my first ability with the 850 Virtual Coins I have earned.There is no real money involved, yet I feel like I just got my lunch money taken from me.I feel... disillusioned. NBA 2k 23 is a pale shadow of it's former gloryful self. The music, the menus, the lack of meaningful improvements in gameplay, a backstory that could have been done better for 5 $ by some guy/gal from Fiverr in 10 minutes.I really really wanted to like this game, I really wanted to play some virtual basketball in 2022 (btw after 2k Games made 2k16 literally obsolete and unplayable even offline!) but I just can not stand this piece of ♥♥♥♥ garbage. For the love of Kobe Bryant please stop buying this garbage game, show the developers that this is not what we want in a game!Or maybe it is me? Am I so out of touch? No, it's the children who are wrong!

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid gamer and a basketball enthusiast, I eagerly anticipated the release of NBA 2K24, hoping for an immersive experience that would capture the excitement of the sport. However, after spending hours with the game, I'm deeply disappointed to say that NBA 2K24 falls far short of expectations, delivering a lackluster and frustrating gaming experience.One of the most glaring issues with NBA 2K24 is its lack of innovation. Instead of building upon the successes of previous installments, the game feels like a mere rehash of its predecessors with minimal improvements. The gameplay mechanics are virtually unchanged, leaving players with a sense of déjà vu as they dribble, shoot, and dunk their way through the same tired motions.Moreover, NBA 2K24 suffers from numerous technical glitches and bugs that detract from the overall immersion. From players clipping through each other during intense moments to the occasional game-breaking crash, these issues constantly pull you out of the experience and make it difficult to enjoy the game.Another major disappointment is the lack of meaningful updates to the game's graphics and presentation. While NBA 2K24 boasts slightly improved visuals, they fail to impress in comparison to other contemporary titles. Character models lack detail, animations feel stiff and unnatural, and the overall aesthetic lacks the polish expected from a flagship sports title.Furthermore, the game's monetization practices are predatory and exploitative. From the incessant barrage of microtransactions to the egregious pay-to-win mechanics, NBA 2K24 prioritizes profit over player enjoyment. It's disheartening to see such a beloved franchise succumb to greed, alienating its fanbase in the process.In conclusion, NBA 2K24 is a disappointing entry in the franchise that fails to deliver on its promise of an immersive basketball experience. With its lack of innovation, technical issues, subpar graphics, and predatory monetization, the game falls short of expectations and ultimately leaves players feeling frustrated and unsatisfied. Save your money and skip this lackluster installment – there are far better basketball games out there deserving of your time and attention.

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews, but this game is such an egregious step backwards I really felt compelled to share my experiences as someone who played a lot of NBA 2k23 WITHOUT purchasing any microtransactions.Despite 2k23's notorious and very real predatory monetization practices I was able to play the game as a SINGLE-PLAYER game due to a relatively robust MyCareer mode in '23.  There was a "story" with "choices" of varying quality, but regardless provided a way to play the game and develop your player without having to spend money on microtransactions.  The career mode was more than enough "game" for me that I never felt the need to play online until I had completed several full seasons, and by then had a pretty solid build that I could at least keep up online if I wanted to (again, without spending any money on VC because I was able to earn it through the pretty fun single-player game).2k24 essentially REMOVES THE SINGLE PLAYER MODE FROM THE GAME.  Yes you can still create a player, but they've removed all of the actual content down to just the basketball games, so there is little motivation to grind game after game without it being broken up by the story beats, player choices, and some interesting challenges that fed into the overall narrative in '23 (ex, playing through your college games).So what is 2k24 offering players other than a new location and updated rosters?  After 2 hours it felt like LITERALLY the exact same game as '23 but with a large chunk of content removed.  I refunded and will just re-install '23 if I want to play more bball.I understand that the majority of NBA 2k players are in it to spend a ton of money on VCs so they can "compete" online...  If you are someone who just enjoys the NBA and the game of basketball 2k23 at least gave us a story mode which gave me some fun and a reason to "grind" up my character.  With this removed 2K is telling me they only want me playing online and they removed the most interesting (and microtransaction-free) way to build my character, essentially pushing players strongly to skip everything and go straight into online, which obviously will encourage players to spend more $.Yuck.  Don't buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a basketball enthusiast, it's hard not to be intrigued by NBA 2K24. This annual installment of the popular basketball video game franchise has always been a go-to for fans like me. However, as much as I enjoy the gameplay, there's a critical element that I feel has been lacking - a compelling narrative in the MyCareer mode.For many of us, MyCareer is the heart and soul of the NBA 2K series. It's the mode where we get to experience the journey of a budding basketball star firsthand. Each year, we anticipate that this mode will evolve, offering us richer and more immersive storytelling options. With the advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), there's tremendous potential to take MyCareer to new heights. In conclusion, Dont take me wrong! I enjoy playing this game but while I remain a devoted fan of basketball and the NBA 2K franchise, I cannot help but express my profound disappointment with NBA 2K24's MyCareer mode. It's disheartening to see such potential go unrealized. As fans, we long for a MyCareer experience that truly captivates us, with rich storytelling and impactful decision-making. It's my hope that the developers will heed this feedback and prioritize the narrative aspect in future releases, so we can once again embrace the MyCareer mode as the heart and soul of NBA 2K.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: NBA 2K24: A Disappointing Struggle with Microtransactions and Unfulfilled PromisesNBA 2K24 has arrived, and while it promised improvements and innovation, it seems to have stumbled in several critical areas, leaving fans and gamers disappointed. The most glaring issue that continues to plague the series is the presence of egregious microtransactions, which, sadly, seem to be even more pervasive than ever.One of the most significant letdowns for players is the game's failure to deliver on the promise of cross-play functionality. This was a feature that was eagerly anticipated and much-hyped prior to the game's release. Yet, upon playing, gamers discovered that this long-awaited feature was nowhere to be found. The absence of cross-play is a major setback, especially in a sports game that thrives on the community aspect and competition among players across different platforms.On the positive side, the gameplay in NBA 2K24 has seen improvements, making for a more enjoyable on-court experience. The mechanics feel smoother, and there's a certain level of realism in player movements and interactions that enhance the immersion. However, these improvements are overshadowed by the persistent bugs that continue to haunt the franchise. Glitches, AI quirks, and animation issues can disrupt the flow of the game and diminish the overall experience.Furthermore, there's a noticeable lack of polish throughout NBA 2K24. It feels rushed, as if the developers didn't have enough time to refine the game before release. This lack of attention to detail is particularly evident in the presentation and various modes, leaving players longing for the level of quality they expect from a franchise of this caliber.Perhaps one of the most disheartening aspects of NBA 2K24 is its failure to represent the values and ethos that Kobe Bryant, a beloved basketball icon, stood for. Kobe was known for his dedication, work ethic, and passion for the game, and his untimely passing left a profound impact on the basketball world. It's unfortunate that the game bearing his name falls short in capturing the essence of what he represented, both as a player and as an inspirational figure.In conclusion, NBA 2K24 arrives as a disappointing addition to the franchise. While it does show promise with improved gameplay, it falters due to its continued reliance on microtransactions, the absence of promised cross-play, persistent bugs, and a lack of overall polish. This game fails to honor the legacy of Kobe Bryant and leaves fans hoping for better days for the NBA 2K series.

_childDocuments_.review: NBA 2K24: A Steep Shot with Glittering RewardsNBA 2K24, the latest iteration of the popular basketball simulation game, delivers an undeniably polished and exciting on-court experience. Yet, much like a dazzling alley-oop overshadowed by an overzealous traveling call, the game's brilliance is marred by intrusive monetization strategies.For basketball purists, NBA 2K24 is a dream. The "ProPLAY" technology seamlessly translates real-life NBA footage into in-game animations, resulting in smoother player movement and a heightened sense of authenticity. Whether mimicking Giannis Antetokounmpo's powerful drives or Stephen Curry's lightning-quick releases, the gameplay feels incredibly responsive.Beyond technical prowess, the variety of game modes keeps players engaged. MyCAREER, the story-driven mode where you build your own basketball superstar, boasts a revamped narrative and a vibrant city hub to explore. MyTEAM, the card-collecting mode, allows you to curate your dream roster of current and historic players.However, the path to competitive glory in these modes feels paved with microtransactions.  The virtual currency, VC, is essential for upgrading your MyCAREER player's abilities and acquiring top players in MyTEAM. Earning enough VC through gameplay can be a tedious grind, incentivizing players to purchase it with real money. This nickel-and-diming approach casts a shadow over the otherwise immersive experience.Ultimately, NBA 2K24 is a game of two halves. On the court, it's a slam dunk, delivering the most realistic and engaging basketball simulation to date.  Off the court, however, the aggressive monetization tactics leave a bitter aftertaste.  For casual fans, the core gameplay might be enough. But for serious players, the pay-to-win elements may feel like a foul call.Recommendation: Purchase game off . For die-hard basketball fans, the gameplay improvements may outweigh the monetization issues.

_childDocuments_.review: 2K24 is another disappointment from 2K. PC version is stripped to bare bones and is a generally trash experience. You'll find Auto-Greeners making half court shots fully contested, green everytime. Not only does 2K not care about hackers, they encourage it. With no anti-cheat system in place, at all, AND YOU CAN'T EVEN REPORT PLAYERS IN GAME. That's even if you CAN get online. There's so many server issues and frustrating Alt+F4 escapes, that even if you DO play the disappointing, and lackluster "Story Mode" MyCareer.. you'll be forced to stick to the worn-out gameplay of 2K. Play games, deal with frustrating mechanics, useless AI, Sim to next appearance, and on to play the next game. Rinse repeat. If you need a break and are considering playing some Park games, good ♥♥♥♥♥♥' luck. Between the hackers and the "Connection Failed" messages, you'll be havin' a rough time. The Rec? Nah, good luck finding a team, and then after 20 minutes of being held hostage in the lobby "Waiting for Teammates".. you'll finally be given a sweet, SWEET escape with the "Exit" button appearing.  You'll get a connection error then be stuck in the purgatory of The Rec locker rooms for eternity.. or until you Alt+F4Career mode is so barren it makes me miss those half-ass attempts at a "Story" they try to shoehorn in every year. There is no story this year, I mean.. there's barely ever one, but I mean NO STORY. You get the occasional interview, but that's it. And even less often than 2K23. You're stuck with regularly scheduled games. (Refer to previous complaint regarding Rinsing and Repeating)Usually I play a Glass Cleaning Power Forward.. but this year I wanted to try something different. Unfortunately for me, so did 2K. They made shots almost impossible to hit unless you're hitting the green window. Which they made even harder to hit than before. Another reason I prefer 2K23 over this dumpster bonfire. I can not Not Recommend this "game" more, it's impossible. Game is even more trash and lackluster than 2K23 (Which is saying a lot). Paid $6 and that's too much. Stick with a previous year/for them to pay YOU to play.

_childDocuments_.review: **NBA 2K24: A Slam Dunk of Basketball Gaming Brilliance**NBA 2K24 continues the legacy of excellence set forth by its predecessors, delivering a basketball simulation experience that's unparalleled in its depth and realism. Developed by Visual Concepts, this installment raises the bar yet again with stunning graphics, immersive gameplay, and a plethora of features that cater to both casual fans and hardcore basketball enthusiasts alike.**Gameplay and Realism**From the moment you step onto the virtual court, NBA 2K24 impresses with its attention to detail. Player movements, animations, and physics are meticulously crafted to mirror the intricacies of real basketball. Dribble moves, shooting mechanics, and defensive strategies feel intuitive and responsive, allowing for strategic gameplay that rewards skill and practice. Whether you're executing a perfect pick-and-roll or sinking a buzzer-beating three-pointer, every action feels impactful and true to the sport.**Modes and Content**NBA 2K24 offers a wealth of game modes to keep players engaged for hours on end. The MyCareer mode returns with a compelling story-driven experience where you create your own player and navigate their journey from rookie to NBA superstar. The MyTeam mode lets you build and manage your dream team through card packs and player auctions, adding a layer of strategy and collection to the game. Additionally, the revamped MyLeague mode provides deep customization options for those who prefer to manage every aspect of a franchise.**Presentation and Visuals**Visually, NBA 2K24 is a feast for the eyes. Player models are incredibly detailed, capturing the likeness and unique characteristics of NBA stars with astonishing accuracy. Arenas are meticulously recreated, complete with dynamic crowds and broadcast-style presentation that enhances the immersion. Whether playing on current-gen or next-gen consoles, the game showcases Visual Concepts' commitment to pushing the boundaries of graphical fidelity in sports gaming.**Community and Online Play**The online multiplayer experience in NBA 2K24 is robust and engaging. Compete against friends or players from around the world in head-to-head matches, participate in online leagues, or test your skills in weekly challenges and events. The community aspect of the game is thriving, with active forums, social media integration, and regular updates that keep the gameplay experience fresh and dynamic.**Critique**While NBA 2K24 excels in almost every aspect, there's one area where many players, myself included, wish for improvement: in-game prices and microtransactions. The cost of virtual currency and the pricing of in-game items can feel steep at times, making it challenging for players who wish to progress or customize their experience without significant investment. Better deals and more accessible pricing options would undoubtedly enhance the overall player experience and foster a more inclusive community.**Conclusion**In conclusion, NBA 2K24 sets a new benchmark for basketball gaming with its unparalleled gameplay, stunning visuals, and extensive content offerings. Whether you're a die-hard NBA fan or simply enjoy immersive sports simulations, this game delivers in spades. While there's room for improvement in the pricing structure, the sheer quality and depth of NBA 2K24 make it a must-have for any gaming library. Lace up your virtual sneakers, hit the court, and experience the thrill of NBA action like never before.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played every NBA2K since 2K11 and I have never been so disappointed that I wanted to write a review. This has been the best basketball game available for the last decade and still is, but the experience for a returning fan is poor. I knew this game would still be current gen before buying it so I'm not going to say that I was expecting next gen. But there are some huge flaws with the game that I will share from my offline experiences.MyCareer:The story mode in this game is terrible. The devs constantly adjust the story mode to please online park players, and it damages the MyCareer experience. Not having a story line is not an issue for me because MyCareer didn't used to have a story line, but my issue is that everything in this 2k is spoon-fed to you. You begin your career as the worst player in the NBA who somehow is starting at your position no matter what, even ahead of superstars. The game should punish you or reward you for your play, not just hand you minutes. The ridiculous prices for upgrades wouldn't be as unreasonable if they just started you at a normal rating. I created a player that is supposed to be a good three point shooter, and started with a bad three point rating. To completely upgrade just the three point rating, it would take me 200,000 VC, which costs $50 to purchase. I play 12 minute quarters and make about 1000 VC every game, to upgrade just one attribute it would take me 200 games, that is ridiculous. They need to separate the offline story from the park. If the story mode is your favorite part of the 2K games, this is definitely not worth it.MyLeague:I play MyLeague the most and I could go on forever about the flaws. The 2 biggest flaws are that they did not add the Clutch Player of the Year award to the game, and there still is no Transition Take Foul in the game. The Take Foul has been in the NBA for a while now, and this game is supposed to be a realistic simulator of NBA basketball, how have they not added this. Playing past more than a few seasons is not enjoyable, the default progression system results in really good players stuck in free agency and teams full of all-star level ratings from top to bottom. If you look at team stats, teams have record high Offensive Ratings every season and horrible defensive ratings, that is not realistic. MyLeague in its default state, in which it is supposed to simulate the real NBA season experience, is not playable for more than one season.2K fans complain every year and still buy the game, but this is the first time that the game is actually worse than it is good. The game will never change because there aren't any competitors. This game is a slap in the face to Kobe Bryant, the NBA, and 2K fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Although it's still not "next gen" I'm still going to give this game a thumbs up. I hated 2k23 one of the worst things about it were the RNG shooting and adrenaline bars. In this game, that's fixed. As long as you time your shot perfectly, you can make anything that's not 100% smothered, and personally, I like that way better. You don't lose an adrenaline bar from doing basic dribbles anymore. And the layup meter closes in or out depending on how contesting you are midair, meaning and1s are actually makeable something with 3 point and1s. The Ais actually feel like real NBA players; instead of being a straight brick, they actually make shots. Of course, with all this, there are some shots that are kind of odd and shouldn't go in that these Ais make, but at least for me, thats rare, and the only couple of ones Ive seen was when luka made a logo three that was 43% contested, but he did avg 40 pts, so ig 2k. One thing I dislike is that I legit get a clean block on someone, and the refs will call a foul, and even when I challenge it, the call stands, and there are a lot of refs that will rig fouls. Another thing is the free throw rework. Instead of being able to green a free throw its RNG i have a big man with a 51 free throw. I could full bar it, and it would say 71% and brick, and then the next one would say excellent release, 71%. So unless you have curry at the line, its rng for free throw greens. There are also more dunk animations, crossovers, stepbacks, and overall, a lot more animations. For right now, at least with the game being on sale for 21 bucks, I think it's a game you should get if you like basketball. My rating for 2k23 4/10My rating for 2k24 6.5/10 Overall much better of an upgrade 2k23 was to 2k22 and i think atleast for me its decent.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is terrible. Last 2k game I played was 2020, this is a copy/paste of that yet somehow worse. Like, timeout animations, commentary are literally exactly the same. Controls are not responsive, things like steal and shooting under the hoop especially will happen seconds later, with no way to cancel of course. Animations make no sense most of the time, you'll have an open layup on the side of the basket you're driving to, and your player will just decide to try it on the other side where half the other team is standing. It's easier to make a 3 pointer with 2 guys in your face than a defended layup with a guy 6 inches shorter guarding you right under the basket. The AI is the worst. Players will have their defender beat on a run to the basket and just stop. Defenders will pick up a guy on the wing while the man with the ball strolls down the lane on a fast break. There's at least 3-4 illegal screens called every game, and the refereeing in general is just bad. I get that replay challenge is part of the NBA now, but can't the refs in a video game just make accurate calls? Getting a charge called when the defender never even began to set his feet, and you don't have a challenge is just tons of fun. I play nba mycareer, have little interest in online or anything else. It really feels like wins and losses are just decided most of the time, and your play has little to do with the outcome. The thing that just put me over the edge- down by 4 with 3 minutes left, leading my team in every stat category, the game sends me to the bench, and I just get to sim to the end and lose. I hate to be so negative, but everyone involved in making, promoting, and selling this game should be ashamed of their work. I could write 10 more chapters in this book about all the little things wrong and just unfun about this game. I would be really upset if I hadn't purchased for 80% off. And I would much rather play mycareer offline in 2k20, but since the servers are down so you can't buy vc (which I also would never do) that's not an option either. I guess like most business, the most money with the least amount of work is the goal, but this is just sad...

name: Monster Hunter Stories
detailed_description: Monster Hunter Stories Collection Both Monster Hunter Stories games included in one collection! Contents: - Monster Hunter Stories - Monster Hunter Stories 2: Wings of Ruin (Standard Edition) Note: Monster Hunter Stories and Monster Hunter Stories 2: Wings Of Ruin are both available separately. Please take care to avoid duplicate purchases. *Please note that these titles are available in two bundles, 'Monster Hunter Stories Collection' and 'Monster Hunter Stories Deluxe Collection'. Monster Hunter Stories Deluxe Collection Both Monster Hunter Stories games included in one deluxe collection! Contents: - Monster Hunter Stories - Monster Hunter Stories 2: Wings of Ruin (Deluxe Edition) Note: Monster Hunter Stories and Monster Hunter Stories 2: Wings Of Ruin are both available separately. Please take care to avoid duplicate purchases. *Please note that these titles are available in two bundles, 'Monster Hunter Stories Collection' and 'Monster Hunter Stories Deluxe Collection'. About the Game *This content is also available as part of one or more bundles. Please check your previous purchases to avoid duplication. Monster Hunter Stories is an RPG that takes the world of Monster Hunter and expands upon it in new and exciting ways! No longer are you hunting monsters, but raising them! In this deep story featuring heroes known as Monster Riders, you will live alongside monsters and form lifelong bonds with them. The first installment of the Monster Hunter Stories series returns, fully voiced in Japanese and English, with additional features such as a new museum mode where you can listen to music and view concept art, allowing you to dive even deeper into the world of Monster Hunter Stories. Story: As the hero of the story, you were born in a village of Riders who raise monsters for a living. You’ll overcome trials and tribulations as you grow as a Rider, and leave your village to embark on an adventure. Your destination: the world of Hunters, who make their living by hunting monsters. Although their lifestyles are vastly different, you must learn to live and work together with Hunters, and in turn, bring the world of Hunters and Riders ever closer. Things take a dark turn as a calamity known as the Black Blight appears, threatening the entire world and upending peaceful lives that were taken for granted... Both Riders and Hunters alike will be put to the test in order to challenge this threat. The keys to saving the world are the Kinship Stone and its hidden power, along with the truth of the “Legend of Redan,” which describes the long-kept secret of the Riders’ origins! Along your epic journey, you will discover the true meaning of Kinship, which grows as your bonds deepen! A story of friendship and triumph await you—ride on into the world of Monster Hunter Stories! Game Features: ■ A turn-based RPG set in the world of Monster Hunter! Monster Hunter Stories features a strategic battle system which is easy to get the hang of, even for those who struggle with action games. Use Power, Speed, and Technical attacks to guess and overcome your opponent's attack patterns to inflict heavy damage and win head-to-head battles! Build up your Kinship Gauge to use skills or try your Monsties' unique Kinship Skills! ■ Turn popular monsters from the series into your Monsties! Explore the field using Monstie abilities, hatch eggs that you find along the way, and turn various monsters into Monsties! This game features many popular monsters from the Monster Hunter series, including Zinogre, Nargacuga, and Lagiacrus. The Rite of Channeling is a ritual that awakens dormant abilities in your Monsties, allowing you to raise original Monsties and take on powerful enemies! ■ Online Features Create a powerful party with the Monsties you have raised and enjoy battles with other players! New Features: ■ Fully voiced in Japanese and English! The narrative is even more immersive with full Japanese and English voices! ■ Bonus Museum content Enjoy more than 200 pieces of concept art, including some which have never been seen before, and numerous music tracks. Some tracks are being featured in surround sound for the first time! ■ All updates are included Includes all the monsters added in updates to the original game, such as Kushala Daora, Teostra, and Rajang, as well as expanded endgame content and additional character editing parts, making this the complete package!

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely some fun, at least in my opinion.Ages ago I got it imported along with a 3ds from Japan, playing it because I never thought it would come to the west. I didn't expect is the port over to western 3ds systems, later phones iPhone and Android and now finally the version 1.3 release, reserved only for japan 3DS is here on steam, so you can get things like Teostra and Kushala Daora in your team and also now it's up-scaled with new voices and content never seen in the west. The port also seems to run really quite good.As a game it was interesting to see and appreciate the monster part of monhun as much as the hunter part. and for that i'm kinda grateful to have a game that you could collect and have mons fight on your side for a change.Now it's a more cartoony version of the series, and being the first game it's not so refined as Stories 2, the major critiques of the time cited the chibi/squished look of the charas and monsters, so you'll need to perhaps look past that a littleAs for general content and my thought on the series side rant, a lot was reconnected in the second game from this one, especially the content that came with the anime along with some of the character depth and explanation for motives Some of the cut content was from the anime published on crunchy roll for western audiences but also had an exclusive second arc/season "ebon riders" with at least 20+ more episodes following not aired in the west due to copyright, this involved Cheval, Anivia's brother, Gale which we never hear from again, and missing entirely from Stories 2, so the bigger picture is a bit all over the place..I would definitely recommend playing this one though, I'd say it's a bit easier to get into and the combat and mechanics are much more simplified than the second game, of course being the first one, it's not perfect but it's totally worth having a play

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my time on the Steam version, I played the heck outta this on the 3DS, and let me tell you, it is a great experience. I was very skeptical at first when I saw my girlfriend playing it, but later on I found a copy at Walmart for... I think $15? I found out pretty quickly why she liked it, because this game charmed me proper. You have many of the monsters people love (and some that people don't), a vibrant world filled with color and life, a great soundtrack that lends to the atmosphere of the game, and simple mechanics that never overstay their welcome. After playing Stories 2 and seeing what it had to offer (great game as well, by the way, you should totally check it out), I just HAD to come back to where it all began. The Gene system in this game is by far the standout feature, what with many ways to customize your Monsties and even change their elemental affinities, such as having a dragon element Silver Rathalos (like I had in the 3DS version). This re-release may not have the 3rd-party collaboration content, like the Zelda collab, but what it does have is the content that was missing from the US release of Stories. Rajang, Teostra, and Kushala Daora are all here, and available as Monsties to collect! I sound like I'm trying to sell you guys the game, don't I? I can't help it, though. It's just such a great title, and a worthwhile addition to the Monster Hunter franchise. Navirou's English voice still grates on me, but everything else is in tip-top shape with this remaster, and for just $30? Seriously, if ever you were considering trying Stories out, this really is the perfect time and the perfect place to start.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I've made it to , one of the checkpoint cities in this game, and I wanted to make some comparisons between the Nintendo 3DS version and this remake and what they added/changed.The 3DS version's camera isn't bad, since it was meant to be controlled using the d-pad/c-stick. But in the remake, it's !  (SOLVED). It's even worse if your using a mouse to move the camera because the camera's max speed is too sensitive to trigger. If your trying to move the camera slower, you have to move the mouse veeeery slowly to slow it down. Moving the camera up/down using the mouse doesn't feel natural on mouse either. So if you are going to play this game, either use a controller or use your keyboard keys to move your camera.The graphics made a huge jump in this remake and I love it! Capcom kept the simplistic feel from the 3DS version and polished it up a lot. I'm glad they didn't try to remake the graphics too detailed. It still looks modern while keeping the feel from it's 3DS counterpart. The only time I see a graphical change is when there are certain cutscenes, where the style changes to a "Dragon Quest Builders"-like style. And since they made the graphics how they are, the framerate is very smooth at all times with no dips whatsoever (your results may vary depending on your computer's specs), even during cutscenes. The render distance is also higher than before.There isn't much to talk about here. The audio is higher quality, and you can change some settings now to fit whatever audio device you're using. Plus, you can now change more than just BGM/SFX volume and sound settings (mono, stereo, surround)! There are now options to change your overall, voice, and system volume too! Sometimes, mainly in the main menu screen, the sound effect quality can sound like it was ripped straight from the 3DS version, but it's not too major.Finally, the juiciest part of this review! The story, at my current part of the game, is the same as in the 3DS version. But straying away from the main story, the subquests are a tad different. The speech bubbles for subquests and quests have been made bigger and thusfore, more noticable. So it'll be harder to be missing or accidently skipping over some speech bubble subquests. The combat, gathering, egg hunting, movement, shopping, forging, and crafting is the same from what I can tell. The character customization has been improved quite a bit! Not only does it have more features, but it also allows for you to select bits from some of the characters in-game! So now you can be Cheval's doppelganger or just take certain features from Dan, Hyoro, Reverto, and other side characters! The voice acting has been improved, now with English and Japanese voiceovers. But they also have the option to do the original Monster Hunter language found in the 3DS version. There are some new settings such as the ability to change your resolution, framerate, brightness, and v-sync for your display settings. The option to change keybinds for controller and keyboard were added, and rumble toggle and autosave were also added as well.Yes, this game is amazing! Despite having small annoyances like the camera controls, those kinds of things aren't a dealbreaker for it. The concept for this game was amazing enough to get a sequel after all! However, I wouldn't recommend this to you if you don't like turn based battles and/or a little bit of grinding.EDIT: Disable camera acceleration in the settings for a better experience

Navirou is a show stealer and like always he makes the best of it. Love the little bugger. So many emotions and drama ^^ Everyone who hates him are fake Monster hunter franchise fans. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer / TL;DR - I cannot recommend this game when the second game exists. Every single thing I am about to complain about is handled in MHS2. Just buy that one (when it's on sale).For the record, I 100% completed this game. I got every unique collectable, every monstie, did every subquest, and I fought every single thing that could be fought in this entire game. I even beat the Rider arena, and got the platinum trophy for defeating my rival at the final round. I did it all.Do you want to know what achievement i got LAST? Was it visiting all of the fast travel points? No.Was it completing the end game dungeon? No.Was it getting 1 million dollars? No.Was it collecting all the poogies? No.You want know what achievement took me 50+ hours of playing the game to get?"Get five head to heads in a row."This should be all you need to know about how this game is the most inconsistent, random, and stupidly executed RPG I have played in a long time. To give you an example of the existential terror this game gave me, I went against a Deviljhoe, and i fought this pickle 40 times, because someone on a forum in 2017 on the 3DS wrote that all he does is spam power attacks, even when he's enraged. Brother, THIS PICKLE would throw out a tech attack at RANDOM, EVEN as his first attack, which he did 1/3rd of the time. This is just one monster in this sea of 100+ zoo animals that you can not predict.And don't even get me started on the RIDER ARENA. Lord forgive me for the profanity I yelled at these AI hunters reading my inputs and spamming traps to guarantee I lose on the platinum tier. The soul of my grandma is floating above me, sobbing at my behavior while playing a children's Pokemon knock-off at 1:30 am.The battle pouch is stupid, the crafting system makes no sense, which is insane because this is a monster hunter game where collecting everything is the strategy for completing quests and crafting armor, but most of the stuff you get is useless. But you wont know how useless it is until you beat the game and you have to collect a whole new tier of parts at high rank.I spent 4 hours hunting for a Kirin only to discover that I had to go to an area with Cherry Blossoms that just so happens to be the ALL BLUE that the cook from One Piece is trying to find because every monster in the game can spawn there, so finding the one homie you need to complete your book is a nightmare of poopoo eggs. It's a needle in a haystack. Every single monstie has FOUR DIFFERENT COLOR COMBINATIONS so I had to have a page open and compare shades of purple in photoshop just to figure out if its a Rathian or a small goat.Just buy the second one. I don't care if they got the same voice actors from the second game, I don't care if its for children, I dont care if someone replies to this calling me a big man-baby for whining about this game, I don't care. I'm upset and the world must know about how this game wronged me on the 3DS AND the PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter Stories--------------------------------------I've played Monster Hunter Stories on the 3DS, and now I'm enjoying the PC version. _childDocuments_.review: This version looks and runs significantly better than the original mobile and 3DS releases from 2016, with upgraded textures, smoother animations, and a higher resolution that ups the overall visual experience.The art style is vibrant and colorful and the soundtrack is also amazing. Unlike many open-world games that can feel vast but empty, this game offers a world that feels a lot more lively.While aimed primarily at a younger demographic, the storyline is deeper and less childish than you would expect, offering a surprisingly engaging narrative that appeals to a broader audience.The cast of monsters is nothing compared to the mainline games but still features a satisfying and diverse range of choices for you to collect, train, and battle with.Returning to this game after playing "Stories 2" highlights the limitations of the original’s combat. Battle mechanics feel way simpler and less refined in comparison to the sequel, lacking additional strategic layers introduced in "Wings of Ruin", like swapping your weapon mid-fight.I really enjoyed playing this game again after so many years and I'm hopeful the "MH Stories" lineup will grow in the future.

If you like Monster Collecting games, are a fan of Monster Hunter or played Monster Hunter Stories 2 and want more of that formula, this game will leave you very satisfied.
