_childDocuments_.review: People, probably many of those that are fans of the main Monster Hunter series, will look at this and think it is a cheap spinoff for little kids, and in doing so will miss one of the greatest MH related games till this day. I am fan of the MH franchise from MH Tri on the Wii and haven't missed a game in the series. I was a little late with MH Stories, also thinking it wasn't a real MH game, but was I wrong. Every tiny detail in MHST is an ode or tribute to the whole franchise. If you think the Monster are the heroes of the main series, they really shine in Stories. Nothing beats fighting aside the monsters you are normally hunting and the way they are portraied in the game makes you instantly feel a connection to them. Every movement, every attack, every backlash from a hit, every little detail in this game harkens back to the main series. I ADORE Lagiacrus since I first saw the creature in Tri. I love it's battle tune, I love it's roar, I can dream its fight, it is my number one Monster. And nothing gives me greater pleasure than to beat up enemy monsters and Riders with my Ivory Lagiacrus by my side. Every monster looks awesome, every attack comes straight from the Main series, every detail is loingly created to honor the source material.Yes, the game is super colorful. Yes, the story is written for 6-10 year old Japanese boys and girls, real shounen, including 'irritating' mascotte that talks way too much and is waaaay to hyperactive with a very annoying voice. But then i am used to that. I watched enough anime with lots of female actors with super high and cutesy voices doing many a animal/doll mascotte. But if you can look past that, then there is a reall long, deep MH experience to be found, including many deep RPG mechanics, looting, gear crafting, etc, etc,The music is great, the fighting is great, the story is great and sometimes very dark and while you are fighting next to Monsters instead of only hunting them, this game is through and through Monster Hunter.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this game but by the end of the story I was feeling incredibly tired of it all and just wanted it to be over. There's so many little issues with this game that drag it down and the only thing holding it up is the fact it's incredibly cute and has excellent aesthetic both visually and audibly. I have a lot of harsh things to say, but it should be noted I have this much to say because I did have positive feelings towards the experience for the most part, so I do recommend giving it a try if you love monster hunter and have A LOT of patience.- The story is kinda weak honestly. It is very much an anime for young boys where friendship triumphs over all, the best friend turns into an angsty rival, and the villains are comically evil to the point its annoying. I think the general writing and most characters are fine, but the overall story points feel childish without merit.- The game has a strong narrative focus on the bonds you form with your monsters, but gameplay encourages you to treat them as disposable given the system of egg hatching and channeling where you essenetially re-roll until you get a good monster, and then use up other monsters to make them stronger. It almost felt like playing a gacha game.- While travelling the world there are various obstacles that require specific monsters to overcome e.g. you need a monster that can Jump to cross a gap, or a monster that can Swim to cross a river. It's extremely similar to Pokemon's Hidden Machine moves, except in this case, you cannot teach a monster how to swim, it must simply be a monster that can innately swim. This means your party composition is extremely heavily influence by what utility they have rather than your enjoyment of the monster or even their combat potential. This problem is reinforced by the fact you can only carry 5 monsters (6 later), and can only change them by going back to a town.- Simply finding monsters to obtain materials, eggs or quest clears felt extremely tedious a lot of the time. I get that the point was to have rare monsters, but this ended up dragging things out in a way that wasn't enjoyable. If you look up guides, most people recommend you obtain a specific monster that has the ability to force an encounter with a random monster which you use repeatedly until you find the monster you want. This is heavily reliant on chance, and is extremely dull.- Your character's equipment strongly dictates how well you'll fair against enemies, so logically you should switch equipment for better elements/skills to face specific foes, but so many story important enemies are given to you by surprise and offer no chance to change equipment without reloading a save.- Combat revolves around a scissors-paper-rock system where certain attacks trump other attacks, and the dialogue given when you lose such a match-up insists that there's a "pattern" but in most encounters it feels the enemy monster picks at random, though admittedly biased towards certain attacks depending on the monster. Regardless, it didn't feel good to play.- The other parts of the battle system are fine, but overall lacking in enjoyable complexity.

_childDocuments_.review: GameplayMonster Hunter Stories uses a turn-based battle system, and Rock, Paper, Scissor mechanic as their way of battling. Meanwhile players must consider the abilities, strengths and weaknesses of their monsters when planning their attacks.The turn-based system also introduces an element of planning and strategy, making battles feel more like a tactical puzzle than a frantic action sequence. Even though it introduce us to PVP which is abit out on point due to the monster always target player and if player lost, you lost so is more like Player Hunting instead of Monster HuntingGame story and settingMonster Hunter Stories is a fascinating narrative that revolves around the relationship between hunters and their monstrous partners, set in a lively world where people and monsters coexist. Gamers assume the character of a young Rider with the ability to develop a close bond with monsters, referred to as "Monsties". As you set out on a quest to discover the truth behind an old legend, the plot develops as you encounter a range of characters and navigate exquisitely designed settings. With well-developed characters and an endearing yet daring tale, the premise is captivating.Graphics and designMonster Hunter Stories is characterized by its charming, anime-inspired graphic style. The colorful, cel-shaded graphics deviate from the more realistic look of the main series and give the game a whimsical and inviting feel. The environments are richly detailed and varied, from lush forests to arid deserts and toward icy plains, and are complemented by fluid animations and expressive character designs.Meanwhile it doesn't require you to have a strong GPU or PC Spec to even play this game.Sound and musicThe game's soundtrack is an absolute delight with an orchestral score that adds to the sense of adventure and immersion in the game scenarioTo summarise,Monster Hunter Stories is an excellent entry to the Monster Hunter series for younger generations as an exposure slowly heading toward the GRUESOME SLAUGHTERING in monster hunting of the main series.

There is no depth, no plot twist and the story itself is terrible generic and makes very often even no sense.- Our character isn't the main character but Navirou instead. Does our character even says one word? I can't remember a single one... Navirou talks for us everytime, this is unbelievable annoying. - Post game is terrible. He deals tons of damage, makes aoe attacks and can act twice a round. On top of that is the terrible rock paper scissors combat system that seems kinda rigged. - Denuvo

_childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me!I went into this game without a whole lot of expectations, but ended up sinking a lot of hours in without ever really getting tired of it.I enjoy the monster designs, music, sound design, and storytelling. _childDocuments_.review: A great JRPG and monster collector. Capcom somehow made this formula work with Monster Hunter back on the 3DS, and I'm happy I finally got to play it, even after it's sequel. I think it's a pretty good starting point for anyone interested in the Monster Hunter series.The voice acting is good, and it does a lot to give personality to the supporting cast. The story is pretty average for a JRPG, but it has a few standout scenes. There are some dark moments you wouldn't generally expect from a game like this, much like the sequel. I found Navirou to be a lot less annoying here, and it was great seeing the origins of the companion characters.The Monsters and character models look pretty good, the textures and environments however... Let's just say, it's obvious it's a 3DS port. Not a deal-breaker for me, but it might be for some. Weapons and Armor really steal the show. You expect the variety on display if you've played MH before, but the amount of weapon and armor sets available here are vastly superior than your average RPG. All the weapons and armors you know and love from the main series look great in this artstyle.Combat is unique. I think the sequel improves on it, but it's still good here. It's strategy based with some RNG elements, but it can be reduced with the right team and build. It's really important to learn monster "types" or preferences. It's kinda like rock-paper-scissors, except the enemy only has 2 options available, and you can't directly control the move your monster chooses without kinship (mana). If you have knowledge from the main games, a lot of it applies. Like using sonic bombs on monsters when they're underground.Overall, it's a smaller, more digestible package in comparison with it's sequel. It feels a lot more feasible to achieve "everything" if that's your kinda thing. I really like that. It's a ton of fun. If you're into Monster Hunter, Pokemon, or both, I'd say it's a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter Stories 1 is one of those games where you end up Monday morning quarterbacking, wishing the devs had tweaked just a few things to turn a good game into a great one. It’s a turn-based JRPG spin on the beloved Monster Hunter series, and despite some gripes, I enjoyed my 40 hours with it. This was only my second Monster Hunter game (after World), but Stories retained a lot of the series’ DNA, with fan-favorite monsters to hunt down and gear to craft from their parts. Each new area brings a new set of monsters and upgrades, and I appreciated the relatively low grind. You rarely need more than a few of each monster to complete armor or weapon sets, which keeps things moving at a nice pace.The characters are a high point, especially Navirou, your Felyne companion, who brings humor and charm to the adventure. The story itself is simple yet engaging, and I was happy to see it through to the end. Visually, you can tell it’s a 3DS game, so don’t expect too much graphically. That said, the art style does justice to the gear and monster designs, and I loved browsing the new gear options after unlocking an area. One big downside, though, is the lack of music during exploration in open areas. It makes things feel empty and, honestly, I ended up playing my own music in the background. It’s one of those small things that would’ve made a big difference.Where MHS1 stumbles is in the battle system, which has both promise and flaws. The rock-paper-scissors combat with Power, Technical, and Speed attacks feels like it should add depth, but instead, it often relies on luck. Your monster’s actions are AI-controlled, and while you can use points to command special moves, you can’t choose their basic attacks. This limitation becomes frustrating, especially since enemies don’t follow predictable attack patterns. This, along with the slow leveling for new monsters, means you’ll likely stick with the same roster most of the game. Despite these issues, I did enjoy my time with MHS1—just not enough to jump into the post-game content, which was disappointing since it promises new monster options and challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: A really good remaster.Story:It pretty much follows the original story, but with some slight unnecessary dialogue changes at times. Anyway, the story really doesn't get started until midway really. Which it is about a character hatching a Rathalos, who protected them at the cost of an eye. Later reuniting, as you see how they rise and overcome their challenges. The black dread that spread, and a legend that foretold a legendary Elder Dragon. The conflict between two friends, and how their hatred for monsters pushed them to try and seek to end the blight in their own way. Everyone once being apart, eventually joining together to tackle their challenges. Though, the notable point is seeing Ratha endure and continuously rise to meet their challenge.This game is still far better than Monster Hunter Stories 2, which the story amongst other things was terrible in other words.Battle System:It follows a triangular rock, paper, scissors system. Power, Tech, and Speed. Power beats Tech, Tech beats Speed, and Speed beats power. If you are successful in a clash, your endured damage is reduced, and you will not fall below one HP.Skills also cost Kinship to use, and can be used to offset some of the RNG. Unlike the second game, there is a pattern in this game, but it is not set. Which makes it a bit harder than the second game. Another thing is the Ride option, when the Kinship gauge is filled. You can mount the monster. Each time you are successful in a clash, you raise the level by 1, up to a level of 3. The Ride skill can be used at lvl 1, and does major damage in a cutscene, which are very well crafted. At the expense of dismounting, using this effectively can turn battles in your favor.One more thing to note, are the equipment. Using the same as your monster will reduce Kinship cost. Not the most useful, but something to consider. While the system is a bit simplistic, it is better executed than the second game, which kinda falls flat.Exploration:While not as wide as the second game, there are tons of wide open spaces to explore. And even the Den's have subsections. Going into Monster Den's is how you get eggs, and there might be a guard as well.Egg Hatching/Traits:Far better and more complex than Stories 2. Balancing on natural level up learned skills, changing gene elements, etc. The tons of customization makes Stories 1 amazing as well.Side Quests:Tons, too much for me to list.Music: Still amazing.Art Style/ Graphics:Way better than the original.Overall:I am glad I bought this again, it was a nice run down to the past with a good touch up. The story still slams hard, and unlike 2. The main character is actually relevant in this game. I don't know how they managed to do this with a silent protagonist, but they did, so got my respect for that.I just hope if there is a Monster Hunter Stories 3, they follow a similar line to the first. However, while also doing something new and engaging.

_childDocuments_.review:
The World of Monster Hunter Stories
In a world where large monsters roam, and people everywhere make a living hunting, there's a remote village of people who follow a different set of customs. They are the Monster Riders, a people who don't hunt but instead form bonds with monsters.

Unlike hunters, they raise and live in harmony with monsters, forming inseparable bonds with them using mysterious artifacts known as Kinship Stones.

The monsters that form kinships with Riders, known as "Monsties," possess incredible powers. By becoming a Rider, you too can befriend countless Monsties, riding them as you explore a vast, exciting world. Join the adventure and "Ride On!"

 Game Features
- Recruit countless Monsties!
Monsties, and the bonds you form with them, are the backbone of your adventure. Explore vast environments and dungeons to find monster dens, and bring back the eggs you find to hatch new Monsties!

- Fight with your Monsties in Network Battles!
Take your hero and the Monsties you've raised into battles with other Riders! Build a team of your favorites to challenge other players.

- New features for the smartphone version!
New improvements include beautiful high-resolution graphics, improved user interface, and a new auto-save feature!

 Story
The story begins in a forest near the village of Riders. Three young friendsthe hero, Lilia, and Chevalstumble upon a shining egg.

The trio perform a playful imitation of the Rite of Kinship, only to be shocked when it actually succeeds!

The egg hatches, revealing a baby Rathalos, a flying wyvern also known as "the King of the Skies." The trio affectionately name him "Ratha," and take him back to the village.

Days later, without warning, the village is beset upon by a monster infected by "the Black Blight." They manage to drive it away, but not before it devastates the townand leaves indelible scars in the hearts of Cheval and Lilia.

A year passes...

The hero receives a Kinship Stone from the Village Chief and officially becomes a Rider. Cheval and Lilia both leave the village, each on their own path. The hero, though separated now from childhood friends, partners up with the cheerful Navirou, and embarks upon a new adventure into the world of hunters.

A story of friendship and triumph await youride on into the world of Monster Hunter Stories!

detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition includes: Mary Skelter Finale digital game Character Art Collection Rough Art Collection Original Soundtracks and Art Inlays (78 tracks total) x10 PC Wallpapers x7 Mobile Wallpapers PC Theme About the Game The last installment of the dungeon-crawling RPG trilogy reaches its stunning conclusion! Will the Blood Maidens finally get their happily ever after? Jail - a living prison for humans, buried 666 meters underground. It appeared suddenly several decades ago, giving birth to monsters called Marchen and patrolled by madness-inducing Nightmares. A group of prisoners, Jack and the Blood Maidens, were reincarnations of fairy tales who dared to escape. They climbed from the bottom of the tower up to the surface, filled with hope... But outside were thousands of corpses soaking in a sea of blood. There stood beings known as Massacre Pink, smiling. In that moment, hope was destroyed. The group was torn asunder, with Jack and the Blood Maidens scattered to their own paths. Separated, they are each drawn to the devouring Jail that floats in the sky... This is the finale to the tale of the Blood Maidens. Both the Steam game and Deluxe Edition includes Mary Skelter: Locked Up in Love - True End and Locked Up In Love - Blood High (DLCs in previous versions of the game). Locked Up in Love - True End is canonical to the Mary Skelter series, while Locked Up In Love - Blood High (also included in-game), is a spinoff of the Mary Skelter characters in a school setting. Please note that the True End and the spin-off, Blood High, uses Japanese voices with the options of English, Japanese, or Traditional Chinese subtitles. The base game will still have English and Japanese voiceover options.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to discuss about this game, from its conclusion, to the PC port and baffling translation decisions. The series has suffered from poor PC ports outsourced to a developer known for lying and lacking quality control, which is sad given how criminally underrated this game series is. I'm writing this review out of tough love.My playtime on Steam might seem short. I spent most of my time on the Switch port. I pre-ordered the Switch LE for $100 and played mostly on a Switch emulator using my own ROM dump w/ DLC and the day one patch. The game on the Switch had issues with slowdown from double-buffered VSync and a 30FPS cap in battles. This review is from someone who spent 180+ hours w/ the entire series, unlike some reviewers and YouTubers who lack prior experience.I will refer to Ghostlight by GL.My complaints w/ the story is the lack of development for new characters, and no downtime between towers. Unlike MS 1 and 2, there's little room for character interactions or building connections. While  focus on the main cast, new characters aren't. Interviews revealed the character artist, Nanameda Kei, wanted Mary and Charlotte to appear earlier, which explains them feeling less fleshed out compared to other new characters like Toh or Shira. The writer of these games, Otono Yomoji, comes from writing LNs, I believe he's more qualified to write than failed Hollywood director hacks.The conclusion ends on a good note, despite predictable twists.  I enjoyed how NPC characters in previous games, like Clara (Haru's assistant), were fleshed out. I'm relieved the game concluded satisfyingly, avoiding cheap subversions or vagueness for potential sequels. It contrasts sharply w/ Danganronpa V3, which exemplifies what not to do.QoL improvements, like viewing other endings w/o replaying the final boss, are appreciated. This game includes events from MS 1 and 2 in the Extras. Despite that, you're doing yourself a massive disservice by not playing those games. Most people aren't going to the extras. and will end up lost. Read the prequel novels for more context after playing.The MS series is an accessible entry into dungeon crawler RPGs because it's streamlined gameplay, and how you form connections w/ the characters, rather than having blank slate hires.Turn based combat in these games can be a gauntlet if you don't take advantage of various gameplay mechanics. Like FromSoft games, the difficulty depends on how you use game mechanics, jobs, jail mutators, or even the storage glitch. The swimsuit job provide a huge HP boost at first, but you later need to experiment. Abilities like Little Mermaid's or Sleeping Beauty's arrows help clear areas quick. The insectimares were frustrating. I enjoyed the party-switch and item sharing gimmicks, a great example of gameplay serving the story and vice versa.What does this port offer? Steam sales make it cheaper ($20 for the series vs. $40 for just one), and you avoid the hassle of managing DLC on the eShop. But the convenience is outweighed by issues.Even buying the downgraded Switch port (What this port is based on), then dumping a ROM backup w/ the DLC, gives you a better experience than these ports.Every issue I listed in my MS2 review exists here. Consider this section to be Part 2 of that review:The new issues:I believe GL chose to port from the Switch due to their familiarity w/ Switch ports, even if they had access to the PS4 code, or could request it (MS2). They got CN and JP support in Finale's PC port, despite not releasing the previous 2 games in those regions (GL cited licensing issues), and lied about not having access to uncensored builds of Mugen Souls 1 & Z (The uncensored EAS Switch ports of those games are based on the PC ports w/ checks in the game .EXEs that verify specific files before unlocking censored content). I can't forgive devs who lie and make excuses.The devs had their hands tied by Sony w/ the purification minigame. There's images of characters in black one-pieces in the game's extras, so it's clear it was planned. Cutting that wasn't enough, as it still got banned from Australia despite nothing their classifications board cited being in the game to "justify" it. MS2 DIDN'T get banned despite being raunchier. It calls back to the bogus Atelier rating that birthed the "High Impact Sexual Violence" meme.Judging by the past 3-4 IF games, and CH's new "corporate policies", which even affected retailer specific JP only bonuses, it's a mistake to release on PlayStation. Their Switch sales are far better. They stated in 2015 they wouldn't release games if forced to censor, a statement now at odds w/ their recent actions.While parts of the TL seem fine, there's typos in dialogue. Action descriptions, and item descriptions appear hastily machine TL'd and make no sense. While 1 and 2's TLs were dry, I appreciate how straight-forward it was to read and wasn't littered w/ slang or memes that age poorly. They were serviceable. This one has issues.Character names were changed in the EN TL, noticeable in the JP audio. For example, Juu is now Toh, , and Genocide Pink is now Massacre Pink, a change I think removes intent and downplays their motives. , doesn't make it a Nazi allegory.Hameln's dialogue was TL'd in a way that conflicts w/ her character. Several scenes involving Mary have garbled text related to the word "Baby," such as "Acting like baby" or "Smells like baby," which doesn't make sense in context.Gretel's Blood Ability, "Bread Portal", got changed to "Breadcrumbs" in Finale, despite tutorial text, the icon being bread, and the previous 2 games referring to it normally.Around release, an Otome game published by IFI (Cupid Paradise) was delayed for TL issues, but Finale wasn't. While IFI generally preserves the intent better than many, their practices, like Nexon's Blue Archive TL, still have blatant issues flying under noses.This isn't as great as 2, and 1 feels more fleshed out. But this has the strongest OST and more Clara.Wait for a sale. $7 (as of 2024) is a fair deal, but not $40. Buy on PS4, and get the JP PS4 version of MS2 if you have the chance.EDIT: Video playback issues have been resolved with the current Proton 9 and Experimental builds as of writing. Setting aside some CPU scheduler issues, this is now playable on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game in the state that it is currently. I knew that the game would be based on the Switch version, but I did not realize that it would actively hinder the experience of the game. It also appears this version has other issues as well. Starting with one of the larger ones, there is a voice file missing in an early cut scene that causes the game to either crash or lock up when it tries to load the file. it seems like the issue is exclusive to the English dub as well as the scene plays without issue when set to the Japanese voice option. Ironically, the cut scene in question isn't even voiced in English. As a bit of a side note, the lack of a full English dub is no surprise to me. It seems like Idea Factory games have been getting progressively less English voice acting in the recent years, and I was not expecting this game to be different. While this cut scene in question does happen within the first two or so hours of the game, it does make me concerned that it will not be the only instance in which it occurs. And while I would be content with playing the game in Japanese, there are other issues that have already left a strong negative impression within that short period of time.To be fair, issues may be a bit harsh, as none of these cause the game to crash or performance to suffer in any way, these are things that impact the player experience in a negative way. The first, and probably the bigger of the two I want to bring up, is the lighting. The game is extremely bright, and it completely ruins the dark, tense atmosphere that the game is trying to present. The sense of delving into a dark dungeon where a nightmare could be around any corner is gone, instead the lighting removes any sense of tension. Encountering a nightmare feels like someone merely dimmed the lights in the room. The issue is not purely aesthetic either. The bright lighting makes seeing some of the gimmicks in the dungeon much harder than it should be or could have ever been intended to be. What's worse, in my opinion at least, is that this issue then encourages you to either constantly look at the top of the screen as it is the only place you can see them easily, or have the map fully expanded so that it provides a darker background through which you can see the beams created by the gimmicks in question. Finally, there appears to be other issues with the sound other than what I mentioned previously. While I could not say for certain if these are intentional, it does seem odd that these would be missing. The first thing that stood out to me was the lack of music in one of the dungeon areas. While this could be intentional, it feels strange one dungeon would no background music or sound at all. The other thing I've noticed is that the nightmares do not growl or yell when you encounter them at the start of Chase Mode, formerly Murder Hunt. Again, this could be intentional, but it feels like such a strange decision as it again takes away from the atmosphere of the game. All in all, I'm disappointed by the game. I do intend to complete it even in the state that is in currently, but it feels lacking and underwhelming. While I do want to be optimistic and believe that these issues could be be fixed in an update patch, I feel that it is very unlikely to happen anytime soon. These issues would have been known during both development and testing of the port, and considering the game still released in this state, I feel it is a bit foolish to think it will be corrected.

_childDocuments_.review: Mary Skelter 2 on Steam I could put aside it's obvious issues because they weren't horrendous, the game didn't look terrible (although the PS4 graphics should've been an option even if the Switch version was the only English release, this is Steam after all), the price was good, censorship issue got a patch and you got 2 games that were both brilliant.And now we're here and this port is... uh not great and not worth buying without a deep discount or a love for this series.This is a port of the Switch version of the game and is missing the PS4 (which got an English release) graphics which add detail to the levels and make them much more readable. Some areas in this game have blinding brightness levels and it looks bad and feels bad.The only graphical options are the Resolution and if the game is Windowed, Borderless and Full Screen, again PS4 game why can't we have options for that stuff on Steam. Why are we stuck with Switch graphics.There's a missing wall in the Forzen Jail TowerVideos don't work on Steam Deck / Linux* despite them clearly having set up input options for Steam Deck so support was most likely intended (A selected Steam Deck Layout is provided and there's Deck Touch Screen Configurations.). And not port related but game releated why is Hameln so different in the English "Localisation"???She was one of my favourite characters in MS2/MS and here she is just different with sparks here and there of her in the previous games.There's also quite a lot noticeable script changes in the ENG Localisation with quite a lot being cut just from listening to the audio and then reading the text.Feels rushed, poor and low quality.Aside from this so far it's been more Mary Skelter, just with giant floors and surprisingly awesome music. A lot of the music makes me feel right at home with Sonic & the Black Knight and the Nightmare chase music is just a straight banger now rather than attempting to sound creepy. I am supposed to be running away from Nightmares, right?It's just now there's some unexcusable issues that ruin the experience that come from a publisher that doesn't care and hasn't for a long while now (Hello IFI, where's Neptunia Game Maker on Steam?) and a bad porting studio ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up another game to add to their list of ruined games. (Hello Ghostlight, when are you going to fix Mugen Souls + Z?).A (so far) great game slashed with issues.Edit: Also this game has terrible loading times, I'm not sure what's going on but a game like Forza Horizon 5 or Call of Duty: Cold War load instantly but here they take a while, not counted how long but it's around 10 seconds ish and it builds up and gets annoying when you have to zap constantly.Edit 2: Forgot to mention that buying the Digital Deluxe Edition forces you to download the Digital Deluxe content which I find annoying as I would untick it from the DLC menu on PC's other than my main to save time downloading. So thanks IFI.Edit 3: Eiserne Tower has 2 missing walls, because of course it does. And Grave Tower stutters. Badly. It's almost like I'm playing an Unreal Engine title. Looking at the Frametime graph it looks so bad with massive spikes.Edit 4: Got the True Ending, Locked up in Love True End had the main story unlocked but after restarting the game to have a break the option is now gone. Bravo.Edit 5: It seems like this game has been left abandoned. This is a complete shame considering how amazing MS:F is. This port doesn't do this game good enough. Thanks IFI, I guess?* Edit 6: Valve have supplied re-encoded videos for Linux & Steam Deck for both the English and Japanese videos making the game playable on Linux now.However the game is near unplayable on Steam Deck on the Stable Branch (unsure of Beta) in gamemode now due to the game most of the time crashing as it attempts to load the videos. Desktop mode (and a normal Linux desktop) works perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, look. So I've been reading the reviews and a whole lotta cats have been talking about the port and its issues for the most part, taking the rest of the game as a no-brainer or just something the reader's already familiar with. That's fine, and the port DOES have issues, but I figure a lot of people are also curious to know what this game actually is and whether or not it's actually even worth playing. Short answer: if you're a big fan of the Mary Skelter franchise, yes. Otherwise, probably not? If you've never heard of Mary Skelter before, straight up just don't play this game yet. It's the conclusion to a years-long story arc. It does come with a full recap of the previous two game's storylines including an (unvoiced) cutscene collection but, it's an objectively inferior way of experiencing the previous games. So, get outta here, go play Nightmares or 2 first. Preferably 2. And *then* you can come back.The game itself... It should be noted that this game was developed at the peak of the pandemic, and appears to have been made on somewhat short notice. So, with that in mind I think what's important to realize about the game is that it feels like an ambitious project that was marred by budget constraints, time constraints, and a troubled development cycle.You're gonna be surprised to find that this game is SUBSTANTIALLY more gameplay-oriented than it is story-oriented, much to my chagrin. It's got a whole lot of story at the beginning and at the end, but, the midsection of the game, where, you know, you'd expect quite a bit of development, is marked by hours and hours of entirely plotless gameplay.  This is odd compared to the previous two games, where every dungeon has plenty of story. This is a huge disappointment because the story would really be improved with more development for characters, especially the newer characters and NPCs.  A lot of the NPCs, returning and new, don't get to do much the whole game (despite getting hints and teases), and unlike a certain OP ANGEL, don't get an excuse for it.In general, this game prioritizes exploring the newer characters much more than it values the older characters, and the thing is, it doesn't even actually have enough story content to develop all of its newer characters. As a game that sets itself up to be the grand finale of the entire franchise, the fact you don't get to see as much of the older characters that you got to know and love over 2 very lengthy games and mini-novels is really sad. Hameln especially gets the short end of the stick especially given just how great she was in 2. Jack's team gets the worst of this, as at least Toh and Clara's teams revolve around their new characters.This game has fewer dungeons compared to 1 and 2, but they're also much longer. The four 'main dungeons' you spend the most time in are massive. I actually don't think this is a good thing. Exploration can get really tedious, especially with the new three party system. You're constantly swapping back and forth to get items and exchange them which can only be done in specific spots in the dungeon. The puzzles are not innovative for the standards of the franchise, either.Towards the end of the game I was so tired of doing the dungeons that I started ignoring rooms that weren't part of the critical path, which is, like, uh, REALLY BAD for a dungeon crawling game, where, you know, the EXPLORATION is the MAIN POINT! This is not in any way helped by the fact that, even though they severely nerfed Blood Farming from 2, Blood Farming is STILL strong, and makes it so that going out of your way to find chests is just not very rewarding. The gameplay balance is what you'd expect from the franchise. I actually think this game is a bit harder than 2 and 1 but, still pretty easy to cheese. EXP and Blood Crystal gain is very slow and getting an achievement required me to use an item duplication glitch which is again not the greatest look.The ending of this game is... it's certainly conclusive, but, I think it's a bit abrupt, and, sadly, didn't feel all that satisfying to me. It's overall not terrible, but I questioned a lot of its logic.This game has a lot of odd decisions like this that are only explainable if you presume that the game had development issues and ran out of money or time before they could properly finish it. This game has so, so many amazing ideas that just desperately needed more time to bake. There's a huge, shining gem underneath all the soil surrounding this game that they just... couldn't get to.That being said, you may have noticed that this is a positive review, despite my criticism all this time. There's three major reasons why I recommend this game to longtime fans of the series, and one minor reason.The minor reason is that the three party system is genuinely unique and interesting. I actually had fun doing the dungeons early on and if they had been better paced with story content, I would've loved it the whole way through. It's an unique idea with lots of unique applications, though it's a shame each individual party doesn't get more creative puzzles despite having fixed party members. The only real downsides are the fact that the parties are badly balanced due to the class distribution between them (FWIW if we had Warrior Hameln from 2 all of Clara's party's problems would be solved) and because transferring items between parties  is a huge pain.The three major reasons are Toh, Pyre and the bonus DLC content. Toh and Pyre have amazing arcs and a really good dynamic with their parties, and Toh alone does so much for the franchise as a whole that he's easily the best character introduced in this game. Really, their parties were designed for them. It's a shame I can't say that about Mary and Charlotte. My only real criticisms are that Toh has an ending to his arc that feels conclusive, but really unfair given what his character's been through (not really that big of a deal just a subjective opinion especially given this franchise's tendency to treat the characters softly) and that a certain character associated with Toh does not get to talk or do much, and in fact that does not even get a design, which is a bit disappointing given that we get a description of their appearance.The bonus content was originally released as DLC for 2 and Finale but is bundled with the PC version for free. They're ""dating sim"" VNs with a school theme for the first one and a beach theme for the second one. It's great stuff and gives a lot of characterization and cute moments for all the old characters, especially TsuuHime. Charlotte, Mary and Pyre unfortunately get shafted, with no unique CGs. This alone made the game worth it for me.So, if you absolutely LOVED 2 and 1, then you will get some closure in this game and I still think you'll enjoy yourself even if it's an inferior experience to the first two games. If you only just kinda enjoyed them or didn't like them, this game will not fix the issues they had, in fact it'll make them worse. Unless you were just there for the dungeon crawling gameplay. Then enjoy yourself I guess. You weirdo. Why not just play Etrian Odyssey or something?P.S. I. Hameln's old JP voice actress retired, so they got a new one for her this game. It took some getting used to, but she does her best and it shows. As always, the English dub is not complete, so I do not recommend using it. And if you're a weeb, - and let's be honest, look at you - you'd probably gravitate towards the JP dub anyways.P.S. II. Due to Sony's newer content guidelines, this game lacks the purge minigame and censors some of the Blood Skelter designs (though not all for whatever reason). Not a huge loss for me, but if fanservice is one of your main angles of enjoyment for this franchise, keep that in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: The start of the game is a bit slow. All the characters are separated and you have to complete each starting dungeon with small parties of 2 or 3 characters before they reunite. But once they reunite it really gets going. Combat is really engaging with a full team. Each girl can chose from 5 jobs at the start that change their skills and stats and give them new outfits. There are dungeon modifiers to make them more difficult in exchance of extra rewards. There a lot blood related mechanics that may sound a bit much at first but are actually well balanced.If you never played the first 2 games you can view their stories in the bonus section. The game includes a VN where you can date each of the girls (you have to press LB/RB on the main menu screen). The PC version includes all of the DLC including the extra jobs.

_childDocuments_.review: Mary Skelter Finale - A Gripping Conclusion to a Dark Fairytale! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)In the realm of dungeon-crawling RPGs, where the descent into madness and the unknown often await around every corner, Mary Skelter Finale stands as a shining testament to storytelling and gameplay mastery. As the third and final chapter of the Mary Skelter trilogy, this game takes players on an exhilarating journey that challenges their wits and immerses them in a dark fairytale world. Set in the enigmatic confines of the Jail, a living prison buried deep underground, Mary Skelter Finale is a rollercoaster ride of emotions, suspense, and strategic combat.The story picks up where the previous installment left off, with the protagonists, Jack and the Blood Maidens, struggling to find their way in a world overrun by grotesque creatures known as Marchen and haunted by the nightmarish Nightmares. The central narrative question that has plagued players throughout the series is whether the Blood Maidens, reincarnations of fairy tale characters, will ever attain their elusive happily ever after. In Mary Skelter Finale, this question looms larger than ever as the stakes reach their zenith.The game's setting is nothing short of mesmerizing. The Jail, a prison 666 meters beneath the earth's surface, is a captivatingly eerie and oppressive environment, effectively setting the stage for the nightmarish tale that unfolds. The juxtaposition of whimsical fairy tale elements against the grim backdrop of the Jail is a masterstroke in storytelling, drawing players into a world that is both enchanting and horrifying.The character development in Mary Skelter Finale is nothing short of remarkable. Players have been on a long journey with Jack and the Blood Maidens, and in this final chapter, the emotional depth and complexity of these characters are brought to the forefront. Their individual struggles, past traumas, and dreams of escape create a strong emotional bond between players and the cast, making every victory, every loss, and every plot twist hit home with a resounding impact.Gameplay is where Mary Skelter Finale truly shines. The dungeon-crawling mechanics are finely tuned, offering a challenging and rewarding experience for both newcomers and series veterans. The game introduces innovative features like the Massacre Pink, formidable adversaries that add a layer of tension and strategy to battles. The combination of turn-based combat, character customization, and the need for careful resource management keeps players engaged and constantly adapting their strategies as they delve deeper into the mysterious Jail.Mary Skelter Finale's presentation is another standout aspect. The game's visuals are a testament to the developers' commitment to creating a captivating atmosphere. From the grotesque yet mesmerizing Marchen designs to the eerie and haunting locations within the Jail, the art and graphics are nothing short of breathtaking. The soundtrack, with its haunting melodies and evocative compositions, further enhances the immersive experience, effectively pulling players into the twisted fairytale world.However, it's worth noting that Mary Skelter Finale isn't without its flaws. The game's intricate plot can be a bit convoluted at times, requiring players to pay close attention to the unfolding events. Additionally, newcomers to the series might find themselves overwhelmed by the wealth of lore and backstory that has accumulated over the trilogy. However, for those who have followed the series from the beginning, these elements are more of a reward than a hindrance, adding depth and layers to the overall narrative.In conclusion, Mary Skelter Finale is a magnificent conclusion to a captivating RPG trilogy. It expertly weaves a dark fairytale narrative with strategic gameplay, compelling characters, and a visually stunning world that will leave players spellbound from start to finish. While it may not be the most accessible entry point for newcomers, for fans of the series, it is a rewarding and emotionally resonant experience that beautifully ties together the threads of a mesmerizing tale. Mary Skelter Finale is a testament to the power of storytelling in gaming and cements its place as a must-play title for RPG enthusiasts.Interested in discovering great Steam games? _childDocuments_.review: The port is not that bad if you compared it to the switch version, its the same game but with better framerate and loading time. I wished they port from the PS4 version, like everyone else, but i dont expect too much from IFI at this point.I didnt have any issues with the game from start to finish, no crashes and no visible framedrops (the "classic" IF constant 63fps). If you played the second game on PC, you can expect the same level of port quality for this game, not that great for PC standards but playable. Just be aware that the lightning, on 3D or 2D elements, and 3D textures arent looking good in this version but you can make the lightning more bearable with Reshade. Moreover this game seems to have a proper 2k resolution compared to the previous one.About the game, its more of the same previous games except you need to manage 15 characters this time and the dungeon are way bigger with better level design, it's "quality over quantity" for the dungeons this time. The story was enjoyable with nothing suprising going on.It took me 87h to 100% the game. The last chapter is a point of no return for the characters events so be careful of that.For The DLCs, there are two differents ones despite their names. It's highly suggested that you finish the main game before doing them because they serve as an epilogue for each girls.The first "Mary Skelter: Locked Up in Love" is a short VN focused on fan-service following the second bad ending of the game. With a common route who takes about 20min + 5min per girls (main Blood Maidens casts without Otsuu, Little Mermaid, Mary, Charlotte and Pyre). You can't save during the VN part but you can skip the common route to a heroine route after you complete the VN at least once. Furthermore you unlock an extra route with Otsuu after one completion. It's ok if you want more lovely events with the differents heroines, there are new models for each heroines and new CGs but you can skip this and only do the second DLC.The sescond VN "Mary Skelter: Locked Up in Love True end" is a short VN focused on fan-service following the true ending of the game. There is a route for each characters, Blood Maidens and humans ones. You need to finish the main game to unlock all the events for each characters. Took about 10min per girls and 5 for the "main game" story. Like the previous DLC you have new and more CGs and one swimsuit model for each Blood Maidens compared to the first DLC. It's a sweet epilogue for each girl in the game. Don't expect more than that story-wise. The only downside of the VN is that each girls have 3 events to watch and the game go back to the main menu each time at the end of an event.Overall score : 6.5/10The good :-All of the mains characters in the series are used in battle. You have to manage 3 differents team each have his own dungeon parts to explore.-The level design is overall better than the previous game. In general each floor of a dungeon relies on a mechanic for each team, you need to use one specific blood abilities to resolve the puzzle.-The story is great and i loved the new characters. All of them are japanese dubbed which is a big plus.-Best OST of the series in my opinion. One different for each tower, same for the normal battle depending of the tower.-Overall the jobs balance is better than the previous games.The bad :-Straight port from the Switch version : the lightning/post processing/textures issues are still there, its clearly visible if you compared it to the PS4 version. The loading time are a bit long but still better than the Switch. You can make it look a bit better with Reshade if needed. I dont know if it's the same in the PS4/switch version but there are 1 missing wall textures in the Froze Jail Tower and 2 in the Eiserne Tower.-The dungeons are overall too long, one less floor should have been perfect. Some rooms/puzzles required a lot of back and forth and an extensive use of blood skills, in partcular Hameln attraction animation is too long.-In chapter 3 onward you can encounter previous mini bosses as standard ennemies, they hit like a truck specially on normal/fear and are not worth the trouble, the xp and loot arent that great if you kill them. It forces you to escape the battle everytime you encounter them (the encounter rate of these monsters is more important in the last dungeon) and it's a high chance of a game over if two of them ambush you. It makes the overall gameplay experience a bit laborious.-The bloodfarm is limited, same as the previous game. It's bad since you need to farm for 3 teams of 5 characters. Furthermore, Hameln is the only one who can pull all the flowers and who can improve "rng" the loot making her team the best to bloodfarm.-The new xp make the blood devolution system worthless. We gain twice less xp than before so re-leveling up characters is a chore.-Like the previous games, a lot of skills are useless.

_childDocuments_.review: ok, finally finished the game and see the endingsi love it, a great ending to the seriesi would rate it about 8.5/10which one did i buy ? deluxe editioni know from what everyone here says this is the switch version ported here on to pc, unfortunately i dont have the luxury of having a switch to really compare between the two myselfso this is just my perspective of going into this finale after waiting years for it to come out on pc and not knowing that much about the switch version it selflikes :- great soundtracks (deluxe edition will give you all of the soundtracks of the game from the first game to this finale game)- great story- zapping between party is unique to me- "before story" is really nice to have especially when you havent played the previous part of the game or forgot certain parts of it- pretty op new characters- after true end endings(will add more when i remember)dislikes :- straining my eyes on the salvation tower- translation feels kinda off/iffy at times, sometime making jokes lands pretty weirdly- no purification mini game like in the previous games, it feels like i need to work twice as hard to manage anyone from entering blood skelter mode but at the same time it does feel like its more forgiving even when the corruption almost near to the max- sometimes i see a few missing walls on the early towers (not game breaking though, so dont worry about that)(will add more when i remember)TLDR :i loved it, i would give it 8.5/10. despite having some problems when playing i still enjoy it very much since i love the series anyway, great ending to the series story.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally like how this game with how it ends and much more.Pros: More exploration since the dungeons are biggerDifferent Parties to go through the different chapters which is neat since not a lot of games that I play uses this mechanic and it makes it more funMore uses for the girls during the chapters as in MS2 whenever you get a girl or more their use in the skills during the time wondering the dungeon is only limited to that dungeon where in MSF its expanded and more frequent in almost every area which is goodYou really gotta think things through and explore the area to get the stuff you need where in MSN and MS2 you just ram yourself at the nearest wall to progress to the next place or just fight an enemy or to do itThe Dustbins are really useful since you can give items to different parties which I loveCons:There is a couple of issues that I noticed:One of which is the XP and Grinding, Jesus its horrible, absolutely God awful, I can't stand it, I cannot begin to say how horrible it is, took me 3+ hours to gain 30+ levels just so I won't lose any of my party members, and this is on Nightmare Mode, somehow you made getting XP horrible. I have no clue why but you collectively decided to make XP quite low and I personally hate it, its a living nightmare trying to them to a good level just to progress. Its to the point where I am forced to be on Easy Mode because Grinding XP on Easy would give me the same amount like it would give me on Nightmare and Normal more. Please fix this issue, its awful, just awful.The game runs poorly, movement does not run smoothly at all, like there is a significant delay in how you move in the game, even when in combat whether against Nightmares or Marchens. Its so bad that I had step away from the game several times just because of how insufferable it is. Its as if it is lagging and by no means my PC is slow, it is pretty damn decent  if not better at running almost every game I have on Steam, but somehow it runs like a Sloth if I play MSF.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, I really liked the 1st game, I played it back then on PS4. Then kuSony censored the f*ck out of the 2nd game, destroying it in process. I thought with Finale I could catch up on story I missed in the 2nd game then enjoy the game but no.The structure of the game is gimmicky to say the least. It's basically managing 3 whole parties with different characters that each have their own progression obviously. The feeling of progression is all over the place even though we can jump to any team at any time, most of the time (except when the story progress prevents it). It's like playing 3 sub stories at once at as far as I know, they don't really meet up (gameplay wise) even at the end of the game so there's no way to make that one team with only the characters we like unless they happen to be in the same team. I don't think it's a bad game, I've played much worse JRPG but this is definitely not for me. So I personally don't recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: This one is a love and hate mixed bag, but in the end, that's a thumb up:Multi-party crawler, with active party switching. You must switch from time to time in order to progress. It can get messy ^^ (more on this below).Exploration with active skills: Each character has a special skill usable during exploration such as a short teleportation or the ability to destroy obstacles. Unsettling environments (maze themes and monsters are truly unique, no spoiler).Multi-layered combat system: Managing Hit Points and Mana is just the tip of the ice cream cone.Each character also has a rage meter to manage and dungeons have shifting parameters you have to keep in check.Did i mention elemental resistances and traps activating even during combat?Character evolution is pretty solid, from class change to gear enhancement, there's a lot to do.What i didn't enjoy is the early game filled with poorly translated VN sections that don't bring context nor lore.Party switching is great "on paper" but it can really get confusing at times and people who do not want to manage multiple parties shouldn't get this one as there is no way to "leave x group" to the AI.The affinity system consisting on gifting stuff to characters so they like their leader a bit more is time consuming imho.I see zero appeal there but it requires a lot of clicks to get through.Graphics aren't that sharp with the switch port and some UI portions require way too many clicks/key strokes.Thumb up because of the crawling section and unusual monsters and themes along with character evolution/customization.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a negative review, but a mixed one. If you like the franchise, you can still enjoy it, but stick to play on Easy (which is not as easy as you may think) and enjoy the ending of this story.Going for the review, I get what they were trying to do for this game, and the idea in itself wasn't bad, but there are a couple of design choices that make this game a pain in the arse to navigate and enjoy:- Resources and Exp are halved compared to previous games: there is no other way around this, I am at Chapter 4 last floor, and I finally reached level 30~. Even normal enemies are a pain to deal with due to my low damage + low SP compared to their HP. It took me a while to get enough blood for some job changes, and I struggle to have enough Skill slots unlocked for my teams until chapter 4 approx.- Bad map designs: They have gone out of their way to design some maps as annoyingly as possible, having doors requiring keys from other teams just to not have a sharing box anywhere nearby (kudos for adding a shortcut immediately after opening the door). Even worse was the one time that one key needed to be send to Thumbelina first to minimize it, then to another team to use... BS!!- Unless for key items, chests are worthless (same issue as MS2): Farming gives such good rewards comparing to whatever you find on the shop or a chest that you don't actively care anymore. If they had at least weapons with elements and abilities on those chests, it could be worth it, but half the time I don't even care. They could have improved the Factory to be able to give abilities to weapons, but nah.- English translation is mediocre and even wrong at times. Some characters get gender bent or mixed up in certain dialogues, some skills don't make what they say they do (it's a bit better nowadays, but the dialogues are asinine half the time).- Salvation Tower was badly coloured and optimized: Leaving aside the extremely white environment with the random nooses hanging from the ceiling filling the map to the point you cannot tell what they are. Not sure what happened, but when my resolution was at 1080p, all maps were alright until I reached Salvation tower... then my framerate when to ♥♥♥♥, and the game started slowing down. At least the area was more enjoyable once I changed the in-game resolution to 720p.- When a character enters Blood Skelter they attack themselves: This is more or less a rant, but is BS lore-wise. During MS2, Cinderella and other Blood Maidens stayed in Bloody Skelter for several years surviving alone which is in itself was a plot point at the time. How come they allowed characters in Blood Skelter to attack themselves? Even with AoE attacks, that's still stupid. Rage /= suicidal.Again, not a fully negative review, the game still has a good amount of positives, but I started feeling the frustration accumulate while playing on Normal due to a couple of unexpected wipes and loss of progress. Would have be more welcome with an auto-save feature I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is okay, focuses much more on mechanical dungeon crawling than story for the most part. Some of the new characters are interesting, some aren't.The reason I'm giving this a negative review is due to one singular stupid bug. If your audio device switches at any point during your play session (your headphones die, something gets unplugged, etc) you are now unable to save your game. If you attempt to save your game anyway, you softlock. This wouldn't be a big deal if MS had the decency to put any sort of auto save into the game. But given that the "Can't save" Jail Trial is so valuable it's easy to go an hour or more without saving, and then lose that to a bug that is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ easy to fix.

_childDocuments_.review:
Jail - a living prison for humans, buried 666 meters underground.

A group of prisoners, Jack and the Blood Maidens, were reincarnations of fairy tales who dared to escape. They climbed from the bottom of the tower up to the surface, filled with hope...

But outside were thousands of corpses soaking in a sea of blood. There stood beings known as Massacre Pink, smiling.

In that moment, hope was destroyed. 

Separated, they are each drawn to the devouring Jail that floats in the sky...

This is the finale to the tale of the Blood Maidens.
